mtha' dag ri yi bdag po'i shar ni dag pa'i in+d+ra nI la lho ni pad+ma rA ga ste/ / nub ni ka rbe ta ni ser po byang ni ri bong 'dzin pa ltar dkar zla ba chu shel lo/ / dbus ni ljang gu[8] / zhes gsungs pa ltar lhun po'i dbus shar lho nub byang rnams rim pa bzhin ljang gu dang sngo nag dang dmar po dang ser po dang dkar po yin zhing / dbyibs ni zlum por lnga dang ldan pa rtsa ba phra la rtse mo rgya che ba'o/ / de la rwa lnga'i gnas tshul la 'dod pa mi 'dra ba mang na'ang 'dir don la gnas pa'i phyogs shig brjod par bya ste/

What is the color and shape of Meru, home of some of the gods of desire? In the Gnosis chapter it says:
This emperor of mountains, on the east is pure indranīla, on the south ruby, the west is yellow, the north, like the moon, is white crystal, the center is green.[13] As this quote indicates, the center, east, south, west, and north are green, blue, red, yellow, and white respectively. The shape of Meru is circular, and it has five horns that are slender at the base but with large tips. There are many differing assertions about these horns, but I will write of something approaching the truth. /56/

d.div: [8] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka169_118_ba4
[13] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, v. 169, 118b4.

f.d: rwa zlum po 'og ma bzhi lhun po la ske rags bcings pa'i tshul du bskor ba ste/ de yang rwa 'og ma thur la 'phyang nas 'khor ba dang rtsa ba'i 'gram stegs lta bu'i khor yug gi phyi mtha' mnyam zhing rwa 'og ma de'i mtshams nas ri rab gyi rtse bar la cha mnyam pa bzhir byas pa'i 'og ma gsum gyi cha re re'i mtshams nas rwa re re 'phyang ba/ de yang 'og ma las steng ma rnams rgya je che je cher song ba sder 'gag kha 'phyang chung ngu'i steng du chen po brtsegs pa lta bu'o/ / rwa lnga pa steng ma ni ri rab kyi rtse dang khad mnyam pa phyogs rnams su phyi la bsil ri'i thod bar gyes pa kha 'phyang gi rtse bsil ri'i rtse mo la reg pa'o/ / rwa steng ma bzhi'i khongs skyibs kyi nang na gling drug mtsho drug ri lnga dang bcas pa gnas so/ / de lta bu'i ri rab kyi rtse mo'i mtha' gcig nas mtha' cig shos kyi bar la dpag tshad stong phrag lnga bcu yod do/ /

The four lower circular horns girdle Meru like belts. The lowest horn hangs down like a platform as far as the outer rim of the immediate environs. The distance from the girdle of this lower horn to the peak of Meru is divided into four equal parts, and from the cusp of each of the first three parts a horn arches down. The girdling of these horns becomes progressively larger, like small bowls mounted by successively larger bowls. The topmost horn is at the level of the summit of Meru, spreading out into all directions and reaching down to touch the peaks of the Śīta Mountains. Included within the covering of the four upper horns are the six continents, six seas, and five mountain ranges. The diameter across the summit of Meru is fifty thousand yojana.

de ltar na 'grel chen las/
lhun po yi ni steng gi rgya shar dang nub dang byang dang lho'i cha'i bar du stong phrag lnga bcu'o/[9] / zhes dang /
steng gi rtse mo lnga po rnams ni sa gzhi'i gnas rnams la phyir son pa ste phyogs kun tu ni khor yug kyang ngo / / de'i phyi rol gling dang ri bo dag dang zhes pa ni khor yug de'i phyi rol rtse mo bzhi'i khongs skyibs kyi gnas su gling drug dang /[10] zhes sogs rnams kyang legs par drangs par 'gyur ro/ /

In the Great Commentary it says:
The size of the upper surface of Meru is fifty thousand between the east and west, north and south.[14] And:
Above, five points[15] reach out to the surfaces and in all directions to the environs also. “Outside of that the continents, mountains,” means that outside the environs of Meru, within the covering of the four tips, are the six continents.[16] These quotes also explain the point well.

d.div: [9] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 65_na4
[10] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 65_na4
[14] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 65a4.
[15] rtse mo.
[16] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 65a4.

f.d: de nas ri rab kyi rtse mo'i mgrin pa'i sum cha mar bzhag pa'i mtshams nas ya mtha'i bar cha bzhir phye ba'i cha re re ni rim pa bzhin dkar po'i bskal pa zhes pa'i ming can tshangs ris dang tshangs pa mdun na 'don dang tshangs chen dang 'od chung ba rnams kyi gnas dang / de bzhin du lhun po'i gdong la dpag tshad stong phrag lnga bcu yod pa la cha gsum du phye ba'i cha re la dpag tshad khri drug stong drug brgya drug cu re drug rgyang grags gnyis gzhu 'dom stong sum brgya so gsum khru gang sor brgyad rnams 'ong de'i cha de re la lhun po'i ko sko [11] dang sna dang dpral bar tha snyad byas pa'i ko sko'i [12] ma mtha' nas sna la thug gi bar la cha bzhir phye ba'i cha re re rim pa bzhin dpal gyi bskal ba zhes pa'i ming can tshad med 'od dang 'od gsal dang dge chung dang tshad med dge rnams kyi gnas dang / lhun po'i sna'i ma mtha' nas dpral pa'i ma mtha' la thug gi bar la cha bzhir phye ba'i cha re re rim pa bzhin tshangs pa'i 'jig rten las 'das pa zhes pa'i ming can dge rgyas dang sprin med dang bsod nams skyes dang 'bras bu che ba rnams kyi gnas dang / de bzhin du dpral ba'i ma mtha' nas gtsug tor gyi 'og la thug gi bar la cha bzhir phye ba'i cha re re rim pa bzhin tshangs pa'i bskal pa'i ming can mi che ba dang mi gdung ba dang shin tu mthong dang 'og min pa rnams kyi gnas so/ /

The throat of Meru, from the top of its lower third to the upper limit of the throat, is divided into four parts. These are known as the realms of the white eon and are the form realms Sphere of Brahmā, Chanting in the Presence of Brahmā, Great Realm of Brahmā, and Little Light. Similarly the 50,000-yojana face of Meru is divided into three parts, and each part is 16,666 yojana, two krośa, 1,333 armspans, one cubit, and eight fingerwidths. These three parts are known as the chin, nose, and forehead of Meru. The bottom of the chin to the nose is divided into four parts. These four are known as the glorious eon and comprise the form realms Limitless Light, Illuminating Light, Little Virtue, and Limitless Virtue. The lower limit of /57/ the nose to the lower limit of the forehead, known as beyond the world of Brahmā, is in four parts comprising the realms Vast Virtue, Without Cloud, Creation of Merit, and Great Fruition. Similarly the area from the lower limit of the forehead to the base of the crown is divided into four parts known as the eon of Brahmā, comprising the realms Lesser, Untroubled, Farsighted, and None Higher.

d.div: [11] ma dper ko sko gsal yang yongs grags rtsis gzhung rnams su kos ko zhes gsal ba bshad/
[12] ma dper ko sko'i gsal yang yongs grags rtsis gzhung rnams su kos ko'i zhes dgos nges lta bu snang /

f.d:
de bzhin du gtsug tor gyi 'og gi mtha' nas rtse'i bar la cha bzhir phye ba'i cha re re rim pa bzhin chos bzang bskal pa zhes pa'i ming can nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched dang rnam shes mtha' yas skye mched dang ci yang med pa'i skye mched dang 'du shes med 'du shes med min gyi skye mched de gzugs med khams pa rnams kyi gnas so/ / 'dir 'grel chen las/
chos bzang gi sgras ni gzugs med pa'i srid pa zhes brjod do|_|bskal pa zhes pa ni gang du lha rnams tshe bskal par gnas pa'o/[13] / zhes gsungs pa ltar 'og ma rnams la yang shes par bya'o/ /

The base of the crown to its tip is also divided into four parts. These are known as the eon of pure dharma and comprise the formless realms, namely Source of Limitless Space, Source of Limitless Consciousness, Source of Nothingness, and Source of No Recognition Yet No Nonrecognition. On the formless realms the Great Commentary says:
“Pure dharma” refers to the formless existence. “Eon” refers to the length of time the gods remain there.[17] The form realms can be understood similarly.

d.div: [13] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 23_ba6
[17] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 23b6.

f.d: de ltar na gzugs med kyi gnas bzhi re re'i ya mtha' nas 'og gi ma mtha'i bar la dpag tshad drug stong nyis brgya lnga bcu re dang / gzugs khams gnas ris bcu drug gi gnas re re'i ya mtha' nas rang rang gi 'og gi ma mtha'i bar la dpag tshad bzhi stong brgya drug cu re drug rgyang grags gnyis gzhu 'dom stong sum brgya so gsum khru gang sor brgyad re rnams su 'gyur ro/ / gal te gzugs med kyi gnas bzhi 'og min gyi gong dang / kho rang bzhi la yang bla 'og gis phye ba'i khyad par de ltar yod na 'dod khams lta bu nas tshe 'phos nas gzugs med khams su skye ba'i tshe bar do yod dgos par 'gyur te/ 'dod khams su 'chi srid grub nas de'i rjes su 'og min gyi gong dpag tshad 'bum phrag gcig dang bdun khri lnga stong gi sar skye srid len pa la 'chi srid dang skye srid kyi bar du bar do brgyud dgos pa'i phyir te/ 'bru yi rgyun dang chos mthun phyir/[14] /zhes gsungs pa ltar yin pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod par mi nus te/ chos mngon pa'i mdo dang bstan bcos rnams las gzugs med khams su skye ba la bar do med par bshad pas so/ / de ltar na gzugs med bzhi'i gnas 'og min gyi gong na bla 'og gi khyad par dang bcas par gsungs pa'i dgongs pa de gang yin snyam na/ dogs pa'i gnas de ltar 'ong ba bden na'ang / de'i dogs sel cung zad tsam zhig brjod par bya ste/

Each of the formless realms, therefore, measures 6,250 yojana from top to bottom. Each of the sixteen form realms, from its upper to its lower limit, measures 4,166 yojana, two krośa, 1,333 armspans, one cubit, and eight fingerwidths. If the four formless realms are actually positioned above the form realm of None Higher, and if these four are also arranged above and below each other, then migration from an existence such as the desire realm to the formless realm would require a bardo existence. This is because, between the state of death in the desire realm and the taking of birth in realms above None Higher, which begin at 175,000 yojana above the earth, there must be a continuation between death in one state and birth in another in the form of an intermediate state, “like the growth of corn.”[18] However this cannot be accepted. The Abhidharma teachings and commentaries state that birth in the formless realms requires no bardo. So what is the thinking behind the statement that the four formless realms are positioned above the form realm of None Higher and are also arranged on top of one another? /58/ These doubts do occur. However I will write a little in order to dispel them.

d.div: [14] sde dge_4089_bstan/ mngon pa/ kuchos mngon pa mdzod/ gnas/ 3_sh+loka11_7_na6

[18] Toh 4089 Tengyur, mngon pa, ku, gnas 3, v. 11, 7a6. As there is an intervening period of germination in the growth of corn from seed, so there must be an intermediate state or bardo when rebirth is from place to place.

f.d: de yang / gzugs med gang du shi ba'i 'o/[15] /zhes pa ltar khams 'og ma gnyis nas shi 'phos te gzugs med du skye ba'i tshe gang du shi ba'i sa de nyid du skye ba len pa yin pas gzugs med du skye ba la skye srid dang de'i sngon ma'i 'chi srid kyi bar du bar do brgyud mi dgos pa yin pas mngon pa'i mdo sogs las gzugs med du skye ba la bar do med par gsungs pa yin pas gzugs med kyi gnas rnams 'og min gyi gong na bla 'og gis phye ba'i tshul gyis yod na gzugs med du skye ba la de'i sngon du bar do dgos pa bden na'ang / rgyud 'grel 'dir 'og min gyi gong na gzugs med pa bzhi la gnas bla 'og gi khyad par bshad pa ni khams gsum gyi sems can la skye ba mthong ba'i rim pa yod pa ltar gang du skye ba'i gnas la yang rim pa yong ba'i dbang du byas na 'di ltar 'thob bo zhes gzugs khams kyi gnas las gong du brgal ba'i nam mkha' la thob thang brtsis pa'i tshad rnam par bzhag nas phyi nang sbyor ba'i dgos pa'i dbang gis gsungs pa tsam yin gyi/ dngos gnas la chos mngon pa nas bshad pa ltar gzugs med bzhi la gnas bla 'og gis phye ba 'og min las gong du brgal ba na yod par khas mi len pa'am/

“The formless is at the place of death.”[19] This quote from the Abhidhamakośa explains that when migrating from the two lower realms to the formless realms, rebirth occurs at the very place of death. Therefore, to take birth in the formless realm, an intermediate continuum of a bardo between the state of birth and the previous death state is not necessary. Because of this the Abhidharma teachings say that for birth in the formless realms, there is no bardo. It is true that if the formless realms were actually above the realm of None Higher and were stacked on top of one another, then taking birth in a formless realm would necessarily require a bardo existence. However the reason for the assertion in this tantra and its commentaries that the four formless realms are above None Higher and are stacked on top of each other is that, just as there are levels of birth for the sentient beings of the three realms, so there are levels of birthplaces. On that basis to say, “I will attain this level” is to give these realms their own measurable status by positing them in space above the form realms, which is then used for the practice of outer and inner correspondence. However, in actuality, and as it is stated in the Abhidharmakośa, four formless realms divided into higher and lower and positioned above and beyond None Higher are not accepted.

d.div: [15] sde dge_4089_bstan/ mngon pa/ kuchos mngon pa mdzod/ gnas/ 2_sh+loka15_4_ba2
[19] Toh 4089 Tengyur, mngon pa, ku, gnas 2, v. 15, 4b2.

f.d: yang na 'di ltar du bshad par bya ste/ mngon pa sogs nas gzugs med khams su skye ba la bar do med par bshad pa ni rtsa ba gzugs med khams pa'i sems can la gzugs med pa la thug pa yin la/ de yang / gzugs med pa na gzugs med do/[16] /zhes bshad pa ltar phar phyin theg pa'i dgongs pa la gzugs med khams pa'i sems can la gzugs med pa yin yang / bla med kyi rgyud sde'i dgongs pa la gzugs med khams pa'i sems can la yang gzugs yod pa yin te/ gsang ba 'dus pa sogs kyi rgyud pa'i dgongs 'grel dang bcas pa rnams las sems can thams cad la shin tu phra ba'i rlung sems yod par bshad cing rlung de yang 'od zer lnga par bshad pas gzugs med khams pa'i sems can la gzugs phung tsam yod par ma zad kha dog sngo ser la sogs pa'i gzugs kyi skye mched kyang yod pa dang /

There is, however, an alternative explanation. The teachings of the Abhidharma and so forth, which state that birth in the formless realms has no preceding intermediate state, rest upon the premise that a being of the formless realm is without form. As it says, “Because there is no form, there is formlessness.”[20] Therefore, in the thinking of the Perfection Vehicle, sentient beings of the formless realms are without form. However the position of highest tantra is that beings of the formless realms do have form, because according to the tantras and commentaries of Guhyasamāja and others, every sentient being possesses the very subtle mind and the very subtle wind. Moreover, this subtle wind is explained as being of five-colored light rays. Therefore, not only do beings of the formless realms possess the aggregate of form, they also possess source forms such as blue, yellow, and so forth.

d.div: [16] sde dge_4090_bstan/ mngon pa/ kumadzod rang 'grel/ gnas/ 3_110_na1
[20] Toh 4089 Tengyur, mngon pa, ku, gnas 3, 110a1.

f.d:
gzhan yang rgyud 'grel 'di nyid las khams lnga'i rdul phra rab dang khu ba phra mo yang yod par bshad de/[17] mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus las/
gzugs med pa'i ris rnams kyi lus ni stong pa'i khams kyi bdag nyid can sems kyi bag chags tsam ste sgra'i yon tan gyi bdag nyid can no/[18] / zhes gzugs med pa'i lus sgra'i yon tan gcig bu gtso bor ldan pa'i nam mkha'i khams kyi bdag nyid du gsungs nas

Moreover, in the Kālacakra Tantra and its commentaries, /59/ it is explained that these beings also possess the subtle particles of the five elements. In the Gnosis chapter, in the Supreme and Unchanging Gnosis summary, it says:
The bodies of those of the formless realms are of the element of emptiness, as mere potentials within the mind and of the quality of sound.[21] This says that the bodies of formless beings possess sound alone as their primary quality and are of the nature of the space element.

d.div: [17] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 419_ba1
[18] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 419_ba3
[21] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 419b1.

f.d:
de nyid kyi 'phro las/
khu ba yang sa dang chu dang me dang rlung dang dri dang gzugs dang ro dang reg bya'i yon tan spangs pa'o/[19] / zhes gzugs med khams pa'i sems can gyi khu ba yang sa chu me rlung dri gzugs ro reg bya ste 'byung ba'i khams dang 'byung gyur bzhi gtso bor mi ldan par gsungs nas

The quote continues :
Moreover fluid is without earth, water, fire, air, smell, form, taste, and tangibility.[22] This states that the fluid of beings of the formless realms does not possess in primary form the elements of earth, water, fire, and air, as well as the four element-derived forms.

d.div: [19] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 419_ba4
[22] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 419b4.

f.d:
de'i 'phro nyid las/
sa la sogs pa bzhi po 'di rnams kyi gtso bo'i yon tan 'di la phal pa tsam gyi yon tan yod de rnam pa gzhan du na tshogs pa'i yon tan rnams med par yon tan gcig las 'khor ba'i bag chags su mi 'gyur ro/[20] / zhes sa chu me rlung bzhi dang de bzhi'i yon tan ni gzugs sogs bzhi ste brgyad po de gzugs med khams kyi sems can rnams kyi khu ba'i thig le la phal pa'i tshul gyis ldan par bshad la/ de yang 'byung bzhi sogs dang khu ba'i rdul phra mo zhad tsam yod pa la dgongs pa ste 'dus pa sogs kyi dgongs pa bkral ba rnams las kyang sems can thams cad kyi rgyud la skad cig kyang rgyun chad ma myong ba'i mi shigs pa'i khams dkar dmar rlung sems shin tu phra ba rnams tshogs pa gcig pa'i tshul gyis yod par gsungs shing / mi shigs pa zhes pa yang gang gis kyang gzhom du med pa'i don yin pas so/ /

The quote continues:
The primary qualities of these four, earth and so forth, exist as mere general qualities. Without a collection of qualities, the potentialities of samsara would not arise from one quality alone.[23] This explains that earth, water, fire, and air together with their qualities of form and so forth are present in the fluid drop of formless beings as qualities in general form only. This means that the four elements, their sense forms, and the subtle particle of fluid are to be understood as being in minuscule form. Also, in the explanations of tantras such as the Guhyasamāja, the indestructible red and white elements of the very subtle mind and wind exist together as a single unit, which has been present in the mindstreams of all beings without a moment of interruption since beginningless time. “Indestructible” means nothing can destroy it.

d.div: [20] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 419_ba4
[23] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 419b4.

f.d: de ltar na gzugs med khams pa'i sems can la mdo phyogs nas gzugs med par bshad kyang / gzugs yod pa rgyud dang 'grel chen sogs bla med kyi rgyud 'grel pa dang bcas pa'i dgongs pa yin pa bzhin du gzugs med bzhi'i gnas kyang 'og min gyi gong rol na steng 'og rim can du gnas par bshad pa sgra ji bzhin par bya rigs te/ gzhan du na 'jig rten gyi khams spyi'i tshad la dpag tshad 'bum phrag bzhi pa sogs snod kyi 'jig rten gyi tshad dbyibs dang / dmyal ba la sogs ba'i tshe tshad sogs mngon pa'i phyogs nas bshad pa dang ches mi 'dra ba rnams sgra ji bzhin par khas len pa ji ltar mi 'gal snyam du bsam dgos shing / 'chad tshul gnyis las ci zhig 'thad snyam du dpyad par bya'o/ /

Therefore, although beings of formless realms are said to be without form by the sutra tradition, it is the position of this tantra, the Great Commentary, as well as other highest tantras, that they do possess form. Similarly it is correct to accept as literal the statement that the four formless realms are above None Higher and are stacked one on top of another. Otherwise I would have to wonder how it could not be contradictory to accept as literal the other glaring differences with the Abhidharma tradition, such as the general size and shape of the world as being four hundred thousand yojana, the length of time spent in the hells, and so on. /60/ Which of the two above explanations is the more valid is something to be examined.

de ltar na rang cag rnams gnas pa'i gling bzhi pa'i snod gyi 'jig rten gyi tshad dbyibs sogs zhib par bshad nas 'di'i phyi rol gyi gnas tshul cung zad 'chad pa ni rgyud rtsa 'grel las/
de'i phyi rol stong pa gcig pu srid pa gsum bral yon tan med cing de nyid kyis dman pa'o/[21] /zhes pa ni 'og rlung gi dkyil 'khor dang steng gtsug tor te de'i phyi rol stong pa gcig pu ni rdul phra rab so so'i ngo bo khams lnga pa stong pa gcig pu'o/ / zhes rlung gi dkyil 'khor gyi 'og gi phyi rol dang ri rab kyi gtsug tor gyi steng gi phyi rol rnams ni sa khams sogs khams lnga'i rdul phra rab tshur mthong gi dbang po'i yul du ma gyur pa'i phan tshun 'dabs ma 'byar ba'i sil bur so sor gnas pa'i ngo bo stong pa gcig pu'i ming can gyi rang bzhin bar snang stong pa lta bur snang ba'o/ /

Having explained in detail the size, divisions, and so forth of our four-continent world realm, a little of the situation outside of that world will be explained. The Great Commentary says:
“Outside of that, only emptiness, no three worlds, no qualities, lacking all these.” This means that outside the air mandala, at the bottom and the crown at the top, is only emptiness. This emptiness is solely an entity of individual particles of the five elements.[24] Therefore, below the lower limit of the air mandala and above the upper limit of the crown, the subtle particles of the five elements of earth and so forth exist as individual and disconnected particles undetectable to the senses of ordinary beings. This is known as mere emptiness and appears as empty space.

d.div: [21] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ khams kyi le'u/ sh+loka10_23_ba3_sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 63_na5
[24] P2064 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ka-2, 67a3.

f.d: de ltar bshad pa'i shugs kyis gling bzhi pa'i 'jig rten 'di'i phyogs dang mtshams rnams kyi phyi rol yang stong pa gcig pu'i ming can khams lnga'i rdul phra rab sil bur gnas pa'i bar snang stong pa'i ngo bo yin par go nus so/ /

On the strength of this explanation, we can understand that beyond this four-continent world in the eight directions also lies the empty space of the disconnected particles of the five elements known as total emptiness.

('jig rten khams 'di'i phyi rol rdul phran 'dabs ma 'byar ba'i stong pa gcig bu 'di la mkhas pa 'ga' zhig_stong pa 'di la 'bum phrag gcig ste/ ye ler 'jig rten khams kyi tshad 'bum phrag lnga bshad pa 'di la dgongs pa ste/ dgos pa shes pa'i ma zin pa'i lus kyi cha shas skra sen sogs khru gang yod pa de spyod byed yin gsung /)

(Some scholars maintain the size of this emptiness of unconnected particles outside this world realm to be a hundred thousand yojana. They base this measurement on the Gnosis chapter, where it mentions the size of the world to be five hundred thousand yojana. They assert that the purpose is to include the one-cubit part of the body not grasped by consciousness, such as the nails and hair, as part of the basis of purification.)

stong pa gcig pu'i ming can rdul phra rab 'dabs ma 'byar ba sil bur gnas pa de rnams kyi phyi rol rnams na ni mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus las/
stong gcig ces bya ba ni mi mjed kyi 'jig rten gyi khams kyi dbus nas steng dang 'og tu stong phrag re re ste/ 'og dang steng bzhin du shar dang nub dang byang dang lho dang bden bral dang dbang ldan dngarlu nga dang mer ro/ / de bzhin du stong phrag gnyis dang gsum mo/ / de nas stong chen po zhes bya ba grangs med pa chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams rnams te/[22] zhes gsungs pa ltar rang cag rnams gnas pa'i mi mjed 'jig rten gyi khams 'di dbus

Existence outside of this total emptiness of disconnected and individual particles is spoken of in the Gnosis chapter in the Supreme and Unchanging Gnosis summary:
“One thousand” means that above and below the center of this saha[25] world realm are a thousand each. As above and below, so it is in the east, west, north, south, the unreal, the powerful, the air, and fire.[26] It is the same with the two and three thousand. Therefore, the great thousand refers to these countless world realms.[27] /61/

d.div: [22] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 428_ba4
[25] mi ’mjed pa. Epithet for our world meaning fearless or powerful, so called because there is no fear, meaning no fear of dharma practice. See Great Lexicon, p. 2068.
[26] unreal = southwest, the powerful = northeast, air = northwest, fire = southeast.
[27] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 428b4.

f.d: su byas pa'i phyogs bcu po re rer gling bzhi pa lta bu'i 'jig rten gyi khams stong stong gnas pa tshun chad stong gcig gi 'jig rten gyi khams dang / de rnams dang bcas pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams stong phrag gnyis gnyis gnas pa tshun chad ni stong gnyis pa bar ma'i 'jig rten dang / yang de rnams dang bcas pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams stong phrag gsum gsum tshun chad ni stong gsum gyi 'jig rten dang / de rnams dang bcas pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams grangs med pa chen po tshun chad ni stong chen mo'i 'jig rten gyi khams zhes bya ba ste de rnams gnas so/ / de nyid kyi phyir na/ kha cig (mkhas pa chen po bcom ldan rigs ral/)dus 'khor rgyud 'grel la stong gsum chad do zhes pa yang ma brtags pa'o/ /[23]

Therefore, with this saha world of ours as the center, there are a thousand four-continent worlds in each of the ten directions, and these worlds make up the thousand-world realm. Two thousand worlds at each of the ten directions, including the worlds of the thousand-world realm, make up the two thousand, or intermediate, world realm. Three thousand worlds at each of the ten directions, including the previous world realms, make up the three-thousand-world realm. The great thousand-world realm includes all these worlds and encompasses countless world realms. Therefore, although there are those (such as the great scholar Chomden Rikral)[28] who state that the Kālacakra Tantra and its commentaries omit mention of the three thousands, they have not investigated this.

d.div: [23] 'dir yig chung du bcom ldan rig ral gyi bzhed par ngos 'dzin mdzad kyang rig ral gyi gzhung ma brnyed/
[28] Thirteenth-century Kadampa master and opponent of the Kālacakra.

f.d:
'o na 'jig rten gyi khams dpag tshad 'bum phrag bzhi zhes bshad na/ dpag tshad kyi tshad ji lta bu snyam na/ bsdus rgyud las/
phra rab brgyad rnams kyis ni phra mo 'di gcig phra mo brgyad kyis sku yi rtse mo phra mo ste/[24] / zhes sogs gsungs pa ltar gzugs can rnams kyi chung mtha' mthar thug pa ni rdul phra rab yin zhing / de 'phreng bar brtsegs pa brgyad ni rdul phran gcig gi tshad dang / de 'phreng bar brtsegs pa brgyad ni skra'i rtse mo zlum po gcig gi tshad dang / skra rtse zlum po brgyad 'phreng bar brtsegs pa ni ske tshe'i tshad dang / ske tshe brgyad brtsegs pa shig gi tshad dang / shig brgyad brtsegs pa nas kyi tshad dang / nas brgyad brtsegs pa sor gyi tshad dang / sor nyi shu rtsa bzhi khru'i tshad dang/ khru bzhi gzhu 'dom gang gi tshad dang / gzhu 'dom stong phrag gnyis rgyang grags kyi tshad dang / rgyang grags bzhi dpag tshad kyi tshad yin no/ /

It is said that a world realm is four hundred thousand yojana across. But what is the length of a yojana? In the Condensed Tantra it says:
Eight most subtle make one subtle. Eight of the subtle make up the fine tip of a hair.[29] Therefore, according to this and further quotes, the ultimate diminution of form is the very subtle particle, and eight of them strung together is the linear measurement of one subtle particle. A string of eight subtle particles is the width of a hair at its tip. Eight hairbreadths are one black mustard seed, eight mustard seeds are one louse, eight lice make one barley grain, and eight such grains are one fingerwidth. Twenty-four fingerwidths are one cubit, four cubits are one armspan, two thousand armspans are one krośa, and four krośa make one yojana.[30]

d.div: [24] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ khams kyi le'u/ 1_sh+loka13_23_ba7_'gyur cung mi mthun/
[29] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, khams v. 13, 23b7/23a6.
[30] About nine miles, as compared to the Abhidharma yojana of about five miles.

f.d:
rgyud 'grel pa dang bcas pa'i skor 'dir 'jig rten gyi khams gzhan gyi rnam gzhag cher ma gsungs par snod kyi 'jig rten 'di nyid kyi tshad dbyibs sogs gsungs pa ni 'grel chen las/
de ltar thams cad yongs su mkhyen nas drang srong rnams yongs su smin par bya ba'i don du 'jig rten gyi khams kyi tshad dang lus kyi tshad dkyil 'khor gyi don du bcom ldan 'das kyis gsungs so/[25] / zhes gsungs pa ltar lha'i dkyil 'khor sgom pa'i sbyang gzhi phyi snod kyi 'jig rten dang nang sgrub pa po'i lus chos mthun sbyar ba'i ched dang / de gnyis chos mthun sbyor ba yang de gnyis kyi sbyong byed rten gyi dkyil 'khor de gnyis dang chos mthun par sgom pa'i ched du yin pas

This tantra and its commentaries do not deal a lot with other worlds but concentrate on the presentation of the dimensions of this world. The reason for this is spoken of in the Great Commentary:
And so, with omniscient knowledge, in order to ripen the ṛṣi, the Conqueror spoke of the dimensions of the world and the dimensions of the body for the purpose of the mandala.[31] /62/ The reasons, therefore, are firstly to bring about correspondence between the inner world of the practitioner’s body and the outer world, which form the two bases for purification in the deity mandala meditation, and secondly to bring about correspondence between these two bases of purification and the mandala itself, which is the actual purifier.

d.div: [25] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 60_ba4
[31] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 60b4.

f.d: snod kyi 'jig rten gyi tshad dang lus kyi tshad chos mthun sbyar bar bya ste/ snod kyi 'jig rten rlung gi 'og mtha'i nas lhun po'i gtsug tor gyi tha snyad byas pa'i rtse mo'i bar dpag tshad 'bum phrag bzhi yod pa/ lus kyi rkang mthil nas spyi gtsug gi bar la rang rang gi khru bzhi yod pa dang chos mthun/ snod kyi rlung gi dkyil 'khor gyi phyi mtha' nas phyi mtha' cig shos kyi bar dpag tshad 'bum phrag bzhi yod pa/ lus kyi lag pa g.yas kyi mdzub rtse nas g.yon gyi mdzub rtse'i bar khru bzhi yod pa dang chos mthun/ rlung gi 'og gi mtha' nas lhun po'i rtsa ba'i bar la dpag tshad 'bum phrag gnyis yod pa lus kyi rkang mthil nas dpyi'i bar la khru do yod pa dang chos mthun/ rlung gi 'og gi mtha' nas lhun po'i rtsa ba'i bar la dmyal ba'i gnas bdun dang gdengs can gyi gnas dang bcas pa'i brgyad du phye ba'i gnas re re la dpag tshad 'bum phrag gcig gi bzhi cha dpag tshad stong phrag nyer lnga nyer lnga yod pa dpyi nas rkang mthil gyi bar la khru do yod pa la cha brgyad du phye ba'i cha de la khru gang gi bzhi cha sor drug drug yod pa dang rim pa bzhin chos mthun/ lhun po la dpag tshad 'bum phrag gcig yod pa dpyi'i mtshams nas mgrin pa'i 'og gi bar gyi sgal tshig sa la khru gang yod pa dang chos mthun/ lhun po'i mgrin pa'i tha snyad byas pa'i 'thab bral sogs 'dod lha bzhi dang tshangs ris sogs bzhi'i gnas bsdoms pa la dpag tshad 'bum phrag gcig gi bzhi cha dpag tshad stong phrag nyer lnga yod pa lus kyi mgrin pa la khru gang gi bzhi cha sor drug yod pa dang chos mthun/ lhun po'i gdo+ong gi tha snyad byas pa'i tshad med 'od nas 'og min pa'i gnas kyi ya mtha' bar la dpag tshad 'bum phrag gcig gi phyed dpag tshad stong phrag lnga bcu yod pa lus kyi ko sko'i [26] ma mtha' nas dpral ba'i ya mtha' bar la khru gang gi phyed sor bcu gnyis yod pa dang chos mthun lhun po'i gtsug tor gyi tha snyad byas pa'i rtsa ba nas rtse'i bar gyi gzugs med bzhi'i tshad la dpag tshad 'bum phrag gcig gi bzhi cha dpag tshad stong phrag nyer lnga yod pa lus kyi skra mtshams nas spyi bo'i bar la khru gang gi bzhi cha sor drug yod pa dang chos mthun/ zhing khams gong ma'i lha gnas de rnams la lhun po'i mgrin pa dang gdong dang gtsug tor gyi tha snyad 'dogs pa'i rgyu mtshan yang nang lus kyi mgrin pa sogs dang chos mthun sbyar ba'i ched du yin no/ /

The dimensions of the outer world, therefore, are given to correspond with the dimensions of the body. From the lower limit that is the base of the air mandala to the tip of the crown of Meru is a distance of four hundred thousand yojana. This corresponds to the distance of four cubits from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head of a person. The distance across the air mandala from rim to rim is four hundred thousand yojana. This corresponds to the distance of four cubits between the fingertips of the right hand and the fingertips of the left. From the lower limit of the air mandala to the base of Meru is a distance of two hundred thousand yojana, corresponding to the two-cubit distance between the soles of the feet and the hips. The lower limit of the air mandala to the base of Meru is divided into seven hell locations[32] and one nāga realm, each realm occupying a quarter of a hundred thousand, or twenty-five thousand, yojana. This corresponds to the distance of two cubits between the hips and the soles of the feet, which is divided into eight sections, each section being a quarter of a cubit or six fingerwidths. Meru itself is one hundred thousand yojana. This corresponds to the spine, which stretches the distance of one cubit from the hips to the base of the throat. The four desire realms, Free of Conflict and so forth, and the first four form realms of Sphere of Brahmā and so forth stretch for twenty-five thousand yojana up the throat of Meru. This corresponds to the measurement of the throat, which is a quarter of a cubit or six fingerwidths. From Limitless Light to None Higher upon the face of Meru is a distance of half of one hundred thousand yojana, corresponding to the distance of half a cubit, or twelve fingerwidths, from the base of the chin to the upper limit of the forehead. The span of the formless realms from the base of the crown of Meru to its tip is a quarter of one hundred thousand yojana, which corresponds to the distance of a quarter cubit, or six fingerwidths, from the hairline to crown of the head. The reason that these higher god realms are called the throat, face, and /63/ crown of Meru is to match them with the corresponding parts of the body.

d.div: [26] ma dper ko sko'i gsal yang yongs grags rtsis gzhung ltar na kos ko'i zhes bkod na legs pa mngon/
[32] There are actually eight hell realms and seven hell locations. The Vajra Flame hell and the Crying hell share the lower half of the air mandala.

f.d: yang lhun po'i dbus nas g.yas kyi sa'i dkyil 'khor gyi mtha' tshun chad la dpag tshad 'bum phrag gcig gi phyed dpag tshad stong phrag lnga bcu yod pa lus kyi brang gi dbus nas g.yas kyi dpung mgo tshun la khru gang gi phyed sor bcu gnyis yod pa dang chos mthun/ de nas lhun po'i g.yas phyogs kyi chu'i dkyil 'khor gyi kha zheng dpag tshad 'bum phrag gcig gi phyed dpag tshad stong phrag lnga bcu yod pa ni lag pa g.yas kyi dpung pa la khru gang gi phyed sor bcu gnyis yod pa dang chos mthun/ de bzhin du lhun po'i g.yas phyogs kyi me'i dkyil 'khor gyi kha zheng la dpag tshad stong phrag lnga bcu yod pa lag pa g.yas pa'i lag ngar la khru gang gi phyed sor bcu gnyis yod pa dang chos mthun/ yang lhun po'i g.yas phyogs kyi rlung gi dkyil 'khor gyi kha zheng la dpag tshad 'bum phrag gnyis kyi phyed dpag tshad stong phrag lnga bcu yod pa g.yas kyi lag mgo'i rtsa ba nas sor rtse bar la khru gang gi phyed sor bcu gnyis yod pa dang chos mthun no/ / des lhun po dang lus kyi g.yon phyogs rnams chos mthun sbyor tshul yang shes par bya'o/ /

The distance from the center of Meru to the righthand outer rim of the earth mandala is half of one hundred thousand, or fifty thousand, yojana. This corresponds to the measurement of half a cubit, or twelve fingerwidths, from the center of the chest to the edge of the right shoulder. The thickness of the water mandala on the right of Meru is half one hundred thousand, or fifty thousand, yojana. This corresponds to the half cubit, or twelve-fingerwidth, length of the right upper arm. Similarly the thickness of the fire mandala on the right side of Meru is fifty thousand yojana, corresponding to the half cubit, or twelve fingerwidth, length of the right forearm from the wrist to the elbow. The thickness of the air mandala on the right of Meru is half one hundred thousand, or fifty thousand, yojana. This corresponds to the half-cubit distance from the wrist to the fingertips of the right hand. The same correspondence can be applied to the left side of Meru and the left side of the body.
nang bcud kyi sems can spyi'i rnam gzhag bshad pa/
5. The Inhabitants of This World
gnyis pa der gnas pa'i bcud kyi sems can spyi'i rnam gzhag bshad pa

d.i: A general presentation of the inhabitants of this world

f.d: ['di ]la gsum/ sems can ris so so'i grangs bstan pa dang / sems can de rnams so so'i tshe tshad bshad pa dang / sems can de rnams su skye ba'i rgyu bshad pa'o/ /
This is under three headings: 1. The kinds of sentient beings 2. Their life spans 3. Causes for their birth
dang po [sems can ris so so'i grangs ]ni

rgyud las/
srid pa sum cu rtsa gcig rnams kyis 'dir ni srid gsum du 'gyur/ /[27] zhes gsungs pa ltar srid pa sum cu rtsa gcig ste lha ma yin dang mi dang dud 'gro dang yi dwags dang dmyal ba dang / 'dod lha drug ste rgyal chen ris bzhi pa dang sum cu rtsa gsum pa dang 'thab bral ba dang dga' ldan pa dang 'phrul dga' ba dang gzhan 'phrul dbang byed pa ste de rnams ni 'dod pa'i srid pa bcu gcig go/ / gzugs kyi khams kyi lha ni bcu drug ste tshangs ris pa dang tshangs pa mdun na 'don dang tshangs chen pa dang / 'od chung ba dang tshad med 'od pa dang 'od gsal ba dang / dge chung ba dang tshad med dge ba dang dge rgyas pa dang / sprin med pa dang bsod nams skyes pa dang 'bras bu che ba dang / mi che ba dang mi gdung ba dang shin tu mthong ba pa dang 'og min pa'o/ / gzugs med pa'i srid pa'i lha ni bzhi ste nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched pa dang rnam shes mtha' yas skye mched pa dang ci yang med pa'i skye mched pa dang 'du shes med 'du shes med min pa'i skye mched pa'o/ / srid pa sum cu rtsa gcig po rnams bsdus na 'dod pa'i srid pa gzugs kyi srid pa gzugs med pa'i srid pa ste srid pa gsum dang 'dod khams gzugs khams gzugs med khams te khams gsum dang / sa 'og sa steng sa bla gsum du yang 'gyur ro/ /

The Condensed Tantra says:
The thirty-one existences combine into three.[33] The thirty-one existences are: asuras, humans, animals, ghosts, hells, the /64/ six celestial desire realms, comprising Realm of the Four Great Monarchs, Heaven of Thirty-Three, Free of Conflict, Joyful, Magical Creations at Will, and Using at Will Creations of Others. These make up the eleven desire realms. The sixteen gods of the form realms are those of Sphere of Brahmā, Chanting in the Presence of Brahmā, Great Realm of Brahmā, Little Light, Limitless Light, Illuminating Light, Little Virtue, Limitless Virtue, Vast Virtue, Without Cloud, Creation of Merit, Great Fruition, The Lesser, Untroubled, The Farsighted, and None Higher. The formless realms are made up of Source of Limitless Space, Source of Limitless Consciousness, Source of Nothingness, and Source of No Recognition Yet No Nonrecognition. These thirty-one can be condensed into the three existences of desire, form, and formless, the three realms of desire, form, and formless, or to the three levels below, on, and above the earth.

d.div: [27] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ khams kyi le'u/ 1_sh+loka15_24_na3_'gyur cung mi mthun/
[33] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, khams v. 15, 24a3.

f.d: gnyis pa sems can de rnams so so'i tshe tshad bshad pa

['di ]la lnga/ dmyal ba klu dang bcas pa'i tshe tshad dang / 'dod lha rnams kyi tshe tshad dang / gzugs khams pa rnams kyi tshe tshad dang / gzugs med khams pa rnams kyi tshe tshad dang / tshe tshad gzhan gyi bshad tshul la dwogs pa dpyad pa'o/ /

This is under five headings: 1. Life span of hell beings and nāgas 2. Life span of the desire realm gods 3. Life span of the form realm gods 4. Life span of the formless realm gods 5. Resolving doubts concerning life spans within other realms
dang po [dmyal ba klu dang bcas pa'i tshe tshad ]ni

d.i: Life span of hell beings and nāgas

f.d: gseg ma'i chu'i dmyal ba pa dang klu rnams kyi tshe tshad ni bskal pa chung ngu gcig gi tshad do/ / dmyal ba gnyis pa bye ma'i chu dang gsum pa 'dam gyi chu'i dmyal ba pa gnyis kyi tshe tshad ni bskal pa bar ma'i tshad dang / de bzhin du dmyal ba bzhi pa mi bzad pa'i du ba dang lnga pa me'i dmyal ba pa gnyis kyi tshe tshad ni mchog gi bskal pa'i tshad do/ / dmyal ba drug pa mun pa chen po dang bdun pa ngu 'bod chen po pa gnyis kyi tshe tshad ni bskal pa chen po'i tshad dang / dmyal ba brgyad pa rdo rje'i me lce dang bcas pa ni 'jig rten gyi khams sdud pa'i bar gyi tshe'o/ /

The life span of beings in the hell of Gravel Water and of the nāgas is one short eon. The life span for the second and third hells known, as Sandy Water and Swamps, is one intermediate eon. Beings of the hell of Endless Smoke and the hell of Fire have a life span of one supreme eon, while those in the sixth and seventh hells, known as the hell of Great Darkness and the hell of Crying, live a life of one great eon. The life span of the eighth hell, called Vajra Flame, is for as long as the world realm exists. /65/
gnyis pa ['dod lha rnams kyi tshe tshad ]

d.i: Life span of the desire realm gods

f.d: rgyal chen ris bzhi nas gzhan 'phrul dbang byed kyi bar gyi 'dod lha drug gi tshe tshad ni 'og nas rim pa bzhin bskal pa chung ngu gcig nas bskal pa chung ngu drug gi bar rim pa bzhin yin no/ /
These six realms from the Four Great Monarchs to Using at Will the Creations of Others enjoy life spans ranging from one short eon to six short eons respectively.
gsum pa [gzugs khams pa rnams kyi tshe tshad ]

d.i: Life span of the form realm gods

f.d:
gzugs khams kyi tshangs ris nas 'og min pa'i bar bcu drug gi tshe tshad ni 'grel chen las/
de ltar na gzugs can rnams kyi bskal pa bcu drug ste bskal pa bcu drug nas brtsams te bskal pa re re'i bar gyi tshe'o/[28] / zhes gsungs pa ltar tshangs ris pa'i tshe tshad bskal pa gcig yin pa nas 'og min pa'i tshe tshad bskal pa bcu drug yin pa'i bar sbyar bar bya zhing 'di'i bskal pa yang bskal pa chung ngu ma yin te/ gzhan 'phrul dbang byed pa'i tshe tshad bskal pa chung ngu drug tu bshad pas tshangs ris pa gzhan 'phrul dbang byed pa las tshe ring dgos pa'i phyir ro/ / bskal pa chen po yang ma yin te/ 'og min pas 'di nas bshad pa'i bskal pa 'di bcu drug thub par bshad cing srid rtse ba'i tshe tshad bskal chen bzhir bshad pas 'og min pa las srid rtse ba tshe ring dgos pa'i phyir ro/ / des na 'di'i bskal pa la bskal pa bzhi po'i nang gi 'di yin gyi gsal kha ma byung yang bskal pa bar ma dang bskal pa mchog gnyis gang rung yin par bya dgos shing / de yang mi che ba nas 'og min pa'i bar 'phags pa'i gnas bzhi'i tshe tshad 'jal ba'i bskal pa rnams mchog gi bskal pa dang / tshangs ris sogs gzhan rnams kyi tshe tshad 'jal ba'i bskal pa bskal pa bar ma la byed pa 'thad dam snyam mo/ /

The life span of the sixteen realms from Sphere of Brahmā to None Higher are spoken of in the Great Commentary:
Therefore the sixteen eons of the form realms range from sixteen eons to one eon.[34] Life span ranges from one eon for Sphere of Brahmā to sixteen for None Higher. These eons are not short eons, because the life span of Using at Will the Creations of Others is explained as being six short eons, and Sphere of Brahmā must have a longer life span than Using at Will the Creation of Others. They cannot be great eons either, because beings of None Higher have been explained as having a life span of sixteen eons, whereas the Peak of Existence[35] has been explained as enjoying a life span of four great eons, and the Peak of Existence must have a longer life span that None Higher. Therefore, although it is not stated which of the four kinds of eons these eons refer to, it must be either intermediate or supreme eons. My opinion is that the eons used to measure the life spans of the four ārya abodes from the Lesser to None Higher must be supreme eons, and those used to measure the life spans of the other form realms must be intermediate eons.

d.div: [28] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 63_na1
[34] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 63a1.
[35] srid rtse. Another term for the highest formless realm.

f.d:
'o na bskal pa mchog dang bskal pa chen po don gcig pa min nam de gnyis so sor byed pa gang las shes snyam na/ de gnyis so sor byed pa ni 'grel chen las gsal bar gsungs te de yang 'grel chen las/
klu'i 'jig rten dang por bsod nams kyi stobs dang dmyal ba'i gnas dang por sdig pa'i stobs kyis bskal pa chung ngu'i tshe'o/ / dmyal ba'i gnas gnyis pa dang gsum par bskal pa bar ma'i tshe'o/ / dmyal ba'i gnas bzhi pa dang lnga par bskal pa mchog gi tshe'o/ / dmyal ba'i gnas drug pa dang bdun par bskal pa chen po'i tshe'o/[29] / zhes bskal pa la chung ngu bar ma mchog chen po bzhir gsungs nas mchog gi bskal pa'am bskal pa mchog gi ming can de bskal pa bar ma las che ba dang bskal pa chen po las chung bar gsungs pas so/ /

But aren’t the terms “supreme eon” and “great eon” synonyms? Where is it taught that they are different? That these two are different is clearly stated in the Great Commentary:
The first world of nāgas and the first realm of hell, by the power of virtue and evil respectively, have life spans of one short eon. The second and third hell both have life spans of an intermediate eon. In the fourth and fifth hells the life spans are of one supreme eon. In the sixth and seventh life is for one great eon.[36] This quotes talks of eons as being small, intermediate, supreme, and great, which indicates that a supreme eon is longer than an intermediate eon and shorter than a great eon. /66/

d.div: [29] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 64_na2
[36] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 64a2.

f.d: bzhi pa gzugs med khams pa bzhi'i tshe tshad ni

d.i: Life span of the formless realm gods

f.d: 'og nas rim pa bzhin bskal chen gcig dang gnyis dang gsum dang bzhi rnams yin no/ /
Beginning with the lowest, the life span is one, two, three, and four great eons respectively.
lnga pa tshe tshad gzhan gyi bshad tshul la dwogs pa gcod pa ni/

d.i: Resolving doubts concerning life spans within other realms

f.d:
'o na mi dang dud 'gro dang yi dwags rnams kyi tshe tshad ji ltar yin snyam na/ lha la sogs pa rnams kyi tshe tshad 'chad pa'i skabs 'dir gsal por ma gsungs kyang / shin tu phra ba'i dbugs la sogs pas nyin mo'i tshad la sogs pa 'chad pa'i 'grel chen las/
phra zhes pa ni mi'i dbugs 'jug pa dang 'byung ba gcig drug brgya lhag pa'i stong phrag nyi shu rtsa gcig tu gyur pa'i cha gcig ni phra mo'i dbugs so/[30] / zhes pa la sogs pa rnams kyis bstan te/ de yang mi'i dbugs gcig la nyi khri chig stong drug brgya'i char che ba'i cha gcig ni lus rgyas kyi srin bu'i rigs kyi dbugs gcig yin la de 'dra ba nyis khri chig stong drug brgya la zhag gcig dang de 'dra ba'i zhag sum cu la zla ba dang zla ba de bcu gnyis lor byas pa'i rang lo brgya dud 'gro'i nang tshan srin bu phra mo'i tshe tshad dang / de bzhin du mi'i dbugs sum cu la 'byung po yi dwags rnams kyi dbugs gcig ste de nyi khri chig stong drug brgya la yi dwags rnams kyi zhag gcig de 'dra ba sum cu la zla ba dang zla ba de bcu gnyis la lor byas pa'i rang lo brgya yi dwags rnams kyi tshe tshad dang / mi rnams kyi nyin zhag gcig lha min rnams kyi dbugs gcig ste de 'dra ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya la zhag gcig dang / de 'dra ba sum cu la zla ba sogs su byas pa'i rang lo brgya lha min gyi tshe tshad dang / mi'i dbugs nyi khri chig stong drug brgya la mi rang nyid kyi zhag tu byas pa'i rang lo brgya mi'i tshe tshad do/ /

But what are the life spans of humans, animals, and ghosts? In this section on the life spans of gods and so forth, the tantra is not clear on this question. However, when explaining how the very subtle breath is used for calculating the length of days, the Great Commentary says:
“Subtle” means that one inhalation and one exhalation of a human breath divided into six hundred more than 21,000 is one subtle breath.[37] This and further quotes reveal the answers to this question. This is because one breath of a human is divided into 21,600 parts. One such part is the length of one breath of a fully formed insect. 21,600 of such insect breaths is one of its days, thirty of such days are a month, twelve such months are one year, and one hundred of its years is the life span of a tiny insect. Similarly thirty human breaths are equal to one breath of a ghost, and 21,600 of such breaths is one ghost day. Thirty of its days are a month, twelve months are a year, and one hundred of its years is the life span of a ghost. One human day is the length of one asura breath. 21,600 such breaths are one asura day, thirty days one month, twelve months one year, and one hundred such years the life span of the asura. 21,600 human breaths make up one human day, and one hundred human years is the human life span.

d.div: [30] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 67_na1
[37] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 67a1.

f.d:
de rnams kyang spyir btang ba mchog gi tshe ste ring mtha'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi/ nges pa ni ma yin te/ 'grel chen las/
de bzhin du dbugs 'bum phrag bdun cu rtsa drug lhag pa'i bye ba phrag bdun cu rtsa bdun gyis nyin zhag brgya dang lo brgyar 'gyur ro/ / mchog gi tshe 'di ni las kyi dbang gis rang rang gi tshad las lhag pa dang dman par 'gyur ro/ / rnal 'byor ba rnams kyi rnal 'byor gyi stobs dang dka' thub pa rnams kyi ting nge 'dzin gyi stobs kyis lhag par 'gyur te dbugs gcig chu tshod du 'gyur ro/ / sems can sdig pa can rnams kyi sdig pa'i stobs kyis dman par 'gyur ro/[31] / zhes gsungs pas so/ /

Generally these life spans are those of a complete life and depict maximum life span, but they are not fixed. The Great Commentary says:
Likewise 777,600,000 breaths are one hundred days[38] and one hundred years. Depending on karma, this complete life span could be more or could be less. For the yogis, by the power of their yoga and by the power of the meditative concentration of their asceticism, it will be more, and one breath will become hours. For those of nonvirtue, /67/ by the force of their nonvirtue, it will become less.[39]

d.div: [31] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 68_na4
[38] This amount of human breath is one hundred days for asuras but one hundred years for humans.
[39] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 68a4.

f.d:
'o na mi rnams kyi lo gcig nus pa 'og min pa'i dbugs gcig dang / drag po 'khor lo can gyi gling bcu gnyis kyi dus bzhi bsdoms pa'i tshad mi lo nyis khri chig stong drug brgya gtso bo'i ming can 'du shes med 'du shes med min skye mched pa'i dbugs gcig tu byas/ de gnyis nyi khri chig stong drug brgya drug brgya la rang rang gi zhag la sogs par byas pa'i rang lo brgya brgya yang 'og min pa dang srid rtse ba'i yang tshe tshad yin nam snyam na/ de ni ma yin te/ bsdus rgyud las/
phra dbugs d+hu dang chu tshod nyin zhag d+hu dang dus bzhi dag ni stong phrag nyi shu rtsa gcig dang / / drug brgya rnams ni rim pas lus skyes phra dang mi dang 'byung po lha dang lha min rnams dang ni/ / nus dang gtso bo'i nyin zhag gcig gi+i tshad de sa gzhi dag la dus bzhi nus pa'i tshad du 'jug[32] / ces 'og min pa dang srid rtse ba'i rang rang gi dbugs kyi tshad dang / de la brten pa'i zhag gi rnam gzhag sogs srin bu phra mo dang / mi dang / 'byung po yi dwags dang / lha min rnams kyi tshe tshad 'chad pa dang chabs cig tu bshad na'ang 'og min pa dang srid rtse ba'i tshe tshad shes pa'i phyir du bshad pa ma yin te/ 'og min pa dang srid rtse ba dang 'dod lha rnams kyi tshe tshad rang lo brgya brgya las ches ring bar gong du bshad zin pa'i phyir dang /

One human year is equal to one breath of the śakti[40] of None Higher, and the 21,600 human years, which is the length of Rudracakrī’s establishment of the four ages in the twelve sectors, are equal to one breath of those in the formless realm Source of No Recognition Yet No Nonrecognition, who are referred to here by the name prakṛti. If that is so, it may be assumed that 21,600 of such breaths equal one day in each of these realms and so on, thereby arriving, as in previous examples, at the hundred-year life span of None Higher and Peak of Existence. This, however, is not the case. In the Condensed Tantra it says:
21,600 subtle breaths, breaths, dhru,[41] hours,[42] solar days,[43]dhru,[44] and the four ages[45] are, respectively, one day in the life of a small body, humans, ghostly spirits, gods, asura, śakti, and the prakṛti. On Earth the four ages are the measurements of the śakti.[46] The breath measurements in None Higher and Peak of Existence and the corresponding length of the days and so forth are explained alongside the life spans of small insects, humans, ghosts, and asuras, but they are not there for the purpose of explaining the life span in None Higher and Peak of Existence. The lives of the gods of None Higher, Peak of Existence, and the desire realm are far longer than a hundred of their own years, as has been previously explained.

d.div: [32] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ khams kyi le'u/ 1_sh+loka24_25_na2
[40] Śakti here refers to the inhabitants of the form realm None Higher, not to be confused with the eight śakti of the mandala.
[41] According to Edward Henning, the Sanskrit dhru normally means fixed, certain, or firm, but here refers to thirty human breaths × 21,600 = thirty human solar days = one solar day for a ghost.
[42] One hour (twenty-four minutes) = 360 human breaths = one breath of the gods of the desire realm. That multiplied by 21,600 equals one celestial day.
[43] One solar day = 21,600 human breaths = one breath of an asura.
[44] Here dhru refers to one human year, which equals one breath of the inhabitants — the śakti — of the realm None Higher.
[45] Four ages = 21,600 human years = one breath of an inhabitant — a prakṛti or pradhāna — of the fourth formless realm.
[46] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, khams v. 24, 25a2.

f.d:
'grel chen las/
tshad 'di rnams las nus pa'i tshad ni 'og min gyi lha'i tshad des gzhi dag la 'khor lo can gyi dus bzhi nus pa'i tshad du 'jug ces so/[33] / zhes gsungs pa ltar 'og min pa'i dbugs dang zhag gi tshad drag po 'khor lo can gyi dus bzhi'i yun tshad rtogs pa'i don du gsungs pa sogs dgos pa gzhan gyi phyir gsungs pa yin no/ /

In the Great Commentary it says:
From these measurements, the measurements of the śakti, which are the measurements of the gods of None Higher, correspond to the four ages of Rudracakrī on the earth.[47] The measurements of a breath and a day in None Higher are taught in order to know the length of the four ages of Rudracakrī and therefore are mentioned here for a different purpose.

d.div: [33] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 67_na7
[47] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 67a7.

f.d:
'o na dmyal ba la sogs pa rnams kyi tshe tshad bskal pa chung ngu la sogs pa rnams kyis gzhal bar gsungs na bskal pa rnams kyi tshad ji lta bu snyam na/ 'grel chen las/
bskal pa chung ngu'i char chu dang zheng la dpag tshad gcig pa'i dong ste de yang skra'i rtse mo phra mo rnams kyis yongs su bkang ba las lo brgya na skra'i rtse mo de phyung bas gang gi tshe stongs par gyur pa de'i tshe bskal pa chung ngu'i nyin zhag gcig go/ / nyin zhag de sum cu'i tshad kyis zla ba dang zla ba bcu gnyis kyis lo dang lo brgya la bskal pa zhes brjod do/ / de bzhin du de'i sde ni bskal ba bar ma ste/ bskal pa bar ma'i sde mchog gi bskal pa'o/[34] / zhes chu dang zheng dang rngams rnams dpag tshad re re bar mnyam pa'i dong gru bzhi pa gcig skra'i rtse mo zlum pos bkang ba las lo brgya brgya na skra rtse re re phyung bas skra rtse rnams zad de stong bar gyur pa'i tshe bskal chung gi zhag gcig/de sum brgya drug cu la lor byas pa'i rang lo brgya bskal pa chung ngu'i tshad dang / bskal pa chung ngu de'i sdes bskal pa bar mar 'gyur zhing / bskal pa bar ma'i sdes mchog gi bskal pa dang / mchog gi bskal pa'i sdes bskal pa chen por 'gyur ro/ /

The life spans of the hells and other realms are measured in different types of eons. But how long are these eons? The Great Commentary says:
Concerning the divisions of a short eon, a pit one yojana wide and one deep is completely filled with tiny tips of hair. In a hundred years a hair tip is taken out. The time taken for the pit to be emptied is one day of one short eon. Thirty of those days are a month, twelve of those months are a year, and one hundred years is said to be one eon. /68/ Likewise, a group of those eons is one intermediate eon, and a group of those is one supreme eon.[48] Therefore a four-sided pit with length, width, and depth of one yojana is filled with round tips of hair. Every one hundred years one hair is removed until there are no more. The time taken for the pit to be emptied is one day of one short eon. 360 of those days make a year, and one hundred such years is the measurement of one short eon. A group of such eons forms one intermediate eon, and a group of intermediate eons forms one supreme eon. A group of supreme eons makes up one great eon.

d.div: [34] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 64_na4

f.d:
'o na de lta bu'i dong gi skra rtse'i grangs ji lta bu yin zhing bskal chung gcig la mi'i lo grangs ji tsam zhig yod snyam na/ de yang zhib tu bshad par bya ste/ dpag tshad gcig la skra rtse 'phreng bar gnas pa'i grangs ni/
nam mkha' stong pa nam mkha' dang / / klu mig ri dbang yid dang me/ / zhes pa 'di 'ong /

But what amount of hair is in this pit, and how many human years make up a short eon? That, too, can be explained. The number of hairwidths lined up to make one yojana has been expressed as follows:
Space, emptiness, space, nāga, eyes, mountain, sense organ, mind, and fire. [49]

d.div: [49] Word numerals; read backward it gives 3,145,728,000 hairwidths. To understand this and the following verses, see appendix 5 on word-numerals.

f.d:
grangs 'di 'di nyid kyis bsgyur bas dong de'i logs gcig gi srab 'thug skra rtse tsam gyi skra rtse'i grangs ni/
mkha' mkha' thig le stong pa dang / / nam mkha' thig le rig byed klu/ / bu ga bu ga mtsho dus mtsho/ / mkha' dus mda' phug klu phug [35] rnams/ / zhes pa'i grangs 'di 'ong /

This number multiplied by itself will give the number of hairs making up a single hairwidth layer of hair in the pit. This is expressed as:[50]
Space, space, drop, emptiness, space, drop, veda, nāga, opening, opening, ocean, time, ocean, space, time, arrows, opening, nāga, and opening.[51]

d.div: [35] rtsis gzhung spyi'i dgongs tshul ltar na mda' phub klu phub kyi tshab tu mda' bub klu bub zhes dgos pa gsal/
[50] The following four versed citations have not been traced.
[51] This is the previous number squared, i.e., 9,895,604,649,984,000,000. The following verse below can be worked out likewise.

f.d:
grangs 'di/ nam mkha' stong pa nam mkha' dang/ /klu mig ri dbang yid dang me/ /zhes pa'i grangs 'di nyid kyis bsgyur pas dong de skra rtses gang ba'i skra rtse ji snyed yod pa de snyed kyi grangs ni/
thig le dgu yi mtshams nas ni/ / mig mda' me klu ro klu mtsho/ / klu me rgyal ba ro dang mkha'/ / gdengs can klu klu nyi zla me/ / zhes pa 'di rnams 'ong /

This figure multiplied by “emptiness, space, space, nāga, eyes, mountain, sense organ, mind and fire” will give the total number of hairs in the pit when it is full. This is expressed as:
From the position of nine drops, eyes, arrows, fire, nāga, taste, nāga, ocean, nāga, fire, conqueror, taste, and space, nāga, nāga, nāga, sun, moon, fire.[52]

skra rtse'i grangs 'di brgyas bsgyur bas mi lo'i grangs/
thig le drag po'i mtshams nas ni/ / mig mda' me klu ro klu mtsho/ / klu me rgyal ba ro dang mkha'/ / gdengs can klu klu nyi zla me/[36] / zhes pa 'di 'ong ste bskal chung gi zhag gcig yin no/ /

This is the number of hairs, which multiplied by a hundred gives the number of human years that make up one day of a short eon. This is expressed as:
From the position of eleven drops, eyes, arrows, fire, nāga, taste, nāga, ocean, nāga, fire, conqueror, taste, and space, nāga, nāga, nāga, sun, moon, fire.

d.div: [36] 'dir drangs pa'i tshigs bcad rnams kyi mjug de ma thag tu gong du drangs pa'i shong 'gyur dang jo nang 'gyur gsar ltar na zhes 'byung bas de bzhin du go dgos par snang yang 'gyur de rnams ma brnyed/

f.d: grangs 'di sum brgya drug cus bsgyur ba'i mi lo'i grangs de bskal chung gi lo gcig yin zhing / de brgyas bsgyur ba'i mi lo'i grangs de bskal pa chung ngu'i tshad yin no/ /
This figure multiplied by 360 gives, in human years, the length of one year of a short eon, and one hundred short-eon years is the length of one short eon.

(bskal chung 'di la mi lo'i grangs du [37] yod ce na/
thig le bcu gcig mig ri ro/ / mkha' cho mig dbang 'byung klu ri/ / ri mtsho mig mkha' thub pa bug / me ro mkha' nyi gzugs rnams ni/ / bskal pa chung ngu'i mi lo'i grangs/ / zhes pa 'di 'byung la/ 'di grangs kyi ming dang sbyar na/ mi lo rab bkram che gnyis gtams bdun dang / / che drug dkrigs chen drug dang mi 'khrugs gnyis/ / che lnga khyad phyin lnga dang chen po brgyad/ / pang steng bdun dang che bdun ded 'dren bzhi/ / che gnyis mtha' gnad che bdun rgyu rigs dgu/ che gsum 'od mdzes drug dang dbang che gnyis/ / legs phyin gcig dang chen po gcig rnams so/ / zhes pa 'di 'byung /)

(This, in human years, is expressed as:
Fourteen drops, eyes, mountain, taste, space, taste, eyes, sense organs, elements, nāga, mountain, mountain, ocean, eyes, space, mighty one, opening, fire, taste, space, sun, and form are the human years of a short eon. /69/ Expressed as numerals this becomes two mahāprasuta, seven kaṃkara, six mahākaṃkara, six mahābimbara, two akṣobhya, five mahākṣobhya, five vivā, eight mahāvivā, seven utsaṃgah, seven mahotsaṃgah, four vāhana, two mahāvāhana, seven mahātiṭibha, nine hetu, three mahāhetu, six karabha, two indra, one samāpta, and one mahāsamāpta.)[53]

d.div: [37] ma dper grangs su gsal na'ang grangs du yin nam snyam/

[53] The text from “This, in human years, is expressed as” up to “one mahāsamāpta” looks like an annotation. It is using the Abhidharma numeration system, whose units increase tenfold. In numerals this comes to 112,063,970,247,785,526,067,200,000,000,000,000 years.

f.d: 'o na bskal pa chung ngu'i tshad de ltar yin na bskal ba chung ngu'i sdes bskal pa bar ma sogs su 'gyur ba'i tshul ji lta bu snyam na/ 'di'i don la gnyis su dwogs te/ gong du drangs ma thag pa'i shong 'gyur dang jo nang 'gyur gsar ltar na/ de'i sde ni bskal pa bar ma ste/ bskal pa bar ma'i sdes mchog gi bskal pa'o/ /zhes gsungs pa'i sdes zhes pa sde rtsis byed dgos pa'i don yin la/ sde rtsis kyi don ni ye shes le'u'i mdor bsdus bzhi pa las/ gnyis kyi sde ni bzhi ste zhes dang / gsum gyi don ni dgu'o zhes pa nas/ dgu'i sde ni brgyad cu rtsa gcig dang bcu'i sde ni brgya ste/[38] zhes grangs rang nyid kyis rang nyid bsgyur ba yin la/ de ltar du byas na bskal pa chung ngu'i lo brgya po de brgyas bsgyur bas bskal pa chung ngu'i lo khri 'ong ba bskal pa bar ma'i tshad dang / de 'dra ba'i lo khri po de khris bsgyur bas bskal pa chung ngu'i lo dung 'phyur gcig 'ong ba bskal pa mchog gi tshad dang / dung 'phyur gcig pu de nyid dung 'phyur de nyid kyis bsgyur bas bskal pa chung ngu'i lo grangs grangs kyi gnas gzhan bcu bdun pa gtams chen po gcig 'ong ba bskal pa chen po'i tshad yin no/ /

If that is the length of a short eon, then how is an intermediate eon formed from a “group”[54] of short eons. There are two schools of thought on this. According to the new Jonang translation and the Shong[55] translation as quoted above, “Likewise, a group of those eons is one intermediate eon, and a group of those is one supreme eon.” Here group means a mathematical grouping, and in the fourth summary of the Gnosis chapter it says “a two group is four” and “a three group is nine,” and so on, until “a nine group is eighty-one and a ten group is one hundred.”[56] Therefore each number is multiplied by itself to form a “group.” In this way the hundred years of a short eon is multiplied by a hundred to make ten thousand short-eon years. This is the length of an intermediate eon. These ten thousand years are multiplied by ten thousand to make a hundred million. This is the number of short-eon years in a supreme eon. That one hundred million multiplied by one hundred million gives, in short-eon years and by using another numeration system, the seventeenth numeric unit[57] or mahākaṃkara. This is the length of one great eon.

f.d:
dwogs pa gnyis pa ni 'di'i 'gyur mang du/
de bzhin de'i sde'i tshad kyis bsgre ba ni bskal pa bar ma'i tshad do/ / bskal pa bar ma'i tshad kyis bsgre ba ni bskal pa mchog gi tshad do/ / zhes pa dang /
rwa 'gyur du yang de ltar de'i tshogs kyi 'gyur la bskal pa bar ma zhes pa'o/ / bskal pa bar ma'i tshogs kyi 'gyur la bskal pa mchog tu 'byung ba zhes pa'o/ / zhes 'byung ba ltar na bskal chung gi lo de lta bu brgya brgya na sngar bshad pa'i dong skra rtses bkang ba de nyid nas skra'i rtse mo re re phyung bas zad pa ni bskal pa bar ma'i zhag gcig tu byas pa'i rang lo brgya ni bskal pa bar ma'i tshad dang / bskal pa bar ma'i lo de lta bu brgya brgya na skra'i rtse mo re re sngar bzhin du phyung bas zad pa ni mchog gi bskal pa'i zhag gcig tu byas pa'i rang lo brgya ni mchog gi bskal pa'i tshad yin pa nyid legs par rnam bshad de kho na nyid snang bar byed pa las gsungs so/ /

Concerning the second school of thought, in many translations it says:
Similarly, to replicate using the measurements of that category is to arrive at the length of an intermediate eon. Similarly, to replicate using the measurements of an intermediate eon is to arrive at the length of a supreme eon. The Ra translations also state:
A multiplication of that group will form an intermediate eon. A multiplication of a group of intermediate eons will form a supreme eon. In this way of thinking, every hundred short-eon years a single hair is pulled from a pit filled with hairs as previously detailed, until the pit is emptied. This would be the length of one day of an intermediate eon. One hundred years of such intermediate-eon days would make up the duration of one intermediate eon. If every hundred intermediate-eon years one hair was pulled from the pit, one day of a supreme eon would have passed. A hundred such years is the duration of a supreme eon. /70/ This is spoken of in the commentary Illuminating Reality.

'o na bskal pa'i tshad rnams grangs kyi gnas ji snyed pa dag gis rtogs dgos na/ grangs kyi gnas rnams kyi ming ji lta bu snyam na/ 'di ni gnas skabs gzhan du yang mkho bas bshad par bya'o/ / de yang grangs kyi gnas la bshad pa'i tshul gnyis las/ mdzod 'grel las bshad pa mkhas pa shAn+ti pas mdo kun las btus pa'i 'grel par bshad pa ni 'grel pa de nyid las/
grangs kyi khyad par gyi ming chos mngon pa las gsungs te/ grangs ni rkyang pa dang khug pa'o/ / de la grangs rkyang pa ni gcig dang / bcu dang / brgya dang / stong dang / khri dang / 'bum dang / sa ya dang / bye ba dang / dung 'phyur te gnas dgu'o/ / khug pa'i gnas ni gsum ste/ ther 'bum dang / khrag khrig dang / rab bkram dang / gtams dang / dkrigs dang / mi 'khrugs pa dang / khyad phyin dang / pad steng dang / ded 'dren zhes bya ba dgu ste/ chen po dgu bsnan pas khug pa dang po'o/ / mtha' snang dang / rgyu rig dang / 'od mdzes dang / dbang po dang / legs phyin dang / rtogs 'gro dang / 'gying rdul dang / rta rgyags dang / stobs 'khor ste dgu ni snga ma ltar chen po dgu bsnan pa ni khug pa gnyis pa'o/ / brda shes dang / rnam 'byung dang / stobs mig ces bya ba gsum ni snga ma ltar chen po gsum bsnan pas khug pa gsum pa ste/ de ltar na rkyang pa dgu dang khug pa'i gnas gsum du grangs bzhi bcu rtsa gnyis te/ bsdus na lnga bcu rtsa gcig ni chos mngon pa las snang ngo / / lhag ma grangs brgyad ni gzhung du mi song mod kyi/ 'on kyang khug pa'i gnas su brgyad bsnan na lnga bcu rtsa dgu ni grangs kyi ming du btags la/ drug cu pa ni de lta bu'i ming las gsungs pa grangs med pa zhes bya'o zhes slob dpon dbyig gnyen gyis bshad do/[39] / zhes bshad pa ltar grangs kyi gnas gzhan drug cu gzhan rnams la rang rang gi ming re dang drug cu pa la grangs med ces btags so/ / de yang khug pa dang bcas pa'i bgrang tshul ni ther 'bum dang ther 'bum chen po zhes sogs 'og ma rnams la yang 'gre ba'o/ /

If these measurements of eons are to be understood by using systems of enumeration, then what are the numerical units? Such knowledge will be necessary in other contexts and so will be explained. There are two traditions of enumeration. The first is from the Abhidharma commentaries and is explained by the scholar Śāntipa[58] in his Commentary on the Compendium of Sūtra. In it he says:
The different names of the numbers are taught in the Abhidharma. Numerical units are solitary and coupled. Solitary numerical units are, eka, daśa, śatam, sahasram, prabhedaṃ, lakṣam, atilakṣam, koṭī, madhya.[59] These are the nine solitary numerical units. There are three divisions of coupled numerical units. They are ayuta, nayuta, prasuta, kaṃkara, bimbara, akṣobhya, vivā, utsaṃgah, and vāhana. These nine together with their nine “greater” units make up the first division of coupled units. Tiṭibha, hetu, karabha, indra, samāpta, gati, nimbaraja, mudrā, and balaṃ, together with their “greater” units make up the nine numerical units of the second division of coupled units. Saṃjñā, vibhūta, and balākṣaṃ make up, together with their respective “greater” units, the third division of coupled units. Therefore, the nine solitary and the forty-two numerical units that make up the three divisions of the coupled units together total fifty-one. These appear in the Abhidharma. The remaining eight numerical units do not appear in the text. However adding them to the category of coupled units makes fifty-nine. These fifty-nine have been given the name “numbers.” The sixtieth is said to be apart from these names and is known as asaṃkhyāṃ. This has been taught by the master Vasubandhu.[60] As this quote explains, there are sixty numerical units. Each unit has its own name, and the sixtieth is known as asaṃkhyāṃ.[61] Moreover each coupled unit consists of the unit and its greater unit, as in ayuta and mahāyutah, for example. This doubling up is repeated for the others.

d.div: [39] sde dge_3935_bstan/ dbu ma/ ki_mdo kun las bsdus pa'i bshad pa/ 248_na5
[58] Ratnākaraśāntipa.
[59] These nine run from one to a hundred million, increasing tenfold each time. The rest are similar. These and the other Abhidharma units are found in the Mahāvyutpatti.
[60] Toh 3935 Tengyur, dbu ma, 248a5.
[61] grang med pa. Beyond number.

The names of the divisions of numerical units are spoken of in the sutras: “Numerical units are of two kinds, coupled and solitary. Of the solitary there are 116. They are jewa (spelled bye ba), khökhö (khod khod), thegu (thad dgu), traktrik (khrag khrig), thamtham (thams thams), nyangnying (myang mying), gangyang (gang yang), bendün (ban dun), charchur (phyar d.div: [62] Specifically the Buddhāvataṃsaka. However the units as given here do not match with the units from the same sutra as presented in the ninth-century Tibetan-Sanskrit lexicon the Mahāvyutpatti, and I have been unable to find Sanskrit equivalents elsewhere. Therefore these are left in Tibetan.

f.d: khug pa'i gnas ni bcu ste dpag yas dang / yal phyong dang / mu yal dang / bgrang yol dang / mi 'jal dang / bsam phyod dang / mtha' 'byam dang / dpag thag dang / brjod du med pa dang / brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa ste/ de'i steng du bgrang 'phyos bsgres pa la sogs pa nas brjod du med pa bsgres pa'i bar du bcu bsnan pa ni khug pa'i gnas bcu ste nyi shu dang spyir bsdoms nas brgya sum cu rtsa drug tu ni ming gis bstan pas so/ /[40] zhes bshad pa'i grangs ni rkyang khug bsdoms pa brgya sum cu rtsa drug ste/ de yang de'i steng du rtsa ba'i grangs bdun bsnan pa zhes pa'i rtsa ba'i grangs bdun ni gcig dang bcu dang brgya dang stong dang khri dang 'bum dang sa ya rnams yin la/ de rnams grangs rnams kyi thog mar sbyar bar bya zhing / gcig gi gnas nas la lo'i gnas kyi bar la rkyang pa'i grangs brgya dang bcu drug yod la/ de nas bgrang 'phyos nas brjod du med pa'i bar bcu yod pa khug par byas pas nyi shu ste/ de rnams snga ma rkyang pa rnams kyi steng du brtsegs pas brgya sum cu rtsa drug go/ /

Of the coupled units there are ten. They are, pakyé (dpag yas), yalchong (yal phyong), muyal (mu yal), drangyöl (bgrang yol), mijal (mi ’jal), samchö (bsam phyod), thayam (mtha’ ’byam), pakthak (dpag thag), jödu mepa (brjod du med pa), and jödu mepai yang jödu mepa (brjod du med pa’i yang brjod du med pa). Onto these ten are added replicated units from drangchö to jödu mepa to make twenty. In total 136 units have been named.[63] As this quote explains, the total of solitary and coupled units is 136. The seven units referred to in the line “Onto these are added the seven root numerical units” are one, ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, hundred thousand, and million. These seven are put at the beginning. The units from one to lalo total 116 solitary units.[64] There are ten units from drangchö to jödu mepa, and because they are coupled units, that becomes twenty. These twenty added to the previous solitary units makes 136.

d.div: [40] sde dge_3935_bstan/ dbu ma/ ki_mdo kun las bsdus pa'i bshad pa/ 250_ba4
[63] Toh 3935 Tengyur, dbu ma, 250b4.
[64] In which case one unit is missing from the list, because from one to lala totals 115.

f.d: de ltar na mdo'i tshig de yang / gam gum dang la lo ste de'i steng du rtsa ba'i grangs bdun bsnan pa zhes sogs dang / khug pa'i gnas ni bcu ste bgrang 'phyos dang dpag yas dang zhes sogs su 'ong rgyur snang ngo / / de yang khug pa'i bgrang tshul ni bgrang 'phyos dang bgrang 'phyos kyi bgrang 'phyos dang / dpag yas dang dpag yas kyi dpag yas zhes sogs dang / brjod du med pa dang brjod du med pa'i yang brjod du med pa zhes sbyar ba'o/ /

Therefore it seems that the text of the sutra should run, “… gamgum and lalo. Onto these are added the seven root numerical units… ”; and “Of the coupled units there are ten. They are, drangchö, pakyé… ”. Furthermore the coupled units would run from drangchö and drangchö replicated up to jödu mepa and jödu mepai yang jödu mepa.
gsum pa sems can de rnams su skye ba'i rgyu bshad pa ni/

sdig pa chen pos dmyal ba dang / 'bring gis yi dwags dang / chung ngus dud 'gror skye ba'i rgyu byed do/ / 'phen byed dge ba dang rdzogs byed sbyin pa stobs dang ldan pas lha ma yin du skye ba'i rgyu byed/ 'phen byed dge ba dang rdzogs byed dge mi dge ci rigs pas mir skye ba'i rgyu byed/ 'phen byed dge ba'i las dang rdzogs byed sbyin pa stobs ldan dang sngags bzlas rjod kyi stobs kyis 'dod pa'i lha rnams su skye ba dang / 'phen byed mi dge ba dang rdzogs byed bsod nams kyi stobs kyis klu'i 'jig rten du skye'o/ /

Great nonvirtuous actions create birth in hell, middling nonvirtuous actions result in birth as a ghost, while small nonvirtuous actions bring about birth as an animal. Virtuous throwing karma together with the powerful completing karma of giving are causes for birth as an asura.[65] Virtuous throwing karma alongside either virtuous or nonvirtuous completing karma results in birth as a human. Virtuous throwing karma coupled with the completing karma of powerful acts of giving together with the force of mantra recitation results in birth as a god of the desire realm. /73/ Nonvirtuous throwing karma with virtuous completing karma will bring about birth in the world of nāgas.

d.div: [65] Throwing karma ripens at death and determines the realm or status of rebirth by throwing the consciousness into a bardo being of that particular realm. Completing karma determines the quality of life in that particular realm.

f.d: gzugs khams gnas ris bcu drug tu skye ba'i rgyu ni mi dge bcu spongs kyi bsam gtan gyi sdom pa dang rang rang gi nyer bsdogs kyi snyoms 'jug gis 'phen byed dang / rang rang gi dngos gzhi'i snyoms 'jug gis rdzogs byed kyi rgyu byas pa las gzugs khams gnas ris bcu drug rnams su skye ba dang / gzugs med kyi'ang rang rang gi nyer bsdogs rnams kyis 'phen byed dang / dngos gzhi rnams kyis rdzogs byed kyi rgyu byas pa las gzugs med rnams su skye ba yin no/ /

Birth in any of the sixteen realms of form requires a meditative absorption[66] vow that has discarded the ten nonvirtuous actions, plus throwing karma consisting of an individual preparatory meditative equipoise[67] for each of the sixteen realms, and a completing karma in the form of the meditative equipoise of the actual absorption[68] for each of the sixteen. Similarly, for birth in the formless realms, the preparatory meditative equipoise for each realm becomes the throwing karma, and the actual absorption is the completing karma.

d.div: [66] bsam gtan, dhyāna.
[67] nyer sdogs kyi snyoms ’jug, sāmantaka samāpatti.
[68] dngos gzhi’i snyoms ’jug, maula samāpatti.

f.d:
gal te de ltar yin na 'grel chen las/
tshul khrims kyi stobs dang zad par rlung la sogs pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi stobs kyis 'og min la sogs pa gzugs can bcu drug tu 'gyur ro/[41] / zhes sogs kyis zad par sa bsgoms pa las tshangs ris sogs gnas bzhi dang / zad par chu bsgoms pa las tshad med 'od sogs bzhi dang / zad par me bsgoms pa las dge rgyas sogs bzhi dang / zad par rlung bsgoms pa las mi che ba sogs bzhi dang / zad par nam mkha' bsgoms pa las gzugs med bzhir skye bar bshad pa dang 'gal lo snyam na/ de ltar 'gal ba'i skyon med de/ rgyu snyoms 'jug gi bsam gtan dang gzugs med la zad par sa la sogs pa'i sgra bshad du yod pa'i sgo nas zad par sa la sogs par gsungs pa yin gyi/ gzugs khams dang gzugs med du skye ba'i rgyur zad par bcu'i nang tshan gyi zad par sa'i snyoms 'jug sogs dgos pa 'grel chen gyi dgongs pa ma yin pa'i phyir te/ de ltar 'grel chen gyi dgongs pa yin na khams gong ma gnyis su skye ba la sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa la zhugs pa dang lam zhugs yin pas khyab pa dang/ mu stegs can gyi lta ba ma dor bzhin du khams gong du skye mi srid pa 'grel chen gyi dgongs pa yin par thal ba'i skyon yod pa'i phyir ro/ /

However, if this is true, the Great Commentary says:
By the force of morality and by the meditative concentration of extinction by air[69] and so forth, the sixteen form realms, such as None Higher, will come to be.[70] This and further quotes explain that from the meditation of extinction by earth comes birth in the Sphere of Brahmā and the following three form realms. From the meditation of extinction by water arises birth in Limitless Light and the next three form realms. From the meditation of extinction by fire comes birth in Vast Virtue and the following three form realms. From the meditation of extinction by air comes birth in the Lesser and the following three form realms. And from the meditation of extinction by space arises the four formless realms. Does this not contradict the previous explanation? There is no contradiction here, for although extinction by earth and so forth are used as terminology for the causal meditative equipoises of the form and formless realms, it is not the thinking of the Great Commentary that the meditative equipoises of the ten extinctions,[71] such as extinction by earth and so forth, are necessary causes for birth in the form and formless realms. If this were the Great Commentary’s thinking, then it would mistakenly follow that it was also the Great Commentary’s thinking that birth in these two higher realms would necessarily entail entering the teachings of the Buddha and the paths of the Buddha, and that without casting aside non-Buddhist philosophy it would impossible to gain birth in these higher realms.

d.div: [41] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 63_ba6
[69] These are powerful meditations focused upon each of the five elements, transforming everything into one particular element.
[70] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 63b6.
[71] Four elements, four colors, limitless space, and limitless consciousness.

f.d: 'o na rgyu snyoms 'jug gi bsam gtan dang gzugs med la zad par sa la sogs pa'i sgra bshad du ji ltar yod snyam na/ de yang rim pa bzhin du bshad par bya ste/ tshangs ris tshangs pa mdun na 'don tshangs chen 'od chung bzhir 'phen byed dang rdzogs byed kyi bsam gtan gyi snyoms
