How are the terms extinction by earth and so forth used for the causal meditative equipoise of the absorptions and the formless realms? These can be described in sequence. The throwing and completing meditative equipoises of the absorptions of the realms of Sphere of Brahmā, Chanting in the Presence of Brahmā, Great Realm of Brahmā, and /74/

'jug rnams rang rang gi 'og sa'i 'dod chags zad pa'i zad byed yin pas zad par dang / khams sa yin pas zad par sa zhes bshad pa dang / de bzhin du tshad med 'od 'od gsal dge chung dge rgyas rnams su 'phen byed dang rdzogs byed kyi snyoms 'jug rnams rang rang gi 'og sa'i 'dod chags zad pa'am zad byed yin pas zad par dang / khams chu yin pas zad par chu zhes bshad pa dang / de bzhin du tshad med dge la sogs pa bzhi dang / mi che ba la sogs pa bzhi dang / gzugs med nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched la sogs pa bzhi po rnams kyi 'phen byed dang rdzogs byed kyi snyoms 'jug rnams rang rang gi 'og sa rnams kyi 'dod chags zad byed dam zad pa yin pas zad par dang / khams rnams rim pa bzhin me dang rlung dang nam mkha' yin pas zad par me dang zad par rlung dang zad par nam mkha' zhes pa rnams su bshad pa yin no/ /

Little Virtue extinguish the desires found in lower levels. They are therefore known as extinctions. Because the element is earth, they are extinctions by earth. Similarly the throwing and completing meditative equipoises for birth in Limitless Light, Illuminating Light, Little Virtue, and Limitless Virtue extinguish the desires found in their respective lower levels and are therefore extinctions. The element is water, and they are therefore extinctions by water. The throwing and completing meditative equipoises for the four realms beginning with Vast Virtue, the four realms commencing with the Lesser, and for the four formless realms commencing with Source of Limitless Space also extinguish the desires of their respective lower levels and are known as extinctions. Because their elements are, respectively, fire, air, and space, they are therefore known as extinctions by fire, air, and space.

'o na bsam gtan dang gzugs med rnams kyi rang rang gi 'phen byed nyer bsdogs kyi snyoms 'jug rnams dang / rang rang gi rdzogs byed dngos gzhi'i snyoms 'jug rnams rang ming gis mi rjod par zad par sa la sogs pa'i ming gis brjod pa la dgos pa ci yod snyam na/ dgos pa khyad par can yod de/ dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i dgongs pa chos thams cad khams lnga'i rang bzhin yin pa'i sgo nas gtan la 'bebs pa yin la/ 'dir yang gtso bor gzugs khams gnas ris bcu drug bzhi tshan bzhir byas pa'i bzhi tshan re re'i rgyu snyoms 'jug gi bsam gtan rnams rim pa bzhin sa chu me rlung gi khams pa rnams su go ba dang / gzugs med kyi rgyu snyoms 'jug rnams nam mkha'i khams par go ba'i ched du yin zhing / gzhan yang gzugs dang gzugs med du skye ba la rang rang gi 'gro sa'i 'dod chags mngon gyur zad pa zhig dgos so zhes go ba'i ched du rgyu snyoms 'jug gi bsam gtan dang gzugs med rnams rang ming gis ma smos par zad par sa la sogs pa'i ming gis bstan pa yin no/ /

What is the purpose of referring to these preparatory meditative equipoises, or throwing karmas, and actual meditative equipoises, or completing karmas, not by their own names but as extinctions by earth and so forth? There is a special purpose in this. In Kālacakra thinking all phenomena are ascertained by their being in the nature of the five elements. With this in mind the causal meditative equipoise absorptions that produce the sixteen form realms categorized in sets of four are to be understood as being primarily of the elements of earth, water, fire, and air, respectively, while the causal equipoises that produce the formless realms are to be understood as being of the element of space. Furthermore the reason that these causal equipoises are not mentioned by name, but are taught using terms such as extinction by earth and so forth, is to make it clear that in order to migrate to the form and formless realms, the manifest desires lacking in each destination must first be extinguished.

srid pa so gcig skyed byed sa bon ni/khams le las/
gzugs med bzhi ni a sogs bzhi po ha 'khrig bral ba rnams te i la sogs pa bcu drug gzugs/ / ha sogs la mtha' yang ni 'dod pa rnam bcur rab tu gsal te gsal byed gcig la ka sa'o/ / zhes gzugs med bzhi'i skyed byed sa bon/ a A aM AH_bzhi dang / gzugs khams bcu drug gi sa bon/ i I e ai r-i r-I ar Ar u U o au l-i l-I al Al te bcu druga'adod lha drug gi sa bon ha hA/ ya yA/ ra rA drugalha min dang mi'i sa bon/ wa A/ dud 'gro dang yi dwags gnyis kyi sa bon la lA/ dmyal ba'i sa bon kA'o/ /

The seed syllables that produce the thirty-one realms are mentioned in the Realms chapter:
The four formless are a and so forth, separate from the two of ha.[72] i and so forth are the sixteen of form. ha and so forth are clear as being the ten of desire together with the one consonant kṣa. Therefore, the seeds of the formless realms are, a, ā, aṃ, and āḥ. /75/ The seeds of the sixteen realms of form are, i, ī, e, ai, ṛ, ṛī, ar, ār, u, ū, o, au, ḷ, ḷī, al, āl. The seeds of the six kinds of desire gods are, ha, hā, ya, yā, ra, rā. The seeds of humans and asura are wa and wā. The seeds of ghosts and animals are la and lā. The seed of hell is kṣa.

d.div: [72] The commentary explains that the formless realms are without the two syllables ha and hā, and that this line is there to make it clear that there are not six formless realms.

f.d: skar khyim rnams dang gza' rnams kyi byung tshul bshad pa/
6. The Stars and the Planets
gsum pa sa'i steng du lhun po la 'khor ba'i go la'i rnam gzhag bshad pa

d.i: The gola circling Mount Meru above the Earth

f.d: ['di ]la gsum/ skar khyim rnams dang gza' rnams kyi byung tshul bshad pa dang / de rnams nam mkha' la 'khor tshul gyi go la bshad pa dang / sa'i go la/ dus rnams kyi 'ong tshul bshad pa'o/ /
This has three outlines: 1. Lunar mansions, houses, and the emergence of the planets 2. How the stars and planets orbit the skies 3. The gola of the earth: Emergence of the seasons
dang po [skar khyim rnams dang gza' rnams kyi byung tshul ]ni
Lunar mansions, houses,[73] and the emergence of the planets

d.div: [73] House (khyim) refers to the twelve signs of the zodiac — Aries and so on — and not to the usual astrological meaning of “house” as a stationary division of the zodiac.

f.d:
de yang gza' rnams kyi skyes khyim shes pa la rag las pas de bshad na/ ye shes le'u'i mdor bsdus bzhi pa las/
da ni gza' rnams kyi skye ba'i khyim gsungs pa lug ces pa la sogs pa ste/ 'dir grangs bzhin du lug dang 'khrig pa dang kar ka Tar ni ri bong can dang pa sangs dang nyi ma 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ / seng+ger sa skyes dang bu mor phur bu dang srang du sgra gcan dang sdig par gza' lhag dang gzhu'i thog mar spen pa dang de'i tha mar mjug ring ngo /[42] / zhes gsungs pa ltar yin la/ de la thog mar skar khyim 'khor dang bcas pa rnams chags pa'i rjes su kar ka Ta'i khyim gyi thog mar nyi ma skyes te lo dngos gzhi'i dang po yin no/ /

Understanding this topic depends on understanding the birth houses of the planets and so forth. Therefore this will be explained. In the Gnosis chapter of the Great Commentary, in the fourth summary, it says:
Now the birth houses are spoken of as Aries and so forth. The moon, Venus, and the sun arose in Aries, Gemini, and Cancer respectively. Mars was born in Leo, Jupiter in Virgo, Rāhu in Libra, Mercury in Scorpio, Saturn at the beginning of Sagittarius, and Ketu in the last.[74] Therefore, in the beginning, the lunar mansions, houses, and the other stars were formed. Then the sun was born in the beginning of the house of Cancer. This marked the first actual year, and the sun became the ruler of the solar days.

d.div: [42] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 454_ba4
[74] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 454b4.

f.d: de nas nyi mas nyin zhag rnams la dbang byed / de'i rjes su nyi mas rgyu skar rnams la g.yon skor du longs spyod pa las nyi ma tha skar gyi steng du sleb ste nyi ma tha skar dang bcas pa shar gling dbus ma'i tshangs thig gi thad kar sleb pa dang mnyam du zla ba tha skar gyi steng du skyes pas zla ba'i skyes khyim lug khyim yin par bshad cing de'i tshe zla ba skyes pa dang thog ma'i tshes zhag gi 'go rtsom pa dang zla ba'i dkar cha dang po skye ba dang nyin zhag de'i 'go rtsom pa dang zla bas nyin zhag de la dbang byed pa dang byed pa'i lo rnams kyi thog ma'i 'go rtsom pa rnams dus mnyam pa yin no/ / rgyu mtshan de nyid kyi phyir na lug khyim khyim rnams kyi dang po dang tha skar rgyu skar rnams kyi [43] dang po dang zla ba'i yar ngo phyogs rnams kyi dang po'i 'ang zla ba de'i tshes bco lnga la zla skar nag pa 'ong bas nag zla zla ba rnams kyi dang por bzhag pa yin no/ /

The sun then moved counterclockwise, occupying the different lunar mansions, until it arrived at the beginning of the lunar mansion of aśvinī. In aśvinī the sun arrived directly in line with the meridian of the central sector of the east, and there, simultaneously, the moon was born in aśvinī. Therefore it is explained that the moon was born in Aries.[75] At the same time, the first lunar day began,[76] the first light of the moon was born, and it was the beginning of that particular solar day. The moon became the ruler of that day, and the first karaṇa year[77] began. Because of this, Aries is posited /76/ as the first of the houses, aśvinī as the first of the lunar mansions, the waxing is posited as the first of the two halves of the month, and because the lunar mansion on the fifteenth day of that moon was citrā, the month of that name[78] was posited as the first of the months.

d.div: [43] ma dper rgyu skar rnams kyang byung yang rnams kyi zhes bcos/
[75] Because Aries overlaps aśvinī — the first of the twenty-seven lunar mansions.
[76] As the sun and moon were in conjunction.
[77] I.e., the calendar year.
[78] Spelled caitra as a month but citrā as a lunar mansion.

f.d: de nas bzung ste mig dmar ma skyes bar la nyi ma dang zla ba gnyis kyis gnyis res byas te nyin zhag re la dbang byed pa yin no/ / de nas nyi mas nam zhig na seng+ge'i khyim gyi skar ma mchu'i steng du sleb ste nyi ma mchu dang bcas pa shar gling dbus ma'i tshangs thig gi steng thad du sleb pa dang dus mnyam du mig dmar mchu'i steng du skyes te de mig dmar gyis nyin zhag de la dbang byed cing de'i sang nyin nyi mas dbang byed pa sogs lhag pa ma skyes kyi bar nyi zla gnyis dang mig dmar dang gsum gyis nyin zhag re re la dbang byed pa gsum res su byed do/ /

From then on until Mars was born, the sun and the moon alternated in their rule over the days. The sun then arrived at the beginning of the lunar mansion magha within Leo. In magha the sun arrived directly in line with the meridian of the central eastern sector. At the same time Mars was born in the lunar mansion magha and became ruler of that day. The following day was ruled by the sun, and until Mercury was born, the sun, moon, and Mars rotated their lordship over the days.

de nas yang nyi mas g.yon skor du rgyu skar la spyod kyin phyin pas nam zhig na sdig pa'i khyim gyi skar ma lha mtshams kyi phyed du sleb ste nyi ma lha mtshams dang bcas pa shar gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi steng thad du sleb pa dang dus mnyam du lhag pa lha mtshams kyi steng du skyes te nyin zhag de la lhag pas dbang byed cing / de'i sang nyin nyi mas dbang byas pa'i sgo nas des gza' bzhi po des phur bu ma skyes kyi bar la bzhi res byed do/ /

The sun continued in its counterclockwise occupation of the lunar mansions and arrived at the halfway point of the lunar mansion anurādha within Scorpio. There, in anurādha, it arrived directly in line with the meridian of the central eastern sector. Simultaneously Mercury was born in anurādha to become ruler of that day. The following day the sun ruled, and in this way, until Jupiter was born, these four planets[79] rotated in their ruling of the days.

d.div: [79] Sun and moon are regarded as “planets.” The Sanskrit term graha carries the meaning of “to seize or grab,” in the sense of their abilities to influence and rule.

f.d: de nas sngar bzhin nyi mas rgyu skar la spyad pa las nyi ma bu mo'i khyim gyi skar ma me bzhi'i 'gor sleb ste nyi ma me bzhi dang bcas pa shar gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi steng thad du sleb pa dang dus mnyam du phur bu me bzhi'i steng du skyes te rang nyid skyes ba'i nyin zhag de la dbang byed cing de'i sang nyin nyi mas dbang byed pa nas res gza' lnga po des pa sangs ma skyes kyi bar la nyin zhag re re dbang byed pa lnga res byed do/ /

As it had done previously, the sun continued to occupy the lunar mansions until it arrived at the beginning of the lunar mansion hasta in Virgo. In hasta it arrived directly in line with the meridian of the central eastern sector. Simultaneously Jupiter was born in hasta and became ruler of the day on which it was born. The following day the sun ruled, and until the birth of Venus, these five ruled the days by rotation.

de bzhin du nyi mas 'khrig ba'i khyim gyi skar ma nab so'i 'gor sleb ste nyi ma nab so dang bcas pas shar gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi steng thad du sleb pa dang dus mnyam du pa sangs nab so'i steng du skyes te rang nyid skyes pa'i nyin zhag de la dbang byed cing de'i sang nyin re yang nyi mas dbang byed pa nas spen pa ma skyes kyi bar la res gza' drug po des re mos byas te rim pa bzhin nyin zhag re rer dbang byed pa yin no/ /

The sun then reached the beginning of the lunar mansion punarvasu in Gemini. Together with punarvasu the sun arrived directly in line with the center of the central eastern sector, and at the same time Venus was born in punarvasu, where it became ruler of the day in which it was born. The following day was ruled by the sun, and until Saturn was born, these six planets ruled, in order, successive days. /77/

de bzhin du spen pa gzhu'i khyim gyi skar ma snubs kyi 'go la skyes ba yin pas nyi ma skar ma snubs dang bcas pa shar gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi steng thad du sleb pa dang dus mnyam du spen pa skyes pa sogs gong ma rnams kyi bzhin du shes par bya'o/ /

Likewise Saturn was born at the beginning of the lunar mansion mūla within Sagittarius. Therefore, when the sun together with mūla arrived directly in line with the center of the central eastern sector, Saturn was born, and the ensuing process was as described above.

de yang gza' rnams kyi skyes rim de ltar du byed dgos pa'i rgyu mtshan ni/ gza' rnams dus mnyam du skyes pa ni ma yin te/ skyes khyim dang skyes skar mi gcig pa so sor bshad cing / res gza' bdun po thams cad kyang shar gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi steng thad du skyes pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na rim can du skyes bar grub bo/ /

The reason why the planets must have been born in this order is that, firstly, they could not have been born at the same time, because it is taught that they each had different birth houses and birth lunar mansions, and all seven alternating planets were born directly in line with the center of the central eastern sector. They were, therefore, born successively.

rim can la yang gza'i thog ma nyi ma yin pa nas tha ma spen pa yin par bshad pa 'di yang skyes pa'i rim pa nyid yin gyi/ gzhan bshad pa'i rim pa dang nyams len gyi rim pa gang la yang sbyar du med pa'i phyir dang / res gza' zhes pa yang re mos kyis nyin zhag la dbang byed pas yin la/ de yang skyes rim gyis dbang byas pas res gza' zhes pa yin pas so/ /

The order of the planets is taught as beginning with the sun and ending with Saturn. This is the order of birth, and is not the order found in the explanations from the chapters on the Other Kālacakra or in the order of practice. Furthermore the term alternating planets refers to their alternating lordship of successive days, which in turn is decided by order of planetary birth, hence the term alternating planets.

yang gza' rnams skyes pa'i sa khyon ni shar gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi steng thad yin pa dang / de yang nyi ma de na yod pa'i dus der skyes pa yin pa ni lho gling dbus ma'i dbus drang po'i res gza'i 'pho mtshams lho gling dbus ma'i dbus drang po'i nam langs kyi dus de yin pa nyid kyis shes so/ /

Moreover the birthplace of the planets is directly above the center of the central eastern sector, and it can be known that they were born while the sun was there also by the fact that the changeover time for the alternating planets directly at the center of the central eastern sector is at dawn from the standpoint of the direct center of the central southern sector.[80]

d.div: [80] Dawn on the southern continent is midday on the eastern continent.

f.d:
de ltar skyes pa'i gza' de rnams phan tshun dgrar gyur pa ni 'grel chen las/
de bzhin du slar yang gsal bar 'dir ni phan tshun 'thab ste dgra yin phyir zhes pa ni zhi ba dang drag po ni gza' lhag dang bkra shis dag dang phur bu dang pa sangs dag dang spen pa dang mjug ring 'di dag phan tshun 'thab par 'gyur te dgra nyin yin pa'i phyir ro/[44] / zhes gsungs pa ltar mig dmar gyi zhing lug khyim dang sdig pa'i khyim la mig dmar gnas pa'i tshe khyim de gnyis la gza' lhag longs spyod par gyur pa'i tshe mig dmar dang gza' lhag 'thab bo/ /

These planets are enemies to each to other. The Great Commentary says:
Similarly, to clarify once more: “They fight with each other and are enemies.” This means that there are the peaceful and the wrathful. Mercury and Maṅgala,[81] Jupiter and Venus, Saturn and Ketu — these fight each other and are enemies.[82] The houses of Aries and Scorpio are the dominion of Mars, and if Mercury occupies these houses when he is dwelling in them, Mars and Mercury will fight.

d.div: [44] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 82_ba7
[81] bkra shis. Another name for Mars. See Lochen, p. 45ff, for synonyms of the planets.
[82] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 82b7.

f.d: de bzhin du lhag pa'i zhing 'khrig pa dang bu mo'i khyim du lhag pa gnas pa'i tshe khyim de nyis la mig dmar rgyu bar gyur na yang gza' de gnyis 'thab bo/ / de bzhin du phur bu'i zhing gzhu dang nya'i khyim la phur bu gnas pa'i tshe khyim de gnyis la pa sangs longs spyod na yang gza' phur bu dang pa sangs gnyis 'thab bo/ / pa sangs kyi zhing glang dang srang gi khyim la yang de bzhin no/ / spen pa'i zhing chu srin dang bum pa'i khyim la du ba mjug ring zhugs par gyur na spen pa dang mjug ring 'thab bo/ / zla ba'i zhing kar ka Ta la spen pa zhugs na zla ba dang mjug ring lhan cig tu byas te spen pa la rtsod do/ /

Similarly Mercury has dominion over Gemini and Virgo, and if Mars enters while he dwells there, Mars and Mercury will fight. The houses of Sagittarius and Pisces are the dominion of Jupiter, and if Venus enters while Jupiter is dwelling there, /78/ then Venus and Jupiter will fight. The dominions of Venus are the houses of Taurus and Libra, and if Jupiter should enter, these two planets will fight. Saturn has dominion over Capricorn and Aquarius, and if Ketu enters, Saturn and Ketu[83] will fight. Moon’s dominion is Cancer, and when Saturn enters, the moon and Ketu combine to cause trouble for Saturn.

d.div: [83] The Tibetan translates as “long tail of smoke,” hence its alternate translation of “comet.”

f.d: de bzhin du rang gi zhing la dgra zhugs na 'thab par ma zad rang rang gi skyes skar gyi steng du rang gi dgra byung na dgra zun rnams phan tshun 'thab bo/ / de yang gza' rnams skyes skar gyi steng du dgra zun lhan cig tu tshogs pa'i tshe yin no/ / skar ma dang khyim gzhan gyi steng du phan tshun dgrar gyur pa rnams lhan cig tu tshogs kyang mi 'thab bo/ /

Similarly trouble not only occurs when an enemy enters the dominion of another. Should an enemy appear in the birth lunar mansion of another, then those two will fight. This occurs when the planets gather as friends and enemies in each other’s birth lunar mansions. In other houses and lunar mansions, mutual enemies will gather but will not fight.

yang gza' thams cad khyim bcu gnyis la longs spyod cing 'khor ba'i tshul ni gza' dang rgyu skar la sogs pa'i skar ma thams cad go la rlung gis bskyod pa'i stobs kyis bgrod [45] pa rlung 'gros ni lhun po la dus nam yang gang bri med pa'i tshul gyis g.yas su skor ba 'ba' zhig go/ / rang 'gros kyi dbang du byas na sgra gcan dang dus me ma gtogs pa'i gza' thams cad kyang khyim rgyu skar dang bcas pa la g.yon nor du spyod do/ / de yang ji tsam du spyod na gza' lnga nyi ma dang bcas pa'i dal rkang rnams rim pa'i snga rkang dang rim min gyi phyi rkang du rkang pa rnams bu lon du spyod cing / rim min gyis rkang dang rim pa'i phyi rkang du rkang pa rnams nor du spyod pa rang rang gi skyes skar gyi steng du gza' lnga pos sleb pa'i tshe dal rkang gi nor bu lon kha dag cing / gza' lnga'i myur rkang gi rim pa'i snga rkang dang rim min gyi phyi rkang du rkang pa rnams nor dang / rim min gyi snga rkang dang rim pa'i phyi rkang du rkang pa rnams bu lon du spyod pa rang rang gi rkang 'dzin dag pa stong par gyur pa de'i tshe myur rkang rnams kyi nor bu lon kha dag ste rkang 'dzin dag pa stong pa'i gza' lnga po gang yin pa de nyi ma la nub cing nyi ma dang lhan cig tu gnas so/ /

Concerning the way the planets orbit and occupy the twelve houses, all the stars, lunar mansions, and planets are themselves propelled by the power of the gola[84] winds. This movement is known as gola wind movement and is solely a clockwise motion around Meru, at no time varying in its regularity. Concerning the individual movements of the planets, all planets except Rāhu and Kālāgni occupy the houses and lunar mansions in a counterclockwise motion by incremental steps. Concerning how they occupy the houses and lunar mansions, the progressive early steps and regressive later steps of the slow stages of the five planets and the sun are decremental, and the regressive early steps and progressive later steps are incremental.[85] When the five planets arrive in their own birth sign, all increment and decrement in the slow stages is canceled out. The progressive early steps and the regressive later steps of the fast stages of the five planets are incremental, while the regressive early steps and progressive later steps are decremental. When the step index is at zero, all increment and decrement in the fast steps are canceled out, and any of the five planets whose index is zero has disappeared into the sun and is conjunct with the sun.

d.div: [45] ma dper 'grod gsal na'ang bgrod ces bcos/
[84] gola. Dome, sphere, etc. This term is explained fully later on.
[85] Henning explains that steps are incremental or decremental, progressive or regressive, depending on whether a planet is speeding up or slowing down, ahead of its mean or behind its mean.

f.d: de yang gza' lnga po rang rang gi skyes skar gyi steng du nyi ma dang lhan cig tu 'dzom pa'i tshe rang rang gi dal myur gyi rkang pag nyis char gyi nor bu lon kha dag ste dang po skyes pa nas brtsams te rang gi skyes skar gyi steng du nyi ma dang lhan cig 'dzom pa'i bar gyi yun ji snyed pa dag la rang rang gi rtag longs nyid spyad pa'i lag rjes 'byung bas rtag longs ni gza' rang rang gis rgyu skar 'khor lo 'khor ba'i khar snyoms pa'i longs spyod yin no/ / de yang gza' rnams kyi rtag longs ni gza' rang rang gi zhag gsum gyi dkyil 'khor gang dang gang yin pa des rgyu skar gyi chu tshod stong drug brgya nyi shu la bgos pas thob pa gang yin pa de rnams gza' rnams kyi rang rang gi zhag gsum so so'i rtag longs yin no/ /

When any of the five planets gather at their individual birth signs conjunct /79/ with the sun, any increment and decrement in both fast and slow stages is canceled out. Therefore, within the period of time from the birth of a planet until it again becomes conjunct with the sun in its own birth sign can be found the imprint[86] of its fixed or mean motion. Therefore fixed motion is the averaged-out planetary orbit through the complete circle of lunar mansions. The fixed motion of the three kinds of days for each of the planets is found by dividing a planetary orbit in terms of its three kinds of days among the 1,620 hours of the lunar mansions.[87]

d.div: [86] lag rjes. A planet will eventually return to its birth sign conjunct with the sun with all increment and decrement canceled out. The intervening time, therefore, provides the basis for the calculation of the fixed motion of that planet.

[87] Zodiacal day, lunar day, and solar day are the three kinds of days. (See Gojo, p. 40ff, and Shawo, chap. 6). Therefore the number of, say, lunar days a planet takes to complete its orbit is divided into 1,620 (twenty-seven lunar mansions multiplied by sixty hours or degrees for each lunar mansion = 1,620 hours) to arrive at the fixed motion in terms of degrees.

f.d: des na gza' lnga po 'char ba dang nub pa yang nyi ma las 'char ba dang nyi ma las nub pa la bya ste/ nyi ma las logs su bya ba ni mig gis mthong bar gyur ba dang / nyi ma dang lhan cig tu gnas pa'i tshe mig lam du mi 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ /

The appearance and disappearance of the five planets is to be understood in terms of the sun, because a planet separate from the sun is visible to the eye, while a planet conjunct with the sun is not.

de ltar yang 'grel chen las/
da ni gza' rnams kyi 'char ba dang nub pa'i dus gsungs pa/ gang dag su zhig nyi ma'i longs spyod la ni rab zhugs gza' de dag kyang nges par nub par 'gyur/ /zhes pa ni nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi 'od zer gyis mi mthong ba'i phyir nub par gyur pa zhes rjod kyi gza' rnam pa thams cad du med pa ni ma yin no/[46] / zhes gsungs pa dang gzhan yang /
nyi ma dor las 'char bar 'gyur te/ zhes pa ni nub par 'gyur ba'i gza' de nyid kyis rang gi rgyu ba'i dbang gis nyi ma dor bar gyur pa na 'char bar 'gyur te nyi ma'i 'od zer gyis yongs su dor ba'i phyir ro/[47] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Great Commentary says:
Now the text speaks of the appearance and disappearance of planets. “Whatever planets dwell within the tenancy of the sun will definitely disappear.” By the rays of the sun it will not be seen, and is said to have disappeared. However such a planet has not completely disappeared.[88] Also:
“Abandoning the sun, it will rise.” By the power of its own movement, the planet that has set will leave the sun and rise, because it has left the rays of the sun.[89]

d.div: [46] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 82_ba7
[47] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 83_na2
[88] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 82b7.
[89] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 82a2.

f.d: de bzhin du zhi ba'i gza' lhag pa dang pa sangs dang mjug rings rnams nyi ma la nub par 'gyur ba'i tshe nyi ma'i g.yon phyogs nas nub pa dang / 'char ba'i tshe nyi ma'i g.yon phyogs nas 'char zhing / drag gza' mig dmar phur bu spen pa gsum ni nyi ma'i g.yas phyogs nas 'char nub byed do/ / de bzhin du drag gza' zhi gza' phrad pa'i tshe'ang drag gza' zhi gza'i g.yas nas 'gro zhing zhi gza' rnams drag gza'i g.yon nas 'gro 'ong byed do/ /

Similarly, when the peaceful planets Venus, Ketu, and Mercury set into the sun, they set from the left of the sun, and when they rise they do so also from the left. The wrathful planets — Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn — rise and set from the right of the sun. Similarly, when peaceful and wrathful planets meet, the wrathful will pass to the right of the peaceful, and the peaceful will pass to the left of the wrathful.

sgra gcan ni khyim srang khyim dang skar ma nag pa'i steng du skyes shing dus me nam gru'i steng du skyes te/ skyes pa'i dus de nas bzung ste khyim mam rgyu skar la g.yas skor du longs spyod cing / gdong nas mjug dus me'i bar gyis g.yon du bskor ba'i tshul gyis khyim dang rgyu skar 'khor lo phyed khyab nas gnas la/ de yang sgra gcan rtsa ba'i ri mor shar ba'i skar ma dang chu tshod sogs kyi grangs ni nam gru nas lugs bzlog tu bgrangs pa'i grangs dang gdong mjug la shar ba'i skar ma chu tshod sogs ni tha skar nas lugs 'byung du bgrangs pa'i grangs yin no/ /

Rāhu was born in Libra in the lunar mansion of citrā while Kālāgni was born in the lunar mansion revatī, and from the time of their birth they occupy the houses or lunar mansions in clockwise motion. The Rāhu head to his Kālāgni tail covers half the house and lunar-mansion circle in a counterclockwise direction. The number of lunar mansions /80/ and degree hours to appear in the chart of the body of Rāhu are counted backward from the lunar mansion revatī, while the numbers that appear in the charts of the head and tail are counted forward from the lunar mansion aśvinī.

de yang bsdus rgyud rtsa 'grel las/ nya dang gnam stong gi mthar zla ba la sgra gcan 'jug tshul rags pa tsam zhig gsungs nas zhib par ma gsungs so/[48] / de yang zla nyi la sgra gcan 'jug pa ji lta ba bzhin rtogs pa la sgra gcan 'khor tshul shes dgos te/ 'grel chen las/
g.yon du rgyu ba dag la g.yas min du ste zhes pa ni g.yon du sgra gcan 'khor ba la g.yas min g.yon du zla ba 'dzin par 'gyur rozhes dang /
g.yas la ste g.yas su 'khor ba la g.yas su zla ba 'dzin par 'gyur ro/[49] / zhes gsungs shing /

The Condensed Tantra and the commentary talk in general terms about how Rāhu engages the moon at the times of full moon and no moon, but these are not discussed in depth.[90] In order to understand how Rāhu engages with the sun and moon, it is important to know how Rāhu orbits. The Great Commentary states:
“Moving to the left and not to the right.” This means that Rāhu moves to the left and not to the right, and that it grasps the moon from its left. And:
“To the right,” means moving to the right and grasping the moon from its right.[91]

d.div: [48] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 84_na2
[49] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 84_na3
[90] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 84a2.
[91] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 84a3.

f.d:
sgra gcan rang 'gros kyis lhun po dang rgyu skar la 'khor tshul tsam ma gtogs/ sgra gcan rang gi g.yas g.yon du 'khor tshul ma gsungs shing / rtsa rgyud dang mu stegs pa'i byed rtsis la kha 'phangs mdzad pa yin te/ de yang 'grel chen las/
de nyid sgra gcan 'khor ba'i dbang gis shes par bya ste/ byed pa gzhan thams cad la rab tu grags pa'i phyir 'dir bcom ldan 'das 'jam dpal gyis 'bad pa ma mdzad do/[50] / zhes dang / yang 'grel chen las/
rtsa ba'i rgyud dam gzhan gyi byed pa gzhan la yang sgra gcan 'khor ba la sogs pa shes par bya'o/[51] / zhes gsungs so/ /

This, and Rāhu’s self-orbiting around Meru and through the lunar mansions, is all the Great Commentary mentions on this topic, and it does not expound on any left and right movements. These are explained by reference to the Root Tantra and to karaṇa astronomy. The Great Commentary states:
Know that this is due to Rāhu’s orbits. This is well known in all karaṇa systems, and therefore here the conqueror Mañjuśrī did not persist.[92] Also:
The orbiting and so forth of Rāhu can be known from the Root Tantra and from the karaṇa works of others.[93]

d.div: [50] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 84_na3
[51] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 84_na6
[92] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 84a3.
[93] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 84a6.

f.d:
des na zla nyi la sgra gcan 'jug pa ri mo la shar ba bzhin mi 'ong ba ni sgra gcan 'khor tshul ji lta ba bzhin ma shes pa'i skyon yin no/ / de yang sgra gcan la rang gi g.yas g.yon du 'khor ba'i lho bgrod byang bgrod ni yod de/ 'grel chen las/
'dir khyim gyi 'khor lo la gza' thams cad byang du 'gro ba dang lhor 'gro ba yod de/ dper na nyi mas rgyu skar longs spyod pa'i dbang dang khyim drug longs spyod pa'i dbang gis bzhin no/[52] / zhes gza' thams cad la lho bgrod byang bgrod yod par gsungs pas so/ /

Therefore Rāhu’s engagement with the sun and moon not occurring as calculated in the charts is due to the fault of not knowing precisely its orbiting habits. Within its left and right orbiting, Rāhu has its northward and southward journeys. The Great Commentary says:
In the circle of houses, every planet travels south and north. The sun, for example, occupies the lunar mansions and the six houses.[94] Therefore every planet has its northward and southward passages. /81/

d.div: [52] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 85_na3
[94] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 85a3.

f.d: gnyis pa de rnams nam mkha' la 'khor tshul gyi go la bshad pa

d.i: How the stars and planets orbit the skies

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ gzhan gyi 'dod pa la brtag pa dang / rang gi lugs rnam par gzhag pa'o/ /
This is under two outlines: 1. Examination of the assertions of others 2. Presentation of our own position
dang po [gzhan gyi 'dod pa la brtag pa ]ni/

d.i: Examination of the assertions of others

f.d:
mkhas pa phal che ba (jo zhal 'khrul sel/ zhal lung sogs mang por/)dag 'di ltar bzhed de/
de yang gzhu'i rnam pa'i dus khyim dag la go la'i dbus nas lhor ni me'i dkyil 'khor la gnas shing /[53] /zhes pa ni gzhu'i rnam pa'i khyim drug la go la nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i ri mo'i dbus nas rgyu skar gyi 'khor lo phyed kyi rgyu skar gyi 'khor lo lhor gnas so/ / byang du de ni bsil ba'i ri ste pad 'dab bzang po bzhin du shar du lug dang srang sogs la'o/ /zhes pa ni lhor khyim drug la so sor rgyu skar gyi 'khor lo phyed gnas pa ji lta ba de bzhin du go la'i ri mo'i dbus nas byang du khyim so so'i dbye bas khyim drug la gnas so/ / shar du lug dang srang sogs te bu mo'i mthar thug pa la gnas shing / de bzhin du srang la sogs pa nya'i mthar thug pa la gnas so/ / zhes sogs rgyud 'grel 'di rnams kyi don

The Great Commentary says:
“South from the center of the gola, the bow-shaped houses of time,[95] dwelling in the fire mandala.” This means that from the center of the gola chart drawn at the time of equal day and night, the bow-shaped formation of six houses, half of the circle of stars, dwell in the south. “In the north, the Śīta Mountains and, like fine lotus petals, Aries in the east, Libra, and so forth.” This means that just as in the south the six houses dwell within half the circle of stars, similarly, north from the center of the gola chart, there dwell, by division, six houses. “Aries in the east, Libra, and so forth” means that it stretches as far as Virgo. Similarly Libra and the others reach as far as Pisces.[96] According to most scholars, the meaning of this passage from the Great Commentary, which incorporates citations from the Condensed Tantra, is the following.

d.div: [53] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 85_na7
[95] dus. Time or season; word-numeral for six, probably referring to either the six seasons of a year or simply to the six houses in the southern half of the gola chart.
[96] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 85a7.

f.d: lho gling dbus ma 'dir dpyid mnyam 'ong ba'i dus kyi snga dro nyi ma lug khyim dang bcas pa shar gling gi steng gi nam mkha' la lho byang gi cha gnyis su byas pa'i cha gnyis po de'i mtshams nas nub gling gi steng gi nam mkha' la lho byang gi cha gnyis su byas pa'i cha gnyis kyi mtshams tshun chad kyi lhun po'i steng la yid kyis ri mo bris pa'i ri mo'i byang shar gyi cha gnyis kyi cha shar mar lug khyim dang / de bzhin du dbang ldan du glang dang / byang la cha gnyis su byas pa'i byang nub mar 'khrig pa dang / phyed byang shar mar kar kaT dang / rlung du seng+ge dang nub kyi'ang cha gnyis kyi nub nub mar bu mo ste byang gi khyim drug dang / de bzhin du nub shar mar srang ngad / bden bral du sdig pa dang / lho'i yang cha gnyis kyi lho'i cha nub mar gzhu dang / lho shar mar chu srin dang / mer bum pa dang / shar gyi phyed nub mar nya ste srang nas nya'i bar lho'i khyim drug go/ /

From here in the central southern sector on the morning of the spring equinox, the sun is in Aries above the skies of the eastern sector. These skies are divided into northern and southern parts. This division stretches across to the western sector, where the skies are also divided north and south. From this dividing line and above Meru, a chart is projected with the mind. In the northern part of the chart, in the eastern section[97] of the east, is Aries. In the northeast is Taurus. The north is in two parts. To the west of the north is Gemini, and in the half of the north to the east dwells Cancer. In the northwest is Leo. The west is also in two parts. In its western half lies Virgo. These are the six houses of the north. Similarly, in the eastern half of the west is Libra. In the southwest is Scorpio. The south is in two parts. In the western part is Sagittarius and in the eastern part, Capricorn. In the southeast is Aquarius, and in the western half of the east lies Pisces. The houses from the Libra to Pisces are the six houses of the south.

d.div: [97] East as used here refers to a counterclockwise direction or a direction to the right from any point on the circumference while facing the center. West is the opposite.

f.d: de yang shar gling gi steng thad nas nub gling gi steng thad kyi bar lhun po'i dbus kyi nam mkha' la yid kyis ri mo bris pa'i byang gi khyim lug nas bu mo'i bar drug gi dbyibs pad 'dab bzang po'i rnam pa dang / srang nas nya'i bar lho'i khyim drug gi dbyibs gzhu'i rnam par gnas pa/ pad 'dab bzang po bzhin du zhes sogs dang / gzhu'i rnam pa'i dus kyi khyim dag la zhes sogs rtsa 'grel gyi don yin par 'chad par byed do/ /

Furthermore, in this mentally constructed chart projected from the skies above Meru, /82/ which is the midway point between the skies directly above the eastern sector and the skies directly above the western sector, the six northern houses from Aries to Virgo are said to be in the shape of fine lotus petals, and the six southern houses from the Libra to Pisces are said to be arranged in the shape of a bow. This is explained as being the meaning of the phrases “like fine lotus petals” and “the bow-shaped houses of time,” as found in the tantra and its commentary.

de ni mi 'thad de/ lho gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi dpyid mnyam gyi snga dro nyi ma lug khyim dang bcas pa shar gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi steng thad na gnas pa'i dus der khyim rnams gling bcu gnyis kyi rang rang gi rgyu lam la bkod pa'i tshe byang gi khyim drug gi dbyibs pad ma'i 'dab ma'i rnam par 'ong yang / bsil ba'i ri ste zhes pa'i don ma tshang ba dang / lho'i khyim drug gi dbyibs gzhu'i rnam par yang mi 'ong ba'i phyir ro/ /

This explanation is incorrect. When the sun is in Aries directly above the central meridian of the central eastern sector on the morning of the spring equinox at the central meridian of the central southern sector, and the houses are arranged upon their paths over the twelve sectors, it is true that the six houses of the north are of the shape of lotus petals. However, in this depiction, the phrase “In the north, the Śīta Mountains” makes no sense. The formation of the six houses of the south are also not in the shape of a bow.

de la kha cig na re/ de'i tshe snga dro byang du pad 'dab kyi rnam par 'ong zhing / phyi 'phred nyi ma lug khyim dang bcas pa nub gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi steng thad du sleb pa'i tshe lho'i khyim drug gi dbyibs gzhu'i rnam par yod pas skyon med cing / 'grel chen rgyud dang bcas par de ltar gsungs pa yang nyin de'i thog mtha' gnyis la dgongs pa yin no zhes gsung ste de yang 'thad par ma mthong ste/ rgyud 'grel las/ byang khyim drug bkod pa'i dbyibs pad 'dab kyi rnam par gnas pa dang /[54] lho khyim drug bkod pa'i dbyibs gzhu'i rnam par gnas par gsungs pa dus gcig la 'ong ba la dgongs pa'i phyir ro/ /[55]

Some say that in the morning, the houses in the north are in the formation of lotus petals, while in the afternoon, the sun together with Aries will arrive at the center of the central western sector. At that time the six houses of the south are in the formation of a bow. Therefore the thinking behind the passage from the tantra and commentary is that it should be applied to both the beginning and the end of the day. However I cannot see this as being valid, because the statement from the Great Commentary that the six houses of the north are arranged as lotus petals and the six of the south are in the formation of a bow refers to an event happening at one particular time.

d.div: [54] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 85_ba1_'gyur cung mi mthun/
[55] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 85_na7_'gyur cung mi mthun/

f.d: gzhan yang lugs de smra ba thams cad kyis go la nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i ri mo'i dbus nas zhes sogs kyi ri mo shar gling nas nub gling gi bar gyi lhun po'i steng gi nam mkha' la yid kyis bris pa'i ri mo'i byang phyogs kyi khyim drug lhun po'i byang dang / ri mo'i lho phyogs kyi khyim drug lhun po'i lho na yod pa gzhu'i rnam pa'i dus khyim dag la go la'i dbus nas zhes sogs kyi rgyud 'grel pa dang bcas pa'i don du 'chad pa ni shin tu mi rigs te/ khyim bcu gnyis kyi go la'i ri mo zlum por bskor ba'i dbus su ri mos bcad pa'i byang du khyim drug bkod pa de ni/ byang du de ni bsil ba'i ri ste zhes bsil ri la thug pa'i rnam par bkod cing / lhor khyim drug bkod pa yang / gzhu'i rnam pa'i dus khyim dag la go la'i dbus nas lhor ni me'i dkyil 'khor la gnas shing zhes me ri la thug pa'i rnam par dgod par gsungs shing / khyed rnams ltar na byang du pad 'dab bzang po'i dbyibs kyi mtha' me ri'i phyogs su 'ong ba dang / lhor gzhu'i dbyibs su byung ba'i dus der bsil ri'i phyogs su 'ong dgos pas/ gzhu'i rnam pa'i dus khyim zhes sogs rtsa 'grel gyi don las phyin ci log tu 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ /

Furthermore, all those who follow the above traditions say that in the chart (mentioned in the phrase “from the center of the gola chart drawn at the time of equal day and night”) that is projected in the skies above Meru from the eastern sector across to the western sector, the six houses arranged in the north of that chart are north of Meru, and the six houses placed in the south of the chart are south of Meru. To posit this as the meaning of the commentary and tantra passage beginning “South from the center of the gola, the bow-shaped houses of time” is completely incorrect. What the commentary is saying is that a circular gola chart of the twelve houses is to be bisected, and six houses placed in the northern section. This depiction reaches the Śīta Mountains, as in the phrase “In the north the Śīta Mountains.” /83/ Six houses are placed in the south, and these are depicted as reaching the Mountains of Fire, as in the sentence, “South from the center of the gola, the bow-shaped houses of time, dwelling in the fire mandala.” If the arrangement were as you have stated above, the outer edge of petal-shaped formation in the north would reach to the Mountains of Fire, and the northern part of the bow-shaped formation would reach to the regions of the Śīta Mountains. This would be completely outside the meaning of quotes from the tantra and commentary, such as those beginning “South from the center of the gola, the bow-shaped houses of time.”

des na byang khyim drug gi rnam par bkod pa lho gling dbus ma 'di nyid kyi thad ka'i bsil ri'i rnam par bkod pa la thug pa dang / lho'i khyim drug gi rnam par bkod pa lho gling dbus ma 'di nyid kyi thad ka'i me ri'i rnam par bkod pa la thug pa'i rnam par byed dgos te/ de las gzhan du na 'grel chen las/
dbus su 'khor lo phyed kyi ri mo zhes pa ni khyim gyi 'khor lo'i dbus su nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i ri mo ste dpag tshad stong phrag bdun cu rtsa lnga'i dbus su phyed dang bcas pa'i stong phrag sum cu rtsa bdun gyi mthar 'gyur ro/[56] / zhes gsungs pa'i ri mo yang bsil ri dang me ri'i bar gyi nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i nyi ma'i 'gro lam mtshon byed la mi 'dri bar lhun po'i steng gi bar snang la yid kyis 'di dgos par thal ba'i phyir ro/ /

Therefore it must be that the depiction of the six houses of the north meets the depiction of Śīta Mountains directly in line with our central southern sector, and the depiction of the six houses of the south meets the depiction of the Mountains of Fire also directly in line with our central southern sector. If it were otherwise, consider this quote from the Great Commentary:
“In the center the chart of half the circle” refers to the chart of the equinox in the center of the circle of houses, at the point of 37,500 yojana, half of the 75,000 yojana.[98] According to your assertion, this chart showing the sun’s path on the equinox between the Śīta Mountains and the Mountains of Fire would also have to be projected from the skies above Meru.

d.div: [56] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 85_ba5
[98] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 85b5. 75,000 yojana is the distance between the Śīta Mountains and the Mountains of Fire, and on the equinox the sun travels overhead on the midway point.

f.d: gnyis pa rang gi lugs rnam par gzhag pa

['di ]la gsum/ gang zhig 'khor ba khyim gyi gnas lugs bshad pa dang / khyim de rnams sa dum bu bcu gnyis kyi steng du 'khor ba'i tshul bshad pa dang / de la nyi mas longs spyad pa las nyin mtshan ring thung sogs su 'gyur ba'i tshul bshad pa'o/ /

This is under three headings: 1. An explanation of the orbiting houses 2. How the houses orbit above the twelve sectors 3. An explanation of how the length of day and night are formed by the sun’s occupation of the houses
dang po ni

d.i: An explanation of the orbiting houses

f.d: skar khongs re la cha bzhi bzhir byas pa'i cha re la rkang pa'i tha snyad byas te/ de lta bu'i rkang pa dgu dgu la khyim mam dus sbyor rer byas pa'i khyim bcu gnyis ni lug /glang / 'khrig pa/ kar kaT/ seng+ge/ bu mo/ srang / sdig pa/ gzhu/ chu srin/ bum pa/ nya'i khyim rnams so/ / de yang tha skar dang bra nye dang smin drug gi rkang pa gcig gi bar lug khyim dang / de nas smin drug gi rkang pa gsum dang snar ma dang mgo'i rkang pa gnyis kyi bar glang khyim dang / de nas mgo'i rkang pa phyi ma gnyis dang lag dang nab so'i rkang pa gsum gyi bar 'khrig pa'i khyim dang / de nas nab so'i rkang pa phyi ma dang

Each lunar mansion is divided into four, and each quarter is known as a step. Nine such steps make up one house or lagna.[99] The twelve houses are those of Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces.[100] The lunar mansions of aśvinī, bharaṇī, and one step of kṛttikā make up Aries. Three steps of kṛttikā, the whole of rohiṇī, and two steps of mṛgaśīrṣa make up Taurus. The last two steps of mṛgaśīrṣa, all of ārdrā, and three steps of punarvasu make up Gemini. The last step of punarvasu, plus all of puṣya and āśleṣa make up Cancer. /84/

d.div: [99] dus sbyor, lagna. Here refers to the twelve houses or signs of the zodiac. As all twelve houses pass over any given meridian in a day, a new ascendant, or lagna, rises about every two hours. See glossary for other meanings; also Lochen, chap. 15.

[100] The twelve houses taught in Kālacakra correspond to the twelve zodiacal signs portrayed in Indian and Western astronomy. The names are virtually the same also. They are called houses rather than signs but do not correspond to the system of fixed houses used in astrology.

f.d: rgyal dang skag gi bar kar kaTa'i khyim dang / mchu dang gre dang dbo'i rkang pa dang po'i bar seng+ge'i khyim dang / dbo'i rkang pa phyi ma gsum dang me bzhi dang nag pa'i rkang pa dang po gnyis kyi bar bu mo'i khyim dang / nag pa'i rkang pa phyi ma gnyis dang sa ri dang sa ga'i rkang pa snga ma gsum gyi bar srang gi khyim dang / sa ga'i rkang pa phyi ma dang lha mtshams dang snon gyi bar sdig pa'i khyim dang / snubs dang chu stod dang chu smad kyi rkang pa dang po'i bar gzhu'i khyim dang / chu smad kyi rkang pa phyi ma gsum dang / gro bzhin dang byi bzhin skar khongs gcig tu byas pa dang / mon gre'i phyed rkang pa snga ma gnyis kyi bar chu srin gyi khyim dang / mon gre'i rkang pa phyi ma gnyis dang mon gru dang khrums stod kyi rkang pa snga ma gsum gyi bar bum pa'i khyim dang / khrums stod kyi rkang pa phyi ma dang khrums smad dang nam gru rnams ni nya'i khyim mo/ /

Magha, pūrvaphalgunī, and the first step of uttaraphalgunī make up Leo. The last three steps of uttaraphalgunī, all of hasta, and the first two steps of citrā make up Virgo. The last two steps of citrā, the whole of svātī, and the first three steps of viśakhā make up Libra. The last step of viśakhā, all of anurādha, and jyeṣṭha make up Scorpio. Mūla, pūrvāṣāḍhā, and the first step of uttarāṣāḍhā make up Sagittarius. The last three steps of uttarāṣāḍhā, all of śravaṇa and uttarāṣāḍhā counted as one, and the first half of dhaniṣṭha make up Capricorn. The last two steps of dhaniṣṭha, all of śatabhiṣak, and the last three steps of pūrvabhādra make up Aquarius. The last step of pūrvabhādra, all of uttarabhādra, and revatī make up Pisces.

de ltar byas pa'i khyim bcu gnyis so so'i mtshams ni/
skar mig dbyug tshes lug gi tshad/ / rig byed mkha' me glang du brjod/ / ro dang zhe lnga 'khrig pa yi+in/ / dgu dang nam mkha' kar ka Ta/ / drug dang bco lnga seng+ge la/ / bcu gsum sum cu bu mor dran/ / bco lnga zhe lnga srang yin zhing / / nor zla stong pa sdig par go/ / nyi shu bco lnga gzhu yi tshad/ / zung mig sum cu chu srin khyim/ / rgyal ba mda' chu bum par grags/ / 'khor lo nya ru shes par bya/[57] / zhes dbyangs 'char las bshad pa ltar ro/ /

The boundaries of each of the twelve houses are as explained in Arising Letters:
Eyes, lunar mansions, and lunar-day hours is the measure of Aries,[101] veda, sky, and fire is said to be Taurus, taste and forty-five is Gemini, nine and space is Cancer, six and fifteen Leo, thirteen and thirty is thought of as Virgo, fifteen and forty-five is Libra, wealth, moon, and emptiness is Scorpio, twenty and fifteen is the measure of Sagittarius, union, eyes, and thirty is Capricorn, conqueror and arrows is known to be Aquarius, circle is known to be Pisces.[102]

d.div: [57] sde dge_4322_bstan/ bzo rig pa/ ngo g.yul las rnam par rgyal ba zhes pa'i dbyangs 'char/ le'u/ 254_na6

[101] Using word-numerals, these verses denote how many lunar mansions make up the boundary of each house, as detailed in the previous paragraph. The first figure is the number of lunar mansions passed if aśvinī, the first mansion, is counted as one, or the number of the actual lunar mansion if aśvinī is counted as zero. The second figure(s) is(are) number(s) of hours. Each position marks the far boundary of each of the houses. For example, Two (eyes) lunar mansions (the first two — aśvinī and bharanī) and fifteen (lunar-time) hours of the third is the measurement of the house of Aries, which takes up the first two and one quarter lunar mansions. Taurus extends to the fourth (veda) lunar mansion and thirty hours (sky = 0, fire = 3) of the fifth.
[102] Toh 4322 Tengyur, bzo rig pa, ngo chap. 2, 54a6.

f.d: gnyis pa khyim de rnams sa dum bu bcu gnyis kyi steng du 'khor ba'i tshul bshad pa

d.i: How the houses orbit above the twelve sectors

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ 'dzam gling chung ngu 'di'i steng gi khyim bcu gnyis kyi 'gro lam rtogs pa'i thabs kyi go la bshad pa dang / de la brten nas sa dum bu bcu gnyis po thams cad kyi steng gi go la'i 'khor tshul go nus par bstan pa'o/ /

This is under two headings: 1. An explanation of the term gola as a way of understanding the path of the twelve houses above our Lesser Jambudvīpa 2. By understanding the above, how it is possible to understand the orbiting of the gola over each of twelve sectors
dang po [go la bshad pa ]ni/

d.i: An explanation of the term gola

f.d:
go la zhes pa saM skr-i ta'i skad sor bzhag yin zhing / de bod du bsgyur na sbubs dang khong dang zlum po dang sgang gshongs zhes pa rnams kyi don can du gnas pa las 'dir ni zlum po'i don can du gnas pa yin la/ de yang khyim gyi 'khor lo zlum po'i tshul gyis sa dum bu bcu gnyis kyi steng du 'khor ba la khyim gyi go la zhes bya zhing / de rtogs par byed pa'i thabs/
tha skar la sogs nag pa phyed du nyin dang mtshan mo mnyam pa'i dbus su go la'i ri mo'o/ / zhes sogs rgyud rtsa 'grel gyis bstan pa'i shog khra'i ri mo sogs bkod pa'i ri mo zlum po la yang go la zhes bya'o/ /

Gola is a transliteration of a Sanskrit word. If it were translated into Tibetan, it could be rendered as cylindrical, interior, round, and uneven in height. Here it means round,[103] and the spherical orbiting by the circle of lunar mansions over the twelve sectors is known as the gola of the houses. The way to understand this gola is from the circular charts drawn on paper and described in the tantra and its commentary with quotes such as:
In the center, from aśvinī up to to half of citrā,[104] the gola chart of the equinox of day and night. /85/ These charts, therefore, are also known as gola.

d.div: [103] zlum po. Round in the sense of spherical or domelike as well as circular. Gola lends itself to a variety of interpretations. To paraphrase the Great Lexicon, p. 368, because it holds up the planets and stars above, it is that which “holds up high.” Because it rotates the houses above and the seasons on earth, it is that which “rotates.” Because it looms over the continents and the mountain ranges like a parasol, it is “domelike.” Above Meru it is high, but above the fire mandala it is low. Therefore, it is “uneven in height.” Because it possesses the force of the supporting wind, it is heavy, but because it possesses the force of the expelling wind, it is also light. There is the gola of the skies, of the sun, and of the moon traversing the houses and lunar mansions of the earth and so on. This topic is treated to its own chapter in most astronomical treatises. See Lochen, chap. 13, and Gojo, chap. 2.
[104] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 85b2.

f.d: de yang / gzhu'i rnam pa'i dus khyim dag la zhes sogs rtsa 'grel gyi don shog khra'i ri mo rnams la brten nas 'dzam gling chung ngu 'di'i steng thad kyi khyim rnams kyi 'gro lam rtogs par byed tshul ni/ dang por gong du bshad pa ltar bsil ri nas me ri'i bar gyi chu'i dkyil 'khor dang sa dum bu bcu gnyis rnams mtshon byed kyi ri mo bkod la/ de nas lho gling dbus ma 'dzam gling chung ngu 'di mtshon byed kyi ri mo de'i dbus kyi thad kyi bsil ri nas me ri+i mtshon byed kyi+i ri mo la thug gi bar gyi dbus der de'i thad kyi nam mkha' zlum po mtshon byed kyi ri mo zlum po gcig bkod pa ni go la'i ri mo zhes pa'i don te/ de nas zlum po de'i shar nub kyi dbus drang por ri mo gcig gis bcad pa'i ri mo de ni go la nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i ri mo'i dbus nas zhes pa'i don gling 'di'i tshangs thig gi nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i nyi ma'i 'gro lam mtshon byed yin/

The meaning of such quotes beginning “South from the center of the gola, the bow-shaped houses of time” is expressed in charts drawn on paper, and through them the path of the houses over our Lesser Jambudvīpa can be understood. First a diagram[105] is drawn to depict the water mandala and the twelve sectors between the Śīta Mountains and the Mountains of Fire, as previously described. Then, from the midway point between the Śīta Mountains that directly face the central point of the depiction of Lesser Jambudvīpa, the central sector of the south, to the depiction of the fire mandala, a circle is drawn to illustrate the circular skies above this central point. This is the meaning of the term gola chart. Then this circle is bisected directly along its east-west diameter to illustrate the path of the sun on the equinox at the central meridian of this sector. This diagram is the “chart” in the quote, “from the center of the gola chart drawn at the time of equal day and night.”

d.div: [105] ri mo. Drawing, diagram, chart, line.

f.d: de nas ri mo zlum po de la shar lho nub byang bzhir cha gnyis gnyis dang mtshams bzhir cha re re ste cha bcu gnyis su phye ba'i shar gyi cha byang mar lug dang / dbang ldan gyi char glang dang / byang gi cha shar mar 'khrig pa dang / byang gi cha nub mar kar ka Ta dang / rlung gi char seng+ge dang / nub kyi cha byang mar bu mo ste byang gi khyim drug gi 'gro lam mtshon byed do/ / slar yang nub kyi cha lho mar srang dang / bden bral gyi char sdig pa dang / lho'i cha nub mar gzhu dang / lho'i cha shar mar chu srin dang / me'i char bum pa dang / shar gyi cha lho mar nya ste lho'i khyim drug gi 'gro lam mtshon byed do/ / 'di dag ni 'grel chen las/ 'dir shar gyi phyed du lug dang / zhes pa nas/ shar gyi phyed du nya'o zhes pa ni go la la khyim dgod pa'o [58] zhes pa'i bar gsungs pa'i dgongs pa yin no/ /

Within that circle, east, south, west, and north are each divided into two parts. Together with the four intermediate directions, this makes twelve parts in all. In the northern part of the east is Aries, in the northeast is Taurus, in the eastern part of the north is Gemini, in the western part of the north is Cancer, in the northwest is Leo, and in the northern part of the west is Virgo. This illustrates the path of the six northern houses. In the southern part of the west is Libra, in the southwest is Scorpio, in the western part of the south is Sagittarius, in the eastern part of the south is Capricorn, in the southeast is Aquarius, and in the southern part of the east is Pisces. This illustrates the path of the six southern houses. This is the thinking behind the passage in the Great Commentary beginning “in one half of the east is Aries” up to “in one half of the east is Pisces is an explanation of the houses in the gola.”

d.div: [58] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 85_ba2

f.d: de ltar na nyi bar khyim bcu gnyis po gang dang gang du sleb ma thag gi nyin de'i nyi ma'i lho gling dbus ma'i tshangs thig gi thad kyi 'gro lam yang khyim de dang de'i thog ma'i skar ma'i 'gro lam nyid yin no/ / de yang dper na nyi bar lug khyim du sleb ma thag gi nyin nyi ma lug khyim dang bcas pa lho'i gling dbus ma'i tshangs thig gi steng thad gyi nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i lam la 'gro ba bzhin no/ / des na tha skar la sogs nag pa phyed du zhes sogs nas/ shar du lug dang srang sogs la'o/ / zhes pa'i bar gyi rtsa 'grel rnams kyis ni lho gling dbus ma 'dzam gling chung ngu 'di'i go la bye brag tu bshad pa yin no/ /

In this way, as soon as the mean sun arrives in any of the twelve houses, the path of the sun of that solar day at the central meridian of the central southern sector is also the path of the first stars of that particular house. For example, on the day on which the mean sun enters Aries, the sun together with Aries travels the path of the equinox over the central meridian of the central southern sector. Therefore the text from the tantra and commentary from “In the center, from aśvinī up to half of citrā” to “Aries in the east and Libra” /86/ is explaining particularly the gola of Lesser Jambudvīpa at the center of the southern sector.

'o na gzhu'i rnam pa zhes pa dang / pad 'dab bzang po bzhin zhes pa'i don ji ltar yin snyam na/ de'i don ni lho gling dbus ma 'di'i steng thad kyi khyim rnams kyi 'gro lam mtshon byed du bkod pa'i byang khyim drug dang lho khyim drug gi dbus su nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i ri mos bcad pa'i lho khyim drug dbyibs 'od ma'i gzhu'i rnam pa can lho me ri'i phyogs la gnas pa dang / byang khyim drug dbyi+ibs pad+ma_'i 'dab ma phyed kyi dbyibs can byang bsil ri'i phyogs la gnas zhes pa yin te/ de las gzhan du snga ma rnams bzhed pa ltar yin na gong du bshad pa ltar gzhu'i rnam pa can me ri'i phyogs la gnas pa dang / pad+ma'i rnam pa can bsil ri'i phyogs la gnas pa'i don bshad du med par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / de yang lho khyim dang byang khyim drug drug bkod pa'i dbyibs zlum po phyed pa'i rnam par 'dra na'ang / me tog 'phreng 'dzin gyi sdeb sbyor bsgrig pa'i phyir du pad 'dab bzang po zhes gsungs pa yin no/ /

But what is the meaning of “bow-shaped” and “like fine lotus petals”? It is this. In the depiction of the path of the houses directly over the central southern sector, the six houses of the south and the six of the north are bisected by a line representing the equinox path. The six houses of the south are then in the shape of a bamboo bow and are depicted in the regions of the Mountains of Fire in the south. The six houses of the north are in the shape of the petals of half a lotus and are depicted in the regions of the Śīta Mountains in the north. If it were otherwise, as those mentioned above have maintained, then the bow formation in the regions of the Mountains of Fire and the lotus formation in the regions of the Śīta Mountains could not be explained. Also, the shapes of both sets of six houses may be similar in that they are both semicircular, but in order to put these shapes into sragdhara meter,[106] the words “fine lotus petals” were used.

d.div: [106] Sragdhara, or “garland” meter: four-line verses with twenty-one syllables per line.

f.d:
gnyis pa de la brten nas sa dum bu bcu gnyis po thams cad kyi steng gi go la'i 'khor tshul go nus par bstan pa ni 'grel chen las/
da ni 'jig rten spyi lugs kyi go la'i rgya gsungs pa/ me nas bsil ba'i ri yi mtshams su dpag tshad stong phrag mkha' dang nam mkha' mkha' dang mda' ri bo/ / zhes pa ste 'dir lho me'i dkyil 'khor nas byang kha ba can chen po'i mtshams su go la'i tshad dpag tshad stong phrag bdun cu rtsa lnga'o/[59] / zhes sogs kyis sa dum bu bcu gnyis po thams cad kyi rang rang gi steng thad kyi bsil ri nas me ri la thug gi bar gyi steng gi dbus drang por rang rang gi nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i nyi ma'i 'gro lam mtshon byed kyi ri mos bcad pa'i ri mo'i byang phyogs bsil ri ngos la dpag tshad stong phrag bdun cu rtsa lnga'i phyed dpag tshad stong phrag sum cu rtsa phyed dang brgyad dang / de bzhin du ri mo'i lho phyogs me ri ngos la dpag tshad kyi grangs stong phrag sum cu rtsa phyed dang brgyad yin par dngos su bstan nas/ sa dum bu lhag ma bcu gcig gi steng thad kyi khyim bcu gnyis po rang rang gi 'gro lam ni lho gling dbus mas mtshon nas bstan to/ /

By understanding the above, how it is possible to understand the orbiting of the gola over each of the twelve sectors The Great Commentary says:
Now the gola of the world is spoken of in detail. “From the fire to the borders of the Śīta Mountains is a distance of space, space, space, arrows, and mountains, as thousands of yojana.” This means that from the southern fire mandala to the borders of the great snows of the north is a distance of 75,000 yojana.[107] This and subsequent passages clearly reveal that when charts are drawn depicting meridians running from above the Śīta Mountains directly in line with each of the twelve sectors stretching to a similar point above the Mountains of Fire, and when these meridians are bisected midway by lines illustrating the path of the equinox sun over each of the sectors, then the northern parts of these intersections would stretch for a distance of half of 75,000 yojana, or 37,500 yojana, to the edge of the Śīta Mountains. Similarly, south of the intersection, the distance to the edge of the Mountains of Fire would also be 37,500 yojana. From this the pathway of the twelve houses over the other eleven sectors can be known and is illustrated by the chart of the central southern sector. /87/

d.div: [59] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 85_ba4
[107] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 85b4.

f.d: 'o na gling ngam sa dum bu lhag ma bcu gcig gi steng thad kyi khyim bcu gnyis kyi rang rang gi 'gro lam ji ltar yin snyam na/ de ni 'di ltar yin te de yang sa dum bu bcu gcig po thams cad kyi+i rang rang gi steng thad kyi bsil ri nas me ri la thug gi bar zlum por bskor ba'i shar nub kyi dbus drang por ri mos bcad pa ni gling rang rang gi nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i dus kyi nyi ma khyim dang skar ma gang gi steng du 'ong ba'i khyim dang skar ma'i 'gro lam mtshon byed yin no/ / de yang gling rang rang gi shar nub kyi dbus dang po'i tshangs thig gi dbang du byas na lho gling shar mar nya khyim dang / shar gling nub mar bum pa dang / shar gling dbus mar chu srin dang / de bzhin du g.yon skor du shar gling shar mar gzhu khyim yin pa nas/ lho gling nub mar glang khyim yin pa'i bar du yin no/ /

What is the pathway of the twelve houses over the other eleven sectors? A circle is drawn from the Śīta Mountains directly facing each of the sectors to a similar point directly above the Mountains of Fire, and its east-west diameter is bisected. This illustrates the path of the houses and lunar mansions in which the sun has arrived at the time of the equinox for each of the sectors. Therefore, from the central meridian at the east-west center of the eastern sector of the south, the sun is in Pisces at the spring equinox. In the western sector of the east, it is in Aquarius, and in the central eastern sector it is in Capricorn. Moving to the left, this continues from Sagittarius in the eastern sector of the east up to Taurus in the western sector of the south.

de la gling bcu gcig po rang rang gi steng thad kyi khyim bcu gnyis po tshang ba'i 'gro lam mtshon byed ni/ gling rang rang gi steng thad zlum por bskor ba'i zlum po rnams la shar lho nub byang gi phyogs bzhi la cha gnyis gnyis dang mtshams bzhir cha re re ste cha bcu gnyis bcu gnyis su phye ba'i lho gling shar ma'i shar gyi cha byang mar nya khyim dang / dbang ldan du lug dang / byang gi cha shar mar glang dang / byang gi cha nub mar 'khrig pa dang / rlung du karka Ta dang / nub kyi cha byang mar seng+ge ste gling de nyid kyi byang khyim drug dang / de bzhin du nub kyi cha lho mar bu mo dang / bden bral du srang dang / lho'i cha nub mar sdig pa dang / lho'i cha shar mar gzhu dang / mer chu srin dang / shar gyi cha lho mar bum pa ste lho khyim drug go/ /

To illustrate the pathway of all twelve houses above each of the eleven sectors, the four directions of east, south, west, and north within the charts are divided into two parts each. Together with the four intermediate directions, this makes twelve sectors. Applying this to the eastern southern sector, in the northern section of the east lies Pisces, in the northeast is Aries, in the eastern section of the north is Taurus, in the western part is Gemini, in the northwest is Cancer, and in the northern section of the west is Leo. These are the six northern houses. Similarly, in the southern section of the west is found Virgo, in the southwest is Libra, in the western section of the south lies Scorpio, in the eastern section of the south is Sagittarius, in the southeast is Capricorn, and in the southern section of the east lies Aquarius. These are the six southern houses.

de bzhin du shar gling nub ma la yang cha bcu gnyis su che ba'i shar gyi cha byang mar bum pa dang / dbang ldan du nya dang / byang gi cha shar mar lug dang / byang gi cha nub mar glang dang / rlung du 'khrig pa dang / nub kyi cha byang mar ka rkaT ste byang khyim drug dang / nub kyi cha lho mar seng+ge dang / bden bral du bu mo dang / lho'i cha nub mar srang dang / lho'i cha shar mar sdig pa dang / mer gzhu dang / shar gyi cha lho mar chu srin te lho'i khyim drug go/ /

Likewise, in the western southern sector, the directions are divided into twelve parts. In the northern section of the east is Aquarius, in the northeast Pisces, in the eastern section of the north Aries, in the western section of the north Taurus, in the southwest Gemini, and in the northern section of the west Cancer. These are the six northern houses. In the southern section of the west lies Leo, in the southwest Virgo, in the western section of the south Libra, in the eastern section of the south Scorpio, in the southeast Sagittarius, and in the southern section of the east Capricorn. These are the six southern houses. /88/

de bzhin du shar gling dbus ma la yang cha bcu gnyis su phye ba'i shar gyi cha byang mar chu srin dang / de nas g.yon bskor gyi gnyis pa dbang ldan du bum pa dang / gsum pa byang gi cha shar mar nya dang / bzhi pa byang gi cha nub mar lug dang / lnga pa rlung du glang dang / drug pa nub kyi cha byang mar 'khrig pa ste byang khyim drug go/ / de nas bdun pa nub kyi cha lho mar karka Ta dang / brgyad pa bden bral du seng+ge dang / dgu pa lho'i cha nub mar bu mo dang / bcu pa lho'i cha shar mar srang dang / bcu gcig pa mer sdig pa dang / bcu gnyis pa shar gyi cha lho mar gzhu ste lho'i khyim drug go/ /

Similarly the central eastern sector is divided into twelve parts. In the northern section of the east is found Capricorn. Then in the northeast, the second section moving to the left, is found Aquarius, in the third, the eastern section of the north, is Pisces, in the fourth, the western section of the north, is Aries, in the fifth, the northwest, is Taurus, and in the sixth, the northern section of the west, is Gemini. /89/ These are the six northern houses. In the seventh section, the southern section of the west, is Cancer; in the eighth, or the southwest is Leo; in the ninth, the western section of the south, is Virgo; in the tenth, or the eastern section of the south, is Libra; in the eleventh, or the southeast, is Scorpio; and in the twelfth, the southern section of the east, is Sagittarius. These are the six southern houses.

shar gling shar ma la yang cha bcu gnyis su phye ba'i shar gyi cha byang mar gzhu dang / dbang ldan du chu srin dang / byang gi cha shar mar bum pa dang / byang gi cha nub mar nya dang / rlung du lug dang / nub kyi cha byang mar glang ste byang khyim drug dang / nub kyi cha lho mar 'khrig pa dang / bden bral du karka Ta dang / lho'i cha nub mar seng+ge dang / lho'i cha shar mar bu mo dang / mer srang dang / shar gyi cha lho mar sdig pa ste lho khyim drug go/ /

The eastern sector of the east is also divided into twelve parts. In the northern section of the east is Sagittarius, in the northeast Capricorn, in the eastern section of the north Aquarius, in the western section of the north Pisces, in the northwest Aries, and in the northern section of the west Taurus. These are the six northern houses. In the southern section of the west lies Gemini, in the southwest Cancer, in the western section of the south Leo, in the eastern section of the south Virgo, in the southeast Libra, and in the southern section of the east Scorpio. These are the six southern houses.

yang byang gling nub ma la yang cha bcu gnyis su phye ba'i shar gyi cha byang mar sdig pa dang / dbang ldan du gzhu dang / byang gi cha shar mar chu srin dang / byang gi cha nub mar bum pa dang / rlung du nya dang / nub kyi cha byang mar lug ste byang khyim drug go/ /

In the western sector of the north the directions are also divided into twelve parts. In the northern section of the east lies Scorpio, in the northeast Sagittarius, in the eastern section of the north Capricorn, in the western section of the north Aquarius, in the northwest Pisces, and in the northern section of the west Aries. These are the six northern houses.

de nas nub kyi cha lho mar glang dang / bden bral du 'khrig pa dang / lho'i cha nub mar karka Ta dang / lho'i cha shar mar seng+ge dang / mer bu mo dang / shar gyi cha lho mar srang ste lho khyim drug go/ /

In the southern section of the west is Taurus, in the southwest is Gemini, in the western section of the south is Cancer, in the eastern section of the south is Leo, in the southeast is Virgo, and in the southern section of the east is Libra. These are the six southern houses.

yang byang gling dbus ma la cha bcu gnyis su phye ba'i shar gyi cha byang mar srang dang / dbang ldan du sdig pa dang / byang gi cha shar mar gzhu dang / byang gi cha nub mar chu srin dang / rlung du bum pa dang / nub kyi cha byang mar nya ste byang khyim drug go/ /

In the central sector of the north the directions are also divided into twelve parts. In the northern section of the east lies Libra, in the northeast Scorpio, in the eastern section of the north Sagittarius, in the western section of the north Capricorn, in the northwest Aquarius, and in the northern section of the west Pisces. These are the six northern houses.

de nas nub kyi cha lho mar lug dang / bden bral du glang dang / lho'i cha nub mar 'khrig pa dang / lho'i cha shar mar karka Ta dang / mer seng+ge dang / shar gyi cha lho mar bu mo ste lho khyim drug go/ /

In the southern section of the west is Aries, in the southwest is Taurus, in the western section of the south is Gemini, in the eastern section of the south is Cancer, in the southeast is Leo, and in the southern section of the east is Virgo. These are the six southern houses.

yang byang gling shar ma'i steng thad cha bcu gnyis su phye ba'i shar gyi cha byang mar bu mo dang / dbang ldan du srang dang / byang gi cha shar mar sdig pa dang / byang gi cha nub mar gzhu dang / rlung du chu srin dang / nub kyi cha byang mar bum pa ste byang khyim drug go/ /

In the eastern sector of the north the directions are divided into twelve parts. In the northern section of the east lies Virgo, in the northeast Libra, in the eastern section of the north Scorpio, in the western section of the north Sagittarius, in the northwest Capricorn, and in the northern section of the west Aquarius. These are the six northern houses.
nub gyi cha lho mar nya dang / bden bral du lug dang / lho'i cha nub mar glang dang / lho'i cha shar mar 'khrig pa dang / mer karka Ta dang / shar gyi cha lho mar seng+ge ste lho khyim drug go/ /

In the southern section of the west is Pisces, in the southwest is Aries, in the western section of the south is Taurus, in the eastern section of the south is Gemini, in the southeast is Cancer, and in the southern section of the east is Leo. These are the six southern houses.

yang nub gling nub ma'i steng thad cha bcu gnyis su phye ba'i shar gyi cha byang mar seng+ge dang / dbang ldan du bu mo dang / byang gi cha shar mar srang dang / byang gi cha nub mar sdig pa dang / rlung du gzhu dang / nub kyi cha byang mar chu srin te byang khyim drug go/ /

In the westernmost sector of the west the directions are divided into twelve parts. In the northern section of the east lies Leo, in the northeast Virgo, in the eastern section of the north Libra, in the western section of the north Scorpio, in the northwest Sagittarius, and in the northern section of the west Capricorn. These are the six northern houses.
nub kyi cha lho mar bum pa dang / bden bral du nya dang / lho'i cha nub mar lug dang / lho'i cha shar mar glang dang / mer 'khrig pa dang / shar gyi cha lho mar karka Ta ste lho khyim drug go/ /

In the southern section of the west is Aquarius, in the southwest is Pisces, in the western section of the south is Aries, in the eastern section of the south is Taurus, in the southeast is Gemini, and in the southern section of the east is Cancer. These are the six southern houses.

yang nub gling dbus ma'i steng thad cha bcu gnyis su phye ba'i shar gyi cha byang mar karka Ta dang / dbang ldan du seng+ge dang / byang gi cha shar mar bu mo dang / byang gi cha nub mar srang dang / rlung du sdig pa dang / nub kyi cha byang mar gzhu ste byang khyim drug go/ /

In the central sector of the north the directions are also divided into twelve parts. In the northern section of the east lies Cancer, in the northeast Leo, in the eastern section of the north Virgo, in the western section of the north Libra, in the northwest Scorpio, and in the northern section of the west Sagittarius. These are the six northern houses.
nub kyi cha lho mar chu srin dang / bden bral du bum pa dang / lho'i cha nub mar nya dang / lho'i cha shar mar lug dang / mer glang dang / shar gyi cha lho mar 'khrig pa ste lho khyim drug go/ /

In the southern section of the west is Capricorn, in the southwest is Aquarius, in the western section of the south is Pisces, in the eastern section of the south is Aries, in the southeast is Taurus, and in the southern section of the east is Gemini. These are the six southern houses.

yang nub gling shar ma'i steng thad cha bcu gnyis su phye ba'i shar gyi cha byang mar 'khrig pa dang / dbang ldan du karka Ta dang / byang gi cha shar mar seng+ge dang / byang gi cha nub mar bu mo dang / rlung du srang dang / nub kyi cha byang mar sdig pa ste byang khyim drug go/ /

In the easternmost sector of the west the directions are also divided into twelve parts. In the northern section of the east lies Gemini, in the northeast lies Cancer, in the eastern section of the north is Leo, in the western section of the north is Virgo, in the northwest is Libra, and in the northern section of the west is Scorpio. These are the six northern houses.
nub kyi cha lho mar gzhu dang / bden bral du chu srin dang / lho'i cha nub mar bum pa dang / lho'i cha shar mar nya dang / mer lug dang / shar gyi cha lho mar glang ste lho khyim drug go/

In the southern section of the west is Sagittarius, in the southwest is Capricorn, in the western section of the south is Aquarius, in the eastern section of the south is Pisces, in the southeast is Aries, and in the southern section of the east is Taurus. These are the six southern houses.

yang lho'i gling nub ma'i steng thad cha bcu gnyis su phye ba'i shar gyi cha byang mar glang dang / dbang ldan du 'khrig pa dang / byang gi cha shar mar karka Ta dang / byang gi cha nub mar seng+ge dang / rlung du bu mo dang / nub kyi cha byang mar srang ste byang khyim drug go/ /

In the western sector of the south the directions are also divided into twelve parts. In the northern section of the east lies Taurus, in the northeast Gemini, in the eastern section of the north Cancer, in the western section of the north Leo, in the northwest Virgo, and in the northern section of the west Libra. These are the six northern houses.
nub kyi cha lho mar sdig pa dang / bden bral du gzhu dang / lho'i cha nub mar chu srin dang / lho'i cha shar mar bum pa dang / mer nya dang / shar gyi cha lho mar lug ste lho khyim drug go/ /

In the southern section of the west is Scorpio, in the southwest is Sagittarius, in the western section of the south is Capricorn, in the eastern section of the south is Aquarius, in the southeast is Pisces, and in the southern section of the east is Aries. These are the six southern houses.

de ltar na gling bcu gnyis po rang rang gi steng thad kyi khyim bcu gnyis kyi 'gro lam so sor ma 'dres par rtogs pa'i thabs shog khra sogs kyi bya tshul 'di ni sne mo gcig nas zin na kun g.yos 'ong ba'i gnad dam pa 'grel pa'i dgongs pa dpyis phyin pa 'di sngar med pa'i legs par bshad par dgongs par mdzod cig/

Therefore this particular way of constructing charts on paper and other materials is a method of knowing, clearly and unmistakably, the path of the twelve houses over each of the twelve sectors. This is an illustration of the profound point “If one corner is held, the whole can be moved” and is the definitive position of the commentary. You who assert the above should look on this as new advice. /90/

gzhan yang khyim rnams kyi 'gro lam bsil ri nas me ri la thug gi bar gyi steng thad la bshad pa ni skar khyim 'khor dang bcas pa'i 'gro lam gyi dbang du byas pa yin gyi/ khyim rgyu skar dang bcas pa dang nyi ma zla ba sogs gza' rnams kyi 'gro lam dngos gzhi ni sa'i dkyil 'khor gyi dpag tshad stong phrag phyed dang bcu gsum phan chad dang chu'i dkyil 'khor gyi bzhi gsum tshun chad kyi steng dpag tshad stong phrag lnga bcu yod pa de yin par mkhas pa ('khrul sel ba/)dag gis bshad pa de legs so/ / de'i rgyu mtshan ni rang cag rnams gnas pa'i bod kyi sa 'dir nyi ma byang bgrod mthar thug pa'i nya ni phyed kyi dus su thur shing gtsugs pa na thur shing gi grib ma byang ngos su cung zad 'ong bas/ dus de'i tshe nyi ma dang nyi ma gang du gnas pa'i khyim skar ma dang bcas pa rang cag rnams gnas pa'i bod 'di'i lho phyogs kyi steng thad na gnas par grub la/ bod 'di ni yul drug byang nas rim pa bzhin gangs ldan dang / kai la sha dang / rgya nag dang / li dang / bod dang / 'phags yul zhes bgrang ba'i yul lnga pa yin pas yul drug pa 'phags yul gyi lho mthar rang grib rang la 'khor ba tsam 'ong bas so/ /

The explanation that the path of the houses runs above a region stretching from the Śīta Mountains to the Mountains of Fire is based upon the path of the lunar mansions and houses together with the other stars. However, the actual path of the houses with the lunar mansions, sun, moon, and other planets is within an area that covers 12,500 yojana of the earth mandala and reaches outward up to three quarters of the water mandala to make an area of 50,000 yojana. This has been correctly taught by scholars (such as those of the Elimination of Error Oral Tradition). The reason for their assertion is as follows. If a gnomon is planted in the ground at midday here in our land of Tibet on the day the sun has traveled its farthest north, its shadow will still face slightly to the north. Therefore, this establishes that the sun, as well as the house and lunar mansion that the sun occupies, dwells to the south of our land of Tibet.
