Tibet is the fifth land of the six lands, which in order from the north are Himālaya, Kailash, China, Khotan, Tibet, and India. Therefore, in the sixth land, at the southern limit of India, one’s shadow would simply surround oneself.

'on te lho gling dbus ma 'dir nyi ma byang bgrod mthar thug pa'i dus su'ang nyi ma skar khyim dang bcas pa 'phags yul gyi lho mtha' tshun la mi 'ong du chug mod/ chu'i bzhi gsum tshun po'i dpag tshad stong phrag phyed dang bcu gsum phan chad kyi steng dpag tshad stong phrag lnga bcu po de nyid nyi ma skar khyim dang bcas pa'i 'gro lam yin pa cis grub snyam na/ de ni 'grel chen las/
'dir lho me'i dkyil 'khor nas byang kha ba can chen po'i mtshams su go la'i tshad dpag tshad stong phrag bdun cu rtsa lnga'o/[60] / de bzhin du shar dang nub 'khor ba nas te gsal bar le'u lnga pa las brjod par bya'o/ / zhes gling bcu gnyis po so so'i steng thad kyi khyim bcu gnyis rang rang gi 'gro lam mtshon pa'i phyir du mnyam lam gyi dbus nas bsil ri dang me ri mtshon byed kyi ri mo la thug gi bar zlum por bskor ba'i khyim skar nyi ma dang bcas pa'i 'gro lam mtshon par bshad pa spyir btang rags pa'i dbang du byas par bshad nas/

While it can be accepted that even at the time of the northernmost point of its travels the sun does not come up beyond the southern limit of India,[108] how is it established that the path[109] of the sun along with the houses and lunar mansions stretches for 50,000 yojana up to three quarters of the water mandala, 12,500 yojana inward from its edge? The Great Commentary says:
Here the measurement of the gola is 75,000 yojana from the fire mandala of the south to the snows of the north. “Similarly orbiting east and west,” this is taught clearly in the fifth chapter.[110] Therefore a circular chart is drawn from the center of an equinox path and stretches to depictions of the Śīta Mountains and the Mountains of Fire in order to illustrate the path of the twelve houses above each of the twelve sectors. /91/ However this illustration of the pathway of the houses, lunar mansions, and sun is a generalized and rough depiction.

d.div: [60] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 85_ba5

[108] The Tropic of Cancer runs just below Delhi, India. However the six regions, ending in “India,” or āryadeśa, finish halfway down the southern continent. Therefore, if the southern continent is regarded as present-day India, the “India” of the six regions would finish halfway down its north-south axis.
[109] ’gro lam. Here refers to the ecliptic but in other contexts better rendered as “path” or “pathway.”
[110] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 85b5.

f.d:
dmigs kyi bsal ba'i 'gro lam ji lta ba ni ye shes le'ur bshad pa las shes dgos par bshad pa las ye shes le'u'i de ltar 'chad pa'i rgyud tshig shong 'gyur dang jo nang gsar 'gyur sogs la chad kyang / gyi jo dang sma'i 'gyur las 'byung ba tshigs bcad brgya gya dgu pa'i rjes su/
nyin mor byed pa'i bgrod pa lho dang byang gi mthar ni rkang pa gsum bcas ba tsha'i chu gter dang / / ke la sha yi ji snyed nyid du 'gro ste phyogs kyi bgrod pa dag la dpag tshad stong phrag ni/ / lnga bcu'i gong du 'og la phyed kyi re khar nyin mo dang ni mtshan mo chu tshod mkha' me spyod/ / gang zhig khri phrag lnga la mig dang klu dang zla ba'i cha yis thob pa nyin dang nyin la bgrod/[61] / ces pa'i tshigs bcad 'di yod pa de'i don yin pas mkhas pa dag gis bshad pa de legs pa nyid yin no/ /

The specific path should be known from explanations found in the Gnosis chapter. The text of these explanations is missing from some translations, including the Shong and new Jonang translations. However, after verse 190 from the Gyijo and Ma translations, there is this verse:
The limits of the sun’s travels north and south stretch three quarters of the Salt Ocean and up to Kailash for a distance of 50,000 yojana. In a halved chart, day and night are of space fire[111] hours. 50,000 is completed in eyes, nāga, and moon,[112] traveling from day to day.[113] This verse is the reference for the previous commentary quote, and so those previously mentioned scholars who have taught this are correct.

d.div: [61] da lta gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[111] Thirty hours (space = 0, fire = 3). Sixty hours make one solar day.
[112] 182 days (eyes = 2, nāga = 8, moon = one) plus half a day completes one 50,000-yojana northward or southward passage of the sun.
[113] Unable to trace.

f.d: gsum pa de la nyi mas longs spyad pa las nyin mtshan ring thung sogs su 'gyur ba'i tshul bshad pa ni khyim skar ma dang bcas pa ni lhun po la g.yas skor nyid byed cing / rlung gis khyim bskyod pa'i stobs kyis khyim la gnas pa'i nyi ma sogs gza' rnams kyang lhun po la g.yas skor byed la/ rang 'gros ni sgra gcan ma gtogs nyi ma la sogs pa gza' rnams lhun po la g.yon du skor ba'i tshul gyis rgyu skar rnams la longs spyod par byed do/ / de yang gza' rnams ni lho bgrod dang byang bgrod so sor byed cing / khyim skar rnams ni lho bgrod byang bgrod dang rang 'gros sogs med par sa dum bu gang gi thad du yang sngar 'gro ba'i lam gcig pu de nyid la rnam pa kun du 'gro ba yin te/

An explanation of how the length of day and night are formed by the sun’s occupation of the houses The houses and the lunar mansions orbit Meru in a clockwise direction to the right, and by the force of the wind carrying the houses, the sun and the planets that occupy the houses also orbit Meru to the right. However, in terms of their individual movements, the sun and the other planets, with the exception of Rāhu, enter and occupy the lunar mansions by orbiting Meru in a counterclockwise direction to the left. The planets make both southward and northward journeys, while the houses and the lunar mansions have no southward or northward path and no individual movements. They move over the same path they have always followed, regardless of the sector they are traversing.

'grel chen las/
de'i phyir 'khor ba'i shugs 'di ni khyim gyi yin gyis khyim gyi gzhi la gnas pa'i nyi ma yis ni ma yin no/ / 'dir khyim gyi 'khor lo ni g.yas skor gyis 'khor te gza' rnams ni khyim dag la g.yas min gyis rgyu'o/ / ji ltar khyim gyi 'khor lo 'khor ba de bzhin du sgra gcan yang nub tu mngon par phyogs nas ri rab la g.yas skor byed cing yang dag par rgyu'o/ / shar du phyogs pa'i gza' rnams ni lhun po la g.yas min du skor ba byed cing khyim gyi 'khor lo la yang dag par bgrod par byed do/[62] / zhes gsungs pas so/ /

The Great Commentary says:
Therefore this orbiting force is that of the houses but not that of the sun that dwells in the houses. The circle of the houses orbits to the right, the planets move into the houses to the left. Just as the circle of houses orbit, likewise Rāhu, facing west, travels to the right. The east-facing planets travel around Meru to the left and move through the circle of houses.[114] /92/

d.div: [62] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 90_na1
[114] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 90a1.

f.d: de ltar na nyi ma ni dus kyi khyad par la sogs pa ston par byed pa po'i gtso bo yin pas de'i 'gros la brten na sa dum bu bcu gnyis kyi khyon so sor nyi ma khyim gang zhig na gnas pa'i tshe lho byang gi bgrod pa dang [63] nyin mtshan mnyam pa sogs shes dgos pas de bshad par bya'o/ /

It is in this way that the sun is the main indicator of the differences in time and so forth. Therefore it is necessary to know, among other things, which house the sun is occupying in the regions of the twelve sectors at the times of the limits of sun’s northward and southward passages and of the equinoxes. This will be explained.

d.div: [63] ma dper lho byang gi bgrod pa rang nyin mtshan mnyam sogs zhes 'byung yang lho byang gi bgrod pa dang zhes bcos/

f.d: de la thog mar nyin mtshan mnyam pa'i dpyid dus bshad na/ nyi bar gyi skar gnas thams cad thig ler shar te nyi bar lug khyim du sleb ma thag gi tshe lho gling dbus ma'i dbus su dus kyi dang po dpyid mnyam thog mar 'ong / de bzhin du g.yas skor gyi lho gling nub ma sogs gling lhag ma bcu gcig gi dbus drang por dpyid mnyam 'ong ba dang / glang khyim sogs khyim lhag ma bcu gcig tu nyi bar sleb ma thag rnams rim pa bzhin sbyar bar bya ste/ de yang lho gling nub ma'i dbus drang por nyi bar glang khyim du sleb tsam gyi tshe dpyid mnyam dang / de bzhin du g.yas skor gyi gsum pa'i 'khrig pa dang / bzhi pa'i karka Ta dang / lnga pa'i seng+ge dang / drug pa'i bu mo dang / bdun pa'i srang dang / brgyad pa'i sdig pa dang / dgu pa'i gzhu dang / bcu pa'i chu srin dang / bcu gcig pa'i bum pa dang / bcu gnyis pa lho gling shar ma'i dbus drang por dpyid mnyam gyi tshe nya khyim du sleb ma thag gi nyi bar ri mo la 'char ba'o/ /

First let us explain the spring equinox. The lunar mansion position of the mean sun is set at zero in all places.[115] As soon as the mean sun arrives at Aries, it marks the beginning of the seasons and of the spring equinox at the central meridian of the central sector of the south. Likewise the spring equinox occurring at the direct center of the other eleven sectors clockwise from the south, such as the western sector of the south, can be matched to the immediate arrival of the mean sun in the other houses, such as Taurus. Therefore, by the arrival of the mean sun in Taurus, a spring equinox occurs at the direct center of the western sector of the south. Similarly, moving clockwise, when the spring equinox occurs at the third sector, the mean sun will appear in the charts in Gemini, at the fourth in Cancer, at the fifth in Leo, at the sixth in Virgo, at the seventh in Libra, at the eighth in Scorpio, at the ninth in Sagittarius, at the tenth in Capricorn, at the eleventh in Aquarius, and when spring equinox occurs at the direct center of the twelfth, or the eastern, sector of the south, the mean sun arrives in Pisces.

d.div: [115] Henning explains that in astronomical calculations, figures representing lunar mansions, hours, minutes, etc., are arranged in rows or “places” and are further mathematical configurations. The sun at the spring equinox is at the beginning of the zodiac, and figures such as lunar mansions are at zero.

f.d: de yang gling rnams kyi dbus drang po'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi/ zhib tu byas na gling re rer yang dpyid mnyam sum cu lhag tsam re 'ong ste/ de yang nyi bar lug khyim du sleb ma thag nas glang khyim du sleb kyi bar lho gling dbus ma'i dbus nas lho gling nub ma'i dbus kyi bar la sa khyon sum cur phye ba'i cha re rer nyin zhag sum cu'i bar la rim pa bzhin nyin re la dpyid mnyam re 'ong ba dang / de bzhin du nyi bar glang khyim du sleb pa nas 'khrig khyim du sleb ma thag gi bar la lho gling nub ma'i dbus nas nub gling shar ma'i dbus kyi bar la sa khyon sum cur phye ba'i cha re rer nyin zhag sum cu'i bar la nyin re bzhin dpyid mnyam re 'ong ngo / /

The above are the equinoxes over the direct center of the sectors, but to be more precise, within each sector more than thirty equinoxes can occur. From the moment the mean sun enters Aries until it enters Taurus, the area of land from the center of the central southern sector to the center of the western sector of the south can be divided into thirty parts that constitute thirty solar days, and on each day a spring equinox will occur. Similarly, from the arrival of the mean sun in Taurus until the moment of its arrival in Gemini, the area from the center of the western sector of the south to the center of the eastern sector of the west is divided into thirty parts, each covering a solar day, and on each day a spring equinox will occur.

de bzhin du sa dum bu gzhan rnams la yang de'i rigs pas 'ded par bya zhing / dmigs bsal ni nub gling shar ma'i dbus nas nub gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi bar la sa khyon so gcig tu 'byed pa dang / byang gling shar ma'i dbus nas byang gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi bar la yang so gcig tu 'byed pa dang / de bzhin du shar gling shar ma'i dbus nas shar gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi bar la'ang so gcig dang / lho gling shar ma'i dbus nas lho gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi bar la sa khyon so gnyis su phye ba rnams su dpyid mnyam re re 'ong ba ni snga ma rnams kyi dmigs bsal lo/ /

The same applies to the other areas. The exceptions are the area from the center of the eastern sector of the west to the center of the central sector of the west, the area from the center of the eastern sector of the north to the center of the central sector of the north, and the area from the center of the eastern sector of the east to the center of the central sector of the east: all these are divided into thirty-one. /93/ The area from the center of the eastern sector of the south to the center of the central sector of the south is divided into thirty-two. The spring equinox occurs on each of these solar days. These are exceptions to the above.

yang nya skar dang bstun te rab 'bring po la sogs pa'i zla ba rnams dang nyi ma khyim gang na yod pa rnams sbyor ba ni de yang nyi ma lug khyim du zhugs pa'i nyi bar 'char ba'i zla ba phyed pa'i dus ni gnyis su nges te/ yar ngo sngon 'gro'i nag zla'i phyogs gnyis su'o/ / de yang phyogs dang po'i tshes gcig nas bco lnga'i bar phyi tshes gang yang rung ba la nyi ma lug khyim du zhugs pa'i nyi bar ri mo la shar na lug khyim yar ngo sngon 'gro'i nag zla dang sbyar zhing / phyogs gnyis pa'i tshes gcig nas bco lnga'i bar gyi tshes gang yang rung ba la nyi ma lug khyim du zhugs pa'i nyi bar ri mo la shar ba'i tshe lug khyim mar ngo sngon 'gro'i sa ga zla ba dang sbyar nas lo'i 'gor bya ste/

The months, named according to their full-moon lunar mansions[116] and designated as early, middle, and later,[117] are linked to particular houses in which the sun dwells. The half-month in which the mean sun enters Aries will be one of the two halves of a waxing-led Caitra. If the mean sun entering Aries appears in the chart on any date from the first to the fifteenth of the waxing, Aries is assigned to Caitra. When the mean sun entering Aries appears in the chart on any date from the first to the fifteenth of the waning, Aries is assigned to a waning-led Vaiśākha, which is then designated as the beginning of the year.

d.div: [116] The month is usually named after the lunar mansion in which the full moon appears (Henning).
[117] The three months that make up each of the four seasons are graded early, middle, and later.

f.d:
'grel chen las/
lhun po'i lho 'dzam bu gling chung ngu 'dir lug la sogs pa'i khyim rnams dang dpyid la sogs pa'i dus rnams dang nag pa la sogs pa'i zla ba rnams dang de bzhin du phyogs rnams thams cad rab tu grags so/[64] / zhes pa 'dis lug khyim yar ngo sngon 'gro'i tshe nag pa zla ba dang sbyor ba bstan cing /

The Great Commentary says:
In this Lesser Jambudvīpa, south of Meru, the houses of Aries and so forth, the times of spring and so forth, the months of Caitra and so forth, and the halves are all well known.[118] This shows Aries assigned to a waxing-led Caitra.

d.div: [64] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 88_na7
[118] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 88a7.

f.d:
yang 'grel chen las/
lhun po'i lho'i dum bu 'dir lug la nyi ma gnas pas dpyid kyi dus su sa ga'i zla ba byed do/[65] / zhes pa 'dis mar ngo sngon 'gro'i tshe lug khyim sa ga zla ba dang sbyor ba bstan to/ /

Again the Great Commentary states:
In this continent south of Meru, the sun dwells in Aries, and Vaiśākha is the spring.[119] This illustrates the house of Aries assigned to a waning-led Vaiśākha.

d.div: [65] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 88_ba2
[119] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 88b2.

f.d: de ltar na yar ngo sngon 'gro'i tshe lug khyim dang sbyar ba'i zla ba de sa dum bu bcu gnyis pa thams cad du nag zla dang / mar ngo sngon 'gro'i tshe lug khyim dang sbyar ba'i zla ba sa dum bu bcu gnyis po thams cad du sa ga'i zla bar byed do/ / yang nyi ma lug khyim du zhugs pa'i zla ba de yar ngo sngon 'gro dang sbyor ba'i tshe lho gling dbus ma 'dir dpyid 'bring nag zla dang / g.yon skor gyi dum bu gnyis pa lho gling shar mar dpyid tha nag zla dang / de bzhin du g.yon skor gyi gsum par dbyar ra nag zla dang / bzhi par dbyar 'bring nag zla dang/ lnga pa dbyar tha nag zla dang/ drug par ston ra nag zla dang / bdun par ston 'bring nag zla dang / brgyad par ston tha nag zla dang / dgu par dgun ra nag zla dang / bcu par dgun 'bring nag zla dang / bcu gcig par dgun tha nag zla dang / bcu gnyis pa lho gling nub mar dpyid ra nag zla'o/ /

In this way, the month assigned to Aries when that month is waxing-led will be Caitra in all of the twelve sectors, and when waning-led, the month assigned to Aries will be Vaiśākha in all twelve sectors. When the month of the sun entering Aries is designated a waxing-led month, here in our central sector of the south, middle spring is the month of Caitra. Proceeding counterclockwise, in the second sector, or the eastern sector of the south, later spring is Caitra. In the third sector counterclockwise, early summer is Caitra. In the fourth, middle summer is Caitra. In the fifth, later summer is Caitra. In the sixth, Caitra is in early autumn; in the seventh, Caitra is middle autumn; and in the eighth, it is later autumn. /94/ In the ninth sector Caitra occurs in early winter, in the tenth in middle winter, and in the eleventh in later winter. In the twelfth sector, the western sector of the south, Caitra is in early spring.

yang zla ba de mar ngo sngon 'gro dang sbyor ba'i tshe lho gling dbus ma 'dir dpyid tha sa ga zla ba dang / de bzhin du g.yon skor gyi gnyis par dbyar ra sa ga zla ba dang / gsum par dbyar 'bring sa ga zla ba dang zhes sogs su sbyar te bcu gnyis pa lho gling nub mar dpyid 'bring sa ga zla ba'o/ /

When the month of the sun’s residence in Aries is designated a waning-led month, in this central sector of the south, later spring is the month of Vaiśākha. Similarly, moving counterclockwise, in the second sector, early summer is Vaiśākha. In the third, middle summer is Vaiśākha, and so on, until the twelfth sector, the western sector of the south, where middle spring would be Vaiśākha.

gzhan yang nyi mas lug khyim nas rim gyis bgrod de karka Ta'i khyim du sleb ma thag gi tshe lho gling dbus ma'i dbus 'dir byang bgrod mthar thug cing / de bzhin du g.yas skor gyi sa dum bu lhag ma bcu gcig po rnams kyi rang rang gi dbus drang por nyi ma byang bgrod mthar thug pa dang nyi bar seng+gaེ'i khyim la sogs pa khyim lhag ma bcu gcig po rnams su sleb ma thag pa rnams rim pa bzhin du sbyar bar bya ste/ de yang lho gling nub ma'i dbus drang por nyi ma seng+ge'i khyim du sleb ma thag gi tshe nyi ma byang bgrod mthar thug pa/ de bzhin du g.yas skor gyi nyi bar bu mo'i khyim du sleb ma thag gi tshe sa dum bu gsum pa nub gling shar ma'i dbus drang por nyi ma byang bgrod mthar thug go/ / de bzhin du g.yas skor gyi bzhi pa'i srang dang / lnga pa'i sdig pa dang / drug pa'i gzhu dang / bdun pa'i chu srin dang / brgyad pa'i bum pa dang / dgu pa'i nya dang / bcu pa'i lug dang / bcu gcig pa'i glang dang / bcu gnyis pa lho gling shar ma'i dbus drang por nyi bar 'khrig pa'i khyim du sleb ma thag gi tshe byang bgrod mthar thug go/ /

When the sun, on its journey from Aries, arrives in Cancer, it has reached the limit of its northward journey from the standpoint of the center of this central sector of the south. Similarly, proceeding clockwise, the northern limit of the sun’s journey from the standpoint of the direct center of each of the remaining eleven sectors can be applied to the moment the mean sun arrives in Leo and the other eleven houses. For example, at the direct center of the western sector of the south, it is the moment of the sun’s arrival in Leo that marks the limit of the sun’s northward journey. Similarly, moving clockwise, the moment of the mean sun’s arrival in Virgo marks the limit of the sun’s northward journey at the direct center of the third sector, or the eastern sector of the west. Similarly it is Libra at the fourth clockwise, Scorpio at the fifth, Sagittarius at the sixth, Capricorn at the seventh, Aquarius at the eighth, Pisces at the ninth, Aries at the tenth, Taurus at the eleventh. And the moment of the mean sun’s arrival at Gemini marks the limit of the sun’s northward journey at the direct center of the eastern sector of the south.

'dir yang zhib tu byas na nyi ma karka Ta nas seng+ge'i khyim du sleb ma thag gi bar la lho gling dbus ma'i dbus nas lho gling nub ma'i dbus kyi bar las khyon sum cur phye ba'i sa khyon re rer nyi ma byang bgrod mthar thug ste dbyar nyi ldog thengs re re 'ong bas dbyar nyi ldog thengs sum bcu 'ong ngo / / de bzhin du nyi ma seng+ge'i khyim nas bu mo'i khyim du sleb ma thag pa'i bar la lho gling nub ma'i dbus nas nub gling shar ma'i dbus kyi bar la sa khyon so so ba sum cur phye ba'i sa khyon re rer nyi ma byang bgrod mthar thug ste dbyar nyi ldog thengs sum cu 'ong ngo / / des gzhan rnams la yang rigs pa bsgres te shes par bya zhing / dmigs bsal rnams kyang nyin mtshan mnyam pa la bshad pa las rigs pas shes so/ /

This can be looked at in more detail. Between the sun’s journey from Cancer and the moment of its arrival in Leo, the area from the direct center of the central sector of the south to the center of the western sector of the south can be divided into thirty parts. In each part the sun will travel to its northern limit, which means a summer solstice,[120] occurring each time. A summer solstice, therefore, occurs thirty times. Likewise, between the sun’s journey from Leo and the moment of its arrival in Virgo, the area from the direct center of the western sector of the south to the center of the eastern sector of the west can be divided into thirty parts. In each part the sun will travel to its northern limit, bringing about a summer solstice each time. Here, too, a summer solstice occurs thirty times. This process can be applied to the other sectors. /95/ The exceptions can be known from the section above on the equinoxes.

d.div: [120] nyi ldog. Literally, “sun turning around.”

f.d: yang nyi bar srang khyim du sleb ma thag pa'i tshe lho gling dbus ma 'di'i dbus drang por ston mnyam 'ong zhing / de bzhin du nyi bar sdig khyim sogs khyim lhag ma bcu gcig tu rim pa bzhin sleb ma thag pa rnams dang / g.yas skor gyi lho gling nub ma sogs sa dum bu lhag ma bcu gcig po rnams kyi dbus drang por ston mnyam 'ong ba sogs dpyid mnyam gyi skabs su bshad pa bzhin shes par bya'o/ /

The moment of the mean sun’s arrival in Libra is the autumn equinox at the direct center of our central sector of the south. Similarly, the moments of the mean sun’s arrivals at Scorpio and the other eleven houses, and, clockwise, the corresponding autumn equinoxes at the direct center of the western sector of the south and the other eleven sectors, can be known in the same way that the spring equinoxes were known.

yang nyi ma chu srin gyi khyim du sleb ma thag pa'i tshe lho gling dbus ma 'di'i dbus drang por nyi ma lho bgrod mthar thug cing dgun nyi ldog go/ / de bzhin du nyi bar bum pa'i khyim la sogs pa khyim lhag ma bcu gcig tu sleb ma thag pa rnams rim pa bzhin g.yas skor gyi lho gling nub ma sogs dum bu lhag ma bcu gcig po rnams kyi dbus dang por nyi ma lho bgrod mthar thug ste dgun nyi ldog pa dang sbyar bar bya ste/ de yang dper na nyi bar bum pa'i khyim du sleb ma thag gi tshe lho gling nu ba ma'i dbus drang por nyi ma lho bgrod mthar thug cing dgun nyi ldog pa dang / de bzhin du nyi bar nya'i khyim du sleb ma thag pa'i tshe nub gling shar ma'i dbus drang por nyi ma lho bgrod mthar thug cing dgun nyi ldog pa nas nyi bar gzhu'i khyim du sleb ma thag pa'i tshe lho gling shar ma'i dbus drang por nyi ma lho bgrod mthar thug cing dgun nyi ldog go/ /

The moment of the sun’s arrival in Capricorn marks the limit of the sun’s southward passage at the direct center of the central sector of the south, and is the winter solstice. Similarly the moment of arrival of the mean sun in Aquarius and the other eleven houses marks the limits of the sun’s southward passages and winter solstices at, clockwise, the western sector of the south and the other eleven sectors respectively. For example, the moment of the mean sun’s arrival in Aquarius marks the limit of the sun’s southward passage as well as the winter solstice at the direct center of the western sector of the south. Similarly, as soon as the mean sun arrives in Pisces, the sun’s southward journey is at its limit for the direct center of the eastern sector of the west, and that moment marks its winter solstice. This continues until the moment of the mean sun’s arrival in Sagittarius, which marks the winter solstice and limit of the sun’s southward journey at the direct center of the eastern sector of the south.

de yang zhib mor byas na nyi ma chu srin gyi khyim du sleb ma thag nas bum pa'i khyim du sleb ma thag gi bar la lho gling dbus ma'i dbus nas lho gling nub ma'i dbus kyi bar la sa khyon cha sum cur phye ba'i cha re rer nyi ma lho bgrod mthar thug pa re re 'ong bas dgun nyi ldog pa'ang re re 'ong ngo / / de bzhin du khyim lhag ma bcu gcig dang sa dum bu lhag ma bcu gcig sbyor ba yang rigs pa snga mas shes par bya'o/ /

If this is looked at in more detail, between the moment of the sun’s arrival in Capricorn and the moment of its arrival in Aquarius, the area from the center of the central sector of the south to the center of the western sector of the south is divided into thirty parts. At each part the sun reaches the limit of its southward passage, and therefore the winter solstice also occurs. Correspondence between the remaining eleven houses and eleven sectors can be understood in the same way.

de ltar na nyi bar lug khyim du 'khor ba lta bu'i lo gcig gi bar la nyi mas ri rab la g.yas skor gyi grangs sum brgya drug cu rtsa lnga lhag tsam re byed pas sa dum bu bcu gnyis la sa khyon tha dad pa sum brgya drug cu rtsa lngar phye ba'i sa khyon re rer nyi ma lho bgrod mthar thug pa re re dang dgun nyi ldog pa'ang re re 'ong zhing / des dbyar byang bgrod mthar thug pa dang / dpyid mnyam dang / ston mnyam 'ong tshul sogs kyang shes par bya'o/ /

In this way, during the course of a year illustrated by the mean sun circling from Aries to Aries, the sun makes a little over 365 clockwise orbits of Meru. Therefore the area of the twelve sectors can be divided into three 365 parts, and at each part the sun will reach the limit of its southward passage, and at each limit a winter solstice will occur. In the same way the limits of the northward summer journeys as well as the spring and autumn equinoxes can also be known. /96/

da ni de dag gi shes par byed pa'i lung dang rigs pa dag brjod par bya ste de yang 'grel chen las/
'dir chad pa dang lhag pa ji ltar shes na byang du bgrod pa'i zla ba dang po la nyi ma bcu'i bar du thur ma'i grib mas yongs su brtag par bya ste/ nyin zhag gang nus brtsams te thur ma'i grib ma byang nas log par gyur pa de ni gza' de dang tshes de dang sbyor ba de dang byed pa des nyi ma 'pho ba'i nyin zhag go/ / nyin zhag de la nyi ma'i longs spyod skar ma'i gnas su nyi shu dang chu tshod kyi gnas su bco lnga zhes pa rtsa ba'i nges pa'o/[66] / zhes dgun nyi ldog pa'i nyin zhag bcu'i gong nas thur shing gi grib mas brtag pa byas pa las grib ma byang nas log pa'i dus su dgun nyi log cing de'i nyin nyi ma'i skar gnas su nyi shu dang chu tshod du bco lnga byung ste nyi ma gzhu khyim rdzogs nas chu srin gyi khyim du sleb ma thag pa yin par gsungs pa'i sa khyon de ni lho gling dbus ma'i dbus drang po de yin te/ rgyud las byed pa'i rtsis gsungs pa'i rtsis kyi lag len byed pa'i yul lam sa khyon gyi gtso bo ni lho gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi 'phags yul yin la/ byed rtsis kyi lag len byed pa'i sa khyon gyi gtso bo 'di yin zhes dgongs pa'i sa khyon de nyid nyi ma'i skar gnas su nyi shu dang chu tshod du bco lnga byung ste nyi ma chu srin gyi khyim du sleb ma thag pa'i tshe dgun nyi ldog par gsungs pa'i sa khyon de yin pa'i phyir te/

Now I will discuss the scriptural references and reasonings that substantiate the above. The Great Commentary says:
How are the additions and omissions to be known? Before the first month of the northward passage, ten days are to be studied by the shadow of the gnomon. As soon as the shadow of the sun stick turns from north, that day, that date, that yoga, that karaṇa is the solar day on which the sun changes its movement. On that solar day the sun is at twenty in the lunar mansion place[121] and at fifteen in the hours place. This is the primary definition. Ten days before the winter solstice, the shadow of a gnomon is examined, and the time when the shadow turns from heading north is the time of the winter solstice. The sun on that day is twenty lunar mansions and fifteen hours. This is explained as being the moment the sun leaves Sagittarius and enters Capricorn. The region where this occurs is the direct center of this central sector of the south. The country or region where the karaṇa astronomy taught in the tantra was mainly practiced is the noble country of India at the center of this central sector of the south. It is with this region in mind that it was taught that the sun’s position of twenty lunar mansions and fifteen hours corresponds to the winter solstice at the moment the sun enters Capricorn.

d.div: [66] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 76_ba7

[121] “Place” here and further on refers to the position of the sun and to the place in the table of calculations reserved for the position of the sun. When the numbering system for the lunar mansions begins with one and not zero, this quote means that the sun is in the twenty-first mansion (twenty mansions completed) at fifteen degrees, or “hours.” Fifteen hours is one quarter of a mansion (sixty “hours of distance,” or degrees = one lunar mansion).

f.d:
byed rtsis kyi nyi rkang nor bu g.yon du [67] 'gro tshul 'chad pa'i skabs kyi 'grel chen las/
bgrod pa 'gro ba'i dbang gis nyi ma la ni sbyin dang dor te gzhan du dag pa yod ma yin/[68] / zhes pa'i tshig 'di ni nges pa'i don to zhes pa'i don 'chad pa na de'i 'phro nyid las/
cha des thob pa ni chu tshod kyi tshogs te/ chu tshod kyi gnas su nor du 'gyur ro/ / bgrod pa 'gro ba'i dbang gis bu lon du yang 'gyur te bgrod pa 'gro ba'i dbang gis chu srin la sogs pa la nor dang karka Ta la sogs pa la bu lon du 'gyur ro/[69] / zhes byed rtsis kyi lag len ltar na nyi ma chu srin gyi khyim du sleb ma thag nas byang bgrod kyi 'go rtsom pa dang / nyi ma karka Ta'i khyim du sleb ma thag pa nas lho bgrod kyi 'go rtsom par bshad pas so/ /

In the section from the Great Commentary explaining increment and decrement in the sun’s stages according to karaṇa it says:
“Because of its travels there is increment and decrement concerning the sun. Others have no accurate positions.” These words are definitive.[122] Explaining this line, the commentary continues:
The result obtained by that fraction is a number of hours, and in the place of hours it is an increment. Because of its travels there is decrement. Because of its travels, there is also an increment in Capricorn and so forth and a decrement in Cancer and so forth.[123] According to karaṇa methodology, the moment of the sun’s arrival in Capricorn is the start of the northward journey, and the moment of the sun’s arrival in Cancer is the start of the southward passage. /97/

d.div: [67] ma dper g.yon du gsal yang don la lon du yin nam snyam/
[68] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 73_ba7
[69] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 73_ba7
[122] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 73b7.
[123] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 73b7.

f.d: de bas na kha cig (chos rgyal byang pa/[70] )gis nyi ma'i skar gnas su nyi shu dang chu tshod du bco lnga byung ba'i tshe dgun nyi ldog par gsungs pa de lho gling dbus ma'i nub mtha' la dgongs pa yin zhes zer ba yang mi rigs so/ / de'i rgyu mtshan ni gzhan yang nyi ma lug khyim du sleb ma thag gi tshe lho gling dbus mar dpyid mnyam 'ong bar gsungs pa de yang lho gling dbus ma'i nub mtha' la dgongs par 'gyur te/ rgyu mtshan mtshungs pas so/ / 'dod par mi nus te/ de ltar yin na nyi ma lug khyim dang bcas pa shar gling dbus ma'i dbus drang por gnas pa'i tshe lho gling dbus mar nyin mo'i thog ma 'ong bar gsungs pa de yang lho gling dbus ma'i nub mtha' la dgongs par 'gyur dgos pa las de ltar du dgongs pa ma yin pa'i phyir te/ de lta yin na lam phyed 'bum phrag gsum po dag la [71] zhes sogs dang 'gal bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ /

Therefore those scholars (such as Chögyal Jangpa)[124] are not correct when they maintain that the statement asserting twenty in the position of the lunar mansions and fifteen in the position of hours to be the winter solstice refers to the western edge of the central sector of the south. Here’s why. It would follow that the statement positing the moment of the sun’s arrival in Aries as being the spring equinox on the central sector of the south also refers to the western edge of the central sector of the south. This cannot be, because if that were the case, the statement that the sun in Aries at the direct center of the central sector of the east corresponds to the beginning of the day at the central sector of the south would also have to refer to the western edge of the central sector of the south. It cannot mean that, because it would contradict the quote beginning “For half the path of 300,000.”[125]

d.div: [70] 'dir yig chung du chos rgyal byang pa zhes pa byams pa rnam rgyal grags pa bzang po (1395-1475) yin pa mngon/
[71] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 89_na4_sde dge_362_rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka60_28_ba6
[124] Jangpa Namgyal Drakpa Sangpo (1395–1475).

[125] From the Condensed Tantra quoted in the Great Commentary, Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, v. 60, 89a4: “For half the path of three hundred thousand, in front of the sun is daytime, behind the sun is night” referring to the circumference of the earth mandala. Therefore, at the equinox, half the circle is night, half is day, and when the sun is directly above the central point of the eastern continent, it must be seen as being on the cusp of nighttime and daytime (i.e., sunrise) from a point halfway around the semicircle south of Meru (i.e., the central point of the southern continent).

f.d: de ltar na gong du bshad pa ltar nyi ma gzhu khyim du sleb ma thag gi tshe lho gling shar ma'i dbus drang por lho bgrod mthar thug ste de nas nyin zhag sum cu lhag tsam zhig gi bar la nyin zhag re re bzhin lho gling shar ma'i dbus nas lho gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi bar la sa khyon sum cu'i char phye ba'i sa khyon re rer nyi ma lho bgrod mthar thug ste dgun nyi ldog thengs re re 'ong ba yin par grub ste/

Therefore, as explained above, the moment of the sun’s arrival in Sagittarius marks the limit of the sun’s southward passage for the eastern sector of the south at its the direct center. Then, for each of a little over thirty days, the area from the center of the eastern sector of the south to the center of the central sector of the south is divided into thirty parts, and it is established that the limit of the sun’s southward passage occurs at each part, with a winter solstice occurring each time. This can be established.

de'i rgyu mtshan ni slob dpon ab+ha yas dus 'khor la 'jug pa las/
de bas na grub pa'i mtha'i lam brjod par bya ste de'i rim pa 'di dag go/ / sa gzhi mnyam po la gru gang gi tshad kyi maN+Dal gyi dbus su btsugs pa'i mtho gang gi tshad kyi shing gi grib ma snga dro re kha'i phyi rol nas rim gyis bskums pa na gang gi tshe maN+Dal gyi mtha'i re kha'i dbus su zhugs pa de'i tshe gnas der bya rog gi rjes kyi mtshan ma bya ste de nyid nub kyi phyogs so/ / phyi dro ni maN+Dal gyi dbus nas rim gyis brkyang ba na gang gi tshe zhes pa la sogs pa sngar bzhin mtshan ma ste de nyid shar gyi phyogs so/ / 'dir mtshan ma gcig gi steng du skud pa bzung ste mtshan ma gzhan gyi mdun nas maN+Dal thod le kor gyis bya zhing mtshan ma gzhan gyi steng du skud pa bzung ste de bzhin du byas pas ji ltar nya'i rnam par 'gyur ro/ / maN+Dal gnyis po 'di dag gi dbus kyi nya'i rnam pa'i kha'i dbus lho phyogs so/ / mjug ma'i dbus ni byang phyogs so/ / de ltar phyogs gtan la phab nas maN+Dal gnyis po dbye bar bya'o/ / byang du bgrod pa'i nyi ma las gong gi nyi ma bcu pa nas brtsams te nyi ma'i gung la brtag par bya'o/ / de la thog ma'i maN+Dal gyi byang phyogs kyi mtha'i re kha'i dbus nas maN+Da_la gyi nang du nyin mo gang la grib ma 'jug pa de nyi ma byang du bgrod pa'i 'pho ba'i nyi mo'o/ /[72]

The master Abhaya[126] says in his Kālacakrāvatāra:
Therefore I will speak on the path of siddhānta. These are the stages. On level ground in the middle of a circle of one cubit diameter, plant a stick in the ground that measures the length from the tip of your thumb to the tip of your middle finger. The line of the stick’s morning shadow gradually shortens from outside the mandala. When it reaches the edge of the mandala, at that time and in that place, make the mark of the crowfoot.[127] That is the west. In the afternoon the shadow gradually lengthens from the center of the mandala. Repeat the process as before, and the mark will indicate the east. Anchoring thread at one of the marks, and beginning directly in front of the other mark, draw a circle with chalk. Anchor thread at the other mark and do the same, thereby creating the shape of a fish. In the middle of the two circles, the center of the mouth of the fish is the south, and the center of the tail is the north.[128] Having ascertained the directions rub out the circles. /98/ Starting from the tenth day before the sun makes its northward journey, make observations at midday. When the shadow begins to move inside from the northern edge of the original circle, that is the day the sun changes to its northward journey.[129]

d.div: [72] sde dge_1383_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa.a b+ha ya dus 'khor la 'jug pa/ 280_ba3
[126] Abhayākaragupta (Tib. Jikmé Jungné Bepa) (1004–1125), Indian Kālacakra master.
[127] The mark “x” or the sign of a cross.

[128] This entails the drawing of two further circles, with centers at the two crosses, each with the radius of the distance between the two crosses. Their intersections mark north and south. North, or the tail of the fish, will be larger than the south, or mouth, because the shadow marks are north of the original circle’s diameter due to the Tropic of Capricorn being in the south.
[129] Toh 1383 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 280b3.

f.d: zhes gsungs pa dang cha mthun par 'das lo'i thog ma rab byung me yos nas lo drug cu skor bdun dang lo rkyang nyi shu pa mi zad pa me pho khyi'i dgun nyi ldog dus la thur shing gis (thams cad mkhyen pa dpal grags pa'i bka' bzhin blo gsal zhing yid gzhungs pa dag dang lhan cig par bdag gis/) brtags pas lo de'i hor zla bcu gnyis pa'i tshes lnga'i nyin thur shing gi grib ma byang nas log par mngon sum gyis mthong bas de'i sngon ma'i tshes bzhi de la rang cag rnams gnas pa'i sa khyon 'dir dgun nyi log par grub la/ tshes bzhi de'i yang bcu gsum cha bzhi song ba'i 'tshams su yin te/ tshes bzhi de'i bcu gsum cha bzhi song ba'i nyi bar la grub mtha' gzhir bzhag na nyi ma'i skar mar bco brgyad/ chu tshod so gcig /chu srang sum cu/ dbugs dang re bdun cha rnams stong pa'o/ / de'i steng du tshes zhag nyer gsum dang tshes zhag gcig gi bcu gsum cha gsum gyi nyi ma'i rtag longs bsnan pas nyi skar nyi shu dang chu tshod bco lnga 'ong bas hor zla bcu gnyis pa de'i tshes nyer brgyad pa'i bcu gsum cha gsum rdzogs pa'i 'tshams su lho gling dbus ma'i dbus drang por dgun nyi log par grub bo/ / de ltar grub pa nyid kyis rang cag rnams gnas pa'i sa khyon 'di lho gling dbus ma'i dbus nas lho gling shar ma'i dbus kyi bar la sa khyon tha dad pa sum cur phye ba'i nang gi lho gling dbus ma'i dbus nas shar la bgrangs pa'i sa khyon nyer gsum pa dang / sa khyon der lo de'i hor zla bcu gnyis pa'i tshes bzhi la dgun te log par grub bo/ / de ltar grub pa'i rigs pa la dpags nas sa dum bu bcu gnyis po bsdoms pa la sa khyon tha dad pa sum brgya drug cu rtsa lngar phye ba'i sa khyon re rer dgun nyi ldog thengs re re 'ong bar shes par nus so/ /

In an experiment similar to this, seven sixty-year cycles after Fire Rabbit year, the first of the past years, plus twenty single years, in the unfinished year of the male Fire Dog[130] (in the company of bright and intelligent scholars and in accordance with the words of the omniscient Paldrak[131]), I carried out observations using the gnomon at the time of the winter solstice. On the fifth day of the twelfth month of the Hor calendar,[132] the shadow was seen to turn from heading northward. Therefore on the fourth, the previous day, the winter solstice was established for the place where we had been standing. It was also at the point where 4/13 of the fourth calendar day had passed. Using siddhānta astronomy, the mean sun of 3/13 of the fourth day was calculated to be at the position of eighteen lunar mansions and thirty-one hours, thirty minutes exactly.[133] A position of twenty lunar mansions and fifteen hours[134] is reached by adding twenty-three days plus 3/13 of one day of the sun’s fixed motion.[135] Therefore the winter solstice is established for the direct center of the central sector of the south at the point of the completion of 3/13 of the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth Hor month. This established that the region we were occupying was the twenty-third region east of the center of the central sector of the south from among the division of thirty separate regions ranging from the center of the central sector of the south to the center of the eastern sector of the south, and in that region the winter solstice occurred on the fourth day of the twelfth Hor month of that year. Using the same reasoning, it is possible to know the winter solstice for each of the 365 regions divided among the twelve sectors.

d.div: [131] Probably a teacher of the author.
[132] System of numbering the months, still in use today, dating from the magha month in 1227, in which the Mogul king Janghir conquered the region of Minyak. See The Great Lexicon, p. 3073.
[133] As mentioned previously, this means that eighteen mansions have passed, and the hours and minutes are of the nineteenth lunar mansion of mūla. This can be written 18:31:30.

[134] The sun moves four and half “hours” a day (approx. one degree). Therefore twenty-three days is 103.5 hours. This is the distance from 18:31:30 to the first point of Capricorn (28.5 hours remaining of mūla, the sixty hours of pūrvāṣāḍhā, plus fifteen hours of uttarāṣāḍhā).
[135] This figure is added to the completion of the fourth day.
[136] Collected Works, vol. ka, 90b1.

f.d: yang bu ston thams cad mkhyen pas nyi skar bcu dgu dang chu tshod bco lngar longs pa'i tshe rang cag rnams gnas pa'i sa khyon 'dir nyi ma lho bgrod mthar thug ste dgun nyi ldog pa'i sa tshigs mdzad pa ltar ding sang ba rnams 'dod pa ltar na yang 'grel chen las/ rgyud kyi rgyal po 'di la nges pa ni mi rtag pa ste lo drug cu'i mthar slar yang nges pa 'god pa'i phyir ro/[73] / zhes gsungs pa ltar 'das lo'i thog ma rab byung me yos nas da ltar chu yos 'di 'das pa yan la lo bzhi brgya dang lnga bcu nga bdun yod pa de'i bar gyi nyi ma la gnas gsum dbus ma dbang phyug gis bsgyur ba'i byed rtsis kyi mang cha bsags pas chu tshod nyer gsum lhag tsam 'ong la chu tshod nyer gsum po des ding sang ba rnams kyi dgun nyi ldog pa'i sa tshigs su byas pa'i nyi skar bcu dgu dang chu tshod bco lnga la phri ba na lhag ma skar ma bco brgyad dang chu tshod nga gnyis 'ong bas ding sang ba'i byed rtsis pa rnams kyi ltar na'ang rang cag rnams gnas pa'i sa khyon 'dir dgun nyi ldog pa'i dus de las da dung yang nyi skar nyi shu dang chu tshod bco lnga longs pa la tshes zhag bcu dgu tsam gyi nyi ma'i longs spyod snon dgos par grub bo/ /

The omniscient Butön calculated the sun’s southern limit and winter solstice in our particular region as being the sun’s occupation of nineteen lunar mansions and fifteen hours.[136] /99/ However, the Great Commentary says:
In the king of tantras, definitions[137] are not fixed. At the end of sixty years, the definitions are to be done again.[138] Therefore, from the prabhava Fire Rabbit first year of the past years until this present Water Rabbit year,[139] 457 years have passed. Over that time in karaṇa astronomy, the middle place multiplied by Śiva[140] has accumulated an excess of about twenty-three hours for the sun. If those twenty-three hours are subtracted from nineteen lunar mansions and fifteen hours, which is asserted these days as being the position of the winter sun’s solstice, the result is eighteen lunar mansions and fifty-two hours. Therefore this establishes that even according to those who use karaṇa astronomy these days, and who maintain the same mansion position as the omniscient Butön, at the time of the winter solstice in this land of ours, about nineteen days of the sun’s coursing still has to be added before it arrives at the position of twenty lunar mansions and fifteen hours.

d.div: [73] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ 'grel chen dri med 'od/ shrI_69_ba6
[137] nges pa, dhruvaka.
[138] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 69b6.
[140] The middle place or position in a three-row arrangement multiplied by a constant of eleven or Śiva. (Henning)

f.d: de ltar grub pas de dag gi ltar na'ang rang cag rnams gnas pa'i sa khyon 'di lho gling dbus ma'i dbus dang po nas shar la bgrangs pa'i sa khyon bcu dgu pa dang / lho gling shar ma'i dbus nas lho gling dbus ma'i dbus kyi+i bar la sa khyon tha dad pa sum cur phye ba'i nang gi lho gling dbus ma'i dbus nas shar la bgrangs pa'i sa khyon bcu dgu pa der dgun nyi ldog pa yod par 'dod dgos so/ /

Therefore, by this reasoning, even according those who assert the above would have to agree that our land was the nineteenth land eastward from the center of the central sector of the south among the thirty separate lands apportioned from the eastern sector of the south to the central sector of the south, and that there would be a winter solstice on that nineteenth land counted eastward from the central sector of the south.

de las gzhan du byed rtsis spyi lugs pa rnams dgun nyi ldog par 'dod pa'i dus der nyi skar nyi shu dang chu tshod bco lnga longs (chos rje kumA ra/)par byas nas sa dum bu bcu gnyis po re rer lo re la dgun nyi ldog pa re re nyid yin par byas pa'i rnam gzhag mdzad pa rnams ni gzhan du rgyas par bkag pa las shes par bya'o/ /[74]

Contrary to the above, the presentations of those (such as Kumāra) who adhere to general karaṇa astronomy (which maintains that at the time of the winter solstice the sun is at a position of twenty lunar mansions and fifteen hours, and that that position is the winter solstice each year at each of the twelve sectors) can be known from their extensive refutation elsewhere.[141]

d.div: [74] 'dir zhal 'phangs mdzad yul ni mkhas grub nor bzang rgya mtsho rang nyid kyis mdzad pa'i rtsis gzhung pad dkar zhal lung gi bu yig tu gtogs pa rtsis gzhung pad dkar zhal lung las sa dum bu bcu gnyis su dbyar dgun nyi ldog gsal bar byed pa'i sgron me zhes pa de yin nges/ gzhung 'di mi rigs dpe skrun khang nas deb gzugs su dpar du btab pa'i rtsis gzhung pad dkar zhal lung shog grangs 524_nas 536_bar bzhugs/

[141] Reference to a work composed by the author himself: Lamp Illuminating Summer and Winter Solstices in the Twelve Sectors as Taught in the Astronomical Treatise, the Puṇḍarīka Transmission, pp. 524–36.

f.d: gzhan yang 'grel chen las/ 'dir lhun po'i phyogs kyi cha thams cad du khyim gyi 'khor lo 'khor ba'i dbang gis me la reg pa gang yin pa de ni bdun pa'i phyogs thob pa na lhun po'i rtse mo la (shong 'gyur la rwa zhes pa 'byung )reg cing gangs kyi ri'i steng du 'gro'o zhes pa'i rigs pas nyi ma khyim so sor gnas pa'i dus kyi tshogs la sogs pa mtha' dag ste thams cad du rig par bya'o/[75] / zhes gsungs pa 'dis kyang sa dum bu re rer la de la dgun nyi ldog pa rags par byas na sum cu re yod par bstan te/

Furthermore, the Great Commentary says:
“Orbiting the circle of houses in all regions of Meru, when the sun reaches the Fire in the region of the seventh, it touches the peak[142] of Meru and journeys above the mountains of snow.” By this reasoning, the lengths of time and so forth of the sun dwelling in each house can be known in all.[143] This passage indicates that the time of the winter solstice is ascertained generally at each of the sectors each year, and from that it can be understood that thirty winter solstices occur on each of these sectors. /100/

d.div: [75] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 88_na5
[142] A note inserted here indicates that the Shong translation has “horns” instead of “peak.”
[143] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 88a5.

f.d: de yang ji ltar du bstan pa ni lho gling dbus ma la mtshon na nyi ma karka Ta'i khyim du sleb ma thag gi tshe lho gling dbus ma'i dbus drang po'i thad kyi lhun po'i rtse mo'am rwa la nyi ma'i gdung byed kyis reg pa'i nyin zhag de la lho gling dbus ma nas bgrangs pa'i sa dum bu bdun pa byang gling dbus ma'i dbus drang po'i thad kyi me ri'i nang mtha'i steng thad du nyi ma'i gdung byed kyis sleb pa dngos bstan rnams kyis go nus shing / nyi bar la skar ma bcu dgu dang chu tshod bdun chu srang sum cu byung ste nyi mas gzhu khyim gyi phyed du sleb pa'i nyin zhag re la lho gling dbus ma la sa khyon tha dad pa sum cur phye ba'i shar mtha'i sa khyon de'i thad kyi lhun po'i rtse mo'am rwa la nyi ma'i gdung byed kyis reg pa dang nyin zhag de nyid la lho gling dbus ma nas bgrangs pa'i sa dum bu bdun pa byang gling dbus ma'i yang shar mtha'i sa khyon de'i thad kyi me ri'i nang mtha'i steng thad du nyi ma'i gdung byed kyis sleb pa lta bu mtshon pa ni/ 'dir lhun po'i phyogs kyi cha thams cad du zhes gsungs pa 'dis bstan pa yin no/ /

How is this understood? Using the central sector of the south as an illustration, the passage explains that the moment the sun arrives in Cancer, the peak or horns of Meru directly facing the direct center of the central sector of the south are touched by the rays of the sun. On the same solar day the rays of the sun will also reach the regions above the inner limit of the Mountains of Fire that directly face the central sector of the north, which is the seventh sector counting from the central southern sector.[144] When the mean sun is at nineteen lunar mansions and seven hours and thirty minutes, which is the sun’s arrival at the halfway point of Sagittarius, the rays of the sun touch the peak or horns of Meru facing the land of the eastern edge of the central sector of the south divided into thirty separate parts. On that day also on the seventh sector from the central sector of the south, the central sector of the north, on the land at the eastern edge, the rays of the sun will reach the regions above the inner limit of the Mountains of Fire. This can be inferred by the phrase “Orbiting the circle of houses in all regions of Meru.”

d.div: [144] On the summer solstice, when the sun is in Cancer, the rays of the sun will reach Meru during the daytime on Jambudvīpa. On the same solar day, when the sun has moved around to the seventh continent directly opposite Jambudvīpa, the rays of the sun will reach the inner limit of the Mountains of Fire.

f.d: de las gzhan du gling rer lo re la lho bgrod mthar thug dang byang bgrod mthar thug re re dang / yang mkhas pa (rje ku mA ra )dag gling rer lo re la dbyar nyi dang dgun nyi ldog pa re re yin par bzhed pa ltar 'thad na nyi ma chu srin gyi khyim du sleb ma thag gi tshe kai la sha'i shar nub kyi dbus drang por nyin chu tshod nyer lnga yin pa ltar kai la sha'i shar mtha'i sa khyon der yang nyin chu tshod nyer lngar 'gyur dgos te/ sa khyon de gnyis dgun nyi ldog dus gcig yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Assertions contrary to the above say that there is only one limit to the sun’s northward and southward passages on each sector each year. Other scholars (such as Kumāra) maintain that there is only one winter and summer solstice each year in each sector. If these were correct, consider the following. When the sun arrives in Capricorn, the length of the day of the direct center of the east-west meridian of Kailash is twenty-five hours. According to the above, it would follow that the day must be twenty-five hours long also at the eastern edge of Kailash, because these two regions share the same time of winter solstice.

'dod do zhe na/ 'o na nyi ma chu srin gyi khyim du sleb ma thag gi tshe lho gling shar ma'i kai la sha dang khyon mtshungs kyi dbus kyi dgun nyi log nas khyim zla gcig song bas sa khyon der nyin chu tshod nyer drug chu srang bzhi bcu yin pa ltar lho gling shar ma'i kai la sha dang khyon mtshungs kyi nub mtha'i sa khyon der yang nyin chu tshod nyer drug chu srang bzhi bcu yin par 'gyur dgos te/ lho gling shar ma'i dbus drang po dang de'i nub mtha' gnyis dgun nyi ldog dus gcig yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

If that is asserted, then consider this. As soon as the sun enters Capricorn, one zodiacal month[145] has passed since the winter solstice in the eastern sector of the south in the center of a region corresponding to Kailash, and the length of the day in that region is twenty-six hours and forty minutes. Similarly, in the eastern sector of the south, at the western edge of a region corresponding to Kailash, it would follow that a day would also have to be twenty-six hours and forty minutes, /101/ because the winter solstice at the center of the eastern sector of the south and at the western edge of that sector occurs at the same time.

d.div: [145] The time taken for the sun to pass from house to house, or approximately thirty days.

f.d: de yang 'dod na/ lho gling dbus ma'i kai la sha'i shar mtha'i nyin tshad chu tshod nyer lnga dang / nyin zhag de nyid kyi lho gling shar ma'i kai la sha dang khyon mtshungs kyi nub mtha'i sa khyon der nyin chu tshod nyer drug chu srang bzhi bcur khas len pa mi rigs te/ lho gling dbus ma'i kai la sha'i shar mtha' dang lho gling shar ma'i kai la sha dang khyon mtshungs kyi nub mtha' gnyis 'dabs 'byar du gnas pa'i phyir ro/ / 'di dag la nyi ma'i gdung byed mtho dman du 'gyur ba'i sgo nas kyang brjod par bya ba yod de re zhig de tsam mo/ /

If that is so, then it would be incorrect to hold that the length of a day at the eastern edge of Kailash of the central sector of the south was twenty-five hours, and on that very day the length of a day on the western edge of a region corresponding to Kailash on the eastern sector of the south was twenty-six hours and forty minutes, because the eastern edge of Kailash of the central sector of the south and the western edge of a corresponding region on the eastern sector of the south border each other. This matter can also be discussed by looking at the extent of the sun’s rays, but that is enough for now.

gal te 'grel chen las/ 'dir lhun po'i phyogs kyi cha thams cad du zhes sogs kyis nyi ma'i bgrod pa gnyis mthar thug pa'i tshe nyi ma'i gdung byed lhun po'i rwa'am rtse mo la reg pa dang me ri'i nang mtha'i steng thad du 'gro bar bstan gyi/ nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor de gnyis su 'gro bar ma bstan na/ 'grel chen las/
lan tshwa'i rgya mtsho 'gongs nas nyin mor byed pa dag ni lho ru me yi bar du 'gro bar byed/ /ces pa ste 'dir rtsibs bcu gnyis kyi sa la dum bu so sor re rer khyim gyi dbang gis lan tshwa'i rgya mtsho 'gongs nas lhor bgrod pa la gnas pa'i nyi ma me'i dkyil 'khor gyi dang po'i bar rgya mtsho'i mtha'i mtshams su 'gro bar byed do/ / me'i dkyil 'khor gyi mtshams de nas kai la sha'i byang du 'gro ste gangs can gyi ri la byang gi lam du yang byang du bgrod la/[76] zhes sogs gsungs pas gnod do zhe na/

Some say that the Great Commentary passage “Orbiting the circle of houses in all regions of Meru” and so on may indeed teach that at the time of the limits of the two passages of the sun, the rays of the sun reach the peak or horns of Meru and the regions above the inner limit of the Mountains of Fire. However, if this means that the disk of the sun itself does not travel to these two places, then consider this quote from the Great Commentary:
“Having covered the Salt Ocean, the sun travels as far as the fire in the south.” This means that the sun, having covered the Salt Ocean by way of the houses over each of the sectors divided by the twelve spokes, it travels to dwell in the south as far as the beginning of the fire mandala at the end of the oceans. From that point of the fire mandala, it travels to the north of Kailash, to Himālaya, moving north on its northward journey.[146] Doesn’t this quote preclude such an assertion?

d.div: [76] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 87_ba5
[146] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 87b5.

f.d:
mi gnod de/ 'grel tshig de rnams kyis kyang nyi ma'i gdung byed nyid me ri'i nang mtha'i steng thad dang / lhun po'i rtse'am rwa la reg gi bar du 'gro bar bstan pa'i phyir te/ rgyud las/
steng du drug dang klu yi grangs ni nyi ma'i gdung byed dag kyang byang du bgrod pa dag gi mthar/ / de nas g.yas phyogs su yang zad par 'gyur te mi yi bdag po stong phrag dag ni drag po'i grangs/ / stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa gcig mda' ni brgya dang bral bar gyur pa dbus nas go la'i ri mo ste/ / de las gang zhig 'phel dang 'grib par 'gyur ba mkha' mkha' mda' dang mda' ni byang dang lhor yang ngo / / lan tshwa'i rgya mtsho 'gongs nas nyin mor byed pa dag ni lho ru me yi bar du 'gro bar byed/[77] / ces sogs gsungs pas ni gong gi nyi ma'i gdung byed ces pa 'og ma lan tshwa'i rgya mtsho'i 'gongs nas zhes sogs rnams la yang gsal byed du sbyor dgos par bstan pa yin la/

It does not, because these words from the Great Commentary teach that it is the rays[147] of the sun that travel to the regions above the inner rim of the Mountains of Fire and as far as the peak or horns of Meru. The Condensed Tantra says:
Above at six and nāga, the rays of the sun at the northward limit. Then, in clockwise direction, lord of men, ceasing at 11,000. From the center at 81,000, less arrows hundred, the gola chart, increasing and decreasing space, space, arrows, and arrows, to the north and south. Having covered the Salt Ocean, the sun travels as far as the fire in the south.[148] This quote shows that the phrase “rays of the sun” is to be applied as clarification to the subsequent lines beginning, “Having covered the Salt Ocean.”

d.div: [77] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ khams kyi le'u/ 1_sh+loka58_28_ba2
[147] gdung byed. “That which burns or heats.” This term refers to the shafts or shoots of light that can be seen radiating from the sun as opposed to the disk of the sun itself.

[148] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, khams v. 59, 28b2. Essentially this verse is saying that the rays of the sun at its northern limit, or summer solstice, travel from a height of 86,000 yojana (six and “nāga”). Then it descends eleven thousand yojana on its southern journey. A chart mapping this would have the sun rising and falling 5,500 yojana (space, space, arrows, arrows) from a central meridian placed at a height of 80,500 yojana (arrows hundred = 500).

f.d:
de bzhin du/
phyed bcas mig klu zlas thob nyin dang nyin la 'dor ba [78] zhes pa ni phyed dang bcas pa'i brgya brgyad cu rtsa gnyis kyi cha thob pa ni stong phrag bdun cu rtsa lnga las nyin zhag so sor dpag tshad rnams kyi phyogs kyi cha nyi mas 'dor ro/ / zhes gsungs pa'i don yang gdung byed kyis 'dor ba yin la/ de yang 'dor ba pos non pa'i go sa logs su phye ba'i rnam par gzhag pa ma yin gyi/ non pa'i go sa dang bcas pa'i rnam gzhag dang / stong phrag bdun cu rtsa lnga las zhes pas kyang nyi ma'i gdung byed kyis dor bar bya ba'i khyon bstan pa yin no/ /

Similarly:
“Together with a half, eyes, nāga, moon, day after day is spent.” /102/ This means a total of 182½.[149] These are the individual solar days of one direction of the 75,000 yojana traveled by the sun.[150] “Spent”[151] in this passage means spent by the rays of the sun. This is not a presentation that excludes the area covered by the “spender” but one that includes it, and so the line ending “the 75,000 yojana spent by the sun” is also talking of the area spent by the rays of the sun.

d.div: [78] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 88_na2
[149] 182.5 solar days, or half a year.
[150] P2064 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ka-2, 99a1.
[151] ’dor ba. To dispel, leave behind. The sun as an indicator of time dispels or leaves behind the days. “Spender” (‘dor ba po) is an epithet for the sun.

f.d: gal te 'dor pa po rang gis non pa'i go sa de yang 'dor ba'i cha la mi bgrang na nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi zlum po'i tshad rgyud 'grel 'dir gsal por ma bshad kyang mdzod las/ dpag tshad lnga bcu gcig dang bcas/[79] /zhes nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi tshad dpag tshad lnga bcu rtsa gcig tu bshad pas dpag tshad stong phrag bdun cu rtsa lnga'i steng nas dpag tshad lnga bcu rtsa gcig gi gsum cha bcu bdun phri ba nyi mas nyin zhag phyed bcas mig klu zla ba'i bar la 'dor bar khas len dgos pas/ stong phrag bdun cu rtsa lnga las zhes sogs dang ci'i phyir khyed rang la'ang mi 'gal bar 'gyur ba soms shig/

If the “spender’s” reach were not included in the portion spent, then the following consequence would occur. The circumference of the sun’s disk is not clearly taught in this tantra and its commentaries, but in the Abhidharmakośa it says, “of fifty-one yojana,”[152] thereby explaining the measurement of the disk of the sun to be fifty-one yojana. Therefore you would have to accept that the sun travels for “Together with a half, eyes, nāga, moon” or 182½ days over 75,000 minus a third of fifty-one, or seventeen, yojana.[153] In that case, ask yourself how, even for you, that does not contradict the quote ending, “75,000 yojana traveled by the sun.”

d.div: [79] sde dge_4089_bstan/ mngon pa/ kumangon pa mdzod/ gnas/ 3_sh+loka60_9_na5
[152] Toh 4089 Tengyur, mngon pa, gnas v. 60, 9a5.
[153] The diameter being seen as one third of the circumference.

f.d: de yang mngon pa nas bshad pa rags pa mthun snang ba'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi/ zhib mor na skar khongs re la nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor 'phreng bar bsgrigs pa drug cu'i tshad las lhag pa med la/ skar khongs gcig la yul gyi chu tshod drug cu yod pas nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi byang mtha' nas lho mtha'i bar la yul gyi chu tshod gcig yan chad tsam yod par 'dod dgos la/ yul gyi chu tshod gcig la ni dpag tshad nyis brgya so gcig lhag pa tsam zhig yod pas so/ / de lta ma yin par byang bgrod mthar thug gi tshe nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor nyid kyis lhun po'i rwa'am rtse mo la reg par khas len pa ni gong du bshad pa ltar rang cag rnams gnas pa'i bod kyi sa khyon 'dir nyi ma'i byang bgrod mthar thug pa'i nyin gyi nyi ma byed pa'i dus der thur shing gi grib ma byang du 'ong ba mngon sum du mthong ba 'di dang 'gal ba yin no/ /

The Abhidharma assertion is a rough estimate made on the basis of commonly accepted views. This can be examined in more detail. A chain of sun discs arranged in a lunar mansion would not exceed sixty in number, and in each lunar mansion there are sixty hours of distance. Therefore it must be that the distance between the northern and southern edge of the sun’s disk is at least one hour of distance, and one hour of distance is a little over 231 yojana. To believe that at the time of the sun’s northern limit, the sun’s disk actually reaches the peak or horns of Meru would contradict our actual experience that here in this land of Tibet, the shadow of the gnomon still shows north on the day of the sun’s northern limit, as previously described.

des na bgrod pa gnyis kyi tshe nyin zhag ra le nyi mas lho byang du ji tsam re bgrod pa ni dpag tshad stong phrag lnga bcu la nyin zhag brgya dang brgyad cu rtsa phyed dang gsum gyi thob nor te/ de yang dpag tshad nyis brgya don gsum rgyang grags gsum gzhu 'dom stong bdun brgya brgyad cu lhag (khru gsum sor drug nas bdun nas kyi sum brgya re lnga'i cha gya lnga/)tsam re dgong ngo / /

How far does the sun travel on each day of its northward journey? 182 ½ days are divided among 50,000 yojana. That results in a little over 273 yojana, three krośa, and 1,780 armspans. /103/ (To be precise, it is over by three cubits, six fingerwidths, seven barley grains, and 85/365 of a barley grain.)

yang nyi ma sa'i dkyil 'khor las steng du 'gro ba'i tshad ni sa'i khyon gang dang gang gi thad du byang bgrod mthar thug pa'i tshe sa las nyi ma'i gdung byed dpag tshad stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa drug gi steng nas 'gro sa'i khyon de nas bgrangs pa'i sa dum bu bdun pa'i sa khyon nyi ma lho bgrod mthar thug pa'i sa la ni stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa drug gi steng nas dpag tshad stong phrag bcu gcig phri ba stong phrag bdun cu rtsa lnga'i steng nas 'gro zhing / nyi ma lhun po la g.yas skor du sgang gshongs su 'khor ro/ / de bas na sa khyon gang dang gang gi thad du yang nyi ma'i byang bgrod mthar thug pa'i sa dang nyi ma'i gdung byed gyi bar la dpag tshad stong phrag brgyad cu rtsa drug re dang / lho bgrod mthar thug gi tshe stong phrag bdun cu rtsa lnga re 'ong bar bshad pas nyi ma byang bgrod mthar thug pa'i sa khyon de nyid kyi thad kar nyin re bzhin lho bgrod ma rdzogs kyi bar la nyi ma gdung byed dang bcas pa dpag tshad drug cu rgyang grags gcig gzhu 'dom brgya go gcig khru gsum sor gnyis sor gyi sum brgya re lnga cha sum brgya lnga bcu rnams kyis dma' bar 'gyur zhing / lho bgrod mthar thug nas byang bgrod ma rdzogs kyi bar la yang nyin re bzhin de tsam res mtho bar 'gyur ba yang shes par bya'o/ /

The height above the earth mandala that the sun travels is explained as follows. Whichever region the sun may be over at the time of its northern limit of that sector, its rays are at a height of 86,000 yojana. Above the area of the seventh sector from that particular region, which would be a region of the sun’s southern limit, the rays are at a height of 86,000 yojana less 11,000, or 75,000 yojana. The sun therefore travels clockwise around Meru in an undulating[154] fashion. Therefore it is taught that in any region the distance between the ground and the rays of the sun is explained as being 86,000 yojana at the sun’s northern limit and 75,000 yojana at its southern limit. It can be understood, therefore, that from the area of its northern limit until its southward journey is completed, the sun and its rays drop each day by sixty yojana, one krośa, 191 armspans, three cubits, two fingerwidths, and 350/365 of a fingerwidth. Similarly it can be understood that from the time of the sun’s southern limit until its northward journey is completed, each day it gains in height by the same distance.

d.div: [154] sgang gshongs. The sun’s daily motion around Meru is in an uneven plane to the Earth. In Western astronomy this is attributed to the tilt of the Earth’s meridian. This undulating passage is repeated in the two annual passages. (Henning)

f.d: 'o na nyi ma'i gdung byed la tshad ji tsam snyam na/ 'di la kha cig dpag tshad stong phrag bcu bzhir 'dod pa dang gzhan dag stong phrag phyed dang bcu gsum du 'dod pa gnyis las gong du 'grel pa drangs pa'i 'gyur/ lhun po'i rtse mo la reg cing zhes pa ltar na nyi ma'i 'og gzhi'i gdung byed dpag tshad stong phrag bcu bzhir 'dod pa ltar byas te byang bgrod mthar thug gi tshe nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor lhun po'i rtse dang khang mnyam du 'gro bar bya zhing / nyi ma'i lho phyogs lta bu'i phyogs kyi gdung byed kyi tshad ni dpag tshad stong phrag phyed dang bcu gsum du phyed dgos te/ nyi ma byang bgrod mthar thug gi tshe gdung byed kyi rtse mo lhun po'i rwa la reg tsam du byed dgos shing / byang bgrod mthar thug gi tshe nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor dang lhun po'i bar na dpag tshad stong phrag phyed dang bcu gsum las med pa'i phyir ro/ /

What is the reach of the sun’s rays? Some say that it is 14,000 yojana, and others say 12,500 yojana. If the previous quote is to be translated, “touches the peak of Meru,” then the rays of the lower regions of sun extend for 14,000 yojana, because at the time of its northern limit the disk of the sun is level with the peak of Meru.[155] The length of the directional rays, such as those from its southern side, for example, must be 12,500 yojana, because at the time of its northern limit the tip of the sun’s rays must be posited as reaching the peak of Meru, and at such a time the distance between the disk of the sun and Meru is not more than 12,500 yojana.

d.div: [155] Because Meru is 100,000 yojana high and the rays are 86,000 yojana above Earth, leaving 14,000 yojana for the extent of the rays.

f.d: yang shong 'gyur las lhun po'i rwa la reg cing [80] zhes 'byung ba ltar byas na nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi 'og gi gdung byed kyang dpag tshad stong phrag phyed dang bcu gsum du bshad par byar yod do/ /
If we read the quote according to the Shong translation as “touches the horns of Meru,”[156] /104/ the rays from the lower regions of the sun disk also travel for 12,500 yojana.

d.div: [80] sde dge_1347_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tha'agrel chen dri med 'od/ 193_na5
[156] Toh 1345 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tha, 193a5.

f.d: de ltar na nyi mas nyin zhag re la sgang gshongs su 'khor ba'i zlum po'i khyon dang / nyi ma'i mnyam lam zlum por bskor ba'i khyon dang / tha skar nas nam gru rdzogs kyi bar gyi khyon rnams ni dpag tshad sum 'bum bdun khri lnga stong dang / chu tshod du byas na yul gyi chu tshod stong drug brgya dang nyi shur mnyam mo/ /

The circumference of the sun’s undulating daily motion, the sun’s ecliptic, and the distance from the lunar mansion of aśvinī to the lunar mansion of revatī[157] is 375,000 yojana. In hours that is equal to 1,620 hours of distance.

d.div: [157] In other words, all twenty-seven lunar mansions.

f.d: yang nyi ma lhun po la sgang gshongs su 'khor ba las khyim so sor yul drug tu nyin mtshan ring thung tha dad par 'gyur ba'i tshul ni/ de yang yul drug ni bsil ri'i phyi mtha' nas chu'i nang mtha'i bar gyi sa'i dkyil 'khor la dpag tshad stong phrag nyer lnga yod pa'i phyed byang ma la cha tha dad pa drug tu dbye dgos te/ yul byang ma gangs ldan bsil ri dang 'dabs 'byar du gnas shing / 'phags yul gyi lho mtha' nyi ma byang bgrod mthar thug pa'i nyin byed kyi dus kyi nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi thad so na gnas pa de'i dus kyi thur shing gi grib mas 'grub pas so/ /

During the sun’s undulating revolution around Meru, there are six places in each sector where night and day are of different lengths. These six places are explained as follows. Of the 25,000 yojana of the earth mandala that stretches from the outer edge of the Śīta Mountains to the inner rim of the water mandala, the northern half is divided into six separate parts. Of these the northernmost part of Himālaya borders the Śīta Mountains. The southern edge of the noble land of India directly faces the disk of the sun on the day of the sun’s northern limit.[158] This is established by the shadow of a gnomon on that day.

d.div: [158] As mentioned previously, this cannot refer to the tip of the subcontinent of India, because the sixth land of “India,” or āryadeśa, ends halfway down the earth mandala and the Tropic of Cancer runs roughly across the middle of India.

f.d: de ltar lho gling dbus ma'i sa'i dkyil 'khor gyi bsil ri'i lho mtha' nas chu'i nang mtha'i bar la dpag tshad stong phrag nyer lnga yod pa'i phyed byang ma la byang nas rim pa bzhin gangs ldan kai la sha rgya nag li bod 'phags yul te yul drug cha mnyam du phye ba bzhin du sa dum bu lhag ma bcu gcig po gzhan rnams la yang de dag dang khyon mtshungs kyi yul drug gi rnam gzhag byas te lho gling dbus ma 'di'i yul drug gi dbus drang por nyi ma'i bgrod pa'i dbang gis nyin mtshan ring thung mi 'dra bar 'gyur ba bzhin du sa dum bu gzhan rnams kyi yul drug dang khyon mtshungs rnams su nyin mtshan ring thung du 'gyur tshul yang shes par bya dgos so/ /

In this way, from the southern edge of the Śīta Mountains on the earth mandala of the central sector of the south to the inner rim of the water mandala, the northern half of the 25,000 yojana is divided into six regions comprising, from the north, Himālaya, Kailash, China, Khotan, Tibet, and India. Likewise the remaining eleven sectors can be presented as having six regions of similar proportions. At the direct center of the six regions of this central sector of the south, night and day can be of different lengths due to the sun’s passages. Similarly, on the six regions of the other sectors, it should be understood that differences in the lengths of day and night will also occur.

de la lho gling dbus mar nyin mtshan ring thung mi 'dra bar 'gyur tshul ni lho gling dbus ma'i dbus drang por nyin mtshan ring thung mnyam pa'i tshe yul drug ka'i dbus su nyin mo chu tshod sum cu mtshan mo chu tshod sum cu ste nyin mtshan mnyam par mtshungs pa las nyin zhag re re la gangs ldan du chu srang gsum dbugs lnga de'i lnga cha gsum de'i yang sum brgya re lnga cha brgya sum cu dang / kai la shar chu srang gsum dbugs gcig de'i drug cha bzhi de'i yang sum brgya re lnga cha

The way night and day differ in length in the central sector of the south is as follows. At the time of equal day and night on the central meridian of the central sector of the south, daytime is thirty hours and nighttime is thirty hours in each of the six regions. Each day on from this time of a common equinox, the time of day increases and the length of night decreases by the following times on the six regions as the sun moves north. /105/

brgya sum cu dang / rgya nag tu chu srang gnyis dbugs bzhi de'i bdun cha drug de'i yang sum brgya re lnga cha brgya sum cu dang / lir chu srang gnyis dbugs gnyis de'i brgyad cha drug de'i yang sum brgya re lnga cha brgya sum cu dang / bod du chu srang gnyis dbugs gcig de'i dgu cha gcig de'i yang sum brgya re lnga cha brgya sum cu dang / 'phags yul du chu srang gcig dbugs lnga de'i bcu cha brgyad de'i yang sum brgya re lnga cha brgya sum cu rnams byang bgrod kyi tshe nyin mo 'phel zhing mtshan mo 'grib pa las lho gling dbus ma'i dbus drang por nyi ma byang bgrod mthar thug pa'i tshe nyin mo'i tshad gangs ldan nas 'phags yul gyi bar rim pa bzhin chu tshod so drug dang / chu tshod so lnga dang / chu tshod so bzhi chu srang bcu bdun dbugs thig dbugs kyi bdun cha drug dang / chu tshod so gsum chu srang zhe lnga dang / chu tshod so gsum chu srang nyi shu dang / chu tshod so gsum rnams 'byung zhing / mtshan mo'i tshad kyang gangs ldan nas rim pa bzhin chu tshod nyer bzhi dang / chu tshod nyer lnga dang / chu tshod nyer lnga dang chu srang zhe gnyis dbugs lnga dbugs kyi bdun cha gcig rnams dang / chu tshod nyer drug chu srang bco lnga dang / chu tshod nyer drug chu srang bzhi bcu dang / chu tshod nyer bdun rnams 'byung ngo / /

At Himālaya it increases by three minutes,[159] five breaths, 3/5 of a breath, and 130/365 of that again. At Kailash it is three minutes, one breath, 2/3 of a breath, and 130/365 of that again. In China it is two minutes, four breaths, 6/7 of a breath, and 130/365 of that again. In Khotan it is two minutes, two breaths, 3/4 of a breath, and one 130/365 of that again. In Tibet it is two minutes, one breath, 1/9 of a breath, and 130/365 of that again. In India it is one minute, five breaths, 4/5 of a breath, and 130/365 of that again. When the sun reaches the limit of its northward journey at the central meridian of the central sector of the south, the length of the daytime is thirty-six hours; thirty-five hours; thirty-four hours, seventeen minutes, and 6/7 of a breath; thirty-three hours and forty-five minutes; thirty-three hours and twenty minutes; and thirty-three hours, respectively, in the six regions from Himālaya to India. The nighttime also decreases to twenty-four hours; twenty-five hours; twenty-five hours, forty-two minutes, five breaths, and 1/7 of a breath; twenty-six hours and fifteen minutes; twenty-six hours, forty minutes; and finally twenty-seven hours from Himālaya to India, respectively.

d.div: [159] Again, one “minute” equals twenty-four seconds.

f.d: de bzhin du nyin mtshan mnyam pa las lho bgrod kyi tshe'ang yul drug po de dang der nyin zhag re re bzhin gong du bshad pa'i chu srang sogs mtshan mo 'phel zhing nyin mo 'grib pas lho bgrod mthar thug pa'i tshe gong du bshad pa las nyin mtshan go log ste shes par bya'o/ /

Similarly, when the sun moves south from the equinox, the length of night increases and daytime decreases each day at each of the six regions by the same amounts as above. At the southern limit of the sun’s travels, the lengths of day and night are the reverse of the above and can be known accordingly.

de yang 'di dag rgyud 'grel gyi shes byed dang sbyar te dwogs pa'i gnas dag kyang dpyad par bya ba la khams le'i so brgyad pa'i 'grel chen las/
tshad 'di la lhor bgrod pa'i 'pho ba'i nyin zhag la chu tshod sum cu rtsa drug gis nyin mor 'gyur zhing nyi shu rtsa bzhis mtshan mor 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du byang du bgrod pa la mtshan mo dang nyin mo'i tshad bzlog pas shes par bya'o/[81] / zhes gangs ldan du lho bgrod mthar thug nas byang bgrod mthar thug gi bar la chu tshod bcu gnyis kyis nyin mo 'phel ba dang mtshan mo 'grib par bshad pa'i lho'i bgrod mtha' nas byang gi bgrod mtha'i bar la chu tshod drug cu'i lnga cha'i nyin mtshan 'phel 'grib byed par grub pa de bzhin du

To match all this with supporting references from the tantra and commentaries, and to look at points of doubt, the Great Commentary says, on the thirty-eighth verse of the Realms chapter:
Concerning this measurement, on the day of moving south, thirty-six hours are of daytime and twenty-four are of night. Similarly, when traveling north, the length of day and night can be known by reversing this.[160] This explains that in Himālaya, daytime increases by twelve hours and nighttime decreases by twelve hours between the time of the sun’s southern limit and the time of the sun’s northern limit. In Kailash, from the southern limit to the northern limit, a fifth of a sixty-hour day and night is established as being the increase and decrease.

d.div: [81] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 78_na5
[160] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 78a5.

f.d:
khams le'i nga bzhi pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir drug chas 'grib par 'gyur zhing 'phel bar 'gyur te chu tshod drug cu'i drug cha chu tshod bcus chu srin nas 'khrig pa'i mthar thug pa'i bar du mtshan mo 'grib cing nyin mo 'phel lo/ / karka Ta nas gzhu'i mthar thug pa'i bar du nyin mo 'grib cing mtshan mo 'phel te nges par nyi ma ri bong can ni 'grib par 'phel [82] zhes pa drug chas so/ / kai la sha'i dum bu la grib ma'i nges pa'i de ni 'phags pa'i yul du ma yin te/ 'phags pa'i yul du ni byang du bgrod pa nas lhor bgrod pa'i mtha' dang lhor bgrod pa nas byang du bgrod pa'i mthar grib ma'i nges pa'i dbang gis bcu'i chas 'grib cing 'phel lo/ / de bzhin du bod dang li dang rgya nag la sogs pa'i yul rnams su dgu cha dang brgyad cha dang bdun cha dag gis sham+b+ha la'i yul la thug gi bar du grib ma'i dbang gis 'grib cing 'phel bar rig par bya'o/ /

The Great Commentary says on the fifty-fourth verse of the Realms chapter: /106/
Here increase and decrease is by one sixth. By a sixth part of sixty, or ten hours, nighttime decreases and daytime increases from Capricorn to the end of Gemini. From Cancer to the end of Sagittarius, daytime decreases and nighttime increases. “Definitely sun and moon decrease and increase” means by one sixth. On the continent of Kailash, the ascertainment of the shadow is not that of India. In India, on the sun’s journey from the north to its southern limit and from the south to the northern limit, the increase and decrease, as ascertained by the shadow, is by a tenth. Likewise, in the lands of Tibet, Khotan, China, and so forth, it is by a ninth, an eighth, a seventh, and so on. In this way, as far as the land of Shambhala, increase and decrease can be known by the reading of the shadow.[161]

d.div: [82] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 86_na2
[161] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 86a2.
