There are many phenomena supported by the body of a being endowed with the six elements. They include the six elements, namely, space, air, fire, water, earth, and gnosis; the six aggregates, consisting of consciousness, mental formations, feelings, recognition, form, and gnosis; the six organs of ear, nose, eyes, tongue, body, and mind; the six sensory source objects, namely, sound, smell, form, taste, contact, and mental phenomena; the six faculties, made up of the secret place, the voice, the hands, the legs, the anus, and the supreme organ; /143/

mchog gi dbang po ste las kyi dbang po drug dang / dri chu 'dor ba/ smra rjod/ len pa/ 'gro ba/ bshang ba 'dor ba khu ba 'dor 'dzin te las dbang gi bya ba drug dang / srog 'dzin gyi rlung / mnyam gnas/ gyen rgyu/ khyab byed/ klu/ thur sel te rlung drug dang / slar yang dga' ba'i rlung / rus spal/ rtsangs pa/ lhas byin/ nor las rgyal/ lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba'i rlung ste yang rlung drug dang / gtsug tor gyi rtsa 'khor/ snying ga'i rtsa 'khor/ mgrin pa'i rtsa 'khor/ smin ma'i dbus kyi rtsa 'khor/ lte ba'i rtsa 'khor/ gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'khor te rtsa 'khor drug dang / de bzhin du rlung nyi khri chig stong drug brgya dang / rtsa bdun khri nyis stong dang / gong du dga' bo mngal gnas kyi mdo drangs pa ltar rus pa sum brgya drug cu dang / tshigs sum brgya drug cu la sogs pa rnams so/ /

the six activities of these faculties, namely, urinating, speaking, taking, moving, excreting, and emitting fluid; the six winds, namely, life-sustaining, coexisting, upwardly moving, pervading, nāga, downwardly expelling; another classification of winds, namely, joyful wind, turtle, lizard, devadatta, dhanaṃjaya, and the inborn joyful wind; the six cakras, consisting of the crown, heart, throat, forehead, navel, and secret place. Also included are the 21,600 winds, the 72,000 channels and, as mentioned in the Womb States of Nanda Sutra, the 360 bones and 360 joints.

de yang de dag thams cad khams dru ga gi rang bzhin gyi chos las mi 'da' ste/ rnam shes kyi phung po nas ye shes kyi phung po'i bar phung po drug ni rim pa bzhin nam mkha'/ rlung / me/ sa/ chu/ ye shes kyi khams kyi chos so/ / de yang phung po drug dang khams drug thabs shes te/ phung po drug thabs dang / khams drug shes rab bo/ / de yang rim pa bzhin sbyar na ye shes kyi phung po dang nam mkha'i khams thabs shes/ gzugs kyi phung po dang rlung gi khams thabs shes / 'du shes kyi phung po dang me'i khams thabs shes/ tshor ba'i phung po dang chu'i khams thabs shes/ 'du byed kyi phung po dang sa'i khams thabs shes/ rnam shes kyi phung po dang ye shes kyi khams thabs shes so/ /

None of the above phenomena are beyond the nature of the six elements. The six aggregates from consciousness to gnosis are respectively phenomena of space, air, fire, earth, water, and gnosis. Moreover the six aggregates and the six elements are classified as method and wisdom, with the six aggregates as method and the six elements as wisdom. If they are individually matched up, the aggregate of gnosis is method and the element of space is wisdom. The aggregate of form is method and the element of air is wisdom. The aggregate of discernment is method and the element of fire is wisdom. The aggregate of feelings is method and the element of water is wisdom. The aggregate of mental formations is method and the element of earth is wisdom. The aggregate of consciousness is method and the element of gnosis is wisdom.

de bzhin du rna ba/ sna/ migalce/ lus/ yid kyi dbang po rnams rim pa bzhin nam mkha'/ rlung / me/ chu/ sa/ ye shes kyi khams kyi chos so/ sgra/ dri/ gzugs/ ro/ reg bya/ chos kyi skye mched rnams ni rim pa bzhin ye shes/ sa/ chu/ me/ rlung / nam mkha'i khams kyi chos so/ / de yang dbang po drug dang yul drug phan tshun yul dang yul can du sbyar ba'i yul drug shes rab dang / yul can drug rang rang gi yul la ltos pa'i thabs so/ /

Similarly the organs of the ears, nose, eyes, tongue, body, and mind are, respectively, phenomena of the elements of space, air, fire, water, earth, and gnosis. The sound, smell, form, taste, contact, and phenomena sensory source objects are respectively phenomena of gnosis, earth, water, fire, air, and space elements. Moreover the six organs and the six source objects correlate with each other as subject and object, and in this context the six objects are wisdom and the six subjects, in dependence on their individual objects, are method.
de bzhin du gsang gnas sam b+ha ga dang rtags/ ngagalag pa/ rkang pa/ bshang lam/ mchog gi dbang po'i dung can ma rnams rim pa bzhin nam mkha'/ rlung / me/ chu/ sa/ ye shes kyi khams kyi chos so/ /

Similarly the six faculties, namely, the secret place (the bhaga[45] and male organ), the voice, hands, legs, anus, and the śaṅkhinī[46] supreme organ are respectively phenomena of the elements of space, air, fire, water, earth, and gnosis. /144/

d.div: [45] Usually refers to the female sex organ.
[46] dung can ma. Usually refers to the central channel below the navel.

f.d: dri chu 'dor ba/ rjod pa/ len pa/ gro ba/ bshang ba 'dor ba/ khu ba 'dor 'dzin rnams rim pa bzhin ye shes/ sa/ chu/ me/ rlung / nam mkha'i khams kyi chos so/ / de yang las kyi dbang po rnams thabs dang / las dbang gi bya ba rnams shes rab yin pas thabs shes rim pa bzhin sbyar ro/ /

Urinating, speaking, taking, moving, excreting, and holding and emitting fluid are respectively phenomena of the elements of gnosis, earth, water, fire, air, and space. Furthermore the faculties are method and the activities they control are wisdom. In this way each can be paired up with its respective counterpart.

yang srog 'dzin/ mnyam gnas/ gyen rgyu/ khyab byed/ klu/ thur sel gyi rlung rnams ni rim pa bzhin nam mkha'/ rlung / me/ chu/ sa/ ye shes kyi khams kyi chos so/ / de bzhin du dga' ba'i rlung / rus sbal/ rtsangs pa/ lhas byin/ nor las rgyal ba/ lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba'i rlung rnams kyang rim pa bzhin nam mkha'/ rlung / me/ chu/ sa/ ye shes kyi khams kyi chos so/ / de bzhin du gtsug tor/ snying ga_mgrin pa/ smin dbus/ lte ba/ gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'khor rnams rim pa bzhin nam mkha' rlung me chu sa ye shes kyi khams kyi chos so/ / yang lus kyi cha shas rkang pa dang lag pa'i sor mo nyi shu po rnams ni mthe chung nas mthe bo'i bar rim pa bzhin nam mkha' rlung me chu sa'i khams kyi chos so/ /

The life-sustaining, coexisting, upwardly moving, pervading, nāga, and downwardly expelling winds are phenomena of the space, air, fire, water, earth, and gnosis elements. Similarly, joyful, turtle, lizard, devadatta, dhaṃnajaya, and the innate joyful wind are phenomena of the space, air, fire, water, earth, and gnosis elements, respectively. The crown, heart, throat, forehead, navel, and secret-parts cakras are phenomena of the space, air, fire, water, earth, and gnosis elements respectively. Fingers and toes from the little finger or toe to the thumb or big toe are phenomena of the space, air, fire, water, and earth elements respectively.

rus pa'i cha shas so rnams ni dang por byis pa la steng du so gnyis skyes par gyur na de'i tshe so g.yas pa sa'i khams kyi chos g.yon pa chu'i khams kyi chos so/ / de nas 'og tu so gnyis skyes par gyur pa na de'i tshe g.yas pa me'i khams kyi chos/ g.yon pa rlung gi khams kyi chos so/ /

The teeth are a part of the bone structure, and when the first two upper teeth appear in a child, the right tooth is an earth-element phenomenon and the left a water-element phenomenon. When the two lower teeth appear, the right is a fire-element phenomenon and the left tooth an air-element phenomenon.

de bas na steng gi sa khams pa dang 'og gi rlung khams pa thabs shes/ steng gi chu khams pa dang 'og gi me khams pa thabs shes/ de bzhin du slar yang steng du so gnyis skyes pa'i tshe g.yas ma me khams pa dang g.yon ma rlung khams pa'o/ / yang 'og tu gnyis skyes pa'i tshe g.yas ma sa khams pa dang g.yon ma chu khams pa'o/ /

Therefore the earth element of the upper tooth and the air element of the lower are method and wisdom, and the water element of the upper and fire element of the lower are method and wisdom. When the next two upper teeth appear, the right is of the element of fire and the left of the element of air. When the next two lower teeth appear, the right is of the earth element and the left of water.

de'i yang steng 'og gi me chu gnyis thabs shes dang / sa rlung gnyis thabs shes so/ / slar yang g.yas g.yon gong gi rim pa bzhin rab tu me dang rlung / steng du chu dang sa'i khams kyi chos te de ltar steng 'og sngar bzhin spel bas so/ /

The fire and water elements of the upper and lower match up as method and wisdom, as do the earth and air elements. The next right and left teeth, as above, are of fire and air in the lower and of water and earth in the upper, and so on. In this way the upper and lower teeth grow and increase in number.

so sum cu rtsa gnyis khams bzhi'i chos su shes par bya zhing sa rlung gnyis thabs shes dang / me chu gnyis thabs shes dang / nam mkha' dang ye shes gnyis thabs shes yin pa ni rnam pa thams cad pa yin no/ / de ltar khams drug gi chos rnams kyi kha dog ni nam mkha'i khams pa rnams ljang khu/ rlung gi khams pa rnams nag po/ me'i khams pa rnams dmar po/ chu'i khams pa rnams dkar po/ sa'i khams pa rnams ser po/ ye shes kyi khams pa rnams sngon po ste 'di yang rnam pa thams cad pa yin no/ /

The thirty-two teeth should be understood as being phenomena of these four elements with pairings of earth and air as method and wisdom and fire and water as method and wisdom. Space and gnosis as method and wisdom cover all phenomena. The colors of the phenomena of the six elements are as follows. Those of the element of space are green, those of the element of air are black, those of the element of fire are red, those of the water element are white, those of the earth element are yellow, and those of gnosis are blue. /145/ This last element covers all phenomena.

de bzhin du rigs drug dang sbyor na yang nam mkha'i khams pa'i chos rnams rdo rje'i rigs dang / rlung gi khams pa'i chos rnams las kyi rigs dang / me'i khams pa'i chos rnams rin po che'i rigs dang / chu'i khams pa'i chos rnams pad+ma'i rigs dang / sa'i khams pa'i chos rnams 'khor lo'i rigs dang / ye shes kyi khams pa'i chos rnams gri gug gi rigs yin no/ /

If the elements are applied to the six families, then phenomena of the element of space are of the vajra family, those of the element of air are of the karma family, those of the element of fire are of the jewel family, those of the water element are of the lotus family, those of the earth element are of the wheel family, and those of the element of gnosis are of the curved knife family.
gnyis pa rtsa rlung thig le'i rnam gzhag khyad par du bshad pa
9. Channels, Winds, and Drops

['di ]la gnyis/ rgyud 'grel 'dir bshad pa'i rtsa rlung thig le'i rnam gzhag bshad pa dang / 'dir bshad pa'i rtsa rlung gi rnam gzhag dang rgyud sde gzhan nas bshad pa'i rtsa rlung gi rnam gzhag mi mthun par gyur pa'i dogs pa dpyad pa'o/ /

This is under two headings: 1. Explanation in accord with this tantra and commentary 2. An examination of the queries arising from the inconsistencies between this explanation of channels, winds, and drops and that of other tantras
dang po [rgyud 'grel rnam gzhag ]

d.i: Explanation in accord with this tantra and commentary

f.d: ['di ]la rtsa rlung thig le gsum gyi gnas tshul bshad pa dang / rtsa rnams kyi nang nas rlung rnams kyi rgyu tshul bshad pa'o/ /
This has two outlines: 1. A description of the channels, winds, and drops 2. How the winds move within the channels
dang po [gnas tshul ]

d.i: A description of the channels, winds, and drops

f.d: ['di ]la rtsa'i gnas tshul bshad pa dang / rlung gi gnas tshul bshad pa dang / thig le'i gnas tshul bshad pa'o/ /
This has three outlines: 1. channels 2. winds 3. drops
dang po [rtsa'i gnas tshul ]ni

rtsa rnams kyi gtso bo ro ma rkyang ma dbu ma gsum ni lus kyi g.yas g.yon gyi dbus drang po na gnas shing / rgyab mdun gyi rgyab ngos sgal tshigs pa phyogs la cung zad nye ba na gnas so/ / de yang ro ma g.yas dang rkyang ma g.yon dang dbu ma de gnyis kyi dbus drang po na gnas te|_gsum ga'ang steng gi rtse mo smin ma'i mtshams dang / 'og gi sne mo rtags sam b+ha ga'i rtse mo dang bshang lam gyi mthar sleb nas gnas so/ /

The primary channels are the right, left, and central channel. These are located midway between the left and right halves of the body. They are closer to the back of the body and near the spine. The central channel runs in between the left and right channels. The upper tips of all three are located between the eyebrows. The lower tips are found at the bhaga or male organ and at the tip of the anus.

rtsa 'khor rnams gnas pa'i thad sor ro rkyang gnyis kyis dbu ma la lu gu rgyud du 'khyud pa'i rtsa mdud re yod cing / rtsa gsum gyi lte ba yan chad kyi ming gi rnam grangs ni nyi ma'i rtsa/ dmar ser/ ras nA/ nyi ma'i lam zhes sogs ni g.yas kyi rtsa ro ma'i ming gi rnam grangs so/ /

At the cakras the left and right channels entwine themselves around the central channel to form a channel knot. Above the navel the three channels are known by various names. /146/ Sun channel, piṅgalā, rasanā, path of the sun, and so forth are terms used to denote the right channel.

zla ba'i rtsa/ i ga sa/ la la nA/ zla ba'i lam zhes sogs ni g.yon gyi rtsa rkyang ma'i ming gi rnam grangs so/ / sgra gcan gyi rtsa/ mchog gi rtsa zhes sogs ni rtsa dbu ma'i ming gi rnam grangs so/ / lte ba man chad kyi rtsa gsum gyi rkyang ma dang ro ma'i rtsa rgyun la bshad pa'i rtsa dang gci ba'i rtsa zhes bya zhing / dbu ma'i rtsa rgyun la dung can ma dang / dus me'i rtsa dang / khu ba bab pa'i rtsa dang / mchog gi rtsa zhes bya la/ dung can ma dang dbu ma gnyis ka la yang d+d+hU tI zhes bya'o/ /

Moon channel, igasa,[47] lalanā, path of the moon, and so forth are names given to the left channel. The Rāhu channel, supreme channel, and so forth are names of the central channel. The left and right channels below the navel are known as the excrement and urine channels. Similarly the central channel below the navel is known as śaṅkhinī, the Kālāgni channel, the channel of descending fluid, and the supreme channel. The śaṅkhinī and the central channel are also referred to as dhūtī.

d.div: [47] As transliterated.

f.d: de yang a wa d+d+hU tI la ro rkyang gis 'khyud pa'i gnas na rtsa 'khor yod pa'i rtsa 'khor ni drug ste/ gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab so gnyis pa dang / lte ba'i rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab re bzhi pa dang / snying ga'i rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab brgyad pa dang / mgrin pa'i rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab so gnyis pa dang / dpral pa'i rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab bcu drug pa dang / gtsug tor gyi rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab bzhi pa rnams so/ /

At points on the avadhūtī[48] are cakras entwined by the left and right channels. Of these there are six: the cakra of the secret place with its thirty-two channel petals, the cakra of the navel with sixty-four channel petals, the cakra of the heart with its eight channel petals, the cakra of the throat with thirty-two channel petals, the cakra of the forehead with sixteen channel petals, and the cakra of the crown with its four channel petals.

d.div: [48] Although dhūtī and avadhūtī are often interchangeable, it seems that avadhūtī is used to indicate the central channel at the point of the cakras.

f.d:
de la gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'khor gyi rtsa 'dab so gnyis ni rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba las gyes pa nang gi rtsa 'dab drug/drug po de'i bzhi las gnyis gnyis su gyes pas brgyad dang ma gyes pa gnyis te rim gyi rtsa 'dab bcu bcu po'i drug las gnyis gnyis su gyes pas bcu gnyis/ ma gyes pa bzhi ste phyi rol gyi rtsa 'dab bcu drug go/ / de yang gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'dab so gnyis su byed tshul ni rtsa 'khor la rtsa 'dab rim pa gsum yod pa'i nang ma la drug/ bar ma la bcu/ phyi ma la bcu drug yod pa rnams bsdoms pa'i grangs so gnyis su byed pa yin te/ nang le'i zhe drug pa'i 'grel chen las/
gsang ba'i 'dab ma sum cu rtsa gnyis pa ste phyi rol gyi 'dab ma bcu drug rnams la dbyangs kyi rtsa'o/ / nang gi 'dab ma bcu la phung po dang khams kyi rtsa'o/ / de las nang gi 'dab ma rnams la stong pa drug gi rtsa'o/[29] / zhes rtsa 'dab so gnyis su byed tshul gsal bar gsungs pas so/ /

Concerning the makeup of the thirty-two channel petals of the secret- place cakra, six petals branch off from the hub of the cakra. These are the six inner channel petals. Four of these split into two to make eight, and together with the remaining undivided petals make up the ten intermediate channel petals. Of these ten, six split into two to make twelve petals, and with the remaining four make up the sixteen outer petals. The formation of the thirty-two channel petals of the secret-place cakra then is in three layers. The inner layer has six petals, the intermediate has ten, and the outer sixteen. The Great Commentary, on the forty-sixth verse of the Inner chapter, clearly describes the thirty-two petals:
The secret place has thirty-two petals. On the sixteen outer petals are the vowel channels. On the ten inner petals are the channels of the aggregates and the channels of the elements. On the innermost petals are the six empty[49] channels.[50]

d.div: [29] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 134_ba3
[49] No wind flows through empty channels.
[50] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 134b3.

f.d: lte ba'i rtsa 'khor la rtsa 'dab drug cu rtsa bzhir byed tshul ni rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba las dang por rtsa 'dab bzhir gyes/ de nas bzhi po de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pas brgyad/ brgyad po yang re re las gnyis gnyis su gyes pas bcu drug/ bcu drug po de'i mtshams bzhi'i rtsa ma gtogs pa'i bcu gnyis po re re las lnga lngar gyes pas drug cu dang / mtshams bzhi'i re re dang bcas pas drug cu rtsa bzhi'o/ /

The formation of the sixty-four petals of the navel cakra is as follows. Four channel petals branch out from the center of the cakra. Each of these petals branches off into two to make eight petals. /147/ These eight again split up to make sixteen petals. Except for the four petals located at the four intermediate points among these sixteen, each of the other twelve divide into five to make sixty petals, making a total of sixty-four.

'o na nang le'i zhe gcig pa'i 'grel chen las/
lte ba'i 'khor lo ni snying por 'dab ma bzhi pa'i bdag nyid do/ / de'i phyi rol du 'dab ma brgyad kyi bdag nyid do/ / de'i phyi rol du 'dab ma bcu gnyis kyi bdag nyid do/[30] / zhes 'dab ma brgyad la bcu gnyis su gyes par gsungs pa ma yin nam/ ji ltar bcu drug tu gyes pa yin zhe na/ de'i phyi rol du 'dab ma bcu gnyis kyi bdag nyid do zhes pa ni brgyad la bcu drug tu gyes pa'i bzhi stong pa'i rtsa dang / bcu gnyis 'pho ba'i rtsa yin pas rlung 'pho ba'i rtsa bcu gnyis kyi bdag nyid ces pa'i don yin gyi/ de lta ma yin par brgyad las gyes pa bcu gnyis kho na yin na stong pa'i rtsa bzhi med par 'gyur ba dang / rtsa 'dab drug cu rtsa bzhi yang ma tshang bar 'gyur bas so/ /

However on the forty-first verse of the Inner chapter of the Great Commentary it says:
The heart of the navel wheel possesses four petals. Outside of that there are eight. Beyond that are twelve.[51] Doesn’t this say that eight petals branch off into twelve? How, then, could it divide into sixteen? Of the sixteen petals that branch off from the eight, four are empty channels and twelve are the wind-movement channels.[52] Therefore the quote “Beyond that are twelve” refers to these twelve wind- movement channels. If this were not the case and the eight channels divided only into twelve, then the four empty channels would not exist and the sixty-four channel petals would be incomplete.

d.div: [30] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 132_ba5
[51] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 132b5.
[52] In which the major and minor movements, or shifts, of wind take place.

f.d: lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus de nas sor phyed dang bcas pa'i bcu gnyis kyi steng na snying ga'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i dbus gnas pa'i snying ga'i rtsa 'khor ni rtsa 'dab brgyad pa'o/ / rtsa 'dab brgyad po de'i ming ni shar gyi rtsa 'dab la snar ma zhes bya zhing / de bzhin du me mtshams kyi 'dab ma la lag ldan lce dang / lho'i 'dab ma la dmar ser dang / bden bral gyi 'dab ma la rgyal dang / nub kyi 'dab ma la rgyal ba dang / rlung gi 'dab ma la a lam bu Sha dang / byang gi 'dab ma la i Da dang / dbang ldan gyi 'dab ma la kuhA zhes pa'o/ /

Twelve and a half fingerwidths above the center of the navel cakra is the center of the heart cakra. It has eight channel petals, each of which is named. The eastern petal is named rohinī, the southeastern petal is hastijihvā, the southern is piṅgalā, the southwestern petal is puṣya, the western is jaya, the northwestern is alambuṣa, the northern is meṣa, and the northeastern is kuha.

yang snying ga'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus nas steng du sor mo phyed dang bcas pa'i bcu gnyis kyi mtshams na mgrin pa'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i dbus gnas pa'i mgrin pa'i rtsa 'khor ni rtsa 'dab so gnyis pa ste/ de yang dang por lte ba la sa rtsa 'dab brgyad du gyes shing / brgyad po re re la sa gnyis gnyis su gyes pas rtsa 'dab bcu drugabacu drug po re re las kyang gnyis gnyis su gyes pas sum cu rtsa gnyis so/ / de'i yang rtsa 'dab bzhi ni rlung rags pa mi 'bab pa'i stong pa'i rtsa'o/ /

Twelve and a half fingerwidths above the center of the heart cakra lies the center of the throat cakra. This cakra has thirty-two channel petals. Eight petals branch out from its center, each of which splits into two to make sixteen channel petals. Each of these sixteen in turn divides into two to make thirty-two. Four of those are empty channels, in which coarse wind does not flow.

yang mgrin pa'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i dbus nas steng du sor mo phyed dang bcas pa'i bcu gnyis kyi mtha'i dpral ba'i gnas na rtsa 'khor gyi dbus gnas pa'i dpral pa'i rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab bcu drug pa ste/ de yang dang por rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba las rtsa 'dab brgyad du gyes shing brgyad po re re las gnyis gnyis su gyes pas bcu drug go/ / de'i yang rtsa 'dab gnyis ni rlung rags pa mi rgyu ba'i stong pa'i rtsa'o/ / gtsug tor gyi rtsa 'khor ni rtsa 'dab bzhi pa'o/ /

Twelve and a half fingerwidths above the center of the throat cakra at the forehead is a cakra of sixteen petals. From its center eight petals branch out, each of which divides into two to make sixteen. Two of them are empty channels, in which coarse wind does not flow. /148/ The cakra of the crown has four channel petals.

de ltar na rtsa 'khor drug po de'i rtsa 'dab kyi rtsa'i grangs ni brgya dang lnga bcu rtsa drug go/ / des na 'dir rtsa 'khor drug dngos su bshad pa ni rtsa 'dab lha grangs sogs dang sbyar ba'i ched du yin gyi rtsa 'khor lo drug po der nges pa ni ma yin te/ dbang mdor bstan las/
lte gsang nor bu'i chu skyes la/ / lus ngag sems ni 'bab pa rnams/[31] / zhes nor bu'i dbus na'ang rtsa 'khor yod par gsungs shing /

In total, then, there are 156 channel petals within the six cakras. The descriptions here of six cakras are for the purpose of assigning channel petals to deities and so forth, but the cakras are not limited to six. In A Short Teaching on Initiations it says:
To the lotuses of navel, secret, and jewel, body, speech, and mind descend.[53] This quote indicates that at the center of the jewel also there is a cakra.

d.div: [31] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan/ 16_na4
[53] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 16a4.

f.d:
nang le'i zhe lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
dpal ldan rtsa yi 'khor lo 'di ni rnam pa mang por 'gyur te tshigs kyi dbye ba du mas so/ /zhes pa ni 'dir lus la tshigs kyi dbye ba'i grangs sum brgya drug cu ste tshigs kyi dbye ba de dag gis rtsa'i 'khor lo'i dbye ba sum brgya drug cur 'gyur zhing srog la sogs pa'i rlung gi bya ba'i dbye ba yang de bzhin du shes par bya'o/[32] / zhes tshigs sum brgya drug cu'i gnas re re na rtsa 'khor dang / rtsa 'khor gar yod na rlung gi bya ba rnams kyang yod par gsungs pas so/ /

The Great Commentary, on the forty-fifth verse of the Inner chapter, says:
“By there being numerous joints, these glorious cakras take many forms.” This means that because there are 360 joints in this body, there are 360 cakras, and a similar number of wind activities, such as those of the life-sustaining wind, and so forth.[54] This states that at each of the locations of the 360 joints there is a cakra, and wherever there is a cakra there are the activities of the winds.

d.div: [32] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 133_ba7
[54] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 133b7.

f.d:
yang 'grel chen las/
lte ba'i 'khor lo de'i steng du sor mo phyed dang bcas pa'i bcu gnyis kyi steng snying ga'i phyogs su rtsa'i 'khor lo rtsibs brgyad pa [33] zhes pa dang /
'dir snying ga'i pad+ma'i steng du sor mo phyed dang bcas pa'i bcu gnyis kyi mthar mgrin pa'i 'khor lozhes pa dang /
mgrin pa'i pad+ma'i de'i yang steng du sor mo phyed dang bcas pa'i bcu gnyis kyi mthar dpral ba'i pad+ma 'dab pa bcu drug lazhes gsungs pa rnams kyi don la mkhas pa (bu ston thams cad mkhyen pa/)dag
lte ba nas snying ga'i bar dang / snying ga nas mgrin pa'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi bar dang / de nas dpral ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi bar rnams la mi phal pa'i sor phyed dang bcu gsum med par dgongs te/ phyed dang bcas pa'i sor mo bcu gnyis zhes pa sangs rgyas kyi khru phyed la sor phyed dang bcu gsum yod pa'i dbang du byas pa yin no/ / zhes gsung pa la 'grel bshad de kho na nyid snang bar byed pa las/
'grel tshig 'di rnams la mi phal pa'i gzhi dus la snying gar thun tshod kyi rlung rgyu ba'i rten gyi rtsa 'khor 'chad pa'i skabs yin pas 'gal ba spong tshul de 'brel par ma mthong [34] zhes gsung pa de kho na ltar yin zhing /

In the Great Commentary it says:
Twelve and a half fingerwidths above the navel wheel in the region of the heart is a cakra of eight spokes. And, further on:
Twelve and a half fingerwidths above the lotus of the heart is the throat cakra. And:
Twelve and a half fingerwidths above the lotus of the throat lies the lotus of the forehead with sixteen petals.[55] Concerning the above quotes, scholars such as the omniscient Butön say:
The measurement of twelve and a half fingerwidths from the navel to the heart, from the heart to the center of the throat cakra, and from there to the center of the forehead cakra does not refer to the fingerwidths of an ordinary human but to the twelve and half fingerwidths that make up half the length of a buddha’s forearm. However the commentary Illuminating Reality is correct when commenting on this assertion:
These words of commentary are from the section that speaks of the cakras acting as supports for the regular movement of wind at the heart of an ordinary being during ordinary existence. Therefore I do not see the relevance of that particular way of dispelling the contradiction.[56] /149/

d.div: [33] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 132_ba6
[34] mkhas grub rje'i gsung 'bum/ gnang gi le'u'i 'grel bshad/ 40_ba2
[55] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 132b6.

[56] Khedrup Jé, Collected Works, vol. kha, Inner Chapter, 40b2 (includes Butön’s quote). The seeming contradiction being that twelve and a half fingerwidths exceeds the actual distance from the navel to the heart. Here Khedrup Jé is dismissing Butön’s way of resolving this contradiction.

f.d:
'grel bshad kyis ni
lte ba'i bug pa yod sa nas snying ga bar la mi phal pa'i rang sor phyed dang bcu gsum med kyang / lte ba'i rtsa 'khor phyi'i lte ba'i bug pa'i thad las cung zad dma' bar yod pa'am/ snying ga'i rtsa 'khor yang lha la sogs pa'i chag tshad la snying ga rang gi gnas la tshad ji tsam bshad pa'i tshad de'i ma mtha'i mtshams na med kyi snying ga'i gnas kyi yan man gyi dbus drang po na rtsa 'khor yod pas de 'dra cig gi sgo nas 'gal spong dgos sam snyam mozhes bshad do/ /

The commentary goes on to explain:
There are not twelve and a half of a particular being’s fingerwidths between his or her actual navel and heart. However either the navel cakra is a little lower than the actual navel, or alternatively the heart cakra also is not to be found at the bottommost point of a heart of a size proportionate to the dimensions of beings such as gods and so forth, but is found halfway along the heart’s vertical axis. I think the contradiction has to be resolved in this way, and that this is what the commentary is saying.

de ltar gsung pa gnyis kas kyang lte ba'i dbus nas nu ma gnyis kyi thad drang gi dbus kyi snying ga'i bar la mi phal pa'i sor mi phyed dang bcu gsum med par dgongs nas 'gal spong mdzad par snang na'ang lte ba'i dbus rked pa'i thad nas mgrin pa'i bar la sor nyer bzhi/ lhun po'i mgrin pa ste lus la sor drug go zhes gsungs pa ltar mgrin pa la sor drug_mgrin pa nas dpral ba'i mtha'i bar du ste lus la sor bcu gnyis so zhes gsungs pa ltar mgrin pa'i ya mtha' nas dpral ba'i ma mthar bar la sor bcu gnyis yod pa'i mgrin pa'i ya mtha' nas sna'i bar la sor bzhi/ sna'i rtse nas smin mtshams bar la sor bzhi ste dril bas lte ba'i bug pa nas smin mtshams bar la sor sum cu rtsa brgyad yod cing / 'grel chen las gsungs pa ltar lte ba nas snying ga dang / snying ga nas mgrin pa dang / mgrin pa nas dpral ba'i bar la sor phyed dang bcu gsum re yod pa rnams bsdoms pas sor phyed dang so brgyad 'ong bas lte ba nas snying ga dang / snying ga nas mgrin pa dang / mgrin pa nas dpral ba'i bar la sor phyed dang bcu gsum rer byas kyang lte ba nas dpral ba'i ma mtha'i bar la sor so brgyad yod pas da dung dpral bar sor phyed kyis ma sleb pas so/ /

It seems that both the above passages have tried to resolve the contradiction on the basis of there not being twelve and a half fingerwidths of an ordinary being between the central point of the navel and the heart at a point midway between the two nipples. However the distance from the central point of the navel to throat is twenty-four fingerwidths. The height of the throat is six fingerwidths, as in the line “the throat of Meru is six fingerwidths on the body.” There are twelve fingerwidths between the upper edge of the throat and the upper edge of the forehead, as stated by the line “from the throat to the edge of the forehead is twelve fingerwidths on the body.” Of these, there are four fingerwidths from the upper edge of the throat to the nose, and from the tip of the nose to the point between the eyebrows there are also four fingerwidths. In total, therefore, the distance between the navel and the point between the eyebrows is thirty-eight fingerwidths. The Great Commentary states that from the navel to the heart, from the heart to the throat, and from the throat to the forehead are each twelve and a half fingerwidths, which gives a total of thirty-seven and a half fingerwidths. Therefore, although the distance between each of these points is given as twelve and a half fingerwidths, the distance from the navel to the lower edge of the forehead is thirty-eight fingerwidths. Therefore the previous measurement falls short of the forehead by half a fingerwidth.

de ltar na lte ba'i bug pa nas smin mtshams bar la cha mnyam gsum du byas ba'i cha re la sor phyed dang bcu gsum re mi 'ong ba'i skyon med do/ / de ltar na cha re la sor phyed dang bcu gsum re byas kyang dpral bar sor phyed kyis ma sleb ba'i sor phyed pa de cha gsum du byas pas nas re dang nas kyi sum cha re 'ong ba lte ba nas snying ga'i bar sogs kyi sor phyed dang bcu gsum rnams kyi steng du bsnan dgos so/ /

In this way, when the distance between the actual navel and the point between the eyebrows is divided into three sections of equal length, there is no mistake in each part not coming out at twelve and a half fingerwidths. Therefore, although each part is given as twelve and a half fingerwidths, the half a fingerwidth distance of the forehead is to be divided into three, giving a distance of one barley seed and one thirtieth of a barley seed, and this measurement has to be added to each distance of twelve and a half fingerwidths from the navel to the heart, and so forth. /150/

mdor na 'grel chen gyi skabs 'dir rtsa 'khor rnams yod pa'i gnas bshad pa ni rtsa 'khor gang gi lte ba'i dbus su gnad du bsnun ba'i gnas shes par bya ba'i phyir du gsungs pa yin pas sgra ji bzhin par shes par bya zhing / lte ba nas snying ga bar la sor phyed bcas bcu gnyis su bshad pa sogs rags pa thob thang brtsis ba'i dbang du byas pa sogs su shes par bya dgos so/ /

This section of the Great Commentary explaining the location of the cakras is taught for the purpose of knowing where the centers of the cakras to be penetrated are located and, therefore, is to be taken literally. The measurements of twelve and a half fingerwidths given for the distances between the navel and the heart, etc., are to be understood as being on the basis of equal allotment and as an approximate calculation.
gnyis pa rlung gi gnas tshul bshad pa ni/

rlung ni bcu ste srog rlung nam mkha'i khams pa dang / mnyam gnas rlung gi khams pa dang / gyen rgyu me'i khams pa dang / khyab byed chu'i khams pa dang / klu sa'i khams pa dang / rus sbal rlung gi khams pa dang / rtsangs pa me'i khams pa dang / lhas byin chu'i khams pa dang / nor las rgyal sa'i khams pa dang / thur sel ye shes kyi khams pa dang bcu'o/ /

There are ten winds. The life-sustaining wind is of the element of space. The coexisting wind is of the element of wind. The upwardly moving wind is of the element of fire. The pervading wind is of the element of water. The nāga wind is of the element of earth. The turtle wind is of the element of air. The lizard wind is of the element of fire. The devadatta wind is of the element of water. The dhanaṃjaya wind is of the element of earth. The downwardly expelling wind is of the element of gnosis.

srog rlung la yang rgyu lam gyi sgo nas phye na gsum ste/[35] g.yon gyi rtsa rkyang ma la rgyu ba dang / g.yas kyi rtsa ro ma la rgyu ba dang / dbu ma'i rtsa la rgyu ba ste gsum mo/ / thur sel yang byed las kyi sgo nas gsum ste/ 'og sgo gnyis nas bshang ba dang gci ba 'dren par byed pa dang / mchog gi rtsa dung can ma nas khu ba 'dren par byed pa dang gsum mo/ /

The life-sustaining wind in terms of its pathways can be divided into three — the wind that moves through the left channel, the wind that moves through the right channel, and the wind that moves through the central channel. In terms of its function, the downwardly expelling wind can be divided into three — two that push excrement and urine through the two lower orifices and one that carries fluid through the śaṅkhinī, or supreme channel.

d.div: [35] ma dper phyed gsum ste gsal yang phye na gsum ste zhes bcos/

f.d: de yang rlung bcu'i gnas ni/ mnyam gnas sogs brgyad na snying ga'i rtsa 'dab brgyad la rim pa bzhin gnas te/ mnyam gnas ni shar gyi rtsa 'dab snar ma la gnas so/ / gyen rgyu ni shar lho'i rtsa 'dab lag ldan gyi lce la gnas so/ / de bzhin du khyab byed lho'i rtsa 'dab dmar ser la dang / klu ni lho nub kyi rtsa 'dab rgyal la dang / rus sbal ni nub kyi rtsa 'dab rgyal ba la dang/ rtsangs pa ni nub byang gi rtsa 'dab 'phyang ba la dang / lhas byin ni byang gi rtsa 'dab lug la dang / nor las rgyal ni byang shar gyi rtsa 'dab tshul 'chos pa la gnas shing / rtsa 'dab de rnams ni rlung de dag rang rang gi skye ba'i gnas kyang yin no/ / de yang rtsa de rnams rlung de rnams kyi skye ba'i gnas kyi gtso bo yin pa la dgongs pa ste/ gzhan du na rlung rnams kyis rtsa stong phrag bdun cu rtsa gnyis po thams cad la khyab nas gnas te/

Concerning the locations of the winds, eight winds beginning with the coexisting wind are to be found in the eight petals of the heart cakra. The coexisting wind is located in the eastern rohinī channel petal. The upwardly moving wind is in the southeastern hastijihvā channel petal. The pervading wind is located in the southern piṅgalā petal. The nāga wind is found in the southwestern puṣya petal. The turtle wind is found within the western jaya petal. The lizard wind is within the northwestern alambuṣa petal. The devadatta wind is within the northern meṣa channel petal. The dhanaṃjaya wind is within the northeastern kuha petal. These channels are the primary birthplaces of these winds, although these winds also pervade and inhabit all the 72,000 channels. /151/

nang le'i zhe gnyis pa'i 'grel chen las/
srog la sogs pa 'di dag rtsa stong phrag bdun cu rtsa gnyis po rnams la khyab pa ste 'on kyang gnas brgyad nas rlung brgyad skye ba'i phyir te/[36] zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ / rlung rnams mgon po gang gi rlung yin pa ni srog 'dzin mi bskyod pa'i rlung dang / de bzhin du thur sel rdor sems dang / mnyam gnas don grub dang / gyen rgyu rin 'byung dang / khyab byed snang ba mtha' yas dang / klu rnam snang dang / rus sbal don grub dang / rtsangs pa rin 'byung dang / lhas byin snang mtha' dang / nor las rgyal rnam snang gi rlung ngo / /

With this in mind the Great Commentary says on the forty-second verse of the Inner chapter:
The life-sustaining wind and others pervade the 72,000 channels. However the eight winds are created within the eight places.[57] The guardians of the winds are as follows. The life-sustaining wind is the wind of Akṣobhya. The downwardly expelling is the wind of Vajrasattva. The coexisting is the wind of Amoghasiddhi. The upwardly moving is the wind of Ratnasaṃbhava. The pervading is the wind of Amitābha. The nāga is the wind of Vairocana. The turtle wind is the wind of Amoghasiddhi. The lizard wind is the wind of Ratnasambhava. The devadatta is the wind of Amitābha. The dhanaṃjaya is the wind of Vairocana.

d.div: [36] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 133_na5
[57] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 133a5.

f.d: gsum pa thig le'i gnas tshul bshad pa ni/

gong tu bshad pa ltar mngal du chags pa nas zla ba bcu gsum song ba'i mthar thig le dkar dmar dang por 'phel ba'i 'go rtsom zhing skyes pas lo bcu drug lon gyi bar dang / bud med kyis lo bcu gnyis lon gyi bar la 'phel ba gyur la/ bud med lo bcu gnyis lon pa'i tshe rdul gsang gnas nas 'byung bas rdul lam thig le dmar po'i 'phel ba gtong zhing / skyes pa la lo bcu drug lon pa'i tshe khu ba dbang po'i sgo nas 'byung bas thig le'am khu ba'i 'phel ba gtong ngo / /

As previously explained, the end of the thirteenth month after conception marks the first growth in the red and white drops. These drops continue to grow in the case of a boy until the age of sixteen and in a girl until the age of twelve. When a girl reaches the age of twelve, menstrual blood emerges from the secret place, and the growth of menstrual blood, or the red drop, is complete. When a boy reaches the age of sixteen, fluid emerges from the organ, and the growth in the drop, or fluid, is complete.

de lta bu'i thig le dkar dmar rnams spyir lus kyi cha thams cad la til la til mar gnas pa'i tshul du gnas shing / dkar po'i cha gtso bor spyi bo bde chen gyi 'khor lo dang / dmar po'i cha gtso bor gsang gnas dang lte ba'i 'khor lo la gnas pa dang / yang khu ba byang sems dkar po'i cha rtsa rkyang ma la gnas shing rkyang ma nas 'byung ba dang / rdul lam byang sems dmar po'i cha rtsa ro ma la gnas shing ro ma nas 'byung ba dang / lte ba man chad du rtsa gsum gyi nang tshan gyi dung can ma'am mchog gi rtsa nas dkar dmar gnyis ka 'byung ngo / /

In general, red and white drops are to be found in every part of the body, like sesame oil in a sesame seed. The white is primarily situated in the cakra of great bliss in the crown of the head, while the red is primarily to be found in the cakras of the secret place and the navel. In its form of fluid, or white bodhicitta, the white drop dwells in and emerges from the left channel. In its form of menstrual blood, or red bodhicitta, the red drop dwells in and emerges from the right channel. The śaṅkhinī, or supreme channel, one of the three channels below the navel, carries both red and white drops.

yang rtsa 'khor gyi dbang du byas na dpral ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte bar sad pa'i gnas skabs skyed par byed pa'i thig le dang / mgrin pa'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte bar rmi lam gyi gnas skabs skyed par byed pa'i thig le dang / snying ga'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte bar gnyid 'thug gi gnas skabs skyed par byed pa'i thig le dang / lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte bar bzhi pa'i gnas skabs skyed par byed pa'i thig le gnas shing / de bzhin du lte ba man chod na yid gnas skabs bzhi skyed pa'i thig le gnas pa'i lte ba'i thig le gcig pu de nyid la bzhi pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa dang sad pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa'i nus pa gnyis ka yod pas thig le gcig pu de nyid gnyis ka'i bzhi mthun yin zhes gsung ngo / / de ltar na lte ba na sad pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le dang / gsang gnas na rmi lam gyi gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le dang / nor bu'i dbus na gnyid 'thug gi gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le dang / nor bu'i rtse na bzhi pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le gnas so/ /

At the center of the forehead cakra is found the drop that creates the waking state. In the center of the throat cakra is the drop that creates dream states. In the center of the heart cakra is the drop that creates the state of deep sleep. /152/ In the center of the navel cakra is the drop that creates the fourth state.[58] Similarly locations of drops that create the four states are also found from the navel downward. The one drop at the navel has the potential to create the fourth state as well as the waking state, and so it is said that both states share a common basis on that one drop. Therefore at the navel is found the drop that creates the waking state. At the secret place is the drop that creates dream states. In the center of the jewel lies the drop that creates deep sleep. At the tip of the jewel lies the drop that creates the fourth state.

d.div: [58] The fourth state = the bliss of orgasm.

f.d: de yang dpral ba dang lte ba na gnas pa'i sad pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le 'di dag gi steng na tha mal pa rnams la gnyid sad pa'i gnas skabs kyi rnam rtog grangs med pa rnams skyed pa'i nus pa cig dang / sangs rgyas pa'i tshe sprul pa'i sku mtha' yas pa skyed pa'i nus pa cig dang gnyis yod do/ /

In the drops at the forehead and at the navel, which create the waking state, resides the potential to create the endless conceptions of the waking state in ordinary beings as well as the potential to create limitless emanated bodies at the time of becoming a buddha.

de bzhin du mgrin pa dang gsang gnas gnyis na gnas pa'i thig le 'di'i steng na tha mal pa la rmi lam sna tshogs rmi ba skyed pa'i nus pa cig dang / sangs rgyas pa'i tshe longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku gsung rnam pa thams cad pa skyed pa'i nus pa cig dang gnyis yod cing / yang snying ga dang nor bu'i dbus na gnas pa'i gnyid mthug gi gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le 'di gnyis kyi steng na tha mal pa la gnyid dran med skyed pa'i nus pa cig dang / sangs rgyas pa'i tshe chos kyi sku spros pa'i mtha' thams cad dang bral ba'i mi rtog pa skyed pa'i nus pa cig dang gnyis yod do/ /

Similarly, in the drops contained at the throat and secret place can be found the potential to create dreams in ordinary beings and saṃbhogakāya speech[59] in all its aspects in the enlightened state. In the drops at the heart and in the center of the jewel that create the state of deep sleep is found the potential to create the unconsciousness of sleep in ordinary beings as well as the nonconceptual dharmakāya freed of all fabrication at the time of enlightenment.

d.div: [59] In Kālacakra the saṃbhogakāya, or enjoyment body, is also used to describe the speech of the buddha.

f.d: yang lte ba dang nor bu'i rtse gnyis na gnas pa'i bzhi pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le 'di gnyis kyi steng na tha mal pa la 'dzag bde skyed pa'i nus pa cig dang / sangs rgyas ba'i tshe bde pa'i sku mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed pa'i nus pa cig dang gnyis yod do/ /

In the drops at the navel and at the tip of the jewel responsible for creating the fourth state can be found the potential to create contaminated pleasure in ordinary beings as well as the body of bliss that is the supreme and unchanging bliss of a buddha.

de bas na sbyor ba yan lag drug la sogs pa bskyed rdzogs kyi lam rnams kyi thig le brgyad po de rnams kyi steng gi tha mal pa'i gnas skabs su 'byung ba'i skyon gyi cha rnams skyed pa'i nus pa rnams sbyangs te/ sku bzhi la sogs pa yon tan gyi cha rnams skyed pa'i nus pa rnams yon tan yar ldan du skyed pa'i sgo nas mthar thug gi 'bras bu mngon du byed pa yin no/ /

Therefore, on the paths of the generation and completion stage six-branched yoga, the potential of these eight drops to create the faults that arise in ordinary beings is purified, and the potential to create the qualities of the four bodies is developed in terms of ever-increasing quality until the ultimate result is actualized. /153/

mdor na bshad ma thag pa'i thig le dkar dmar 'di dag mngal skyes kyi lus skyed pa la med mi rung gi rgyu dang / tshe thog ma med pa nas khams dkar dmar 'dzag pa'i 'pho ba'i bag chags yang yang bzhag pa'i 'pho ba'i bag chags kho nas 'khor bar yang yang 'khyam pa yin pa dang / rdo rje'i lus kyi rtsa rlung la gnad du bsnun pa'i rdo rje'i rnal 'byor goms pa las khams dkar dmar 'dzag pa med cing 'pho med du bcings pa kho na las stong gzugs kyi gzugs sku dang mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde stong dbyer med chos sku gnyis ngo bo dbyer med du sbyor ba'i zung 'jug mngon du byed pa ni sems 'grel skor gyis rgyud rnams kyi dgongs pa 'grel tshul yin pas lam gyi bgrod tshul 'di la brten nas mchog sgrub par 'dod pa rnams kyis khams byang chub kyi sems la gces spras su bya dgos te/

To summarize: the red and white drops explained above are indispensable causes for the creation of a womb-born body. From beginningless time the imprints of the emission of the red and white elements have been planted again and again, and it is by these imprints of emission alone that the wandering in samsara continues. By meditative familiarization with the vajra yoga of penetrative focusing on the channels and winds of the vajra body, the red and white elements do not fall, and their movement is restrained. This alone will bring about the actualization of the indivisible union of the form body of empty form and the dharmakāya of supreme and unchanging bliss[60] inseparable from emptiness. This is how the Three Bodhisattva Commentaries explain the tantra. Therefore those who wish for the supreme siddhi by following this particular path of practice should value the bodhicitta elements.

d.div: [60] The highest form of bliss, actualized on the sixth yoga of the completion stage.

f.d:
khams le'i mdor bsdus dang po las/
shes rab 'grogs las gang gi dkar po zag / de yi bde ba ci yis 'phel bar 'gyur/ / dpyid dang 'grogs la me tog ma rgyas pa/ / lhung na tsu ta'i 'bras bu gang gis 'byung /[37] / zhes dang /
ji ltar lo yi 'tshams su rgya lam na/ / ri dwags zas can 'khrig pa'i bde ba tshol/ / rdo yi phye ma dag gi kha zas can/ / phug ron rnams ni rtag tu byed pa ste/ / lan cig rtag tu khu ba ltung ba'i phyir/ / gnyi ga la yang mchog gi bde ba med/ / de bzhin dka' thub can dang 'dod ldan yang / / rmi lam sad pa dag la 'dzag phyir ro/ / ji ltar gnyid log la yang sbrul gyi ni/ / sos btab mi 'tsho de bzhin dka' thub pa/ khu ba sdud pa med phyir stobs med ma'i/ / skye gnas de yis nyams par byas pa'o/[38] / zhes sogs mang du gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

In the first summary from the Realms chapter of the Great Commentary it says:
Those whose white fluid falls during their companionship with wisdom,[61] by what will their bliss increase?[62] And:
Occasionally, at the appropriate time of year, the deer-eating lion seeks the bliss of mating, while the gravel-eating pigeon does so constantly. Because their fluid falls once or many times, neither finds supreme bliss. Similarly the ascetic and the lustful lose their fluid in dreams and while awake. Bitten by a snake while asleep, one will not live; Similarly the ascetic weakened by not keeping his fluid is ruined by a woman’s womb.[63]

d.div: [37] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 4_ba1
[38] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 4_ba3
[61] Prajñā: consort or women generally.
[62] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 4b1.
[63] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 4b3.

f.d: gnyis pa rtsa rnams kyi nang nas rlung rnams kyi rgyu tshul bshad pa

d.i: How the winds move within the channels

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ 'khor lo bzhi'i rtsa 'dab rnams la rlung rgyu ba'i tshul dang / sna bug la rlung rnams kyi 'pho tshul lo/ /
This is dealt with under two headings 1. The flow of wind through the petals of the four cakras 2. Movement of wind through the nostrils
dang po ['khor lo bzhi'i rtsa 'dab rnams la rlung rgyu ba'i tshul ]ni
The flow of wind through the petals of the four cakras

nang le'i re gnyisapa'i 'grel chen las/
mngal nas skyes pa rnams kyis bzung ba'i zla ba ni chu srin no/ / de nas bdun pa ni srog skye ba'i zla ba ste karka Ta'o/[39] / zhes gsungs pa'i don ni mngal skyes thams cad chu srin gyi zla ba mtshan nyid pa kho na la mngal 'dzin pa yin na ha cang thal bas mngal skyes kyi ming mngal bzung ba'i zla ba de zla ba gang yin yang chu srin gyi zla ba'i ming btags te/ mngal bzung ba de nas bgrangs pa'i zla ba bdun pa de la yang de yang karka Ta'i zla ba'i ming btags pa'i sgo nas chu srin gyi zla ba ba'i ming btags pa mngal bzung ba'i zla ba de nas bgrangs pa'i zla ba bdun pa karka Ta'i ming can gyi zla ba la srog gi rlung thog mar skye'o/ /

The Great Commentary says on the sixty-second verse of the Inner chapter:
For those born from a womb, the month of conception is Capricorn. From there the seventh, the month of Cancer, is the month of the creation of the life-sustaining wind.[64] If this quote meant that every womb birth was conceived only in the actual month of Capricorn,[65] the consequences would be absurd. /154/ It means that whatever the month of conception, it is to be known as the month of Capricorn, and that the seventh month on from conception is known as the month of Cancer. In this way the passage means that seven months on from the month of conception, labeled Capricorn, in the month labeled Cancer, the first life-sustaining wind is formed.

d.div: [39] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 143_ba6
[64] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 143b6.
[65] The month of the sun’s occupation of Capricorn.

f.d: rlung skyes pa de nas ji srid mngal na gnas kyi bar la rtsa dbu mar rlung dbyug pa'i rnam pa ltar 'byung 'jug mi byed par gnas pa las phyis mngal nas btsas ma thag pa'i tshe dang po'i rtsa dbu ma las rlung nga drug rkang bcas rgyu'o/ / de nas g.yas g.yon gang rung gi khyim gyi rtsa rnams la rgyu bar byed do/ /

From that time onward, and for as long as the being remains in the womb, the wind stays within the central channel as rigid as a stick, without moving through exhalation and inhalation. However, immediately after birth, fifty-six and a quarter winds flow from the central channel. From then on wind moves through either the left or right zodiac channels.

de yang mngal nas skyes pa rnams kyi mngal bzung ba'i zla ba ni chu srin no/ /zhes sogs kyi don la chu srin gyi zla ba zhes pa ma'i nang gi chu srin gyi khyim gyi rtsa la rlung rgyu bo chu srin gyi zla bar byas nas de'i dus su mngal skyes rnams kyis mngal bzung ba la byed pa ni mi 'thad de/ de ltar yin na ma'i chu srin gyi khyim gyi rtsa nas bgrangs pa'i bdun pa ma'i karka Ta'i khyim gyi rtsa nas rlung rgyu ba'i tshe mngal du zhugs pa'i sems can de la rlung skye dgos la/ de lta yin na mngal du zhugs pa'i zhag ngo de nyid la rlung skye dgos par 'gyur la/ de ni mi 'thad do/ / mngal du zhugs pa'i zhag ngo re la rlung gi rten rtsa la sogs pa'ang chags pa'i gzhi ma tsam yang med pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na chu srin gyi zla ba dang karka Ta'i zla ba zhes pa yang phyi'i zla ba la byed dgos so/ /

It is incorrect to understand the above line “For those born from a womb, the month of conception is Capricorn” as referring to the time of the flow of wind within the mother’s Capricorn channel, and that conception for womb-born beings will always occur at that time. If that were the case, it would have to mean that the time when wind flows through the mother’s Cancer channel, which is the seventh channel on from the channel of Capricorn, would be the time of the formation of the life-sustaining wind of the being in the womb. It would then follow that this wind would be created on the very day that the being entered the womb, and this cannot be so, because on the day of entering the womb not even the beginnings of the channels that carry the winds are present. Therefore “month of Capricorn” and “month of Cancer” must refer to external months.

phyi'i zla ba la byed pa la yang mi mngal skyes gang zhig chu srin gyi zla ba mtshan nyid pa la mngal du zhugs pa'i gang zag cig gi dbang du byas nas/ mngal nas skyes pa rnams kyi zhes gsungs pa yin gyi/ mi mngal skyes thams cad kyi dbang du byas pa min zhes gsungs yang / nang le'i so brgyad pa'i 'grel chen las/
de yang dus sbyor karka Ta nas mi'i dbang po zhes pa phyi rol du nyi ma'i skye ba'i khyim ni karka Ta'o/ /de bzhin du skyes pa thams cad kyi dus sbyor gang du skyes par gyur pa'i khyim de ni karka Ta'i ming can du rig par bya ste srog skye ba'i gnas su 'gyur ro/[40] / zhes pa'i rigs pas te/ zhes gsungs pa'i skyes pa thams cad ces pa 'dis mi mngal skyes thams cad 'dzin pa yin pa'i phyir na gong du bshad pa ltar 'thad do/ /

Some have said that as well as referring to an external month, the quote beginning “For those born from womb, the month of conception is Capricorn” is made on the basis of those womb-born human beings conceived in the actual month of Capricorn and does not refer to every womb-born human. However the Great Commentary says on the thirty-eighth verse of the Inner chapter:
“Lord of men, from the lagna[66] of Cancer” refers to the fact that in the external world, the birthplace of the sun was the house of Cancer. Similarly, in whatever lagna every birth takes place, that house is known by the name of Cancer and is the birthplace of the life-sustaining wind.[67] “Every birth” includes every womb-born human, and so the previous explanation is correct. /155/

d.div: [40] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 131_ba3_'gyur cung mi mthun/
[66] Although lagna often refers to the ascending sign of the zodiac, here it refers to months that correlate to the sun’s occupation of the twelve houses or signs.
[67] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 131b3.

f.d: de ltar nges par byas nas mngal nas btsas ma thag pa'i tshe rlung 'byung 'jug khug pa re dbugs re re byas pa'i lnga bcu rtsa drug rkang bcas dbu mar rgyus te sna bug tu mnyam rgyu byas nas de'i rjes de ma thag tu g.yon gyi lug gi khyim mam lug gi dus sbyor gyi rtsa la nam mkha'i dkyil 'khor gyi rlung rgyu ba nas mthar g.yas kyi nya'i dus sbyor gyi rtsa la sa'i dkyil 'khor gyi rlung rgyus zin pa'i bar la nya ni zhag gcig dang rlung nyi khri chig stong drug brgya rgyus zin dus mnyam du 'ong ngo / / de yang khyim mam dus sbyor gyi rtsa rnams ni lte ba'i bar skor gyi rtsa 'dab bcu gnyis te/ de yang lus kyi mdun shar dang / g.yon byang dang / g.yas lho dang / rgyab nub tu bshad cing / phyogs bzhi'i chos gzhan rnams grangs bgrang ba'i tshe yang shar dang por byas nas bgrang ba bzhin du 'dir yang shar mdun gyi phyogs nas bgrang bar bya ba yin la/ de ltar byas pa na lus kyi g.yon phyogs kyi mdun gyi rtsa 'dab dang po lug gi khyim dang / de nas rim pa bzhin gnyis pa 'khrig pa dang / gsum pa seng ge dang / bzhi pa srang dang / lnga pa gzhu dang / g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab drug pa bum pa'i khyim mam dus sbyor min pa'i bar ro/ / de bzhin du g.yas phyogs kyi mdun gyi rtsa 'dab dang po glang gi khyim dang / de nas rim pa bzhin gnyis pa karka Ta dang / gsum pa bu mo dang / bzhi pa sdig pa dang / lnga pa chu srin dang / g.yas kyi rgyab phyogs kyi rtsa 'dab drug pa nya'i khyim mam dus sbyor yin pa'i bar du yin no/ /

Having established this, as soon as a being emerges from the womb, fifty-six and a quarter breaths of wind move through the central channel and flow equally through both nostrils. Each unit of breath is one exhalation and one inhalation. Immediately afterward, the space mandala wind flows through the Aries channel, or Aries lagna channel, on the left. This process continues until finally the earth mandala wind flows through the Pisces lagna channel on the right, at which time 21,600 winds will have flowed and one day will have passed. The house, or lagna, channels are explained as follows. The intermediate circle of the navel cakra has twelve channel petals. Those at the front of the body are in the east. Those on the left are in the north, those on the right in the south, and those at the back in the west. In the same way that other phenomena of the four directions are enumerated by beginning with the east, here too they are counted from east at the front of the body. Therefore the first channel petal at the front left of the body is the house of Aries. Moving counterclockwise around the body, the second is Gemini, third Leo, fourth Libra, fifth Sagittarius, and the house of Aquarius is the sixth channel petal of the left. Likewise the first channel petal at the front of the body on its right is the house of Taurus. The second is Cancer, the third Virgo, the fourth Scorpio, the fifth Capricorn, and the sixth channel petal at the back on the right is the house of Pisces.

de ltar shes par byas nas de rnams la rlung rgyu ba'i tshul ni/ btsas ma thag gi tshe dbu ma nas rlung nga drug rkang bcas rgyus pa'i rjes su g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab dang po lug gi khyim la nam mkha'i rlung dbugs 'byung 'jug khug pa re la grangs re rer byas pa'i dbugs nga drug rkang bcas kyi dman pa'i stong brgyad brgya rgyu zhing / de nas ye shes kyi rlung nga drug rkang bcas g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab dang po lug khyim gyi rtsa 'dab nas g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab dang po glang khyim gyi rtsa 'dab tu 'pho ba'i 'pho 'tshams su dbu ma nas rgyu'o/ /

Having established these channels, the movement of wind through them can be explained. Immediately after birth, fifty-six and a quarter winds[68] flow from the central channel. After that, 1,800 breaths of the space-mandala wind, less fifty-six and a quarter, each breath consisting of one unit of inhalation and exhalation, flow through the Aries channel petal, the first petal of the left. Then fifty-six and a quarter of gnosis-mandala winds flow from the central channel at the point of the changeover of wind movement from the Aries channel petal, the first petal of the left, to the Taurus channel petal, the first petal of the right.

d.div: [68] Here wind (rlung) is best thought of as “inner breath.” Any enumeration, therefore, is not of types of wind but of the number of inner breaths.

f.d: de'i rjes su g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab dang po glang khyim gyi rtsa 'dab nas dbugs nga drug rkang bcas kyis dman pa'i stong brgyad brgya rgyu zhing / dpe de ji lta ba de bzhin du khyim gyi rtsa 'dab rnams kyi 'pho 'tshams rnams su ye shes kyi rlung nga drug rkang bcas re dbu ma nas rgyu ba dang / g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab dang po glang khyim nas sa rlung rgyu ba'i rjes su g.yon gyi gnyis pa nas rlung gi rlung dang / de'i rjes su g.yas kyi gnyis pa nas chu'i rlung dang / de nas g.yon gyi gsum pa nas me'i rlung dang / de nas g.yas kyi gsum pa nas kyang me'i rlung dang / de nas g.yon gyi bzhi pa nas chu'i rlung dang / de nas g.yas kyi bzhi pa nas rlung gi rlung dang / de nas g.yon gyi lnga pa nas sa'i rlung dang / de nas g.yas kyi lnga pa nas nam mkha'i rlung dang / de nas g.yon gyi drug pa nas kyang nam mkha'i rlung dang / de nas g.yas kyi drug pa nya'i khyim gyi rtsa 'dab nas sa'i rlung stong brgyad brgya las nga drug rkang bcas kyis dman pa rgyu'o/ /

After that, 1,800 breaths minus fifty-six and a quarter flow from the house of the Taurus petal, the first petal of the right. Similarly, at the times of the other house channel petals’ changeover of wind movement, fifty-six and a quarter gnosis winds will flow from the central channel. /156/ After earth wind has flowed from the Taurus petal, the first channel petal of the right, the air-mandala wind flows from the second petal of the left. After that the water-mandala wind flows from the second petal of the right, followed by the fire-mandala wind from the third on the left. The fire wind also flows from the third on the right, the water-mandala wind from the fourth on the left, the air-mandala wind from the fourth on the right, the earth-mandala wind from the fifth on the left, the space-mandala wind from the fifth on the right, the space wind also from the sixth on the left, and, finally, 1,800 breaths less fifty-six and a quarter of the earth-mandala wind flow from the house of Pisces, the sixth petal on the right.

de ltar na khyim bcu gnyis kyi rtsa 'dab 'pho chen bcu gnyis kyi rtsa re re la nam mkha'i rlung la sogs pa dkyil 'khor lnga'i rlung stong brgyad brgya la nga drug rkang bcas kyis dman pa stong bdun brgya dang zhe gsum rkang pa gsum dang bcas pa rgyun re la rgyu zhing 'pho 'tshams bcu gnyis su nga drug rkang bcas re dbu ma nas rgyus pas rlung drug brgya dang don lnga re nyin zhag re la dbu ma nas rgyu'o/ / 'pho chen bcu gnyis po re re la stong bdun brgya dang zhe gsum rkang pa gsum dang bcas pa rnams rgyus pa bsdoms pas nyi khri dgu brgya nyer lnga 'ong ba 'pho 'tshams su dbu mar rgyus pa'i drug brgya don lnga po dang bsres pas dbugs nyi khri chig stong drug brgya 'ong ste/ lte ba'i 'pho chen bcu gnyis kyi nyin zhag gcig gi rlung gi rgyu tshul lo/ /

In this way, in each of the channel petals of the twelve houses where these twelve major wind movements[69] occur, 1,800 winds of the five mandalas of space and so forth, less fifty-six and a quarter winds, to make 1,743 3/4 breaths, flow within each period. Also, at the changeover point of each of the twelve wind movements, fifty-six and a quarter winds flow from the central channel, making a total of 675 winds flowing from the central channel each day. 1,743 3/4 breaths in each of the twelve major movements totals 20,925. To this is added the 675 winds, making a total of 21,600 breaths. This is the way the wind moves in one solar day of twelve wind movements at the navel cakra.

d.div: [69] A wind movement refers to the duration of wind flow in each of the twelve petals, and to the changeover period when the winds move to a new petal, which occurs about every two hours. These changeovers correspond to a new sign or house appearing on the horizon every two hours, hence the term lagna.

f.d: de nas nyin zhag gnyis pa'i thog mar g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab dang po lug gi 'pho ba'i rtsa la rlung gi rlung dang / de nas g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab dang po glang gi 'pho ba'i rtsa la chu'i rlung dang / de bzhin du g.yon gyi gnyis pa nas drug pa'i bar la rim pa bzhin me'i rlung / chu'i rlung / sa'i rlung / nam mkha'i rlung / rlung gi rlung rgyu ba dang / de bzhin du g.yas kyi'ang gnyis pa nas drug pa'i bar la rim pa bzhin me'i rlung/ rlung gi rlung / nam mkha'i rlung / sa'i rlung / chu'i rlung rgyu ste nyin zhag gnyis pa'i rlung gi rgyu tshul lo/ /

At the beginning of the second solar day, air-mandala wind flows in the first channel petal on the left, which is the Aries wind-movement channel. Then in the first petal on the right, water-mandala wind flows in the Taurus channel. Similarly, from the second on the left to the sixth on the left, fire-mandala wind, water-mandala wind, earth-mandala wind, space-mandala wind, and air-mandala wind flow, respectively. Similarly, from the second on the right to the sixth on the right, fire-mandala wind, air-mandala wind, space-mandala wind, earth-mandala wind, and water-mandala wind flow, respectively. This is how the wind moves on the second day.

de nas nyin zhag gsum pa'i thog mar g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab dang po la me'i rlung / de bzhin du gnyis pa nas drug pa'i bar la rim pa bzhin chu'i rlung / sa'i rlung / nam mkha'i rlung / rlung gi rlung / me'i rlung rgyu ba dang / g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab dang po la me'i rlung rgyus pa'i rjes su g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab dang po la me'i rlung / gnyis pa la rlung gi rlung / gsum pa la nam mkha'i rlung / bzhi pa la sa'i rlung / lnga pa la chu'i rlung / drug pa la me'i rlung rgyu ba ste nyin zhag gsum pa'i rlung gi rgyu tshul lo/ /

At the beginning of the third day, fire-mandala wind flows in the first channel petal on the left. Similarly, from the second petal to the sixth, water-mandala wind, earth-mandala wind, space-mandala wind, air-mandala wind, and fire-mandala wind flow, respectively. /157/ After fire-mandala wind flows in the first petal of the left, fire-mandala wind flows in the first channel petal of the right, air-mandala wind in the second, space-mandala wind in the third, earth-mandala wind in the fourth, water-mandala wind in the fifth, and fire-mandala wind in the sixth petal. This is how the winds move on the third day.

de nas nyin zhag bzhi pa'i thog mar g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab dang po la chu'i rlung/ de'i rjes su g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab dang po la rlung gi rlung / de bzhin du g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab gnyis pa la sa'i rlung / gsum pa la nam mkha'i rlung / bzhi pa la rlung gi rlung / lnga pa me'i rlung / drug pa la chu'i rlung rgyu ba dang / de bzhin du g.yas kyi'ang gnyis pa la nam mkha'i rlung / gsum pa la sa'i rlung / bzhi pa la chu'i rlung / lnga pa la me'i rlung / drug pa la rlung gi rlung rgyu ba ste nyin zhag bzhi pa'i rlung gi rgyu tshul lo/ /

At the beginning of the fourth day, water-mandala wind flows in the first channel petal on the left. After that air-mandala wind flows in the first petal on the right. In the same way earth-mandala wind flows in the second petal on the left, space-mandala wind in the third, air-mandala wind in the fourth, fire-mandala wind in the fifth, and water-mandala wind in the sixth. Similarly, on the right, space-mandala wind flows through the second, earth-mandala air through the third, water-mandala wind through the fourth, fire-mandala wind through the fifth, and air-mandala wind through the sixth. This is how the winds flow on the fourth day.

de nas nyin zhag lnga pa'i thog mar g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab dang po la sa'i rlung / de'i rjes su g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab dang po la nam mkha'i rlung / de bzhin du g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab gnyis pa la nam mkha'i rlung / gsum pa la rlung gi rlung / bzhi pa la me'i rlung / lnga pa la chu'i rlung / drug pa la sa'i rlung rgyu ba dang / de bzhin du g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab gnyis pa la sa'i rlung / gsum pa la chu'i rlung / bzhi pa la me'i rlung / lnga pa la rlung gi rlung / drug pa la nam mkha'i rlung rgyu ba ste/ nyin zhag lnga pa'i rlung gi rgyu tshul lo/ /

At the beginning of the fifth day, earth-mandala wind flows through the first channel petal on the left. After that space-mandala wind moves through the first petal on the right. Similarly space-mandala wind moves through the second petal on the left, air-mandala wind through the third, fire-mandala wind through the fourth, water-mandala wind through the fifth, and earth-mandala wind through the sixth. Likewise earth-mandala wind moves through the second petal on the right, water-mandala wind through the third, fire-mandala wind through the fourth, air-mandala wind through the fifth, and space-mandala wind through the sixth on the right. This is the movement of the winds on the fifth day.

de nas yang nyin zhag drug pa'i thog mar g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab dang po la nam mkha'i rlung rgyu ba dang / g.yas kyi'ang rtsa 'dab dang po la sa'i rlung rgyu ba sogs nyin zhag lnga lnga la snga 'khor bzhin du 'khor nas rgyu ba yin te/

At the beginning of the sixth day, space-wind moves through the first channel petal on the left, and earth wind moves through the first channel petal of the right, as on the first day. The process is repeated every five days, with the winds flowing and circulating as before. The process has to be this way.

nang le'i re lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
lug la sogs pa'i mi mnyam pa'i 'dab ma drug po rnams la stong pa'i dkyil 'khor rab tu 'bab pa srog gi rlung gis 'dor ro/ / g.yas pa la rgyu ba'i nyin zhag drug dang / 'pho ba'i nyin zhag drug rnams kyis glang la sogs pa'i mnyam pa'i dus spyod drug po rnams la sa'i dkyil 'khor gyi rab tu 'bab pa srog gis 'dor ro/[41] / zhes sogs kyis rtsa 'dab bcu gnyis po re re la yang nam mkha'i rlung sogs dkyil 'khor lnga char gyi rlung rgyu ba yod par gsungs shing / de yang rtsa 'dab re re la dkyil 'khor lnga char gyi rgyu tshul sngar bshad pa ltar byed dgos pa'i phyir dang /

The Great Commentary says on the sixty-fifth verse of the Inner chapter:
In the six uneven petals of Aries and so forth, the emptiness[70] mandala flows, expelled by wind. In the right there are six days of flow, and with six days of changeover, the earth mandala flows in the even houses of Taurus and so forth expelled by the life wind.[71] This says that the winds of the five mandalas of space and so forth flow within each of the twelve channel petals, and the way that each of the five mandalas flows through the petals has to be as explained above. /158/

d.div: [41] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 147_ba4
[70] Space mandala.
[71] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 147b7.

f.d: g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab dang po la nam mkha'i rlung rgyus pa nas g.yon pa'i rtsa 'dab drug pa la yang nam mkha'i rlung rgyus pa'i rjes su slar yang g.yon pa'i rtsa la rlung rgyu ba na rtsa 'dab dang po la rgyu ba dang / rlung yang nam mkha'i rlung gi rjes su rlung gi rlung rgyu bar byed dgos pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na g.yon dang g.yas kyi 'pho chen gyi rlung rgyu ba'i tshe gong du bshad pa bzhin phan tshun spel nas rgyu ba yin no/ /

Furthermore, when the space-mandala wind has flowed through the first channel petal on the left, it will again flow through the sixth channel petal on the left. After that, when winds flow again through the left channels, they begin from the first petal on the left, and that wind will be the air-mandala wind, which comes after the space-mandala wind. In this way, the left and right major changeovers in the flow of the winds must occur, as previously explained, alternately left and right.

khyim gyi rtsa re rer rlung rgyu ba'i tshe na'ang rtsa sbubs la phyogs bzhi dbus dang cha lngar phye ba'i dbus mar 'byung ba chung ba'i nam mkha'i dkyil 'khor dang / shar du rlung gi dang / lhor me'i dang / byang du chu'i dang / nub tu sa'i dkyil 'khor 'bab ste re re la dbugs sum brgya drug cu'i steng nas bcu gcig rkang bcas res dman pa yod do/ /

When wind flows through each of the house channels, the channel tubes are divided into five sections — four in the four directions and one in the center. The minor-element space mandala flows through the center, the air mandala through the east, the fire mandala through the south, the water mandala through the north, and the earth mandala through the west. For each of these there are 360 breaths less eleven and a quarter.[72]

d.div: [72] One fifth of 1,800 minus one fifth of 56 ¼.

f.d: 'byung ba chung ba'i dkyil 'khor ni nyer lnga yod do/ / nam mkha'i nam mkha'/ nam mkha'i rlung / nam mkha'i me/ nam mkha'i chu/ nam mkha'i sa'i dkyil 'khor dang / de bzhin du rlung gi nam mkha'/ rlung gi rlung/ rlung gi me/ rlung gi chu/ rlung gi sa'i dkyil 'khor dang / de bzhin du me'i nam mkha' nas me'i sa'i bar lnga dang / chu'i nam mkha' nas chu'i sa'i bar lnga dang / sa'i nam mkha' nas sa'i sa'i dkyil 'khor gyi bar lnga ste nyer lnga'o/ /

There are twenty-five mandalas of the minor elements. They are the space mandala of space, the air mandala of space, the fire mandala of space, the water mandala of space, and the earth mandala of space; the space, air, fire, water, and earth mandalas of air; the five mandalas from the space mandala of fire to the earth mandala of fire; the five from the space mandala of water to the earth mandala of water; and the five from the space mandala of earth to the earth mandala of earth. This makes twenty-five.

de yang 'byung ba chung ba'i dkyil 'khor lnga rgyu ba'i tshul ni 'pho chen gyi rtsa 'dab bcu gnyis po gang dang gang la 'byung ba che ba'i rlung gang rgyu ba de la 'byung ba chung ba lngar phye ba rnams rgyu ba ste/ de ltar rgyu ba yang lnga po rim can kho nar rgyu'o/ / de yang dper mtshon na g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab dang po la 'byung ba che ba'i nam mkha'i dkyil 'khor rgyu ba'i tshe nam mkha'i nam mkha' nas nam mkha'i sa'i bar lnga rgyu ba dang / g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab dang po la 'byung ba che ba'i sa'i dkyil 'khor rgyu ba'i tshe sa'i sa nas sa'i nam mkha'i bar lnga rgyu ba lta bu yin no/ /

The flow of the five mandalas of the minor elements is as follows. Whatever wind of the major elements is flowing in the one of the major wind movements of the twelve channel petals, the five minor elements also flow in that wind. Such a flow, moreover, is strictly ordered. To illustrate this, when the mandala of the major element of space flows through the first channel petal of the left, the minor mandalas from the space mandala of space to the earth mandala of space also flow. When the mandala of the major element of earth flows through the first channel petal on the right, the mandalas from the earth mandala of earth to the space mandala of earth also flow.

de rnams byang rim can du rgyu tshul ni g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab rnams la rgyu ba'i tshe 'byung ba chung ba rnams kyang nam mkha' rlung me chu sa'i rim pas rgyu ba dang / de bzhin du g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab rnams la rlung rgyu ba'i tshe sa chu me rlung nam mkha'i rim pas rgyu'o/ /

The order in which they flow is as follows. When flowing through the left channel petals, the minor elements also flow in the order of space, air, fire, water, and earth. Similarly, when wind flows through the right channel petals, they flow in the order earth, water, fire, air, and space. /159/

de ltar na 'pho chen gyi rtsa 'dab g.yon nas g.yas su rlung 'pho ba'i tshe 'byung chung gi sa nas sar 'pho ba dang / g.yas nas g.yon du 'pho ba'i tshe 'byung chung gi nam mkha' nas nam mkhar 'pho ba ni nges pa can yin no/ /

In this way, when the major wind movements change from the left to the right, the minor elements move from earth to earth,[73] and when moving from right to left, from space to space. This movement is fixed.

d.div: [73] This is because the minor element of the sixth channel on the left is earth, which is a repeat of the fifth channel element, and the minor element of the first channel on the right is also earth.

f.d: yang 'pho chen gyi rtsa 'dab bcu gnyis po re re la 'pho chung gi rtsa 'dab lnga lngar gyis pa'i rtsa 'dab rnams la rlung rgyu tshul ni 'pho chen gyi rtsa sbubs rnams la shar nub sogs cha lnga lngar phye ba'i cha rnams su 'byung chung gi nam mkha' rlung me chu sa rgyus pa rnams 'pho chung gi rtsa 'dab lnga shar nub lho byang dbus ma dang bcas par gnas pa rnams su yang shar nub sogs 'pho chen gyi ji lta ba bzhin rgyu zhing 'pho chung gi rtsa 'dab re re yang dbugs sum brgya drug cu la bcu gcig rkang bcas kyis dman pa sum brgya zhe brgyad rkang pa gsum dang bcas pa re rgyu'o/ /

Each of the twelve channel petals of the major wind movements splits up into five petals of these five minor wind movements. The channel tubes of the major wind movements are divided east, west, south, north, and center, and the space, air, fire, water, and earth minor elements flow along these five directions. The five channel petals of the minor elements are also arranged east, west, south, north, and center, and the flow of winds within them mirrors the directional flow of the major wind elements. In each petal of minor wind movement, the flow is 360 breaths minus eleven and a quarter, or 348 3/4.

de ltar lte ba'i rtsa 'dab rnams la rgyus te de nas snying ga'i rtsa 'dab rnams la rgyu ba'i tshul ni nang le'i zhe gcig pa'i 'grel chen las/
snying ga'i chu skyes rtsibs brgyad pa 'di la thun tshod 'pho ba'i rtsa rnams rig par bya ste sna'i bug par dkyil 'khor lnga 'bab par byed pa ni 'di rnams su 'gyur ro/ / rtsa dang rtsa yi dbugs 'byung ba dang 'jug pa brgya phrag nyi shu rtsa bdun gyis srog yang dag par rgyu bar 'gyur te dbyug gu phyed dang bcas pa'i bdun gyis so/[42] / zhes snying ga'i rtsa 'dab re re la dbugs nyi khri chig stong drug brgya la brgyad kyis bgos pa'i rnyed nor dbugs nyis stong bdun brgya dang / de chu tshod du byas na chu tshod phyed dang brgyad rgyu bar gsungs pa ni nyin zhag re la dbugs drug brgya don lnga re dbu ma la rgyus pa logs su ma phye ba'i dbang du byas pa yin la/ gnas tshod la ni lte ba'i 'pho chen bcu gnyis kyi 'pho 'tshams nas dbugs nga drug rkang bcas re dbu ma nas rgyu bar bshad pa de dag ni lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbu ma nas dbu ma'i yar sna'i bar dbu ma nyid nas rgyu bas snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral pa'i rtsa 'dab rnams la mi rgyu bar nges pa yin no/ /

This is how winds flow within the petals of the navel. The flow in the channel petals of the heart is mentioned in the Great Commentary on the forty-first verse of the Inner chapter:
It should be known that within the eight petals of the lotus of the heart are channels of periodic wind movement. The five mandalas flow to the nostrils from these channels. The winds flow because of the channels, and the inhalations and exhalations of each channel number 2,700, or seven and a half hours.[74] This quote says that in each of the eight petals of the heart, 21,600 divided by eight, or 2,700, breaths flow. This in hours comes to seven and a half.[75] This quote is made on the basis of not excluding the 675 breaths that flow in one day through the central channel. The actual measurement is explained as follows. At the changeover times of the twelve major wind movements of the navel channel, fifty-six and a quarter breaths flow from the central channel. These breaths flow in the central channel from the navel cakra to the upper opening of the central channel. Therefore they do not flow into the channel petals of the heart, the throat, and the forehead.

d.div: [42] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 133_na1
[74] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 133a1.
[75] 360 breaths = 1 hour. See appendix 3.

f.d: de ltar na dbugs nyi khri chig stong drug brgya la drug brgya dang don lngas dman pa'i lhag nyi khri dgu brgya dang nyer lnga la brgyad kyis bgos pa'i thob nor dbugs nyis stong drug brgya dang bco lnga dbugs kyi brgyad cha lnga re rnams snying ga'i rtsa 'dab re re la nyin zhag re la rgyu ba yin no/ / de yang rgyun re la rgyu ba ni ma yin te/

21,600 breaths less 675 leaves 20,925 breaths. This divided by eight comes to 2,615 5/8, and this is the actual number of breaths that flow within each petal of the heart cakra each day. This is not the amount of wind that flows during each period of flow. /160/

rgyun re la rgyu ba'i dbang du byas na lte ba'i 'pho chen gyi rtsa 'dab re la rgyun ji tsam zhig rgyus pa de nyid snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral ba'i rtsa 'dab re re la yang rgyun re la rgyu dgos te/ lte ba'i g.yon gyi 'pho chen gyi rtsa 'dab gcig la dbugs stong brgyad brgya la nga drug rkang bcas kyis dman pa rgyus pa de nyid sna bug gi'ang sna g.yon pa la rgyus te de nas lte ba'i rtsa 'dab g.yas la 'pho nas g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab gcig nas dbugs stong brgyad brgya la nga drug rkang bcas kyis dman pa rgyu ba dang dus mnyam du sna bug gi rgyu ba yang g.yon nas g.yas su 'phos te grangs de dang mtshungs pa de rgyu ba yin la/ de bzhin du snying ga mgrin pa dpral ba rnams kyi rtsa 'dab g.yon dang g.yas la yang dbugs rgyu thengs re la lte ba'i 'pho chen re dang sna bug la rgyun re la ji tsam re rgyu ba mnyam par bya dgos pas so/ /

On the basis of the flow within each period, whatever quantity of wind flows during the period of each major wind movement at the navel, that much has to flow at each period within the petals of the heart, throat, and forehead. This is because, in one major wind movement on the left at the navel, 1,800 breaths minus fifty-six and a quarter will flow. That amount of wind will also flow through the left nostril. Moving to the right, 1,800 breaths minus fifty-six and a quarter will flow from one channel petal on the right. At the same time, the flow moves from the left nostril to the right, and a similar number of breaths will flow. Likewise, during each period of flow, the number of breaths at the left and right channel petals of the heart, throat, and forehead must be the same as the flow at the nostrils and at each of the wind movements at the navel-channel petals.
