[9] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 262a3.

f.d: gnyis pa bla mar bsten du mi rung ba'i mtshan nyid bshad pa ni

d.i: Characteristics of those unsuitable to be gurus

f.d:
dbang le'i gsum pa las/
nga rgyal dang ldan khro bas zil mnan dam tshig rnams bral rdzas la brkam zhing thos pa dag kyang med/ / slob ma rnams ni slu ba don du gnyer zhing mchog gi bde ba'i gnas las sems nyams dbang ma bskur/ / longs spyod dag la kun chags bag med rtsub mo'i tshig dang bcas shing dbang po'i don du 'dod ldan pa/ / de nyid dmyal ba bzhin du slob ma mkhas pa rnams kyis rdzogs pa'i byang chub rgyur ni spang bar bya/[7] / zhes gsungs pa'i skyon rnams dang ldan pa'i gang zag ni rdo rje theg pa'i bla mar bsten du mi rung ste/ de 'dra ba bla mar bsten nas dbang bskur zhu ba sogs byas kyang dbang thob pa'i go mi chod cing / de'i skyon gyi cha shas kyis gos nas 'di phyi'i gong ma'i khyad par las nyams par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ /

The third verse of the Initiations chapter says:
Proud, ruled by anger, and lacking vows, greedy, without knowledge, working to deceive disciples, a mind that has fallen from great bliss, without initiation, totally attached to wealth, unaware, of harsh and coarse words, filled with carnal desire, the wise disciples should abandon taking such people as causes of complete enlightenment as they would abandon hell.[10] People with such faults are not fit to be relied upon as gurus in the Vajra Vehicle. Even if one takes such a person as a guru and requests initiations and so forth, there can be no meaningful receiving of the initiation. Moreover one will become infected by a measure of his faults and fall from all elevated status in this and future lives.

d.div: [7] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka3_58_na4
[10] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 3, 58a4.

f.d: de yang rgyud tshig de rnams kyi phal mo che go sla la|_de'i thos pa dag kyang med ces pa ni dam pa'i lam sbyor ba yan lag drug lta bu'i man ngag dang bral ba'o/ / slob ma rnams ni slu ba don du gnyer zhing zhes pa ni rdzun gyis slob ma'i mgo skor ba'o/ / mchog gi bde ba'i gnas las sems nyams dbang ma bskur/ zhes pa ni rang nyid kyis dbang bskur ma thob cing gzhan la rgyud 'chad pa'o/ / dbang po'i don du 'dod ldan pa zhes pa ni dbang po gnyis sprod kyi bde ba tsam don du gnyer ba dang ldan pa'o/ /

Most of the above verse is easy to understand. “Without knowledge” means to be without the essential teachings on the six-branched yoga, for example. “Working to deceive his disciple” means to delude disciples by telling lies. “A mind that has fallen from the great bliss, without initiation” means that without having received the initiation he is bestowing, he nevertheless teaches it to others. “Filled with carnal desire” means working only for the pleasure gained from the sexual union of the two organs.

de ltar slob dpon du bsten par 'os pa dang mi 'os pa'i mtshan nyid rnams shes par byas te bla mar rung mi rung legs par brtags nas bla ma bsten par bya dgos te/ dbang le'i gnyis pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir sngags kyi tshul la 'jig rten dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dngos grub 'dod pa'i slob ma rnams kyis dang por bla ma bsten par bya ste de yang rdo rje slob dpon yongs su brtag pa gsungs pa'i cho gas yang dag par yongs su brtags nas so/ / rnam pa gzhan du yongs su brtag pa'i mtshan nyid dang bral ba'i bla ma bsten pas slob ma rnams kyi chos phyin ci log tu 'gyur te chos phyin ci log pas dmyal bar 'gro bar 'gyur ro/[8] / zhes gsungs shing

Therefore the way to rely upon a guru is firstly to know the characteristics worthy and unworthy of devotion and then to examine thoroughly who is and who is not fit to be a guru. The Great Commentary says on the second verse of the Initiations chapter:
Disciples who wish to gain worldly and nonworldly powers by way of mantra should first devote themselves to a guru. Furthermore one should examine the vajra master thoroughly. One should thoroughly examine his words. Otherwise, relying upon a guru unexamined, the disciples’ dharma will be perverse, and perverse dharma will send them to hell.[11] /179/

d.div: [8] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 260_ba3
[11] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 260b3.

f.d:
don dam bsnyen pa las kyang / 'a
dod pa'i dngos grub slob dpon zhal gyi rjes 'brang bar/ / ma lus rdo rje theg par thams cad mkhyen pas gsungs/ / de phyir slob ma dam pa rnams kyis gser bzhin du/ / yongs su brtags na sdig pa cung zad yod ma yin/[9] / zhes pa la sogs pa mang du gsungs pas so/ /

Also the Paramārthasevā says:
He, omniscient in the complete Vajra Vehicle, has said that very wished-for siddhi follows the master. If perfect disciples examine the master, therefore, as they would gold, they will not accrue even the tiniest of faults.[12]

d.div: [9] sde dge_1348_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ nadapal don dam bsnyen pa/ sh+loka3_1_na4
[12] Toh 1348 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, v. 3, 1a4.

f.d:
'on te bla mar bsten du mi rung ba'i mtshan nyid de dag dang ldan pa'i gang zag bla mar gyur zin na ji ltar bya zhe na/ de ni 'grel chen las/
'dir sngags kyi tshul la bla ma gang zhig nga rgyal la sogs pa'i skyon dang bcas pa'i bla ma de ni bla mar byas kyang dmyal ba bzhin du slob ma mkhas pa ste shes ldan rnams kyis rdzogs pa'i byang chub rgyur ni spang bar bya'o [10] zhes dang /

However what should one do if one already regards as a guru someone endowed with those unworthy characteristics? The Great Commentary says:
In mantra, even though one has taken as a guru a person with the faults of pride and so forth, wise disciples, meaning those of intelligence, will abandon him as a cause of complete enlightenment as they would abandon hell.[13]

d.div: [10] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 261_na5
[13] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 261a5.

f.d:
yang 'grel chen las/
gsung 'di'i phyir bla mar byas kyang bya ba ma yin pa byed pa ni thar pa don du gnyer ba'i slob mas spang bar bya ba nyid do/[11] / zhes gsungs te/ de dag gi don ni gong du bshad pa'i skyon rnams dang gzhan yang 'grel chen du lung drangs pa las/
snying rje med cing khro la gdug/ khengs shing chags la ma gdams dang / / rang bstod bla mar slob ma ni/ / blo dang ldan pas mi bya'o/[12] / zhes pa'i skyon rnams dang ldan pa'i gang zag rang gi bla mar gyur zin na thar pa don gnyer gyi slob ma des de dang 'grogs pa spangs te phyis mi 'grogs par bya dgos pa yin no/ /

Also:
Because of these words, even though he has been taken as a guru, if he does these wrong deeds, disciples who strive for freedom should leave him.[14] A passage quoted in the Great Commentary says:
Without compassion, angry and malicious, arrogant, grasping, uncontrolled, and boastful, the intelligent disciple will not take such a one as guru.[15] Therefore, if one has taken someone with these faults as a guru, then the disciple who is seeking freedom should part company with him and not associate with him again.

[12] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 262_na1
[14] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 262a2.
[15] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 262a1.

f.d:
de yang 'grel tshig de dag gis de tsam zhig bstan pa yin gyi/ skyon mthong ba rgyu mtshan du byas nas ma dad par bya ba ston pa ni ma yin te/
de rgyu mtshan du byas nas phyin chad bla mar 'dzin pa dang bsnyen bkur ba'i zhing du 'dzin pa'i khur dor na rtsa ltung 'byung ba'i go skabs kyang yod pas spang blang bya ba'i spong tshul rnams dbye ba phyed dgos so/[13] / zhes gsungs pa ltar rigs pa yin no/

These quotes from the Great Commentary teach just this point and this point only. They do not teach that one should lose one’s faith due to seeing faults because, as it is so rightly said:
Once that is used as a reason and one casts off the undertaking of holding him as a guru and as a field of reverence, one opens up the opportunity for a root downfall to occur. One must learn, therefore, to distinguish what is to be developed from what is to be discarded.[16]

d.div: [13] 'di bla ma lnga bcu pa'i rnam bshad yin nges pa'i dpyad/
[16] Probably from a commentary to Fifty Verses on the Guru.

f.d: kha cig ni bla mar byas kyang zhes pa gong 'og gnyis kyi don gzhan gyis bla mar byas kyang zhes par 'chad par byed do/ /
Some explain the two instances of the phrase “taken as a guru” in the two Great Commentary passages above as applying to gurus taken by others.

'o na mtshan nyid de rnams dang ldan pa'i bla ma ma rnyed na ji ltar bya snyam na/ don dam bsnyen pa las/
rtsod ldan dbang gis bla ma skyon dang yon tan 'dres/ / rnam pa kun du sdig pa med pa yod ma yin/ / gang zhig yon tan lhag pa la'ang [14] ni legs dpyad nas/ / bu rnams kyis ni de la brten [15] par 'gyur ba'o/[16] / zhes gsungs pa ltar mtshan nyid yongs su rdzogs pa'i bla ma ma rnyed na yang yon tan shas che ba la brten par bya zhing / khyad par du dbang yongs su rdzogs pa thob cing sngags kyi sdom pa dang ldan pa dbang bskur ba'i cho ga la mkhas pa nges par dgos so/ /

What should one do if a qualified lama with all characteristics cannot be found? The Paramārthasevā says:
In these troubled times faults and good qualities in gurus are mixed. None are completely without fault. The disciples will come to rely upon those discovered, after careful examination, to have a predominance of good qualities.[17] /180/ As this quote says, even if one is unable to find someone possessed of all the worthy characteristics of a lama, one should rely upon those whose good qualities predominate. In particular, it is essential that they have received the complete initiation, hold the tantric vows, and are wise in the rituals of initiation.

d.div: [14] ma dper lhag pa lang gsal bas la'ang yin nam snyam/
[15] ma dper brten gsal yang bsten yod na legs/

f.d: gsum pa bla mar gyur pa bsten tshul dmigs bsal dang bcas pa

d.i: Ways of devoting oneself to someone who has become one’s guru, plus exceptional circumstances

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ bla ma'i bsten tshul dngos dang / de'i dmigs bsal lo/ /
This is under two headings: 1. Ways of devoting oneself to a guru 2. Exceptional circumstances
dang po [bla ma'i bsten tshul dngos ]ni

d.i: Ways of devoting oneself to a guru

f.d:
'grel chen las/
'dir ngur smrig 'dzin pa dge slong rnams kyis dus gsum du rdo rje slob dpon la phyag 'tshal bar bya ste/[17] zhes gsungs pa dang de bzhin du bla ma lnga bcu pa las kyang /
mchog tu dang bas dus gsum du/ / dkyil 'khor me tog bcas thal mos/ / ston pa bla ma bsnyen bkur zhing / / zhabs la spyi bos phyag bya'o/[18] / zhes gsungs pa ltar snga dro phyi dro nyi ma gung dang gsum/ dus gsum po der rang la dbang bskur ba sogs rdo rje theg pa'i lam ston pa'i bla ma'i zhabs la spyi bos gtugs pa'i phyag bya ba'i sgo nas bsnyen bkur bya'o/ / 'o na phyag nyi tshe'am snyam na/ dkyil 'khor de maN+Dal me tog gi tshom bu bkod pa dang bcas pa dbul ba sngon du btang nas thal mo sbyar te phyag bya ba yin no/ /

The Great Commentary says:
Monks who wear the saffron robes should prostrate to the vajra master at all times.[18] Fifty Verses on the Guru also states:
With great faith and at all times, with flower mandalas, and with palms pressed together devote yourself to the teacher guru, bowing your head to his feet.[19] As these quotes state, at all times, morning, noon, and night, devote yourself to the guru by bowing your head to the feet of one who has shown you the path of the Vajra Vehicle by bestowing upon you initiations and so forth. Is this then a partial prostration? It is not, because the mandala decorated with flowers is offered before pressing the palms together and prostrating.

d.div: [17] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 263_na2
[18] sde dge_3721_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tshubla ma lnga bcu pa/ 10_na4
[18] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 263a2.
[19] Toh 3721 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tshu, 10a4.

f.d:
'o na bsnyen bkur ji lta bus zhe na/ 'grel chen las/
dang por yang dag par bsten par bya ste bu dang chung ma la sogs pas kyang mnyes par bya'o zhes pa'i don to/[19] / zhes gsungs pa ltar bla ma lnga bcu pa las kyang /
rang gi dam tshig slob dpon ni/ sbyin min bu dang chung ma dang / / rang srog gis rtag bsten bya na/ / longs spyod g.yo bas smos ci dgos/[20] / zhes dang /

What exactly is meant by devotion? The Great Commentary says:
“Firstly, the guru to devote oneself to” means devoting yourself by pleasing him with your children, wife, and so forth.[20] Fifty Verses on the Guru also says:
If to one’s samaya master one devotes oneself constantly by giving that which is not to be given — one’s children, one’s wife, and one’s life — what need to mention fleeting wealth.[21]

d.div: [19] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 260_ba5
[20] sde dge_3721_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tshubla ma lnga bcu pa/ 10_ba4
[20] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 260b5.
[21] Toh 3721 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tshu, 10b4.

f.d:
sam bu Ta'i brtag pa gnyis pa'i rab byed dang po las kyang /
rang gi chung ma bu mo dang / bran pho bran mo sring mo nyid/ / phyag 'tshal nas ni dbul bar bya/ / bdag gi dngos po thams cad kyis/ / blo dang ldan pas bla mar dbul/ / de ring tshun chad bdag bran du/ khyod la bdag ni dbul lags zhes/ / de ltar zhu ba byas gyur pas/[21] / zhes gsungs pa ltar chung ba zang zing gi longs spyod nas che ba rang nyid kyi lus 'bul ba'i bar gyi bsnyen bkur bya zhing /

In the first chapter of the second section of the Sampuṭa Tantra it says:
Prostrate and offer your wife, your daughter, your maids, and manservants. Pledge, “All that I own, with a mind of faith, I offer to the guru. From this day on I offer myself to you as servant.”[22] As the quotes indicate, you should serve the lama with offerings ranging from your possessions to your own life. /181/

d.div: [21] sde dge_381_bka'/ rgyud/ gsam pu Ta'i brtag pa gnyis pa'i rab byed dang po/ 85_na5
[22] Toh 381 Kangyur, rgyud, kha, 85a5.

f.d:
de byed tshul phan yon dang bcas pa ni lnga bcu pa las/
cung zad yid 'ong gang dang gang / / shin tu khyad par gyur pa nyid/ / de dang de ni bla mar dbul/ / de byin sangs rgyas thams cad dang / / rtag tu byin pa nyid du 'gyur/ / de byin bsod nams tshogs yin te/ / tshogs las dngos grub mchog tu 'gyur/[22] / zhes gsungs pa dang /

The way to accomplish that and the benefits of doing so are taught in Fifty Verses on the Guru:
Whatever is in the smallest way beautiful, whatever is extraordinarily special, offer it all to the guru. Such giving becomes constant giving to every enlightened being. Such giving is the accumulation of merit, from which comes the supreme accomplishment.[23]

d.div: [22] sde dge_3721_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tshubla ma lnga bcu pa/ 10_ba6
[23] Toh 3721 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tshu, 10b6.

f.d:
gzhan yang rang gi lus tshun chad phul nas mnyes par byed dgos pa'i rgyu mtshan ni/ bla ma lnga bcu pa las/
gang phyir bskal pa bye ba ni/ / grangs med par yang rnyed dka' ba'i/ / sangs rgyas nyid kyang brtson ldan la/ / tshe 'di nyid la ster bar byed/[23] / ces gsungs pas so/ / de ltar na bshad pa ltar gyi rnyed pa dang bkur ste sogs kyis bla ma sgo du ma nas mnyes par bya'o/ /

Furthermore the reason why one should please the guru by offering even one’s own body is stated in the same text:
Because the state of a buddha, so hard to reach even over millions of eons, is given in this very life to those who strive.[24] Therefore you should please the guru in many ways with wealth and devotion.

d.div: [23] sde dge_3721_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tshubla ma lnga bcu pa/ 10_ba5
[24] Toh 3721 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tshu, 10b5.

f.d: gnyis pa de'i dmigs bsal ni

'grel chen las/
'dir ngur smrig 'dzin pa'i dge slong rnams kyis dus gsum du rdo rje slob dpon la phyag 'tshal bar bya ste khyim pa dang gsar bu rnams la ni dam pa'i chos 'chad pa ma gtogs par ma yin no/[24] / 'di lta ste/
'jig rten smod pa spang ba'i phyir/ / dam chos la sogs mdun bdar te/ khyim pa 'am ni gsar bu la/ / brtul zhugs 'dzin pas blos phyag bya/ / de bzhin du/
mchog min las dang phyag spangs nas/ / stan bstab pa dang ldang ba dang / / don bya la sogs bsnyen bkur 'dir/ / thams cad brtul zhugs can gyis bya/[25] zhes pa ni 'dir gal te khyim pa'am gsar bu dag kyang dge slong gi rdo rje slob dpon du mtshungs par gyur na de'i tshe ji ltar bya zhe na/ mchog min gyi las rkang pa bkru ba la sogs pa dang yan lag lnga'i phyag spangs nas rang gi gnas su bla ma byon pa la nor la sogs pa'i bkur bsti bya'o/ / 'chad pa'i dus su 'jig rten smod pa spang pa'i phyir dam pa'i chos la sogs pa mdun du bdar nas phyag 'tshal bar bya'o/[26] / zhes gsungs shing /

The Great Commentary says:
Monks who wear the saffron robes should prostrate to the vajra master at all times. To householders and to novices, except at times of teaching, they should not. As it is said:
“To avoid criticism from the worldly, place the holy dharma in front of one, and to householders and to novices, holders of vows should mentally prostrate.” Similarly:
“Avoiding lowly tasks and prostration, holders of vows should make their devotions by arranging his seat, rising in his presence, and helping with his needs.”[25] Therefore, if one is a householder or novice of the same status as a fully ordained vajra master, how should one act? One should avoid lowly acts, such as washing his feet, and one should not perform the five-limbed prostration,[26] but when the guru visits, one should perform devotions of offering gems, money, and so forth. At times of teaching, in order to avoid criticism from the worldly, prostrate to the holy dharma and so forth in front of one.[27]

d.div: [24] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 263_na2
[25] sde dge_3721_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ tshubla ma lnga bcu pa/ 10_na4_tshig sna cung mi mthun/
[26] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 263_na4
[25] Fifty Verses on the Guru, Toh 3721 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, tshu, 10a4.
[26] A full prostration, touching the ground with feet, hands, and head.
[27] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 263a2.

f.d: de ltar gsungs pa'i/ 'jig rten smod pa spang ba'i phyir/ /zhes sogs dang / mchog min las dang phyag spangs nas/ /zhes sogs 'grel chen du drangs pa ltar bla ma lnga brgya par [27] yang 'byung bas rgyud gcig nas drangs par bya dgos la/ de dag ni gong du bla ma bsten tshul bshad pa'i dmigs bsal te/ rang nyid rab byung yin zhing rdo rje slob dpon khyim pa dang / rang nyid bsnyen par rdzogs pa yin pa'i tshe rdo rje slob dpon rab byung yin yang bsnyen par rdzogs pa ma yin pa'i gsar bu la bstan bstab pa dang ldang ba dang / de'i don bya ba la sogs pa'i bsnyen bkur bya'i phyag 'tshal ba dang / dam pa min pa'i las rkang pa bkru ba la sogs pa mi bya'o/ / de yang rang la bla ma khyim pa'am gsar bu chos 'chad pa'i tshe dam pa'i chos glegs bam dang sku gzugs sogs mdun du bdar ba ste bzhag nas lus kyis de rnams la phyag 'tshal zhing blos bla ma de la phyag byed pa yin no/ /

The two verses beginning, “To avoid criticism from the worldly” and “Avoiding lowly tasks and prostration” appear in Fifty Verses on the Guru as they are quoted here in the Great Commentary. Therefore they must both have been taken from the same tantra. The above are exceptions to the previously taught ways of devotion. When one is a monk and one’s vajra master is a householder, or when one is a fully ordained monk and one’s vajra master, although a monk, is not fully ordained and thus a novice, one should arrange his seat, rise in his presence, cater to his needs, and perform other such devotions, but one should not prostrate or perform lowly tasks such as washing his feet. Also, when one’s guru is a householder or novice and is teaching, /182/ one places a volume of the holy dharma or a statue in front of oneself and physically prostrates to it while in one’s mind prostrating to the guru.

d.div: [27] ma dper bla ma lnga brgya par gsal yang lnga bcu pa yin nam snyam/

f.d: de yang rdo rje slob dpon khyim pa dang / gsar bu rab byung yin yang bsnyen par ma rdzogs pa la bsnyen par rdzogs pas phyag mi byed pa'i rgyu mtshan ni skye bo rnams bstan pa la ma dad pa 'byung ba'i dgag bya 'gog pa'i phyir yin par 'grel chen nas kyang bshad la/ rje thams cad mkhyen pas/ de ltar phyag mi byed par bshad pa de bstan pa la ma dad pa 'byung ba 'gog pa'i phyir bshad pa yin pas dgag bya de dag yul 'ga' zhig na gtan log tu song ste med pa'i skabs su dge slong gis rang gi rdo rje slob dpon khyim pa sogs la dus nam yang phyag byed dgos par [28] gsungs so/ /

The Great Commentary explains that the reason why a fully ordained monk should not prostrate to a householder or to a new monk who is not fully ordained is to prevent the people from losing faith in the doctrine. On this point the omniscient master [Jé Tsongkhapa] says that the teaching on not prostrating was taught to prevent a loss of faith in the doctrine, and therefore, on occasions where the possibility of such a loss does not exist, a fully ordained monk should always prostrate to his householder or novice-monk vajra master.[28]

d.div: [28] rje tsong kha pa'i gsung 'bum/ pod/ ka_bla ma lnga bcu pa'i rnam bshad/ 5_ba5
[28] Jé Tsongkhapa, Fulfilling the Hopes of Disciples: Commentary on the Fifty Verses on the Guru, ka, 5b5.

f.d:
'on kyang / bde mchog stod 'grel gyi rigs sum cu rtsa drug gi pho nya mo rnams kyi bza' ba dang btung ba'i cho ga rjod pa'i skabs las/
khyim na gnas pa dang dge tshul gnyis po de dag bla mar gyur kyang chos 'chad pa'i dus na dge slong brtul zhugs 'dzin pa rnams kyis dam pa'i chos la sogs pa mdun du byas te phyag 'tshal bar bya yi/ chos 'chad pa ma gtogs pa gzhan gyi dus na ni ma yin no/ / gzhan gyi dus na dam pa ma yin pa'i las dang phyag 'tshal ba spangs te sngon du ldang ba dang gdan bstab pa la sogs pa bkur ba thams cad bya'o/ / dam pa ma yin pa'i las rkang pa bkru ba la sogs pa dang ngag dang yid kyi phyag spangs nas nor la sogs pas bkur ba bya ste khyim na gnas pa dang dge tshul dag la dge slong rnams kyis zhes pa'o/[29] / zhes chos 'chad pa'i skabs min pa'i tshe dge slong gis rang gi rdo rje slob dpon khyim pa dang dge tshul la ngag dang yid kyis kyang phyag mi byed par bshad pa 'di la brtag par bya dgos sam snyam mo/ /

However, in the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary, when describing the food and drink ritual of the thirty-six kinds of maidservants, it says:
If a householder or a novice monk becomes one’s guru, during teachings the fully ordained holder of vows places the holy dharma and so forth in front and prostrates. However, at times other than teaching, that is not the case. At these other times, lowly tasks and prostrations should be avoided, while every other devotion, such as rising before he enters, arranging his seat, and so forth, should be performed. Lowly tasks, such as washing his feet as well as verbal and mental prostrations, are to be avoided, and devotions are to be made with offerings of wealth. This is to be done by the fully ordained for the householder and novice monk.[29] This passage says that at times other than at teachings the fully ordained should not prostrate, even verbally and mentally, to his householder or novice-monk vajra master. I think this needs some investigation.

d.div: [29] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ bamangon par brjod pa 'bum pa las phyung ba nyung ngu'i rgyud/ 116_na3
[29] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 116a3.

f.d:
de yang gsar bu zhes pa ni dge tshul 'ba' zhig la bya dgos te/ dge slong gis rang gi rdo rje slob dpon dge slong yin na rang las bslab pa gzhon pa sogs thams cad la phyag bya dgos par stod 'grel las bshad pa'i phyir te/ de'i 'phro nyid las/
sngar dge slong gis rdo rje slob dpon gyi dbang bskur te rdo rje 'dzin par byas pa'i bla ma ni dge slong rnams kyis dus thams cad du phyag bya'o zhes pa nges pa'o/[30] / zhes gsungs pa'i shes par byed pa las so/ /

Furthermore “novice” refers only to being a novice monk, because the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary explains that a fully ordained monk should prostrate to his fully ordained vajra master, even though the master be younger in learning and so forth. /183/ This can be known from the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary further on from the previous quote, where it says:
The fully ordained monk who has received the initiation of a vajra master and become the vajra-holder guru is to be prostrated to by fully ordained monks at all times.[30]

d.div: [30] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ bamangon par brjod pa 'bum pa las phyung ba nyung ngu'i rgyud/ 116_na5
[30] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba 116a5.

f.d: gnyis pa gang la dbang bskur ba slob ma'i mtshan nyid ni/

d.i: Upon whom initiations are bestowed: A definition of the disciple

f.d:
de yang rdo rje slob dpon mtshan nyid dang ldan par bsdu bar bya ba'i slob ma'i rigs ni gsum ste tha ma dang 'bring dang mchog go/ / dang po ni 'grel chen las/
tha ma ni dbang gis yang dag par bsdu bar bya ba ma yin te dge bsnyen gyi bslab pas yang dag par bsdu bar bya'o zhes pa ni nges pa'o/[31] / zhes gsungs pa ltar brtag gnyis las kyang /
dang por gso sbyong sbyin par bya/ / de nas bslab pa'i gnas bcu sbyin/ / de la bye brag smra ba bstan/ / mdo sde pa yang de bzhin te/ / rnal 'byor spyod pa de las phyis/ / de yi rjes su dbu ma bstan/[32] / ces gsungs pa ltar theg pa gsum gang gis kyang rgyud smin par ma byas pa dbang po dman pa ste/ de yang dang po dge bsnyen gyi bslab pas bsdu ba nas rim pa bzhin dbu ma'i lta ba'i bar 'khrid pa'o/ /

Disciples to be gathered by a completely qualified vajra master are of three kinds — lowest, middling, and best. Of the first kind, the Great Commentary says:
The lowest are not to be brought together by initiation but by lay disciplines.[31] Similarly the Hevajra Tantra states:
First they are given purification practice,[32] then the ten areas of practice. They are taught the Vaibhāṣika tenets, then the Sautrāntika, followed by Yogacāra, and finally the Madhyamaka.[33] Of low intelligence are those whose minds are yet to be ripened by any of the three vehicles. Initially they are gathered by lay disciplines and gradually led to the Madhyamaka view.

d.div: [31] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 264_na1
[32] sde dge_418_bka'/ rgyud/ nga brtag gnyis/ le'u/ 8_27_na7
[31] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 264a1.
[32] gso sbyong, poṣadha.
[33] Toh 418 Kangyur, rgyud, nga, chap. 8, 27a7.

f.d:
gnyis pa 'bring po ni theg pa thun mong gi lam gyis rgyud sbyangs shing rdo rje theg pa'i lam la mos pa yod la skye ba 'di nyid la phyag rgya chen po mchog gi dngos grub la 'dod pa med cing zhi sogs kyi las rab 'byams kyi dngos grub dang grub pa brgyad la sogs pa thun mong gi dngos grub tsam don du gnyer ba dbang po 'bring por gyur pa ste/ dbang po 'bring po de ni bskyed rim sgom du gzhug ba'i don du byis pa'i dbang bdun tsam bskur nas bsdu bar bya ste/ de ltar yang 'grel chen las/
gang 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub sgrub pa don du gnyer ba de ni sngags dang phyag rgya dang dkyil 'khor gyi 'khor lo bsgom pa'i don du dbang bdun gyis yang dag par bsdu bar bya ste/ 'bring po bsod nams dag gi rgyur/[33] /zhes so/ / zhes gsungs par ltar ro/ /

Middling disciples have minds ripened by the path of the common vehicle. They are also attracted by the Vajra Vehicle, but they have no desire for the supreme siddhi of mahāmudrā in this life and strive only for various siddhis such as those of “peaceful activity” and common siddhis such as the eight siddhis. They are of middling intelligence, and in order to lead them into the meditations of the generation stage, they are gathered only by the seven initiations of childhood.[34] The Great Commentary says:
Those who strive for the accomplishment of worldly powers are to be gathered by the seven initiations in order to bring them to the meditations upon mantra, mudrā, and mandala. This is the merit of the middling disciple.[35]

d.div: [33] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 264_na1
[34] The seven initiations of childhood are the first initiations given in the Kālacakra initiation ceremony. They are discussed in detail below.
[35] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 264a1.

f.d:
gsum pa slob ma mchog ni 'grel chen las/
gang phyag rgya chen po'i dngos grub sgrub pa don du gnyer ba de ni stong pa nyid kyi lam bsgom pa'i don du bum pa dang gsang ba la sogs pa'i dbang gis yang dag par bsdu bar bya'o/[34] / zhes gsungs pa ltar phyag rgya chen po'i dngos grub don du gnyer ba sogs rgyud nas bshad pa'i mtshan nyid 'di dag dang ldan pa rnams dbang bcu gcig rim can du bskur ba'i sgo nas mthar bum dbang sogs dbang gong ma rnams bskur te bsdu bar bya'o/ /

On the best disciple the Great Commentary says:
Those who strive for the mahāmudrā are to be gathered by the initiations of the vase, the secret, and so forth, in order to bring them to the meditations of the path of emptiness.[36] /184/ Therefore those possessed of characteristics such as determination to attain the mahāmudrā siddhi and other characteristics taught in the tantra are gathered by the bestowal of the eleven initiations followed by the higher initiations of the vase, the secret, and so forth.

d.div: [34] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 263_ba7
[36] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 263b7.

f.d:
'o na rgyud nas bshad pa'i mtshan nyid ji lta bu snyam na/ de ni dbang le'i tshigs bcad bzhi pa'i/
zab cing rgya che la sems bla ma'i nges pa la dga' gtong ba'i ngang tshul dang ldan yon tan shes/ / thar pa don gnyer rgyud la gus shing g.yo ba min pa'i sems ldan de nyid thob pa shin tu sbed/ / gdug pa rnams kyi grogs nyams slob ma [35] zhes pa 'dis bstan cing /
de nyid bla ma shin tu mkhas pa rnams kyis bsdu bya ba/ / shes rab dbang la sogs pa'i rgyur te [36] zhes pas bla mas bsdu ba'i tshul bstan to/ /

What are the characteristics of this disciple as taught in the tantra? The fourth verse of the Initiations chapter of the Condensed Tantra says:
A disciple with a mind for the profound and the vast, taking joy in the certainties of the guru, with the spirit of renunciation, a knowledge of the qualities, striving for freedom, respect for the tantras, of an undistracted mind, of that received well hidden, whose friends of the wicked become weaker.[37] This verse teaches the characteristics of the disciple. The following lines teach how such a disciple is gathered by a guru:
Such a one is gathered by the very wise gurus, with the wisdom initiation and so forth as the cause.[38]

d.div: [35] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ le'u/ 3_dbang gi le'u/ sh+loka4_58_na5
[36] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 264_na7
[37] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, dbang v. 4, 58a5.
[38] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 264a7.

f.d: de yang de dag gi don rigs pa cig bshad na/ zab cing rgya che ni zab pa dmigs med kyi snying rje mi 'gyur ba'i bde stong gi ye shes dang rgya che ba dmigs bcas kyi stong nyid rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong gzugs dbyer med pa de la sems shing don du gnyer ba'o/ /

To explain roughly these characteristics: in the line “a mind for the profound and the vast,” profound refers to compassion without apprehension, or the gnosis of unchanging bliss and emptiness. Vast refers to aspected emptiness, or empty form endowed with every supreme aspect. These two, the vast and the profound, are indivisible. The disciple has “a mind for” and strives for the profound and vast.

bla ma'i nges pa la dga' ba ni rtsa ltung bcu bzhi dang bral zhing dge bcu'i chos la dga' ba'o/ / gtong ba'i ngang tshul dang ldan pa ni 'du 'dzi spangs shing nor rdzas la ltos pa med pa'o/ / yon tan shes pa ni dkon mchog gsum la mi phyed pa'i dad pa'o/ / thar pa don gnyer zhes pa ni zhi sogs kyi dngos grub la ltos pa med par 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dngos grub don du gnyer ba'o/ / rgyud la gus zhes pa ni rgyud las gsungs pa'i sdom pa srung ba'o/ / g.yo ba min pa'i sems ldan zhes pa ni 'jig rten pa'i lam bskyed rim sogs kyis sems mi g.yo ba ste chog par mi 'dzin pa'o/ /

“Taking joy in the certainties of the guru” means to be free of the fourteen root downfalls and to take joy in the ten virtues. “With the spirit of renunciation” means to have left behind the busy life and to have no regard for wealth and possessions. “A knowledge of the qualities” means to have an unshakable faith in the Three Jewels. “Striving for freedom” means to have no regard for the attainment of worldly siddhis, such as those of peace, and to strive only for nonworldly siddhis. “Respect for the tantras” means guarding the vows taught in the tantras. “Of an undistracted mind” means not to be distracted by or content with the worldly paths of the generation stage and so forth.

de nyid thob pa shin tu sbed ces pa ni de kho na nyid rdzogs rim zab mo'i gdams ngag thob pa na ji srid rang gi nyams su myong bar ma gyur pa de srid du sbed pa'o/ / gdug pa rnams kyi grogs nyams zhes pa ni nor don du gnyer ba'i khyim pa sogs mi dge bcu spyod pa rnams ni gdug pa yin la de dag gi grogs ni mi dge bcu'i lam ste de nyams pa'o/ /

“Of that received well hidden” means that for as long as it falls outside the realm of one’s experience, all profound instruction received on the completion stage is kept well hidden. The “wicked” in the line “whose friends of the wicked become weaker” refers to those who live lives of nonvirtue, such as householders, and who work for material gain. Their “friends” are the paths of the ten nonvirtues, and in the disciple these become “weaker.” /185/

de ltar mdor bsdu na theg chen sems bskyed sogs thun mong gi lam gyis rgyud sbyangs shing bskyed rim mthar phyin pa'am/ de mthar ma phyin kyang / bskyed rim sgom pa'i smin byed kyi dbang byis pa'i dbang bdun thob pa/ thun mong gi dngos grub la 'dod pa med cing phyag rgya chen po mchog gi dngos grub snying thag pa nas don du gnyer bas dbang po rab tu gyur ba'o/ /

To summarize, the best disciple is one whose mind has been purified by the Mahāyāna mind[39] along with other practices of the common path, and who has completed the generation stage. Alternatively, if the generation stage has not been completed, the best disciple is one who has received the seven initiations of childhood to ripen the mind for the generation stage and who has no desire to attain the common powers but strives from the depths of his heart to achieve the supreme siddhi of mahāmudrā.

d.div: [39] Literally, generation of the Mahāyāna mind, referring to bodhicitta, the entrance to the Mahāyāna.

f.d: gang du dbang bskur ba dkyil 'khor gyi mtshan gzhi ngos gzung ba/
12. Description of the Mandala
gnyis pa gang du dbang bskur ba dkyil 'khor gyi mtshan gzhi ngos gzung ba ni

d.i: Where the initiation is bestowed: A description of the mandala

f.d:
dril bu zhabs kyis/
dbang bskur dkyil 'khor sngon 'gro bar/ / rdo rje 'chang gis gsungs pa yin/[37] / zhes gsungs pa ltar 'dir bshad pa'i dbang bdun dang gzhan nas bshad pa'i bum dbang ni rdul tshon sogs kyi dkyil 'khor du bskur bar bya ba yin zhing 'dir bshad pa'i bum dbang sogs gong ma'i dbang rnams ni phyag rgya'i lus dang b+ha ga dang byang chub sems kyi dkyil 'khor rnams su bskur bar bya ba yin te/

Ghaṇṭāpāda said:
Before the initiation, the mandala, these are the words of Vajradhara.[40] The seven initiations taught here and the vase and other initiations taught elsewhere are bestowed in mandalas of colored powder and other substances, whereas the vase initiation and the other higher initiations taught here are to be conferred in mandalas constructed from the body of the mudrā consort, the female organ, or bhaga, and the bodhi mind.

d.div: [37] sde dge_1431_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ wadapal 'khor lo sdom pa'i dbang gi bya ba mdor bsdus pa/ 219_ba5
[40] Śrīcakrasaṃvaraṣekaprakriyopadeśa, by Ghaṇṭāpāda (Vajraghaṇṭa), Toh 1431 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, wa, 219b5.

f.d:
'grel chen las/
'dir ye shes bsgrub pa'i slad du gzhan dkyil 'khor gsum bcom ldan 'das kyis gsungs pa 'di lta ste/
lus kyi dbang po b+ha ga sems/ / sku gsung thugs kyi rdo rje yis/ / dkyil 'khor rnam pa gsum du 'gyur/ / gzhan pa tshon lnga ldan pa min/ / zhes pa ste/ de'i phyir bde ba chen po bsgrub pa dang mchog gi dbang bskur ba sbyin pa'i don du rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor mi 'gyur ro/[38] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

The Great Commentary says:
For the accomplishment of gnosis, the Buddha spoke of three other mandalas:
“The body, bhaga, and mind, by vajras of body, speech, and mind, become three kinds of mandala, the other of five colors is not used.” Therefore, to attain the great bliss, and for the supreme initiation, the mandala of colored powder is not used.[41]

d.div: [38] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 260_na6
[41] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 260a6.

f.d: spyir rigs lnga'i dbang bskur ba'i dkyil 'khor la rdul tshon dang ras bris dang lus dkyil dang bsam gtan gyi dkyil 'khor sogs mang du bshad kyang 'dir bshad pa'i dbang bdun bskur pa'i dkyil 'khor la mkhas pa (rje btsun red mda' ba )kha cig na re/ dbang po 'bring du gyur ba'i slob ma la ni thog mar rdul tshon nam ras bris sam lugs ma dang 'bur ma la sogs pa phyi'i dkyil 'khor gang yang rung bar chu dang cod paN la sogs pa dbang bdun bskur bas/ smin par byed do zhes gsung yang / 'di ni spyir btang ba dang dmigs kyis bsal ba gnyis kyi sgo nas shes par bya dgos so/ /

Generally, for the initiations of the five tathāgatas, many kinds of mandalas have been described. These include those of colored powder, those drawn on cloth, body mandalas, and mandalas of meditative concentration. Concerning the mandala for the bestowal of the seven initiations as described here, some lamas say that the disciple of middling intelligence is first initiated or ripened by the seven initiations of water, crown, and so forth, in external mandalas of colored powder, drawn on cloth, cast in metal, or in three dimensions, and so forth. /186/ However this should be understood in terms of normal and exceptional circumstances.

de yang spyir btang gi dbang du byas na 'dir bshad pa'i dbang bdun rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor kho nar bskur dgos te/ dbang mdor bstan gyi/
dbang bskur bdun po 'di rnams yin/ / dkyil 'khor bzhengs nas sbyin par bya/[39] / zhes pa'i nA ro pa'i 'grel pa las/
dbang bskur bdun po 'di rnams rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor rnam par spangs nas gzhan ras bris la sogs pa'i dkyil 'khor du sbyin par bya ba ma yin no/[40] / zhes gsungs shing /

Usually the seven initiations as taught here are only to be bestowed in mandalas of colored powder. A Short Teaching on Initiations says:
These seven initiations are given with mandala constructed.[42] And Nāropa’s commentary states:
These seven initiations are only to be given in mandalas of colored powder and not in those drawn on cloth and so forth.[43]

d.div: [39] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_dbang mdor bstan/ 14_ba3
[40] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad don dam bsdus pa/ 238_na1
[42] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 14a3.
[43] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 238a1.

f.d:
sA d+hu pu tra'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa las kyang /
mngon par dbang bskur ba bdun po ni rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor kho nar sbyin par bya ba yin ras bris la sogs pa'i dkyil 'khor du ni ma yin te/ bcom ldan 'das kyis rgyud rnams su ma gsungs pa nyid kyi phyir ro/[41] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

Sādhuputra’s commentary to the same text says:
The seven initiations are bestowed only in mandalas of colored powder and not in mandalas drawn on cloth and so forth, because these were not taught by the Buddha in the tantras.[44]

d.div: [41] sde dge_1352_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i mdor bshad/ 292_na4
[44] Toh 1352 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 292a4.

f.d:
dmigs bsal ni/ dbang le'i tshigs bcad nyis brgya pa'i 'grel chen las/
da ni rdzas rnams med pa zhes pa la sogs pas kun spangs kyi slob ma la dbang bskur ba'i nges pa gsungs pa 'dir gang gi tshe kun spangs kyi slob ma la rjes med na de'i tshe bla mas rdzas rnams med pa'i mngon par dbang bskur rgyal ba'i bdag po'i bka' yis kun spangs la ni sbyin par bya ste rim pa ji lta bas dbang bdun dang de nas bum pa la sogs pa rnams gsum sbyin par bya'o/ / de bzhin du bzhi pa du ba la sogs pa'i lam sbyin par bya zhes pa ste/ tshig gis brjod par bya'o/[42] / zhes kun spangs kyi slob ma la rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor bri ba sogs kyi rdzas med na yang slob dpon gyis dbang bcu gcig po tshang bar bskur bar gsungs pas bsam gtan gyi dkyil 'khor sogs su kun spangs kyi slob ma la dbang bdun bskur chog pa dmigs bsal dang /

There are exceptions. In the Great Commentary, regarding verse 200 of the Initiations chapter of the Condensed Tantra, it says:
“Lacking the material” refers to bestowing initiations upon ascetic disciples. In such cases, if there is no material for these disciples, the guru “bestows the initiations without material, and by the words of the victorious master they are given to ascetics.” This means that the seven initiations are given in order, and then the three, beginning with the vase, are given. “Similarly the fourth, with the paths of smoke and so forth” is to be given. Thus it is written.[45] For ascetic disciples,[46] even when there are no materials for the drawing of the colored-powder mandala, it is taught that the master bestows the eleven initiations in their entirety. Therefore it is acceptable for ascetic disciples to be given the seven initiations in mandalas of meditative absorption and so forth. These are exceptions.

d.div: [42] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 352_ba3
[45] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 352b3.
[46] kun spangs. Those who have given all away.

f.d:
gzhan yang khams le'i mdor bsdus gsum pa las/
'dir bdag gis bcom ldan 'das dus kyi 'khor lo'i dkyil 'khor gyi khang pa 'dir khyed rnams gzhug par bya zhing 'jig rten dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang sbyin par bya'o/[43] / zhes nyi ma'i shing rta la sogs pa'i drang srong rnams rin po che sna lnga las grub pa'i blos bslang gi dkyil 'khor du bcug cing dbang bskur bar gsungs pa yang dmigs bsal du byed dgos so/ /

Also it says in the third summary from the Realms chapter:
I will lead you into this mandala palace of the conqueror Kālacakra and bestow upon you worldly and nonworldly initiations.[47] Thus Sūryaratha and the other ṛṣi were lead into and initiated inside a mind-created mandala of the five precious substances. /187/ This too was an exception.

d.div: [43] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 23_ba6
[47] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 23b6.

f.d:
gal te kun spangs kyi slob ma la de ltar bshad pa ni dbang bskur ba'i yon du zang zing gi 'bul ba med pa'i kun spangs la dbang bskur ba bstan pa yin gyi/ kun spangs la'ang dbang bdun bskur ba la rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor nges par dgos so snyam na/ de yang kun spangs kyi slob ma la rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor bzhengs ba'i longs spyod kyi 'byor pa med na gong du bshad pa bzhin byed dgos pa 'grel tshig de dag gi dgongs pa yin te/ dbang bskur bdun po 'di rnams yin/ /zhes pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa dus zhabs pas mdzad pa las/
da ni dbang bdun po de yang longs spyod dang ldan pa rnams rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor sngon du song ba las bla ma las blang bar bya ba yin te/ dbang bdun po ni 'di rnams yin/ / dkyil 'khor bzhengs nas sbyin bar bya/ / zhes gsungs pa yin no/[44] / zhes rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor bzhengs pa longs spyod dang ldan pa'i dbang du byas par bshad pa yin zhing / de yang kun spangs kyi gang zag khyad par ba cig gi dbang du byed dgos so/ /

It may be wondered if the mention of ascetic disciples in the commentary refers to the bestowing of initiation on ascetic disciples who lack the necessary wealth to be used as an offering for the initiation, and that even for these ascetic disciples the seven initiations must be conferred in a mandala of colored powder. However the meaning of the commentary passage is that the above procedure must be followed when an ascetic disciple lacks the material wealth for constructing a powder mandala. This is so because, as Kālacakrapāda says regarding the above lines in his commentary to A Short Teaching on Initiations:
Now the seven initiations, in a mandala of colored powder previously built by those with wealth, are taken from a guru. As it is said: “These seven initiations are given with mandala constructed.”[48] This says that the mandala of colored powder is constructed on the assumption of the presence of wealth, and that special provision must be made for ascetic disciples.

d.div: [44] sde dge_1353_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ padabang mdor bstan pa'i rgya cher 'grel ba/ 8_na3
[48] Toh 1343 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba 8a3.

f.d: de lta ma yin na dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grub pa gnyis kyis rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor dgos pa la nan tan cher mdzad pa mi 'thad par 'gyur ro/ / gzhan yang dbang bdun bskur ba la rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor byed pa la yang sku gsung thugs yongs rdzogs ma grub na thugs dkyil nyid la brten nas dbang bskur ba yang rung ste/

If this were not so, then the insistence on a mandala of colored powder as found in the two commentaries to A Short Teaching on Initiations would be incorrect. A further point on this topic of using a colored-powder mandala in the seven initiations is that if the body, speech, and mind mandalas are not complete, it is acceptable to bestow the initiations using the mind mandala.

sgrub le'i tshigs bcad nyer lnga pa las/
dbang gi don du yang na dkyil 'khor rigs kyi dbang gis phyi yi 'khor lo rab tu dman par 'gyur/[45] / zhes phyi'i 'khor lo sku dkyil dang gsung dkyil gyis dman pa'i thugs dkyil rkyang pa la brten nas kyang dbang bskur bar gsungs pa dang /

The twenty-fifth verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter of the Condensed Tantra says:
Of the types of mandalas for initiation, the outer are inferior.[49] This teaches that the initiations can be bestowed using the mind mandala, without the body and speech mandalas.

d.div: [45] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 211_na5
[49] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 211a5.

f.d:
'phreng ba las kyang /
yang dbang gi don du dbus kyi dkyil 'khor tsam zhig bri bar rjes su gnang ste/[46] zhes bshad pas so/ /

The Garland also says:
For initiations just the central mandala is drawn and the initiation given.[50]

d.div: [46] rje tsong kha pa'i gsung 'bum/ pod/ thalha bcu gsum ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi cho ga rin chen phreng ba/ 5_na6_tshig sna cung mi mthun/
[50] A Precious Garland: The Ritual of the Thirteen-Deity Mandala, Jé Tsongkhapa, tha, 5b1.

f.d: de ltar na/ bsnyen sogs dag par ma byas par/ /dkyil 'khor las la 'jug mi bya/[47] /zhes sogs kyi bsnyen pa yang lha gang gis dbang bskur ba'i lha thams cad thugs dkyil la tshang bar bzhugs pas thugs dkyil gyi lha'i bsnyen tshad song bas chog par gsungs pa ltar legs pa yin no/ /

Concerning the practices of approximation[51] mentioned in the lines, “Without purification by approximation, there is no engaging in mandala activities,”[52] all initiating deities are complete within the mind mandala, and so the approximation practices of the mind-mandala deities fulfill all necessary criteria. Therefore the teaching that such practice is acceptable is correct. /188/

d.div: [47] rje tsong kha pa'i gsung 'bum/ pod/ tha_5_ba1
[51] bsyen. To approach or to come closer.
[52] A Precious Garland: The Ritual of the Thirteen Deity Mandala, Jé Tsongkhapa, tha, 5b1.

f.d:
'o na sku gsung thugs kyi dkyil 'khor yongs rdzogs kyi lha'i bsnyen pa ji ltar bya zhe na/ dbang le'i so lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
bcom ldan 'das kyi sngags rkang pa bcu drug pa ste 'di bye ba bzlas pas las thams cad dang sbyin sreg 'bum phrag bcus grub pa chen po brgyad po thams cad 'grub par 'gyur te sngon du bsnyen pa'i nges pa'i/[48] zhes gsungs shing / rkang pa bdun cu rtsa gnyis pa la yang de bzhin du gsungs pas bsnyen pa dgos la/ de yang lha grangs ji snyed pa'i bsnyen tshad sngags kyi grangs ngag nyid kyis bzlas pa dgos na mkhas pa chen po dag gis gsungs pa bzhin da ltar gyi dus su bsnyen pa tsam yang 'khyol ba dka' bas thabs la mkhas pa'i bsnyen pa byed tshul zhig dgos so/ /

How are the deity approximation practices to be performed for a complete mandala of body, speech, and mind? The Great Commentary says, on the thirty-fifth verse of the Initiations chapter:
The sixteen-line mantra of the Conqueror recited ten million times accomplishes all tasks. Ten times 100,000 fire rituals will achieve all of the eight great siddhis, but before that, the approximation practices are required.[53] A similar point is made for the seventy-two-line mantra. Approximation practice, therefore, is necessary. Great scholars have said, however, that if it were necessary to recite as many approximation practice mantras as there are deities, these days it would be difficult to complete even the approximation practices. Therefore one should use a skillful approach to the practice of approximation.

d.div: [48] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 287_na7
[53] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 287a7.

f.d:
ji ltar byed na ye shes le'u'i tshigs bcad so brgyad pa'i 'grel chen las/
da ni 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub bsgrub pa'i slad du sngags bzlas pa [49] gsungs pa zhes pa nas/
de ltar 'phreng ba'i sngags nyin zhag so sor dbugs kyi 'khor lo'i grangs bzlas par bya'o/ / 'dir bgrang 'phreng med cing sngags rjod pa med de dbugs 'jug pa dang 'byung ba ngag dang lhan cig sngags kyi yi ge rnams rab tu 'jug pa dang 'byung ba'i me tog gi 'phreng ba bzhin du zla ba dang nyi ma'i rang bzhin lugs dang mthun pa dang lugs dang mi mthun pas blta bar bya'o/ / de ltar nang du nyin zhag lngas stong phrag brgyad lhag pa'i 'bum phrag gi bzlas pa rnal 'byor pas bya'o/ / nyin zhag lnga brgya rnams kyi dbugs 'bum phrag brgyad lhag pa'i bye ba bzlas pa'o/ / de nas lus ngag ste de bzhin du ngag dag pa dang de bzhin du sems rnam par dag pa'ozhes pa'i bar gyis sku gsung thugs kyi sa bon oM yig sogs gsum gyi bar du 'phreng ba'i sngags rkang pa bdun cu rtsa gnyis kyi rkang pa re dang mkha' 'gro ma dang mkha' 'gro'i ming sngags spel ba'i mthar phaTa? yig sbyar ba'i sngags kyi yi ge 'pho chung drug cu'i rlung dang 'pho 'tshams bcu gnyis kyi ye shes kyi rlung rnams dang lhan cig sbyar ba'i dbugs 'byung 'jug gi grangs sngags kyi grangs su byed par gsungs pa ltar bsnyen pa'i grangs kyang bsnyen pa'i sngags bgrang ba'i dus kyi dbugs kyi grangs su song ba nyid la byed ces bla ma mkhas (chos rje shes rin pa/)[50] pa'i dbang phyug nyid gsung pa 'thad dam snyam ste dpyod ldan rnams kyis brtag par rigs so/ /

How is that to be done? The Great Commentary, on the thirty-eighth verse of the Gnosis chapter of the Condensed Tantra, begins:
The text speaks of reciting mantras in order to achieve worldly siddhis. and continues until:
In this way, the mantra chains are recited each day as complete circles of breath. Here do not count or say the mantra, but together with the breath entering and leaving, concentrate on the letters of the mantra entering and leaving, like a garland of flowers, in the nature of moon and sun, in forward and reverse order. In this way, inwardly the yogi performs 108,000 recitations in five days.[54] In five hundred days the yogi recites on 10,800,000 breaths. Then the body becomes pure. Likewise the speech is purified and similarly the mind.[55] Each line of the seventy-two-line mantra chain lies between the three syllables oṃ āḥ hūḥ, which are the seeds of enlightened body, speech, and mind. The lines are also intertwined with the syllables of the ḍākinī and ḍāka name mantras and finalized with the syllable phaṭ. The seventy-two lines of this mantra chain are joined to the winds of the sixty minor movements of wind, as well as the gnosis wind that flows at the changeover point of the twelve major movements of wind. The count of corresponding in- and out-breaths are taken as the count of mantras. In this way, the count of the approximation practices also becomes the count of the breaths at the time of the mantra count. This is the assertion of a lama and great scholar (dharma master Sherinpa), but I wonder if it is correct.[56] It would be right for the discriminating to investigate. /189/

d.div: [49] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 371_ba7

[50] 'dir yig chung du chos rje shes rin pa zhes pa stag tshang lo tsA ba shes rab rin chen yin nges la/ khong dus 'khor la shin tu mkhas par grags pas mkhas grub nor bzang rgya mtshos 'dir bla ma mkhas pa'i dbang phyug nyid ces che bstod mdzad gnang / dus 'khor spyi don bstan pa'i rgya mtsho/
[54] 21,600 breaths in one day times 5.
[55] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 371b7.
[56] Takstang Lotsāwa Sherap Rinchen (b. 1405), the translator and reputed teacher of Khedrup Norsang Gyatso.

f.d: der dbang bskur ba'i dbang nyid kyi rnam gzhag bshad pa/
13. The Initiations
gsum pa der dbang bskur ba'i dbang nyid kyi rnam gzhag bshad pa

d.i: A presentation of the initiations to be bestowed

f.d: ['di ]la gsum/ dbang rnams kyi grangs dang / go rim dang / dbang so so'i don bshad pa'o/ /
This is under three headings: 1. The number of initiations 2. The order of initiations 3. An explanation of each initiation
dang po [dbang rnams kyi grangs bshad pa ]ni

phyag rdor stod 'grel las/
de bzhin du mkha' 'gro ma rdo rje gur du bcom ldan 'das kyis dbang bskur ba gsum pa las bzhi pa tha dad par gsungs pa/ bum pa'i dbang ni dang po ste/ / gnyis pa gsang ba'i dbang du 'dod/ / shes rab yeshes gsum pa ste/ / de ni ji ltar de bzhin min/[51] / zhes pa dang / de bzhin du slar yang de nyid kyi le'u bco lnga par/ chu yi dbang ni dang po ste/ / cod pan dbang bskur gnyis pa'o/ / gsum pa dar dbyangs dbang bskur te/ / rdo rje dril bu bzhin pa'o/ / lnga pa rang gi bdag po nyid/ / ming gi dbang ni drug pa ste/ / sangs rgyas rjes gnang bdun par 'dod/ / brgyad pa bum pa'i dbang yin te/ / gsang ba'i dbang ni dgu pa yin/ / shes rab dbang bskur bcu pa'o/ / de nyid rdo rje'i rab sbyor gyis/[52] / zhes gur gyi rgyud rnams drangs te/

The Vajrapāṇi Commentary of the Three Bodhisattva Commentaries states:[57]
Similarly, in the Ḍākinī Vajra Tent Tantra, the Conqueror taught the fourth initiation apart from the third: “The vase initiation is the first, the second is stated to be the secret. Wisdom-knowledge is the third, the fourth is not like that.” Also in the fifteenth chapter: “The water initiation is the first, the crown initiation the second, third is the ribbon empowerment, fourth the vajra and bell, the fifth is one’s own conduct, name is the sixth, the Buddha’s permission, the seventh, the eighth is the vase initiation, the secret initiation the ninth, the wisdom initiation is the tenth, reality is by the vajra yoga.”[58] Here passages from the Ḍākinī Vajra Tent Tantra are quoted.

d.div: [51] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ bamangon par brjod pa 'bum pa las phyung ba nyung ngu'i rgyud/(bde mchog stod 'grel/) 128_na7
[52] sde dge_419_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ brdo rje gur/ 128_ba1
[57] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, passage begins from 128a7. Also called Cakrasaṃvara Commentary.
[58] Toh 419 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 128b1.

f.d:
de'i mjug tu/
de nyid rdo rje'i rab sbyor gyis/ /zhes pa gtso bor dbang bcu gcig pa bcom ldan 'das kyis rab tu gsal ba'i gsung las mkhas pa rnams kyis dbang bzhi pa'am bcu gcig pa tha dad par rtogs par bya'o/ / zhes gsungs pa ltar bskur ba'i dbang la grangs nges pa yin te chu dbang sogs byis pa ltar 'jug pa'i dbang bdun/ bum dbang gsang dbang shes rab ye shes kyi dbang ste 'jig rten pa'i dbang gong ma gsum/ 'jig rten las 'das pa'i gong ma'i yang gong ma don dam pa'i dbang bzhi pa dang bcu gcig tu nges pa'o/ /

Immediately after this, the text continues:
“Reality is by the vajra yoga.” Clearly the eleventh was taught by the Conqueror principally so that the wise should understand the fourth or the eleventh initiation as separate. This ascertains the number of initiations to be conferred. There are seven initiations, beginning with the water initiation, which proceed in accordance with the stages of childhood. These are followed by the three higher worldly initiations of the vase, secret, and wisdom-knowledge, and finally the nonworldly higher-than-high ultimate fourth initiation.

de ltar nges pa'i rgyu mtshan yang rdo rje slob dpon gyi dbang gi sgo nas bsdu bar bya ba'i gang zag gi rigs de la re zhig 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub tsam don du gnyer ba'i sgo nas bskyed rim tsam sgom par 'dod pa'i gang zag cig dang / mchog gi dngos grub 'ba' zhig don du gnyer ba'i sgo nas rdzogs pa'i rim pa sgom 'dod pa'i gang zag gnyis su yod la/ de'i dang po'i dbang du byas nas byis pa ltar 'jug pa'i dbang bdun tsam bskur ba dang / gang zag gnyis pas dang por bskyed rim bsgoms te/ de mthar phyin pa na rdzogs rim rdzogs par sgom pa'i dbang du byas te dbang bcu gcig po thams cad bzhag pa yin la/ gang zag de gnyis kyi lam sgom tshul de ltar byed pa'i snod rung du sgrub pa'i dbang la bcu gcig po de tsam zhig ni dgos shing de las mang ba yang mi dgos pa'i phyir ro/ /

There is a reason for determining the number of initiations. This concerns the type of person to be gathered by the vajra master giving initiation. /190/ There are those who for the time being seek only worldly siddhis and, therefore, wish to practice only the generation stage. Then there are those who seek only the supreme siddhi and, therefore, seek the practices of the completion stage. For the first of these types, only the seven childhoodlike initiations are conferred. The second type of person starts their meditations on the generation stage and, when that is perfected, practices the meditations of the completion stage in their entirety. For such a person all eleven initiations are bestowed. Just these eleven and no more are required to create suitable vessels for the meditation paths of these two types of persons.

de bzhin du dbang la bcu gcig po der nges par dbang mdor bstan las kyang gsungs te|_de nyid las/
dang por dbang bskur bdun po gang / / byis pa rnams ni gzhug pa'i phyir/ / rnam gsum 'jig rten kun rdzob kyi/ / dam pa'i don gyi bzhi pa'o/[53] / zhes gsungs shing / de dag gi don 'chad pa'i tshe/ de nyid las/
bum pa gsang ba'i dbang bskur dang / / shes rab ye shes mngon brjod pa/ / slar yang shes rab chen po nyid/ / de yi ye shes mngon rjod byed/ / 'gyur dang 'gyur dang de nas 'dzag / de nas gzhan yang mi 'dzag pa'o/[54] / zhes dbang bcu gcig pa'am bum dbang nas kyi bzhi pa don dam pa 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang la bshad pa ltar ro/ /

The number of initiations is also ascertained as eleven in A Short Teaching on Initiations:
First, the seven initiations for the children to enter by: three by worldly convention, the fourth by ultimate reality.[59] Also, farther on, when explaining their meanings:
The initiations of the vase and the secret, that known as wisdom-knowledge, and again the gnosis of that great wisdom: change, change, and fall, and then no farther fall.[60] Thus the eleventh, or the fourth counting from the vase initiation, is explained as being the ultimate nonworldly initiation.

d.div: [53] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan/ 14_na6
[54] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_dbang mdor bstan/ 14_ba3
[59] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 14a6.

[60] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 14b3. “Change, change” refers to “changing bliss” and to the vase and secret initiation. “Fall and then no farther fall” refers to the falling of the elemental bodhicitta and to the wisdom-knowledge and fourth initiation.

f.d: 'o na dbang gong ma la bzhi dang gong ma'i gong ma bzhi ste bco lnga bshad pa ji ltar yin zhe na/ de ltar bshad kyang skyon med de/ gong ma dang gong ma'i gong ma'i bum dbang gnyis bum dbang du mtshungs pa dang / de bzhin du gsang dbang gnyis gsang dbang du mtshungs pa dang / shes rab ye shes gnyis shes rab ye shes su mtshungs shing / 'jig rten pa'i dbang bzhi par bshad pa de dbang gsum pa shes rab ye shes kyi dbang nyid la bzhi pa'i ming gis btags pa yin pas so/ /

However four higher initiations and four higher-than-high initiations have been taught, making fifteen altogether. How is this explained? There is no error here, because the higher vase initiation and the higher-than-high vase initiation are similar insofar as they are both vase initiations. Likewise the two secret initiations are both secret initiations. The wisdom-knowledge initiations are both wisdom-knowledge initiations. That which is explained as the worldly fourth initiation is actually the third, or wisdom-knowledge initiation, and is given the name “fourth initiation.” /191/
gnyis pa go rim ni/

de yang dbang bcu gcig gi go rim ni/ dang po chu dbang nas mthar don dam pa'i dbang bzhi pa'i bar rim can kho nar bskur dgos te/ slob dpon klu sgrub kyis rim lnga las/
bskyed pa'i rim la legs gnas shing / / rdzogs pa'i rim pa 'dod rnams la/ / thabs 'di rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyis/ / skas kyi rim pa lta bur gsungs/[55] / zhes gsungs pa ltar bskyed rim la bslabs nas rdzogs rim sgom pa la 'jug pa'i rim pa nges pa ltar dang po bskyed rim sgom pa'i snod rung du byed pa'i dbang bdun bskur ba sngon du btang nas de'i rjes su rdzogs rim sgom pa'i snong rung du byed pa'i dbang gong ma rnams bskur dgos pa yin zhing /

The eleven initiations begin with the water initiation and end with the ultimate fourth initiation. As Ācārya Nāgārjuna says in his Five Stages:
Well established within the generation stage, they yearn for the stage of completion. This method, like the steps of a ladder, the fully enlightened Buddha has taught.[61] As this verse says, one moves to the completion stage having trained well in the generation stage. This is the defined order. Similarly one must first be made into a suitable vessel for the generation-stage meditations with the seven initiations and then turned into suitable vessels for the meditations of the completion stage by means of the higher initiations.

d.div: [55] sde dge_1802_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ngi klu sgrub kyi rim lnga/ 45_na6
[61] Toh 1802 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ngi, 45a6.

f.d: dbang bdun po yang rim pa de ltar nges pa ni byis pa mngal nas skyes nas bskyed bsring ba'i phyir dang por 'khru ba dang / de nas gtsug phud gzhag pa dang / de nas rna ba 'bugs pa la sogs pa dang / de nas byis pa dgod cing smra ba dang / de nas longs spyod la gnas pa dang / de nas ming 'dogs pa dang / de nas bri klog sogs byed pa dang rim pa mthun par dbang bdun rim can du bskur ba ste/

The order of the seven initiations is also clearly defined. When a child is born, it is washed in order to help it grow. Later its hair is tied to the top of its head. Its ears are pierced and so forth. The child is encouraged to laugh and talk, it discovers pleasures, it is given a name,[62] and finally it is taught to read and write. The seven initiations are conferred in correlation with this sequence.

d.div: [62] In ancient India a child was not named until a year after its birth.

f.d:
de ltar yang rdo rje snying 'grel las/
byis pa skyes la ma rnams kyis/ / chu yis 'khru ba'i dbang bskur byed/ / de yi gtsug phud rab 'jog pa/ / cod pan du ni yongs su btags/ / de yi rna ba 'bugs pa sogs/ / dar dpyangs dbang bskur byed par bshad/ / byis pa smra dang dgod pa ni/ / dril bu rdo rje'i dbang bskur ro/ / lnga pa longs spyod brtul zhugs yin/ / ming ni ming gi dbang bskur yin/ / klog pa la sogs rjes gnang ma/ / pha dag gis ni rtag tu ster/ / de la rnam pa bdun gyi ni/ / dbang bskur bdun du rab tu grags/[56] / zhes byis pa ltar 'jug pa'i dbang yin pas byis pa'i dbang bdun zhes gsungs pa yin no/ /

The Vajragarbha Commentary says:
At birth women wash the child, and the water initiation is given. Its hair is tied upon its head, this is known as the crown. The ears are pierced, and so forth, explained as being the ribbon initiation. The child laughs and speaks, the bell and vajra initiation is conferred. The fifth, childhood pleasures, is the conduct initiation. The name is the name initiation. Reading and so forth is the permission. These are given by mother and father, of which there are seven, known as the seven initiations.[63] Therefore, because they follow in the footsteps of a child, they are taught as the seven childhood initiations.

d.div: [56] sde dge_1180_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ka_rdo rje snying 'grel/ 39_ba2
[63] Toh 1180 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ka 39b2.

f.d: dbang gong gi snga ma bzhi'i go rim yang dbang don rnams snga ma las phyi ma rim gyis skye ba'i rgyu mtshan gyis yin no/ /
The order of the four higher initiations is defined by the significance of a preceding initiation that necessarily leads into the following initiation. /192/

kha cig na re/ byis pa'i dbang bdun dang dbang gong ma la go rim nges pa can med de/ dbang bdun bskur ba rdul tshon sogs phyi'i dkyil 'khor du bcug nas byed dgos pa/ /dbang gong ma rnams bskur ba la rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor rnams bkag pa'i phyir te/

Some say that there is no clearly defined order to the seven childhood initiations and the four higher initiations because the seven initiations must be conferred within an external colored-powder mandala, and in the higher initiations the colored-powder mandalas are rejected.

dbang le'i tshigs bcad dang po'i 'grel chen las/
don dam pa'i bden pas ni rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor bri ba med de bcom ldan 'das kyis bkag pa'i phyir ro/ / de skad du dang po'i sangs rgyas las bcom ldan 'das kyis gsungs pa/ / rdo rje'i thig rnams gdab pa dang / / rdul tshon dag kyang gdab pa ni/ / sngags kyi de nyid kyis mi bya/ / byed na byang chub 'thob par dka'/ / zhes pa nas/
de'i phyir bde ba chen po bsgrub pa dang mchog gi dbang bskur ba sbyin pa'i don du rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor du mi 'gyur ro/[57] / zhes pa'i bar gyis dbang gong ma rnams bskur ba la rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor mi dgos par gsungs shing / dbang bdun bskur ba la rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor dgos par gsungs pas so/ /

The Great Commentary says, on the first verse of the Initiations chapter:
For the ultimate truth, the colored-powder mandala is not drawn, because it was rejected by the Conqueror. This is stated in the Original Buddha by the Conqueror: “Construction of vajra lines, construction by colored powder also, are not to be done within mantra reality. If they are, enlightenment is difficult.” And so on until:
Therefore, for the achievement of great bliss and for the giving of supreme initiation, the colored-powder mandala is not used.[64] This, they say, clearly states that for the higher initiations, the colored-powder mandala is not necessary, whereas it is necessary for the seven initiations.

d.div: [57] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 260_na3
[64] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 260a3.

f.d:
de ltar na dbang bdun bskur ba sngon du ma song bar yang gong ma'i dbang rnams bskur bas sbyor ba yan lag drug sgom par rung ba rgyud 'grel gyi dgongs par bsams nas sngon dang da ltar gyi sbyor drug pa 'ga' zhig de ltar byed par snang yang de ni mi 'thad de/ dbang mdor bstan gyi/ dbang bskur bdun po 'di rnams yin/ /zhes pa'i 'grel par nA ro pa chen pos/
sngar mdor bstan pa'i dbang bcu gcig po rnams kyi nang nas 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dngos grub kyi khang bzang gi them skas su gyur pa 'og ma kun rdzob kyi gzugs can dbang bdun po rnams rnam par bshad nas [58] zhes dbang gong ma rnams kyi 'bras bu 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dngos grub sgrub pa la dbang bdun po khang bzang gi them skas dang 'dra bar gsungs pas dbang gong ma rnams kyi sngon du dbang bdun po nges par 'gro dgos par grub bo/ /

They think, therefore, that it is acceptable to practice the six-branched yoga with just the four higher initiations and without the preceding seven initiations. This, they believe, is the intention of the tantra and its commentaries, and it seems that some past and present practitioners of the six-branched yoga practiced and continue to practice that way. This, however, is not correct. Nāropa’s commentary to the line “these seven initiations” in A Short Teaching on Initiations says:
Within the eleven initiations mentioned in A Short Teaching are the steps to the palace of the nonworldly siddhis. These are explained as the seven lower and conventional initiations with form.[65] This teaches that in the achievement of the nonworldly siddhis, which are the fruits of the higher initiations, the seven initiations are compared to steps leading to a palace. Therefore the seven initiations must precede the higher initiations.

d.div: [58] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad don dam bsdus pa/ 238_na2
[65] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 238a2.

f.d:
gzhan yang dam gzhag gi skabs su
khyod kyis 'di dkyil 'khor du ma zhugs pa rnams la smra bar mi bya ste/ khyod dam tshig nyams par 'gyur ta re/ zhes gsungs pa'i dkyil 'khor yang skabs 'dir rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor la bya dgos kyi/ b+ha ga sogs kyi dkyil 'khor slob ma thog mar 'jug pa'i dkyil 'khor du 'ong don med cing / dus na gang smras pas dam tshig nyams par 'gyur ba'i gsang ba ni sngags kyi gsang ba yin la/ de yang dbang gong ma'i gsang ba las lhag pa'i gsang ba smra rgyu med pas ma smin mi la gsang ba bsgrags pa'i rtsa ltung du 'gyur bas so/ /

Furthermore, at the time of taking the secrecy pledges, it is commanded:
Do not speak of this to those who have not entered the mandala, or your pledges will weaken. The mandala mentioned here has to be a colored-powder mandala. It makes no sense for the bhaga mandala and so forth to be the first mandala that the disciple enters. /193/ Moreover the secrets, which if revealed result in a weakening of one’s pledges, are secrets of mantra, and there are no greater secrets to be revealed than those of the higher initiations. Telling them, therefore, to those not ripened constitutes a root downfall.

gzhan yang dbang gong ma rnams bskur ba'i rim pa yang bzhed tshul mi 'dra ba du mar gyur te/ mkhas pa'i dbang po (rje btsun chen po red mda' ba/)dag ni 'di ltar bzhed de/ bum dbang sogs 'jig rten pa'i dbang gong ma bzhi thob pa tsam gyis rgyud nyan pa dang sbyor ba yan lag drug sgom pa'i snod rung du gyur cing dbang gong ma'i gong ma don dam pa'i dbang bzhi pa dang bcas pa bskur ba ni rgyud rdzogs par ston pa'i bdag po chen po'i slob dpon gyi phyir yin pa dang /

There are also a number of different assertions concerning the order of the higher initiations. Some great scholars (such as the noble Rendawa), maintain that by just the initiations of the vase and the other three higher worldly initiations, one becomes a fit vessel to listen to the tantra and to meditate upon the six-branched yoga, and that the higher-than-high initiations, including the ultimate fourth initiation, are the initiations of the vajra-master great lord,[66] enabling one to teach the entire tantra.

d.div: [66] Usually called the vajra-master initiations but the additional “great lord” is relevant to a later discussion.

f.d:
yang kha cig (red mda' nyid/)'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa bskur tshul 'dir ma bshad cing de bas na gsang dbang dang kun rdzob shes rab ye shes kyi dbang gnyis kyis ni bzhi pa'i lam sgom pa'i snod du rung bar byed pa yin zhes gsung la/ de dag kyang dbang le'i brgya bcu dgu pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir dbang gong ma ni rnam pa gnyis te gcig ni sems can gzhug pa'i don dang lam yongs su shes pa'i don dang rgyud nyan pa la dbang ba'i don du'o/ / gzhan ni slob dpon chen po'i gnas sbyin pa dang stong pa po byed pa'i slad du'ozhes pa nas/
sems can gzhug pa'i slad du 'jig rten kun rdzob kyi dbang rnam pa bzhi'i nges pa'o/[59] / zhes gsungs pa'i bar gyis 'jig rten pa'i dbang bzhi dang gnyis gnyis 'khyud pa'i bde ba 'di'i dbang bzhi par bstan nas

One scholar (Rendawa) says that the method of bestowing the nonworldly fourth initiation is not explained here, and therefore the secret initiation and the nonultimate wisdom-knowledge initiation renders one a fit vessel for the meditations on the path of the fourth initiation. On these points the Great Commentary, discussing verse 119 of the Initiations chapter, says:
The higher initiations are of two kinds. One kind is for leading sentient beings,[67] for complete knowledge of the path, and for listening to the tantra. The other confers the status of great vajra master and creates the teacher. And so on until:
For the purpose of leading sentient beings, there are four nonultimate initiations.[68] The above passage contains explanations of the four worldly initiations and a description of the fourth as “the bliss of embrace.”

d.div: [59] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 328_na7
[67] Into the mandala.
[68] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 328a7.

f.d:
de'i 'phro nyid kyi 'grel chen las/
de nas rgyas 'grel dang bcas pa'i rgyud thams cad thos shing shes par gyur pa na bdag po chen po nyid kyi ched duzhes pa nas/
de ltar don dam pa'i le'u lnga pa las phyag rgya chen po'i ye shes rgya cher brjod par bya ste/ des na 'dir rgyas par ma byas so/[60] / zhes pa'i bar gyis rdo rje slob dpon bdag po chen por byed pa'i dbang gong ma'i gong ma bzhi bstan pa rnams kyi don du dgongs shing / 'grel tshig de dag gi dngos bstan gyi don de tsam zhig yin na'ang / rgyud rdzogs par nyan pa sogs kyi snod rung la 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa tshig gi sgo nas nges par thob dgos te rgyu mtshan 'og tu 'chad do/ /

The quote continues:
Then, if they have studied and know every tantra and its extensive commentary, the initiation of the great lord is conferred. Until:
In the fifth chapter on the ultimate, the mahāmudrā gnosis will be explained extensively. Therefore it is not taught in detail here.[69] The above passages explain the four higher-than-high initiations as being the initiations of the vajra-master great lord, and that is the literal meaning of the text. However, to become a fit vessel to listen to the tantras and so forth, the ultimate fourth initiation, in the form of a word initiation, must be bestowed. /194/ The reason for this will be explained later.

d.div: [60] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 328_ba7
[69] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 328b7.

f.d:
yang phal che ba (jo mo nang pa rjes 'brang dang bcas pa )dag ni rdo rje slob dpon bdag po'i dbang la dbang gong ma'i gong ma bzhi bskur bar mi byed par/ kha cig (chos rje mtshal man pa )[61] dbang gong ma dang po bzhi'i mthar 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa tsam zhig bskur nas/ bdag po'i dbang la dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i dbang bzhi mi bskur bar 'dod la/ /de ni gong du drangs pa'i 'grel pa
gzhan ni slob dpon chen po'i gnas sbyin pa dang ston pa po byed pa'i slad duzhes sogs dang 'gal te/

The common assertion (of the Jonang followers) is that for the vajra-master lord initiation, the four higher-than-high initiations do not have to be conferred, and some (such as the dharma master Tsalmin)[70] maintain that at the end of the first four higher initiations, just the nonworldly fourth is conferred, and for the lord initiation, the four higher-than-high initiations are not conferred. That, however, contradicts the previous quote that runs:
The other confers the status of great vajra master and creates the teacher.

d.div: [61] 'dir yig chung du chos rje tshal min pa zhes byung ba 'di'i lo rgyus mdor bsdus shig bod kyi rtsis rig kun 'dus chen mo deb dang po shog grangs 60_phreng 12_nas 161_bar bzhugs pa ltar na khong jo nang phyogs rgyal ba dang / sa bzang ma ti paN chen/ nya dbon kun dga' dpal sogs kyi zhabs la gtugs shing / dus phyis karma pa de bzhin gshegs pas tshal min dgon pa phul bas der dbang bshad khrid gsum gyis gdul bya bskyangs par mdzad pas dus rabs 14_nang gi bod kyi mkhas pa zhig yin par snang ngo / /
[70] Tsalmin Chökyi Drakpa, fourteenth-century master who served under Jonang Chögyal and others. Brief details of his life found in Great Compendium of Tibetan Astronomy.

f.d:
gzhan ni zhes pa'i dbang ston byed kyi 'grel pa ni/ rig ma bcu po rnams khyim na gnas pa'i slob mas bla ma la dbul bar bya'o zhes sogs kyi 'grel tshig rnams yin la|_'grel pa de dag gis rdo rje slob dpon bdag po'i phyir du phyag rgya bcu la 'khyud pa'i bum pa'i dbang la sogs pa gong ma las kyang gong ma'i dbang rnams bskur bar bshad pa'i phyir ro/ khong dag na re/ skyon med de/ slob dpon gyi dbang la rdo rje slob dpon bdag po'i dbang dang bdag po chen po'i dbang gnyis yod pa las dang po ni 'grel chen las/
de nas rgyud thams cad shes shing dam bca' ba la gnas pa'i slob ma ni rdo rje slob dpon bdag po'i slad du bla mas dbang bskur bar bya'ozhes pa nas/
rdo rje slob dpon bdag po'i dbang gi cho ga'i nges pa'o/[62] / zhes pa'i bar gyis bstan pa yin zhing /

Here the word “other” refers to initiations, and is the commentary to “The disciple who is a householder offers the ten consorts to the guru” and so forth. This commentary explains that for the vajra-master lord, the higher-than-high initiations of the vase and so forth, in which one sits in union with the ten mudrās, are conferred. They would reply that there is no fault, because for the vajra-master initiation there is the vajra-master lord initiation and vajra-master great lord initiation. Concerning the first, the Great Commentary says:
Then the disciple who knows all tantras and dwells in the pledges is initiated by the guru into vajra lord. The passage continues up to:
This is the initiation ceremony of the vajra-master lord.[71]

d.div: [62] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 326_na2_nas 327_ba3
[71] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 326a2 to 327b3.

f.d:
de dag gi skabs su dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i dbang chog ma bstan pa dang / gnyis pa bdag po chen po'i dbang ni 'grel chen las/
de nas rgyas 'grel dang bcas pa'i rgyud thams cad thos shing shes par gyur pa na bdag po chen po nyid kyi ched du go rim ji lta ba bzhin gsungs pa'i rig ma bcu po rnams [63] zhes sogs kyis bstan pa yin pa'i phyir bdag po chen po'i dbang la rig ma bcas 'khyud pa'i bum dbang sogs gong ma'i yang gong ma'i dbang chog khas len pas skyon med do snyam na/ skabs 'dir rdo rje slob dpon gyi dbang la bdag po'i dbang dang bdag po chen po'i dbang gnyis su byas nas 'grel tshig gong 'og de dag gis so sor bsnan par 'dod pa ni rigs pa ma yin te/ de ltar rigs na dbang gong ma la rgyud nyan pa'i don du gcig dang rdo rje slob dpon bdag po'i don du gcig dang / bdag po chen po'i don du gcig ste gsum yod dgos pa las/ 'grel chen las gnyis su nges par gsungs pa'i phyir te/

At this point the ceremonies for the higher-than-high initiations have not been taught. The second initiation, the vajra-master great lord, is explained by the Great Commentary in the passage:
Then, if they have heard and learned every tantra and its commentaries, the initiation of the great lord in its proper order is taught, and the disciple who is a householder offers the ten consorts to the guru.[72] Thus they maintain that the vajra-master great lord initiation can be accepted as being the initiation ceremony of the vase and other higher-than-high initiations that include the union of the ten consorts. One may think this way, but dividing the vajra-master initiation into a lord initiation and a great lord initiation and claiming based on the two quotes above that these two initiations are individually taught is not correct. If it were, then there would be three kinds of higher initiations — one for listening to the tantras, one for the vajra-master lord, and one for the vajra-master great lord. /195/

d.div: [63] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 328_ba7
[72] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 328b7.

f.d:
'grel chen las/
'dir dbang gong ma ni rnam pa gnyis te gcig ni sems can gzhug pa'i don dang lam yongs su shes pa'i don dang rgyud nyan pa la dbang ba'i don du'o/ / gzhan ni slob dpon chen po'i gnas sbyin pa dang ston pa po byed pa'i slad du'o/[64] / zhes rgyud nyan pa sogs kyi don du dbang gong ma tsam dang / rgyud slob ma la ston pa sogs kyi don du rdo rje slob dpon bdag po chen po'i dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma gnyis su nges par gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

The Great Commentary, however, divides them into two:
The higher initiations are of two kinds. One kind is for leading sentient beings, for complete knowledge of the path, and for listening to the tantra. The other confers the status of great vajra master and creates the teacher.[73] Therefore the higher initiations are for listening to the tantra and so forth, and the higher-than-high initiations of the vajra-master great lord are for teaching the tantra to disciples and so forth.

d.div: [64] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 328_na7
[73] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 328a7.

f.d:
gzhan yang rdo rje slob dpon bdag po'i don du dbang bskur bar bya ba'i slob ma 'chad pa'i 'grel pa gong mar/
