de nas rgyud thams cad shes shing dam bca' ba la gnas pa'i slob mazhes dang
/ kye dpal ldan bla ma khyod kyi bka' drin las da ni bdag gis bde bar gshegs pa'i lam thams cad shes so/ / zhes dang /
yon tan thams cad dang ldan pi 'aslob ma dam bca' ba la gnas pa gzigs te/[65] zhes gsungs shing /

Furthermore, in the earlier commentary passage, there are descriptions of the disciple on whom the vajra-master lord initiation is bestowed:
Then the disciple who knows all tantras and dwells in the pledges. And:
Ah! Wonderful guru! Because of your kindness I now know all the paths of those who have traveled to bliss. Also:
He sees the disciple endowed with every good quality dwelling in the pledges.[74]

d.div: [65] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 326_na2_nas 327_ba3
[74] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 326a2 to 327b3.

f.d:
de lta bu'i slob ma 'chad pa'i 'grel pa 'og mar yang /
de nas rgyas 'grel dang bcas pa'i rgyud thams cad thos shing shes par gyur pa na/ / zhes dang /
kye bcom ldan 'das pha rol tu phyin pa thams cad thob pa da ni bdag gis ci zhig bgyi/[66] / zhes gsungs pas 'grel pa gong 'og gnyis kyi slob dpon gyi dbang bskur bar bya ba'i rten la khyad par ma byung zhing /

Descriptions of such a disciple also occur in the later passage:
Then, if they have studied and know every tantra and its commentaries… And:
Ah! The Conqueror has attained every perfection! What can I do?[75] Therefore there are no differences between the earlier and later passages concerning the subject on whom the vajra-master lord initiation is conferred.

d.div: [66] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 328_ba7
[75] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 328b7.

f.d:
'grel pa gong 'og gnyis kyi slob dpon gyi dbang bskur ba'i dgos pa la yang khyad par ma byung ste/ dbang bskur ba'i dgos pa 'chad pa na 'grel pa gong ma las/
dge slong dang dge tshul dang khyim pa rnams la rdo rje slob dpon gyi dbang bskur ba dang rgyud bstan pa'i don du gsung gi rjes su gnang ba sbyin par bya'o zhes pa ni nges pa'o/[67] / zhes dang /
'dir ston pa po'i dbang la mngon par dbang bskur ba'i dge slong ngamzhes gsungs shing /

There are also no differences between the passages on the reason for conferring the vajra-master initiation. To explain the need for the initiation, the former passage says:
The vajra-master initiation is conferred upon the monks, novice monks, and laymen, and speech permission to teach the tantra is given. And:
The monk who is initiated into the teacher initiation.[76]

d.div: [67] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 326_ba3
[76] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 326b3.

f.d:
'grel pa 'og mar yang /
bdag po nyid byed pa'i slad du dkyil 'khor chen po'i slob dpon gyi go 'phang mngon par 'dod pas phyag rgya bcu dbul bar bya'o/[68] / zhes gsungs pa 'grel pa gong 'og gnyis kas bstan pa'i dbang bskur ba'i dgos pa dkyil 'khor chen po'i slob dpon gyi go 'phang thob ste dbang bskur ba po dang rgyud ston pa por mtshungs pas so/ /

In the later passage Also:
To become a lord, those who wish for the level of the vajra master of the great mandala should offer the ten mudrās.[77] /196/ Therefore the earlier and later passages are similar in that they both teach the purpose of the initiation to be the achievement of the status of vajra master of the great mandala — a bestower of initiations and a teacher of tantra.

d.div: [68] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 328_ba1
[77] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 328b1.

f.d: gang yang 'grel pa gong mar bdag po'i slad du zhes pa tsam byung zhing / 'grel pa 'og mar bdag po chen po nyid kyi ched du zhes chen po byung ma byung gi khyad yod pas snyam pa 'di yin na ni/ 'grel pa 'og mar yang / bdag po nyid byed pa'i slad du zhes bdag po rkyang pa las ma byung bas gnod do/ /

Whatever the reason may be, in the earlier passage just the word “lord” appears and in the later passage the words “great lord” appear, and if these assertions arise because the word “great” might or might not appear, they are damaged by the quote in the later passage beginning “To become a lord,” which only mentions the word “lord.”

'o na ci zhig yin snyam na/ mdor bsdus lnga pa 'di'i thog mar/
'dir dpal mchog gi dang po'i sangs rgyas las rab tu gnas pa'i cho ga [69] zhes sogs gsungs pa ltar rab gnas kyi cho ga 'chad pa'i rab gnas la mi la rab gnas byed pa bdag po chen por dbang bskur ba dang / lha la dbang bskur te rab gnas byed pa sogs yod pa las klu dang zhes sogs 'grel pa gong ma rtsa ba dang bcas pas bdag po chen por dbang bskur ba'i cho ga'i cha 'ga' zhig bshad pa'i sgo nas mdor bstan cing /

So what is the difference between the two passages? At the beginning of this fifth summary from the Great Commentary, it says:
The rituals of consecration from the gloriously supreme Original Buddha.[78] This section then is to be an explanation of consecration rituals. These include the consecration of human beings to initiate them as great lords and the consecration, or initiation, of the gods as taught by the words “Nāgas and so forth.” In this way, by explaining parts of the initiation ceremony of the great lord, the earlier passage, as well as the root tantra, is giving a condensed explanation.

d.div: [69] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 325_ba7
[78] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 325b6.

f.d:
don de nyid 'grel pa 'og ma las/
de nas rgyas 'grel dang bcas pa'i rgyud thams cad thos shingzhes sogs rtsa 'grel rnams kyis rgyas par bshad pa yin no/ /

That same topic is explained in detail by the root tantra and commentary in the later passages where it says:
Then, if they have studied and know every tantra and its commentaries…

dper na/ dang por chu dag la ni zhes sogs rtsa 'grel rnams kyis dbang gi rnam gzhag sogs cha 'ga' zhig bstan pa'i sgo nas dbang gong ma rnams mdor bstan pa de nyid/[70] dpal ldan shes rab nu ma la yang [71] zhes sogs rtsa 'grel rnams kyis rgyas par bshad pa bzhin yin no/ /

For example, by giving a partial presentation of the initiations, the passage beginning “First the water” is the root tantra and commentary giving a condensed explanation of the higher initiations,[79] whereas the passage beginning “The glorious wisdom śakti”[80] is the root tantra and commentary giving a more detailed explanation.

d.div: [70] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 328_ba7
[79] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 328b7.
[80] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, dbang v. 119, 69b4. Here śakti refers to the ten goddesses of the gnosis mandala.

f.d:
yang gzhan dag ni rgyud nyan pa dang sbyor ba yan lag drug sgom pa la dbang ba'i don du dbang gong ma bzhi dang gong ma'i yang gong ma bzhi ste brgyad po thams cad bskur bar byed pa ni mi 'thad de/ 'grel chen las/
'dir dbang gong ma ni rnam pa gnyis te gcig ni sems can gzhug pa'i don dangzhes sogs kyis mtshams sbyar nas/
sems can gzhug pa'am rgyud nyan pa sogs la dbang bar byed pa'i dbang gong ma ni dang por dbang 'di la re zhig skrag pa dang 'khrul pa'i sems la sogs pa'i skyon dang bral ba [72] zhes pa nas/
sems can gzhug pa'i slad du 'jig rten kun rdzob kyi dbang rnam pa bzhi'i nges pa'ozhes pa'i bar gyis 'jig rten pa'i dbang gong ma bzhi dang / bzhi pa de'i mtshon don gyi dbang bzhi pa tsam bskur pas rgyud nyan pa sogs la dbang bar bstan cing /

Others maintain that to be empowered to listen to tantra and to practice the six-branched yoga, all four higher and all four higher-than-high initiations are to be given. This is not correct. The Great Commentary says:
The higher initiations are of two kinds. One kind is for leading sentient beings… This leads into the subject, and continues:
Concerning the higher initiations for leading sentient beings or for listening to tantra: initially the faults of fear and confusion regarding these initiations are driven from the mind. And up to:
In order to lead sentient beings, four kinds of conventional and worldly initiations are ascertained.[81] /197/ This teaches that by just the four worldly higher initiations and the fourth initiation, as illustrated by the worldly fourth, one is empowered to listen to tantra and so forth.

d.div: [71] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ le'u/ 3_dbang gi le'u/ sh+loka119_69_ba4
[81] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 328a7.

f.d:
yang 'tshams sbyar du/
gzhan ni slob dpon chen po'i gnas sbyin pa dang ston pa po byed pa'i slad du'ozhes pa'i gzhan ni dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma bzhi la byed pa dang / de yang gong ma'i yang gong ma bzhi 'chad pa'i mtshams sbyar du/
de nas rgyas 'grel dang bcas pa'i rgyud thams cad thos shing shes par gyur pa na bdag po chen po nyid kyi ched duzhes mtshams sbyar nas de'i 'phro nyid las/
go rim ji lta ba bzhin du gsungs pa'i rig ma bcu po rnams khyim na gnas pa'i slob mas bla ma la dbul bar bya'o [73] zhes sogs rtsa 'grel rnams kyis rdo rje slob dpon bdag po chen po'i don kho nar dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma bskur bar gsungs pa rnams dang 'gal ba dang /

The Great Commentary, again as a lead-in, says:
The other confers the status of great vajra master and creates the teacher. Here “other” refers to the four higher-than-high initiations. Again, the Great Commentary, leading into an explanation of the higher-than-high initiations, says:
Then, if they have studied and know every tantra and its commentaries, the initiation of the great lord is conferred. And continues:
…in its proper order is taught, and the disciple who is a householder offers the ten mudrās to the guru.[82] The tantra and it commentary is saying that the four higher-than-high initiations are for the sole purpose of the vajra-master great lord initiation. This contradicts the above assertion.

d.div: [72] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 328_na7
[73] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 329_na1
[82] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 329a1.

f.d: gzhan yang dbang gong ma bzhi dbang bdun dang bcas pa dang 'jig rten pa'i bzhi pas mtshon don 'jig rten las 'das pa'i bzhi pa ste dbang bcu gcig po de tsam zhig bskur bas rgyud rdzogs par nyan pa dang bskyed rdzogs rdzogs par sgom pa'i snod rung du sgrub mi nus par 'gyur te/ snod rung du sgrub pa la gong ma'i yang gong ma bzhi char bskur dgos pa'i phyir ro/ /

Furthermore such an assertion would mean that the eleven initiations, comprising the four higher initiations and the seven childhood initiations plus the nonworldly fourth illustrated by the worldly fourth, would be unable to create vessels suitable for listening to the entire tantra and to practice the stages of generation and completion in their entirety, for to create such suitable vessels, separate initiations into the four higher-than-high initiations would be required.
gsum pa dbang so so'i rnam gzhag bshad pa
['di ]la gnyis/ byis pa'i dbang bdun gyi rnam gzhag bshad pa dang / dbang gong ma rnams kyi rnam gzhag bshad pa'o/ /
This is under two headings: 1. The seven childhood initiations 2. The four higher initiations
dang po [byis pa'i dbang bdun gyi rnam gzhag bshad pa ]ni
14. The Seven Childhood Initiations

rtsa ba'i rgyud dbang mdor bstan pa las/
chu dang cod pan dar dpyangs dang/ / rdo rje dril bu brtul zhugs che/ / ming dang rjes gnang yang dag ldan/ / dbang bskur rnam bdun mi yi bdag[74] / ces gsungs pa'i chu dbang nas rjes gnang gi dbang gi bar bdun ni byis pa ltar 'jug pa'i dbang bdun yin la/ de yang bdun ga la chu'i bya ba rjes su 'gro bas chu dbang bdun zhes pa'i tha snyad mdzad na'ang bum dbang gi tha snyad ni mi mdzad do/ /

The root tantra, A Short Teaching on Initiations, states:
Water, crown, and silk ribbon, vajra and bell, great conduct, name, and permission: these well bestowed, great king, are the seven initiations.[83] /198/ The seven initiations, from the water to the permission initiation, are the seven initiations that proceed according to childhood. All seven are rounded off by a water ritual and are therefore known as “the seven water initiations,” but the term vase initiation[84] is not used.

d.div: [74] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan pa/ 14_na7
[83] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka,14a7.
[84] As in initiations other than Kālacakra.

f.d: de yang dbang bdun ni rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor gyi sgo bzhi'i thad sor slob ma bzhag nas bskur ba yin la/ de yang byang sgo'i thad sor gtso bo'i sku'i zhal dkar po byang phyogs na gnas pa la mngon par phyogs pa'i slob ma sku rdo rjer bskyed pa la/ dbang lhas dbang bskur ba'i tshul yang rgyud gzhan dang mi 'dra bar bsgrubs pa'i rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor gyi nang gi yum lngas chu'i dbang dang / de bzhin gshegs pa lngas cod pan gyi dbang bskur/

These seven initiations are bestowed upon the disciple, who is placed opposite the four entrances to the colored-powder mandala. In front of the northern entrance, facing the white northern form-face of the main deity, the disciple stands in the form of the body vajra. The initiation deities then confer initiation. This is performed in a way that differs from other tantras. The five mothers within the colored-powder mandala bestow the water initiation, and the five tathāgatas bestow the crown initiation.

de nas slob ma lho sgo'i thad sor khrid de lho phyogs gsung gi zhal dmar po la mngon du phyogs pa'i slob ma gsung rdo rjer bskyed pa la nus ma bcus dar dpyangs kyi dbang dang / gtso bo yab yum gyi rdo dril gyi dbang bskur/ de nas slob ma shar sgo'i thad sor khrid de shar phyogs shugs [75] kyi zhal nag po la mngon du phyogs pa'i slob ma thugs rdo rjer bskyed pa la sems dpa' sems ma rnams kyis brtul zhugs kyi dbang dang / khro bo khro mo rnams kyis ming gi dbang bskur/ de nas slob ma nub sgo'i thad sor khrid de nub phyogs ye shes kyi zhal ser po la mngon du phyogs pa'i slob ma ye shes rdo rje bskyed pa la rdo rjer sems dpa' yab yum gyis rjes gnang gi dbang bskur ba'o/ /

The disciple is then led to the southern entrance to be in front of the red speech-face of the south. There he generates himself in the form of the speech vajra and is empowered with the ribbon initiation by the ten śakti, and with the vajra and bell initiation by the main deity and consort. The disciple is then led to the eastern entrance to face the black mind face and generates himself as the mind vajra. There the male and female bodhisattvas confer the conduct initiation, and the male and female wrathful deities bestow the name initiation. The disciple is led to the western entrance and faces the yellow gnosis face, where he generates himself as gnosis vajra and is initiated into the permission initiation by Vajrasattva and consort.

d.div: [75] ma dper shugs kyi gsal yang don la thugs kyi yin nam snyam/

f.d: de ltar byed pa'i don ni/ thog mar chu dbang la mtshon nas bstan na dbang rdzas bum chu rnams slob ma'i khams lnga yum lngar bskyed de zhu ba las byung ba'i bum chu byang chub sems kyi ngo bor gyur pa yum lngas thogs te chu dbang bskur bas khams lnga'i dri ma 'khrud cing yum lnga'i dngos grub 'grub pa'i skal ba can du byed do/ /

These initiations can be illustrated by way of the water initiation. The water of the vases, which is the initiation substance, and the five elements of the disciple are generated into the five mothers. These deities melt, and the resultant vase water, in the nature of bodhicitta, is held aloft by the five mothers, who confer the water initiation. This purifies the five elements of all defilements and grants the disciple the fortune to achieve the powers of the five mothers.

de bzhin du cod pan dang slob ma'i phung po lnga gshegs pa lngar bskyed nas cod pan gyis dbang bskur bas phung po lnga'i dri ma 'khrud cing gshegs pa lnga'i dngos grub 'grub pa'i skal ba can du byed do/ / dag cha de gnyis kyang lus kyi chos yin pas de dag byed gtso bo'i sku'i zhal dkar po gang du phyogs pa'i sgor slob ma bzhag nas sku rdo rjer bskyed pa la dbang bskur ba yin no/ /

Likewise the crown and the five aggregates of the disciple are generated into the five tathāgatas. The crown initiation purifies the aggregates of defilements and grants the disciple the fortune to achieve the powers of the five tathāgatas. Phenomena of the body are purified by these two initiations, and the purifier of these phenomena is the white body-face of the main deity. The disciple, therefore, is placed at the mandala entrance opposite this face, where, in the form of body vajra, he receives the initiation. /199/

dar dpyangs kyi dbang la dar dpyangs bcu dang slob ma'i rlung bcu nus ma bcur bskyed nas dar dpyangs kyi dbang bskur bas rlung bcu sbyangs te las rung du gyur nas d+hU tIr sdom nus par byed do/ / rdor dril gyi dbang la rdor dril dang slob ma'i rtsa ro rkyang gtso bo yab yum du bskyed nas rdor dril gyi dbang bskur bas ro rkyang gi rlung dbu mar sdom pa'i nus pa can du byed do/ / rlung bcu dang rtsa ro rkyang gnyis dag gi chos yin pas de dag byed gtso bo'i gsung gi zhal dmar po gang du phyogs pa lho'i sgor slob ma bzhag nas gsung rdo rjer bskyed pa la dbang bskur ba yin no/ /

In the ribbon initiation the ten ribbons and the ten winds of the disciple are generated as the ten śakti. The initiation purifies the ten winds so they become workable and capable of being brought into the central channel. In the vajra and bell initiation, the vajra and bell and left and right channel are each generated as the main deity and consort. The initiation renders the winds of the left and right channel capable of being gathered into the central channel. The ten winds and the left and right channel are phenomena of speech. Therefore the disciple is placed at the southern entrance facing the red speech-face, the purifier of these phenomena. There, in the form of speech vajra, the initiation is conferred on the disciple.

brtul zhugs kyi dbang la mtho bo'i rdo rje dang slob ma'i rgyud kyis bsdus pa'i dbang po drug dang yul drug sems dpa' sems mar bskyed nas brtul zhugs kyi dbang bskur bas dbang po drug yul drug la 'jug pa'i dri ma sbyong ba'i nus pa can du byed de/ ming gi dbang la gdu bu dang las dbang bya ba dang bcas pa khro bo khro mor bskyed nas ming gi dbang bskur bas las dbang drug las dbang gi bya ba la 'jug pa'i dri ma sbyong ba'i nus pa can du byed do/ / de yang 'dir ming dbang la dbang rdzas gdu bu byed pa ni sA d+hU pu tras/ de nas lag pa dang rkang pa rnams la lag gdub bam me tog phreng ba bcings la [76] zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ / brtul zhugs dang ming dbang gnyis kyi dag bya sems kyi chos yin pas de dag byed gtso bo'i thugs kyi zhal nag po gang du phyogs pa shar gyi sgor slob ma bzhag nas thugs rdo rjer bskyed pa la dbang bskur ba yin no/ /

In the conduct initiation, the thumb vajra, the six sense powers, and the six sense objects of the disciple’s continuum are generated as male and female bodhisattvas. The initiation is bestowed, creating the potential to remove the defilements of sense power moving to sense object. In the name initiation, the initiation bracelet and the action faculties and their activities[85] are generated into the male and female wrathful deities. The name initiation is conferred, and seeds for the removal of the defilements of the six action faculties and their six activities are planted. The bracelet used as initiation substance is said by Sādhuputra to be “a bracelet or garland of flowers tied around the arms and legs.”[86] Phenomena purified by the conduct and name initiation are those of the mind. The disciple, therefore, is placed at the eastern entrance in front of the black mind-face of the main deity, which is the purifier of those phenomena. There in the form of the mind vajra he receives the initiation.

d.div: [76] sde dge_1359_bka'/ rgyud 'grel/ padapal dus kyi 'khor lo'i dkyil 'khor gyi cho ga122_ba6
[85] See appendix 7 for a list of these phenomena.
[86] Kālacakra Mandala Ritual, Toh 1359 Kangyur, rgyud, ba, 122b6.

f.d: rjes gnang gi dbang la dbang 'di'i sbyang gzhi ye shes kyi phung po dang ye shes kyi khams yin pa dang / de sbyong byed ye shes rdo rje yin pas gtso bo'i ye shes kyi zhal ser po gang du phyogs pa nub sgor slob ma bzhag nas ye shes rdo rjer bskyed pa la chos 'chad pa sogs kyi rjes gnang dngos dang rjes gnang gi 'dogs la sogs pa ster ba yin no/ /

In the permission initiation the phenomena to be purified are the aggregate of gnosis and the element of gnosis. The purifier is the gnosis vajra, and the disciple, therefore, is placed at the western entrance facing the yellow gnosis-face of the deity, where in the form of the gnosis vajra the actual permission to teach and so forth and the permission appendages are given.

dbang dang po drug gi dag bya gnyis gnyis rim pa bzhin lus ngag sems gsum gyi chos yin pa dang / de dag byed dbang gnyis gnyis yin pa ni dbang mdor bstan las/
lus ngag sems ni legs dag pa/ / mngon par dbang bskur gnyis gnyis so/[77] / zhes dang /

The phenomena to be purified by the first six initiations are those of body, speech, and mind in two sets each respectively. The purifiers are the three pairs of initiations. A Short Teaching on Initiations says:
Body, speech, and mind well purified by pairs of initiations.[87]

d.div: [77] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan pa/ 14_na7
[87] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, 14a7.

f.d:
rjes gnang ye shes kyi phung khams dag byed yin pa ni/
rjes gnang ye shes yang dag dag[78] / ces gsungs pa yin no/ /

Regarding the aggregate and element of gnosis to be purified by the permission initiation, the same tantra says:
The permission purifies gnosis.[88] /200/

d.div: [78] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan pa/ 14_ba1
[88] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, 14b1.

f.d:
de bzhin du dbang bdun gyis gong du bshad pa ltar rim pa bzhin khams dang phung po sogs sbyong bar byed pa ni dbang mdor bstan las/
chu ni khams kyi dag pa ste/ / cod pan phung po rnam sbyong byed/ / dar dpyangs pha rol phyin pa dag / rdo rje dril bu mi 'gyur che/ / sangs rgyas skad rgyun mi 'chad pa/ / nyi zla gcig tu dag par byed/ / yul dang dbang po legs dag pa/ / 'pho med rdo rje brtul zhugs 'gyur/ / ming ni byams sogs yang dag dag / rjes gnang sangs rgyas nyid dag byed/ / dbang bskur bdun po 'di rnams yin/[79] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis bstan te/ / de yang / rdo rje dril bu mi 'gyur che/ / zhes sogs kyi don ni mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po mtshon byed rdo rje dang /

Concerning the seven initiations purifying the elements, aggregates, and so forth, as explained above, the same tantra states:
Water is the purification of the elements, the crown purifies the aggregates, the ribbon purifies the perfections.[89] By the vajra and bell, the great unchanging, and the unbroken voice of the Buddha, the sun and moon are purified as one. Purification of object and sense is by the unmoving vajra of conduct. Name purifies love and so forth, [90] permission purifies the very Buddha.[91] These are the seven initiations.[92] The meaning of “by the vajra and bell, the great unchanging,” is that the great unchanging bliss is symbolized by the vajra.

d.div: [79] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan pa/ 14_ba1
[89] The ten winds are also known as the ten perfections (pha rol tu phyin pa, pāramitā).
[90] Love, compassion, joy, and equanimity — the four immeasurables — but here refers to the action faculties and their activities.
[91] The gnosis element and aggregate.
[92] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, 14b1.

f.d: sangs rgyas kyi gsung rgyun mi 'chad pa gzhom du med pa'i sgra mtshon byed dril bu dang / rdor dril de gnyis dang ldan pa'i lag pa gnyis kyis 'khyud pa'i tshul byed pa'i rdor dril gyi dbang gis nyi zla gcig tu zhes pa srog dang thur sel gyi rlung ro rkyang la 'bab pa dag a wad+hU tIr gcig tu zhugs par byed pa'i nus pa can du byas pa ste nA ro pa'i 'grel pa las gsungs pa ltar bkod pa'o/ / dbang bdun po thob pas bskyed rim yan lag dang bcas pa tsam sgom pa la dbang zhing / gdul bya 'bring po 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub tsam don du gnyer ba la dbang bdun po 'di tsam zhig bskur bar bya yi/ dbang gong ma rnams bskur mi rung bar shes par bya'o/ /

The unbroken continuum of the Buddha’s voice, which is an indestructible sound, is represented by the bell. The vajra and bell initiation is performed by the embrace of the two hands holding vajra and bell, and “the sun and moon are purified as one,” which means that the life-sustaining wind and the downwardly expelling wind that flow through the right and left channel are capable of dwelling as one within the avadhūtī. This has been taken from Nāropa’s commentary. With the seven initiations one is empowered only to meditate upon the generation stage and its branches. For the middling disciple who only strives for worldly powers, only these seven are conferred, and it is not proper to confer the higher initiations on them.
gnyis pa dbang gong ma rnams kyi rnam gzhag bshad pa
15. The Four Higher Initiations
['di ]la gnyis/ dbang gong ma rnams kyi grangs nges bskur ba'i rim pa dang bcas pa bshad pa dang / dbang so so'i rnam gzhag bshad pa'o/ /
This has two outlines: 1. Ascertaining the number of initiations and the order in which they are conferred 2. A description of each initiation /201/
dang po [dbang gong ma rnams kyi grangs nges bskur ba'i rim pa dang bcas pa bshad pa ]ni

d.i: Ascertaining the number of initiations and the order in which they are conferred

f.d:
'grel chen las/
'dir dbang gong ma ni gnyis te gcig ni sems can gzhugs pa'i don dang lam yongs su shes pa'i don dang rgyud nyan pa la dbang ba'i don du'o/ / gzhan ni slob dpon chen po'i gnas sbyin pa dang ston pa po byed pa'i slad du'o/[80] / zhes gsungs pa ltar dbang gong ma tsam dang gong ma'i yang gong ma gnyis su grangs nges pa yin la/ de ltar nges pa'i rgyu mtshan yang rgyud 'di'i ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo dbang po yang rab de la rgyud rdzogs par nyan nas rdzogs rim rdzogs par sgom pa'i snod rung du dngos su bya dgos pa'i gang zag cig dang de ltar snod du gyur nas rdzogs rim rdzogs par rgyud la skyes kyang rung ma skyes kyang rung ste rgyud don rdzogs par shes nas rgyud ston pa por 'os pa'i gang zag gnyis su nges la/ de'i dang po la dbang bskur ba'i dbang du byas nas dbang gong ma tsam dang / gnyis pa la dbang bskur ba'i dbang du byas nas dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i rnam gzhag mdzad pa yin no/ /

The Great Commentary says:
The higher initiations are of two kinds. One kind is for leading sentient beings, for complete knowledge of the path, and for listening to the tantra. The other confers the status of great vajra master and creates the teacher.[93] As this quote states, these initiations are determined as being of two kinds — the higher and those that are higher than high. The reason for this division is as follows. The primary intended disciple of the tantra, who is of the highest intelligence, listens to the complete tantra and is made into a suitable vessel for comprehensive practice of the completion stage. That is one kind of person. Having become such a suitable vessel, and whether or not the completion stage has been consummated within his mind, he comprehensively understands the meanings of the tantra and is worthy of teaching it to others. That is another type of person. The presentation of just the higher initiations is made on the basis of conferring initiation upon the first type of person, while the presentation of the higher-than-high initiations is made on the basis of conferring initiation upon the second.

d.div: [80] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 328_na7
[93] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 328a7.

f.d: dbang gong ma tsam la yang bum dbang dang gsang dbang dang 'jig rten pa'i dbang bzhi pa shes rab ye shes kyi nang du bsdus pa'i shes rab ye shes kyi dbang dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa dang bcas pa'i bzhir nges pa yin te/ rgyud nyan pa dang rdzogs rim rdzogs par sgom pa'i snod rung du byas pa'i gang zag des bsgom par bya ba'i rdzogs rim de la sbyor ba yan lag drug tu grangs nges shing / bum pa'i dbang dang gsang dbang dang shes rab ye shes kyi dbang gsum gyis sor sdud nas rjes dran gyi bar yan lag lnga sgom pa la dbang bar byed la/ 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa tshig gi dbang bskur bas ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag sgom pa la dbang bar byed pa'i phyir ro/ /

Individually, the four higher initiations are the vase initiation, the secret initiation, the wisdom-knowledge initiation, which includes the worldly fourth initiation, and lastly the nonworldly fourth initiation. These are determined as follows. The disciple has listened to the tantra and has become a suitable vessel for all the meditations of completion stage, which consists of the six-branch yoga. The vase, secret, and wisdom-knowledge initiations will empower the disciple to practice the first five of the six-branched yoga. The nonworldly fourth initiation is the word initiation, and therefore empowers the disciple to practice the sixth branch of meditative concentration.

de ltar na gong du drangs pa ltar phyag rdor stod 'grel du gur gyi rgyud drangs nas dbang la bcu gcig tu grangs nges mdzad pa yang rgyud rdzogs par nyan pa sogs kyi snod rung du bya ba'i dbang la dgongs pa yin la/ de'i yang dbang bcu gcig pa de 'jig rten las 'das pa'i bzhi pa/ bzhi pa de yang de bzhin no/ /zhes pas sbas pa'i nges don gyi dbang bzhi pa yin pa gur gyi rgyud tshig de rnams kyi don yin pa phyag rdor stod 'grel [81] gyi dgongs pa yin pa'i phyir dang /

The thinking of the previous passage from the Vajrapāṇi Commentary, which quotes the Ḍākinī Vajra Tent Tantra and then determines the number of initiations to be eleven, is also that these initiations are conferred in order to create suitable vessels for listening to the complete tantra and so forth. It is the thinking of the Vajrapāṇi Commentary that the meaning of the Ḍākinī Vajra Tent Tantra verse is that, of these eleven, the eleventh is the nonworldly fourth initiation, /202/ which is the definitive fourth initiation of the hidden tantras as taught by the line “the fourth is likewise.”

d.div: [81] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ bamangon par brjod pa 'bum pa las phyung ba nyung ngu'i rgyud/(bde mchog stod 'grel/) 126_na2

f.d:
dbang mdor bstan las kyang /
bum pa gsang ba'i dbang bskur dang / / shes rab ye shes mngon brjod pa/ / slar yang shes rab chen po nyid/ / de yi ye shes mngon rjod byed/[82] / ces dbang gong ma gsum dang / 'jig rten las 'das pa'i bzhi pa'i bcu gcig pa bshad byar bkod nas

A Short Teaching on Initiations also says:
Initiations of vase and secret, that known as wisdom-knowledge, again the knowledge of great wisdom.[94] Here the three higher initiations and the eleventh, or nonworldly fourth, are listed as topics to be explained.

d.div: [82] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan pa/ 14_ba3
[94] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 14b3.

f.d:
de dag gi don 'chad pa na de'i 'phro nyid las/
'gyur dang 'gyur dang de nas 'dzag/de nas gzhan yang mi 'dzag pa'o/ / lus ngag sems ni legs dag pas/ / dbang bskur gsum po rim pa yis/ / bzhi pa ye shes yang dag dag / lus ngag sems ni dag par skyed/ / byis pa dar ma de nas rgan/ / bzhi pa skye dgu'i bdag po'o/[83] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis kyang rgyud nyan pa dang sgom pa'i snod rung du skyed pa'i dbang rnams bstan pa yin zhing /

Then, as an explanation, the text continues:
Change, change, and fall, and then no farther fall. Purification of body, speech, and mind, the three initiations leading respectively to the fourth, the pure gnosis. Purifying body, speech, and mind, first a child, then a youth, and finally old, the fourth is the master of sentient beings.[95] These quotes teach the initiations that create suitable vessels for listening to and meditating on the tantra.

d.div: [83] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan pa/ 14_ba3
[95] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 14b3.

f.d: de yang dbang bzhi bstan tshul ni/ slar yang shes rab chen po nyid/[84] /ces pa dang / de nas gzhan yang mi 'dzag pa'o/ /zhes pa dang / bzhi pa ye shes yang dag dang / /ces pa dang / bzhi pa skye dgu'i bdag po'o/ /zhes pa rnams kyis 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa'i bcu gcig pa bstan cing /

The lines “again the knowledge of great wisdom,” “and then no farther fall,” “to the fourth, the pure gnosis,” and “the fourth is the master of sentient beings” all teach the eleventh, or nonworldly fourth, initiation.

d.div: [84] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan pa/ 14_ba4

f.d:
bum pa gsang ba'i dbang bskur dang / /zhes pa'i tshig rkang gnyis dang / 'gyur dang 'gyur dang de nas 'dzag /ces pa dang / lus ngag sems ni legs dag pas/ /dbang bskur gsum po rim pa yis/ /lus ngag sems ni dag par byed/ /byis pa dar ma de nas rgan/[85] /zhes pa rnams kyis dbang gong ma dang gong ma'i yang gong ma gnyis su phye ba'i gong ma'i dbang gsum yang bstan pa yin te/ bum pa gsang ba'i dbang bskur dang / /zhes sogs kyi snga 'grel du nA ro pas/
gang zhig rnal 'byor pa la kun rdzob tu gyur pa 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub sgrub par skyed cing / don dam pa'i rjes su mthun pa'i dbang gsum po rnams bum pa zhes pa la sogs pas mdor bstan to/[86] / zhes gsungs shing /

The two lines beginning “Initiations of vase and secret” and the lines “change, change, and fall,” “Purification of body, speech, and mind, the three initiations leading respectively,” and “Purifying body, speech, and mind, first a child, then a youth, and finally old”[96] all teach the three higher initiations from the division of higher and higher than high. This is so because, in earlier commentary on the lines beginning “Initiations of vase and secret,” Nāropa says:
For those yogis to develop the conventional worldly powers, three initiations of the vase and so forth are taught as semblances of the ultimate.[97]

[97] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 238a3.

f.d:
phyi 'grel gyi de dag gi don 'chad pa na dbang gong ma'i bum dbang sogs gsum 'chad byed kyi bsdus rgyud kyi/
ji srid phyogs kyi lo ni gcig tu rnam pa bcu ru 'gyur te lta ba dang ni reg par bya/ / zhes pa nas/
dpal ldan shes rab nu ma la yang dang por reg pa gang yin bum pa'i dbang ni de nyid do/ / gsang ba dag las ri bong 'dzin pa myang ba dang ni lta ba dag gis gsang ba'i dbang du 'gyur/ / shes rab ye shes dbang la mtha' dag rgyal ba'i rigs kyi yan lag zhal gyi sbyang ba byas nas ni/ / rgyal ba dag kyang 'dir ni bla mas dbang por byas nas slob ma la ni phyag rgya sbyin par bya/[87] / zhes pa'i bar dang /

In later commentary on these lines, Nāropa quotes passages from the Condensed Tantra in its explanation of the higher initiations of vase and so forth. These run from:
Up to “direction” years, the one with ten aspects,[98] >look, and touch. /203/ And up to:
The first touch of the breasts of glorious wisdom is the initiation of the vase. Experiencing and looking at the “moon”[99] in its secret place is the secret initiation. Within the wisdom-knowledge initiation, all are purified by the families of the conquerors, and the guru, having bestowed initiation, gives the mudrā to the disciple.[100]

d.div: [87] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ le'u/ 2_dbang gi le'u/ sh+loka118_119_69_ba4
[98] Advice to stay with the consort for ten years because the perfection of wisdom is of ten kinds and in each year one type is developed.
[99] “That which holds the rabbit” commonly refers to the moon, but here even moon is a metaphor.
[100] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, dbang v. 118/9, 69a4.

f.d: rgyud tshig de dag 'chad byed kyi 'grel chen gyi tshig/ 'dir bum pa la sogs pa'i don du phyag rgya lo bcu'i bar gzhon nu ma spang bar bya/ zhes pa nas/ rlung gi khams ni rdul med pa nyid kyi phyir gzung bar mi bya'o [88] zhes pa nges pa'o zhes pa'i bar rnams nA ro pa'i 'grel par drangs nas bshad pa'i phyir dang /[89] yang 'grel chen gyi de'i 'phro nyid las/ 'dir dbang gong ma ni rnam pa gnyis te/ zhes pa nas/ sems can gzhug pa'i slad du 'jig rten kun rdzob kyi dbang rnam pa bzha'i+i nges pa'o [90] zhes pa'i bar/ bum pa gsang ba'i dbang bskur dang / /shes rab ye shes mngon brjod pa/ /zhes pa'i nA ro pa'i 'grel par drangs nas de dag gi don bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du/ bum pa gsang ba'i dbang bskur dang / /zhes sogs kyis dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma bzhi yang bstan pa nA ro pa'i 'grel ba'i dgongs pa yin no/ /

The text of the Great Commentary on this passage is quoted and explained in Nāropa’s commentary. The Great Commentary runs from “For the vase and the other initiations, do not leave the young mudrā for ten years” up to “The air element, being devoid of particles,[101] is not to be held. This is thereby ascertained.”[102] Moreover, when Nāropa quotes the Great Commentary from “The higher initiations are of two kinds” up to “In order to lead sentient beings, four kinds of conventional and worldly initiations are ascertained,”[103] he does this as commentary to “Initiations of vase and secret, that known as gnosis.” Similarly it is the position of Nāropa’s commentary that the lines beginning “Initiations of vase and secret” also teach the four higher-than-high initiations.

f.d:
yang bum dbang gsang dbang shes rab ye shes kyi dbang gsum po bshad zin pa'i mjug tu nA ro pa'i 'grel pa las/
'jig rten pa'i dngos grub sgrub par byed pa'i dbang rnam pa gsum mdor bstan nas 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dngos grub kyi thun mong ma yin pa dbang bcu gcig pa gsungs pa slar yang zhes pa la sogs pa'o/[91] / zhes/ slar yang shes rab chen po nyid/[92] /ces pa des 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa bstan par mdzad cing /

After explaining the vase, secret, and wisdom-knowledge initiations, Nāropa’s commentary continues:
Having briefly explained the three kinds of initiations for the accomplishment of worldly powers, the special eleventh initiation for the nonworldly powers is spoken of beginning with the words[104] “and again.”[105] This explains that the line “and again the gnosis of great insight” teaches the nonworldly fourth initiation.

d.div: [91] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 242_ba7
[92] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan/ 14_ba3
[104] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 242b7.
[105] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, 14b3.

f.d:
de'i don 'chad pa na 'grel pa de nyid las
shes rab chen po zhes pa rnam par rtog pas kun tu ma btogs pa 'chad par 'gyur ba'i phyag rgya chen mo'o/ / de'i ye shes ni de bsgoms pa las skyes pa mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po ste dbang bcu gcig pa'o/[93] / zhes gsungs shing /

On this line Nāropa’s commentary says:
“Great insight” is the mahāmudrā, which will be explained, where nothing is posited by thought. Its gnosis is the great unchanging bliss produced by meditating upon it. This is the eleventh.

d.div: [93] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 243_na1

f.d:
yang de'i 'phro nyid las
mkha' 'gro ma rdo rje gur du yang dbang bcu gcig nyid du gsungs te/[94] zhes 'tshams sbyar nas/
gur gyi rgyud phyag rdor stod 'grel du drangs pa'i/ chu yi dbang ni dang po ste/ / zhes sogs drangs nas

And later:
The Vajra Ḍākinī Tent Tantra also speaks of the eleven initiations.[106] /204/ This leads into:
The Tent Tantra is quoted in Vajrapāṇi’s commentary: “The vase initiation is the first.” And so on.

d.div: [94] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 128_ba1
[106] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 243a1.

f.d:
de'i mjug tu 'grel pa de nyid las/
de ltar de nyid rdo rje'i rab sbyor gyis zhes pas gtso bor dbang bcu gcig pa bcom ldan 'das kyis gsal por gsungs pa'i phyir mkhas pa rnams kyis dbang bzhi pa'am bcu gcig pa tha dad pa nyid du rtogs par bya'o [95] zhes gsungs pa'i/ dbang bzhi pa'am bcu gcig pa tha dad pa nyid du rtogs par bya'o zhes pa'i bzhi pa'am bcu gcig pa 'jig rten las 'das pa don dam pa'i dbang bzhi pa yin zhing / dbang bcu gcig nyid du gsungs te zhes pa'i nyid kyi nges tshig gis dbang bcu gcig tu grangs nges pa'i grangs nges kyang bstan pas rgyud rdzogs par nyan pa dang bskyed rdzogs rdzogs par sgom pa'i snod rung du byed pa la dbang gong ma'i bum dbang sogs gsum gyi mthar 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa tshig gis bskur dgos pa rgyud 'grel dang grub chen nA ro pa'i dgongs pa yin no/ /

Nāropa’s commentary continues:
“Reality is by the vajra yoga.” Primarily, the eleventh was clearly taught by the Conqueror so that the wise should understand the fourth or the eleventh initiation as being separate.[107] The fourth, or the eleventh, as mentioned in the above line “should understand the fourth or the eleventh initiation as being separate,” is the nonworldly and ultimate fourth initiation. Moreover the decisive “the” from the phrase “also speaks of the eleven initiations” is a word that determines the number of initiations to be eleven. Therefore, to become a fit vessel for listening to the whole tantra and for meditating on the generation and completion stages in their entirety, at the end of the three higher initiations of the vase and so forth, the nonworldly fourth must be given verbally. This is the thinking of the Kālacakratantra, of its commentary, and of mahāsiddha Nāropa.

d.div: [95] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 128_ba3
[107] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 128b3.

f.d:
de bzhin du sA d+hu pu tras kyang bshad de/ des mdzad pa'i dkyil chog las/
dal gyis btang bas pad+ma nas lces blangs la de kho na'i blos dam tshig gi rang bzhin byang chub kyi sems btung bar bya'o/ / 'di ni yid rnam par dag pa shes rab ye shes kyi dbang gi cho ga'i rim pa'o/ / de nas tshig dbang rin po che sbyin pa zhes bya ba'i don gyi khyad par gyi dga' ba'i mtha' ste byang chub kyi sems bsgoms pas thig le gsum gyi mthar rab tu skyes pa nyon mongs pa dang bral ba'i rang bzhin de kho na chos thams cad bsam du med pa rdo rje 'dzin pa chen po'i rang bzhin la dbang bzhi par brjod do/[96] / zhes rgyud nyan pa sogs kyi snod rung du byed pa'i dbang gong ma bum dbang sogs gsum gyi mtha' de nyid du dbang bzhi pa 'jig rten las 'das pa don dam pa'i dbang bskur bar bshad pas so/ /

Sādhuputra says the same in his Mandala Ritual:
Slowly taken by the tongue from the lotus, the mind of suchness drinks of the bodhicitta in the nature of samaya.[108] This is the purification of mind, the ritual of the initiation of the wisdom knowledge. “Then the precious word initiation is given.” After the special bliss, the bodhicitta is meditated upon and is developed after the three drops. It is totally free from all deluded thought, with no concept of any phenomena, in the nature of the great Vajradhara. This is the fourth initiation.[109] This passage explains that after the three higher initiations of the vase and so forth, which are conferred to create suitable vessels for listening to the tantra and so forth, the fourth, or nonworldly, ultimate initiation is bestowed.

d.div: [96] sde dge_1359_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pasAng+hU pu tra'i dkyil chog_142_ba6
[108] Here elemental bodhicitta is visualized as being in the nature of tantric samaya.
[109] Toh 1359 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 142b6.

f.d: des na/ de nas tshig dbang rin po che sbyin pa zhes bya ba'i don gyi khyad par gyis zhes pa 'dis dbang bzhi pa'i don tshig gis bshad nas slob ma la dbang bzhi pa'i go ba skyed pa nyid dbang bzhi pa bskur ba'i don du bshad pas kha cig /(chos rje mtshal man pa/)chos thams cad kyi gnas lugs spros pa dang bral ba'i ngang du cir yang mi rtog par mnyam par zhog ces brjod nas slob mas de ltar mi rtog par cung zad cig 'jog pa dbang bzhi pa bskur ba'i don du byed pa mi rigs par shes par bya'o/ /

Therefore the words “Then the precious word initiation is given” teach that the fourth initiation is expressed in words and that the disciples’ actual understanding of the initiation is the meaning of the fourth initiation. Therefore those (such as the dharma master Tsalmin) are incorrect who maintain that after the instruction, “to place the mind in total nonconceptuality in a state in which there is no fabrication of the actual way phenomena exist,” the disciple places his mind a little in nonconceptuality and that this is the bestowal of the fourth initiation. /205/

de la gzhan dag na re/ sA d+hu pu tras dbang gsum pa shes rab ye shes kyi mthar dbang bzhi pa'i 'jig rten las 'das pa bskur bar bshad pa de dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i shes rab ye shes kyi mtha' la dgongs pa yin no zhe na/ de ni ma yin te/ dkyil chog de nyid las gong du drangs pa/ de nas tshig dbang rin po che sbyin pa zhes bya ba'i don gyi khyad par gyi dga' ba'i mtha' ste zhes pa nas/ 'di ni rig pa'i brtul zhugs kyi cho ga'o [97] zhes pa'i bar gyis dbang gong ma gsum gyi mthar 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa yan lag dang bcas pa bskur ba bstan nas/ brtul zhugs kyi cho ga'o zhes pa'i de ma thag tu dkyil chog de nyid las/ de nas dbang thams cad thob pa dang thos pa dang bsam pa dang bsgoms pa las byung ba'i rgyud kyi don thams cad bde bar gshegs pa thams cad kyi lam dpal gyi bla ma khyod kyi bka' drin gyis ding sang shes rab zhes pa nas/ 'di ni shes rab ye shes kyi dbang bskur ba'i [98] zhes pa'i bar gyis dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i shes rab ye shes kyi dbang gi bar yan lag dang bcas pa bstan cing / de'i de ma thag tu dkyil chog de nyid las/ lhag ma rnams ni snga ma ltar ro [99] zhes gsungs pa 'dis dbang bzhi pa 'jig rten las 'das pa bskur tshul la sogs pa snod rung du byed pa'i skabs su sngar bshad pa de la kha 'phangs pa yin pas rig ma dgu la 'khyud pa'i bum dbang dang rigs dgu la brten pa'i gsang dbang dang rig ma bcu la snyoms 'jug byas pa'i shes rab ye shes kyi dbang ste dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma gsum ni snod rung gi bum dbang sogs gsum gyi mtha' 'jig rten las 'das pa'i bzhi pa bskur ba'i mjug tu bskur bar bshad pas so/ /

Others ask if Sādhuputra’s description of the nonworldly fourth bestowed after the wisdom-knowledge third initiation actually refers to the higher-than-high wisdom-knowledge third initiation. This is not so, because the lines “Then the precious word initiation is given. After the special bliss” up to “This is the ritual of the conduct of the mind”[110] teach that after the three higher initiations, the nonworldly fourth together with its appendages is given. Then, immediately after the line “This is the ritual of the conduct of the mind,” the text continues:
The receiving of every initiation, the meanings of every tantra, the path of those gone to bliss arising from hearing, thinking, and meditation, is by your kindness, glorious guru. Up to:
This is the bestowing of the wisdom-knowledge initiation.[111] These lines teach up to the higher-than-high wisdom-knowledge initiation together with its appendages. Immediately after these lines, the Mandala Ritual says: “The remaining are as the previous.”[112] This line is pointing for reference to the preceding explanation given when the nonworldly fourth initiation was conferred for the purposes of creating suitable vessels. Therefore the three higher-than-high initiations, which consist of the vase initiation in which the nine consorts are embraced, the secret initiation in which the nine consorts are relied upon, and the wisdom-knowledge initiation in which one enters union with the ten consorts, are conferred after the nonworldly fourth, which comes at the end of the three suitable-vessel-creating initiations of the vase, and so forth.

f.d: yang 'ga' zhig (rje red mda' ba/)na re/ rgyud rdzogs par nyan pa'i snod rung gi dbang la 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa dgos na/ 'grel chen las/ sems can gzhug pa'i slad du 'jig rten kun rdzob kyi dbang bzhi'i nges pa'o/ / de nas rgyas 'grel dang bcas pa'i rgyud thams cad thos shing shes par gyur ba na [100] zhes sogs kyis rgyud rdzogs par nyan pa sogs kyi snod rung du byed pa'i dbang la 'jig rten pa'i bzhi pa shes rab ye shes kyi dbang nyid la bzhi pa'i tha snyad btags pa de yan chad bskur bas chog par gsungs pa de ji ltar yin zhe na/

Some (such as the noble Rendawa) say that if the nonworldly fourth was necessary to create suitable vessels for the complete hearing of the tantra, then what does the following quote from the Great Commentary mean?
For the purpose of leading sentient beings, there are four nonultimate initiations. Then, when they have heard and learned every tantra and its commentary…[113] Does this quote not teach that in order to become fit vessels for a complete hearing of the tantra, /206/ initiations up to the worldly fourth, in which the wisdom-knowledge initiation itself is given the name of the fourth, are sufficient?

d.div: [100] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 328_ba7
[113] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 328b7.

f.d:
'grel chen gyi dngos bstan la de ltar gsungs pa bden na'ang bde mchog stod 'grel las/
dang po bum pa'i dbang yin te/ / gnyis pa gsang ba'i dbang du 'dod/ / shes rab ye shes gsum pa ste/ / bzhi pa de yang de bzhin no/[101] / zhes pa dang / de bzhin du kye'i rdo rjer yang /
slob dpon gsang ba shes rab dang / / bzhi pa de yang de bzhin no/[102] / zhes pa de ltar rgyud gzhan gnyis su dbang bskur ba bzhi ste/ zhes 'dus pa phyi ma dang kye'i rdo rje'i dbang bzhi pa ston pa rnams bshad byar bkod nas de dag gi don 'chad pa ni 'grel pa de nyid las/
'dir 'jig rten kun rdzob tu bum pas dbang bskur ba ni slob dpon gyi dbang bskur ba'o/ / gsang bar lta bas bdud rtsi myang bas gsang ba'i dbang bskur ba'o/ / las kyi phyag rgya gtad pa'i dang po gnyis las skyes par gyur pa'i bde ba rtogs pa shes rab ye shes kyi dbang bskur ba'o/ / nor bu'i nang du chud pa'i byang chub kyi sems kyi bde ba rtogs pa bzhi pa shes rab ye shes kyi dbang bskur ba'o zhes pa 'jig rten gyi bden pas drang pa'i don gyi dbang bskur ba'i cho ga rnam pa bzhi'o/[103] / zhes sbas rgyud kyis dbang bzhi dngos su bstan tshul brjod de/ bzhi pa de yang de bzhin no/ /zhes pa'i rgyud tshig des dngos su shes rab ye shes nyid bzhi bar bstan nas don dam pa 'jig rten las 'das pa'i bzhi pa sbas pa'i tshul gyis bstan pa sems 'grel skor gsum gyi dgongs pa yin la/

As far as what the words of the Great Commentary actually say, such a claim is true. However, in the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary it says:
First the vase initiation, the second is said to be the secret, gnosis the third, the fourth also is likewise.[114] In the Hevajra Tantra Also:
“The vajra master, secret, and wisdom, the fourth also is likewise.”[115] In two other tantras, therefore, there are four initiations. In this commentary the fourth initiation as taught in the Later Guhyasamāja and the Hevajra Tantra are presented as topics for explanation. The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary continues:
Here the worldly nonultimate vase initiation is the master initiation. By looking upon the secret place, nectar is experienced, and that is the secret initiation. The activity mudrā consort[116] is given, and from the two organs arises bliss. Knowledge of this is the wisdom-knowledge initiation. The bodhicitta enters the jewel. Knowledge of its bliss is the gnosis fourth. By worldly truths, therefore, these are the four rituals of the interpretive initiations.[117] Therefore it is the thinking of the Three Bodhisattva Commentaries that this quote describes how the hidden tantras literally teach the four initiations, and that the tantra line “the fourth also is likewise” literally teaches the wisdom-knowledge initiation to be the fourth while actually teaching the ultimate nonworldly fourth initiation in a concealed way.

f.d: 'grel chen gyis kyang dbang gong ma bzhi 'chad pa'i skabs su/ bzhi pa de yang de bzhin no/ /zhes pa'i dngos bstan gyi bzhi pa dngos su bshad nas/ des mtshon nas 'jig rten las 'das pa'i bzhi pa yang rgyud rdzogs par nyan pa sogs kyi snod rung du byed pa'i skabs der bskur ba 'grel chen gyi dgongs par yang byed dgos te/ gzhan du na sA d+hu pu tras de ltar bshad pa dang 'gal zhing rjes dran man chad sgom pa'i snod rung du byed pa'i dbang la shes rab ye shes kyi dbang gi bar dgos la ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag sgom pa'i snod rung du byed pa la 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa mi dgos pa'i khyad par mi 'thad pa'i phyir ro/ /

The Great Commentary also, when explaining the four higher initiations, literally teaches an actual fourth initiation, as in the line “the fourth also is likewise,” and it has to be the thinking of the Great Commentary that the nonworldly fourth initiation, which is illustrated by this worldly fourth, is also conferred at this time in order to create fit vessels for hearing the tantra in its entirety. If this were not the case, it would contradict Sādhuputra’s explanation. Moreover it cannot be correct to say that the first three initiations are necessary for creating fit vessels for the practice of the six-branched yoga up to the yoga of recollection but that the nonworldly fourth is not necessary for creating fit vessels for the meditation upon the sixth yoga of meditative concentration. /207/
gnyis pa dbang so so'i rnam gzhag bshad pa
['di ]la gnyis/ dbang gong ma'i rnam gzhag bshad pa dang / dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i rnam gzhag bshad pa'o/ /
This has two outlines: 1. A description of the higher initiations 2. A description of the higher-than-high initiations
dang po [dbang gong ma'i rnam gzhag bshad pa ]

d.i: A description of the higher initiations

f.d: ['di ]la
This has four topics: 1. The higher initiation of the vase 2. The secret initiation 3. The wisdom-knowledge initiation 4. The worldly fourth
[dang po] dbang gong ma'i bum pa'i dbang ni/

d.i: The higher initiation of the vase

f.d:
dpal ldan shes rab nu ma la yang dang por reg pa gang yin bum pa'i dbang ni de nyid do/[104] /zhes gsungs pa ltar phyag rgya mtshan nyid dang ldan pa la bla mas slob ma 'khyud pa dang nu ma la reg par byed du gzhug ste/ de ltar slob mas phyag rgya'i lus la 'khyud pa dang nu ma la reg pa la brten nas khams byang chub kyi sems lus kyi char g.yo zhing 'gyur ba las byung ba'i bde ba stong nyid dang sbyar ba'i bde stong ni bum dbang gi ngo bo dang / de yang phyag rgya'i dkar 'dzin gyi bum pa las thob pas bum pa'i dbang zhes bya zhing / slob dpon gyi dbang zhes kyang bya ste/
dgod pas dga' ba thob pa ni/ / dgod pa dag pa slob dpon nyid/[105] / ces pa ltar ro/ / de yang rig ma'i lus la brten nas thob pas lus kyi dkyil 'khor du thob pa zhes bya'o/ /

“The first touch of the breasts of glorious wisdom is the initiation of the vase.” [118] As this line indicates, the guru leads the disciple to embrace and touch the breasts of a suitably qualified mudrā consort. By embracing her body and touching her breasts, the elemental bodhicitta stirs within the body. From this bliss arises, which is applied to emptiness to become the bliss and emptiness that is the nature of the vase initiation. Because it is received from the vases of the mudrā’s breasts, it is known as the vase initiation. It is also known as the initiation of the master, as the Hevajra Tantra says:
By laughing, joy is attained. Pure laughing is the master.[119] Also, because it is obtained by relying upon the body of a wisdom woman,[120] the initiation is taken within the body mandala.

f.d: gnyis pa gsang dbang ni/

gsang ba dag las ri bong 'dzin pa myang ba dang ni lta ba dag gis gsang ba'i dbang du 'gyur/[106] /zhes gsungs pa ltar bla mas phyag rgya mtshan nyid tshang ba cig dang snyoms par zhugs pas spyi bo nas khams zhu ba d+hU tI'i lam nas phabs te nor bu'i rtser lhan cig skyes pa'i bde ba mtshon par byas pa'i bde ba'i rten du bstan pa lha [107] thams cad bla ma'i lus la bsdus pa zhu ba'i ngo bor gyur pa'i thig le de nyid mtheb srin gyis slob ma'i lce la bzhag pa myangs pa dang / mig dar bkrol nas rig ma'i pad+ma rgyas pa la bltas pa las chags pa'i 'gyur ba drag pos drangs pa'i thig le lus kyi char g.yo zhing 'gyur ba la brten nas byung ba'i bde ba stong nyid dang sbyar ba'i bde stong ni gsang dbang gi ngo bo dang / gsang dbang zhes pa rdzas gsang ba myangs pa las thob pa dang / dkyil 'khor b+ha ga'i dkyil 'khor du thob pa'o/ / de ltar yang /
lta bas dga' ba thob pa ni/ / lta ba gsang ba de bzhin no/[108] / zhes gsungs so/ /
