f.d: gsum pa shes rab ye shes kyi dbang ni/

slob mas bla mas gnang ba'i rig ma mtshan nyid tshang ba cig la man ngag bzhin du rtsa 'tshol ba byas te rnyed pa'i rtags phyung ba man ngag ltar snyoms par zhugs te las la gnas bar byas pas khams zhu ba gsang gnas kyi 'khor lo sleb pa las bde ba skyes stong nyid dang sbyar ba'i bde stong gi ye shes ni skabs 'di'i dbang gsum pa shes rab ye shes kyi dbang gi ngo bo dang / de yang shes rab ma la brten nas thob pas shes rab ye shes kyi dbang dang / kun da lta bu'i byang sems zhu ba las thob pas kun rdzob byang chub kyi sems kyi dkyil 'khor du thob pa'o/ / 'di dang 'jig rten pa'i bzhi pa gnyis rig ma la brten nas bskur ba'i tshe rig ma'i rtsa btsal dgos pa ni sA ng+hu pu tras bshad de/ de'i dkyil chog las/
g.yon pa'i g.yon gyi rtsa mdzub mo la hrIHdmar po bsams la skyod pa ni lce'i shI zhes brjod pas so [109] zhes sogs skabs 'dir bshad pas so/ /

The disciple is presented with a fully qualified wisdom woman by the guru. In accordance with his guru’s instruction, the disciple searches for her channel, and when the indications are that it has been found, he sits in union with the wisdom lady in accord with instruction. During union the element melts and arrives at the secret-place cakra. The resulting bliss is applied to emptiness to form bliss-and-emptiness gnosis. This is the third initiation of wisdom-knowledge. Because it is gained by relying upon a wisdom woman, it is known as the wisdom-knowledge initiation, and because it is gained from the melting of the jasminelike[123] bodhicitta, it is taken within the nonultimate bodhicitta mandala. When this initiation and the fourth worldly initiation are conferred using a wisdom woman, it is necessary to seek the channel of the wisdom woman. Sādhuputra mentions this in his Mandala Ritual when he says:
With the finger visualized as a red hri, the left of the consort’s channel is moved, the śī on the tongue is uttered.[124]

d.div: [109] sde dge_1359_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pasAng+hU pu tra'i dkyil chog_142_ba1
[123] kunda, as transliterated in Tibetan.

[124] g.yon pa’i g.yon gyi rtsa ’dzub mo hrīṃ dmar po bsams la skyod pa ni lce’i shī zhes brjod pas so. Kirti Tsenshap Rinpoché explains this line provisionally: the casing of the ritual bell is seen as a lotus and mentally divided into eight petals, and the bell’s “finger” strikes the left of the left petal. An explanation can also be found in the Great Exposition of Secret Mantra by Tsongkhapa, p. 375, where he explains the first g.yon pa as referring to the consort and the second as meaning “left.” There could be a play on words here. The channel is known as the Vajradhātvīśvarī channel and is found to the left of the center of the consort’s lotus. The finger is used to stimulate this channel, and the syllable śī is uttered before the main mantra. Toh 1359 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 142b1.

f.d: 'jig rten pa'i bzhi pa ni/

de ltar rig ma la snyoms 'jug byas pa las khams rdo rje'i rtser sleb pa de nyid ji tsam bzung bar nus kyi bar du bzung ba la brten pa'i lhan skyes kyi bde ba dang stong nyid sbyar ba'i bde stong gi ye shes ni 'jig rten pa'i dbang bzhi pa/ bzhi pa de yang de bzhin no/ / zhes pa'i dngos bstan drang don gyi dbang bzhi pa dang / de yang gsum pa shes rab ye shes nyid la bzhi par btags pa'o/ / de ltar yang bde mchog stod 'grel las/
nor bu'i nang du chud pa'i byang chub kyi sems kyi bde ba rtogs pa bzhi pa shes rab ye shes kyi dbang bskur ba'o/[110] / zhes gsungs pa ltar yin no/ /

From sitting in union with the wisdom woman, the element moves to the vajra tip, and for as long as the state of retention can be maintained, innate bliss arises. This bliss applied to emptiness creates the gnosis of bliss and emptiness. This is the worldly fourth initiation. The line “the fourth also is likewise” literally teaches this interpretive fourth initiation, and it is labeled the fourth within the wisdom-knowledge third. In this connection the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
The bodhicitta enters the jewel. Knowledge of its bliss is the gnosis fourth.[125] /209/

d.div: [110] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 126_ba3
[125] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 126b3.

f.d: gnyis pa dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i rnam gzhag bshad pa
16. The Higher-than-High Initiations
['di ]la gnyis/ dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i bum dbang sogs dang po gsum bshad pa dang / 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa bshad pa'o/ /
This is under two headings: 1. The first three initiations 2. The nonworldly fourth
dang po [dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i bum dbang sogs dang po gsum bshad pa ]ni/

de yang gong ma'i yang gong ma rnams ni rdo rje slob dpon bdag po nyid du byed pa'i dbang kho na la byed par 'grel chen las dngos su bshad la/[111] 'on kyang rgyud rdzogs par nyan pa sogs kyi snod rung du byed pa la yang 'jig rten pa'i gong ma gsum gyi mthar 'jig rten las 'das pa'i bzhi pa yang bskur dgos pa ni sA ng+hu pu tras bshad pa ltar byed dgos pa rgyud 'grel gyi dgongs pa yin par bshad zin pa ltar yin no/ /

Taken literally, the Great Commentary talks of the four higher-than-high initiations as being solely for the creation of the vajra-master lord.[126] However, in order to create suitable vessels for hearing the tantra in its entirety and so forth, the nonworldly fourth has to be conferred after the three worldly higher initiations. This has to be performed as explained by Sādhuputra and is the intention of the tantra and commentary as already explained.

d.div: [111] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 326_na2_327_ba3
[126] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 326a2 to 327b3.

f.d: cho ga'i rim pa rnams ni dkyil chog rnams las shes par bya zhing / 'dir dbang gsum gyi thun mong ma yin pa'i khyad par rnamasacu nga zad brjod na/ 'di'i bum dbang ni rig ma la slob dpon gyis slob ma 'khyud du gzhug pa ltar 'khyud cing nu ma la reg pa las byang chub kyi sems khu ba bdud rtsi'i rgyun gtsug gtor nas dpral ba'i rtsa 'dab bcu drug yod pa'i bar 'ongs pa'i bde ba la sku gsung thugs ye shes kyi dga' ba bzhir phye ba'i bde ba stong pa dang sbyar ba'i bde stong ye shes kyi ngo bo dang / gsang dbang ni 'khyud cing nu ma la reg pa'i rig ma de'i gsang gnas su slob ma de'i rdo rje cung zad gsor ba las byang chub kyi sems mgrin pa'i rtsa 'dab sum cu rtsa gnyis pa las snying ga'i rtsa 'dab brgyad par 'ongs pa'i bde ba la sku gsung thugs ye shes kyi mchog dga' bzhir phye ba'i bde ba dang stong nyid sbyar ba'i bde stong gi ye shes kyi ngo bo dang / shes rab ye shes kyi dbang ni rig ma'i gsang gnas su rdo rje gsor ba de nyid drag por bskyod pa las lte ba'i rtsa 'dab drug cu rtsa bzhi pa las gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'dab sum cu rtsa gnyis bar byang chub kyi sems 'ongs shing khu ba shin tu dwangs pa zhu zhing g.yo ba rdo rje nor bu'i bu ga'i mthar thug par bgrod pa las byung ba'i bde ba la sku gsung thugs ye shes kyi khyad par gyi dga' ba bzhir bye ba'i bde ba stong nyid dang sbyar ba'i bde stong gi ye shes te dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i dang po gsum gyi bshad tshul gcig ste/

The rituals and their order can be known from the texts on mandala rituals, so here I will just mention a few of the special characteristics of the first three initiations. In this vase initiation the disciple embraces the wisdom woman as encouraged by the guru and touches her breasts. From this action the nectar stream of the bodhicitta fluid descends from the crown to the sixteen petals of the forehead cakra. The resulting bliss divides into the joys of body, speech, mind, and gnosis. This is applied to emptiness to create the gnosis of bliss and emptiness. In the secret initiation the disciple’s vajra slightly penetrates the secret place of the wisdom woman he has embraced and whose breasts he has touched. This causes the bodhicitta to descend from the thirty-two petals of the throat cakra to the eight petals of the heart cakra. The resultant bliss divides into the supreme joys of body, speech, mind, and gnosis, which is applied to emptiness to create the gnosis of bliss and emptiness. In the wisdom-knowledge initiation the vajra enters the secret place of the wisdom woman. From its vigorous movement bodhicitta moves down from the sixty-four petals of the navel cakra to the thirty-two petals of the secret-place cakra. /210/ The very clear semen is liquid and moves to the opening of the vajra jewel. The resulting bliss divides into the special joys of body, speech, mind, and gnosis, which is applied to emptiness to create the gnosis of bliss and emptiness. This is one way of describing the first three higher-than-high initiations.

'di dag ni dbang mdor bstan las/
shes rab nu mar yan lag ni/ / reg pas byang chub sems 'pho'i bde/ / 'o ma 'dzin pas dbang bskur ba/ / gang las bde thob de byis pa/ / yun ring gsang bar spros las skyes/ / byang chub sems ni 'pho ba'i bde/ / gsang ba'i dbang bskur gsang ba ni/ / gang las bde thob de dar ma/ / yun ring gsang bar spros las skyes/ / rdo rje rtse mor g.yo ba'i bde/ / shes rab ye shes dbang bskur ba/ / gang las g.yo ba'i bgrod de rgan/[112] / zhes pa rnams kyi don rje nA ro pa'i 'grel pas bshad pa ltar bkod pa ste/

A Short Teaching on Initiations states:
By touching the breasts of wisdom comes the bliss of moving bodhicitta. Initiation is by the breasts,[127] from its bliss it is conferred. This is the child. From moving to the secret place, the bliss of moving bodhicitta and the initiation of the secret. From its bliss is it conferred. This is the youth. From moving to the secret place, the moving bliss at the vajra tip, the initiation of wisdom-knowledge, from which comes movement and travel. This is the adult.[128] I have presented above the meaning of these lines according to the venerable Nāropa’s commentary,

d.div: [112] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan/ 14_ba1
[127] ’o ma ’dzin pa. Literally, “holders of milk.”
[128] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, 14b1.

f.d:
rgyud tshig de dag ni nA ro pa'i 'grel pa las/
shes rab ces pa lo bcu gnyis ma nas brtsams te lo nyi shu ma'i bar du ste/ dbang bskur bas na rang gi sems dga' ba'i skal pa dang ldan ma de yi nu mar yan lag ni reg pas byang chub sems 'pho zhes pa gtsug tor gyi pad+ma 'dab ma bzhi pa las zhu ba bdud rtsi'i rgyun dpral ba'i pad+ma 'dab ma bcu drug pa'i bar 'ongs pas sku'i dga' ba dang gsung gi dga' ba dang thugs kyi dga' ba dang ye shes kyi dga' ba'i bdag nyid kyi bde ba nyams su myong bar byed pa gang yin pa de ni byis pa ste rnal 'byor ma'i 'o ma 'dzin pas dbang bskur ba ni dbang dang po thob pa nyid kyi phyir byis pazhes brjod do/ /

which says:
The “wisdom” is a woman from the age of twelve to twenty. By conferring initiation she is the giver of the mind’s joy. By touching her breasts, “comes the bliss of moving bodhicitta.” This means that the stream of molten nectar moves from the four petals of the crown lotus to the sixteen petals of the forehead lotus. This produces the experience of bliss whose nature is bodily joy, the joy of speech, the joy of the mind, and the joy of gnosis. This is the child. Initiation is bestowed by the breasts of the yoginī. This is the first initiation and so is known as the child.

de nas de'i gsang bar cung zad rdo rje gsor bas byang chub sems ni 'pho ba zhes pa mgrin pa'i pad+ma 'dab ma sum cu rtsa gnyis pa las snying ga'i pad+ma 'dab ma brgyad pa'i lte bar sku'i mchog dga' dang gsung gi mchog dga' dang thugs kyi mchog dga' dang ye shes kyi mchog dga'i bdag nyid kyi bde ba nyams su myong bar byed pa gang yin pa de ni snga ma las khyad par du gyur ba nyid kyi phyir dar ma ste gsang ba'i dbang bskur ba'o/ /

Then the vajra slightly penetrates her secret place to produce “the bliss of moving bodhicitta.” This means that it moves from the throat lotus of thirty-two petals to the center of the heart lotus of eight petals to create the experience of bliss whose nature is supreme bodily joy, supreme joy of speech, supreme joy of the mind, and supreme joy of gnosis. This, because it is higher than the previous joy, is known as the “youth,” and is the secret initiation.

de nas drag por bskyod pas g.yo ba'i bgrod ces pa lte ba'i pad ma 'dab ma drug cu rtsa bzhi pa las gsang ba'i pad+ma 'dab ma sum cu rtsa gnyis par bgrod pa dang / khu ba thig le'i cha bco lnga'i rtse mo shin tu dwangs pa'i zhu ba g.yo ba rdo rje nor bu'i bu ga'i mthar thug par bgrod pas kyang chen po ste sku'i khyad par dga' ba dang gsung gi khyad par dga' ba dang thugs kyi khyad par dga' ba dang ye shes kyi khyad par dga' ba'i bdag nyid bde ba nyams su myong bar byed pa gang yin pa de ni rgan po ste shes rab ye shes kyi dbang bskur ba'o/[113] /zhes gsungs so/ /

Then vigorous motion produces “movement and travel,” which means traveling from the navel cakra of sixty-four petals to the secret cakra of thirty-two petals. /211/ The molten drops of fluid, in fifteen parts whose tips are very clear, travel to the very opening of the vajra jewel, producing the experience of bliss whose nature is the special bodily joy, special joy of speech, special joy of the mind, and special joy of gnosis. This is the “adult” and the initiation of wisdom-knowledge.[129]

d.div: [113] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel bshad don dam bsdus pa/ 243_na6
[129] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 243a6.

f.d: gzhan yang rtsa 'khor gong ma rnams nas 'og ma rnams su byang sems rim gyis 'bab pa'i tshul la dpral ba'i rtsa 'khor nas snying ga'i rtsa 'khor du 'bab pa'i mchog dga'i ye shes la gsang dbang dang / snying ga nas gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'khor du sleb pa'i khyad par gyi dga' ba shes rab ye shes kyi dbang dang / slar yang gsang gnas nas 'ongs te rdo rje nor bu'i rtser sleb pa'i lhan skyes kyi bde stong shes rab ye shes kyi dbang dngos gzhi yin pa sogs/ shes rab nu mar yan lag ni/ /reg pas byang chub sems 'pho'i bde/[114] /zhes sogs kyi don du 'chad pa ni legs bshad do/ /

Nevertheless to explain the secret initiation as being the supreme-joy gnosis produced from bodhicitta falling from the throat cakra to the heart cakra, the wisdom-knowledge initiation as being the special joy produced by the descent from the heart cakra to the secret cakra, and the actual wisdom-knowledge initiation as being the innate bliss applied to emptiness formed from the fluid arriving at the tip of the vajra jewel, is a good explanation[130] of the lines beginning “By touching the breasts of wisdom comes the bliss of moving bodhicitta.”[131]

d.div: [114] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan/ 14_ba5

[130] This is how Tsongkhapa’s disciple Gyaltsap Jé explains these lines in his Abbreviated Explanation of The Six-Branched Yoga of Kālacakra, but here the author has explained them according to Nāropa’s commentary.
[131] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, 14b5.

f.d:
nA ro pas de ltar bshad pa rnams rgyud tshig de rnams kyi don ji lta ba bzhin yin pa 'di nyid bde mchog stod 'grel las kyang bshad do/ /de dag kyang dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i dbang du byas pa yin pa ni/ de nyid las 'jig rten pa'i dbang gong ma bzhi bshad zin pa'i mjug tu/ don dam pas ni slar yang 'di phyin ci log pa dang don med pa'o [115] zhes sogs kyis de dag don dam pa min par bshad pa'i mjug tu na de nyid las/
'dir rgyud gzhan dang dgongs pa'i skad gzhan dang nges pa'i don gyis slar yang bum pa'i sgras bstan pa brjod de de la reg pa la 'gyur ba'i bde ba gang yin pa de ni bum pa'i dbang bskur ba'o/ / gsang bar rdo rje spros pa las 'gyur ba'i bde ba gang yin pa de ni gsang ba'i dbang bskur ba'o/ / dbang po gnyis snyoms par zhugs pa na gang zhig 'dzag pa'i bde ba de ni shes rab ye shes kyi dbang bskur ba'o/ / phyag rgya chen po rjes su chags pas gang zhig 'gyur ba med pa'i bde ba de ni bzhi pa de yang de bzhin gyi dbang bskur ba'o/ / de ltar 'gyur ba dang / 'gyur ba dang / 'dzag pa dang / 'gyur ba med pa'i dbye bas dbang bskur rnam pa bzhi'o/ / 'dis dbang bskur bar byed pa ni dbang ste [116] zhes bshad nas

Nāropa’s explanation of these lines from the tantra is also that of the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary, whose explanation is also made on the basis of these initiations being higher-than-high initiations. This is so because after its explanation of the higher worldly fourth initiation, this commentary, referring to these initiations, says “The ultimate is to come; these are deluded and not ultimate.”[132] The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary continues:
Here, using different language from other tantras and with a meaning that is definitive, it is taught again using the name “vase.” The changing bliss that arises from touching is the initiation of the vase. The changing bliss arising from the vajra approaching the secret is the initiation of the secret. When the two organs dwell together to produce the bliss of the descending fluid, this is the initiation of wisdom-knowledge. The unchanging bliss formed by desire for the mahāmudrā is the initiation described in the line “the fourth also is likewise.” Therefore the four initiations are differentiated as “changing, changing, falling, and unchanging.”[133] /212/ In this way initiation is conferred. These are the initiations.

d.div: [115] sde dge_1402_bka'/ rgyud 'grel/ bamangon par brjod pa 'bum pa/ 126_ba3
[116] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ bamangon par brjod pa 'bum pa/ 126_ba5
[132] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 126b3.
[133] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 126b5.

f.d:
de dag gi shes byed du/
mchog gi dang po'i sangs rgyas su gsungs pa/ dang por dbang bskur bdun po gang /[117] / zhes sogs dang /
bum pa gsang ba'i dbang bskur dang / / zhes pa nas/
lus ngag sems ni dag par byed/[118] / ces pa'i bar gyi dbang mdor bstan gyi rgyud drangs nas bshad do/ /

As reference for the above, the commentary quotes A Short Teaching on Initiations:
As spoken of in the Supreme Original Buddha, “First, the seven initiations.”[134] And:
“The initiations of the vase and the secret,” up to
“Purification of body, speech, and mind.”[135]

d.div: [117] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan/ 14_na6
[118] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan/ 14_ba3
[134] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, 14a6.
[135] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, 14b3.

f.d:
'di lta bu'i gsang dbang dang shes rab ye shes kyi dbang dngos dbang du bskur ba rab byung la mi rung ba la dgongs nas dpal ldan a ti shas lam sgron las/
dang po'i sangs rgyas rgyud chen las/ / rab tu 'bad pas bkag pa'i phyir/ / gsang ba shes rab dbang bskur ni/ / tshangs par spyod pas blang mi bya/ / gal te dbang bskur de 'dzin na/ / tshangs spyod dka' thub la gnas pas/ / bkag pa spyad par gyur pa'i phyir/ / dka' thub sdom pa de nyams te/ / brtul zhugs can de pham pa yi/ / ltung ba dag ni byung gyur cing / / de ni ngan song nges ltung bas/ / grub pa nam yang yong ma yin/[119] / zhes gsungs pa yin te/

Actual initiations of secret and wisdom-knowledge as described here are not suitable for the ordained. With this in mind the glorious Atiśa says in his Light on the Path:
Because it is forcefully forbidden in the great tantra of the Original Buddha, the secret and wisdom-knowledge initiation should not be taken by those of brahma conduct.[136] If such initiations are taken within the asceticism of the brahmacarya, it becomes forbidden conduct. The vows of asceticism will weaken, becoming a downfall for those of disciplined behavior, they fall certainly to lower realms, with never a chance of attainment.[137]

d.div: [119] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_byang chub lam gyi sgron ma/ 240_ba7
[136] brahmacarya. Celibacy.
[137] Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 240b7.

f.d: rdzas gsang ba myang ba'i gsang dbang bskur ba tsam gyis/ brtul zhugs can de pham pa yi/ /ltung ba dag ni byung gyur cing / /zhes gsungs pa'i pham pa mi 'byung bas so/ /
By merely experiencing the secret substances of the secret initiation, the downfall mentioned in the line “becoming a downfall for those of disciplined behavior” will not occur.

gzhan yang dbang gong ma'i yang gong ma dang po gsum ni phyag rgya dgu la 'khyud cing nu ma la reg pa las byung ba'i bde ba stong nyid dang sbyar ba'i bde stong gi ye shes ni bum dbang gi ngo bo dang / phyag rgya lo bcu gnyis ma nas nyi shu ma'i bar dgu la bla mas snyoms par zhugs shing shes rab ma'i nar nA si ka rtsa dbu ma'i mas sna ba zhib par byas nas khams byang chub kyi sems theg le dang bcas pa'i rdo rje slob ma lam gyi sems rgyud dag par byas pa de'i khar bcug nas byang sems 'phang bar bya zhing de ltar 'phangs ba'i byang chub kyi sems myangs ba las byung ba'i bde stong sbyar ba'i ye shes ni gsang dbang gi ngo bo dang / dang por rang gi chung ma la snyoms par 'jug pa nas lo bcu gnyis ma nas nyi shu ma'i bar dgu po gang dang gang la 'dod pa spyod par nus pa rnams la snyoms 'jug byed pa ste mtshan phyed nas chu tshod gnyis na nyi ma 'char ba de srid du'o/ / de ltar snyoms par zhugs pa las byung ba'i bde stong gi ye shes ni shes rab ye shes kyi dbang gi ngo bo yin no/ /

Furthermore the vase initiation consists of bliss arising from embracing the nine mudrās and from touching the breasts, which is then applied to emptiness to produce the gnosis of bliss and emptiness. The secret initiation consists of the guru sitting in sexual union with the nine mudrās, whose ages range from twelve to twenty, and sucking the naranāsika,[138] or lower tip of the wisdom woman’s central channel. The vajra containing the elemental bodhicitta drops is placed in the mouth of the disciple, whose mindstream of practice has been purified. The bodhicitta is ejected, and the bliss arising from the experience of the ejected bodhicitta is applied to emptiness, producing bliss-and-emptiness gnosis. The wisdom-knowledge initiation consists of first sitting in sexual union with one’s wife and then with those mudrās from among the nine twelve- to twenty-year-olds with whom one is able to perform the act of union, from the middle watch of the night for two hours until the sun rises.[139] /213/ The bliss of this union is applied to emptiness to produce bliss-and-emptiness gnosis.

d.div: [138] As transliterated in Tibetan.

[139] A possible explanation of this could be that a complete day from dawn to dawn is divided into twelve watches of five “hours” each. From the middle watch of the night until dawn therefore is fifteen hours, with another five hours to sunrise. Therefore two hours are spent with one’s wife and two hours with each of the nine mudrās.

f.d: de ltar bshad pa'i dbang gong ma dang gong ma'i yang gong ma'i dbang bskur tshul rnams ni khyim pa la dbang de rnams dngos dbang du bskur ba'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi/ dge slong sogs rab tu byung ba la ni mos pa yid byed tsam gyis dbang don ngo 'phrod nges su byas nas bskur dgos pa yin te/ dge slong rdo rje 'dzin pa sdags 'chang rnams kyi mchog tu yang yang gsungs shing / dge slong dang dge tshul sogs la 'dir bshad pa'i thun mong ma yin pa'i gsang dbang dang shes rab ye shes kyi dbang dngos dbang du bskur na bslab pa las nyams par 'gyur bas so/ /

This explanation of the ways to confer the higher and higher-than-high initiations is made on the basis that these are actual initiations to be given to laypeople. For fully ordained monks and other monastics, however, these initiations are to be conferred by using just the imagination to introduce them to the real significance of the initiation. Vajradhara said again and again that the fully ordained monk is the best of mantra practitioners, and if a fully ordained or novice monk were to actually take the particular secret and wisdom-knowledge initiations as described above, they would fall from their precepts.
gnyis pa 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa bshad pa

['di ]la gsum/ skabs 'dir bstan dus kyi 'khor lo nas gsungs pa'i dbang bzhi pa bshad pa dang / sbas rgyud rnams kyi dgongs pa grub chen rnams kyis bkral ba'i dbang bzhi pa ngos gzung ba dang / de gnyis phan tshun dod thub [120] yin tshul bshad pa'o/ /
This is under three headings: 1. The fourth as taught in the Kālacakra 2. The fourth initiation in the hidden tantras as taught by the mahāsiddhas 3. How these two are interchangeable

d.div: [120] ma dper dor thub gsal na'ang dod thub yin nam snyam/

f.d: dang po [dus kyi 'khor lo nas gsungs pa'i dbang bzhi pa bshad pa ]ni

d.i: The fourth as taught in the Kālacakra

f.d:
ye shes le'u'i brgya bcu gnyis pa'i 'grel chen las/
dgod pa dang lta ba dang lag pa bcang ba dang gnyis gnyis sbyor ba zhes pa dbang rnam pa bzhi ni de kho na nyid du mi 'gyur ro/ / 'dir de kho na nyid ni gnyis gnyis 'khyud pa med pa ste las kyi phyag rgya'i rgyu las skyes pa ni rnam par dpyad na gnyis su med pa'i ye shes su mi 'gyur ro/[121] zhes de kho na nyid 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa ni gnyis su med pa'i ye shes su gsungs la/ gnyis su med rgyu'i gnyis ni stong pa dang bde ba la rgyud 'grel gnyis ka las yang yang bshad cing / stong pa yang bden stong tsam ma yin gyi rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong gzugs dang / bde ba yang bde ba khyad par can mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po ste/ stong gzugs yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can gyi sku dang mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde stong gi ye shes ngo bo dbyer med pa'i zung 'jug de nyid dbang bzhi pa yin la/

The Great Commentary on verse 112 of the Gnosis chapter says:
Laughing, looking, holding hands, and joining together: these four kinds of initiation do not become suchness. Here suchness is not found within the embrace. That resulting from an activity mudrā, if examined, does not become nondual gnosis.[140] In this passage suchness, or the nonworldly fourth, is referred to as nondual gnosis. The duality that becomes nondual in the term nonduality refers to emptiness and bliss, and this is explained again and again by the tantra and the commentary. Emptiness does not only refer to an emptiness of true existence but to “empty form endowed with every supreme aspect.”[141] Bliss also refers to a special bliss known as great unchanging bliss. /214/ Empty form in its aspect of father and mother in union indivisibly united with the gnosis of supreme unchanging bliss and emptiness is the fourth initiation.

d.div: [121] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 387_ba4
[140] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 387b4.
[141] rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong gzugs.

f.d:
de yang de'i bde ba mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba la byed dgos pa ni ye shes le'u tshigs bcad brgya bcu bzhi pa las/
de las mya ngan 'das pa'i bde ba 'pho med lhan cig skyes pa 'gyur med nyid ni bzhi pa ste/[122] zhes gsungs shing /

This bliss has to be unchanging bliss, because the Great Commentary says on verse 114 of the Gnosis chapter:
From that arises the bliss beyond sorrow, unmoving, innate, unchanging. This is the fourth.[142]

d.div: [122] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ khams kyi le'u/ 1_sh+loka114_113_na1
[142] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, ye shes v. 114, 113a1.

f.d:
stong pa yang de'i 'grel par/
las kyi phyag rgya dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya'i rgyu dang bral ba stong pa nyid rnam pa thams cad pa rab tu gsal ba'i mtshan nyid do/[123] zhes rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong gzugs la gsal bar gsungs so/ /

Concerning the emptiness also, the commentary states:
The emptiness not produced by activity mudrā and wisdom mudrā is one clearly endowed with every aspect.[143] This clearly talks of empty form endowed with every supreme aspect.

d.div: [123] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 388_na6
[143] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 388a6.

f.d:
gzhan yang khams le'i mdor bsdus dang po las/
mchog tu mi 'gyur bzhi pa de nyid ni/ / sangs rgyas rnams kyi shes rab ye shes te/[124] / zhes pa 'dis/ bzhi pa de yang de bzhin no/ /zhes gsungs pa'i bzhi pa zhes pa'i bstan don mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba bstan pa dang /

Furthermore, in the first summary of the Realms chapter, the Great Commentary says:
The supreme and unchanging fourth is the gnosis of the buddhas.[144] This explains that “the fourth” from the line “The fourth also is likewise” refers to the supreme and unchanging bliss.

d.div: [124] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 4_ba1
[144] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 4b1.

f.d: gang zhig de ni slar yang de bzhin 'dis/ / rang gi phyag rgya chen mor rgyal bas gsungs/[125] / zhes pa 'dis/ de bzhin zhes pa'i bstan don rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong gzugs bstan pa'i sgo nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde stong dang stong gzugs ngo bo dbyer med dbang bzhi bar bstan pa yin no/ /

The Great Commentary continues:
That which again is likewise, was taught by the Buddha to be one’s mahāmudrā.[145] This teaches that the term likewise refers to empty form endowed with every supreme aspect, and that the inseparability of empty form with unchanging bliss and emptiness is the fourth initiation.

d.div: [125] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 4_ba1
[145] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 4b1.

f.d:
gzhan yang dbang mdor bstan gyi nA ro pa'i 'grel pa las/
phyag rgya chen po zhes pa nam mkha' las byung ba'i gzugs te de'i rjes chags phyi rol rang gi nyams su myong ba sgom pa zhes bya ba las skyes pa g.yo med ces pa rdo rje nor bu las phyi rol du g.yo ba las 'dzag pa 'gog pa sku'i lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba dang gsung gi lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba dang thugs kyi lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba dang ye shes kyi lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba'i bdag nyid zla ba bdud rtsi mi 'pho ba'i bde ba gang yin pa de ni shes rab ye shes chen po zhes bya ba dbang bskur ba bzhi pa ste/ bzhi pa de yang de bzhin no/ /zhes pa'i gsung gis brjod pa'o/ / 'di ni sgrib pa med pa 'jig rten las 'das pa'i ye shes lhag par rtogs pa des grub pa'i ros zangs la sogs pa'i khams rnams gser gyi ngo bo bzhin du sgrib pa dang bcas pa'i phung po dang khams lnga la sogs pa rnams de bzhin gshegs pa lnga dang lha mo lnga la sogs pa skye dgu'i ngo bos rdzogs par byed pa nyid kyi phyir skye dgu'i bdag po'o/[126] /

Furthermore, in Nāropa’s Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations, he says:
The mahāmudrā is of a form arising from space. From one’s meditational experience arising from the subsequent desire for this form comes the “unmoving.” This means that emission is prevented and does not move beyond the vajra jewel. The bliss of nonemission of the moon nectar in the form of the innate bodily joy, the innate joy of speech, the innate joy of mind, and the innate joy of gnosis is the great wisdom-knowledge and is the conferring of the fourth initiation as taught by the words “The fourth also is likewise.” This is the unobstructed and nonworldly gnosis of great insight, whose taste changes the obstructed aggregates, the five spheres and so forth, into the five tathāgatas, the five goddesses, and so forth as copper is changed into gold. This is the completed development of a sentient being and is, therefore, known as the master of sentient beings.[146] /215/

d.div: [126] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel bshad don dam bsdus pa/ 243_ba2
[146] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 243b2.

f.d:
zhes gsungs pa 'di dag ni/
phyag rgya chen po rjes chags las/ / skyes pa g.yo med bde ba ni/ / shes rab chen po'i dbang bskur ba/ / gang las g.yo med rtogs pa ste/ / skye dgu'i bdag por rnam shes bya/[127] / zhes pa'i 'grel pa yin la/

The above is commentary to the verses:
From desire for the great mudrā arises the unmoving bliss, the initiation of the great wisdom, from which comes the unmoving insight known as the master of sentient beings.[147]

d.div: [127] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan/ 14_ba6
[147] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, na, 14b6.

f.d: rtsa 'grel 'di rnams kyis ni nam mkha' las byung ba'i gzugs rjes dran gyi skabs su stong gzugs yab yum dngos gnas la grub pa'i yum sna tshogs yum gyi rnam pa can la rjes su chags pa'i rnal 'byor pa rang gi nyams myong bsgoms pa las skyes pa zla ba bdud rtsi byang chub kyi sems rdo rje nor bu las mi 'pho ba'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba la sku'i lhan skyes sogs bzhir phye ba'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba dang po de 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi par bstan la/ de ltar bstan pa nyid kyis mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya'i thog ma dang por thob pa ting nge 'dzin gi yan lag dang por thob pa nas dbang bzhi pa'i ya mtha' 'jog pa yin no/ /

This root text and commentary explains that in the branch of recollection, “form arising from space” refers to an actual mother-and-father empty form, for the mother of which, in her form of Viśvamātā, the yogi develops desire. From his meditation experience arises the unchanging bliss of the moon-nectar bodhicitta not being emitted from the vajra jewel. This is divided into the four joys of body and so forth, and this initial unchanging bliss is the nonworldly fourth initiation. From this explanation it can be understood that the initial attainment of the first of the 21,600 instances of bliss, from the beginning of the branch of meditative concentration, is the lower limit of the fourth initiation.

de lta bu'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'di ring du bsgoms pa las sgrib pa med pa 'jig rten las 'das pa'i ye shes lhag par rtogs pa des grub pa'i ros zangs la sogs pa gser du sgyur ba bzhin du sgrib pa dang bcas pa'i phung po lnga khams lnga la sogs pa gshegs pa lnga gshegs ma lnga la sogs pa skye dgu'i ngo bor rjogs par byed pa nyid kyi phyir dbang bzhi pa la skye dgu'i bdag po zhes bya'o/ /zhes bshad do/ /

From sustained meditative development of this unchanging bliss there arises an unobstructed and nonworldly gnosis of great insight. The taste of this development completes the transformation of the five obscured aggregates, the five spheres, and so forth into sentient beings who are the nature of the five male and five female tathāgatas and so forth, as copper is changed into gold. The fourth initiation, therefore, is known as the master of sentient beings.

'o na 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba kho na la 'jog gam snyam na/ de ni dbang bzhi pa'i cha shas yin pas dbang bzhi pa zhes rjod pa yin gyi dbang bzhi pa yongs rdzogs ni gong du bshad pa ltar mi 'gyur ba'i bde stong gi ye shes dang rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong gzugs ngo bo dbyer med pa'i zung 'jug la 'jog pa nA ro pa'i 'grel pa'i dgongs pa yang yin te/

But is the nonworldly fourth identified solely with unchanging bliss? It is part of the fourth initiation and therefore is called the fourth, but the complete fourth initiation is, as explained above, the gnosis of unchanging bliss and emptiness indivisibly united with the empty form endowed with every supreme aspect. This is also the thinking of Nāropa’s commentary.

'grel pa drangs ma thag pa de'i 'phro nyid las/
mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i ye shes kyi rnal 'byor dang ldan pa'i lus la sogs pa'i rnam par gzhag pa ste/ dpal dus kyi 'khor lor gsungs pa/ lus ni dwangs shing rdul phran nyams pa nam mkha' dang mtshungs mtshan la sogs pa rnams kyis rab rdzogs 'gyur/ / sna tshogs 'jig rten gsum po nyid ni dwangs shing sgrib pa rnam par bral ba rmi lam bzhin du snang / / skad ni kun nas chad pa ming cing du ma'i skad gzhan dag gis gzhan gyi snying la 'jug pa ste/ / sems ni dam pa'i bde bas gang zhing mi g.yo thams cad dus su lhan cig skyes pas 'khyud pa'o/ /

The previous quote continues:
A presentation of the body and the yoga of the supreme and unchanging gnosis is spoken of in the Glorious Kālacakra: “The body is of clarity, devoid of atoms, like the sky, well completed by the signs and so forth. The three worlds are free of obscuration, like appearances in a dream. “Speech is completely unbroken, in languages of many, entering the hearts of others. Mind is full of the highest bliss, unmoving, at all times embraced by the innate.”[148] /216/

d.div: [148] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 243b6.

f.d: zhes mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i ye shes kyi rnal 'byor dang lus te sku tshogs pa de dbang bzhi par bshad nas/[128] de'i lus dang bde ba'i sems dang de gnyis lhan cig tu tshogs pa'i tshul rgyud nyid kyis 'chad par bzhed nas ye shes le'u tshigs bcad brgya re bzhi pa/ lus ni dwangs shing [129] zhes sogs drangs pa yin no/ / de la/ lus ni dwangs shing rdul phran nyams pa zhes sogs kyis 'bras dus kyi sangs rgyas kyi sku gsung thugs ngos bzung ba na dwangs shing thogs pa med pa nam mkha' dang mtshungs shing rdul phran ba dang bral ba'i stong gzugs mtshan dang dpe byad kyis brgyan pa sku dang mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba thugs su gsungs pa nyid la dgongs te lus stong gzugs ye shes kyi sku dang thugs mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba stong nyid la ro gcig tu zhugs pa gnyis ngo bo dbyer med du zung 'jug tu chud pa de dbang bzhi pa yin pa'i shes byed du/ lus ni dwangs shing zhes sogs kyi rgyud drangs pas so/ /

Having explained the “yoga of the supreme and unchanging gnosis” and the “body,” or enlightened form, to be the fourth initiation, Nāropa states that this body and this mind of bliss, together with the way they are united, are explained in the tantra. He then quotes verse 164 of the Gnosis chapter of the Condensed Tantra beginning, “The body is of clarity.”[149] These verses are saying that when the resultant body, speech, and mind of a buddha is identified, the clear empty form, obstruction-free like space, devoid of atoms, adorned with the signs and features,[150] is the body of a buddha and the unchanging bliss is the mind of a buddha. With this in mind Nāropa quotes the above verses, beginning “The body is of clarity, devoid of atoms,” to show that the “body,” which is an empty-form gnosis body indivisibly united with the mind of unchanging bliss inseparably absorbed into emptiness, is the fourth initiation.

d.div: [128] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel don dam bsdus pa/ 243_ba6
[129] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ khams kyi le'u/ 1_sh+loka164_118_na3
[149] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud ka, ye shes v. 164, 118a3.
[150] The eighty signs or major marks and the 112 features or minor marks.

f.d: mdor na dbang bzhi pa 'jig rten las 'das pa ni ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag thob ma thag pa'i gnas skabs kyi mi 'gyur ba'i bde stong gi ye shes dang yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can gyi stong gzugs ngo bo dbyer med kyi zung 'jug nas bzung ste sangs rgyas kyi zung 'jug gi bar gyi 'gyur med kyi bde stong gi ye shes dang stong gzugs ngo bo dbyer med kyi zung 'jug thams cad la 'jog pa sems 'grel skor gsum dgongs 'grel dang bcas pa'i dgongs pa yin no/ /

To summarize, the nonworldly fourth initiation begins from the achievement of empty form in the aspect of mother and father in embrace indivisibly united with the unchanging bliss-and-emptiness gnosis gained from the first moment of the branch of meditative concentration and continues up to the union of buddhahood. In this way every instance of unchanging bliss and emptiness indivisibly united with empty form can be posited as the fourth initiation. This is the thinking of the Three Bodhisattva Commentaries and other commentaries.
gnyis pa sbas rgyud rnams kyi dgongs pa grub chen rnams kyi bkral ba'i dbang bzhi pa ngos bzung ba ni/

d.i: The fourth initiation in the hidden tantras as explained by the mahāsiddhas

f.d:
dbang bzhi pa'i don mthar thug pa ni mi slob pa'i zung 'jug dag pa'i sgyu ma'i sku dang bde stong gi ye shes mthar thug pa'i 'od gsal gyi ye shes ngo bo dbyer med pa'i kha sbyor yan lag bdun ldan de yin no/ / yan lag bdun ni ngag dbang grags pas/
longs spyod rdzogs dang kha sbyor bde chen rang bzhin med/ / snying rjes yongs gang rgyun mi 'chad dang 'gog pa med/ / yan lag bdun bshad [130] ces pa ltar mtshan dpes spras pa'i longs sku dang / de yang yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can gyi kha sbyor dang / rgya che ba zag pa med pa rgya nom pa de yang 'khor ba ji srid du gnas pa'i bde chen dang / de yang bden par med pas rang bzhin med pa dang / snying rje chen pos sems can thams cad la khyab pas snying rjes nges par gang ba dang / longs sku de rgyun mi 'chad du 'byung bas rgyun mi 'chad pa dang / sprul sku rnams rgyun mi 'chad pa yin na'ang snang ba yang yang sdud pa dang mi 'dra bar longs sku de nyid nam mkha' ma zhig bar du snang ba sdud mi srid pas 'gog pa med pa'o/ /

The ultimate meaning of the fourth initiation is the union at the stage of no further practice where the pure illusory body is indivisibly united with the ultimate clear-light bliss-and-emptiness gnosis. This is the seven-limbed embrace. Vāgiśvarakīrti explains the seven limbs as follows:
The complete enjoyment body, the embrace, great bliss, of no nature, filled with compassion, unending, and unceasing.[151] /217/ These seven characteristics of the enjoyment body are: being adorned with the signs and features of enlightenment; being in the aspect of father-and-mother embrace; a great bliss that is unsullied, vast, of the highest quality, and in existence for as long as samsara exists; not truly existing and therefore of no nature; filled with compassion because it is a great compassion that pervades all sentient beings; unending, in that its continuity is never broken; and unceasing, because although emanated bodies are unending also, their appearance is transitory, whereas the appearance of the enjoyment body cannot possibly vanish until the destruction of space itself.

d.div: [130] sde dge_1888_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pi_yan lag bdun ldan ma/ 190_na4
[151] Seven Features, Toh 1888 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, bi, 190a4.

f.d: de lta bu'i mi slob pa'i zung 'jug dbang bzhi par bshad pa de yang dbang bzhi pa'i gtso bo la dgongs pa yin gyi/ gzhan du na rim pa bzhi pa'i don gyi 'od gsal dag pa'i sgyu ma'i skur bzhengs pa'i dag pa'i sgyu ma'i sku dang don gyi 'od gsal ngo bo dbyer med du tshogs pa'i slob pa'i zung 'jug rnams kyang dbang bzhi pa 'jig rten las 'das pa yin no/ /

This explanation of the union at the level of no further practice as being the fourth initiation is made on the basis of the primary or highest level of fourth initiation. Other than that, indivisible unions of the pure illusory body and the actual clear light at the level of the practitioner in which the clear light of the fourth stage[152] arises in the form of the pure illusory body, are also nonworldly fourth initiations.

d.div: [152] Fourth of the five stages of the completion stage, as taught in other tantras.

f.d: gal te mi slob pa'i zung 'jug gi sku de la kha sbyor sogs yan lag bdun tshang du chug mod/ yan lag bdun ldan de dbang bzhi pa yin pa la shes byed ci yod snyam na/
It may be that the body of the union at the level of no further practice is complete with all seven features, but how is it known that this is the fourth initiation?

de dbang bzhi par grub pa ni yan lag bdun ldan las/
de ltar dgra dang ldan nyid phyir/ / yang gi sgra don ldan phyir dang / / de bzhin sgra don skyes nyid phyir/ / bzhi pa de bzhin nyid bdag 'dod/[131] / ces bshad do/ /

This is established from Vāgiśvarakīrti’s Seven Features:
Because it contains the words “like that,” because it contains the words “also,” because it contains the words “likewise,” I assert the fourth to be likewise.[153]

d.div: [131] sde dge_1888_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pi_yan lag bdun ldan ma/ le'u/ 3_198_na5
[153] Seven Features, Toh 1888 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, bi, chap. 3, 198a7.

f.d: de'i don ni rgyud rnams las/ bzhi pa de yang de bzhin no/[132] /zhes dang / la lar/ de ltar de bzhin bzhi pa yang / /zhes 'byung ba'i bzhi pa ston pa na dbang gsum pa'i shes rab ye shes dper blangs te des mtshon nas dbang bzhi pa ston la/ de ltar de bzhin bzhi pa yang / /zhes pa'i tshig de la ni de ltar gyi sgra dang de bzhin gyi sgra dang yang gi sgra dang gsum yod pa'i don bshad na dbang bzhi pa ni yan lag bdun ldan du grub pas bzhi pa ni sngar bshad pa de bzhin du bdag ngag dbang grags pa 'dod ces bshad pa'o/ /

In some tantras this is rendered as “The fourth also is likewise”[154] and by some as “Like that, likewise the fourth also.”[155] Therefore, when the fourth initiation is taught, it is done by taking the third initiation of wisdom-knowledge as an example. In the phrase, “Like that, likewise the fourth also,” when the meanings of the individual words “like that,” “likewise,” and “also” are explained, the fourth initiation is established as possessing the seven features. Therefore “I,” Vagisvarakirti, “assert the fourth to be likewise,” meaning “as previously explained.”

d.div: [132] sde dge_443_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_gsang 'dus rgyud phyi ma/ le'u/ 18_153_na5
[154] Later Guhyasamāja, Toh 443 Kangyur, rgyud, ca, chap. 18, 153a5.
[155] Tib. de ltar de bzhin bzhi pa wang, or in its more common version as written in the previous line, bzhi pa de yang de bzhin no.

f.d: 'di dag ni mtshon pa tsam ste rgyas par ni sngags rim chen mo las shes par bya'o/ /[133]
This section has been a mere illustration. A more extensive explanation can be known from the Great Path of Mantra.[156] /218/

f.d: gsum pa de gnyis phan tshun dod thub yin tshul bshad pa ni/
How these two are interchangeable

sbas rgyud rnams kyi dgongs pa mkhas grub rnams kyis bkral ba'i dbang bzhi pa dag pa'i sgyu lus dang don gyi lhan skyes kyi bde ba ngo bo dbyer med pa'i sgyu lus de ni don gyi 'od gsal gyi gzhon pa'i rlung 'od zer lnga pa las grub pa dang / bde ba yang lhan skyes kyi bde ba tsam la bshad pa ma gtogs mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i bshad pa med la/ dus 'khor nas ni sor bsam gyis bsgrubs pa'i stong gzugs kyi snang ba je bzang du 'phel ba las rjes dran gyi skabs su dngos gnas la stong gzugs yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can grub pa de nyid je bzang la song ba'i ting nge 'dzin yan chad kyi stong gzugs ni rnal 'byor pa'i sems kyi snang ba tsam las sgrub pa ma gtogs bsgrub gzhi gzhi la med pa dang / bde ba yang lhan skyes kyi bde ba tsam gyis mi chog par mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba la bshad pas lugs gnyis kyi zung 'jug ji lta ba bzhin ma mthun na'ang dbang bzhi pa mthar thug pa ni yan lag bdun ldan gyi sku gnyis ngo bo dbyer med la 'dod par ni lugs gnyis mthun pa yin no/ /

The masters who have written on the thinking of the hidden tantras explain the fourth initiation as being the indivisibility of the pure illusory body and the actual innate bliss. The illusory body is formed from the five lights of the winds that act as the mount of the clear-light mind, while the bliss is described merely as being innate and not as unchanging bliss. In the Kālacakra the branches of withdrawal and meditative absorption produce empty forms, whose appearances continue to develop until, on the branch of recollection, an actual mother and father in embrace is created. This empty form continues to develop, and from the sixth branch of meditative concentration onward, it is produced merely within the yogi’s mind. The basis for the accomplishment of this empty form is not found in ordinary existence. Concerning the bliss, it is not sufficient for it to be merely innate, it is also explained as being “unchanging.” Therefore there are some differences in the understanding of “union” in these two systems. Never theless, in their defining of the ultimate fourth initiation as being the indivisibility of the two bodies endowed with the seven features, there is agreement.

de yang ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag yan chad kyi stong gzugs yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can gyis dag pa'i sgyu lus yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can gyi dod thub cing / bde stong gi ye shes ni gnyis ka las bshad pa ltar yin no/ / 'on kyang sbas rgyud kyi dgongs pa 'grel ba'i mkhas grub rnams kyi bshad srol la mchog mi 'gyur gyi bde ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgyar bshad pa dang / de dngos su 'dren par byed pa'i phyag rgya'i rnam gzhag dang bcas pa dngos su ma byung ba rnams kyi don la dpyad par bya dgos so/ /

Moreover the empty form in the aspect of the mother and father in embrace gained from the branch of meditative concentration onward can substitute for the pure illusory body in the aspect of mother and father in embrace, and the explanation of bliss-and emptiness gnosis is similar in both traditions. However, in the explanations of those masters who have commentated on the meanings of the hidden tantras, there is no mention of the 21,600 levels of unchanging bliss, nor is there any actual presentation of the mudrā consorts that induce these levels. This is something to be investigated.

de ltar na lugs gnyis ka'i dbang bzhi pa bskur ba'i tshul ni dbang bzhi pa'i don tshig gis legs par brda sprad de slob mas de'i go ba rnyed pa tsam gyis dbang bzhi pa tshig gi sgo nas bskur ba dang thob par 'jog pa yin no/ / de yang don dam byang chub sems kyi dkyil 'khor du thob pa dang / sgo gsum gyi dri ma phra mo sbyong ba dang / rdo rje gsum dbyer mi phyed pa'i sku 'grub pa'i skal ba can du byed cing / zung 'jug gi rdzogs rim sgom pa la dbang bar byed do/ / de dag gis dbang gi rnam gzhag mdor bsdus pa tsam zhig bshad zin to// //

Therefore the way of conferring the fourth initiation in both systems is that the meaning of the fourth initiation is communicated by words, and merely by gaining an understanding of them, the disciple is conferred with and receives the fourth initiation verbally. Furthermore the fourth initiation is received within the mandala of ultimate bodhicitta, subtle contamination of body, speech, and mind is removed, one is blessed with the great fortune to develop the body of the three indivisible vajras, and one is empowered to meditate upon the union of the completion stage. This has been just a brief and condensed presentation of the initiations. /219/
le'u bzhi pa/ sgrub pa'i le'u/
Part 4. Sādhana: Methods of Accomplishment
17. The Two Stages
gnyis pa bskyed rdzogs 'bras bu dang bcas pa'i rnam gzhag bshad pa

d.i: Stages of generation and completion and the results of their practice

f.d: ['di ]la gsum/ bskyed pa'i rim pa dang rdzogs pa'i rim pa'i grangs nges dang go rim bshad pa dang / rim pa gnyis so so'i rnam gzhag bshad pa dang / rim pa gnyis kyi 'bras bu'i rnam gzhag bshad pa'o/ /
This section is under three headings: 1. Ascertaining the two stages and their correct order 2. Presentations of each stage 3. A presentation of the results of practice
dang po [bskyed pa'i rim pa dang rdzogs pa'i rim pa'i grangs nges dang go rim bshad pa/]

d.i: Ascertaining the two stages and their correct order

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ rim gnyis kyi grangs nges dang / go rim mo/ /
This has two outlines: 1. Ascertaining the two stages 2. Ascertaining the correct order
dang po [grangs nges ]ni

dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i thun mong ma yin pa'i bsgom bya'i lam la bskyed pa'i rim pa dang rdzogs pa'i rim pa gnyis su grangs nges te/ dus kyi 'khor lo'i dbang gis lam sgom pa'i snod rung du byas pa'i gang zag de la dngos grub tha ma dang 'bring po 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub tsam don du gnyer ba'i gang zag gcig dang mchog gi dngos grub bla na med pa rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas don du gnyer ba'i gang zag gnyis su nges shing / gang zag dang pos bsgom par bya ba'i lam la bskyed rim nyid du nges pa dang / gang zag gnyis pas mchog gi dngos grub 'grub pa'i nye rgyu rdzogs rim skye ba'i rgyud smin byed kyi lam la bskyed rim nyid du nges shing / de ltar rgyud smin nas mchog gi dngos grub 'grub pa'i nye rgyu la rdzogs rim nyid du nges pa'i phyir ro/ /

In the glorious Kālacakra the special path to be developed is ascertained as consisting of the two stages of generation and completion. This is because those who are made into suitable vessels by the Kālacakra initiation for meditation on the paths are of two types. One type of person will aim only for the lower and middling worldly siddhis, and one type will strive for the highest siddhi of unsurpassed enlightenment. The path of practice for the first type of practitioner is ascertained to be the generation stage. For the second type, the generation stage is ascertained as being the path that ripens the practitioner for completion-stage practice. Once the mindstream has been ripened, the completion stage is ascertained as being the main cause for the attainment of the highest siddhi.
gnyis pa go rim ni

gsang 'dus rim lngar slob dpon klu sgrub kyis/
bskyed pa'i rim la legs gnas shing / / rdzogs pa'i rim pa 'dod rnams la/ / thabs 'di rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyis/ / skas kyi rim pa lta bur gsungs/[1] / zhes gsungs pa ltar dang po nas sngags bla med kyi lam gyis bgrod pa gzhir bzhag pa la dang por bskyed rim mthar phyin par byas te de nas rdzogs rim mtshan nyid tshang ba skye ba'i go rim nges pa yin te/ phyi nang gi skyon rags pa sbyong byed kyi bskyed rim gyis rgyud smin par ma byas par phyi nang gi skyon phra mo nas 'gog pa'i rdzogs rim mtshan nyid tshang ba mi skye ba'i phyir dang / khyad par du yang rdzogs rim gyi skabs su stong gzugs sna tshogs pa shar ba de nyid mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'dren nus kyi mtshan dpes brgyan pa'i stong gzugs yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can du dngos su sgyur bar byed pa la bskyed rim gyi lha sku zhal phyag gi rnam pa can la reg mthong gi mtshan ma can gyi bskyed rim mthar phyin pa sngon du 'gro dgos pa'i phyir ro/ /

In his Five Stages, composed upon the Guhyasamāja Tantra, the master Nāgārjuna said:
Dwelling well within the stage of generation, wishing for the stage of completion, this method, the Buddha has said, is like the steps of a ladder.[1] Therefore, assuming that one is traveling by the highest path of mantra from its very beginning, there is a definite order in which one first completes the generation stage, from which will arise a full completion stage. This is a definite sequence, because without ripening one’s continuum with the generation stage in order to remove the coarse outer and inner faults, a full completion stage, which brings about cessations beginning from subtle outer and inner faults, will not arise. /220/ Particularly at the time of the completion stage, various empty forms appear, and in order to transform them into empty forms in the aspect of father and mother in embrace adorned with the signs and features, one must have first completed a generation stage with attributes, which involves seeing and coming into contact with deities with their particular forms, numbers of hands, and faces.

d.div: [1] sde dge_1802_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ di_rim pa lnga pa/ rim pa dang po/ 45_na6
[1] Toh 1802 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, di, 45a6.

f.d:
'di la kha cig na re/ dang po nas sngags bla med kyi lam gyis bgrod pa gzhir bzhag pa la yang rdzogs rim gyi sngon du nges par bskyed rim 'gro dgos pa ma grub ste/ gal te dang po nas sngags bla med kyi lam gyis bgrod pa bzhir bzhag pa la yang bskyed rim rdzogs rim gyi sngon du nges par 'gro dgos na bla med kyi lam gyis 'tshang rgya ba la nges par bskyed rim sgom pa sngon du 'gro dgos pa las de ni ma yin te/ bskyed rim sgom pa mthar phyin pas 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub tsam 'grub kyi/ dngos grub chen po sangs rgyas 'grub pa'i rgyur mi 'gyur ba'i phyir te/ khams le'i mdor bsdus dang po las/
gzugs la sogs par rtog pa dkyil 'khor gyi/ / 'khor lo sgom pa goms par gyur pas ni/ / grub pa 'jig rten pa dag 'grub 'gyur gyi/ / 'dod pa'i dngos grub chen po ga la zhig[2] / ces gsungs pas so zhe na/ de ni dang po nas sngags bla med kyi lam la zhugs nas 'tshang rgya ba la bskyed rim nges par sgom mi dgos pa'i shes byed du mi 'gyur te/ 'grel tshig de dag gis bskyed rim rkyang pa mthar phyin pas 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub tsam dngos su sgrub nus kyi/ mchog gi dngos grub dngos su sgrub mi nus zhes bstan pa tsam yin pas so/ /

Some say that even on the basis of traveling by the highest path of mantra from its very beginning, it is not the case that the generation stage necessarily precedes the completion stage. If it were the case that when traveling by the highest path of mantra from its very beginning, the generation stage had necessarily to precede the completion stage, then to reach enlightenment by the highest path of mantra, generation-stage meditation would definitely have to precede the completion stage. However, they say, this is not the case, because the completion of the generation stage only ensures the attainment of worldly siddhis and is not a cause for the great siddhi of enlightenment. This is so, they say, because the first summary from the Realms chapter of the Great Commentary says:
By meditating on the mandalas with thoughts of form and so forth, one will attain worldly siddhis, but where is the great desired siddhi?[2] This is true, but this quote does not prove that when one enters the highest path of mantra from the beginning of its practice, it is not necessary to meditate on the generation stage in order to attain enlightenment. These words from the commentary merely teach that fulfillment of the generation stage alone will result only in the accomplishment of worldly siddhis and not in the achievement of the highest siddhi.

d.div: [2] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 5_na4
[2] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 5a4.

f.d:
de la khong dag na re/ dang po nas sngags bla med kyi lam la zhugs nas 'tshang rgya ba la bskyed rim sngon du ma song bar rjogs rim rkyang pas chog pa mi srid par 'gyur te/ dang po nas sngags bla med kyi lam la zhugs nas 'tshang rgya ba la nges par bskyed rim sgom pa sngon du 'gro dgos pa'i phyir ro/ / 'dod par mi nus te khams le'i mdor bsdus dang po de nyid las/
bskyed pa'i rim par gsungs pa'i hUM dang ni/ / phaT yig la sogs rtog pa dang bral ba/ / rdzogs pa'i rim pa'i rnal 'byor de nyid de/ / de nyid kyi ni sgrub thabs gzhan yod min/[3] / zhes bskyed rim gyi skabs su gsungs pa'i hUM dang phaT la sogs pa'i ngag gi rjod pa dang lha la sogs pa dmigs pa'i rtog sgom gyi rtog pa dang bral ba rdzogs pa'i rim pa'i rnal 'byor de nyid kho na las gzhan pa'i de nyid de 'bras bu mthar thug gi sgrub thabs yod pa min/ zhes gsungs pas so snyam na/ 'grel tshig de dag gi don de ltar yin na rdzogs rim min pa'i sangs rgyas kyi rgyu med par 'gyur bas ha cang thal ba dang / 'di ltar gsung ba po rnams bskyed rim mchog gi dngos grub kyi rgyu ma yin par 'dod pa ni de kho na nyid snang bar byed pa zhes bya ba'i rgya cher bshad pa las le'u lnga po'i go rim bshad pa sogs dang 'gal ba'i sgo nas bkag pa las shes par bya'o/ /

To this the others reply, if that is so, then it follows that having entered the highest path of mantra from its beginning, the attainment of enlightenment is not possible by the completion stage alone without the prerequisite of the generation stage, because to attain enlightenment having entered the highest path of mantra from the beginning, the meditations of the generation stage are a necessary prerequisite. However it is not possible, they continue, for you to agree with this, because in the first summary from the Realms chapter of the Great Commentary it says:
The yoga of the completion stage, freed from the concepts of hūḥ, phaṭ, and others, as spoken of in the generation stage, is the method for accomplishment. There is no other.[3] /221/ Therefore, they ask, does this not mean that the yoga of the completion stage, devoid of the thoughts of the conceptual meditation upon deities and of the speech of hūḥ, phaṭ, and so forth spoken of during the generation stage, is the one and only method of attaining the final goal? In reply to this, it can be said that if your explanation represents the meaning of the above passage, then you must accept the serious consequence that there is no other cause of enlightenment than the completion stage. Those who speak such things maintain that the generation stage is not a cause of the highest siddhi. This is refuted in Illumination of Reality, where it states that such a position is in direct contradiction to the sequence of the five chapters of the Kālacakra.

d.div: [3] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 5_na2
[3] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 5a5.

f.d:
'o na 'grel tshig de dag gi don ji ltar yin snyam na/ bskyed pa'i rim pa zhes sogs kyi gong de nyid du/
sna tshogs rnam rtog la sogs lam gyis ni/ / de nyid de bzhin gshegs pas gang gsungs pa/ / bcu drug bzhi yi rab tu dbye ba can/ / lam dang bral bas 'thob pa ma yin no/[4] / zhes de bzhin gshegs pas gang gsungs pa'i de nyid de mchog gi dngos grub ni rnam pa bcu drug dang dga' ba bzhi'i rab tu dbye ba can gyi lam dang bral ba'i lha'i zhal phyag sogs sna tshogs la dmigs pa'i rnam rtog la sogs pa'i bskyed rim gyi lam rkyang pas 'thob pa min zhes bshad nas/ rnam pa bcu drug sogs dang bral bas 'thob par ma nus pa'i mchog gi dngos grub de'i rgyu'i gtso bo gang yin snyam na/ rgyu'i gtso bo de ni bskyed pa'i rim par gsungs pa'i hU~M dang phaT yig gi rjod pa dag dang / zhal phyag gi rnam pa sogs sgom pa'i rtog pa dang bral ba'i rdzogs pa'i rim pa'i rnal 'byor sbyor ba yan lag drug po de nyid yin te/ mchog gi dngos grub de nyid kyi ni sgrub thabs kyi gtso bo rdzogs rim de las gzhan yod pa ma yin pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes pa'i don yin no/ /

So what do these words from the commentary mean? The verse preceding the one beginning “The yoga of the completion stage” runs:
The path of various concepts lacks the path of the sixteen and the four and will not arrive at the suchness spoken of by the Tathāgata.[4] “The suchness spoken of by the Tathāgata” refers to the highest siddhi, and such a goal will not be reached by the generation stage alone, for it is a “path of various concepts” of hands, faces, and so forth of the deities, and it lacks the divisions of the sixteen aspects and the four joys. So what is the primary cause of the accomplishment of the highest siddhi that cannot be attained by a path lacking the sixteen aspects and so forth? The main cause is “the yoga of the completion stage” of the six-branched yoga, divorced from spoken words such as hūḥ and phat and from the conceptual meditations taught in the generation stage. This is because the primary method for the accomplishment of the highest siddhi is the completion stage, and “there is no other.”

d.div: [4] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 5_na2
[4] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 5a2.

f.d:
de ltar na bskyed rim gyis rdzogs rim mtshan nyid tshang ba skye ba'i rgyud smin par byed pa'i sgo nas bskyed rim sangs rgyas kyi rgyur 'gyur pa sems 'grel rnams kyi dgongs pa yin te/ sgrub le'i zhe brgyad pa'i 'grel chen las/
de lta na yang blun po'i blo can byis pa rnams gzhug pa dang sems ni dag pa'i don gyi slad du kye mi'i bdag po zla ba bzang po khyod kyis sgrub thabs dag ni brjod par bya ste don dam par ni rtag pa dang mi rtag pa'i dngos po snying por gyur pa 'ga' yang 'dir ni bsgrub par bya ba med do/ / de'i phyir sangs rgyas nyid kyi slad du gang zhig bsgrub par bya ba sgrub pa de nyid ni zhes pa nges pa ste/ 'dir gang zhig btags pa'i sgrub thabs de ni 'khrul pa zhes pa rdo rje can gyi sgrub thabs mtha' dag gang yin pa'o/[5] / zhes gsungs pa'i sems ni dag pa'i skad du zhes pas sems dag par byed pa'i rgyud bskyed rim bsgom par bshad pa dang / sangs rgyas nyid kyi slad du zhes pas sangs rgyas kyi rgyur btags pa'i sgrub thabs bskyed rim sgom par bshad cing / de dag kyang rdzogs rim skye ba'i smin byed la bskyed rim dgos pa la dgongs pa yin no/ /

Therefore the generation stage ripens the mind for the creation of a full and complete completion stage. In this way the generation stage is a cause of buddhahood, and this is the thinking of the Three Bodhisattva Commentaries. The Great Commentary states on the forty-eighth verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter:
In this way, to lead the foolish and to purify their minds, lord of men, Sucandra, teach the methods of accomplishment. Ultimately phenomena that are of “the essence of permanence or impermanence are not to be practiced here.” Therefore, for the accomplishment of buddhahood, “the methods to be practiced” are ascertained. Here those practices that are conceptually created methods of accomplishment are “false.” This is for all Vajradhara methods of accomplishment.[5] /222/ The phrase “In this way, to lead the foolish and to purify their minds” refers to the practice of the generation stage as a cause of purifying the mind. The phrase “for the accomplishment of buddhahood” refers to the practices of a conceptually created method of accomplishment,[6] or generation stage, as causes of buddhahood, and these practices are necessary as ripening agents for the creation of the completion stage.

d.div: [5] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 217_na4
[5] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 217a4.
[6] Contrived yoga and conceptually created yoga are synonyms for the generation stage.

f.d:
gzhan yang brtag gnyis kyi brtag pa gnyis pa'i le'u gnyis pa'i/
nam mkha' lta bu'i chos kun la/ / rgya mtshor gu ba ji lta bar/ / rang 'dod lha yi gzugs kyis ni/ / sems can ji ltar 'grub par 'gyur/ / zhes rdo rje snying pos gsol ba'i lan du/
bcom ldan 'das kyis bka' stsal pa/ bdag med rnal 'byor ldan pa'am/ / yang na he ru ka dpal brtson/ / gzhan pa'i sems kyis skad cig kyang / / dngos grub 'dod pas mi gnas so/[6] / zhes gsungs pa'i rdo rje snying 'grel las/
kye rdo rje snying po de lta yin gyi yang las kyi dang po la gnas pa'i rnal 'byor pas gong du bstan pa'i dkyil 'khor du zhugs la bskyed pa'i lha'i nga rgyal gyi dus dang de yongs su rdzogs nas bdag med pa'i rnal 'byor la gnas par byas na nges par kye'i rdo rjer 'gyur ro/ / de'i phyir dngos grub 'dod pas rim pa gnyis la brten pa ma gtogs pa gzhan gyi sems kyis skad cig kyang mi gnas so/[7] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Moreover the second chapter of the second part of the Hevajra Root Tantra says:
Floating like gourds upon the ocean, amid phenomena vast as space, how do sentient beings reach attainment through the forms of desired deities? This question, asked by Vajragarbha, is answered:
The Conqueror said, “Either by the yoga of no-self or by effort in glorious Heruka, wishing for siddhis, do not remain with other minds, even for an instant.”[7] Regarding this verse, the Vajragarbha Commentary says:
Vajragarbha, it is like this. Furthermore the yogi who dwells in the beginning stages has been led into the mandala as previously taught. This is the time for the pride of deity generation. When that has been accomplished, the yogi dwells in the yoga of no-self,[8] where he will without doubt become Hevajra. Therefore those who wish for siddhis should rely only upon the two stages and should not remain with other minds even for an instant.[9]

d.div: [6] sde dge_418_bka'/ rgyud/ nga _rgyud brtag gnyis/ le'u/ 2_14_na6
[7] sde dge_1180_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ka_rdo rje snying 'grel/ 79_ba4
[7] Toh 418 Kangyur, rgyud, nga, chap. 2, 14a6.
[8] bdag med pa’i rnal ’byor. Yoga of no-self, but could also refer to Nairātmya (bdag med ma), the consort of Hevajra.
[9] Toh 1180 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ka, 79b4.

f.d: de yang las dang po pas thog mar kha dog dang dbyibs kyi bdag nyid la mngon par zhen pas gnas/ de yongs su rdzogs nas te mthar gyur pa na bdag med pa'i rnal 'byor la gnas par byas na ste bslab par byas na zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis ni bskyed pa'i lha'i nga rgyal bskyed rim yongs su rdzogs pa ste mthar phyin pas bdag med pa'i rnal 'byor rdzogs rim la gnas par byas na kye'i rdo rjer 'gyur bar gsungs pa dang / de'i phyir mchog gi dngos grub kye'i rdo rje thob par 'dod pas rim pa gnyis la bslab par bya'o/ / de ma gtogs pa gzhan gyi sems kyis skad cig kyang mi gnas par gsungs pa dang /

In the beginning stages, the yogi first dwells in the apprehension of shape and color. “When that has been accomplished” or completed, “the yogi dwells in” or practices “the yoga of no-self.” These words teach that when the generation stage of the pride of deity generation has been accomplished or completed, the yogi dwells in the completion stage of no-self yoga, “where he will without doubt become Hevajra.” Therefore those who wish for the supreme siddhi of becoming Hevajra should practice only the two stages /223/ “and not remain with other minds even for an instant.”

bskyed rim la slob tshul ni/
las dang po pas thog mar lha'i kha dog dang dbyibs kyi bskyed rim gyi bdag nyid la mngon par zhen pas gnas la/ bskyed rim de mthar gyur ba ste mthar phyin pa na bdag med pa'i rnal 'byor rdzogs rim la bslab par bya'o/ / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis rdzogs rim mtshan nyid tshang ba skye ba'i rgyud smin byed du bskyed rim sngon du 'gro dgos pa'i bskyed rdzogs kyi go rim nges pa gsal bar bstan pa yin no/ / gzhan yang rdo rje snying 'grel gyi de'i 'phro nyid las/
de las skal ba dang ldan pa gang la bskyed pa'i rnal 'byor rdzogs te yang dag pa'i shes rab kyi yan lag drug gi dang po so sor sdud pas bsdus te goms par byed pa na mtshan ma de dag 'byung bar 'gyur la/[8] zhes skal ba dang ldan pa'i gang zag gis bskyed rim mthar phyin par byas te sbyor ba yan lag drug gi dang po sor sdud sgom par byas na du sogs kyi mtshan ma'am rtags rnams 'byung bar gsungs pas 'dis kyang bskyed rdzogs kyi go rim nges pa bstan pa yin no/ /

Concerning the way to practice the generation stage, the commentary says:
The beginner first dwells with the apprehension of the generation-stage practices of deity shape and color. When the generation stage has been accomplished or completed, he practices the completion stage of no-self yoga. These words teach the generation stage as a ripening agent for the creation of a fully endowed completion stage, thereby clearly illustrating the order of these two stages. Immediately following the above passage, the Vajragarbha Commentary continues:
From that the fortunate one completes the yoga of generation and develops the withdrawal process of the first of the six branches of perfect wisdom, known as withdrawal. From this will arise the signs.[10] This passage explains that the fortunate meditator completes the generation stage and practices the branch of withdrawal, the first yoga of the six-branched yoga, from which will arise the signs of smoke and so forth. Therefore this passage also clearly lays out the order of the generation and completion stages.

d.div: [8] sde dge_1180_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ka_rdo rje snying 'grel/ 80_ba3
[10] Toh 1180 Tengyur, rgyud, ka, 80b3.

f.d: de lta bu'i bskyed rdzogs kyi go rim nges pa bshad pa rnams ni spyir btang ba dang po nas sngags bla med kyi lam gyis bgrod pa'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi/ phar phyin theg pa'i lam gyis sa bcu'i bar bgrod pa'i srid pa tha ma ba lta bu sngags lam du zhugs nas 'tshang rgya ba'i rdzogs rim gyi sngon du bskyed rim 'gro mi dgos pa sogs ni dmigs bsal lo/ /

These teachings on the order of the two stages are mainly given on the basis of someone who enters the highest path of tantra right from its beginning. A practitioner who has become a “last-existence,” tenth-level bodhisattva by the path of sutra and then enters tantra does not need to travel through the generation stage before embarking on the completion stage for enlightenment. Such examples are exceptions.

gal te srid pa tha ma'i byang sems sa bcu pa ba 'tshang rgya ba la sngags bla med kyi lam du 'jug dgos na/ phar phyin theg pa'i lam rkyang pa la brten nas 'tshang rgya mi nus sam snyam na/ de ltar mi nus pa ni 'dus pa sogs kyi dgongs pa yin par ma zad dus 'khor gyi rgyud rtsa 'grel rnams kyi dgongs pa'ang yin te/ khams le'i mdor bsdus drug pa'i 'grel chen las/
de'i phyir gang gis mchog gi dang po'i sangs rgyas mi shes pa des mtshan yang dag par brjod pa mi shes so/ / gang gis mtshan yang dag par rjod pa mi shes pa des rdo rje 'dzin pa'i ye shes kyi sku mi shes so/ / gang gis rdo rje 'dzin pa'i ye shes kyi sku mi shes pa des sngags kyi theg pa mi shes so/ / gang gis sngags kyi theg pa mi shes pa de thams cad ni 'khor ba pa ste bcom ldan 'das rdo rje 'dzin pa'i lam dang bral ba'o/[9] / zhes gsungs pas so/ /

It may be asked if a “last-existence,” tenth-level bodhisattva has to enter the highest path of tantra in order to reach buddhahood, is enlightenment through the sutra path alone not possible? Such a thought is not only the opinion of the Guhyasamāja and others but also of the Kālacakra and its commentaries. The Great Commentary in the sixth summary of the Realms chapter says /224/:
Therefore those who do not know the Supreme Original Buddha do not know the Saṃgīti.[11] Those not knowing the Saṃgīti will not know the gnosis body of Vajradhara. Those who do not know the gnosis body of Vajradhara do know the Vajra Vehicle. All those not knowing the Vajra Vehicle are of samsara, bereft of the path of the conqueror Vajradhara.[12]

d.div: [9] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 48_ba4
[11] Mañjuśrī-nama-saṃgīti. See bibliography.
[12] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 48b4.

f.d: bskyed pa'i rim pa'i rnam gzhag bshad pa/
18. The Generation Stage
gnyis pa rim pa gnyis so so'i rnam gzhag bshad pa
['di ]la gnyis/ bskyed pa'i rim pa'i rnam gzhag bshad pa dang / rdzogs pa'i rim pa'i rnam gzhag bshad pa'o/ /
This is under two main outlines: 1. Generation stage 2. Completion stage
dang po [skyed pa'i rim pa'i rnam gzhag bshad pa ]
['di ]la bzhi/ bskyed rim gnas gang du bsgom pa dang / gang zag ji lta bus bsgom pa dang / dgos pa gang gi don du bsgom pa dang / ji ltar du sgom pa'i tshul bshad pa'o/ /
This has four headings: 1. The place of meditation 2. The meditator 3. The purpose of the meditation 4. The way to meditate
dang po [bskyed rim gnas gang du bsgom pa bshad pa sogs bzhi ]ni

sgrub le'i gsum pa las/
skyed mos tshal lam ri bo dang ni rgyal ba mchog gi gnas dang lha yi gnas ni stong pa dang / / grub pa'i gnas dang dur khrod dang ni mtsho dang bzang po'i gnas dang de bzhin nyid du sbas pa'i sa/ / gang du sems ni rab tu tshim par 'gyur ba der ni bsgrub par bya'o mi yi bdag po kye/ / nges par 'jam pa'i mal cha dag dang gdan la nye bar 'dug nas sngar brjod srung ba byas nas ni/[10] / zhes bskyed rim sgom pa'i gnas so sor gsungs pa ltar te/

The third verse of the Methods for Accomplishment chapter from the Condensed Tantra says:
In pleasant groves, on mountains, in places of the great Conqueror, in empty temples, in the places of great practitioners, in cemeteries, by lakes and places of beauty, and in places hidden away, wherever the mind is content, there one should practice, great king. With soft bedding, there on a seat, one first recites the protection.[13] This passage mentions places for the practice of the generation stage.

d.div: [10] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka10_78_na7
[13] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 10, 78a7.

f.d: skyed mos tshal du dbang dgug dang / ri bor rmongs rengs phur bus gdab pa dang / rgyal ba mchog gi gnas byin rlabs dang bcas pa'i mchod rten chen por grub chen brgyad dang / lha khang stong pa dang rgya mtsho chen po'i 'gram du bskrad dbye dang / grub pa'i gnas su las kyi phyag rgya'i dngos grub dang / dur khrod du gsang ba dang / mtsho dang bzang po'i gnas te phyug cing rgyas par 'gyur ba'i gnas su zhi rgyas dang / sbas pa'i sa zhes pa phug gam sa'i khang par 'jig rten gsum gyi rgyal srid bsgrub pa'i don du bskyed rim bsgom par bya zhing / de dag kyang las tshogs rnams 'grub pa dang mthun pa'i dbang du byas pa'o/ /

These include pleasant groves for the feats of gaining power and of summoning; mountains for the feats of stupefying, paralyzing, and stabbing; shrines blessed by the Conqueror for the eight siddhis; empty temples and the sides of the ocean for the feats of expelling and separating; the places of great practitioners for the siddhis of activity mudrā consorts; cemeteries for the secret practices; by lakes and places of beauty, meaning rich and expansive, for the two siddhis of peace and increase; and hidden places, meaning caves or mud huts, for the feat of ruling over the three worlds. /225/ These places are mentioned on the basis of being conducive to the attainment of tantric powers.[14]

d.div: [14] The four activities of peace, increasing, power, and wrath.

f.d:
gnas de rnams la thun mong du dgos pa ni/ de nyid kyi 'grel chen du lung drangs par/ de bzhin du yang gsungs pa/
gang na sa skyong chos ldan zhing / / gang zhig kho nar skye dgu rnams/ / bder gnas sa 'dzin rtsod med pa/ / der ni rnal 'byor brtsam par bya/[11] / zhes gsungs pa ltar gyi gnas su 'jam pa'i mal stan la nye bar 'dug ste 'og nas 'byung ba ltar gyi bskyed pa'i rim pa'i rnal 'byor rnams bsgom par bya'o/ /

These places all have common requirements, which are mentioned in a verse from the Great Commentary:
A place of dharma, where inhabitants live in peace, a place free of strife, there the yogi practices.[15] In such a place, seated on soft bedding, one should practice the yoga of the generation stage, which will be explained later.

d.div: [11] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 201_ba7
[15] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 201b7.

f.d: gnyis pa gang zag ji lta bus sgom pa ni/
sngar ji skad bshad pa'i byis pa'i dbang bdun thob cing / dam tshig dang sdom pa la gnas pas bsgom par bya ba yin no/ /
The meditator should be one who has received the seven childhood initiations, as previously explained and who abides by the vows and samaya pledges.
gsum pa dgos pa gang gi don du bsgom pa ni/

dus kyi 'khor lo'i ched du bya ba'i gdul bya phal pa rnams kyis ni 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub zhi rgyas la sogs pa dang grub chen brgyad la sogs pa thob par bya ba'i don du sgom pa dang / ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo rnams kyis ni sbyang gzhi phyi nang gnyis kyi ma dag pa'i cha rags pa mgo gnon zhing / rtsa ba nas dag par byed pa'i gnyen po rdzogs rim mtshan nyid tshang ba skye ba'i smin byed du bsams pa'i sgo nas mchog gi dngos grub sangs rgyas nyid 'thob pa'i don du sgom par byed pa yin no/ /

The common disciples of the Kālacakra meditate in order to attain the worldly siddhis, such as those of peace and increase, as well as the eight great siddhi. The primary disciples of the Kālacakra meditate in order to attain the highest siddhi of enlightenment by suppressing the coarse impurity of the inner and outer bases of purification with generation-stage practices and by regarding this stage as a ripening agent for the creation of a fully endowed completion stage, which has the power of complete and total purification.
bzhi pa ji ltar du sgom pa'i tshul bshad pa ni/

sngar brjod srung ba byas nas/ zhes gsungs pa ltar sngar dbang ler bshad pa'i srung 'khor sgom pa sngon du btang nas sgrub ler gsungs pa'i tshogs zhing nas thun gyi mthar gshegs su gsol ba'i bar rnams la bslab par bya'o/ / de yang sngags kyi theg pa mtshan nyid kyi theg pa las khyad par 'byed pa'i khyad chos kyi gtso bo ni 'bras bu'i gnas skabs kyi gnas gzhal yas khang dang / lus mtshan dpes brgyan pa'i sku dang / longs spyod zag pa med pa'i bde ba dang / 'khor sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' sogs lha dang lha mo'i rnam pa can rnams dang / mdzad pa sku'i 'od zer dpag tu med pa sogs kyis sems can thams cad sangs rgyas kyi sa la 'god pa sogs phun sum tshogs pa lnga dang da lta nas rnam pa mthun par bsgoms nas gzugs sku'i rigs 'dra'i rgyu la slob pa'i 'bras bu lam byed rgyud sde bzhi ga la yod kyang / sbyang gzhi srid pa skye 'jig gi rim pa dang mthun pa'i lha'i rnal 'byor dang / de yang rdzogs rim skye ba'i smin byed du 'gro ba bla med min pa la med pas skabs 'di'i bskyed rim sgom pa la khyad chos de gnyis dang ldan pa cig dgos so/ /

“One first recites the protection.” As this line says, the yogi performs a preliminary meditation on the protection wheel, as taught in the Realms chapter, then engages in practices that begin from the merit-field visualization as taught in the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, and finishes with the final requests at the end of the session. The main features of Mantra Vehicle that distinguish it from the Sutra Vehicle are the practices of the five perfections,[16] whose aspects are replicated and meditated upon, from the time of practice onward, to produce similar-type causes of an enlightened form body. These five, which will be present at the final result of practice, are one’s environment as a celestial palace, one’s body as a form adorned with the signs and features of enlightenment, one’s enjoyments as undefiled bliss, one’s entourage as buddhas and bodhisattvas in the forms of gods and goddesses, and one’s deeds and actions performed by light rays emitting from one’s body to bring all sentient beings to buddhahood. /226/ This “path of the result” is present in all four classes of tantra, but deity yoga correlating to the birth and destruction bases of purification within samsara together with a generation stage that becomes a ripening process for the creation of a completion stage is only found in highest yoga tantra. Therefore the generation stage discussed here must be one endowed with these two characteristics.

d.div: [16] phun sum tshogs pa.
