f.d: de yang rgyud 'grel 'dir phyi nang gzhan gsum sbyor ba'i rnam gzhag dang / lha'i rnal 'byor gyi spros pa shin tu rgyas par gsungs pa 'di ni phyi nang gnyis sbyang gzhi dang / gzhan de sbyong byed du byas te sbyang gzhi phyi nang gnyis dang chos mthun pa'i gzhan bskyed rim sgom pas rgyud smin par byas nas gzhan rdzogs rim sgom pa mthar phyin par byas pa las phyi nang gi ma dag pa'i snang ba 'char ba'i bag chags ma lus par sbyangs te gzhan 'bras bu dus kyi 'khor lo sku bzhi'i bdag nyid can mngon du 'gyur ba zhig dgos pa'i gtso bo yin la/ de yang lha'i rnal 'byor gyi spros pa ji tsam rgyas pa tsam gyis phyi nang sbyong ba dang rdzogs rim skye ba'i rgyud smin byed du 'gro ba'i phul che ba la dgongs nas rgyud 'dir bskyed rim la lha sgom pa'i spros pa rgya cher mdzad pa yin gyi/ de lta min na lha'i rten dang brten pa'i spros pa rgya cher gsungs pa'i dgongs pa gang yin gyi dgongs pa dpyad dgos so/ /

This tantra talks of the correlation of the Inner, Outer, and Other, as well as giving a very extensive presentation of deity yoga. The main reason for this is that the Inner and Outer are the bases of purification while the Other is the purifier. By meditating on the Other in its aspect of the generation stage and correlating it to inner and outer bases of purification, one’s mindstream is ripened, and by accomplishing and completing the meditations on the Other in its aspect of the completion stage, every imprint that arises in the form of the impure appearances of the Outer and Inner is removed, and the yogi becomes the Other, or resultant Kālacakra, whose nature is the four bodies. Furthermore the more extensive a presentation of deity yoga, the more fruitful will be the purification of the Outer and Inner, and the more fruitful will be the development of a generation stage as a ripening agent for the creation of a completion stage. It is with this in mind that the deity yoga of the generation stage in this tantra is so extensive. If that were not the case, then what other reason would there be for such an extensive presentation of the deities and mandalas?

de lta bu'i bskyed rim de yang srid pa skye 'jig gi rim pa dang mthun par sgom pa'i tshul ni spyir sngags bla med kyi ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo dang khyad par du yang rgyud 'di'i ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo ni dbang po mchog tu rno ba rgyud 'di'i brjod bya bskyed rim dang rdzogs rim sbyor ba yan lag drug gi lam gyis tshe gcig la 'tshang rgya ba'i rten gyi gang zag 'dzam bu gling gi mi khams drug ldan zhig yin pa rgyud dang 'grel chen na shin tu gsal bas na nga gtan la 'bebs pa'i skabs su yang 'dzam bu gling pa'i mi mngal skyes kyi srid pa skye 'jig gnyis gtso bor gtan la phab pa ltar de'i srid pa skye 'jig gi rim pa dang mthun par bskyed pa'i rim pa sgom pa yin no/ /

The way that such a generation stage simulates the processes of birth and destruction within samsara is as follows. The primary disciples of highest mantra in general and the primary disciples of this tantra specifically, are those of the highest intelligence who, as human beings of this world of Jambudvīpa, are endowed with the six elements and possess a form for the attainment of enlightenment within one life by the practices of the generation stage and the six-branched yoga of the completion stage, the main topics of this tantra. This is stated very clearly in the tantra and in the Great Commentary. Therefore, when determining the Inner, one is primarily determining the birth and death of a womb-born human being of this world. Similarly the generation stage is a meditation simulating the processes of birth and destruction of such a human being. /227/

de ltar na bskyed pa'i rim pa sgom tshul bshad pa la gnyis/ bsod nams kyi las bsags pa'i mthar 'chi ba dang chos mthun par tshogs gnyis gsag pa dang / shi nas nying 'tshams sbyar te lus skye ba'i rim pa dang chos mthun par yan lag bzhi'i rnal 'byor sgom pa'o/ /

Therefore the way of meditating upon the generation stage is under two main headings: 1. Gathering the two kinds of accumulations, which correlates with the death process that occurs at the end of gathering of merit 2. The yoga of four branches, correlating with the after-death process of linking up to a new birth and taking a body
[tshogs gnyis gsag pa ]
19. The Two Accumulations
dang po [tshogs gnyis gsag pa ]

d.i: Gathering the two kinds of accumulations, which correlates with the death process that occurs at the end of gathering of merit

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ 'chi ba'i snga rol du las gsog pa dang mthun par tshogs zhing la bsod nams kyi tshogs gsag pa dang / shi ba dang chos mthun par rnam par thar pa'i sgo bzhi sgom pa'i ye shes kyi tshogs gsag pa'o/ /

This is under two outlines: 1. Accumulation of merit from the merit field, which correlates with the gathering of karma before one dies 2. Accumulation of wisdom by meditating upon the four gateways to freedom, correlating with death
dang po [bsod nams kyi tshogs gsag pa ]ni

d.i: Accumulation of merit from the merit field, which correlates with the gathering of karma before one dies

f.d: bskyed pa'i rim pa'i rnal 'byor ji lta ba bzhin skye ba'i mthun rkyen du bsod nams kyi tshogs gsag pa'i phyir du tshogs zhing dus kyi 'khor lo'i dkyil 'khor gyi lha tshogs spyan drangs nas 'grel pa nas bshad pa ltar gyi yan lag bdun pa sogs byed pa'o/ / de yang tshe phyi mar mir skye ba'i rgyur las bzang po gsog pa dang chos mthun no/ /

This is the practice of merit accumulation, which acts as a conducive circumstance for determining the quality of the creation of a generation-stage yoga. The merit field of the Kālacakra mandalas and deities are invited, and the seven-limbed practice and other rites as taught in the commentaries are performed. This correlates with the gathering of good karma as a cause for birth in the future life.
gnyis pa shi ba dang chos mthun par rnam par thar pa'i sgo bzhi sgom pa'i ye shes kyi tshogs gsag pa ni/

d.i: Accumulation of wisdom by meditating upon the four gateways to freedom, correlating with death

f.d:
de yang rnam thar sgo bzhi sgom pa ni 'og nas 'chad par 'gyur ba'i rten dang brten pa'i lha'i rnal 'byor sgom pa rnams bde stong gi ting nge 'dzin gyi rnam rol du 'char ba'i don du sgom pa yin la/ de yang khamasadru ga ldan gyi mi 'chi ba'i rim pa dang mthun par sgom pa ste/ chos mthun yul khams drug ldan gyi mi 'chi ba'i rim pa ni 'grel chen las/
mi'i 'jig rten 'dir mngal nas skyes pa rnams 'chi ba'i dus su chu yis me rnam par nyams par byed do/[12] / zhes dang /
phyis me med pa'i phyir 'dzin ma dag ni sra ba nyid spangs te lan tshwa bzhin du zhu bar gyur nas chur 'gyur te chu'i dbus su rab tu zhugs so/ / de nas rlung gis chu de rnams mtha' dag bskams nas nam mkha' la mi snang bar 'gyur ro/ / de ltar khams kyi tshogs myur du rnam par nyams te de nas sems ni mun pa'i mtha'i me ste zhes pa nam mkha'i khams rnam pa thams cad pa'i gzugs yul dang rnam par bral ba dbus kyi sa la kun gzhi rnam par shes pa gzhag par bya'o [13]zhes pa rnams kyis bstan cing / de dag gi don ni lus kyi chus me nyams par byas/ de nas chus sa zhu bar byas te de nas rlung gis chu bskams par byas nas rlung nyid kyang mi snang bar 'gyur te sems ni mun pa'i mtha'i me zhes pa nyer thob kyi mtha' 'od gsal stong gsal gyi ngang la rnam pa thams cad pa'i stong gzugs sna tshogs snang ba'i 'chi ba'i 'od gsal chos mthun gyi yul du ston pa'o/ /

This practice, which correlates with death, is the accumulation of wisdom by meditating upon the four gateways to freedom. The meditations upon the four gateways to freedom are deity yoga meditations involving the dependent deities and supporting mandalas, which will be explained later, arising as the play of meditative concentration of bliss and emptiness. This is a meditation that correlates with the death process for a human endowed with the six elements. The death process of a human endowed with the six elements is the actual object of correlation and is described in the Great Commentary:
At the time of death of those born from a womb in this human world, water weakens fire.[17] And further:
Then, because of there being no fire, earth loses its solidity and dissolves like salt to become liquid, dwelling within the water element. Then the element of air dries up every drop of water and disappears into space. Like this the elements quickly weaken. Then “the mind is the fire at the end of darkness,”[18] which means that the foundation consciousness is placed in the realm of space, in fully aspected forms empty of all objects, dwelling in the middle.[19] These quotes are referring to the dying process in which first the water element of the body weakens the fire element. Then water dissolves earth, air dries up water, and air itself disappears. /228/ “The mind is the fire at the end of darkness” refers to the end of the process of near-attainment,[20] when a clear light in its state of clear vacuity arises, and in which various aspected empty forms appear. This is death clear light and is an object of correlation with the above meditation.

d.div: [12] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 203_ba2
[13] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 203_ba2_nas ba4_bar/
[17] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 203b2.

[18] As this passage is written in the Great Commentary, it would appear to say that the mind is the fire at the end of darkness, with “fire” referring to the death clear light, or foundation consciousness. Gyaltsap Darma Rinchen, however, in his Practice of the Two Stages of Kālacakra, comments on this using the root quote from the Condensed Tantra that speaks of the mind after the fire and the darkness, referring to two appearances of light and darkness that arise just before the death clear light dawns.
[19] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 203b2 to 203b5.
[20] nyer thob. So called because it is close to the dawning of the death clear light.

f.d: de ltar na 'dus pa sogs kyi dgongs pa 'phags pa yab sras sogs kyis bkral ba'i 'chi ba'i dus kyi 'byung ba sdud rim dang 'chi ba 'od gsal gyi yul snang bshad pa rnams dang ma mthun pa ni rgyud nyid kyi ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo'i 'chi rim gyi khyad par yin par bya dgos par nang 'chad pa'i skabs su bshad zin pa ltar ro/ /

This explanation differs from the explanation given by the Guhyasamāja tradition of Nāgārjuna and his disciples on the order of dissolution and on the objects appearing within the death clear light. Such a difference must be attributed to a difference in the stages of the death process of the primary disciples of the tantras. This has already been dealt with in the Inner chapter.

de lta bu'i 'chi ba'i rim pa dang mthun par rnam thar sgo bzhi sgom pa ni 'grel chen las/ de'i phyir ting nge 'dzin de nyid kyis chu yis me ni rnam par nyams pa dang por 'di ni lus kyi dbus su sdom brtson rnams kyis bya/ phyi nas/ zhes pa nas/ gzhag par bya'o zhes pa'i bar sngar drangs pa rnams kyis bstan pas bde ba chen po'i ye shes rnam thar sgo bzhi'i stong pa nyid dang dbyer med pa'i stong sang gi ngang las stong gzugs pra phab pa'i rnam pa can du mos nas sgom dgos pa yin no/ / de yang stong gzugs pra phab pa'i rnam pa can du mos dgos pa ni drangs ma thag pa'i/ rnam pa thams cad pa'i gzugs yul dang rnam par bral ba dbus kyi sa la kun gzhi rnam par shes pa gzhag par bya'o/ / zhes pa'i don rnam pa thams cad pa'i stong gzugs rdul phra rab kyi yul dang rnam par bral ba rtag chad kyi mtha' dang bral ba'i dbus kyis rnam thar sgo bzhi'i stong pa nyid dang dbyer med par mos pa kun gzhi rnam shes kyi ming can 'chi ba'i 'od gsal dang mtshungs par mnyam par gzhag par bya'o/ / zhes pa yin pas so/ /

The meditations of the four gateways to freedom correlating with this death process are taught in the Great Commentary, beginning, “Therefore, through the power of this meditative concentration, the process of fire is weakened by water, and this is the meditator’s[21] first practice within the body.” As quoted above, the passage continues from “Then because of there being no fire” up to “empty of all objects.” Therefore, in the vacuity that is the indivisibility of the great-bliss gnosis and the emptiness of the four gateways, an empty form like an image in a prognostic mirror is to be visualized. The necessity of visualizing this empty form in the aspect of an image in a prognostic mirror can be found in the line “the foundation consciousness is placed in the realm of space, in fully aspected forms empty of all objects, dwelling in the middle.” This means a fully aspected empty form devoid of all objects of materiality is visualized as indivisible from the four-gateway emptiness “dwelling in the middle,” meaning divorced from the extremes of existence and nonexistence, and this visualization is a meditative equipoise in conjunction with the death clear light and goes under the name foundation consciousness.

d.div: [21] sdom brtson pa. One who practices restraint (saṃvara), an ascetic, a monk.

f.d: gal te 'grel tshig de dag gis rnam thar sgo bzhi'i stong pa nyid dang ngo bo dbyer med pa'i ye shes stong gzugs kyi rnam pa can du mos nas bsgom par bstan pa 'thad na 'dir chos sku'i rnam pa lam byed dgos pa dang ye shes kyi tshogs kyi don du sgom pa mi 'thad par 'gyur ro/ / 'o na rdul phra rab kyi chos nyid las 'das pa'i stong pa nyid kyi gzugs su rnam par bsgom par bya'o/ /zhes dang / nam mkha'i khams rnam pa thams cad pa'i gzugs zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal lo snyam na/

If those words of the Great Commentary meant that the gnosis indivisible from the emptiness of the four gateways to freedom was itself to be visualized in the aspect of empty form, it would follow that this meditation could not become a path that takes on the aspect of the dharmakāya, and neither could it be a means for the practice of accumulating wisdom. But doesn’t this contradict the two phrases “meditate upon them as empty forms beyond the reality of matter” and “in the realm of space, in fully aspected forms”? /229/

de ni mi 'gal te/ gzugs zhes pa'i skad dod rU pa zhes pa gzugs dang rang bzhin gnyis ka la 'jug pas skabs 'dir rang bzhin zhes sgyur dgos pa la gzugs zhes bsgyur ba 'gyur skyon yin zhes dwogs gcod dang bcas nas gsungs so/ / de dag la cung zad brjod par bya ste/ rU pa zhes par de bzhin du bsgyur bas chog na'ang rnam pa thams cad pa yul dang rnam par bral ba zhes pa dang / rdul phra rab kyi chos nyid las 'das pa'i stong nyid ces gsungs pa rnams stong gzugs kyi ming gi rnam grangs yin par skabs gzhan rnams su du mar gsungs pa rnams kyi don dang mi 'byor bas rU pa zhes pa gzugs su shong 'gyur sogs 'gyur du ma zhig las bsgyur ba legs so/ /

They do not because of the following reason. “Form” in Sanskrit is rūpa, which has the meaning of both “form” and “nature.” Here it should have been translated as “nature.” “Form” is a mistranslation. This is a query and resolution that has been spoken of before.[22] It should be discussed a little. It is perfectly acceptable to translate rūpa in this way,[23] but that meaning is not to be applied to the phrases “devoid of all aspects” and “emptiness beyond the nature of matter,” when used many times as synonyms of empty form in other places. Therefore, in the Shong and other translations, rūpa is often translated as “form.”[24]

d.div: [22] By Gyaltsap Darma Rinchen in his Practice of the Two Stages of Kālacakra.
[23] As “nature” and not as “form.”

[24] The gist of this discussion is that the Vimalaprabhā passage “meditate upon them [the three realms] as empty forms beyond the reality of matter,” which follows on from the above passage and is a summary of the section, appears to say that here in the meditations of the four gateways to freedom, the meditation is not one on the ultimate-truth emptiness but on conventional-truth empty form. This would contradict the assertion that this section is a meditation on the accumulation of wisdom. However Gyaltsap Jé says that the translation is at fault and that “form” (gzugs, rūpa) in the above sentence should have been translated as “nature.” This would make the sentence an instruction to meditate on ultimate or nonaspected emptiness. However not all instances of rūpa can be rendered as “nature,” because phrases such as “devoid of all aspects” and “emptiness beyond the nature of matter” are often used as synonyms of conventional-truth empty form.

f.d:
de lta na yang chos sku'i rnam pa lam byed sogs 'dir byed pa yang mi 'gal te/ skabs 'dir rnam thar sgo bzhi bsgom par gsungs pa gzhi la mi mngal skyes kyi 'chi rim dang rnam pa mthun pa dang 'bras bu la chos sku dang rnam pa mthun pa cig dgos pa'i dang po ni bshad zin pa ltar yin zhing / gnyis pa chos sku dang rnam pa mthun pa'i tshul ni/ pra phab pa lta bu'i stong gzugs kyi rnam pa can gyi mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chos thams cad rang ngos nas grub pa rdul tsam yang mi dmigs pa'i stong nyid dang dbyer med du gyur pa'i ye shes mthar thug pa ni chos sku yin la/ de dang rnam pa mthun par 'grel chen las/
rgyu ba dang mi rgyu ba dang bcas pa'i khams gsum po tshigs su bcad pa 'dis rnam par dpyad par bya ste/ dngos po med la sgom pa med/[14] / ces sogs gsungs pa ltar rgyu ba sems can dang mi rgyu ba snod kyi 'jig rten gyi khams gsum po sogs chos thams cad don dam dpyod byed kyi rigs pas rnam par dpyad de chos rnams kyi ngo bo rgyu 'bras bya byed dang bcas pa rang bzhin med par gtan la bab pa'i don stong nyid mtshan med smon med mngon par 'du byed pa med pa'i rnam thar sgo bzhi la rtse gcig tu bzhag pa'i ngang nas bde ba chen pos stong nyid rtogs bzhin pa'i ngor pra phab ba lta bu'i stong gzugs sna tshogs pa shar ba mos pa yid byed kyi sgo nas sgom pa yin no/ /

However it is not contradictory here to also practice taking on the aspects of the dharmakāya, and so forth, because the teaching here on meditations of the four gateways to freedom must teach a correlation with the basic death process of a womb-born human as well as with the resultant dharmakāya. The former has been explained. Correlation with the latter is that unchanging bliss in the aspect of a prognostic-mirror–image empty form, and indivisible from the emptiness in which not even an atom of existence exists from in its own side, is the ultimate gnosis of the dharma-kāya. On this subject of correlation the Great Commentary says:
The three realms of animate and inanimate are to be examined with this verse: “There is no meditation upon no phenomena… ”[25] This and the remaining lines of the verse mean that all phenomena, comprising the three realms of animate sentient beings and the inanimate world, are examined using ultimate reasoning, which determines that phenomena, although functioning under the process of cause and effect, have no nature. This is expressed as the four gateways to freedom — namely, being empty, without attributes, without aspiration, without engagement — and is single-pointedly concentrated upon. From within this state great bliss arises, and while this bliss is perceiving emptiness, one meditates on various visualized prognostic-mirror–like empty forms. /230/

d.div: [14] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 203_na4
[25] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 203a4.

f.d: yan lag bzhi'i rnal 'byor sgom tshul bshad pa sogs bzhi/
20. The Body Vajra
gnyis pa shi nas nying mtshams sbyar te lus skye ba'i rim pa dang chos mthun par yan lag bzhi'i rnal 'byor sgom pa

d.i: The yoga of four branches, correlating with the after-death process of linking up to a new birth and taking a body

f.d: ['di ]la bzhi/ mngal du lus grub pa dang chos mthun par dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog sgom pa sku rdo rje bsnyen pa'i yan lag dang / phyi rol du bcas te las dbang rang rang gi bya ba la 'jug pa dang chos mthun par las rgyal mchog sgom pa gsung rdo rje nyer sgrub kyi yan lag dang / thig le spro ba dang chos mthun par thig le'i rnal 'byor sgom pa thugs rdo rje sgrub pa'i yan lag dang / lo bcu drug gi mthar bde ba rdzogs pa dang chos mthun par phra mo'i rnal 'byor sgom pa ye shes rdo rje sgrub chen gyi yan lag go/

This is under four headings: 1. The branch of body-vajra approximation: A meditation on the sovereign mandala, correlating with body formation inside the womb 2. The branch of speech-vajra near accomplishment: A meditation on the sovereign activities, correlating with birth and the activities of the faculties 3. The branch of mind-vajra accomplishment: A meditation on drop yoga, correlating with the expansion of the drop 4. The branch of gnosis-vajra great accomplishment: A meditation on the yoga of the subtle, correlating with the completion of bliss at the age of sixteen
dang po dang po sku rdo rje bsnyen pa'i yan lag bshad pa/
The branch of body-vajra approximation: A meditation on the sovereign mandala, correlating with body formation inside the womb
['di ]la gnyis/ rten gzhal yas khang skyed pa gzhi dang chos mthun sbyor tshul dang / brten pa lha skyed pa gzhi dang chos mthun sbyor tshul lo/ /
This has two main outlines: 1. How the generation of the celestial mansion correlates with the ordinary base 2. How the generation of the dependent deities correlates with the ordinary base
dang po [rten gzhal yas khang skyed pa gzhi dang chos mthun sbyor tshul ]

d.i: How the generation of the celestial mansion correlates with the ordinary base

f.d: ['di ]la gsum/ gang du skye ba len pa'i gnas snod kyi 'jig rten dang chos mthun sbyar ba dang / gang gi mngal du skye ba 'dzin pa'i ma'i lus dang chos mthun sbyar ba dang / sgrub pa po rang gi lus dang chos mthun sbyar ba'o/ /

This is under three headings: 1. Correlation with the outside world, the place where one is to be born 2. Correlation with the mother’s body where womb conception takes place 3. Correlation with the practitioner’s body
dang po ni rten gzhal yas khang skyed pa gzhi dang chos mthun sbyor tshul/

d.i: Correlation with the outside world, the place where one is to be born

f.d: dkyil 'khor gyi gdan skyed pa'i skabs kyi nam mkha'i khams mtha' yas pa'i chos 'byung ni rlung gi dkyil 'khor gang du 'chags pa'i gzhi'i nam mkha' dang chos mthun/ chos 'byung gi nang du rlung gi dkyil 'khor sogs 'byung ba rim brtsegs sgom pa ni rlung gi dkyil 'khor nas sa'i dkyil 'khor gyi bar bzhi dang chos mthun/ sa'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng du lhun po rdo rje'i rang bzhin zhes sogs kyi ri rab sgom pa ni phyi'i lhun po dang chos mthun/ lhun po'i steng du sna tshoDa pad+ma sgom pa ni ri rab kyi lte ba dang chos mthun/ pad+ma'i lte ba'i dbus su zla nyi sgra gcan dang bcas pa gsum sgom pa ni phyi rol du gnam stong gi mthar zla nyi sgra gcan gsum tshoDa pa dang chos mthun no|_|

The limitless-space source triangle[26] that is produced when creating the seat of the mandala correlates with the space of the air mandala. The meditation on the stacking of the mandalas of air and so forth within the source triangle correlates with the four mandalas from air up to earth. /231/ The meditation on Meru as mentioned in the line “Upon the earth mandala, Meru, the nature of the vajra” correlates with the external Meru. The meditation on a variegated lotus upon Meru correlates with the center of Meru. The meditation on the sun, moon, and Rāhu in the center of the lotus correlates with the sun, moon, and Rāhu gathering externally at the end of the day of the empty sky.[27]

d.div: [26] chos ’byung, dharmabhava.
[27] The 30th or final day of a month.

f.d: 'og gzhi chos 'byung nas sgra gcan gyi bar mtha' dag gcig tu 'dres par gyur pa hakaShamalawarayaM zhes pa'i sa bon gyi yi ger sgom pa ni 'byung ba rim brtsegs sogs sgom pa de dag gi chos mthun gyi yul phyi nang rnams so so tha dad pa yin yang gzhal yas khang gi 'og bzhi'i 'byung ba rim brtsegs soDa dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i ye shes gcig nyid de dag gi rnam par shar bar go ba'i ched du yin no/ /

All phenomena from the source triangle up to Rāhu are visualized as blending into one and meditated upon as the seed syllables haṃ kṣa ma la wa ra ya. Although the objects of both outer and inner correlation of this stacked meditative arrangement are separate from each other, this blending into one is to show that the one gnosis of Kālacakra manifests as the stacked arrangements of the foundation below the celestial mansion.

slar yang hakaShamalawarayaM gi yi ge de dag so so las skyes pa'i nam mkha'arlu nga me chu sa ri rab pad+ma zla nyi sgra gcan gyi gdan dang bcas pa yongs su rdzogs pa'i steng du rdo rje'i gur dang / de'i nang du sku gsung thugs yongs rdzoDa kyi dkyil 'khor sgom pa'i nam mkha' rlung me chu sa lhun po pad+ma zla nyi sgra gcan gyi bar sgom pa snga phyi gnyis pa phyi dang nang la chos mthun sbyar bar bzhed nas 'byung ba rim brtsegs snga ma 'chad pa'i skabs su 'grel chen las/
'dir phyi dang nang du bskyed pa'i mtshan ma ni nam mkha'i khams mtha' yas pa dang shes rab kyi chos 'byung gru gsum mo/[15] / zhes gsungs shing /

Again the letters of the syllables haṃ kṣa ma la wa ra ya individually produce space, air, fire, water, earth, Meru, lotus, moon, sun, and Rāhu,[28] on top of whose completed forms is the vajra tent. Inside the vajra tent are the complete mandalas of body, speech, and mind. These preceding and succeeding meditations on space, air, fire, water, earth, Meru, lotus, moon, sun, and Rāhu are taught by the Great Commentary. On the first meditation it says:
The features to be created inside and out are limitless space and the three-cornered wisdom source.[29]

d.div: [15] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 203_ba7

[28] The seed syllable has ten component parts, because the haṃ is broken down into four. These are the letter ha, the crescent of the moon, the disk of the full moon, and the nāda or twist at its very top.
[29] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 203b7.

f.d:
phyi ma 'chad ba'i skabs su 'grel chen las/
hakaShamalawarayaM zhes pa sa bon gyi yi ger rnam par bsgom par bya ste de las 'jig rten gyi khams grub par bsam par bya'o zhes pa ni phyi rol du'o/ /nang du ni sngar gsungs pa'i rnam pas ma'i lus la [16]zhes sogs gsungs pa yin no/ /

On the second meditation it says:
Meditate upon the seed letters haṃ kṣa ma la wa ra ya. From them visualize that the world is produced. This is the external. The inner as previously taught is the mother’s body.[30]

d.div: [16] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 204_na6
[30] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 204a6.

f.d: de ltar lhun po'i steng du pad+ma zla nyi sgra gcan rnams kyi steng du gzhal yas khang sgom pa phyi dang chos mthun sbyar na bri bya'am bsgom pa'i gzhal yas khang khru stong ngam khru gang pa gang yin yang rung dkyil 'khor rang nyid kyi khru bzhi pa yin par nges la/ 'dir bsgom par bya ba'i dkyil 'khor ram gzhal yas khang sku gsung thugs yongs rdzogs ni che chung ji ltar sgom yang rung gzhal yas khang rang gi khru bzhi pa'i tshad can yin pas sku'i dkyil 'khor khru bzhi yod pa phyi'i rlung gi dkyil 'khor gyi phyi mtha' gcig nas cig shos kyi bar la dpag tshad 'bum phrag bzhi yod pa dang chos mthun/ sku'i dkyil 'khor gyi phyed khru do gsung dkyil la yod pa dang chu'i dkyil 'khor gyi mtha' gcig nas mtha' cig shos kyi bar la dpag tshad 'bum phrag gnyis yod pa chos mthun/ gsung dkyil gyi phyed khru gang thugs dkyil la yod pa dang sa'i dkyil 'khor la dpag tshad 'bum phrag gcig yod pa chos mthun/ thugs dkyil gyi phyed sor bcu gnyis bde chen 'khor lo la yod pa dang lhun po'i steng dpag tshad stong phrag lnga bcu yod pa chos mthun/ bde chen 'khor lo'i phyed sor drug gtso bo'i gdan gyi pad+ma la yod pa dang lhun po'i steng gi lte ba la dpag tshad stong phrag nyer lnga yod pa chos mthun/ pad+ma'i steng gi zla nyi sgra gcan brtsegs pa'i gtso bo'i gdan ni gnam stong gi mthar zla nyi sgra gcan gsum brtsegs pa dang chos mthun no/ /

When this meditation on the celestial mansion resting upon lotus, moon, sun, and Rāhu on top of Meru is applied to its outer correlation, it may be drawn or meditated upon as a thousand cubits or just one cubit square. However it is still ascertained as being a four-cubit mansion of the mandalas themselves. The mandalas or celestial mansion of complete body, speech, and mind mandalas to be meditated upon can be visualized as being of any size, but they still represent a four-cubit mandala system of the celestial mansion. The body mandala, therefore, is four cubits square. This correlates with the outer air mandala, which has a diameter of 400,000 yojana. /232/ The speech mandala, which is half the size of the body mandala at two cubits, correlates with the water mandala, which has a diameter of 200,000 yojana from rim to rim. The mind mandala, which at one cubit square is half the size of the speech mandala, correlates with the 100,00 yojana of the earth mandala’s diameter. The wheel of great bliss is twelve fingerwidths and half the size of the mind mandala, correlating with the 50,000-yojana diameter of the summit of Meru. The six-fingerwidth diameter of the lotus seat of the main deities is half the diameter of the wheel of great bliss and correlates with the 25,000-yojana diameter of the center of Meru.[31] The stacked arrangement of the moon, sun, and Rāhu upon the lotus, forming the seat of the main deities, correlates with the moon, sun, and Rāhu stacked at the end of the day of the empty sky.

d.div: [31] Meru tapers toward its base and is half its upper diameter at its midway point.

f.d: gnyis pa gang gi mngal du skye ba 'dzin pa'i ma'i lus dang chos mthun sbyar ba'o/ /

d.i: Correlation with the mother’s body where womb conception takes place

f.d: gong du bshad pa ltar nam mkha'i khams mtha' yas pa'i chos 'byung nas sgra gcan gyi bar sgom pa snga phyi gnyis ka ma'i lus dang chos mthun sbyor ba chabs cig pa yin par shes par bya zhing / de ltar chos mthun sbyor ba ni de ltar bsgom pa'i chos 'byung ni gang gi mngal du skye ba len pa'i ma'i gsang gnas kyi chos 'byung gru gsum dang chos mthun/ chos 'byung gi nang du bsgom pa'i rlung gi dkyil 'khor ni ma'i spyi bo nas dpral ba'i bar dang chos mthun/ de bzhin du ma'i dkyil 'khor sgom pa dpral pa nas mgrin pa'i bar dang chos mthun/ chu'i dkyil 'khor sgom pa mgrin pa nas snying ga'i bar dang chos mthun/ sa'i dkyil 'khor sgom pa snying ga nas lte ba'i bar dang chos mthun/ sa'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng du lhun po sgom pa ma'i lte ba nas gsang gnas kyi bar dang chos mthun/ lhun po'i steng du pad+ma sgom pa ni gsang gnas kyi pad+ma dang chos mthun/ pad+ma'i steng du bsgom pa'i zla nyi sgra gcan gsum ni ma'i bshang gci khu ba gsum 'bab pa'i rtsa gsum gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'khor gyi lte bar 'dus pa dang chos mthun/ pad+ma zla nyi sgra gcan dang bcas pa'i steng du rdo rje'i gur sgom pa ni ma'i pad+mar pha'i rdo rje zhugs pa dang chos mthun/ der gzhal yas khang sgom pa ni gang du skye ba len pa'i ma'i mngal dang chos mthun/

The two meditations explained above, involving the phenomena of the source triangle of limitless space up to Rāhu, correlate simultaneously with phenomena within the mother’s body. The visualized source triangle correlates with the triangular source of the mother’s secret area, the womb where one takes birth. The visualized air mandala correlates with the area between her crown and forehead. The visualized fire mandala correlates with the area from the forehead to the throat. The visualized water mandala correlates with the area between the throat and the heart. The visualized earth mandala correlates with the area from the heart to the navel. Meru visualized on top of the earth mandala correlates with the area from the mother’s navel to the secret area. The lotus visualized on Meru correlates with the lotus of the secret place. The moon, sun, and Rāhu visualized within the lotus correlate with the three channels carrying excrement, urine, and fluid that come together at the center of her secret-place cakra. The vajra pavilion visualized above the lotus, moon, sun, and Rāhu correlates with the vajra of the father entering the lotus of the mother. /233/ The celestial mansion visualized there correlates with the womb in which one is to be reborn.

de ltar gzhal yas khang mtshan nyid thams cad yongs su rdzogs pa'i lte bar pad+ma zla nyi sgra gcan nam dus me'i gdan gyi steng du dbyangs so gnyis kyis mtshan pa'i zla ba'i dkyil 'khor sgom pa ni mngal 'dzin pa'i pha'i khu ba dang chos mthun/ zla ba'i 'og tu gsal byed brgyad cus mtshan pa'i nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor sgom pa ni mngal 'dzin pa'i ma'i rdul dang chos mthun/ zla ba'i dbus su hUM yig ri bong gi mtshan ma lta bu las rdo rje hUM dang bcas par sgom pa ni khu khrag gi dbus su 'jug pa'i bar do'i rnam shes dang chos mthun/ de dang lhan cig pa'i hi yig sgom pa ni bar do'i rnam shes kyi bzhon pa'i rlung dang chos mthun/[17] dbyangs gsal dang bcas pa'i zla nyi dang rdo rje hUM dang haM bcas pa rnams gcig tu 'dres pa las byung ba'i sku rdzogs pa haM yig dang ldan par sgom pa ni khu khrag rnam shes bzhon pa'i rlung dang bcas pa 'dres pa yongs su gyur pa las mngal du lus thog mar grub pa dang chos mthun no/ /

At the center of the complete and fully endowed celestial mansion on the lotus, moon, sun, and Rāhu or Kālāgni seat is a moon mandala marked with the thirty-two vowels correlating with the father’s fluid at conception. The sun mandala visualized beneath the moon and marked with the eighty consonants correlates with the mother’s blood at conception. The meditation on the syllable hūḥ resting in the center of the moon, like the sign of a rabbit, from which arises a vajra marked by the syllable hūḥ, correlates with the bardo consciousness entering the blood and fluid. The syllable hi visualized at the same time correlates with the wind acting as the mount of the bardo consciousness. The meditation involving the vowels, consonants, moon, sun, vajra, merging together as one into the syllables hūḥ and haṃ, from which arises the complete form endowed with the syllable haṃ, correlates with the fluid, blood, consciousness, and its mount of wind blending together to produce the first signs of a body in the womb.

d.div: [17] ma dper cha mthun gsal/

f.d: gsum pa sgrub pa po rang gi lus dang chos mthun sbyar ba ni/

sku dkyil ni snying ga nas 'og gsang gnas kyi bar dang steng spyi bo'i bar tshun chad dang chos mthun/ gsung gi dkyil 'khor ni lte ba nas mgrin pa'i bar dang chos mthun thugs kyi dkyil 'khor ni snying ga nas lte ba'i bar gyi phyed tshun dang mgrin pa'i bar gyi phyed tshun dang chos mthun no/ / yang na thugs dkyil gsung dkyil sku dkyil gsum rim pa bzhin snying ga nas g.yas g.yon gyi dpung mgo'i bar dang nye ba'i dpung pa la drug gi bar dang sen mo'i mtha'i bar dang chos mthun no/ /

The body mandala correlates with the area of the body stretching from the heart down to the secret area and from the heart up to the crown. The speech mandala correlates with a body area ranging from the navel to the throat. The mind mandala reaches down from the heart halfway to the navel and up halfway to the throat. Alternatively the mind mandala, speech mandala, and body mandala correlate respectively with the area from the heart out to both shoulders, the area from the heart out to the elbows, and the area from the heart to the left and right fingertips. /234/
gnyis pa brten pa lha skyed pa gzhi dang chos mthun sbyor tshul

d.i: How the generation of the dependent deities correlates with the ordinary base

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ gtso bo yab yum skyed pa dang nus ma rnams dang bum pa mtshams dang bcas pa skyed pa mngal gyi zla ba gsum gyi gnas skabs dang chos mthun sbyar ba dang / gshegs pa gshegs ma sogs spro ba mngal gyi zla ba lhag ma rnams kyi gnas skabs dang chos mthun sbyar ba'o/ /

This has two outlines: 1. The generation of the main mother-and-father deity, the śakti, and the direction vases correlating with the first three months in the womb 2. The male and female tathāgatas and so forth correlating with the remaining period of growth in the womb
dang po [gtso bo yab yum skyed pa ]ni

d.i: The generation of the main mother-and-father deity, the śakti, and the direction vases correlating with the first three months in the womb

f.d: mtshan so gnyis kyi ngo bor dbyangs yig so gnyis kyis mtshan pa'i zla ba me long lta bu'i ye shes las byang chub pa dang / dpe byad brgyad cu'i ngo bo gsal byed brgyad cus mtshan pa'i nyi ma mnyam nyid ye shes las byang chub pa dang / zla ba'i steng du hUM yig las byung ba'i rdo rje hUM gis mtshan pa sor rtog ye shes las byang chub pa dang / de dang lhan cig pa'i taM yig bya grub ye shes las byang chub pa dang / de thams cad gcig tu 'dres pa las byung ba'i sku rdzogs pa hi yig dang ldan pa chos dbyings ye shes las byang chub pa mngon byang lnga las bcom ldan 'das dus kyi 'khor lo gtso bo skyed pa nas mtshan ma skyed pa'i bar ni ma rig pa dang 'du byed dang rnam shes kyi zla ba ste dang po mngal du zhugs pa nas zla ba gsum gyi bar gyi mngal 'phel ba'i gnas skabs dang chos mthun no/ /

The moon marked by the thirty-two vowels, which have the nature of the thirty-two physical signs, is the manifest enlightenment of the mirrorlike gnosis. The sun marked by the eighty consonants, which have the nature of the eighty physical marks, is the manifest enlightenment of the gnosis of equality. The vajra marked by hūḥ, arising from a hūḥ syllable upon the moon disk, is the manifest enlightenment of the gnosis of analysis. The syllable hi, coexisting with the hūḥ, is the manifest enlightenment of the wisdom of accomplishment. The fusion of these to produce the compete form endowed with the syllable haṃ is the manifest enlightenment of the wisdom of reality. These are the five manifest enlightenments from which the main deity, the conqueror Kālacakra, is formed. That moment until the generation of the emblems is a time correlating with the first three months of development in the womb, known as the months of ignorance, volition, and consciousness.

de yang gtso bo nyid kyi sku'i cha shas so sor gzhi dang chos mthun tshul ni sku gcig gi rnam pa can ni nang du dus sbyor bcu gnyis kyi bdag nyid can gyi zhag gcig dang phyi rol du lo gcig dang chos mthun/ zhabs gnyis ni nang du rlung 'pho ba'i dus sbyor drug tshan gnyis dang phyi rol du zla ba drug tshan gnyis kyi bgrod pa gnyis dang chos mthun/ mgrin pa gsum ni nang du rlung 'pho ba'i dus sbyor bzhi tshan gsum dang phyi rol du lo gcig gi zla ba bzhi tshan gsum dang chos mthun/ zhal bzhi ni nang du rlung 'pho ba'i dus sbyor sum tshan bzhi dang phyi rol du lo gcig gi zla ba sum tshan bzhi dang chos mthun/ shar dang nub dang dbus kyi g.yas g.yon gyi phrag pa drug ni nang du zhag gcig gi rlung 'pho ba'i dus sbyor nyis tshan drug dang phyi rol du lo gcig gi zla ba nyis tshan drug dang chos mthun/

The ways that various parts of the body of the main deity correlate with outer and inner phenomena are as follows. The single body correlates with a single inner solar day of twelve lagna[32] wind movements and outwardly to a single year. The two feet of Kālacakra correlate inwardly with the two sets of six lagna wind movements and outwardly to the passing of the two sets of six months. Three throats correlate inwardly with three sets of four lagna wind movements and outwardly with the three sets of four months in a year. Four faces correlate inwardly with four sets of three lagna wind movements and outwardly with the four sets of three months in a year. The six shoulders that stretch from the east to the west correlate inwardly with the six sets of two lagna wind movements and outwardly with the six sets of two months in a year.

d.div: [32] Just as lagna refers externally to the twelve zodiacal constellations appearing in a single day over the horizon at a rate of one every two hours, so here it refers to the twelve inner “ascendants” or wind movements that occur about every two hours between the petals of the navel cakra.

f.d: dpung pa bcu gnyis ni nang du rlung 'pho ba'i dus sbyor bcu gnyis dang phyi rol du lo gcig gi zla ba bcu gnyis dang chos mthun/ phyag nyi shu rtsa bzhi ni nang du rlung 'pho ba'i dus sbyor phyed pa nyi shu rtsa bzhi dang phyi rol du lo gcig gi zla ba phyed pa nyer bzhi dang chos mthun/ sor mo'i tshigs sum brgya drug cu ni nang du dbugs nyi khri chig stong drug brgya la drug cus bgos pa'i rnyed nor zhag gcig gi dbugs kyi drug cu cha sum brgya drug cu dang phyi rol du lo gcig gi zhag sum brgya drug cu dang chos mthun/ de yang phyag nyi shu rtsa bzhi po re re la sor mo lnga lnga/ sor mo re re la tshigs gsum gsum ste sum brgya drug cu'o/ /

The twelve upper arms correlate inwardly with the twelve lagna wind movements and outwardly with the twelve months of a year. Twenty-four lower arms correlate inwardly with twenty-four half lagna wind movements and outwardly with twenty-four half months in a year. The 360 joints of the fingers correlate internally with the 360 breaths that make up 1/60 of the 21,600 breaths of one day. Externally they correlate with the 360 days of a year.[33] /235/ There are 360 joints because each of the twenty-four hands has five fingers and each of the fingers has three joints.

d.div: [33] The 360 zodiacal days it takes for the sun to move once through all twelve houses.

f.d: de ltar na dus kyi 'khor lo'i sku'i cha shas rnams phyi nang de dag dang chos mthun par bsgoms pas sbyang gzhi gnyis sgrib bral du dngos su byed pa'i rdzogs rim skye ba'i rgyud smin par byas pa las 'bras dus kyi dus kyi 'khor lo'i sku da lta sgom pa ltar gyi sku'i cha shas rnams ni bshad ma thag pa'i phyi nang gi lo dang zhag dang de dag gi cha shas rnams so sor dag pa'i cha yin no/ / des na da ltar sgom pa'i skabs kyi zhabs dag gis bdud dang drag po skrag bzhin par rol pa'i stabs kyis mnan pa ni 'bras dus kyi sku'i zhabs kyis phung po dang nyon mongs pa dang 'chi bdag dang lha'i bu'i bdud de bdud bzhi dang drag po'i mtshon don 'dod chags zhe sdang gti mug nga rgyal phrag dog rnams mnan te mi gnas pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa 'khor 'das gcig tu 'dres pa mngon du byas pa mtshon pa yin no/ /

By meditating upon the correlation of the parts of the Kālacakra body with inner and outer phenomena, the mind becomes ripe for the creation of a completion-stage practice that will actually render these two bases free of obscuration. The completion-stage practice produces the resultant Kālacakra body, which is meditated upon at this point of practice and whose divisions or parts are the purified aspects of the inner and outer years, months, days, and their constituent parts as mentioned above. Therefore the feet of Kālacakra that are meditated upon at this point of practice, and that stand in a position of sport or play upon the terrified forms of Māra and Rudra, are the feet of resultant Kālacakra. One foot stands upon the four māras — the aggregates, afflictions, death, and the desire god Kāma — and the other upon the attachment, resentment, ignorance, pride, and jealousy symbolized by Rudra. The two feet symbolize the actualization of nondwelling nirvana, in which samsara and nirvana are as one.

gzhan yang sku'i rnam pa 'di nyid kyis de ltar rgyud smin par byas pa las rdzogs rim gyi rnal 'byor skye ba'i tshul yang mtshon par byed de/ gdan gyi zla nyi dus me gsum gyis rdzogs rim gyis gnad du bsnun sa'i rtsa ro rkyang dbu ma gsum mtshon/ dus me'i steng gi bdud dang drag po gnyis kyis g.yas g.yon gyi rtsa ro rkyang gnyis nas dbugs 'bab pa mtshon/ zla nyi dus me bdud drag po dang bcas pa'i steng du rol pa'i zhabs g.yas brkyang gi stabs kyis mnan pas ni ro rkyang la 'bab pa'i g.yas g.yon gyi rlung dang khams dkar dmar gnyis dbu mar bcug ste bcings pa mtshon no/ /

These features of the body also illustrate how the yoga of the completion stage is produced from this ripening of the mindstream. The deity seats comprising the moon, sun, and Kālāgni illustrate the right, left, and central channels, which are areas of penetrative focusing within the completion stage. The conch and Rudra on the Kālāgni seat illustrate the breath flowing from the left and right channels. The right leg extended in a position of sport and standing upon the moon, sun, and Kālāgni, with its conch and Rudra, illustrates the winds of the right and left channels and the red and white bodhicitta flowing into and held in the central channel.

de ltar rlung dang khams dkar dmar dbu mar bcings pa las khams dkar po spyi bor brtan pa zhabs g.yon dkar po bskums pa'i stabs kyis mtshon/ khams dmar po nor bu'i rtser brtan pa zhabs g.yas dmar po brkyang pa'i stabs kyis mtshon/ khams dkar dmar gtsug tor dang nor bu'i rtser brtan pa la brten nas rnam par shes pa mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i ngo bor skyes pa ni brla gnyis kyi dbus yan chad kyi sku mdog sngon por yod pas mtshon/ mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba de dngos su 'dren byed rjes dran gyi skabs nas 'byung ba'i stong gzugs yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can ni bcom ldan 'das dus kyi 'khor lo la sna tshogs yum gyis 'khyud pa'i yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can 'dis mtshon/

The winds and red and white bodhicitta held in the central channel causes the white bodhicitta to stabilize at the crown, which is symbolized by the white and bent left leg. The red bodhicitta stabilized at the tip of the jewel is illustrated by the extended red right leg. With the white and red bodhicitta stabilizing at the crown and the jewel, the consciousness transforms into supreme and unchanging bliss, and this is symbolized by the body of Kālacakra being blue from the top of the thighs upward. The supreme and unchanging bliss is actually induced by the yoga of recollection, where an empty form in the aspect of father-and-mother embrace arises. /236/ This is illustrated by the conqueror Kālacakra embraced by Viśvamātā in father-and-mother union.

de lta bu'i rdzogs rim gyi rnal 'byor mthar phyin pa las thob pa'i 'bras dus kyi dus kyi 'khor lo'i sku'i cha shas so so ba rnams kyi mtshon don nam dag pa ni phyi nang gi dus kyi cha shas so sor dag tshul gong du bstan zin pa rnams so/ /

From the perfection of these completion-stage yogas comes the resultant Kālacakra body, and the purified phenomena, as illustrated by the different parts of this body, will be the inner and outer time divisions explained above.
gnyis pa gshegs pa gshegs ma sogs spro ba mngal gyi zla ba lhag ma rnams kyi gnas skabs dang chos mthun sbyar ba

d.i: The male and female tathāgatas and so forth correlating with the remaining period of growth in the womb

f.d: ['di ]la lnga las/
This has four points:
dang po gshegs pa gshegs ma khro bo lnga dang bcas pa spro ba zla ba bzhi pa ming gzugs kyi zla ba'i gnas skabs kyi mngal 'phel ba dang chos mthun sbyar ba ni/

d.i: 1. The male and female tathāgatas and the five wrathful guardians correlate with the increase in the womb during the fourth, or name-and-form, month of growth

f.d: nus ma bum pa mtshan ma rnams dang bcas pa bskyed pa'i mjug tu dkyil 'khor gyi gtso bos thog mar mi bskyod pa yab yum spros nas gtso bo rang nyid kyi sku la bcugardo rje dbyings phyug ma la rdor sems kyis 'khyud pa spros nas yum la bcug ste de nas gshegs pa bzhi dang gshegs ma bzhi khro bo lnga dang bcas pa spro ba ni mngal du zhugs pa'i zla ba bzhi pa ming gzugs kyi zla ba'i gnas skabs kyi mngal na gnas pa'i lus 'phel ba dang chos mthun no/ /

After the generation of the śakti goddesses, vases, and emblems, the principal deity emanates Akṣobhya and consort, which then enter the principal deity’s body. Then Vajradhātvīśvarī embraced by Vajrasattva is emanated and enters the consort Viśvamātā’s body. Then the four male and four female tathāgatas and the five wrathful guardians are generated. This process correlates with the growth of the body within the womb during the time of the fourth month, known as name-and-form month.
gnyis pa sems dpa' sems ma spro ba zla ba lnga pa dang drug pa skye mched drug dang reg pa'i zla ba'i gnas skabs kyi mngal 'phel ba dang chos mthun sbyar ba ni/

d.i: 2. The generation of the male and female bodhisattvas correlates with the expansion of the womb during the fifth and sixth, or six sources and contact, months

f.d: khro bo lnga spros [18] pa'i rjes su nam snying sogs sems dpa' drug yum dang bcas pa spro ba dang reg bya rdo rje ma sogs sems ma drug yab dang bcas pa spro ba ni zla ba lnga pa dang drug pa skye mched drug dang reg pa'i zla ba'i gnas skabs kyi mngal na gnas pa'i lus 'phel ba zla ba lnga pa nas skye mched rnams 'grub pa'i 'go brtsams te drug pa rjogs pa'i bar gyi skye mched rnams 'phel ba dang chos mthun no/ /

After the five wrathful guardians have been generated, Khagarbha and the other five male bodhisattvas with consorts are generated. Sparśavajrā and the other female bodhisattvas with their consorts are also generated. This process correlates with the expansion of the body in the womb during the fifth, or six sources, month and the sixth, or contact, month. The six sources begin their development in the fifth month and are completed in the sixth.

d.div: [18] ma dper khro bo lnga sgros pa'i rjes su byung 'dir spros zhes bcos/

f.d: de yang lha de dang de spro ba'i ldog pa nas mngal 'phel ba'i cha de dang de chos mthun du bshad pa min zhing / gzhan yang rdor sems mi bskyod pa don grub rin 'byung snang mtha' rnam snang rnams rim pa bzhin ye shes rnam shes 'du byed tshor ba 'du shes gzugs kyi phung po ste phung po drug dang chos mthun zhing sbyang gzhi sbyong byed dang / phung po drug dag pa las gong gi rim pa bzhin gshegs pa drug dang / de bzhin du sher phyin ma rdo rje dbyings phyug ma sgrol ma gos dkar mo mA ma kI spyan ma rnams rim pa bzhin ye shes nam mkha' rlung me chu sa'i khams drug dang chos mthun zhing sbyang gzhi sbyong byed dang / khams drug dag pa las rim pa bzhin gshegs ma drug dang / de bzhin du khro bo lnga las dbang lnga dang chos mthun zhing sbyang gzhi sbyong byed dang / las dbang rnams dag pa las khro bo lnga dang / de bzhin du phyag rdor nam snying sa snying 'jig rten dbang phyug sgrib sel kun bzang rnams rim pa bzhin rna ba sna mig lce lus yid kyi dbang po ste dbang po 'am nang gi skye mched drug dang chos mthun zhing sbyang gzhi sbyong byed dang nang gi skye mched drug dag pa las rim pa bzhin phyag rdor sogs sems dpa' drug dang / de bzhin du sgra rdo rje ma reg bya rdo rje ma ro rdo rje ma gzugs rdo rje ma dri rdo rje ma chos dbyings rdo rje ma rnams rim pa bzhin sgra reg bya ro gzugs dri chos kyi skye mched de phyi'i skye mched drug dang chos mthun zhing sbyang gzhi sbyong byed dang / phyi'i skye mched drug po de dag pa las rim pa bzhin sgra rdo rje ma nas chos dbyings rdo rje ma'i bar sems ma drug go/

This does not mean that a particular generation of a celestial figure correlates only with a particular development within the womb. Vajrasattva, Akṣobhya, Amoghasiddhi, Ratnasambhava, Amitāyus, and Vairocana /237/ correlate with and are the purifiers of the six basic aggregates of gnosis, consciousness, volition, feelings, recognition, and form, respectively, and from the purified six aggregates will arise these six male tathāgatas. Similarly Prajñāpāramitā, Vajradhātvīśvarī, Tārā, Pāṇḍarā, Māmakī, and Locanā correlate with and are the purifiers of the six basic elements of gnosis, space, air, fire, water, and earth respectively. From the six purified elements will arise the six female tathāgatas. The five wrathful guardians correlate with and are purifiers of the five basic faculties, and the five wrathful guardians will arise from the purified faculties. Vajrapāṇi, Khagarbha, Kṣitigarbha, Lokeśvara, Sarvanivaraṇaviṣkambhī, and Samantabhadra correlate with and are purifiers of the six basic sense faculties, or inner sources, of ear, nose, eye, tongue, body, and mind. From the six purified inner sources of consciousness arise these six male bodhisattvas. Similarly Śabdavajrā, Sparśavajrā, Rasavajrā, Rūpavajrā, Gandhavajrā, and Dharmadhātuvajrā correlate with and purify the six basic outer sources of sound, tangibles, taste, form, smell, and mental phenomena. From the six purified outer sources will come the above six female bodhisattvas.
gsum pa gsung dkyil gyi rnal 'byor ma rnams spro ba zla ba bdun pa tshor ba'i zla ba'i gnas skabs kyi mngal 'phel ba dang chos mthun sbyar ba ni/

d.i: 3. The generation of the speech-mandala yoginīs correlates with the growth in the womb during the seventh, or feeling, month

f.d: thugs dkyil gyi lha rnams spros pa'i rjes su gsung dkyil gyi rnal 'byor ma tsA ra tsi ka la sogs pa bdun cu rtsa gnyis spro ba ni mngal du zhugs pa nas brtsams pa'i zla ba bdun pa tshor ba'i zla ba'i gnas skabs kyi mngal na gnas pa'i lus 'phel ba dang chos mthun no/ / gzhan yang gsung dkyil gyi lha mo bdun cu rtsa gnyis ni lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi rtsa 'dab drug cu rtsa bzhi dang / mgrin pa'i rtsa 'khor la dang por rtsa 'dab bzhir gyes/ de bzhi po re re la gnyis gnyis su gyes pa'i rtsa 'khor gyi zlum sgor gnyis pa'i rtsa 'dab brgyad dang bcas pa'i rtsa bdun cu rtsa gnyis dang chos mthun zhing rtsa bdun cu rtsa gnyis po de dang lha mo bdun cu rtsa gnyis po sbyang gzhi sbyong byed dang / rtsa de rnams dag pa las lha mo bdun cu rtsa gnyis so/ / de yang rten gyi gsung gi dkyil 'khor ni mgrin pa nas lte ba'i mthar thug pa gru bzhir gnas pa dang chos mthun pa'i gnad kyis so/ /

After the figures of the mind mandala have been generated, the seventy-two yoginīs of the speech mandala, such as Carcikā and so forth, are generated. This process correlates with the growth in the womb seven months after conception during the feelings month. Furthermore the seventy-two goddesses of the speech mandala correlate with the sixty-four channel petals of the navel channel plus the eight channel petals on the second rim of the throat cakra, which have split off and doubled from the first four petals of that cakra. These seventy-two channel petals and seventy-two goddesses are phenomena to be purified and purifiers respectively. From the purified channel petals come the seventy-two goddesses. /238/ This correlation is due to the speech mandala itself correlating with the square area formed between the throat and the navel.
bzhi pa tshes lha sum brgya drug cu spro ba zla ba brgyad pa sred pa'i yan lag gi zla ba'i gnas skabs kyi mngal 'phel ba dang chos mthun sbyar ba ni/

d.i: 4. The generation of the 360 lunar-day deities correlates with growth in the womb during the eighth, or grasping, month

f.d: gsung gi rnal 'byor ma rnams spros pa'i rjes su sku dkyil gyi lha tshes lha sum brgya drug cu spro ba ni mngal du zhugs pa'i zla ba brgyad pa'i gnas skabs kyi mngal na gnas pa'i lus 'phel ba dang chos mthun zhing gzhan yang tshes lha sum brgya drug cu ni nang du lag pa dang rkang pa'i las kyi 'khor lo dang bya ba'i 'khor lo gnyis kyi nang nas las kyi 'khor lo rkang lag gi tshigs chen bcu gnyis kyi tshigs re re la rtsa sum cu re yod pa'i nyi shu rtsa brgyad kyi rtsa re re dang 'khor gyi tshes lha re re chos mthun/ pad+ma'i lte ba rnams na gnas pa'i gtso bo yab yum zung re dang rtsa 'dab lhag ma gnyis re chos mthun zhing phyi'i lo gcig gi tshes zhag sum brgya drug cu dang yang chos mthun no/ / de bzhin du phyi nang gi tshes zhag dang rtsa de rnams sbyang gzhi dang / tshes lha rnams sbyong byed dang / phyi nang gi tshes dang rtsa de dag dag pa las tshes lha sum brgya drug cu'o/ /

After the emanation of the speech-mandala yoginīs, the 360 deities of the lunar days are generated within the body mandala. They correlate with the growth of the body within the womb during the period of the eighth month after conception. These 360 deities of the days also correlate with the channels of the action-faculty cakras, as opposed to the activity wheels, found within the hands and feet. On each of the twelve major limb joints, there are thirty channels. Of these, twenty-eight channels correlate with the twenty-eight entourage deities of the days. The two remaining channel petals correlate with the main deities in father-and-mother aspect in the center of the lotus. The 360 deities also correlate with the 360 lunar days[34] of an external year. The inner and outer phenomena of the channels and lunar days are the basic phenomena to be purified. The deities of the lunar days are the purifiers. From the purified outer and inner lunar days and from the purified channels come the 360 deities of the days.

d.div: [34] The fifteen days of waxing and fifteen of waning, multiplied by twelve.

f.d: de yang rkang lag gi tshigs chen phrag pa dang dpung pa'i bar dang / dpung pa dang nye ba'i dpung pa'i bar dang / nye ba'i dpung pa dang lag mgo'i bar g.yas g.yon gnyis su phye bas drug dang / dpyi dang brla'i bar dang / brla dang byin pa'i bar dang / byin pa dang rkang mgo'i bar g.yas g.yon gnyis su phye bas drug ste bcu gnyis la las kyi 'khor lo zer ba'i rgyu mtshan ni tshigs chen de rnams las kyi dbang po bya ba la 'jug pa'i dang por gyur pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis yin no/ / de bzhin du rkang lag gi sor mo nyi shu'i tshigs drug cu po la bya ba'i 'khor lo zer ba'i rgyu mtshan yang rkang lag gi sor tshigs de rnams kyis len pa dang 'gro ba la sogs pa'i bya ba byed pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis yin no/ / rkang lag gi sor mo nyi shu re re la tshigs gsum gsum tshigs re la rtsa drug drug ste sum brgya drug cu'o/ / rtsa de rnams kyang tshes lha rnams dang chos mthun zhing sbyang gzhi sbyong byed dang / tshes lha rnams rtsa de rnams dag pa yang yin no/ /

The major joints of arm and leg comprise one joint between shoulder and upper arm, one between upper and lower arm, and one between lower arm and hand, making six joints on the arms. On the legs there is a joint between the hip and the thigh, between the thigh and the lower leg, and between the lower leg and the foot, making six joints on the legs. These twelve major joints are known as action-faculty cakras. The reason is that these major joints are action faculties that initiate activities. Similarly the sixty joints of the twenty digits of hands and feet are known as activity cakras, because the joints of hands and feet engage in the activities of taking, going, and so forth. Each of twenty digits of the hands and legs has three joints, and each joint has six channels, to make a total of 360. These channels correlate with the deities of the days and are the basic phenomena to be purified by them. The deities of the lunar days are the purified channels.

de rnams kyang sbyang gzhi sbyong byed so sor zhib tu phye na nag pa zla ba'i tshes lha sum cu ni g.yon pa'i dpung pa dang nye ba'i dpung pa'i tshigs [19] kyi rtsa sum cu dang / lag pa g.yon pa'i mthe'u chung gi tshigs dbus ma nas mthe bo'i tshigs dbus ma'i bar gyi tshigs rnams re re la rtsa drug drug ste sum cu yod pa dang rim pa bzhin sbyor/

The correlation between purifier and phenomena to be purified can be broken down in more detail. /239/ The thirty deities of the lunar month Caitra correlate with the thirty channels of the cakra on the joint between the left upper arm and lower arm. The five joints from the middle joint of the little finger of the left hand to the middle joint of the left thumb each contain six channels, and the thirty deities of Caitra also correlate with these thirty channels.

d.div: [19] ma dper tshogs zhes snang /

f.d: de bzhin du sa ga zla ba'i tshes lha rnams dang g.yas pa'i nye ba'i dpung pa dang lag mgo'i tshigs kyi rtsa sum cu dang / lag pa g.yas pa'i mthe bong nas mthe'u chung gi bar gyi tshigs gong ma'i tshigs re la rtsa drug drug ste sum cu yod pa dang rim pa bzhin sbyor/

There is a similar correlation between the lunar-day deities of the month of Vaiśākha and the thirty channels of the cakra between the right lower arm and right hand, as well as the thirty channels comprising the six channels on each of the joints from the upper joint of the right thumb to the upper joint of the right little finger.

ston gyi zla ba'i tshes lha rnams dang g.yon pa'i nye ba'i dpung pa dang lag mgo'i tshigs kyi rtsa sum cu dang / lag pa g.yon pa'i mthe'u chung nas mthe bo'i bar gyi tshigs gong ma rnams re re la rtsa drug drug ste sum cu yod pa dang rim pa bzhin sbyor/

The lunar-day deities of the month of Jyeṣṭha correlate with the thirty channels of the cakra on the joint between the left lower arm and the left hand, as well as with the thirty channels of the five upper joints from the left little finger to the left thumb.

de bzhin du chu stod zla ba'i tshes lha rnams g.yas pa'i dpyi dang brla'i tshigs kyi rtsa dang rkang pa g.yas pa'i mthe bong nas mthe'u chung gi bar gyi tshigs 'og ma rnams kyi rtsa dang rim pa bzhin sbyor/

The lunar-day deities of the month of Aṣaḍha correlate with the thirty channels of the cakra on the joint between the right hip and right thigh, as well as with the thirty channels of the lower joints from the big toe to the little toe of the right foot.
gro zhun zla ba'i tshes lha rnams g.yon gyi brla dang dpyi'i tshigs kyi rtsa dang / rkang pa g.yon pa'i mthe'u chung nas mthe bo'i bar gyi tshigs 'og ma rnams kyi rtsa dang sbyor/

The thirty lunar-day deities of the month of Śrāvana correlate with the channels of the joint between the left thigh and left hip, as well as with the channels of the lower joints running from the little toe to the big toe of the left foot.

khrums kyi zla ba'i tshes lha rnams g.yas kyi brla dang byin pa'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa dang / rkang pa g.yas pa'i mthe bong nas mthe'u chung gi bar gyi tshigs bar pa rnams kyi rtsa dang rim pa bzhin sbyor/

The lunar-day deities of the month of Bhādra correlate with the channels of the joint between the thigh and the calf of the right leg, as well as with the thirty channels of the middle toe joints that run from the big toe to the little toe of the right foot.

tha skar gyi zla ba'i tshes lha rnams g.yon pa'i brla dang byin pa'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa rnams dang / rkang pa g.yon pa'i mthe'u chung nas mthe bo'i bar gyi tshigs bar pa rnams kyi rtsa dang sbyor/

The lunar deities of the month of Aśvinī correlate with the channels of the joint between the thigh and the calf of the left leg, and with the channels that run across the left foot from the middle joint of the little toe to the middle joint of the big toe.

smin drug gi zla ba'i tshes lha rnams g.yas pa'i byin pa dang rkang mgo'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa rnams dang / rkang pa g.yas pa'i mthe bo nas mthe'u chung gi bar gyi tshigs gong ma rnams kyi rtsa dang sbyor/

The lunar-day deities of the month of Kārttikā correlate with the channels of the joint between the calf and foot of the right leg, and with the channels of the upper joints of the toes of the right foot from the big toe to the little.

mgo'i zla ba'i tshes lha rnams g.yon pa'i byin pa dang rkang mgo'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa rnams dang / rkang pa g.yon pa'i mthe'u chung dang mthe bo'i bar gyi tshigs gong ma rnams kyi rtsa dang rim pa bzhin sbyor/

The lunar-day deities of the month of Mṛigaśira correlate with the channels of the joint that lies between the calf and the foot of the left leg, and with those that run across the left foot from the upper joint of the little toe to the upper joint of the big toe.

rgyal gyi zla ba'i tshes lha rnams g.yas pa'i phrag pa dang dpung pa'i tshigs kyi rtsa rnams dang / lag pa g.yas pa'i mthe bo nas mthe'u chung gi bar gyi tshigs 'og ma rnams kyi rtsa dang rim pa bzhin sbyor/

The lunar-day deities of Puṣya correlate with the channels of the joint between the right shoulder and right upper arm, and with those of the lower joints that stretch from the thumb to the little finger of the right hand.

mchu'i zla ba'i tshes lha rnams g.yon pa'i phrag pa dang dpung pa'i tshigs kyi rtsa rnams dang / lag pa g.yon pa'i mthe chung nas mthe bo'i bar gyi tshigs 'og ma rnams kyi rtsa dang rim pa bzhin sbyor/

The lunar-day deities of Maghā correlate with the channels of the joint between the left shoulder and left upper arm, and with the channels of the bottom joints of the fingers of the left hand running from the little finger to the thumb. /240/

dbo'i zla ba'i tshes lha rnams g.yas pa'i dpung pa dang nye ba'i dpung pa'i tshigs kyi rtsa rnams dang / lag pa g.yas pa'i mthe bong nas mthe chung gi bar gyi tshigs bar pa rnams kyi rtsa dang rim pa bzhin sbyor te/

The lunar-day deities of Phālguna correlate with the channels of the joint between the right upper and lower arm, and with the channels of the middle finger joints that run from the thumb to the little finger of the right hand.
de yang gong du bshad pa bzhin chos mthun dang sbyang gzhi sbyong byed dang lha rnams rtsa rnams kyi dag pa yin pa sogs su yang shes par bya'o/ /

As explained previously, the correlation between the deities and channels above is one of purifier and phenomenon to be purified, and the above lunar-day deities are the purified forms of the channels.

gal te sbyang gzhi'i rtsa rnams dang / de dag sbyong byed kyi tshes lha rnams dang / zla ba de dang de'i tshes lha de rnams mthun pa cig dgos pa ma yin nam/ sgrub pa las ni tsa sde la dbyangs thung ngu srog tu zhugs pa las lugs bzlog tu nag zla'i tshes lha rnams bskyed par bshad cing / sa ga'i tshes lha rnams ni tsa sde la dbyangs ring po lnga tsheg drag dang bcas pa'i drug srog tu zhugs pa las lugs 'byung du bskyed pa sogs su bshad la/ nang le'i re bdun pa'i 'grel chen las/
de bzhin du g.yas pa'i nye ba'i dpung pa'i tshigs la nag pa'i zla ba'i rtsa rnams dang g.yon pa'i nye ba'i dpung pa'i tshigs la sa ga'i zla ba'i rtsa rnams dang[20] zhes sogs rgya cher gsungs pa rnams kyis nag zla'i tshes rnams g.yas kyi dpung pa dang nye ba'i dpung pa'i tshigs kyi rtsa dang sbyar ba dang / sa ga zla ba'i tshes rnams g.yon gyi dpung pa dang nye ba'i dpung pa'i tshigs kyi rtsa la sbyar zhing / nag zla'i tshes rnams kyi sa bon tsa sde la dbyangs ring po lnga tsheg drag dang bcas pa'i drug srog tu zhugs pa lugs 'byung dang / sa ga zla ba'i tshes rnams kyi sa bon tsa sde la dbyangs thung ngu lnga rjes su nga ro dang bcas pa'i drug srog tu zhugs pa lugs bzlog tu bshad pa sogs dang ji ltar mi 'gal snyam na/ dwogs pa skye ba ni shin tu bden te/ de la mi 'gal ba'i rgyu mtshan yang dag par brjod par bya'o/ /

The following doubt can arise here. Surely there is agreement on the channels to be purified and the lunar-day deities that purify them, as well as which deities are of which months? However the Methods of Accomplishment chapter explains that the lunar-day deities of Caitra are created from the ca consonant group in reverse order and with short vowels embedded, and that the Vaiśākha lunar-day deities are created from the ca consonant group in forward order, and with the five long vowels and the visarga[35] embedded. This contrasts with the Great Commentary on the sixty-seventh verse of the Inner chapter, which says:
Similarly on the joint of the right lower arm are the channels of Caitra, and on the joint of the left lower arm are the channels of Vaiśākha.[36] This quote, which continues with extensive explanation, says that the lunar days of Caitra are to be applied to the channels of the right upper and lower arm joint, and that the lunar days of Vaiśākha are to be applied to the channels of the joint between the left upper and lower arm. It also states that the Caitra lunar-day seed syllables of the ca consonant group with five long vowels plus the visarga embedded are created in forward order, and that the Vaiśākha lunar-day seed syllables of the ca consonant group with five short vowels plus the anusvāra[37] embedded are created in reverse order. How can these two not be contradictory? This is a very valid doubt, and the reason why it is not contradictory will be well explained.

d.div: [20] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 150_na4
[35] tsheg drag (or rnam bcad). Echo-like aspiration of preceding vowel, romanized as ṃ.
[36] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 150a4.
[37] rjes su nga ro (or thig kor). Nasalizing of previous vowel, romanized as ṃ.

f.d: de la thog mar 'di ltar du shes dgos te/ nyi bar lug khyim du zhugs pa nas glang khyim du zhugs pa'i bar gyi khyim zhag sum cu ni g.yon pa'i dpung pa dang nye ba'i dpung pa'i tshigs kyi rtsa sum cu dang sbyar bar bya ba dang / de bzhin du glang khyim gyi zhag rnams g.yas pa'i nye ba'i dpung pa dang lag mgo'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa dang sbyor ba nas/ 'khrig khyim g.yon gyi nye ba'i dpung pa dang lag mgo'i tshigs kyi rtsa dang / karka Ta g.yas kyi dpyi dang brla'i tshigs kyi rtsa dang / seng ge g.yon gyi dpyi dang brla'i tshigs kyi rtsa dang / bu mo g.yas kyi brla dang byin pa'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa dang / srang g.yon gyi brla dang byin pa'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa dang / de bzhin du sdig pa g.yas kyi byin pa dang rkang mgo'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa dang / gzhu g.yon gyi byin pa dang rkang mgo'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa dang / chu srin g.yas kyi phrag pa dang dpung pa'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa dang / bum pa g.yon gyi phrag pa dang dpung pa'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa dang / nya'i khyim du nyi bar zhugs pa'i khyim zhag sum cu ni g.yas kyi dpung pa dang nye ba'i dpung pa'i bar gyi tshigs kyi rtsa sum cu dang sbyor/

First of all, understand this. The thirty zodiacal days from when the mean sun enters the house of Aries until it enters the house of Taurus are to be applied to the thirty channels of the left elbow joint. Similarly the days of Taurus are applied to the channels of the right wrist joint. The days of Gemini are applied to the channels of the left wrist joint. /241/ The days of Cancer are applied to the channels of the right hip joint. The days of Leo are applied to the channels of the left hip joint. The days of Virgo are applied to the channels of the right knee joint. The days of Libra are applied to the channels of the left knee joint. The days of Scorpio are applied to the channels of the right ankle joint. The days of Sagittarius are applied to the channels of the left ankle joint. The days of Capricorn are applied to the channels of the right shoulder joint. The days of Aquarius are applied to the channels of the left shoulder joint. The thirty zodiacal days of the mean sun entering the house of Pisces are applied to the thirty channels of the right elbow joint.

de ji lta bar 'grel chen la gsungs pa ste/ nang le'i re bdun pa'i 'grel chen de nyid las/
de rnams las g.yas pa'i phrag pa dang dpung pa'i tshigs la chu srin gyi tshes grangs sum cu'i dbyibs rtsa sum cu'o/[21] / zhes chu srin gyi khyim zhag sum cu g.yas kyi phrag pa dang dpung pa'i tshigs kyi rtsa dang sbyor bar gsungs shing / yang nang le'i re brgyad pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir mchu'i zla ba dang chu srin gyi 'pho ba la tshes kyi dbye bas/[22] zhes chu srin gyi khyim dang / mchu'i zla ba sbyor bar gsungs/

How that is taught in the Great Commentary can be found in its text on the sixty-seventh verse of the Inner chapter of the Condensed Tantra:
Among them, on the joint of the right shoulder and upper arm, are the thirty channels of the thirty-day division of Capricorn.[38] This teaches that the thirty zodiacal days of Capricorn are to be applied to the channels of the right shoulder joint. The Great Commentary continues on the sixty-eighth verse:
The divisions of days of Maghā and the passage of Capricorn…[39] Thus the house of Capricorn and Maghā are linked.

d.div: [21] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 150_na3
[22] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 152_ba7
[38] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 150a3.
[39] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 152b7.

f.d:
de bzhin du de nyid kyi 'grel chen las/
'dir dbo'i zla ba dang bum pa'i 'pho ba g.yon pa'i phrag pa dang dpung pa'i tshigs kyi las kyi 'khor lo'i rtsa sum cu po rnams la/[23] zhes bum khyim dang dbo zla sbyar zhing / de gnyis g.yon gyi phrag pa dang dpung pa'i tshigs la sbyar ba dang / de bzhin du nya khyim dang nag zla/ lug dang sa gaglang dang snron/ 'khrig pa dang chu stod/ karka Ta dang gro zhun/ seng+ge dang khrums/ bu mo dang tha skar/ srang dang smin drug /sdig pa dang mgo/ /gzhu'i khyim dang rgyal gyi zla ba sbyar te/

On the same verse, the Great Commentary continues:
Here Phālguna and the passage of Aquarius are the thirty channels of the faculty cakra of the joint between the left shoulder and upper arm.[40] Thus the house of Aquarius and the month Phālguna are paired, and both are applied to the left shoulder joint. Similarly the house of Pisces is paired with Caitra, Aries with Vaiśākha, Taurus with Jyeṣṭha, Gemini with Asaḍha, Cancer with Śrāvana, Leo with Bhādra, Virgo with Aśvinī, Libra with Kārttikā, Scorpio with Mṛigaśira, and Sagittarius with Puṣya.

d.div: [23] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 152_ba7
[40] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 152b7.

f.d:
yang nang le'i re bdun pa'i 'grel chen las/
g.yon pa'i phrag pa dang dpung pa'i tshigs la dbo'i zla ba'i tshes grangs sum cu'i dbye bas rtsa sum cu'o/[24] / zhes dang / de bzhin du g.yas pa'i nye ba'i dpung [25] pa'i tshigs la nag pa'i zla ba'i zhes dang / g.yon pa'i nye ba'i dpung pa'i tshigs la sa ga'i zla ba'i zhes dang / g.yas pa'i lag pa dang nye ba'i dpung pa'i tshigs la snron gyi zla ba'i zhes dang / g.yon pa'i lag pa dang nye ba'i dpung pa'i tshigs la chu stod kyi zla ba'i zhes dang / g.yas pa'i brla dang dpyi'i tshigs la gro bzhin gyi zla ba'i zhes dang / g.yon pa'i brla dang dpyi'i tshigs la khrums kyi zla ba'i zhes dang / g.yas pa'i brla dang byin pa'i tshigs la tha skar gyi zla ba'i zhes dang / g.yon pa'i brla dang byin pa'i tshigs la smin drug gi zla ba'i zhes dang / g.yas pa'i rkang pa dang byin pa'i tshigs la mgo'i zla ba'i zhes dang / g.yon pa'i rkang pa dang byin pa'i tshigs la rgyal gyi zla ba'i tshes sum cu'i rang bzhin gyi rtsa sum cu ste/ zhes khyim zla dang tshes zla sbyor tshul 'di ltar gsungs pa sogs kyi 'grel pa rnams gong 'og bsgrigs pa na rkang lag gi tshigs chen bcu gnyis kyi rtsa rnams dang khyim rnams sbyor tshul gong du bshad pa ltar yin par grub la/

Moreover the Great Commentary continues on the sixty-seventh verse:
On the joint of the left shoulder and upper arm are the thirty channels of the thirty-day division of Phālguna.[41] The text continues, “Caitra is on the right upper arm joint,” “Vaiśākha is on the joint of the left upper arm,” /242/ “Jyeṣṭha is on the joint of the right lower arm and hand,” “Aṣaḍha is on the joint of the left lower arm and hand,” “Śrāvana is on the joint of the right hip and thigh,” “Bhādra is on the joint of the left hip and thigh,” “Aśvinī is on the joint of the right thigh and calf,” “Kārttikā is on the joint of the left thigh and calf,” “Mṛigaśira is on the joint of the right calf and foot,” and “on the joint of the left foot and calf are thirty channels of the nature of the thirty days of Puṣya.” If the earlier and later passages from the Great Commentary on the pairing of zodiacal months and lunar months[42] are compared, it can be seen that they verify the way the houses linked with the channels of the twelve major joints of the arms and legs have been explained here.

d.div: [24] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 150_na3_'di man chad lung 9_nye 'gram du yod pas mchan zur du bkod med/
[25] ma dper dgung gsal yang 'grel chen du dpung zhes gsal bas bcos yod/
[41] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 150a3.
[42] Each of the houses of Aries, Taurus, etc., mentioned above is one house or zodiacal month of thirty days, and each of the months of Caitra, Vaiśākha, etc., is a lunar month of thirty days.

f.d: de ltar yin pa gzhir bzhag ste tshes zla rnams dang bsgrigs pa'i tshe tshes zla rnams la yar ngo sngon 'gro dang mar ngo sngon 'gro gnyis su yod pa'i mar ngo sngon 'gro'i dbang du byas pa'i tshes zla dang khyim zla sgrig tshul ni lug khyim sa ga zla ba dang sbyor ba sogs 'grel pa drangs ma thag pa rnams kyis bshad pa ltar yin la/ de ltar byas pa'i tshe lug khyim gyi khyim zhag rnams kyi sa bon tsa sde la dbyangs thung ngu lnga rjes su nga ro dang bcas pa drug srog tu zhugs pa'i rtsa sde lugs bzlog tu bshad pa de sa ga zla ba'i tshes rnams kyi'ang sa bon du bshad dgos shing / de bzhin du nya khyim gyi zhag rnams kyi sa bon tsa sde la dbyangs ring po lnga tsheg drag dang bcas pa drug srog tu zhugs pa'i tsa sde lugs 'byung du bshad pa de nag pa zla ba'i tshes rnams kyi'ang sa bon du 'gyur ba sogs su bshad dgos so/ /

This can be taken as a basis. Lunar months are either waxing or waning-led.[43] On the basis of being waning-led, the way that lunar months and zodiac months are paired is that the house of Aries is paired with Vaiśākha and so forth, as taught by the Great Commentary above. When that occurs, the seed syllables of the zodiacal days of Aries, which comprise the ca consonant group with the five short vowels and anusvāra embedded, and which occur in reverse order, must also be explained as being the seed syllables of the lunar day deities of Vaiśākha. Similarly, the seed syllables of the zodiacal days of Pisces, which comprise the ca consonant group with the five long vowels and visarga embedded, and which occur in forward order, must also be explained as being the syllables the lunar-day deities of Caitra.

d.div: [43] They either begin from the new moon (waxing-led) or from the full moon (waning-led).

f.d: 'o na khyim zhag dang tshes zhag sogs kyi sa bon gyi yi ge la mtha' gcig tu nges pa med dam snyam na/ de ni nges pa med de/ nang le'i re bdun pa'i 'grel par bshad pa rnams ni dus kyi 'chi ba lo brgya lon ba'i mthar 'chi ba'i tshe de'i sngon rol du lo gsum phyogs gsum gyi rtsa gcod pa'i zhag gi dbang du byas pa'i zhag gi sa bon rnams gsungs pa yin la/ de yang 'chi ltas kyi rtsa gcod pa'i zhag yin pas khams rnams sdud rim gyis gcod pa dang / gsal byed kyi yi ge ka sde nas gcod pa dang / rkang lag gi tshigs chen drug gi nang nas thog mar g.yas pa'i phrag pa dang dpung ba'i tshigs dang / de nas g.yon pa'i phrag pa dang dpung pa'i tshigs dang / de nas g.yas pa'i dpung pa dang nye ba'i dpung pa'i tshigs dang / de bzhin du g.yas g.yon spel ma'i g.yon gyi byin pa dang rkang pa'i tshigs kyi bar du'o/ /

But isn’t it possible to ascertain definitive sets of seed syllables for the lunar days and zodiacal days? There are no fixed seed syllables. The explanations from the sixty-seventh verse of the Inner chapter describe the seed syllables of the days belonging to the period of the gradual disintegration of the channels that begins three years and three months before the timely end of a hundred-year life. As this channel disintegration is a sign of oncoming death, it is a disintegration brought on by the elements gradually withdrawing. The consonants disappear beginning with the ka group, and from the major joints of the arms and legs, /243/ the channels of the right shoulder and upper arm joint are the first to die, followed by those of the left shoulder joint, those of the right elbow joint, and so on, alternating right and left as far as the channels of the left ankle.

de yang g.yas kyi tshigs kyi rtsa rnams shes rab kyi phyogs yin pas sa bon gyi gsal byed rnams brtsegs pa dang / gsal byed sde tshan rnams lugs 'byung dang / dbyangs ring po tsheg drag dang bcas pa lugs bzlog tu srog tu zhugs pa'o/ / g.yon gyi tshigs kyi rtsa rnams thabs kyi phyogs yin pas gsal byed rkyang pa dang sde tshan rnams lugs bzlog dang / dbyangs thung ngu rjes su nga ro dang bcas pa lugs mthun du srog tu zhugs pa rnams gcod do/ /

The channels of the joints on the right arm and leg are those of wisdom. In the process of dying, their seed-syllable consonants are therefore stacked, the consonant groups are in forward order, and the long vowels plus visarga are embedded in the consonants in reverse order. The channels of the left arm and leg are method channels, and the consonant groups therefore are single, in reverse order, and the short vowels plus anusvāra are embedded in the consonants in forward order

de yang dper mtshon na g.yas kyi phrag pa dang dpung pa'i tshigs kyi rtsa sum cu la rim pa bzhin/ k+kA k+k+l-I k+kU k+k+r-Ik+kIk+kAM/ de bzhin du kha dang ga dang g+ha dang nga la yang sbya ra bas sum cu'o/ /

This can be illustrated with an example. The stacked syllables kkāṃ, kkḷīṃ kkā, kkī, kkū, kkṛī, kkī, kkā, together with the same vowels on each the consonants kha, ga, gha, and ṅa to make thirty syllables in total, are applied to the thirty channels of the right shoulder joint.
