[61] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 363a4.

f.d: sgrub le'u 'grel pa gong du drangs pa ltar lha chen bcu gnyis kyi zhal phyag gi rnam pa dang phyag mtshan dang ra ba'i rtsig pa'i phyogs dang mtshams su gang dang gang dgod pa shin tu gsal por bstan cing / phyogs mtshams gang dang gang du bkod pa'i lha chen bcu gnyis kyi sku mdog kyang thugs dkyil gyi phyogs mtshams gang dang gang du bkod pa'i sems dpa' sems ma bcu gnyis po de dang de'i sku mdog dang 'dra bar byed par 'grel chen gyi/ nam mkha'i snying po la sogs pa bzhin du bden bral la sogs pa rnams grangs bzhin du zhes gsungs pa 'dis gsal bar bstan pas sgo rnams kyi g.yon phyogs su bkod pa'i khyab 'jug dang gshin rje dang drag po dang nor sbyin rnams gong du bshad pa ltar gyi sku mdog sngon po dang ljang gur byed pa thugs dkyil gyi sgo'i g.yon phyogs rnams su bkod pa'i sems dpa' sems ma phyag rdor dang kun bzang dang sgra rdo rje ma dang chos dbyings rdo rje ma rnams sngon mo dang ljang gur byed pa dang 'dra bar byed pa yin no/ / gal te 'grel tshig de dag gis de ltar ma bstan na 'di'i skabs kyi 'grel tshig gzhan rnams kyis ma bstan pas/[37] nam mkha'i snying po la sogs pa bzhin du zhes nam snying sogs dang 'dra bar ston pa'i brjod bya'i don med par 'gyur te/ tshes lha rnams kyi sku mdog ma gtogs ra ba'i rtsig pa'i phyogs gang du dgod pa la sogs pa nam snying sogs dang 'dra ba'i cha gzhan rnams skabs 'di'i 'grel tshigs gis dngos zin la gsal por bstan pas so/ /

Moreover the previous passage from the Methods of Accomplishment chapter clearly lays out the twelve great deities with their number of hands, faces, hand implements, and where and in what direction of the wall they are placed. With the words “like Khagarbha and the others, Nairtya and so on are numbered,” the colors of these twelve deities in their respective places are clearly stated as being similar to the colors of the twelve male and female bodhisattvas in their respective places in the mind mandala. Therefore the deities Viṣṇu, Yama, Rudra, and Kubera positioned on the left of the four gates are green and blue, as explained above, in the same way that the male and female bodhisattvas Vajrapāṇi, Dharmadhātuvajrā, Samanta bhadra, and Śabdavajrā in the mind mandala are also green and blue. If that is not the meaning of the above passages, then the line “like Khagarbha and the others,” which teaches a similarity to Khagarbha and other bodhisattvas, and which is not taught elsewhere in this section, would become meaningless, because except for the colors of the lunar-day deities, all other features such as their positions in the wall being similar to those of Khagarbha and so forth are dealt with and clearly taught in this section of text.

d.div: [37] ma dper ma bstan pa'i zhes byung yang ma bstan pas zhes bcos/

f.d:
gzhan yang sgrub le'i zhe gnyis pa'i 'grel chen las/
rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor la nam mkha' dang 'og na gnas pa'i lha mo gang su yang rung ba de rnams ni shar dang nub kyi rta babs kyi 'og tu blta bar bya ste phyogs skyong la sogs pa rnams bsgom pa ni ji ltar gsungs pa'i gnas nyid du'o/ / sgo'i g.yon gyi kun du bzang po la sogs pa bzhi yang de bzhin no zhes pa nges pa'o/[38] / zhes nam mkha' dang [39] 'og na gnas pa'i lha mo nam mkha'i khams pa dang ye shes kyi khams pa ljang gu dang sngon mo gang su yin yang rung rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor la 'god pa'i tshe shar nub kyi rta babs kyi 'og tu dgod ces bshad nas steng 'og gi lha phyogs skyong khyab 'jug drag po gshin rje nor sbyin rnams dang / sems dpa' sems ma kun du bzang po la sogs pa nam mkha' dang ye shes kyi khams pa ljang gu dang sngon po rnams steng 'og gi lha mo bzhin du nam mkha' dang 'og tu sgom dgos sam snyam pa'i dwogs pa sel ba la/ phyogs skyong la sogs pa rnams sgom pa ni ji ltar gsungs pa'i gnas nyid du'o/ / sgo'i g.yon gyi kun tu bzang po la sogs pa bzhi yang de bzhin no zhes gsungs pa 'dis kun bzang sogs bzhi dang / khyab 'jug sogs bzhi po steng dang 'og gi lhar bstan kyang sgrub thabs sgom pa'i tshe sgrub le'i der ji ltar gsungs pa'i gnas nyid du sgom dgos par bstan la/ de ltar khyab 'jug sogs bzhi po steng dang 'og gi lhar bstan pa nyid kyis khyab 'jug sogs bzhi po gong du bshad pa bzhin gyi sku mdog ljang gu dang sngon por byed dgos par grub ste/ dus kyi 'khor lo'i lha steng gi nam mkha'i khams pa rnams ljang gu dang 'og gi ye shes kyi khams pa rnams sngon por byed dgos pas so/ /

Furthermore the Great Commentary says on the forty-second verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter:
In the colored-powder mandala all the goddesses who dwell in space and below, whoever they may be, are below the portals of the east and west gates. The direction protectors and so forth are meditated upon as dwelling in the places as taught. The four, Samantabhadra and others, on the left of the gate are similar.[62] Therefore when the powder mandala is drawn, /252/ the green and blue space-element and gnosis-element goddesses dwelling above in space and in the lower regions are all placed under the east and west portals. To resolve a doubt as to whether the green and blue space-element and gnosis-element deities among the upper and lower direction protectors Viṣṇu, Rudra, Yama, and Kubera, and the male and female bodhisattvas Samantabhadra and so forth, should be visualized as being above and below like the upper and lower goddesses, the passage continues, “The direction protectors and so forth are meditated upon as dwelling in the places as taught. The four, Samantabhadra and others, on the left of the gate are similar.” This illustrates that although Samantabhadra and so forth and Viṣṇu and so forth have been taught as being upper and lower gods, when meditating on the sādhana, one should meditate on their positions as taught in the Methods of Accomplishment chapter. Therefore explaining Viṣṇu and the others as being upper and lower gods establishes these four as being green and blue as previously explained. This is because the space-element upper deities of Kālacakra are green and the lower gnosis-element goddesses are blue.

d.div: [38] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 215_ba2
[39] ma dper nam mkha'i dang 'og na zhes byung yang nam mkha' dang zhes bcos/
[62] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 215b2.

f.d:
gzhan yang sA ng+hu pu tra'i sgrub thabs las/
'di rnams dang bcas shar lho'i g.yon du bya khyung pad+ma dmar po'i steng nas kaM yig dang / / 'khor lo las byung khyab 'jug ljang gu'i lus la dpal mo gnod sbyin dang ni mtshungs pas 'khyud/[40] / ces dang / yang de nyid las/
saM yig dang ni rtsa gsum las byung 'phrog byed sngon po rtse gsum mda' dang kha T+wAM ga[41] / zhes khyab 'jug ljang gu dang / 'phrog byed [42] dam drag po sngon por gsungs shing gnod sbyin drag po dang mtshungs par 'ong rgyu la/ gnod sbyin nor bu dbyug pa sre mo dang / pad+ma rnams ni phyag na 'dzin pa khyab 'jug dang mtshungs/ zhes nor sbyin nam gnod sbyin khyab 'jug dang sku mdog mtshungs par bshad pa dang / gshin rje khyab 'jug dang mtshungs par 'ong rgyu yin pa la/ dus kyi phyag gis 'dzin la 'phrog byed dang mtshungs gshin rje zhes gshin rje drag po dang sku mdog mtshungs par bshad pa rnams ni dpe ma dag pa 'am 'gyur skyon gang rung du shes par bya dgos te/ dper na sgrub thabs de nyid las/ a yig dang ni rdo rje dag las byung ba'i sgra yi rdo rje ma ste sgra yi rang bzhin dang / dpal ldan phyag rdor dang bcas [43] zhes pa 'ong rgyu la/ dpal ldan phyag rdor dang mtshungs zhes sgra rdo rje ma phyag rdor dang mtshungs par bshad pa bzhin no/ /

The sādhana composed by Sādhuputra states:
These are in the south. Left of the east on a red garuda and lotus the letter kam and a wheel, from which arises a green Viṣṇu in embrace with Lakṣmī, who is similar to Yakṣa.[63] Also:
From the letter sam and a trident arises a blue Hari with a trident, arrow, and a khaṭvāṅga[64] staff.[65] This text therefore states that Viṣṇu is green and Hari, or Rudra, is blue. In the same text, where one would expect Yakṣa to be similar to Rudra, the sādhana states, “Yakṣa holds a jewel, club, mongoose, and lotus and is like Viṣṇu,” thereby explaining that Kubera, or Yakṣa, is of a color similar to Viṣṇu. Where one would expect Yama to be similar to Viṣṇu, the text has, “Yama, similar to Hari,” thereby explaining that Yama is similar in color to Rudra. These must be misprints or mistranslation. /253/ For example, in what should read, “From vajras and from the letter a arises Śabdavajrā, of the nature of sound, together with Vajrapāṇi,” the sādhana reads, “similar to Vajrapāṇi,”[66] thereby stating that Śabdavajrā is similar to Vajrapāṇi.[67]

d.div: [40] sde dge_1358_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pasAd+hU pu tra'i sgrub thabs/ 106_ba1
[41] sde dge_1358_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pasAd+hU pu tra'i sgrub thabs/ 107_na4

[42] ma dper sA ng+hu pu tra'i lung drangs pa na 'phrog byed la 'phreng byed dang / gsham du 'phros byed ces gsal yang yig nor yin te 'di dbang phyug gi ming gi rnams grangs yin pas 'phrog byed du bcos yod/
[43] sde dge_1358_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pasAd+hU pu tra'i sgrub thabs/ 104_na5
[63] Toh 1358 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 106b1.
[64] Club or staff with skull at one end, often carried by Śiva.
[65] Toh 1358 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 107a4.
[66] Toh 1358 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 104a5.
[67] Instead of saying that she is embraced by Vajrapāṇi.

f.d: de ltar na sA ng+hu pu tras kyang khyab 'jug ljang gu dang drag po sngon por bshad kyi khyab 'jug nag po dang drag po dkar po dang nor sbyin ser po dang gshin rje dmar po sogs su tshes lha'i skabs 'dir zur tsam yang ma bshad pa dag gis gnod do/ /

Therefore Sādhuputra also explains Viṣṇu as green and Rudra as blue, whereas in this section on the lunar-day deities, there is no mention at all of Viṣṇu as black, Rudra as white, Kubera as yellow, and Yama as red. This damages the former assertion.

'on te tshes lha'i skabs 'dir de ltar du ma bstan kyang skabs gzhan du bstan pa las tshes lha'i skabs 'dir yang khyab 'jug nag po len pa sogs su shes pa la dgongs nas skabs 'dir ma gsungs pa yin no snyam na/

They may reply that it may not be mentioned in this section on the lunar-day deities but it is taught elsewhere, and so cannot we infer, in this section on lunar-day deities, that also Viṣṇu is black and so forth and that is the reason it was not taught in this particular section?

de yang srung 'khor gyi skabs su ni dbang le'i 'grel chen las/
lha g+hA las grub pa tshangs pa dang khyab 'jug ljang gu dang sngon po dag ni ra ba'i khyon gyi tshad kyis steng du tshangs pa dang 'og tu khyab 'jug ste/[44] zhes khyab 'jug sngon por bshad cing / khyab 'jug 'og tu 'god pa sngon por bshad pas 'og ye shes kyi khams pa sngon por byed pa dang tshes lha sa sde las skyed pa ye shes kyi khams pa sngon por byed pa dang mthun/

In the Initiation chapter, in the section on the protection wheel, the Great Commentary says:
From gha and ghā arise Brahmā and Viṣṇu, green and blue. Brahmā is above the fence area and Viṣṇu below.[68] This describes Viṣṇu as being blue and says that Viṣṇu is placed below. Therefore this accords with the gnosis element below being blue and with the lunar deity emanating from the gnosis sa consonant series as being blue.

d.div: [44] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 275_ba3
[68] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 275b3.

f.d:
yang de'i mjug de ma thag tu/
de bzhin du lho dang bden bral du b+h+r-i D+h-I las grub pa gshin rje dang me lha dag ni/[45] zhes gshin rje dmar por bshad pa dang khyed kyis tshes lha'i gshin rje 'khor bcas dmar por bshad pa mthun yang / srung 'khor gyi gshin rje ni sa bon D+h+r-i las bskyed pa me khams pa lho phyogs pa yin la tshes lha'i gshin rje 'khor bcas ni sa bon ka sde las bskyed pa nam mkha'i khams pa steng phyogs kyi lha yin pas gshin rje zhes pa'i ming 'dra ba tsam mo/ / yang de nyid las/
byang dang dbang ldan du b+hu b+hU las grub pa rgya mtsho dang bde byed dag ni [46] zhes/ drag po dkar por gsungs pa dang khyed kyis tshes lha'i drag po dkar por byas pa mthun yang / srung 'khor gyi drag po'am bde byed ni sa bon b+hu las bskyed pa chu khams pa byang phyogs kyi lha dang / tshes lha'i drag po 'khor bcas ni sa bon sa sde las bskyed pa ye shes kyi khams pa 'og phyogs kyi lha yin pas drag po zhes par ming 'dra ba tsam mo/ / de bzhin du nor sbyin yang de dang 'dra bar shes par bya ste de rnams rang rang gi sa bon khams gang yin gyi kha dog can du snang ba dang /

The Great Commentary continues:
Similarly, in the south and southwest from ḍhṛ and ḍhṛī, Yama and Agni.[69] This describes Yama as being red, which agrees with your[70] description of the lunar-day deity Yama and entourage as being red. However the protection-wheel Yama, which emanates from the syllable ḍhṛī, is of the fire element and is in the south. The lunar-day Yama and entourage is produced from the ka consonant series, is of the space element, and is a deity of the upper direction. Therefore they are similar in name only. Furthermore the Great Commentary says:
In the north and northeast from bhu and bhū come Samudra and Śaṅkara[71] This passage talks of a white Rudra, which agrees with your assertion of a white lunar-deity Rudra. However the Rudra, or Śaṅkara, of the protection wheel is produced from the syllable bhū, is of the water element, and is in the north. The lunar-day Rudra and his entourage emerges from the sa consonant group, is of the gnosis element, and is a god of the lower directions. They are, therefore, similar in name only. The same is true of Kubera. /254/ They all arise in the colors of the element of their syllables.

d.div: [45] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 275_ba5
[46] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 275_ba4
[69] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 275b4.
[70] Those who follow Abhayākaragupta in their presentation of the colors.
[71] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 275b5.

f.d: gzhan yang sA d+hu pu tra'i sgrub thabs las/ haHyig dbyug pa dag las byung ba'i phag mo dmar mo dang ni bde byed dkar po dang bcas/[47] zhes phag mo dmar mo la drag po dkar pos 'khyud par bshad pa dang / de bzhin du drag mo dkar mo la gshin rje dmar pos 'khyud pa dang / tshangs ma ser mo la 'phrog byed dam khyab 'jug nag pos 'khyud par bshad pa'i phag mo tshor ba'i rigs can ma la 'khyud pa'i drag po ni 'du shes kyi rigs can chu'i khams pa yin pas dkar po dang / tshangs ma gzugs kyi rigs can ma la 'khyud pa'i khyab 'jug ni 'du byed kyi rigs can rlung gi khams pa yin pas nag po dang / drag mo 'du shes kyi rigs can ma la 'khyud pa'i gshen rje ni tshor ba'i rigs can me'i khams pa yin pas sku mdog dmar por rigs pa yin te/

Moreover Sādhuputra’s sādhana says, “From the syllable haḥ and from a club arises a red Vārāhī and a white Śaṅkara,”[72] explaining that red Vārāhī is embraced by white Rudra. Similarly it is explained that white Rudrī is embraced by red Yama, and yellow Brahmāṇī is embraced by a black Hari,[73] or Viṣṇu. The white Rudra who embraces the feelings-aggregate Vārāhī is of the recognition aggregate, of the water element, and is therefore white. The Viṣṇu embracing the form-aggregate Brahmāṇī is of the volition aggregate, of the air element, and is therefore black. The Yama who embraces the recognition-aggregate Rudrī is of the feeling aggregate, of the fire element, and is therefore red.

d.div: [47] sde dge_1358_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pasAd+hU pu tra'i sgrub thabs/ 105_na4
[72] Toh 1358 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 105a4.
[73] ’phrog byed. Hari is a title given to different gods. Previously it was listed as epithet of Rudra, and here as an epithet of Viṣṇu.

f.d:
de ltar yang sgrub le'i gya gsum pa'i 'grel chen las/
phag mo dang gzhon nu ma ni tshor ba'i rigs can ma'o/ / de dag la mngon du phyogs pa ni 'du shes kyi rigs can thabs te u yig las skyes pa'o/ / dbang mo dang tshangs ma ni gzugs can ma'o/ / de dag la mngon du phyogs pa ni 'du byed kyi rigs can thabs te e yig las skyes pa'o/ / drag mo dang dpal mo ni 'du shes kyi rigs can ma'o/ / de dag la mngon du phyogs pa tshor ba'i rigs can ni thabs te r-i yig las skyes pa'o/[48] / zhes gsungs pas so/ /

The Great Commentary says on the eighty-third verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter:
Vārāhī and Kaumārī are of the feeling aggregate. Those facing them are of the recognition aggregate and arise from the letter u. Aindrī and Brahmāṇī are goddesses of the form aggregate. Facing them are those of the volition aggregate, who arise from the syllable e. Rudrī and Lakṣmī are of the recognition aggregate, and those facing them are of the feeling aggregate, arising from the letter ṛ.[74]

d.div: [48] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 225_na2
[74] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 225a2.

f.d: de ltar na srung 'khor du khyab 'jug 'og gi srung ma yin pas sngon por bshad pa dang / de bzhin du srung 'khor gyi drag po sogs dang / gsung dkyil gyi gtso mo rnams la 'khyud pa'i drag po sogs rang rang gi sa bon dang 'byung ba che ba'i dbang du byas pa'i khams dang phyogs gang yin gyi sku mdog can du bshad pa bzhin du tshes lha'i skabs 'dir yang rang rang gi sa bon dang 'byung ba che ba'i dbang du byas pa'i khams dang phyogs gang yin gyi sku mdog can du byed dgos pa yin te/ dper na dbang le'i 'grel chen las/ de bzhin du lho dang bden bral du ng+h+r-i ng+h+r-I las grub pa gshin rje dang me lha dag ni zhes ng+h+r-i yig gi ng+ha 'di 'byung ba chung ba'i dbang du byas na rlung yin yang / Ta sde 'byung ba che ba'i khams yin pa dbang btsan par byas nas gshin rje dang me lha dmar por mdzad pa dang /[49] de bzhin du de'i 'phro las byang dang dbang ldan du b+hu b+hU las grub pa rgya mtsho dang bde byed dag ni/[50] zhes b+hu yig gi b+ha 'di 'byung ba chung ba'i dbang du byas na rlung yin yang / pa sde 'byung ba che ba'i chu'i khams yin pa dbang btsan par byas nas rgya mtsho dang bde byed sku mdog dkar por mdzad pa bzhin no/ /

Therefore, in the protection wheel, Viṣṇu is a protector of the lower directions and is therefore blue. Likewise the Rudra and the other figures of the protection wheel and the Rudra and other deities embracing the main female deities of the speech mandala are of elemental and directional colors determined by their individual syllables and major elements. In the same way, here in this section, the lunar-day deities must necessarily be of elemental and directional colors determined by their individual syllables and major elements. For example, in the Initiation chapter, the Great Commentary says, “Similarly, in the south and southwest from ḍhṛ and ḍhṛī, Yama and Agni.”[75] On the basis of the minor elements, the syllable dha as the root of ḍhṛ is air, but the ṭa consonant group is predominant and determined as being of the major element of fire, thereby creating in that section a red Yama and Agni. Similarly, the text continues, “In the north and northeast from bhu and bhū come Samudra and Śaṅkara.”[76] /255/ The bha of the syllable bhu is space on the basis of the minor elements, but the pa consonant group predominates and is determined to be of the major water element, and so Samudra and Śaṅkara are posited as white.

d.div: [49] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 275_ba4
[50] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 275_ba5
[75] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 275b4.
[76] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 275b5.

f.d: de dag gi phyir na/ tshes zla re re'i yum rnams ma gtogs pa'i tshes lha sum bcu po sde tshan lngar byas pa'i sde tshan lnga po'i sa bon rnams 'byung ba chung ba'i dbang du byas na khams mi 'dra ba nyid yin yang 'byung ba che ba'i dbang du byas na tshes lha nyer dgu nyer dgu'i sa bon thams cad 'byung ba'i khams gcig tu mtshungs pas tshes lha re re'i tshes lha yum rnams ma gtogs pa'i nyer dgu nyer dgu sku mdog mtshungs pa yin no/ /

Therefore, with the exception of the individual consorts of the main lunar-day deities, the thirty lunar deities are put in five groups. On the basis of the minor elements, the syllables of these five groups will produce varying elements. However, on the basis of the major elements, every syllable of the twenty-nine deities is the same, and apart from the consort of each lunar-day main deity, the colors of the twenty-nine are the same.

a b+ha ya'i dgongs pa ltar byed pa'i sgrub byed la/ sgrub thabs sgom pa dang rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor la 'god pa'i tshe khyab 'jug shar du 'god pas nag por byed pa sogs ni sgrub byed du mi che ste/ de ni thugs dkyil gyi sgo'i g.yon rnams su bkod pa'i sems dpa' sems ma rnams la yang mtshungs pas so/ / de ltar na gsung dkyil gyi rang rang gi gtso mo la 'khyud pa'i khyab 'jug nag po dang drag po dkar po dang gshin rje dmar por mdzad pa 'di sgrub byed kyi gtso bor byed rigs te/ de yang ji ltar na gsung dkyil gyi skabs su gtso mo la 'khyud pa'i tshul gyis spros pa'i khyab 'jug sogs de nyid sku dkyil gyi'ang dbo zla sogs kyi tshes zla'i gtso bor spros pa yin pas tshes lha'i skabs kyi khyab 'jug sogs dang / gsung dkyil gyi gtso mo la 'khyud pa'i khyab 'jug sogs sku mdog nag po sogs su mtshungs pa yin no/ /zhes pa nyid sgrub byed kyi dam par mthong ngo / /

Using Abhayākaragupta’s assertion, it is not much of a reason to say that Viṣṇu is black because when meditating on the sādhana and placing deities in the mandala he is in the east,[77] for the same would have to apply to the male and female bodhisattvas placed on the left of the gates of the mind mandala also. Therefore the main reason for his position must be that in the speech mandala there is a black Viṣṇu, a white Rudra, and a red Yama, all embracing the main female deities. Viṣṇu and the others who emanate embracing the main female deities of the speech mandala also emanate as the main deities of Phālguna and the other lunar months in the body mandala. Therefore Viṣṇu and the others as lunar-day deities, and Viṣṇu and the others embracing the main female deities of the speech mandala, must be similar in being black and so forth. This I think is the best reason.

d.div: [77] The colors normally assigned to the four directions in Kālacakra are black in the east, white in the north, red in the south, and yellow in the west.

f.d: de dag ni mgo rgyal mchu dbo rnams kyi tshes lha'i sku mdog mtha' cig tu ljang gu dang sngon por 'dod pa dang / mtha' gcig tu nag po sogs phyogs mdog tu 'dod pa yin la/ bdag cag gi bla ma mkhas pa (rje shes rin pa )[51] dag ni sku mdog de dag gdam nga can du bzhed de/ 'on kyang gzu bor gnas pa'i blos zhib pa'i rnam dpyod kyis dpyad par bya bar rigs so/ /

Again, these two assertions are (1) that the colors of the lunar-day deities of Mṛigaśira, Puṣya, Maghā, and Phālguna are definitely green and blue or (2) that they are definitely black and so forth in accord with the colors of the directions. Our wise gurus (such as the great Sherap Rinchen) maintain that either position is acceptable. Nevertheless this is a topic to be thoroughly and honestly examined.

d.div: [51] 'dir yig chung du bdag cag gi bla ma mkhas pa dag ni zhes pa stag tshang lo tsA ba shes rab rin chen la ngos bzung mdzad 'dug mod dpyad gzhir snang /

f.d: de nas tshes lha rnams spros pa'i rjes su zla ba brgyad pa sred pa'i zla ba de nyid la mngal du gnas pa'i lus kyi cha shas rkang lag gi mthil bzhi dang gtsug tor dang bshang lam gyi rtsa rnams rdzogs par 'phel ba dang chos mthun par sku dkyil gyi khro bo yab yum rnams spro ba dang / de'i rjes su mngal du zhugs pa nas brtsams pa'i zla ba dgu pa len pa la mngal na gnas pa de'i lus kyi cha shas rkang lag gi sor mo nyi shu'i rtsa rnams rjogs par 'phel ba dang chos mthun par rtsa de rnams dag pa'i klu dang rab gtum ma rnams spro ba ste/ de yang rkang sor gyi rtsa bcu dag pa'i klu bcu dang / lag sor gyi rtsa bcu dag pa'i rab gtum ma bcu'o/ / mngal du zhugs pa nas brtsams pa'i zla ba dgu pa de nyid la mngal na gnas pa de'i pags pa'i mthar ba spu dang skra skyes pa dag chos mthun par rlung gi 'khor yug gi mthar 'byung po bye ba phrag phyed dang bzhi spro ba'o/ /

After the emanation of the lunar-day deities, /256/ the wrathful male and female guardians are generated to correlate with the eighth “grasping” month of pregnancy, during which the channels of the palms of the hands, the soles of the feet, the crown, and the anus are completed. After that, the nāgas and the fierce females generated in correlation with the ninth or “taking” month of pregnancy, when the twenty finger and toe channels are completed. The ten nāgas are the purified forms of the channels of the ten toes, and the ten ferocious females represent the purified forms of the channels of the ten fingers. The thirty-five million elemental spirits inhabiting the far regions of the air mandala correlate with the period in the ninth month of pregnancy when hair and body hair has grown.

de ltar na mngal du zla ba dgu gnas pa'i mthar mngal na gnas pa'i mi khams drug ldan gyi lus rdzogs pa dang chos mthun par 'byung po bye ba phrag phyed dang bzhi spros pa yan chad kyis sbyang gzhi dang mthun pa'i dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi sku gsung thugs kyi dkyil 'khor gyi lha tshogs rdzogs par spros zin par bya dgos te/ sgrub le'i so brgyad pa'i 'grel chen las/
de bzhin du ba spu dang skra rnam par dag pas phyed dang bcas pa bye ba phrag gsum gyi 'byung po'i skye gnas g.yo ba'i mthar zhes pa rlung gi dkyil 'khor gyi mthar te pags pa'i mthar spu rnams so zhes pa sngags pas phyi rol du spro bar bya ste de ltar zla ba dgu pa'i mthar lus dang lha'i tshogs rdzogs pa'o/[52] /zhes gsungs pas so/ /

This generation process, up to the emanation of the thirty-five million elemental spirits, correlates with the completion of a human body endowed with the six elements after nine months in the womb. It also represents the completion of the deity generation within the body, speech, and mind mandalas of the sovereign mandala as applied to the bases of purification. The Great Commentary, on the thirty-eighth verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, states:
Likewise the purified hair on head and body represented by the thirty-five million elemental spirits are born at the “far edges of movement,” which means at the farther reaches of the air mandala. They are generated outside because hair is known to be on the skin at the far reaches of the body. In this way the body at the end of nine months and the collection of deities is complete.[78]

d.div: [52] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 214_ba6
[78] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 214b6.

f.d: 'o na thugs dkyil gyi mchod lha rnams dang 'dod ma rnams dang phyir 'dod ma rnams dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi skabs 'dir spros pa rnams sku gsung thugs gsum gyi dkyil 'khor gyi lha sbyang gzhi dang mthun par spros pa yin nam snyam na/ 'di dag ni 'dus pa sogs dkyil 'khor gzhan la 'dod snam la mchod pa'i lha mo sgom pa dang 'dra bar sbyang gzhi dang chos mthun mi sbyor bar mngon te/ 'byung po bye ba phrag phyed dang bzhi spros pa yan chad kyis mngal gyi gnas skabs dang chos mthun sbyor ba'i lha spro ba rdzogs par gsungs shing / thugs dkyil gyi mchod lha dang 'dod phyir 'dod rnams mngal gyi gnas skabs dang chos mthun sbyor ba 'grel chen las kyang ma gsungs la/ dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi lha spro ba gzhi dang sbyor na mngal gyi gnas skabs dang sbyor dgos pa'i phyir ro|_|

The offering goddesses of the mind mandala and the goddesses of desire and nondesire are generated here in the sovereign mandala, and it may be wondered if they are generated as deities of the body, speech, and mind mandalas correlating to particular bases of purification. It would appear that they are not applied to bases of purification in the same way that the terraced offering goddesses are in other mandalas, such as those of Guhyasamāja. This is because the emanation of the thirty-five million elemental spirits represents the completion of deity manifestation applied to the duration of pregnancy, and the mind-mandala offering goddess and the desire and nondesire goddesses are not mentioned in the Great Commentary as correlating with a period of pregnancy. /257/ Moreover, if the deities generated within the sovereign mandala are to be applied to particular bases, they must be applied to the periods of pregnancy.

'on kyang zhe gnyis pa'i 'grel chen las/
de bzhin du de nas snying ga'i rtsa bcu'i rang bzhin gyi thugs kyi dkyil 'khor gyi sgo bzhi'i g.yas dang g.yon gyi stegs bu la mchod pa'i lha mo spro bar bya ste shar du dri ma dang phreng ba ma dang /[53] zhes thugs dkyil gyi mchod lha bcu snying ga'i rtsa bcu'i dag par ni gsungs so/ /

However the Great Commentary says on the forty-second verse:
Then, in the nature of the ten channels of the heart, on terraces to the left and right of the four doors of the mind mandala, offering goddesses emanate. In the east the goddesses of scent and of garlands.[79] This passage says that ten mind-mandala offering goddesses are purified forms of the ten channels at the heart cakra.

d.div: [53] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 215_ba1_tshig sna cung mi mthun/ ma dper phreng ba ma byung yang phreng ba mar bcos/
[79] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 215b1.

f.d: de ltar na yang snying ga'i rtsa dang chos mthun sbyor ba ni min te/ dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi lha spro ba gzhi dang chos mthun sbyor ba'i tshe lha spro ba sde tshan sde tshan du bcad de mngal du zla ba re re zhing lus kyi cha shas 'phel ba dang chos mthun sbyor ba yin la/ snying ga'i rtsa bcu ni gsung dkyil gyi rnal 'byor ma rnams spro ba dang chos mthun pa'i lte ba'i rtsa 'dab re bzhi mgrin pa'i rtsa 'dab brgyad rnams skyes pa'am 'phel ba'i snga rol du rdzogs par skyes zin cing / mchod lha spro ba ni/ de bzhin du de nas zhes 'byung po rnams spros pa'i rjes su spro bar gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

However they cannot be correlated with the ten channels of the heart, because when the deities in the sovereign mandala are applied to various bases, each group of deities correlates with a particular month of pregnancy and to a stage of development in the womb. The ten channels at the heart develop before the sixty-four channels at the navel and eight channels at the throat, which correlate with the speech-mandala yoginīs. These offering goddesses, on the other hand, are generated after the elementals, as is stated by the words “Then, in the nature of” above.

de ltar na dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi skabs su dngos su gsungs pa'i lha zhal phyag gi rnam pa can gyi grangs ni gtso bo yab yum gnyis nus ma brgyad de bcu/ de'i steng du gshegs pa bzhi la gshegs ma bzhis 'khyud pa dang / de bzhi la gshegs pa bzhis 'khyud pa ste bcu drug bsnan pas nyi shu rtsa drugade'i steng du sems dpa' drug la sems ma drug gis 'khyud pa dang / de drug la sems dpa' drug gis 'khyud pa ste nyi shu rtsa bzhi dang thugs dkyil gyi khro bo yab yum bcu ste sum cu rtsa bzhi bsnan pas drug cu/ de'i steng du thugs dkyil gyi mchod pa'i lha mo bcu bsnan pa'i lha yab yum so sor bgrangs pa'i bdun cu ni thugs dkyil gyi lha grangs so/ /

Therefore the sum total of deities actually described in terms of their number of faces and hands in this section on the sovereign mandala is as follows. The main father and mother plus the eight śakti are ten. Four male tathāgatas are embraced by four female tathāgatas, and those four females are separately embraced by four male tathāgatas to make sixteen tathāgatas. This totals twenty-six deities. Six male bodhisattvas are embraced by six female bodhisattvas, and those six female bodhisattvas are embraced by six male bodhisattvas, to make twenty-four bodhisattvas,[80] which together with the ten father-and-mother wrathful guardians from the mind mandala makes thirty-four and brings the total to sixty. With the ten mind-mandala offering goddesses, this makes seventy mother-and-father deity figures. This is the number of deities in the mind mandala.

d.div: [80] Therefore each male and female tathāgata and bodhisattva appears twice.

f.d: de'i steng du gsung dkyil gyi nya ba'i gtso mo brgyad [54] la rang rang gi yab kyis 'khyud pa dang bcas pa'i yab yum bcu drugagatso mo re la 'khor gyi lha mo brgyad brgyad de drug cu rtsa bzhi dang bcas pa'i brgyad cu bsnan pas brgya lnga bcu/ de'i steng du 'dod ma so drug bsnan pas brgya gyadru ga ste gsung dkyil yan chad kyi lha grangs so/ /

In the speech mandala each of the eight main goddesses is embraced by a god, making sixteen mother-and-father deities. Each of the main goddesses has an entourage of eight goddesses, making sixty-four and bringing the total to eighty. This totals 150 deities so far. The thirty-six desire goddesses make 186 deities up to and including the speech mandala.

d.div: [54] 'dir ma dper gsung dkyil gyi nya ba'i gtso mo brgyad ces byung yang / nya ba'i zhes pa de ldi lir ma dpe dpar bskrun skabs bris bcos byas pa yin snang bas phal cher ma dag par nges shing rtsa ba'i gtso mo brgyad ces pa min nam snyam yang yid brtan ma brnyed pas rang sor bzhag yod/

f.d: de'i steng du tshes lha sum brgya drug cu dang / sku dkyil gyi khro bo drug yab yum bcu gnyis dang bcas pa'i sum brgya don gnyis bsnan pas lnga brgya nga brgyad/ de'i steng du klu yab yum nyi shu/ rab gtum ma yab yum nyi shu ste bzhi bcu bsnan pas lnga brgya go brgyad/ de'i steng du phyir 'dod ma sum cu rtsa drug bsnan pas drug brgya dang so bzhi 'byung ba ni sku mdog dang zhal phyag gsal por gsungs shing / sku mdog dang zhal phyag sogs mi gsal ba'i tshul gyis 'byung po bye ba phrag phyed dang bzhi spro bar gsungs pa rnams ni sgrub le'i dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi skabs su gsal bar gsungs pa rnams so/ /

There are the 360 lunar-day deities and twelve body-mandala wrathful guardians comprising six father-and-mother pairs, which makes 372 and 558 in total. /258/ There are ten nāgas in mother-and-father union and ten fierce females also in mother-and-father union. This makes 598 deities. The thirty-six nondesire goddesses make 634. These are figures whose colors, numbers of hands, and faces are all clearly taught. The emanations of the thirty-five million elemental spirits are taught in a way that does not clarify the numbers of hand and faces. These are clearly described in the Methods of Accomplishment chapter in the section on the sovereign mandala.

gzhan yang de'i steng du dur khrod brgyad po re re na lha bcu gcig bcu gcig gnas par gsungs pa'i brgyad cu gya brgyad bsnan na bdun brgya dang nyer gnyis 'ong ba ni 'byung po bye ba phrag phyed dang bzhi ma gtogs pa'i dus kyi 'khor lo sku gsung thugs yongs rdzogs kyi dkyil 'khor gyi lha grangs so/ /

Furthermore it is taught that there are eleven deities in each of the eight cemeteries, to make eighty-eight figures in the cemeteries. This makes a total of 722. Apart from the thirty-five million elemental spirits, these are the total number of deities in the complete body, speech, and mind mandalas of Kālacakra.

de dag kyang spyir btang la lus bsam gnyis kyi lus kyi dbang du byas na lha steng phyogs pa rnams sku mdog ljang gu dang / 'og phyogs pa rnams sngon po dang / shar dang shar lho pa rnams nag po dang / lho dang lho nub pa rnams dmar po dang / byang dang byang shar ba rnams dkar po dang / nub dang nub byang ba rnams sku mdog ser po dang / bsam pa'i dbang du byas na de las bzlog ste shes par bya ste/ lus steng phyogs pa'i yab rnams bsam pa 'og phyogs pa'i rang rang gi yum rnams la zhugs pa dang / de bzhin du lus steng phyogs pa'i yum rnams bsam pa 'og phyogs pa'i rang rang gi yab rnams la zhugs pas so/ / de bzhin du shar dang shar lho pa rnams dang nub dang nub byang pa rnams thabs shes dang / lho dang lho nub pa rnams dang byang dang byang shar pa rnams thabs shes yin no/ /

In terms of mind and body, “body” deities are generally green in the upper regions, blue in the lower regions, black in the east and southeast, red in the south and southwest, white in the north and northeast, and yellow in the west and northwest. “Mind” deities are the reverse. “Body” upper-region fathers embrace “mind” lower-region mothers, and “body” upper-region mothers embrace “mind” lower-region fathers. Those of the east and southeast and those of the west and northwest are method and wisdom respectively. Likewise those of the south and southwest and those of the north and northeast are method and wisdom respectively.

de'i rgyu mtshan gyis steng gi lha ljang gu pho mo la 'og gi lha sngon po pho mos 'khyud pa dang / 'og gi lha sngon po pho mo la steng gi lha ljang gu pho mos 'khyud pa dang / de bzhin du shar dang shar lho'i lha nag po pho mo la nub dang nub byang gi lha ser po pho mos 'khyud pa dang / de bzhin du lho dang lho nub kyi dmar po rnams la byang dang byang shar gyi dkar po rnams kyis 'khyud pa dang / byang dang byang shar gyi dkar po rnams la lho dang lho nub kyi dmar po rnams kyis 'khyud par yang shes par bya'o/ /

Because of this, the green upper male and female deities are embraced by the blue lower female and male deities, and the blue lower male and female deities are embraced by the green upper female and male deities. Similarly the black male and female deities of the east and southeast are embraced by the yellow female and male deities of the west and northwest. The yellow deities of the west and northwest are embraced by the black deities of the east and southeast. The red deities of the south and southwest are embraced by the white deities of the north and northeast. The white deities of the north and northeast are embraced by the red deities of the south and southwest.

de yang spyir btang ba yin gyi/ dmigs bsal bye brag gi dbang du byas na sgrub le'i don lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
de bzhin du mchog gi rgyal ba'i bdag po ye shes kyi phung po dang sna tshogs yum ye shes kyi khams ni phan tshun lus dang bsam pa'i/[55] zhes ye shes kyi phung po rdor sems dang ye shes kyi khams sna tshogs yum sher phyin ma thabs shes su bshad pa dang /

This is only a general explanation. More specifically the Great Commentary, on the seventy-fifth verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
Similarly the great one, the master, the aggregate of gnosis and Viśvamātā, the element of gnosis, are body and mind for each other.[81] /259/ This means that the gnosis-aggregate Vajrasattva and the gnosis-element Viśvamātā Prajñāpāramitā are method and wisdom.

d.div: [55] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 223_ba5
[81] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 223b5.

f.d:
yang de'i 'phro nyid las/ rnam par shes pa dang nam mkha'i khams so zhes rnam shes kyi phung po mi bskyod pa dang nam mkha'i khams rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma thabs shes su bshad cing / de bzhin du sgrub le'i nga bzhi pa'i dam tshig pa dang ye shes pa ro mnyam du 'chad pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir bskyed pa'i rnal 'byor gyis bskyed pa'i rim pa dag la rnam par shes pa ni nam mkha'i dang bcas [56] zhes pa rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma dang lhan cig tu snying po'i pad+mar zhes pa bde ba chen po la me'i steng du zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan dang dus me'i steng du dam tshig sems dpa' dang ye shes sems dpa' ro mnyam pa nyid du 'gyur ro/ / de yang zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan dang dus ma'i steng du zhes pa shong 'gyur yin zhing / 'gyur gzhan las gzhan 'byung ngo / /

The text continues, “Consciousness and the element of space,” which means that the consciousness-aggregate Akṣobhya and the space-element Vajradhātvīśvarī are method and wisdom. Likewise the Great Commentary, on the fifty-fourth verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, states when explaining how the samaya beings and gnosis beings become of one taste:
Here, in the generation yoga, in the stages of generation, “consciousness is together with space,” meaning together with Vajradhātvīśvarī, “within the central lotus,” meaning the great bliss, and upon fire, moon, sun, Rāhu, and Kālāgni, the samaya being and the gnosis being come to be of one taste.[82] The phrase “fire, moon, sun, Rāhu, and Kālāgni” is taken from the Shong translation. Other translations can be somewhat different.

d.div: [56] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 221_na4_tshig sna cung mi mthun/
[82] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 221a4.

f.d:
rnam shes kyi phung po mi bskyod pa'i ngo bo gtso bo dang nam mkha'i khams rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma thabs shes yab yum du bshad do/ / de ltar bshad pa ni khyab par byed ba rnam shes dang ye shes gtso bo'i ngang du 'dres pa'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi thabs shes so so ba'i dbang du byas na rnam shes kyi phung po mi bskyod pa lta bus rang gi rigs nam mkha'i khams rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma lta bu la thabs shes su byas nas 'khyud pa mi 'ong ste/ dpal 'dus pa sogs sbas rgyud rnams kyi dgongs pa la rnam snang dang spyan ma lta bu rang rigs kyi thabs shes phan tshun 'khyud pa yin yang / dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i dgongs pas thabs shes gzhan rigs la phan tshun 'khyud pa yin gyi rang rigs la 'khyud pa bkag pa'i phyir te/ 'grel chen las/
dkyil 'khor las ni bde ba dam pa'i don du'o zhes pa ni gzhan gyi rigs la 'khyud pa'o/[57] / zhes gsungs pas so/ /

It is taught that the consciousness-aggregate Akṣobhya, whose nature is the main deity, and the space-element Vajradhātvīśvarī are mother-and-father method and wisdom. Such a statement is made in terms of pervading consciousness and gnosis being fused together within the being of the main deity and are not statements made on the basis of individual method and wisdom where, for example, consciousness-aggregate Akṣobhya in the form of method embraces one of his family, such as space-element Vajradhātvīśvarī, in the form of wisdom. This is so because in the thinking of the hidden tantras, such as Guhyasamāja, Vairocana and Locanā, for example, embrace each other as same-family method and wisdom, whereas in Kālacakra thinking, method and wisdom involves mutual embracing between different families, while union within the same family is rejected. As the Great Commentary says:
“From the mandala, for the sake of the highest bliss.” This refers to union between different families.[83]

d.div: [57] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 224_na5
[83] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 224a5.

f.d: de ltar na rgyud 'grel las dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi skabs 'dir sku mdog dang zhal phyag dngos su gsungs pa'i lha drug brgya dang so bzhi'i nang gi 'dod phyir 'dod ma gtogs pa'i gzhan thams cad kyi sku mdog phyag mtshan bzhugs stabs gdan la sogs pa rgyud 'grel nyid las gsal bar bstan pas rgyud 'grel nyid las shes par bya zhing / tshes lha'i sku mdog gi dpyad pa ni gong du bshad zin pa ltar shes par bya'o/ /

Of the 634 figures whose colors, hands, and faces are actually mentioned in this section from the tantra and commentary on the sovereign mandala, apart from the desire and nondesire goddesses, the colors, implements, positions, seats, and so forth of all of them are clearly described, /260/ and they can be known in the same way as the colors of the lunar-day deities described in the discussion above.

'dod phyir 'dod kyi sku mdog ni phyogs mdog dang / phyag mtshan ni sgrub thabs pad dkar zhal lung las [58] gsungs pa ltar rang rang gi skyed byed kyi phyag mtshan ltar byed pa rgyud 'grel gyi dgongs pa yin te/ 'grel chen las/
de'i phyir rdo rje lcags sgrog ma la sogs pa 'di rnams mngon du phyogs pa'i gnas su 'gro ba ni shar la sogs pa'i rigs so/ / rigs kyi dbang des ni lcags sgrog ma'i g.yas kyi phyag dang po na ral gri dang /[59] zhes sogs kyis khro mo rnams kyi phyag dang po'i phyag mtshan ral gri sogs su byed pa'i rgyu mtshan rang nyid de dang de'i rigs yin pa rgyu mtshan du gsungs pa ltar 'dod phyir 'dod rnams kyi phyag mtshan gsal por ma gsungs pa rnams kyang rang rang gang las skyes pa'i rigs de'i phyag mtshan gyi dang po rnams phyag mtshan du byed par go nus so/ /

The colors of the desire and nondesire goddesses[84] are the colors of the directions. Determining their hand implements in line with the implement symbols from which they are individually created, as the Puṇḍarīka Transmission Sadhana has done[85] is in tune with the thinking of the tantra and commentary. The Great Commentary says:
Therefore Vajra Śṛṅkhalā and the others go to their facing positions in families of the east and so forth. Because of the family, in the first right hand of Śṛṅkhalā is a sword.[86] This quote explains that the reason why the implements of the first hands of the wrathful goddesses are swords, for instance, is because they belong to that particular family. Similarly, although the hand implements of the desire and nondesire goddesses are not clearly taught, they can be known from the implements of the first hand of the families from which they are born.

d.div: [58] mkhas grub rje/ gsung 'bum/ cha_sgrub thabs pad dkar zhal lung / 55_na2
[59] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 214_na3
[84] The thirty-six desire goddesses inhabit the speech mandala; the thirty-six non-desire goddesses inhabit the body mandala.
[85] Khedrup Jé, Collected Works, vol. cha, 55a2.
[86] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 214a3.

f.d: 'on te de rnams gang dang gang las skyes snyam na/ de la shar du sgrol ma las skyes pa dbye bar 'dod ma dang zhes sogs 'grel chen nyid na gsal bar bzhugs pa las shes par bya zhing / 'dod ma de dang de gang las skyes pa de las de dang de'i phyir 'dod ma yang skyes pa yin no/ /

So from which families are they born? This is clearly set out in the Great Commentary beginning from the line, “In the east born from Tārā, dividing into desire goddesses.” Wherever a particular desire goddess is born, so the corresponding nondesire goddess is also born.

'o na zhal phyag gi rnam pa ji ltar byed snyam na/ de yang rang rang gi skyed byed ji lta ba bzhin byas na zhal phyag gi grangs rnam pa sna tshogs su 'gyur pas sA ng+hu pu tras thams cad zhal gcig phyag gnyis par bshad pa 'thad dam snyam mo/ / de ltar yang sA ng+hu pu tra'i sgrub thabs las/
lho sgo'i g.yon gyi 'dod yon rnams la ka kha ga g+ha nga rnams tsheg drag dang ni bcas pa yi/ / sa bon rnams dang so so'i phyag mtshan rnams las byung ba'i 'dod ma lnga rnams phyag gnyis ri bong zhal/[60] / zhes sogs gsungs shing / phyir 'dod ma rnams la'ang de bzhin du gsungs so/ /

How can the number of faces and hands be determined? If they are to be determined by whoever creates each goddess, then the numbers of hands and faces would vary. Therefore I think that Sādhuputra’s assertion that they all have one face and two hands is correct. His sādhana says:
In the offering substances to the left of the southern door are ka, kha, ga, gha, ṅa together with visarga. From these syllables, and from individual implements, arise five desire goddesses with two hands and rabbit[87] face.[88] He also applies these descriptions to the nondesire goddesses.

d.div: [60] sde dge_1358_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pasAd+hU pu tra'i sgrub thabs/ 109_na1
[87] Not a facial description but a word-numeral for “one,” there being one moon, or “that with rabbit.”
[88] Toh 1358 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 109a1.

f.d:
yang 'grel chen las/
rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma las skyes pa ni srid gsum skyed ma gsod par 'dod ma'o/ / sna tshogs yum las skyes pa ni skyed par 'dod ma'o/[61] / zhes gsungs pa ltar de gnyis so sor bgrangs na 'dod ma so brgyad du 'gyur bas de gnyis gcig tu bgrang dgos te/

In the Great Commentary it says:
From Vajradhātvīśvarī comes the goddess Tribhavāprāṇāpahārinecchā. From Viśvamātā comes the goddess Utpādanaecchā.[89] If these two were counted separately, as is quoted here, there would have to be thirty-eight desire goddesses. Therefore they should be counted as one.

d.div: [61] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 215_ba6
[89] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 215b6.

f.d:
'grel chen las/
'dod ma sum cu rtsa bdun rnams ni gsung gi dkyil 'khor la rang gi rigs kyi dbye bas rang rang gi phyogs rnams su'o/[62] / zhes 'dod ma so bdun du gsungs pas so/ /

As the Great Commentary states:
The thirty-seven desire goddesses are in the speech mandala, divided into their families, in their respective positions.[90] /261/ This states the number of desire goddesses to be thirty-seven.

d.div: [62] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 216_na7
[90] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 216a7.

f.d: de yang de gnyis gcig tu bgrangs pa yang so drug po la khyab par byed pa yin pas stegs bu la dgod pa'i grangs la mi bgrang zhing phyir 'dod ma rnams kyang de bzhin du gsungs so/ / rang gi rigs kyi dbye bas rang rang gi phyogs rnams su'o/ /zhes pas dgod pa gsal por bstan to/ /

These two counted as one pervade all thirty-six and therefore are not counted in the placement upon the mandala terraces. This is also applied to the nondesire goddesses. The line “divided into their families, in their respective positions” clearly teaches placement.

'on kyang sgrub thabs zhal lung las/
'dod phyir 'dod rnams rang rang gi skyed byed ji lta ba bzhin du a b+ha ya dang bi b+hU ti tsan+d+ras bshad pa ltar 'dir bkod la/[63] zhes gsungs la/ de lta na gtum mo rnams las skyes pa'i 'dod ma dang phyir 'dod ma rnams khyi dang phag la sogs pa'i gdong pa can du byed dgos so/ /

However the Puṇḍarīka Transmission Sādhana says:
The desire and nondesire goddesses are presented here in forms similar to their creators, as was taught by Abhaya and Vibhūticandra.[91] This means that desire and nondesire goddesses who are born from the caṇḍālī[92] should have the faces of dogs, pigs, and so forth.

d.div: [63] mkhas grub rje/ gsung 'bum/ chasgrub thabs pad dkar zhal lung / 55_na2
[91] Khedrup Jé, Collected Works, vol. cha, 55a2. Vibhūticandra was a twelfth-century Nepalese master.
[92] gtum mo, caṇḍālī. Fierce woman. This refers not to the caṇḍālī, or inner fire, of the completion stage but rather to wrathful female deities.

f.d: lnga pa [64] skabs 'dir gtso bo bskyed tshul sogs dwogs pa'i gnas 'ga' zhig la dpyad pa/
22. Resolving Doubts Concerning the Process of Generation

d.div: [64] ma dper lnga pa zhes pa chad/

f.d: skabs 'dir dwogs pa'i gnas 'ga' zhig dpyad par bya ste/ 'di la bzhi/ gtso bo skyed tshul la dwogs pa dpyad pa dang / 'khor gyi lha spro tshul la dwogs pa dpyad pa dang / lha'i gdan 'ga' zhig la dwogs pa dpyad pa dang / de las 'phros pa'i pad+ma gdan can gyi lha'i grangs la dwogs pa dpyad pa'o/ /

There are a few further areas of doubt to be examined. These doubts can be put under four headings: 1. The generation of the main deities 2. The generation of the entourage deities 3. The seats of the deities 4. The number of deities on lotus seats
dang po [gtso bo skyed tshul la dwogs pa dpyad pa ]ni

d.i: The generation of the main deities

f.d:
sA d+hU pu tra'i sgrub thabs las/
aM yig dkar po yongs su gyur pa las zla ba'i dkyil 'khor me long lta bu'i ye shes dang / AH yig dmar po yongs su gyur pa las nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor mnyam pa nyid kyi ye shes kyi rang bzhin [65] zhes mtshan dpe'i rang bzhin gyi dbyangs gsal gyi yi ge dgod pa'i gzhi zla nyi gnyis rim pa bzhin aM AH'i sa bon las bskyed par bshad la/

Sādhuputra’s sādhana states:
From a completely formed white letter aṃ arises a mirrorlike gnosis moon mandala. From a completely formed red āḥ arises a sun mandala whose nature is the gnosis of equality.[93] Thus the moon and sun, which are the bases for the placement of the vowels and consonants whose natures are the physical signs and marks of an enlightened being, arise from aṃ and āḥ respectively.

d.div: [65] sde dge_1358_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pasAd+hU pu tra'i sgrub thabs/ 96_na3
[93] Toh 1358 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 96a3.

f.d:
phyis kyi mkhas pa (chos rje ku mA ra/)dgazla ba dbyangs so gnyis dang nyi ma gsal byed las bskyed par mdzad nas/ de dag gi shes byed du rdo rje snying po'i 'grel par/
sangs rgyas mtshan gyi rgyu las ni/ / zla bar dbyangs rnams sum cu gnyis/[66] / zhes dang /
a sogs ka sogs ldan pa dag las de ltar khams gsum dag ni nges par skyed 'gyur mi yi bdag/ces dang / mchog tu mi 'gyur ba las/
de'i steng du A li dang kA li las zla ba dang nyi ma [67] zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / zhes shes byed dang bcas te gsung ngo / /

Later scholars (such as the dharma master Kumāra) maintain that the moon arises from the thirty-two vowels and the sun from the consonants. Their sources come from the Vajragarbha Commentary:
From the causes of a buddha’s signs, the moon on which are thirty-two vowels. Also:
From a and so forth, from ka and so forth, the three realms made pure will arise, lord of men.[94] /262/ Also the Supreme and Unchanging Bliss summary says:
On top of that, from the chain of vowels and chain of consonants the moon and the sun.[95] Thus they assert their positions with scriptural authority.

d.div: [66] sde dge_1180_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ kargyud brtag gnyis/ le'u dang po'i nang gses lha'i le'u/ 37_ba1
[67] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 396_na7
[94] Toh 1180 Tengyur, rgyud, ka, chap 1. (Deities subchapter), 37b1.
[95] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 396a7.

f.d: rong pa'i dus zhabs rjes 'brangs dang bcas pa [68] rnams dang / sgrub thabs zhal lung sogs las ni 'grel chen gyi dngos bstan ltar zla nyi sa bon las mi skyed pa'i phyogs de mdzad do/ /[69] de dag gi nang nas gang zhig 'thad snyam na/

Rongpa Kālacakrapāda and his followers, as well as the Puṇḍarīka Transmission Sādhana,[96] maintain as actually taught in the Great Commentary that the moon and sun are not created from seed syllables. So who is right?

d.div: [68] ma dper dus zhabs la rjes 'brang dang bcas pa gsal/
[69] mkhas sgrub rje'i gsung 'bum/ chasgrub thabs pad dkar zhal lung / shog grangs/ 30_na5_nas gzigs/
[96] See Khedrup Jé, Collected Works, vol. cha, 30a5.

f.d:
mkhas pa dag gis shes byed du bkod pa'i/ a sogs ka sogs kyis dngos su khams gsum gyi chos rnams dbyangs gsal gyi yi ge las bskyed par bstan pa dang / mchog mi 'gyur gyi lung des gtso bo'i gdan gyi zla nyi dbyangs gsal las bskyed par bstan pas phyogs mthun gyi shes byed du 'gyur la/ yang mchog mi 'gyur las/
a sogs ka sogs dag las ri bong can dang nyin byed de yang na ha yig dang k+Sha yig dag gis so/[70] / zhes ha las zla ba bskyed pa dang / k+Sha yig las nyi ma bskyed pa ste/ yi ge re re las zla nyi bskyed par bshad cing /

Scholars have presented as scriptural authority the teaching that the phenomena of the three realms are produced from the letters a and ka and so forth, while the Supreme and Unchanging Bliss quote above teaches that the moon and sun seat of the main deity arises from the vowels and consonants. Therefore there is common ground in the scriptural authority. Moreover the Supreme and Unchanging Bliss summary also says:
From a and so forth and ka and so forth, the moon and sun are produced by ha and kṣa.[97] The moon is created from ha and the sun from kṣa, thereby explaining that the sun and moon arise from individual letters.

d.div: [70] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 393_na2
[97] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 393a2.

f.d:
de'i 'phro nyid las/
a yig gi bdag nyid can nam ha yig gi bdag nyid can zla ba'i dkyil 'khor dang ra yig gi bdag nyid can nam k+Sha yig gi bdag nyid can nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor ro/[71] / zhes a yig dang ra yig las gtso bo'i gdan gyi zla nyi bskyed par yang gsungs la/ de ltar na rnam gcad ni ra yig dang sa yig gang rung gi lus 'gyur yin pas sA ng+hu pu tras bshad pa ltar AHlas nyi ma skyed pa 'thad pa dang/ AH yig gi thabs dngos aM yig yin pas aM las zla bskyed pa 'thad cing / sangs rgyas kyi mtshan so gnyis kyi rgyu dbyangs so gnyis kyi nang na aM yig kyang yod pas/ sangs rgyas mtshan gyi rgyu las ni/ /zla bar dbyangs rnams sum cu gnyis/[72] /zhes pa'ang 'di'i shes byed du 'brel lo/ /

The text continues:
The moon mandala is of the nature of the letter a or the letter ha, and the sun mandala is of the nature of the letter ra or the letter kṣa.[98] This quote explains that the moon and sun as seats of the main deity also arise from the letter a and ra. The visarga can be a development of either the letter ra or the letter sa, and therefore Sādhuputra’s assertion that the sun is created from āḥ is correct. The syllable aṃ is a development of āḥ, and therefore his statement that the moon is created from aṃ is correct. The letter aṃ exists within the thirty-two vowels that are the causes of the thirty-two signs of a buddha, and therefore this conforms with the scriptural authority of the quote, “From the causes of a buddha’s signs, the thirty-two vowels as the moon.”[99]

f.d: spyir na 'di'i skabs kyi zla nyi gnyis sa bon las nges par skyed dgos te/ gnas skabs gzhan du zla nyi sogs skyed pa'i tshe sa bon las skyed pa bzhin du 'dir yang mtshungs pa'i phyir ro|_| de nyid kyis na sA ng+hu pu tras kyang oM dang AHlas 'di'i zla nyi bskyed par mdzad pa yin no/ / mngon byang lnga las gtso bo skyed pa'i skabs su rong pa'i dus zhabs pa rnams dang zhal lung las/ hUM las phyag mtshan bskyed pa ma mdzad cing /

In general, the sun and moon at this particular time should definitely arise from seed syllables, because at other times when the sun, moon, and so forth are created, they are created from seed syllables, and it is no different here. Because of this Sādhuputra says that the moon and sun at this point arise from the letters aṃ and āṃ. At the time of the main deity generation from the five enlightenments, Rongpa Kālacakrapāda and the Puṇḍarīka Transmission Sādhana do not develop the hand implement[100] out of hūḥ. /263/

d.div: [100] The vajra.

f.d:
de yang 'grel pa'i tshig zin ltar bkod pa yin la/ zhal lung mkhan po'i dgongs pa yang zla nyi dbyangs gsal gyis mtshan pa'i dbus kyi hUM yig las rdo rjer skyed pa sor rtog ye shes su mdzad pa yin te/ nges don gyi dus kyi 'khor lo la phyag 'tshal ba/ AHli kA li snyoms 'jug dang / /zhes sogs kyis bstan pa'i bskyed rim gang dang bral ba'i bskyed rim 'chad pa'i 'grel bshad de kho na nyid snang ba las/ 'dud ces drang ngo / /
gang la na/ 'bras dus kyi dus kyi 'khor lo de yang / / de nyid kyi khyad par ji lta bu zhe na/ / a li kA lis mtshan pa'i zla nyi snyoms par 'jug pa ste kha sbyar ba dang / sa bon hUM dang rdo rje'i bug par khams 'gyur ba 'gog pa'i phaT kyi yi ge 'god pa dang / sogs pas sa bon yongs su gyur pa'i phyag mtshan sgom pa sogs spangs pa ste/[73] zhes mngon byang lnga bskyed kyi A li kA lis mtshan pa'i zla nyi kha sbyor gyi dbus kyi sa bon hUM yongs su gyur pa las phyag mtshan bsgom par gsungs pas so/ /

This accords with the literal meaning of the Great Commentary. The thinking of the Puṇḍarīka Transmission masters, however, is that the gnosis of analysis arises in the form of a vajra from the hūḥ in the center of the sun and moon marked with the consonants and vowels. Illuminating Reality, when explaining the “generation stage devoid of generation stage,”[101] expressed by verses such as the one beginning “Vowels and consonants in union”[102] in the section on making prostrations to the definitive Kālacakra, states:
Prostration is to whom? To resultant Kālacakra. How does it differ? The union of moon and sun, meaning in embrace and marked by vowels and consonants, the placement of the seed syllable hūḥ and the letter phaṭ blocking the flow of the elements at the tip of the vajra, and the meditations of the hand implement formed from the syllable as taught by the phrase “and so forth,” are all “abandoned.”[103] This passage speaks of a meditation in which the five enlightenments are created by the moon and sun in embrace, marked by the vowels and consonants, in the center of which a hand implement arises from the hūḥ seed syllable.

d.div: [73] mkhas sgrub rje'i 'grel bshad de kho na nyid snang ba'i lung brnyed son ma byung /
[101] A section in the sādhana when prostrations are made to the definitive Kālacakra.

[102] This verse is from the opening prostrations of the Vimalaprabhā:
Vowels and consonants in union, hūḥ, phaṭ, and so forth abandoned, body born from the unchanging, I bow to Kālacakra.
[103] Khedrup Jé, Collected Works, vol. kha, quote not traced.

f.d:
de ltar mdzad pa rgyud kyi dgongs pa yang yin te/ sgrub le'i bcu pa las/
zla ba nyi ma la yang a sogs ka sogs rdo rje dang bcas me long la sogs lnga rnams kyis/ / 'od zer lnga rnams 'gyed par byed cing dri ma med pa'i 'od 'phro dus kyi 'khor lo bsgom par bya/[74] / zhes A li kA lis mtshan pa'i zla nyi kha sbyor gyi dbus su phyag mtshan rdo rjer bsgom par gsungs pas so/

This is also the thinking of the tantra because the tenth verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter of the Condensed Tantra states:
On moon and sun, the vowels a and so forth, the consonants ka and so forth, together with the vajra, and from the five, such as the mirrorlike, five light rays spread, pure light radiates. Meditate upon Kālacakra.[104] Thus a meditation is taught in which moon and sun in embrace are marked with the vowels and consonants, and in their center is the vajra hand implement.

d.div: [74] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 206_na4
[104] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 206a4.

f.d:
de bzhin du sgrub le'i don gsum pa'i 'grel chen las/
de ltar sa bon gyis mtshan ma bskyed pa dang mtshan mas lha bskyed pa ni rnal 'byor pas thams cad du rtogs par bya'o zhes brgyud kyi nges pa'o/[75] / zhes gsungs shing / sA ng+hu pu tra'i sgrub thabs las kyang / de nas de'i steng du a yig zhes pa nas/ gsal byed brgyad cu zhes so/[76] / zhes pa'i bar gyis zla nyi dbyangs gsal gyis mtshan pa bskyed par bstan nas/ de'i de ma thag gi mjug tu/
de nas de dag gi dbus su hUM yig sngon po las byung ba'i sna tshogs rdo rje hUM gis mtshan pa'i so sor rtog pa'i ye shes kyi bdag nyid bsgom par bya'o/ / de nas gsum po gcig chu 'dres pa la hi yig gis spras pa bya ba grub ba'i ye shes kyi bdag nyid bsgom par bya'o/ / de nas lus kyi yan lag thams cad rdzogs pa haM yig gi bdag nyid chos kyi dbyings shin tu rnam par dag pa'i rang bzhin/ 'og nas phyag 'tshal ba'i skabs su 'chad pa'i dpal dus kyi 'khor lo ste 'on kyang phyag nyi shu rtsa drug pa[77] zhes sogs gsungs pa'i sna tshogs rdo rje zhes pa dang / phyag nyi shu rtsa drug pa zhes pa rdo rje shugs la dngos su sbyar nas gzhan rnams skabs 'di'i gtso bo skyed pa la yang sbyor bar dgongs pa yin no/ /

Similarly the Great Commentary, on the seventy-third verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
The seed syllable creates the implement, the implement creates the deity, and this is understood at all times by the yogi. This is affirmed by the tantra.[105] Sādhuputra’s sādhana also, from “Then on top of that the letter a” up to “the eighty consonants,”[106] teaches the generation of the sun and moon marked by the vowels and consonants. Immediately after this line the sādhana continues:
Then meditate that in their center is a blue letter hūḥ, from which arises a crossed vajra marked by hūḥ and which is of the nature of gnosis of analysis. Then meditate on all three blending as one, adorned with the letter hi of the nature of gnosis of accomplishment. Then every part of the body is complete, and the nature of the letter haṃ is the very pure gnosis of reality. This is the glorious Kālacakra explained below in the section on prostration. However the twenty-six armed one….[107] /264/ “Crossed vajra” and “twenty-six armed one” refer to Vajravega. The rest applies to the creation of the main deity at this particular time.

f.d: de ltar na 'dir 'gyur te/ zla nyi dbyangs gsal gyis mtshan pa me long lta bu dang mnyam pa nyid kyi ye shes las byang chub pa de'i dbus su hUM las rdo rje lte ba la hUM gis mtshan pa so sor rtog pa'i ye shes las byang chub pa de rnams lhan cig tu tshogs pa'i gnas skabs kyi rdo rje'i lte ba 'am/ de rnams gcig tu 'dres pa las rdo rje hUM dang bcas par gyur ba la haM yig ldan pa ste hi yig gis mtshan pa bya ba grub pa'i ye shes las byang chub pa/ de las bcom ldan 'das dus kyi 'khor lo'i sku'i cha shas yongs su rdzogs par gyur pa'i sku la haM yig dang ldan pa ni chos kyi dbyings kyi ye shes las byang chub pa'o/ /

At this time the following occurs. Sun and moon marked with consonants and vowels are the manifest enlightenments arising from the mirror like gnosis and the equality gnosis. In the center is a hūḥ from which arises a vajra marked with a hūḥ at its center. This is the enlightenment arising from the gnosis of analysis. The heart of this vajra together with the other previously mentioned manifest enlightenments, or alternatively, the heart of a vajra and hūḥ that has arisen from these manifest enlightenments blending into one, is “possessed of the letter hi,” meaning marked by the letter hi. This is the enlightenment of the gnosis of accomplishment. From that comes the conqueror Kālacakra, all body parts complete, together with the letter haṃ. This is enlightenment of the reality gnosis.

don de nyid rgyud 'grel dang sbyar nas bshad par bya ste/ de yang rgyud las/ zla ba nyi ma la yang a sogs ka sogs rdo rje dang bcas zhes gsungs pa'i 'grel pa las/ zla ba dang khu ba dbyangs dang ldan pa ni zhes pa dang / yang nyi ma dang rdul gsal byed dang ldan pa ni [78] zhes pas ldan gzhi nyi zla gnyis la ldan chos dbyangs gsal dang ldan par bshad nas/ rtsa ba'i/ rdo rje dang bcas zhes pas ldan gzhi rdo rje bstan nas 'di'i 'grel par/ dri za'i sems can hUM yig dang ldan pa ni zhes pas ldan chos hUM yig rdo rje la ldan par bshad do/[79] /

The above should be explained in connection with the tantra and commentary. The tantra states, “On moon and sun, the vowels a and so forth, the consonants ka and so forth, together with the vajra,” to which the commentary remarks, “Moon and seminal fluid are with the vowels” and further, “Sun and blood are with the consonants.”[108] This explains that the vowels and consonants are held on moon and sun bases. “Together with a vajra” indicates the vajra as a base. The commentary on this begins, “Together with the gandharva letter hūḥ,”[109] indicating the hūḥ held in the vajra.

d.div: [78] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 206_na4_nas na5_bar/
[79] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 206_na6

f.d: 'di la dgongs nas sA ng+hu pu tras kyang de dag gi dbus su hUM yig sngon po las byung ba'i sna tshogs rdo rje hUM gis mtshan pa [80] zhes gsungs so/ / yang de rnams lhan cig tu tshogs pa'i rdo rje 'am/ de rnams gcig tu 'dres pa las rdo rje hUM dang bcas pa'i ldan gzhi la ldan chos he yig ldan pa ni 'grel pa las/ de rnams gcig pa nyid dang srog gi haM yig dang ldan pa ni [81] zhes pas bstan te/ zla nyi la dbyangs gsal ldan pa bzhin du hi yig ldan gzhi gzugs can zhig la ldan dgos la/ de yang rdo rje nyid la bya dgos pas so/ /

With this in mind Sādhuputra says, “In their center is a blue letter hūḥ from which arises a crossed vajra marked by a hūḥ.” This vajra and the other enlightenments, or the vajra arising from these enlightenments blending into one, are marked by a hūḥ. This vajra is that which “possesses,” and the letter hi is that which is “possessed.” On this the commentary says, “They become one together with the wind letter hi.” Just as the moon and sun “possess” the vowels and consonants, the letter hi must have a base, and that has to be the vajra. /265/

d.div: [80] sde dge_1358_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pasAd+hU pu tra'i sgrub thabs/ 96_ba2
[81] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 206_na6

f.d:
'di la dgongs nas sA ng+hu pu tras kyang / de nas gsum po gcig tu 'dres pa la hi yig gis spras pa bya ba grub pa'i ye shes kyi bdag nyid bsgom par bya'o/[82] /zhes gsungs pa yin no/ / rdo rje hUM dang haM yig dang bcas pa de las dus kyi 'khor lo sku'i cha shas yongs su rdzogs par bskyed pa la haM yig dang ldan par bsgom pa ni 'grel pa las/
de nas yan lag thams cad kyi cha shas yongs su rdzogs pa dang / rnam par shes pa haM yig dang ldan pa ni chos kyi dbyings shin tu rnam par dag pa'i ye shes te [83] zhes pas bstan to/ /

With this in mind Sādhuputra writes, “All three blend as one, adorned with the letter hi of the nature of the gnosis of accomplishment.” From the vajra, the letter hūḥ, and the letter hi arises Kālacakra, every part of his body complete and marked by the letter haṃ. This is indicated by commentary:
Then all parts of the body are complete, together with the consciousness syllable haṃ. This is the very pure gnosis of reality.[110]

f.d:
'di la dgongs nas sA ng+hu pu tras kyang /
de nas lus kyi yan lag thams cad rdzogs pa haM yig gi bdag nyid chos kyi dbyings shin tu rnam par dag pa'i rang bzhin 'og nas phyag 'tshal pa'i skabs su 'chad pa'i dpal dus kyi 'khor lo ste [84] zhes gsungs pa yin no/ /

Sādhuputra also says:
Then every part of the body is complete, and the nature of the letter haṃ is the very pure gnosis of reality. This is the glorious Kālacakra explained below in the section on prostration. However the twenty-six armed one…
