f.d: gtso bo mngon byang lnga las skyed tshul 'di la mi mthun pa mang na'ang / rgyud 'grel gyi don bshad pa'i sgo nas nges par byas pa yin no/ /

How the main deity is actually created from the five enlightenments is subject to much disagreement. However it has been settled by the strength of the explanations of the material from the tantra and commentary.[111]

d.div: [111] The above text on the generation of the main deity from the mandalas, syllables, and implements is fraught with corruption in the rendering of the Sanskrit syllables. I am grateful to Kirtī Tsenshap Rinpoché for clarification.

f.d: de ltar bskyed pa'i gtso bo dus kyi 'khor lo 'di ngo bo ye shes kyi phung po rnam par dag pa rdo rje sems dpa' nyid zhal phyag sogs kyi rnam pa gtso bo'i rnam pa can du bsgom pa yin te/ nus ma brgyad dang bcas pa'i gtso bo yab yum rnams bskyed zin pa'i mjug sdud kyi 'grel chen las/ rang gi phyag rgya dang bcas pa ste rdo rje sems dpa' rdzogs pa'o/[85] / zhes gtso bo skyed pa rdzogs pa rdo rje sems dpa' rdzogs par gsungs pas so/ / 'dir nus ma brgyad gtso bo'i yum du yang bstan pa yin no/ /

The main deity Kālacakra that has been generated this way is meditated on as having the nature of Vajrasattva, the purified gnosis aggregate whose hands and faces, etc., are in the form of the main deity. In the section on the withdrawal of the main mother-and-father deities and the eight śakti, the Great Commentary says, “Together with mudrā, the complete Vajrasattva.”[112] This indicates that the complete generation of the main deity is the complete Vajrasattva. This also teaches that the eight śakti are consorts of the main deity.

d.div: [85] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 208_ba5
[112] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 208b5.

f.d: gnyis pa 'khor gyi lha spro tshul la dwogs pa dpyad pa ni/

d.i: The generation of the entourage deities

f.d: bod kyi mkhas pa phal che ba dag mi bskyod pa sogs dkyil 'khor gyi 'khor lo'i rnam pas gtso bo'i lus la zhugs pa chags pa chen po'i mes zhu ba'i byang chub kyi sems rdo rje'i lam nas yum gyi pad+mar babs pa'i thig le so so yongs su gyur pa las lha so so'i sa bon dang / de las lha so so'i phyag mtshan dang / de las lha so sor gyur pa yum gyi pad+ma nas spros te phyi'i dkyil 'khor gyi rang rang gi gdan la 'god par mdzad la/

Most Tibetan scholars say that Akṣobhya and so forth in the form of the mandala assembly enter the body of the main deity and are melted by the fire of great desire into the form of bodhicitta, which then flows from the vajra to fall into the lotus of the mother. There individual drops become the seed syllables of deities, which in turn transform into hand implements and finally into deities who emanate from the mother’s lotus to take their places on their seats within the external mandalas. /266/

mkhas pa kha cig dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi lha spro ba na dang por lha mo'i pad+mar rten gyi dkyil 'khor sngar bzhin du bskyed nas de nyid du brtan pa lha spro ba yin gyi phyi rol gyi dkyil 'khor du spro ba ni ma yin te|_yin na der dam tshig gi dkyil 'khor grub pas las rgyal mchog gi skabs su dam tshig gi dkyil 'khor spro bar gsungs pa mi rigs par thal ba'i phyir ro zhes gsung zhing / de'i shes byed du/ 'dir rang gi rig ma'i pad+ma_ra zhes sogs 'dren par mdzad de/ /

Some scholars maintain that when generating the deities of the sovereign mandala, first the base mandala is created again within the lotus of the consort, and then the dependent deities are generated in this lotus mandala and not to an outside mandala. If they were emanated to an outside mandala, “this would mean that the samaya mandala would be complete, and the instruction to emanate a samaya mandala in the section on the sovereign activity would be incorrect.” As verification of this assertion they quote, “Here in the lotus of one’s consort” and so on.

de ltar mdzad pa yang sgrub le'i bcu dgu pa'i 'grel chen las/
zhu ba zla bar gyur pa rnams rang gi rdo rje nas spros te rang gi rig ma'i pad+mar de rnams yongs su gyur pa las lha dang lha mo'i tshogs kyi dkyil 'khor rten dang brten pa'i mtshan nyid can no/[86] / zhes gsungs pa'i rten dang brten pa zhes pas yum gyi pad+mar rten gyi dkyil 'khor yang skyed dgos par bstan pa dang / rdo rje nas spros te rang gi rig ma'i pad+mar zhes pas pad+ma_ra rten dang brten pa'i lha skyed pa tsam bstan pa yin gyi/ yum gyi pad+ma nas phyi'i dkyil 'khor du spro ba ma bstan to snyam du dgongs pa 'dra'o/ /

Moreover the Great Commentary says on the nineteenth verse of the Condensed Tantra:
The melted moon emerges from one’s vajra into the lotus of one’s consort to transform into the mandala assembly of gods and goddesses, the full and complete base and dependents.[113] They apparently think that “base and dependents” indicates that the mandala base, too, has to be created within the mother’s lotus, and that the line “emerges from one’s vajra into the lotus of one’s consort” teaches that the dependent deities and the base mandalas are only created within the lotus and are not emanated to an outside mandala.

d.div: [86] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 209_na2
[113] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 209a2.

f.d:
de dag las/ yum gyi pad+mar babs pa'i thig le las pad+ma'i nang du rten gyi dkyil 'khor dang brten pa'i lha gnyis ka skyed dgos pa 'grel ba de'i don du mdzad pa ni legs par bshad pa ltar snang yang dam pa snga ma dag gis rten zhes pa sa bon la bshad pas de dag gang 'thad dpyad par bya'o/ / 'on kyang dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi lha'i 'khor lo yum gyi pad+ma'i nang du bskyed pa nyid kyis rdzogs nas phyi'i dkyil 'khor du yum gyi pad+ma las mi spro bar bzhed pa ni mi 'thad de/ de 'thad na dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi lha rnams kyi gtso bo gtso mo yab yum nus ma rnams dang bcas pa yum gyi pad+ma'i nang du skyed tshul 'chad dgos pa las de ltar rgyud 'grel las kyang ma bshad cing / don thob la yang med pa'i phyir dang / gzhan yang yum gyi pad+mar rten dang brten pa'i dkyil 'khor bskyed pa nyid kyis dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog rdzogs pa yin na/ sgrub le'i lnga bcu pa'i 'grel chen las/
des na rdo rje can yang ri bong 'dzin pa zhu ba bzhin bltas nas yang yig gis shes rab kyang ste shes rab dang bcas pa'i thugs dang ye shes rdo rje a wa ng+hU tI dang dung can ma la brten pa'o/[87] / zhes gtso bo zhu ba'i tshe yum yang zhu bar gsungs pas yum zhu ba na yum gyi pad+ma'i nang gi lha rnams kyang zhu bar khas len dgos shing len yang len la/ de lta na lha mo bzhis klus skul ba yang ji ltar byed pas ma dgos so/ /

To conclude from this that the meaning of the commentary is that from the drops falling into the mother’s lotus, both mandala base and dependent deities must be created within the lotus seems like a good explanation, but great masters of the past have explained “base” as meaning “seed.” Therefore who is correct needs to be investigated. However to assert that the whole deity assembly of the sovereign mandala is completed by their creation within the mother’s lotus and that they do not emanate from the mother’s lotus to an outside mandala is not correct. If it were, there would have to be an explanation on how the mother and father of the sovereign mandala along with the śakti are created within the lotus of the mother, but no such explanation is found in the tantra and commentary, nor can any such understanding be inferred. Furthermore, if the sovereign mandala were complete merely by the creation of the base mandala and the dependent deities within the mother’s lotus, consider this quote from the Great Commentary on the fiftieth verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter:
“Then the vajra holder also dissolves into the ‘moon.’” The word “also” means that the wisdom also dwells with mind vajra and gnosis vajra inside the avadhūtī and the śaṅkhinī.[114] /267/ This says that when the main deity dissolves, the mother also dissolves. Therefore, when the mother dissolves, it must be accepted that the deities within the lotus of the mother also dissolve. If that is the case, you must ask how it could be possible for the four goddesses to perform the arousal by song.[115]

d.div: [87] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 219_na6
[114] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 219a6.
[115] The arousal by song is the first meditation in the branch of the speech-vajra near-accomplishment, and is presented later.

f.d:
gzhan yang dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi skabs su yum gyi pad+ma las phyi'i rten gyi dkyil 'khor du lha rnams mi spro bar bzhed pa ni rgyud 'grel dang 'gal te/ 'grel chen las/ zhu ba zla bar gyur pa rnams rang gi rdo rje nas spros te rang gi rig ma'i pad+mar zhes pa nas/ rten dang brten pa'i mtshan nyid can no [88] zhes pa'i bar gyis yum gyi pad+mar spros pa'i thig le las pad+ma'i nang du rten dang brten pa'i lha bskyed par bstan/ de'i mjug tu 'grel chen las/
mi bskyod pa lhag pa'i bdag por bsgoms nas dang por bcom ldan 'das kyi sku la gzhug par bya'o/[89] / zhes gsungs pa 'dis mi bskyod pa yum gyi pad+ma las spros nas gtso bo'i sku la gzhug par bstan nas de'i mjug tu/
de nas phyogs kyi pad+ma_ra chu gter zhes pa sangs rgyas bzhi rnams ni nges par spyan dgu pa me zhal zhes pa zhal gsum pa dus kyi phyag ces pa phyag drug pa rnams spro bar bya'o/ / zhes pa'i spro ba 'di yum gyi pad+ma las spro ba la byed dgos te/ yab kyi rdo rje las pad+mar spro ba gong du bstan ma thag yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

Furthermore to assert that during the meditation of the sovereign mandala the deities do not emanate from the mother’s lotus to an outside mandala contradicts the tantra and commentary. The Great Commentary from “The melted moon emerges from one’s vajra into the lotus” until “the full and complete base and dependents” teaches the formation of the base mandala and dependent deities within the mother’s lotus from the drops that have traveled there. The Great Commentary continues:
Meditate upon Akṣobhya as the great lord who enters the body of the primordial buddha.[116] This shows that Akṣobhya travels from the mother’s lotus to enter the body of the main deity. The text continues:
Then on the direction lotuses are emanated “ocean” buddhas, meaning four buddhas, of nine eyes, with “fire” faces, meaning three faces, and “time” hands, meaning six hands. This emanation must be an emanation from the mother’s lotus, because the emanation from the father’s vajra into the lotus is taught immediately prior to this passage.

d.div: [88] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 209_na2
[89] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 209_na2
[116] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 209a2.

f.d: de'i phyir na 'grel tshig 'di rnams kyis lha rnams yum gyi pad+ma las spros nas gzhal yas khang gi phyogs dang mtshams rnams su dgod par bstan cing / de yang phyi'i rten gyi dkyil 'khor nyid la dgod pa'i don yin no/ /

Therefore these passages from the Great Commentary teach that the deities emanate from the mother’s lotus and are placed in their cardinal and intermediate positions within the celestial mansion, and that means being placed within an external base mandala.

gzhan yang las rgyal mchog gi lha spro ba'i skabs kyi sgrub le'i nga gcig pa'i 'grel chen las/
dam tshig gi dkyil 'khor gyi don du rang gi lus la bcug ste shes rab kyi pad+mar sngags kyi rang bzhin yi ge so so rnams so/ / de nas pad+ma las sngon bzhin du zhal dang phyag dang mtshan ma dang dbyibs kyi mtshan nyid can rnams ye shes dang thugs dang gsung dang sku'i dkyil 'khor rnams la spro bar bya'o/ / de ltar dkyil 'khor rab tu spro ba dag kyang ngo / / kyang yig gis sngon bzhin zhes pa'o/[90] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis las rgyal mchog gi skabs 'dir lha zhal phyag mtshan dbyibs kyi rnam pa can rnams ye shes thugs gsung sku'i dkyil 'khor rnams la yum gyi pad+ma las spro ba ni sngon gyi dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog bzhin du spro bar bstan pas 'grel pa 'di dag dang yang 'gal ba yin no/ /

Furthermore the Great Commentary, on the fifty-first verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, in the section on deity emanation during the sovereign activities says:
For the sake of the samaya mandala, they enter one’s body and arrive at the wisdom lotus, on which stand the individual letters in the form of a mantra. Then from the lotus, as before, characterized by their faces, hands, hand symbols, and forms, they emanate to the gnosis, mind, speech, and body mandalas. In the phrase “again the mandalas are manifested,” the word again means “as before.”[117] This means that in the section on the sovereign activity, the deities manifest with faces, hands, hand symbols, and forms and emanate to the gnosis, mind, speech, and body mandalas from the mother’s lotus, and all this is done in the same way that the previous emanation of the sovereign mandala was performed. /268/ Therefore the above assertion contradicts this tantra and commentary passage also.

d.div: [90] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 220_na1
[117] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 220a1.

f.d: de ltar yin na'ang der dam tshig gi dkyil 'khor sgrub pas las rgyal mchog gi skabs su dam tshig gi dkyil 'khor spro bar gsungs pa mi rigs par thal bar 'gyur ro zhes pa'i skyon med de/ dang por phyi'i rten gyi dkyil 'khor sgom pa gang du skye ba'i ma'i mngal sbyang ba'i don dang / dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi skabs su yum gyi pad+ma_ra bskyed pa'i lha rnams pad+ma las spros nas rten gyi dkyil 'khor la 'god pa ni mngal gyi gnas skabs kyi sems can gyi phung khams skye mched sogs sbyang ba'i don dang / las rgyal mchog gi skabs su lha spros te rten gyi dkyil 'khor la 'god pa ni btsas pa'i gnas skabs kyi phung sogs sbyang ba'i don du yin pas dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi lha spro ba rdzogs pa'i dus su dam tshig pa'i lha rdzogs par thal ba'i nyes pa med de/ da dung sbyang gzhi la ltos pa'i dam tshig gi dkyil 'khor spro ba ma rjogs pa'i phyir ro/ /

However the previous consequence, “this would mean that the samaya mandala would be complete, and the instruction to emanate a samaya mandala in the section on the sovereign activity would be incorrect,” still does not follow. The purpose of initially visualizing an outside base mandala is to purify the mother’s womb into which one is conceived. Creating the deities in the mother’s lotus during the sovereign-mandala meditation and sending them out from the lotus to take their place within the base mandala is for the purpose of purifying the aggregates, elements, and sources of the being inside the womb. Emanating the deities and placing them within the base mandala during the sovereign-activity meditation is for the purpose of purifying the aggregates at birth. Therefore it does not follow that when the deity emanation of the sovereign-mandala meditation is complete, the creation of the samaya deities is also complete, because in terms of its base of purification, the samaya mandala emanation is not complete.

de ltar na gshegs pa gshegs ma rnams dang por spro ba'i tshe mi bskyod pa lhag pa'i bdag por bsgoms pa'i mi bskyod pa nyid yum sher phyin mas 'khyud pa yum gyi pad+ma las spros nas gtso bo rang nyid la gzhug ste/ 'di ni gong du drangs pa'i/ mi bskyod pa lhag pa'i zhes sogs dang / mi bskyod pa rab tu zhugs pa'o/ /zhes pa rnams kyis bstan la/ rdo rje sems dpa' la yum gyis 'khyud pa gtso bo la gzhug pa 'grel chen las ma gsungs shing don la'ang mi 'thob ste/ gtso bo nyid ngo bo rdor sems nyid yin pa 'grel chen nyid na gsal ba gong du drangs zin pa ltar yin pas so/ /

When the male and female tathāgatas are first emanated, Akṣobhya is meditated upon as the great lord embracing the consort Prajñāpāramitā and sent from the mother’s lotus to enter the body of the main deity. This is taught by the previous quotes, beginning “Meditate upon Akṣobhya as the great lord” and “Akṣobhya enters.” However Vajrasattva embraced by consort and entering the main deity is not taught by the Great Commentary, nor is it implicit. This is because the nature of the main deity is Vajrasattva, as has been made clear in the Great Commentary in a previous quote.[118]

d.div: [118] “Together with mudrā, the complete Vajrasattva.”

f.d: gtso bo'i yum la nus ma bcu bshad pa'i sher phyin ma dang ye shes kyi pha rol tu phyin ma gnyis ma gtogs pa'i brgyad ni sbyin sogs phar phyin brgyad kyi ngo bo dang snying po'i pad+ma'i 'dab ma rnams la bkod pa'i nag mo 'bar ma sogs brgyad yin zhing/ de yang shar dang shar lho'i gnyis rlung khams ma dang / lho dang lho nub kyi gnyis me khams ma dang / nub dang nub byang gi gnyis sa khams ma dang / byang dang byang shar gyi gnyis chu khams ma dang / sher phyin ma ye shes kyi khams ma dang / ye shes kyi phar phyin ma nam mkha'i khams ma yin la/ sna tshogs yum ni shes phyin ma dang ye shes kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i ngo bo yin la rnam pa sna tshogs yum gyi rnam pa can du bskyed pa yin te/

The ten śakti are explained as being consorts of the main deity. Eight of them, excluding Prajñāpāramitā and Jñānapāramitā, are of the nature of the other eight perfections, beginning with the perfection of giving and so forth, and these are the eight goddesses, Kṛṣṇadīptā and so forth, placed upon the petals of the central lotus. The two śakti in the east and southeast are of the air element. Those of the south and southwest are of the fire element. Those of the west and northwest are of the earth element, and those of the north and northeast the water element. Prajñāpāramitā is of the element of gnosis, and Jñānapāramitā is of the element of space. Viśvamātā is of the nature of both Prajñāpāramitā and Jñānapāramitā while being generated in the aspect of Viśvamātā. /269/

gtso ba'i yum la nus ma bcur nges shing sna tshogs yum yang skabs 'dir nus ma'i ngo bo la 'jog dgos pa'i phyir te/ sgrub le'i bcu drug pa'i 'grel chen las/
ye shes kyi pha rol tu phyin pa na sna tshogs yum de'i nang du 'dus shing pha rol tu phyin pa gzhan sbyin pa la sogs pa rnams te pha rol tu phyin pa brgyad na 'dab ma rnams la lha mo brgyad de/[91] zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

This is because the consorts of the main deity are ascertained as being the ten śakti, and at this part of the generation stage, Viśvamātā also has to be established as being of the nature of a śakti. The Great Commentary, on the sixteenth verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
Jñānapāramitā is included within Viśvamātā. The other eight paramitas of giving and so forth are the eight goddesses on the petals.[119]

d.div: [91] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 208_na2
[119] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 208a2.

f.d: de bzhin du mi bskyod pa spros nas rang la bcug pa'i rjes su rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma la rdo rje sems dpas 'khyud pa yum gyi pad+ma las spros nas sna tshogs yum la gzhugs dgos te/ de'i rgyu mtshan ni pad+ma gdan can gyi lha brgya ngadru ga gi grangs 'chad pa'i skabs su bshad par bya'o/ / sher phyin ma la mi bskyod pas 'khyud pa yum la gzhug pa mi dgos te/ sna tshogs yum nyid shes phyin ma'i ngo bo yin pas so/ /

Similarly, after Akṣobhya has been sent forth and has merged into one’s body, Vajradhātvīśvarī embraced by Vajrasattva is sent forth from the mother’s lotus and enters Viśvamātā. The reason for this will be explained in the section dealing with doubts concerning the numbers of deities on lotus seats. There is no need for Prajñāpāramitā embraced by Akṣobhya to enter the mother because Viśvamātā is of the nature of Prajñāpāramitā.

gal te gtso bo'i ngo bo rdo rje sems dpa' byed na/ 'grel chen las/ rdo rje sems dpa'i dbu rgyan can/[92] /zhes 'dir gtso bo la rdo rje sems dpa'i dbu rgyan byed par bshad pa dang / ye shes le'u las/ ye shes la rnam shes dang rnam shes la ye shes kyis rgyas gdab par [93] gsungs shing / sgrub le'i drug cu pa'i 'grel chen las kyang /
da ni cod pan zhes pa la sogs pas lha rnams kyi rigs kyi rgyas gdab pa gsungs pa 'dir mchog gi dang po'i sangs rgyas kyi dkyil 'khor du cod pan dag la phan tshun rdo rje yis ni rdo rjer 'gyur te/ ci'i phyir na ye shes dang rnam par shes pa phan tshun yang dag par sbyor ba'i phyir ro/ / de bas na ye shes kyis rnam par shes pa dang rnam par shes pas ye shes la ste gnyis ka'i spyi bo la/[94] zhes ye shes rdo rje sems dpa' dang rnam shes mi bskyod pa phan tshun gcig gis gcig la rgyas gdab par bshad pa dang 'gal lo snyam na/ 'gal ba'i skyon med de/ ngo bo rdo rje sems dpar gyur pa'i gtso bo la rdor sems kyi dbu rgyan byed par gsungs pa ni dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi skabs 'dir gtso bo dus kyi 'khor lo'i rnam pa can 'di rdor sems kyi ngo bo yin par mtshon pa dang / gtso bo skye ba'i dus su de ltar du skyes pa yin pas de'i dbang du mdzad pa yin la/ rgyas gdab kyi skabs su ye shes dang rnam shes phan tshun rgyas 'debs byed du gsungs pa ni rdor sems dang mi bskyod pa gzugs tha dad pa dang / de yang dbang bskur nas rigs bdag gi rgyas 'debs pa'i dbang du mdzad nas gsungs pas 'gal ba'i skyon med do/ /

If the nature of the main deity is Vajrasattva, then the following doubt might occur. The Great Commentary says “with the crown of Vajra sattva,”[120] thereby affirming that at this stage, the main deity has Vajrasattva as his crown. However, in the Gnosis chapter, it says that gnosis is sealed by consciousness, and consciousness is sealed by gnosis. Moreover the Great Commentary, on the sixtieth verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
“Now the crown” and so forth talks of the deities being sealed by their families. Here in the mandala of the supreme original buddha, on the crown is a vajra in the manner of two vajras crossed. Why? Because consciousness and gnosis are perfectly united. Therefore gnosis is applied to consciousness, and consciousness is applied to gnosis.[121] Therefore gnosis Vajrasattva and consciousness Akṣobhya are sealed by each other. Is this not contradictory? There is no fault here. The quote that the main deity, who has the nature of Vajrasattva, is adorned with the crown of Vajrasattva illustrates that here in the sovereign-mandala meditation, the main deity in the form of Kālacakra has the nature of Vajrasattva, and is a statement made on the basis of the main deity being generated in that way during the process of deity creation. During the process of sealing, the statement that gnosis and consciousness are sealed by each other is made on the basis of Vajrasattva and Akṣobhya being of distinct forms /270/ and being sealed by their family lord after the initiation meditation.[122]

d.div: [92] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 207_na2
[93] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 363_na1
[94] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 222_na7
[120] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 207a2.
[121] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 222a7.
[122] Sealing is the fourth part of the branch of the speech-vajra near-accomplishment and will be presented later.

f.d: gsum pa lha'i gdan 'ga' zhig la dwogs pa dpyad pa ni/

de la gzhal yas khang gi 'og gzhi 'byung ba rim brtsegs sogs sgom pa'i tshe zla nyi'i steng du sgra gcan nyid bsgom par bya ba yin gyi sgra gcan gyi steng du dus me sgom pa rgyud 'grel gyi dgongs pa ma yin te/ 'grel chen las/
de'i steng du haM yig yongs su gyur pa las zla ba'i dkyil 'khor lte ba dang mnyam pa'o/ / de'i steng du rnam par gcad pa yongs su gyur pa las nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor ro/ / de'i steng du thig le yongs su gyur pa las me zhes pa sgra gcan gyi dkyil 'khor kha dog mthon mthing ste de ltar mtha' dag gcig tu 'dres par gyur pa ni hakaShamalawarayaM_zhes pa sa bon gyi yi ger rnam par bsgom par bya ste de las 'jig rten gyi khams grub par bsam par bya'o/[95] / zhes zla nyi'i steng du sgra gcan bsgom par bshad kyi/ sgra gcan gyi steng du dus me bsgom par ma bshad pa'i phyir dang / srog gi a la sogs pa'i rnam bcu+i dbang ldan gyi yi ge bcu po 'og nas rim pa bzhin nam mkha' rlung me chu sa lhun po de'i lte ba zla ba nyi ma sgra gcan rnams kyi sa bon yin la/ sgra gcan gyi sa bon las logs su dus me'i sa bon ma bshad pa'i phyir dang / 'byung ba rim brtsegs sogs sgom pa nang la sbyor ba'i tshe na'ang 'grel chen las/
bshang ba dang gci ba dang khu ba 'bab pa'i rtsa gsum ni zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan gyi dkyil 'khor te gsang ba'i pad+ma'i lte bar de rnams 'dus pa'o [96] zhes gsungs nas sgra gcan las logs su dus me nang la sbyor ba la gsungs pas so/ /

In the meditation on the celestial mansion foundation in its stacked arrangement, Rāhu is visualized on top of the moon and sun, but it is not the thinking of the tantra and commentary that Kālāgni is visualized on top of Rāhu. The Great Commentary says:
On that is the letter haṃ, from which arises a moon mandala the size of the lotus center. On that is a visarga, from which arises a sun mandala. On that there is a drop, from which arises “fire,” meaning the mandala of Rāhu, dark blue in color. These all fuse into one to become haṃ kṣa ma la wa ra ya. Meditate on this as the seed syllable and think that from this the realms of the world are created.[123] This teaches that Rāhu is visualized on top of a moon and sun, but it does not teach that Kālāgni is to be visualized on top of Rāhu. Moreover, in ascending order, the ten letters of the powerful ten-syllable stack, such as the life-giving a and so forth, are the seed syllables of space, air, fire, water, earth, and Meru, in whose center is a lotus, moon, sun, and Rāhu. There is no letter for Kālāgni separate from Rāhu. On the meditation of this stacked arrangement as it is applied to the inner world, the Great Commentary says:
The three channels of excrement, urine, and fluid are the mandalas of the moon, sun, and Rāhu coming together at the center of the secret lotus.[124] Thus no inner application is taught for Kālāgni separate from Rāhu.

f.d:
gal te thig le'i steng gi nA da dus me'i sa bon yin no zhe na/ de lta na rnam bcu dbang ldan du mi 'gyur te/ sa bon gyi yi ge bcu gcig dang ldan par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang dkyil 'khor gyi 'og gzhi'i 'byung ba rim brtsegs sogs sgom pa'i skabs 'dir sgrub le'i 'grel pa drangs zin pa ltar nA da bsgom par ma bshad cing / 'jig rten khams le'i rnam bcu dbang ldan gyi sgra sgrub 'chad pa'i skabs kyi 'grel chen las
hakaShamalawarayaM zhes pa ni 'jig rten gyi khams kyi tshogs rdo rje'i sku ste nam mkha'i khams la ya yig rlung gi dkyil 'khor dang 1_de'i steng du ra yig me'i dkyil 'khor dang 2_de'i steng du wa yig chu'i dkyil 'khor dang 3_da'i+e steng du la yig sa'i dkyil 'khor dang 4de'i steng du ma yig lhun po rnam pa lnga pa'o/ 5_de'i steng du k+Sha yig pad+ma_'i tshul gyis g.yo ba'i tshoDa dang 6_de'i steng du gzugs med pa'i tshogs ha yig go7 /ha yig las rnam par gcad pa nyi ma dang 8_thig le zla ba dang 9_nA da rdo rje gcig pa'i mtshan ma ste [97] 10 zhes nA da thig le'i rtser 'dri bar bshad kyang sa bon gyi yi ger ma bshad par rdo rje rtse gcig pa'i mtshon byed du gsungs la|_de yang gzhom med yin pa mtshon byed du gsungs pa yin gyi/ sa bon du ma bshad la/ khyad par du sgra gcan dang dus me'i sa bon du ni zur tsam yang gsungs pa med do/ /

Some may wonder if the nāda[125] of the drop is the seed syllable of Kālāgni? If that were so, the powerful ten-syllable stack would not add up, because it would have to contain eleven seed syllables. Furthermore, in this section on the meditation upon the stacked arrangement of the foundation mandalas, there is no mention of nāda visualization in the commentary on the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, as the previous quote reveals. /271/ Also the Great Commentary on the Realms chapter, in the section on the formation of the mantra, says:
Haṃ kṣa ma la wa ra ya is the assembly of the worlds and the vajra body. In space the letter ya, the mandala of air. On top of that the ra fire mandala. On top of that the wa water mandala. On top of that the la earth mandala. On top of that the ma Meru. That is the fifth. Above that the kṣa lotus of animate beings. On top of that the formless worlds ha. From the ha the visarga is the sun, the drop is the moon, and the nāda is the sign of the one-pointed vajra.[126] The nāda, therefore, is drawn on top of the drop. However it is not a seed syllable letter but symbolizes a one-pointed vajra, which in turn illustrates indestructibility. Nowhere is it spoken of as being the seed syllable of Rāhu or Kālāgni.

d.div: [97] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 52_na3
[125] The wavy line, or squiggle, rising from the circle that sits upon the crescent atop the syllable.
[126] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 52a3.

f.d:
gzhan yang hakaSha_malawarayaM_zhes pa 'di sa bon gyi yi ge bcu nyid dang de'i mtshon don yang bcu nyid yin pa la dgongs nas 'di'i skabs kyi 'grel chen du/
rnam pa bcu po don bcu'i don/ / thub dbang stobs bcu khyab pa'i bdag / kun gyi don ni ma lus byed/ / rnam bcu dbang ldan che ba po/[98] / zhes sogs kyi mtshan brjod kyi lung drangs pa yin no/ /

Furthermore haṃ kṣa ma la wa ra ya is the mantra of the ten seed syllables, and there are ten corresponding phenomena that they illustrate. With this in mind, the Great Commentary quotes a passage from the Saṃgītī.
Ten parts of ten meanings, the mighty one of ten powers, the all-pervading master, accomplishing the wishes of all, the great and powerful in ten aspects.[127]

d.div: [98] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 52_ba1
[127] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 52b1.

f.d:
gal te 'grel chen las/
gsang ba'i pad+ma ni bcom ldan 'das kyi pad+ma bzhin no/ / bshang ba dang gci ba dang khu ba 'bab pa'i rtsa gsum ni zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan gyi dkyil 'khor te gsang ba'i pad+ma'i lte bar de rnams 'dus pa'o/[99] / zhes gsungs pa la/ gsang gnas kyi pad+mar zla nyi'i rtsa dang 'dus pa de ni dus me'i rtsa dung can ma ma yin nam zhe na/ spyir bshang gci khu ba'i rtsa gsum la zla nyi dus me'i tha snyad mdzad pa rgyud 'grel na du ma yod kyang 'dir/ bshang ba dang gci ba dang khu ba 'bab pa'i rtsa gsum ni zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan gyi dkyil 'khor te zhes gsungs pa 'dis rtsa gsum zla nyi dus me'i rtsar bstan pa ma yin gyi/ rtsa gsum phyi'i zla nyi sgra gcan gsum dang chos mthun du bstan pa yin te/ dper na gsang ba'i pad+ma ni bcom ldan 'das kyi pad+ma bzhin no zhes gsungs pa 'dis ma'i gsang ba'i pad+ma dang pad+ma sgom pa chos mthun du bstan pa bzhin no/ /

However the Great Commentary says:
The secret lotus is like the lotus of the Conqueror. The three channels of excrement, urine, and fluid are the mandalas of the moon, sun, and Rāhu coming together at the center of the secret lotus.[128] Concerning this quote the question might arise, “In the secret lotus are found the moon and sun channels, and isn’t the central channel the śaṅkhinī channel of Kālāgni?” Generally there are many instances in the tantra and commentary of the three channels of excrement, urine, and fluid being termed the channels of the moon, sun, and Kālāgni. However here the line “The three channels of excrement, urine, and fluid are the mandalas of the moon, sun, and Rāhu” does not teach the three channels to be those of the moon, sun, and Kālāgni but teaches that these three channels correlate with the outer phenomena of the moon, sun, and Rāhu. Likewise “The secret lotus is like the lotus of the Conqueror” explains that the mother’s secret lotus and the visualized lotus are correlated phenomena. /272/

d.div: [99] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 204_ba1
[128] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 204b1.

f.d: de bzhin gtso bo'i gdan la yang zla nyi'i steng du sgra gcan nam dus me gang yang rung ba gcig byed pa 'thad kyi sgra gcan dang dus me gnyis ka byed pa rgyud 'grel gyi dgongs pa ma yin te/ zla nyi sgra gcan nam dus me ste gdan gsum nyid rgyud 'grel las yang yang bshad pa dang / de yang phyi nang gnyis ka dang shin tu 'byor zhing / gdan bzhi byed pa phyi nang gnyis ka dang mi 'byor ba'i phyir ro/ /

Similarly it is also correct to say that the seat of the main deity is either Rāhu or Kalāgni upon a moon disk, but to posit both Rāhu and Kālāgni is not the intention of the tantra and commentary. Again and again the tantra and commentary talk of the three seats of moon, sun, and Rāhu or Kālāgni, and that arrangement perfectly fits the outer-inner correlation, whereas four seats does not.

de yang rgyud 'grel las yang yang gsungs tshul ni 'jig rten khams le'i mdor bsdus dang po las/
rlung me chu dang sa yi dkyil 'khor lhun po pad+ma dang / zla nyi dus me'i steng du dbang phyug dang ni dud kyi mgor/ / zhabs ni srid pa'i yum gyi zhabs dang lhan cig bkod gyur pa/[100] / zhes dang /

How is this taught in the tantra and commentary? In the first summary from the Realms chapter it says:
Mandalas of air, fire, water, and earth, Meru, lotus, moon, sun, and Kālāgni, on top of these, upon Īśvara and the head of Māra, his feet with those of the mother of existence.[129]

d.div: [100] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 3_na2
[129] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 3a2.

f.d:
de bzhin du khams le'i mdor bsdus gnyis pa las/
rdo rje seng ge'i khri la bzhugs pa ni rdo rje seng ge'i khri zla ba dang nyi ma dang me'i dkyil 'khor gcad du med cing dbyer med pa'am e yig na ma mkha'i dbyings ni rdo rje seng ge'i khri'o/[101] / zhes dang /

Similarly, from the second summary from the Realms chapter:
“Sitting on the vajra lion throne.” The vajra lion throne is of moon, sun, and Agni mandalas, indestructible and indivisible. Alternatively the letter e of the element of space is the vajra-lion throne.[130]

d.div: [101] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 13_ba6
[130] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 13b6.

f.d:
yang khams le'i mdor bsdus bzhi pa las/
sangs rgyas de seng ge'i khri la bzhugs pa ste seng ge'i khri ni nam mkha'i khams yin la gzhan zla ba dang nyi ma dang me'i dkyil 'khor ni seng ge'i khri steng la bzhugs pa ni seng ge'i khri la bzhugs pa'o/[102] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis rgyud kyi ston pa dkyil 'khor gyi gtso bo'i rnam pas dkyil 'khor gyi dbus su bzhugs pa'i gdan zla nyi dus me dang gsum nyid yin par bstan cing / de dang bsgom pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi gtso bo'i gdan mtshungs pa yin no/ /

In the fourth summary from the Realms chapter it says:
“The Buddha sat upon the lion throne.” The lion throne is of the element of space. Alternatively, sitting upon the lion throne of moon, sun, and Agni mandalas, he “sat upon the lion throne.”[131] These quotes show that the teacher of the tantra in the form of the main deity of the mandala sat in the center of the mandala on a seat of moon, sun, and Agni, and the seat of the visualized mandala should be similar.

d.div: [102] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 35_ba3
[131] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 35b3.

f.d:
gzhan yang sgrub le'i gnyis pa las/
zhabs dag gis ni zla ba nyi ma bsreg za'i dkyil 'khor rnams la bdud dang drag po [103] zhes dang /

The second verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter says:
Feet on moon, sun, and Agni mandalas, upon Māra and Rudra.[132]

f.d:
yang sgrub le'i dgu pa'i 'grel chen las/
de'i yang phyed ni bcom ldan 'das kyi pad+ma'o/ / pad+ma'i sum cha ni lte ba ste de bzhin du zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan gyi dkyil 'khor rnams so/[104] / zhes dang /

The Great Commentary on the ninth verse of Methods of Accomplishment chapter says:
Half that size is the lotus of the Conqueror. Its center takes up one third of the lotus, as does the moon, sun, and Rāhu mandalas.[133]

yang bcu pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir dkyil 'khor gyi lte ba'i steng gi zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan gyi dkyil 'khor gyi steng du zla ba'i dkyil 'khor la [105] zhes sogs dang /

In the center of the mandala, the mandalas of the moon, sun, and Rāhu, and on the moon mandala are thirty vowels.[134]

f.d:
yang bcu gcig pa'i 'grel chen las/
snying po'i pad+mar zla ba nyi ma me'i steng du ni zhes pa la la nA dang ra sa nA dang a wa ng+hU tI'i steng du [106] zhes dang /

On the eleventh verse:
“On the central lotus, on moon, sun, and Agni,” means upon the lalanā, rasanā, and avadhūtī.[135] /273/

d.div: [106] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 206_ba5

f.d:
yang dbang le'i nga bdun pa'i lha mtshan dgod pa'i 'grel chen las/
rgyal ba'i bdag po'i pad+ma sna tshogs mdog la zhes pa ljang gu'i mdog la zla ba nyi ma me'i steng du hUM yig ste zhes pa ni 'di gnam stong gi mthar 'dzin pa'i dus su zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan rnams sbyor ba ste zla ba dang nyi ma dang me yang dag par ldan pa de nyid dkyil 'khor gyi gdan no/ / nang du ni la la nA dang ra sa nA dang a wa ng+hU tI dang yang dag par ldan pa snying ga'i pad+ma ste de'i lte bar zla ba nyi ma dang sgra gcan gyi steng du hUM yig gi sa bon rngul tshon sngon pos bri bar bya'o/[107] / zhes pa la sogs pa rnams so/ /

The Great Commentary on the fifty-seventh verse of the Initiation chapter, in the section on the placing of the deity symbols, says:
“The color of the variegated lotus of the conquering lord” refers to the color green.[136] “On a moon, sun, and Agni is the letter hūḥ.” At the end of the empty sky, the moon, sun, and Rāhu join, and the seat of the mandala is well endowed with the moon, sun, and Agni. Inside, well endowed with lalanā, rasanā, and avadhūtī, is the heart lotus. On top of that the moon, sun, and Rāhu, on top of that the letter hūḥ to be drawn using blue powder. [137]

d.div: [107] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 300_na1
[136] Although the central lotus is multicolored, in the powder mandala it is colored green.
[137] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 300a1.

f.d:
'grel tshig de dag gi yang 'ga' zhig tu sgra gcan zhes dang / la lar dus me zhes 'byung ba dang / rtsa bar dus me zhes 'byung ba'i 'grel par sgra gcan zhes bkod pa rnams ni sgra gcan dang dus me gdam nga can du go ba'i ched du yin no/ / de bzhin du gtso bo'i gdan gyi sa bon 'chad pa'i dbang le'i re gcig pa'i 'grel chen las/
lte ba'i steng du aM AHa ste zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan gyi gdan rnams so/[108] / zhes zla nyi sgra gcan gsum gyis sa bon las ma bshad pas kyang shes so/ /

In some of these passages the name “Rāhu” is used and in others “Kālāgni” is used. Sometimes when the term “Kālāgni” is used in the tantra, it is commented upon using the name “Rāhu.” This is done to indicate that either name can be understood as Rāhu or Kālāgni. Likewise the Great Commentary on the sixty-first verse of the Initiation chapter, when explaining the seed syllables of the seat of the main deity, says:
In the center the letters aṃ, āṃ, and a. These are the individual seats of the moon, sun, and Rāhu.[138] Here only the three syllables of moon, sun, and Rāhu are taught.

d.div: [108] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 302_na1
[138] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 302a1.

f.d:
sgrub le'i nga bzhi pa'i 'grel chen gyi shong 'gyur las/
bde ba chen po la me'i steng du ste zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan dang dus me'i steng du dam tshig sems dpa' dang ye shes sems dpa' ro mnyam pa nyid du 'gyur [109] zhes 'byung yang 'gyur gzhan dag las/ me'i steng du ste zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan nam dus me'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng du zhes 'byung bas 'dis kyang sgra gcan dang dus me gdam nga can du bshad do/ / de ltar na 'gyur dag pa'i dbang du byas na sgra gcan dang dus me brtsegs pa gtso bo'i gdan du ston pa'i 'grel tshig zur tsam yang med do/ /

In the Shong translation of the Great Commentary, on the fifty-fourth verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, it says:
“In the great bliss and upon fire,” meaning on moon, sun, Rāhu, and Kālāgni, the samaya being and the gnosis being come to be of one taste.[139] However other translations say, “‘on fire,’ meaning on moon, sun, Rāhu, or Kālāgni mandalas,” thereby positing either Rāhu or Kālāgni. Therefore, using an accurate translation, there are no passages teaching a stacking of both Rāhu and Kālāgni as seats of the main deity.

d.div: [109] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 221_ba5
[139] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 221b5.

f.d: gzhan yang gtso bo'i gdan zla nyi sogs gsum nyid brtsegs pa phyi nang gnyis ka dang mthun pa'i tshul ni dbang le'i 'grel pa gong du drangs pa ltar/ zla ba nyi ma dus me'i steng du zhes rtsa bar dus me bkod nas/ de'i 'grel par/ gnam stong gi mthar 'dzin pa'i dus su zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan rnams sbyor ba ste [110] zhes sgra gcan bshad la/ de yang phyi rol du gnam stong gi mthar zla nyi res 'ga' dus mes sgrib/ res 'ga' sgra gcan gyis sgrib pa ste gang rung re res sgrib pa la dgongs pa yin pa ltar dpe de bzhin du gtso bo'i gdan yang zla nyi'i steng du sgra gcan dang dus me gang yang rung ba gcig bya bar dgongs pa yin no/ / de ltar ma yin na gnam stong gi mtha' sogs dus nam yang zla nyi sgra gcan dang dus mes dus cig car du sgrib pa mi srid pas phyi rol de bzhin gzhan du mi 'gyur ro/ /

Furthermore the way that these three stacked seats of the main deity are applied to inner and outer phenomena is as taught in the previous quote from the Initiation chapter, where Kālāgni is used in the line “on a moon, sun, and Agni,” which is from the tantra, and Rāhu is used in the commentary in the line “At the end of the empty sky, the moon, sun, and Rāhu join.”[140] In the external world, in the empty sky, the sun and moon are sometimes eclipsed by Kālāgni and sometimes by Rāhu, and the thinking behind the above quote is that just as eclipses can be caused by either Rāhu or Kālāgni, /274/ so the seat of the main deity can have either Rāhu or Kālāgni on top of the moon and sun. If this were not the case, the external world would not correlate with either the Other or the Inner, because it is impossible for the sun or the moon to be eclipsed simultaneously by Rāhu and Kālāgni.

d.div: [110] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 300_na2
[140] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 300a2.

f.d:
de bzhin du nang la yang 'grel chen las/
nang la la la nA dang ra sa nA dang a wa ng+hU tI dang yang dag par ldan pa snying ga'i pad+ma ste de'i lta bar zla ba nyi ma sgra gcan gyi steng du/[111] zhes zla nyi'i steng du sgra gcan brtsegs pa sgom pa'i tshe gdan gsum snying gar ro rkyang dbu ma gsum 'dus pa dang sbyar/ dus me dang brtsegs pa sgom pa'i tshe gdan gsum bshang gci khu ba'i rtsa gsang gnas su 'dus pa dang sbyar ro/ /

As the Great Commentary says:
Inside, well endowed with lalanā, rasanā, and avadhūtī, is the heart lotus. On top of that the moon, sun, and Rāhu.[141] Therefore, when meditating on the stacked arrangement with Rāhu on top of moon and sun, the three seats correlate with the left, right, and central channel at the heart. When meditating on the stacked arrangement with Kālāgni, the three seats correlate with the channels of excrement, urine, and fluid gathered at the secret area.

d.div: [111] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 300_na2
[141] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 300a2.

f.d: gtso bo'i gdan zla nyi sgra gcan nam dus me gang rung ste gsum nyid du byas pa 'di ni rgyal tshab dam pa'i sbyor drug dang rje nyid kyi zin bris kyi dgongs pa ltar bkod pa'o/[112] /
This assertion of three seats consisting of moon, sun, and Rāhu or Kālāgni is in accord with the thinking of venerable Gyaltsap’s Six Yogas and with the Jé Tsongkhapa’s Notes on Kālacakra.

d.div: [112] rgyal tshab rje/ gsung 'bum/ kadapal dus kyi 'khor lo'i rnal 'byor yan lag drug gi khrid bsdus dang / rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum/ da_sbyor ba yan lag drug gi rdzogs rim kyi gnas bsdus pa/

f.d: gzhan yang klu brgyad dang gtum mo brgyad la pad+ma'i gdan sgrub ler dngos su ma bshad kyang zhal lung las gsungs pa ni legs pa yin te/ nang ler pad+ma gdan can gyi lha brgya nga drug tu gsungs pa'i nang na klu brgyad dang rab gtum ma brgyad kyang yod pa'i phyir ro/ / 'o na pad+ma gdan can gyi lha'i grangs bgrang tshul ji lta bu snyam na/

Although it is not actually taught in the Methods of Accomplishment chapter that the eight nāgas and the eight fierce females are on lotus seats, such an assertion, as taught in the Kālacakrapāda Transmission, is valid, because in the Inner chapter, 156 lotus-seated deities are mentioned, and the eight nāgas and eight fierce females are included among them. So how are these lotus-seated deities counted?
bzhi pa de las 'phros pa'i pad+ma gdan can gyi lha'i grangs la dwogs pa dpyad pa

d.i: The number of deities on lotus seats

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ bshad bya'i rgyud 'grel gyi tshig dgod pa dang / de dag gi don bshad pa'i sgo nas lha'i grangs nges par bya ba'o/ /
This is under two headings: 1. The tantra and commentary passages to be explained 2. Determining the number of deities by explaining the above passages
dang po [bshad bya'i rgyud 'grel gyi tshig dgod pa ]ni

d.i: The tantra and commentary passages to be explained

'grel chen las/
pha rol tu phyin pa bcu ni nus ma bcu dang gtsug tor la sogs pa'i khro bo bcu ste so sor bcu'o/[113] / zhes dang /

The Great Commentary says:
The ten perfections are the ten śakti. Uṣṇīṣa and so forth are the ten wrathful ones. Thus there are ten of each.[142]

yang /

Also:
“Five are the buddhas and goddesses” refers to the five buddhas Akṣobhya and so forth and the five goddesses Vajradhātvīśvarī and so forth. Thus there are five of each.[143] /275/

Rūpavajrā and others making six, and Kṣitigarbha and the others to make six. Thus there are six of each.[144]

d.div: [115] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 138_na7
[144] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 138a7.

dbang po la sogs pa bcu gnyis kyi grangs so/[116] / zhes dang /

Also:
Of Indra and so forth there are twelve.[145]
