[145] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 138b1.

f.d:
yang
tsar tsi kA la sogs pa brgyad dang mtha' yas la sogs pa brgyad dang khyi gdong ma la sogs pa brgyad de/[117] zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis ni nus ma khro bo dang bcas pa nyi shu/ de'i steng du gshegs pa gshegs ma bcu dang sems dpa' sems ma bcu gnyis bsnan pas zhe gnyis dang / de'i steng du tshes lha'i gtso bo lha chen bcu gnyis dang / rnal 'byor ma dang klu mo brgyad brgyad de nyer bzhi dang bcas pa'i so drug bsnan pas don brgyad 'byung la/

Also:
Carcikā and others make eight, Ananta and others make eight, and Śvānavaktrā and others make eight.[146] Therefore the śakti and the wrathful protectors make twenty. The ten male and female tathāgatas and the twelve male and female bodhisattvas bring the total to forty-two. Twelve main lunar-day deities and the twenty-four deities consisting of eight yoginīs, eight wrathful females, and eight female nāgas make thirty-six, bringing the total to seventy-eight.

d.div: [117] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 138_ba1
[146] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 138b1.

f.d:
yang 'grel chen las/
slar yang 'di rnams thams cad shes rab dang thabs kyi dbye bas nyis 'gyur te 'di rnams dpal ldan dus kyi 'khor lo bzhi lhag brgya ste de'i phyed kyang lha lnga bcu rtsa gnyis kyi bdag nyid do/[118] / zhes dang /

The Great Commentary states:
Again these are divided into wisdom and method. Therefore, multiplied by two, there are 104 Kālacakras. Half of that comes to fifty-two deities.[147]

d.div: [118] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 231_ba1

[147] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 231b1. This is a partial count consisting of the ten śakti, ten tathāgatas, twelve bodhisattvas, eight speech goddesses, and twelve lunar-day deities. In the previous paragraph the count of seventy-eight is multiplied by two to total 156.

f.d:
yang /
slar yang de dag gcig nyid kyis lha lnga bcu rtsa drug lhag pa'i brgya phrag gcig gi bdag nyid kyi dus kyi 'khor lor rig par bya'o/[119] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis lha zung du byas na don brgyad dang / yab yum so sor bgrangs na brgya nga drug tu bstan to/ /

Also:
Again, individually, 156 deities should be known within the Kālacakra.[148] These quotes talks of deities individually and in union. Therefore in union they number seventy-eight and individually 156.

d.div: [119] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 138_ba2
[148] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 138b2.

f.d: yang de'i mjug tu pad+ma'i lte ba la gnas pa'i lha'i tshogs kyi nges pa'o/[120] /zhes lha de rnams rang rang gi gdan gyi pad+ma'i lte ba la gnas par yang gsungs so/ /

After the above quote the text continues: “These are determined as being the assembly of deities within the center of lotuses,” thereby ascertaining that each of these deities is positioned within the center of a lotus.

d.div: [120] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 138_ba3

f.d:
'di dag ni bsdus rgyud kyi dkyil 'khor la bkod pa'i lha'i gtso bo rnams yin pa ni/ khyi gdong ma la sogs pa brgyad de zhes pa'i 'phro nyid las/
lha'i tshogs 'di rnams mtha' dag ni sgrub thabs kyi le'u las so sor ming gi dbye bas brjod par bya'o/[121] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

These are the principal deities of the mandala as presented in the Condensed Tantra. This can be understood from the text following “Śvānavaktrā and others to make eight,” which says:
All these deities are each differentiated by name in the Methods of Accomplishment chapter.[149]

d.div: [121] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 138_ba1
[149] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 138b1.

f.d: 'o na lha de rnams yab yum so sor bgrangs pas brgya nga drug tu bya tshul ji lta bu snyam na/ de ni 'di ltar yin te/ don grub sogs gshegs pa bzhi/ sgrol ma sogs gshegs ma bzhi/ sems dpa' sems ma bcu gnyis/ rnal 'byor ma brgyad/ lha chen bcu gnyis/ klu brgyad/ gtum mo brgyad rnams ni yab yum zung dang so sor bgrang tshul sgrub ler dngos su gsal ba ltar yin la/ nus ma bcu yab yum zung dang so sor bgrang tshul ni gong du drangs pa ltar/ ye shes kyi pha rol tu phyin ma ni sna tshogs yum de'i nang du 'dus shing zhes sher phyin ma'i ngo bor gyur pa'i sna tshogs yum gyi nang du ye shes kyi pha rol tu phyin ma 'dus par gsungs nas/ nus ma gnyis kyi ngo bo 'dzin pa sna tshogs yum gtso bo dang sbyar ba'i yab yum zung gnyis dang / pad+ma'i 'dab ma la bkod pa'i nus ma brgyad rim gyis pad+ma'i lte bar gtso bo dang mnyam par sbyor ba'i yab yum zung brgyad do/ / de dag ni nus ma bcu yab yum zung bcur 'dren tshul lo/ /

By counting the deities and consorts individually, how does one arrive at 156? It is like this. The four tathāgatas, Amoghasiddhi and so forth, the four female tathāgatas, Tārā and so forth, the twelve male and female bodhisattvas, the eight yoginis, the twelve deities of the lunar months, the eight nāgas and the eight wrathful females are clearly enumerated both individually and with consort in the Methods of Accomplishment chapter. The ten śakti can be counted individually and with consort as follows. As quoted above, “Jñānapāramitā is included within Viśvamātā,” which means that Jñānapāramitā is combined within Viśvamātā, who has the nature of Prajñāpāramitā. /276/ Viśvamātā being of the nature of two śakti and embracing the main deity thus forms two mother-and-father pairs. The eight śakti arranged upon the lotus petals one by one embrace the main deity in the center, thereby forming eight mother-and-father pairs. This is how the ten śakti become the ten mother-and-father pairs.

de nas mi bskyod pa la sher phyin mas 'khyud pa gtso bo la bcug pa dang / rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma la rdor sems kyis 'khyud pa yum la bcug pa'i yab yum zung gnyis kyang gtso bo yab yum gyi gnas kyi pad+ma'i lte ba la gnas pa'o/ / de yang rdo rje dbyings phyug ma la rdo rje sems dpas 'khyud pa yum la gzhug pa sgrub thabs le'u las dngos su ma bshad kyang de ltar byed dgos pa ni rdo rje dbyings phyug ma la yab kyis 'khyud pa bsdus rgyud kyi lha pad+ma'i gdan can du bshad cing / de la pad+ma'i gdan logs pa ma bshad pa'i phyir ro/

Akṣobhya embraced by Prajñāpāramitā enters the main deity, and Vajradhātvīśvarī embraced by Vajrasattva enters the mother to form two mother-and-father pairs in union and also to stand in the main mother-and-father lotus center. Vajradhātvīśvarī embraced by Vajrasattva and entering the mother is not explicitly taught in the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, but it has to be this way because Vajradhātvīśvarī embraced by a father deity is explained as being a lotus-seated deity in the Condensed Tantra, but no separate lotus seat is mentioned for them.

khro bo bcu yab yum zung bcu ni thugs dkyil gyi lnga dang sku dkyil gyi gtsug tor 'khor los sgyur ba ma gtogs pa'i lnga'o/ / de yang sku dkyil gyi gtsug tor 'khor sgyur ni thugs dkyil gyi de dang gcig pa nyid kyis de las logs su ma bgrangs pa ste/ de las gzhan du 'dren na khro bo bcu gcig tu 'gyur bas 'grel chen dang dngos su 'gal lo/ / yang 'ga' zhig nus ma bcu yab dang bcas pa'i zung bcur mi 'dren pa dang / rdor sems yab yum gtso bo las logs su 'dren pa dang / rdo rje dbyings phyug ma la yab kyis 'khyud pa mi 'dren pa rnams ni 'grel chen dang dngos su 'gal lo/ / yang yum la bcug pa'i rdo rje dbyings phyug ma la yab kyis 'khyud pa mi bgrang ba'i rgyu mtshan du thabs kyi pang par shes rab gtso bo ma yin zhing / shes rab kyi pang par thabs gtso bo ma yin par gsungs pa 'dren pa ni shin tu mi rigs te/ rdo rje dbyings phyug ma la yab kyis 'khyud pa'i tshe shes rab kyi pang par yab gnas pa yin pas yum gtso bo yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang brjod par bya ba yod de re zhig de tsam mo/ /

The ten mother-and-father wrathful-protector pairs comprise five from the mind mandala and, excluding Uṣṇīṣacakrī, five of the body mandala. Uṣṇīṣacakrī of the body mandala is one with Uṣṇīṣacakrī of the mind mandala and is therefore not counted separately. If it were, the wrathful protectors would number eleven, which would directly contradict the Great Commentary. Moreover those who do not count the ten śakti as being ten consort pairs, those who count Vajrasattva mother and father apart from the main deity, and those who do not count Vajradhātvīśvarī embraced by consort also contradict the Great Commentary. Furthermore to use the quote “in the lap of method, wisdom is not the main deity, and in the lap of wisdom, method is not the main deity” as the reason for not including Vajradhātvīśvarī who enters the mother embraced by the father is just wrong, because when Vajradhātvīśvarī is embraced by the father, it is a case of the father being in the lap of wisdom.[150] The mother, therefore, becomes the main deity. That will be discussed later, and this will suffice for the time being.

d.div: [150] The “lap” belongs to the dominant partner of the pair in union. Therefore a deity in the lap of wisdom refers to a “method” deity embraced by a dominant “wisdom” deity.

f.d:
de yang pad+ma gdan can gyi lha brgya nga drug rgyas 'debs kyi lha drug dang bcas pa ni 'grel chen las/
mchog gi dang po'i sangs rgyas 'di las bsdus pa'i rgyud 'byung ba gsungs te 'dir mchog gi dang po'i sangs rgyas nyi shu lhag pa'i brgya phrag bcu drug las sum cu'i cha yis thob pa ni lha lnga bcu rtsa bzhir 'gyur ro/ / slar yang gsum gyis bsgyur ba ste sku dang gsung dang thugs kyis bsgyur ba ni drug cu rtsa gnyis lhag pa'i brgyar 'gyur ro/[122] / zhes gsungs pa ltar rtsa rgyud kyi dkyil 'khor gyi lha grangs stong drug brgya nyi shu las gtso bor 'gyur ba'i lha rnams bsdus kyi de yang lha'i gtso bo bsdus pa'o/ /

Concerning the 156 lotus-seated deities plus the six sealing deities, the Great Commentary says:
Now it is taught how the Condensed Tantra arose from the Supreme and Original Buddha. The twenty more than 1,600 supreme and original buddhas were divided by thirty to become fifty-four deities. This again was multiplied by the three mandalas of body, speech, and mind to become sixty-two more than a hundred.[151] /277/ The principal deities were compiled and condensed from the 1,620 deities of the Root Tantra mandala.

d.div: [122] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 139_na6
[151] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 139a6.

f.d:
de yang rtsa rgyud kyi dkyil 'khor la dpal ldan rgyu skar gyi dkyil 'khor zhes tha snyad 'dogs pa ni 'grel chen las/
dpal ldan rgyu skar gyi dkyil 'khor dang po'i sangs rgyas la lha'i tshogs ni rgyu skar gyi chu tshod kyi grangs kyi bdag nyid du bcom ldan 'das kyis gsungs so/[123] / zhes gsungs pa ltar yin no/ /

The mandala of the Root Tantra is known as the glorious constellation mandala. On this the Great Commentary says:
The Buddha has said that the assembly of deities in the Supreme and Original Buddha mandala of constellations are of the number of hours in the constellations.[152]

d.div: [123] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 139_na3
[152] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 139a3. 27 constellations, 60 hours in each = 1620.

f.d: dpal ldan rgyu skar gyi dkyil 'khor gyi lha'i tshogs las pad+ma gdan can gyi lha rgyas 'debs kyi lha drug dang bcas pa'i brgya re gnyis su bsdus nas gsungs pa'i dgongs pa ni dus kyi 'khor lo'i lha bsgoms nas sbyang bar bya ba'i sbyang gzhi'i rtsa'i gtso bo rnams rtsa 'khor drug gi rtsa brgya nga drug dang rigs drug gi rtsa rnams ni la la nA dang ra sa nA dang a wa ng+hu tI dang / bshang ba dang gci ba dang khu ba 'bab pa rnams so/ /zhes gsungs pa ltar gyi rtsa brgya re gnyis su bsdus nas gsungs so/ /

162 lotus-seated deities, including the six sealing deities, were compiled and taught from the assembled deities of the glorious constellation mandala. The thinking behind this is that after meditating upon the Kālacakra deities, the bases are to be purified, and these are the 156 main channels of the six cakras plus the channels of the six families. The channels of the six families are, “lalanā, rasanā, and avadhūtī, and the flow of excrement, urine, and fluid.” Thus 162 channels are taught.

de yang rtsa brgya dang nga drug ni 'grel chen las/ de bzhin du dus kyi 'khor lo'i rtsa rnams gsungs pa/ gtsug tor la ni chu gter zhes pa nas/ sum cu rtsa gnyis 'khor bar byed pa rnams so/[124] / zhes pa'i bar gyis bstan pa ltar gyi gtsug tor gyi rtsa 'dab bzhi/ snying ga'i rtsa 'dab brgyad/ de bzhin du dpral ba'i bcu drug/ mgrin pa'i so gnyis/ lte ba'i re bzhi/ gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'dab so gnyis rnams so/ / de dag gi yang gsang gnas kyi nang skor gyi rtsa 'dab drug dang bar skor gyi bcu ni rlung mkhris bad kan gsum 'dus pa'i nad skyed pa'i cha can dang / gtsug tor gyi bzhi dang dpral ba'i bcu drug ste nyi shu ni bad kan skyed pa'i cha dang bcas pa dang / mgrin pa'i so gnyis dang snying ga'i brgyad de bzhi bcu ni mkhris pa'i nad skyed pa'i cha dang ldan pa dang / lte ba'i rtsa 'dab re bzhi dang gsang gnas kyi phyi rim gyi rtsa 'dab bcu drug ste brgyad cu po de dag ni rlung gi skyon skyed pa'i cha shas dang ldan pa yin la/

The 156 channels are mentioned in the Great Commentary in a passage that runs from “Likewise the channels of Kālacakra are taught. There are four at the crown” until “encircled by thirty-two”[153] These are the four channel petals at the crown, eight at the heart, sixteen at the forehead, thirty-two at the throat, sixty-four at the navel, and thirty-two in the secret place. Of these, six inner petals and ten intermediate petals of the secret-area channels act as bases for the creation of illnesses caused by a combination of wind, bile, and phlegm. The four petals of the crown and the sixteen of the forehead are bases for phlegm illnesses. The thirty-two petals of the throat and the eight of the heart are bases for bile-related illnesses. The sixty-four petals of the navel and the sixteen outer petals of the secret area are bases for wind-related problems. /278/

d.div: [124] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 39_ba7
[153] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 39b7.

f.d:
de lta bu'i rtsa brgya nga drug ni 'grel chen las/
de ltar na lnga bcu rtsa drug lhag pa'i brgya ni dus kyi 'khor lo'i rtsa lha dang lha mo'i rang bzhin gyis gnas pa byis pa rnams la 'chi ba ster bar byed pa ste/[125] zhes rtsa brgya nga drug po de dag gang zhig dag pas lha dang lha mo'i rang bzhin gyis gnas pa'i rtsar gsungs shing / rtsa de dag thabs mkhas dang bral ba'i byis pa rnams la 'chi ba ster bar byed pa dang / thabs mkhas kyis zin na tshe dang nad med pa dang / der yang ma zad mchog 'grub par yang gsungs te/

Of the 156 channels in these particular aspects, the Great Commentary says:
Therefore the 156 are channels that dwell in the nature of the Kālacakra gods and goddesses and that bring death to ordinary beings.[154] Therefore the 156 channels in purified form are in essence the male and female deities. Those same channels bring death to ordinary beings who lack the skilful means. When possessed of these means, they enjoy not only long life and health but also the achievement of supreme enlightenment.

d.div: [125] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 140_ba3
[154] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 140b3.

f.d:
'grel chen las/
de ltar 'khor lo drug po rnams la [126] rtsa lnga bcu rtsa drug lhag pa'i brgya rnam par gnas pa ni dus kyi 'khor lo'i rtsar rtogs par bya'o/ / 'di rnams nges par 'chi ba ster byed bla ma'i nges pa'i dbang gis tshe dang nad med dag kyang ster/ 'khor lo drug la dus kyi 'khor lo'i rtsa brjod pa rnams bla ma'i man ngag gis bsgoms par gyur na 'chi ba'i 'jigs pa 'phrog ste rnal 'byor pa rnams kyi 'di la ngo mtshar med do/[127] / zhes rtsa brgya lnga bcu rtsa drug po de dus kyi 'khor lo'i pad+ma gdan can gyi lhar bsgom par bya ba 'am/ dag bya'i rtsar rtogs par bya'o/ /

The Great Commentary says:
Within the six cakras the 156 channels are to be understood as channels of Kālacakra. These death-bringing channels, by the power of the guru’s teaching, also bring long life and health. The Kālacakra channels are said to dwell within the six channel wheels, and when meditated upon in accord with the guru’s instruction, the fear of death will be destroyed. To the yogi this is nothing special.[155] Therefore the 156 channels are to be meditated upon as being Kālacakra lotus-seated deities or are to be perceived as channels for purification.

d.div: [126] ma dper drug po rnams lo rtsa zhes byung yang drug po rnams la rtsa zhes bcos/
[127] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 140_na5
[155] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 140a5.

f.d: de ltar rtogs nas pad+ma gdan can gyi lha brgya nga drug tu bsgoms na tshe dang nad med pa ster ro/ / rnal 'byor pa la de tsam ster ba la ngo mtshar med kyi/ de bas lhag pa mchog gi dngos grub sangs rgyas kyang ster ro/ / rtsa de dag dag byed kyi bskyed rim tsam bsgoms pas 'bras bu de rnams 'byung ngam snyam na/ de tsam las mi 'byung yang bskyed rim de dag bsgoms pas rdzogs rim skye ba'i rgyud smin par byas te/ de nas bla ma'i nges pa ste/ bla ma'i man ngag gis sbyor ba yan lag drug gi rdzogs rim bsgoms par gyur na tshe dang / nad med pa gnas skabs kyi 'bras bu dang mchog gi dngos grub thob par 'gyur bar gsungs so/ /

If they are meditated upon as the 156 lotus-seated deities, long life and health will follow. For the yogi this alone is nothing special, for far greater is the attainment of the supreme siddhi of enlightenment that will follow. Will such attainments come about by meditating only upon the generation stage as a purifier of the channels? From this practice alone they will not, but generation-stage meditations ripen the mind for the creation of the completion stage, and then with “certainty from the guru,” meaning instructions of the guru, if one meditates upon the six-branched yoga of the completion stage, the temporary achievements of long life and good health, as well as the permanent attainment of the supreme siddhi, will come about.

yang 'grel chen las/
slar yang drug cu rtsa gnyis lhag pa'i brgya pa de rnams kyi rtsa so so la rlung bcu rab tu rgyu ba dang phung po dang khams bcu'i rang bzhin gyi rnam pa bcur 'gyur ro/ / de ltar thams cad bcus bsgyur ba ni nyi shu lhag pa'i brgya phrag bcu drug gi grangs su 'gyur te rgyu skar nyi shu rtsa bdun gyi chu tshod 'bab pa rnams so/ / de bzhin du dpal ldan rgyu skar gyi dkyil 'khor mchog gi dang po'i sangs rgyas la shes rab dang thabs kyi 'di snyed kyi lha'o/ / rgyu skar gyi dkyil 'khor rgyas pa 'di las 'jig rten kun rdzob kyi bad kan la sogs pa'i khams 'bab pa'i lha rnams 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub bsgrub pa'am rang gi lus bsgrub pa'i slad du 'jam dpal gyis 'byung ba ni 'khor lo drug gi gtso mo rnams so/ / dus kyi 'khor lo'i rtsa bsdoms pa'i nges pa'o/[128] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis rtsa brgya drug cu rtsa gnyis po re re la rlung bcu rgyu ba dang / phung po lnga dang khams lnga ste bcu rgyu bas phye na stong drug brgya nyi shur 'gyur ba sbyong byed rgyu skar gyi dkyil 'khor rtsa rgyud kyi lha pho mo thabs shes kyi dbye bas stong drug brgya nyi shur 'gyur ba'i bskyed rim bsgoms pas 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub zhi sogs dngos su 'grub pa dang / brgyud nas gnas skabs kyi 'bras bu nad med 'chi med dang / mthar thug gi 'bras bu mchog gi dngos grub 'grub par bstan cing /

The Great Commentary states:
Again, in each of the 162 channels flow the ten winds and forms in the nature of the ten elements and aggregates. These in total multiplied by ten become twenty more than 1,600, the number of hours within the twenty-seven constellations. Similarly there are that number of main deities of wisdom and method within the glorious constellation mandala of the Supreme and Original Buddha. From this vast constellation mandala the deities of the nonultimate mundane flowing elements of phlegm and so forth bring about the accomplishments of physical or worldly siddhis. For these attainments Mañjuśrī taught the six main cakras and ascertained the number of Kālacakra channels.[156] /279/ This passage explains that ten winds together with the five aggregates and five elements flow within each of the 162 channels. Therefore externally there are 1,620 Root Tantra gods and goddesses divided into method and wisdom within the glorious mandala of constellations, and that by 1,620 generation-stage meditations, worldly siddhis such as the siddhi of peace, are directly achieved, while indirectly the temporary achievements of health and extended life and the permanent attainment of the supreme siddhi will be attained.

d.div: [128] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 140_ba4
[156] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 140b4.

f.d: rgyu skar gyi dkyil 'khor rgyas pa 'di las zhes sogs kyis ni 'jig rten kun rdzob kyi bskyed rim gyis gong du bshad pa'i bad kan la sogs pa'i khams 'bab pa'i rtsa rnams skyong bar byed pa'i lha rnams bsgom ste/ 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub dngos su sgrub pa'am/ brgyud nas rang gi lus nad med 'chi med dang mchog gi dngos grub bsgrub pa'i slad du bcom ldan 'das 'jam dpal gyis rtsa rgyud las bsdus rgyud du phyung ba'i lha ni rtsa'i gtso bo 'khor lo drug gi rtsa 'dab brgya dang lnga bcu rtsa drug sbyong byed pad+me gdan can gyi lha rnams so/[129] /zhes bstan pa yin no/ /

The part of the passage beginning “From this vast constellation mandala” teaches that in the nonultimate worldly generation stage, one meditates upon the deities that nourish the element channels of phlegm and so forth, as mentioned above, and directly attain worldly siddhi or, indirectly, health and long life, as well as the supreme siddhi. To this end the conqueror Mañjuśrī compiled the Condensed Tantra deities from the Root Tantra, and these deities are the lotus-seated deities that purify the 156 channels of the six main cakras.

d.div: [129] ma dper pad+me gdan can zhes gsal yang 'dir pad+ma zhes bcos/

f.d:
yang / rtsa bsdoms pa'i nges pa'o zhes pa'i de ma thag gi 'grel chen las/
da ni drug ces pa la sogs pas rigs drug gi rtsa bsrung ba gsungs te 'dir lus la gang zhig rtsa drug gi 'khor lo 'gog par brjod pa rnam pa gsum gyi lam la gnas pa ni steng du zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan te g.yon dang g.yas dang dbu ma'i lam la gnas pa dang / 'og tu zla ba dang nyi ma dang me'i dbye bas bshang ba dang gci ba dang khu ba'i lam la gnas pa'o/ / des ni rnal 'byor pa'i lus la bsrung bar bya'o/ / gang gis zhe na bla ma'i nges pa'i dbang gis zhes pa bla ma'i nges pa ni sbyor ba yan lag drug ste des 'chi ba las bsrung bar bya'o/ / gang zhig srog chags rnams la 'chi ba ster ba ni drug po'i de rnams la srog gzhugs so/ / drug po rnams la gal te srog ni rab zhugs gyur na de tshe mi rnams dus thams cad du 'chi bas 'joms par nges te mtha' gcig tu'o/ / drug po 'di rnams kyi nang nas phra mo ni dbus a wa ng+hU tI ste phra mo de la srog ma zhugs par 'gyur na rnal 'byor pa rnams kyis 'chi ba'i yul ni gang du gcod par byed de nges par 'chi ba'i yul gcod par mi byed do/[130] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyi nang nas/ gang zhig srog chags rnams la 'chi ba ster ba ni zhes pa nas/ nges par 'chi ba'i yul gcod par mi byed do zhes pa'i bar gyis steng gi rtsa ro rkyang dbu ma gsum dang 'og gi rtsa bshang gci khu ba'i rtsa gsum ste rtsa drug po de la las rlung zhugs te rgyu ba bkag nas dbu ma a wa ng+hU tI 'ba' zhig tu zhugs par ma gyur ba de srid du 'chi bas 'joms pa bstan cing / 'dir lus la gang zhig ces pa nas/ des ni rnal 'byor pa'i lus la bsrung bar bya'o/ /zhes pa'i bar gyis steng gi ro rkyang dbu ma gsum dang 'og gi bshang gci khu ba'i rtsa gsum la gnas shing rgyu ba'i srog thur gyi rlung dbu mar bkag pa'i sgo nas gnas skabs kyi 'bras bu lus 'chi ba dang nad las bsrung ba dang / mthar thug gi 'bras bu mchog bsgrub par bya'o/ /zhes bstan to/ /

Immediately after the sentence ending “ascertained the number of Kālacakra channels,” the Great Commentary continues:
“Six” and so forth talks of guarding the channels of the six families. It is said that in the body, the cakras of these six channels are to be halted. They are in three pathways. Above, the moon, sun, and Rāhu dwell in the paths of the left, right, and center. Below, divided into moon, sun, and Agni, they dwell in the paths of excrement, urine, and fluid. These the yogi protects in the body. How? “By the instruction of the guru.” The instruction of the guru is the six-branched yoga, and that will bring protection from death. “They bring death to living creatures,” because the winds flow within these six. If the winds flow in the six, at that time and at all times, men will definitely be destroyed by death. Among the six is “the subtle,” or the central avadhūtī. If the winds do not enter “the subtle,” “how will the yogis destroy the realm of death?” Definitely they will not destroy the realm of death.[157] /280/ In this passage the text beginning from the sentence, “They bring death to living creatures” up to the last sentence, “Definitely, they will not destroy the realm of death,” teaches that the winds of karma enter the six channels — the three upper left, right, and central channels and the three lower channels of excrement, urine, and fluid. And as long as their flow is not halted and the winds do not flow solely in the central avadhūtī, then for so long will death continue to destroy. The text from “In the body” until “These the yogi protects in the body” teaches that the life-sustaining wind and downwardly expelling wind, which flow and dwell in the three upper and three lower channels, are halted and brought to the central channel, and that the yogi will accomplish the temporary fruits of protection from physical death and illness as well as the permanent attainment of the supreme siddhi.

d.div: [130] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 140_ba7
[157] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 140b7.

f.d: de yang gang gis bsgrub snyam na/ rtsa'i gtso bo rtsa 'khor drug gi rtsa 'dab brgya nga drug dang rigs drug gi rtsa ro rkyang dbu ma gsum dang bshang gci khu ba'i rtsa gsum ste rtsa brgya dang re gnyis sbyong byed du dmigs pa'i pad+ma gdan can gyi lha brgya nga drug rgyas 'debs kyi lha drug dang bcas pa lta bu sgom pa'i bskyed rim gyis rgyud smin par byas pa'i rjes su bla ma'i nges pa sbyor ba yan lag drug gi lam bsgoms nas rtsa so sor rgyu ba'i rlung dbu mar zhugs pa'i sgo nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde chen drangs te nad dang 'chi ba las srung ba dang mchog sgrub par ni/ gang gis zhe na/ bla ma'i nges pa'i dbang gis zhes pa la bla ma'i nges pa ni sbyor ba yan lag drug ste des 'chi ba las bsrung par bya'o/[131] /zhes pa 'di dag gis bstan to/ /

How is this accomplished? The 156 lotus-seated deities together with the six sealing deities are focused on as being the purifiers of 162 channels comprising the 156 channel petals of the six main cakras together with the right, left, and central channel and the three channels of excrement, urine, and fluid, known collectively as the channels of the six families. This generation-stage practice ripens the continuum, after which the six-branched yoga, as instructed by the guru, is meditated upon. The winds of each channel then enter the central channel to induce the unchanging bliss. The yogi is protected from illness and death and accomplishes the supreme siddhi. This process is taught in the lines, “How? ‘By the instruction of the guru.’” The instruction of the guru is the six-branched yoga and that will bring protection from death.”

d.div: [131] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 141_na2

f.d:
mdor na nang le'i nga gsum pa nas drug cu pa'i phyed kyi bar rgyud rtsa 'grel rnams kyis/
da ni nus ma zhes pa la sogs pas dus kyi 'khor lo'i lha dang lha mo'i grangs gsungs te 'dir 'khor lo drug gi rtsa sna tshogs pa'i rang bzhin rnams lha'i tshogs so/[132] / zhes gsungs pa lta bus mtshon pa'i rtsa 'grel rnams kyis lus kyi rtsa rnams dang rtsa rgyud dang bsdus rgyud kyi lha rnams sbyar nas bstan cing / de ltar sbyar bas ni rtsa de rnams lha dang lha mo de dang de'i ngo bor mos nas sgom pa 'am de rnams sbyong byed du dmigs nas sgom pa'i bskyed rim bstan la

To summarize: from the fifty-third verse through to half of the sixtieth verse of the Inner chapter of the Condensed Tantra, the tantra and commentary teach the application of the deities of the Root Tantra and Condensed Tantra to the channels of the body, as illustrated by the quote:
“Śakti” and so forth teach the number of Kālacakra gods and goddesses. The assembly of deities is in the nature of the various channels of the six cakras.[158] /281/ This meditative application teaches a generation stage in which the channels are visualized as being deities or concentrated on as purifiers.

d.div: [132] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 138_na5
[158] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 138a5.

f.d:
de yang de ltar bsgoms pa'i dgos pa ston pa'i gzhung rim pa gsum ste/
rnal 'byor pa de ni dpal ldan 'jam pa'i rdo rje srid pa'i 'jigs 'joms sangs rgyas skye ba 'di nyid kho na la'o zhes pa ni bsdus pa'i rgyud dang rtsa ba'i rgyud kyi lha 'byung ba'i nges pa'o/[133] / zhes dang / yang gong du drangs pa'i 'chi ba'i 'jigs pa 'phrog ste rnal 'byor pa rnams kyi 'di la ngo mtshar med do/ /zhes dang / yang gong du drangs pa'i/ de ni rnal 'byor pas lus la bsrung bar bya'o/ /zhes sogs so/ /

The purpose of these meditations is taught by three quotes:
The yogi, who is “the glorious Mañjuvajra, destroys the fears of samsara, and this alone creates a buddha.” This determines the arising of deities of the Root Tantra and Condensed Tantra.[159] Two previous quotes run, “the fear of death will be destroyed. To the yogi this is nothing special” and “These the yogi protects in the body.”

d.div: [133] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 139_ba2
[159] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 139b2.

f.d: de yang gzhung de dag gis bstan pa'i dgos pa 'grub pa ni rlung dbu mar bcings pa la rag las shing / de ni dngos su rdzogs rim sbyor ba yan lag drug gi byed pa yin yang de lta bu'i rdzogs rim khyad par can skyed pa la ni nges par bskyed rim gyis rgyud smin par byas pa dgos pas bskyed rim bsgoms pa'i dgos pa'i gtso bo ni srog dbu mar 'ching ba'i rdzogs rim khyad par can skye ba'i rgyu'i gtso bo rgyud smin byed du song ba de yin no/ /

The attainments taught in these quotes depend upon the winds being held in the central channel. This actually occurs during the six-branched yoga of the completion stage. However, to create such a completion stage, the mind must definitely be ripened by the generation stage. Therefore the main purpose of the generation stage is to ripen the mind, which then becomes the main cause of the creation of the special completion stage in which the winds are held within the central channel.

de ltar rgyud 'grel gyi tshig de dag gis bstan pa'i don phyin ci ma log par go na bskyed rim sangs rgyas kyi rgyu ma yin par sgro 'dogs pa'i dwogs pa 'bad med du zlog pa dang / rdzogs rim khyad par can skye ba'i rgyud smin byed du bskyed rim mthar phyin pa nges par sngon du 'gro dgos pa'i bskyed rdzogs kyi go rim la nges pa bskyed pa'i don du rgyud 'grel gyi gzhung de dag gi don gsal bar bshad pa yin no/ / de lta na dwogs pa'i gnas dag sel ba'i tshul cung zad tsam bshad zin to/ /

Therefore, if the words of these quotes from the tantra and commentary are correctly understood, the maligning of the generation stage as not being a cause of enlightenment is easily refuted. A complete generation stage acting as a ripening agent of the mind in order to create the special completion stage must come first in the sequence of generation and completion stages, and it is in order to make this very clear that the meaning of these quotes has been explained. This has been just a brief explanation of how certain doubts arising at this point can be cleared up.

gong du bshad pa ltar 'dod phyir 'dod rnams spros zin pa'i rjes su 'grel chen las/ de ltar ye shes lnga'i bdag nyid ces pa nas/ brtse ba'i don du dbang bskur byin pa'o/[134] /zhes pa'i bar gyis bstan pa ltar rang nyid ye shes lnga'i bdag nyid gtso bo bcom ldan 'das dus kyi 'khor lor gsal ba'i thugs ka nas spros pa'i 'od zer gyis 'gro ba drug na gnas pa'i sems can thams cad bkug nas dkyil 'khor du bcug par bsgoms la/ de nas yang thugs ka'i 'od zer gyis rnam snang sogs de bzhin gshegs pa yab yum rnams bkug nas rang gi snying gar bcug ste de nas rang nyid yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa'i 'dod chags chen po'i mes de bzhin gshegs pa yab yum rnams byang chub kyi sems su zhu bar gyur pa rang gi gsang gnas kyi rdo rje nas spros te byang chub kyi sems des sems can thams cad la dbang bskur bar bsgom par bya'o/ /

The meditations that follow the previously explained emanations of the desire and nondesire goddesses are discussed in the Great Commentary by the lines “In the nature of the five kinds of gnosis” until “are initiated for compassion.”[160] /282/ From the heart of oneself as the conqueror Kālacakra, who has the nature of the five kinds of gnosis, light rays emanate to bring into the mandala every sentient being of the six types. Light rays again emanate from one’s heart to summon Vairocana and the other mother-and-father tathāgatas and to place them in one’s heart. There the fire of desire arising from oneself in mother-and-father embrace melts the mother-and-father tathāgatas into bodhicitta, which then flows to the secret area and from one’s vajra to initiate the sentient beings.

d.div: [134] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 217_ba3_nas 218
[160] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 217b3 to 218a5.

f.d: de nas byang chub kyi sems kyi 'od zer gyis reg pa'i sems can de rnams thams cad zhal gsum pa dang zhal sna tshogs pa'i lha shes rab dang thabs kyi bdag nyid can mchog gi dga' ba'i bde bas gang bar bsgom par bya'o/ / de nas sems can de rnams lus dkyil 'khor gyi 'khor lo'i rang bzhin du gyur par skad cig gis bltas la de nas rim gyis gsal gdab pa ni sems can de rnams kyi phung po lnga gshegs pa lnga dang / khams lnga yum lnga dang / phyi nang gi skye mched bcu gnyis sems dpa' sems ma bcu gnyis dang / las dbang lnga khro bo lnga dang / las dbang gi yul lnga khro mo lnga ste lha sum cu rtsa gnyis su rang rang gi sa bon k+Sha yig la rim pa bzhin a i r-i u l-i lnga thung ngu dang ring po dang / de rnams kyi yon tan gyi yi ge lnga aM dang bcas pa dang / 'phel ba'i yi ge lnga AHdang bcas pa dang / ya Nar bsgyur ba lnga thung ngu dang ring po rnams srog tu zhugs pa rnams las bskyed/ de nas lha de rnams rang rang gi sangs rgyas kyi zhing du gshegs par gyur par sgom pa ni snying rje'i dbang bskur ba ste 'di sangs rgyas pa'i dus kyi mdzad pa dang chos mthun par sgom pa yin gyi gzhi dang sbyor bar mi mdzad do/ /

Every sentient being touched by these bodhicitta light rays is transformed into a deity having three or a varying number of faces. Their essence is method and wisdom, and they are filled with the happiness of the supreme joy. With a brief glance these sentient beings become of the nature of the body-mandala assembly. Then they are focused upon in sequence, which involves the following. To their seed syllable kṣa is added the vowels a, i, ṛ, u, ḷ in both long and short form, the five guṇa letters plus aṃ, the five vṛddhi[161] letters plus āḥ, and the five semivowels in short and long form.[162] These thirty-two syllables merge into their winds and reemerge as thirty-two deities. The five aggregates of these sentient beings become the five tathāgatas, their five elements become the five mothers, the twelve inner and outer sources become the twelve male and female bodhisattvas, their five action faculties become the five wrathful guardians, and the activities of the five action faculties become the fierce females. These deities then travel to their respective buddha realms. This meditation is a compassion initiation and correlates with one’s deeds as a buddha and not to normal existence.

d.div: [161] yon tan, guṇa; vṛddhi, ‘phel ba. Secondary quality and growth or increment; grades of vowel strength. For example, guṇa increases the vowel i to e, and vṛddhi increases it to ai.

f.d:
'di'i 'grel chen las/
'dir gsal byed thams cad kyi tshogs ni k+Sha yig ste shes par byed pa des gang gi ming gi gsal byed dang po gang yin pa des de thams cad bya'o/[135] / zhes gsungs pa'i don ni k+Sha ni gsal byed kyi dang po ka dang tha ma sa'i lus 'gyur gyi Sha brtsegs pa yin la|_de yang gsel byed thog mtha' klag pa yin pas sems can thams cad thun mong du dmigs par byas nas dbang bskur ba na k+Sha yig sa bon du 'gyur ba dang / lha rnams kyi rang ming gi gsal byed dang pos kyang sa bon du 'gyur zhing / gang zag bye brag pa la dbang bskur na yang gang zag gang yin pa de'i ming gi gsal byed dang pos sa bon bya ba'i don yin no/ /

On this meditation the Great Commentary says:
The letter of the whole consonant group is kṣa. Therefore whatever the first consonant of the name, this covers all.[163] This means that the letter kṣa is a combination of the first consonant ka and the last consonant sa, which is changed to the retroflex ṣ. This conjunct covers the whole range of consonants, and therefore, when all sentient beings are visualized and initiated as one, kṣa becomes the seed syllable, and the first consonant of the name of the deities also becomes a seed syllable. /283/ When individual beings are being initiated, the first consonant of that individual’s name becomes the seed syllable.

d.div: [135] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 217_ba7
[163] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 217b7.

f.d: 'o na sa yig Sha yig tu lus 'gyur tshul ji lta bu snyam na/ de ni ka yig las pha rol gyi sa yig Sha'o/ /zhes pa ltar sa yig Sha yig tu bsgyur te ka srog med sa'i steng du drangs pas k+Shar 'gyur ba yin no/ /

How does the letter sa develop into retroflex ṣa? The grammar texts say: “From the letter ka the following sa becomes ṣa.” Therefore sa is changed to ṣa. The letter ka, without its life-giving vowel a, is placed on top of the letter sa to become kṣa.

yang rgyas par byed na/ yang ni rgyas par te zhes sogs gsungs pa ltar sems thams cad rang gi thugs kar bcug pa byang chub kyi sems su zhu ba yum gyi gsang bar spros pa sems can rang rang gi ming gi dang po'i gsal byed sa bon du gyur pa las lha so sor bskyed de/ de nas sngar bzhin du bsgom par bya'o/ / de rnams kyis mngal du lus 'grub pa dang chos mthun pa rnam pa lngas mngon par byang chub pa dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog sku rdo rje bsnyen pa'i yan lag bshad zin to/ /

If this meditation is to be performed more extensively, every sentient being enters one’s heart, where they are melted into bodhicitta. They are brought into the mother’s womb, where the first consonant of every sentient being’s name becomes a seed syllable to be transformed into the deity. The rest of the meditation proceeds as before. This has been an explanation of the branch of the body-vajra approach, a meditation on the sovereign mandala, correlating with the formation of a body inside the womb.
gnyis pa gsung rdo rje nyer sgrub kyi yan lag bshad pa/
23. The Speech Vajra
gnyis pa phyi rol du btsas te las dbang rang gi bya ba la 'jug pa dang chos mthun par las rgyal mchog sgom pa gsung rdo rje nyer sgrub kyi yan lag bshad pa

d.i: The branch of the speech vajra near accomplishment: A meditation on sovereign activities, correlating with birth and the engaging in the activities of the action faculties

f.d: ['di ]la drug /zhu ba la glus skul ba/ de las bzhengs te dkyil 'khor spro ba/ de la ye shes pa dgug gzhug bya ba/ de la rigs kyis rgyas gdab pa/ sku gsung thugs byin gyis brlab pa/ de dag gi rnam dag sgom pa'o/ /
This has six outlines: 1. Arousing by song 2. Arising and mandala generation 3. Summoning the wisdom beings to enter 4. Sealing by family 5. Blessings of body, speech, and mind 6. Purity meditation
dang po [zhu ba la glus skul ba ]ni

de yang mngal gyi zla ba dgu pa rdzogs pa'i dus der mngal gyi lus rdzogs kyang dkyil 'khor lnga'i rlung ngam srog thur sogs rlung bcu nang du bcings te steng 'og gi sgo las 'byung 'jug mi byed par rlung dbu ma'i nang du srog gi dbyug pa ltar gnas pa las zla ba bcu pa srid pa'i yan lag gi zla ba la rlung rnams steng gi sgo la 'byung 'jug byed pa'i sgo nas ngag gi bya ba rdzogs par byed pa dang / rnam par shes pa dbang po so so'i sgo nas phyi rol gyi yul rnams longs spyod pa dang / lo bcu drug dang bcu gnyis kyi mthar khams 'gyur ba'i bde ba la longs spyod pa'i don du nang gi 'byung ba bzhi'i rlung g.yos pa'i sgo nas phyi rol du btsa' ba'i don du bskul ba dang mthun par gtso bo yab yum rnams thig le'i ngo bor zhu ba las 'byung bzhi'i rang bzhin gyi lha mo bzhis bzhengs par bskul ba yin la/

At the end of the nine months in the womb, the development of the body is complete, but the winds of the five mandalas, or the ten winds such as the life-sustaining wind, downwardly expelling wind, /284/ and so forth are still rigidly bound inside the central channel, not entering or leaving through the upper and lower openings. However, in the tenth or “becoming” month, the winds operate through the upper openings, which results in the development of vocal capacity and in the engaging of consciousness with outer objects through the individual senses. At the end of the sixteenth year for males and the twelfth year for females, these beings will be able to engage in the joys of the movements of their elements. It is for these purposes that the winds of the four inner elements stir and encourage birth into the outside world. In correlation with that process, the mother-and-father main deities, who have dissolved and transformed into a drop, are encouraged to emerge by the four goddesses of the four elements.

de la gtso bo yab yum rnams zhu ba'i tshul ni 'grel chen las/
lha la lte ba dang gtsug tor gyi a wa ng+hU tI'i lam du ho yig thog ma tha mar bkod de de nas dpral bar sku rdo rje oM dang mgrin par gsung rdo rje AH dang snying gar thugs rdo rje hUM ste de ltar sku gsung thugs yang dag par byung ba zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan gyi mtshan nyid do/[136] / zhes gsungs pa ltar mngal du sku gsung thugs yang dag par 'byung ba zla nyi sgra gcan gyi rtsa ro rkyang dbu ma gsum dang chos mthun par rang nyid gtso bor gsal ba'i dpral bar oM mgrin par AHthugs kar hUM dang lte ba dang gtsug tor gyi a wa ng+hU tI'i nang du hoH yig re re bkod do/ /

On the dissolution of mother and father, the Great Commentary says:
On the deity the letter ho is inscribed in the avadhūtī path at the navel and crown. At the forehead is the body-vajra oṃ, at the throat the speech-vajra āḥ, and at the heart the mind-vajra hūḥ. This arising of body, speech, and mind are of the characteristics of the moon, sun, and Rāhu.[164] With oneself as the main deity, oṃ appears at the forehead, āḥ at the throat, hūḥ at the heart, and hoḥ[165] appears in the avadhūtī at the navel and crown. This arising of the enlightened body, speech, and mind correlates with the left, right, and center channels of moon, sun, and Rāhu in the womb.

d.div: [136] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 219_na4
[164] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 219a4.
[165] The quote has ho. Kīrti Tsanshap Rinpoché says that at the crown is the short ho and the navel long hoḥ.

f.d:
yang 'grel chen las/
lte bar hoH yig ye shes kyi 'od zer gyis zhu ba bde mnyam pad+ma la ni sku gsung thugs kyi rdo rje ste de ni shes rab chags pas zhu ba khyab bdag rdo rje can yang zhes pa yang yig gis shes rab dang lhan cig ri bong 'dzin pa bzhin du rnam par bltas nas/[137] zhes gsungs pa ltar shes rab yum la snyoms par zhugs pa'i chags pa chen pos lte ba'i hoHyig gtum mo'i me 'bar ba'i ye shes kyi 'od zer gyis rdo rje gsum gyi rang bzhin gtso bo khyab bdag rdo rje 'chang bde mnyam ste bde ba chen po nyams su myong ba'i sgo nas ri bong 'dzin pa zla ba lta bur byang chub sems kyi thig le'i ngo bor zhu bar gyur to/ / gtso bo nyid du ma zad yang yig gis shes rab ma sna tshogs yum nus ma rnams dang bcas pa yang gtso bo dang lhan cig tu zhu bar gyur to/ /

The Great Commentary continues:
By the lights of gnosis of the letter hoḥ at the navel, dissolution and bliss is experienced. On the lotuses the body, speech, and mind vajras are melted by the passion for Prajñā. In the line, “As well as the all-pervading vajra master,” the words “as well as” mean becoming like the moon together with Prajñā.[166] The great passion of the embrace of the wisdom mother causes the caṇḍālī fire of the navel letter hoṃ to blaze. Its rays of gnosis bring about great bliss in the main deity, the all-pervading Vajradhara of the three vajras, who then dissolves into a moonlike bodhicitta drop. This involves not only the main deity, because the words “as well as” indicate that the wisdom woman Viśvamātā and the eight śakti also dissolve with the main deity.

d.div: [137] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 218_na6
[166] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 218a6.

f.d: de ltar zhu ba la glus bskul tshul ni/ de yang glus skul ba po'i lha mo bzhi ni mngal na gnas pa phyi rol du btsa' ba'i phyir skul ba'i dkyil 'khor bzhi'i rlung dang chos mthun/ lha mo bzhi ni dkyil 'khor la 'god pa'i spyan ma mA ma kI gos dkar mo sgrol ma rnams te de rnams kyang rim pa bzhin sa chu me rlung gi khams pa dang / btang snyoms dang dga' ba dang snying rje dang byams pa rnams kyi rang bzhin yin no/ /

The arousing by song from this dissolution is performed as follows. /285/ The four goddesses who perform the song arousal correlate with the winds of the four mandalas that encourage the unborn child’s birth into the outside world. The four goddesses are the mandala goddesses Locanā, Māmakī, Pāṇḍarā, and Tārā. They are of the essence of earth, water, fire, and air and of equanimity, joy, compassion, and love.

de rnams kyis glus bskul bar bya ba'i gzhi gtso bo yab yum zhu ba thig le'i ngo bor gnas pa ni 'grel chen las/
rmi lam gyi gnas skabs su zhugs pa'i rnam par shes pa la sad pa'i gnas skabs kyi don du skul bar byed pa de bzhin du sems can gyi don gyi slad du spyan ma la sogs pa'i lha mo rnams rig par bya'o/[138] / zhes gsungs pa ltar mngal gyi zla ba bdun pa nas rmi lam gyi gnas skabs su zhugs pa'i rnam par shes pa mngal nas btsa' kha ma'i bar dang chos mthun no/ /

The objects to be aroused by their songs are the mother-and-father deities, who have dissolved into a drop. This correlates with the point of birth, up to when the consciousness has been in a dream state since the seventh month. The Great Commentary says:
Like consciousness in a dream being urged into the waking state, the goddesses, Locanā and the others, urge for the sake of sentient beings.[167]

d.div: [138] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 219_na3
[167] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 219a3.

f.d:
de ltar zhu ba las bskul ba'i tshul dngos ni 'grel par drangs pa'i rtsa rgyud kyi tshigs su bcad pa rnams te/ de yang spyan ma gtso bo bcom ldan 'das kyi ye shes rdo rje bskul ba ni/
spyan ma bdag ni 'gro ba'i yum/ / rnal 'byor pa yi rgyu mthun gnas/ / bdag gi dkyil 'khor rang bzhin gyis/ / dus 'khor bzhengs la bdag 'dod mdzod/[139] / ces pa ste/

The actual arousing from dissolution is found in Root Tantra verses quoted in the commentary. Locanā arouses the gnosis vajra of the main conqueror with these words:
I, Locanā, mother of sentient beings, dwell in the “similar to cause” effect within the yogi[168] by the nature of my mandala. Arise, Kālacakra, fulfill my desire.[169]

d.div: [139] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 219_ba2
[168] Generally a karmic effect will be similar to its cause, for instance, virtue as a cause will bring virtue as an effect.
[169] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 219b2.

f.d: de dag gi don ni sa khams dag pa'i ngo bo spyan ma bdag ni skye 'gro rnams la 'phags pa'i ye shes skyed pa'i yum ste spyan ma bdag gi rlung sa rlung rnal 'byor pa rnams kyi lte ba'i ng+hU tIr bcings te mi g.yo bar byas pa las rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu khu ba nor bu nas lte bar byon pa la brten nas byung ba'i bde ba chen por gnas la/ des na ye shes rdo rje'i rang bzhin dus 'khor khyed khu ba'i ngo bo las bzhengs la ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor gyi lha spro ba bdag gi 'dod pa bzhin mdzod cig ces pa'o/ /

The meaning of these words is that I, Locanā, the purified form of the element of earth, am the mother that produces the gnosis of the ārya in sentient beings. My winds of the earth element are held unmoving in the avadhūtī at the yogi’s navel. This brings about an effect similar to the cause, which means that the fluid travels from the jewel to the navel to produce the dwelling in great bliss. Therefore Kālacakra, gnosis vajra, arise from the fluid and fulfill my desires by emanating the deities of the gnosis mandala.

mA ma kIs sku rdo rje bskul ba ni/
mA ma kI bdag sring mo ste/ / rnal 'byor pa yi rnam smin gnas/ / bdag gi dkyil 'khor rang bzhin gyis/ / dus 'khor bzhengs la bdag 'dod mdzod/[140] / ces pa'i don ni chu khams dag pa'i ngo bo mA ma kI bdag rnal 'byor pa bde ba chen po'i skal ba can du ston pas sring mo ste de nyid rnal 'byor pa'i lam gyi gnas skabs su khu ba chu'i khams snying gar byon pa'i bde ba chen po rnam smin gyi 'bras bur gnas so/ / de ni mA ma kI bdag gi khams chu'i rang bzhin gyis snying gar rlung mi g.yo bar bcings pa'i mthu las yin no/ /

Māmakī arouses the body vajra with these words:
I, Māmakī, the sister, dwell in the ripening within the yogi by the nature of my mandala. Arise, Kālacakra, fulfill my desire. [170] /286/ This means that I, Māmakī, the purified form of the element of water, am the sister showing the yogi the fortune of great bliss. I dwell within the ripened result that occurs during the yogi’s path of practice — the great bliss of the fluid reaching the water-element heart center. This bliss arises by my element of water holding the winds unmoving at the heart.

d.div: [140] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 219_ba2
[170] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 219b2.

f.d: des na sku rdo rje'i rang bzhin dus kyi 'khor lo zhu ba las bzhengs te chu'i khams kyi rigs kyi lha spro ba bdag gi 'dod pa bzhin mdzod cig ces pa'o/ /
Therefore Kālacakra, body vajra, arise from the fluid and fulfill my desires by emanating the deities of the water-element family.

gos dkar mos gsung rdo rje bskul ba ni/
gos dkar mo bdag bu mo ste/ / rnal 'byor pa yi skyes bur gnas/ / bdag gi dkyil 'khor rang bzhin gyis/ / dus 'khor bzhengs la bdag 'dod mdzod/[141] / ces pa'i don ni me dag pa'i ngo bo gos dkar mo bdag yon tan 'jo ba'i bu mo ste|_de nyid rnal 'byor pa'i lam gyi gnas skabs su khu ba me'i khams mgrin par byon pa'i bde chen skyes bu byed pa'i 'bras bur gnas so/ / de ni gos dkar mo bdag gi khams me'i rang bzhin gyis mgrin par rlung mi g.yo bar bcings pa'i mthu las yin no/ /

Pāṇḍarā arouses the speech vajra:
I, Pāṇḍarā, the daughter, dwell in the personally created result within the yogi by the nature of my mandala. Arise, Kālacakra, fulfill my desire.[171] I, Pāṇḍarā, the purified form of the fire element, am the daughter, the granter of good qualities, who dwells in the personally created result[172] that is the great bliss arising during the yogi’s path of practice when the fluid travels to the fire-element throat center. This arises because my element of fire holds the winds unmoving at the throat.

d.div: [141] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 219_ba3
[171] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 219b3.
[172] skyes bu byed pa’i ‘bras bu. One of the so-called five results, referring to a result directly produced by the labors of a person. The harvest produced by the toil of the farmer is an example.

f.d: des na gsung rdo rje'i rang bzhin dus kyi 'khor lo khu ba las bzhengs la bdag gi 'dod pa me'i rigs kyi lha spro ba mdzod cig ces pa'o/ /
Therefore, Kālacakra, in the nature of the speech vajra, arise from the fluid and fulfill my desires by emanating the deities of the fire-element family.

sgrol mas thugs rdo rje bskul ba ni/
sgrol ma bdag ni tsha mo ste/ / rnal 'byor pa yi dri bral gnas/ / bdag gi dkyil 'khor rang bzhin gyis/ / dus 'khor bzhengs la bdag 'dod mdzod/[142] / ces pa'i don ni rlung khams dag pa'i ngo bo sgrol ma bdag ni snying gar khu ba bcings pa'i sring mo las byung ba'i tsha mo ste/ de nyid rnal 'byor pa'i lam gyi gnas skabs su khu ba mgrin pa nas spyi bor byon pa'i bde chen dri bral te bral ba'i 'bras bur gnas so/ / de ni sgrol ma bdag gi khams rlung gi rang bzhin gyis spyi bor rlung mi g.yo bar bcings pa'i mthu las yin no/ /

Tārā arouses the mind vajra:
I, Tārā, the niece, dwell in the eradication result within the yogi by the nature of my mandala. Arise, Kālacakra and fulfill my desire.[173] I, Tārā, the purified form of the element of air, am the niece born from the sister that is the fluid held at the heart. I dwell in the eradication result that is the great bliss of the fluid having traveled from the throat to the crown during the yogi’s path of practice. This arises because my element of air holds the airs unmoving at the crown.

d.div: [142] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 219_ba3
[173] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 219b3.

f.d: des na thugs rdo rje'i rang bzhin dus kyi 'khor lo khu ba las bzhengs la bdag gi 'dod pa rlung gi rigs kyi lha rnams spro bar mdzod cig ces pa'o/ /
Therefore Kālacakra, in the nature of the mind vajra, arise from the fluid and fulfill my desires by emanating the deities of the air-element family.

'on te byang sems spyi bor byon pa'i bde chen bral 'bras su ji ltar 'ong snyam na/ de ni tshul gzhan dang mi 'dra bar sangs rgyas pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde chen ngo bo nyid kyi skur bshad pa dang cha 'dra bas skyon med do/ / thun mong du bskul ba ni/
stong pa'i dkyil 'khor nyams myong nas/ / sku gsung thugs kyi dkyil 'khor ni/ / 'gro ba gdon pa'i bsam pa yis/ / 'gro ba'i mgon po spro bar mdzod/[143] / ces gsungs te de'i don ni stong pa nam mkha'i dkyil 'khor gyi rang bzhin khu ba'i ngo bor zhu ba'i bde ba nyams su myong zhing mngon du mdzad nas ni 'gro ba sems can rnams 'khor ba las gdon pa'i bsam pa brtse ba chen po sngon du 'gro ba yis sku gsung thugs kyi dkyil 'khor gyi lha tshogs rnams ni 'gro ba sdug bsngal las skyob pa'i mgon po khyod kyis spro bar mdzod cig ces glus bskul lo/ /

How can the great bliss arising from the bodhicitta arriving at the crown be an eradication result? This differs from the other three and is similar to the unchanging bliss of the Buddha being equated with the nature body. Therefore there is no fault here.[174] In unison all four goddesses sing:
From the experiences of the emptiness mandala, with the thought to save sentient beings, great protector of sentient beings, emanate the mandalas of body, speech, and mind.[175] /287/ This means that “You, mighty protector who shields sentient beings from suffering, with the greatly compassionate thought of bringing sentient beings out of samsara, emanate the deity assembly of the body, speech, and mind mandalas from your accomplishment and experience of the emptiness, or space, mandala that is the bliss of dissolution into fluid.”

d.div: [143] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 219_ba4

[174] An eradication result is the negation of a phenomenon and is therefore not created by cause. Strictly speaking, then, it is not a result, as great bliss is, for example. Similarly, of the four bodies of a buddha, the nature body (ngo bo nyid kyi sku, svabhāvikakāya) is also noncreated but is included as if it were a product of cause.
[175] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 219b4.

f.d:
glus bskul gyi skabs 'dir 'grel chen las/
'dir bskul ba rnam pa gnyis te gcig ni srog rdzogs pa'i slad du yin la gnyis pa ni lo bcu drug gi mthar bde ba rdzogs pa'i slad du'o/[144] / zhes gsungs pa'i don la mkhas (rje ku mAr/)pa dag 'di skad gsung ste/
'dir glus bskul ba gnyis te gcig srog rdzogs pa'i ched du yin pa dang / gcig bde ba rdzogs pa'i ched du yin par gsungs pas thig le'i rnal 'byor gyi mthar yang glus bskul ba dgos par mngon mod kyi sngon gyi bla ma rnams bskul ba dang po 'di las mi mdzad do/[145] / zhes gsung yang /

On this section of arousal by song, the Great Commentary says:
The arousing is of two kinds. The first is to complete the winds; the second is for the completion of the joy at the end of the sixteenth year.[176] On the meaning of this quote, scholars (such as Kumāra)[177] have said:
Two kinds of arousal are taught: one for the completion of the winds, one for the completion of joy. Therefore it is evident that there also has to be a song arousal at the end of the drop yoga, but the lamas of the past only posited it once.

'dir bskul ba rnam pa gnyis te zhes sogs kyi don ni gzhi la bskul ba rnam pa gnyis las/ dang po ni srog phyi rol du rgyu ba rdzogs pa'i slad du mngal na gnas pa mngal gyi phyi rol du bskul ba dang / bskul ba gnyis pa ni mngal nas btsas te lo bcu drug lon pa'i mthar khams 'pho ba'i bde ba rdzogs pa'i slad du khu ba dbang po'i sgor bskul ba yin la/ gzhi'i bskul ba dang po dang chos mthun par zhu ba glus bskul dang / gzhi'i bskul ba gnyis pa dang chos mthun par dga' ba la dmigs pa'i thig le dang phra mo'i rnal 'byor sgom pa yin zhing / de ltar sgom pa'i tshe gtso bo zhu ba med pas zhu ba glus bskul mi dgos pa la dgongs nas sngon gyi bla ma rnams bskul ba dang po 'di las mi mdzad pa yin no/ /

The meaning, however, of the quote beginning “The arousing is of two kinds” is that there are two ordinary bases to which the arousal is directed. The first is the sentient being inside the womb being aroused to emerge into the outside world in order to complete the development of the winds flowing externally. The second is the fluid, which is aroused to travel to the opening of the organ in order to complete the development of the joy of element emission at the end of the sixteenth year of life. The dissolution song arousal correlates with the first. The subtle and drop yoga meditations that focus on joy correlate with the second kind of arousal, during which there is no dissolution of the main deity, and so arousal from dissolution by song is not necessary. It is with this in mind that lamas of the past only posited it once. /288/

d.div: [144] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 219_na5_129_ma dper pad+me gdan can zhes gsal yang 'dir pad+ma zhes bcos/ na5_bar/

[145] 'di dang skabs gzhan du yig chung du rje ku mA ra zhes byung ba ni phal cher 'gos lo tsA ba gzhon nu dpal la go dgos par snang la/ des mdzad pa'i dus 'khor gyi dka' 'grel zhig yod snang bas de'i bzhed pa bkod pa min nam snyam yang dpyad/
[176] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 219a5.

[177] As noted previously, it is likely that Kumāra here refers to Kumāraśrī, or Shönu Pal Gö Lotsāwa (1392–1481), rather than to Rendawa as it has done previously, because the quote was written by a proponent of Kālacakra, and Rendawa opposed the tantra.

f.d: gnyis pa de las bzhengs te dkyil 'khor spro ba
['di ]la gnyis/ zhu ba las gtso bo yab yum rnams kyi skur bzhengs pa dang / de nas dkyil 'khor spro ba'o/ /
This is under two headings: 1. Arising from the fluid into the forms of the main mother and father 2. Emanation of the mandalas
dang po [zhu ba las gtso bo yab yum rnams kyi skur bzhengs pa ]ni/

d.i: Arising from the fluid into the forms of the main mother and father

f.d: de ltar lha mo bzhis glus bskul ba la brten nas/ stong pa nyid la rab tu zhugs ba'i bcom ldan 'das rab tu sad par gyur te 'gro ba mtha' dag sgyu ma lta bur gzigs nas khu ba zla ba zhu ba de las hUM yig sngon po dang / de las rdo rje snon po rtse lnga pa dang / de yongs su gyur pa las gtso bo dus kyi 'khor lo'i rnam pa can mi bskyod pa'i ngo bor gyur pa de ltar yin pa mtshon pa'i don du mi bskyod pa'i cod pan can la rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma sna tshogs yum gyis [146]zhes gsungs pa ltar rdo rje dbyings phyug ma'i ngo bor gyur pa'i sna tshogs yum gyis 'khyud pa dang / nus ma rnams bskyed pa de nas lha gzhan rnams spro ba yin no/ /

The conqueror, well immersed in emptiness, is awoken by the four goddesses’ melodic arousal and sees all beings as like illusions. From the melted moon fluid arises a blue hūḥ, from that a five-pointed blue vajra, and from that arises the main deity in the form of Kālacakra, in essence Akṣobhya. To indicate that, he wears the crown of Akṣobhya and is embraced by Vajradhātvīśvarī Viśvamātā. As this passage from the Great Commentary indicates, the main deity embraced by Viśvamātā, who is in essence Vajradhātvīśvarī, is generated together with the eight śakti and is followed by the other deities.

d.div: [146] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 219_ba5

f.d:
de yang dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi gtso bo rgyu rdo rje 'dzin pa ngo bo mi bskyod pa dang / las rgyal mchog gi gtso bo rdo rje 'dzin pa rdo rje sems dpar kha cig bzhed kyang / rgyu rdo rje 'dzin pa ngo bo rdor sems yin par rgyud 'grel las gsungs pa gong du drangs zin cing / 'bras bu rdo rje 'dzin pa ngo bo mi bskyod pa yin pa dang / 'di'i yum ngo bo rdo rje dbyings phyug ma yin pa ni gtso bo yab yum dam tshig pa la ye shes pa ro mnyam pa 'chad pa'i 'grel chen las/
'di la bskyed pa'i rnal 'byor gyi bskyed pa'i rim pa dag la rnam par shes pa ni nam mkha' dang bcas zhes pa rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma dang lhan cig snying po'i pad+mar zhes pa bde ba chen po la me'i steng du ste zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan nam dus me'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng du dam tshig sems dpa' dang ye shes sems dpa' ro mnyam pa nyid du 'gyur ro/[147] / zhes gsungs pa'i rnam par shes pa ni zhes pa rnam shes kyi ngo bo mi bskyod pa la dgongs pa yin no/ /

Some assert the causal Vajradhara main deity of the sovereign mandala to be in essence Akṣobhya and the Vajradhara of the sovereign activities to be of the nature of Vajrasattva. However, as evidenced by a previous quote, the tantra and commentary assert the causal Vajradhara to be of the nature of Vajrasattva.[178] Moreover that resultant Vajradhara is in the nature of Akṣobhya, and that his consort is in the nature of Vajradhātvīśvarī can be understood from the Great Commentary when it explains that the main deity mother-and-father samaya beings are of one taste with the gnosis beings:
Here, in the generation yoga, in the stages of generation, “consciousness is together with space,” meaning together with Vajradhātvīśvarī, “within the central lotus,” meaning the great bliss, and upon fire, moon, sun, Rāhu or Kālāgni, the samaya beings and the gnosis beings come to be of one taste.[179] In this passage, “consciousness” refers to Akṣobhya, who is in the nature of consciousness.

d.div: [147] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 221_na4_tshig sna cung mi mthun/
[178] “Together with mudrā, the complete Vajrasattva.”
[179] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 221a4.

f.d: de lta na'ang gzhan rigs la 'khyud dgos par gsungs pa dang 'gal ba'i skyon spong ba'i tshul ni gong du bshad zin pa ltar ro/ / de ltar glus bskul ba las gtso bo yab yum rnams kyi skur bzhengs pa ni sbyang gzhi mngal na gnas pa phyi rol du bcas pa dang chos mthun no/ /

Any contradiction arising from the statement that this embrace has to be with different families can be resolved as previously explained.[180] /289/ Arising from the arousal by song into the forms of the main mother and father correlates with birth from the womb as a basis of purification.

d.div: [180] In a previous section, when discussing method and wisdom deities, it says: “It is taught that consciousness-aggregate Akṣobhya, whose nature is the main deity, and the space-element Vajradhātvīśvarī are mother-and-father method and wisdom. Such a statement is made in terms of pervading consciousness and gnosis being fused together within the being of the main deity and are not statements made on the basis of individual method and wisdom.”

f.d: gnyis pa de nas dkyil 'khor ba spro ba ni/

'di la kha cig_ye shes dang thugs dang gsung dang sku'i dkyil 'khor rnams spros te lha so so la zhugs par bsam par bya'o/ /zhes lha rnams yum gyi pad+ma las spros nas dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi skabs su spros pa'i lha rten gyi dkyil 'khor la gnas pa rnams la zhugs par sgom pa yin par bzhed do/ / de ni 'grel chen las/ dam tshig gi dkyil 'khor gyi don du [148] zhes las rgyal mchog gi lha spros pa rnams dam tshig gi dkyil 'khor du gsungs pa dang 'gal zhing /

Some say, “Visualize that they enter their respective deities of the emanated gnosis, mind, speech, and body mandalas.” They maintain that the deities are emanated from the mother’s lotus and visualized as entering the deities dwelling on the base mandala who were emanated during the sovereign-mandala practice. That contradicts the Great Commentary quote beginning, “For the sake of the samaya mandala,”[181] which states that the deity emanation in the sovereign activities is to the samaya mandala.

d.div: [148] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 220_na1
[181] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 220a1.

f.d:
gzhan yang 'grel chen las/
de ltar dkyil 'khor rab tu spro ba dag kyang ngo / / kyang yig gis sngon bzhin zhes pa'o/[149] / zhes gsungs pa 'dis kyang skabs 'di'i lha spro tshul dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog dang 'dra bar gsungs pas gnod do/ /

Furthermore the Great Commentary states:
In the phrase “again the mandalas are manifested,” the word again means “as before.”[182] This quote also damages the above assertion, because it says that the deity emanation here is similar to that of the sovereign mandala.

d.div: [149] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 220_na3
[182] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 220a3.

f.d:
des na gtso bo yab yum nus ma rnams dang bcas pa dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi skabs su bskyed zin pa'i rjes su/ 'grel chen las/
shes rab dang thabs snyoms par zhugs pas dkyil 'khor lnga'i rang bzhin gyi sangs rgyas nam mkhar gnas pa phung po dang khams dang skye mched la sogs pa'i rang bzhin gyis dam tshig gi dkyil 'khor gyi don du rang gi lus la bcug ste shes rab kyi pad+ma_ra sngags kyi rang bzhin yi ge so so rnams so/[150] / zhes gsungs pa ltar gtso bo yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa'i dga' ba'i sgras dkyil 'khor lnga'i rang bzhin gyi sangs rgyas gshegs pa gshegs ma nas 'dod ma dang phyir 'dod ma rnams kyi bar sngar spros pa dkyil 'khor la 'khod pa thams cad spyan drangs te rang gi steng gi nam mkha' la bzhugs pa rnams phung khams skye mched la sogs pa'i rang bzhin gyi dam tshig gi dkyil 'khor gyi don du rang gi lus la zhugs pa chags pa chen po'i mes zhu ba yum gyi pad+mar spros pa rnams lha so so'i sa bon dang / de las lha so so'i phyag mtshan dang / de las lha so so bskyed pa yum gyi pad+ma las spros te rten gyi dkyil 'khor la 'god pa dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi skabs ji lta ba bzhin byed dgos pa ni 'grel chen las/ de nas pad+ma la sngon bzhin du [151] zhes sogs kyis gsal bar bstan pa yin no/ /

Therefore, after the main deity father and mother plus the śakti have been created during the sovereign-mandala meditations:
By the power of method-and-wisdom union, the five mandala buddhas come to the space above and enter one’s body for the sake of the samaya mandala possessing the nature of the aggregates, elements, sources, and so forth. They come to the lotus of Prajñā as mantras in the form of individual letters.[183] As this passage indicates, the sound of bliss that emanates from the main deity mother and father in union calls the male and female tathāgatas of the nature of the five mandalas, and all the other deities placed in the previously emanated mandala up to the desire and nondesire goddesses, into the space above, and for the purpose of a samaya mandala, which is in the nature of the aggregates, elements, and sources, they enter one’s body, where they are melted by the fire of great bliss and sent to the mother’s lotus. There in the form of the individual letters of the deities, they transform into the symbols of the different deities and then to the deities themselves, and are sent from the mother’s lotus to the base mandala. In the quote beginning, “Then in the lotus, as before,”[184] the Great Commentary confirms that this has to be done as it was during the sovereign-mandala practice /290/.

d.div: [150] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 220_na1
[151] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 220_na2
[183] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 220a1.
[184] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 220a2.

f.d:
de ltar las rgyal mchog gi 'khor gyi lha spro ba ni byis pa mngal nas btsas ma thag phru ma'i chos gos 'dzin pa'i lus rdzogs pa'i rnam par phyi rol du gsal bar sgrub ste ngu zhing khams lnga'i rlung ngam srog 'dzin sogs rlung bcu phyir spro ba dang chos mthun par 'grel chen las gsal bar gsungs te/ de yang 'grel chen las/
sngar bzhin du slar yang shes rab grabs kyi bdag nyid thugs dang gsung dang sku'i chos kyi dkyil 'khor rab tu spro bar bya ste skyes pa'i byis pa rab tu sad pa ngu bar byed pa'i phyir ro [152] zhes dang / yang /
de ltar dkyil 'khor rab tu spro ba dag byung ngo / / kyang yig gis sngon bzhin zhes pa'o/ / byis pa mngal nas 'byung ba'i dus su srog la sogs pa'i rlung bcu skye'o/ / slob ma rnams dkyil 'khor du 'jug pa'i dus su me tog 'thor ro/ / gcer bu mngal gyi phru ma'i gos 'dzin pa byis pa zhes pa'i rnam par dag pas lha'i dam tshig gi dkyil 'khor rdzogs pa'o/[153] / zhes sogs gsungs pa rnams kyis gsal bar bstan pa yin no/ /

Therefore deity emanation within the sovereign activities correlates with the moment immediately after birth when the fully developed body, still wrapped in the “clothes of the placenta,” clearly exists in the outside world. It starts to cry, and the ten winds, or winds of its five elements, engage with the outside. This is confirmed by the Great Commentary:
As before, again the mandalas of mind, speech, and form, in the nature of method and wisdom, are emanated, and the newborn child awakens and cries.[185] Also:
In the phrase “again the mandalas are manifested” the word again means “as before.” When the child emerges from the womb, the ten winds, such as the life-sustaining and so forth, are born. When the disciples enter the mandala, flowers are scattered. The purification of “the naked child in the clothes of the placenta” is the completion of the mandala of the samaya deities.[186]

[153] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 220_na3

f.d: gzhan yang / nang du dkyil 'khor lnga 'bab pa'i don dang zhes pa 'dis kyang chos mthun gyi yul dang sbyang gzhi bstan pa yin no/ /
Furthermore the lines beginning “Inside, the five mandalas flow” also teach the objects of correlation and the bases for purification.
gsum pa de la ye shes pa dgug gzhug bya ba ni/

d.i: Summoning the wisdom beings to enter

f.d: 'dod ma dang phyir 'dod ma spros zin pa'i rjes su ye shes pa dgug gzhug bya ste/ de la ye shes pa dgug pa ni rdo rje shugs kyis byed la/ de yang rdo rje shugs ni/ dbu ma'i srog rnam par dag pas rdo rje shugs zhes gsungs pa ltar ye shes kyi rlung dag pa'i ngo bo yin la/ de ni/ 'od zer sngon po zhes sogs sgrub le'i 'grel chen nas bshad pa'i sku mdog zhal phyag sogs kyi rnam pa can du/ hUM yig rdo rje'i sprul pa [154] zhes gsungs pa ltar hUM las rdo rje dang de las skyed cing de yang / shes rab dang thabs las rab tu byung ba [155]zhes gsungs pa ltar shes rab yum dang thabs yab mnyam par sbyar ba las byung ba yum gyi pad+ma las spro ba yin la/

After the desire and nondesire goddesses have been emanated, the wisdom beings are summoned. This is done by Vajravega, who is in essence the purified gnosis wind, as indicated by the line “The pure winds of the central channel, Vajravega.” His color and number of faces and hands are as described in the lines “of blue light” and so forth in the Methods of Accomplishment chapter of the Great Commentary. He emerges in that form from a vajra, which in turn has emerged from hūḥ, as indicated by the line “an emanation of hūḥ and vajra.”[187] “Arising from wisdom and method”[188] indicates that he arises from the wisdom mother and the method father in embrace and is emanated from the lotus of the mother.

d.div: [154] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 220_ba4
[155] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 220_ba3
[187] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 220b4.
[188] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 220b3.

f.d: yang 'grel chen las/ 'dir byis pa skyes pa'i dbu ma'i srog 'byung ba ni 'od zer sngon po ste de'i 'byung bas dbang po rnams rab tu sad cing phyi rol gyi yul rnams la rnam par shes pa drug po rnams 'jug pa ni nang du'o/[156] / zhes gsungs pa ltar rdo rje shugs spro ba ni byis pa skyes ma thag dbu ma nas ye shes kyi rlung drug rkang bcas rgyus te de rgyus pa'i dbang gis dbang po rnams sad nas phyi rol gyi yul rnams la rnam shes drug 'jug pa dang chos mthun no/ /

On this the Great Commentary says:
Here the winds of the central channel within the newborn child arise. They are of blue light. Their arising awakens the sense organs, and the six consciousnesses engage with external phenomena. This is the inner.[189] /291/ Therefore the emanation of Vajravega correlates with the time when the fifty-six and a quarter gnosis winds in the central channel of the newborn child begin to flow. This awakens the sense organs, and the six consciousnesses engage with external objects.

d.div: [156] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 220_ba1
[189] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 220b1.

f.d:
de ltar spros pa'i rdo rje shugs de yang [157] 'grel chen las/
de nas lte ba'i pad+ma las phyi rol du 'byung ba'i srog gis phyi rol gyi dngos po rnams bkug nas slar yang ldog go/ / de'i phyir rnam par dag pa dri med 'od zer 'phro ba ye shes 'khor lo'i dbang phyug nges par lte bar rdo rje lcags kyus bsnun byas shing phyag nyi shu rtsa bzhi po rnams rang gi rdo rje sbrul gyi zhags pa dag gis bcings nas rang gi mtshon cha rnams kyis 'jigs par byas te/ de ltar ye shes kyi 'khor lo bsgrub pa byas shing dngos po'i mtshan nyid sna tshogs pa'i 'khor lo mtha' dag bskyod par byas nas slar yang rang gi gnas su 'gro'o/[158] / zhes gsungs pa ltar de ltar spros pa'i rdo rje shugs des 'khor lo'i dbang phyug ye shes pa'i gtso bo dus kyi 'khor lo de'i lte bar rdo rje lcags kyus bsnun cing / ye shes pa'i phyag nyi shu rtsa bzhi po rnams rdo rje shugs rang gi rdo rje sbrul gyi zhags pas bcings nas rdo rje shugs rang gi mtshon cha lhag ma rnams kyis 'jig par byas te 'khor lo'i dbang phyug dgug pa dang dkyil 'khor pa'i lha sna tshogs rnams spyan drang bar byas nas rdo rje shugs rang gi gnas gtso bo'i thugs kar thim par bsam pa yin no/ / 'di ni byis pa btsas pa'i tshe lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi pad+ma las phyi rol du 'byung ba'i srog rlung gis rnam shes rnams rang rang gi yul 'dzin byed du bkug nas slar yang srog lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi pad+mar ldog pa dang chos mthun no/ /

Concerning the emanation of Vajravega the Great Commentary says:
Then from the lotus of the navel the winds emerge, summon external phenomena, and then return. Therefore the pure, stainless light goes forth and decisively pierces with vajra hook the navel of the mighty one of the wisdom assembly and binds his twenty-four arms with a vajra-serpent[190] lasso. He frightens him with his weapons, gathers the wisdom assembly, moves the entire assembly of various phenomena, and then returns home.[191] As this passage says, this is a meditation in which the manifested Vajravega pierces with his vajra hook the navel of Kālacakra, the mighty one of the wisdom assembly and the principal deity of the wisdom beings. He binds Kālacakra’s twenty-four arms with his vajra-serpent lasso, summons the mighty one of the wisdom assembly by terrifying him with his other weapons, invokes the various deities of the mandala, and then returns to absorb into his abode within the heart of the main deity. This correlates with the time of birth when the life-sustaining wind emerges from the lotus of the navel cakra to summon the consciousnesses to their respective objects and then returns to the lotus of the navel cakra.

d.div: [157] ma dper des yang zhes byed sgra byung yang de yang zhes par bcos/
[158] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 220_ba6
[190] The text and the new critical edition has sprul (emanation), which may be a misspelling of sbrul (snake). The Vimalaprabhā has klu (nāga), and the Condensed Tantra has gdengs chen (nāga).
[191] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 220b6.

f.d:
'grel chen las/ de ltar ye shes kyi 'khor lo yang dag par mchod de/[159] zhes gsungs pa ltar de ltar spyan drangs pa'i ye shes pa'i 'khor lo la mchod nas/ yang 'grel chen las/
de nas gzhugs na kun gzhi rnam par shes pa dang mig gi dbang po las skyes pa mig gi rnam par shes pa rmugs byed dozhes pa nas/
ro mnyam pa nyid du gyur par bsgom par bya'o [160] zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis bstan pa ltar rdo rje shugs kyis ye shes pa bkug pa'i rjes su byis pa'i mig gi rnam shes dang / lus kyi rnam shes dang / lce'i rnam shes dang / sna'i rnam shes rnams dang rim pa bzhin chos mthun pa'i khro bo rmugs byed dang / rengs byed dang / khengs byed dang / shin tu stobs rnams kyis rim pa bzhin ye shes pa rnams dam tshig pa rnams la gzhug pa dang / bcing ba dang / mnyes pa dang / ro mnyam par byed par bsgom zhing / de ltar sgom pa'i tshe dgug pa la dzaHyig dang / gzhug pa la hUM yig dang bcing ba la baM yig dang / mnyes pa la hoH yig dang / ro mnyam pa la hi yig rnams drag tu brjod cing de'i tshe phyag rgya ni rim pa bzhin rdo rje lcags kyu dang / rdo rje dang / rdo rje zhags pa dang / rdo rje dril bu dang rdo rje dbyug pa'i phyag rgya rnams bya'o/ /

The Great Commentary says, “The wisdom assembly is well served,”[192] meaning that offerings are made to the invited assembly of wisdom beings. It continues:
Concerning the absorption, the consciousness of sight born from the foundation consciousness and the sense organ of sight is Jambhaka. And so on until:
Meditate upon them as being of one taste.[193] /292/ This states that after Vajravega has summoned the wisdom beings, one meditates that the wrathful protectors, Jambhaka, Stambhaka, Māṇaka, and Atibala, correlating respectively with the eye, body, tongue, and nose consciousnesses of the newborn, bring about the absorption, binding, delight, and one-taste union, respectively, of the wisdom and samaya beings. At the same time, when summoning one utters jaḥ, when absorbing one utters hūḥ, when binding one utters baṃ, when delighting one utters hoṃ, and when becoming of one taste one utters the syllable hi. These are to be said forcefully. The mudrās are vajra hook, vajra, vajra noose, vajra and bell, and vajra staff respectively.

d.div: [159] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 221_na3
[160] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 221_na1
[192] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 221a3.
[193] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 221a1.

f.d: de ltar ye shes pa dang dam tshig pa re re nas ro mnyam du sgom pa ni 'grel chen las/ 'dir bskyed pa'i rnal 'byor gyi zhes pa nas/ snying ga'i pad+ma la'o [161] zhes pa ni nges pa'o/ / zhes pa'i bar gyis thugs dkyil gyi ro mnyam gsal bar bstan pa ltar dang / de'i zhar byung du sku dkyil gyi khro bo rnams kyi ro mnyam dngos su gsungs nas gsung dkyil dang sku dkyil gyi lha gzhan rnams kyi ro mnyam rtsa bar gsungs pa go slar mdzad do/ /

Concerning the individual wisdom beings and samaya beings becoming of one taste, the Great Commentary explains the one-taste merging as it occurs in the mind mandala from the line beginning “Here, in the yoga of generation” until “on the central lotus.”[194] The merging of the body-mandala wrathful protectors is described incidentally. The explanation of the merging of the remaining deities of the body and speech mandalas is left uncommented on as found in the Condensed Tantra, because it is deemed “easy to understand.”

d.div: [161] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 221_na4
[194] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 221a4.
