f.d: de yang 'grel par dngos su gsungs pa rnams ni bklags pa nyid kyis shes la/ go slar gsungs pa rnams kyi ro mnyam mdor bsdus te bshad na rgyud las/ gsung las skyes pa'i dkyil 'khor ni zhes pa nas/ sa yi dkyil 'khor la gnas zla nyi dag kyang bsgom par bya/[162] /zhes pa'i bar gyis gsung dkyil gyi lha mo rnams kyi ro mnyam dang sa'i 'khor yug la 'char ba'i zla nyi dam tshig pa la ye shes pa ro mnyam pa'i bar bstan pa'i gsung gi rnal 'byor ma'i gtso mo yum ni shar du tsA muN+TI la lha'i dbang pos 'khyud pa dang / de bzhin du me mtshams su khyab 'jug ma la tshangs pas 'khyud pa dang / lhor phag mo la drag po ste dbang phyug gis 'khyud pa dang / bden bral du gdong drug ma la tshogs kyi bdag pos 'khyud pa dang / nub tu dbang mo la bden bral te srin pos 'khyud pa dang / rlung du tshangs ma la khyab 'jug gis 'khyud pa dang / byang du drag mo'am dbang phyug ma la gshin rjes 'khyud pa dang / dbang ldan du dpal mo la gdong drug pas 'khyud pa'o/ / de rnams kyi gtso 'khor rnams dam tshig pa la ye shes pa ro mnyam pa dang /

Those merging processes that are actually taught in the commentary can be understood by reading them, but the one-taste process as described in the “easy to understand” sections of the Condensed Tantra will be explained very briefly. The text from “The mandala born from speech” until “meditate also on the moon and sun on the earth mandala”[195] describes the one-taste merging from the remaining speech-mandala goddesses up to the wisdom and samaya merging of the sun and moon that rise over the land surrounding the mandala. Within this, of the main mother speech yoginīs, Cāmuṇḍi[196] in the east is embraced by Indra; Vaiṣṇavī in the northeast is embraced by Brahmā; Vārāhī in the south is embraced by Rudra, or Īśvara; Ṣaṇmukhī in the southwest is embraced by Gaṇapati; Aindrī in the west embraced by Nairtya, or Rakṣā; Brahmāṇī in the northwest is embraced by Viṣṇu; Rudrī, or Īśvarī, in the north is embraced by Yama; and Lakṣmī in the northeast is embraced by Ṣaṇmukha. /293/ Together with their entourage deities, they all undergo the one-taste merging of samaya and wisdom beings.

d.div: [162] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 222_na7
[195] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 222a7.
[196] Or Carcikā.

f.d: de bzhin du tshes lha rnams kyi gtso bo yab yum ni shar sgo'i g.yas su pad+ma_'i lte bar lha min bdag po srin po la srin mos 'khyud pa dang / me mtshams su rlung lha la rab gtum mas 'khyud pa dang / lho sgo'i g.yas su me lha la chu lha mos 'khyud pa dang / bden bral du gdong drug pa la dpal mos 'khyud pa dang / nub sgo'i g.yas su lha'i dbang po la rlung lha mos 'khyud pa dang / rlung du tshangs pa la glog mas 'khyud pa dang / byang sgo'i g.yas su rgya mtsho ste chu lha la phag mos 'khyud pa dang / dbang ldan du tshogs kyi dbang po tshogs bdag la gzhon nu gdong drug mas 'khyud pa dang / byang sgo'i g.yon du drag po dbang phyug la ri sras mas 'khyud pa dang / lho sgo'i g.yon du gshin rje la gshin rje mas 'khyud pa dang / shar sgo'i g.yon du khyab 'jug la dpal mos 'khyud pa dang / nub sgo'i g.yon du gnod sbyin la gnod sbyin gyi dbang mos 'khyud pa'o/ / de rnams gtso 'khor dam tshig pa rnams la ye shes pa ro mnyam pa dang /

A similar process occurs with the main mother-and-father lunar-day deities. To the right of the east gate in the center of the lotus, Rakṣā the asura king is embraced by Rakṣī. In the southeast Vāyu is embraced by Pracaṇḍī. To the right of the south gate, Agni is embraced by Varuṇī. In the southwest Ṣaṇmukha is embraced by Lakṣmī. To the right of the western gate, Devendra[197] is embraced by Vāyudevī. In the northwest Brahmā is embraced by Vidyutī. To the right of the northern gate, Samudra, or Varuṇa, is embraced by Vārāhī. In the northeast Gaṇapati is embraced by Ṣaṇmukhī. To the left of the north gate, Rudra, or Īśvara, is embraced by Gaurī. To the left of the south gate, Yama is embraced by Yamārī. To the left of the east gate, Viṣṇu is embraced by Lakṣmī. To the left of the west gate, Yakṣa is embraced by Yakṣiṇī. Wisdom beings merge into these deities and their entourage and become of one taste.

d.div: [197] Indra, or Śakra.

f.d: sku dkyil gyi rtsig pa'i phyi rol gyi phyogs bzhi'i stegs bu dag la klu rnams gnas so/ / de yang ji ltar gnas na shar gyi stegs bu la rlung gi dkyil 'khor gyi steng du pad+ma dang stobs rgyu gnyis gnas shing / de bzhin du lhor me'i dkyil 'khor la nor rgyas kyi bu dang dung skyong gnas pa dang / byang du chu'i dkyil 'khor la rigs ldan dang mtha' yas gnas pa dang / nub tu sa'i dkyil 'khor la 'jog po dang pad+ma chen po gnas so/ /

Outside the walls of the body mandala, on platforms in the four directions, are the nāgas. On the eastern platform, on air mandalas, stand Padma and Karkoṭaka. In the south, on fire mandalas, stand Vāsuki and Śaṅkhapāla. In the north, on water mandalas, stand Kulika and Ananta. In the west on earth mandalas stand Takṣaka and Mahāpadma.

yang de bzhin du rab gtum ma rnams kyang dur khrod kyi sa la gnas te rlung gi dkyil 'khor la gnas pa'i shar gyi dur khrod rtse mos 'bigs par khyi gdong ma dang / lho'i dur khrod sreg par phag gdong ma dang / byang du rul ba dang bcas pa'i dur khrod du stag gdong ma dang / nub tu rnag gi dur khrod du ce spyang gdong ma dang / me mtshams su lhag ma can gyi dur khrod du bya rog gdong ma dang / bden bral du mi bzad pa'i g.yul gyi dur khrod du bya rgod gdong ma dang / rlung du sbrul gyi zos pa'i dur khrod du bya khyung gdong ma dang / dbang ldan du byis pa shi ba'i dur khrod du 'ug gdong ma gnas pa ste/ de yang yab klu rnams la yum rab gtum ma rnams 'khyud pa dang / yum rab gtum ma rnams la'ang yab klu rnams kyis 'khyud cing /

Similarly the fierce females are in the grounds of the cemeteries. In the eastern cemetery called Pierced lives dog-faced Śvānavaktrā. In the southern cemetery called Blazing lives the pig-faced Śūkarāsyā. In the northern cemetery called Putrid lives the tiger-faced Vyāghravaktra. In the western cemetery called Wolf lives the wolf-faced Jambukāsyā. In the southeastern cemetery called Remainder lives the crow-faced Kākavaktrā. In the southwestern cemetery called Unending War lives the vulture-faced Gṛidha vaktrā. In the northwestern cemetery called Magical Food lives the hawk-faced Khagapativadanā. In the northeastern cemetery called Death of the Foolish lives the owl-faced Ulūkavaktrā. The nāgas are embraced by fierce females, and the fierce female mothers are embraced by nāgas. /294/

de yang gzhan rigs la 'khyud dgos pas shar phyogs pa rnams dang nub phyogs pa rnams phan tshun du 'khyud pa dang / byang phyogs pa rnams dang lho phyogs pa rnams phan tshun du 'khyud pa dang / de bzhin du me mtshams pa dang nub byang pa rnams phan tshun du 'khyud pa dang / bden bral ba rnams dang dbang ldan pa rnams phan tshun du 'khyud dgos pa ni/
de bzhin sa yi dkyil 'khor la gnas rigs kyi dbang gis 'jog po dang ni pad+ma chen por 'gyur/ / de rnams shes rab rab gtum ma rnams dur khrod sa la gnas pa'i khyi gdong ma la [163] sogs pa ste/ de rnams thabs ni pad+ma la sogs gzhan gyi rigs kyi dbang gis bde ba dam pa'i don du 'gyur/ / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyi don yin no/ /

The embracing has to involve different families, and so those of the east and west mutually embrace, as do those of the north and south, southeast and northwest, southwest and northeast. This is the meaning of quotes from the Condensed Tantra that state:
Similarly, on the earth mandala, in families, stand Takṣaka and Mahāpadma in the cemeteries with Śvānavaktrā and other fierce females as their wisdom consorts, who in turn stand with Padma and the others as their method consorts. Therefore it is with other families that they are paired for the highest bliss.[198]

d.div: [163] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ dbang gi le'u/ 3_sh+loka63_84_na6
[198] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, dbang v. 63, 84a6.

f.d: de ltar na klu dang rab gtum ma yab yum rnams dam tshig pa la ye shes pa ro mnyam pa dang zla nyi dam tshig pa la zla nyi ye shes pa ro mnyam par sgom pa ste ro mnyam gyi rgyud go slar bzhag pa rnams kyi don bsdus pa'o/ /

Therefore one should meditate on the nāgas and fierce female mother-and-father samaya beings as being of one taste with the wisdom beings, and the samaya moon and sun as being of one taste with the wisdom moon and sun. This is a brief explanation of text from the Condensed Tantra deemed “easy to understand.”
bzhi pa de la rigs kyis rgyas gdab pa ni/

'grel chen las/
da ni cod pan [164] zhes pa la sogs pas lha rnams kyi rigs kyis rgyas gdab pa gsungs pa 'dir mchog gi dang po'i sangs rgyas kyi dkyil 'khor du cod pan dag la phan tshun rdo rje yi ni rdo rjer 'gyur te de ci'i phyir zhe na ye shes dang rnam par shes pa phan tshun yang dag par sbyor ba'i phyir ro/ / de bas na ye shes kyis rnam par shes pa dang rnam par shes pas ye shes la ste gnyi ga'i spyi bo la thugs rdo rje chos gos dang gtsug tor 'dzin pa rdo rje skyil krung gis gnas pa sa la reg pa'i phyag rgyas de bzhin gshegs pa'i dbugs dbyung bas so/ / ngo bo nyid kyi rigs la ni rigs lngas rgyas gdab pa bkag ste sangs rgyas rnams kyi skyed par byed pa po yin pa'i phyir ro/ / yang na ye shes dang rnam par shes pa'i chos kyis sangs rgyas lnga'i bdag nyid kyi cod pan ni res 'ga' na'o zhes pa nges pa'o/[165] / zhes gsungs pa'i don la mi mthun pa mang ste/ gnyis ga'i spyi bo la zhes pa mkhas pa kha cig yab yum gnyis ka'i spyi bo la zhes 'chad/ kha cig rdor sems dang mi bskyod pa gnyis ka'i spyi bo la zhes 'chad do/ /

The Great Commentary says:
Now “the crown” and so forth talks of the deities being sealed by their families. Here in the mandala of the supreme original buddha, on the crown, “a vajra in the manner of two vajras crossed.” Why? Because consciousness and gnosis are perfectly united. Therefore gnosis is on consciousness and consciousness is on gnosis. On the heads of both is the mind vajra in robes and with crown protrusion, in lotus posture, with earth-touching mudrā, giving the breath of the tathāgatas. It is rejected that the essence family is sealed by the five families. This is because it is the creator of buddhas. Alternatively, because of the phenomena of gnosis and consciousness, the crown, in essence the five buddhas, sometimes seals. Thus it is ascertained.[199] /295/ This passage has produced many differing explanations. Some scholars say that the phrase “On the heads of both” refers to the heads of the mother-and-father main deities. Some say it refers to Vajrasattva and Akṣobhya.

d.div: [164] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 222_na7
[165] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 222_ba1
[199] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 222a7.

f.d: ngo bo nyid kyi rigs la ni zhes pa kha cig rab byung gi cha byad can la 'chad/ kha cig rdor sems la 'chad/ kha cig rigs lnga rang gis rang la rgyas 'debs pa bkag pa'i 'chad kyang / 'di ltar du bshad par bya ste rigs drug po rdo rje la sogs pa'i rigs su byed pa'i tshe don grub ral gri'i rigs dang rin 'byung rin po che'i rigs dang snang mtha' pad+ma_'i rigs dang rnam snang 'khor lo'i rigs dang rdor sems dang mi bskyod pa rdo rje'i rigs su byed pas/ rdo rje yi ni rdo rjer 'gyur te zhes pa'i 'grel par/ de bas na ye shes kyis rnam shes zhes sogs byung ba yin la/ de dag gis rdo rje sems dpa' ye shes kyi rigs dang mi bskyod pa rnam shes kyi rigs gnyis rdo rje'i rigs su mtshungs pa des na phan tshun gcig gis gcig la rgyas 'debs pa dang / rdor sems dang mi bskyod pa gnyis ka'i spyi bo la thugs rdo rje mi bskyod pa chos gos dang gtsug tor 'dzin pa sogs kyis rgyas gdab ces pa'i don no/ /

Concerning “the essence family,” some explain it as referring to the form of a monk. Some say it refers to Vajrasattva. Others say it means that the five families do not crown-seal themselves. However it will be explained as follows. When the six families are explained as those of the vajra family and so forth, Amoghasiddhi is of the sword family, Ratna-sambhava is of the jewel family, Amitābha is of the lotus family, Vairocana is of the wheel family, and Vajrasattva and Akṣobhya are both of the vajra family. Therefore the commentary to the Condensed Tantra text, “a vajra in the manner of two vajras crossed” says, “Therefore gnosis is on consciousness” and so on. This teaches that Vajrasattva of the gnosis family and Akṣobhya of the consciousness family are similar in that they both belong to the vajra family. Therefore they are crown-sealed by each other, and the heads of both Vajrasattva and Akṣobhya are crown-sealed by mind-vajra Akṣobhya in robes with crown protrusion and so on.

yang ngo bo nyid kyi rigs la zhes sogs kyi don ni/ ngo bo nyid ye shes kyi phung po'i rigs rdo rje sems dpa' la ni rigs lnga ral pa'i cod pan can gyis rgyas gdab pa bkag ste/ ye shes kyi phung po'am khams phra ba 'od gsal gyi sems de 'khor 'das thams cad skyed pa po yin pa bzhin du de rnam par dag pa'i rdo rje sems dpa' yang sangs rgyas rnams kyi skyed par byed pa po yin pa'i phyir ro/ /zhes pa'o/ / yang na/ ye shes dang zhes sogs kyi don ni 'gyur mang du yang na 'on kyang zhes 'byung ba ltar yang na 'on kyang ye shes dang rnam shes phan tshun rgyas 'debs pa'i chos yin pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis sangs rgyas lnga'i bdag nyid can mi bskyod pa ljang gus rdor sems sngon po la res 'ga' na rgyas 'debs par yang rung ngo / /zhes pa ste snga ma'i dmigs bsal lo/ /

The meaning of the lines beginning “It is rejected that the essence family” is that Vajrasattva is of the essence family, or gnosis-aggregate family, and he is not crown-sealed by the five families with crowns of tied-up hair, because the gnosis aggregate, or the subtle clear-light mind, is the creator of all things in samsara and nirvana and, similarly, its purification in the form of Vajrasattva is the creator of buddhas. Concerning the line beginning “Alternatively, because of the phenomena,” in many translations “alternatively” is rendered as “however,” and in keeping with that translation, this line means that “However, because gnosis and consciousness are crown-sealed by each other, it is fitting that sometimes green Akṣobhya, who is in essence the five buddhas, crown-seals a blue Vajrasattva.” “Thus” indicates that this is an exception.

de rnams kyis mi bskyod pa dang rdor sems la rgyas 'debs tshul bstan nas rigs lhag ma bzhi la rgyus 'bras bu la rgyas 'debs tshul ston pa ni/
gzugs kyi steng du mi bskyod pa ste sku'i rnam pa thugs kyi [166] zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / gsal bar pad+ma 'dzin pa'i rnam par snang mdzad nyid du 'gyur te lus kyis gsung so so brjod pa zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / rin chen dbang po'i chu skyes 'dzin te rdul gyi chos can nyid kyi phyir ro/ / don yod grub pa'i cod pan la ni rab mchog nor bu'i phyag ste khrag las sha 'byung ba'i phyir ro/ /zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis bstan te/ de yang sku'i rnam pa thugs las 'byung ba dang / lus sam skus gsung so sor rjod pa dang / snang mtha'i rang bzhin gsher ba chu las rdul 'byung ba dang / rdul te khrag las sha 'byung bas rim pa bzhin mi bskyod pas rnam snang dang / rnam snang gis 'od dpag med dang / 'od dpag med kyis rin 'byung dang / rin 'byung gis don grub la rgyas 'debs pa yin no/ /

Having explained the way Vajrasattva and Akṣobhya are crown-sealed, the Great Commentary continues:
“On form is Akṣobhya,” teaches enlightened mind in its aspect of enlightened form. “Becoming Vairocana holding a lotus” talks of the body, which expresses individual speech. “Holder of a mighty jeweled lotus” refers to blood. “In the crown of Amoghasiddhi the supreme jewel” teaches that from the blood arises flesh.[200] /296/ This explains that the other four families are crown-sealed in the manner of the cause crown-sealing the result. Enlightened form arises from enlightened mind, and this body, or enlightened form, expresses speech. From water, which has the nature of Amitābha, arises blood. From blood arises flesh. Therefore, in order, Akṣobhya seals Vairocana, Vairocana seals Amitābha, Amitābha seals Ratnasambhava, and Ratnasambhava seals Amoghasiddhi.

d.div: [166] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 222_ba3
[200] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 222b3.

f.d:
yang 'grel chen las/
rnam par snang mdzad dang g.yon gyi lha ste snang ba mtha' yas dang mi 'jig pa ste rin chen 'byung ldan dang de'i skyes bu ste don yod grub pa dang dbang ldan te mi bskyod pa dang dus kyi me ste rdo rje sems dpa' rnams ni sa dang chu dang me dang rlung dang nam mkha' dang ye shes kyi rang bzhin tha mal pa'i phung po rnams te dag pa'i phung po gtsug tor dang chos gos 'dzin pa rnams kyis rgyas gdab bo/ / de ltar drug ni ral pa'i cod pan can zhes bya'o/[167] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyi don la kha cig /rigs drug ral pa'i cod pan can la rigs drug chos gos gtsug tor 'dzin pas rgyas gdab pa tsam bshad nas rigs drug gang gis gang la rgyas 'debs pa mi gsal lo|_|

The Great Commentary continues:
“Vairocana and the deity to the left,” or Amitābha; Avināśa, or Ratnasambhava; his son, or Amoghasiddhi; Vaśin, or Akṣobhya; Kālāgni, or Vajrasattva: these in the nature of earth, water, fire, air, space, and gnosis, the ordinary aggregates are sealed by the pure aggregates with robes and crown protrusion. These six have crowns of tied-up hair.[201] Some just explain this passage as meaning that the six families with crowns of tied-up hair are sealed by the six families with crown protrusion and robes, but which family is sealed by which is not clear.

d.div: [167] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 222_ba6
[201] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 222b6.

f.d: mkhas pa kha cig rgyas gdab de dag sus rgyas btab kyang rung ste/ rgyas gdab de'i spyi bo la thugs rdo rje rab byung gi rnam pa sprul pa'i skus rgyas gdab pa ni bdag nyid gcig pa'i 'brel pa la brten pa ste 'dir dkyil 'khor na gnas pa gtso bo dang rigs lnga la sogs pa thams cad shA_kya thub pa'i bdag nyid yin pa'i phyir ro/ /zhes gsung ste/ rigs drug ral pa'i cod pan can la rgyas 'debs pa'i chos gos dang gtsug tor 'dzin pa shAkya thub pa la mdzad par mngon no/ / 'di ni phung po rnams re re dag pa'i phung po gtsug tor dang chos gos 'dzin pa zhes rgyas 'debs byed gtsug tor dang chos gos 'dzin pa rnams tha mal pa'i phung po drug dag pa'i phung po'i rang bzhin du bshad pa dang 'gal lo/ /

Other scholars say that it is acceptable for the crown-sealing to be performed by any of them, because “The crown sealing is performed on the heads by the mind vajra as the emanation body in the form of a monk. This is done on the basis of being of identical nature, because the main deity, the five families, and all the others in the mandala are of one nature with Śākyamuni.” It appears that, according to this statement, the sealer with crown protrusion and robes who seals the six families with crowns of tied-up hair is Śākyamuni. This contradicts the teaching that those with crown protrusion and robes who perform the sealing are of the same nature as the purified aggregates, as evidenced by the line /297/ “the ordinary aggregates are sealed by the pure aggregates with robes and crown protrusion.”

sgrub thabs zhal lung las/ rnam snang snang mtha' rin 'byung don grub mi bskyod pa rdor sems te drug ral pa'i cod paN can rnams la rim pa bzhin rnam snang sogs chos gos dang gtsug tor 'dzin pa rnams kyis rgyas gdab pa mdzad la/[168] de'i dgongs pa ltar byed na/ ngo bo nyid kyi rigs la ni zhes sogs kyi don rigs lnga po rang gis rang la rgyas gdab tu mi rung ba'i don can du bshad na 'gal 'dur 'gyur bas ngo bo nyid kyi rigs zhes sogs kyi don bdag gis gong du bshad pa ltar khas blang bar bya dgos so/ /

The Puṇḍarīka Transmission Sādhana states that Vairocana, Amitābha, Ratnasambhava, Amoghasiddhi, Akṣobhya, and Vajrasattva with crowns of tied-up hair are crown-sealed respectively by Vairocana and the others with crown protrusion and robes.[202] If this interpretation is followed, then to say that the line “It is rejected that the essence family” means that that the five families do not crown-seal themselves would be contradictory. Therefore the meaning of this line has to be as I have explained it above.

d.div: [168] mkhas grub rje/ gsung 'bum/ cha_sgrub thab pad dkar zhal lung / 57_ba5
[202] Khedrup Jé, Collected Works, vol. cha, 57b5.

f.d: yang na/ de bas na ye shes kyis rnam par shes pa dang zhes pa nas/ don yod grub pa'i cod pan la ni rab mchog nor bu'i phyag ste zhes pa'i bar gyis rigs drug po gang la gang gis rgyas 'debs pa bstan nas/ de ltar rgyas 'debs pa'i gdab par bya ba sku'i rnam pa ji lta bu la rgyas 'debs byed sku'i rnam pa ji lta bus rgyas gdab snyam na/ de'i tshul ni/ drug ni ral pa'i cod pan du 'gyur te zhes pa nas/ dag pa'i phung po gtsug tor dang chos gos 'dzin pa rnams kyis rgyas gdab pa'o/ / de ltar drug ni ral ba'i cod pan can zhes bya'o [169] zhes pa'i bar gyis ston te/ de yang tha mal pasbya nga gzhi ma dag pa'i phung po 'am khamasadru ga mtshon byed rigs drug ral pa'i cod pan can drug la dag pa'i phung sogs mtshon byed rigs drug gtsug tor dang chos gos 'dzin pa rnams kyis rgyas 'debs zhes pa'i don can du bshad par bya'o/ / de ltar na mi bskyod pa rab byung gi rnam pa can gyis rnam snang ral pa'i cod pan can la rgyas gdab ces bya ba la sogs pa yin no/ /

The Great Commentary lines from “Alternatively, because of the phenomena of gnosis and consciousness” up to “In the crown of Amoghasiddhi the supreme jewel” explains who crown-seals whom in the six families. Concerning the bodily form of those who seal and the bodily form of those who are sealed, an explanation is given in the lines that run from “The six have crowns of tied-up hair” up to “the ordinary aggregates with crowns of tied-up hair are sealed by the pure aggregates with robes and crown protrusion.” This passage teaches that the six pure aggregates or elements, symbolized by the six families with crown protrusion and robes, crown-seal the six bases of purification in the form of impure aggregates or elements, symbolized by the six families with crowns of tied-up hair. The passage should be explained in this way. Thus, for example, Akṣobhya in the form of a monk crown-seals Vairocana in the form of one possessing a crown of tied-up hair.

d.div: [169] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 222_ba3

f.d:
'khor gyi lha lhag ma rnams la rgyas gdab pa ni 'grel chen las/
lhag ma'i 'khor lo'i lha dang lha mo rnams kyi cod pan ni rin po che sna tshogs pa'i rang bzhin dang rang rang gi rigs kyis rgyas gdab ste [170] zhes gsungs pa ltar rigs drug po gang gi rigs can gang yin pa de la rigs drug po longs sku'i cha byad can gyis rgyas gdab par bya'o/ / de yang nus ma rnams ma gtogs pa'i rigs can gyi lha dang lha mo nag po rnams la don grub kyis rgyas gdab pa dang / dmar po rnams la rin 'byung dang / dkar po rnams la snang mtha' dang / ser po rnams la rnam snang dang / ljang gu rnams la mi bskyod pa dang / nus ma dang sngon po rnams la rdo rje sems dpas rgyas gdab bo/ /

Concerning the crown-sealing of the remaining deities, the Great Commentary says:
The head ornaments of the remaining gods and goddesses are crowned by various jewels and by their respective families.[203] Therefore those belonging to one of the six families are sealed by the six families in enjoyment-body emanation. Furthermore, except for the śakti, black gods and goddesses who belong to a family are sealed by Amoghasiddhi, red deities by Ratnasambhava, white by Amitābha, yellow by Vairocana, and green by Akṣobhya. /298/ The śakti and blue gods and goddesses are sealed by Vajrasattva.

d.div: [170] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 222_ba7
[203] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 222b7.

f.d: lnga pa sku gsung thugs byin gyis brlab pa ni

d.i: Blessings of body, speech, and mind

f.d:
'grel chen las/
'dir byis pa skyes pa'i lus dang ngag dang sems byin gyis brlabs pa sad pa dang rmi lam dang shin tu gnyid log pa'i mtshan nyid du 'gyur ba ji lta ba de bzhin du [171] zhes gsungs pa ltar/ byis pa skyes pa'i lus ngag sems gsum sad rmi gnyid mthug gi skabs gsum du 'gyur ba dang chos mthun par sku gsung thugs byin rlabs byed pa yin la/ de'i byed tshul ni 'grel chen las/
dpral ba dang mgrin pa dang snying ga dang lte ba dang gsang ba dang gtsug tor la oM AHhUM hoHswAhA 'di rnams kyis byin gyis brlabs pa'i yan lag ni byis pa mas 'khru bar byed pa ji lta ba de bzhin du rab mchog rgyal ba'i bdag po'i lha mo rnams kyis zhes pa rnal 'byor ma rnams kyis bkru bar bya'o/[172] / zhes gsungs pa ltar yab yum gnyis ka'i dpral mgrin snying gar oM AHhU~M rim pa bzhin dang / yum gyi lte bar hoH dang gsang bar swA/ gtsug tor la hA bkod de byin gyis brlab ces mdor bstan nas/ byin gyis rlob tshul dngos 'chad pa ni/ 'dir byin gyis brlab pa ni zhes sogs man chad kyis ston la/ de yang dang por byis pa mas 'khru ba dang chos mthun par rab mchog rgyal ba'i bdag po gtso bo la rnal 'byor ma rnams kyis bum pa'i chus bkru bar bsgom par bya'o/ /

The Great Commentary says:
Here the body, speech, and mind of the newborn child are blessed to become the waking state, dreams, and sleep.[204] The blessing by enlightened body, speech, and mind is performed in correlation with the body, speech, and mind of the newborn child in the three states of waking, dreams, and deep sleep. Concerning the procedure the Great Commentary says:
On the brow, throat, heart, navel, secret, and crown are oṃ, āḥ, hūḥ, hoṃ, svā, and hā. These are the stages of the blessings. As a mother washes her child, so the supreme lord is washed by the “goddesses,” or yoginīs.[205] On the brow, throat, and heart center of the mother-and-father deities are oṃ, āṃ, and hūḥ respectively. At the navel of the mother is hoṃ, at her secret area svā, and on her crown hā. This is a synopsis of the blessing procedure. The explanation of the actual blessing starts from the next line in the Great Commentary, which begins “Here the blessing. First one meditates that the yoginīs wash the main deity and supreme lord with vases of water. This correlates with the child being washed by its mother.

d.div: [171] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 222_ba7
[172] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 227_ba7
[204] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 222b7.
[205] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 227b7.

f.d: de nas sku gsung thugs byin gyis brlab pa ni yab yum gnyis ka'i dpral bar a las zla ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng du oM yig yongs su gyur pa las 'khor lo rtsibs brgyad pa/ de yongs su gyur pa las sku rdo rje sku mdog dkar po zhal phyag dang phyag mtshan sogs 'grel chen las gsal bar gsungs pa ltar shes rab yum dang bcas pa bskyed la/ de nas dpral ba las spros pas sku rdo rje de las de lta bu dpag med byung ste nam mkha'i khams kun nas yongs su gang bar bsgom par bya'o/ / de nas de rnams kyis sku rdo rjes gdul bar bya ba'i sems can rnams la chos ston pa mdzad nas slar log gcig tu 'dus te bdag nyid kyi mdun du yang dag par bkod pa la/ sku'i rdo rje 'dzin pa bdag la dbang skur du gsol zhes gsol ba gdab par bya'o/ / de nas sku'i rigs kyi lha mo rnams kyis bdud rtsi'i bum pas mngon par dbang bskur bar bsgom par bya'o/ / de ltar dbang bskur ba la byin gyis brlab pa ni/ rang gi dpral bar zla ba'i dkyil 'khor la bsgom pa'i sku rdo rje bcug nas/ dpal ldan sku yi rdo rje 'dzin/[173] /zhes sogs tshigs su bcad pa gnyis po 'di brjod nas sku byin gyis brlab bo/ / dpal ldan sku yi zhes sogs kyi don ni gnyis su med pa'i ye shes kyi dpal lus kyi thig le mi 'gyur bar 'dzin pa dang ldan pa'i sku rdo rje 'dzin pa zhes bos nas/ lam gyi skabs su sku gsung thugs kyi rdo rje gsum dbyer mi phyed par bsgoms pas sku'i rdo rje mngon du gyur pa can khyed kyis ni skus byin gyis brlab pa'i gnas dpral bar byin gyis brlabs te/ deng ste da lta nyid du bdag gis sku rdo rje thob par mdzod/ ces pa ste/ 'og ma yang des 'gre'o/ /

Now the body, speech, and mind blessing begins. From an āḥ at the brow of both mother-and-father deities arise moon disks on which stand the syllable oṃ. They transform into eight-spoked wheels, which in turn change into the white body-vajra deity in union with his wisdom consort. Their faces and hand implements are clearly described in the Great Commentary. /299/ One meditates that the body vajra emerges from the brow center to produce countless replicas. They fill the realms of space, teaching the dharma to the sentient beings to be tamed by body vajra deities, and then return to merge into a single deity that stands before the meditator. One then makes the request, “Holder of the body vajra, grant me initiation.” Goddesses of the body family perform the actual initiation with vases of nectar. The body-blessing initiation occurs when the visualized body vajra enters the moon disk at one’s brow and one recites the two verses beginning “Glorious holder of the body vajra.” The meaning of the first verse[206] is as follows: “Glorious indivisible gnosis held in the immutable body drop, holder of the body vajra.” This is an address to the deity. “By meditating on the indivisibility of the body, speech, and mind vajras during the practices of the path, you have actualized the body vajra. Bless me in the place upon the brow, grant me now the attainment of the body vajra.”[207] The second verse follows the same pattern.

d.div: [173] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 228_na5
[206] Glorious body-vajra holder, meditator upon three indivisible vajras, to become vajra-body holder, consecrate me in the place of blessing.
[207] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 228a5.

f.d: gsung byin gyis brlab pa ni/ yab yum gnyis ka'i 'grin par ra yig las nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng du AHyig las pad+ma dmar po 'dab ma brgyad pa/ de yongs su gyur pa las gsung rdo rje sku mdog zhal phyag phyag mtshan dang bcas pa 'grel chen du gsal ba ltar la shes rab ma dang bcas pa bskyed de/ des nam mkha'i khams gang ba spros te bsgom par bya'o/ / de nas gsung rdo rje de rnams kyis gdul bar bya ba'i sems can rnams la chos ston pa mdzad nas slar yang bdag nyid kyi mdun du bkod pa la gsung gi rdo rje can gyis bdag la dbang skur du gsol zhes gsol ba btab pas gsung gi rigs kyi lha mo rnams kyis snga ma bzhin du dbang bskur bar bsgom par bya'o/ / de nas mgrin par nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor la gsung rdo rje rnam par bkod nas/ dpal ldan gsung gi rdo rje 'dzin/[174] /zhes tshigs su bcad pa gnyis po 'di brjod par bya'o/ / dpal ldan zhes sogs kyi don ni/ gnyis su med pa'i ye shes kyi dpal ngag gi thig le mi 'gyur bar 'dzin pa las byung ba dang ldan pa'i gsung gi rdo rje 'dzin pa zhes bos nas/ gzhan rnams snga ma dang 'dra ba la sku'i dod du gsung dang / gsung gis byin gyis brlab pa'i gnas mgrin pa zhes bya'o/ /

In the speech blessing one visualizes the letter ra at the throats of mother-and-father main deity. This changes into a sun disk, on top of which is the syllable āṃ. That becomes a red lotus of eight petals, which in turn becomes the speech vajra, whose color, faces, hands, and hand symbols are clearly described in the Great Commentary and who is in union with his wisdom consort. He emanates to fill the realms of space and teaches those to be tamed by speech-vajra emanations, before returning as a single deity in front of oneself. One requests, “Holder of the vajra, grant me initiation,” and as before one visualizes that goddesses of the speech family come to bestow initiation. The speech vajra returns to the sun mandala at the throat, and one recites the two verses beginning “Glorious holder of the speech vajra.” The meaning of the verses is “Glorious indivisible gnosis held in and arising from the immutable speech drop, holder of the speech vajra.”[208] /300/ This is an address to the deity. The remaining lines are similar to the previous verse except that “speech” is substituted for “body” and the place of blessing is the throat.

d.div: [174] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 229_na1
[208] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 229a1.

f.d: thugs byin gyis brlab pa ni yab yum gnyis ka'i snying gar thig le las sgra gcan gyi dkyil 'khor kha dog mthon mthing gi steng du hU~M las rdo rje rtse lnga pa/ de yongs su gyur pa las thugs rdo rje sku mdog nag po zhal phyag dang phyag mtshan sogs 'grel chen las gsal ba ltar shes rab ma yum dang bcas pa bskyed de/ des nam mkha'i khams gang ba spros pa bsgom par bya'o/ / de nas thugs rdo rje rnams kyis gdul bar bya ba'i sems can rnams la chos bstan pa mdzad nas slar log ste bdag nyid kyi mdun du bkod pa la thugs kyi rdo rje can gyis bdag la dbang skur du gsol zhes gsol ba btab pas/ thugs kyi rigs kyi lha mo rnams kyis snga ma bzhin du dbang bskur bar bsgom par bya'o/ / de nas thugs byin gyis brlab pa ni thugs rdo rje snying gar sgra gcan gyi dkyil 'khor la bkod nas/ dpal ldan thugs kyi rdo rje 'dzin/[175] /zhes sogs tshigs su bcad pa gnyis kyis gsol ba gdab par bya'o/ / tshigs bcad de dag gi don ni gnyis su med pa'i ye shes kyi dpal sems kyi thig le mi 'gyur bar 'dzin pa las byung ba dang ldan pa'i thugs kyi rdo rje 'dzin pa zhes bos nas/ gzhan rnams snga ma sku'i skabs dang 'dra ba la sku'i dod la thugs zhes pa dang / byin gyis brlab pa'i gnas snying ga zhes brje bar bya'o/ /

In the mind blessing one visualizes a drop at the heart of both mother and father. This becomes a dark blue Rāhu mandala on top of which is the syllable hūḥ. This transforms into a five-pointed vajra, which in turns becomes a black mind vajra in union with his wisdom consort and whose faces, hands, and implements are clearly taught in the Great Commentary. He emanates to fill the realms of space, where the emanations teach dharma to those who are to be tamed by mind-vajra emanations, and then returns to become a single deity in front of the meditator, who requests, “Holder of the mind vajra, grant me initiation.” Goddesses of the mind family bestow initiation. The mind blessing occurs when the mind vajra returns to the Rāhu mandala and one recites the two verses of request that begin, “Glorious holder of the mind vajra.” The meaning of the verses is “Glorious indivisible gnosis held in and arising from the immutable speech drop, holder of the mind vajra.”[209] This is an address to the deity. The remaining lines are similar to the previous verse except that “mind” is substituted for “body” and the place of blessing is the heart.

d.div: [175] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 228_ba3
[209] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 228b3.

f.d: de ltar thugs byin gyis brlabs pa'i rjes de nas/ oM sarba ta thA ga ta kAya wAka tsit+ta swa b+hA wa At+ma ko’haM/ zhes brjod cing / de'i sngags don ni de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi sku gsung thugs kyi rang bzhin gyi bdag nyid nga'o snyam pa'i nga rgyal rnal 'byor pas gzung bar bya'o/ / sngags de'i don de ltar yin pa'i tshul ni oM dang por brjod pa ni mgo 'dren pa yin la/ sar+b+ba ni thams cad dang / ta thA ga ta ni de bzhin gshegs pa dang / kA ya ni sku dang / wA ka ni gsung dang / tsit+ta ni thugs dang / swa b+hA wa ni rang bzhin dang / A t+ma kaHni bdag nyid dang / a haM ni nga'o zhes pa rnams su 'gyur ro/ / de yang ko haM zhes pa ni mtshams sbyar bas byung ba yin te/

After the mind blessing one recites the mantra oṃ sarva tathāgata kāya vāka citta svabhāva ātmako haṃ. The meaning of this mantra is “I the yogi hold the pride of being of the nature of the body, speech, and mind of all the tathāgatas.” This is because oṃ at the beginning heads the mantra; sarva means all; kāya means body; vāka means speech; citta means mind; svabhāva means nature; ātmakaṃ means self; ahaṃ means I. In the mantra, ko haṃ is a product of amalgamation.[210]

d.div: [210] mtshaṃs sbyor, saṃdhi. The Sanskrit grammatical rules of euphony.

f.d:
de yang ka lA pa las/
a yig dag gi bar du u'o/ / a dang sgra ldan dag gi 'ang ngo /[176] / zhes pas ka'i srog gi a dang sgra ldan gyi yi ge ha'i bar du byung ba'i rnam gcad u yig tu 'gyur zhing / yang /
u yig la o 'ozhes ka'i srog gi a de or 'gyur la pha rol gyi u phyis te ka srog med o'i steng du drangs pas ko haM zhes par 'gyur ba yin no/ /

The Kalāpasūtra says:
Between the letters a it becomes u; between a and voiced letters also.[211] /301/ Thus the visarga between the life-giving letter a of the letter ka and the voiced letter ha becomes the letter u.
On the letter u it becomes the letter o. Thus the life-giving a of ka becomes o. The a on the other side is erased, and k is brought to o to become ko, thereby resulting in ko haṃ.[212]

d.div: [176] sde dge_4282_bstan/ sgra mdo/ le_ka lA pa'i mdo/ 3_na2
[211] Toh 4282 Tengyur, sgra mdo, le, 3a2.
[212] kaṃ+ahaṃ becomes ka + u + ahaṃ; becomes ko + ahaṃ; becomes ko haṃ.

f.d:
de dag ni yab yum gnyis ka'i sku gsung thugs byin gyis rlob pa thun mong ba yin la/ yum gyi thun mong ma yin pa ni 'grel chen las/
de bzhin du shes rab kyi lte bar hoHyig gis so/[177] / zhes sogs gsungs pa ltar shes rab yum gyi lte bar hoHyig gis byin gyis brlab pa dang / gsang bar swA yig dang / gtsug tor la hA yig gis byin gyis brlab pa'o/ / de ltar byin gyis brlab pa yab la gsum yum la drug byed pa'i rgyu mtshan ni 'grel chen las/
khu ba'i chos las thabs rigs gsum dang / rdul dang khu ba'i chos las shes rab rigs drug go[178] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

This has been a shared blessing by the body, speech, and mind of both mother and father. Concerning the individual blessings from the mother, the Great Commentary says:
Similarly the letter hoḥ at the navel of the wisdom consort.[213] The blessings from the wisdom consort are granted by the letter hoṃ at her navel, svā in her secret area, and ha at her crown. The reason why there are three blessings from the father and six from the mother is mentioned in the Great Commentary:
From the fluid phenomena there are three of method. From the blood and fluid phenomena there are six of wisdom.[214]

d.div: [177] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 229_na3
[178] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 229_na3
[213] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 229a3.
[214] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 229a3.

f.d: drug pa rten dang brten pa'i rnam dag sgom pa
['di ]la gnyis/ rten gzhal yas khang gi rnam dag sgom pa dang / brten pa lha'i rnam dag sgom pa'o/ /
This is under two headings: 1. Meditating on the purity of the celestial mansion 2. Meditating on the purity of the resident deities
dang po [rten gzhal yas khang gi rnam dag sgom pa ]

d.i: Mediating on the purity of the celestial mansion

f.d: ['di ]la rnam dag gnyis bshad pa las lus kyi khams dang sbyar ba'i rnam dag ni ye shes le'u'i mdor bsdus dang por bstan pa ltar shes par bya zhing sgrub le 'dir sgrib bral gyi chos kyi rnam dag bstan pa gzhal yas khang 'chad pa'i skabs su bstan pa ni bshad pa'i go rim yin la sgom pa'i rim pa ni gnas skabs 'dir yin pas 'dir de dag gi don bshad par bya'o/ / de yang tha mal gyi snod bcud bzhin du lha dang gzhal yas khang ngo bo tha dad du 'dzin pa bzlog pa'i phyir du gzhal yas khang gi rnam dag dang / lha gtso 'khor dang pho mo la sogs pa'i rnam pa tha dad pa rnams rgyud tha dad du 'dzin pa bzlog pa'i phyir du lha'i rnam dag bsgom par bshad pa yin pas skabs 'dir sgom dgos so/ /

There are two types of celestial mansion purity. Purity as applied to the body is taught in the first summary of the Gnosis chapter and can be ascertained there. Here in the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, the purity of phenomena without obscuration is taught. When the celestial palace was described, the explanation was purely descriptive, but here the purpose is meditation, and so the meanings of that description need to be explained. The purity of the celestial mansion is taught in order to reverse the perception that the deities and the celestial mansion are separate entities, like the ordinary world and its inhabitants. The purity of the deities is taught in order to reverse the perception that because the main deities, their entourage — males and females and so on — have different forms, they must be different beings. /302/

de la gzhal yas khang gi rnam dag ni rtsa rgyud sgrub le'i 'grel chen du drangs pa las/
sangs rgyas chos dang dge 'dun ches/ / thugs gsung sku yi dkyil 'khor ro/ / tshangs pa'i gnas bzhi rnams kyis ni/ / rdo rje'i thig ni bzhi po ste/ / dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi rnams kyis/ / kun nas gru bzhi pa nyid do/ /

d.div: yan lag bcu gnyis 'gags pa yis/ / sgo ni bcu gnyis po rnams te/ / de bzhin sa ni bcu gnyis kyis/ / rta babs rnams ni mdzes pa rnams/ / 'phags lam yan lag brgyad rnams kyis/ / phyogs brgyad du ni dur khrod rnams/ /

stong nyid bcu drug ka ba rnams/ khams rnams kyis kyang khang pa brtsegs/ / rnam thar brgyad kyis sgo khyud rnams/ / gzugs can yon tan brgyad rnams kyis/ / 'gram rnams dang ni logs rnams nyid/ / thugs gsung sku yi dbye bas so/ /

tshul khrims la sogs phung po lngas/ kha dog lnga ni rnam par dag/ theg pa gsum gyis ra ba gsum/ / dad pa'i dbang po sogs kyis lnga/ / dad sogs stobs rnams dag gis lnga/ / thugs gsung sku yi dkyil 'khor la'o/ /

ting nge 'dzin dang gzungs rnams kyis/ / dkyil 'khor gsum la stegs bu ste/ / pha rol phyin bcu rdzogs pa yis/ / rin chen snam bu rnam par bkra/ ma 'dres chos ni bco brgyad kyis/ / do shal do shal phyed pa rnams/ / dbang rnams kyis kyang ba gu lI/ /
dge bas kra ma shIr Sha'o/ / stong nyid la sogs rnam thar gyis/ / dril bu'i sgras ni gang ba ste/ / rdzu 'phrul rkang pas rgyal mtshan gtams/ / spong bas me long rab tu 'bar/ /
the kramaśīraṣa of the virtues, filled with the chimes of freedoms such as emptiness, filled with victory banners of magical power concentrations, shining with mirrors of the eradications;
byang chub yan lag rnga yab g.yo/ / yan lag dgu yis phreng bas brgyan/ / bsdu ba bzhi po rnams kyis ni/ / zur du sna tshogs rdo rjes brgyan/ /
bden bzhis rin po che rnams kyis/ / sgo dang sgo khyud mtshams su spras/ / mngon shes lnga yis rtag tu ni/ / khor yug chen po lnga yis bskor/ /
rnam pa kun mkhyen byang chub pas/ / rdo rje phreng bas legs par bskor/ / bde ba gcig bu'i khor yug gis/ / de bzhin ye shes rdo rje 'bar/ /

f.d: shes rab thabs kyi cha yis ni/ / zla ba nyi ma rtag tu shar/ / thugs gsung sku dang dag pa yis/ / chos kyi 'khor lo bum pa che/ / rnga bo che dang byang chub shing / / de bzhin yid bzhin nor bu sogs/ / 'di ni dpal ldan dus 'khor gyi/ / dkyil 'khor chos kyi dbyings nyid do/[179] / zhes gsungs pa rnams so/ /

d.div: [179] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 205_na3
[215] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 205a3.

f.d: de dag gi don cung zad cig bshad na/ sangs rgyas sogs tshig rkang gnyis kyi don ni/
sangs rgyas chos dang dge 'dun te dkon mchog gsum rnam par dag pa ni rim pa bzhin thugs gsung sku'i dkyil 'khor gsum mo/ /
The Three Jewels of Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha are the mind, speech, and body mandalas respectively.
byams pa tshad med sogs tshangs pa'i gnas bzhi ni tshangs zur gyi rdo rje'i theg bzhi'o/ / lus tshor sems chos dran pa nyer gzhag bzhi rnams dag pas rtsa thig kun nas gru bzhi pa'o/ /

The four places of Brahmā,[216] immeasurable love, and so on are the four vajra gridlines. The four pure forms of the four foundations of mindfulness[217] of body, feelings, mind, and phenomena are the perfect squares of the gridlines.

d.div: [216] These are the meditations on the four immeasurables — love, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity — so called because Brahmā is said to reside within them, and their accomplishment results in birth in the Brahmā realms.
[217] dran pa nyer bzhag, smṛityupasthāna.

f.d: ma rig pa sogs rten 'brel yan lag bcu gnyis 'gags pas thugs gsung sku'i dkyil 'khor gyi sgo bcu gnyis so/ / 'phags pa'i sa bcu gnyis kyis rta babs bcu gnyis so/ /
The cessation of the twelve limbs of dependent origination, ignorance, and so on are the twelve gates of the mind, speech, and body mandalas. The twelve ārya levels are the twelve portals.

yang dag pa'i lta ba sogs 'phags lam yan lag brgyad dag pas phyogs dang phyogs mtshams brgyad kyi dur khrod brgyad rnams so/ / phyi nang stong pa nyid la sogs pa stong nyid bcu drug dag pas nang gi ka ba nag po bcu drug go/ /

The pure forms of the eight limbs of the noble path, right view, and so on are the eight cremation grounds of the eight directions. The pure forms of the sixteen kinds of emptiness, such as inner and outer emptiness and so on, are the sixteen black inner pillars.

khams lnga dag pas gzhal yas khang phyi nang dang steng 'og kun du brtsigs pa'o/ / gzugs can gzugs la lta ba'i rnam thar sogs rnam thar brgyad dag pas thugs gsung sku'i dkyil 'khor gsum gyi sgo khyud brgyad brgyad rnams te/ de yang / thugs gsung sku yi dbye bas so zhes pa nas/ sgo logs rnams nyid do/[180] /zhes pa'i bar la sbyar bar bya ba yin pas so/ /

The five pure elements are represented by the complete enclosure of the celestial palace above, below, outside, and inside. The pure forms of the eight freedoms, such as regarding form as form and so on,[218] are the eight protective porch walls on each of the mind, speech, and body mandalas.

d.div: [180] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 205_na5

[218] These are eight transforming meditative concentrations developed in order to reduce mental afflictions: regarding form as form, regarding formlessness as form, freedom from attachment to beauty, the four freedoms of the formless realm, and the freedom of cessation.

f.d: gzugs can gyi yon tan brgyad sa chu me rlung bzhi dri gzugs ro reg bya ste brgyad sgrib pa dang bral ba'i rnam dag gis dkyil 'khor gsum gyi sgo 'gram brgyad brgyad do/ / nyi ma'i yon tan rdul mun snying stobs gsum dang zla ba'i yon tan sgra dri ro reg bya gzugs lnga ste brgyad rnams dag pas dkyil 'khor gsum gyi sgo logs brgyad brgyad rnams nyid do/ /

The eight material qualities devoid of obscuration, which are the pure forms of earth, water, fire, air, smell, form, taste, and touch, are the eight facing door walls of the three mandalas. The pure forms of the three sun qualities of activity, darkness, and lightness,[219] and the five moon qualities of sound, smell, taste, touch, and form, are the eight side-door walls of the three mandalas.

d.div: [219] rajas, tamas, and sattva.

f.d: tshul khrims dang / la sogs pas ting nge 'dzin shes rab rnam par grol ba rnam par grol ba'i ye shes mthong ba'i phung po ste phung po lnga dag pas tshon kha dog lnga'o/ / nyan rang theg chen gyi theg pa gsum dag pas thugs dkyil gyi ra ba gsum mo/ /

The five pure aggregates of morality, meditative concentration, wisdom, freedom, and the gnosis of freedom are the five colors. The three pure vehicles of Hearer, Solitary Realizer, and Mahayana are the three surrounding walls of the mind mandala.

dad pa'i dbang po dang / sogs pas brtson 'grus dran pa ting nge 'dzin shes rab kyi dbang po rnams dag pas gsung dkyil gyi rwa ba lnga'o/ / dad pa brtson 'grus dran pa ting nge 'dzin shes rab kyi stobs rnams dag pas sku dkyil gyi rwa ba lnga'o/ / de ltar thugs gsung sku'i dkyil 'khor gsum gyi rwa ba rnams kyi dag pa'o/ /

The pure forms of the five forces of faith, effort, memory, meditative concentration, and wisdom are the five surrounding walls of the speech mandala. The pure forms of the five powers of faith, effort, memory, meditative concentration, and wisdom are the five surrounding walls of the body mandala. /304/ These are the pure forms of the walls of the mind, speech, and body mandalas.

dpa' bar 'gro ba nam mkha' mdzod rdo rje lta bu seng ge rnam bsgyings te ting nge 'dzin bzhi dang / tshig dang / don dang / sngags dang / bzod pa'i sgo gyur te gzungs bzhi rnams dag pa nyid kyis dkyil 'khor gsum la stegs bu ste/ pha rol tu phyin pa bcu rdzogs pa dag pas rin chen snam bu rin po che sna tshogs pa'i 'ching pas spras pas bkra ba'o/ / sangs rgyas kyi chos ma 'dres pa bco brgyad dag pas do shal dang do shal phyed pa rnams so/ /

The four pure meditative concentrations — the warrior, treasury of space, vajralike, and lion pose — plus the four pure meditative retentions, or dhāraṇī, of words, meanings, mantra, and forbearance are the terraces on the three mandalas. The ten pure perfections are the jeweled friezes studded and beautifully decorated with precious stones. The eighteen pure and exclusive qualities of a buddha are represented by the single and double hanging jeweled net garlands.

tshe/ las/ yo byad/ mos pa/ smon lam/ chos/ sems/ skye ba/ rdzu 'phrul/ ye shes la dbang ba'i dbang bcu dag pas phaku lI shar bu dang / dag pa bcu dag pas kra ma shIr Sha mda' yab dang / stong nyid/ mtshan med/ smon med/ mngon par 'du mi byed pa'i rnam thar bzhi dag pas dril bu'i sgra sgrogs pas gang ba dang / 'dun pa/ brtson 'grus/ sems/ dpyod pa'i rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa bzhi dag pas rgyal mtshan sna tshogs pas gtams pa dang / sdig pa ma skyes pa rnams ma skyed pa dang / skyes pa rnams spong ba dang / dge ba ma skyes pa rnams skyed pa dang / skyes pa rnams spel ba'i yang dag spong ba bzhi dag pas me long rab tu 'bar bas spras pa'o/ /

The ten pure powers: namely, power over life, karma, necessities, wishes, prayers, dharma, mind, birth, magical creation, and gnosis, are the phakulī,[220] or ornamented guttering. The ten pure virtues are the kramaśīraṣa, or parapets.[221] The pure forms of the four freedoms, namely, emptiness, no sign, no wish, and no activity, are the all-pervading chimes of bells. The pure forms of the four magical-power meditative concentrations, namely, aspiration, effort, mind, and investigation, are the profusion of victory banners. The four perfect eradications — namely, not developing those nonvirtues as yet undeveloped, eradicating those already developed, developing virtues not yet developed, and increasing those already developed — when purified are the decorative and shining mirrors.

d.div: [220] Transliterated in the verse as bagulī, but written here as phakulī. Identified in Tibetan as shar bu. Henning and Jado Rinpoché identify these as ornamented water outlets, drainpipes, or guttering.
[221] mda’ yab. Henning identifies this feature as parapets, battlements, or eaves.

f.d: dran pa/ chos rab tu rnam 'byed/ brtson 'grus/ dga' ba/ shin sbyangs/ ting nge 'dzin/ btang snyoms yang dag byang chub yan lag bdun dag pas rnga yab rnams g.yo ba'o/ mdo sde/ dbyangs bsnyad/ lung bstan/ tshigs bcad/ ched rjod/ gleng gzhi/ de lta bu byung ba/ skyes rabs/ shin tu rgyas pa ste gsung rab yan lag dgu dag pa'i ye shes me tog gi phreng ba sna tshogs pas brgyan pa'o/ /

The purification of the seven limbs of enlightenment, namely, memory, analysis, effort, joy, pliancy, meditative concentration, and equanimity, are the yaktail fans. The pure gnosis that produces the nine branches of scripture[222] — namely, sutras, occasional-verse teachings, specific prophecy, verse teachings, person-nonspecific teachings, person-specific teachings, stories, Buddha’s previous lives, and vast teachings — are the decorative profusion of flower garlands.

d.div: [222] Reduced from the twelve branches of scripture. Traditions vary on which of the nine are included.

f.d: sbyin pa/ tshig snyan/ don mthun/ don spyod de bsdu ba bzhi dag pas gzhal yas khang gi zur du sna tshogs rdo rjes brgyan pa'o/ / sdug kun 'gog lam ste bden pa bzhi dag pas rin chen bzhi rnams kyis sgo dang sgo khyud kyi mtshams su spras pa'o/ /

The purified forms of the four ways of gathering disciples, namely, giving, kind words, according with disciples’ behavior, and according with disciples’ wishes, are the decorative crossed vajras in the corners of the celestial mansion. The purified forms of the four truths of suffering, source, path, and cessation are the four jewels that decorate the gates and porch walls.

lha'i mig /lha'i rna ba/ gzhan gyi sems shes pa/ sngon gnas rjes su dran pa/ rdzu 'phrul gyi mngon shes te mngon shes lnga dag pas sa'i khor yug sogs khor yug chen po lngas bskor ba'o/ / rnam pa kun mkhyen pa'i byang chub dag pa phyi rol du rdo rje 'phreng bas legs par bskor ba'o/ / zag med kyi bde ba chen po'i bdag nyid du gnas pa'i rdo rje 'phreng ba'i lcags ri'o/ /

The purified forms of the fivefold clairvoyance, namely, celestial sight, celestial hearing, knowing the minds of others, remembering past lives, and knowledge of magical powers, are the five great surrounding circles, such as the earth circle and so on. The pure omniscient enlightenment is the outer encirclement by the vajra garland. /305/ The vajra-garlanded iron fence is in essence the uncontaminated great bliss.

de bzhin du ye shes lnga'i rang bzhin gyi rdo rje me lce 'bar bas bskor ba'o/ / shes rab dang thabs kyi cha gnyis dag pas dbang ldan du zla ba nya gang ba 'char ba dang / bden bral du nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor nub bzhin pa'o/ /

Similarly the vajra flames are in essence the five kinds of gnosis. The pure form of wisdom is the moon constantly shining in the northeast, and the pure form of method is the sun constantly shining in the southwest.

thugs gsung sku ye shes kyi rdo rje bzhi dag pas sku dkyil gyi rta babs la gnas pa'i chos kyi 'khor lo dang bum pa chen po dang rnga bo che chen po dang byang chub kyi shing ngo / / de bzhin du rdo rje bzhi po dag pas bde chen 'khor lor gnas pa'i yid bzhin gyi nor bu dang sogs pas dpag bsam gyi shing dang / chos kyi gaN+Di dang / chos kyi dung rnams so/ /

The pure forms of the mind, speech, body, and gnosis vajras are respectively the wheel of dharma, the great vase, the great drum, and the Bodhi tree that stand on ledges within the body mandala. The pure forms of the four vajras are also the wish-fulfilling jewel, wish-fulfilling tree, dharma gong, and dharma conch that stand within the great bliss mandala.

de ltar na rten gyi dkyil 'khor sna tshogs par shar ba 'di ni dpal ldan dus 'khor gyi nges don gyi dkyil 'khor chos kyi dbyings rnam par dag pa de nyid sgrib bral gyi yon tan phun tshogs sna tshogs pa kun dang ldan pa mtshon byed du bsgom par bya ba yin no/ /

Therefore this is a meditation to reveal these various aspects of the base mandala as the definitive and pure dharmadhātu mandala of glorious Kālacakra, endowed to perfection with every possible obscuration-free excellence.
gnyis pa brten pa lha'i rnam dag bsgom pa

d.i: Meditating on the purity of the resident deities

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis las/
This is in two sections: 1. Channel purity 2. Aggregate and sphere purity
dang po rtsa'i dag pa ni

sgrub le'i brgya gcig pa las/ bum pa rnams dang du ba la sogs brgyad po rnams kyis snying gar chos kyi 'khor lor rab tu 'gyur/ /zhes pa nas/ sor mo'i tshigs kyi mtshams la bya ba zhes byar 'gyur/[181] /zhes pa'i bar gyi rtsa 'grel rnams kyis ston te/ de yang snying ga'i rtsa 'dab brgyad dag pas bum pa brgyad dang nus ma brgyad do/ / dpral ba'i rtsa 'dab bcu drug dag pas gshegs pa bzhi yum dang bcas pa dang / gshegs ma bzhi yab dang bcas pa ste bcu drug go/ / gtsug tor gyi rtsa rtsa 'dab bzhi pa dag pas chos kyi dung dang nor bu dang chos kyi gaN+Di dang dpag bsam gyi shing ngo / / mgrin pa'i rtsa rtsa 'dab so gnyis pa dag pas sems dpa' drug yum dang bcas pa dang / sems ma drug yab dang bcas pa dang / khro bo bzhi yum dang bcas pa'i so gnyis so/ /

This is taught in verse 101 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter of the Condensed Tantra, from the line beginning “The vases and the eight, such as Dhūmā, are the dharma wheel at the heart” until “the finger joints.”[223] This is explained as follows. The purified forms of the eight channel petals of the heart are the eight vases and the eight śakti. The purified forms of the sixteen channel petals at the brow are the four male tathāgatas with consorts and the four female tathāgatas with consorts. The purified forms of the four channel petals at the crown are the dharma conch, the jewel, the dharma gong, and the wish-fulfilling tree. The purified forms of the thirty-two channel petals of the throat are the six male bodhisattvas with consorts, the six female bodhisattvas with consorts, and the four wrathful protectors with consorts.

d.div: [181] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka101_88_na2_'gyur cung mi mthun/
[223] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 101, 88a2.

f.d: lte ba'i rtsa rtsa 'dab drug cu rtsa bzhi pa dag pas gsung dkyil gyi 'khor gyi lha mo 'jigs ma sogs drug cu rtsa bzhi'o/ / gsang gnas kyi rtsa rtsa 'dab so gnyis pa dag pas tsa mu Na TA la sogs pa'i gsung dkyil gyi gtso mo brgyad dang / sgeg mo la sogs pa brgyad de bcu drug po thabs shes kyi dbye bas so gnyis so/ / lag pa dang rkang pa'i tshigs chen bcu gnyis kyi tshigs re re la rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab sum cu pa re re yod pa'i rtsa 'dab sum brgya drug cu dag pas tshes lha sum brgya drug cu'o/ / rkang lag gi sor mo'i tshigs kyi mtshams gyi rtsa sum cu pa tshan pa gnyis dang / khyab byed chen po gnyis te sum cu rtsa gnyis pa tshan pa gnyis dag pas klu brgyad gtum mo brgyad de bcu drug po thabs shes kyi ldog pa'i dbye bas so gnyis pa tshan pa gnyis so/ /

The purified forms of the sixty-four channel petals of the navel are the sixty-four goddesses, such as Bhīma and so on, of the speech mandala. The purified forms of the thirty-two channel petals of the secret area are the eight main goddesses, Cāmuṇḍi and so on, of the speech mandala and the eight offering goddesses, Lāsyā and so on, each in method and wisdom aspect to make thirty-two. The purified forms of the 360 channel petals arrived at by totaling the thirty petals on each of the twelve cakras of the twelve major arms and leg joints, are the 360 lunar-day deities. /306/ The purified forms of the two sets of thirty cakras on the finger and toe joints plus the two sets of two pervading channels are the sixteen figures of the eight nāgas and eight fierce females divided up twice into method and wisdom to make two sets of thirty-two.
gnyis pa phung khams sogs kyi dag pa ni/

sgrub le'i brgya gnyis pa'i phyed 'og ma dus kyi dag pas dpal ldan rdo rje can 'gyur zhes pa nas/ ba spu rnams kyis dur khrod sa gzhi la gnas 'byung po'i tshogs [182] zhes pa'i bar gyi rtsa 'grel rnams kyis bstan pa'i don ni de yang phyi rol gyi dus nyi mas khyim 'pho ba bcu gnyis dang / nang du rten 'brel yan lag bcu gnyis kyi rgyu dang 'bras bu'i chos 'phags pas rdo rje can dkyil 'khor gyi gtso bo dus kyi 'khor lo'o/ /

This is taught in the second half of verse 102 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter of the Condensed Tantra, from the line beginning “Time in its pure form is the vajra holder” up to “The body hairs are the host of spirits in the cemeteries.”[224] This is explained as follows. External time is the sun moving through the twelve houses, while internal time is the cause- and-effect phenomena of the twelve links of dependent origination. In their purified form these become the vajra holder Kālacakra, the main deity of the mandala.

d.div: [182] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka102_88_na4_nas 88_ba3
[224] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 102, 88a4 to 88b3.

f.d:
rten 'brel yan lag bcu gnyis rgyu dang 'brasabu ra 'gyur tshul ni 'di'i 'grel chen las/
nang du chu srin la sogs pa khyim gyi 'khor lo yan lag bcu gnyis kyi bdag nyid ni rgyu dang 'brasabu 'i bdag nyid de de la lnga ni rgyu'i chos so/ / bdun ni 'bras bu'i chos so/ / rgyu'i chos ni nyon mongs pa dang las kyi bdag nyid do/ / 'bras bu'i chos ni sdug bsngal gyi bdag nyid de 'jig rten khams kyi le'ur gsungs so/[183] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ma rig pa/ 'du byed/ sred pa/ len pa/ srid pa ste lnga po rgyu dang / rnam shes/ ming gzugs/ skye mched drugareg pa/ tshor ba/ skye ba/ rga shi ste bdun po 'bras bu'o/ /

The way the twelve links of dependent origination are causes and effects is explained by the Great Commentary:
Internally the twelve links of the cycles of houses, Capricorn and so forth, are of the nature of cause and effect. Five are causes, seven are effects. The causes have the nature of afflictions and karma. The effects have the nature of suffering. This is taught in the Realms chapter.[225] Thus ignorance, compositional karma, grasping, taking, and becoming are causes. Consciousness, name and form, the six sources, contact, feeling, birth, and aging and death are all effects.

d.div: [183] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 229_ba7
[225] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 229b7.

f.d: de dag rgyu 'bras su byas pa las 'khor bar 'khor tshul ni nyon mongs dang las kyi dbang gis 'khor bar 'khor ba yin la/ de yang ma rig pa dang sred pa dang len pa gsum nyon mongs dang / 'du byed dang srid pa gnyis la las zhes bya zhing / srid pa ni las kyi bag chags yang srid 'grub pa'i nus pa mthu can du song ba la las zhes btags pa tsam yin no/ /

The way that one circles in samsara within these causes and effects is as follows. Affliction and karma drive the cycle of samsara. From the twelve links, ignorance, grasping, and taking are afflictions, while compositional karma and becoming are karma. The link of becoming is the point when the seeds of karma gain in strength to develop the capacity to create a new birth and, therefore, is not actually karma but is merely labeled as such.

de la rgyu de dag gis 'bras bu de rnams 'byin tshul ni/ ma rig pa'i dbang gis 'du byed kyi las dge mi dge bsags/ 'du byed des rnam shes nas tshor ba'i bar 'grub rung du 'phangs pa'i tshul gyis sems rgyud kyi steng du bag chags bzhag bag chags de 'dod chags kyi ngo bo sred len gnyis kyis rim can du gsos btab pas bag chags de yang srid phyi ma skyed pa'i nus pa mthu can du gyur pa'i srid pa de grub/ srid pa de las ma'i mngal du nying mtshams sbyar ma thag pa'i rnam shes dang / de las ming gzugs dang / de las skye mched drug dang / de las reg pa dang / de las tshor ba rnams rim gyis 'byung ba yin no/ /

The way these effects are produced from these causes is as follows. Because of ignorance, virtuous and nonvirtuous compositional karma is accumulated. /307/ This compositional karma, which is capable of creating the links from consciousness to feeling through the process of impelling,[226] plants seeds on the mindstream. These seeds, nourished by the link of grasping and then by the link of taking, both of which have the nature of attachment, grow in strength and form the link of becoming, which has the capacity to create a future birth. From the link of becoming comes the link of consciousness that has just linked to a mother’s womb. From consciousness arises name and form, the six sources, contact, and feeling, all arising from preceding links.

d.div: [226] ’phangs pa. To cast, throw, impel; specifically, by planting a cause in the present, thereby “impelling” it’s effect in the future.

f.d:
de yang rnam shes nying mtshams sbyar ma thag pa'i gnas skabs la skye ba zhes dang / ming gzugs nas tshor ba'i bar gyi gnas skabs gzhan nas gzhan du 'gyur ba la rga ba zhes btags shing / shi ba ni srog 'gags pa la 'jog pa rgyud 'grel gyi dgongs pa yin pas slob dpon klu sgrub kyis rten 'brel snying por/
gsum po dag las gnyis 'byung zhing / / gnyis las bdun 'byung bdun las kyang / / gsum 'byung srid pa'i 'khor lo ni/ / yang dang yang du 'khor bar 'gyur/[184] / zhes gsungs pa dang dgongs pa gcig go/

The moment of the consciousness linking to a mother’s womb is known as birth, and the process of moving from name and form to feeling is labeled aging. Death is posited as the cessation of life. The above is the thinking of the tantra and commentary and therefore is at one with the thinking of Master Nāgārjuna when he says in his Verses on the Essence of Dependent Origination:
Two come from three, seven come from two, and three come from seven; this wheel of existence turns again and again.[227]

d.div: [184] sde dge_3836_bstan/ dbu ma/ tsarten 'brel snying po/ sh+loka3_146_ba3
[227] Toh 3836 Tengyur, dbu ma, tsa, v. 3, 146b3.

f.d: de ltar na dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog gi lha spro ba sogs gzhi dang chos mthun sbyor ba'i tshe/ ma rig pa dang 'du byed dang rnam par shes pa rnams zhes sogs kyis mngal gyi gnas skabs ma rig pa sogs rten 'brel gyi yan lag rnams dang sbyor bar gsungs pa'i ma rig pa sogs ni mngal du gnas pa'i gnas skabs kyi zla ba rnams la rten 'brel gyi yan lag de dang de'i ming gis btags pa yin la/ de'i rgyu mtshan yang gong du bshad pa ltar mngal du zhugs ma thag gi zla ba de zla ba gang yin yang chu srin gyi zla ba dang / de nas zla ba bdun pa de la mngal na gnas pa de'i lte ba'i rtsa 'dab tu rlung skye bas zla ba de la karka Ta'i zla ba zhes ming 'dogs la/ de ltar byas pa na mngal du zhugs ma thag gi zla ba de la ma rig pa zer zhing / de ltar byas pa'i tshe mngal du zhugs pa'i zla ba gnyis pa sogs la rim pa bzhin 'du byed dang rnam shes sogs zer bar grub bo/ / de yang chu srin gyi zla ba la ma rig pa'i zla ba zer ba ni rten 'brel yan lag bcu gnyis dang khyim zla bcu gnyis phyi nang sbyor ba'i tshe rten 'brel yan lag dang po dang mngal du zhugs pa'i khyim zla'i zla ba dang po sbyor dgos pas 'grel chen gyi skabs 'dir yang nang du chu srin la sogs pa khyim gyi 'khor lo yan lag bcu gnyis kyi bdag nyid ces gsungs pa dang / khams le'i brgya bcu gnyis pa las/ rgyal gyi zla bar nyi ma chu srin la son ma rig pa ste [185] zhes sogs gsungs pa yin no/ /

During the deity emanations of the sovereign-mandala deity, when a correlation is made with the ordinary base, the passage beginning “Ignorance, compositional karma, and consciousness” teaches that the length of time in the womb is applied to the links of dependent origination, in which the names of the links are given to the months of pregnancy. The reason for this is as follows. As previously explained, the month of conception, regardless of what the actual month might be, is known as the month of Capricorn. Seven months on from then, the winds are created in the navel channel petals, and therefore that month is known as the month of Cancer. Because of this the month of conception is known as the month of ignorance, and the following months of pregnancy are named compositional karma, consciousness, and so on. The reason why Capricorn is the month of ignorance is that when the twelve links of dependent origination and the twelve zodiacal months are assigned to each other as an internal and external correlation, the first of the twelve links and the first zodiacal month of pregnancy have to be assigned to each other, /308/ and in this part of the generation stage, the Great Commentary comments, “Internally, the zodiac cycle of Capricorn and so on are the twelve links,” while in verse 112 of the Realms chapter of the Condensed Tantra it says, “Ignorance is in the month of Puṣya when the sun enters Capricorn.”[228]

d.div: [185] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka113_34_na6
[228] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 113, 34a6

f.d:
'grel chen las/
de bzhin du yan lag bcu gnyis 'gags pas shes rab ma 'ang dag pa'o/[186] / zhes gsungs pa ltar rten 'brel yan lag bcu gnyis 'gags pas kyang sna tshogs yum mo/ /

The cessation of the twelve links of dependent origination is Viśvamātā. The Great Commentary states:
Similarly the cessation of the twelve links is the pure Prajñā.[229]

d.div: [186] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 330_na4
[229] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 330a4.

f.d: snying ga'i pad+mar gnas pa'i rtsa mnyam gnas la sogs pa'i rlung rnams kyi rten du gyur pa'i rtsa brgyad dag pas du ba ma sogs brgyad dang a wa ng+hU tI dang dung can ma dag pa'i cha rnam gcad kyis mtshon pa'i ye shes kyi khams ma ye shes kyi pha rol tu phyin ma dang / thig les mtshan pa'i nam mkha'i khams ma sher phyin ma ste nus ma bcu'o/ /

The purified forms of the eight channels at the heart, which are the supports for the equalizing wind and so on, are the eight śakti, Dhūmā and so forth. The purified forms of the two parts of the central channel, avadhūtī above and śaṅkhinī below, are the two other śakti, Jñānapāramitā of the gnosis element, symbolized by the visarga, and Prajñāpāramitā of the space element, symbolized by the drop.

dug gsum nga rgyal dang bcas pa'i nyon mongs pa bzhi zad pas zhabs g.yon pa'i 'og tu drag po'o/ / nyon mongs 'chi bdag phung po lha'i bu'i bdud de bdud bzhi zad pas zhabs g.yas pa'i 'og tu bdud do/ / lus kyi sgrib pa zad pas dung dang / ngag gi sgrib pa zad pas gaN+Di dang / sems kyi sgrib pa zad pas nor bu dang / ye shes kyi sgrib pa zad pas dpag bsam gyi shing ngo / / de bzhin du g.yas g.yon gyi rkang 'gags pas shar gyi bum pa gnyis/ 'og ma rnams la'ang g.yas g.yon zhes sbyar te khrag 'gags pas lho'i bum pa gnyis/ gci ba mi 'dzag pas byang gi bum pa gnyis/ bshang ba mi 'dzag pas nub kyi bum pa gnyis/ khu ba mi 'dzag pas steng du rgyal ba'i bum pa'o/ / rdul mi 'dzag pas rnam par rgyal ba'i bum pa 'og tu'o/ / de yang dkyil 'khor la dngos su bkod pa brgyad dang rgyal rnam rgyal gnyis ni khyab byed do/ /

The ending of pride and the three poisons is Rudra under the left foot. The ending of the four kinds of māras, namely mental afflictions, lord of death, the aggregates, and Devaputra, is Māra under the right foot. The ending of obstructions to the body is the conch. The ending of obstructions to speech is the gong. The ending of obstructions to mind is the jewel. The ending of obstructions to gnosis is the wish-fulfilling tree. The cessation of the right and left bone marrow is represented by the two vases in the east. Assigning left and right to the following also, the cessation of blood is symbolized by the two vases of the south. The nonemission of urine is illustrated by the two vases of the north, and the nonemission of excrement by the two vases of the west. The nonemission of seminal fluid is illustrated by the upper vase, the nonemission of menstrual blood by the lower. Eight vases are actually placed in the mandala, while the jaya and vijaya vases pervade them all.

de bzhin du 'du byed tshor ba 'du shes gzugs rnam shes kyi phung po rnams kyi sgrib pa zad cing rnam par dag pas rim pa bzhin don grub rin 'byung snang mtha' rnam snang mi bskyod pa rnams so/ / ye shes nam mkha' rlung me chu sa'i khams rnams kyi sgrib pa zad cing rnam par dag pas rim pa bzhin sna tshogs yum rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma sgrol ma gos dkar mo mA ma kI spyan ma rnams so/ / rna ba sna mig lce lus yid rnams kyi sgrib pa zad cing rnam par dag pas rim pa bzhin phyag rdor nam snying sa snying 'jig rten dbang phyug sgrib sel kun tu bzang po rnams so/ /

The purification and freedom from obscuration of the aggregates of compositional factors, feelings, recognition, form, and consciousness are Amoghasiddhi, Ratnasambhava, Amitābha, Vairocana, and Akṣobhya respectively. The purified and obscuration-free elements of gnosis, space, air, fire, water, and earth are Viśvamātā, Vajradhātvīśvarī, Tārā, Pāṇḍarā, Māmakī, and Locanā respectively. The purification and freedom from obscuration of the ear, nose, eyes, tongue, body, and mind /309/ are Vajrapāṇi, Khagarbha, Kṣitigarbha, Lokeśvara, Viṣkambhī, and Samantabhadra respectively.
sgra dri ro gzugs reg bya chos kyi skye mched rnams rnam par dag pas rim pa bzhin sgra rdo rje ma dri rdo rje ma ro rdo rje ma gzugs rdo rje ma reg bya rdo rje ma chos dbyings rdo rje ma rnams so/ /
The purified sources of sound, smell, taste, form, touch, and phenomena are Śabdavajrā, Gandhavajrā, Rasavajrā, Rūpavajrā, Viśvamātā, and Dharmadhātuvajrā respectively.

dad pa'i stobs brtson 'grus kyi stobs dran pa'i stobs ting nge 'dzin gyi stobs shes rab kyi stobs rnams rnam par dag pas rim pa bzhin gtsug tor bgegs mthar byed shes rab mthar byed pad+ma mthar byed gshin rje mthar byed de khro bo'i rgyal po rnams so/ / de bzhin du b+ha ga ngag lag pa rkang pa bshang lam gyi dbang po rnams rnam par dag pas rim pa bzhin gnod mdzes dbyug sngon can 'dod rgyal mi g.yo ba stobs po che rnams so/ / las kyi dbang po'i bya ba rnams rnam par dag pas drag spyan ma la sogs pa khro bo'i lha mo rnams so/ / thun tshod brgyad dag pas tsA muN DA la sogs pa'i gsung dkyil gyi gtso mo brgyad do/ /

The purified forms of the powers of faith, effort, memory, concentration, and wisdom are the wrathful protectors Uṣṇīṣa, Vighnantaka, Prajñā taka, Padmantaka, and Yamāntaka respectively. The purified forms of the organs of the female organ, speech, arms, legs, and anus are Sumbha, Nīla daṇḍa, Takkirāja, Acala, and Mahābala respectively. The purified forms of the organ faculties are the wrathful goddesses, Raudrākṣī and so forth. The purified forms of the eight periods are the eight main goddesses of the speech mandala, Cāmuṇḍi and so forth.

zhag gcig gi dus sbyor bcu gnyis kyi chu tshod drug cu'i rlung 'bab pa'i rtsa 'dab drug cu dang / stong pa'i rtsa bzhi ste lte ba sprul pa'i 'khor lo sgrib pa zad cing dag pas 'jigs ma la sogs pa'i gsung dkyil gyi 'khor gyi lha mo drug cu rtsa bzhi'o/ /

The purified forms of the sixty channel petals carrying the winds of the sixty hours of the twelve lagna or ascendants of one day, plus the four empty channels to make up the sixty-four channel petals of the navel or emanation cakra, are Bhīma and so on, the sixty-four goddesses of the speech mandala.

nag pa'i zla ba sogs zla ba bcu gnyis sgrib pa zad cing dag pas bden bral dang rlung dang me lha dang gdong drug dang rgya mtsho dang tshogs kyi dbang po dang brgya byin dang tshangs pa dang drag po dang gnod sbyin dang khyab 'jug dang gshin rje ste tshes lha'i gtso bo bcu gnyis so/ / nang du chu tshod gcig gi dbugs kyi grangs sum brgya drug cu dang / lo gcig gi zhag sum brgya drug cu dag pas pad+ma'i 'dab mar gnas pa'i tshes lha'i 'khor sum brgya sum cu rtsa drug/ gtso mo bcu gnyis/ sgeg mo la sogs pa bcu gnyis te sum brgya drug cu'o/ / gsang gnas kyi rtsa sum cu rtsa gnyis rnam par dag pas klu brgyad dang rab gtum ma brgyad de de dag thabs shes kyi dbye bas sum cu rtsa gnyis po rnams so/ /

The purified and obscuration-free forms of the twelve months of Caitra and so on are the twelve main lunar-day deities — Nairtya, Vāyu, Agni, Śaṇmukha, Samudra, Gaṇapati, Śakra, Brahmā, Rudra, Yakṣa, Viṣṇu, and Yama. The purified forms of the 360 breaths of one hour and the 360 days of one year are the 336 entourage deities of the lunar-day deities plus the twelve consorts of the lunar-day deities and the twelve goddesses of the mind mandala, Lāsyā and so forth. The pure forms of the thirty-two channel petals of the secret area are the eight nāgas and eight fierce females, each in method and wisdom aspect, to make thirty-two.

yon tan gyi dbang gis lus kyi bya ba sa slog pa sogs kyi sgrib pa zad cing dag pas 'dod ma so drug dang phyir 'dod ma so drug rnams so/ / skra rnams dag pas grub pa rnams so/ / ba spu bye ba phrag phyed dang bzhi dag pas dur khrod du 'byung po bye ba phrag phyed dang bzhi'o/ /

In terms of their qualities, the purified and unobstructed forms of bodily actions, such as digging in the earth, are the thirty-six desire goddesses and the thirty-six nondesire goddesses. Hairs in their purified forms are the siddhas. The purified forms of the thirty-five million pores are the thirty-five million elementals in the cemeteries. /310/

de ltar bshad pa'i rten dang brten pa'i rnam dag 'di la/ phung sogs rnam par dag pa'i zag med kyi chos rnams rten brten pa'i dkyil 'khor du shar ba rnams dngos gnas la rten dang brten pa'i dkyil 'khor du grub pa cig dang / dngos gnas la rten dang brten pa'i dkyil 'khor du ma grub kyang de ltar grub par mos nas sgom pa gnyis las / dang po ni ston pa shAkya thub pas dkyil 'khor gyi gtso bo dus kyi 'khor lo'i rnam par mdzad nas dus kyi 'khor lo'i sku gsung thugs kyi rten dang brten pa'i dkyil 'khor sprul pa lta bu yin no/ /

In the purity of the base mandalas and dependent deities as explained here, the purified and untainted forms of the aggregates and so on appear in the forms of these mandalas and deities. On this point, there are those phenomena that actually exist as the base mandalas and dependent deities and those that, while not actually existing that way, are meditated on as being so. The first type is illustrated by Śākyamuni in the form of the Kālacakra, lord of the mandala, manifesting the body, speech, and mind mandalas of the Kālacakra mandala.

gnyis pa ni bskyed rim sgom pa'i sgrub pa pos rang nyid gtso bo dus kyi 'khor lo'i nga rgyal la gnas pas sbyang gzhi rtsa dang phung sogs dag pa'i zag med kyi chos rnams rten dang brten pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi rnam par shar bar mos nas sgom pa ste 'di ni rten dang brten pa'i rnam dag sgom pa'i don yin no/ /

For the second type, the generation-stage meditator dwells in the pride of being Kālacakra, lord of the mandala, visualizing and meditating upon the bases of purification, such as the aggregates, channels, and so forth, appearing as the pure and untainted phenomena of the base mandalas and dependent deities. This is the meaning of the meditation upon the purity of the base mandalas and dependent deities.

des na 'grel chen las/ khams rnams 'gags pas khams gzhan de rnams rnam par dag pas 'gyur ro [187] zhes dang / gzugs gzhan la sogs pa dang mig gzhan la sogs pa de rnams [188]zhes sogs skabs 'di dag tu gzhan zhes gsungs pa rnams ni bskyed rim pa'i sgrub pa po'i blo ngor shar ba'i rten dang brten pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi rnam pa la bya dgos shing / khyad par du yang 'grel chen las/
'dir kun rdzob kyi chos 'gags par gyur pa na 'du byed gzhan la sogs pa de rnams so/ / des na rnam par dag pa'i 'du byed ni don yod grub pa ste 'du byed kyi sgrib pa zad pas so/[189] / zhes gsungs pa 'di dag gi [190] 'du byed gzhan zhes pa 'dis 'du byed lha gang du bsgom pa'i bskyed rim gyi lha bstan cing / sogs pas tshor ba gzhan dang 'du shes gzhan tshor ba dang 'du shes sogs lha gang du bsgom pa'i bskyed rim pa'i lha bstan la/ de'i rgyu mtshan ni/ des na zhes sogs 'grel tshig 'og mas ston te/ de yang 'du byed ni don yod grub pa ste zhes pa'i don yod grub pa ni bskyed rim gyi lha don grub la byed dgos pa'i phyir te/ skabs 'di'i rgyud 'grel rnams bskyed rim gyi dag pa bsgom pa'i skabs yin pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar na rigs pa 'di 'og ma rnams la'ang sbyar ro/ /

Therefore, when the Great Commentary says, “With the cessation of the elements, the pure other elements arise”[230] and “The other forms and so forth, the other eyes and so forth,”[231] the term other in this context must refer to the aspects of the base mandalas and dependent deities that appear to the mind of the generation-stage practitioner. In particular the Great Commentary says:
When conventional phenomena have ceased, there are other compositional factors and so forth. Therefore the pure compositional factors are Amoghasiddhi, the end of obscuration to compositional factors.[232] “Other compositional factors” of this passage indicates the generation-stage deity that the aggregate of compositional factors is to be visualized as. The phrase “and so forth” refers to “other feelings” and “other recognition,” which indicate the generation-stage deities that the aggregates of feeling and recognition are to be visualized as. The reason why this has to be the explanation of the term other is stated in the part of the quote beginning “Therefore the pure compositional factors are Amoghasiddhi.” The Amoghasiddhi mentioned here must be the generation-stage deity Amoghasiddhi, because this part of the tantra and commentary deals with the purity meditation of the generation stage. This reasoning can be applied to the other phenomena of the purity meditation also.
