f.d: gzhan yang sgrub le'i zhe bdun pa'i 'grel chen las/ 'dir phyi 'jig rten gyi

Furthermore the Great Commentary, on the forty-seventh verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
Here the emanation and withdrawal of the world-realm outer, the bodily inner, and imputed other mandalas.[233] /311/

d.div: [233] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 216b4.

f.d: khams dang nang lus dang gzhan btags pa'i dkyil 'khor la spro ba dang bsdu ba ni [191] zhes phyi nang gzhan gsum gyi gzhan 'di bskyed rim gyi skabs su btags pa'i dkyil 'khor la zhes blos btags pa'i bskyed rim gyi rten dang brten pa'i dkyil 'khor la gsal ba na gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / rgyu mtshan de bas na dus kyi 'khor lo'i rgyud rtsa 'grel las/ gzhan zhes gsungs pa thams cad bde gshegs snying po rtag brtan kho na la go bar mi bya'o/ /[192]

The “other” mandalas mentioned here clearly refer to the base mandalas and dependent deities imputed or mentally conceived during the generation stage. Because of these reasons, every instance of the term “other” in the Kālacakra tantra and commentary should not be understood as referring to a permanent and unchanging tathāgata essence.[234]

d.div: [191] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 216_ba4
[192] lunga'adi phal cher jo nang pa'i mkhas pa rnams la dgongs pa min nam snyam/
[234] Previous Jonang masters have interpreted this “other” as referring to Shentong, or extrinsic emptiness, in the form of an eternal tathāgata essence.

f.d: gsum pa thugs rdo rje sgrub pa'i yan lag bshad pa/
24. The Mind Vajra
thig le spro ba dang chos mthun par thig le'i rnal 'byor sgom pa thugs rdo rje sgrub pa'i yan lag bshad pa

d.i: The branch of mind-vajra accomplishment, a meditation on drop yoga correlating with the expansion of the drop

f.d: ['di ]la/ gzhan gyi lugs mdor bsdus nas brjod de 'thad mi 'thad dpyad pa dang / rang gi lugs gzhag pa'o/ /
This has two outlines: 1. A brief description of the assertions of others and examination of their validity 2. Our own assertions
dang po [gzhan gyi lugs ]ni

d.i: A brief description of the assertions of others and examination of their validity

f.d: mkhas pa kha cig(rje ku mA ra/)skabs 'di'i phra thig la bskyed rdzogs gnyis su mdzad de bskyed rim ni las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas thig le nor bu'i bar du 'ongs te slar yang rlung stobs kyis gyen du gshegs te thig le yas babs mas brtan zo chu'i 'phrul 'khor lta bu la yang dang yang du sbyangs pa las gang gi tshe 'jig rten pa'i lhan cig skyes pa brtan por gyur pa yang bskyed rim gyi thig le'i rnal 'byor dang / phyag rgya chen po la brten pa'i phra thig ni rdzogs pa'i rim pa'i phra thig yin par bzhed cing / skabs 'dir 'grel chen du rtsa rgyud drangs pa'i/ bcu drug lo lon rigs can ma/[193] /zhes sogs sbyor ba yan lag drug nyid ston byed du 'chad par mdzad do/[194] /

Some scholars (such as the master Kumāra[235]) assert the subtle and drop yogas as taught here to be both generation-stage and completion-stage meditations. They maintain that the generation stage involves relying upon an activity mudrā consort to move the drop to the jewel and then to draw it up by the power of the winds. This “waterwheel” descent and ascent is practiced again and again until the worldly innate bliss becomes stable. This, they maintain, is the drop yoga of the generation stage, while drop yoga and subtle yoga using a mahāmudrā consort are yogas of the completion stage. They also explain the Root Tantra line “A qualified consort aged sixteen” as teaching the six-branched yoga.

d.div: [193] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba2
[194] 'dir gong du zhus pa ltar yig chung du ku mA ra zhes byung ba 'go lo gzhon nu dpal yin snyam pas des mdzad pa'i dus 'khor rgyud kyi dka' 'grel la dgongs sam snyam yang dpyad/
[235] Probably Kumāraśrī Shönu Pal Gö Lotsāwa.

f.d: las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas thig le nor bu'i bar du babs pa rlung stobs kyis steng du drangs pa las byung ba'i lhan skyes bskyed rim yin pa mi 'thad de/ de 'dra ba'i lhan skyes skye ba la rnal 'byor gyis rlung dbu mar 'jug nus pa cig dgos shing / rnal 'byor gyis rlung dbu mar zhugs pa'i stobs kyis byung ba'i lhan skyes kyi bde ba yin na bskyed rim yin pa 'gal ba'i phyir te/ bskyed rim la rlung dbu mar 'jug pa'i thabs ma bshad pa'i phyir dang / rlung stobs kyis khams byang chub kyi sems zo chu'i 'khrul 'khor ltar yas babs mas brtan yang dang yang sbyong ba'i rnal 'byor ni rdzogs rim du 'jog dgos pa'i phyir ro/ /

It is not correct to say that the practice of relying on an activity mudrā consort to move the drop down to the jewel and then through the force of the winds to draw it up again to produce innate bliss is a generation-stage meditation, because the development of such an innate bliss requires the ability through yoga to move the winds into the central channel, and the innate bliss produced from the winds entering the central channel cannot be a generation-stage practice. This is because a method for moving the winds into the central channel is not taught in the generation stage, /312/ and the yoga in which the bodhicitta element ascends and descends again and again like a waterwheel using the power of the winds must be within the completion stage.

bcu drug lo lon zhes sogs sbyor drug nyid ston byed du mdzad pa yang legs par ma go ste/ 'grelachen las
'dir bskyed pa'i rim pa thams cad la sku rdzogs pa ni dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog go/ / gsung rdzogs pa ni las rgyal mchog ste/ las kyi dbang po bya ba la 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ / byang chub sems kyi thig le rdzogs pa ni thig le'i rnal 'byor ro/ / khu ba 'pho ba las bde ba la dmigs pa ni phra mo'i rnal 'byor te [195] zhes skabs 'di'i phra thig gi rnal 'byor bskyed rim du bshad cing / 'di'i phra thig de ltar bsgom pa'i shes byed du rtsa rgyud kyi lung / bcu drug lo lon rigs can ma/[196] /zhes sogs drangs pa yin pas so/ /

Furthermore it is hard to understand how the line “A qualified consort aged sixteen”[236] teaches the six-branched yoga. The Great Commentary says:
In the generation stages the completion of the enlightened body is within the sovereign mandala. The completion of enlightened speech is within the sovereign activities, because the action faculties engage in activity. The completion of the drops of bodhicitta is within the drop yoga. Bliss arising from the movement of the fluid is within the subtle yoga.[237] This passage explains that the subtle and drop yogas as taught here are generation-stage practices, and the Root Tantra line “A qualified consort aged sixteen”[238] is quoted here as scriptural authority for this way of meditating on the subtle and drop yoga at this time.

f.d: gnyis pa rang gi lugs gzhag pa
Our own assertions
['di ]la gnyis/ sbyang gzhi dang chos mthun sbyor tshul bshad pa dang / rnal 'byor pas nyams su len tshul rtsa rgyud kyi lung dang sbyar nas bshad pa'o/ /
This is under two headings: 1. Correlation with bases of purification 2. An explanation of the practice based upon Root Tantra quotes
dang po [sbyang gzhi dang chos mthun sbyor tshul bshad pa ]ni

byis pa skyes nas lo bcu drug lon ba'i tshe khams kyi nus pa rdzogs te thig le 'byin pa'i bde ba don du gnyer ba'i sgo nas bag ma len pa dang de'i lag pa nas 'dzin pa sogs byed pa dang chos mthun par dbang gi dus su slob dpon gyis slob ma la shes rab ma gtod par byed do/ khra thig sgom pa'i rnal 'byor pas las kyi phyag rgya dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya ci rigs pa bsten par byed pa yin zhing / gzhi dus su lo bcu drug yan chad lon pa des phyag rgya dang snyoms 'jug byas pas gsang gnas nas gtum mo phal pa 'bar bas thig le zhu ba sbyi bo nas rim gyis rtags kyi rtser babs pa la brten nas bde ba gong 'phel du byung ba dang chos mthun par phyag rgya gnyis gang yang rung ba la brten nas khams byang chub kyi sems spyi bo nas rdo rje'i rtse'i bar du babs pa'i dga' ba bzhi stong pa nyid dang sbyor ba'i thig le'i rnal 'byor sgom pa yin no/ /

When a child reaches the age of sixteen, the power of his white element is complete. Seeking the bliss that comes from emission of the drop, he takes a bride and leads her by the hand and so forth. In correlation with this the vajra master gives a wisdom mudrā consort to the student during the initiation. Yogis meditating on the subtle and drop yogas will rely upon an activity or wisdom mudrā consort as appropriate. In normal existence, from the age of sixteen onward, a man sits in union with a mudrā, and the common caṇḍālī fire blazes from the secret area. The drop melts and gradually descends from the crown to the tip of the organ, thereby increasing the bliss. In correlation with this the bodhicitta element descends from the crown to the tip of the vajra through reliance on one of the two types of mudrās and produces the four joys, which are applied to meditation upon emptiness. This is drop yoga meditation.
gnyis pa rnal 'byor pas nyams su len tshul rtsa rgyud kyi lung dang sbyar nas bshad pa ni/

d.i: An explanation of the practice based upon Root Tantra quotes

f.d: rgyud 'grel las skabs 'di'i bskyed rim gyi phra thig sgom tshul gsungs pa 'di ni gtso bor rgyud kyi ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo tshe gcig la rdo rje 'chang gi go 'phang mngon du byed pa'i rin po che lta bu'i gang zag gis bskyed rim rags pa'i lha'i rnal 'byor mthar phyin nas phra thig sgom pa'i dbang du byas pa yin pas de'i dbang du byas nas bshad par bya ste/ de yang de lta bu'i gang zag des thog mar thig le'i rnal 'byor sgom pa la 'jug pa'i tshe phyag rgya gnyis gang rung la brten nas 'jug go/ /

The teachings from the tantra and commentary on the meditations of the subtle and drop yogas of the generation stage in this part of the text are intended for the primary disciples of the tantra. /313/ These are jewellike persons destined in one life to actualize the state of Vajradhara. They complete the deity yoga of the coarse generation stage and then meditate on the subtle and drop yogas. The explanation from the tantra, therefore, is given on this basis. Such a person enters the practice of drop yoga by relying upon one of the two types of consort.

de ltar 'jug pa'i tshe las kyi phyag rgya la brten pa yin na/
bcu drug lo lon rigs can ma/ / gzugs dang lang tshos brgyan pa la/ / dang por legs par bslab byas nas/ / dbang bskur nas ni sgrub pa brtsam/[197] / zhes gsungs pa ltar lo bcu drug mas mtshon pa'i bcu gnyis ma nas nyi shu ma'i bar gzugs dang lang tshos brgyan pa phyag rgya'i mtshan nyid tshang ba btsal te/ de dang por lam thun mong ba sogs bslab pa'i gnas rnams la legs par bslab/ de ltar bslabs pa'i rjes su dbang bskur nas sngags sdom dang ldan par byas te lha'i rnal 'byor sgom pa la bslab bo/ / de nas thig le'i rnal 'byor gyi sgrub pa brtsam mo/ /

If he uses an activity consort, the Root Tantra says:
A qualified consort aged sixteen, adorned with youth and beauty; teach her well, then initiate and begin the practice.[239] A mudrā consort should be sought. She should have all the right characteristics of youth and beauty and be between the ages of twelve and twenty, as indicated by the phrase “aged sixteen.” She should be taught thoroughly the fundamental points of practice, receive initiation, be given tantric vows, and be instructed in the deity-yoga meditation. Then the practice of drop yoga can begin.

d.div: [197] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba2
[239] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 233b2.

f.d:
de yang tshul ji ltar brtsam na/
sku gsung thugs dang chags pa ni/ / dpral pa la sogs rnams la dgod/ / swAhA gsang ba gtsug tor cher/[198] / zhes gsungs pa ltar rang gtso bo dus kyi 'khor lo dang / yum las kyi phyag rgya dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya gang yin yang sna tshogs yum du gsal ba'i yab yum gnyis ka'i dpral ba dang / la sogs pa snying ga dang mgrin pa dang lte ba rnams la rim pa bzhin sku rdo rje oM dang / gsung rdo rje AHdang / thugs rdo rje hU~M dang / ye shes rdo rje hoHyig rnams dgod cing / swA gsang gnas dang / hA gtsug tor la dgod do/ /

What is the procedure of practice?
Body, speech, mind, and desire, placed at the brow and so forth, svā, hā, at the secret and crown.[240] Oneself is clearly visualized as main-deity Kālacakra, and the activity consort or wisdom consort as Viśvamātā. At the brow, heart, throat, and navel of both mother and father are placed the oṃ body vajra, the āḥ speech vajra, the hūḥ mind vajra, and the hoṃ gnosis vajra. The syllable svā is placed in the secret area and hā at the crown.

d.div: [198] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba2
[240] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 233b2.

f.d:
de nas mkha' gsang sbyong ba ni/
de nas pad+ma rnam par sbyang /[199] / zhes mdor bstan nas/ sbyor tshul dngos ni/
AHyig pad+ma 'dab brgyad pa/ / hU~M yig gis ni rdo rjer ldan/ / de ltar rdo rje dang bcas pa'i/ / shes rab pad+ma skyong rgyu las/ / hU~M gis rang gi rdo rje ni/ / rtse mo lnga par rnam par bsgom/ / de dbus pad+ma 'dab brgyad pa/ / A yig gis ni rab tu brtag[200] / ces gsungs pa ltar yum gyi gsang gnas mi dmigs pa'i ngang las AH yis te AHlas pad+ma 'dab ma brgyad pa/ de'i lte bar hU~M yig gis ni ste hU~M las byung ba'i rdo rje ldan pa ste rdo rje mtshan pa bsgom zhing de ltar rdo rje dang bcas pa ste rdo rjes mtshan pa'i shes rab ma'i pad+ma skyod par byed pa'i rgyu las te rgyur/ hU~M gis te hU~M las rang gtso bor gsal ba'i gsang gnas mi dmigs pa'i ngang las rdo rje ni rtse mo lnga par rnam par bsgoms nas/ rdo rje de'i dbus su pad+ma 'dab ma brgyad pa AHyig gis te AHyig las rab tu byung ba brtag pa ste bsgom mo/ /

Next is the purification of the secret space:
Then the lotus is purified.[241] This is an introduction. The next lines teach the actual purification:
From the syllable āṃ, an eight-petal lotus; by the syllable hūḥ, it is with vajra; the cause of movement of the wisdom lotus with vajra, one’s vajra by the syllable hūḥ visualized with five points; in its center an eight-petal lotus conceived with the syllable āṃ.[242] From the nonapprehension of the secret area of the consort arises the letter āṃ. This becomes a lotus of eight petals. Its center is “with vajra,” which means marked with a vajra that arises from or “by the syllable hūḥ.” Then “by the syllable hūḥ” or from a hūḥ within the nonapprehension of one’s secret area while clearly visualizing oneself as the main deity, a vajra “visualized with five points,” which is “the cause of movement of the wisdom lotus with vajra.” /314/ In the center of this vajra is an eight-petal lotus “conceived with the syllable āṃ,” meaning visualized as arising from the syllable āṃ.

d.div: [199] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba3
[200] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba3
[241] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 233b3.
[242] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 233b3.

f.d:
de ltar mkha' gsang sbyangs nas las la sbyor ba ni/
de ltar rdo rje pad+ma dang / / bcas pa byas nas pad+mar gzhug / de nas rdo rje 'dzin pa'i bsnyems/ / 'dzin cing rnal 'byor hU~M phaT bya/ / b+ha gar ling ga rab bkod nas/ / byang chub sems ni spro mi bya/[201] / zhes gsungs pa ltar de ltar rang gi gsang gnas rdo rje rtse lnga pa pad+mas mtshan pa dang bcas pa byas nas yum gyi pad+mar gzhug go/ /

That is the purification of the secret organs. Now the practice:
With the pride of vajra holder, the vajra with lotus enters the lotus. With liṅgam placed into the bhaga, the yogi performs hūḥ phaṭ; the bodhicitta is not emitted.[243] One’s own secret-area five-pointed vajra marked with a lotus enters the consort’s lotus.

d.div: [201] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba4
[243] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 233b4.

f.d: de ltar 'jug pa de'i ngang nas rang nyid rdo rje 'dzin pa gtso bo dus kyi 'khor lo'i bsnyems pa ste nga rgyal 'dzin pas rnal 'byor pa'i ngag tu hU~M phaT ces brjod cing snyoms par 'jug pa'i las la gnas par bya'o/ / de ltar yum gyi b+ha gar yab kyi ling ga rab tu bkod nas snyoms 'jug byas pa las khams byang chub kyi sems thig le nor bu'i rtse'i bar babs pa phyi rol du spro bar mi bya'o/ /

Within that state the yogi holds the pride of being the vajra holder main-deity Kālacakra, he utters the syllables hūḥ phaṭ, and dwells within the activity of union arising from placing the father’s liṅgam into the mother’s bhaga. This brings the elemental bodhicitta drop down to the tip of the jewel, where it is not to be emitted.

yab yum snyoms 'jug byas pa las byang sems spyi bo nas nor bu'i rtse'i bar du 'bab tshul dang de las dga' bzhi skye ba'i tshul ston pa ni/
lte bar gtum mo 'bar ba yis/ / de bzhin gshegs pa lnga sreg cing / / spyan ma mig la sogs pa yang / / bsregs nas ri bong can haM 'dzag / bdud rtsi khu ba'i chos can ni/ / thig le'i gzugs kyis 'jig par byed/ / thig le'i rnal 'byor zhes par grags/[202] / zhes gsungs pa'i don bsdus rgyud rtsa 'grel gyis 'chad pa ltar bskyed rim rags pa sgom pa'i gnas skabs su lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi khyim gyi rtsa 'dab bcu gnyis dang dkyil 'khor drug cu 'bab ba'i rtsa 'dab drug cu ste bdun cu rtsa gnyis gsung dkyil gyi rnal 'byor ma bdun cu rtsa gnyis bsgoms pas sbyangs shing byin gyis brlabs pa las yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa'i rkyen gyis gtum mo'i me 'bar ba yis lte ba sprul pa'i 'khor lo rnam par snang mdzad la sogs pa de bzhin gshegs pa lnga'i rlung g.yon la gnas pa'i dkyil 'khor lnga dang / spyan ma la sogs pa g.yas la gnas pa'i dkyil 'khor lnga'i rlung dang / mig la sogs pa'i dbang po rnams dang / gzugs la sogs pa'i yul rnams rang rang gi bya ba byed pa re zhig bkag ste bsregs nas spyi bo'i haM yig las ri bong can byang chub kyi sems 'dzags te de yang bdud rtsi khu ba'i chos can de ni thig le'i gzugs kyis nor bu'i rtse'i bar du 'dzag par byed do/ /

The way the bodhicitta travels down from the crown to the tip of the jewel during this union and how the four joys are created from that process is taught in the next lines:
At the navel the caṇḍālī fire blazes, the five tathāgatas are burnt, Locanā, eyes, etc., are burnt, the haṃ moon syllable falls with the characteristics of nectar fluid, in the form of a drop it descends. This is drop yoga.[244] These lines can be explained in accord with the Condensed Tantra and commentary. When meditating on the coarse generation stage, seventy-two channel petals, consisting of the twelve zodiac channel petals of the navel cakra and the sixty channel petals that carry the sixty mandala winds, are purified and blessed by meditation upon seventy-two yoginīs of the speech mandala. From these and from mother and father in union, the caṇḍālī fire blazes, and at the emanation navel cakra, the mandala winds of the five tathāgatas, Vairocana and so forth, on the left, the five mandala winds of Locanā and so forth on the right, the five sense organs of the eyes and so forth, the five objects of form and so forth, are all “burnt,” /315/ meaning that they are temporarily halted from performing their individual functions. The moon bodhicitta arises from the syllable haṃ at the crown and falls.

d.div: [202] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba5
[244] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 233b5.

f.d: de ltar spyi bo nas nor bu'i rtse'i bar babs pa de las spyi bo nas mgrin pa'i bar du babs pa las dga' ba dang / mgrin pa nas snying ga'i bar du babs pa las mchog dga' dang / snying ga nas lte ba'i bar babs pa las khyad par gyi dga' ba dang / lte ba nas gsang gnas sam nor bu'i rtse bar babs pa las lhan skyes kyi dga' ba'o/ / de ltar yas babs kyi dga' ba bzhi stong pa nyid dang sbyar ba'i bde stong gi rnal 'byor ni bskyed rim gyi thig le'i rnal 'byor ro/ / 'di dag ni 'grel chen las/ 'dir lte ba la rtsa'i 'khor lo dgu yis bsnun pa'i lag 'gro ste zhes pa nas/ mgrin par ye shes kyi thig le'o [203] zhes pa'i bar gyi/ lte bar gtum mo 'bar ba yis/ /zhes pa nas/ thig le'i rnal 'byor zhes par grags/ /zhes pa'i bar gyi don bkral ba ltar bkod pa yin no/ /

The nectar fluid in the form of a drop descends from the crown to the tip of the jewel. It descends from the crown to the throat to produce joy. Falling from the throat to the heart, it produces supreme joy. Falling from the heart to the navel, it produces special joy. Falling from the navel to the secret area or tip of the jewel, it produces innate joy. These four joys of descent are applied to emptiness to create bliss-and-emptiness yoga. This is the drop yoga of the generation stage. This description accords with the Great Commentary beginning from the line, “The nine of the navel cakra” until “at the throat the gnosis drop,”[245] which is commentary on the above root text passage.

d.div: [203] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 234_na3
[245] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 234a3.

f.d:
de yang 'grel chen las/
gtum mo'i ye shes me ni rab rgyas pa [204] zhes pa kun rdzob kyi ye shes 'dod pa ste de'i me ni 'dod pa'i me'o/ / 'dod pa'i me de rab tu rgyas bar gyur pa na lte ba sprul pa'i 'khor lo rnam par snang mdzad la sogs pa g.yon la dkyil 'khor lngar gyurzhes sogs gsungs pa'i lte ba zhes sogs kyis rlung bcu lte bar sreg pa dang / de nyid 'dod pa'i me rgyas pas sreg par gsungs pas 'di'i gtum mo ni gsang gnas kyi gtum mo dang / de yang kun rdzob kyi ye shes 'dod pa ste de'i me ni 'dod pa'i me'o/ / zhes gsungs pa'i 'dod pa'i me ni phyag rgya la chags pa'i 'dod chags kyis spar ba'i phyi'i gtum mo phal pa'i me'o/ / de ltar du byed dgos pa'i rgyu mtshan yang skabs 'di'i gtum mo 'bar ba'i stobs kyis byang sems zhu bar byed pa'i gtum mo 'di dung can ma'i nang gi gtum mo la byed na skabs 'di'i dga' ba bzhi yang dbu ma'i nang nas byang sems babs pa'i dga' ba bzhi la byed dgos la/ de lta bu'i dga' bzhi de ni rdzogs rim pa'i dga' bzhi yin pas bskyed rim yin par mi rung ba'i phyir ro/ /

Within that commentary are the lines:
“The fire of the caṇḍālī gnosis blazes up” refers to conventional gnosis, desire, and the fire is the fire of desire. When that fire of desire blazes, Vairocana and the others of the five mandalas of the left at the emanation navel wheel…[246] These and following lines teach that ten airs are burnt at the navel and that they are burnt by the fire of desire. Therefore this caṇḍālī fire is the caṇḍālī of the secret area. Also the line “conventional gnosis, desire, and the fire is the fire of desire” teaches that this fire of desire is fanned by the desire for the mudrā consort, and therefore this fire is of the ordinary external caṇḍālī. Another reason why this must be so is that if the caṇḍālī that melts the bodhicitta were the inner caṇḍālī of the śaṅkhinī channel, the four joys at this juncture would have to be the four joys of the bodhicitta descending within the central channel, and those four joys are only found in completion-stage practice and not in the generation stage.

d.div: [204] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 234_ba1
[246] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 234b1.

f.d: bzhi pa ye shes rdo rje sgrub chen gyi yan lag bshad pa/
25. The Gnosis Vajra
bzhi pa lo bcu drug gi mthar bde ba rdzogs pa dang chos mthun par phra mo'i rnal 'byor sgom pa ye shes rdo rje sgrub chen gyi yan lag ni/

d.i: The branch of gnosis-vajra great accomplishment: A meditation on the subtle yoga correlating with the completion of bliss at the age of sixteen

f.d:
bcu drug phyed phyed thig le 'chang / / cha med cha las 'das pa ste/ / bsam gtan bzhi pa'i rtse mo 'chang / / phra mo'i rnal 'byor zhes par grags/[205] / zhes rtsa rgyud las gsungs pa'i don 'grel chen gyis 'chad pa ni 'grel chen las/
de ltar shes rab chos dag la gnas la byang chub kyi sems ni slar yang zhes pa ji ltar byon pa de bzhin gshegs pa ste spro ba byas [206] zhes gsungs so/ /zhes sogs gsungs pa ltar nor bu'i rtse bar du babs pa'i thig le de nyid slar yang sngar byon pa ji lta ba de bzhin du steng du gshegs te gsang gnas nas lte bar rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu'i tshul du gshegs pa dga' ba dang / lte ba nas snying gar rnam smin gyi 'bras bu'i tshul du gshegs pa mchog dga' dang / snying ga nas mgrin par skyes bu byed pa'i 'bras bu'i tshul du gshegs pa khyad dga' dang / mgrin pa nas dpral bar bral ba'i 'bras bu'i tshul du gshegs pa lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba nyams su myong ba'i bsam gtan gyi dga' bzhi stong pa nyid dang sbyar ba'i bde stong gi rnal 'byor ni phra mo'i rnal 'byor sgrub pa chen po'i yan lag go/ /

Sixteen, half and half[247] holding the drop, partless beyond parts, held at the peak of the four meditative absorptions.[248] This is the subtle yoga.[249] /316/ The meaning of these Root Tantra lines is explained by the Great Commentary in the lines beginning:
“Dwelling in the pure wisdom[250] the bodhicitta again,” means, as it arrives so it returns.[251] The commentary states that the drop descends to the tip of the jewel and travels back up again in the manner of its descent. Traveling from the secret area to the navel as a similar-to-cause result, the meditative absorption of joy is experienced. Traveling from the navel to the heart as a ripening result, the meditative absorption of supreme joy is experienced. Traveling from the heart to the throat as a personally created result, the meditative absorption of special joy is experienced. Traveling from the throat to the brow as an eradication result, the meditative absorption of innate joy is experienced. The four joys are mixed with emptiness, and the resulting bliss-and-emptiness yoga is the “subtle yoga great accomplishment.”

d.div: [205] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba6
[206] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 234_ba1
[247] Refers to the fact that sixteen joys are expressed as four: half of sixteen is eight, half of that is four.
[248] bsam gtan, dhyāna. The four absorptions of the four realms of form, but here referring to the four joys.
[249] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 233b6.
[250] Vimalaprabhā has shes rab chos ’byung — wisdom source.
[251] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 234b1.

f.d: de yang / bcu drug lo lon zhes pa nas/ phra mo'i rnal 'byor zhes par grags/[207] /zhes pa'i bar gyis gtso bor bskyed rim gyi phra thig bstan nas/ rgyu mthun la sogs steng du 'gro/ /zhes pa nas/ rnal 'byor bsam gtan sogs de yang /[208] /zhes pa'i bar gyis rdzogs rim nyid bstan pa yin no/ /

The root text from “A wisdom consort aged sixteen” until “This is the subtle yoga” teaches mainly the generation-stage subtle and drop yogas.[252] The lines from “moving up, similar to the cause, etc.” up to “yoga, meditative absorptions, and so on”[253] teach the completion stage.

d.div: [207] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba2
[208] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba6

[252] Most of these lines have been reproduced above: A qualified consort aged sixteen, / adorned with youth and beauty; / teach her well, / then initiate and begin the practice. / Body, speech, mind, and desire, / placed at the brow and so forth, / svā, hā, at the secret and crown. / Then the lotus is purified. / From the syllable āḥ an eight-petal lotus; / by the syllable hūḥ it is with vajra; / the cause of movement / of the wisdom lotus with vajra, / one’s vajra by the syllable hūḥ / visualized with five points; / in its center an eight-petal lotus / conceived with the syllable āḥ. / With the pride of the vajra holder, / the vajra with lotus enters the lotus. / With liṅgam placed into the bhaga, /the yogi performs hūḥ phaṭ; / the bodhicitta is not emitted. / The three realms in their entirety / meditated as forms of buddhas. / At the navel the caṇḍālī fire blazes, / the five tathāgatas are burnt, / Locanā, eyes, etc., are burnt, / the haṃ moon syllable falls /with the characteristics of nectar fluid, / in the form of a drop it descends. / This is drop yoga. / Sixteen, half and half, / holding the drop / partless beyond parts / held at the peak of the four meditative absorptions. / This is the subtle yoga.
[253] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 233b6.

f.d:
'di la kha cig sgrub thabs pad dkar zhal lung gi dgongs par bsams nas/
bskyed rim pas mos pa yid byed kyis thig le'i rnal 'byor sgom tshul rdzogs rim pa'i thig le'i rnal 'byor dngos su bstan pas mtshon nas shes par bya ba ni/ lte bar gtum mo 'bar ba yis/[209] / zhes sogs smra ba ni sgrub thabs zhal lung dang 'gal ba yin te/ sgrub thabs de nyid las/ gtum mo'i mthur sel gyi rlung gis bskul bas zhes pa nas/ ri bong 'dzin pa lta bu zhu ba'i thig le'i gzugs kyis spyi bo nas mgrin par sleb pa na dga' ba/[210] zhes sogs kyi bar gsungs pa rnams kyis/ lte bar gtum mo 'bar ba yis/ /zhes pa nas/ thig le'i gzugs kyis 'dzag par byed/[211] /ces sogs kyi don dngos zin ltar bkod nas/

On this point, some people, imagining it to be the position of the Puṇḍarīka Transmission Sādhana, say:
The drop-yoga simulation practice of the generation-stage practitioner can be understood from the actual teaching of the completion-stage drop yoga found in the lines beginning “At the navel the caṇḍālī fire blazes.”[254] Such statements contradict the Puṇḍarīka Transmission Sādhana. A passage of the Sādhana that runs from “Urged by the downwardly expelling wind of the caṇḍālī” to “The moonlike melted drop form arrives at the throat from the crown to create joy”[255] /317/ comments on the root text from “At the navel the caṇḍālī fire blazes” until “in the form of a drop, it descends,” in accord with its the literal meaning.

d.div: [209] 'di phal cher rje btsun shes rab seng ge'i gsung dus 'khor zin bris mkhas grub gsung rgyun zhes pa der dgongs pa min nam snyam yang / ma dpe lag son ma byung bas dpyad gzhir gnas/
[210] mkhas sgrub rje'i gsung 'bum/ chapad ma dkar po'i zhal lang / 56_na5
[211] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba5
[254] Possibly referring to Notes on Kālacakra: A Continuation of Khedrup by Jetsün Sherap Sengé (1383–1445), a student of Khedrup Jé.
[255] Khedrup Jé, Collected Works, vol. cha, 56a5.

f.d:
de dag gi mjug tu
bskyed rim gyi skabs su'ang gtum mo 'bar nas khams dngos su zhu ba dang / de las skyes pa'i bskyed rim pa'i dga' bzhi bde stong sbyar ba mtshan nyid pa 'ong zhing / de'i stobs kyis dkyil 'khor dang khams gsum po thams cad bde stong gi rnam rol gyi lha'i gzugs dang dkyil 'khor gyi rnam par yid ngor shar ba ches gsal bar 'byung la [212] zhes gsungs pa rnams dang 'gal ba'o/ /

After that it goes on to say:
Even during the generation stage the caṇḍālī blazes, causing the element to actually melt. From this arises the generation-stage four joys applied to emptiness to produce a true bliss and emptiness. This causes the element mandalas and the entire three realms to arise vividly before the mind as the sport of bliss and emptiness in the form of the deities and mandalas.[256] This is stated in the Sādhana, and the above assertion, therefore, would contradict it.[257]

d.div: [212] mkhas sgrub rje'i gsung 'bum/ chapad ma dkar po'i zhal lang / 62_na3
[256] Khedrup Jé, Collected Works, vol. cha, 62a3.

[257] This is because these Root Tantra verses do not actually teach the completion stage as asserted above but teach the generation stage in a literal sense, as if its processes were actually happening. The reason for this is explained in the next paragraph.

f.d: de ltar bshad pa ltar bskyed rim gyi phra thig gi skabs su/ lte bar gtum mo 'bar ba yis/[213] /zhes sogs kyi dngos bstan ltar 'ong ba'i tshul ni/ rgyud 'grel gyi ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo rin po che lta bu'i gang zag gis bskyed rim rags pa mthar phyin pa'i tshe gsal btab pa'i dmigs pa gang yin yang mngon sum lta bur gsal bar snang ba dang / ci la nga rgyal bzhag kyang nga rgyal 'phos pa lta bu dang / dmigs rten gang la sems gtad pa'i dmigs pa de nyid la sems g.yo med du gnas pa'i zhi gnas dngos sam rjes mthun pa grub pa cig 'ong la/ de ltar byung ba'i las kyi phyag rgya de nyid sna tshogs yum du sgom pa'am/ ye shes kyi phyag rgya gsal btab pa'i tshe mngon sum du mthong ba lta bu dang reg tu rung ba lta bu'i rnam pa 'char la/ de la snyoms 'jug gi dmigs pa yang mngon sum lta bu 'char bas byang sems spyi bo nas nor bu'i rtse bar du 'bebs nus shing / de nyid phaT yig nor bu'i bug par sgom pa shin tu gsal bas byang sems nor bu'i phyi rol du 'dzag pa 'gog nus la de 'dzag pa bkag pa'i byang sems de nyid steng du 'dren pa'i dmigs pa brtan cing gsal bas spyi bo'i bar 'dren nus pa yin no/ /

The reason why the lines beginning “At the navel the caṇḍālī fire blazes” express such a literal meaning during the subtle and drop yoga practices of the generation stage is as follows. When the primary and jewellike disciple of the tantra and commentary has completed the coarse generation stage, whatever he visualizes will vividly appear as if it were the actual object. Divine pride will transfer to wherever it is placed, the mind will not wander from whatever object it is placed upon, and will remain with a real or contrived peaceful abiding. In such circumstances the activity mudrā consort is visualized as Viśvamātā. If a wisdom mudrā consort is used, she is visualized as an actual person, real enough to touch. The visualized sexual union also appears as real, and the bodhicitta is able to travel from the crown to the tip of the jewel. With a vivid meditation of the syllable phaṭ at the opening of the jewel, the bodhicitta emission is stopped. With a clear and firm visualization of the stopped bodhicitta being drawn upward, the meditator is able to draw it back to the crown.

d.div: [213] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba5

f.d: de lta bu'i phra thig gi rnal 'byor 'di ni dbu ma'i nang gi gtum mo khyad par can ro rkyang la rlung gi rgyu ba bkag nas dbu mar bcug pa'i rlung gis spar te spyi bo'i haM yig las byang sems dbu ma'i nang nas babs pa'i yas babs mas brtan gyi dga' bzhi 'am dga' ba bcu drug gi rdzogs rim dngos su skye ba'i smin byed khyad par can du gyur pa yin te/

These particular subtle and drop yogas are special ripening practices that develop into an actual completion stage in which the special caṇḍālī fire inside the central channel stops the winds of the left and right channels and is itself fanned by the winds that enter the central channel. The bodhi citta arisen from the syllable haṃ at the crown moves through the central channel to create the four or sixteen joys of descent and ascent. /318/

de la dgongs nas 'grel chen las/
byis pa'i skye bo rnams la las kyi phyag rgya des bde ba de sgrub par byed par gsungs so/ / 'bring po rnams la ye shes kyi phyag rgyas so/ / mchog gi rnal 'byor pa rnams la phyag rgya chen mos so/ / zhes bskyed rim gyi phra thig gi dga' bzhi 'dren byed kyi phyag rgya dngos su bstan nas/ byis pa'i skye bo zhes pa nas/ ye shes kyi phyag rgyas so/[214] /zhes pa'i bar gsungs pa'i de ma thag tu/ mchog gi rnal 'byor pa zhes sogs mchog mi 'gyur gyi bde ba'i rdzogs rim 'dren byed thun mong ma yin pa phyag rgya chen mor gsungs pa dang / rtsa rgyud du yang / phra mo'i rnal 'byor zhes par grags/[215] /zhes pa'i de ma thag tu rdzogs rim rnams gsungs pa yin no/ /

With this in mind the Great Commentary says:
It is taught that the undeveloped accomplish that bliss through the activity mudrā consort. The middling practitioner relies upon a wisdom consort. The supreme yogi uses a mahāmudrā consort.[258] Therefore, having explained the kinds of mudrā consort that can induce the four joys of generation-stage subtle and drop yogas, the commentary says “the undeveloped accomplish that bliss through the activity mudrā consort. The middling practitioner relies upon a wisdom consort.” Immediately after this line, it says, “The supreme yogi uses a mahāmudrā consort,” thereby teaching the exclusive mahāmudrā consort that induces completion-stage supreme unchanging bliss. In the Root Tantra also, immediately after the line “This is the subtle yoga,” the texts talks of the completion stage.

d.div: [214] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba1
[215] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba6
[258] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 233b1.

f.d:
gal te de lta bu'i rnal 'byor pas las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya la brten nas byang sems nor bu'i rtse bar phab pa'i yas babs dang / de nas spyi bo'i bar drangs pa'i mas rten gyi dga' bzhi skyed par byed pa yin na/ 'grel chen las/
las kyi phyag rgya ni 'dzag pa'i bde ba sbyin pa mo dang / ye shes kyi phyag rgya ni g.yo ba'i bde ba sbyin pa mor [216] gsungs pa'i don ji ltar yin snyam na/

If this yogi uses an activity mudrā and wisdom mudrā to bring the bodhicitta to the tip of the jewel for the four joys of descent and then to draw it up to the crown for the four joys of stable ascent, what is the meaning of the following lines from the Great Commentary?
The activity mudrā is she who grants the falling bliss. The wisdom mudrā is she who grants the moving bliss.[259]

d.div: [216] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 234_na3
[259] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 234a3.

f.d: de ltar gsungs pa ni thabs mkhas kyis ma zin pa'i phyag rgya nyid kyi rang stobs kyi dbang du byas na las kyi phyag rgyas khams 'dzag pa'i bde ba ster ba dang / ye shes kyi phyag rgyas khams byang chub kyi sems lus kyi cha shas rnams su g.yo ba'i bde ba tsam ster ba la dgongs pa yin pas skyon med do/ / de ltar na bskyed rim rags pa [217] mthar phyin pas byed pa bzhin du bskyed rim rags pas [218] mthar ma phyin pa rnams kyis byed par mi nus kyang mos pa yid byed kyis byed dgos par yang shes par bya'o/ /

Activity mudrā here refers to the power of a mudrā consort lacking skillful means who grants the bliss of emission. A wisdom mudrā merely grants the bliss of the bodhicitta element moving throughout the parts of the body. Therefore there is no contradiction here. Those who have not completed the coarse generation stage do not have the abilities of those who have, and they should practice by way of simulation.

d.div: [217] ma dper bskyed rim rigs pas mthar phyin pas zhes byung yang bskyed rim rags pa zhes bcos/
[218] ma dper bskyed rim rigs pas mthar ma phyin pa zhes byung yang bskyed rim rags pas zhes bcos/

f.d: de ltar phra mo'i rnal 'byor bsgoms pa'i rjes su bzlas pa mchod pa stod pa bdud rtsi myang ba gshegs su gsol ba rnams rim pa bzhin du bya dgos pa'i gzhan rnams sgrub thabs zhal lung sogs las bshad pa ltar shes par bya zhing / 'dir bzlas pa bya ba'i tshul cung zad cig bshad par bya ste/

After the meditations of the subtle yoga come the mantra recitations, offerings, tasting the nectar, and the requests to return. These can be learned from the Puṇḍarīka Transmission Sādhana among others. Here I will explain a little about mantra repetition.
'di la gsum/ sngags kyi dgra grogs la mkhas par bya dgos par bstan pa dang / yi ge rnams kyi dgra grogs rtsi ba'i tshul dang / de ltar dgra grogs shes pas bzlas pa bya ba'i tshul lo/ /

This has three outlines /319/: 1. The need to become skilled in friends and enemies in mantra practice 2. The way to calculate friends and enemies within letters 3. The way to recite mantras armed with the knowledge of friends and enemies
dang po [sngags kyi dgra grogs la mkhas par bya dgos par bstan pa ]ni

d.i: The need to become skilled in friends and enemies in mantra practice

f.d:
sgrub le'i brgya re brgyad pa'i 'grel chen las/
de bzhin du bsgrub bya'i ming gi yi ge gal te sgrub pa po'i ming gi yi ge dang po'i dgrar gyur na de'i tshe sgrub pa po 'chi bar 'gyur zhing ci ste tha mal par gyur na de'i tshe nyon mongs par 'gyur la ci ste grogs por gyur na de'i tshe lha 'grub par 'gyur ro/ / dbyangs dgra yis 'chi ba ste gsal byed dgra yis na ba'o/[219] / zhes gsungs pa ltar bsgrub bya lha'i ming gi yi ge dang po dbyangs dang sgrub pa po yi ming gi yi ge dang po'i dbyangs dgrar gyur na sgrub pa po la 'chi ba'i 'jigs pa dang ming gi yi ge dang po gnyis gsal byed dgrar gyur pa yin na na ba'i 'jigs pa dang / lha dang sgrub pa po'i dbyangs gsal gang yin yang ming gi yi ge dang po gnyis grogs por gyur pa yin na bsgrub bya'i lha gang yin pa de 'grub par 'gyur ba yin no/ / ming gi yi ge dang po gnyis dgra grogs gang du yang ma gyur pa'i tha mal par gyur na skyon yon gnyis ka mi 'byung ngo / / de ltar na yi ge'i dgra grogs la mkhas par bya'o/ /

The Great Commentary, on verse 168 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
It is the same with the letters of the name of the practice. If the first letter of the name of the practitioner is an enemy, the practitioner will die. If it is neutral, he will remain with affliction.[260] If it is a friend, he will become the deity. An enemy vowel brings death. An enemy consonant brings illness.[261] This means that if the vowel of the first letter of the name of the deity of practice and the vowel of the first letter of the name of the practitioner are enemies, there is the danger that the practitioner will die. If the two first consonants of practitioner and deity are enemies, there will be a risk of illness. If the first letters of the names of deity and practitioner are friends, regardless of whether they are vowels or consonants, the practitioner will become the deity of that practice. If the first two letters of the names are neither enemies nor friends but of a neutral relationship, neither advantage nor disadvantage will occur. Therefore one should know about friends and enemies within letters.

d.div: [219] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 251_ba2

f.d: gnyis pa yi ge rnams kyi dgra grogs rtsi ba'i tshul

d.i: The way to calculate friends and enemies within letters

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ khams lnga'i yi ge rnams dgra dang grogs dang tha mal par 'gyur tshul dang / yi ge de rnams kyi khams sam 'byung ba gang yin ngos gzung ba'o/ /
This is under two headings: 1. How the letters of the five elements become friends and enemies 2. Recognizing the elements of the different letters
dang po [khams lnga'i yi ge rnams dgra dang grogs dang tha mal par 'gyur tshul ]ni

d.i: How the letters of the five elements become friends and enemies

f.d:
'grel chen las/
rlung gi yi ge thams cad chu'i yi ge rnams kyi dgra ste dbyangs rnams kyi dbyangs dang gsal byed rnams kyi gsal byed rnams so/ / de bzhin du chu'i yi ge rnams me'i yi ge rnams kyi'o/ / me'i yi ge rnams sa'i yi ge rnams kyi'o/ / sa'i yi ge rnams rlung gi yi ge rnams kyi'o/ / nam mkha'i yi ge rnams thams cad kyi grogs po ste thams cad kyi yi ge rnams nam mkha'i grogs po'o/ / de bzhin du sa'i grogs po chu dang me'i grogs po rlung dang rlung gi grogs po me dang chu'i sa te de ltar na grogs po'i sde tshan no/ / rlung gi tha mal pa ni chu dang me'i tha mal pa ni sa dang chu'i tha mal pa ni me dang sa'i tha mal pa ni rlung ngo /[220] zhes gsungs pa ltar yin te/

The Great Commentary says:
All air letters are enemies of water letters. The vowels are of the vowels, and the consonants are of the consonants. Likewise water letters are enemies of fire letters, as fire letters are of earth letters, and earth letters of air letters. Space letters are friends of all, and all letters are friends of space letters. Likewise the friend of earth is water. The friend of fire is air, and the friend of air is fire. The friend of water is earth. These are the classes of friends. The neutral of air is water, the neutral of fire is earth, the neutral of water is fire, and the neutral of earth is air.[262] /320/

d.div: [220] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 251_ba3
[262] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 251b3.

f.d:
de yang sdom du bsdus na/
chu dgra rlung yin rlung dgra sa/ / sa dgra me yin me dgra chu/ / nam mkha' kun gyi grogs po ste/ / kun kyang nam mkha'i grogs po yin/ / sa chu phan tshun grogs po dang / / me rlung phan tshun grogs po ste/ / rlung gi tha mal chu dang ni/ / me yi tha mal sa yin la/ / chu yi tha mal me yin zhing / / sa yi tha mal pa ni rlung /[221] / zhes pa'i tshul gyis khams lnga'i yi ge rnams dgra dang grogs dang tha mal par 'gro tshul de ltar yin no/ / de yang dbyangs rnams nang phan tshun du dgra grogs tha mal ba ji ltar yin pa dang / gsal byed rnams kyang phan tshun dgra grogs sogs ji ltar yin rtsi dgos pa ni/ dbyangs rnams kyi dbyangs dang zhes sogs kyis bstan pa ltar ro/ /

When these are put in an abbreviated verse form:
The enemy of water is air, earth the enemy of air, the enemy of earth is fire, water the enemy of fire, space is the friend of all, all are friends of space, earth and water are mutual friends, fire and space are mutual friends, the neutral of air is water, the neutral of fire is earth, the neutral of water is fire, the neutral of earth is air.[263] These are the ways in which the letters of the five elements become friends, enemies, or neutrals. The calculation of friend enemy and neutral should be done vowel to vowel and consonant to consonant. This is taught by the lines “The vowels are of the vowels and the consonants are of the consonants.”

d.div: [221] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 251_ba3_'grel chen nang tshigs bcad mi gsal yang don rgyas pa sdom du bkod pa snang /
[263] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 251b3.

f.d: gnyis pa yi ge rnams kyi khams sam 'byung ba gang yin ngos gzung ba ni /

d.i: Recognizing the elements of the different letters

f.d:
dbyangs kyi a ring thung gnyis dang / ka sde'i yi ge lnga dang / ha yig dang / lce rtsa can th+ka yig rnams ni gnas mgrin pa las 'byung ba dang nam mkha'i khams pa yin te/ rtsa rgyud 'grel chen du drangs pa las/
a ku ha th+ka mgrin byung gang / / dbyangs dang gsal byed mtshan nyid rnams/ / stong pa rlung sogs khams rnams kyi/ / grogs po nyid kyis rtag tu gnas/[222] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ / de bzhin du i ring thung gnyis/ e dang ai ste yon tan dang 'phel ba gnyis/ tsa sde'i yi ge lnga/ a yig dang sha yig rnams ni gnas rkan las byung ba dang rlung gi khams pa yin pa ni rtsa rgyud las/
i tsu ya sha rkang las byung / / dbyangs dang gsal byed mtshan nyid rnams/ / rlung gi khams las yang dag byung / / chu las skyes pa rnams kyi dgra[223] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

The vowels ā and a, the five consonants of the ka group, the letter ha, and the thka are all guttural and of the element of space. The Root Tantra, quoted in the Great Commentary, says:
a, ku,[264] ha, thka, from the throat, whether vowels or consonants, are of emptiness and are constant friends of air and so forth.[265] Likewise ī and i, the guṇa vowel e, and the vṛiddhi vowel ai, the five letters of the ca group, the letter ya, and the letter śa are all palatal and are of the air element. The Root Tantra says:
i, cu, ya, śa arise from the palate; these vowels and consonants, arising from the element of air, are enemies of those arising from water.[266]

d.div: [222] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 251_ba7
[223] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 251_ba7
[264] The vowel u added to the first letter of a consonant group will include all consonants of that group.
[265] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 251b7.
[266] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 251b7.

f.d:
r-i yig ring thung gnyis dang / yon tan gyi yi ge ar dang / 'phel ba'i yi ge Ar dang / Ta sde'i yi ge lnga dang / ra yig dang Sha yig rnams ni spyi bo nas byung ba dang me'i khams pa yin pa ni/
ri Tu ra Sha spyi bo skyes/ / dbyangs dang gsal byed mtshan nyid ni/ / me yi khams las yang dag byung / / sa las skyes pa rnams kyi dgra[224] / zhes sogs gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

The vowels ṛ and ṛī, the guṇa letter ar, the vṛiddhi letter ār, the five letters of the ṭa group, and the letters ra and ṣa are all produced from the crown[267] and are of the element of fire. The Root Tantra says:
ṛ, ṭu, ra, ṣa are born from the crown; these vowels and consonants, arising from the element of fire, are enemies of those born from earth.[268] /321/

d.div: [224] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_na1
[267] Cerebral or linguals.
[268] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252a1.

f.d:
u ring thung gnyis dang / yon tan dang 'phel ba'i yi ge o dang au gnyis dang / pa sde'i yi ge lnga dang / wa dang k+pa yig rnams mchu las byung ba dang chu'i khams pa yin pa ni/
u pu wa k+pa mchu skyes gang / / dbyangs dang gsal byed mtshan nyid rnams/ / chu yi khams las yang dag byung / / me las skyes pa rnams kyi dgra[225] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

The vowels u and ū, the guṇa and vṛiddhi letters o and au, the five letters of the pa group, the letter wa and kpa are all labial and are of the water element. The Root Tantra says:
u, pu, wa, kpa[269] are produced from lips; these vowels and consonants, arising from the water element, are enemies of those from fire.[270]

d.div: [225] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 251_na1
[269] Vimalaprabhā has nypa.
[270] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 251a1.

f.d:
l-i ring thung gnyis ta sde'i yi ge lnga l-i yig gi yon tan dang 'phel ba al dang A_la dang la yig dang sa yig rnams ni so las byung ba dang sa'i khams pa yin pa ni/
l-i tu la sa so skyes gang / / dbyangs dang gsal byed mtshan nyid rnams/ / sa yi khams las yang dag byung / / rlung las skyes pa rnams kyi dgra / rtag tu rlung gi grogs po me/ / tha mal pa chu nus med phyir/ / me yi grogs po rlung yin te/ / tha mal pa sa nus med phyir/ / chu yi grogs po sa yin te/ / tha mal pa me nus med phyir/ / sa yi grogs po chu yin te/ / tha mal pa ni rlung nyid do/[226] / zhes 'grel par rtsa rgyud drangs pa rnams kyis gsal bar bshad pa ltar ro/ /

The vowels ḷ and ḷī, the five letters of the ta group, the guṇa and the vṛiddhi letters al and āl, the letter la, and the letter sa are all dental and are of the earth element. The Root Tantra says:
ḷ, tu, la, sa are produced from the teeth; these vowels and consonants, arising from the element of earth, are the enemies of those of air. Constantly the friend of air is fire, the neutral water has no power, so the friend of fire is air. Because the neutral earth has no power, the friend of water is earth. Because the neutral fire has no power, the friend of earth is water, and the neutral is air. [271] These passages from the Root Tantra quoted in the Great Commentary explain this subject clearly.

d.div: [226] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_na2
[271] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252a2.

f.d: de yang ka sde nam mkha'/ tsa sde rlung / Ta sde me/ pa sde chu/ ta sde sa'i khams pa rnams su bshad pa ni 'byung ba che ba'i dbang du byas pa yin zhing / ku tsu zhes sogs kyis rang rang gi sde pa'i yi ge lnga char 'dzin pa ni/ ung kyis [227] sde dang bcas pa'o/ / zhes pa'i shes par byed pa las so/ /

The description of the ka group as space, the ca group as air, the ṭa group as fire, the pa group as water, and the ta group as earth, is made on the basis of the major elements. The syllables ku, cu, and so forth, as presented in the Root Tantra, represent the five letters in their respective groups. This can be understood by the line “u includes the group.”

d.div: [227] ud kyis sde dang bcas pa'o/ yin nam dpyad/

f.d:
der ma zad 'byung ba chung ba'i dbang du byas pa'i gsal byed rnams kyi yang dgra grogs shes par byas te bsgrub bya lha dang sgrub pa po'i ming yig dang po'i dgra grogs kyang rtsi dgos te/ yang rtsa rgyud 'grel chen du drangs pa las/
sde pa gcig la'ang ka la sogs/ / gsal byed chos can lnga rnams gang / / de rnams sa la sogs pa'i rigs/ / sngags sgrub pa la shes par bya/[228] / zhes 'byung ba chung ba'i rtsi tshul yang sngags sgrub pa la byed dgos par gsungs so/ /

Moreover one has to know the consonant friends and enemies of the minor elements also and be able to calculate the friend-enemy relationship on the basis of the first letters of the name of the practitioner and the deity of practice. The Root Tantra quoted in the Great Commentary says:
The five consonants of earth and so forth of the letters ka, etc., of one group, should be known for mantra practice.[272] Therefore, in mantra practice, calculations should be made for the minor elements also.

d.div: [228] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_na7
[272] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252a7.

f.d:
'o na 'byung ba chung ba'i yi ge rnams ji lta bu/ de dag gi dgra grogs ji ltar brtsi snyam na/ de yang de nyid las/
nga nya Na ma nan 'di rnams/ / rlung sogs skyes pa rnams kyi grogs/[229] / zhes nga nya Na ma na'i yi ge lnga po 'di 'byung ba chung ba'i nam mkha'i khams pa dang / rang dang sde pa gcig pa dang mi gcig pa gang yin yang rung ste rlung gi khams pa la sogs pa khams lhag ma bzhi char gyi yi ge thams cad kyi grogs dang / yi ge gzhan yang nga nya sogs lnga po'i grogs yin no/ /

What are the letters for the minor elements, and how can their enemy-friend relationships be calculated? The Root Tantra says:
ṅa, ña, ṇa, and ma are the friends of those born from air and so forth.[273] The five letters ṅa, ña, ṇa, and ma belong to the space element of the five minor elements and are friends of all the letters of the remaining elements, air and so forth, regardless of whether they belong to the same group. Similarly the remaining letters are friends of these five.

d.div: [229] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_na7
[273] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252a7.

f.d:
de bzhin du de nyid las/
g+ha dz+ha D+ha b+ha d+had+ha 'di rnams/ / chu las skyes pa rnams kyi dgra / ga dza Ta ba dad 'di rnams/ / sa las skyes pa rnams kyi dgra / kha tsha Tha pha thatha 'di rnams/ / me las skyes pa rnams kyi dgra / ka tsa Ta pa tata 'di rnams/ / rlung las skyes pa rnams kyi dgra / sngags kyi dang por gnas yi ge/ / rang gi sde pa'am gzhan la yang /[230] /

Likewise:
gha, jha, ḍha, bha, dha are enemies of the water produced. ga, ja, ḍa, ba, da are enemies of the earth produced. kha, cha, ṭha, pha, tha are enemies of the fire produced. ka, ca, ṭa, pa, ta are enemies of the air produced. This applies to the letter at the head of the mantra and the letter of the practitioner, whether of one’s group or another.[274] /322/

d.div: [230] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_ba1
[274] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252b1.

f.d: zhes gsungs pa ltar g+ha dz+ha D+ha b+ha ng+ha rnams 'byung ba chung ba'i rlung khams pa yin pas rang gzhan gyi snge pa gang yin yang chu khams pa rnams kyi dgra dang / ga dza Da ba da rnams me khams pa yin pas sa khams pa rnams kyi dgra dang / kha tsha Tha ba tha rnams chu khams pa yin pas me khams pa rnams kyi dgra dang / ka tsa Ta pa ta rnams sa khams pa yin pas rlung khams pa rnams kyi dgra yin par shes par bya zhing / grogs dang tha mal par 'gyur tshul yang khams kyi ngos nas gong du bshad pa'i rigs pas shes par bya'o/ /

Therefore the five letters gha, jha, ḍha, bha, and dha are of the air element of the minor elements and are enemies of those of the water element, whether or not they are from the same group. The letters ga, ja, ḍa, ba, and da are of the fire element and are enemies of those of the earth element. The letters kha, cha, ṭha, pha, and tha are of the water element and are enemies of the fire element. The letters ka, ca, ṭa, pa, and ta are of the earth element and are enemies of the air element. Friends and neutrals can be worked out from the elements by following the process used in the major elements.
gsum pa de ltar dgra grogs shes nas bzlas pa bya ba'i tshul

d.i: The way to recite mantras armed with the knowledge of friends and enemies

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ bzlas bya'i sngags bshad pa dang / de dag la bzlas pa byed tshul lo/ /
This has two outlines: 1. The mantras to be recited 2. The way they are to be recited
dang po [bzlas bya'i sngags bshad pa ]ni

'go bor oM dang mthar swA hA lta bu'i mtha' rten bzhag pa'i lha gang dang gang yin pa'i ming sngags kyi yi ge dang po ni thugs rdo rje'i sngags dang / ming sngags tshang ma ni gsung rdo rje'i dang / yan lag so so'i sngags ma gtogs pa'i ming sngags kyi sngags kyi steng du de las lhag pa bsnan pa'i sngags rnams sku rdo rje'i sngags dang / yan lag so so'i sngags rnams ni phreng ba'i sngags so/ /

Leaving aside the oṃ at the beginning and the svāhā, for example, at the end of the mantra, the first letter of a deity’s name mantra is the mind-vajra mantra. The whole of the name mantra is the speech-vajra mantra. Except for the branch mantras, other mantra letters added onto the name mantra are body-vajra mantras. Branch mantras are chain mantras.

de yang lha rnams ni mtshon byed yin gyi/ gzhan du na brtan g.yo'i chos thams cad la sbyar bar bya dgos pa ni sgrub le'i brgya re bdun pa'i 'grel chen las/
da ni sngags kyi mtshan nyid gsungs pa ming gi dang po zhes pa la sogs pa te khams gsum po 'dir brtan pa dang g.yo ba'i chos rnams kyi gang gi ming gang yin pa de'i ming gi dang po'i yi ge ni ming gi dang po'o/ / de nyid thugs kyi rdo rjer 'gyur te mi yi bdag po lha dang lha mo rnams kyi'o/ / gsung gi rdo rjer ming thams cad de 'dir dper na tA rA pA N+Da rA mA ma kI lo tsa nA zhes pa ming de nyid gsung gi rdo rje'o/ / de bzhin du dngos po thams cad kyi ming yang ngo / / de ltar thams cad kyi ming gi yi ge de las lhag pa dag kyang sku'i rdo rje ste zhes pa ni 'dir dper na oM tA re tuta tA re tu re swAhA [231] zhes sogs gsungs pa dang /
sku rdo rje de las gzhan pa phreng ba'i sngags gang yin pa de ni yan lag so so'i sngagszhes gsungs pa rnams kyi don yin no/ /

The deity mantras are examples. This procedure can be applied to all animate and inanimate phenomena. The Great Commentary, on verse 167 of the Condensed Tantra, says:
Now the text speaks of mantras. “The first name” and so on refers to the first letter of the name of whatever moving or nonmoving phenomenon found in these three worlds. “That becomes the mind vajra, lord of men, of the gods and goddesses.” The whole of the name becomes the speech vajra — for example, Tārā, Pāṇḍarā, Māmakī, Locanā. These names are the speech vajra. This is likewise with the whole name of every phenomenon. Letters “other than the complete name are those of the body vajra,” for example, oṃ tāre tutāre ture svāhā.[275] /323/ The commentary continues with examples of the other goddesses’ mantras and then states:
All chain mantras apart from the body-vajra mantras are branch mantras.

d.div: [231] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba1
[275] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 233b1.

f.d: gnyis pa de dag la bzlas pa byed tshul

d.i: The way they are to be recited

f.d:
['di ]la gsum las/ dang po thugs rdo rje'i sngags la bzlas pa byed tshul ni/ rtsa rgyud 'grel chen du drangs pa las/
sngags kyi dang por gsal byed dam/ / dbyangs rnams bsgrub par bya ba'i slad/ / bsnyen dang bzlas pa byed rnams la/ / 'di yi las ni rnam drug gsungs/[232] / zhes sngags kyi ming yig dang po de gsal byed dam dbyangs yig gang yin yang rung ste bsnyen pa dang bzlas pa byed pa rnams kyis las rnam pa drug byed dgos par gsungs so/ /

This is in three parts. First, the way to recite mind-vajra mantras. The Root Tantra, quoted in the Great Commentary, says:
In meditation and recitation, for the practice of the first of the mantra, whether consonant or vowel, it is taught that the activities are of six types.[276] Therefore those who meditate upon and recite the first letter of the name mantra, whether it is consonant or vowel, must perform six kinds of activities.

d.div: [232] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_ba3
[276] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252b3.

f.d:
de la las drug ni de nyid las/
dang por bsnun par bya ba ste/ / de nas dbab dang bsreg pa dang / / de nas sngags pas bslang ba dang / / de nas rgyas dang mnyes pa'o/[233] / zhes gsungs pa ltar bsnun pa dang / dbab pa dang / bsreg pa dang / bslang ba dang / rgyas pa dang / mnyes pa'i las dang drug go/

Concerning these six, the Root Tantra says:
First, piercing, then descent, followed by burning, raising up by mantra, increase, and pleasing.[277] Therefore the six activities are piercing, descending, burning, raising, increase, and pleasing.

d.div: [233] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_ba3
[277] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252b3.

f.d:
de'i dang po bsnun pa'i las ni yang de nyid las/
rnam par bcad byas stong pa yin/ / sngags kyi sngon 'gro mnan pa ni/ / mtshon cha'i rgyal pos bsnun pa ste/ / brgyal ba'i gnas skabs thob par 'gyur/[234] / zhes rnam bcad dang bcas pa'i stong pa ste nam mkha'i khams pa ha yig gis sngags kyi sngon 'gro ste sngon ma yi ge dang po de'i steng nas mnan pa bzlas pa ni lha de la mtshon cha'i rgyal pos bsnun pa ste des lha de brgyal ba'i gnas skabs thob par 'gyur ro/ /

Concerning piercing, the text continues:
Emptiness with visarga added before the mantra, pierced by the king of weapons, and attained while unconscious.[278] “Emptiness with visarga,” meaning the element of space-letter ha with a visarga, is added “before the mantra,” meaning on top of the first letter of the mantra, and recited. This pierces the deity with the king of weapons, and the practitioner attains the deity while it is unconscious.

d.div: [234] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_ba4
[278] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252b4.

f.d:
de'i bzlas pa'i grangs ji tsam zhig bya ba dang de'i byed las ni de nyid las/
thugs kyi bzlas pa 'bum gyis ni/ / brgyal bar gyur pa'i sngags kyi lha/ / nga rgyal yongs su spangs pa ni/ / sgrub pa po yi dbang du 'gyur/[235] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

On the number of recitations to perform and the function of this activity the text says:
With a hundred thousand recitations of the mind vajra, the mantra deity loses consciousness, abandons all pride, and is under the power of the yogi.[279]

d.div: [235] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_ba5
[279] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252b5.

f.d:
gnyis pa dbab pa'i las ni de nyid las/
de bzhin rlung gis mnan na de/ / rnal 'byor pa la phebs par 'gyur/[236] / zhes rnam bcad dang bcas pa'i rlung gi khams pa'i yi ge ya yig gis ming yig dang po'i steng nas mnan pa bzlas na lha de rnal 'byor pa la phebs par 'gyur ro/ / de yang grangs 'bum phrag gcig bzlas pa ni dbab pa'i las so/ /

On the second activity, called descending, the text says:
Similarly if air is added, the deity comes to the yogi.[280] If the air-element letter ya with a visarga is added on top of the first letter of the name and recited, the deity will come to the yogi. This activity of descending will be accomplished by one hundred thousand recitations.

d.div: [236] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_ba5
[280] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252b5.

f.d:
gsum pa bsreg pa'i las ni de nyid las/
me yis mnan na bsregs par 'gyur/[237] / zhes rnam bcad dang bcas pa'i me'i yi ge ra yig gis sngags gang yin pa'i yi ge dang po de'i steng nas mnan pa bzlas pa ni sreg pa'i las su 'gyur zhing grangs tshad 'bum phrag gcig go/ /

On the activity of burning, the Root Tantra says:
If fire is added, burning is accomplished.[281] /324/ If the fire letter ra plus visarga is added to the top of the first letter of a particular mantra and recited, the fire activity is initiated. It will be accomplished by one hundred thousand recitations.

d.div: [237] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_ba5
[281] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252b5

f.d:
bzhi pa bslang ba'i las ni/
de bzhin chu yis bslang bar 'gyur/[238] / zhes rnam bcad dang bcas pa'i chu'i yi ge wa yig gis sngags gang yin gyi yi ge dang po'i steng nas mnan pa bzlas pa ni bslang ba'i las su 'gyur ro/ / 'di yang 'bum phrag gcig go/ /

On the activity of raising, the text says:
Similarly, by water, raising is performed.[282] If the water letter wa plus visarga is added to the top of the first letter of a particular mantra and recited, the raising activity is initiated. It will be accomplished by one hundred thousand recitations.

d.div: [238] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_ba6
[282] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252b6.

f.d:
lnga pa rgyas pa'i las ni/
sa ni spyi bor gnas pa dag / bzlas na lha ni rgyas par 'gyur/[239] / zhes rnam bcad dang bcas pa'i sa'i yi ge la yig gis sngags de'i yi ge dang po de'i steng nas mnan pa bzlas na lha de ni rgyas par 'gyur ro/ /

On the activity of increase the text says:
If earth resting on the crown is recited, the deity increases.[283] If the earth letter la plus visarga is added to the top of the first letter of a particular mantra and recited, increase is initiated.

f.d:
drug pa mnyes pa'i las ni/
spyi bor thig le'i chas mnan na/ / mnyes pa'i mchog ni ster bar 'gyur/[240] / zhes sngags gang yin pa de'i yi ge dang po de'i spyi bo ste mgo bo'i steng du thig le'i cha rjes su nga ros mnan pa bzlas pa ni lha de mnyes par byed pa'i las so/ / de ltar las thug po de'i bzlas pa byas na bsgrub bya'i lha gang yin des mchog ni ster bar 'gyur zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

On the activity of pleasing, the text states:
If “drop” is added to the crown, it grants the greatest delight.[284] If “drop” or an anusvāra is added to the crown or head of the first letter of a particular mantra and recited, the activity of pleasing the deity is initiated. As the Condensed Tantra says:
If the recitations of these six activities are performed, the deity being practiced will grant the supreme.[285]
