f.d:
phyi ma gnyis kyi'ang grangs tshad 'bum phrag re re ste/ de ltar yang de nyid las/
de ltar drug 'bum bzlas pa ni/ / dang po'i sangs rgyas rgyud chen las/ / 'dod pa grub slad bde gshegs kyis/ / sngon du bsnyen pa rnams su gsungs/[241] / zhes las drug po re re'i sngags 'bum phrag re re ste drug 'bum bzla bar gsungs pa ltar ro/ / las drug po de'i sngags kyi mtha' rten ni rim pa bzhin phaT dang hU~M dang boSha TaM dang na maHdang / swA hA dang baSha Ta rnams yin zhing / sngon du oM gzhag par bya ba yin te/

The last two activities are also accomplished by one hundred thousand recitations. The text states:
Six hundred recitations will fulfill one’s wishes. In the Original Buddha Mahātantra the Buddha has taught this as preliminary meditation.[286] Therefore each of the six activities requires a hundred thousand recitations. The endings of the mantras of the six activities are respectively phaṭ, hūḥ, boṣaṭaṃ,[287] namaṃ, svāhā, and baṣaṭa. The beginning of each is oṃ.

d.div: [241] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 252_ba6
[286] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 252b6.
[287] Vimalaprabhā has bau ṣa ta.

f.d:
de'i 'phro nyid las/
phaT yig de bzhin hU~M bauShaT/ / na maHswA hA baShaT rnams/ / las drug la ni grangs bzhin du/ / sngags mthar brtul zhugs can gyis bya/ / dang por rnam snang mdzad byin nas/[242] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ / de ltar na dang por las drug gi bzlas pa 'bum phrag drug dang de'i bcu cha'i sbyin sreg bya/ de'i rjes su lha'i ming sngags tshang ma gsung rdo rje'i bzlas pa 'bum phrag bcu dang de'i bcu cha'i sbyin sreg dang /

The text continues:
The syllable phaṭ, likewise hūḥ, boṣaṭa, namaṃ, svāhā, baṣaṭa: these the meditator puts onto the mantras of the six activities respectively. At the beginning, Vairocana.[288] First the six hundred thousand mantra recitations of the six activities are performed. Then fire offerings of one tenth of the recitations are offered. After that ten million speech vajra recitations of the deity’s whole name mantra are performed, and fire offerings of one tenth of the recitations are performed. /325/

d.div: [242] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 251_ba7
[288] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 251b7.

f.d:
de'i rjes su ming sngags las lhag pa'i sku rdo rje'i bzlas pa bya ba dang de'i bcu cha'i sbyin sreg byas pas lha gang bsgrub pa de 'grub par gsungs te/ snga ma'i 'phro de nyid las/
slar yang bzlas pa yang dag brtsam/ / de nas bye ba bzlas byas nas/ / sbyin sreg bcu yi cha shes kun/ / rgyud las gsungs pa'i cho gas bya/ / de nas lha ni 'grub 'gyur te/ / sngags pa rnams la grub pa des/ / mchog dang gang zhig don gnyer ster/[243] / zhes so/ /

After that, body-vajra recitations of mantras other than the name mantra are performed, and fire offerings of one tenth of the recitations are performed. The text goes on to say that whatever deity one is practicing, it will be accomplished by these activities:
Again the recitations are performed. After ten million have been completed, fire offerings of one tenth; perform the rituals taught in the tantra, and deity practice will be accomplished. With these powers the mantra practitioner is granted the supreme deity and all desires.[289]

d.div: [243] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 253_na1
[289] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 253a1.

f.d:
'o na de ltar bshad pa'i bzlas pa de tsam gyis lha 'grub cing gang zhig don du gnyer ba'i zhi rgyas sogs kyi las rnams 'grub par 'gyur ram snyam na/ de yang rang lha gang gi rigs yin pa dang / las gang sgrub pa'i cho ga'i bya ba dang / dus tshod dang / sngags kyi sa bon dang / khams kyi rigs dang / las bsgrub pa'i gnas dang / phyogs dang / gdan la sogs pa rgyud 'grel las ji ltar gsungs pa bzhin tshang ba'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi/ de ltar ma tshang bar gzhan du byas na las rnams kyi 'bras bu mi 'grub par gsungs te/ de nyid kyi 'phro las/
rigs gzhan dang ni bya ba gzhan/ / dus dang de bzhin sngags kyi rigs/ / gnas dang phyogs dang gdan gzhan gyi/ / las rnams kun la 'bras bu med/[244] / ces gsungs pas so/ /

However will the deity practice and other attainments that one strives for, such as the siddhis of peace, increase, and so forth, be accomplished merely by these recitations as they are explained here? The teachings in the text are given on the basis that certain conditions such as the family of one’s deity, the rituals used to accomplish the activity, the time of practice, the seed syllables of the mantras, the element family, the place of practice, the direction, the practitioner’s seat, and so on are all complete and are followed as taught in the tantra and commentary. If these conditions are not met, the activities will not be accomplished. The text continues:
All activities of other families, other rituals, other times, mantra families, places, directions, and seats, will produce no result.[290]

d.div: [244] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 253_na2
[290] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 253a2.

f.d:
de ltar na 'grel chen las/ las drug gi bya tshul dang / thugs gsung sku rdo rje gsum gyi bzlas pa bya ba'i tshul rnams sgrol ma'i sngags la dngos su sbyar nas de gzhan la rigs spo ba'i tshul gsal bar gsungs te/[245] de yang sgrub le'i brgya re brgyad pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir sngags la bsnun pa la sogs pa ni 'di lta ste/ dang por sgrol ma'i sngags bstan par bya ste rnam pa dang gzhan la yang shes par bya'o/ / oM h+tAHphaT ces pa'i sngags kyis bsnun pa ste 'bum bzla'o/ / oM yatA: hU~M zhes pa ni dbab pa'o/ / oM rtA:bau Sha Ta ces pa ni bsreg pa'o/ / oM watAHna maHzhes pa ni bslang ba'o/ / oM ltAHswA hA zhes pa ni rgyas pa'o/ / oM tAM wa Sha Ta ces pa ni mnyes pa'o/ / bzlas pa drug 'bum dang sbyin sreg drug khri bya ste/ de nas oM tA re swA hA zhes pa gsung rdo rje'i bzlas pa 'bum phrag bcu dang sbyin sreg bcu cha'o/ / de nas oM tA re tuta tA re tu re swA hA zhes pa sku rdo rje'i bzlas pa bye ba'i mthar thug pa dang 'bum phrag bcu'i sbyin sreg bya ste/ de ltar na rnal 'byor pa rnams la sngags kyi mchog ster bar 'gyur gyi rnam pa gzhan du ni ma yin no/[246] / zhes gsal bar gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

On this point, the Great Commentary, on verse 168 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, clearly explains how the six activities and the mind-vajra, speech-vajra, and body-vajra mantra recitations are to be performed in application to the mantra of Tārā before moving on to other families:
Concerning the mantras, piercing, etc., is as follows. First it is taught using the mantra of Tārā. With this one can know the others. The mantra oṃ hatāṃ[291] phaṭ accomplishes the piercing and is to be recited one hundred thousand times. Oṃ yatāṃ hūḥ accomplishes the descent. Oṃ ratāṃ bauṣaṭa accomplishes the burning. Oṃ watāḥ namaṃ accomplishes the raising. Oṃ latāṃ svāhā accomplishes the increase. Oṃ tāṃ waṣaṭa[292] accomplishes the pleasing. Six hundred recitations and sixty thousand fire offerings are to be performed. Then the speech vajra oṃ tāre svāhā is recited ten million times, and fire offerings of one tenth are made. Then the body vajra oṃ tāre tutāre ture svāhā is recited ten million times, at the end of which one million fire offerings are made. In this way the yogi is granted the supreme deity of the mantra, but in other ways not.[293] /326/

d.div: [245] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 253_na1
[246] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 253_na6
[291] The element letter ha is added on top of or before ta, the first letter of Tārā’s name mantra, and the visarga is added as a suffix.
[292] Or baṣaṭa.
[293] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 253a6.

f.d: de ltar na thugs rdo rje'i bzlas pa las drug sngon du btang nas gsung rdo rje dang sku rdo rje'i bzlas pa grangs tshad dang bcas pa 'di ni/ lha gang gi bzlas pa byed kyang shes par byas nas byed dgos shing / de yang lha 'grub cing las rnams ji ltar brtsams pa ltar 'grub pa la lha'i rigs la sogs pa rgyud so so nas bshad pa bzhin ma 'chol ba yang byed dgos pa rgyud 'grel chen dang bcas pa'i dgongs pa bla na med pa yin no/ / sgrub thabs le'u'i don che long du btus nas bskyed pa'i rim pa'i rnam gzhag bshad zin to// //

Therefore the mind-vajra recitations and the six activities followed by speech-vajra and body-vajra meditations, each with the requisite number of recitations, must be learned before the practice of each deity. Moreover, to accomplish deity practice and to accomplish the activities, these practices must be performed without confusion regarding deity family and so on as described in the individual tantras. This is the peerless thinking of the tantra and the Great Commentary. This has been a presentation of the generation stage roughly compiled from the Methods of Accomplishment chapter. /327/
le'u lnga pa/ ye shes le'u/
Part 5. Gnosis: The Completion Stage
rdzogs pa'i rim pa'i rnam gzhag bshad pa/
26. The Six-Branched Yoga
gnyis pa rdzogs pa'i rim pa'i rnam gzhag bshad pa

['di ]la gsum/ dmigs pas gang la gnad du bsnun sa rdo rje lus kyi gnas tshul thun mong ma yin pa bshad pa dang / de la gnad du bsnun byed yan lag drug gi thun mong gi rnam gzhag bshad pa dang / sbyor ba yan lag drug po so so'i rnam gzhag bshad pa'o/ /

This has three outlines: 1. The sites of penetrative focusing: A special explanation of the vajra body 2. Penetrative focusing: A common presentation of the piercing six-branched yoga 3. Presentation of each of the six yogas
dang po [dmigs pas gang la gnad du bsnun sa rdo rje lus kyi gnas tshul thun mong ma yin pa bshad pa ]

d.i: The sites of penetrative focusing: A special explanation of the vajra body

f.d: ['di ]la gsum/ gnas pa rtsa'i rnam gzhag bshad pa dang / g.yo ba rlung gi rnam gzhag bshad pa dang / bkod pa byang chub kyi sems thig le'i rnam gzhag bshad pa'o/ /
This is under three headings: 1. The host channels 2. The winds 3. The placed bodhicitta drops
dang po [gnas pa rtsa'i rnam gzhag bshad pa ]

['di ]la gsum/ rtsa chen drug dang rtsa 'khor drug gi gnas tshul bshad pa dang / de rnams dmigs pas gnad du bsnun pa'i gnas su bstan pa dang / yan lag drug gang gi skabs su de rnams gang la gnad du bsnun pa'i tshul bstan pa'o/ /
This is in three sections: 1. The six great channels and the six cakras 2. The channels as sites of penetrative focusing 3. Which channels are to be penetrated during which of the six yogas
dang po [rtsa chen drug dang rtsa 'khor drug gi gnas tshul bshad pa ]ni

d.i: The six great channels and the six cakras

f.d: ro rkyang dbu ma gsum po mar sna rtags kyi rtse dang bshang sgor zug nas lus kyi dbus kyi thad drang sgal gzhung phyogs la cung zad nye ba na yar gyen du langs nas thod pa'i nang la brgyud de 'ongs pa'i yar sna rnams ro ma sna bug g.yas dang rkyang ma g.yon dang sna bug gnyis kyi dbus kyi ka ba'i thad sor dbu ma zug nas gnas so/ / de yang lte ba yan chad kyi dbu ma la sgra gcan dang gnyis spangs dang a wa ng+hU tI zhes bya zhing kha dog ljang khu khams nam mkha'i khams pa dang / lte ba yan chad kyi g.yas kyi rtsa de la ro ma dang ra sa nA dang nyi ma'i rtsa zhes bya zhing kha dog dmar po khams me khams pa dang gtso bor khrag 'bab pa'o/ /

The right, left, and central channels reach down to the tip of the genital organ and the anus, and up through the center of the body just in front of the spine. Inside the skull they bend, so that the upper tip of the right channel is at the right nostril, the left channel is at the left nostril, and the tip of the central channel reaches the bridge of the nose directly between the nostrils. The central channel above the navel is known variously as the Rāhu channel, dual elimination,[1] and avadhūtī. It is green in color and belongs to the element space. /328/ The right channel above the navel is known as rasanā and as the sun channel. It is red, of the fire element, and mainly carries blood.

d.div: [1] gnyis spang, dvayatiga. “An overcoming or elimination of the two,” referring to the other two channels.

f.d: g.yon gyi lte ba yan chad kyi rtsa de la rkyang ma dang la la nA dang zla ba'i rtsa zhes bya zhing kha dog dkar po khams chu'i khams pa gtso bor khu ba 'bab pa'o/ / de yang lte ba yan chad kyi rtsa de gsum la ni srog 'dzin gyi rlung gis dbang byed cing rgyu ba yin no/ /

The left channel above the navel is known as lalanā and as the moon channel. It is white, of the water element, and mainly carries seminal fluid. These three channels above the navel are dominated by the life-sustaining wind, which flows within them.

lte 'og man chad kyi dbu ma'i rtsa rgyun dang ro ma'i rtsa rgyun gnyis kyi mar sna rtags kyi rtse mor zug cing / dbu ma'i rtsa rgyun lte ba man chad la gnas pa la dud can ma dang kun dar ma dang dus ma'i rtsa zhes bya zhing kha dog sngon po khams ye shes kyi khams dang gtso bor khu ba 'bab pa dang / ro ma'i rtsa rgyun la lug dang gci ba'i rtsa zhes bya zhing kha dog nag po khams rlung khams gtso bor dri chu 'bab pa dang / rkyang ma'i rtsa rgyun gyi mar sna bshang sgor zug cing / ming ni dmar ser dang bshang ba'i rtsa zhes bya zhing kha dog ser po khams sa'i khams pa gtso bor bshang ba 'bab pa yin la/ rtsa de gsum la thur sel gyis dbang byed cing rgyu ba yin no/ / de ltar na lte ba yan chad kyi rtsa chen gsum man chad kyi rtsa chen gsum ste rtsa chen drug go /

Below the navel the central and right channels continue to the tip of the genital organ. The continuation of the central channel below the navel is known variously as śaṅkhinī, the all-pervading channel, and the Kālāgni channel. It is blue, of the gnosis element, and mainly carries seminal fluid. The right channel below the navel is known as meṣa[2] and as the urine channel. It is black, of the wind element, and mainly carries urine. The contin uation of the left channel below the navel reaches to the anus. It is known as piṅgalā[3] and as the excrement channel. It is yellow, of the earth element, and mainly carries excrement. These three are ruled by the downwardly expelling wind, which flows through them. In this way the three channels above the navel and the three below make up the six great channels.

d.div: [2] lug. Sheep, ram; also Aries.
[3] dmar ser. Reddish brown, orange, gold-colored, etc. In the Inner chapter piṅgalā is one of the names of the right channel above the navel.

f.d: rtsa 'khor drug ni nang 'chad pa'i skabs su bshad zin pa ltar/ gtsug tor gyi rna 'khor rtsa 'dab bzhi pa dang / dpral ba'i rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab bcu drug pa dang / mgrin pa'i rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dabs gnyis pa dang / snying ga'i rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab brgyad pa dang / lte ba'i rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab re bzhi pa dang / gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'khor rtsa 'dab so gnyis pa rnams so/ / de yang rtsa 'khor drug po de gar yod sar ro ma dang ro ma'i rtsa rgyun gyis dbu ma la 'khyud cing / rkyang ma dang rkyang ma'i rtsa rgyun gyis dbu ma la 'khyud de lu gu rgyud du bcings pa'i rtsa mdud nyis sbrag re yod la/ rtsa mdud rnams kyi thad sor rtsa mdud rang rang gi thad kyi rtsa 'dab g.yas na yod pa rnams ro ma dang dbu ma sbrags pa la zug pa dang / g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab rnams kyang rkyang ma dang dbu ma sbrags pa la zug nas gnas so/ /

As previously explained in the section on the Inner chapter, the six cakras comprise the four-petal crown cakra, the sixteen-petal brow cakra, the thirty-two-petal throat cakra, the eight-petal heart cakra, the sixty-four-petal navel cakra, and the thirty-two-petal secret-place cakra. At the locations of these six cakras, the right channel and its continuation below the navel is coiled around the central channel, and the left channel and its continuation is also coiled around the central channel, thereby producing a series of double channel knots. At each of these channel knots the channel petals on their immediate right reach into the entwined central and right channels, and the channel petals on the immediate left reach into the joined left and central channels.

de yang gtsug tor nas dpral ba/ de nas mgrin pa/ de nas snying ga/ de nas lte ba/ de nas gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'khor gyi bar la dbu ma dbus dang / ro rkyang dang de gnyis kyi rtsa rgyun gci ba dang bshang ba'i rtsa gnyis rim pa bzhin g.yas g.yon du gnas pa'i sgo nas lam gsum gsum byas te gnas shing / gsang gnas nas bshang ba'i rtsa dbus su byas nas bshang lam bar du 'gro ba dang gci ba'i rtsa g.yon dang dung can ma g.yas su byas nas rtags sam b+ha ga'i rtse bar du 'gro ste/

Between cakras, from the crown cakra to the brow cakra, brow to the throat, throat to the heart, heart to the navel, and navel to the secret place, /329/ the central channel is in the center, while rasanā and lalanā and their two urine and excrement continuations are on the right and left respectively. Therefore between each cakra there are three pathways. From the secret area onward, the excrement channel is in the center and travels to the anus. The urine channel is on the left, and the śaṅkhinī is on the right, and they both travel to the tip of the sex organ.

de rnams kyi shes byed ni ye shes le'u'i brgya nyi shu pa'i 'grel chen las/
bdud rtsi'i gnas su son pa lu gu rgyud du bcings pa'i rtsa [1] zhes pa la bdud rtsi'i gnas na dpral ba'o/ / der son pa ni bdud rtsi'i gnas su son pa ste la la nA dang ra sa nA dang a wa ng+hU tA'o+i/ / de rnams kyang lu gu rgyud du bcings pas lte ba dang snying ga'i bar du lam gsum byas nas slar yang a wa ng+hU tI ni dbus su snying ga'i lte ba phug nas 'gro'o/ / la la nA dang ra sa nA ni g.yon dang g.yas kyi 'dab mar rab tu rgyu bas so/ / de nas snying ga dang mgrin pa'i bar du slar yang lam gsum byas nas 'gro'o/ / de bzhin du mgrin pa dang dpral ba'i bar du lam gsum dang dpral ba dang gtsug tor gyi bar du lam gsum ste de ltar lam gsum bzhi byas nas la la nA ni sna g.yon pa'i bug nas gzhan gyi gnas bcu gnyis mtha' dang cha'i mthar 'gro ste nang gi le'u las gsungs so/ / ra sa nA ni g.yas nas so/ / a wa ng+hU tI ni cig car sna bug gnyis nas 'gro'o/ / de bzhin du 'og tu lte ba dang gsang ba'i bar du lam gsum byas nas bshang ba dang gci ba'i rtsa ni g.yon dang g.yas nas song ste gsang ba'i pad+ma la dbus su dung can ma'o/ / gsang ba'i pad+ma'i 'og tu dri chen gyi rtsa dbus nas 'gro ste rtags sam b+ha ga la g.yon nas gci ba'i rtsa 'gro zhing g.yas nas khu ba'i rtsa 'gro'o/ / zhes gsungs pa ltar yin no/ /

The authority for this explanation comes from the Great Commentary on verse 120 of the Gnosis chapter:
“Arriving at the place of nectar, channels are knotted in series.” The place of nectar is the brow. “Arriving at the place of nectar” refers to lalanā, rasanā, and avadhūtī. They are knotted in series, and so between the navel and the heart there are three pathways. The avadhūtī is central, traveling from the center of the navel. The lalanā and rasanā flow into the left and right petals. Then, between the heart and the throat, there are three pathways. Similarly there are three pathways between the throat and the brow and three between the brow and the crown. In this way there are four lots of three paths. The lalanā travels from the left nostril to other locations for a distance of twelve and “part.”[4] This is taught in the Inner chapter. The rasanā travels from the right. The avadhūtī travels from between the two nostrils. Between the navel and the secret area are the three pathways. The excrement and urine channels travel from the left and right. The śaṅkhinī in the center travels to the secret lotus. Below the secret lotus the excrement channel travels from the center. The urine channel travels from the left to the male or female organ. The seminal fluid channel travels from the right.[5]

d.div: [1] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 390_na4
[4] A minimum distance of twelve fingerwidths and a maximum of sixteen (word numeral “part”).
[5] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 390a4.

f.d: de las gzhan du lte 'og man chad du dbu ma g.yas su 'khyogs nas gnas pa dang / g.yon gyi rtsa rkyang ma'i rtsa rgyun dbus su 'khyogs nas gnas pa dang / g.yas ma ro ma'i rtsa rgyun g.yon du 'khyogs par gsungs pa rnams ni 'grel tshig 'di rnams dang 'gal bar shes par bya'o/ / de yang rtsa 'dab rnams kyi grangs dang khams dang gnas tshul rnams ni nang gi le'u rtsa 'grel rnams kyis gsal bar bstan pa nang 'chad pa'i skabs su bshad zin cing shes byed kyang nang le rtsa 'grel rnams yin la/ 'dir rtsa chen drug gi gnas tshul ston pa ye shes le'u rtsa 'grel rnams shes byed du bkod pa yin no/ /

Other descriptions state that below the navel, the central channel bends to a position on the right, the continuation of the lalanā left channel bends to the center, and the continuation of the rasanā right channel bends to the left. This description is in contradiction to the above commentary text. The numbers of channel petals, the elements they belong to, and their descriptions are clearly taught in the Inner chapter of the tantra and commentary and have been explained in the section on the Inner chapter. The source for those descriptions is the Inner chapter, whereas the sources for the descriptions of the /330/ six great channels in this section are in the Gnosis chapter.

de yang rtsa 'dab rnams ro rkyang dang dbu ma sbrags pa la zug pa'i g.yon gyi rtsa 'dab rnams la nam mkha' rlung me chu sa'i rim pas rgyus nas rtsa rkyang ma dang sna bug g.yon dang / g.yas kyi rtsa 'dab rnams la sa chu me rlung nam mkha'i rim pas rgyus nas rtsa ro ma dang sna bug g.yas la rgyu zhing / nang du sa rlung lte ba bar dang / chu khams pa lte ba'i+i sor gcig gi 'og dang / me khams pa sor gnyis kyi 'og dang / rlung khams pa sor gsum gyi 'og dang / nam mkha'i khams pa sor bzhi'i 'og tshun chad du rgyu'o/ / de bzhin du dbu ma'i yar sna la 'pho chen bcu gnyis kyi 'pho 'tshams rer dbugs nga drug rkang bcas re rgyu ba dang / rtsa 'khor gang yod kyi sar rlung dbu mar 'jug pa'i sgor yod pa 'di pa'i lugs so/ /

The channel petals penetrate the entwined left, right, and center channels. In the channel petals on the left, the winds of the elements flow in the order of space, air, fire, water, and earth before flowing through the left channel and through the left nostril. In the right channel petals they flow earth, water, fire, air, and space into the right channel and through the right nostril. As for the inward flow of wind, the earth wind flows as far as the navel, the water-element wind reaches one fingerwidth below the navel, the fire wind reaches two fingerwidths below the navel, the air-element wind reaches three fingerwidths, and the space-element wind reaches four fingerwidths below the navel. Fifty-six and a quarter breaths flow through the upper opening of the central channel during each of the twelve great wind movements. Moreover, at the locations of each of the cakras, there are entrances for the winds to flow into the central channel. These tenets are particular to this system.
gnyis pa dmigs sa de rnams dmigs pas gnad du bsnun pa'i gnas su bstan pa ni/

d.i: The channels as sites of penetrative focusing

f.d: gnad du bsnun pa zhes pa ni rtsa 'khor sogs lus kyi gnad gang du dmigs pa bzung na ye shes skye ba'i lus kyi gnad che sar dmigs pas bsnun par byed pa la lus la gnad du bsnun pa zhes zer la|_lus kyi gnad che sa yang sngar bshad pa'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi dbu ma'i nang dang dbu ma'i yar sna dang mar sna rnams yin la/ de rnams su gnad du bsnun nas bsgoms pas myong ba skye tshul yang mi 'dra ba so sor 'byung ngo / /

Penetrative focusing[6] means that mental focus is fixed on points of the body, such as the cakras, and major points of the body are pierced or penetrated to produce gnosis. This is penetrative focusing on the body. These major points are inside the central channel, at locations in the middle of the cakras, and also at the central channel’s upper and lower openings. The experiences arising from piercing these points and meditating upon them are different for each point.

d.div: [6] gnad du bsnun pa.

f.d: gsum pa yan lag drug gang gi skabs su de rnams gang la gnad du bsnun pa'i tshul bstan pa ni/

d.i: Which channels are to be penetrated during which of the six yogas

f.d: sor bsam gyi skabs su dbu ma'i yar snar gnad du bsnun pa dang / srog rtsol dang rjes dran gyi skabs su lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus dang / 'dzin pa'i skabs su rtsa 'khor drug ga'i dbus kyi dbu ma'i nang dang/ ting nge 'dzin gyi skabs su dbu ma'i mar sna nas brtsams te yar sna la thug gi bar du gnad du bsnun pa yin no/ /

During the yogas of withdrawal and meditative absorption, the focus is on the upper opening of the central channel. During prāṇāyāma and recollection it is the point at the center of the navel cakra. During the yoga of retention the focus for penetration is inside the central channel at the centers of the six cakras. During meditative-concentration yoga, focus is from the lower opening of the central channel to the upper opening.
gnyis pa g.yo ba rlung gi rnam bzhag bshad pa ni

sngar nang 'chad ba'i skabs su bshad pa bzhin rlung bcu ste/ srog 'dzin/ thur sel/ mnyam gnas/ gyen rgyu/ khyab byed/ klu/ rus sbal/ rtsangs ba/ lhas byin/ nor las rgyal rnams so/ / rlung de rnams dang po gang nas skye ba'i gnas dang bar du gang du gnas pa'i gnas ni snying ga'i rtsa 'khor gyi rtsa 'dab bcu yin te/ de yang rtsa 'khor de'i rtsa mdud kyi steng gi ng+hU tI'i sbubs ni srog 'dzin dang por skye ba dang bar du gnas pa'i gnas dang / 'og gi ng+hU tI'i sbubs ni thur sel gyi skye ba dang gnas pa'i gnas yin zhing / srog 'dzin dang thur sel la gang rgyu ba ni rim pa bzhin steng gi rtsa chen gsum dang / 'og gi gsum la ci rigs par rgyu'o/ / de bzhin du snying ga'i rtsa 'dab shar ma mdun phyogs kyi rtsa 'dab nas byang shar gyi rtsa 'dab kyi bar rnams ni rim pa bzhin mnyam gnas dang / rus sbal dang / gyen rgyu dang / rtsangs pa dang / klu dang / nor las rgyal dang / khyab byed dang / lhas byin rnams dang po skye ba dang bar du gnas pa'i gnas yin no/ / rlung de rnams rgyu ba'i lam ni dper na yur po che re re nas 'bab pa'i chu yur phran du ma la gyes nas 'bab pa bzhin du rtsa 'dab bcu po de rnams na gnas pa'i rlung bcu po re re yang du mar gyes nas rtsa phran du mar rgyu ba'i tshul gyis lus kyi rtsa thams cad la khyab pa yin no/ /

As explained previously during the section on the Inner chapter, there are ten winds. /331/ They are: life-sustaining, downwardly expelling, coexisting, upwardly moving, pervading, nāga, turtle, lizard, devadatta, and dhanaṃjaya. The places where these winds are first created and where they reside in the meantime[7] are the ten channel petals of the heart cakra.[8] The inside of the dhūtī above the upper channel knot of the heart cakra is where the life-sustaining wind is first produced and where it resides. Inside the lower dhūtī, the downwardly expelling wind is first created and resides. The currents of the life-sustaining wind are in the three great upper channels, and the downwardly expelling winds are in the three lower great channels. The eight channel petals from the one at the east, or front, of the body clockwise around to the northeastern petal are the birthplaces and locations of the equalizing, turtle, upwardly moving, lizard, nāga, dhanaṃjaya, pervading, and devadatta winds. The pathways of these winds are like the waters of large irrigation canals, which divide up and flow into many more smaller canals. Each of the ten winds that dwells within the ten channel petals divides off into many other smaller channels, thereby spreading through all the channels of the body.

d.div: [7] Until they dissolve at death.
[8] The eight petals plus the two interiors of the avadhūtī above and below the heart.

f.d: gsum pa bkod pa byang chub kyi sems thig le'i rnam gzhag bshad pa ni
The placed bodhicitta drops

lus la thig le dkar dmar spyi'i gnas tshul sogs nang 'chad pa'i skabs su bshad zin pa ltar yin zhing / 'dir skabs su bab pa ni gnas skabs rigs bzhi skyed pa'i thig le yin bas de bshad na/ lus ngag sems ye shes kyi thig le/ sku gsung thugs ye shes kyi thig le/ gnas skabs rigs bzhi skyed pa'i thig le zhes pa rnams don gcig ming gi rnam grangs yin la/ de rnams kyi gnas gang yin pa ni dpral ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus na sad pa'i gnas skabs skyed par byed pa sku 'am lus kyi thig le gnas/ de bzhin du mgrin pa'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus na rmi lam gyi gnas skabs skyed par byed pa gsung ngam ngag gi thig le gnas/ snying ga'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus na gnyid mthug gi gnas skabs skyed par byed pa thugs sam sems kyi thig le gnas/ lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus na bzhi pa'i gnas skabs skyed par byed pa ye shes kyi thig le gnas so/ /

A general description of the red and white drops was given in the Inner chapter. Here the focus will be on the drops that produce the four periods. The body, speech, mind, and gnosis drops, the four enlightened body, speech, mind, and gnosis drops, and the drops of the four periods are synonymous. Their locations are as follows. In the center of the brow cakra is the body or enlightened body drop, which creates the waking period. In the center of the throat cakra is the speech or enlightened speech drop, which creates the dream period. In the center of the heart cakra is the mind or enlightened mind drop, which creates the deep sleep period. In the center of the navel cakra is the gnosis drop, /332/ which creates the fourth or bliss period.

de bzhin du slar yang lte ba dang gsang gnas dang nor bu'i dbus kyi rtsa 'khor rnams kyi dbus dang / nor bu'i rtse/ dbu ma'i mar sna rnams na sad pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le sogs rim pa bzhin gnas so/ / de yang lte ba dang nor bu'i rtser bzhi pa'i gnas skabs 'jog pa'i rgyu mtshan ni 'dod pa spyad pa sogs kyi mthus gnas de gnyis su khams zhu ba sleb pa na gnas gzhan du sleb pa bas bde ba'i 'gyur ba che ba re gzhi dus su 'byung ba yin la/ de ltar 'byung ba yang gnas de gnyis na bzhi pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le yod pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis yin no/ /

The four drops that create the four periods are also found, in the above order, at the center of the navel, secret, and jewel cakras, and at the tip of the jewel, the lower opening of the central channel. The reason for positing the fourth period at the navel and at the tip of the jewel is as follows. In ordinary existence, when the element melts and falls — for instance, during sexual desire — the bliss experienced is greater when it arrives at these two places than at other places. This is because the drop that creates the fourth period is located in these two places.

de yang khams dkar dmar gyi gnas ni dpral ba dang nor bu'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus dang nor bu'i rtse'i dbu ma'i mar sna rnams na khams dkar po gtso bor gnas shing dmar po yang cung zad gnas la/ dkar cha 'phel bar byed pa'i gzhi'i khams dkar po dngos gzhi ni dpral ba'i rtsa 'khor la gnas so/ / lte ba dang mgrin pa dang gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'khor rnams kyi dbus na gtso bor khams dmar po gnas shing dkar po yang cung zad re gnas pa dang / snying ga'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su ni khams dkar dmar cha mnyam du gnas pa yin no/ /

Concerning the locations of the red and white elements, a predominance of the white element with a little of the red is found in the center of the brow and jewel cakras and also at the tip of the jewel at the lower end of the central channel. However the actual basic white element that is responsible for its own increase is found at the brow cakra. A predominance of the red element with a little white is found at the centers of the navel, throat, and secret cakras. At the heart cakra the red and white elements dwell in equal quantities.

gnas de rnams na gnas pa'i thig le de rnams kyi ngo bo ni khams dkar dmar bsres pa gong bu che chung yongs 'bru tsam re yod de bshad rgyud rdo rje 'phreng ba las de ltar gsungs pas shes nus so zhes sbyor drug 'di pa'i lugs kyi bla ma gong ma dag gsung ngo / /

As for the nature of these drops located in these places, previous lamas of this tradition of the six yogas have said that we can understand them as taught in the Vajra Garland Explanatory Tantra, namely, droplike mixtures of the red and white elements the size of mustard seeds.

gzhan yang rgyud 'grel 'di dag gi lugs la sgrib pa thams cad kyi rtsa ba gnas skabs rigs bzhi'i sgrib pa yin pa dang / sgrib pa de dag gi mtshan gzhir sad pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa sogs kyi thig le de rnams bshad byung ba ji ltar yin snyam na/ mkhas pa'i dbang po dag gis ni thig le 'di rnams bem por zhal gyis bzhes nas/ thog med nas zhugs pa'i sgrib pa'i mtshan gzhir bem po dang de'i nang nas kyang tshe 'dir gsar du grub pa'i bem po 'jog par mi rung snyam du dgongs nas/ thig le de rnams la sim pa'i rnam par gnas pa'i shin tu phra ba'i rlung sems re yod cing / rlung de rnams la sgrib [2] pa'i bag chags bsgos nas gnas la/ de las nyon sgrib/ de las shes sgrib sogs skye bar 'gyur ro zhes gsung ngo / /

According to the tradition of this tantra and its commentary, the root of all obscuration is the obscuration of the four periods. How then are the drops that create the waking period and so forth explained as obscurations? The great scholars have asserted these drops to be matter.[9] Moreover, considering that it would be unsuitable to posit matter, particularly matter that is newly produced in this life, as actual obscurations present since beginningless time, these scholars have said that very subtle mind and wind are hidden /333/ within each of these drops, and on these winds is imprinted the potential for obscurations. From these potencies, the obscurations of mental afflictions arise, from which arise phenomena obscurations.

d.div: [2] ma dper sgrig gsal yang sgrib yin nam snyam pas de ltar du bcos/
[9] bem po. Composed of atoms, inanimate.

f.d:
gnas de rnams la thig le bzhi yod tshul ni ye shes le'u'i brgya nyi shu pa'i 'grel chen las/
nA da ni snying gar thugs kyi thig le shin tu gnyid log pa'i gnas skabs skyed par byed pa'o/ / thig le zhes pa ni dpral bar sku'i thig le sad pa'i gnas skabs skyed par byed pa'o/ / cha zhes pa ni mgrin par gsung gi thig le rmi lam skyed par byed pa'o/ / ye shes zhes pa ni lte bar ye shes kyi thig le bzhi pa'i gnas skabs skyed par byed pa'o/[3] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

The way these four drops exist in the four places is spoken of in the Great Commentary on verse 120 of the Gnosis chapter:
“Nāda” refers to the enlightened mind drop at the heart that creates the periods of very deep sleep. “Drop” refers to the enlightened body drop at the brow that creates the waking periods. “Part” refers to the enlightened speech drop at the throat that creates dreams. “Gnosis” refers to the gnosis drop that creates the fourth period.[10]

d.div: [3] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 390_na3
[10] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 390a3.

f.d: de yang thig le bzhi po de gnyid mthug gi gnas skabs skyed pa sogs su 'jog pa'i rgyu mtshan ni gzhi dus su rlung rags pa 'ga' zhig nor bu'i dbus dang snying gar 'dus pa shas che ba'i rmi lam med pa'i gnyid mthug po 'ong ba dang / rlung gnas de gnyis nas gyes te gsang gnas dang mgrin par gnas pa'i tshe rmi lam yun ring du shas cher 'char ba dang / gnas de gnyis nas gyes te lte ba dang dpral bar sleb pa'i tshe gnyid sad nas yul snang sna tshogs 'char ba dang / bzhi pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig ler 'jog pa'i rgyu mtshan ni bshad ma thag pa ltar ro/ /

The reasons why these four drops are said to create deep sleep and so forth are as follows. In ordinary existence coarse winds gather at the center of the jewel and at the heart. When this happens, mostly dreamless sleep occurs. The winds spread out from those places, and when they arrive at the secret place and at the throat, mostly long dreams occur. Spreading out from these two places, the winds arrive at the navel and the brow, where sleep ceases and the appearance of various objects occurs. The reason the other drop is said to create the fourth period has already been explained.

spyir sngags bla med kyi dgongs pa ni gzhi la rang rgyud la yod pa'i chos shig thabs mkhas kyi lam gyis sangs rgyas kyi yon tan du sgyur bar byed pa yin la/ khyad par du 'grel chen las/ thig le bzhi po de la sku gsung thugs ye shes kyi thig le zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis ni thig le bzhi po de'i steng na rim pa bzhin sprul sku sogs gzugs kyi sku sna tshogs skyed pa'i nus pa dang / gsung rnam pa thams cad pa'i longs sku skyed pa'i nus pa dang / thugs rnam par mi rtog pa'i chos sku skyed pa'i nus pa dang / bde chen gyi sku ngo bo nyid sku skyed pa'i nus pa rnams yod par bstan la/ de ltar na sad rmi gnyid mthug bzhi pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le bzhi po de'i steng na gzhi dus su rim pa bzhin ma dag pa'i yul snang sna tshogs skyed pa'i nus pa dang / 'khrul pa'i ngag gi smra rjod sna tshogs skyed pa'i nus pa dang / gnyid mthug lta bu sems mi gsal zhing mi rtog pa skyed pa'i nus pa dang / 'dzag bde skyed pa'i nus pa rnams yod pa las nus pa de rnams lam gyis sbyangs nas/ yul snang sna tshogs tsam zhig 'char ba'i cha dang / sgra sna tshogs 'byung ba'i cha dang / mi rtog par gnas pa'i cha dang / bde ba'i cha skyed pa'i nus pa rnams lam du khyer bas lam dus su rim pa bzhin stong gzugs sna tshogs 'char ba dang / gzhom med kyi sgra dang / mi rtog ye shes dang / mi 'gyur ba'i bde bar 'gyur zhing / de ltar gyur pa rnams slar yang lam gyis sbyangs pa las gong nas gong du khyad par du gyur pa'i sgo nas 'bras dus su rim pa bzhin sangs rgyas kyi sku gzugs sna tshogs dang / gsung rnam pa thams cad pa longs sku dang / thugs rnam par mi rtog pa'i chos sku dang / ye shes mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po'i skur 'gyur ba yin no/ /

Generally highest yoga tantra asserts that we possess within us something that, by skillful means, can be transformed into the qualities of enlightenment. In particular the Great Commentary talks of the four drops as being drops of enlightened body, speech, mind, and gnosis. Such passages teach that the body drop possesses the capacity to create various enlightened forms, such as the nirmāṇakāya, the speech drop has the capacity to produce the saṃbhogakāya of fully aspected speech, the mind drop has the capacity to produce the nonconceptual dharmakāya mind, and the gnosis drop has the capacity to produce the svabhāvikakāya, the nature body, of great bliss. Within these four drops, which produce the periods of waking, dream, deep sleep, and the fourth state of bliss, is found the capacity to produce during ordinary existence, respectively, various appearances, faulty utterances such as lies, unclear nonconceptual minds such as deep sleep, and the bliss of emission. /334/ These capacities are purified by practice on the path. This means that their capabilities to merely produce various forms, sounds, nonconceptual states, and bliss are brought into the path and these are transformed into various empty forms, indestructible sound, nonconceptual gnosis, and unchanging bliss. These in turn are further purified and developed by the path to produce the final results of practice, the various nirmāṇakāya forms, the fully aspected saṃbhogakāya of speech, the nonconceptual dharmakāya mind, and the svabhāvikakāya of great unchanging bliss.

de ltar bshad pa bzhin du spyir rdo rje lus kyi gnas tshul dang / khyad par du yang rtsa thig rlung gsum gyi gnas tshul ji lta ba bzhin shes dgos te/ rdzogs rim gyi lam thams cad rtsa thig rlung gsum la gnad du bsnun pa'i rnam 'phrul yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

One should learn this general description of the vajra body, and specifically the descriptions of the channels, winds, and drops, because the whole path of the completion stage is a piercing of the channels, winds, and drops.
gnyis pa de la gnad du bsnun byed yan lag drug gi thun mong gi rnam gzhag bshad pa

d.i: Penetrative focusing: A common presentation of the six-branched yoga

f.d: ['di ]la gsum/ rdzogs rim yan lag drug gi spyi'i chings dang / yan lag drug gi grangs dang go rim nges pa'i tshul dang / yan lag drug 'chad byed kyi gzhung gang la brten pa'i tshul lo/ /

This is under three headings: 1. General structure of the six-branched completion-stage yoga 2. Determining the number and order of the yogas 3. Texts to rely on for explanations of the six-branched yoga
dang po [rdzogs rim yan lag drug gi spyi'i chings ]ni/

d.i: General structure of the six-branched completion-stage yoga

f.d: sbyor ba yan lag drug po 'di yang bsdus na dang por dge ba/ bar du dge ba|_tha mar dge ba ste dag pa gsum dang / rdo rje bzhi dang / rnal 'byor bzhi dang / bsnyen sgrub yan lag bzhi dang / gzugs sgrub kyi yan lag dang srog sgrub kyi yan lag dang bde ba sgrub pa'i yan lag dang bde ba grub pa'i yan lag ste yan lag bzhi rnams su 'dus so/ /

The six yogas can be condensed into three — virtue at the beginning, virtue in the middle, and virtue at the end. These are known as the three purities. They may also be condensed into the four vajras, the four yogas, the four branches of approximation and accomplishment, and the four branches of accomplishment of form, accomplishment of wind, accomplishing bliss, and accomplished bliss.

'o na sbyor ba yan lag drug po gang gang du sdud snyam na/ sor bsam gnyis ni dang por dge ba/ sku rdo rje/ dbyibs kyi rnal 'byor/ bsnyen pa dang / gzugs sgrub kyi yan lag go/ / srog 'dzin gnyis ni bar du dge ba/ gsung rdo rje/ sngags kyi rnal 'byor/ nyer sgrub dang / srog sgrub kyi yan lag go/ / rjes dran dang 'dzin pa gnyis ni tha mar dge ba'i rnal 'byor dang / de yang rjes dran ni thugs rdo rje/ chos kyi rnal 'byor/ sgrub pa dang / bde ba sgrub pa'i yan lag go/ / ting nge 'dzin ni ye shes rdo rje/ dag pa'i rnal 'byor/ sgrub chen dang / bde ba sgrub ya'i yan lag go/

How do the six yogas fit into these structures? /335/ The first two yogas, withdrawal and meditative absorption, make up the purity of virtue in the beginning, the body vajra of the four vajras, shape yoga of the four yogas, approximation from the four branches of approximation and accomplishment, and the branch of accomplishment of form. The next two yogas, prāṇāyāma and retention, make up the purity of virtue in the middle, the speech vajra, mantra yoga, the branch of near accomplishment, and the branch of wind accomplishment. The last two yogas, recollection and meditative concentration, make up the purity of virtue at the end. The yoga of recollection is the mind vajra, the dharma yoga, the branch of accomplishment, and the branch of accomplishing bliss. The yoga of meditative concentration is the gnosis vajra, the purity yoga, the branch of great accomplishment, and the branch of accomplished bliss.
gnyis pa yan lag drug gi grangs dang go rim nges pa'i tshul ni/

d.i: Determining the number and order of the yogas

f.d:
'di yang 'bras bu mthar thug la ltos pa'i grangs dang go rim nges pa'i tshul yin te/ skabs 'di'i thob bya mthar thug ni sangs rgyas pa'i gnyis su med pa'i ye shes mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po dang stong gzugs ngo bo dbyer med kyi thabs shes zung 'jug de yin la/ de thob par byed pa'i nye rgyu la ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag dgos shing / ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag las ma gtogs pa'i de'i gong na lam gyi rim pa gzhan la slob mi dgos pa ni rim lnga las/
zung 'jug ting 'dzin la gnas nas/ / slar zhing gang la'ang mi slob bo/[4] / zhes gsungs pa ni/ 'dir yang ting 'dzin yan lag la gnas nas/ /slar zhing gang la'ang mi slob bo/ /zhes bya bar 'brel lo/ /

The number and order of the yogas are determined by the nature of the final attainment. In this practice the final attainment is the nondual gnosis of enlightenment, which is a method-and-wisdom indivisible union of unchanging great bliss and empty form. The immediate cause of such an attainment must be the yoga of meditative concentration, because there is no need to train on any path higher than the branch of meditative concentration. The Five Stages says:
Dwelling in meditative concentration of union, there is no training again in any other.[11] In Kālacakra practice, likewise, when dwelling in the branch of meditative concentration, “there is no training again in any other.”

d.div: [4] sde dge_1802_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ rim lnga/ di_45_ba1
[11] Toh 1802 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, di, 45a1.

f.d: ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po 'dren pa la de'i sngon du phyag rgya gsum la brten pa'i lhan skyes kyi bde ba chen po nyams su myong ba dang / stong gzugs phyag rgya chen mo dngos gnas la grub pa'i rjes dran nges par 'gro dgos te/ stong gzugs yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can dngos gnas la ma grub na mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po skyed pa'i gzhi stor ba'i phyir ro/ / phyag rgya gsum la brten nas khams byang chub kyi sems 'dzag med du rtsa 'khor rnams su 'ching ba la bde ba chen po nyams su myong ba'i rjes dran gyi sngon du rtsa 'khor rnams kyi lte ba'i dbus su rlung dang thig le g.yo med du 'dzin pa'i 'dzin pa 'gro dgos shing / de lta bu'i 'dzin pa'i sngon du yang ro rkyang gi rlung gi rgyu ba bkag nas dbu ma 'ba' zhig nas rgyu bar byed pa'i srog rtsol 'gro dgos so/ /

For the yoga of meditative concentration to induce the great unchanging bliss, it must be preceded by the yoga of recollection, which consists of an experience of great innate bliss induced by relying upon the three kinds of mudrā consorts. This includes the creation of an actual empty-form mahāmudrā consort, because if an actual empty-form mother and father in union is not created, the basis for the creation of the great unchanging bliss is missing. While relying on the three kinds of mudrā consorts, the bodhicitta element is not emitted but held at the cakras to produce the great bliss of the yoga of recollection. This must be preceded by the yoga of retention, in which the winds and drops are held unmoving at the very center of the cakras. This yoga of retention must be preceded by the yoga of prāṇāyāma, in which the flow of wind /336/ in the left and right channels is halted and made to flow only in the central channel.

ro rkyang gi rlung gi rgyu ba bkag nas dbu ma 'ba' zhig nas rgyu bar byed pa la thog mar rlung dbu mar bcug nas dbu ma sbyong ba dang / rjes dran gyi stong gzugs kyi sku mtshan nyid pa 'grub pa la thog mar re khA nag po dri med 'od zer 'phro ba'i nang du longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku mthong ba'i sor sdud thob dgos shing bsam gtan gyis sor sdud kyi rtags rnams brtan par byed pas sor bsam gnyis thog mar sngon du 'gro dgos so/ / de ltar mthar thug gi 'bras bu sangs rgyas kyi sa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba dang stong gzugs kyi sku ngo bor byer med 'grub pa la yan lag drug po 'di sngon du nges par 'gro dgos shing / rdzogs rim gyi lam la 'di bas mang ba mi dgos pas grangs nges 'dod dgos shing / go rim yang gong du bshad ma thag pa ltar 'dod dgos te/

Before the winds of the right and left channels are halted and made to flow only in the central channel, they must first enter the central channel and purify it. Before an actual empty-form body can be created for use in the yoga of recollection, a saṃbhogakāya within a “black line emitting pure light rays”[12] must be developed. These attainments are achieved by the yoga of withdrawal. The yoga of meditative absorption stabilizes the signs attained by the yoga of withdrawal. These two yogas, therefore, precede the others. In this way the attainment of the final goal, wherein unchanging bliss and the empty-form body of enlightenment are indivisibly united, must be preceded by the six yogas. Moreover, because the completion stage requires no more yogas than these six, the number of the yogas is determined as six, while the order of the yogas is determined as above.

d.div: [12] One of the empty-form signs that appear at the accomplishment of the yoga of withdrawal.

f.d:
'di la dgongs nas dpal gsang ba 'dus pa'i rgyud phyi ma las/
bsnyen pa'i yan lag drug tu ni/ / byas nas mchog tu bsgrub par bya/ / gzhan dag gis ni bsgrubs gyur na/ / dngos grub mchog tu mi 'gyur ro/[5] / zhes yan lag drug po 'di ma tshang ba med pas ma bsgrubs na mchog mi 'grub ces dngos su bstan nas rdzogs rim gyi lam la yan lag drug po 'di tshang ba nyid kyis mchog 'grub po zhes shugs la bstan pas grangs nges bstan cing / snga phyi rim par bstan pa nyid kyis go rim yang gong du bshad pa bzhin bstan pa yin no/ /

With this in mind the Later Guhyasamāja Tantra says:
With the branches of meditation at six, practice to accomplish the supreme. Practices using other means do not become the supreme siddhi.[13] This verse states explicitly that if these six branches are not completed in their entirety, there will be no supreme accomplishment, which means conversely that a complete practice of the six branches on the completion stage will bring the supreme accomplishment. Therefore the practices are enumerated as six, and the sequence of practice is similar to the above explanation.

d.div: [5] sde dge_443_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_gsang 'dus rgyud phyi ma/ 154_na5
[13] Toh 443 Kangyur, rgyud, cha, 154a5.

f.d:
'o na yan lag drug po gang yin snyam pa la de'i 'phro [6] nyid las/
so sor sdud dang bsam gtan dang / / srog rtsol de bzhin 'dzin pa dang / / rjes su dran dang ting 'dzin dang / / sbyor ba yan lag drug tu 'dod/[7] / ces gsungs pa yin no/ /

What are these six branches? The text continues:
Withdrawal, meditative absorption, prāṇāyāma, retention, recollection, and meditative concentration:[14] this is the six-branched yoga.[15]

d.div: [6] ma dper 'gro nyid las gsal yang 'phro nyid yin nam snyam/
[7] sde dge_443_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_gsang 'dus rgyud phyi ma/ 154_na5
[14] In this work meditative concentration is a translation of ting nge ’dzin (samādhi), while meditative absorption is bsam gtan (dhyāna).
[15] Toh 443 Kangyur, rgyud, cha, 154a5.

f.d: gsum pa yan lag drug 'chad byed kyi gzhung gang la brten pa'i tshul ni

d.i: Texts to rely on for explanations of the six-branched yoga

f.d:
rje thams cad mkhyen pas/
so sor sdud dang bsam gtan yan lag gis/ / a wang+hUtI'i yar snar srog sdud shes/ / sgra gcan lam nas rlung sngags ma phyed pas/ / lhun gyis grub pa'i zab mo'i rdor bzlas shes/ bum pa can gyis srog dang thur sel gnyis/ / dbu ma'i nang du kha sbyar 'dzin tshul shes/ / 'dzin pas thig le la ni srog zhugs pas/ / dag pa'i sku las spro dang bsdu ba shes/ / rjes dran stong gzugs phyag rgya'i chu skyes kyis/ / mi 'gyur bde ba chen po'i 'dren tshul shes/ / de phyir lugs 'di dus 'khor tshul smra ba/ / lugs gzhan dag las khyad par 'phags pa ste/ / de ltar mi shes dus 'khor tshul smra ba/ / de dag chu nang shar ba'i zla gzugs bzhin/[8] / zhes gsungs pa'i rdo rje'i tshig gi don rje nyid kyis gsungs pa snga ma dag gis zin bris su mdzad pa la gzhi byas/ de dag ye shes byed kyi nges pa skyed pa'i yan lag tu bsdus rgyud sems 'grel skor gsum/ rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa/ don dam bsnyen pa/ nA ro pas mdzad pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa/ grub chen dpe med 'tshos mdzad pa'i sbyor drugade'i 'grel pa nyi ma dpal gyis mdzad pa/ dus zhabs pa tsi lu pa sha ba ri pa rnams kyis mdzad pa'i sbyor drug_a wa ng+hU tI pas mdzad pa'i rgyud kyi dka' 'grel la sogs pa rnams kyi legs pa'i cha rnams kyi gzhung la brten par 'dod pa yin no/ /

The omniscient Tsongkhapa said:
Know that withdrawal and meditative absorption gather winds into the upper opening of avadhūtī. Know the spontaneous, profound vajra recitation performed with mantra and wind inseparable in the Rāhu path. Know how the life and downward winds, by vaselike meditation, are in the central channel in the form of embrace. Know how winds enter the drops by retention /337/ and emanations go forth from and withdraw back into the pure body. Know how the lotus of the empty-form mudrā consort in recollection yoga induces great unchanging bliss. Therefore, teachers of Kālacakra, this system is superior to other systems; not to know that, teachers of Kālacakra, is to be like reflections of the moon in water.[16] The meanings of these vajra words were taught by Jé Tsongkhapa himself and were transcribed by others in the past in the form of notes. Using these words as a basis, further supplemental texts that provide a sure and firm knowledge of these topics include the Condensed Tantra, the Three Bodhisattva Commentaries, Short Teachings on the View, Paramārthasevā, Nāro pa’s Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations, the Six Yogas by the mahāsiddha Anupamarakṣita and its commentary by Sūryaśrī, three works, all entitled Six Yogas, by Kālacakrapāda, Cilupa, and Śavaripa, and Commentary to the Six Yogas of Kālacakra Tantra by Avadhūtipa.

d.div: [8] rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum pod/ da_sbyor drug rdo rje'i tshigs bcad/ 1_na1
[16] Jé Tsongkhapa, Vajra Verses, Collected Works, vol. da, 1a1.

f.d: gsum pa sbyor ba yan lag drug so so'i rnam gzhag bshad pa na

d.i: Presentation of each of the six yogas

f.d:
zin bris las/
sa gcod kyang 'di ltar byas na lam gyi lus la go ba'i nges pa che'o/[9] / zhes gsungs nas 'di ltar mdzad de/ de la gnyis/ bde chen dngos su 'dren byed stong gzugs sgrub byed kyi yan lag dang / bsgoms pas grub pa bsgrub bya ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag go/ /

Jé Tsongkhapa’s Notes on Kālacakra says:
If the outlines also are presented this way, it will engender great certainty of understanding regarding the body of the path.[17] Therefore this topic will be presented under two headings: 1. The accomplishment of empty form, the actual creator of great bliss 2. The branch of meditative concentration: The final attainment of the meditations

d.div: [9] rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum pod/ dardzogs rim gyi gnad bsdus pa/ 3_ba3
[17] Jé Tsongkhapa, Collected Works, vol. da, 3b3.

f.d: dang po [bde chen dngos su 'dren byed stong gzugs sgrub byed kyi yan lag ]

d.i: The accomplishment of empty form, the actual creator of great bliss

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ brgyud nas sgrub byed dang / dngos su sgrub byed rjes dran gyi yan lag go/ /
1. Indirect accomplishment 2. Actual accomplishment
dang po [brgyud nas sgrub byed ]
['di ]la gnyis/ gzugs sgrub byed kyi yan lag dang / srog sgrub byed kyi yan lag go/
1. Accomplishment of form 2. Accomplishment of the winds
dang po [gzugs sgrub byed kyi yan lag ]
['di ]la gnyis/ gzugs ma grub pa sgrub par byed pa sor sdud kyi yan lag dang / grub zin brtan par byed pa bsam gtan gyi yan lag go/ /
1. Accomplishment of form as yet unachieved: The branch of withdrawal 2. Stabilizing form once accomplished: The branch of meditative absorption /338/
[gzugs ma grub pa sgrub par byed pa sor sdud kyi yan lag ]

d.i: Accomplishment of form as yet unachieved: The branch of withdrawal

f.d: de yang dus zhabs snyan brgyud las/ kun la drug tu shes byas te/[10] /zhes bshad pa ltar sbyor ba yan lag drug po thams cad kyang don tshan drug drug gi sgo nas 'chad par byed pas dang po gzugs ma grub pa sgrub par byed pa sor sdud kyi yan lag la drug ste/ sor sdud kyi sgra don dang / gang gi dus su bsgom pa'i dus kyi nges pa dang / ji ltar sgom pa'i tshul dang / tshad ma gang yin pa dang / dag dbye dang / 'bras bu'o/ /

According to the Kālacakrapāda Transmission, “All have six divisions.”[18] This means that each of the six yogas are to be explained in six sections. Therefore this outline of the achievement of form as yet unachieved, or the branch of withdrawal, has six parts: 1. The meaning of the term withdrawal 2. The time for meditation 3. The way to meditate 4. Valid cognition 5. Purification divisions 6. Results

d.div: [10] sde dge_1372_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_dus zhabs snyan rgyud/ 224_na5
[18] Toh 1372 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 224a5.

f.d: dang po [sor sdud kyi sgra don ]ni

d.i: The meaning of the term withdrawal

f.d:
sgrub le'i brgya bcu drug pa las/
so sor sdud pa lus la yul dang yul can bcu po rnams ni rab tu 'jug pa med pa'o/[11] / zhes gsungs pa'i 'grel chen las/
da ni so sor sdud pa la sogs pa'i mtshan nyid gsungs pa so sor zhes pa la sogs pa ste 'dir so sor sdud pa zhes bya ba ni lus la yul dang yul can bcu po rnams kyi 'brel bas rnam par shes pa rab tu 'jug pa med pa ste stong pa'i gzugs kyi yul rnams la mig gzhan la sogs pa rnam pa lnga po rnams kyis rab tu 'jug pa'o/[12] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis sor sdud kyi mtshan don nam sgra bshad bstan la|

Verse 116 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter says:
In withdrawal within the body, the ten subjects and objects are not engaged.[19] The Great Commentary on this verse says:
Now the definition of withdrawal and so forth is taught. Withdrawal means that within the body, consciousness is not engaged in the conjunction of the ten subjects and objects. The five others, eyes and so forth, are engaged in empty-form objects.[20] These two passages teach the etymology of the term withdrawal.

d.div: [11] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka116_89_ba3
[12] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 237_na5
[19] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 116, 89b3.
[20] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 237a5.

f.d:
de dag gi don ni mig sogs dbang po lnga phyi rol gyi gzugs sogs yul lnga la so sor 'jug pa 'gog cing / nang du sdud par byed pas na so sor sdud pa zhes bya zhing / dbang yul gyi 'brel ba so sor spong ba dang gcod par byed pas sor spong dang sor gcod [13] ces kyang bya'o/ / de yang dbang yul gyi 'brel ba gcod pa dang dbang po lnga yul la 'jug pa 'gog tshul yang skabs 'dir dran shes bsten nas 'gog pa dang / yid des yul la rtse gcig tu zhugs pa na dbang shes yul la mi 'jug pa lta bus mi chog ste/ de ni rnam 'grel las/
rnam shes don gzhan chags pa yis/ / nus med don gzhan mi 'dzin phyir/[14] / zhes gsungs pa lta bu'i de ma thag rkyen ma tshang ba'i dbang gis dbang shes yul la mi 'jug pa yang yod pa dang / thun mong ba'i zhi gnas brtan po la gnas pa'i tshe yang dbang po lnga yul la mi 'jug pa yod pas so/ /

The five sense organs of the eyes and so forth are halted from engaging with their individual objects of external form and so forth and are withdrawn inside. Therefore this branch is called withdrawal. Because the connections between individual sense organs and individual objects are abandoned or cut, this yoga is also known as individual abandonment and individual severing. How are connections to the sense objects severed, and how are the senses prevented from engaging their objects? Stopping the sense consciousnesses from engaging their objects by the power of mindfulness and awareness[21] and by one-pointedly fixing the mind upon an object is not sufficient here. In those cases, the sense consciousnesses do not engage their objects simply because the immediate preceding cause is missing or because the mind is dwelling firmly in common peaceful abiding.[22] The Compendium of Valid Cognition says:
Consciousness absorbed by something has no power to engage anything else.[23]

d.div: [13] ma dper por gcod ces byung yang sor gcod du bcos/
[14] sde dge_4210_bstan/ tshad ma/ ce_tshad ma rnam 'grel/ tshad ma grub pa'i le'u/ sh+loka113_111_ba6
[21] dran shes.
[22] zhi gnas, śamatha.
[23] Toh 4210 Tengyur, tshad ma, che, v. 1, 111b6.

f.d: 'o na 'jog tshul ji lta bu cig dgos snyam na/ lus la gnad du bsnun nas dbang shes kyi bzhon pa'i rlung ng+hU tI'i nang du zhugs pa'i stobs kyis dbang shes yul la 'jug pa log pa'i yul yul can gyi 'brel ba chad pa zhig dgos pa yin no/ / de yang dbang po lnga dang yul lnga'i 'brel ba chad pa yin gyi/ yid dang yul chos kyi 'brel ba chad pa ni min no/ /

So where is the mind placed in this context? By focusing on and penetrating the points on the body the winds will enter the dhūtī. Because the winds are vehicles of the sense consciousnesses, the sense consciousnesses themselves are turned away from their objects, /339/ and the connection between sense and object is broken. This is a severing of the connection between the five senses and the five objects and not a break between mental consciousness and its objects.

dbang po lnga'i yul yul can gyi 'brel ba 'gog pa de sor sdud kyi dgag phyogs nas mtshan don bshad pa yin gyi/ sgrub phyogs kyi mtshan don nam sgra bshad pa ni/
stong pa'i gzugs kyi yul rnams la mig gzhan la sogs pa rnam pa lnga po rnams kyis rab tu 'jug pa'o/[15] / zhes gsungs pa ltar sha'i mig la sogs pa dbang po gzhan lnga stong gzugs kyi yul lnga la 'jug cing so sor yul du sdud pas na so sor sdud pa zhes bya'o/ /

Severing the connection between sense and sense object is an explanation of the term withdrawal in terms of what is negated. As an explanation of its etymology in terms of what is accomplished, the Great Commentary says:
The five others, eyes and so forth, are engaged in empty-form objects.[24] The other five senses, such as the fleshly eye[25] and so forth, are engaged in five other objects, such as empty form and so forth, with each withdrawing into its own individual object. This is also why this yoga is called withdrawal.

d.div: [15] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 237_na6
[24] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 237a6.
[25] sha’i mig. Does not refer to the physical eye but to one of the five clairvoyant “eyes.”

f.d: sgra bshad tshul 'di ni sgron gsal gyi sor sdud kyi mtshan don bshad pa dang cha 'dra ste/ de yang sgron gsal las bshad pa ni rnam smin gyi mig dbang sogs kyis phyi rol gyi gzugs sogs la longs spyod tshul khyad par ba cig yin la/ 'dir rnam smin gyi mig sogs las gzhan pa'i sha'i mig sogs kyis stong gzugs kyi yul lnga la longs spyod tshul khyad par ba zhig yin no/ /

This explanation of the meaning of this term has certain similarities to the etymology of withdrawal found in Bright Lamp. One difference is that in the Bright Lamp explanation, the ripened sense organs[26] engage in external form and so forth, while here the fleshly eye, rather than the ripened eye, engages with empty forms and so forth.

d.div: [26] The ordinary sense organs produced at birth as a result of ripening karma.

f.d:
de ltar byas pa'i tshe stong gzugs kyi gzugs du ba smig rgyu sogs dang / stong pa'i sgra ni ye le'i brgya bco lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
de nas gzugs kyi rnal 'byor gyis gzhom du med pa'i sgra gang yin pa de nyid thos te de ltar gzugs snang ba las sprul pa'i sku dang sgra snang ba las longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku'o zhes pa'i don to/[16] / zhes gsungs pa 'di dag gis bstan pa ltar stong gzugs kyis mtshon pa'i stong pa'i dri ro reg bya gsum yang 'dod dgos pa dang / mig gzhan sha'i mig dang 'dra ba'i dbang po gzhan bzhi yang 'dod dgos par shes par bya'o/ /

Concerning these empty sounds and empty forms, such as smoke and mirages, the Great Commentary says on verse 115 of the Gnosis chapter:
With the yoga of forms one hears all manner of indestructible sound. From the appearance of form comes the nirmāṇakāya, and from the appearance of sound comes the saṃbhogakāya.[27] From the above, we must also infer empty form, smells, tastes, and touch. Therefore four “other” senses, in addition to the “other” eye, or fleshly eye, can be asserted.

d.div: [16] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 388_ba7
[27] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 388b7.

f.d:
gzhan yang sgrub le'i brgya bcu gsum pa'i 'grel chen las/
da ni nye ba'i sgrub pa gsungs pa so sor zhes pa la sogs pa ste 'dir so sor sdud pa zhes pa la 'khor ba pa rnams kyi sdud pa ni mig la sogs pa'i dbang po rnams kyis gzugs la sogs pa'i yul 'dzin pa'o/ / de yongs su spong ba ni so sor sdud pa zhes brjod de stong pa nyid kyi gzugs la gzhan sha la sogs pa'i mig la sogs pa rnams kyis gzhan gzugs la sogs pa'i yul 'dzin pa ni nye ba'i sgrub pa'o/[17] / zhes gsungs pa 'dis kyang sor sdud kyi sgra don snga ma bzhin du bshad pa yin no/ /

The Great Commentary, on verse 103 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
Now near accomplishment is taught. “Individual” and so on refers to withdrawal. The withdrawal of the surroundings refers to the sense organs of the eyes and so forth apprehending their objects of form and so forth, and the abandoning of that is called withdrawal. Concerning empty forms, other eyes such as eyes of flesh, apprehend other forms as their objects. This is near accomplishment.[28] This passage mirrors the explanation of withdrawal as described above.

d.div: [17] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 235_ba5
[28] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 235b5.

f.d: 'o na sor bsam bsnyen pa'i yan lag ma yin nam/ 'dir nyi sgrub ces pa ci yin snyam na/ rdzogs rim nyid bsnyen sgrub yan lag bzhir bsdu ba'i tshe sor bsam bsnyen par 'jog kyang / 'dir phyi nang gi dam tshig sogs bsnyen par bzhag pa'i dbang du byas pas skyon med do/ /

But isn’t this section /340/ the branch of approximation consisting of withdrawal and meditative absorption? What does near accomplishment refer to here? When the completion stage is divided into its four branches of approximation and accomplishment, withdrawal and meditative absorption do comprise the branch of approximation. But the quote above is based on the inner and outer samaya and so forth being posited as the branch of approximation, and so there is no fault.[29]

d.div: [29] The inner and outer samaya are practices that precede the yoga of withdrawal. Therefore, if they are posited as approximation, withdrawal becomes near accomplishment.

f.d: gnyis pa gang gi dus su bsgom pa dus kyi nges pa ni/

kha cig sna bug g.yas nas sa rlung g.yas kyi mchu ngos la bdar te rgyu ba'i tshe bsgom zhes zer ba ni der ma nges te/ mchu ngos la bdar te rgyu ba'i sa rlung ni 'byung ba chung ba'i sa rlung yin la/ sna bug g.yas la sa rlung rgyu ba'i tshe sor sdud dang por bsgom par gsungs pa ni mtshon pa'i dbang du byas pa yin pas so/ / de ltar yang ye le'i brgya nyer gnyis pa'i 'grel chen las/
sa zhes pa ni nye bar mtshon pa ste gang gi tshe g.yas su sa rab tu 'bab pa'i dus su rnal 'byor pa sgom par byed na de'i tshe cho ga 'di'o/ / g.yon pa'i rtsa la rab tu 'bab pa'i dus su ni ma yin te nam mkha'i dkyil 'khor la sogs pa'i rim pa las so/[18] / zhes gsungs pa 'dis sor sdud dang por sgom pa'i dus bstan pa yin la/ de yang sna bug g.yas nas sa rlung rgyu bas nye bar mtshon pa ste/ rlung gang yin yang sna bug g.yas nas rgyu ba'i tshe rlung rnams sdud rim gyis rgyu bas rlung bsdu sla ba'i [19] rgyu mtshan gyis de'i dus su sor sdud bsgom par gsungs shing / sna bug g.yon nas rgyu ba'i tshe nam mkha'i rlung me chu sa'i rim gyis skye rim gyis rgyu bas na rlung bsdu dka' bas de'i dus su bsgom par ma gsungs pa yin no/ /

Some say that the time for meditation is when the earth wind flows from the right nostril onto the right side of the lips. However this is not conclusive, because the earth wind that flows onto the lips is to the earth wind of the minor elements, and the instruction that one should begin the meditation of withdrawal when earth wind flows from the right nostril is given for purposes of illustration only. Therefore the Great Commentary on verse 122 of the Gnosis chapter says:
“Earth” is an illustration. If the yogi meditates when it flows through the right channel, this is the time for the ritual, but not when it flows through the left channel, because that is in the order of space and so forth.[30] This passage teaches the time for beginning withdrawal meditation. Illustrating this with the earth wind passing through the right nostril means that when any kind of wind passes through the right nostril, it will be in the dissolution order,[31] and therefore withdrawal is easier. This is the reason for beginning withdrawal meditation at that time. When the winds flow through the left nostril, they flow in the creation order of space, air, fire, water, and earth. This makes withdrawal harder, and therefore it is not taught as the time for withdrawal meditation.

d.div: [18] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 391_na3
[19] ma dper rlung bsdu ba'i zhes byung yang sla ba'i zhes bcos/
[30] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 391a3.
[31] Earth, water, fire, air, and space is the dissolution order.

f.d: gsum pa ji ltar sgom pa'i tshul

['di ]la lnga/ sor sdud kyi skabs su bsgoms stobs kyis rlung dbu mar tshud dgos pa'i shes byed dgod pa dang / sor sdud la gnyis su phye ba rgyu mtshan dang bcas pa dang / phye ba so so'i sgom tshul bshad pa dang / ma grub na spogs chog bya tshul dang / sgom 'phro la shi yang rnal 'byor goms stobs kyis 'jug par bstan pa'o/ /

This has five outlines: /341/ 1. Sources for the assertion that during withdrawal, winds must enter the central channel by the force of meditation 2. Division of withdrawal into two parts, plus reasons for the division 3. The meditations of the two parts 4. Ritual of enhancement at times of nonaccomplishment 5. Even if one dies with the remainder of the meditations unfinished, the power of the yoga ensures continuation
dang po [sor sdud kyi skabs su bsgoms stobs kyis rlung dbu mar tshud dgos pa'i shes byed dgod pa ]ni/

d.i: Sources for the assertion that during withdrawal, winds must enter the central channel by the force of meditation

f.d:
rtsa rgyud mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus su drangs pa las/
du ba la sogs bsgoms byas shing / / sems ni g.yo ba med byas te/ / dbu ma sbyang ba byas nas ni/[20] / zhes dang / yang mdor bsdus de nyid las/
du ba la sogs pa'i mtshan ma bsgoms pa/ las dang po pa dbu ma rnam par sbyangs pa/[21] zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis sor sdud kyi skabs su rtsa dbu ma sbyangs pa cig dgos par bstan la/ de'i sbyong tshul yang zin bris las/
yur ba la chu 'dren pa'i sngon du yur ba sel ba lta bur bshad pas dbu ma sbyor mkhan nam sel mkhan ni rlung yin la/ rlung gis dbu ma'i nang du ma phyin par dbu ma'i phyi nas dbu ma'i nang ji ltar sel/ yur ba'i phyi nas yur ba sel zhes pa ni ngo mtshar ro/[22] / zhes gsungs pa ltar rtsa dbu ma'i nang rlung gis sel ba la rlung dbu mar zhugs pa cig dgos so/ /

The Root Tantra, quoted in the Supreme and Unchanging Gnosis summary of the Gnosis chapter, says:
Meditating on smoke and so forth mind is made immovable, the central channel is purified.[32] And in the same summary:
Meditating on the signs of smoke and so forth, the beginner purifies the central channel.[33] These quotes teach that during withdrawal, the central channel is purified. On how this is done, Notes on Kālacakra says:
Using the comparison of an irrigation canal that must be cleaned before feeding water into it, the cleaner or purifier of the central channel is the wind. Without entering the central channel, how could the winds clean the inside of the channel from the outside? To say that one could clean the inside of an irrigation channel from the outside would be strange indeed![34] As this quote makes clear, it is necessary for the winds to enter the central channel in order to clean the inside of it.
