Vighnantaka in the line “The look of Vighnantaka” refers to amṛtavarta. His “look” reaches the place of nectar, which means reaching the brow. By this the near accomplishment of the six branches will be achieved. The word “also” refers to prāṇāyāma and retention.[99]

d.div: [86] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 250_na7
[99] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 250a7.

f.d:
de bzhin du dus zhabs snyan brgyud las kyang /
dpral ba'i thig ler srog bcug la/ / g.yas la rlung ni rgyu dus bsgom/[87] / zhes dpral bar gnad du bsnun par gsal bar gsungs pa dang /

d.div: [87] sde dge_1372_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_dus zhabs snyan rgyud/ 224_ba2
[100] Toh 1372 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 224b2.

f.d:
gzhang yang a wa d+hU tI pa'i sbas pa mig 'byed las/
de'i spyod lam ni mig mi 'dzums pa dang / kha gdangs shing dbugs sor bzhag pa dang / dngos por mi 'dzin pas gzung ba dang 'dzin pa'i yul dang bral ba dang / dbugs smin mtshams su phugs rdugs kyi rtsal rang bzhin du zhugs shing gnas pa ni khro bo de'i spyod lam yin no/ / de bzhin du rnal 'byor sgrub pa nyams su len pa rnams kyis kyang de bzhin spyod lam bya ste/ rnal 'byor pa'i mtshan mo'i sbyor ba la rtags lnga 'byung bar 'gyur ro/[88] / zhes sor sdud kyi lta stangs kyi skabs su gsungs pa'i smin mtshams kyi phugs rdugs kyi rtsa smin mtshams kyi ng+hU tI yin la/ de la dbugs zhugs pa zhig sor sdud kyi mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor pas sgom par byed dgos par bshad pa 'dis der rlung 'dzud pa'i sems kyi dmigs pa gtod sa yang de la byed dgos par grub bo/ /

Furthermore, in Avadhūtipa’s Opening the Eyes to What Is Hidden, it says:
The manner is as follows: the eyes are not closed, the mouth is open, breath is natural, there is no holding to phenomena, nothing that grasps and nothing to be grasped, the breath entering and dwelling within the deep channel between the eyebrows. This is the stance of that wrathful one. Similarly those who practice to accomplish the yoga must adopt a similar stance, and the five signs of the night yoga will arise.[101] “The deep channel between the eyebrows” mentioned during the positioning of the eyes in withdrawal yoga refers to the dhūtī between the eyebrows, and this passage teaches that the practitioner of the nighttime yoga must meditate on the breath entering at that point. This establishes that the focus of the mind, which brings the winds with it, must also be at this point.

d.div: [88] sde dge_1373_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pasbyor ba yan lag drug gi dka' 'grel/ 235_ba4
[101] Toh 1373 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 235b4.

f.d: mdor bsdu na smin ma gnyis kyi dbus kyi nang thad na rtsa dbu ma'i yar sna sbu gu dang de yong ba'i sbubs stong pa'i nam mkha' de la mig gnyis mas lcibs kyis phyed tsam bkab ste gyen du lta ba de yang mig 'bras gnyis mig zur nang ma gnyis na yar la bsgril te sems dang lhan cig tu rtse gcig tu lta ba'i tshul gyis mig 'byed 'dzums sgul skyod sogs cung zad kyang med pa'i lta stangs dang / de bzhin du sems kyang dbu ma'i yar sna'i sbubs stong gi bar snang stong pa de nyid la ro mnyam du zhugs pa'i tshul gyis rtse gcig tu mnyam par 'jog pa ni sems kyi 'jog tshul lo/ /

To summarize: The eyes half covered by the eyelids look upward to the point midway between the eyebrows, to the opening of the upper tip of the central channel in the space of its empty aperture. The eyeballs are rolled up toward the inner corners of the eyes. Together with the mind these half-closed eyes are one-pointedly focused, and they do not move at all from this position. This is the placement of the eyes. Likewise the mind dwells within the emptiness that is the space of the empty aperture of the upper tip of the central channel and is held there in single-pointed equipoise. /360/ This is the placement of the mind.

de yang 'di dag ni rje nyid kyis/
so sor sdud dang bsam gtan yan lag gis/ / a wa ng+hU tI'i yar snar srog sdud shes/[89] / zhes gsungs pa'i lta stangs dang sems 'jog tshul dang / de la brten nas rlung dbu mar 'jug tshul sgrub byed dang bcas pa yin no/ /

This validates the placement of the eyes and mind and the way the winds enter the central channel in dependence on that placement, as taught by Jé Tsongkhapa:
Know that withdrawal and meditative absorption gather winds into the upper opening of avadhūtī.[102]

d.div: [89] rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum pod/ da_sbyor drug tshigs bcad/ 1_na1
[102] Jé Tsongkhapa, Vajra Verses, Collected Works, vol. da, 1a1.

f.d:
gzhan yang chos rje bu'i sbyor drug las/
mig gi lta stangs sngar gyi de nyid la gnas pas mig 'bras mi bsgul rdzi ma mi bkra ba/ sa gcig tu bltas pas rnam rtog gi rlung rgyu ba'i rtsa ro rkyang gnyis kyi rtsa kha 'ching la/ de chings pas mig gi sgo nas ldang zhing rgyu ba zhes bya ba'i rlung mig shes dang lhan cig rgyu ba de 'ching / de chings pas sems chings shing des dbang po gzhan rnams kyang chings par 'gyur ro/[90] / zhes gsungs te/

However, in his Six Yogas, the great dharma master Butön says:
Holding the previous position of the eyes, with eyeballs unmoving, eyelashes not fluttering, and the eyes looking at one place, the entrances of the right and left channels that carry the flow of conceptual winds are blocked. By this restriction the winds, which rise and flow through the eyes, together with the eye consciousness, are halted. By this restriction the mind is held, which in turn halts the other senses.[103]

d.div: [90] bu ston rin chen grub/ gsung 'bum pod/ gsor bsam khrid yig_12_na6_91
[103] Collected Works, vol. ga, Instructions on Withdrawal and Meditative Absorption, 12a6.

f.d:
de'i dgongs pa ni lta stangs nyid kyis dbang shes lnga'i bzhon pa'i rlung dbu mar tshud de rtags rnams 'char bar bzhed pa yin pa 'dra zhing / de yang dpe med 'tshos/
gang du dri med nam mkha' la/ / mig phyed brtan par gtad pa na/ / bde chen stong rtogs rtog med las/ / du ba la sogs rtog med 'byung /[91] / zhes pa'i don du dgongs par mngon no/ /

The meaning of this passage seems to be that by positioning the eyes, the winds, which act as mounts for the five sense consciousnesses, will enter the central channel, and the signs will arise. This also appears to be his understanding of the following verse from Anupamarakṣita:
When the half eyes are firmly placed upon the pure space, smoke and so forth will nonconceptually appear from the nonconceptual consciousness of great bliss and emptiness.[104]

d.div: [91] lung 'di brnyed son ma byung /
[104] Quote not found.

f.d:
yang rje bu'i sbyor drug de nyid las/
sems kyi 'jog tshul gcig la 'di ltar gsungs te/ lus gnad lta stangs sngar dang 'dra ba'i ngang nas yod med la sogs pa'i blo'i 'dzin pa thams cad bshig la ma bcos pa'i ngang du lhod kyi glod nas dmigs med kyi ngang du bzhag ste/[92] zhes gsungs nas/ de'i shes byed du phyag rdor stod 'grel las/
de'i phyir yod pa dang med pa'i blo yongs su spangs te zhen pa med par byas nas zab mo stong pa dmigs pa med pa bsgom pa ste/[93] zhes sogs 'dren par mdzad nas sgom tshul 'di de kho na nyid stong nyid sgom tshul du yang bzhed do/ /

Furthermore, regarding placement of the mind in the same Six Yogas, dharma master Butön said:
Within the state of this previous positioning of the eyes and physical posture, all grasping to existence, nonexistence, and so forth will be destroyed. One relaxes into an uncontrived state and dwells within nonapprehension.[105] As a source for this assertion, he quotes the Vajrapāṇi Commentary:
Therefore, abandoning all perception of existence and nonexistence, not grasping, meditate on the profound nonapprehended emptiness.[106]

d.div: [92] bu ston rin chen grub/ gsung 'bum pod/ ga_sbyor drug gi khrid yig_13_ba4
[93] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 131_na7
[105] Collected Works, vol. ga, 13b4.
[106] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 131a7.

f.d: 'di yang rdo rje snying 'grel las/ bdag med pa'i rnal 'byor 'di zhes dang / stong pa nyid gang la sems rtse gcig par bzhag na [94] zhes sogs gsungs pa rnams dang / stod 'grel gyi zab mo stong pa dmigs pa med pa bsgom par bya ste zhes gsungs pa rnams kyi dgongs par bsams pa 'dra na'ang / 'thad par ma mthong ste/ yod med sogs kyi blo'i 'dzin pa thams cad bshig nas ma bcos pa'i ngang du lhod kyi glod nas sems 'jog pa ni de kho na nyid sgom pa min la/ gal te yin du chug kyang sor sdud kyi skabs 'dir rnam med kyi stong nyid sgom pa min te/ lam 'di'i sgrub pa pos thos bsam gyis stong nyid rtogs pa tsam ni dbang zhu ba'i dus na'ang yod dgos la/ gtso bor sgom pa'i tshe ni srog 'dzin gnyis kyi rlung dbang du byas pas ng+hU tI'i nang gi gtum mo 'bar nas khams zhu ba las byung ba'i bde ba chen po sogs kyis rnam med kyi stong nyid yul du byas nas sgom pa'i chos sku'i rigs 'dra'i rgyu sgrub pa yin zhing / sor bsam gyi skabs 'dir gzugs sku'i rigs 'dra'i rgyu stong gzugs sngar ma grub pa gsar du bsgrub pa dang / grub zin brtan pa'i phyir sgom pa yin pas so/ /

Therefore he also asserts this meditation to be one on actual emptiness. The Vajragarbha Commentary also talks of “this yoga of nonself” and “placing the mind one-pointedly in emptiness,”[107] and although he seems to think that this is the meaning of these quotes and of “meditate on the profound nonapprehended emptiness” from the Vajrapāṇi Commentary, I cannot see this assertion as being correct. For a mental placement in which all grasping to existence, nonexistence, and so forth is eliminated, /361/ the mind released into an uncontrived state, is not a meditation on the nature of reality.[108] Even assuming that it were, it could not be a nonaspected emptiness meditation at this time in the practice of withdrawal. Practitioners of this path need a mere understanding of emptiness produced by listening and contemplating, even at the time of requesting initiation, but the time for its primary meditation is during the two yogas of prāṇāyāma and retention, when mastery is gained over the winds, and the caṇḍālī fire blazes within the dhūtī to melt the elements and produce the great bliss. This bliss takes nonaspected emptiness as its object of meditation to develop a similar-in-type cause of dharmakāya. However, here in the yogas of withdrawal and absorption, the meditations are on empty forms, either by creating them anew or stabilizing those already produced in order to develop similar-in-type causes of the enlightened form body.

d.div: [94] sde dge_1180_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ka_rdo rje snying 'grel/ dngos grub kyi le'u gnyis pa/ 80_ba7
[107] Toh 1180 Tengyur, rgyud, ka, chap. 2, 80b7.
[108] de kho na nyid. Actual emptiness, reality itself.

f.d:
'o na stod 'grel las/
de'i phyir yod pa dang med pa'i blo yongs su spangs te zhen pa med par byas nas zab mo stong pa dmigs pa med pa bsgom par bya ste rnal 'byor pas du ba la sogs pa'i rtags 'byung ba mthong bar 'gyur ro/[95] / zhes sogs gsungs pa rnams kyi don ci yin snyam na/ /

In that case, it may be wondered what the meaning of this passage from the Vajrapāṇi Commentary is?
Therefore, abandoning all perception of existence and nonexistence, not grasping, meditate on the profound, nonapprehended emptiness, and the yogi will see the signs of smoke and so forth arise.[109]

d.div: [95] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 131_na7
[109] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 131a7.

f.d: de dag gi don ni/ bsam pa thams cad yongs spangs nas/ /zhes pa'i don bshad zin pa dang 'dra bar sor sdud kyi dmigs pa las gzhan pa'i yod pa dang med par 'dzin pa'i blo yongs su spangs te yod med kyi yul de dag la zhen pa med par byas la gong du bshad pa'i sor sdud kyi dmigs pa de nyid la dmigs nas bsgoms pa las sor sdud kyi lam gyi ngo bo zab mo rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong pa dmigs pa med pa de 'byung bas de bsgom par bya ste/ de yang ji lta bu snyam na/ rnal 'byor pas du ba la sogs pa'i rtags 'byung ba mthong bar 'gyur ba de rnams so/ /zhes pa ltar yin te/

The meaning of this passage is similar to that given previously on the line, “Having abandoned all thoughts.” Having abandoned all perception of objects existing and nonexisting, except for those of withdrawal meditation, there will be no grasping to those existing and nonexisting objects. Focusing and meditating on the /362/ previously described meditation objects of withdrawal will bring about the profound nature of the path of withdrawal, which is the “nonapprehended emptiness,” endowed with every supreme aspect. How does this occur? “The yogi will see the signs of smoke and so forth arise.”

'grel tshig de dag gi don 'chad pa la dgongs nas nA ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa las/
de'i phyir yod pa dang med pa'i blo yongs su spangs te rten med par byas nas stong pa zab mo dmigs pa med pa'i rtags su 'gyur te du ba la sogs pa'i rtags kyi don du rnal 'byor pas bsgom par bya'o/[96] / zhes gsal bar gsungs so/ /

Moreover Nāropa, in his Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations, with an explanation of the meaning of these Great Commentary words in mind, clearly says:
Therefore, abandoning perception of existence and nonexistence, with no support, the signs of the profound, nonapprehended emptiness will arise. The yogi meditates for the arising of the signs of smoke and so forth.[110]

d.div: [96] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 252_ba5
[110] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 252b5.

f.d:
'di'i don yang gzhan snga ma dang 'dra ba la/ rten med par byas nas zhes pa'i don ni rdos bcas kyi dmigs rten med pa gong du bshad pa'i nam mkha' bar stong la dmigs pa'o/ / de bzhin du dpe med 'tsho'i sbyor drug dang / de'i 'grel pa nyi ma dpal gyis mdzad pa'i yon tan gyis 'gengs pa rnams las kyang gsungs te/ sbyor drug de nyid las/
des na yod pa dang med pa'i blo yongs su spangs te rten med par byas nas zab mo stong pa la dmigs pa med par bsgom par bya ste yid ches byed du 'gyur ro/ / yid ches byed de yang du ba la sogs pa rnal 'byor pas bsgom par bya'o/[97] / zhes dang /

The meaning of this passage is similar to others quoted previously. “With no support” means no material or objective support but having instead a focus of empty space, as previously described. Similarly Anupamarakṣita says in his Six Yogas:
Therefore, abandoning thoughts of existence and nonexistence, with no support, meditate on the deep nonapprehended emptiness, and signs of verification will occur. The signs of verification are those of smoke and so forth, and the yogi meditates upon these.[111]

d.div: [97] sde dge_1387_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pasbyor ba yan lag drug pa/ 297_ba5
[111] Toh 1387 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 297b5.

f.d:
yon tan gyis 'gengs pa las/
stong pa nyid sgom pa ni rnam pa thams cad pa'i stong pa nyid rtogs pa'o/ / mtshan ma ni mun pa la ste nyin bar ni snang ba la'o/[98] / zhes gsal bar gsungs pas zab mo stong pa dmigs pa med pa zhes sogs gsungs pa rnams sor sdud kyi lam gyi ngo bo grub pa'i gnas skabs kyi rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong pa rnams la go bar bya'o/ /

Also Sūryaśrī in Filled with Good Qualities says:
The meditation on emptiness is a perception of fully aspected emptiness. “Night” refers to darkness. “Day” refers to light.[112] Therefore “profound, nonapprehended emptiness” and so on should be understood as referring to an emptiness endowed with every supreme aspect developed during the actualization of the path of withdrawal.

d.div: [98] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 325_ba5
[112] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 325b5.

f.d: de bzhin du rdo rje snying 'grel las/ bdag med pa'i rnal 'byor 'di zhes pa dang / stong pa nyid gang la sems rtse gcig par bzhag na zhes sogs kyang sor sdud kyi lam gyi ngo bo stong gzugs la dgongs pa yin te/ rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong gzugs ni thabs shes gnyis kyi shes rab kyi phyogs yin pas bdag med pa'i rnal 'byor [99] zhes sogs gsungs pa yin no/ /

Likewise the lines “this yoga of nonself” and “placing the mind one-pointedly in emptiness” from the Vajragarbha Commentary[113] are also referring to an empty form that is the very path of withdrawal. This is so because the empty form endowed with every supreme aspect belongs to the wisdom category of method and wisdom, and so it is referred to as “this yoga of nonself” and so forth.

d.div: [99] sde dge_1180_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ka_rdo rje snying 'grel/ dngos grub kyi le'u gnyis pa/ 80_ba7
[113] Toh 1180 Tengyur, rgyud, ka, chap. 2, 80b7.

f.d: bshad tshul 'di ni 'grel tshig de dag gi don dpyis phyin pa yin zhing / khyad par du yang rje btsun tsong kha pa'i dgongs pa ltar 'chad pa dag gis ni 'chad tshul 'di bzhin du nges par byed dgos so/ /

This explanation of the above topics is the definitive meaning of these words from the Great Commentary, and those whose explanations are to accord with the thinking of Jé Tsongkhapa should definitely explain them in this way.
lnga pa de ltar bsgoms pas nyams rtags 'char tshul gyi nges pa

d.i: The signs of meditative accomplishment and their appearance

f.d: ['di ]la gnyis/ rgyud 'grel dang rgya gzhung rnams las bshad tshul dgod pa dang / nyams rtags 'char tshul mdor bsdus te bstan pa'o/ /
This is under two headings: 1. Descriptions in the tantra and commentary and in Indian texts 2. Summarized description of how the signs arise
dang po [rgyud 'grel dang rgya gzhung rnams las bshad tshul dgod pa ]ni
Descriptions in the tantra and commentary and in Indian texts

dbang mdor bstan las/
kun rtog yongs su spangs pa'o/ / du ba smig rgyu me khyer dang / / mar me 'bar dang /[100] zhes dang /

A Short Teaching on Initiations states:
With all conceptuality abandoned, smoke, mirage, fireflies, and the flame of a butter lamp arise.[114]

d.div: [100] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan/ 15_na2_tshig sna cung mi mthun/
[114] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 15a2.

f.d:
bsdus rgyud las
stong pa las ni du ba smig rgyu rab gsal dri ma med pa'i mkha' snang nyid dang mar me dang /[101] zhes dang

The Condensed Tantra says:
From the emptiness arises smoke, mirage, a clear uncontaminated appearance within space, and a butter-lamp flame.[115]

d.div: [101] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka115_113_na2
[115] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud ka, v. 115, 113a2.

f.d:
de'i 'grel par/
stong pa las ni du ba smig rgyu rab gsal dri ma med pa'i mkha' snang nyid dang mar me dang zhes pa na mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor gyis mthong ngo /[102] / zhes rtags bzhi po de mtshan mo'i rtags su gsungs shing / mtshan rtags de rnams gang las gsungs pa'i khungs ni 'grel chen las/
de ltar mtshan ma rnams bcu ste 'dus pa la sogs pa las mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor dang /[103] zhes 'dus pa dang / la sogs pas rdo rje gur las mtshan rtags rnams bshad par gsungs so/ /

On this the Great Commentary says:
“From the emptiness arises smoke, mirage, a clear uncontaminated appearance within space, a butter-lamp flame.” These are seen by the night yoga.[116] /363/ These four signs, therefore, are described as being night signs. As for their scriptural source, the Great Commentary says:
Of the ten signs, those of the night are found in the Guhya samāja and others.[117] “Others” refers to the Vajra Tent Tantra. Therefore the Great Commentary teaches that the night signs are spoken of in these two tantras.

d.div: [102] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 388_ba3
[103] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 388_ba5
[116] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 388b3.
[117] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 388b5.

f.d:
de bzhin du bde mchog stod 'grel las kyang /
de ltar du ba ni mtshan ma dang po'o/ / smig rgyu ni mtshan ma gnyis pa'o/ / mkha' snang ni mtshan ma gsum pa'o/ / sgron ma ni mtshan ma bzhi pa'o/ / sprin med pa'i nam mkha' lta bu ni mtshan ma lnga pa'o/ / zhes 'dus pa phyi ma dang mkha' 'gro ma rdo rje gur du bcom ldan 'das kyis gsungs so/[104] / zhes mtshan rtags rnams gsang 'dus kyi rgyud phyi ma dang rdo rje gur nas gsungs par gsungs so/ /

The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary also speaks of the night signs as coming from the Later Guhyasamāja Tantra and the Vajra Tent Tantra:
Smoke is the first sign, mirage the second, lights in the sky the third, a lamp the fourth, and the clarity of a cloudless sky is the fifth. These are spoken of by the Buddha in the Later Guhyasamāja and the Dakinī Vajra Tent.[118]

d.div: [104] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 131_ba3
[118] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 131b3.

f.d:
'dus pa phyi ma nas ji ltar gsungs pa ni de nyid las/
'gog pa rdo rje bgrod sems la/ / mtshan ma nyer 'dzin 'byung 'gyur te/ / mtshan ma de ni rnam lngar 'gyur/ / byang chub rdo rjes bshad pa yin/ / dang po smig rgyu'i rnam pa ste/ / gnyis pa du ba'i rnam pa yin/ / gsum pa mkha' snang rnam pa ste/ / bzhi pa sgron ma 'bar ba 'o/ / lnga pa rtag tu snang ba ni/ / sprin med nam mkha' lta bu'o/[105] / zhes gsungs pa rnams so/ /

In the Later Guhyasamāja Tantra itself, these signs are taught as follows:
To the mind of vajra cessation, signs, closely held, will appear. These signs are of five kinds, Bodhivajra[119] has explained. The first is the form of a mirage, the second that of smoke, third is light in the sky, fourth is a burning lamp, and fifth is a constant clarity, like a cloudless sky.[120]

d.div: [105] sde dge_443_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_gsang 'dus rgyud phyi ma/ 154_ba3_tshig sna cung mi mthun/
[119] The Buddha manifest as the tantric Vajradhara.
[120] Toh 443 Kangyur, rgyud cha, 154b3.

f.d:
gzhan yang 'dus pa phyi ma dang mthun par 'jam dpal gyi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan par gsungs pa ni/
yid ches don can bsgom par bya/ / dang po smig rgyu'i rnam pa ste/ / gnyis pa du ba 'dra ba'o/ / gsum pa me khyer rnam pa ste/ / bzhi pa mar me 'dra ba'o/ / lnga pa rtag tu snang ba ni/ / sprin med nam mkha' 'dra ba nyid/[106] / ces mtshan rtags rnams 'dus pa nas gsungs tshul bzhin du gsungs nas/

In accord with the Later Guhyasamāja, A Short Teaching on the Views of Mañjuśrī also states:
Meditate on signs of reliability: the first the form of a mirage, the second is like smoke, the third, fireflies, the fourth, like a lamp, the fifth is a constant clarity, like a cloudless sky.[121] These lines list the signs as they are spoken of in the Guhyasamāja.

d.div: [106] pe cing bstan 'gyur nas kha bskang ba dar thang dpar ma'i pod/ pu/ chos tshan ang / 4530_rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa/ 23_na6
[121] Text not found; possibly, Short Teachings on the View (Lta ba mdor bsdud pa, Dṛiṣṭisaṃkṣipta), Toh 2304.

f.d:
de'i 'phro nyid las/ nam mkha' las byung rang byung ba/[107] /zhes sogs kyi rtags rnams 'chad pa'i mtshan rjod kyi lung rnams bkod nas/ de dag gi mjug tu dus 'khor nas gsungs pa ltar nyams su blangs pa las rtags rnams 'byung tshul ston pa ni/ /
du ba smig rgyu me khyer dang / / sgron ma 'bar ba zla nyi dang / / mun can cha dang thig le che/ / sna tshogs gzugs brnyan 'od gsal ba/ / btsums dang ma btsums mig dag gis/ / stong par gang zhig rjes btags min/ / rmi lam bzhin du gzugs mthong 'gyur/ / gzugs de rtag tu bsgom par bya/[108] / zhes sogs gsungs so/ /

The text continues with the lines “Arising from space, self-arising,”[122] and so on, which is a description of the signs taken from the Saṃgīti.[123] After these lines the order of signs as listed in the Kālacakra are quoted:
Smoke, mirage, fireflies, lamp alit, moon and sun, darkness, great drops, various forms, and clear light; with eyes closed and unclosed, in the emptiness, not imputed, dreamlike forms are seen. Meditate constantly on these forms. /364/

d.div: [107] sde dge_443_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_gsang 'dus rgyud phyi ma/ 132_na3 sde dge_360_bka'/ rgyud/ ka'ajam dpal mtshan brjod/ 4_na7
[108] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan/ 15_na2
[122] See Toh 443 Kangyur, rgyud, cha, 132a3.
[123] Toh 360 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 4a7.

f.d:
'o na 'dus pa nas smig rgyu lta bu'i rtags dang por bshad pa dang / 'dir du ba lta bu rtags rnams kyi dang por bshad pa gnyis 'gal lo snyam na/ 'di'i 'gal spong la kha cig na re/ 'dus par bshad pa de zab don sbas te gsungs pas drang don yin/ 'dir ma sbas par gsal bar gsungs pas nges don yin pas mi 'gal lo zhes gsung ste/ de'i shes byed ni dbang mdor bstan gyi nA ro pa'i 'grel pa las/
mtshan ma nyer 'dzin 'byung 'gyur te zhes pa du ba la sogs pa'i mtshan ma rnams kyi nyer 'dzin rab tu gsal ba 'byung 'gyur te skye bar 'gyur ro/ / dang po dang gnyis pa'i mtshan ma bzlog ste bstan pa ni bla ma'i gzhan dbang nyid du bstan pa'i don to/[109] / zhes gsungs pa'i don du dgongs par mngon no/ /

In the Guhyasamāja the miragelike sign comes first. Here in the Kālacakra the smokelike sign is said to be the first. Is this not a contradiction? In order to resolve this, some say that there is no contradiction, because the Guhyasamāja quote is taught with its deep meaning hidden and is, therefore interpretative, whereas here the meaning is taught clearly and openly and is therefore definitive. It appears they think this is the meaning of a passage from Nāropa’s Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations, which is their authority for their assertion:
“Signs, closely held, will appear” means that the signs of smoke and so on closely held will appear very clearly. The reversal of the first and second signs is due to the teachings of the gurus.[124]

d.div: [109] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 247_na4
[124] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 247a4.

f.d: 'gal spong de ni mi 'thad de/ 'dus pa'i dgongs pa rim lnga dang 'jam dpal zhal lung sogs kyis bkral ba ltar nyams su blangs pas smig rgyu lta bu'i rtags dang por 'char ba klu sgrub sogs grub chen rnams kyi myong bas grub pa sgra sor bzhag tu rgya gzhung rnams su bkod pa dang / nA ro pas kyang 'dus pa phyi ma'i 'grel par smig rgyu lta bu'i rtags dang po yin pa sgra ji bzhin du bshad cing / sor sdud dus 'khor nas bshad pa ltar nyams su blangs pas du ba lta bu'i rtags dang por 'char ba dus 'khor ba'i sor sdud nyams len pa rnams kyi myong bas grub pa ltar rgyud 'grel rnams su yang bkod pa yin no/ /

However this is not a correct resolution of the contradiction. Meditative practices that follow such texts as the Five Stages and the Oral Tradition of Mañjuśrī,[125] which teach according to the thinking of Guhyasamāja, will produce the miragelike sign first. This has been verified by the experiences of the great siddhas, such as Nāgārjuna, who have recorded them literally in the great Indian texts. Nāropa also, while commenting on the Later Guhyasamāja, is writing literally when he says that the miragelike sign is the first. The smokelike sign arising first, as described in the Kālacakra withdrawal, is also established by the actual experience of Kālacakra withdrawal practitioners and is presented in the tantra and commentary accordingly.

d.div: [125] Toh 1853/54 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, di.

f.d:
mdor na man ngag nyams su len tshul mi 'dra ba'i gnas rtags kyi 'char tshul go rim mi 'dra ba byung ba yin te/ bde mchog stod 'grel las/
'dir bla ma'i nye bar bstan pa las nam mkha' la rnal 'byor pas dang por du ba mthong ste smig rgyu ni ma yin no zhes rang gi nyams su myong bas shes par bya'o/ / de'i phyi nas smig rgyu ste/[110] zhes bshad la/ de dag gi don ni bde mchog nyung ngu'i rgyud kyi sbyor drug dus 'khor ltar nyams su len pa'i skabs 'dir bla ma'i man ngag dus 'khor bzhin du nye bar bstan pa las nam mkha' la rnal 'byor pas dang por du ba mthong ste smig rgyu ni ma yin no/ /

To summarize: different traditions of practice mean that signs arise in different orders. The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
From the instructions of the guru, the yogi who practices in the space of night first sees smoke, not a mirage. This will be known from his experience. After that comes the mirage.[126] This passage explicitly teaches that when the six yogas of the Short Guhyasamāja are practiced according to Kālacakra, the instructions of the guru are given in accordance with Kālacakra, from which “the yogi who practices in the space of night first sees smoke, /365/ not a mirage.”

d.div: [110] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 131_ba2
[126] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 131b2.

f.d: de yang rnal 'byor pa rang gi nyams su myong bas shes par bya'o zhes dngos su bstan nas/ de'i shugs bstan ni bde mchog nyung ngu'i rgyud kyi sbyor drug zhal lung dang sgron gsal ltar nyams su len pa'i skabs der ni bla ma'i nye bar bstan pa las rnal 'byor pas dang po smig rgyu mthong ste du ba ni ma yin no zhes rang gi nyams su myong bas shes par bya'o/ / de'i phyi nas du ba ste zhes bya bar go bar bya dgos te/ 'grel tshig de dag ni mtshan rtags rnams 'dus pa phyi ma dang rdo rje gur du gsungs pa shes byed du bkod pa'i dwogs spong yin la/ de yang man ngag nyams su len tshul mi 'dra ba'i sgo nas rtags dang po'i 'char tshul mi 'dra ba min par/ smig rgyu dang por bshad pa rnam pa thams cad du drang don nyid yin na 'dir yang de ltar bshad dgos pa la 'dir rang gi nyams su myong bas shes par bya'o/[111] / zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

Furthermore “this will be known from his own experience.” Implicitly it teaches that when the six yogas of the Short Guhyasamāja are practiced according to the Oral Tradition of Mañjuśrī and Bright Lamp, the yogi, by following the instructions of the guru, will know from his own experience that “first comes the mirage, not the smoke,” after which comes the smoke. This has to be the way to understand it, because the above commentary passages refer to the verses of the Later Guhyasamāja and the Vajra Tent in order to dispel any doubts concerning the sources for the night signs. If it were not the case that different signs appear first depending on the tradition of practice, and if the teaching of the mirage appearing first was solely a provisional teaching, then that fact would have been mentioned in the commentary. Instead it says, “This will be known from his experience.”

d.div: [111] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 131_ba2

f.d:
gzhan yang nyi ma dpal gyis yon tan gyis 'gengs pa las/
rgyud gzhan du/ dang por smig rgyu lta bu ste/ / zhes pa lugs las bzlog pas rtogs par bya'o/[112] / zhes pa'i bar ro/ / zhes sogs 'grel skor nas 'dus par smig rgyu dang por bshad pa de du ba dang lugs bzlog tu bshad tshul bkod nas/ skabs 'dir lugs bzlog phyed pa'i rgyu mtshan 'chad pa ni/ de'i 'phro nyid las/
'di yang bla ma dam pa'i nye bar bstan pa las dang / byang chub sems dpas mdzad pa'i rgya cher 'grel pa las dang / rang gi nyams su myong ba las kyang rnam par shes par bya ste/[113] zhes gsungs so/ /

Furthermore, Sūryaśrī in his Filled with Good Qualities says:
Other tantras say “first the miragelike.” It should be understood therefore that the order is reversed.[127] Therefore the description in the Guhyasamāja of the mirage as the first sign reverses the order of the tradition that begins with the smokelike sign. He goes on to explain the reasons for this reversal:
This can be understood from the instructions of the holy guru, the extensive commentary of the bodhisattva, and from one’s own experience.[128]

d.div: [112] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 323_na7
[113] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 323_na7
[127] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 323a7.
[128] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 323a7.

f.d: de dag gi don ni/ smig rgyu dang po dang du ba gnyis par bshad pa skabs 'dir lugs las bzlog dgos pa 'di yang bla ma dam pa'i sbyor drug gi gdams ngag dus 'khor ltar nye bar bstan pa las dang / de ltar bstan pa ltar nyams su blangs pa las du ba lta bu dang po dang smig rgyu lta bu de'i rjes su 'char ba rang gi nyams su myong bas kyang rnam par shes par bya zhing / byang chub sems dpa' pad+ma dkar pos mdzad pa'i rgya cher 'grel pa dri med 'od las du ba dang por bshad pa las kyang shes par bya'o/[114] /zhes pa'o/ /

This means the teaching that the first sign is the mirage followed by smoke has to be reversed here. This is due to the instructions of the holy gurus on the six yogas being taught according to the Kālacakra. By practicing these instructions as taught by the gurus, the smokelike sign arising first followed by the miragelike sign will be known from one’s own experience. This can also be known from Stainless Light, “the extensive commentary of the bodhisattva” Puṇḍarīka.

d.div: [114] sde dge_1398_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pha'ajam dpal mtshan brjod kyi 'grel pa dri ma med pa'i 'od/ 198_ba3

f.d:
de yang 'dus pa phyi ma'i sbyor drug gi don bla ma'i man ngag gis dus 'khor ltar nyams su blangs na du ba dang po dang de nas smig rgyu lta bu 'char bar bstan nas dngos bstan ltar nyams su blangs pa'i rtags kyi 'char tshul ston pa ni 'grel pa de'i 'phro nyid las/
gtso bor khams lnga rnam par dag pa'i ngo bo mtshan ma lnga rnams dpal 'dus pa la sogs par rab tu rtogs par mdzad de/ nam mkha'i khams kyang der gsungs pa nyid kyi phyir ro/[115] / zhes smig rgyu dang por byas pa'i rtags lnga 'byung ba rim gyis thim pa'i rtags su bshad nas

Therefore, when the six yogas of the Later Guhyasamāja are practiced according to a guru’s teachings in keeping with the Kālacakra, /366/ the first sign will be smoke followed by the mirage. The commentary continues with an explanation of the arising of the signs in accord with their actual presentation in the Later Guhyasamāja:
Primarily the five signs, of the nature of the five pure elements, are to be understood as being those of the Guhyasamāja Tantra and others. This is so because the text also talks of the element of space.[129] Therefore, beginning with the mirage, the five signs are explained as being the signs of the elements dissolving into each other.

d.div: [115] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 323_ba7
[129] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 323b7.

f.d:
de nyid 'dus pa'i rgyud dang sbyor ba ni de'i 'phro nyid las/
le'u bco brgyad par gsungs pa yang / chu dang me dang rlung dang sa/ / nam mkha' de rnams thams cad ni/ / byang chub sems dpa' dang 'dra bar rnam pa dmigs bzhin pa yin no zhes so/[116]/zhes bshad bya bkod nas/

Applying that to the Guhyasamāja, the commentary continues:
In the eighteenth chapter it states, “Water, fire, air, earth, and space, all of these.” These are similar in form and aspect to those of the bodhisattva.[130]

d.div: [116] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 323_ba1
[130] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 323b1.

f.d:
'di'i don 'chad pa ni de'i 'phro nyid las/
sa chu la thim pa las smig rgyu'i rnam pa'o/ / chu me la thim pa las du ba'i rnam pa'o/ / me rlung la thim pa las mkha' snang gi rnam pa'o/ / phra mo'i khams kyi snang ba gsum nam mkha' la sgron me 'dra bar snang ba'i phung po'i chos nyid kyi phyir sgron ma'i rnam pa'o/ / rang bzhin snang ba nub pa las sprin med pa'i nam mkha' dang 'dra ba'i rtags su snang ba'i ngo bo nyid ni sprin med pa'i nam mkha' dang mtshungs pa'o zhes pa'i mtshan ma lnga rnams so/[117] / zhes gsungs pa

This is the topic to be explained. The explanation follows:
Earth absorbs into water from which arises the mirage. Water sinks into fire from which arises the smoke. Fire is absorbed into air from which arise lights in the sky. The appearance of the three subtle elements is like the appearance of a lamp in space and is therefore known as the sign of the lamp. From the sinking of that appearance arises a constant appearance like the cloud-free sky, known as the cloudless sky–like sign. These are the five signs.[131]

d.div: [117] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 323_ba2
[131] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 323b2.

f.d:
yang /
dang por sa ni chu la 'gro/ / chu ni gtsang byed la 'gro ste/ / gtsang byed rlung la rjes su 'gro/ / rnam par shes pa rlung 'jug byed/ / rnam shes 'dzin pa'i yan lag nyid/ / de na 'od gsal ba la 'jug /ces so/[118] / zhes shes byed dang bcas te/

The commentary then provides the source for this explanation:
First earth goes into water. Water goes into fire, fire sinks into air, air enters consciousness, consciousness, the apprehending, enters the clear light.[132]

d.div: [118] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 323_ba3
[132] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 323b3.

f.d:
'dus pa las smig rgyu lta bu rtags dang por gsungs pa sgra ji bzhin par bshad du rung ba dang / de yang 'byung ba rnams snga ma phyi ma la thim pa'i rtags dang / de bzhin du de'i 'phro nyid las/
sgyu 'phrul 'dra bar nyin mo'i rnal 'byor kyis phung po drug rnam par dag pa'i ngo bo'i mtshan ma drug rnams nam mkha' las byung [119] zhes pa la sogs pas gsungs so/ / dpal ldan dang po'i sangs rgyas rgyud kyi lhag pa'i rgyal po ru ni yul dang dbang po'i shes rab dang thabs rnam par dag pa'i ngo bo'i mtshan ma bcu rnams gtso bor rtogs par mdzad do/ / zhes bshad do/ /

Therefore it is acceptable to explain the Guhyasamāja‘s assertion of the mirage as being the first sign as a literal explanation and, moreover, they are the signs of the elements progressively dissolving. Similarly, the commentary continues:
The Net of Illusion Tantra says that by the daytime yoga, the six signs having the nature of the six pure aggregates arise from the element of space. The glorious Mahārāja Primordial Buddha Tantra primarily speaks of ten signs having the nature of the purified method and wisdom of the senses and their objects.[133]

d.div: [119] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 323_ba4
[133] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 323b4.

f.d: de dag gi don ni 'dus pa las 'byung ba rnams snga ma phyi ma la thim pa'i rtags smig rgyu sogs bzhi/ dus 'khor gyi mtshan rtags bzhi dang mthun pas mtshan rtags zhes bshad cing / sgyu 'phrul dra ba nas phung po [120] drug dag pa'i mtshan ma 'am rtags drug dus 'khor gyi nyin rtags drug dang mthun pas nyin rtags zhes bshad pa yin gyi/ dus 'khor gyi rtags bcu'i ngo bo ni gzugs sogs yul lnga shes rab dang mig sogs dbang po lnga thabs su byas pa'i thabs shes bcu dag pa'i mtshan ma 'am rtags su bshad la/ thabs shes bcu po dag pa yang rlung bcu dbu mar tshud pa las yin zhing / rlung bcu po de yang gzung 'dzin gyi rlung bcu ste/ de yang snying ga na yul can gyi dbang shes lnga yul la g.yo byed kyi rlung lnga yod pa de mig sogs dbang po lnga la brten nas 'jug pa rnams dang / de bzhin du snying ga na gzugs sogs yul lnga gsal bar byed pa'i rlung lnga yod pa des gzugs sgra sogs gsal bar byed pa rnams so/ /

This means that the four signs of the progressive dissolution of the elements as found in /367/ the Guhyasamāja are similar to the four night signs of the Kālacakra and therefore are explained as night signs. The six signs of the six purified aggregates as spoken of in the Net of Illusion Tantra are similar to the six daytime signs of the Kālacakra and are therefore explained as daytime signs. However the nature of the ten signs from Kālacakra is that of purified method and wisdom: the five sense objects, form and so forth, are wisdom, and the five sense organs, eyes and so forth, are method. These ten types of purified method and wisdom arise from the ten winds entering the central channel. These ten winds consist of apprehending winds and apprehended winds. At the heart are located the five winds that move the five sense consciousnesses to the five sense objects. These engage objects in dependence upon the five sense organs. Also at the heart are the five enhancing and clarifying winds of the five sense objects of form and so forth. These winds clarify and enhance forms, sound, and so forth. These ten winds are stopped from flowing into the right and left channels and to the sense-organ entrances and instead enter the dhūtī.

d.div: [120] ma dper yung po gsal yang phung po min nam/

f.d:
de lta bu'i rlung bcu po de ro rkyang dang dbang po'i sgo so so la rgyu ba bkag ste ng+hU tIr chud pa las yul dang yul can bcu po rnams 'jug pa med pas rtags bcu 'char ba yin te/ sgrub le'i brgya bcu drug pa las/
so sor sdud pa lus la yul dang yul can bcu po rnams ni rab tu 'jug pa med pa'o/[121] / zhes pa dang / de'i 'grel par/
'dir so sor sdud pa zhes bya ba ni lus la yul dang yul can bcu po rnams kyi 'brel bas [122] rnam par shes pa rab tu 'jug pa med pa ste stong pa'i gzugs kyi yul rnams la mig gzhan la sogs pa rnam pa lnga po rnams kyis rab tu 'jug pa'o/[123] / zhes sogs gsungs pa rnams kyi don yang 'di nyid yin no/ /

This halts the activity between the five senses and five sense objects, thereby bringing about the appearance of the ten signs. Verse 116 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter also conveys this meaning:
In withdrawal within the body, the ten subjects and objects are not engaged.[134] The Great Commentary on this verse says:
Withdrawal means that within the body, consciousness is not engaged in the connection between the ten subjects and objects. The five, eyes and so forth, are engaged in empty-form objects.[135]

d.div: [121] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka165_89_ba3
[122] ma dper 'grel pa chad pa'i zhes byung yang 'brel pa chad pa'i zhes bcos/
[123] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 237_na5
[134] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 165, 89b3.
[135] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 237a5.

f.d:
gzung 'dzin gyi rlung de dag ni bshad rgyud rdor 'phreng las gsungs pa rnams te/ de ltar yang rdor 'phreng las/
snying gi dbus gnas bde ba'i dngos/ / sangs rgyas nyi ma gsal ba'i 'od/ / gzung dang 'dzin pa'i gzugs kyis kyang / / de na 'od zer bcu gnyis so/ / 'od 'phel 'od zer gzi brjid ma/ / gsal ba 'bar ma 'od 'bar ma/ mig la sogs pa la brten nas/ / phyi rol gzugs sogs 'dzin pa'o/ / 'od zer 'od ma snang ba ma/ / gsal mdzes gsal 'od nyi ma gsal/ / phyi rol gzugs sogs rnam pa'o/[124] / zhes gsungs pa'i 'od 'phel sogs dang po lnga dang / 'od zer sogs dang po lnga 'dir gzung ngo / /

These apprehending and apprehended winds are spoken of in the Vajra Garland Explanatory Tantra:
Within the heart, the light of bliss, the illuminating light of the Buddha sun, the apprehending and apprehension of form: these the ten rays of light. Expanding light, rays of light, brilliance, the illuminating and shining, the shining light: they apprehend external form by way of the eyes and so forth. Light, luminosity, illuminatingly beautiful, illuminating light, illuminating sun: these in aspects of external form.[136] The first five winds are called expanding light and so forth. The second five are called light and so forth and are in the aspect of “objects.” /368/

d.div: [124] sde dge_445_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ cabashad rgyud rdo rje 'phreng ba/ 241_na7
[136] Toh 445 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, cha, 241a7.

f.d: gnyis pa nyams rtags 'char tshul

d.i: Summarized description of how the signs arise

f.d: mdor bsdus te bstan pa ni/ gong du bshad pa ltar gyi lus gnad lta stangs sems kyi 'jog tshul rnams ma 'chugs par byas te bskyangs pas gnas cha cung zad rnyed pa'i tshe lta ltangs byed tshul gyi gnad kyis mig shes yul la g.yo bar byed pa'i rlung rengs nas nang du sdud la/ de'i rjes su dbang shes gzhan rnams yul la g.yo bar byed pa'i rlung rnams kyang rengs nas nang du sdud do/ / de'i tshe dbang yul gyi 'brel ba [125] chad pa'i 'go brtsams pas rtags sna tshogs 'char yang sor sdud kyi rtags dngos gzhi min no/ / de'i rjes su gzung 'dzin gyi rlung rnams sna bug nas 'byung 'jug byed pa'i rlung gzhan rnams dang bcas pa dbu mar 'jug la de'i tshe nyams snang sna tshogs 'char tshul rnams ni bla ma rnams kyis mdzad pa'i 'khrid yig rnams las shes par bya'o/ /

When the yogi has developed some concentration from a correct practice of mental placement, posture, and eye positioning as previously explained, the position of the eyes will cause the winds that move the eye consciousness to its objects to stiffen and withdraw. The winds that move the other sense consciousnesses to their objects will do the same. At this time the connection between sense and sense object is broken, and various signs will appear. However these are not the actual signs of withdrawal. Then the apprehending and apprehended winds along with other winds that flow though the nostrils will enter the central channel. At that time various appearances arise, and the way they arise can be understood from the instruction texts composed by the masters.

d.div: [125] ma dper 'grel ba zhes gsal na'ang 'brel zhes bcos/

f.d:
'dir nges pa'i rtags 'byung tshul sna bug gnyis nas rlung mnyam rgyu byed pa ni dbu ma nyid la rgyu ba yin par nges la/ de la yang gzhi dus su zhag re la dbugs drug brgya dang don lngar dbu ma nas rgyu bas rlung dbu ma nas rgyu ba tsam la nges pa med kyang / gong du bshad pa'i lus gnad lta stangs sems kyi 'jog tshul sogs byas pa'i tshe de'i stobs kyis dus nam yang rlung mnyam rgyur nges can du thengs kyi 'dug na bsgoms stobs kyis rlung dbu mar chud pa yin zhing / de ltar rlung bcu ng+hU tIr tshud pa las mtshan rtags 'char te/ bde mchog stod 'grel las/
mtshan ma zhes bya ba ni sprin dang du ba la sogs pa ltar snang ba ste de yang sgron ma'i mthar thug pa dang por mthong ba'o/[126] / zhes pa dang /

The winds flowing equally though both nostrils indicates that the winds are flowing in the central channel. This ensures the appearance of definitive signs. However, in ordinary existence, 675 breaths flow through the central channel every day, and therefore the winds merely entering the central channel is no guarantee that signs will arise. However, when the winds are definitely flowing equally through both nostrils through the force of practice, with the body, eyes, and mind positioned and placed, the winds will have entered the central channel through the power of meditation. From the ten winds entering the dhūtī, the night signs will arise. The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
“Signs” refers to the appearances that are like clouds, smoke, and so forth. Those ending with the lamp are seen first.[137]

d.div: [126] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 132_na2
[137] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 132a2.

f.d:
'grel pa yon tan gyis 'gengs pa las kyang /
du ba zhes pa la sogs pa la phyi dang nang thams cad du khyab pa du ba'i rnam pa can stong pa'i rnam pa ste 'di yang sprin lta bur snang ba'i bar ma chad du 'byung ngo /[127] / ji skad du gsungs pa/ dang po sprin dang 'dra bar snang / / gnyis pa du ba lta bu'o/[128] / zhes so zhes bshad pa ltar/ dang po sprin lta bu'i rnam pa dang / de nas du ba lta bu dang / de nas smig rgyu lta bu dang / de nas me khyer lta bu dang / de nas sgron me lta bu dang / de nas stong sang nam mkha' g.ya' dag gi rnam pa lta bu 'char ro/ / de ltar 'char yang mtshan rtags bzhir gsungs pa'i skabs 'dir sprin gyi rnam pa lta bu dang sprin med pa'i nam mkha' lta bu gnyis rtags su mi bgrang ngo / /

The commentary Filled with Qualities also says:
Concerning “smoke” and so forth: pervading everything inside and out, a smokelike empty-aspect appearance arises. Here too a cloudlike appearance arises without hindrance. As it is taught, first comes the cloudlike appearance, then the smokelike.[138] In the above passages the first sign is the cloud-like, the second is the smoke-like, followed by the mirage-like, firefly-like, lamp-like, and a vacuity like a clear sky. Although the signs are presented this way, here in the section on night signs the /369/ cloud-like sign and the cloudless sky–like sign are not included.

d.div: [127] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 320_ba6
[128] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 259_ba5
[138] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 320b6.

f.d:
de la yang phyi dang nang thams cad du khyab pa du ba'i rnam pa can zhes bshad pa ltar dang por du sogs kyi rtags bzhi po de shar ba'i tshe lus kyi phyi nang thams cad khyab pa lta bu'i rnam par 'char zhing phyis goms pa brtan pa nang+hU tI 'i nang du 'char ba yin te/ ye le'i brgya nyer gcig pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir dang por rnal 'byor pas dbu mar srog ni rab tu gzhug par bya ste gang gi mtshan ma mthong bar 'gyur ba a wa ng+hU tIr ro/[129] / zhes gsal bar gsungs pas so/ /

The above quote states, “everything inside and out is pervaded by a smoke-like appearance,” meaning that when the four signs first appear, they seem to pervade everything inside and outside the body. Later, as one’s meditational development becomes more stable, the signs appear within the dhūtī. The Great Commentary on verse 121 of the Gnosis chapter clearly says:
Here, initially, the yogi places the winds in the central channel, by which he will see the signs within the avadhūtī.[139]

d.div: [129] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 390_ba5
[139] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 390b5.

f.d: de yang dang por dal po sngo khyug pa'i rnam pa can gyi du ba nyid 'byung zhing gzhan ma 'byung la/ de'i rjes su smig rgyu dal po sngo mer ba'i rnam pa can nyid 'byung ba dang / de bzhin du de sangs pa'i rjes su srin bu me khyer lta bu'i rnam pa nyid 'byung / de yang sangs pa'i rjes su mar me 'bar ba'i rnam pa nyid 'byung / de sangs pa'i rjes su stong pa ston gyi nam mkha' g.ya' dag gi rnam pa 'char ro/ / de yang sor sdud kyi dmigs pa sgom res kyi rlung dbu mar chud de rtags rnams ng+hU tI'i nang du rim pa nges can du 'char na mtshan rtags rnams rdzogs pa yin pas 'tshams 'di nas nyin mo'i rnal 'byor sgom pa la 'jug go/

The first sign gradually appears in the form of blue wisps of smoke. Nothing else is seen. After that a bluish shimmering miragelike appearance occurs. When that has cleared, the fireflies sign arises. After that the form of a flame appears. After that has cleared, a vacuity will dawn, resembling a completely clear sky. With each successive meditation on the objects of withdrawal yoga, the winds enter the central channel, and the signs will gradually but definitely appear in the dhūtī. When that occurs the nighttime signs are complete, and from this point onward the yogi enters the daytime yoga.

'dir 'khrid yig 'ga' zhig las rje'i dgongs par bsams nas sor sdud kyi rtags/ 'char ba la rlung dbu mar zhugs gnas thim gsum dgos zhes 'byung ba ni rje'i dgongs pa min te/ rje nyid kyis dngos su gsungs pa'i sbyor drug gi zin bris rnam dpyod can dag gis btab pa las mtshan rtags rnams ni rlung ng+hU tIr chud tsam las 'char la/ nyin rtags rnams ni de tsam las mi 'char gyi/ ng+hU tIr chud pa phul du byung ba las 'char ro/ /

Some instruction texts, thinking it to be the position of Jé Tsongkhapa, say that for the signs of withdrawal yoga to arise, the winds must enter, abide, and dissolve within the central channel. This is not the position of Jé Tsongkhapa. Notes taken by discerning disciples on Jé Tsongkhapa’s actual words on the six yogas reveal that the night signs arise from the winds merely entering the dhūtī. The day signs do not appear from the winds merely entering the dhūtī but arise from a special way of entering.

sha wa ri pas kyang /
ng+hU tIr rlung bcu tshud gyur pas/ nyin dang mtshan mo'i rtags bcu mthong / / so sor sdud pa'i yan lag go[130] / zhes gsungs so/[131] / zhes rlung dbu mar tshud pa las rtags rnams 'char bar bshad cing gnas pa dang thim pa dgos par ma bshad la/ de bzhin du rgyud 'grel pa dang bcas pa las kyang /
rdo rje'i lam du rab tu zhugs pa zhes pa 'dir dbu mar srog rab tu zhugs pas stong pa kho na las du ba la sogs pa'i mtshan ma mthong ste rlung[132] zhes sogs du ma gsungs pa rnams kyis kyang rlung dbu mar zhugs pa nyid kyis du sogs kyi rtags rnams 'char bar gsungs kyi/ rlung dbu mar gnas pa dang thim pa dgos pa zur tsam yang ma gsungs pa dang /

Śavaripa also says:
By the ten winds entering the dhūtī, the day and night signs will be seen, this is the branch of withdrawal.[140] These lines say that the signs arise from the winds entering the central channel but say nothing about the winds abiding and dissolving there. The tantra and commentary says:
“The vajra path is entered.” Here the winds enter the central channel, and from the total emptiness the signs of smoke and so forth are seen.[141] /370/ Many similar quotes state that the signs of smoke and so on arise from the winds entering the central channel, but nowhere is there a passage that talks of the winds having to abide and dissolve.

d.div: [130] sde dge_1375_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ parnal 'byor yan lag drug pa/ 251_na6 _'di nyid kyi 'ag+r+yur du/ ng+hU tIr rlung bcu tshud gyur pa/ / so sor gcod pa'i yan lag yin/ / rtags rnams brtan par mthong 'gyur la/ / zhes gsal/
[131] rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum pod/ da_sbyor ba yan lag drug gi rdzogs rim gyi gnad bsdus pa/ 9_na2_dang _16_na5
[132] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 388_ba2
[140] Toh 1375 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 251a6.
[141] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 388b2.

f.d:
rgya gzhung tshad ldan rnams las/
mi g.yo ba ni gsum ldan gyis/ / ng+hU tIr rlung bcu chud gyur pas/ / phyi nang rtog 'gags rtags bcu mthong / / so sor gcod pa'i yan lag yin/[133] zhes sogs gsungs pa rnams kyis kyang d+hU tIr rlung tshud pas rtags 'char bar gsungs kyi gnas pa dang thim pa dgos par ma gsungs so/ /

Reliable Indian texts also talk of the signs arising from the winds entering the dhūtī but say nothing of the winds having to abide and dissolve. For example:[142]
By the three unmoving, the ten winds enter the dhūtī, outer and inner conceiving is halted, and the signs arise; this is the branch of individual cutting.

d.div: [133] sde dge_1375_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ parnal 'byor yan lag drug pa/ 251_na6
[142] Śavaripa commentary on the six yogas.

f.d: nyin mo'i rnal 'byor sgom tshul bshad pa/
28. Withdrawal: Day Yoga
gnyis pa nyin mo'i rnal 'byor sgom tshul bshad pa

['di ]la lnga/ gang du bsgom pa gnas kyi nges pa dang / ji ltar 'dug pa lus kyi 'dug stangs kyi nges pa dang / ji ltar lta ba mig gi lta stangs kyi nges pa dang / ji ltar 'jog pa sems kyi 'jog tshul gyi nges pa dang / de ltar bsgoms pas nyams rtogs skye tshul gyi nges pa'o/ /
This has five outlines: 1. Place of meditation 2. Posture 3. Positioning the eyes 4. Mental placement 5. The development of the signs
dang po [gang du bsgom pa gnas kyi nges pa ]ni

ye le'i brgya bcu drug pa las/
nam mkha' chu 'dzin bral ba dag la rnal 'byor pa yis bgrad pa'i mig gis blta bar bya ba ste/[134] / zhes dang / de'i 'grel par/
'dir nyin mo'i rnal 'byor ni nam mkha'i chu 'dzin bral ba dag la rnal 'byor pa yis bgrad pa'i mig gis blta bar bya ba lte snga dro dang phyi dro nyi ma la rgyab bstan nas so/ / rnam pa gzhan du na nyi ma'i 'od zer gyis rab rib tu 'gyur te de yis zhes pa ni gnod pa las so/[135] / zhes nam mkha' chu 'dzin te sprin dang bral ba rgya chen po mthong ba'i gnas su bsgom par gsungs pa ltar khang pa'i g.yab 'og gam/ ri zur lta bur phyin nas mis mi mthong tsam du rtsig pas bskyor ba'i gnas su sprin med pa'i nam mkha' rgya chen po mthong ba/ mig lam du gangs dang chu mi mthong ba/ mgo la ser bu dang 'od 'tsher ba mi 'phog pa'i gnas su bsgom mo/ /

Verse 116 of the Gnosis chapter says:
Into pure cloudless space the yogi should look with eyes wide open.[143] On this line the commentary says:
This is the daytime yoga. Into pure cloudless space the yogi should look with eyes wide open. This is in the morning and evening with the back to the sun. Otherwise the rays of the sun will bedazzle and cause harm.[144] This passage says that the place of meditation should afford an expansive view of cloudless skies. Therefore one should be under the overhang of a house or on a mountain spur surrounded by a wall that prevents others from looking in. There, under the vast expanse of the cloudless sky, where no water or snow is in the line of vision, where the eyes are not exposed to the wind and to the glare of the sun, one should meditate. /371/

d.div: [134] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka116_113_na3
[135] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 389_na1
[143] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 2, 113a3.
[144] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 389a1.

f.d:
der yang snga dro kha nub tu blta ba dang phyi dro kha shar du blta bar gsungs pa ltar de'i rigs pas lho shar dang lho nub la sogs par yang blta yis byang nub tu mi blta bar bla ma gong ma rnams gsung ngo / / de yang nam mkha' chu 'dzin bral ba dag la zhes pa rtsa 'grel gyis bsgom pa'i gnas bstan pa ni snying po gsal ba las/
chu 'dzin dang ni bral ba yis/ / nam mkha' dwangs par gyur pa la/ / snga dro nyi mar rgyab phyogs te/ / phyi dro yang ni de bzhin no/ / nyin phyed mig la gnod phyir spangs/[136] / zhes gsungs pa nyid kyis shes so/ / ji ltar 'dug pa lus kyi 'dug stangs sogs gnyis pa dang gsum pa dang bzhi pa rnams ni mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor ji lta ba bzhin bya'o/ /

The text advises facing west in the morning and east in the evening. Lamas of the past have said that the same criteria apply when facing the intermediate directions. Furthermore this description of the place of meditation from the tantra and commentary is found in Essence of the Three Yogas:
Free of clouds, in the clear sky, in the morning back to the sun, in the evening likewise. The midday sun will harm the eyes, therefore leave the meditation.[145] The second, third, and fourth outlines on the posture and so on are as described in the nighttime yoga.

d.div: [136] sde dge_1371_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ parnal 'byor gsum gyi snying po gsal ba/ 223_na7
[145] Toh 1371 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 223a7.

f.d:
kha cig na re/ nyin mo'i rnal 'byor gyi lta stangs khyod kyis mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor gyi skabs su bshad pa ltar byed pa mi rigs te/ nam mkha' chu 'dzin bral ba dag la rnal 'byor pa yis bgrad pa'i mig gis blta bar bya ba ste/ /zhes nam mkha' sprin dang bral ba la mig bgrad nas blta bar gsungs shing / khyod kyis mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor gyi lta stangs byed par bshad pa'i dbu ma'i yar sna'i sbubs stong gi nam mkha' la sprin dang bral ma bral gyi bshad pa 'ong don med pa'i phyir ro zhe na/ de'i skyon med de nyin mtshan gyi rnal 'byor gnyis mig gi lta stangs mtshungs pa cig dgos pa ni sgrub le'i brgya bcu dgu pa'i 'grel chen las/
'khor lo can gyi zhes pa gtsug tor gyi khro bo'i lta bas zhes pa ni mig 'dzums par steng du lta bas mtshan mar 'gyur te mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor gyi rnam pa bzhi dang nyin mo'i rnal 'byor gyi rnam pa drug ste de nas gzugs so/[137] / zhes pa'i mig mi 'dzums par steng du lta bas zhes pa des rnal 'byor gnyis ka'i mig gi lta stangs thun mong du gsungs shing / mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor gyi lta stangs nged kyis bshad pa ltar yin par gong du lung rigs kyis bsgrubs zin ltar yin pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang bgrad pa'i mig gis blta zhes pa'i don ni 'og tu 'chad do/ /

Some say, “It is not correct to maintain that the positioning of the eyes in day yoga is the same as that of the night yoga because in the above quote it says, ‘Into pure cloudless space the yogi should look with eyes wide open.’ Therefore the eyes are open wide and look into a cloudless sky. In nighttime yoga you have described the positioning of the eyes as being on the space that is the opening at the upper tip of the central channel. For such a positioning it would make no sense to talk of clouds or lack of clouds.” There is no contradiction. The positioning of the eyes for both day and night yogas must be the same. The Great Commentary, on verse 119 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
“Cakrī” means Uṣṇīṣa. “With his wrathful look” means the yogi sits with eyes not closed, looking upward, and the signs will appear. These are the four of the night yoga and the six of the day yoga.[146] This teaches that “eyes not closed and looking upward” is the common position of the eyes for both day and night yogas. I have explained and established by scripture and reason the positioning of the eyes for the night yoga. The line “look with eyes wide open” will be explained later.

d.div: [137] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 238_ba2
[146] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 237b2.

f.d:
yang thams cad mkhyen pa chos rjes bu'i 'khrid yig las/
lta stangs byed bcings bsgom bya la sems kyi 'jog tshul rnams sngar dang 'dra ba la/ khyad par sprin med pa'i nam mkha'i dbyings su rig pa bzhag la g.yas g.yon gyi yul la ma 'phros ma yengs par rtse gcig tu bsgom mo/ /[138] zhes gsungs nas shes byed du/ 'dir nyin mo'i rnal 'byor ni/ nam mkha' chu 'dzin bral ba zhes sogs 'dren par mdzad do/[139] / 'di'i bzhed pa ni lta stangs mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor bzhin du byas nas/ nam mkha' chu 'dzin bral ba zhes sogs kyis sems kyi 'jog tshul khyad par ba bstan pa dang / nam mkha' yang phyi rol gyi nam mkha' sprin med pa la bzhed par mngon zhing / bod kyi bla ma mang po zhig mig gi lta stangs dang de yang phyi rol gyi nam mkha' la byed pa bstan par mdzad do/ / 'di ni dpyad par bya ba'i gzhi che bar snang bas bdag nyid la shar tshod kyi rgyud 'grel gyi dgongs pa bshad par bya'o/ /

In his writings the omniscient dharma master Butön says:
The way of looking, the actions, the bindings, and the mental placement on the object of meditation is similar to the previous. One difference is that the mind is projected /372/ into the sphere of cloud-free space, not traveling to or distracted by surrounding objects but one-pointedly held in meditation.[147] As a source for this assertion the passage beginning “This is the daytime yoga. Into pure cloudless space” is quoted. He is asserting that the positioning of the eyes is similar to that of the night yoga but that there is a difference in the mental placement, as taught by the commentary words “pure cloudless space.” It appears he asserts this “space” to be external cloudless space. Moreover many Tibetan lamas teach that this “space” refers to the positioning of the eyes and is external space. This appears to be an important subject for discussion, and I will explain the thinking of the tantra and commentary as I understand it.

d.div: [138] bu ston rin chen grub/ gsung 'bum pod/ ga_sor bsam khrid yig_15_na6
[139] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka_116_113_na3
[147] Collected Works, vol. ga, Instructions on Withdrawal and Meditative Absorption, 15a6.

f.d: de la nyin mo'i rnal 'byor la 'jug pa'i tshe lus gnad lta stangs sems kyi 'jog tshul rnams mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor gyi skabs su bshad pa ltar bsgoms pas du ba sogs kyi rtags rnams 'dod dgur 'char zhing / de'i stobs kyis de dag dang rgyun 'thud nas nyin rtags rnams kyang myur du 'char ba yin no/ / de dag gi 'char tshul yang du ba sogs kyi rtags bzhi po rnams kyi mthar sprin med pa'i nam mkha' dri ma dang bral ba lta bu'i rnam pa shar ba'i tshe nam mkha' lta bu'i rnam pa de nyid la de ltar du mthong ba'i rnal 'byor pas sha'i spyan nam lha'i mig gi dbang po bgrad pas blta bar bya ste/ de ltar bltas pas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' dri ma dang bral ba ltar snang ba de nyid las 'bar ba la sogs pa'i nyin rtags drug 'char yin no/ / de nas/ nam mkha' chu 'dzin bral ba dag la rnal 'byor pa yis bgrad pa'i mig gis blta bar bya ba ste/ zhes pas nam mkha' ni du sogs kyi rtags bzhi'i mthar byung ba'i sprin med pa'i nam mkha' lta bu la byed pa dang / rnal 'byor pas bgrad pa'i mig gis blta ba'i mig kyang sha'i mig gam lha'i mig la byed dgos te/ nyin mo'i rnal 'byor bsgoms pas thog mar du sogs kyi rtags bzhi'i mthar sprin med pa'i nam mkha' lta bu 'char la/ de'i de ma thag tu nyin rtags rnams 'char ba yin zhing / nam mkha' lta bu 'char ba'i skabs der phyi rol gyi nam mkha' la lta ba 'ong ba'i da ltar gyi mig lta bu rnam smin gyi mig gis lta ba 'ong don med pa'i phyir te/ du ba lta bu'i rtags dang por shar ba'i dus nas mig sogs phyi rol gyi yul la 'jug pa'i yul yul can gyi 'brel pa bkag zin pa'i phyir ro/ /

When entering the day yoga, meditation is first performed with the eye positioning, posture, and mental placement of the night yoga. This will produce the signs of smoke and so forth, which ensures a continuation into the quick appearance of the day signs. The way this happens is as follows. At the end of the four nighttime signs, a totally pure and cloudless space–like appearance arises and appears to the yogi, who looks into it with wide-open celestial eyes or with fleshly eyes. From such a totally pure and cloudless space–like appearance come the six day signs of the blazing and so forth. Therefore, in the quote, “Into pure cloudless space the yogi should look with eyes wide open,” “space” must refer to the cloudless space–like appearance that occurs after the four signs of smoke and so forth have arisen, and the “eyes” that are wide open must refer to either celestial eyes or fleshly eyes. This is so because when meditating on the day yoga, the first appearance is that of the cloudless space that follows on from the last of the four nighttime signs. Immediately after that comes the appearance of the daytime signs. Moreover, during that spacelike appearance, it would make no sense to say that we look at it with the ordinary ripened eyes we possess now, because from the moment the first of the four night signs of smoke and so forth arise, the subject and object connection necessary for /373/ engaging in external form is broken.

gal te nyin mo'i rnal 'byor bsgoms pa las thog mar du sogs kyi rtags sprin med pa'i nam mkha' lta bu dang bcas pa shar ba'i rjes thogs su nyin rtags rnams 'char bar grub na/ khyod kyis bshad pa ltar yin du chug mod kyang / nyin mo'i rnal 'byor bsgoms pa las thog mar du sogs sprin med pa'i nam mkha' lta bu dang bcas pa shar ba'i rjes thogs de ma thag tu nyin rtags rnams 'char ba sogs la shes byed med do zhe na/ 'di'i shes byed shin tu gal che bar snang bas rgyas par brjod par bya'o/ /

Some might reply: “If it could be established that in the practice of daytime yoga meditation, the four signs of smoke and so forth arise first, followed by the cloudless space–like appearance, and then finally the day signs, then it would be as you assert. But where is the scriptural evidence to prove that in the daytime yoga meditation, first the four signs of smoke and so forth arise, followed by the cloudless space–like appearance, and then immediately by the day signs?”

de yang bde mchog stod 'grel las/
'dir rang byin gyis brlab pa zhes bya ba ni so sor sdud pas kun rdzob pa'i stong pa nyid mthong ba'o/ / mtshan ma zhes bya ba ni sprin dang du ba la sogs pa ltar snang ba ste de yang sgron ma'i mthar thug pa dang po mthong ba'o/ / de nas sprin med pa'i na ma mkha' dri ma dang bral ba'o/ / rgyud gzhan rnams su gzhan 'bar ba la sogs pa thig le'i mthar thug mtshan ma rnam pa drug ste bcom ldan 'das kyis sgyu 'phrul dra ba'i ting 'dzin dra ba'i le'ur gsungs pa 'di lta ste/ nam mkha' las byung rang byung ba/ / shes rab ye shes me 'o che/ / 'od chen rnam par snang bar byed/ / ye shes snang ba lam me ba/ / 'gro ba'i mar me ye shes sgron/ / gzi brjid chen po 'od gsal ba/ / rig pa'i rgyal mchog sngags dbang po/ / gsang sngags rgyal po don chen byed/[140] / ces tshigs su bcad pa gnyis kyis sgyu 'phrul dra bar mtshan ma gzhan bcom ldan 'das kyis dgongs pa'i skad gzhan gyis gsungs te/ sngar brjod pa'i sprin med pa'i nam mkha' las byung ba'i snang ba gang yin pa de ni rnam par rtog pa thams cad dang bral ba'i sems las byung bas nam mkha' las byung rang byung ba'o/ / 'dir shes rab ye shes me 'o che zhes pa 'bar ba ltar snang ba'o/[141] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis gsal bar bstan pa yin te/ de yang ji ltar bstan snyam na/

This scriptural evidence is very important and will be explained extensively. The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
Here “self-blessing” refers to withdrawal, wherein conventional emptiness is seen. “Signs” refers to the appearances that are like clouds, smoke, and so forth. Those ending with the lamp are seen first. Then comes a totally pure cloudless space. In other tantras are /374/ found other signs, such as blazing and so forth, ending with drops. These six signs are spoken of by the Buddha in the Net of Meditative Concentration chapter of the Net of Illusion Tantra: “Self-created, created from space, the great fire of wisdom knowledge, the great light illuminating, the brilliance of gnosis, “a lamp for beings, a lamp of wisdom, great radiance and clear light, greatest of knowledge, mighty secret, the king of secret mantra, accomplisher of great purpose.”[148] With these two verses in the Net of Illusion Tantra, the Buddha speaks of the signs using provisional language. The appearances that arise from the previously mentioned cloudless space arise from a mind totally devoid of conceptuality and therefore is “Self-created, created from space.” Here the great fire of wisdom knowledge is the appearance of “blazing.”[149] Scriptural evidence is clearly presented in this passage. How?

d.div: [140] sde dge_360_bka'/ rgyud/ ka'ajam dpal mtshan brjod/ 4_na7_da lta thob bzhin pa'i chos tshan 466 rgyud kyi rgyal po chen po sgyu 'phrul dra bar lung 'di mi snang bas mtshan brjod du gsal ba ltar bkod pa'o/ /
[141] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 132_na2
[148] Toh 466 or 360 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 4a7.
[149] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 132a2.

f.d: 'dir rang byin gyis brlabs zhes pa nas/ de nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' dri ma dang bral ba'o zhes pa'i bar gyis rdo rje gur nas sor sdud kyi mtshan rtags rnams gsungs tshul bstan/ rgyud gzhan rnams su gzhan 'bar ba la sogs pa zhes pa nas/ dgongs pa'i skad gzhan gyis gsungs te/ zhes pa'i bar gyis nyin rtags drug sgyu 'phrul dra ba'i ting 'dzin dra ba'i le'u las gsungs tshul bstan/ de'i rjes kyi/ sngar brjod pa'i sprin med pa'i nam mkha' zhes gsungs pa'i nam mkha' ni sngar mtshan rtags kyi skabs su brjod pa'i/ de nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' dri ma dang bral ba'o zhes gsungs pa'i sprin med pa'i nam mkha' de yin la/ nam mkha' las byung ba'i snang ba gang yin pa de ni zhes pa'i snang ba ni 'bar ba sogs nyin rtags rnams yin zhing / nyin rtags kyi 'bar ba sogs kyi snang ba gang yin pa de ni sprin med pa'i nam mkha' ltar snang ba'i rnam pa can gyi sems rnam par rtog pa thams cad dang bral ba las byung bas na nam mkha' las byung rang byung ba'o/ / nam mkha' las byung rang byung ba [142] de yang ji lta bu snyam na/ de nyid 'chad pa ni/ shes rab ye shes me 'o che/ /zhes sogs te/ de yang shes rab ye shes zhes sogs dgongs pa'i skad gzhan gyis 'chad pa'i skabs 'dir shes rab ye shes me'o che zhes pa ni me 'bar ba ltar snang ba'o/ /zhes pa'i don yin no/ /

The passage from “Here, ‘self-blessing’” up to “Then comes a totally pure cloudless space” describes how the night signs are presented in the Vajra Tent Tantra. From “In other tantras are found other signs” up to “using a provisional language” describes how the day signs are taught in the Net of Meditative Concentration chapter of the Net of Illusion Tantra. The phrase “the previously mentioned cloudless space” in the next sentence refers to the cloudless space of “a totally pure cloudless space” mentioned in the description of the night signs. The “appearances” in the line “the appearances that arise from the previously mentioned cloudless space” are the day signs of blazing and so forth. The appearance of the day signs of blazing and so forth arise from “a mind totally devoid of conceptuality” in its cloudless space–like aspect, hence the line, “Self-created, created from space.” To what does this line refer? This is answered by the lines “the great fire of gnosis” and so forth, which are lines spoken “using provisional language,” and therefore “Here, the great fire of wisdom knowledge is the appearance of ‘blazing.’” This is the meaning of the passage.

d.div: [142] sde dge_360_bka'/ rgyud/ ka'ajam dpal mtshan brjod/ 4_na7

f.d: de ltar na mtshan rtags bzhi pa sgron me 'bar ba'o/ /lnga pa rtag tu snang ba ni/ /sprin med nam mkha' lta bu'o/ /zhes so/ /de nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' dang mtshungs par snang ba sngon du 'gro ba me'i rnam pa zhes pa'i skabs su bshad pa'i sprin med pa'i nam mkha' ltar snang ba ni du ba smig rgyu mkha' snang sgron ma dang bzhi rim pa can du byung ba'i mthar 'byung bar nges pa yin la/ sngar brjod pa'i sprin med pa'i nam mkha' zhes pa/ de nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' dri ma dang bral ba'o zhes pa'i nam mkha' la bya ste/ sngar brjod pa'i sprin med pa'i nam mkha' zhes pa'i nam mkha' ltar snang ba de las de ma thag 'bar ba sogs nyin rtags rnams 'byung ba de'i phyir na nyin mo'i rnal 'byor bsgoms pa las thog mar du sogs kyi rtags sprin med pa'i nam mkha' mtshan rtags lta bu dang bcas pa shar ba'i rjes thogs de ma thag nyin rtags rnams 'char bar grub pa yin no/ /

The “cloudless space” explained in this passage on the night signs, “‘The fourth a burning lamp, the fifth a constant clarity, like a cloudless sky.’ Then the form of fire, preceded by an appearance similar to that of cloudless space” is a cloudless space determined as arising after smoke, mirage, fireflies, and lamp have appeared in that order. On top of that “The previously mentioned cloudless space” refers to the space in the line “Then comes a totally pure cloudless space,” and immediately after the spacelike appearance of “The previously mentioned cloudless space,” the day signs of blazing and so forth appear. This therefore establishes that in the meditation on the day yoga, the day signs will appear immediately after the four preceding night signs and after the cloudless space, which itself is like a night sign.

gzhan yang nA ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa las/
ji skad du dpal 'dus pa la sogs par/ dang po dang gnyis pa bzlog pas gsungs pa/ 'gog pa rdo rjer bgrod sems la/ / mtshan ma nyer 'dzin skye 'gyur ba/ / dang po smig rgyu'i rnam pa ste/ / gnyis pa du ba lta bu'o/ / gsum pa mkha' snang rnam pa ste/ / bzhi pa sgron ma rab 'bar ba'o/ / lnga pa rtag tu snang ba ni/ / sprin med nam mkha' lta bu'o/ / zhes so/ / de nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' dang 'dra bar snang ba sngon du 'gro ba'i me'i rnam pa stong pa'i snang ba ni 'bar ba'o/ / zhes pa nas/ zla ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi rnam par snang ba'o zhes pa'i bar gsungs nas de'i rjes de ma thag tu/
mtshan ma drug po 'di rnams ni sprin med pa'i nam mkha' ltar snang ba las byung ba'i phyir nyin mo'i rnal 'byor dang bla gab med pa'i rnal 'byor ro|[143] |zhes gsungs pa 'dis kyang nyin mo'i rnal 'byor bsgoms pas du ba nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' ltar snang ba'i bar gyi rtags rnams 'dod dgur 'byung ba'i rjes su sprin med pa'i nam mkha' ltar snang ba de nyid las 'bar ba sogs nyin rtags rnams 'byung bar gsal par bstan pa dang /

Furthermore Nāropa in his Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations says: /375/
In the glorious Guhyasamāja and others, the first and second are taught in reverse order: “To the mind of vajra cessation signs, closely held, will appear. The first is the form of a mirage, the second that of smoke, the third is light in the sky, the fourth a burning lamp, the fifth a constant clarity, like a cloudless sky.” Then the form of fire, preceded by an appearance similar to that of cloudless space, blazes in the form of an empty appearance. This continues up to “Appearing in the form of a moon mandala,” and immediately after that the commentary states:
These six signs arise from cloudless space–like appearance. Therefore this is the day yoga and the yoga “without cover.”[150] This passage also clearly teaches that by meditating on the day yoga, the signs of smoke and so on up to the cloudless space–like appearance are deliberately produced initially, after which the day signs of blazing and so forth arise from that very cloudless space–like appearance.

d.div: [143] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 259_ba6
[150] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 259b6.

f.d:
de bzhin du yon tan gyis 'gengs pa las kyang /
dang po smig rgyu nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' ltar snang ba'i rtags rnams dpal 'dus pa nas gsungs tshul bshad pa'i rjes su/ de nas sprin med pa'i nam mkhar snang ba sngon ma can me'i rnam pa stongs pa'i snang ba de ni 'bar ba'o/[144] / zhes nA ro pa bzhin du gsungs so/ /

Similarly Filled with Good Qualities says:
After the Guhyasamāja has explained the signs beginning with the mirage up to the cloudless space–like appearance, it talks of an empty form–like fire blazing out of the cloudless space–like appearance.[151] This is similar to Nāropa’s descriptions.

d.div: [144] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 321_na2
[151] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 321a2.

f.d:
'grel chen las kyang /
de nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' la bltas te nam mkha' de las kyang nyin mo'i rnal 'byor gyi nam mkha' las byung rang byung ba/[145] / zhes gsungs pa'i/ de nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' la bltas te zhes pa'i nam mkha' de yang du ba sogs bzhi'i mthar shar ba'i sprin med pa'i nam mkha' ltar snang ba de nyid la byed dgos te/ nam mkha' de las kyang nyin mo'i rnal 'byor gyi nam mkha' las byung rang byung ba zhes nam mkha' de nam mkha' las byung rang byung ba'i nam mkha' bshad pa gang zhig/ nam mkha' las byung rang byung ba zhes pa'i nam mkha' de du ba sogs bzhi'i mthar byung ba'i sprin med pa'i nam mkha' la byed par bde mchog stod 'grel du gsungs pa'i don bshad zin pa [146] ltar yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

The Great Commentary also says:
Then the yogi looks into the cloudless space, and from that space, the “self-created, created from space” of the yoga of daytime.[152] “Space” in the above line “Then the yogi looks into the cloudless space” has to be the cloudless space–like appearance that arises /376/ after the four signs of smoke and so forth have appeared, because “from that space, the ‘self-created, created from space’ of the yoga of daytime” explains that this “space” is the space of “self-created, created from space,” and the space of “self-created, created from space” is spoken of in the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary as being the cloudless space–like appearance that arises after the appearance of the four signs of smoke and so forth.

d.div: [145] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 388_ba3
[146] don bshad min pa ltar zhes byung bshad zin pa ltar zhes bcos/
[152] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 388b3.

f.d: de bzhin du nA ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa las 'grel chen bzhin du gsungs pa rnams kyi don yang 'di bzhin du shes par bya'o/ /

'o na nyin mo'i rnal 'byor bsgoms pa las du ba nas sgron ma lta bu'i bar gyi rtags bzhi'i mthar shar ba'i sprin med pa'i nam mkha' ltar snang ba de la lta ba'i sha'i mig gam lha'i mig ji lta bu snyam na/ de yang thog mar sor sdud kyi dmigs pa bsgoms pas rlung dbu mar tshud de dbang yul gyi yul yul can gyi 'brel ba chad nas du sogs kyi rtags thog mar shar ba'i tshe rtags rnams gsal bar mthong ba'i sha'i spyan nam lha'i mig rnal 'byor pa de'i rgyud la grub 'ong ba de yin te/

What are these celestial eyes and fleshly eyes that look upon the cloudless space–like appearance that arises in day-yoga meditation following the appearance of the four signs from smokelike to lamplike? First of all, by meditating on the objects of meditation in withdrawal yoga, the winds enter the central channel, the connection between sensory subjects and objects are cut, and then, when the signs of smoke and so forth first arise, they are seen by celestial eyes or fleshly eyes that exist in the mind of the yogi.

'grel chen las/
'dir de bzhin gshegs pa'i sha'i spyan gyis dang por rang gi sems kyi snang ba mthong zhing /[147] zhes gsungs pa dang /

The Great Commentary says:
With tathāgata fleshly eyes one first sees the appearances within one’s own mind.[153]

d.div: [147] sde dge_845_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 389_na4
[153] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 389a4.

f.d:
sgrub le'i brgya bcu drug pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir so sor sdud pa zhes bya ba ni lus la yul dang yul can bcu po rnams kyi 'grel pas rnam par shes pa rab tu 'jug pa med pa ste stong pa'i gzugs kyi yul rnams la mig gzhan la sogs pa rnam pa lnga po rnams kyis rab tu 'jug pa'o/[148] / zhes gsungs pa'i mig gzhan zhes pa sha'i mig la mdzad pa dang / de bzhin du bde mchog stod 'grel las kyang /
'dir so sor sdud pa zhes bya ba ni gzugs la sogs pa'i phyi rol gyi yul rnams la mig la sogs pa'i dbang po rnams kyis mig gi rnam par shes pa la sogs pa rnams mi 'jug par nang gi yul rnams la lha'i mig gi dbang po la sogs pa rnams kyis lha'i mig gi rnam par shes pa la sogs pa rnams 'jug pa ste/[149] zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

On verse 116 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, the Great Commentary says:
“Withdrawal” means that within the body, consciousness is unengaged in the connection between the ten subjects and objects. Five other eyes and so forth are engaged in empty-form objects.[154] Here “other eyes” refers to fleshly eyes. The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary also states:
