Here in withdrawal the five sense organs do not engage the five sense consciousnesses in the external objects, such as form. The celestial sense organs engage the celestial sense consciousnesses in inner objects.[155]

d.div: [148] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 388_ba3
[149] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 130_na7
[154] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 388b3.
[155] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 130a7.

f.d:
sha'i spyan de yang sor sdud kyi skabs kyi dmigs pa bsgoms pa las byung ba yin te/ ye le'i brgya nyer lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
de ltar rim pas sha'i spyan dang lha'i spyan dang sangs rgyas kyi spyan dang shes rab kyi spyan dang ye shes kyi spyan ni bsgoms pa'i stobs kyis 'byung bar 'gyur ro/[150] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

The fleshly eyes also will arise from the withdrawal meditations. The Great Commentary, on verse 125 of the Gnosis chapter, says:
In order, the fleshly eyes, celestial eyes, buddha eyes, wisdom eyes, and eyes of gnosis will arise from meditation.[156]

d.div: [150] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 389_na4
[156] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 389a4.

f.d: de ltar na/ nam mkha' chu 'dzin bral ba dag la zhes sogs kyis nyin mo'i rnal 'byor bsgom pa'i gnas dang / nyin rtags rnams sprin med pa'i nam mkha' lta bu la 'char ba'i nam mkha'i mtshan gzhi bstan par shes par bya ste/ rgyud dang 'grel tshig 'di'i 'chad tshul gcig go/ /

Therefore the passage beginning with the phrase “Into pure cloudless space”[157] teaches the place for day yoga meditation and explains the space of the cloudless space–like appearance /377/ from which the day signs arise. Both the tantra and its commentary agree on this.

d.div: [157] From v. 116 of the Gnosis chapter and corresponding commentary from Great Commentary.

f.d: gzhan yang nam mkha' chu 'dzin bral ba zhes sogs kyi don bla ma 'ga' zhig bzhed pa ltar nyin mo'i rnal 'byor gyi lta stangs bstan par byed na yang / mig mi 'dzums [151] par steng du lta bas/ zhes sogs kyis nyin mtshan gyi rnal 'byor gnyis kyi lta stangs thun mong du bstan nas steng du lta tshul la mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor gyis gong du bshad pa ltar dang / nyin mo'i rnal 'byor gyis phyi rol gyi nam mkha' sprin med pa la mig gnyis bgrad nas lta ba'i lta stangs bya ste/ de ltar byas pas rlung dbu mar mi tshud pa'i skyon yang med de/ mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor sgom pa'i tshe lta stangs dang sems kyi 'jog tshul gong du bshad pa ltar byas pas rlung dbu mar tshud nas mtshan rtags rnams shar ba yin la/ mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor mthar phyin nas nyin mo'i rnal 'byor la 'jug pa yin pas de la 'jug pa'i tshe rlung dbu mar 'jug pa la legs par byang yod pa'i gnad kyis sems kyi 'jog tshul mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor gyi skabs ltar byas te lta stangs kyis phyi rol gyi nam mkha' sprin med pa la mig bgrad nas lta ba'i lta stangs byas te nyin mo'i rnal 'byor bsgoms pas thog mar mtshan rtags myur du 'char zhing / de nas mtshan rtags kyi mtha'i nam mkha' sprin med pa ltar snang ba la me 'bar ba lta bu sogs nyin rtags 'char ba yin no/ / de yang lta stangs ni dbang po'i sgo nas 'jug pa'i rlung rnams rengs pa'i phyir du byed pa yin zhing mig 'byed 'dzums dang sgul skyod med par [152] phyi rol gyi nam mkha' la bgrad nas lta ba'i lta stangs kyis kyang bya ba de 'grub pa'i phyir ro/ /

Furthermore, even if the passage beginning “Into pure cloudless space” were applied to the eye positioning in the day yoga, as some lamas have asserted, the line “eyes not closed, looking upward” would still teach the common eye position for both night and day yogas. The way of looking upward in the night yoga would be as explained previously, whereas in the day yoga, both eyes would be wide open and look into external cloud-free space. This procedure would still not prevent the winds from entering the central channel, because during the night-yoga meditations, with the positioning of the eyes and the placement of mind as explained previously, the winds would enter the central channel, and the night signs would appear. With the night yoga completed, the day yoga would begin, and at that time the winds in the central channel would have become well established. Because of this the mental placement is the same as the night yoga — the eyes are wide open and look into external cloud-free space. After the night signs have quickly arisen, the day signs of the blazing firelike appearance and so forth arise in the cloudless space–like appearance that occurs at the end of the night signs. Concerning the positioning of the eyes, the winds that operate through the entrances of the sense organ become stiff, the eyes do not blink, the eyeballs do not move but stare wide open into external space. This method also will accomplish the practice.

d.div: [151] ma dper mig mig 'dzums par zhes byung yang mig mi 'dzums zhes bcos/
[152] ma dper sgul skyed med par zhes gsal bas bcos/

f.d: sor sdud rje rin po che'i dgongs pa ltar 'chad pa la rgyud dang 'grel tshig 'di'i 'chad tshul shin tu gal che bar snang ba la dgongs pa 'grel pa po gzhan rnams ni ci yang mi gsung la/ bdag ni rnam dpyod nyam chung zhing sbyangs pa'i stobs dman na'ang che long du bshad pa 'di la dpyod ldan rnams kyis legs par brtag par mdzad du gsol lo/ /

To explain withdrawal according to the thinking of Jé Tsongkhapa, an explanation of this passage from the tantra and commentary is very important, and yet other commentators have said nothing on this topic. Now I may be of little intelligence and weak in practice, but I would request the intelligent to examine well my rough explanation.
lnga pa de ltar bsgoms pas nyams rtogs skye tshul gyi nges pa ni

ye le'i brgya bco lnga pa las/
'bar ba dang ni zla ba nyi ma rdo rje rnams dang mchog gi cha dang thig le mthong bar 'gyur/ / de yi dbus su sangs rgyas gzugs ni yul dang rnam par bral ba du ma longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku/ / nam mkha' chu 'dzin bral ba dag la rnal 'byor pa yis bgrad pa'i mig gis blta bar bya ba ste/ / re khA nag po dri med 'od zer 'phro ba dus kyi rtsal mthong bar gyur gyi bar du'o/[153] / zhes dang /

Verse 115 of the Gnosis chapter says: /378/
Blazing, moon, sun, vajras, the supreme part and the drop are seen. In the center the form of the Buddha, the nonobject, manifold saṃbhogakāya; in cloudless space the yogi looks with wide-open eyes, until a black line emitting rays of pure light is seen in the channel of time.[158]

d.div: [153] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ 113_na3
[158] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 113a3.

f.d:
de'i 'grel par/
de nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' la blta ste nam mkha' de las kyang nyin mo'i rnal 'byor gyi nam mkha' las byung rang byung ba/ / shes rab ye shes me bo che zhes pa 'bar ba mthong ste sprin med pa'i nam mkha' la'o/ / de bzhin du 'od chen rnam par snang bar byed/ / ye shes snang ba lam me ba ni zla ba snang ba'o/ / 'gro ba'i mar me ni nyi ma'o/ / ye shes sgron ni rdo rje ste sgra gcan no/ / gzi brjid chen po 'od gsal ba ni glog ste mchog gi cha'o/ / sngags mchog mnga' bdag rig sngags rgyal ni thig le'o/ / de ltar mtshan ma rnam pa bcu ste 'dus pa la sogs pa las mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor dang mtshan yang dag par rjod pa las nyin mo'i rnal 'byor gyis bcom ldan 'das kyis gsungs so/ / de nas gsang sngags rgyal po don chen byed ces pa ni bum pa dang snam bu la sogs pa rnam pa thams cad pa'i gzugs mthong ba'o/ / de'i dbus su ste thig le'i dbus su sangs rgyas gzugs ni rdzas med pa'i phyir dang btags pa med pa'i phyir yul dang rnam par bral ba du ma longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku'o [154] zhes dang /

The commentary on this says:
Then the yogi looks into cloudless space, and from that space comes the yoga of daytime, “self-created, created from space.” “The great fire of wisdom knowledge” is the blazing within the cloudless space. Likewise “the great light illuminating, the brilliance of gnosis” is the moonlike appearance. /379/ “A lamp for beings” is the sun. “The lamp of wisdom” is the vajra or Rāhu. “The great radiance and clear light” is lightning, or the supreme part. “Greatest of knowledge, mighty secret” is the drop. These are the ten signs. The Buddha taught the night signs in the Guhyasamāja and others and the day signs in the Saṃgīti. “The king of secret mantra, accomplisher of great purpose” refers to seeing the fully aspected forms of the vase, friezes, and so forth. “In the center” means in the center of the drop, where is seen “the form of the Buddha.” Because it is nonsubstantial and unimputed, it is “the nonobject manifold saṃbhogakāya.”[159]

d.div: [154] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 388_ba2
[159] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 389a2.

f.d:
yang de nyid las/
nyi ma so sor blta bar bya ste thig le'i dbus su re khA nag po skra'i tshad tsam dri med 'od zer 'phro ba dus kyi rtsa zhes pa a wa ng+hU tI la mthong bar gyur gyi bar du'o/[155] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis nyin rtags drug dang / rtags bcu rdzogs pa'i mthar 'byung ba'i rtags rnams kyang bstan to/ /

Also:
Look each day until, in the center of the drop, “a black line” the width of /380/ a hair “emitting rays of stainless light is seen in the channel of time,” or avadhūtī.[160] The above commentary describes the six signs and other signs arising after the completion of the ten signs.

d.div: [155] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 389_na2
[160] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 389a2.

f.d:
de bzhin du stod 'grel las kyang /
'dir shes rab ye shes me bo che zhes pa 'bar ba ltar snang ba'o/ / 'od chen rnam par snang bar byed ces pa zla ba ltar snang ba'o/ / de nyid ye shes snang ba lam me ba zhes pa'o/ / 'gro ba'i mar me zhes pa nyi ma ltar snang ba'o/ / ye shes sgron ma zhes pa sgra gcan ltar snang ba'o/ / gzi brjid chen po 'od gsal ba zhes pa glog ltar snang ba'o/ / rig pa'i rgyal mchog sngags dbang po zhes pa thig le ltar snang ba'o/ kha dog sngon po zla ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi rnam pa'o/ / gsang sngags rgyal po don chen byed/ / ces pa khams gsum pa'i rang bzhin gyi snang ba'i rnam pa thams cad sgyu ma dang rmi lam dang pra phab pa lta bur so sor sdud pas mig gi dbang po'i byed pas rnal 'byor pas mthong bar 'gyur ro/[156] / zhes gsungs te/ 'grel pa gnyis kas nyin rtags drug dang / de dag gi mthar 'byung ba'i rtags rnams mtshan rjod kyis dgongs pa'i skad gzhan gyis gsungs pa rnams kyi don gsal bar bshad pa yin no/ /

Similarly the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
Here “the great fire of wisdom knowledge” is the appearance of “blazing.” “The great light illuminating” is the moonlike appearance, which is also “the brilliance of gnosis.” “A lamp for beings” is the sunlike appearance. “The lamp of wisdom” is the Rāhu-like appearance. “Great radiance and clear light” is the lightninglike appearance. “Greatest of knowledge, mighty secret” is the droplike appearance. It is blue in color and shaped like the moon. “The king of secret mantra, accomplisher of great purpose” means that with the eyes created by withdrawal, the yogi sees all appearance within the three realms as being like illusions, like dreams, and like forms within a prognostic mirror.[161] These two commentaries clearly decode the “other language” used by the Saṃgīti to describe the six signs and the signs that arise after them.

d.div: [156] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 132_na5
[161] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 132a5.

f.d: de ltar na mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor mthar phyin pa'i rjes su gong du bshad pa'i nyin mo'i rnal 'byor sgom pa'i gnas der lus gnad dang dmigs pa la sems kyi 'jog tshul mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor gyi skabs su bshad pa ltar byas/ mig gi lta stangs gnyis po gang yang rung ba byas te bsgoms pa las du ba nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' ltar snang ba'i bar rnams myur por 'byung la/ de'i rjes su nam mkha' ltar snang ba'i nam mkha' de nyid la thog mar me 'bar ba'i rnam pa lta bu dang / de'i rjes su zla ba lta bu'i rnam pa dang / de'i rjes su nyi ma lta bu'i rnam pa dang / de'i rjes su sgra gcan lta bu'i rnam pa nag khyim pa la mig mang po khra chem chem pa'i rnam pa dang / de'i rjes su mchog gi cha ste glog dmar 'khyug pa lta bu'i rnam pa dang / de'i rjes su thig le sngon po zla ba'i dkyil 'khor lta bu zlum pa'i rnam pa dang / de'i rjes su bum pa dang snam bu la sogs pa rnam pa sna tshogs pa'i gzugs kyi rnam pa mthong ngo / / de dang dus mnyam du thig le sngon po zlum po de'i dbus su re khA nag po skra'i tshad tsam dri med 'od zer 'phro ba dang re khA la yang longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku rdo rje sems dpa' yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can dang de'i bdag nyid rnam pa sna tshogs pa'i 'jig rten gsum mthong zhing thig le re khA dang bcas pa de rnams kyang dus kyi rtsa a wa ng+hU tI'i nang du mthong ba yin no/ /

Therefore, after the completion of the night yoga, in a place for day-yoga meditation, as previously described, the posture and mental placement are the same as was described for the night yoga. Either of the two eye positions can be practiced. From the meditation the signs, from smoke to the cloud-free spacelike appearance, arise quickly. After that, in the very space of that spacelike appearance, the blazing firelike appearance occurs first, followed by the moonlike and the sunlike appearances. Then comes the Rāhu-like appearance, like many sparks glittering in the dark. After that comes the “supreme” or lightning-flash appearance, followed by an appearance similar to a blue drop in the circular shape of a moon disk. After that various forms, such as those resembling a vase and so on, are seen. At the same time, in the center of the blue circular drop, a black line appears. It is the width of a hair and emits rays of stainless light. Within that line is the saṃbhogakāya in the form of Vajrasattva and consort in embrace as well as the three worlds in various forms, all of which are the nature of that saṃbhogakāya. The drop and the black line are seen in the ”channel of time,” meaning the avadhūtī central channel.

de ltar yang yon tan gyis 'gengs pa las/
gtsug tor gyi gzugs ni sangs rgyas kyi gzugs so/ / khams gsum pa zhes pa ni thig le chen po'i dbus su ri mo nag po la so sor snang ba rnam pa sna tshogs pa longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku'i bdag nyid 'jig rten gsum mthong ba'o/[157] / zhes bshad pa ni thig le'i dbus su re khA nag po skra'i tshad tsam dri med 'od zer 'phro ba dus kyi rtsa zhes pa a wa ng+hU tI la mthong bar gyur gyi bar du'o zhes gsungs pa'i don du bsams pas so/ /

Filled with Good Qualities also states:
“Uṣṇīṣa form” is the form of the Buddha. “The three realms” means that in the center of the great drop is a black line in which various forms of the three worlds individually appear, all of which are of the nature of the saṃbhogakāya.[162] This passage appears to be the explanation of the above quote, “In the center of the drop, ‘a black line’ the width of a hair ‘emitting rays of stainless light is seen in the channel of time,’ or avadhūtī.”

d.div: [157] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 323_na5
[162] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 322a5.

f.d:
de yang gang gis mthong ba yin snyam na/ nA ro pa'i dbang mdor [158] bstan gyi 'grel pa las/
nang gi yul rnams la sha'i mig la sogs pa'i dbang po rnams kyi sha'i mig gi rnam par shes pa la sogs pa rnams rab tu 'jug pa nang du stong pa nyid la dmigs pas pra phab pa'i gzhon nu mas me long la mthong ba ltar stong pa ma btags pa la btags pa'i dngos po thams cad mthong ba ni so sor sdud pa'i yan lag tu brjod do/[159] / zhes gsungs pa ltar sor sdud kyi dmigs pa bsgoms pas da ltar gyi mig dbang 'di las gzhan pa'i sha'i mig gi dbang po zhig 'grub la/ mig dbang de las byung ba'i sha'i mig gi dbang shes kyis mthong ba yin no/ /

What sees these phenomena? Nāropa, in his Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations, says:
The fleshly eye consciousnesses and so forth of the fleshly sense organs engage in the inner forms and focus on the inner emptiness. Like forms seen by a clairvoyant maiden looking into her mirror, all imputed phenomena are seen within an unimputed emptiness. This is spoken of as the branch of withdrawal.[163] This passage states that by meditating on the objects of withdrawal yoga, the organ of the fleshly sight is developed. This is an organ other than the normal sight organ. The fleshly eye consciousness that arises from that organ of sight is what “sees” in withdrawal.

d.div: [158] ma dper na ro pa'i dpal mdor bstan zhes byung yang nA ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan zhes bcos/
[159] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 251_ba7
[163] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 241b7.

f.d:
de yang spyir sha'i mig shes kyis yul ji tsam mthong ba ni yon tan gyis 'gengs pa las/
sha'i mig gis ni dpag tshad brgya'i bar du chod pa'i dngos po mthong ba ste [160] zhes bshad pa ltar ro/ /

The kinds of objects that the fleshly eye consciousness can generally apprehend are spoken of in Filled with Good Qualities:
The fleshly eye sees phenomena up to one hundred yojana.[164]

d.div: [160] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 314_ba2
[164] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 314b2.

f.d:
'o na lha'i mig dang khyad par ci yod snyam na/ de nyid las/
lha'i mig gis ni 'jig rten gyi khams mtha' yas pa'i bar du chod pa'i phra mo dang cig shos kyi gzugs mthong bas so/[161] / zhes bshad pa ltar gyi khyad par yod cing gong du stod 'grel drangs par lha'i mig ces gsungs pa yang sha'i mig la go bar bya dgos so/ /

So how does it differ from the celestial eye? The same text says:
The celestial eye sees the subtle and individual forms of limitless world realms.[165] There is this difference, and although the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary talks of “celestial organs of the eyes,” it should be understood as referring to fleshly eyes.

d.div: [161] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 314_ba3
[165] Toh 1388 Tengyur, ’rgyud ’grel, ba, 314b3.

f.d:
de yang stong gzugs de dag gi ngo bo ni sprin med pa'i nam mkha' lta bu'i stong sang gi yul snang can gnyug ma 'od gsal gyi sems de'i gzugs brnyan rdul phra rab kyi rdzas dang bral ba blos ma btags par rang dbang du shar ba'i du sogs kyi snang ba'am rnam pa yin no/ / de ltar yang rgyud 'grel chen dang bcas pa las/ stong pa las ni du ba smig rgyu zhes sogs du ma zhig gsungs pa rnams kyi stong pa las ni zhes pa'i stong pa ni 'od gsal gyi sems kyi rnam pa stong sang de la byas nas/ de las de'i gzugs brnyan gyi stong gzugs rnams 'byung ba la dgongs pa yin te/[162] rgyud 'grel dang dgongs pa mthun par bde mchog stod 'grel las/
nang du stong pa nyid la dmigs pas stong pa la ma btags pa'i dngos po thams cad mthong ba ni pra phab pas me long la gzhon nu mas gzugs mthong ba ltar khams gsum pa'i sangs rgyas kyi gzugs brnyan mthong ba las so sor sdud pa'i yan lag tu brjod do/[163] / zhes nang du 'od gsal gyi sems kyi rnam pa stong du ba la dmigs pa las stong gzugs mthong bar gsungs pa dang /

The nature of these empty forms is that they are images or reflections of the primordial clear-light mind, which itself appears as an object in the form of a cloudless space–like vacuity. These empty forms lack the substantiality of subtle particles, are not imputed by the mind, but are self-arising forms of smoke and so forth. The tantra and commentary say, “From the emptiness, smoke and mirage.”[166] The “emptiness” in this phrase refers to a vacuity that is an aspect of the clear-light mind, and the phrase itself means that from this vacuity arises its empty form images. The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary, which shares the thinking of the tantra and commentary, says:
Inwardly, focusing on the emptiness, all unimputed phenomena are seen. These are like forms seen in a mirror by a prognostic maiden, reflections of the three-world /381/ forms of the Buddha. This is spoken of as the branch of withdrawal.[167] This passage speaks of focusing inwardly on the clear-light mind vacuity from which the empty forms are seen.

d.div: [162] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 388_ba3
[163] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 130_ba2
[166] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 388b2.
[167] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 130b2.

f.d:
gzhan yang rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa las/
yod dang med las rnam par 'das/ / zag pa med pa'i blo ni gang / / zab mo de ni dmigs pa med/ / yid ches don can bsgom par bya/ dang po smig rgyu rnam paste /[164] / zhes sogs gsungs shing / de'i don ni yul yod pa dang med par 'dzin pa'i gnyis snang las rnam par 'das pa'i 'od gsal gyi sems zag pa mngon gyur du med pa'i blo ni gang yin pa'i zab mo de la ni dmigs pa med pa zhes bya zhing / de lta bu'i dmigs med de ni yid ches pa'i don du ba sogs 'char ba yin pas dmigs med de bsgom par bya zhes pa'o/ /

Also Short Assertions on Our Views states:
Beyond existence and nonexistence, this uncontaminated mind, a profundity without apprehension; meditate for the signs of reliability. First comes the mirage.[168] This means that the clear-light mind lacks manifest contamination and is beyond the duality of holding objects as existing or not existing. This profundity is without apprehension, and within this nonapprehended state, smoke and the other signs of reliability will arise. The yogi, therefore, should meditate on this nonapprehended state.

d.div: [164] pe cing bstan 'gyur nas kha bskang ba dar thang dpar ma'i pod/ pu/ chos tshan ang / 4530_rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa/ 23_na6
[168] P4580, nu (supplementary). Attributed to Kālacakra pāda.

f.d:
de bzhin du nA ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel par gsal bar gsungs te/ 'grel pa de nyid las/
gzung ba dang 'dzin pa dang bral ba'i rang bzhin stong pa nyid kyi blo ni shes rab ste de'i gzugs brnyan ni rnal 'byor pa la mngon sum du snang ba'o/[165] / zhes gsungs pa dang /

Likewise Nāropa, in his Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations, clearly says:
The mind of emptiness, devoid of perceiver and perceived, is a wisdom consciousness. Its images appear directly to the yogi.[169]

d.div: [165] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 255_ba2
[169] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 255b2.

f.d:
khams le'i mdor bsdus dang po las kyang /
de bzhin sems kyi 'od gsal rtog pa yi/ / sgom pa'i thabs rnams dag gis mi mthong ste/ / de nyid du 'di rkyang ma dag dang ni/ / ro ma gcig tu sbyor bas mthong bar 'gyur/[166] / zhes bskyed rim gyi rtog pa'i sgom pa'i thabs rnams kyis 'od gsal gyi sems mi mthong ste/ 'o na thabs gang gis mthong snyam na/ de kho na nyid du sems kyi 'od gsal 'di ni rtsa rkyang ma dang ro ma dag la rgyu ba'i rlung dbu mar gcig du sbyar bas mthong bar 'gyur bar bshad do/ / de yang 'grel tshig 'di la sogs pa rnams kyis rlung dbu mar chud pas sems kyi 'od gsal mthong bar bshad cing / gong du drangs pa ltar gyi 'grel tshig mang po zhig gis rlung dbu mar chud pa las du sogs kyi stong gzugs rnams mthong bar gsungs pa rnams kyi don shes par bya'o/ /

The first summary from the Realms chapter also says:
Similarly the clear-light mind is not seen by the methods of conceptual meditation. In its actuality, with left channel and right channel as one, it will be seen.[170] This explains that the clear-light mind will not be seen by the methods of the conceptual meditations of the generation stage. How is it seen? It is seen in its actuality when the winds that flow within the left and right channels combine as one in the central channel. That is the meaning of this passage and others from the commentary that explain how the clear-light mind is seen as a result of the winds entering the central channel. It is the meaning also of many commentary passages previously quoted that talk of empty forms being seen as a result of the winds entering the central channel.

d.div: [166] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 21_ba1
[170] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 21b1.

f.d: de ltar na du sogs kyi stong gzugs 'od gsal de'i gzugs brnyan du 'char tshul ni sor sdud kyi skabs 'dir gong du bshad pa ltar gyi rlung dbu mar 'dzud pa'i thabs bsgoms pas dbu mar rlung thog mar zhugs te 'od gsal gyi sems cung zad nyams su myong ba las de'i gzugs brnyan du ba lta bu dang / de nas rim pa bzhin rlung dbu mar zhugs pa shas je cher song ba las 'od gsal gyi sems de yang je gsal du song ste sems de'i gzugs brnyan smig rgyu dang mkha'asna nga dang sgron me lta bu 'byung ste/ de'i mthar sprin dang bral ba'i nam mkha' stong sang gi rnam pa 'ba' zhig 'byung ngo / /

The way smoke and the other empty forms arise as images of the clear-light mind is as follows. During the yoga of withdrawal the meditations upon the methods for bringing the winds into the central channel, as described previously, cause the winds to enter the central channel for the first time. /382/ A little of the clear-light mind is experienced, from which arises the smokelike clear-light mind image. Then as the amount of wind entering the central channel gradually increases, so the clear-light mind becomes clearer, and the mirage, firefly, and lamplike signs arise as images of that mind until, finally, just a cloud-free spacelike vacuity appears.

de nas mtshan mo'i rnal 'byor mthar phyin nas nyin mo'i rnal 'byor bsgoms pas du ba lta bu nas nam mkha' stong sang gi bar myur bar shar ba'i rjes su nam mkha'asto nga sang lta bu'i rnam pa de nyid la rtse gcig tu bltas te bsgoms pas nyin rtags rnams 'char ba yin pas 'di dag ni 'grel chen las/
'dir dbu mar srog rab tu zhugs pas stong pa kho na las du ba la sogs pa'i mtshan ma mthong ste/[167] zhes dang /
de nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' la bltas te nam mkha' de las kyang nyin mo'i rnal 'byor gyi nam mkha' las byung rang byung ba/[168] zhes sogs gsungs pa rnams kyi dgongs pa dpyis phyin pa yin no/ /

With the signs of the night yoga completed, the day yoga meditations begin. The signs from smoke up to the spacelike vacuity again arise quickly, and by looking at and meditating single-pointedly within this spacelike vacuity, the day signs arise. The preceding explanation is the definitive meaning of the following two passages from the Great Commentary:
Here the winds enter the central channel, and from the total emptiness the signs of smoke and so forth are seen.[171] Also:
Then the yogi looks into the cloudless space, and from that space, the “self-created, created from space” of the yoga of daytime.[172]

d.div: [167] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 388_ba2
[168] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 388_ba3
[171] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 388b2.
[172] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 388b3.

f.d: de yang / de nas sprin med pa'i nam mkha' zhes sogs kyi don bshad ma thag pa ltar yin pa ni bde mchog stod 'grel gyis gsal bar bshad pa gong du drangs zin pa ltar shes par bya'o/ / bla ma snga ma dag gis nam mkha' zhes gsungs pa rnams kyi'i nam mkha' [169] nyid la 'chad pa dang / stong pa las ni du ba smig rgyu zhes sogs stong pa zer ba byung ba rnams rnam med kyi stong nyid dam dmigs med 'ba' zhig la 'chad par mdzad de/ phyogs de la yang bsam par bya ba ni yod do/ /

That the meaning of “Then the yogi looks into the cloudless space” and so on is as it has just been explained is clearly supported by the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary as previously quoted. Lamas of the past have explained the “space” as external or actual space and the “emptiness” of “From the emptiness, smoke and mirage” as referring to nonaspected emptiness or as a totally nonapprehended source. This position also needs deliberation.

d.div: [169] phyi'i nam mkha' les byung yang phyi'i nam mkha' zhes bcos/

f.d: de ltar na rang bzhin 'od gsal gyi sems 'di mngon du gyur pa'i tshe/ de'i gzugs brnyan du sogs kyi stong gzugs me long la pra phapa pa lta bu rnams 'char la/ de yang 'chi ba'i gnas skabs su 'chi ba 'od gsal mngon du gyur pa'i tshe stong gzugs rnams 'char ba'i tshul ni nang 'chad pa'i skabs su bshad zin pa ltar yin zhing / lam gyi skabs su ni rlung bcu dbu mar zhugs pa las gnyug ma 'od gsal gyi sems mngon du gyur pa'i tshe nyi ma dang nyi ma'i 'od zer bzhin du sems de'i gzugs brnyan gyi stong gzugs pra phab pa lta bu sna tshogs pa zhig 'char la/ de ltar shar ba'i stong gzugs rnams ji gsal du song ba las mthar sgri ba pa thams cad dang bral bi 'khams gsum pa'i shes bya dngos po mtha' yas pa'i mtshan nyid can du gyur pa ni 'khor lo ste shes rab dang / 'od gsal gyi sems de nyid rkyen gzhan la brten nas mchog tu mi 'gyur pa'i shes pa sgrib pa thams cad zad pa'i rgyur gyur pa ni dus te thabs so/ /

When this natural clear-light mind is manifest, empty forms such as smoke appear as images of this mind, like forms appearing in a prognostic mirror. When the death clear-light mind is manifest at the time of death, the empty forms are as described in the Inner chapter. When the primordial clear-light mind is made manifest on the path by the ten winds entering the central channel, images of this clear-light mind are formed, like the sun and its rays. These appear as various empty forms, like forms in a clairvoyant’s mirror. /383/ These empty forms become clearer until finally their characteristics are that they become limitless and obscuration-free phenomena of the three worlds. This is the wheel (cakra) of Kālacakra and is the wisdom of method and wisdom. The clear-light mind itself, in dependence on other factors, become the cause for the supreme and unchanging consciousness freed from all obscuration. This is time (kāla) and is the method of method and wisdom.

de lta bu'i shes bya dang shes pa'am shes rab dang thabs ngo bo dbyer med gcig pa nyid kyi dus kyi 'khor lor 'gyur ba yin te/ mchog mi 'gyur gyi 'grel chen las/
bcom ldan 'das dus kyi 'khor lo thabs dang shes rab kyi bdag nyid de nyid shes pa dang shes bya'i 'brel bas gsungs te 'dir mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i shes pa sgrib pa thams cad zad pa'i rgyur 'gyur ba ni dus zhes brjod de thabs so/ / khams gsum pa'i shes bya dngos po mtha' yas pa'i mtshan nyid ni 'khor lo ste de nyid ni shes rab bo/ / shes pa dang shes bya de dag gcig pa nyid ni dus 'khor ro/[170] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

Such phenomena and consciousness, or wisdom and method, become the inseparable and unified wheel of time. The Great Commentary, in the Supreme and Unchanging Consciousness summary in the fifth chapter, states:
The conqueror Kālacakra is of the nature of method and wisdom. This is taught as a relationship between consciousness and phenomena. Here the supreme and unchanging consciousness is the cause that puts an end to all obstruction. This is said to be “time” and method. The limitless phenomena of the three worlds are the “wheel” and the wisdom. That consciousness and those phenomena as one, is the wheel of time.[173]

d.div: [170] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 394_ba2
[173] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 394b2.

f.d: de bzhin du 'od gsal gyi sems dang de'i gzugs brnyan du sogs kyi stong gzugs zung 'jug tu yod pa'i stong gzugs rnams la dmigs nas rtse gcig tu bsgoms pas sgrib bral gyi khams gsum pa'i shes bya mtha' yas par 'gyur zhing / 'od gsal gyi sems mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i ngo bor skyes pa stong pa nyid la rtse gcig tu mnyam par bzhag ste bsgoms pas mi 'gyur ba'i bde chen stong pa nyid dang dbyer med pa'i chos sku 'grub par 'gyur ro/ / de lta bu'i chos kyi sku dang sgrib bral gyi shes bya mtha' yas pa rnams ngo bo dbyer med zung du 'jug pa yin zhing / du sogs kyi stong gzugs de dag dang khyad par du yang re khA nag po skra'i tshad tsam gyi dbus su longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku rdo rje sems dpa' yab yum gyi rnam par shar ba de 'bras dus kyi stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can de'i bsgrub gzhi dang rigs 'dra'i rgyu yin la/ du sogs kyi stong gzugs 'di dag dang khyad par du yang rtags bcu'i mthar shar ba'i bum snam sogs khams gsum pa'i stong gzugs pra phab pa lta bu shar ba 'di rnams sgrib bral gyi stong gzugs sna tshogs pa rnams kyi bsgrub gzhi yin pas 'di dag rtse gcig tu sgom pa gtso bor bya dgos so/ /

By focusing on these empty forms of smoke and so forth that are unified with the clear-light mind and meditating single-pointedly, they become the limitless and obscuration-free phenomena of the three worlds. The clear-light mind itself, developed into unchanging bliss and placed in single-pointed meditative equipoise upon emptiness, will create the dharmakāya indivisibility of emptiness and unchanging great bliss, which is in an inseparable union with the limitless and obscuration-free phenomena. The empty forms of smoke and so forth, especially the enjoyment body in the form of Vajrasattva and consort in embrace that appears in the center of the black hairwidth line, are similar-type causes and bases for the accomplishment of the resultant empty-form Kālacakra in mother-and-father embrace. The empty forms of smoke and so forth, especially those of the three realms such as the vase that appear like the forms in a clairvoyant’s mirror after the ten signs have appeared, are bases for the accomplishment of the various obscuration-free empty forms. Therefore these have to be the primary objects of single-pointed meditation. /384/

'on kyang sor bsam gyi skabs la sogs pa'i stong gzugs rnams shes pa la de dang de'i rnam pa gsal bar shar ba ma gtogs gzugs de dang de'i bya ba byed nus su med cing / 'bras dus kyi stong gzugs thams cad ni gzugs dang me la sogs pa'i bya ba byed nus su yod pas khyad par che ste/ bde mchog stod 'grel las/
de'i phyir bcom ldan 'das kyi gsung las/ dang po du ba la sogs pa'i mtshan ma ni sgom pa'i dus na rtags su 'gyur ro/ / kha cig grub pa'i dus na zhes smra ba de rnams thams cad ni bcom ldan 'das kyi dam bca' ba nyams par byed pa ste/ bsam pa thams cad yongs spangs te/ / nyi ma gcig ni yongs su brtag ces pa'i bcom ldan 'das kyi bka' sun 'byin pa'o/ / grub pa'i dus na 'jig rten pa'i [171] du ba la sogs pa gang zhig sgyu ma dang rmi lam lta bu de ni mtshan mar mi 'gyur te 'dir dngos su du ba dang 'bar ba la sogs pas sreg pa'i bya ba nus pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du gur kum dang me tog dang rin po che dang gser gyi char yang ngo / / de'i phyir yan lag drug gi rnal 'byor las du ba la sogs pa'i mtshan mar 'gyur ro/[172] / zhes gsungs shing /

During the yogas of withdrawal, meditative absorption, and so forth, the features of the individual empty forms clearly appear to the mind, but beyond that these forms cannot perform their individual functions. However every empty form at its resultant stage is capable of performing its own function of form, fire, and so forth. This is a great difference. The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
Therefore the Buddha has said that the initial signs of smoke and so forth are signs at the time of meditation. All those who say “at the time of accomplishment” are finding fault with the assertions of the Buddha. They are dismissing teachings of the Buddha, such as, “All thoughts abandoned, meditate for a day.” At the time of accomplishment, the illusionlike and dreamlike worldly smoke and so forth are no longer signs. Here is actual smoke and fire, capable of performing the function of burning. It is the same with the rain of saffron, flowers, jewels, and gold. Therefore the signs of smoke and so forth appear within the six-branched yoga.[174]

d.div: [171] ma dper 'dzin rten pa'i gsal yang 'jig rten zhes bcos/
[172] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 131_ba5
[174] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 131b5.

f.d: 'dir dngos su du ba dang zhes pa'i 'dir zhes pa ni grub pa'i dus 'dir zhes pa'i don yin pas gsal bar bstan pa yin no/ / gzhan yang 'grel chig 'di dag gis du sogs kyi rtags rnams don dam bden pa yin pa dang / 'di dag mthong bas chos sku mthong ba yin pa yang bkag pa yin te/ 'grel pa 'di dag gis sor sdud kyi skabs kyi stong gzugs las 'bras dus kyi skabs kyi stong gzugs bzang bar song bar bstan cing / don dam bden pa'i ngo bo bzang por bsgyur du med pa'i phyir dang / chos sku yin na 'bar ba sogs kyi don byed nus pa 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ /

The word “here” from the phrase “Here is actual smoke” means “here at the time of accomplishment,” and the passage therefore makes the point clearly. This passage also refutes the assertion that the signs of smoke and so forth are ultimate truths and that to see them is to see the dharmakāya. This is so because this passage teaches that the empty forms of withdrawal yoga transform into perfected resultant empty forms, and that which is an ultimate truth cannot be perfected. Moreover it is contradictory to assert that the dharmakāya can perform functions of burning and so forth.

gzhan yang stod 'grel las/
'dir rang byin gyis brlab pa zhes bya ba ni so sor sdud pa kun rdzob pa stong pa nyid mthong ba'o/ / mtshan ma zhes bya ba ni sprin dang du ba la sogs pa ltar snang ba ste de yang sgron ma'i mtha' thug pa dang po mthong ba'o/[173] / zhes du sogs kyi rtags rnams kun rdzob tu gsungs shing / nA ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa las gzhan rnams stod 'grel bzhin las/ so sor sdud pas kun rdzob kyi bden pa [174] zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis stong gzugs rnams don dam bden pa yin pa bkag par shes par mdzod cig/

Furthermore the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
Here “self-blessing” refers to withdrawal, wherein conventional emptiness is seen. “Signs” refers to the appearances that are like clouds, smoke, and so forth. Those ending with the lamp are seen first.[175] This passage states that the signs of smoke and so forth are conventional truths. Nāropa in his Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations says the same.[176] It should be understood /385/ that these passages refute empty forms as ultimate truths.[177]

d.div: [173] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 132_na2
[174] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 253_na6
[175] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 132a2.
[176] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 253a6.
[177] A Jonangpa assertion.

f.d: gzhan yang rlung ng+hU tIr 'jug pa'i dmigs pa med par ting nge 'dzin thun mong ba rkyang pas kyang zla ba 'dra ba dang nyi ma 'dra ba dang rdo rje 'dra ba la sogs pa'i rtags 'char ba lang gshegs las gsungs pa dang /[175] rlung ng+hU tIr 'dzud pa'i dmigs pa bsgoms pas ng+hU tIr rlung ma tshud pa'i gong du yang du sogs kyi rtags 'char ba 'ong bas de gnyis la sor sdud kyi rtags mtshan nyid par ma 'khrul ba gal che ste/ de yang snga ma la 'khrul na ting nge 'dzin [176] mu stegs pa dang thun mong ba 'ga' zhig la rdzogs rim gyi lam du bzung nas phyin ci log tu 'gyur ba dang / phyi ma la 'khrul na rlung ng+hU tIr ma tshud pa'i gong gi rtags de skyes pa na sor sdud kyi rtags skyes par rlom zhing / sor sdud thob pa'i phan yon rgyud 'grel nas gsungs pa rnams rang nyid la e 'dug bltas pas mi 'dug par shes pa dang rgyud sde nas de ltar bshad pa mi bden no snyam pa'i las sgrib gsog par 'gyur ro/ /

Common meditative concentrations by themselves that do not focus on bringing winds into the dhūtī can bring about the appearance of moonlike, sunlike, and vajralike signs. This is stated in the Laṅkāvatārasūtra.[178] Meditations that do focus on bringing the winds into the dhūtī can also bring about the signs of smoke and so forth before the winds enter the dhūtī. Therefore it is important not to confuse these two with the definitive signs of withdrawal. If the former is confused with definitive withdrawal signs, the practitioner will go astray by holding non-Buddhist meditative concentrations and some common meditative concentrations as being completion-stage paths. If the latter is confused with definitive withdrawal signs, the practitioner will wrongly assume the accomplishment of withdrawal before the winds have entered the dhūtī. You will look to see if you possess the benefits that accrue from attaining withdrawal as taught in the tantra and commentary, and realizing you do not, you will create the karma and obstruction of thinking that what has been taught in the tantras is not true.

d.div: [175] sde dge_107_bka'/ mdo sde/ calang gshegs kyi mdo/ 94_na7
[176] ma dper nyid de 'dzin zhes byung yang ting nge 'dzin zhes bcos/
[178] Toh 107 Kangyur, mdo sde, cha, 94a7.

f.d:
'o na rlung dbu mar chud pa dang ma chud pa'i dus kyi du sogs kyi rtags kyi khyad par gang gis shes par byed snyam na/ 'dus pa phyi ma las/
brtan gyur rdo rje'i lam nas ni/[177] /zhes pa'i 'grel pa sgron gsal las/ rdo rje'i lam nas zhes pa 'da' bar mi bya ba'i mtshan ma lnga'i rim gyis/[178] zhes gsungs pa ltar du sogs kyi rtags rnams rim pa ma 'chol bar rim pa nges can du dmigs pa sgom res kyi 'char gyin 'dug na ng+hu tIr rlung tshud pa'i rtags su shes par bya'o/ /

So how can we differentiate between the signs of smoke and so forth that appear before the winds enter the central channel and those that appear afterward? The Later Guhyasamāja Tantra says, “From the stable vajra path,”[179] and its commentary Bright Lamp says:
“From the stable vajra path” means the progression of the five signs, not transgressed.[180] Therefore, when the signs of smoke and so forth appear in the proper order and are focused on and meditated upon in this order, it is an indication that the winds have entered the dhūtī.

[178] sde dge_1785_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ hasgron gsal/ 98_ba2
[179] Toh 443 Kangyur, rgyud, cha, 154b5.

f.d: bzhi pa sbogs chog ni/

d.i: Ritual of enhancement at times of nonaccomplishment

f.d:
sgrub le'i brgya cu dgu pa las/
so sor sdud pa la sogs rnams kyis gal te sngags pa rnams kyi 'dod pa grub par ma gyur na/[179] / zhes sogs rtsa 'grel rnams kyis sor sdud kyi sbogs chog dang sogs khongs nas srog rtsol gyi sbogs chog kyang bstan pas phyi ma ni rang rang gi skabs su 'chad cing / 'dir skabs su bab pa sor sdud kyi sbogs chog ni sbas pa mig 'byed las/
de la rnal 'byor pa rnams kyis btsan thabs kyi spyod pa shes par bya ste 'dir gang gi tshe so sor sdud pa la sogs pa rnams kyi stong pa nyid kyi sku la sna tshogs gzugs kyi sku mthong ba na srog la rnal 'byor pas ma bsdams pas mi 'dzag pa'i bde ba'i skad cig ma mi skye na de'i tshe rnal 'byor pas 'chad par 'gyur ba'i nA da la btsan thabs kyis goms par byas la nyams su blang bar bya ste de la rnal 'byor pas lus bsrangs te dkyil mo krung bcas la dbugs sor bzhag ste sems mi g.yeng bar gnas shing lag pa g.yas pas rtse'u chung ngam [180] gnyid log rtsa gnyis bags kyis mnan cing mi g.yo bar gnas par bya'o/ / de ltar yang nas yang du mi drag pa ci tsam du grangs mang par byas la ro stod dang spyi bo mi na ba de tsam du byas na rtsa dbu mar srog gi rlung rgyu ba nyid kyis shes rab kyi pad+mar gnas pa'i rdo rje nor bu'i nang du tshud pa'i byang chub kyi sems kyi thig le bzhi mi 'pho ba'i 'gog pa'i bde ba yis brgya 'char yang mi phod pa'i rgyu mthun pa'i mi 'dzag pa'i skad cig ma'i bde ba lhan cig skyes pa'i sku'i don bsgrubs pas mthong bar tshe 'di la 'gyur ro/ / de ni btsan thabs kyi sbyor ba dang po'o/[181] / zhes bshad pa ltar skabs 'dir gang zag gi rigs 'ga' zhig gis sor sdud kyi dmigs pa bsgoms pas du sogs kyi rtags shar yang rlung dbu mar ma tshud na sbogs chog 'di byed pa yin la/

Verse 119 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter says:
If by withdrawal and so forth the wishes of the mantra practitioner are not met…[181] This and following lines in the tantra and commentary teach the enhancement rituals of the withdrawal and prāṇāyāma yogas. Prāṇāyāma is included in the phrase “and so forth” /386/ and will be discussed in its own section. Concerning the enhancement necessary here for the withdrawal yoga, Opening the Eye to What Is Hidden says:
The forceful practice of the yogis should be known. When the yogas of withdrawal and so forth bring about the appearance of various form bodies in the body of emptiness, and yet the yogi has not bound the winds and therefore not developed an instance of the bliss of nonemission, at that time the yogi should practice the wrathful method and the nada meditation, which will be explained later. The yogi straightens the body, sits in vajra position, with breath natural and mind undistracted. With the right hand gradually press the veins of the neck or the two sleep-countering veins, and remain unmoving. Do this gently again and again, many times, for as long as the upper body and the head remain without pain. If this is done, the winds will flow into the central channel, and the four drops of bodhicitta that have entered the vajra jewel placed inside the lotus of wisdom are prevented from leaving, thereby creating bliss. This bliss, not approaching a hundredth part of that nonfalling, similar-to-cause bliss, has nevertheless accomplished the significance of the body comprising instances of innate bliss. Therefore it will be seen in this life. This is the first wrathful method.[182] As this passage explains, some people may meditate on the objects of withdrawal, causing the signs of smoke and so forth to arise, but the winds will not have entered the central channel. If that happens, the ritual for enhancement is as follows.

d.div: [179] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka119_90_na1
[180] ma dpe'i nang du drang pa'i sbas pa mig 'byed dang / sde dge bstan 'gyur nang gi sbas pa mig 'byed gnyis kyi bar tshig sna mi mthun pa mang tsam 'dug
[181] sde dge_1373_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_sbyor ba yan lag drug gi dka' 'grel/ 234_ba6
[181] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 119, 90a1.
[182] Toh 1373 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 234b6.

f.d: de'i byed tshul ni/ de la rnal 'byor pas lus bsrangs te zhes pa nas spyi bo min pa de tsam du byas na zhes pa'i bar gyis bstan pa ltar lus drang por bsrang ba sogs lus gnad dang lta stangs sor sdud kyi skabs ltar byas nas lag pa g.yas pa'i mthe bong dang srin lag gnyis kyis rtse'u chung ngam gnyid log gi rtsa g.yas g.yon gnyis bags kyis te dal bus mnan cing sems dmigs pa la mi g.yo bar rtse gcig tu 'jog pa'o/ / de ltar yang nas yang du mi drag tsam du grangs mang bar bya'o/ / de yang ji tsam re bya snyam na/ ro stod dang spyi bo min tsam gyi bar du bya'o/ / de ltar byas na rlung rtsa dbu mar rgyu'o/ / de ltar rgyus pa nyid kyis byang chub kyis sems thig le nor bu'i bug pa nas 'dzag pa khegs te/ phyag rgya dang mnyam par sbyar ba'i tshe shes rab ma'i pad+mar gnas pa'i rnal 'byor pa rang gi rdo rje nor bu'i nang du chud pa'i byang chub kyi sems sad rmi gnyid 'thug bzhi pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le bzhin nor bu'i bug pa nas mi 'pho zhing 'gog pa'i yas babs kyi lhan skyes kyi bde ba yis brgya'i char yang mi phod pa ste 'gran mi [182] bzod pa'i rgyu mthun pa'i mi 'dzag pa ste mi 'gyur ba'i skad cig ma'i bde ba lhan cig skyes pa'i sku'i don ste rgyu bsgrubs pa yin pas lhan skyes kyi bde ba chen po'i sku mthong ba'i chos tshe 'di la thob par 'gyur ba yin no/ / de yang rtsa dbu mar srog gi rlung rgyu ba nyid kyis zhes pa man chad kyis sbogs chog 'di'i byed las dang phan yon bstan pa yin no/ /

How it is actually performed is described in the lines from “The yogi straightens the body” until “and the head remain without pain.” Straightening the body and so forth means to adopt the body and eye positions of withdrawal. The thumb and ring finger of the right hand gradually press the right and left neck veins or the right and left sleep-countering veins. The mind remains single-pointedly placed and unmoving in its focus. This is to be practiced quite gently again and again. How many times? For as long as the upper body and the head are without pain. If this is done, the winds will flow in the central channel. The winds flowing in the central channel will prevent the bodhicitta /387/ drops falling from the opening of the jewel. When in union with a mudrā consort, the four drops of bodhicitta that create the four periods of waking, dream, sleep, and sexual bliss, and which have entered the yogi’s vajra jewel placed inside the lotus of the wisdom consort, are stopped and do not emerge from the opening of the jewel. This creates the ascending innate bliss. “This bliss, not approaching,” or not standing comparison with, “a hundredth part of that nonfalling,” or unchanging, “similar-to-cause bliss, has nevertheless accomplished,” or created, “the significance,” or cause, of the body comprising instances of innate bliss. Therefore this body of great innate bliss will be seen and accomplished in this life. The lines from “If this is done, the winds will flow into the central channel” onward teach the function and benefits of this enhancement ritual.

d.div: [182] ma dper 'gron mi bzod pa zhes byung yang 'gran mi bzod pa zhes bcos/

f.d: de ltar na sor sdud mthar phyin pa'i skabs su phyag rgya dang snyoms 'jug byed mi byed ji ltar yin yang rung ste/ phyag rgya dang snyoms 'jug byed na'ang khams byang chub kyi sems rdo rje nor bu nas mi 'dzag pa'i nus pa thob pa yin no/ /
At the completion of withdrawal yoga, one can choose to use a mudrā consort or not. If a consort is used, the ability to prevent the bodhicitta from leaving the jewel will have been achieved.

yang sbogs chog snga ma ltar byas pas kyang rlung dbu mar ma chud pas bde ba 'dren pa'i thabs sbas pa mig 'byed las bshad pa ni de nyid las/
yang btsan thabs kyi spyod pa gnyis pa brjod par bya ste/ stong pa nyid kyi rang bzhin shes rab ma dang snyoms par zhugs shing mnyam par 'jog pa'i dus su snying rje'i bdag nyid thabs kyi gsang ba'i gnas thur sel gyi sgo g.ya' ba'am lus la ber ba langs pa'i skabs de nyid du rdo rje nor bu'i rtsa bar lag pa g.yas pas mnan la lus mi g.yo bar sems bde ba la gtad cing yar drang ba dang / rgyu zhabs kyi she tshigs pa la sbyor ba dang / mig bgrad pa dang / rkang pa'i mthe bong nang du bskums pa dang rting pa phyir brkyangs pas shes rab ma dang thabs gnyis ka yang mi 'gul mi g.yo bar bde ba la sems gtad cing gnas pa ni btsan thabs kyi sbyor ba gnyis pa'o/[183] / zhes gsungs pa'o/ / 'grel tshig gzhan rnams go sla zhing / stong pa nyid kyi rang bzhin shes rab ma zhes pa phyag rgya dang / snying rje'i bdag nyid thabs zhes pa rnal 'byor pa la bya'o/ /

If this ritual is performed and the winds have still not entered the central channel, Opening the Eye to What Is Hidden describes a method for inducing bliss:
Now the second forceful method will be described. When in meditative union with wisdom, who is the nature of emptiness, and there arises a hot sensation on the body or the sensation of tingling at the opening of the downwardly expelling wind channel in the secret place of the method, who is the nature of compassion, press the base of the vajra jewel with the right hand. With the body unmoving concentrate the mind in bliss and draw it up. Push the flesh of the lower stomach against the joint.[183] Stare with eyes wide open. Bend the toes in and stretch out the heel. With both wisdom and method unmoving and mind placed on bliss, this is the second forceful practice.[184] The phrase “wisdom, who is the nature of emptiness” refers to the consort. “Method, who is the nature of compassion” refers to the yogi. The rest is not difficult to understand. /388/

d.div: [183] sde dge_1373_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_sbyor ba yan lag drug gi dka' 'grel/ 235_na4
[183] According to Kirti Tsenshap Rinpoché and Ven. Tashi Döndrup, “joint” here could refer to either the meditator’s lower spine or lower ribs.
[184] Toh 1373 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 234a4.

f.d:
'di'i lag len ni bla ma'i gsung las shes dgos so/ / sbas pa mig 'byed las bshad pa 'di dag ni lag len la mkho bas bris pa yin gyi rgyud 'grel gyi dgongs pa ni srog rtsol gyi skabs su bshad par bya'o/ / chos rje bu'i 'khrid yig las/
snyan brgyud las/ so sor sdud pa'i sbogs pa ni/ / byed bcing drag tu brtsam par bya/[184] / zhes pas lus gnad dang lta stangs kyi byed pa gnad du ma song ba yin pas nyin bar snang ba la lus gnad dang lta stangs byed tu bcug la byung ma byung bltas te ma byung na legs par bslabs la sngar ltar sgom du gzhug[185] / ces gsungs nas/ lus gnad dang lta stangs ma byung ba slar 'chos pa nyid 'di'i sbogs chog tu snyan brgyud dang chos rje gnyi ga bzhed pa yin no/ / 'di ni mi 'thad de/ sbogs chog 'di ni lus gnad lta stangs sogs ji ltar bshad pa bzhin byas nas bsgoms pas kyang rlung dbu mar ma tshud na bya dgos pa yin pas dang po'i sgom tshul slob pa sbogs chog tu mi rung ngo / / zhes rje rin po che gsung ba shin tu thugs bden no/[186] /

This practice must be learned from a lama. The above explanation from Opening the Eye to What Is Hidden has been reproduced here because it is necessary for practice, but in the thinking of the tantra it is to be explained in the section on prāṇāyāma. In the writings of the dharma master Butön it states:
In the Kālacakrapāda Transmission it is said: “The enhancement of withdrawal forcefully completes binding and activities.”[185] When the body and eyes are not in their positions, attempt to position them in the daylight, and check if this has been been accomplished. If not, then as before, enter into meditation according to this excellent instruction.[186] Therefore both the dharma master Butön and the Kālacakrapāda Transmission maintain that this particular enhancement practice is for correcting the posture and eye position. This is not correct because this enhancement ritual is to be performed when, having implemented the posture and eye position as described previously, the meditation does not bring the winds into the central channel. Therefore the words of Jé Tsongkhapa, “instruction on the initial meditation is not suitable to be an enhancement ritual”[187] are very true.

f.d: gzhan yang snga ma kha cig zangs chus bkang ba la mig sbrid sbrid du blta/ sbrid pa dang nam mkha' la bltas pas stong gzugs 'char zhes sogs mang po zhig 'di'i sbogs chog tu 'chad pa rnams ni phal mo che stong gzugs 'char ba'i ched du mdzad par snang la/ rgyud 'grel las 'dir sbogs chog gsungs pa ni sor sdud kyi skabs 'dir stong gzugs shar yang rlung dbu mar ma tshud pa 'dzud pa'i phyir yin pas so/ /

Some practitioners of the past have advised, “Stare blankly into a copper vessel full of water. Look at that blankness and into space, and empty forms will arise.” This and many other rituals described as being the enhancement ritual of this section seem mostly to be rituals for producing the appearance of empty forms, whereas the teachings on the enhancement ritual taught in the tantra and commentary at this juncture are for occasions during withdrawal yoga when the empty forms have appeared but the winds have not entered the central channel.
lnga pa sgom 'phro la shi yang rnal 'byor goms stobs kyis 'jug par bstan pa ni

d.i: Even dying with the remainder of the meditations unfinished, the power of the yoga ensures continuation

f.d:
nang le'i go bdun pa las/
rnal 'byor dbang po rnal 'byor ma thob rab tu g.yo ba'i yid kyis gal te shi bar gyur pa na/ / dpal ldan mi yi 'jig rten du ni rab mchog thub pa'i rigs su rnal 'byor lhan par skye bar 'gyur/ / sngon gyi goms pa de yis slar yang ye shes rnal 'byor yangs pa dag ni kun tu 'dzin par 'gyur/ / ye shes thob nas mi zad mchog gi gnas su rab 'gro slar yang gang du'ang skye ba ldan pa min/[187] / zhes gsungs pa ltar sor sdud lta bu rnal 'byor sgom pa'i gang zag rnal 'byor gong ma rnams ma thob pa'i bar skabs su shi bar gyur na yang tshe phyi mar sngags sgrub pa'i rten sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa'i rigs su skyes te rten de la sngar gyi lam gyi 'phro bsgoms nas rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong gzugs dang mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po dbyer med pa'i mthar thug gi go 'phang thob par 'gyur ro/ /

Verse 97 of the Inner chapter states:
With the mighty yogas unachieved, should the migration of the mind bring death, the yogi will be born into a great and powerful family in a glorious human world possessed of the yoga. By past familiarity, once again the yogi will hold the pure and vast gnosis yoga. The yogi, achieving gnosis, travels to a place supreme and eternal, never to take birth anywhere again.[188] /389/ If a practitioner practicing a yoga such as withdrawal dies before attaining the higher yogas, in his next life he will be born in buddha and bodhisattva families endowed with the foundation for the practice of mantra. On that foundation he will meditate on the remainder of the path and attain the highest state of the unity of unchanging great bliss and the empty form endowed with every supreme aspect.

d.div: [187] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka97_50_na1

f.d: bzhi pa tshad ma gang yin pa ni/

rdo rje snying 'grel las dbang po'i mngon sum gyi tshad mar [188] gsungs pa ltar sha'i mig dbang la brten nas byung ba'i sha'i mig gi dbang po'i rnam par shes pas du sogs kyi stong gzugs gsal bar mthong zhing mi slu bas na dbang po'i mngon sum tshad ma'o/ / de bzhin du sbas pa mig 'byed las/
'dir dang por rang gi sems kyi snang ba ni de bzhin gshegs pa'i sha'i mig gis dpag tshad stong mthong bar 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du lha'i spyan rnam par dag pas dpag tshad nyis stong mthong bar 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du sangs rgyas kyi spyan rnam par dag pas gzhan gyi sems shes pa mthong bar 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du chos yang dag par sdud par spyan lnga bcom ldan 'das kyis gsungs so/ / de rnams kyang 'di lta ste rim pa bzhin du sha'i spyan dang / lha'i spyan dang / sangs rgyas kyi spyan dang / shes rab kyi spyan dang / ye shes kyi spyan rnams rnal 'byor pa'i sems a ba ng+hU tIr btsud cing bsgoms pa'i stobs kyis 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ / de nas thams cad mkhyen pas ma gzigs pa dang mi mkhyen pa cung zad kyang med do/[189] / zhes gsungs pa'i 'dir dang por zhes pa nas/ dpag tshad stong mthong zhes pa'i bar gyis sor sdud kyi skabs kyi stong gzugs sha'i mig shes kyis mthong bar bstan/ de bzhin du zhes pa nas gsungs so zhes pa'i bar gyis spyan phyi ma bzhis lam gyi gnas skabs gong ma gong mar stong gzugs mthong tshul dang spyan lnga mdo phyogs nas gsungs pa'i khungs bstan/ de rnams kyang zhes pa nas 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes pa'i bar gyis spyan lnga rlung sems rtsa dbu mar btsud cing bsgoms pa las 'byung bar bstan/ de nas zhes pa nas med do zhes pa'i bar gyis spyan lnga mthar phyin pa'i gnas skabs sangs rgyas kyi ye shes kyis ma gzigs pa dang mi mkhyen pa med par bstan pa yin no/ /

The fleshly eye sensory consciousness arises in dependence upon the fleshly eye sense organ. It sees clearly the empty forms of smoke and so forth, it is undeceiving, and therefore it is a sensory and direct valid cognition. This is in keeping with the Vajragarbha Commentary, which describes withdrawal as a sensory and direct valid cognition.[189] Likewise Opening the Eye to What Is Hidden says:
Here, concerning the objects that appear to the mind, the tathāgata fleshly eye sees for a thousand yojana. Similarly the pure celestial eye sees for two thousand yojana. The pure eye of the Buddha sees the minds and consciousnesses of others. The Buddha taught the five sights in the Dharmasaṃgītisūtra. They are, in order, the fleshly eye, celestial eye, eye of the Buddha, eye of wisdom, and eye of gnosis, and they will arise by the power of the yogi placing the mind in the avadhūtī and meditating. Then there is nothing that the omniscient mind does not see or does not understand.[190] The first sentence of this passage describes how empty forms of withdrawal are seen by the fleshly eye consciousness. The next three sentences from “Similarly” up to “Dharmasaṃgītisūtra” describe how empty forms are seen by the remaining four sights on the progressively higher paths, as well as indicating the sutra source for the five sights. The next sentence, beginning “They are, in order” teaches that the five sights arise from the winds and the mind being brought inside the central channel. The last sentence teaches /390/ that there is nothing the perfection of the five sights or enlightened gnosis does not see or understand.

f.d:
sbas pa mig 'byed las 'di ltar gsungs pa rnams ni ye le'i brgya bcu dgu pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir de bzhin gshegs pa'i sha'i spyan gyis dang por rang gi sems kyi snang ba mthong zhing lha la sogs pa'i spyan gyis gzhan gyi sems shes pa mthong ste des na chos yang dag par sdud pa las/ bcom ldan 'das kyi spyan lnga zhes gsungs so/ / de ltar rim pas sha'i spyan dang lha'i spyan dang sangs rgyas kyi spyan dang shes rab kyi spyan dang ye shes kyi spyan ni bsgoms pa'i stobs kyis 'byung bar 'gyur ro/[190] / zhes gsungs pa'i dgongs pa ltar bkod pa yin no/ / gzhan yang stod 'grel dang nA ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa las bshad pa ni gong du drangs zin pa ltar shes par bya'o/ /

This passage from Opening the Eye to What Is Hidden is similar to the passage in the Great Commentary on verse 119 of the Gnosis chapter, which says:
With tathāgata fleshly eyes one first sees the appearances within one’s own mind. With the celestial and other eyes, the minds and consciousnesses of others are seen. In the Dharmasaṃgītisūtra the Conqueror taught the five sights. They are, in order, fleshly eyes, celestial eyes, Buddha eyes, wisdom eyes, and eyes of gnosis. These will arise from meditation.[191] The descriptions of these sights in Nāropa’s Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations and the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary can be seen in previous quotations from these texts.

d.div: [190] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 389_na4

f.d: lnga pa dag dbye ni/

ye shes kyi phung po'i chos kyi sde tshan ye shes kyi phung po dang khams la sogs pa drug sor sdud kyi rnam par dag bya dang / sor sdud ni de dag dag byed rdo rje sems pa'i rigs so/ / dbye ba ni du sogs kyi rtags bcu ste/ de ltar yang sgrub le'i brgya bco lnga pa las/
so sor sdud pa rgyal ba'i dbang por 'gyur zhing rnam pa bcu ste [191] zhes pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir dang po'i las la so sor sdud pa ni rgyal ba'i dbang po zhes pa ye shes kyi phung po'o/ de yang mtshan ma'i dbye bas rnam pa bcu ste/ du ba dang smig rgyu dang me khyer dang mar me ltar 'bar ba dang zla ba dang nyi ma dang sgra gcan dang cha shas dang thig le mthong ba'i dbye bas ma btags pa ye shes kyi phung po'o/[192] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ / 'o na ye shes kyi phung po'i chos drug po gang yin snyam na|_de dag ni ye shes kyi phung po dang / ye shes kyi khams dang / yid dang / sgra dang / mchog gi dbang po dang / dri chu 'dzag pa dang drug go/ / drug po 'di rdo rje sems dpa'i rigs kyi lam rnams kyi sbyang gzhi dang / de drug sbyangs pa las chos drug po 'di rnams sgrib pa med pa nyid dang / ro mnyam pa nyid dang / gcig tu 'dres par gyur pa nyid du byed pa'o/ / de yang rdo rje sems dpa' rigs thams cad kyi khyab byed yin pa bzhin du sor sdud kyang lam 'og ma thams cad kyi khyab byed du shes par bya'o/ /

The gnosis aggregate, gnosis element, and so forth of the gnosis-aggregate group are the six phenomena to be purified in withdrawal yoga. Withdrawal is the purifier and is of the Vajrasattva family. The divisions are the ten signs of smoke and so forth. Verse 115 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter says:
Withdrawal is Vajrasattva and the ten forms. On this the Great Commentary says:
The first practice is withdrawal. This is Vajrasattva, the gnosis aggregate. Because that is divided into ten signs, there are “ten forms” that appear. They are smoke, mirage, fireflies, lamp, blazing, moon, sun, Rāhu, part, and drop. These form the unimputed gnosis aggregate. What are the six phenomena of the gnosis aggregate group? They are gnosis aggregate, gnosis element, mind, sound, the supreme organ, and the emission of urine. These six are the bases of purification for the paths of the Vajrasattva family. When purified these six become free of obscuration, are of a single taste, and are fused together as one. /391/ Vajrasattva pervades all families, and so it should be understood that withdrawal yoga pervades all lower paths.

f.d: drug pa 'bras bu

['di ]la gnas skabs kyi 'bras bu dang mthar thug gi 'bras bu gnyis las/ dang po ni sgrub le'i brgya bco brgyad pa las/
so sor sdud pas rnal 'byor pa ni yul dang rnam par bral ba sngags rnams kun gyis byin gyis rlob/[193] / ces pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir gang gi tshe so sor sdud pas gzugs brtan par gyur ba'i rnal 'byor pa rnam par dag par gyur ba de'i tshe sngags rnams kun gyis byin gyis rlob par 'gyur te tshig gis mchog sbyin pa la sogs pa sbyin par 'gyur ro/[194] / zhes dang /

There are immediate and final results. On the immediate results, verse 118 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter says:
In withdrawal the yogi apprehends no objects and is blessed by every mantra.[192] On this the Great Commentary says:
By the power of withdrawal, when the forms are stable and the yogi has attained purification, he is blessed by every mantra and is able to perform giving by words and so forth.[193]

f.d:
gsang ba 'dus pa las/
so sor sdud pas snyoms zhugs pa/ / sngags rnams kun gyis byin gyis rlob/[195] / ces gsungs pa ltar sor sdud mthar phyin pa'i rnal 'byor pas sngags thams cad byin gyis rlob pas tshig gis mchog sbyin pa la sogs pa 'grub pa ste/ dper na dug med par gyur cig [196] ces brjod pas dug med par byed nus pa la sogs pa lta bu'o/ / gnyis pa mthar thug gi 'bras bu ni ye shes kyi phung po'i sde tshan gyi chos drug sgrib bral du dag pa rdo rje sems dpa' dang / ye shes kyi pha rol tu phyin pa la sogs pa'i chos drug tshan gcig 'grub pa'o/ /

The Guhyasamāja says:
The meditator by withdrawal is blessed by every mantra.[194] When the yogi has completed withdrawal yoga, he is blessed by every mantra and develops the power of “giving by words.” For example, by saying “Let there be no poison,” the poison disappears. The final result of withdrawal is the complete nonobscuration of the six phenomena of the gnosis aggregate in the form of Vajrasattva, Jñānapāramitā, and so forth.

f.d: gnyis pa grub zin brtan par byed pa bsam gtan gyi yan lag bshad pa/
29. The Yoga of Meditative Absorption
gnyis pa grub zin brtan par byed pa bsam gtan gyi yan lag

d.i: The second yoga, the stabilizing meditative absorption

f.d: ['di ]la drug/ bsam gtan gyi mtshan don dang / bsgom pa'i dus 'tshams dang / ji ltar sgom pa'i tshul dang / tshad ma gang yin pa dang / dag dbye dang / 'bras bu'o/ /
This has six outlines: 1. The meaning of the term meditative absorption 2. The time for meditation 3. The way to meditate 4. Valid cognition 5. Purification divisions 6. Results
dang po [bsam gtan gyi mtshan don ]ni

d.i: The meaning of the term meditative absorption

f.d:
stong gzugs la sems rtse gcig tu 'dzin pas na bsam gtan zhes bya ste/ sgrub le'i brgya bco lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
yul dang yul can bcu po rnams gcig nyid du sna tshogs gzugs la bsam gtan pa'o/[197] / zhes gsungs pa'i don yin no/ / chos rje bu'i 'khrid yig las
stong pa nyid kyi gzugs la yid ma yengs par rtse gcig tu 'dzin pas bsam gtan no/[198] / zhes mtshan don du mdzad cing / chos rje phyogs pa yang 'di dang mthun no/ /

This branch is called meditative absorption[195] because it holds single-pointedly to empty forms. The Great Commentary, on verse 115 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says of its meaning:
In meditative absorption the five object types and five consciousnesses are as one /392/ in various forms.[196] In the writings of the dharma master Butön it says:
Because of the mind undistracted and single-pointedly held on empty forms, it is known as meditative absorption.[197] The dharma master Chogpa[198] says the same.

f.d:
kha cig mkhas grub chos rje'i dgongs par mdzad nas
stong gzugs la sems rtse gcig tu gnas pa brtan par byed pas na bsam gtan zhes pa mtshan don du rung stezhes gsung ba ni rje nyid kyis gsungs pa'i zin bris kyis bkag ste/ zin bris las/
kha cig sor sdud brtan par byed pas bsam gtan zhes zer ba ni ye ge'i don la ma zhugs so/[199] / zhes gsungs pas so/ /

Others who assert the position of the dharma master Khedrup Jé say of the etymology of meditative absorption:
Because it single-pointedly stabilizes the mind upon the empty forms, it is known as meditative absorption. This is refuted by Jé Tsongkhapa in his Notes on Kālacakra:
The assertion by some that “because it stabilizes withdrawal it is known as meditative absorption” does not correspond to the etymology.[199]

d.div: [199] rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum pod/ da_rdzogs rim gyi gnad bsdus pa/ 7_ba3_dus 'khor gyi sbyor ba yan lag drug gi nyer mkho'i zin bris/ 16_ba3_dang 16_na5
[199] Collected Works, vol. da, Essentials of the Six-Yoga Completion Stage, 7b3; and Essential Notes on the Kālacakra Six Yogas, 16b3 and 16a5.

f.d: de yang de'i dgongs pa ni stong gzugs la sems rtse gcig tu gnas pa brtan par byed ces pa'i brtan pa dang/ sor sdud brtan par byed ces pa'i brtan pa gnyis ni ba 'og ra brtan yin zhing / bsam gtan gyi gtan pa ga gtan yin pas de yi ge'i don la ma zhugs zhes pa yin pas thugs bden par mngon no/ /

This means that the term stabilize [brtan] in the lines “it single-pointedly stabilizes the mind upon the empty forms” and in the phrase “stabilizes withdrawal,”and the term absorption [gtan] in “meditative absorption” are of similar pronunciation but of different spellings.[200] Therefore the statement that it “does not correspond to the etymology” is very true.

d.div: [200] In Tibetan “stabilize” is brtan and “meditative absorption” is bsam gtan. The two words brtan and gtan are pronounced the same and are similar in meaning, but there are differences. Gtan is connected with time, often with the meaning of constant, permanent, and so forth. Brtan means firm or stable. The etymology of bsam gtan, therefore, is a mind that is constantly held or fixed, hence meditative absorption. Tsongkhapa is saying that some have confused these two terms.

f.d: gnyis pa bsgom pa'i dus mtshams ni

dus zhabs snyan brgyud las/ dus ni nam mkha' rgyu dus so/[200] /zhes thog mar nam mkha'i rlung rgyu ba nas bsgom par gsungs te/ bsam gtan mi bskyod pa'i yan lag yin pa la dgongs pa 'dra na'ang / rgyud 'grel du de lta bu gsal bar ma byung ngo |_|des na rang lugs ni rtags bcu pa thig le'i dbus kyi re khA'i dbus su longs sku dang de'i mthar stong gzugs sna tshogs pa mthong ba'i 'tshams nas sgom pa yin te/ dbang mdor bstan las/
rmi lam bzhin du gzugs mthong 'gyur/ / rtag tu gzugs de bsgom par bya/[201] / zhes pa'i nA ro pa'i 'grel pa las/
gzugs ni sna tshogs gzugs te bsgom par bya ba ni bsam gtan gyi yan lag gis brtan par bya'o/[202] / zhes dang /

The Kālacakrapāda Transmission says, “The time is the time of the flow of space,”[201] thereby asserting that meditation should begin after the space winds begin to flow. Although this appears to be based on the fact that meditative absorption yoga is the branch of Akṣobhya, it is not clearly stated in the tantra and commentary. Therefore our own position is that the meditation begins after the appearance of the tenth sign and the various empty forms that subsequently appear. The tenth sign is the saṃbhogakāya form seen in the black line inside the drop. A Short Teaching on Initiations says:
Like dreams, forms are seen. Meditate constantly on these forms.[202] Nāropa, in his commentary to this text, says:
“Forms” are various forms. “Meditate” means to stabilize with the branch of meditative absorption.[203]

f.d:
yang dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa 'di nyid las/
bsnyen pa'i dus te dus dang por so sor sdud pa yis bsgom par bya zhing bsam gtan gyi yan lag gis brtan par bya'o/[203] / zhes rtags bcu rdzogs pa'i mthar stong gzugs sna tshogs mthong ba de sor sdud kyis byas te de'i mjug nyid du bsam gtan gyis brtan par byed par gsungs pas so/ /

The same commentary says:
The time for approximation is that firstly one meditates with withdrawal, and then one stabilizes with the branch of meditative absorption.[204] Therefore the ten signs and the subsequent various empty forms are achieved by withdrawal, and stabilization is accomplished by meditative absorption. /393/

f.d: gsum pa ji ltar sgom pa'i tshul
['di ]la lnga/ dgos pa gang gi phyir sgom pa dang / sgom tshul dngos dang / yan lag gi dbye ba dang / bsam gtan grub pa'i tshad dang / nyams rtags 'char tshul lo/ /
This is under five headings: 1. Purpose of the meditation 2. Actual way to meditate 3. Subdivisions 4. Measure of completion 5. Signs of accomplishment
dang po [dgos pa gang gi phyir sgom pa ]ni

sor sdud kyi skabs su grub zin pa'i stong gzugs rnams brtan par bya ba'i phyir sgom pa yin no/ / de ltar yin par ni nA ro pa'i 'grel par/ gzugs ni sna tshogs gzugs te [204] zhes sogs gong du drangs pa nyid kyis shes so/ /
The purpose of the meditation is to stabilize the empty forms achieved during withdrawal. This can be understood from the above quote from Nāropa’s commentary beginning “The time for approximation.”

f.d: sgom tshul dngos ni
Actual way to meditate
gzhan lugs mi 'thad par bstan pa dang rang lugs gnyis las/
This has two outlines: 1. Refuting the position of others 2. Our own position
dang po [gzhan lugs ]ni/
Refuting the position of others

kha cig rje rin po che'i dgongs par bsams nas/
bsam gtan gyi skabs su stong gzugs sna tshogs shar ba na de thams cad rang gi 'dun pas bcos nas rang gang la goms pa che ba'i lha sku yid ngor 'char sla bar bsgyur nas yang yang bsgoms pas de la byang ba na dus kyi 'khor lo'i skur sgyur ba la slob/ de la lobs nas thams cad 'od kyi rnam par gyur te mthar gcig la gcig thim nas dus 'khor rdor sems kyi sku yab yum gyi rnam pa can sngar gyi de la bsdu/ de sngar rang las rgyang chad du snang ba yin yang skabs 'di nas rang gi sems 'di la bcug ste dbyer med du byas nas de la nga rgyal bzhag ste yang yang bsgoms pa'i mthar lha'i rnam pa de rang las rgyang chad du mi 'char bar de la nga rgyal bcos min 'pho thub pa 'byung zhing / de ltar sgom pa ni rjes dran gyi sku bsgrub pa'i gzhi khyad par can du 'gyur ba yin no/[205] / zhes 'khrid yig tu bkod do/ /

Some, thinking it to be the position of Jé Tsongkhapa, say:
Empty forms appearing during meditative-absorption yoga are all conceived by one’s own effort. They are transformed into the forms of deities one has the greater meditative familiarity with and that appear easily to the mind. These are meditated on repeatedly, and upon the culmination of that meditation, one transforms them into forms of Kālacakra. After this practice they all transform into light and absorb into one another to become the form of Kālacakra in the form of Vajrasattva and consort. Previously this form appeared at a distance from oneself, but from here onward one’s mind enters this form and becomes indivisible with it. Pride is generated and meditation is performed again and again. Finally the deity no longer appears at a distance from oneself, and one is able to transfer a natural uncontrived pride to the deity. Such a meditation creates a special basis for the development of deity form in the branch of recollection.[205] This passage is from an instruction manual.

d.div: [205] khrid yig 'di su'i yin ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[205] Unable to trace the author of this citation.

f.d:
'di dag ni zab zab ltar snang na'ang don 'thad par ma mthong ste/ skabs 'di la sogs pa'i stong gzugs rnams ni blos cung zad kyang ma bcos shing ma btags pa rang byung du shar ba dgos pa ni khams le'i mdor bsdus lnga pa las/
gang don dam pa'i bden pas bstan pa de ni 'jig rten las 'das pa rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa phyag rgya chen po'i dngos grub bsgrub pa'i slad du rang gi sems kyis yongs su btags pa'i chos dang bral ba gzhon nu ma rnams kyi me long la sogs pa la pra phab pa bzhin du rnal 'byor pa rnams kyi rang gi sems kyi 'od gsal mngon sum du nam mkha' la snang ba 'dod pa'i don gyi 'bras bu ster ba ste 'bras bu ni 'gyur ba med pa'i bde ba'i ye shes kyi sems so/[206] / zhes dang /

It may sound very profound, but I cannot see it as being correct, because the empty forms in this and other sections are not imputed or conceived by the mind at all but must arise on their own accord. The fifth summary from the Realms chapter says:
That which is taught as ultimate truth is beyond the world, and is for the attainment of the mahāmudrā siddhi endowed with every supreme feature. It grants the desired result, manifestly appearing in the space of the yogi’s clear-light mind, like images in a mirror seen by a maiden, devoid of phenomena imputed by the mind. It produces the gnosis of unchanging bliss.[206]

[206] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 38b2.

f.d:
yang
sangs rgyas kyi gzugs ni rdzas med pa'i phyir dang rtag pa med pa'i phyir/[207] / zhes sogs rgyud 'grel gyi gong 'og du mar gsungs shing / khyed ni bsam gtan gyi skabs 'dir shar ba'i stong gzugs rnams blos bcos nas lha'i skur sgyur ba sogs su 'dod pa'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang sor sdud kyi rtags bcu shar ba'i skabs su yang rtags rnams lha'i rnam par blos bcos nas sgyur dgos pa sogs mtshungs pas ha cang thal lo/ /

Also: /394/
Because the form of the Buddha is without substance and because it is unimputed.[207] Similar passages are found throughout the tantra and commentary, and yet you say that the empty forms that appear during meditative absorption are deliberately conceived by the mind and changed into the forms of deities? It would follow, too, that the ten signs that appear during withdrawal would also have to be transformed by the mind into forms of deities.

[207] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 388b7.

f.d:
'di'i bzhed pa ltar na stong gzugs sna tshogs shar ba lha'i rnam pa dang / khyad par du yang dus 'khor yab yum gcig pu'i rnam par sgyur ma thub na stong gzugs shar ba rnams don med du 'gyur ro snyam du dgongs pa 'dra ste re khA'i nang du dus 'khor rdor sems yab yum mtshan dpes brgyan pa'i rnam pa can bsam gtan gyis brtan par byas pa de rjes dran gyi gnas skabs sogs kyi dus 'khor yab yum gyi stong gzugs kyi bsgrub gzhi yin pa bzhin du rtags bcu'i mthar shar ba'i bum snam sogs rnam pa thams cad pa'i stong gzugs sna tshogs shar ba rnams kyang bsam gtan gyis stong gzugs de dang de brtan par byas pa sangs rgyas pa'i sgrib bral gyi stong gzugs pra phab pa lta bu 'char ba rnams kyi bsgrub gzhi yang dag pa yin pas de rnams lha'i rnam par sgyur dgos [208] pa min te/ ye le'i brgya nyer gnyis pa/
stong pa nges par mtshan ma rnam pa bcu ru 'gyur zhing mtshan ma ni|_| rnam pa thams cad pa ru 'gyur te ma zad mchog gi bde ba gzhom du med pa ye shes sku/[209] / zhes pa'i 'grel chen las/
de bzhin du stong pa nges par du ba la sogs pa'i mtshan ma rnam pa bcu ru 'gyur zhing mtshan ma ni rnam pa thams cad pa'i gzugs su 'gyur ro/ / gzugs las 'gyur ba med pa'i bde bar 'gyur te/[210] zhes 'od gsal gyi sems stong sang gi rnam pa can gyi stong pa de nyid du sogs kyi mtshan ma bcur 'gyur zhing / mtshan ma rnams bum pa dang snam bu sogs stong gzugs sna tshogs pa rnam pa thams cad pa'i gzugs su 'gyur ro/ /

According to the above assertion it seems that if it were not possible to transform the various manifest empty forms into deities and especially into a single Kālacakra mother and father, then the appearance of these empty forms would have no purpose. However Kālacakra in the form of Vajrasattva mother and father adorned with the features and signs in the black line is stabilized by meditative absorption and is the basis of the empty-form Kālacakra of the branch of recollection. Likewise the various aspected empty forms, such as the vase and so forth, that appear after the ten signs are also stabilized by meditative absorption and are the perfect basis for the unobscured empty forms of enlightenment. There is no need to transform them into the forms of deities. Verse 122 of the Gnosis chapter says:
The emptiness becomes the forms of the ten signs. The signs are fully aspected and become the unending, supreme indestructible bliss.[208] On this the commentary says:
Likewise the emptiness becomes the definite forms of the ten signs of smoke and so forth, and the signs are fully aspected form. From the forms comes the unchanging bliss.[209] Therefore the emptiness, which is the clear-light mind in its aspect of vacuity, becomes the ten signs of smoke and so forth, and the signs of the various empty forms such as the vases and friezes are fully aspected forms.

f.d:
rnam pa thams cad pa'i gzugs las 'gyur ba med pa'i bde bar 'gyur bar gsungs kyi/ lha'i rnam par sgyur dgos par ma gsungs so/ / bum pa dang snam bu sogs kyi stong gzugs la rnam pa thams cad pa'i gzugs zhes bya ste/ 'grel chen las/
bum pa dang snam bu la sogs pa rnam pa thams cad pa'i gzugs mthong ba'o/[211] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

The passage says that the unchanging bliss comes from these fully aspected forms. It does not say that they are transformed into the forms of deities. On these empty forms of the vases, friezes, and so forth being fully aspected forms, the Great Commentary says: /395/
The fully aspected forms of the vases, friezes, and so forth are seen.[210]
