f.d:
'di dag ni 'thad par ma mthong ste/ dbugs la sngags rnams me tog gi phreng ba bzhin du sbyor ba'i bzlas pa 'di dag ston pa'i rgyud/ shes rab thabs kyi yi ge dag gi zhes sogs kyi snga 'grel las/
da ni 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub bsgrub pa'i slad du sngags kyi bzlas pa gsungs pa/[258] zhes 'di'i skabs kyi bzlas pa rnams 'jig rten pa'i dngos grub sgrub byed du gsungs pa dang / dbugs 'jug pa dang 'byung ba dag dang lhan cig sngags kyi yi ge rnams rab tu 'jug pa dang 'byung ba me tog gi phreng ba bzhin du zhes dbugs phyi nang du 'gro ba phreng thag dang de dang mnyam du sngags kyi yi ge'i gzugs rnams me tog gi phreng ba star la brgyus pa bzhin du dmigs nas bzla bar bshad pas rlung srog sa tha dad par dmigs pa 'di dang sngags kyi yi ge'i gzugs la dmigs pa 'di rdor bzlas kyi mi mthun phyogs yin pa dang / /gzhan yang 'dir ni 'pho ba bcu gnyis kyi rlung la dmigs par bshad cing 'pho ba bcu gnyis kyi rlung rgyu ba ni ro rkyang la rgyu ba yin la rdor bzlas kyis ni rlung dbu mar 'byung 'jug byed par mos dgos phyir phyir ro/ /

I cannot see these claims as being correct, because in a preceding passage that comments on the tantra lines “the letters of wisdom and method,” which teach these mantra recitations applied to breaths like garlands of flowers, the Great Commentary says:
The text speaks of reciting mantras in order to achieve worldly powers.[258] /412/ Therefore the recitations of this passage are for the achievement of worldly powers. Also the line “together with the breath entering and leaving, concentrate on the letters of the mantra entering and leaving like a garland of flowers” describes a recitation in which the forms of the mantra syllables are strung together like a garland of flowers on the thread of the entering and leaving breath. Focusing on the winds and mantras as being separate in this way and focusing on the forms of the mantras is incompatible with vajra recitation. Moreover, in the above description, focus is placed on the winds of the twelve major movements, which flow within the left and right channels. However, in vajra recitation, the winds are to be visualized as entering and leaving the central channel.

d.div: [258] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 371_ba7
[258] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 371b7.

f.d:
gzhan yang 'di'i skabs kyi 'grel chen las/
de ltar mi phyed pa'i yan lag srog dang ldan pa'i yid kyis sngags bzlas par bya'o/[259] /zhes 'di'i skabs kyi sngags bzla ba 'di yid bzlas su bshad cing bskyed rim gyi skabs kyi yid bzlas byed pa la rdor bzlas su bshad pas 'dir rdo rje'i bzlas pa'i rim pa dang ma ning gi bzlas pa'i rim pa'o/ /zhes gsungs pa yang yid bzlas la rdor bzlas su btags pa la dgongs par byed dgos so/ /

Furthermore the Great Commentary in that section says:
The inseparable branch, the winds together with the mantras, are recited by the mind.[259] This explains that the mantra recitation of that passage is mental recitation. Moreover the Great Commentary refers to the mental recitation of the generation stage as vajra recitation. Therefore, although the passage talks of “vajra recitation and neutral recitation,” it must be the intention of the tantra merely to label mental recitation as vajra recitation.

d.div: [259] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 375_ba7
[259] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 375b7.

f.d: yang kha cig /lta stangs dang sems gnyis smin mtshams kyi d+hU tI'i nang du gtad nas rtse gcig tu bzung ba tsam gyis sngar goms pa'i stobs ches pas stong gzugs khyad par can mthong bar 'gyur la/ de la nga rgyal bzhag ste rlung nang du 'jug pa'i tshe rang gi sems stong gzugs dang gcig tu byas pa ste rlung dang bsres nas rlung sems stong gzugs gsum tha dad du mi lta bar yid ngor gcig tu 'dres pa de la rtse gcig tu dmigs pa gtad nas de nyid d+hU tI'i yar sna dmigs pa gtad sa de nas nang na mar rim gyis 'jug pa'i gdangs te skad oM zhes pa'i sgrar grag par mos zhes sogs rdor bzlas kyi dmigs pa sgom tshul zab par 'dod par byed do/ / 'di ni brtags na mi 'thad par go ste/ lta stangs dang sems gnyis smin mtshams kyi d+hU tI'i nang du gtad nas rtse gcig tu bzung ba tsam gyis stong gzugs khyad par can mthong bar gyur pa de'i tshe spyir ro rkyang la rlung rgyu ba chad de dbu mar tshud pa dang khyad par du yang bsam gtan mthar phyin pa'i skabs yin pas shes dang shes bya byung zad ces pa'i don gzugs sogs yul drug la mig gi rnam shes sogs yul can drug 'jug pa'i yul yul can gyi 'brel pa rnam shes de dag gi bzhon pa'i rlung dbu mar tshud pa'i sgo nas chad pa yin pas de'i tshe rna ba'i shes pa dang lus shes sgra dang reg bya la 'jug pa med la/ de ltar na dus de'i tshe rlung nang na mar rim gyis 'jug pa'i gdangs te skad oM zhes pa'i sgrar mos pa ji ltar byed/

Others say that the eyes and the mind are focused within the dhūtī between the eyebrows, and merely by single-pointed concentration a very special empty form will appear due to the power of previous familiarity. Self-pride is placed in this empty form, and when the winds are inhaled, the mind, which has become one with the empty form, merges with the winds so that winds, mind, and empty form are not regarded as separate entities but are merged in the mind. This is single-pointedly concentrated upon, and during its gradual descent from within the upper opening of the dhūtī, its tone is visualized as the actual sound “oṃ.” This process is asserted as being part of the profound focus of vajra recitation meditation. However, if examined, it can be seen to be faulty. When the eyes and the mind are focused in the dhūtī between the eyebrows and a very special empty form appears just by the power of single-pointed concentration, the flow of winds in the right and left channels will typically have been severed and brought to the central channel. Specifically this is the time of the completion of meditative absorption. /413/ Therefore, as the line “cessation of arising consciousness and objects of consciousness”[260] explains, the object and object-engager connection, which refers to the six consciousnesses of sight and so forth engaging the six objects, form and so forth, has been cut because the winds, or mounts of those consciousnesses, have been brought into the central channel. Therefore, at that particular time, the consciousness of hearing and the bodily consciousness do not engage their objects of sound and bodily sensation. Therefore how would it be possible to visualize the gradual descent from within the upper opening of the dhūtī as emitting the sound oṃ?

d.div: [260] From the Later Guhyasamāja, quoted previously.

f.d: gzhan yang dang po rdor bzlas la 'jug pa'i dus su rlung gnas tshod ro rkyang nas rgyu na'ang dbu mar 'jug pa sogs su mos nas byed pa yin la/ khyed ltar na dang po rdor bzlas la 'jug pa'i dus ni rlung dbu mar zhugs pa'i stobs kyis stong gzugs khyad par can mthong ba'i dus de yin zhing / dus der rlung dbu ma nyid nas 'byung 'jug byed par 'dod dgos pas de yang ji ltar rigs zhes bya ba la sogs pa gnod pa du ma 'bab bo/ /

Furthermore, when beginning the practice of vajra recitation, even if the actual status of the winds is that they are still flowing in the left and right channels, one nevertheless practices by visualizing them as entering the central channel. According to the above assertion, however, the time for beginning the practice of vajra recitation is when a very special empty form appears due to the power of the winds having already entered the central channel. Therefore at that time you would have to say that the winds were already entering and leaving the central channel. How could that be correct? Through this and other reasons a lot of damage can be done to this assertion.

rang lugs kyi sgom tshul mdor bsdus pa ni lus gnad dang lta stangs gong du bshad pa bzhin byas te gnas tshod la rlung ro rkyang dbu ma gsum la ci rigs par rgyu ba yin na'ang / rdo rje bzlas pa la dang po 'jug pa'i dus su dbugs nang du 'jug pa dbu ma'i nang na mar zhugs te lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi dbu ma'i nang der song nas 'byung 'jug gang rung re'i yun tsam re gnas pa dang / phyir 'byung ba'i tshe yang dbu ma'i nang nyid nas 'byung bar mos te de yang dbugs nang du 'jug pa'i rang gdangs oM gyi gdangs dang / gnas pa'i rang gdangs hUM gi gdangs dang / phyir 'byung ba'i rang gdangs A:'i gdangs su mos nas rtse gcig tu 'jog pa'o/ /

To summarize our own position on vajra recitation meditation: the eyes and body are positioned as previously explained, and at the beginning of the practice of vajra recitation, regardless of whether the winds are actually flowing in the right or left channels or the central channel, the incoming breath is visualized as descending within the central channel to arrive at the center of the navel cakra. There it remains for however long the duration of one breath may be. When it arises, it does so again through the central channel. The innate tone[261] of the breath entering is visualized as oṃ, the innate tone of abiding as hūḥ, and the innate tone of leaving or arising is visualized as āḥ. This process is to be single-pointedly concentrated upon.

d.div: [261] rang gi gdangs. This is the innate tone of the breath and not sound as perceived by hearing.

f.d: de yang rlung sngags sbyor tshul dngos gzhi ni dbugs kyi rang gdangs kyi sgra nyid yi ge gsum gyi gdangs su sgrog kyin yod pa nyan pa'i rnam pa lta bur byed pa yin no/ / de yang gnas pa lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i dbu ma'i nang du byed dgos pa'i rgyu mtshan ni sor bsam gyi skabs su stong gzugs khyad par ba dbu ma'i yar sna'i nang du shar pa yin na'ang srog rtsol yan chad du lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi nang gi dbu mar 'char ba cig dgos so/ /

The actual way the mantras are applied to the winds is that the innate tones of the breaths resonate as the sounds of the three syllables as if they were actually being heard. The reason why it takes place in the central channel within the very center of the navel cakra is that although in the branches of withdrawal and meditative absorption the special empty form appears within the upper opening of the central channel, from the branch of prāṇāyāma onward it has to be an appearance in the central channel at the center of the navel cakra. /414/

de'i rgyu mtshan yang mkhas grub rjes rnam bshad de kho na nyid snang ba las/
ma btags pa dngos po la grub pa'i stong gzugs kyi phyag rgya khyad par ba rjes dran gyi skabs su thog mar grub pa ni lte ba'i 'khor lo'i dbus kyi a wa d+hU tI'i nang du rlung zhugs gnas thim gsum byas pa las gnas der shar ba'i stong gzugs su gsungs pas de'i phyir lhan skyes kyi ye shes khyad par ba dngos su 'dren byed khyad par ba thog mar gang du grub pa'i gnas lte ba'i 'khor lo yin pa'i dbang du mdzad nas lte ba'i 'khor lo lhan skyes kyi sku'i rten du gsungs so zhes pa bdag gi rje thams cad mkhyen pa'i gsung ngag thun mong ma yin pa'o/[260] / zhes gsungs pa ltar stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can rnal 'byor pa'i blo la snang ba tsam ma yin pa'i dngos gnas la rjes dran gyi skabs su dang por grub pa'i gnas ni lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi dbu ma'i nang yin la/ stong gzugs khyad par ba de'i nye rgyu'i bsgrub gzhi srog 'dzin gyi skabs kyi stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam pa can ma bcos ma btags par rnal 'byor pa'i blo la snang ba tsam de yang lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi dbu ma'i nang du shar ba cig dgos shing / de 'char ba la 'dzin pa'i skabs su lte ba'i dbus kyi dbu mar rlung gnas pa dang / srog rtsol gyi skabs su der rlung zhugs pa cig dgos pas/ rdor bzlas kyis lte ba nas 'byung 'jug gnas pa dang sbyor ba dang bum pa can gyis lte bar rlung kha sbyor du 'dzin pa sogs byed dgos pa yin no/ /

The reason why is stated by Khedrup Jé in Illuminating Reality:
The special empty-form mudra as an actual phenomenon is first developed on the branch of recollection. This is taught as an empty form arising from the winds entering, abiding, and dissolving within the avadhūtī at the center of the navel cakra. Therefore the special cause that induces the special innate gnosis is first developed at the navel cakra. Because of this the navel cakra is spoken of as the innate deity form. This is a special assertion of my omniscient master.[262] An actual empty-form Kālacakra in mother-and-father embrace that is not just an appearance within the mind of the yogi is first developed during the branch of recollection, and the place where it is developed is in the central channel at the center of the navel cakra. The foundation and immediate cause of this special empty form is the empty-form Kālacakra in mother-and-father embrace developed during the branches of prāṇāyāma and retention, which arises unconceived and unimputed within the yogi’s mind. This too must arise in the central channel at the center of the navel cakra. For the arising of such an appearance, the winds must abide in the central channel at the navel cakra during retention and must enter the central channel at the same location during prāṇāyāma. Therefore vajra recitation is applied to the processes of entering, abiding, and arising at the navel, and it is in that location that vase yoga holds the winds together in union.

d.div: [260] mkhas grub dge legs dpal bzang / gsung 'bum pod/ ga_nang gi le'u 'grel bshad/ 29_ba4
[262] Collected Works, vol. ga, Inner Chapter, 29b4.

f.d:
'o na lte ba'i 'khor lo lhan skyes kyi sku'i rten du ji ltar gsungs snyam na/ nang le'i nyer bdun pa/
gsang ba gtsug tor lte ba la yang lhan skyes rgyal ba'i sku ste rang bzhin med dang rang bzhin no/[261] / zhes pa'i 'grel chen las/
de'i phyir gsang ba'i pad+ma dang gtsug tor gyi pad+ma dang lte ba'i pad+ma la rnam par dag pa'i sku lhag pa'i lha ste rang bzhin med pa ma btags pa dang rang bzhin pra phab pa lta bu'o/[262] / zhes pa 'dis bstan par bzhed do/ /

What does it mean to say, “the navel cakra is spoken of as the innate deity form”? This is taught by the twenty-seventh verse of the Inner chapter, which says:
At the secret, crown, and navel also, the innate form of the Buddha, without and with nature.[263] On this verse the Great Commentary says:
Therefore, at the secret lotus, the crown lotus, and the navel lotus, the pure form, the supreme deity. Without nature, and unimputed, its nature is like form in a clairvoyant’s mirror.[264]

d.div: [261] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka27_42_ba6
[262] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 126_na3
[263] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud ka, v. 27, 42b6.

f.d: mdor na sbyor ba yan lag drug gi skabs la lar rlung dbu mar tshud pa dang / la lar tshud pa phul du phyin pa dang / skabs 'ga' zhig tu rlung dbu mar gnas pa dang / skabs kha cig tu rlung dbu mar sad pa ste thim pa'i stobs kyis gnyug ma'i sems kyi ngo bo 'od gsal dang / de'i gzugs brnyan stong gzugs pra phab pa lta bu dang / khyad par du yang du ma longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku mtha' yas pa rnams zung 'jug tu sbyor ba yan lag drug car [263] gyi mnyam gzhag gi gnas skabs thams cad du 'char ba yin te/ / 'od gsal gyi sems mthar thug pa rnam mkhyen ma thob bar du mngon du byed mi nus kyang / bsgoms stobs kyis rlung dbu mar tshud de 'od gsal gyi sems cung zad nyams su myong ba nas rlung dbu mar tshud pa phul du byung ba dang gnas pa dang thim pa'i gnas skabs rnams su rim pa bzhin je gsal je gsal du song ste stong gzugs rnams kyang je gsal du 'gro'o/ / de yang stong gzugs rnams sor bsam gyi gnas skabs su sha'i mig shes kyis mthong ngo / / bsam gtan mthar phyin te mngon shes thob pa nas srog 'dzin dang rjes dran mthar phyin te dbang po gnyis sbyor gyi 'dod chags dang ma bral gyi bar la lha'i mig gyi mngon shes kyis mthong ngo / / phyag rgya chen mo dngos gnas la grub pa'i rjes dran mthar phyin pa thob ste las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya la 'dod chags dang bral ba nas sangs rgyas kyi spyan gyis gzigs so/ / de nas byang chub sems dpa'i 'tshams sa bcu gnyis kyi dang po mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skad cig dang po thob pa nas shes rab kyi spyan gyis gzigs so/ / yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas thob nas ye shes kyi spyan gyis gzigs so/ /

To summarize: during the practices of the six-branched yoga, sometimes the winds are entering the central channel, sometimes the process of entering is at its peak, sometimes the winds abide in the central channel, /415/ and sometimes the winds are “killed” or dissolved in the central channel. By the power of these processes, the clear light, whose nature is the primordial mind, appears in unification with its images at all stages within the meditations of the six yogas. These images are empty forms, especially the countless saṃbhogakāya forms, which appear like phenomena in a clairvoyant’s mirror. Although the final clear light cannot be actualized until the attainment of omniscience, nevertheless, when the winds are initially brought into the central channel by the power of meditation, a little of the clear-light mind is experienced. During the stages of peak entering, abiding, and dissolution, the clear-light mind becomes progressively clearer, and the empty forms also become clearer. At the stages of withdrawal and meditative absorption, the empty forms are seen with fleshly eye consciousness. From the completion of meditative absorption, when clairvoyance is gained, until the completion of prāṇāyāma, retention, and recollection, and for as long as there is no separation from desire for the union of the two organs, the empty forms are seen with the clairvoyance of the celestial eye. From the completion of the branch of recollection, in which a mahāmudrā consort has been actually created and separation from desire for the karma and wisdom mudrā consorts is attained, the empty forms are seen with the buddha eye. From the very first moment of attaining the unchanging bliss on the first of the twelve bodhisattva levels, the forms are seen with the eye of wisdom. When the perfect and complete enlightenment is attained, empty forms are seen with the eye of gnosis.

d.div: [263] ma dper yan lag drug cur gyi zhes byung yang drug car gyi zhes bcos/

f.d:
de ltar yang sgrub le'i nyis brgya so gnyis pa/
lha yi dmigs pa gang yin mngon sum dang ni rjes su dpag pa rnam pa gnyis su 'gyur ba ste/ / mngon sum dag ni de nyid sbyor bas mkha' la skar ma bzhin du du ma longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku/[264] / zhes pa'i 'grel chen las/
mngon sum dang rjes su dpag pa de dag las mngon sum gang yin pa dag ni de nyid sbyor bas mkha' la skar ma bzhin du 'gyur te skar ma'i tshogs bzhin du du ma longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku zhes pa ni sha la sogs pa'i mig gis gzung bar bya ba srid pa gsum dang dus gsum rmi lam dang sgyu ma dang mtshungs pa'o/ / 'dir dang por las dang po ba'i rnal 'byor pas mngon par shes pa med par sha'i mig gis sna tshogs mthong ngo / / de nas mngon par shes pa'i 'tshams kyi dbang gis lha'i mig gis mthong ngo / / de nas chags pa dang bral ba'i 'tshams kyi dbang gis sangs rgyas kyi spyan gyis gzigs so/ / de nas byang chub sems dpa'i 'tshams kyi dbang gi shes rab kyi spyan gyis gzigs so/ / de nas yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi 'tshams kyi thugs kyi dbang gis ye shes kyi spyan gyis gzigs te lhag ma kun las rnam grol cing zhes so/ / de ltar de bzhin gshegs pa'i sha la sogs pa'i spyan lnga pa rnams ni stong pa nyid gzigs pa'i slad du ste sems can gzhan rnams ni stong pa nyid lta ba'i yul la dmus long ngo /[265] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyi don la legs par brtags na sbyor ba yan lag drug gi gnas skabs gang yin yang rlung dbu mar zhugs pa dang gnas pa dang thim pa gang rung gi mnyam gzhag gi gnas skabs kho nar stong gzugs rnams nges par 'char zhing de ma gtogs rlung ro rkyang la sgyu ma lta bu'i rjes thob kyi gnas skabs su stong gzugs mi 'char bar go nus so/ /

Verse 232 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter says:
Objects of celestial sight are two, those of inferential and of direct cognition. With the application of direct cognition, manifold saṃbhogakāya forms arise, like stars in the sky.[265] On this the Great Commentary says:
There is direct and inferential cognition. With the application of direct cognition, “manifold saṃbhogakāya forms arise, like stars in the sky,” meaning like a host of stars, the forms are seen with the fleshly eye and so forth, and the three worlds and the three times are like dreams and illusions. Here initially the beginner yogi without clairvoyance sees various forms with the fleshly eye. Then, with the attainment of clairvoyance, they are seen by the celestial eye. /416/ With the attainment of separation from desire, they are seen by the buddha eye. With the attainment of the bodhisattva stages, they are seen by the eye of wisdom. With the attainment of full and perfect enlightened mind, they are seen by the gnosis eye, “freed from remainder.” In this way the fleshly eye of the tathāgata and the other sights that make up the five eyes are for the seeing of emptiness. Other living beings are blind to the objects seen within the view of emptiness.[266] If this passage is analyzed, it can be understood that any part of the six-branched yoga is solely a time of meditative equipoise on the winds entering, abiding, or dissolving in the central channel, within which empty forms will definitely arise. In the illusionlike postmeditation times when the winds flow in the right and left channels, the empty forms do not appear.

d.div: [264] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka232_101_na6
[265] sde dge_845_bstan/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 258_na2
[265] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud ka, v. 232, 101a6.

f.d: dper na gsang ba 'dus pa'i dgongs pa la rlung dbu mar zhugs gnas thim gsum byas ba'i mnyam gzhag kho nar lam gyi snang mched thob gsum 'od gsal dang bcas pa 'ong bar nges shing de ma gtogs rjes thob kyi gnas skabs su mi 'byung ba dang 'dra'o/ 'di la dgongs nas rje yab sras rnams kyis kyang / rjes dran gyi skabs nas stong gzugs phyag rgya chen mo dngos gnas la grub kyang rjes dran dang ting 'dzin gyi mnyam gzhag gi gnas skabs ma gtogs rjes thob kyi gnas skabs su rgyun chad 'gro bar [266] gsungs pa yin no/ /

For example, in Guhyasamāja thinking, it is only in the meditative equipoise of the winds entering, abiding, and dissolving in the central channel that the clear light along with the appearances, increases, and attainments of the path will definitely occur, whereas these are not experienced in the postmeditation sessions. With this in mind Jé Tsongkhapa and his disciples maintain that although an actual empty-form mahāmudrā consort is achieved from the branch of recollection onward, its continuum is cut during the postmeditation times and only achieved in the meditative equipoise sessions of the branches of recollection and meditative concentration.[267]

d.div: [266] rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum pod/ da_sbyor drug zin bris/ 3_na7
[267] Essential Notes on the Kālacakra Six Yogas, Collected Works, vol. da, 3a7.

f.d: lnga pa bsgoms pas nyams rtags ji ltar skye ba'i tshul ni/

zin bris las/
bla ma snga ma rnams bde drod dang rtsa dang rlung gi kha dog mthong ba sogs 'byung ngo zhes gsung la/ rtsa dang rlung gi kha dog mthong ba la nyams snang la rtsa'i 'khor lo mthong ba dang / de nas rgyu ba'i rlung gi kha dog mthong ba dang / der ma zad 'jig rten gyi khams du ma mthong ba la sogs pa 'byung ste de dag ni rmi lam du mthong ba dang 'dra bas kha cig bden pa srid kyang yid brtan mi rung ngo / / rdo rje 'phreng ba nas lus dben rdzogs nas rdor bzlas zla ba drug byed par bshad pa'i zla ba bzhi pa la rtsa'i 'khor lo'i kha dog mthong bar bshad pa lta bu ni rang mtshan pa mthong ba yin pas rdor bzlas bsgoms pas myong ba skye tshul phal pa yin yang gtso bo ni rlung d+hU tIr zhugs pa'i rtags 'khrul med rnams 'char dgos so|[267] |zhes gsungs pa ltar shes par bya'o/ /

These can be understood from Notes on Kālacakra, which says:
Lamas of the past have mentioned the heat of bliss, seeing the channels, and the colors of the winds and so on. Seeing the channels and the colors of the winds is the result of practice. However being able to see the cakras and then the colors of the moving winds, as well as being able to see many worlds, is like seeing visions in a dream, and although some may be genuine, they are unreliable. The Vajra Garland teaches that when the isolation of the body is complete, vajra recitation should be performed for six months, and that in the fourth month the colors of the cakras are seen. This is an actual sight of the cakras, and although this is a common experience of vajra recitation meditation, /417/ the most important thing is that the unmistaken signs of the winds having entered the dhūtī must arise.[268]

d.div: [267] rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum pod/ da_sbyor ba yan lag drug gi rdzogs rim gyi gnad bsdus pa/ 14_ba4
[268] Essentials of the Six Yoga Completion stage, Collected Works, vol. da, 14b4.

f.d: gnyis pa bum pa can gyi sgom tshul
32. Vase Yoga
['di ]la gnyis las
This has two main headings: 1. The function or purpose of vase yoga 2. The actual meditation
dang po bum pa can gyi byed las sam dngos kyi dgos pa ni

d.i: The function or purpose of vase yoga

f.d: [bum pa can gyi byed las sam dngos kyi dgos pa ]lte bar srog thur 'dres nas gtum mo 'bar ba'o/ /
The function or purpose of vase yoga is to mix the life-sustaining and downwardly expelling winds at the navel and to ignite the caṇḍālī fire.
gnyis pa sgom tshul dngos
['di ]la lnga/ gang du bsgom pa'i gnas dang / lus gnad dang / lta stangs dang / gang la dmigs nas bsgom pa'i tshul dang / de ltar bsgoms pas nyams rtags skye ba'i tshul lo/ /
This is under five headings: 1. Place of meditation 2. Posture 3. Positioning of eyes 4. Focus and method of meditation 5. Signs of accomplishment
'di'i dang po gnyis pa gsum pa rnams rdor bzlas dang 'dra'o/ /
The first three topics are as described in the section on vajra recitation.
bzhi pa gang la dmigs nas bsgom pa'i tshul ni

rlung 'byung 'jug mi byed par lus kyi nang du 'dzin pa la yang bum pa can du bshad pa yod cing de ni rgyud sde 'og ma la yang yod la/ /der ma zad grangs can la bum pa can yod par bshad cing / paN+Di ta sa'i snying pos/ mu stegs dang ma rgyud kyi rlung sbyor 'byed dka' bar 'dug [268] gsungs pa la bla ma snga ma rnams lta ba dang byang chub kyi sems kyis zin ma zin gyi sgo nas 'byed gsung zhing / rlung sbyor gyi sgo nas mi 'byed gsung ba'i rlung sbyor ngo bo'i sgo nas khyad par ma phyed par snang la/ rlung sbyor de dag ni ngo bo'i sgo nas kyang khyad par shin tu che ste/ grangs can la ni spyir steng 'og gi rlung kha sbyor du byed pa dang / khyad par du bla med nas bshad pa ltar rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su kha sbyor du byas nas bzung bas lhan skyes kyi bde chen 'dren pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / des na rlung 'byung 'jug mi byed par lus kyi nang du gnas pa tsam gyi bum pa can ni mu stegs dang rgyud sde 'og ma la yang yod pas de las khyad par du gyur pa'i bum pa can gyi sgom tshul dgos pas de bshad par bya ste/ 'dil gnyis/ rgyud 'grel pa dang bcas pa las ji ltar gsungs pa dgod pa dang / dmigs pa sgom tshul nyid bshad pa'o/ /

Holding the winds inside without letting them enter or leave can also be explained as vase yoga and is found in the lower tantras. Moreover it has been taught that vase yoga is found in the non-Buddhist Sāṃkhya tradition. Pandit Kṣitigarbha[269] said that it is difficult to differentiate the wind yogas of non-Buddhists and those of the mother tantras.[270] Lamas of the past have maintained that they are differentiated on the basis of their view and by whether or not they encompass bodhicitta but not on the basis of being wind yogas. Although it may seem that the different vase yogas are not differentiated by their individual characteristics, there is actually a huge difference in the fundamental features of these yogas. Generally, in the Sāṃkhya tradition, there is no bringing together of upper and lower winds, and specifically there is no inducing of the innate great bliss by uniting and holding the winds in the centers of the cakras as taught in the highest yoga tantras. Vase yoga in which the winds are merely kept inside without leaving or entering can be found in non-Buddhist traditions and in the lower tantras. Therefore a special vase yoga meditation is necessary here, and that will be explained. It is under two headings: 1. How it is presented in the tantra and commentary /418/ 2. The actual focus and method of the meditation

f.d: dang po [rgyud 'grel pa dang bcas pa las ji ltar gsungs pa dgod pa ]ni
How it is presented in the tantra and commentary

ye le'i brgya bcu bdun pa'i 'grel chen las/
de nas gzugs ni mthong bar gyur na nyin zhag so so'i+i dus su srog gi rlung ni 'gog pa zhes pa bum pa can rab tu bya ste 'od zer 'khor lo rang gi lus la yongs su bskor zhing 'khor bar byed pa mthong gi bar du'o zhes pa sngar brjod pa'i gzugs las nang du'o/[269] / zhes bum pa can byed dgos pa dang dus ji tsam gyi bar du byed pa'i tshad bstan cing / bum pa can byed tshul ni sgrub le'i go sla'i brgya go bzhi pa las/
kha yang btsums te sna yi bug pa gnyi ga dag nas phyi rol dag gi rlung ni ma lus pa/ / srog gi shugs kyis bkug ste dri ma med pa'i glog dang mtshungs pa thur sel rlung dang sbyar byas pa/ / dus kyis goms pa'i sbyor ba dag las zla ba nyi ma me yi dbus su ro ni mnyam par 'gyur/ / lus la zas la sogs pas bkres pa dang ni skom pa 'phrog ste 'chi ba med pa nyid kyang ster/[270] / zhes kha btsums te sna'i bug pa gnyis ka nas phyi rol gyi rlung ma lus pa steng gi srog 'dzin gyi rlung gi shugs kyis bkug ste 'og gi rlung dri ma med pa'i glog rang mdog ser por mtshungs pa thur sel dang lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi dbu ma'i nang du kha sbyar byas pa dus yun ring du goms pa'i sbyor ba dag las zla ba rkyang ma dang nyi ma ro ma la rgyu ba'i rlung gnyis me ste dus me'i rtsa lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi dbu ma'i dbus su ro mnyam par 'gyur ro/ / de ltar bum pa can mthar phyin pa'i gnas skabs kyi phan yon ni bkres pa dang skom pa 'phrog cing 'chi ba med pa nyid kyang ster ba'o/ /

The Great Commentary, on verse 117 of the Gnosis chapter, teaches the need for vase yoga and its duration:
Then, “when form is seen each day, the winds are to be halted” refers to the vase yoga. “Until mandalas of light are seen to encircle the entire body”: these are within and emerging from the forms previously mentioned.[271] The way vase yoga is practiced is taught in verse 194, an “easy to understand” verse of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter:
Mouth too is closed, and from the two nostrils all outer wind is drawn in by the power of prāṇāyāma and joined with pure lightninglike downward wind. From familiarization with the yoga over time, moon and sun are as one in the center of fire. In the body thirst and hunger are destroyed, and freedom from death too is granted.[272] The mouth is closed, and the outer wind is drawn in through the two nostrils by the power of the life-sustaining upper wind. This is joined with the downwardly expelling lower wind, whose color is yellow, like that of pure lightning, in the central channel at the center of the navel cakra. From the practice of this yoga over a long time, the winds that flow in the moon left channel and the sun right channel are as one in the “center of fire,” meaning inside the central channel at the center of the Kālāgni, or navel cakra. The immediate benefits of completing the vase yoga are that thirst and hunger are destroyed and freedom from death is granted.

f.d: de ltar na rgyud tshig 'dis rlung kha sbyor dbu ma'i nang du bsgom pa gsal bar ma bstan snyam du mi bzung ste/ de ltar goms pa'i mthar ro rkyang la rgyu ba'i srog thur gyi rlung dbu ma'i nang du ro mnyam du 'gyur bar gsal por bshad cing / de ltar du 'gyur ba la dbu ma'i nang du srog thur kha sbyar du 'dzin dgos pa'i phyir ro/ /

Therefore do not think that these words from the tantra do not clearly teach that the uniting of the winds is to be meditated upon within the central channel. This verse definitely teaches that when familiarization with this practice has been fully developed, the life and downward winds of the left and right channels are as one inside the central channel, and for that to happen these two winds must be brought together in the central channel.

gzhan yang zin bris las/ 'dus pa phyi ma las/
ye shes lnga yi rang bzhin dbugs/ / 'byung ba lnga yi ngo bo nyid/ / gong bu'i tshul gyis phyung nas ni/ / sna yi rtse mor rab tu brtag[271] / ces gsungs pa'i don bde mchog stod 'grel gyis bshad pas kyang bum pa can gsal bar bstan par mdzad de|_de yang ji ltar mdzad na/ gong bu'i gzugs kyis zhes pa 'gyur kha cig las/ 'dril ba'i gzugs kyis zhes 'byung bas/[272] /zhes 'gyur bcos nas 'chad par mdzad do/ /

Furthermore Notes on Kālacakra quotes a verse from Later Guhyasamāja that says:
Breath, the nature of the five wisdoms, the nature of the five elements, uprooted as a globe-shaped form, meditate at the tip of the nose.[273] Notes on Kālacakra goes on to explain how the commentary on this verse, as found in the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary, clearly teaches vase yoga. /419/ Notes on Kālacakra first corrects the translation — “In some translations ‘globe-shaped form’ is rendered ‘amassed form’”[274] — and then continues with the explanation.

f.d:
de la rgyud tshig de stod 'grel gyis 'chad tshul ni stod 'grel las/
'dir rin chen lnga'i sgras ra sa nA dkyil 'khor lnga'i chos can sa la sogs pa khams lnga po rnams so/ / de'i rang bzhin gyi dbugs ni rin chen lnga'i rang bzhin dbugs te sna bug g.yas pa la'o/ / de bzhin du sangs rgyas lnga'i la la nA da dkyil 'khor lnga'i chos can rnam par shes pa la sogs pa'i phung po lnga po rnams so/ / des byin gyis brlabs pa'i rlung ni sna bug g.yon pa la'o/ / gong bu'i gzugs kyis phyung nas ni zhes pa la 'dir gong bu ni g.yas pa dang cig shos kyi dkyil 'khor rnams kyi srog gi rlung dbu ma A wa d+hU tIr gcig pa nyid do/ / de yang srog gi rlung gong bu'i gzugs kyis phyung nas ni/ sna yi rtse mor rnam bsgom bya zhes pa 'dir sna'i sgras lte ba dang snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral pa dang gtsug tor gyi pad+ma brjod de/ de'i rtse mor bsgom bar bya'o/ / sna yi rtse mor rnam bsgom bya/ / lte ba'i dbus su g.yas pa dang cig shos kyi pad+ma'i 'dab ma gnas pa zhes pa'o/[273] / zhes gsungs pa rnams so/ /

The way that the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary explains this verse from the tantra is as follows:
The term “five jewels” refers to the phenomena of the five rasanā mandalas, which are the five elements of earth and so forth. Breath in the nature of the five elements is of the nature of the five jewels, and is in the right nostril. Likewise the phenomena that are the five lalanā mandalas of the five buddhas are the five aggregates — consciousness and so forth. The winds blessed by these are in the left nostril. “Globe-shaped” in the line “up rooted as a globe-shaped form” means the life winds of the left and right mandalas are as one in the avadhūtī. The life winds are “uprooted as a globe-shaped form, meditate upon the tip of the nose.” The word “nose” here is used to mean the lotuses of the navel, heart, throat, forehead, and crown. Here, to meditate at the tip, as in the line “meditate at the tip of the nose,” refers to the center of the navel at the location of right and other lotus petals.[275]

d.div: [273] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 133_na3
[275] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 133a2.

f.d: de dag gi don cung zad cig bshad na/ rin chen lnga'i sgos bstan pa'i sa chu me rlung nam mkha'i khams te dkyil 'khor lnga'i rang bzhin gyi dbugs rtsa ra sa nA ro ma dang sna bug g.yas par rgyu ba dang / sangs rgyas lnga'i sgras bstan pa'i rnam par shes pa'i phung po sogs phung po lnga'i rang bzhin gyi dbugs rtsa la la nA rkyang ma dang sna bug g.yon pa la so sor rgyu ba'i rlung de rnams a wa d+hU tIr gong bu gcig tu'am/ gcig tu 'dril ba'i gzugs kyis phyung ba ste d+hU tI'i lam nas drangs te sna yi rtse mor rnam bsgom bya ste 'dir sna'i sgras lte ba dang snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral ba dang gtsug tor gyi pad+ma ste rtsa'i 'khor lo brjod de/ rtsa 'khor de'i rtse mor te dbus kyi d+hU tI'i nang du bsgom par bya'o/ /

This passage needs to be explained a little. The term “five jewels” refers to the breath that possesses the nature of the five elements or mandalas of earth, water, fire, air, and space, and that flows through the right rasanā channel and through the right nostril. The term “five buddhas” refers to the breath that possesses the nature of five aggregates of consciousness, and so forth, and that flows through the left lalanā channel and through the left nostril. These winds become as one globe-shaped form or one “amassed form,” which is “uprooted” or “led” through the avadhūtī. “Nose” in the line “meditate at the tip of the nose” is used here to mean the lotuses, or cakras, of the navel, heart, throat, forehead, and crown. The “tip” refers to the central dhūtī of those cakras.

'o na sna'i sgra des bstan pa'i rtsa 'khor la lnga byung ba'i rtsa 'khor gang gi rtse mor bsgom par bya zhe na/ sna yi rtse mor rnam bsgom bya/[274] /zhes pa lte ba'i g.yas dang cig shos g.yon gyi pad+ma'i 'dab ma ste rtsa 'dab gnas ba'i dbus d+hU tI'i nang du bsgom par bya'o/ /zhes pa'i don yin no/ / 'grel tshig de dag gi don de ltar yin pa yang zin bris las/
tshul 'di ni stod 'grel du 'dus pa'i rgyud phyi ma'i lung drangs nas gsal bar bshad de/
ye shes lnga yi rang bzhin dbugs/ / 'byung ba lnga yi ngo bo nyid/ / gong bu'i gzugs kyis phyung nas ni/ / sna yi rtse mor rab tu brtag/ces drangs te/ gong bu'i gzugs kyi+is zhes pa yi 'gyur kha cig las 'dril ba'i gzugs kyis zhes 'byung bas ye shes lnga'i rang bzhin gyi dkyil 'khor lnga'i rlung ro rkyang gnyis la so sor rgyu ba de a wa d+hU tIr gcig tu 'dril ba'i gzugs kyis phyung ba ste d+hU tI'i lam nas drangs te/ sna'i rtse mo zhes pa rtsa 'khor la zer bas skabs 'dir sna'i rtse mo ste lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su rab tu brtag pa ste bsgom mo zhes bstan te/[275] zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ /

The term “nose” refers to the cakras, but at the tips of which cakra is one to meditate? The line “meditate at the tip of the nose” means to meditate within the dhūtī at the center of “the location of the right and other lotus petals,” meaning the right and left channel petals of the navel. /420/ That this is the meaning of the above passage is confirmed by Notes on Kālacakra:
This is clearly explained in the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary, in which a verse from the Later Guhyasamāja is quoted:
“Breath, the nature of five wisdoms, the nature of the five elements, uprooted as a globe-shaped form, meditate at the tip of the nose.” In some translations “globe-shaped form” is rendered “amassed form.” Therefore the five mandala winds, whose natures are the five wisdoms and which flow individually through both channels, become as one amassed form, which is “uprooted” or “led” through the avadhūtī. “Tip of the nose” refers to the cakras, and therefore “tip of the nose” here refers to examining, or meditating, in the center of the navel cakra.[276]

d.div: [274] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 133_na2

f.d:
de bzhin du nA ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel par/ ye shes lnga yi rang bzhin dbugs/[276] /zhes sogs tshigs su bcad pa gcig pu de'i don 'chad pa na 'grel pa de nyid las/
yan lag gsum pa gsungs pa/ ye shes lnga zhes pa la sogs pa ste ye shes lnga ni mi bskyod pa la sogs pa'i sangs rgyas lnga ste la la nA dkyil 'khor lnga'i chos can rnam par shes pa la sogs pa'i phung po lnga rnams so/ / de'i rang bzhin dbugs ni sna bug g.yon pa la'o/ / 'dir byung ba lnga'i sgras ra sa nA dkyil 'khor lnga'i chos can sa la sogs pa'i khams lnga rnams te de'i rang bzhin dbugs 'byung ba lnga'i rang bzhin can ni sna bug g.yas pa la'o/ / gong bu'i gzugs kyis phyung nas ni zhes pa la|_'dir gong bu ni g.yas pa dang g.yon pa'i dkyil 'khor rnams kyi srog gi rlung dbu ma a wa d+hU tIr gcig pa nyid de srog rlung de yang gong bu'i gzugs kyis phyung nas sna'i rtse mor zhes pa sna'i sgras lte ba dang snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral ba dang gtsug tor gyi pad+ma'i lte ba brjod de/ srog gi rlung de phyung nas sna'i rtse mo der brtag par bya ba ni bsgom par bya ba ste lte ba nas lte ba'i dbus su yin gyi g.yas dang g.yon du pad+ma'i 'dab ma la ma yin no/[277] / zhes gsal bar gsungs so/ /

Similarly Nāropa in his Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations, when explaining the meaning of just this one verse, which begins “Breath, the nature of five wisdoms,” says very clearly:
This talks of the third branch. The five wisdoms from the line “Breath, the nature of five wisdoms” are the five buddhas, Akṣobhya and so forth, referring to the five aggregates of consciousness and so forth, which are phenomena of the lalanā mandalas. Breath, which is of their nature, is in the left nostril. Here the term “five elements” refers to the element of earth and so forth, phenomena of the rasanā mandalas. Breath, which is of their nature, is in the right nostril. “Globe-shaped,” from the line “uprooted as a globe-shaped form,” refers to the life winds of the right and left mandalas together as one in the avadhūtī. That wind is “uprooted as a globe-shaped form,” and the “nose” of the phrase “tip of the nose” refers to the centers of the navel, heart, throat, forehead, and crown lotuses. Having uprooted the winds, “meditate at the tip of the nose” refers to the meditation, which is in the center of the navel but not on the left and right lotus petals.[277]

d.div: [276] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na244_ba7_nas 245_na6
[277] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 246_ba3
[277] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 244b7–246b3.

f.d: 'grel tshig 'di rnams kyi don gzhan rnams stod 'grel dang 'dra ba la sna'i sgras lte ba dang snying ga dang zhes pa nas/ lte ba nas lte ba'i dbus su yin gyi g.yas dang g.yon du pad+ma'i 'dab ma la ma yin no zhes pa'i bar gyi don ni/ sna'i sgras zhes pa nas/ gtsug tor gyi pad+ma'i lte bar brjod de zhes pa'i bar gyis sna'i rtse mor zhes pa'i sna rtse ngos bzung nas/ srog gi rlung steng gi srog 'dzin ro rkyang la rgyu ba rnams d+hU tI'i las gcig bu nyid nas phyung ste drangs nas sna'i rtse mo lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi d+hU tI'i nang der brtag par bya ba ste bsgom par bya'o/ / de yang ji ltar du drang snyam na/ sna bug nas d+hU tI'i lam gcig pu nyid nas drangs te gtsug tor gyi pad+ma'i lte ba nas dpral ba mgrin pa snying ga lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi pad+ma'i lte ba'i bar gyi d+hU tI'i dbus su 'dren pa yin gyi/ rtsa 'khor rnams kyi g.yas dang g.yon du pad+ma_'i 'dab ma ste rtsa 'dab rnams dang ro rkyang la rlung 'dren pa ni ma yin no/ /zhes pa'o/ / de ltar na d+hU tIr dmigs pa'i bum pa can dgos pa'i lung don rags pa bshad nas

The meaning of most of this passage is similar to that expressed by the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary passage. The meaning of the lines from “the nose of the phrase,” /421/ up to “which is in the center of the navel but not on the left and right lotus petals” is that the first part, from “the nose” up to “crown lotuses,” identifies the nose of the phrase “tip of the nose.” The “winds,” or life-sustaining upper winds, that flow through the left and right channels are “uprooted,” or led, solely through the pathway of the dhūtī and meditated upon in the dhūtī in the center of the “tip of the nose,” or navel cakra. From where are the winds led? From the nostrils, down through the dhūtī, to the center of the crown-channel lotus, through the forehead, throat, and heart lotuses and as far as the dhūtī at the center of the lotus of the navel cakra. The winds are not led through the “left and right lotus petals” and left and right channels. This rough explanation of the scriptural description of the purpose of vase yoga focused on the dhūtī leads to the second outline:
gnyis pa dmigs pa sgom tshul nyid bshad pa

d.i: The actual focus and method of the meditation

f.d: ['di ]la bzhi/ steng 'og gi rlung 'then pa'i go rim dang / rlung lam gang nas 'then pa dang / then nas gnas gang du kha sbyar bya ba la sems ji ltar gtong ba'i tshul dang / sgom pa'i thun gyi yun tshad bstan pa'o/ /

This is under four headings: 1. The order of drawing the upper and lower winds 2. The pathways from where winds are drawn 3. Mental placement on the winds drawn and brought together 4. Duration of meditation
dang po [steng 'og gi rlung 'then pa'i go rim ]ni

d.i: The order of drawing the upper and lower winds

f.d: zin bris las/ gzhi dus su srog 'dzin steng gi sna sgo nas phyir 'byung ba na thur sel 'og sgo nas phyir 'byung la/ srog 'dzin nang du 'jug pa na thur sel nang du zhugs nas lte ba'i bar du 'ong bas rtog pa gcing pos [278] dus gcig tu kha sbyor byed nus pa srid kyang [279] zhes gsungs shing rim lnga gdan rdzogs las steng 'og gi rlung gnyis 'gros 'ded du yang [280] gsungs pas gang ltar na'ang rim can du 'then par bya ste/ de yang bsgom pa'i gnas dang lus gnad dang lta stangs rnams rdor bzlas kyi skabs bzhin du byas te/ rlung 'then pa'i tshe byang sems 'dzag pa srung ba'i man ngag med na ni srog 'dzin steng rlung nges par sngon du 'then dgos te/ thur sel 'og rlung sngon la 'then na byang sems 'dzag pa'i dgag bya yod pas so/ / byang sems 'dzag pa srung ba'i man ngag yod na ni thur sel sngon la 'then kyang chog par gsungs so/ /

Notes on Kālacakra says:
Ordinarily, when life-sustaining wind leaves from the upper opening, downwardly expelling wind leaves from the lower opening. When life-sustaining wind enters, downwardly expelling wind enters and reaches as far as the navel. Therefore it is possible to bring them together and bind them simultaneously.[278] However, in the Guhyasamāja Completion Stage,[279] it says that the upper and lower winds are drawn one after the other. Whatever the case, here they are to be drawn one after the other. The place of meditation, posture, and position of eyes are arranged as they were in vajra recitation. When drawing in the winds, the upper, life-sustaining wind must be drawn in first if you do not have the instructions for preventing the emission of bodhicitta. If you draw in the lower, downwardly expelling wind first, there is a danger of bodhicitta emission, which must be avoided. If you have the instruction on the prevention of bodhicitta emission, it is taught that drawing in the lower wind first is acceptable.

d.div: [278] rje'i gsung 'bum du rtog pa byang na dus gcig tu zhes byung bas dpyad/
[279] rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum pod/ da_sbyor drug gi rdzogs rim gyi gnad bsdus pa/ 16_na4
[280] ma dper rim lnga gden rdzogs zhes gsal yang 'dir bcos yod/ rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum pod/ nya
