[279] Jé Tsongkhapa, Collected Works, vol. nya.

f.d: gnyis pa rlung lam gang nas 'then pa ni/

d.i: The pathways from where winds are drawn

f.d: steng rlung srog 'dzin ni kha btsums te steng len nam 'og len nam yo ga ma'i sbyor ba gang yang rung bas sna gnyis nas dal bus drangs te d+hU tI'i nang na mar nar te song ste lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi d+hU tI'i nang du phyin nas der gnas pa la dmigs te rlung steng du mi 'phyug par ji ltar te bsnan no/ / de'i rjes su 'og sgo gnyis nas 'og rlung thur sel d+hU tI'i nang na yar gyen du 'then nas lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i d+hU tA'i nang du phyin te der gnas pa la dmigs nas rlung gnyis steng 'og tu mi 'phyug par gzung bar bya'o/ /

For the upper, life-sustaining wind, the mouth is closed, /422/ and with one of the yogas of “taking from above,” “taking from below,” or yogama, the wind is slowly drawn through both nostrils and pulled down the dhūtī until it reaches the center of the navel cakra. There it is focused on and added to without allowing it to stray upward. After that the lower, downwardly expelling wind is drawn up through the dhūtī from the two lower orifices to the center of the navel cakra, where it is to be focused upon. Both winds are held and added to without being allowed to stray up or down.
gsum pa 'thon nas gnas gang du kha sbyor bya ba ni/

d.i: Mental placement on the winds drawn and brought together

f.d:
steng 'og gi rlung srog thur gnyis d+hU tI'i lam nas lte ba'i bar du then pa de d+hU tI la ro rkyang gi mdud pas bcings pa'i lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus a wa d+hU tI'i nang du rlung gnyis kha sbyor du byas te kha sbyar gyi rlung de nyid la dmigs nas sems rtse gcig tu 'jog pa'o/ / bum pa can gyi skabs 'dir yang rlung nyid la dmigs dgos pa ni bgegs mthar byed pa'i lta ba zhes sogs kyis srog rtsol bgegs mthar byed kyi lta bas bsgom par yang bshad la/ nges don gyi bgegs mthar byed dam bdud rtsi 'khyil ba ni rlung la gsungs te/ stod 'grel las/
de nas bdud rtsi 'khyil pa'i gzugs brnyan gyi ming can dgongs pa'i skad gzhan gyis rlung gsungs so/[281] / zhes gsungs pas so/ / de yang skabs 'di'i srog rtsol bum pa can sgom pa ni rdor bzlas mthar phyin nas sgom pa yin la/ rdor bzlas mthar phyin pa'i tshad ni rdo rje'i bzlas pa'i dmigs pa bskyangs pa tsam gyis rlung ro rkyang la rgyu ba 'gags nas dbu mar rtag tu 'bab cing de la brten nas rlung dbu mar tshud pa'i rtags kyi stong gzugs rnams go rim ma 'chol bar nges par can du 'char ba yin no/ /

The life-sustaining upper wind and downwardly expelling lower winds are drawn through the dhūtī as far as the navel. This unites the two winds inside the dhūtī at the center of the navel cakra, where the dhūtī is constricted by the knots of the right and left channels. These united winds are then the focus of a single-pointed placement of mind. The purpose of focusing on the winds themselves in vase yoga is found in the quote beginning “The look of Vighnantaka,” which explains that prāṇāyāma is practiced with the look of Vighnantaka. The definitive Vighnantaka, or amṛtavarta, is said to be the winds. The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
“The images of amṛtavarta” refers to the winds using provisional language.[280] The prāṇāyāma vase yoga taught here is performed after vajra recitation, and the measure of vajra recitation completion is that just by focusing on the vajra recitation objects of meditation, the winds are stopped from flowing in the left and right channels and move constantly within the central channel. Because of this, empty-form signs of the winds having entered the central channel will appear without fail and in the correct order.

d.div: [281] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 133_na1
[280] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 133a1.

f.d:
de ltar rdor bzlas mthar phyin pa'i rjes su bum pa can sgom pa la 'jug pa'i tshe dang por rdor bzlas cung zad cig byas te rlung dbu mar btsud/ de nas steng rlung dal bus dbu ma na mar la 'dren pa yin te/ rgyud las/
kha yang btsums te sna yi bug pa gnyi ga dag nas phyi rol dag gi rlung ni ma lus pa/ / srog gi shugs kyis bkug ste [282] zhes phyi rol gyi rlung bkug ste sna bug gnyis ka nas 'jug par bshad la/ rlung sna bug gnyis ka nas 'jug na dbu ma nas 'jug pa nges pa can yin zhing / bum pa can la dang por 'jug pa'i tshe rlung dbu ma nas 'jug pa la de'i tshe sngon du rdor bzlas lta bus rlung dbu mar bcug pa zhig dgos pa'i phyir ro/ /

When vajra recitation has been mastered and the yogi begins to engage in the practice of vase yoga, a little vajra recitation is first performed to bring the winds into the central channel, after which the upper wind is slowly led down through the central channel. The reason for this is that the tantra states that external wind is drawn in and moves through the nostrils:
Mouth too is closed, and from the two nostrils all outer wind is drawn in by the power of prāṇāyāma.[281] If wind enters through the nostrils, it has to then move through the central channel and in order for the winds to move through the central channel, the first moments of vase yoga must be preceded /423/ by a vajra recitation that brings the winds to the central channel.

d.div: [282] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka194_97_ba1_tshig sna cung mi mthun/
[281] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 194, 97b1.

f.d: de ltar na lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i d+hU tI'i nang du steng 'og gi rlung kha sbyar du gnas pa la sems rtse gcig tu gtad nas bzhug pas rlung sems gang du gnas pa'i lte ba'i d+hU tI'i nang der blos ma btags par stong gzugs dus kyis 'khor lo'i rnam pa can rang dbang du 'char bas steng nas drangs pa'i rlung sems stong gzugs rnams dbyer med du byas pa de dang gcig tu 'dres par mos pa byed don med do/ / des na bsam gtan gyi skabs nas gnyug ma 'od gsal gyi sems dang stong gzugs khyad par can gnyis yul yul can tha dad kyi snang ba nub nas dbyer med par snang ba'i stobs kyis stong gzugs khyad par can dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum gyi rnam par snang ba la nga rgyal 'pho nus pa ltar srog rtsol yan chad kyi skabs thams cad du rlung sems gang du gtad pa'i dbu ma'i nang der rlung sems tshud pa'i stobs kyis stong gzugs khyad par ba shar res kyi de la nga rgyal bcos min du 'pho nus te/ rgyu khyad par can bskyed rim gyi skabs kyi gtso bo la nga rgyal bcos min 'pho nus pa sngon du song ba dang / bsam gtan gyi skabs su bshad pa bzhin sngon du song bas so/ / bum pa can 'dir bshad pa rnams ni rgyud kyi ched du bya ba'i gdul bya rin po che lta bu'i gang zag gis bskyed rdzogs kyi lam snga ma rnams sngon du song ba'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi lam snga ma sngon du ma song ba'i las dang po pa'i bum pa can sgom tshul ni bla ma rnams gyi 'khrid yig las shes par bya'o/ /

The mind is single-pointedly placed upon the upper and lower winds brought together inside the dhūtī at the center of the navel cakra. Wherever the mind and winds dwell within the dhūtī at the navel, there an empty-form Kālacakra will appear by its own volition unconceived by the mind. Therefore any practice that involves drawing down mind and winds, indivisibly united, in order to merge them with this Kālacakra empty form makes no sense. From the branch of meditative absorption onward, the appearances of the primordial clear-light mind and its special empty forms are no longer separate subjects and objects and appear indivisibly as one, thereby enabling self-pride to be assigned to the special empty-form Kālacakra in mother-and-father embrace. Similarly, in all instances from prāṇāyāma onward, wherever mind and winds are focused within the central channel, there mind and winds will enter, thereby enabling a natural, uncontrived self-pride to be assigned to each of the special empty forms that arise there. The special causes of this are the ability to place a natural uncontrived self-pride in the main deity developed during generation-stage practices and similar concentration practices developed in the branch of meditative absorption. The teachings here on vase yoga are for the special disciples of the tantra, those “jewellike persons” who have undertaken all preceding practices of the generation and completion stages. Beginners in vase yoga who have not accomplished these previous practices should learn vase yoga methods from the teachings of the gurus.
bzhi pa sgom pa'i thun gyi yun tshad bstan pa ni/[283]

d.div: [283] ma dper sa bcad 'di lnga par drangs 'dug kyang yig nor yin te gong du bzhi las ma snang ngo /

f.d: de ltar na rlung kha sbyor du bzung nas bsgoms pas mgo bo na ba dang lus la 'od skar mthong ba dang snying rdeb pa la sogs pa mi 'byung gi bar du bsgom zhing / mgo bo na ba sogs byung nas kyang bsgoms na 'chi ba la sogs pa'i nyes dmigs yod do/ / 'o na de lta bu'i rkyen gyis shi ba'i tshe cir 'gyur snyam na/ de yang de lta bu'i rkyen gyis 'chi ba byung na rnal 'byor pa des stong pa nyid kyi gzugs la rtse gcig tu gzhag par bya ste de ltar bzhag na bde ba chen po'i gnas sngon du byed par gyur ro/ / de lta yin pa 'on kyang rnal 'byor pa de lam bsgoms pas shi'o zhes pa'i grags pa ngan pa mi 'byung ba'i phyir du'o/ /

Meditation on the winds held together should continue until the head begins to hurt, until the yogi sees his body encircled by light, or until the heart starts to jump. If meditation continues after these signs appear, there is a danger of death. If one dies under these circumstances, what happens? If death occurs, the yogi should place concentration one-pointedly on the empty forms, and by doing so he will actualize a realm of great bliss. This is what will actually occur. However the previous advice is given to avoid gaining the bad reputation of being a yogi who meditates on the path and then dies. /424/

de ltar yang sgrub le'i brgya nyer gcig pa las/
srog rtsol dag ni kun nas bde mnyam 'bras bu ster ba ji srid mgo yi bar du 'dod pa ste/ / de yis steng du 'dod pa min pa 'chi ba'i 'jigs pa byed de phung po nges par 'jig pa'i rgyu/ / gtsug tor sgo na phug nas 'gro na mchog gi bde ba'i go 'phang dag la nges par sbyar bar bya/ / phung po med kyang rnal 'byor pa ni bde mnyam 'jug ste 'on kyang 'jig rten du ni grags pa min/[284] / zhes pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dir stong pa nyid kyi gzugs mthong bar gyur pa na rnal 'byor pas srog rtsol bya ba gang yin pa de ni ji srid mgo yi bar du zhes pa mgo bo na bar mi byed kyi bar du'o/ / de yang bde mnyam 'bras bu ster bar 'gyur ro/ / de las steng du zhes pa ni mgo bo na ba'i mthu las 'dod pa min pa 'chi ba'i 'jigs pa byed par 'gyur te phung po rnam par nyams pa'i rgyur 'gyur ro/ / ci ste rnal 'byor gyi stobs kyis gtsug tor phug nas srog 'gro na rnal 'byor pas mchog gi bde ba'i go 'phang dag la zhes pa stong pa nyid kyi gzugs la nges par sbyar bar bya ste nges par ni mtha' gcig tu'o/[285] / zhes dang /
'on kyang 'jig rten du ni grags pa min pa rnal 'byor pa 'di shi'o zhes pa ste srog rtsol gyi nges pa'o/ / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

Verse 121 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter says:
Prāṇāyāma grants fruits of complete equalized bliss, desirable for as long as the head is. Beyond that it produces the undesirable, the fear of death, cause of definite destruction of aggregates. To leave through the opening at the crown without doubt joins one to a place of great bliss. Without aggregates, the yogi finds blissful peace, but he has no reputation in the world.[282] On this verse the Great Commentary says:
When he sees the empty forms, the yogi performs prāṇāyāma “for as long as the head is,” which means until the head begins to hurt. This will grant the fruits of equalized bliss. “Beyond that” means that going beyond the bounds of a painful head will produce “the undesirable, the fear of death,” a cause of the loss of the aggregates. If, by the power of yoga, the prāṇāyāma moves through the opening at the crown, the yogi is joined “to a place of great bliss,” meaning to the empty forms. “Without doubt” means definitely. And further:
“But he has no reputation in the world” means a reputation that “this yogi has died.”[283]

d.div: [284] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka121_90_na3
[285] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 239_na4
[282] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 121, 90a3.
[283] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 239a4.

f.d: lnga pa de ltar bsgoms pas nyams rtags skye ba'i tshul ni

'grel chen las/
lte bar srog dang thur sel gyi rlung dag yang dag par phrad pa'i dbus su [286] zhes pa nas/
kyang gi sgras lte ba de nyid la'o/ /zhes pa'i don gong du bshad pa ltar lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i d+hU tI'i nang du srog thur 'dres pa'i dbus su mig sogs kyi rnam par shes pa drug gi bzhon pa'i rlung tshud pa'i stobs kyis gzugs sogs yul drug dang yul yul can gyi 'brel pa chad pa'i sgo nas du ba la sogs pa'i mtshan ma rnams go rim sogs cung zad kyang ma 'chol ba'i nges pa can rnams dang / khyad par du yang re khA nag po skra'i tshad tsam gyi dbus su du ma longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam pa can la nga rgyal 'phos pa'i tshul gyis srog thur 'dres pa'i dbus der gsal bar snang ba dang / de yang srog thur 'dres pa'i stobs kyis lte ba'i gtum mo 'bar te khams byang chub kyi sems zhu nas babs pa rdo rje nor bu'i rtse nas ma 'phos pa'i yas babs kyi dga' bzhi dang / byang chub kyi sems dpral ba'i bar du 'phel ba'i mas brtan gyi dga' ba bzhi drangs nas de lta bu'i bde ba chen po de rnam bcas rnam med kyi stong pa nyid dang sbyar nas sgom pa rnams nyams rtags kyi gtso bo yin zhing rtsa dang rlung gi kha dog mthong ba sogs ni nyams rtags phal pa yin no/ /

The Great Commentary says:
“In the center of the two winds meeting” means in the center at the navel, where the life wind and downward wind meet. “The arising and engaging in the objects by object-engagers” such as eyes and so forth at the navel is a topic that has been discussed previously. The word “object” is a without a grammatical case. “Apprehending the signs of smoke and so forth, also” is by way of the avadhūtī.
The word “also” refers again to the navel.[284] This passage, as previously explained, teaches that the life and downward winds are merged within the dhūtī at the center of the navel cakra. The winds that are the mounts of the six consciousnesses enter this union, resulting in the severing of the six types of objects, form and so forth, from their object-engaging consciousnesses. This in turn produces a definite and ordered sequence of signs, such as smoke and so forth, and particularly the appearance of many saṃbhogakāya forms in the aspect of Kālacakra mother-and-father embrace within a hair-sized black line to which self-pride is assigned. This appears clearly in the midst of this union of life and downward winds. Furthermore this union of life and downward winds ignites the caṇḍālī fire at the navel. This melts the bodhicitta element, which then falls, /425/ and without emerging from the tip of the jewel, induces the four joys of descent and the four joys of stable ascent, in which the bodhicitta increases to reach to the forehead cakra. This great bliss is applied to aspected and nonaspected emptiness. These meditations are the primary signs of accomplishment, while seeing the colors of the channels and their winds are common signs.

d.div: [286] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 390_ba4
[284] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 390b4.

f.d:
'o na bum pa can mthar phyin pa nyid kyis mas brtan gyi dga' bzhi ji ltar 'dren nus snyam na/ 'di ni 'grel chen las/
de nas gzugs ni mthong bar 'gyur nazhes pa nas/
sngar brjod pa'i gzugs las nang du'o/[287] / zhes pa'i bar gyis srog rtsol bum pa can byed pa dang de mthar phyin pa'i tshad bstan nas/ de'i 'jug nyid du
de nas zla ba drug gis sdom brtson te las dang po ba'i tshangs par spyod pa rnams la reg bya dman pa dbang po gnyis kyi 'khrig pa dang bral ba'i bde ba mnyam pa ste mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba lam gyi sems zhes pa stong pa nyid kyi gzugs kyi sems su 'gyur ro/ / zhes gsungs pa 'dis rgyud kyi ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo rin po che lta bu'i gang zag des bum pa can mthar phyin pa de nas 'dzin pa dang rjes dran gyi lam la 'bad pas zla ba drug rdzogs pa'i 'tshams su las dang po ba'i tshe yang byang sems nyams ma myong ba'i tshangs par spyod pa dang ldan pa rnams la reg byas dman pa dbang po gnyis kyi 'khrig pa la chags pa dang bral ba'i bde ba mnyam pa ste mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba lam gyi byang sems stong pa nyid kyi gzugs dang ngo bo dbyer med pa'i sems thob par 'gyur ro zhes bstan to/ / mdor na bum pa can mthar phyin pa'i rin po che lta bu'i gang zag des zla ba drug gi bar du lam la 'bad na ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag 'thob ces pa'i don yin no/ /

How does the completion of vase yoga induce the four joys of descent? The Great Commentary says:
Then, “when form is seen each day, the winds are to be halted” refers to the vase yoga.
“Until mandalas of light are seen to encircle the entire body”: these are within and from the forms previously mentioned. This passage teaches the activity and measure of completion of prāṇāyāma vase yoga. The text continues:
Then, devoid of the inferior sensation of the union of the two organs, “in six months, the meditator who is a beginner in brahmacarya conduct, enters the path of the mind” or mind of empty form “of equalized bliss,” meaning unchanging bliss.[285] The passage teaches that the jewellike persons or primary disciples of this tantra accomplish vase yoga and then strive in the paths of retention and recollection. After six months, even if they are at the stage of a beginner, those of brahmacarya conduct, meaning those who have not experienced the loss of bodhicitta, will come to the path of the mind of equalized or unchanging bliss that is devoid of desire for the inferior sensation of the coupling of the two organs. This path of the mind is an attainment in which mind and the empty forms are indivisible. In short this passage is saying that if jewellike disciples who have completed vase yoga strive on the path for six months, they will achieve the branch of meditative concentration.

d.div: [287] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 389_na5
[285] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 389a5.

f.d: yang gzugs kyi sems su 'gyur ro zhes pa'i mjug nyid du/ de nas skad cig gcig gis mngon par rdzogs par byang chub pa'i zhes pa nas/ gtsug tor du srog thams cad zad pas sa bcu gnyis so zhes pa'i bar gyis mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya'i grangs 'phel tshul dang / des rtsa 'khor drug tu las rlung rnams sad des bcu gnyis 'thob tshul bstan/ de'i mjug tu/ de'i phyir oD+Da 'bar ba'i bar te zhes pa nas/ de'i 'phel ba ste steng du 'gro bar rab tu bya'o zhes pa'i bar gyis bum pa can nas rjes dran gyi bar gyi yas babs mas brtan gyi dga' ba bzhi skyed tshul bstan/

The continuation of the above passage, from “Next, full and perfect enlightenment by single instances” up to “at the crown all winds are ended. This is the twelfth,”[286] teaches how the instances of bliss increase to 21,600 and how these are responsible for “killing” the winds of karma at the six cakras, resulting in the attainment of the twelve levels. The continuation of the passage, from “Therefore, until the blazing of oḍa”[287] until “bliss will increase,” /426/ teaches the development of the four joys in descent and ascent that occurs from the practice of vase yoga up to recollection.

d.div: [286] This passage is quoted and explained in the chapter on the sixth yoga, meditative concentration.
[287] As transliterated in Tibetan; presumably a synonym for caṇḍālī fire, but might be a corruption of iḍa, an epithet of Agni, the god of fire.

f.d:
'o na gtum mo 'bar bas byang sems zhu ba las yas babs 'ong du chug mod mas brtan ji ltar 'ong snyam na/ steng du 'gro bar rab tu bya'o zhes pa'i mjug de nyid du/
bla ma'i nges pa'i dbang gis zhes pa sngar gsungs pa'i srog 'gog pa las dpral ba'i bar du 'phel bar 'gyur te 'di la ngo mtshar med do/ / zhes sngar gsungs pa'i srog rtsol gyis srog 'gog pa sngon du song ba las khams byang chub kyi sems gsang gnas nas dpral pa'i bar du 'phel bar 'gyur ba'i mas brtan 'byung ba 'di la ngo mtshar med do/ / de'i rgyu mtshan ni srog dbu mar 'gog pa las byang sems yas 'dren nus pa de rten 'brel gyi chos nyid yin pa'i phyir ro zhes pa'i don no/ /

It is clear that the blazing of the caṇḍālī fire melts the bodhicitta and induces the descent, but how is the ascent brought about? After “bliss will increase” the passage continues:
“By the certainties of the gurus” means that from the previously taught halting of the winds comes an increase as far as the forehead and that “this is no surprise.” This means that it should come as no surprise that from the prior practice of the prāṇāyāma halting of the winds comes the stable ascent, wherein the bodhicitta increases from the secret place to the forehead. The reason for this is that the ability to draw up the bodhicitta is dependent upon the winds being “halted” in the central channel.
bzhi pa ma grub na sbogs pa'i cho ga ni

sgrub le'i brgya bcu dgu pa las/
so sor sdud pa la sogs rnams kyis gal te sdags pa rnams kyi 'dod pa grub par ma gyur na/ nA da goms pas btsan thabs chu skyes su gnas rdo rje nor bur thig le bkag nas bsgrub par bya/[288] / zhes pa'i 'grel chen las/
da ni btsan thabs kyi rnal 'byor gsungs te 'dir gang gi tshe so sor sdud pa la sogs pas gzugs mthong bar gyur pa la srog ma bcings pa nyid kyis 'gyur ba med pa'i skad cig ma ma skyes na de'i tshe nA da goms pa 'chad par 'gyur bas btsan thabs su dbu mar 'bab par byas nas shes rab kyi chu skyes su gnas pa'i byang chub sems kyi thig le rdo rje nor bur bkag nas mi g.yo bas 'gyur pa med pa'i skad cig bsgrub par bya'o zhes pa ni btsan thabs kyi rnal 'byor ro/[289] / zhes gsungs pa 'dis sor sdud kyi skabs kyi dmigs pa bsgoms pas ma nges pa'i du sogs kyi stong gzugs mthong bar gyur kyang srog rlung dbu mar ma bcings pa nyid kyis byang sems rdo rje nor bu'i bug pa nas 'gyur ba ste 'dzag pa med pa'i bde ba'i skad cig ma ma skyes na de'i tshe nA da goms pa sgrub le'i go sla'i brgya go drug pa/ nus ma gang zhig ces sogs kyis 'chad par 'gyur ba'i drag po btsan thabs kyi sbyor bas dbu mar rlung 'bab par byas nas las kyi phyag rgya la brten pa'i tshe shes rab ma'i chu skyes pad+mar gnas pa'i rnal 'byor pa rang gi rdo rje nor bu'i nang gi rlung dbu mar tshud pa de'i stobs kyis bkaka nas byang sems phyir mi g.yo bas 'gyur ba med pa ste 'dzag med kyi bde ba'i skad cig bsgrub par bya'o/[290] /zhes bstan pas bsgoms stobs kyis rlung dbu mar tshud pa yin phyin chad rlung stobs kyis byang sems 'dzag med du 'ching nus par nges pas sor sdud nas kyang rlung stobs kyis lhan skyes kyi bde chen 'dren nus so/ /

Verse 119 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter says:
If by withdrawal and so forth, the wishes of the mantra practitioner are not met, perform nāda meditation by wrathful means, and they will be accomplished by blocking the drop in the vajra jewel within the lotus.[288] On this the Great Commentary says:
Now wrathful yoga is taught. During withdrawal and so forth, when forms are seen but instances of the unchanging have not been generated, because the winds have not been bound, at that time meditate on the nāda, which will be explained, and by wrathful means bring the winds to the central channel. The bodhicitta drops in the lotus of wisdom are halted within the vajra jewel and are unmoving. By this is accomplished an instance of the unchanging. This is the wrathful yoga.[289] This passage means that by the meditations of withdrawal, nondefinitive signs of smoke and so forth are seen, but the winds have not been bound in the central channel. Therefore an instance of the bliss that arises from the bodhicitta “unchanging,” which means not falling from the opening of the vajra jewel, has not been generated. /427/ When this happens, meditate on the nāda as it is explained in verse 196 of the “easy to understand” verses of the Method of Accomplishment chapter, beginning with the words “The śakti.” With this wrathful yoga the winds are brought to the central channel, and when the yogi relies upon an activity mudrā consort, the winds within the yogi’s vajra jewel, which is placed within the lotus of the wisdom consort, are halted by the force of being brought to the central channel. The bodhicitta does not move outside, and an instance of the unchanging or nonfalling bliss is created. Therefore, once the winds have been moved into the central channel by the power of meditation, the yogi possesses the certainty of being able to hold the bodhicitta from emission by the power of the winds, and it becomes possible to induce the innate bliss through the power of the winds even from the branch of withdrawal.

d.div: [288] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka119_90_na1
[289] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 238_na6
[290] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka196_97_ba4
[288] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 119, 90a1.
[289] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 238a6.

f.d: des na 'dir 'gyur ba med pa'i skad cig ma zhes gsungs pa rnams kyang byang sems phyi rol du 'dzag pa bkag nas rdo rje nor bu'i rtser 'dzag med du bcings pa las skyes pa'i bde ba la zer ba yin gyi mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba mtshan nyid pa mi+in te|_rdo rje nor bur thig le bkag nas bsgrub par bya/ /zhes gsungs pa 'dis shes pas so/ /

Therefore the phrase “instance of the unchanging” mentioned in the passage above is used to describe the bliss that arises from the bodhicitta being held at the tip of the jewel and prevented from falling, but it is not the definitive unchanging bliss. This can be understood from the lines “accomplished by blocking the drop in the vajra jewel” in the above verse.
des na sbogs chog 'di la gsum/ dus nam gyi tshe byed pa/ byed pa'i tshul dngos/ des rlung bcings nas bde ba skyed tshul lo/ /
The enhancement ritual can be dealt with under three headings: 1. When to perform it 2. The actual ritual 3. The creation of bliss from binding the winds
dang po [dus nam gyi tshe byed pa ]ni

sor sdud dang srog rtsol bsgoms pas stong gzugs du ma mthong yang rlung dbu mar tshud pa'i rtags ma byung na 'di byed pa yin te 'di byas pas rlung dbu mar tshud par 'gyur ro/ / de yang srog dbu mar ma tshud pa tshud pa'i phyir du byed pa yin te/ srog dbu mar ma chings pas bde ba ma skyes na btsan thabs su de rlung dbu mar 'bab par byas nas bde ba bskyed par gsungs pa'i phyir ro/ / des na sor sdud bsgoms pas rlung dbu mar 'dzud ma nus pa'i dus dang / sor sdud kyi sogs khongs nas gtso bor srog rtsol bton te srog rtsol bsgoms pas kyang rlung dbu mar 'dzud ma nus pa'i dus dang dus gnyis po der bya'o/ / de yang sor sdud kyis rlung dbu mar tshud nas srog rtsol bsgoms pa yin na ni srog rtsol gyis rlung dbu mar mi tshud mi srid pas sor sdud kyis rlung dbu mar ma tshud par srog rtsol sgom pa cig gi dbang du byas pa yin no/ /

If the meditations of withdrawal and prāṇāyāma have produced many visible empty forms but there are no signs of the winds having entered the central channel, this enhancement ritual is to be performed because its enactment will bring the winds into the central channel. Moreover this ritual is specifically designed to bring winds into the central channel, because the tantra teaches that if bliss is not developed due to the winds not being bound in the central channel, wrathful means are employed to bring that about. Therefore there are two occasions when this ritual is to be performed. One is when the meditations of withdrawal are unable to bring the winds into the central channel. The other is when the meditations of prāṇāyāma, as indicated by the words “and so forth,” are also unable to bring the winds to the central channel. If withdrawal has brought the winds into the central channel, it is impossible for the winds not to be brought into the central channel during prāṇāyāma. Therefore prāṇāyāma enhancement is necessary when the winds have not entered the central channel during withdrawal.

'o na btsan thabs kyi sbyor ba 'dis rlung dbu mar 'dzud na dang po nas 'di byas pas chog gam snyam na/ de yang dang por sor sdud dang srog rtsol gyi sbyor ba 'jam po'i sgo nas yun ring du bsgoms kyang ma grub na de'i tshe byed pa yin gyi/ /dang po nas drag po'i btsan thabs kyi sbyor ba byas na rlung dbu mar 'dzud mi nus kyi steng du gegs chen po skyed pas dang po nas byed du mi rung ngo / / sor sdud lta bu yun ring du bsgoms pa'i rjes su ni rlung shin tu las rung du song nas de'i rjes su btsan thabs kyi sbyor ba byas kyang gegs chen po skyed pa min no/ /

If this wrathful yoga brings the winds into the central channel, /428/ then isn’t it acceptable to perform it at the very outset of practice? If the yogas of withdrawal and prāṇāyāma are first performed gently and over a long time but do not produce results, then this ritual is to be performed. However, if forceful methods are used from the beginning, not only will the yogi not be able to bring the winds to the central channel, but many obstructions will be created. Therefore such a practice is unsuitable at the outset. Practicing a meditation such as withdrawal over a long time makes the winds very pliant, and even if wrathful methods are employed at that time, no obstruction will be created.
gnyis pa byed pa'i tshul dngos ni

sgrub le'i go sla'i brgya go drug pa las/
nus ma gang zhig lte ba'i dbus nas gzhan gyi gnas su bcu gnyis mtha' dang cha yi mthar 'gro ba/ / de ni lte bar 'gog pa dang bcas dri med glog dang mtshungs pa dbyug pa'i gzugs can langs pa yang / / 'khor lo las ni 'khor lo'i bar du nges par dman zhing rol pa'i 'gros pas dbu ma'i rtsa la bskyod/ / ji srid gtsug tor bug par btsan thabs nyid kyis phyi rol gyi ni pags pa dag la khab bzhin reg[291] / ces gsungs pa 'dis bstan te/ 'di'i don cung zad cig bshad na/ nA da zhes pa bsgyur na sgra tsam zhes pa yin pas sgra tsam goms pa zhes pa'i sgra ni hUM gi sgra'o/ / de goms pa ste sgom pa'i tshul ni rkang pa rdo rje'i skyil krung bca'/ lag pa gnyis rdo rje'i khu tshur snying gar bsnol/ mgo yid tsam gug ste [292] nu ma ste srog gi rlung gang zhig lte ba'i dbus nas gzhan gyi gnas sna bug nas phyi rol du sa rlung sor bcu gnyis kyi mtha' dang / de bzhin du chu rlung bcu gsum dang / me rlung bcu bzhi dang / rlung gi rlung bco lnga dang / nam mkha'i rlung cha ste bcu drug gi mthar 'gro ba de ni kha nas ma byung ba byas la sna bug gnyis nas drag tu brdubs te dbu ma'i nang na mar song ba'i rlung gi gdangs hUM gi sgrar mos pa lte ba'i bar du song ba'i srog 'dzin dang de dang lhan cig 'og sgo gnyis gang rung nas dri ma med pa'i glog dang kha dog mtshungs pa dbu ma'i lam nas gyen du drangs pa dbyug pa'i gzugs can gyen du langs pa'i thur sel gnyis lte bar 'gog pa dang bcas pa ste kha sbyar du bzung / de nas rlung de gnyis lte ba'i rtsa 'khor nas gtsug tor gyi rtsa 'khor gyi bar du g.yas g.yon ro rkyang la rgyu ba nges par dman zhing 'khor lo rnams kyi lte ba nas lte ba'i bar du phug ste rol pa'i bgrod pas dbu ma'i rtsa a wa d+hU tI la skyod pa ste bgrod nas ji srid gtsug tor gyi 'khor lo'i bug par btsan thabs te rlung stobs drag po nyid kyis 'gro ste/ de ltar song ba na mgo bo'i phyi rol gyi pags pa dag la khab kyis reg pa bzhin gyi tsha tseg pa 'ong zhing de ni btsan thabs kyis rlung dbu mar tshud pa'i rtags su shes par bya'o/ /

This is taught by verse 196 in the “easy to understand” verses of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter:
The śakti from the center of the navel to another place travel a distance of twelve and a distance of “part,” they are halted at the navel, together with the pure lightninglike, drawn up in the form of a stick. They travel from cakra to cakra and disappear, moving through the central channel. At the crown opening, by wrathful method, a needlelike sensation on the outer skin.[290] To explain this verse a little: nāda translated means “mere sound,” which changes the phrase[291] to “meditate on the sound.” The “sound” is the sound of hūḥ. The way this hūḥ is meditated on is as follows. Feet are placed in vajra position, arms in vajra-fist position are crossed across the heart, and the head is slightly bent. “Śakti” here means the life-sustaining wind. “Another place” in the line “From the center of the navel to another place” refers to the nostrils. From here to the outside, the earth-element wind travels a distance of twelve fingerwidths, the water-element wind a distance of thirteen, fire-element wind fourteen, air-element wind fifteen, and the space-element wind travels a distance of “part,”[292] or sixteen, fingerwidths. These life-sustaining winds are inhaled violently, not through the mouth but through the nostrils, and descend through the central channel as far as the navel. The innate tone of the winds is visualized as the sound of hūḥ. At the same time, from either of the two lower orifices, the downwardly expelling wind, similar in color to pure lightning, is drawn up through the pathway of the central channel and is upright “in the form of a stick.” These two winds are “halted at the navel,” meaning held together at the navel. From the navel cakra to the crown cakra, these two winds “disappear” from the left and right channels /429/ and penetrate instead the centers of succeeding cakras, moving through the central channel. When they reach the opening of the crown cakra by “wrathful method,” meaning moving by the force of the wind, and the skin on the outside of the head feels as if it is being pricked by needles, this is a sign that the winds have been brought into the central channel by these forceful means.

d.div: [291] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka196_97_ba4
[292] ma dper mgo yid tsam dgu ste zhes byung yang gug ste zhes bcos/
[290] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 196, 97b4.
[291] The phrase ”meditate on the nāda” from the previous Great Commentary passage.
[292] cha shas. Word numeral for sixteen.

f.d:
de nyid kyis rlung dbu mar 'dzud pa'i sbogs chog grub mod/ 'on kyang 'tshams 'di nas 'pho ba byed na de'i 'phro nyid las/
de yi dus su thur du sel ba btsan thabs nyid kyis steng gi lam du bskul bar bya/ / zung gi rlung dag 'gags pa na ni gtsug tor phug nas mchog gi grong khyer dag tu 'gro bar 'gyur/[293] / zhes gsungs pa 'dis bstan te/ de yang btsan thabs byas pas khab bzhin reg pa de yi dus su thur du sel ba'i rlung mchog gi btsan thabs te sngar bas kyang rlung stobs drag po nyid kyis a wa d+hU tI'i steng gi lam du bskul bar bya'o/ / de ltar byas pas g.yas g.yon ro rkyang gi rlung dag gi rgyu ba 'gags pa na ni dbu ma'i nang nas gtsug tor phug ste mchog gi grong khyer mkha' spyod du 'gro bar 'gyur zhes pa'o/ /

That is the ritual for bringing the winds into the central channel. However, if consciousness transference is to be performed at this point, the tantra continues:
At that time the downward wind, by supreme wrathful method, is urged into the upward path, and if the two winds are blocked, they travel to the supreme city from the crown opening.[293] “At that time,” meaning when wrathful methods have produced needlelike sensations, the downward wind is urged into the upper avadhūtī path by “supreme wrathful method,” meaning by the power of even more forceful winds. This blocks the winds from flowing through the left and right channels, and instead they travel to the supreme city of the ḍākinī from the central channel at the crown opening.

d.div: [293] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka197_97_ba5
[293] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 196, 97b4.

f.d: gsum pa des rlung bcings nas bde ba skyed tshul ni

d.i: The creation of bliss from the binding of winds

f.d: spyir bla med kyi rgyud phal che ba las rlung d+hU tIr tshud nas 'od gsal gyi sems lhan skyes kyi bde ba skyed pa nyid rdzogs rim gyis skabs su gtso bor 'chad cing / dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i rgyud sems 'grel skor gsum dgongs 'grel dang bcas pa rnams kyis rlung d+hU tIr tshud nas lhan skyes kyi bde chen dang stong gzugs sgrub pa'i tshul gnyis 'chad la/ stong gzugs sgrub pa yang mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba sgrub pa'i yan lag gam thabs su yin pas gtso bor mi gyur ba'i bde ba dang / de sgrub pa'i thabs nyid du stong gzugs 'chad pas dus 'khor gyi rgyud ma rgyud du 'jog ba'i rgyu mtshan yang de yin no/ / de ltar na stong gzugs kyang gang byung shar bas mi chog gi rlung d+hU tIr tshud pa las byung ba'i stong gzugs 'char dgos pas rdzogs rim gyi lam gyi mtshan nyid tshang ba'i bde chen dang stong gzugs 'char ba la rlung dbu mar tshud dgos so/ /

Generally, in most highest yoga tantras, development of clear-light mind and innate bliss is mainly taught in the completion stage. The Kālacakra Tantra and Three Bodhisattva Commentaries, which teach in accord with Kālacakra thinking, teach methods for the development of empty forms and great innate bliss once the winds have entered the dhūtī. The development of empty forms is a limb of or method for the development of unchanging bliss. Therefore the Kālacakra Tantra teaches mainly unchanging bliss and, as a method for its attainment, the development of empty forms. That is the reason for categorizing Kālacakra as mother tantra. Therefore these empty forms cannot be just any appearance of empty forms but must be those brought about by the winds having entered the dhūtī. So for the empty forms and the innate bliss of a definitive completion stage to occur, the winds must have entered the central channel.

des na btsan thabs kyi sbyor ba 'dis rlung dbu mar tshud pa na khams byang chub kyi sems rdo rje nor bu'i bu ga nas mi 'dzag par rlung stobs kyis 'dzin nus la/ de ltar nus pa'i sor sdud nas phyag rgya chen po la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'dren mi nus kyi bar la las kyi phyag rgya la snyoms 'jug byas te thig le rdo rje nor bur bkag nas 'dzag med kyi bde ba yas babs dang mas brtan gyi bde ba skyed pa yin no/ / de bzhin du ye shes kyi phyag rgya la yang shes par bya'o/ /

Therefore, if the winds are brought into the central channel by this wrathful method, /430/ the bodhicitta element is held by the power of the wind and does not fall from the opening of the vajra jewel. From the achievement of that ability on the path of withdrawal until the attainment of the ability to induce the unchanging bliss by reliance upon a mahāmudrā consort, one engages in union with an activity mudrā consort. The drops are held in the vajra jewel, and from the bliss of nonemission comes the development of the bliss of descent and ascent. The same is true for a wisdom mudrā consort.
bzhi pa tshad ma gang yin dpyad pa ni/
dbu ma'i nang gi rlung la dmigs pa'i rtogs pa dang bral zhing mi slu ba'i yid kyi mngon sum tshad ma'o/ /
The cognition is a valid, nonconceptual, direct mental perception focused on the winds within the central channel.
lnga pa dag dbye ni

sgrub le'i brgya bco lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
srog rtsol dag kyang ral gri can no zhes pa 'du byed kyi phung po ste rnam pa bcu ni g.yon dang g.yas kyi dkyil 'khor bcu po gcig tu 'dres par gyur pa'i phyir ro/[294] / zhes gsungs pa ltar 'du byed kyi phung po'i sde tshan gyi chos drug sgrib bral du dag par byed pa ste/ dbye na g.yas g.yon gyi rlung gi dkyil 'khor bcu po dbu mar gcig tu 'dres pa'i tshul gyis 'gog pas rnam pa bcu'o/ /

The Great Commentary, on verse 115 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
“Prāṇāyāma is the sword family”[294] refers to the aggregate of mental formations.[295] “In ten aspects” refers to the ten mandalas left and right combined as one.[296] The six phenomena of the mental formation aggregate group are to be purified into a state of nonobscuration. There are ten divisions — the ten mandala winds on the right and left — which are halted and combined as one in the central channel.

d.div: [294] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 237_na1
[294] Amoghasiddhi.
[295] ’du byed, saṃskāra. Also known as compositional factors or volition, this aggregate is a mental activity responsible for bringing minds and states of mind together with various objects.
[296] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 237a1.

f.d: drug pa 'bras bu
['di ]la gnyis las

dang po gnas skabs kyis 'bras bu ni sgrub le'i brgya bco brgyad pa las/
srog rtsol gyis ni dag pa ri bong can dang nyi ma dang bral byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyis mchod/[295] / ces pas bstan pa ltar nyi zla ro rkyang gi rlung rgyu ba dang bral nas dbu mar bab pa'i rten 'brel gyis byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyis mchod cing sangs rgyas kyis lung bstan pa 'thob/ rlung dbang du 'dus pa'i rten 'brel gyis byang chub sems dpa' la sogs pa thams cad dbang du 'du'o/ / nges don du byang chub sems dpa' ni dbang po drug la byed pas dbang po rnams lha'i mig la sogs par gyur te lkog gyur gyi don mthong ba la sogs pa'o/ / de bzhin du 'grel chen las kyang /
srog rtsol gyis ni dag pa zhes pa ni 'di dbang gi tshe rnal 'byor pa nyi ma dang ri bong can gyi lam dang bral te rtag tu dbu mar 'bab par gyur pa de'i tshe srog rtsol gyis dag par gyur pas na byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyis mchod de bsngags par byed do zhes pa'i don to/[296] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

Immediate results are taught in verse 118 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter:
Purified by prāṇāyāma, divorced from the paths of sun and moon, the yogi is praised by the bodhisattvas.[297] Because the winds move through the central channel divorced from the moon and sun channels on the left and right, the yogi is praised by the bodhisattvas and will receive a prophecy of enlightenment from the buddhas. By mastering the winds, the yogi gains mastery over the bodhisattvas. The definitive meaning of this is that “bodhisattvas” refers to the six organs, and these organs have become celestial eyes and so forth and are able to see hidden phenomena. The Great Commentary says:
“Purified by prāṇāyāma” means that when the yogi is “divorced from the paths of the sun and moon” and is constantly within the central channel, the yogi will be purified by prāṇāyāma and therefore is “praised by the bodhisattvas.”[298] /431/

d.div: [295] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka118_89_ba6
[296] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 238_na1
[297] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 118, 89b6.
[298] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 238a1.

f.d:
gnyis pa mthar thug gi 'bras bu ni/ 'du byed kyi phung po dang rlung gi khams dang sna dang reg bya dang / bshang ba 'dzag pa rnams sgrib bral du gyur pa las don yod grub pa la sogs pa drug tshan gcig 'grub par byed do/ / de ltar na/
sgra gcan lam nas rlung sngags mi phyed pas/ / lhun gyis grub pa'i zab mo'i rdor bzlas shes/ / bum pa can gyi srog dang thur sel gnyis/ / dbu ma'i lam du kha sbyor byed tshul shes/[297] / zhes pa'i rdo rje'i tshig gis bshad pa srog rtsol bshad zin to/ /

For the final results, mental formations, wind element, the nose, touch, the anus, and the discharge of excrement are all purified to a state of nonobscuration and transformed into a group of six consisting of Amoghasiddhi and so on. This has been an explanation of the branch of prāṇāyāma, as taught by the following vajra words:
Know the spontaneous, profound vajra recitation performed with mantra and wind inseparable in the Rāhu path. Know how the life and downward winds, by vaselike meditation, are in the central channel in the form of embrace.[299]

d.div: [297] rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum pod/ da_sbyor drug gi rdo rje'i tshigs bcad/ 1_na1
[299] Jé Tsongkhapa, Vajra Verses, Collected Works, vol. da, 1a.

f.d: bzhi pa d+hU tIr zhugs pa gnas pa'am brtan par byed pa'i 'dzin pa'i yan lag bshad pa/
33. The Yoga of Retention
gnyis pa d+hU tIr zhugs pa gnas pa'am brtan par byed pa'i yan lag 'dzin pa

d.i: The branch of retention: Stabilizing or keeping the winds in the dhūtī

f.d: ['di ]la drug / 'dzin pa'i mtshan don/ dang por bsgom pa'i dus 'tshams/ gang bsgom pa'i yan lag gi nges pa/ tshad ma gang yin pa dpyad pa/ dag dbye/ 'bras bu'o/ /
This is under six main outlines: 1. The meaning of the term retention 2. The time for retention meditation 3. The meditation 4. Valid cognition 5. Purification divisions 6. Results
dang po ['dzin pa'i mtshan don ]ni/

d.i: The meaning of the term retention

f.d:
rtsa 'khor drug gam lnga'i lte ba'i dbu ma'i nang du rlung 'gro 'ong med par thig ler srog bcug nas 'dzin pas na 'dzin pa zhes bya ste/ bde mchog stod 'grel las/
de nas 'dzin pa zhes bya ba ni lte ba dang snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral bar dbang chen dang chu dang me dang rlung gi dkyil 'khor la srog zhugs pa phyi rol tu 'gro ba med par thig le la srog gnas pa [298] zhes pa 'dzin pa'i yan lag brjod do/ / zhes dang yon tan gyis 'gengs pa las kyang /
de nas 'dzin pa zhes bya ba srog dbang chen dang chu dang me dang rlung gi dkyil 'khor la lte ba dang snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral bar zhugs pa phyi rol tu 'gro ba med par thig le la srog 'jug pa zhes bya ba 'dzin pa'i yan lag tu brjod par bya'o/[299] / zhes bshad pa ltar ro/ / 'o na 'grel pa 'di gnyis las ni rtsa 'khor bzhi las ma bshad pas rtsa 'khor lnga'am drug ces pa ji ltar yin snyam na/ 'grel pa 'di gnyis su bzhi bshad pa ni mtshon pa tsam yin pas drug yin pa ni 'og tu 'chad pa las shes par bya'o/ /

This branch is called retention because the winds are brought into the drops in the central channel at the center of six or five cakras and held or retained there. The Vajrapāṇi Commentary says:
Retention means that the winds of the earth, water, fire, and air mandalas enter the navel, the heart, the throat, and the forehead and, without emerging, are held in the drops. This is the branch of retention.[300] Filled with Good Qualities also says:
Retention means that the winds of the mandalas of earth, water, fire, and air enter the navel, heart, throat, and forehead and, without emerging, enter the drops. This is the branch of retention.[301] These two passages only mention four cakras, so how is it possible to talk of six or five cakras? The four mentioned in these two passages are for illustration only. /432/ That they actually refer to six cakras will be understood from later explanations.

d.div: [298] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 130_ba6
[299] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 297_na3
[300] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 130b6.
[301] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 297a3.

f.d: gnyis pa bsgom pa'i dus 'tshams ni

srog rtsol gyi nus pas rlung srog thur gnyis lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi dbu ma'i nang du 'dus nas gcig tu 'dres te bum pa can mthar phyin pa'i 'tshams srog thur 'dres pa'i phyi rtags dbugs gnyis kyi dri yod med/ nang rtags gtum mo'i me/ gsang rtags rlung gnyis gcig bzung na cig shos kyang zin 'ong ba'i rtags rnams shes par byas nas bsgom pa yin te/ rlung gnyis rtsa 'khor gyi dbu ma'i nang du bsre ma nus na rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su rlung gnyis 'gro 'ong mi byed par 'dzin pa'i gzhi gtor ba'i phyir ro/ /

When the power of prāṇāyāma has gathered the life and downward winds in the central channel at the center of the navel cakra and combined them as one, and vase yoga has been completed; when the external sign of the life-sustaining and downwardly expelling winds combining — the two breaths’ lack of smell — has manifested; when the inner sign — the fierce caṇḍālī fire — and the secret sign — when one of the winds is bound, the other is bound also — have both arisen, then this is the time to meditate on retention. If the two winds have not combined in the central channel at the cakras, then the basis for retention, wherein the winds in the cakra centers neither enter nor leave, is not there.
gsum pa gang bsgom pa'i yan lag gi nges pa
['di ]la lnga/ 'dzin pa'i lam gyi ngo bo ngos gzung ba dang / dbye ba dang / ji ltar sgom pa'i tshul dang / bsgoms pas nyams myong skye ba'i tshul dang / zhar byung 'chi med sgrub pa'i yan lag go/
This has five headings: 1. Identifying the path of retention 2. Divisions 3. The way to meditate 4. Experiences gained from meditation 5. Incidental topic: Attaining the nectar of immortality
dang po ['dzin pa'i lam gyi ngo bo ngos gzung ba ]ni

lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus kyi d+hU tI+i'i nang du srog rtsol gyis srog thur bsres pa'i rjes su rlung rnams 'gro 'ong med par byas nas rtsa 'khor drug po gang rung gi lte ba'i dbus kyi d+hU tA'i+i nang du thig le la sems kyi bzhon pa'i rlung brtan par byas pa las byung ba'i bde ba chen po stong gzugs dang ngo bo dbyer med pa'o/ / de ltar yang yon tan gyis 'gengs pa las/
rim pas rlung rnams med pa dang thig le rnams la ste byang chub kyi sems kyi thig le la sems kyi bzhon pa srog gi rlung stong pa nyid dang ro gcig pa nyid ni 'dzin pa'o/[300] / zhes gsungs so/ /

After the downward and life winds have been combined within the dhūtī at the center of the navel cakra by the power of prāṇāyāma, the winds are prevented from entering or leaving, and these mounts of the mind are stabilized within the drops that are inside the dhūtī at the centers of the six cakras. From this there arises an indivisibility of empty forms and great bliss. Filled with Good Qualities says:
“Gradually the winds disappear and are within the drops” means that within the bodhicitta drops, the life winds, the mounts of the mind, are one with emptiness.[302]

f.d: gnyis pa dbye ba ni

gsang gnas sogs rtsa 'khor drug gi lte ba'i dbu mar rlung g.yo med du 'dzin pa'i yan lag drug go/ / de yang rtsa 'khor gyis phye ba'i drug yod pa ni sgrub le'i brgya bco lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
'dzin pa phyag na rin chen po zhes pa ni tshor ba'i phung po ste srog gi 'dzin pa lte ba dang snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral ba dang gtsug tor gyi pad+ma la 'gro ba dang 'ong ba'i dbye bas rnam pa bcu'o zhes [301] stod 'grel nas bshad pa bzhi'i steng du gtsug tor dang bcas pa'i lnga bshad cing / de bzhin du lnga po de nyid yin par nA ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa las/
srog gi 'dzin pa lte ba dang snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral ba dang gtsug tor gyi pad+ma zhes dang /[302] yon tan gyis 'gengs pa las kyang nyi ma dpal gyis/
gnyis ka'i bgrod pa bcom pa zhes pa ni lte ba dang snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral ba dang gtsug tor rnams su bgrod pa dang bral bar 'gro bar byed pa dang bral ba'o/[303] / zhes bshad cing gsang gnas kyi 'khor lo dngos su ma bshad kyang thams cad mkhyen pa bu'i 'khrid yig las/
lte ba la sogs pa'i 'khor lo lnga 'am drug gi lte bar [304] zhes dang / yang de nyid las dbye ba 'chad pa'i skabs su/
rgyud las/ nye bar sgrub pa yan lag drug/ces pa bum pa can drug go [305] zhes gsungs pa la/ zin bris las/
rgyud kyi lung de'i don ma yin na'ang / 'khor la drug tu 'dzin pa'i 'dzin pa drug tu mdzad pa rung bargsungs pa ltar yin no/ /[306]

Retention has six branches corresponding to the winds being held in the central channel at the center of the six cakras, for instance the secret cakra. The Great Commentary, on verse 115 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
“Retention is Ratnasambhava” refers to the aggregate of feeling. The retaining of the winds refers to their entering and leaving the lotuses of the navel, the heart, throat, forehead, and crown. In this way it has ten aspects.[303] This passage adds the crown cakra to the four mentioned by the Vajrapāṇi Commentary to make five. /433/ These same five are mentioned by Nāropa in his Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations:
Retention at the lotuses of the navel, heart, throat, forehead, and crown.[304] Also Sūryaśrī says in his Filled with Good Qualities:
“The movements of both are destroyed” means that within the navel, heart, throat, forehead, and crown, there is no movement and no leaving.[305] Although the secret cakra is not actually mentioned, the writings of Butön state:
In the center of the five or six wheels of the navel and so forth.[306] Also in the same text, in the section on divisions of retention, it says:
The tantra talks of “The six branches of near accomplishment,” which refer to the six vase yogas.[307] On this, Notes on Kālacakra says:
Although that is not the meaning of the quote from the tantra, it is acceptable to posit six kinds of retention in the six cakras.[308]

f.d: gsum pa ji ltar sgom pa'i tshul
['di ]la bzhi las/ gang du bsgom pa'i gnas dang lus gnad dang lta stangs gsum ni srog rtsol dang 'dra'o/ /
This is under four headings. The first three, place of meditation, posture, and eye positioning, are the same as in prāṇāyāma.
bzhi pa gang la dmigs nas sgom pa'i tshul ni

srog thur gyi rlung gnyis gcig tu 'dres par gyur pa'i gong bu de la dmigs nas sgom pa yin te/ snyan brgyud las/
yul ni bde ba'i rlung nyid do/[307] / zhes so/ / de la sems kyi 'jog tshul ni rlung sems gcig tu dril nas rtsa 'khor drug po ra'i lte ba'i d+hU tI'i nang du thig ler rlung bsres pa la rtse gcig tu 'jog pa ste/ rtsa rgyud las/
pad+mar rdo rje rab bkod nas/ / srog ni thig ler gzhug par bya/[308] / zhes gsungs shing / 'dus pa phyi mar/ rin chen lnga yi rang bzhin dbugs/[309] / zhes sogs kyi don stod 'grel gyis bshad pa'i don bum pa can 'chad pa'i bshad pa dang cha 'dra bar 'dir yang 'chad tshul shes par bya dgos te/ stod 'grel gyis rgyud tshig de dag gi don srog 'dzin gnyis ka la sbyor bar bshad pa'i phyir te/ stod 'grel las rgyud tshig de dag bshad zin pa'i mjug tu/
de ltar de rnams kyi thig le'i gnas su gong bu'i gzugs kyis srog 'gags pa de ni 'dzin pa yin par brjod do/ / zhes lus ngag yid ye shes kyi thig le'i gnas rtsa 'khor rnams kyi lte ba'i d+hU tI'i nang du srog thur 'dres pa gong bu'i gzugs su gnas pa ro rkyang la rgyu ba 'gags pa de thig le bzhi po de dang 'dres pa la sems rtse gcig tu gnas pa ni 'dzin pa'i sgom tshul yin par gsungs so/ /

Meditation is focused on the “sphere” of wind that is the combination of the life and downward winds. As it says in the Kālacakrapāda Transmission:
The focus is the wind of bliss.[309] The way mind is placed on this object is that with mind and wind rolled together as one, the mind is one-pointedly focused on the combined winds concentrated within the drops in the dhūtī at the centers of the cakras. The Root Tantra states:
Placing the vajra in the lotus, the winds enter the drops.[310] Also the Later Guhyasamāja says, “Breath, the nature of the five jewels” and so on. The meaning of this quote was explained by the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary in the section on vase yoga and also needs to be understood here, because the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary applies the meaning of these lines from the tantra to both prāṇāyāma and retention. The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary, after the explanation of these lines from the tantra, says:
Like this, within these locations of the drops, the winds, in globe-shaped form, are halted. That is retention.[311] /434/ This passage is saying that in the drops of body, speech, mind, and gnosis located inside the dhūtī at the centers of the cakras, the winds are combined in a sphere or globe-shaped form and are halted from flowing through the left and right channels. Combined with these drops, the mind dwells one-pointedly upon the winds, and this is the way to meditate on the branch of retention.

f.d: de yang rim pa ji ltar du bsgom na/ chos rje bu'i 'khrid dang zin bris gnyis las gsungs pa ltar dang por lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte bar bsgom mo/[310] / de yang srog thur 'dres pa'i gong bu de nyid lte ba sa'i dkyil 'khor rtsa 'dab drug cu rtsa bzhi pa'i lte ba'i dbu ma'i nang du rlung sems thig le gsum dbyer med du bum pa can gyi tshul gyis gzung ngo / / rlung phyir gtong pa'i tshe rtsol bas mi gtong bar 'jam pas btang bar bya'o/ / de la rten nas snga ma ltar sa chu la thim pa'i tshul gyis snying ga dang / de brten nas chu me la thim pa'i tshul gyis mgrin pa dang / de brten nas me rlung la thim pa'i tshul gyis dpral pa dang / de brten nas rlung nam mkha' la thim pa'i tshul gyis gtsug tor dang / de brten nas nam mkha' ye shes la thim pa'i tshul gyis gsang gnas kyi 'khor lor gzung ngo / /

What is the procedure of the meditation? As the notes and writings of the dharma master Butön state, the meditation begins at the center of the navel cakra.[312] There the “sphere” that is the combination of the life and downward winds is held by vase yoga as an indivisible entity of drop, mind, and winds inside the central channel at the center of the sixty-four-petal earth-mandala navel cakra. Expelling the wind outside is done gently and without effort. Because of this, in the manner of earth dissolving into water, the focus of meditation is then held at the heart, in the same way it was held at the navel. In the manner of water dissolving into fire, the focus moves to the throat. In the manner of fire dissolving into air, it moves to the forehead. In the manner of air dissolving into space, it moves to the crown, and in the manner of space dissolving into gnosis, the meditation moves to the secret cakra.

d.div: [310] bu ston rin chen grub/ gsung 'bum pod/ ga_srog rtsol dang 'dzin pa'i khrid yig14_ba6
[312] Collected Works, vol. ga, Instructions on Prāṇāyāma and Retention, 14b6.

f.d:
'dir zhib tu bshad na rdor bzlas mthar phyin pa'i tshe stod 'grel las/
g.yon pa dang g.yas pa'i lam 'gags pa las dbu ma a wa d+hU tI'i nang du srog gi rlung rtag tu 'jug ste [311] zhes gsungs pa ltar rdor bzlas mthar phyin pa'i tshe rdo rje'i bzlas pa la rtse gcig tu gnas pa'i dus su rlung dbu ma 'ba' zhig la 'byung 'jug byed la/ de yang rlung rnams lte ba nas phyir 'gro zhing nang du yang lte ba'i bar du 'gro bas rdor bzlas mthar phyin pa'i rnal 'byor pa rdor bzlas la rtse gcig tu gnas pa'i gnas skabs su lte ba nas sna bug gi bar la rlung dbu ma 'ba' zhig nas 'byung 'jug byed par grub cing / de grub pas rlung rnams rtsa 'khor rnams kyi lte ba'i d+hU tI'i nang 'ba' zhig nas yar mar la 'gro 'ong byed par yang grub bo/ / de grub pas rdor bzlas mthar phyin pa'i tshe rtsa 'khor gyi thad kyi rtsa mdud rnams grol bar grub ste/ rtsa mdud ma grol ba na rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i d+hU tI'i nang la rlung 'gro 'ong byed pa mi 'ong ba'i phyir ro/ /

This can be explained in more detail. The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
From blocking the left and right pathways, the winds constantly flow within the central avadhūtī.[313] As this quote indicates, the accomplishment of the practice of vajra recitation ensures that the winds enter and leave only from the central channel during the one-pointed meditation on vajra recitation. These winds travel from the navel to the outside when leaving and as far as the navel when entering. Therefore the yogi who has accomplished the practice of vajra recitation has mastered the ability, during the single-pointed session on vajra recitation, to move the winds between the navel and the nostrils[314] solely by way of the central channel. The winds only move up and down through the dhūtī at the centers of the cakras. Therefore, on the accomplishment of vajra recitation, the channel knots at the cakras must have loosened, because if they had not, the winds would not flow up and down solely through the dhūtī at the centers of the cakras.

d.div: [311] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 130_ba4
[313] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 130b4.
[314] Vajra recitation involves breathing in the winds from the outside down to the navel.

f.d: de nas rdor bzlas mthar phyin nas bum pa can sgom pa la 'jug pa'i tshe thog mar rdor bzlas cung zad cig byas te rlung dbu mar bcug/de nas steng 'og nas rlung 'dren pa yang mos pa tsam min par dngos gnas la dbu ma'i nang nyid nas drangs te lte bar srog thur bsres nas bum pa can thun 'tshams pa re yang yang bsgoms pas srog thur 'dres pas phyi+i nang gsang ba'i rtags rnams byung ste lte ba'i gtum mo 'bar bas byang sems zhu ba'i yas babs mas brtan gyi dga' bzhi skyed nus pa'i bum pa can mthar phyin pa'i rjes su 'dzin pa sgom pa la 'jug pa'i tshe steng rlung srog 'dzin dang 'og rlung thur sel gnyis steng 'og nas drangs pa'i dbu ma'i nang nyid la song ba lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbu ma'i nang du gcig tu 'dres pa'i rlung dang rtsa mngon sum du mthong ba'i rlung srog thur gcig tu 'dres pa'i gong bu de lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i dbu ma'i nang gi sad pa'i gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le dang gcig tu bsres pa la sems rtse gcig tu bzhag nas rlung yang steng 'og tu ma 'phyugs par rtsol bas gzung / de ltar yang yang byas pas dang po nas rlung gnyis 'dres pa rtsol med du rang gi ngang gis gnas pa med kyang nam zhig nas rlung gnyis 'dres pa thig le dang yang bsres pa rtsol med du rang gi ngang gis gnas pa 'ong la/ de lta byung ba de yang yang bsgoms pas de brtan par 'gyur zhing de brtan pa na gong du bshad pa'i rim pa ltar snying ga sogs su yang bsgom pa yin no/ /

Therefore, when vajra recitation is mastered and before the commencement /435/ of vase yoga, a little vajra recitation is performed to get the winds to enter the central channel. This is followed by the life and downward winds being drawn from above and below. This is not just imagined or visualized; the winds are actually drawn through the central channel to combine at the navel. This vase-yoga meditation is continued session after session to eventually produce the outer, inner, and secret signs. The caṇḍālī fire at the navel blazes up to melt the bodhicitta and create the four joys of descent and stable ascent. After the completion of vase yoga, retention meditation is performed. At this point the upper life wind and the lower downward wind have been drawn from above and below into the central channel and combined as one in the navel cakra. At this point these winds and channels are actually seen. This spherelike amalgamation of life and downward winds is combined with the drop that creates the waking state and that is located in the central channel at the center of the navel cakra. The mind is single-pointedly placed on this and held there determinedly, with the winds not being allowed to stray up or down. This is practiced repeatedly, and at first the combined winds will not naturally stay in place without effort. However the time will come when the two winds mixed with the drops will remain there naturally without effort. When that occurs, it is meditated upon and eventually stabilized. Then the meditation moves on to the heart cakra, as in the procedure explained above.

de ltar bsgoms pas srog rtsol gyi gnas skabs su rlung dbu mar zhugs pa dang / 'dzin pa'i gnas skabs su rlung dbu mar gnas pa'i dus thams cad du 'od gsal gyi sems mngon sum du nyams su myong zhing stong gzugs sna tshogs pa rnams dang khyad par du rlung sems gang du bzung sa der stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum gyi rnam pa can 'od gsal gyi sems dang ngo bo dbyer med pa ma btags ma bcos pa rang gi ngang gis 'char ba rten 'brel gyi chos nyid yin zhing / rdor bzlas kyi skabs su rdor bzlas nyid la brten nas gtum mo 'bar ba sogs ma bshad kyang / bum pa can mthar phyin pa'i tshe gtum mo 'bar bas byang sems bzhus pa'i yas babs mas brtan gyi dga' bzhi skye bar gsungs pa dang 'dzin pa'i skabs 'dir bum pa can gyi skabs las kyang khyad par du gyur pa'i yas babs mas brtan gyi dga' bzhi skye bar gsungs pa ltar gnas skabs de gnyis su dga' bzhi skyes pa de'i tshe 'od gsal gyi sems de bde ba chen po'i ngo bor skyes bas de lta bu'i bde ba chen po'i sems de rang dus su shar ba'i stong gzugs rang bzhin gyi med pa la rtse gcig tu bzhag pa'i ngang nas stong gzugs de nyid kyang gsal bar snang ba'i ngang la rtse gcig tu 'jog dgos pa yin no/ /

By the power of meditation the winds enter the central channel during prāṇāyāma and abide there during retention. At all times during these meditations, the clear-light mind is directly experienced, and various empty forms appear. In particular, wherever the mind and winds are held, there an empty-form Kālacakra in mother-and-father embrace, indivisible from the clear-light mind, unimputed and unconceived, will appear of its own accord. This is a natural cause-and-effect process. In the section on vajra recitation it is not taught that the caṇḍālī fire blazes due to the practice of vajra recitation. However it will blaze on the completion of vase yoga, causing the bodhicitta to melt and to bring about the four joys of descent and ascent. Here, in the section on retention, it is taught that the four joys of descent and ascent are greater than those of vase yoga. /436/ At these two times, when the four joys are generated, the clear-light mind becomes a mind of great bliss. This great-bliss mind is placed one-pointedly on the noninherent nature of the empty forms that arise simultaneously with this mind. Within this state the empty forms clearly appear, and they too are single-pointedly focused upon.

kha cig na re/ steng rlung nang du 'dren pa na rlung sems dang stong gzugs dbyer med du byas nas rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su thig le'i gnas su drang zhes zer ba la ni/ steng rlung nang du 'dren dus na stong gzugs shar ba med pas de rlung sems dang dbyer med du byed pa ga la 'ong zhes bya'o/ /

Some say that when the upper wind is drawn in, the winds and mind are made indivisible from the empty forms and are then drawn to the location of the drop at the center of the cakras. However, when the upper wind is drawn inside, empty forms do not appear, so how could they be made indivisible from the winds and mind?
bzhi pa bsgoms pas nyams myong skye ba'i tshul ni

nyi ma dpal ye shes kyis/
rang dbang rin chen 'gag pa la/ / gzung bar bya'o 'dzin par brjod/[312] / ces so/ / 'di'i so sor rgyas par bshad pa ni rang ni gzugs la sogs pa'i yul rnams so/ / dbang po ni mig la sogs pa rnams te rang dang dbang po 'gags shing thim pa de la de nas yul dang dbang po'i rten du gyur pa'i rin chen te sems kyi rin chen srog rtsol dang lhan cig 'gags shing nub par gyur pa la gang gzung bar bya ba de 'dzin pa'o/ / zhes 'dzin pa mthar phyin pa'i gnas skabs su gzugs la sogs pa'i yul rang dang / mig la sogs pa'i dbang po 'gags shing thim par 'gyur la/ de ltar thim pa de la de'i rjes de nas yul dang dbang po'i rten du gyur pa'i rin chen te sems kyi rin chen srog rtsol te rlung dang lhan cig tu 'gags shing nub par gyur pa'i 'od gsal gyi stong nyams shin tu che ba 'byung bar gsungs shing / rje bus/ de'i tshe stong nyams mtshan nyid pa zhig shar na skrag pa mi skye mi srid pas gdams ngag gis zin par byas nas sgom dgos [313] zhes gsungs so/ /

Sūryaśrī Jñāna says:
“Selves, powers, and the jewel all cease; holding to this is retention.” To explain this in greater detail, “Selves” refers to the objects of form and so forth. “Powers” refers to the eyes and so forth. Selves and powers cease and dissolve. Then the jewel, which is the basis for the objects and sense powers and refers to the jewel of the mind, ceases together with prāṇāyāma and disappears. This is to be focused upon. That is retention.[315] This means that the situation after the completion of retention is that the “selves,” or objects of form and so forth, and the sense powers of the eyes and so forth have ceased and dissolved. Then, after this dissolution, “the jewel, which is the basis for the objects and sense powers and refers to the jewel of the mind, ceases together with prāṇāyāma and disappears.” Here prāṇāyāma means “winds.” This means that the clear light arises as a vast emptiness. The master Butön says that if a definitive clear-light emptiness arises, it is not possible to be without fear, and that one should meditate well armed with instructions.[316]
