f.d:
gzhan yang srog thur lte bar 'dres pas gtum mo'i me 'bar bas bza' btung ci byas pa thamasacad gtum mo'i me la sbyin sreg byas pas dwangs mas lus kyi mdangs 'phel/ snyigs ma gtum mo'i mes bsregs te dri chen dri chu mi 'dzag cing / lus yang zhing tho mdog bde/ de nas bzung ste dus min gyi 'chi bas mi tshugs te/ snyan brgyud las/
ma zos bkres med zos kyang 'ju/ / thur sel mi 'dzag bde ba 'dzag / sgyu 'phrul chen po gsus po che/ / lus ngag la sogs mi rtog bde/[314] / zhes so|_|

Furthermore, when the life and downward winds are combined at the navel, the caṇḍālī fire blazes, and all food or drink taken becomes a fire offering to the caṇḍālī fire. Its nourishment improves the body’s complexion. All waste in the body is burnt away by the caṇḍālī fire, and excrement and urine are no longer passed. The body becomes light and of good odor and color. From this time onward one cannot be harmed by untimely death. /437/ The Kālacakrapāda Transmission says:
No eating, no hunger; even if eating, all is digested. Downward winds do not descend, but bliss descends. Great powers, great stomach, nonconceptual bliss in body, speech, and so on.[317]

d.div: [314] sde dge_1372_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_dus zhabs snyan rgyud/ 225_na5
[317] Toh 1372 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 225a5.

f.d: gzhan yang de ltar bsgoms pas dang por rtsol bas 'dzin pa ma gtogs rang shugs kyis gnas pa mi 'ong yang / rgyun bsrings te bsgoms pas 'tshams shig nas srog thur 'dres pa d+hU tI'i nang du rang shugs kyis gnas pa 'ong la/ de nas rgyun bsrings te bsgoms pas rim pa bzhin zhag gcig dang / zla ba phyed dang / zla ba gcig dang / zla ba drug dang / lo gcig dang / lo las kyang lhag pa'i dus yun ring po gnas pa 'byung la/ de las rim pa bzhin dpral ba/ mgrin pa/ snying ga lte ba/ gsang ba/ nor bu'i rtse rnams su byang sems g.yo med du 'dzin nus pa 'byung ngo / /zhes zin bris las gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

At first this meditation can only be maintained with effort, and under its own power it will not last. However with prolonged meditation there comes a point from which the downward and life winds combined in the dhūtī remain there of their own accord. From that time onward they can remain for a day, half a month, a month, six months, a year, and even beyond a year. In these periods the bodhicitta can be held immobile at the forehead, throat, heart, navel, secret area, and jewel tip. This is explained in Notes on Kālacakra.
lnga pa zhar byung 'chi med sgrub pa'i yan lag ni

d.i: Incidental topic: Attaining the nectar of immortality

f.d:
sgrub le'i+i go sla'i brgya go gsum pa las/
skyil krung bcing ba byas nas phan tshun so dag reg pa min par kha ni rnam par phye ba yis/ / phyi rol rlung dag bkug ste de dang bdud rtsir bcas pa lte ba'i dbus su rab tu bcug pa yis/ / kun tu gdung ba dang ni bkres dang skom pa 'phrog cing mchog gi lus la dug kyang yang dag 'gog / dpral bar thig le dkar po dbyangs kyis yongs su bskor ba bdud rtsi spro bar byed pa yis kyang ngo /[315] / zhes gsungs pa ltar lus gnad rdo rje skyil krung bcing ba byas nas so phan tshun reg pa min pa ste yas mas kyi so dag ma reg par byas/ kha ni cung zad rnam par phye ba yis rlung gi gnad phyi rol gyi rlung dag bkug ste/ bkug pa'i rlung de dang lce chung gi bdud rtsi dang bcas pa lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su bcug pa yis tsha ba'i rim gyi kun tu gdung ba dang bkres pa dang skom pa 'phrog cing 'dzin pa'i yan lag thob pa lta bu rnal 'byor pa mchog gi lus la dug dang / kyang gi sgras dus min 'chi ba 'gog cing bcud len gyi mchog tu 'gyur ro/ /

Verse 193 of the “easy to understand” verses of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter says:
Locked in vajra position, teeth not touching, mouth open, gather in outside air, together with nectar, bringing them to the center of the navel. All torments, hunger, and thirst will be destroyed, and in the supreme body all poison also disappears. Surrounded by the vowels of the forehead white drop, this practice is accomplished by emanating nectar.[318] The body is locked in the vajra position. The upper and lower teeth do not touch each other. The mouth is slightly open. Air is gathered from outside and is brought to the center of the navel cakra together with nectar gathered from the uvula.[319] This will destroy all torments of fever, hunger, and thirst. Together with an attainment such as the branch of retention, all poison and untimely death, which is indicated by the word “also,” will disappear from the body of the supreme yogi. This is the supreme nourishment.

d.div: [315] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka193_97_na7
[318] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud ka, v. 193, 97a7.
[319] lce chung. “Little tongue.”

f.d: 'o na lce chung gi bdud rtsi ji lta bu snyam na/ dpral ba'i rtsa 'dab ma bcu drug pa'i lte bar zla ba'i dkyil 'khor la thig dkar po dbyangs kyi yi ges yongs su bskor ba las bdud rtsi 'dzag pa lce rtse gyen la log nas lce chung la reg par byas te lce chung nas 'bab par bsgoms pas ci zhig ltar goms pa na kha mchil mas gang nas 'ong / de nas je zhim je zhim la song ste mthar bdud rtsi lta bu'i ro mchog tu gyur pa 'byung ba bcud len gyi mchog tu 'gyur ro/ / dang po rgyun gcig la ha cang mangs na lce chung babs nas nad skyed par gsungs pas cung zad cung zad bya'o/ /

What is the uvula nectar? In the center of the sixteen-petal forehead cakra on a moon mandala is the white drop completely encircled by vowels from which nectar descends. /438/ The tongue is turned upward touching the uvula, and one meditates on the nectar falling from the uvula. With practice the mouth becomes filled with saliva, which increases in sweetness until finally it develops the supreme nectarlike taste and becomes the supreme nourishment. It is taught that if this is performed too often during one session, the nectar falling from the uvula can cause illness. Therefore this should be performed gradually.
bzhi pa tshad ma gang yin dpyad pa ni
yid kyi mngon sum yin pa gsungs so/ /
This is taught as being a direct and mental valid cognition.
lnga pa dag dbye ni

tshor ba'i phung po'i sde tshan gyi chos drug dag par byed cing / 'khor lo lnga'i lte bar rlung 'gro ba dang 'ong ba gnyis gnyis kyi dbye bas rnam pa bcu'o/ / de ltar yang sgrub le'i brgya bco lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
slar yang rnam pa bcu ste 'dzin pa phyag na rin chen no zhes pa ni tshor ba'i phung po ste srog gi 'dzin pa lte ba dang snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral ba dang gtsug tor gyi pad+ma la 'gro ba dang 'ong ba'i dbye bas rnam pa bcu'o/[316] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

The six phenomena of the feeling aggregate group are the phenomena to be purified. At each of the five cakras the winds are divided into those that enter and those that leave. Therefore there are ten aspects. The Great Commentary, on verse 115 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
“Again ten aspects: retention is Ratnasambhava” refers to the aggregate of feeling. The retaining of the winds refers to their entering and leaving the lotuses of the navel, heart, throat, forehead, and crown. In this way it has ten aspects.[320]

d.div: [316] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 237_na2
[320] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 237a2.

f.d: 'bras bu
['di ]la gnyis las /

dang po gnas skabs kyi 'bras bu ni rlung ro rkyang la rgyu ba bdud dang nyon mongs nyams pas dus min du 'chi ba med cing rlung phyi nang du 'gro ba zad pas stobs bcu po ste stong pa nyid kyi gzugs la sems 'jug par 'gyur ba ste/ de ltar yang sgrub le'i brgya bco brgyad pa'i 'grel chen las/
bdud dang nyon mongs la sogs nyams shing stobs bcu la ni 'jug par 'gyur te zhes pa ni stong pa nyid kyi gzugs gzung ba'i sems la 'jug par 'gyur te 'dzin pa'i stobs kyis so zhes pa ni srog 'gro ba dang 'ong ba zad pas gcig tu 'dres par gyur bas so/[317] / zhes so|_|

The maras and afflictions that are equated with the movement of the winds in the right and left channels have been weakened, and therefore untimely death is no longer a threat. Winds no longer enter or leave, and so the mind engages the “ten powers,” or empty forms. These are the immediate results. The Great Commentary on verse 118 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter says:
“Maras, afflictions, and so forth weaken, and the ten powers are engaged” refers to the mind apprehending the empty forms. “This is by the power of retention“ means by the power of the winds no longer coming and going and being combined as one.[321]

d.div: [317] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 238_na2
[321] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 238a2.

f.d:
gnyis pa mthar thug gi 'bras bu ni/ tshor ba'i phung po/ me'i khams/ mig gi dbang po/ ro'i khams/ lag pa/ 'gro ba ste chos drug po de sgrib bral du gyur pa'i rin chen 'byung ldan sogs drug tshan gcig 'grub pa'o/ / de ltar na/
'dzin pas thig le la ni srog zhugs pas/ / dag pa'i sku las spro dang bsdu ba shes/[318] / zhes pa'i rdor rje'i tshig gis bshad pa 'dzin pa'i yan lag rgyas par bshad zin to/ /

The final results are that the feeling aggregate, the fire element, the eye sense power, the element of taste, the hands, and the activity of going all become free from obscuration, and take the form of Ratnasambhava and so forth. This has been an extensive explanation of the branch of retention as taught by these vajra words:
Know how winds enter the drops by retention and emanations depart and withdraw into the pure body.[322]

d.div: [318] rje tsong kha pa/ gsung 'bum pod/ da_sbyor ba yan lag drug gi rdo rje'i tshigs bcad/ 1_na2
[322] Jé Tsongkhapa, Collected Works, vol. da, Vajra Verses, 1a2.

f.d: lnga pa mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba dngos su sgrub byed rjes dran gyi yan lag bshad pa/
34. The Yoga of Recollection
gnyis pa mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba dngos su sgrub byed rjes dran gyi yan lag /

d.i: Branch of recollection: The actual creator of unchanging bliss

f.d: ['di ]la drug /rjes dran gyi mtshan don/ bsgom pa'i dus 'tshams/ bsgom pa'i yan lag gi nges pa/ tshad ma gang yin dpyad pa|_dag dbye/ 'bras bu'o/ /
/439/ This is under six main headings: 1. Meaning of the term 2. Time of the meditation 3. The meditation 4. Valid cognition 5. Purification divisions 6. Results
dang po [rjes dran gyi mtshan don ]ni

sor sdud dang bsam gtan gyis bsgrubs shing brtan par byas pa las byung ba'i rang nyid stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum gyi skur dngos gnas la grub pa yang rjes su dran cing / des spros pa'i khams gsum pa'i stong gzugs pra phab pa lta bu nam mkha' la rjes su dran pas na rjes dran no/ / de ltar yang 'dus pa'i rgyud phyi mar/
gang zhig bsgom bya rjes dran pas/ / de yi rnam par yang dag spro/ / rjes su dran pa zhes shes bya/ / rab gsal de la skye bar 'gyur/[319] / zhes pa'i don 'chad byed nA ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa las/
gang zhig bsgom bya ni so sor sdud pa dang bsam gtan gyi yan lag gis brtan par byas pa khams gsum pa rab tu gsal ba'i bdag nyid kun rdzob kyi bden pa ste de rjes su dran pas de'i rnam par yang gad spro/ de'i rnam par ni kun rjob kyi bden pa'i rnam par te yang dag spro ni nam mkha'i mthil mtha' dag khyab pa lta bur bya'o/ / rjes su dran pa zhes shes bya/ dus gsum pa'i srid pa gsum po mtha' dag mthong ba ni rjes su dran pa'i yan lag tu shes par bya'o/[320] /zhes pa'i don to/ de nyid kyi phyir gsungs pa/ rab gsal de la skye bar 'gyur/[321] /zhes pa ste khams gsum pa rab tu gsal ba ni de la zhes pa rjes su dran pa'i yan lag la skye bar 'gyur ro/ / zhes gsungs te/

Oneself as the empty-form father-and-mother Kālacakra that originally arose from the accomplishments and stabilizations developed by the practices of withdrawal and meditative absorption is now to be recollected or recalled as an actual phenomenon. The three-world empty forms, like forms in a clairvoyant’s mirror, that were emanated by this father-and-mother Kālacakra in space are also recollected — hence the term recollection. The Later Guhyasamāja says:
That meditated upon is recalled and its forms perfectly emanate; know this as recollection. Illumination is created there.[323] The meaning of this verse is explained by Nāropa in his Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations:
“That meditated upon” refers to that stabilized by the branches of withdrawal and meditative absorption. By nature it illuminates the three worlds, and it is a conventional truth. That is to be recalled and by doing so, “its forms perfectly emanate.” “Its forms” refers to conventional forms, while “perfectly emanate” means seeing them as pervading all realms of space. “Know this as recollection” means that seeing the three worlds of the three times should be understood as the branch of recollection. Because of that it was taught. “Illumination is created there” means the illumination of the three realms is created “there” in the branch of recollection.[324]

d.div: [319] sde dge_443_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_gsang 'dus rgyud phyi ma/ 154_ba5
[320] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 247_na7
[321] sde dge_443_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_gsang 'dus rgyud phyi ma/ 154_ba5
[323] Toh 443 Kangyur, rgyud. cha, 154b5.
[324] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 247a7.

f.d: de dag gi don cud zad cig bshad na/ bsgom bya zhes pa'i don ni so sor sdud pa dang bsam gtan gyi yan lag gis gtso bor bsgrubs shing brtan par byas pa las byung ba rang nyid kyi 'od kyis khams gsum pa rab tu gsal bar nus pa'i bdag nyid kun rdzob kyi bden pa dngos gnas la grub pa dus 'khor yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can gyi stong gzugs rjes su dran pas na rjes dran no/ / de yi rnam par yang dag spro/[322] /zhes pa'i don ni kun rdzob kyi bden pa stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam par te rnam pa can nam mkha'i mthil mtha' dag khyab par yang dag par spro ba yang rjes su dran pa yin par blta bar bya'o/ / rjes su dran pa zhes shes bya/ /zhes pa'i don ni/ der ma zad sor bsam gyis brtan par byas pa'i dus gsum pa'i srid pa gsum po'i stong gzugs mtha' dag mthong ba yang ni rjes su dran pa'i yan lag tu shes par bya'o/ / rgyu mtshan de nyidakyi phyir gsungs pa/ rab gsal de la skye bar gyur/ /zhes pa ste khams gsum pa rab tu gsal ba'i stong gzugs yid ngor snang ba tsam ma yin par dngos gnas la grub pa ni de la zhes pa rjes su dran pa'i yan lag la skye bar 'gyur ro zhes pa'i don to/ /

To explain this passage a little, “That meditated upon” refers to an empty-form real[325] mother-and-father Kālacakra in embrace arising from the primary accomplishments and stabilizations of the branches of withdrawal and meditative absorption. It radiates light capable of illuminating the three worlds, and itself is a conventional truth. This is to be recalled or recollected, and therefore this branch is known as recollection. /440/ “Its forms perfectly emanate” refers to being in the form of a conventional-truth empty-form Kālacakra in mother-and-father embrace that emanates and pervades the realms of space, and that this too should be regarded as recollection. This is to be focused on or recollected. “Know this as recollection” means that, furthermore, seeing the three-world empty forms of past, present, and future, which were stabilized previously by withdrawal and meditative absorption, should also be known as the branch of recollection. Because of these reasons it was taught. “Illumination is created there” means that the well-illumined empty forms of the three worlds are actual phenomena and not just appearances in the mind, and that they are created “there” in the branch of recollection.

d.div: [322] sde dge_443_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_gsang 'dus rgyud phyi ma/ 154_ba5
[325] dngos gnas la grub pa. A real or actual phenomenon as opposed to mere appearance.

f.d:
des na stod 'grel las stong gzugs dang por sgom pa'i dus kyi rtags dang grub pa'i dus kyi rtags gnyis gsungs pa'i grub pa'i dus kyi rtags ni stod 'grel las/
dngos su du ba dang 'bar ba la sogs pas sreg pa'i bya ba nus pa'i phyir ro/ / de bzhin du gur kum dang me tog dang rin po che dang gser gyi char yang ngo /[323] / zhes gsungs pa'i grub pa'i dus kyi sa 'tshams rjes dran nas byed pa 'dus pa'i rgyud rtsa 'grel bshad ma thag pa de dag gis shes shing / grub ma grub kyi don yang yid ngor snang ba tsam ma yin par dngos gnas la grub ma grub la byed dgos te/ gzhan du na sor bsam gyi skabs kyi stong gzugs dang rjes dran gyi stong gzugs la khyad par med par thal bar 'gyur ro/ /

Therefore the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary talks of signs arising when first meditating on empty forms and of signs arising at the time of accomplishment. Concerning the latter:
Here is actual smoke and fire, capable of performing the function of burning. It is the same with the rain of saffron, flowers, jewels, or gold.[326] The “time of accomplishment” referred to by this passage begins from the attainment of recollection, and this can be known from the Guhyasamāja Root Tantra, as quoted above, and its commentary. Furthermore “accomplishment” must refer to actual creation as opposed to mere appearances in the mind. Otherwise it would follow that there would be no difference between the empty forms of the branches of withdrawal and meditative absorption and the empty forms of the branch of recollection.

d.div: [323] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 131_ba7
[326] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 131b7.

f.d: gnyis pa bsgom pa'i dus 'tshams ni
'dzin pa'i yan lag mthar phyin te byang chub kyi sems rtsa 'khor so sor mi 'jog par 'dzin pa'i nus pa thob pa'i 'tshams nas rjes dran sgom pa la 'jug pa yin no/ /

The time for meditation is when retention has been completed and the bodhicitta can be held and kept at each of the cakras without being allowed to fall. When this attainment is reached, one enters the recollection meditation.
gsum pa sgom pa'i yan lag gi nges pa
['di ]la bzhi/ mtshan nyid/ dbye ba/ ji ltar sgom pa'i tshul/ phyag rgya gnyis ji ltar bsten pa'i tshul lo/ /
This is under four headings: 1. Definition 2. Divisions 3. Actual meditation 4. How to make use of the two mudrā consorts
dang po [mtshan nyid ]ni

'dzin pa'i yan lag mthar phyin te phyag rgya gnyis gang rung dang snyoms par zhugs pa las gtum mo 'bar ba'i snang ba khams gsum gyi nam mkha' la shar ba'i stong gzugs rnams dang / khyad par du yang rnal 'byor pa rang gi lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i d+hU tI'i nang gi dngos gnas la grub pa'i stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can rtse gcig tu dran cing gtum mo 'bar ba des bzhus pa'i yas babs mas brtan gyi dga' bzhi'i ngo bor gyur pa'i 'od gsal rtog pa thams cad dang bral ba de bshad ma thag pa'i stong gzugs khyad par ba de dang / de rang bzhin gyi grub pas stong pa'i stong pa nyid la rtse gcig tu zhugs pa rnams so/ / de ltar yang sgrub le'i brgya bcu bdun pa'i 'grel chen las/
gtum mo'i snang ba gang zhig srid pa gsum gyi nam mkha' la gyur ba de ni rjes su dran pa ste/[324] zhes gtum mo 'bar ba'i snang ba srid pa gsum ste khams gsum gyi nam mkha' la shar bar gyur pa'i stong gzugs rnams dran pas na rjes dran du gsungs so/ /

The branch of retention is completed, and one enters union with one of the two types of consorts. /441/ This ignites the caṇḍālī fire, whose appearance manifests as empty forms in the space of the three realms. In particular, the yogi single-pointedly recollects the empty-form Kālacakra in father-and-mother embrace, now as an actual phenomenon and located within the dhūtī at the center of the navel cakra. The blazing caṇḍālī fire dissolves the element and produces the four joys of descent. The clear-light mind in the nature of these joys is divorced from all conception and is one-pointedly immersed in this special empty form as well as in its emptiness of any inherent existence. The Great Commentary, on verse 117 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
The appearances of the caṇḍālī fire are in the space of the three worlds. This is recollection.[327] This quote is saying that empty-form appearances of the blazing caṇḍālī fire manifest in “the space of the three worlds,” or realms, and that these empty forms are to be recollected, hence the term recollection.

d.div: [324] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 237_ba2
[327] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 237b2.

f.d:
de yang 'dir nam mkha' la gyur pa zhes pa tsam las gsal bar ma gsungs na'ang / brgya bcu dgu pa'i 'grel chen las/
rjes su dran pa legs par dag pa zhes pa 'dir rjes su dran pa zhes pa ni gzugs la 'khyud pa'i sems rnam par rtog pa thams cad dang bral ba'o/[325] / zhes rjes dran gyi ngo bo ni stong gzugs la 'khyud pa ste ngo bo dbyer med du zhugs pa'i sems rnam par rtog pa thams cad dang bral ba 'od gsal gyi sems su gsungs shing / nam mkha' la gyur pa stong gzugs la gsal bar gsungs so/ /

The text here merely says “in the space” and is not that specific. However the Great Commentary says on verse 119:
“Recollection is excellently pure.” Recollection, as spoken of here, refers to a mind embracing the forms and divorced from all conception.[328] This is saying that the nature of recollection is a clear-light mind “embracing” or inseparable from empty forms, divorced from all conception. This quote is clearly referring to empty forms “in the space.”

d.div: [325] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 238_na3
[328] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 238a3.

f.d:
de yang stong gzugs de ji lta bu snyam na/ de'i de ma thag par/
de'i phyir gang gi tshe dag par gyur pa de'i tshe dri med 'od kyi dkyil 'khor du 'gyur ro/ / kyang gi sgra las ba spu'i khung bu nas 'od zer lnga 'phro zhing nges par rgyu'o/ / ye shes gzugs las so zhes pa stong pa nyid kyi gzugs las so/[326] / zhes gsungs pa'i don cung zad cig bshad na/ rjes su dran pa'i ngo bo ni dngos gnas la grub pa'i stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can la 'khyud pa ste ngo bo dbyer med du zhugs pa'i sems rnam par rtog pa thams cad dang bral ba'i 'od gsal gyi sems yin pa de'i phyir gang gi tshe 'dzin pa'i yan lag mthar phyin te stong gzugs rnal 'byor pa'i yid ngor snang ba tsam de rnam par dag par gyur pa de'i tshe dri ma med pa'i 'od kyi dkyil 'khor dang ldan pa'i dngos gnas la grub pa'i stong pa nyid kyi gzugs mtshan nyid pa der 'gyur ro/ / kyang gi sgra las lus rags pa 'di'i nang na gnas pa'i stong gzugs kyi sku khyad par ba de las 'od zer lnga byung ba lus rags pa'i ba spu'i khung bu nas 'phro zhing nges par rgyu'o/ / de yang 'od zer gang las 'phro ba ni/ ye shes gzugs las so zhes pa stong pa nyid kyi gzugs las so/[327] /zhes gsal bar gsungs pa rnams so/ /

How are these forms described? The Great Commentary continues:
Therefore, when they become pure, at that time there are “mandalas of pure light.” The word “also” refers to the five rays of light radiating and traveling through the pores. “From the gnosis form” means from the empty forms.[329] To explain this passage a little: The nature of recollection is a clear-light mind divorced from all conception that embraces or is indivisible from an actual empty-form mother-and-father Kālacakra. Therefore, when the branch of retention is completed, the empty forms, which at that time are mere appearances to the yogi’s mind, are purified and are endowed with “mandalas of pure light” to become actual and definitive empty forms. /442/ The word “also”[330] refers to a special empty-form deity that is within this coarse body[331] and from which the five light rays shine. These rays radiate and travel out through the pores of the coarse body. From where do these light rays radiate? “From the gnosis form,” meaning from that empty form. All this is clearly taught in the above passage.

d.div: [326] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 238_na4
[327] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 238_na4
[329] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 238a4.
[330] The line from the tantra runs, “Recollection is excellently pure. Mandalas of pure light also come from the gnosis form.”
[331] The flesh-and-blood physical body of the yogi, compared to the nonmaterial empty forms.

f.d:
de bzhin du bde mchog stod 'grel las kyang /
de nas rjes su dran pa zhes bya ba ni rang gi 'dod pa'i lha mthong ba gzugs brnyan gyi rnam par rtog pa dang bral ba'o/ / de las 'od zer du ma 'phro ba'i rang bzhin 'od kyi dkyil 'khor te de las rnam pa du mar 'phro ba'i rang bzhin khams gsum par spro ba zhes pa rjes su dran pa'i yan lag brjod do/[328] / zhes gsungs te don ni snga ma'i 'chad tshul dang mthun par shes par bya'o/ /

Similarly the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
In recollection the desired deity is seen in the form of an image, free from conception. From it many rays of light radiate in the form of mandalas of light. From this image many forms emanate in the nature of the three realms. This is spoken of as the branch of recollection.[332] The meaning of this passage should be understood in the way the previous passage was explained.

d.div: [328] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 130_ba7
[332] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 130b7.

f.d: 'o na gtum mo'i snang ba gang zhig ces pa'i gtum mo 'bar ba de ji lta bu snyam na/ de ni 'dzin pa'i yan lag mthar phyin pa'i stobs kyis lte ba'i d+hU tI'i gnas su gtum mo 'bar ba rnal 'byor pas mthong zhing nyams su myong ba de yin la/ gtum mo de'i snang ba gang zhig srid pa gsum gyi nam mkha' la gyur pa de ni gtum mo de 'bar ba'i stobs kyis pra phab pa lta bu'i stong gzugs phyag rgya chen po sangs rgyas kyi 'od zer gyi sprin mtha' yas pa spro bar byed pa'i stong gzugs khyad par ba dngos gnas la grub pa'i dus 'khor yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can 'od kyi dkyil 'khor dang ldan pa de dang / des rnam par spros pa'i stong gzugs sna tshogs pa rnams yin no/ /

What is the caṇḍālī fire mentioned in the line “The appearances of the caṇḍālī fire ”? This refers to the caṇḍālī fire, seen and experienced by the yogi, that blazes in the dhūtī at the navel, brought on by the power of the completion of the branch of retention. “The appearances of the caṇḍālī fire are in the space of the three worlds” means that the blazing caṇḍālī fire produces the special empty form of an actual Kālacakra in mother-and-father union endowed with mandalas of light. These light mandalas emanate countless mahāmudrā buddha light rays of empty forms, like images in a clairvoyant’s mirror. “The appearances of the caṇḍālī fire” refer to this and to the various empty forms emanated by that special empty form.

de ltar yang / lha yi gzugs brnyan sgrub pa la/ /zhes pa'i bde mchog stod 'grel las/
de nas lha'i gzugs brnyan sgrub pa la zhes pa 'dir 'dzin pa'i stobs kyis lte ba'i gnas su gtum mo 'bar ba rnal 'byor pas mthong ste sgrib pa thams cad dang bral ba pra phab pa lta bu phyag rgya chen po sangs rgyas kyi sprin gyi 'od zer gyi sprin mtha' yas pa spro bar byed pa'i 'od kyi dkyil 'khor gyis rnam par spros pa de rjes su dran pa'i yan lag sgrub par brjod de 'dzin pa'i mthar thug pa gtum mo'i rnal 'byor bsgom par bya'o zhes pa nges pa'o/[329] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Furthermore, concerning the line “Achieving the image of the deity,”[333] the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
Concerning “Achieving the image of the deity,” the power of retention causes the yogi to see, divorced from all conception, the caṇḍālī fire blazing at the navel. Like forms in a clairvoyant’s mirror, countless mahāmudrā buddha light-ray clouds are emanated by the mandalas of light. This is said to be the practice of the branch of /443/ recollection, a meditation on caṇḍālī fire upon the completion of retention.[334]

d.div: [329] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 133_ba1
[333] From the Later Guhyasamāja.
[334] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, 133b1.

f.d: gnyis pa dbye ba ni

dbang po rab phyag rgya chen mo ri rab kyi rdul phra rab dang mnyam pa la snyoms par 'jug pa dang / dbang 'bring ye shes kyi phyag rgya dkyil 'khor gyi lha mo'i grangs dang mnyam pa la snyoms par 'jug pa dang / dbang po dman pa las kyi phya rgya dang snyoms par 'jug pa dang gsum mo/ /

There are three divisions. Those of sharp intelligence enter union with as many mahāmudrā consorts as there are atoms in Mount Meru. Those of a middling intelligence enter union with as many wisdom mudrā consorts as there are goddesses in the mandala. Those of low intelligence enter union with an activity mudrā consort.
gsum pa ji ltar sgom pa'i tshul
['di ]la gnyis/ gang zag gsum char gyi sgom tshul thun mong ba bstan pa dang / so sor bshad pa'o/ /
This is under two main headings: 1. The meditation common to all three types of persons 2. The meditations of each type
dang po [gang zag gsum char gyi sgom tshul thun mong ba bstan pa ]ni

d.i: The meditation common to all three types of persons

f.d: 'dzin pa'i yan lag mthar phyin pa'i bar la stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum sogs yid ngor snang ba tsam ma gtogs dngos gnas la grub pa med pas rjes dran gyi skabs 'dir stong gzugs rnams dngos gnas la grub pa zhig sgrub pa yin la/ de la lte ba'i gtum mo khyad par can sbar nas bde ba chen po bskyed cing bde ba des lte ba'i d+hU tI'i nang du shar ba'i stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam par snang ba de la rtse gcig tu dmigs nas bsgoms pas stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam par snang ba de je dag je dag la song ste dngos gnas grub pa'i stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi sku'i rnam pa can du 'gyur ba yin no/ / sku de las 'od zer rnam pa lnga byung ba lus rags pa 'di'i ba spu'i bu ga nas 'phro zhing phyir rgyu ba dang / gzhan yang sku de las sku de'i rnam pa can mtha' yas pa dngos gnas la grub pa nam mkha'i mthil mtha' dag khyab bar spro ba yin no/ /

Up to the completion of retention, empty forms such as the father-and-mother Kālacakra exist only as appearances to the mind and not as actual phenomena. Therefore recollection represents the accomplishment of actual empty forms. By igniting the special caṇḍālī fire at the navel, great bliss is generated. This mind of great bliss focuses on and meditates upon the empty-form Kālacakra in mother-and-father embrace that has appeared in the dhūtī at the navel. By the power of this meditation, the appearance of this Kālacakra mother and father becomes purer and purer and transforms into an actual empty-form Kālacakra mother and father. The five light rays emerge from this deity form, pass through the pores of this coarse body, and radiate outside. Also countless actual deity forms emerge from this inner deity form in identical aspect and pervade the reaches of space. /444/

de yang lte ba'i gtum mo khyad par can spar nas bde chen skyed pa 'di la yang 'dzin pa'i mthar gtum mo 'bar ba nyid la sems rtse gcig tu gtad nas skyed pa dang / las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas skyed pa dang / ye shes kyi phyag rgya la brten nas skyed pa gsum yod cing / gang zag gsum char gyis de gsum ga la brten nas bde chen skyed dgos so/ / de yang gang zag gsum gas las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas skyed pa yod pa ni ye le'i go sla'i bdun cu rtsa gsum pa las/
rgyal ba'i lhan skyes bde ba 'di ni 'phel ba'i don slad dang por las kyi phyag rgya bsten par bya/ / de nas nyi ma'i gzugs ni lus dang gdong dang rkang pa gtsug tor yan lag thams cad rdzogs pa ste/ / glog gi dbyug pa'i rjes mthun 'pho med bde ba skyed par byed ma mtshan nyid yan lag rab tu rdzogs/[330] / zhes gsungs te/

The great bliss arising from the the special caṇḍālī fire at the navel is produced in three ways: by focusing the mind single-pointedly on the caṇḍālī fire blazing at the completion of retention, by reliance on an activity mudrā consort, and by reliance on a wisdom mudrā consort. The three types of person develop the great bliss by relying on these three methods. The assertion that the three types of person will develop the great bliss by relying on an activity mudrā consort, is taught in the “easy to understand” seventy-third verse of the Gnosis chapter:
To increase this innate bliss of the conqueror, first rely upon an activity mudrā consort; then create the sun form, with body, face, legs, crown, all limbs complete; in a flash of lightning resemblance, arises a definitive creator of unmoving bliss, all features complete.[335]

d.div: [330] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka73_108_ba7
[335] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 73, 108b7.

f.d: 'di'i don ni rlung stobs kyis khams byang chub kyi sems 'dzag med du 'ching nus pa nas mchog mi 'gyur gyi bde ba skyed mi nus pa'i bar gyi yan lag dang po lnga'i gnas skabs su lhan skyes kyi bde ba 'di ni 'phel ba'i don du dang por las kyi phyag rgya bsten par bya'o/ / de'i rjes su rjes dran gyi sku nyi ma'i 'od zer dang ldan pa'i gzugs ni lus dang gdong dang rkang pa gtsug tor sogs yan lag thams cad rdzogs pa'i dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can 'grub cing de ltar grub pa'i yum de ni glog gi dbyug pa gtum mo 'bar bas bde chen skyed pa dang rjes su mthun par thig le 'pho ba med pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed par byed ma phyag rgya chen mo'i mtshan nyid dang ldan pa yan lag thams cad rab tu rdzogs par dngos gnas la 'grub par 'gyur ro zhes pa'i don no/ /

The meaning of this is as follows. In the first five branches, from the attainment of the ability to hold the bodhicitta element and prevent it from falling by the power of the winds up to the ability to generate the supreme and unchanging bliss, one first relies upon an activity mudrā consort in order to increase the innate bliss. After that, in recollection, a deity form is created endowed with the rays of the sun, with body, face, legs, crown, and so forth, all completed and in the aspect of Kālacakra in mother-and-father embrace. The consort of this union is the definitive mahāmudrā consort, the creator of the unmoving drop and unchanging bliss, created in the great bliss of the blazing caṇḍālī fire resembling a “flash of lightning.” She is an actually created consort with “all features complete.”

yan lag dang po lnga'i gnas skabs su dbang po rno 'bring rtul po gsum gyis kyang las kyi phyag rgya la brten dgos pa'i rgyu mtshan ni de yang gnas skabs lnga po de ci rigs par byang sems 'dzag pa med pa dang / 'gyur ba med pa'i bde ba dang / stong gzugs rjes mthun pa dang mtshan nyid pa bskyed pa'i phyir du lam la slob pa yin la/ de la yang thabs mkhas kyis zin pa'i sgo nas las kyi phyag rgya la brten te mi 'pho ba'i bag chags bzhag nas byang sems 'dzag med dang / 'gyur med kyi bde ba skyed dgos pa dang / bde ba de nyid kyi gzung rnam stong gzugs rnams su 'char bar byed dgos pa yin no/ /

The reason why all three types of person — sharp, middling, and dull — must rely upon the activity mudrā consort in the first five branches is as follows. In those five branches one practices on the path in order to prevent bodhicitta emission, to develop a nonchanging bliss[336] and to attain similitude and definitive empty forms. For these attainments one relies, with skillful means, on an activity mudrā consort, and having habituated to nonemission, /445/ one must develop nonfalling bodhicitta and nonchanging bliss as well as empty forms, which are the objective aspects of that bliss.

d.div: [336] ’gyur ba med pa’i bde ba. Nonchanging bliss, here differentiated from the definitive unchanging bliss (mi ’gyur ba’i bde ba) achieved on the sixth branch.

f.d:
de ltar yang mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus las/
phyag rgya'i sbyor ba gang gis 'pho ba'i bag chags der 'gyur ba'i sbyor ba de nyid kyis mi 'pho ba'i bag chags su 'gyur te dngul chu dang me bzhin no/[331] / bcom ldan 'das kyis rgyud kyi rgyal po'i sgrub thabs kyi le'u las tshigs su bcad pa nyis brgya nyi shu rtsa bzhi pas gsungs pa/ / me ni dngul chu'i dgra nyid yin te me dang rnam par bral na nam yang dngul chu'i 'ching ba med/ / ma bcings na ni gser byed med de gser dang bral na smra po rnams la longs spyod med pa nyid/ / de bzhin bud med sbyor ba bral na rtag tu rnal 'byor pa rnams dag gi sems ni 'ching mi 'gyur/ / bcings pa med na lus 'bigs med de ma phug lus kyis 'dir ni lhan skyes bde ba ster ba min/[332] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Great Commentary, in the Supreme and Unchanging Gnosis summary, says:
By mudrā consort yoga, instinctual emission is transformed into instinctual nonemission, like mercury and fire. This is spoken of by the Buddha in verse 224 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter of the king of tantras:[337] “Fire is enemy of quicksilver; without fire quicksilver is never bound. Unbound it will not create gold; no gold is of no use to man. Similarly, not in union with a consort, the yogi’s mind is forever unbound. Unbound, his body is not penetrated, a body not penetrated does not grant innate bliss.”[338]

d.div: [331] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 415_na5
[332] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka224_100_ba1
[337] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 415a5.
[338] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud ; ka, v. 224, 100b1.

f.d: des na gang zag gsum char gyi sgom tshul thun mong ba 'di la lnga/ gang du bsgom pa'i gnas dang / lus kyi 'dug stangs dang / lta stangs dang / sgom tshul dngos dang / de las nyams rtags skye tshul lo/ /

Therefore the meditation common to all three types of persons is under five headings: 1. Place of meditation 2. Meditation posture 3. Position of the eyes 4. Actual meditation 5. Signs of accomplishment
dang po [gang du bsgom pa'i gnas ]ni

ye le'i go sla'i don bzhi pa las/
'gyur ba med pa'i bde ba'i 'bras ster phyag rgya bzhi po 'di rnams grong dang 'brog dgon dur khrod dang / / mi gtsang ba dang gtsang ba'i gnas dang khyim dang lha yi khang pa thams cad du ni dus kun du/ / shin tu dga' ba'i dga' ba la gnas 'jig rten lam las rab grol rigs dang rigs min mngon spyod cing / / lus stobs bde ster bza' ba btung ba la sogs longs spyod dang ldan rnal 'byor rnams kyis bsgom par bya/[333] / zhes gsungs pa de lta bu'i gnas gang yang rung ba shin tu dben pa'i gnas su bsgom mo/ /

The “easy to understand” seventy-fourth verse of the Gnosis chapter says:
With these four mudrā consorts giving fruits of unchanging bliss, in towns, in isolation, in cemeteries, in unclean and clean places, in houses, and in temples, at all times in the joy of joys, free from worldly paths, engaging in the accepted and unaccepted, with food and drink giving bodily strength and well-being, the yogi should meditate.[339] The yogi meditates in these places in extreme isolation.

d.div: [333] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka74_109_na1
[339] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud ka, v. 74, 109a1.

f.d: gnyis pa lus kyi 'dug stangs ni
nang gi dmigs pa nyid la brten nas bde ba 'dren pa'i tshe sngar sor bsam gyi lus gnad dang 'dra bas mchog par gsungs pa ltar ro/ /
It is taught that the posture used in withdrawal and meditative absorption when inducing bliss by inner focus is an acceptable posture here.
gsum pa lta stangs ni

lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbu ma'i nang du shar ba'i stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum gyi rnam pa de nyid la rtse gcig tu lta ba yin te/ gsang ba 'dus pa las/
rnal 'byor brtson pas sgrub pa la/ / lha yi gzugs su bsgom par bya/[334] / zhes bsnyen sgrub yan lag bzhi'i sgrub pa rjes dran gyi skabs su lha'i gzugs kyi sku la lta zhing bsgom par gsungs so/ / de yang dngos gzhi'i dus su 'od gsal gyi sems bde ba chen po'i ngo bor skyes pa des lta zhing bsgom pa yin na'ang mig gi lta stangs kyang lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbu ma'i nang du lta ba'i tshul du bya dgos sam snyam mo/ /

The eyes are single-pointedly focused on the empty-form Kālacakra mother and father that has arisen in the central channel at the center of the navel cakra. The Guhyasamāja Tantra says:
The yogi, striving in accomplishment, /446/ meditates on the form of the deity,[340] These lines teach that at the time of the practice of recollection, which is the branch of accomplishment from among the four branches of approximation and accomplishment, the yogi looks at and meditates upon the form of the deity. Although in the actual meditation it is the clear-light mind in the nature of great bliss that looks and meditates, I think the eyes also should be positioned as if they were looking inside the central channel at the navel cakra.

d.div: [334] sde dge_443_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_gsang 'dus rgyud phyi ma/ 155_ba2_tshig sna mi mthun/
[340] Toh 443 Kangyur, rgyud; cha, 155b2.

f.d: bzhi pa sgom tshul dngos ni/

dbang po rno 'bring rtul po'i gang zag gsum gas kyang 'dzin pa'i yan lag mthar phyin pa'i rjes su rgyu rkyen phyi nang gang yang rung ba la brten nas lte ba'i gtum mo 'bar bas byang sems zhu ba'i yas babs mas brtan gyi bde ba chen po drangs te 'od gsal gyi sems bde ba chen po'i ngo bor skyes pa des lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbu ma'i nang du shar ba'i stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam par snang ba de la rtse gcig tu dmigs nas bsgom pa yin la/ de ltar sgom pa'i gnas skabs su stong gzugs kyi skur snang tsam ma gtogs dngos gnas la grub pa med kyang yun bsrings nas bsgoms pas snang tsam de nyid gnas gyur te dngos gnas la grub pa'i stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi skur 'gyur zhing / de'i tshe rjes dran gyi lam dngos gzhi thob par 'jog pa yin no/ /

After the completion of retention, the three kinds of practitioners will ignite the navel caṇḍālī fire by relying on either outer or inner causes. This causes the bodhicitta to melt and to induce the great bliss of descent and stable ascent. The clear-light mind develops into that bliss, focusing and meditating single-pointedly on the empty-form Kālacakra in mother-and-father aspect that has arisen in the central channel at the center of the navel cakra. At this time the empty form in this meditation is only an appearance and not an actuality. However, with prolonged meditation, that appearance is transformed in an actual empty-form Kālacakra mother-and-father deity. This moment represents the attainment of the actual path of recollection.
lnga pa de las nyams rtags skye tshul ni

'dzin pa'i yan lag mthar phyin pa'i rjes su phyi'i rkyen phyag rgya gnyis dang nang gi rkyen lte ba'i d+hU tI'i nang du srog thur bsres pa thig le dang dbyer med du 'dres pa la rtse gcig tu dmigs te bsgoms pas sngar las ches khyad par du 'phags pa'i du ba nas stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum gyi bar gsal bar snang ba tsam dang / gnas skabs de rnams su lte ba'i gtum mo 'bar bas byang sems zhu ba'i yas babs mas brtan gyi dga' bzhi skyes pa rnams ni nyams rtags phal pa yin la/ skabs de'i 'od gsal gyi sems bde ba'i ngo bor skyes pa des stong gzugs yab yum gyi skur snang ba de la rtse gcig tu bltas te bsgoms pas stong gzugs kyi skur snang ba de lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su dngos gnas la grub ba'i dus 'khor yab yum gyi sku'i rnam par gyur te sku de nyid dri ma med pa'i 'od kyi dkyil 'khor dang ldan par gyur cing sku de las byung ba'i 'od zer kha dog lnga byung ba lus rags pa'i ba spu'i khung bu nas 'phro ba dang / dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam pa can gyi sku de las sku de'i rnam pa can mtha' yas pa dngos gnas la grub pa nam mkha'i mthil mtha' dag khyab par spro ba dang / stong gzugs rnams dngos gnas la grub pa nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba ma skyes kyi bar gyi bde ba yas babs dang mas brtan phyag rgya gsum gang la brten nas skyes kyang rjes dran gyi lam dngos dang rjes dran bsgoms pa'i nyams rtags kyi gtso bo yin no/ / 'di rnams kyi shes byed ni stod 'grel sogs kyi don gong du bshad pa rnams so/ /

After the completion of retention, the outer cause of the two mudrā consorts and the inner cause of focusing and meditating single-pointedly on the combined life and downward winds as indivisible from the drop within the dhūtī at the navel cakra will produce signs that are mere appearances but in a more distinct form than previous signs. These range from those of smoke up to the empty-form Kālacakra mother and father. At those times the caṇḍālī fire at the navel blazes and the bodhicitta melts to induce the four joys of descent and stable ascent. These are the ordinary signs. The clear-light mind of that period in the nature of bliss focuses and meditates single-pointedly upon the appearance that is the empty-form Kālacakra mother and father. This causes the empty-form deity appearance to transform into an actual form of a Kālacakra mother-and-father deity, encircled by mandalas of stainless light. From this form /447/ light rays of five colors emerge and emanate through the pores of the coarse physical body. Countless more forms in identical deity aspect emanate as actual phenomena and pervade the reaches of space. The bliss of descent and stable ascent is developed from reliance upon the three kinds of mudrā consorts and experienced from the time of the development of the actual- phenomena empty forms up to the attainment of unchanging bliss. This is the actual path of recollection and the primary signs of accomplishment. The references for this are the passages from the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary and so on, which were explained previously.

'o na yas babs mas brtan gyi bde ba rnams ji lta bu snyam na/ phyag rgya chen mo dngos gnas la grub ste de la rjes su chags pa las byung ba'am/ phyag rgya chen mo ma grub kyang rung ste las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya la brten nas lte ba'i gtum mo khyad par can gyi mes spyi bo'i byang chub kyi sems zhu nas dpral pa'i bar du 'ongs pa dga' ba dang / de nas mgrin pa dang snying ga'i bar du 'ongs pa mchog dga'/ snying ga nas gsang gnas kyi bar du 'ongs pa khyad dga'/ de nas rdo rje nor bu'i rtse'i bar du 'ongs pa lhan cig skyes dga' ste/ dbang mdor bstan las/
mgo bo pad+mar gtsug tor las/ khu ba 'ongs pa dga' ba ste/ / mgrin pa snying gar mchog dga' 'o/ khyad dga'i dga' ba de nas 'gyur/ / sna tshogs dga' ba lte ba dang / / gsang ba'i pad+mar gang 'ongs pa'o/ / gsang gnas rdo rje nor bu'i bar/ / lhan cig skyed dga' mi 'pho ba/[335] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

How is the bliss of descent and stable ascent described? It arises from the creation of and desire for an actual mahāmudrā consort or, if a mahāmudrā consort has not been developed, from reliance upon an activity or wisdom mudrā consort. The special caṇḍālī fire at the navel melts the bodhicitta at the crown, which descends to the forehead, and joy is experienced. Descending to the throat and to the heart, one experiences supreme joy. Falling from the heart to the secret place, one experiences special joy. Arriving at the tip of the jewel, one experiences innate joy. A Short Teaching on Initiations says:
From the crown, the lotus of the head, fluid comes and there is joy; at throat and heart supreme joy. Then comes joy that is special joy, then various joys at the navel and at the secret lotus. From secret place to vajra jewel comes innate joy and the unmoving.[341]

d.div: [335] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_dbang mdor bstan/ 17_na5
[341] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 17a5.

f.d:
gzhan yang bde mchog stod 'grel las/ /
de'i ye shes kyi 'od zer gyis phung po dang khams dang skye mched la sogs pa bsregs te [336] g.yon pa dang g.yas pa'i rtsar son par rnam par shes pa la sogs pa dang sa la sogs pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi rang bzhin rnams gcig tu 'dres par gyur nas dpral bar zla ba'i dkyil 'khor la rab tu zhugs te de nas gtum mo'i ye shes kyi 'od zer gyis zla ba zhu bar gyur pa na gang zhig byang chub kyi sems thig le'i gzugs kyis 'og tu son pa mgrin pa dang snying ga dang lte ba dang gsang ba'i pad+ma_ra dga' ba dang mchog dga' dang dga' bral gyi dga' ba'i rang bzhin dang / ji srid rdo rje nor bu'i mthar lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba'i rang bzhin gyis zhes pa'o/ / yang na rnam pa sna tshogs dang / rnam par smin pa dang / rnam par nyed pa dang / mtshan nyid dang bral ba'i rang bzhin gyis zhes pa'o/[337] / zhes gsungs pa'i don cung zad cig bshad na/ gtum mo nyid la dmigs nas bsgom pa'am/ phyag rgya gsum gang rung la brten nas byung ba'i gtum mo de'i ye shes kyi 'od zer gyis phung khams skye mched la sogs pa bsregs te gtum mo'i drod kyis gdungs pa'i phung khams skye mched de rnams las byung ba'i byang chub kyi sems g.yon pa rkyang ma dang g.yas pa ro ma'i rtsar son pa rnam par shes pa la sogs pa'i phung po lnga dang sa la sogs pa'i khams kyi dkyil 'khor lnga'i rang bzhin gyi byang chub kyi sems rnams dang gcig tu 'dres par gyur nas dpral ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su zla ba'i dkyil 'khor te byang chub kyi sems la rab tu zhugs te/ de nas te de'i rjes su slar yang gtum mo 'bar ba'i ye shesakyi 'od zer gyis dpral ba'i zla ba byang chub kyi sems zhu bar gyur pa na/ byang chub kyi sems thig le'i gzugs kyis 'og tu son pa ste song ba dpral ba nas mgrin par dga' ba dang / mgrin pa nas snying gar mchog dga' dang / snying ga nas lte bar dga' bral gyi dga' ba'i rang bzhin dang / lte ba nas gsang ba'i pad+ma de nas ji srid rdo rje nor bu'i mthar lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba'i rang bzhin no/ / yang na dga' ba bzhi po de la rim pa bzhin rnam pa sna tshogs dang / rnam par smin pa dang / rnam par nyed pa dang / mtshan nyid dang bral ba'i rang bzhin zhes bya'o/ /zhes pa'i don yin no/ /

The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
Light rays of this gnosis burn the aggregates, spheres, sources, and so forth. They travel to the left and right channels, where they combine with the five aggregates of consciousness and so forth and the five mandalas of earth and so forth, and come to reside in the moon mandala at the forehead. Then gnosis light rays melt the moon, and the bodhicitta moves down in the form of a drop. In the lotuses of the throat, heart, navel, and secret place is joy, supreme joy, and joyless joy, /448/ and at the tip of the vajra jewel is innate joy. Also they are of the nature of variety, ripening, rubbing, and being without characteristics.[342] To explain this passage a little, gnosis light rays arise from focusing and meditating on the caṇḍālī fire itself or from the caṇḍālī fire that arises from reliance on one of the three mudrā consorts. These rays proceed to “burn the aggregates, spheres, sources, and so forth,” meaning that these phenomena are scorched by the heat of the caṇḍālī fire. From these aggregates, spheres, and sources arises bodhicitta, which travels to the right and left channels. There it combines with the bodhicitta that is of the nature of the five aggregates of consciousness and so forth and of the nature of the mandalas of the five elements of earth and so forth, and comes to reside in the moon mandala, or bodhicitta, at the center of the forehead cakra. Again the caṇḍālī fire blazes, and its gnosis light rays melt the moon, or bodhicitta, at the forehead. The bodhicitta, in the form of a drop, moves down from the forehead to the throat to produce joy. Moving from the throat to the heart, it produces the supreme joy and from the heart to the navel, joyless joy. Moving from the navel to the secret place and from there to the tip of the vajra jewel, it produces innate joy. Furthermore these four joys “are of the nature of variety, ripening, rubbing, and being without characteristics.”

d.div: [336] ma dper la sogs pa bsrogs te zhes byung yang bsregs te zhes bcos/
[337] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 133_ba3
[342] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 133b3.

f.d:
yang mtshan nyid dang bral ba'i rang bzhin gyis zhes pa'o/ /zhes pa'i mjug gi stod 'grel nyid las/
de ltar cha bcu drug rdzogs pa nor bu'i mthar son pa bsgoms pa'i stobs kyis bde ba ster pa 'dzag pa med pa'i bde ba lta bu ste dpe tsam mo/ / rang gi ngo bos ni dbang po gnyis las skyes par gyur pa'i bde bas mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i bye ba phrag stong gi char yang mi phod do/ / 'dir 'gyur ba med pa'i+i bde ba'i gnas skabs na lhan cig skyes pa'i bde ba'i rang bzhin de ni byis pa'i rang bzhin/ rnal 'byor pa rnams kyis gnas skabs kyi 'bras bur shes par bya'o/[338] / zhes gsungs pa'i don ni de ltar dga' ba bzhir phye ba'i dga' ba bzhi po re re la bzhi bzhir phye ba'i cha bcu drug rdzogs pa byang chub kyi sems rdo rje nor bu'i mthar son pa 'gyur ba med pa bsgoms pa'i stobs kyis bde ba ster ba ste 'gyur ba med pa'i bde ba ni byang sems rdo rje nor bu'i bu ga nas 'dzag pa med pa las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas byung ba'i yas babs kyi bde ba lta bu ste de yang mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba mtshon byed kyi dper bkod pa tsam yin gyi rang gi ngo bo'i sgo nas ni phyogs tsam du yang mtshon par mi nus te/ dbang po gnyis las skyes par gyur pa'i bde bas mi 'gyur pa'i bde ba'i bye ba phrag stong gi char yang mi phod do ste mi phod pa'i phyir ro/ / 'khor lo sdom pa dus 'khor dang mthun par 'chad pa'i skabs 'dir 'gyur ba med pa'i bde ba'i gnas skabs na ste 'gyur med kyi bde ba la ltos na dga' ba bzhi'i nang gi lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba'i rang bzhin de ni byis pa'i rang bzhin dang / rnal 'byor pa rnams kyis gnas skabs kyi 'bras bu rjes dran gyi skabs kyi bde bar shes par bya'o/ /

After this line the text continues:
In this way the sixteen parts are complete. At the tip of the jewel, meditation produces bliss. Such joy of nonemission is only an example. Its nature is bliss born from the two organs and therefore does not come to within even a ten-billionth part of the supreme unchanging bliss. Here, during the time of nonchanging bliss, the innate bliss is that of a child, and yogis should know it as an immediate result.[343] /449/ The meaning of this passage is as follows. The four joys are each divided into four to make sixteen, and “in this way the sixteen parts are complete.” The bodhicitta reaches the tip of the vajra jewel, where it remains, and “meditation produces bliss.” This is the nonchanging bliss of descent arising from the bodhicitta not falling from the opening of the vajra jewel and is produced in reliance upon an activity mudrā consort. Such bliss is only an example presented to illustrate the definitive unchanging bliss. By itself it could not illustrate even a fraction of unchanging bliss, because the “bliss born from the two organs does not come to within even a ten-billionth part of unchanging bliss.” “Here” in the context of explaining Cakrasaṃvara in accord with the Kālacakra, “during the time of nonchanging bliss,” compared to unchanging bliss, the nature of this innate joy of the four joys is that of a child, and yogis should know it as an immediate result of recollection.

d.div: [338] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 133_ba5
[343] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 133b5.

f.d: de ltar na stod 'grel gyi de'i ye shes kyi 'od zer gyis zhes pa nas/ rnal 'byor pa rnams kyis gnas skabs kyi 'bras bur shes par bya'o [339] zhes pa'i bar gyis rjes dran gyi sku grub ste mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba dngos ma skyes pa'i bar gyi ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag skyed pa'i thabs sgom pa'i skabs kyi dga' ba bzhi nyid 'chad pa yin na'ang / mtshan nyid mtshungs pa'i sgo nas dga' bzhi skyed tshul mtha' dag 'dis go bar bya'o/ / de nyid kyi phyir na rtsa rlung la gnad du bsnan pa'am phyag rgya gnyis la brten nas bde ba skyed pa'i tshe lus kyi cha thams cad la gnas pa'i thig le dang por dpral ba'am gtsug tor tu 'dus nas de'i rjes su rdo rje nor bu'i rtsa bar 'bab par shes par bya'o/ /

The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary, from “Light rays of this gnosis” up to “and yogis should know it as an immediate result,” explains the formation of the deity form of recollection and the four joys in the context of meditation methods for developing the branch of meditative concentration, before which the unchanging bliss is not truly developed. Nevertheless all developments of four joys are illustrated by this description because they share similar characteristics. Therefore, whenever bliss is created by targeting the winds and channels of the body or by relying on the two mudrā consorts, the drops that are located in all parts of the body are first gathered at the forehead or crown and then brought down to the channel of the vajra jewel. /450/

d.div: [339] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 133_ba3_dang _133_ba7

f.d: gnyis pa gang zag gsum gyis sgom tshul so sor bshad pa

d.i: The meditations of each type of person

f.d: ['di ]la gsum las/
dang po dbang rnon gyis rjes dran sgom tshul
Recollection meditation for those of high intelligence
['di ]la gnyis/ rjes dran gyi sku 'thob phyir du sgom pa'i tshul dang / sku de thob nas rjes su sgom pa'i tshul lo/ /
is under two headings: 1. Meditation for attaining the recollection deity form 2. Meditation after attaining the recollection deity form
dang po [rjes dran gyi sku 'thob phyir du sgom pa'i tshul ]ni+i

d.i: Meditation for attaining the recollection deity form

f.d: bsgom pa'i gnas lus gnad lta stangs rnams thun mong gi skabs su bshad pa ltar yin zhing / dmigs pa la 'jog tshul ni 'dzin pa mthar phyin pa'i rjes su gtso bor lte bar srog thur bsres pas lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su gtum mo'i me 'bar ba'i 'od kyis snang bar byas pa'i stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi skur snang ba tsam de la rtse gcig tu dmigs nas yang yang bsgom zhing de la bogs dbyung ba'i phyir phyag rgya gnyis la yang brten nas gtum mo khyad par can spar te lhan skyes kyi bde ba drangs nas bde ba de'i ngo bor skyes pa'i 'od gsal gyi sems des rang la gsal bar snang ba'i stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum gyi sku'i snang ba de la rtse gcig tu gzhag nas yang yang bsgoms pas ji zhig ltar la sku de'i snang ba je dag la song ste dngos gnas la grub pa'i stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam pa can gyi rjes dran gyi skur 'gyur ba yin zhing sku de las stong gsum gang ba'i sku mtha' yas pa spros pa snams kyang dngos gnas la grub pa'i rjes dran gyi sku yin no/ /

The meditation place, meditation posture, and position of eyes are as explained in the above section on the common meditation. After the accomplishment of the branch of retention, the life and downward winds are combined at the navel, and so mental placement is primarily a single-pointed focus on the empty-form Kālacakra mother-and-father as just an appearance illumined by the light of the caṇḍālī fire in the center of the navel cakra. Constant meditation on this form, together with enhancement by relying on the two types of mudrā consorts, will ignite the special caṇḍālī fire and generate innate bliss. Clear-light mind is developed into the nature of this bliss and placed one-pointedly into the empty-form Kālacakra mother-and-father deity that vividly appears before it. This is meditated on again and again, and as much as that is undertaken, the appearance of that deity form becomes progressively purer, finally developing into an actual empty form in the aspect of Kālacakra mother and father. This is the recollection body. From that form countless bodies emanate to fill the three realms. These are also actual recollection bodies.
gnyis pa sku de thob rjes su sgom pa'i tshul ni/

d.i: Meditation after attaining the recollection deity form

f.d: stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus dang / stong gsum ma lus par khyab par dngos gnas la grub pa rjes dran gyi sku'i mtshan nyid tshang bar gyur pa de'i tshe de lta bu'i phyi nang gi dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam pa can thams cad rnal 'byor pa rang nyid dang rgyud gcig pa nyid yin pas yang dus kyi 'khor lo'i rnam pa can rnams kyis yum sna tshogs yum gyi rnam pa can rnams la rjes su chags pa'i sgo nas snyoms 'jug byed pa'i tshul la rtse gcig tu mnyam par bzhag ste yang yang goms par byas pas nam zhig na rnal 'byor ba rang gi lus rags pa 'di'i cha shas la gnas pa'i khams byang chub kyi sems rnams dang por dpral ba'i rtsa 'khor du 'dus te de nas rim gyis rdo rje nor bu'i mthar son pa las dga' ba bcu drug mtshon pa'i mthar khams dkar po nor bu'i rtser sleb pa dang de dang dus mnyam du dmar cha gtsug tor du gnas pa gnyis gnas gzhan du mi 'gyur bar de nyid du brtan par gnas pa'i thig le de las byung ba'i brtan pa mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skad cig ma gcig skyes pa na ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag dngos gzhi thob par 'jog pa yin pas dga' ba bzhi 'am cha bcu drug pa'i cha dang po yan chad rjes dran gyi lam du 'jog pa yin no/ /

The empty-form Kālacakras in the aspect of mother-and-father embrace, both that dwelling in the center of the navel cakra and those pervading the three realms, have become actual phenomena and definitive recollection forms. All these outer and inner Kālacakra mother-and-father forms are of the same mental continuum as the yogi and, therefore, by way of attraction to the consort in the form of Viśvamātā, these Kālacakra forms enter into union. Meditative equipoise is held single-pointedly on this union, and after repeated meditation, the yogi arrives at a point when the bodhicitta elements located within parts of the gross body gather at the forehead cakra and gradually travel to the vajra jewel, from which arises the sixteen joys. /451/ As the white element arrives at the tip of the jewel, the red element arrives at the crown. These two do not move elsewhere and are firmly located in their respective places. From these drops an instance of the stable supreme and unchanging bliss arises. This is an indication of the actual attainment of the branch of meditative concentration. Therefore the path from the first of the four or sixteen joys onward is established as being the path of recollection.

'o na dbang rnon gyis rjes dran gyi sku grub pa'i rjes su phyag rgya gzhan gnyis bsten mi dgos par phyag rgya chen po kho na la brten pas chog gam snyam na/ 'di la kha cig/ dbang po rnon pos 'dzin pa'i yan lag mthar phyin pa na 'dzin pa'i ting nge 'dzin la mnyam par bzhag pa de nyid kyi ngang nas bar ma chad par rjes dran gyi skur dngos su ldang bar nus shing de'i tshe stong gzugs kyi sna tshogs yum dang mnyam par sbyar bas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'dren nus pa la/ zhes dbang rnon gyis 'dzin pa'i ting nge 'dzin la mnyam par bzhag pa'i mnyam gzhag thun gcig pu de la rjes dran mthar phyin te teng nge 'dzin gyi yan lag mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'thob par 'dod cing / 'dzin pa'i yan lag mthar phyin pa'i dbang rnon rjes dran sgrub pa'i skabs dang grub nas kyang las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya la mi brten par 'dod do/ /

It may be thought that the yogi of high intelligence, after the attainment of the recollection body, only needs to rely upon the mahāmudrā consort and has no need of the other two types of consort. On this point some say that after completing the branch of retention, the intelligent yogi has the ability to actually raise the recollection body from within the equipoise of the meditative concentration of retention without break or interruption to the session, and to induce the unchanging bliss at that time by entering in union with the empty-form Viśvamātā. Therefore they assert that recollection can be completed within the one continuous meditation session of the meditative concentration of retention, and that the unchanging bliss of the branch of meditative concentration can also be attained in that session. They also maintain that the yogi of high intelligence, while developing the recollection form, and even after it has been developed, does not rely upon activity and wisdom mudrā consorts.

'di ni mi 'thad de/ 'dzin pa mthar phyin pa'i rjes su rjes dran gyi sku 'thob pa'i phyir du gtum mo dang / las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya la brten pa sogs du ma la slob dgos pa'i phyir na 'dzin pa'i mnyam gzhag thun gcig pu de la rjes dran mthar phyin te teng nge 'dzin gyi yan lag thob pa ji ltar 'ong ste mi 'ong ngo / / dbang rnon rjes dran sgrub pa'i skabs su las kyi phyag rgya la brten pa ni gong du drangs pa ltar/
rgyal ba'i lhan skyes bde ba 'di ni 'phel ba'i don slad dang por las kyi phyag rgya bsten par bya/ / zhes 'dzin pa mthar phyin nas rjes dran sgrub pa'i skabs su las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas gtum mo 'bar bas byang sems zhu ba'i bde ba chen pos stong gzugs rjes mthun pa la rtse gcig tu bzhag nas bsgoms pas de nas te de'i rjes nyid du stong gzugs mtshan nyid pa dus 'khor yab yum gyi sku dngos gnas la grub pa dang / de'i tshe phyag rgya chen mo khams 'pho ba med pa'i bde ba skyed par byed ma dngos gnas la grub par ston pa ni/
de nas nyi ma'i gzugs ni lus dang gdong dang rkang pa gtsug tor yan lag thams cad rdzogs pa ste/ / glog gi dbyug pa'i rjes mthun 'pho med bde ba skyed bar byed ma mtshan nyid yan lag rab tu rdzogs/[340] / zhes pa ste don ni bshad zin pa ltar ro/ /

This is not correct. After the completion of retention it is necessary to train in caṇḍālī fire practice, to rely on activity and wisdom consorts, and to undertake many other practices in order to attain the recollection body. Therefore how would it be possible to complete recollection and attain meditative concentration in one continuous session of retention meditation? The yogi of high intelligence, when developing recollection, relies upon an activity mudrā consort as previously quoted in the Condensed Tantra:
To increase this innate bliss of the conqueror, first rely upon an activity mudrā consort. Therefore, after the completion of retention and during the development of recollection, an activity mudrā consort is used. This causes the caṇḍālī fire to ignite, which melts the bodhicitta to produce great bliss, which is then single-pointedly placed on the similitude empty form. With repeated meditation a definitive and actual empty-form Kālacakra mother-and-father form is achieved. /452/ At that time a mahāmudrā consort, the creator of the bliss of the unmoving element, is created as an actual phenomenon. This is taught by the following lines, which have been explained previously:
Then create the sun form, with body, face, legs, crown, all limbs complete; in a flash of lightning resemblance, arises a definitive creator of unmoving bliss, all features complete.[344]

d.div: [340] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka73_108_ba7
[344] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 73, 108b7.

f.d:
der yang ma zad dbang rnon gyis rjes dran gyi sku grub pa'i rjes su yang las kyi phyag rgya la brten pa ni ye le'i brgya nyer gcig pa'i 'grel chen las/
phyag rgya rab tu 'grogs la sems zhes pa gzugs la rjes su chags pa byang chub kyi sems zhu ba dang / mchog gi bde ba la gnas rdo rje yang dag bslang ba yang gsum pa thugs kyi zhal lo/ / ci ste gzugs kyi sgo nas dga' bar ma gyur na de'i tshe pad+mar rdo rje'i sgra 'am zhes pa dal bu dag gis bya'o/ / ci ste bud med ma rnyed na de'i tshe rang gi lag pa'i pad+mas gsor bar bya'o/ / bde ba 'phel ba'i slad du ste ltung ba'i slad du ni ma yin no/[341] / zhes rjes dran gyi stong gzugs dngos gnas la grub pa'i rjes su stong gzugs sna tshogs yum la rjes su chags par byas pa las khams byang chub kyi sems zhu ba dang / de la brten nas mchog gi bde ba la gnas pa dang / rjes chags de la brten nas rdo rje bslang ba rnams rdo rje bzhi'i nang gi gsum pa thugs kyi zhal te thugs rdo rje rjes dran gyi skabs kyi yin pa dang / de'i tshe ci ste de lta bu'i stong gzugs la rjes chags byas kyang gzugs kyi sgo nas dga' bar te dga' ba skyes par ma gyur na de'i tshe las kyi phyag rgya'i pad+mar rdo rje'i sgra 'am zhes pa rdo rje dal bus bskyod nas bde ba 'dren par bshad pa'i phyir ro/ /

Furthermore the yogi of high intelligence relies upon the activity mudrā consort even after the attainment of the recollection form. The Great Commentary, on verse 121 of the Gnosis chapter, states:
“Mind in closeness to the mudrā” means that from desire for the form, the bodhicitta melts, the yogi abides in supreme bliss, and the vajra is raised. This is the third, the face of the mind. If joy is not realized through the use of form, at that time “use the sound of the vajra in the lotus,” which means to move it slowly. If a girl is not found, then penetrate the lotus of the hand. This is to done to increase bliss and not to create a downfall.[345] Therefore, after the development of an actual recollection empty form, the yogi desires the empty-form Viśvamātā. From this “the bodhicitta melts, the yogi abides in supreme bliss,” and because of the desire, “the vajra is raised.” This represents the third of the four vajras, which is Kālacakra’s “face of the mind,” or the mind vajra of recollection. If at this time the yogi has great desire for this empty form but joy is not generated through reliance on this empty form, “use the sound of the vajra in the lotus” of an activity mudrā consort, which means to generate the bliss by moving the vajra slowly in the lotus of an activity mudrā.

d.div: [341] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 390_ba7
[345] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 390b7.

f.d:
gal te 'di dag rjes dran gyi stong gzugs mtshan nyid pa 'thob pa'i skabs la dgongs pa ma yin no snyam na/ 'di dag rjes dran dang rjes dran thob nas ting nge 'dzin sgrub pa'i skabs yin te|_thugs kyi zhal lo zhes dang ltung ba'i slad du ni ma yin no/ /zhes pa'i mjug nyid du/
de ltar sa bon gtong ba min pa'i bde ba de ni 'chi ba'i 'jigs 'phrog tu 'gyur zhing 'di ni dpal ldan bla ma'i zhal bzhi pa ste ye shes rdo rje'o zhes pa rnal 'byor goms pa'i nges pa'o/ / zhes ye shes rdo rjer gsungs shing / ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag rdo rje bzhi'i ye shes rdo rjer gsungs pas so/ /

If it is thought that this passage is not about the attainment of the definitive recollection body, then it should be known that this passage is in the section that comments on recollection as well as on the attainment of meditative concentration following the achievement of recollection, for the passage continues:
This bliss of not expelling the seed destroys the fear of death and is the fourth face of the guru, or the gnosis vajra. This is a confirmation of the yoga meditations. /453/ This passage talks of the gnosis vajra and, of the four vajras, the branch of meditative concentration has been taught as the gnosis vajra.

gal te 'di dag rjes dran thob rjes kyi skabs yin du chug kyang dbang rtul gyis las kyi phyag rgya la brten dgos pa la dgongs pa yin no snyam na/ de ni ma yin te/ skabs 'di'i rgyud 'grel pa dang bcas pa ni dmigs bsal 'chad pa'i skabs ma yin par lam gyi gzhung zhing 'chad pa'i skabs yin zhing / lam gyi gzhung zhing rnams ni rgyud kyi ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo'i dbang du byas nas 'chad pa yin la/ rgyud kyi ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo ni dbang rnon nyid yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

It could be thought that this may indeed be a passage on the attainment and postattainment of recollection but that it is a teaching on the need for the yogi of low intelligence to rely upon an activity mudrā consort. That would not be correct, because this is not a section in which the tantra and the commentary are teaching for any particular type of person but a section that explains the central tenets of the path. The central tenets of the path are taught for the primary intended disciples of the tantra, and the primary intended disciples of the tantra are those of high intelligence.

gzhan yang sgrub le'i brgya nyi shu pa'i 'grel chen las/
shes rab la spros zla ba thig le zhes pa la 'dir shes rab la chags pas spros pa 'di zla ba thig le yin pa ni la spros zla ba theg le ste shes rab la spros pa'i byang chub kyi sems kyi thig le yang rdo rje nor bur gnas pa de'i gsang ba dang lte ba dang snying gar 'gyur med gsum du gyur pa gang yin pa de ni sgrub pa la zhes pa gsum pa sgrub pa'i yan lag la 'gyur ro/ / de ltar sgrub pa'i yan lag bya'o/[342] / zhes rdzogs rim gyi sgrub pa'i yan lag gi skabs 'dir las kyi phyag rgya'i shes rab ma la spros pa'i byang chub kyi sems rdo rje nor bur gnas pa gsang gnas lte ba snying gar drangs pa'i 'gyur med 'dzag med gsum du gyur pa'i mas brtan gyi bde ba bskyed par bshad cing / rdzogs rim gyi bsnyen sgrub yan lag bzhi'i sgrub pa rjes dran nyid la 'jog la/ rgyud 'grel pa dang bcas pa 'di dag kyang lam gyi gzhung zhing nyid 'chad byed yin pas so/ /

Furthermore the Great Commentary, on verse 120 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
Concerning the line beginning “Moved toward the wisdom, the moon drop,” the movement refers to that of the moon drop, whose movement is generated by desire for the wisdom. The moon drop is the bodhicitta drop, which moves to the wisdom but remains in the vajra. Of that, the three nonchanging at the secret area, the navel, and the heart represent accomplishment. This is the third branch known as accomplishment. Practice accomplishment in this way.[346] Therefore, in this section on the branch of completion-stage accomplishment, the bodhicitta, which moves toward the activity mudrā consort, stays in the vajra, thereby inducing the bliss of stable ascent that is the three nonchanging or nondescending states at the secret area, navel, and heart. Moreover, among the four branches of approximation and accomplishment, the branch of accomplishment is established as being recollection. These tantra and commentary passages also explain the central tenets of the path.

d.div: [342] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 238_ba5
[346] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 238b5.

f.d:
gzhan yang / yid ni nang du chud pa yis/ / 'dod pa'i dngos grub bsgom par bya/ / zhes pa'i bde mchog stod 'grel las/
'dir rdo rje nor bu'i nang du gnas pa'i byang chub kyi sems la yid ni nang du chud pa zhes brjod do/ / yid nang du chud pas 'dzag pa med pa'i byang chub kyi sems des las kyi phyag rgya'am ye shes kyi phyag rgya dang 'grogs pa na khams gsum pa'i mtshan nyid sangs rgyas kyi gzugs su bsgom par bya'o zhes pa khams gsum pa 'dod pa dang gzugs dang gzugs med pa'i mtshan nyid brtan pa dang g.yo ba dang dngos po dang dngos po med pa'i rang bzhin rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa'i bdag nyid ma lus par rnal 'byor pas bsgom par bya'o/ / de nyid shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa'o/[343] / zhes rdo rje nor bur byang chub kyi sems 'dzag med du 'ching nus pa na las kyi phyag rgya dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya dang 'grogs te bde chen drangs nas bde ba chen po des khams gsum pa'i mtshan nyid stong gzugs sangs rgyas thams cad kyi gzugs su shar ba de la rtse gcig tu dmigs nas bsgom par bya'o zhes pa'o/ /

Furthermore the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary, on the lines “With the mind placed inside, meditate upon the siddhi of desire,” says:
The bodhicitta dwelling in the vajra jewel is spoken of as the “mind placed inside.” With the mind placed inside, this nonemitting bodhicitta associates with an activity mudrā or wisdom mudrā, and the characteristics of the three-realm world are meditated on as forms of the Buddha. The three-realm world refers to the animate and inanimate characteristics of the desire, form, and formless realms, /454/ and to functional and nonfunctional phenomena, all of which are possessed of supreme characteristics. They are wisdom gone beyond, possessed of supreme characteristics. On all these the yogi meditates.[347] Therefore, when one has the ability to hold the bodhicitta within the vajra jewel without emission, one associates with activity or wisdom mudrā consorts and induces the great bliss. Because of this great bliss the characteristics of the three-realm world appear as the forms of all buddhas in empty form. These are single-pointedly focused upon.

d.div: [343] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 124_na4
[347] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 124a4.

f.d: de yang khams gsum pa zhes sogs rgyas par 'chad pa ni/ khams gsum pa 'dod pa dang zhes pa nas rnal 'byor pas bsgom par bya'o zhes pa'i bar yin la/ de ltar las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya la brten nas drangs pa'i bde ba chen pos stong gzugs la rtse gcig tu dmigs pa'i stong gzugs de nyid ni shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa'i stong gzugs dngos gnas la grub pa'o zhes pa'i don yin pas gang zag dbang po rab 'bring rtul po gsum gas yan lag dang po lnga'i gnas skabs dang khyad par du yang rjes dran gyi skabs su las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya la brten nas bde ba skyed dgos par grub pa yin no/ /

A more detailed explanation of the “three-realm world” follows from the sentence beginning “The three-realm world refers to” up to the sentence “On all these the yogi meditates.” The bliss induced by reliance upon activity and wisdom mudrā consorts is single-pointedly focused on empty forms. These empty forms are “wisdoms gone beyond” and are actual empty forms “possessed of supreme characteristics.” This is the meaning of the above passage, and therefore it can be established that all three kinds of yogis, of sharp, middling, and dull intelligence, when on the first five branches, and especially on the branch of recollection, have to generate bliss by relying upon activity and wisdom mudrā consorts.

gzhan yang / 'dod pa'i dngos grub bsgom par bya/ / zhes pa'i 'grel par/
'dir 'dod pa ni 'dod chags chen po'o/ / rdo rje sems dpa' don chen po mchog tu mi 'gyur pa'o/[344] / zhes 'dod pa'i don mchog mi 'gyur gyi bde ba la bshad cing / de'i mjug thogs nyid du/
dngos grub ni phyag rgya chen po shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa'o/[345] / zhes dngos grub kyi don stong gzugs la bshad nas/ stong gzugs de la rnam pa gnyis su gsungs pa ni 'grel pa'i 'phro de nyid las/
'di nyid sgom pa rnam pa gnyis te sngon du gzugs brnyan sgom pa dang phyi nas gzugs brnyan sgom pa'o/ / sngon du gzugs brnyan sgom pa ni du ba la sogs pa'i mtshan ma gzugs brnyan gyi mthar thug par sgom pa'o/[346] /zhes sngon du gzugs brnyan sgom pa sor bsam gyi skabs kyi du sogs nas du ma longs spyod rdzogs pa'i gzugs brnyan sgom pa'i bar la gsungs shing / de'i mjug nyid du/
phyi nas sgom pa ni gzugs brnyan mthong ba na b+ha gar ling+ga rab tu bkod de mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'phel ba'i don du sgom pa'o/[347] / zhes phyi nas sgom pa rjes dran gyi skabs su sgom pa la mdzad nas/ rjes dran gyi skabs kyi stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi sku dngos gnas la grub pa'i gzugs brnyan mthong ba na las kyi phyag rgya'i b+ha gar rnal 'byor ba'i ling+ga rab tu bkod de bde ba chen po bsgom par bya'o/ / dgos pa ci'i don du sgom pa ni ting nge 'dzin gyi gnas skabs kyi mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba bskyed cing 'phel ba'i don du sgom pa'o/ /zhes pa'i don yin no/ /

Furthermore the commentary on the line “meditate upon the siddhi of desire” runs:
Here “desire” is great desire, is Vajrasattva, of great significance, supreme and unchanging.[348] Therefore “desire” is explained as being the supreme and unchanging bliss. The passage continues:
“Siddhi” is the mahāmudrā, the wisdom gone beyond, possessed of supreme characteristics.[349] “Siddhi” is explained as meaning empty form. This empty form is said to be of two kinds. The commentary continues:
The meditation is of two kinds: earlier meditation on images and later meditation on images. The earlier meditation is the complete meditation on the signs of smoke and so forth.[350] Therefore the earlier meditation refers to those during withdrawal and meditative absorption on images ranging from those of smoke and so forth up to the manifold saṃbhogakāya images. The commentary continues:
Concerning the later meditation, when the image is seen, the liṅgam is placed in the bhaga, /455/ and meditation is performed in order to increase the supreme and unchanging bliss.[351] The later meditation is asserted as being a recollection meditation, and when the image of an actual entity empty-form Kālacakra mother and father of the branch of recollection is seen, the liṅgam of the yogi is placed in the bhaga of an activity mudrā consort, and the yogi meditates upon great bliss. The purpose of this meditation is to develop and increase the supreme and unchanging bliss of the branch of meditative concentration.
