f.d:
yang de'i mjug nyid du/
slar yang bde ba chen po 'phel ba'i phyir las kyi phyag rgya dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya yongs su spangs te phyag rgya chen po bsgom par bya'o/ / 'dir las kyi phyag rgya dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya sgom pa dgag pa ni bcom ldan 'das kyis mchog gi dang po'i sangs rgyas stong phrag bcu gnyis par gsungs so/ / de ltar yang bcom ldan 'das kyis gsungs pa/
las kyi phyag rgya yongs dor cing/ / ye shes phyag rgya rnam spangs te/ / mchog tu mi 'gyur rnal 'byor gyis/ / phyag rgya chen po rnam bsgom bya/[348] / zhes las kyi phyag rgya dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya gnyis la brten nas bde ba chen po sgom pa de las slar yang ting nge 'dzin gyi skabs su mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'phel ba'i phyir du las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya gnyis yongs su spangs te phyag rgya chen po sgom pa ste phyag rgya chen mo nyid la rjes chags kyi rnam pas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba drangs te bsgom par bya'o/ / mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba dngos su 'dren nus pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi lam sgom pa'i skabs 'dir las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya gnyis sgom pa dgag pa'i shes byed ni/ bcom ldan 'das zhes pa nas/ phyag rgya chen po rnam bsgom bya/ /zhes pa'i bar ro/ /

The commentary continues:
Again, to increase the great bliss, the activity mudrā consort and the wisdom mudrā consort are abandoned for meditation on a mahāmudrā consort. Here the abandoning of the activity mudrā consort and the wisdom mudrā consort was spoken of by the Conqueror in the twelve-thousand-verse Supreme Original Buddha:
“Activity mudrā is left behind, wisdom mudrā is abandoned; with supreme unchanging yoga meditate upon the mahāmudrā.”[352] By relying on activity and wisdom mudrā consorts, the yogi meditates on great bliss. “Again, to increase the great bliss,” or unchanging bliss, during the branch of meditative concentration, “the activity mudrā consort and the wisdom mudrā consort are abandoned for meditation on a mahāmudrā consort.” This means inducing the unchanging bliss by meditating on desire for the mahāmudrā consort. The authority for the assertion that in the meditations of the path of meditative concentration, which has the ability to develop the actual unchanging bliss, all meditations on activity and wisdom mudrās are abandoned is stated in the lines beginning “was spoken of by the Conqueror” up to “meditate upon the mahāmudrā.”

d.div: [348] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 124_ba5
[352] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 124b6.

f.d: de ltar na dbang po rab 'bring tha ma gsum char gyis gtso bor brten mi brten gyi khyad par ma gtogs phyag rgya chen mo nyid la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po 'dren mi nus kyi bar la las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya gnyis ka la brten nas yas babs dang mas brtan gyi dga' ba bzhi bskyed de bde stong sbyor ba dang / rjes dran gyi sku stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi sku dngos gnas la grub nas ni de lta bu'i dga' bzhi skyes pa'i tshe 'od gsal gyi sems bde ba chen po'i ngo bor skyes pa des rang dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam pa can snyoms 'jug byed pa la rjes su chags pa'i rnam pa nyid sgom par byed pa yin no/ / de ltar bsgoms pas nam zhig na stong gzugs phyag rgya chen mo sna tshogs yum nyid la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po skyed nus par 'gyur ro/ / de ltar na rgyud 'grel nas gsungs pa ltar gyi las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya gnyis bsten dgos pa dang spang dgos pa'i sa tshigs shes par bya dgos so/ /

Therefore, with the only difference between them being their consort of primary reliance, yogis of sharp, middling, and low intelligence will rely upon activity and wisdom mudrā consorts, generating the four joys of descent and stable ascent and applying that bliss to emptiness until they are able to induce great unchanging bliss through the mahāmudrā consort. /456/ They develop the recollection body, which is an actual entity of an empty-form Kālacakra mother and father, and during the four joys, the mind of clear light develops into the entity of the bliss and takes on the aspect of desire for union between oneself as Kālacakra and his consort. Meditating in this way will eventually create the ability to generate great unchanging bliss through reliance on the empty-form mahāmudrā Viśvamātā. Therefore one must know when to rely on and when to abandon the activity and wisdom mudras, as taught in the tantra and commentaries.
gnyis pa dbang 'bring dang dbang rtul gnyis kyis rjes dran sgom tshul ni

d.i: Recollection meditation for yogis of middling and low intelligence

f.d: 'di gnyis kas rjes dran gyi sku thob phyir du sgom pa dang sku de thob rjes su sgom pa gnyis ka yang phal che ba dbang rnon gyi sgom tshul dang 'dra zhing / khyad par ni dbang 'bring gis gtum mo sbar nas yas babs mas brtan gyi bde ba 'dren pa gtso bor ye shes kyi phyag rgya nyid la brten nas byed pa dang / dbang rtul gyis gtso bor las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas byed pa yin no/ / de yang gang zag gsum kas rjes dran gyi sku thob phyir du sgom pa'i tshe 'dzin pa mthar phyin pa'i rjes su rang rang gi bde ba chen po 'dren pa'i rgyu'i gtso bo gsum la brten nas yas babs dang mas brtan gyi bde ba chen po bskyed de 'od gsal gyi sems bde ba chen po'i ngo bor skyes pa des rang dus su lte ba'i d+hU tI'i nang du rnal 'byor pa rang nyid stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi skur ma bcos ma btags par shar ba de la rtse gcig tu dmigs nas yang yang bsgoms pas mthar dus 'khor yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam par snang ba'i stong gzugs rjes mthun pa de nyid dngos gnas la grub pa'i stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can gyi rjes dran gyi skur 'gyur ba yin gyi/

The meditations for developing the recollection body and the meditations following its development are basically the same as those of the yogi of high intelligence. The difference is that the yogi of middling intelligence relies mainly on the wisdom mudrā consort for inducing the bliss of descent and stable ascent that arises from igniting the caṇḍālī fire, whereas the yogi of low intelligence relies mainly on the activity mudrā consort. All three types of yogis, when meditating for the achievement of the recollection body upon the completion of retention, will rely upon their own primary methods for creating great bliss, which will generate the great bliss of descent and stable ascent. The clear-light mind develops into the entity of great bliss, focusing and meditating single-pointedly again and again on the empty-form Kālacakra mother and father in whose aspect the yogi has appeared, unimputed and unconceived in the dhūtī at the navel cakra. Finally that similitude empty form in its aspect of Kālacakra in mother-and-father embrace becomes an actual empty-form Kālacakra in mother-and-father embrace.

kha cig gi 'khrid yig las/ gtum mo 'bar bas bde ba drangs pa'i bde stong gi ngang nas rjes dran gyi skur ldang ba'i 'phen pa dang bcas te bsgom [349] zhes bkod pa ni dpal gsang ba 'dus pa sogs nas bde stong ngam 'od gsal gyi ngang nas sgyu lus su ldang ba'i 'phen pa dang bcas te sgyu lus kyi skur dngos su ldang ba'i rigs pa sbyar ba yin pa 'dra na'ang / de gnyis ni mi 'dra ste/ 'dus pa sogs nas bshad pa ni bde stong ngam 'od gsal stong nyid dang sbyar ba'i ngang nas 'od gsal gyi bzhon pa'i rlung phra ba de nyid las sgyu ma'i skur ldang ba yin la/ skabs 'di'i stong gzugs kyi sku ni sor bsam gyi skabs su shar ba'i stong gzugs kyi snang ba de nyid srog 'dzin sogs kyi lam gyis sbyangs nas stong gzugs kyi sku'i snang ba de nyid je dag tu song ba las bsgrubs pa yin pas so/ /

In some instruction texts it is written that the caṇḍālī fire blazes, induces bliss, and from within the state of bliss and emptiness, one meditates to impel[353] the arising of the recollection body.[354] This seems to be applying here to the process found in the Guhyasamāja and other tantras, wherein one impels the arising of an illusory body from within either the state of bliss and emptiness or the state of clear light. /457/ However these two are not similar. The explanation from the Guhyasamāja and other tantras is that within bliss and emptiness, or within the clear-light mind applied to emptiness, the illusory body develops from the subtle wind that acts as a mount for the clear-light mind. However the empty-form body taught here is an empty form whose appearance first arose during withdrawal and meditative absorption, was then prepared by the paths of prāṇāyāma, retention, and so on, and whose attainment is accomplished by the gradual purification process of that empty-form body.

d.div: [349] 'phrid yig 'di ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[353] ’phen pa. To throw, cast.
[354] Unable to trace text.

f.d:
yang dbye ba 'chad pa'i skabs su gang zag gsum pa'i dbang po rab phyag rgya chen mo ri rab kyi rdul dang mnyam pa la snyoms par 'jug pa dang / 'bring ye shes kyi phyag rgya dkyil 'khor gyi lha mo'i grangs dang mnyam pa la snyoms par 'jug pa dang / dbang po dman pa las kyi phyag rgya dang snyoms par 'jug par bshad pa rnams ni rjes dran gyi sku grub nas rjes dran gyi lam la slob pa'i tshul yin la/ de yang rje bu dang rje rin po che'i dgongs par bsam pa'i 'khrid yig kha cig las dbye ba 'chad pa'i skabs su dbang po rab phyag rgya chen mo ri rab kyi rdul dang mnyam pa la snyoms par 'jug pa dang zhes gsum du phye nas [350] 'khrid yig de las/
de nas nam mkha'i khams khyab pa'i stong gzugs thams cad nus ma bcu la sogs pa'i rnam par bsgyur ba dang /[351] gzhan yang ri rab kyi rdul phra rab kyi grangs dang mnyam pa'i phyag rgya rnams sngar bzhin bsgyur nas snyoms par zhugs te mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba sngar ltar bskyedces pa tsam zhig bshad la/ rje bus [352] phyag rgya chen mo la snyoms 'jug byed tshul gsal bar ma gsungs so/ /

In the explanations on the divisions of recollection, the explanation that those of sharp intelligence enter into union with as many mahāmudrā consorts as there are atoms in Mount Meru, that those of a middling intelligence enter into union with as many wisdom mudrā consorts as there are goddesses in the mandala, and that those of low intelligence enter into union with activity mudras, are ways of practicing the path of recollection after the recollection body has been attained. On the topic of union with a mahāmudrā consort, one instruction manual that claims to follow Butön Rinpoché and Jé Rinpoché divides recollection up into three divisions and then says:[355]
Then the empty forms that pervade space transform into the ten śaktis and so forth. Also mahāmudrā consorts as many as there are atoms in Mount Meru transform, enter into union, and create unchanging bliss as before. This is all that is written on the subject, and Butön Rinpoché himself does not elucidate on union with a mahāmudrā consort.

d.div: [350] bu ston rin chen grub/ gsung 'bum pod/ ga_rjes dran gyi khrid yig2_ba3
[351] bu ston rin chen grub/ gsung 'bum pod/ ga_rjes dran gyi khrid yig4_na4_tshig ji bzhin mi gsal/
[352] ma dper rje dus phyag rgya chen mo la zhes byung yang rje bus zhes bcos/
[355] Collected Works, vol. ga, Six Yogas: Recollection Manual, 2b4.

f.d: 'on kyang dwogs pa'i gnas cung zad cig dpyad na/ 'on te phyag rgya chen mo la snyoms 'jug byed pa'i tshul ji lta bu yin/ rnal 'byor pa rang gi lus rags pa 'dis byed pa yin nam/ gal te stong gzugs yab yum gyi rnam pa can gyi yab tu rnal 'byor pa rang nyid gyur pa des snyoms par 'jug pa ji ltar yin snyam na/ dang po de ni ma yin te/ stong gzugs sna tshogs yum gyi rnam pa can gyi yum de ni sgrib thogs med pa'i 'ja' lus kyi sku yin pas rnam smin gyi lus rags pa'i des snyoms 'jug byed pa 'ong don med pas phyi ma ltar yin la/ de yang rnal 'byor pa rang nyid dus 'khor yab yum gyi skur gyur pa stong gsum khyab par spros pa'i yum phyag rgya chen mo ri rab kyi rdul gyi grangs dang mnyam pa la rang nyid dus kyi 'khor lo yab kyi rnam pa can du gyur pa ri rab kyi rdul gyi grangs dang mnyam pas snyoms par 'jug pa ni dbang rnon phyag rgya chen mo ri rab kyi rdul dang mnyam pa la snyoms par 'jug pa'i don yin no/ / de ltar snyoms 'jug byas pa las khams zhu ba'i bde ba skye ba'i tshul ni rnal 'byor pa rang nyid dus 'khor yab yum gyi stong gzugs su gyur pa rnams snyoms 'jug byed tshul la dmigs nas rjes chags la rtse gcig tu gnas pas lus rags pa 'di'i spyi+i bo nas dpral ba dang de nas mgrin pa sogs nas rdo rje nor bu'i rtse bar babs pa'i dga' ba bzhi dang bcu drug sogs skye ba yin no/ /

So this should be examined a little. How is union with a mahāmudrā consort achieved? Does the yogi achieve it with his gross body, or does he enter into union as the father of the empty-form father-and-mother aspect? It cannot be the former because the mother in the aspect of empty-form Viśvamātā is in the form of an unobscured and unobstructed rainbow body, and entering into such a union with one’s coarse body would not be possible. Therefore the latter is correct. /458/ The yogi in the form of Kālacakra mother and father has emanated to pervade the three realms. The mother mahāmudrā consorts of that union numbering as many as the number of atoms in Mount Meru and the yogi in the aspect of the Kālacakra father of that union also numbering as many forms as there are atoms in Mount Meru, enter into union. This is the meaning of the assertion that those of sharp intelligence enter into union with as many mahāmudrā consorts as there are atoms in Mount Meru. The way that the bliss of the melting elements is generated from this union is that the yogi focuses upon himself as empty-form Kālacakra mothers and fathers in union, and by dwelling single-pointedly in this desire, the four or sixteen descending joys are generated from the crown of the gross body down to the forehead, then to the throat and so on, and finally to the tip of the vajra jewel.

de ltar na rjes dran gyi skabs su dbang po rab kyis phyag rgya chen mo'i sgo nas bde ba skyed pa'i thabs kyi dmigs pa la yang yang sbyong zhing phyag rgya gzhan gnyis la yang brten nas bogs 'byin pa yin te/ thugs rdo rje rjes dran dang ye shes rdo rje ting nge 'dzin 'chad pa'i 'grel chen las/
gzugs la rjes su chags pas byang chub kyi sems zhu ba dang mchog gi bde ba la gnas rdo rje yang dag bslab pa yang /[353] zhes rgyud 'di'i chad du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bos thugs rdo rje rjes dran gyi skabs 'dir phyag rgya chen mo'i gzugs la rjes su chags pas rnal 'byor pa rang gi rdo rje bslab pa dang / de la brten nas khams byang chub kyi sems zhu ba dang / khams zhu ba de las mchog gi bde ba la gnas bar bya'o/ / gal te gdul bya'i gtso bo des ci ste phyag rgya chen mo'i gzugs la rjes chags byas ba'i sgo nas khams byang sems zhu ba'i dga' bzhi skyes par ma gyur na de'i tshe pad+mar rdo rje'i sgra'am zhes pa las kyi phyag rgya'i pad+ma_ra rdo rje dal bus bskyod pa [354] dag gis bya'o/ /zhes sogs kyi don bshad zin pa ltar yin zhing / rgyud 'di'i ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo ni dbang po rab nyid yin pas so/ /

Therefore, during recollection, the yogi of high intelligence practices repeatedly the method for developing bliss by reliance upon the mahāmudrā consort and enhances the practice by relying on the other two types of mudrā consorts. The Great Commentary, in the section explaining that the mind vajra refers to recollection and the gnosis vajra refers to meditative concentration, says:
Desiring the form, the bodhicitta melts, he abides in supreme bliss, and the vajra is raised.[356] Therefore, in the practice of mind-vajra recollection, the primary intended disciples of this tantra desire the form of the mahāmudrā consort, and the vajra of the yogi is raised. This brings about the melting of the bodhicitta, and the yogi dwells in the bliss that arises from the melting. If such a disciple does not generate the four joys of the melted bodhicitta by desiring the form of the mahāmudrā consort, “use the sound of the vajra in the lotus” of an activity mudrā consort, which means generating bliss by moving the vajra slowly in the lotus of an activity mudrā. These and other lines, which have already been explained, clarify this point. Also the primary intended disciples of this tantra are yogis of high intelligence.

d.div: [353] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 390_ba7
[354] ma dper dal bus bskyed ba zhes byung yang bskyod pa zhes bcos/
[356] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 390b7.

f.d: dbang po 'bring dang dman pa gnyis kyis ni rim pa bzhin gtso bor ye rgya dang las rgya la brten nas yas babs dang mas brtan gyi dga' bzhi bskyed nas bde stong sbyor ba dang / rnal 'byor pa rang nyid stong gzugs yab yum gyi skur shar ba'i yum phyag rgya chen mo la'ang rjes chags yang yang sgom par byed pa yin no/ / gang zag gsum char gyis rjes dran gyi sku grub pa dang ma grub pa'i gnas skabs thams cad du nang gi gtum mo dang las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya la brten nas bde chen drangs te stong nyid dang sbyar ba'i bde stong gi ye shes sgom pa rnams ni ting nge 'dzin gyi mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma nyi khri chig stong drug brgya skye ba'i rig 'dra'i rgyu dang rgyud smin byed yin zhing / rjes dran gyi stong gzugs phyag rgya chen mo ni sbas rgyud pa'i lam srol gzhan rnams las ma bshad pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba thun mong ma yin pa'i rgyu yin pa'i stong gzugs sgrub pa'i thabs la ched cher bya dgos so/ /

Those of middling and low intelligence rely mainly on wisdom and activity mudrā consorts, respectively, from which they develop the four joys of descent and stable ascent and apply the bliss to emptiness. The yogi arises as the empty-form mother and father and meditates repeatedly on the desire for the mahāmudrā mother. /459/ Whether they have achieved the recollection body or not, the three kinds of practitioners at all levels of recollection practice rely on the caṇḍālī fire as well as on wisdom and activity mudrā consorts to induce great bliss, which is then applied to emptiness. The meditations on that bliss-and-emptiness gnosis ripen the mindstream and are similar-type causes for the development of the 21,600 instances of meditative concentration unchanging bliss. Moreover the empty-form mahāmudrā consort is a special cause of an unchanging bliss not found in the hidden tantra traditions. Therefore great significance should be attached to the achievement of empty form.
bzhi pa phyag rgya gnyis bsten pa'i tshul

d.i: Relying on the two mudrā consorts

f.d: ['di ]la gsum las/
This has three headings: 1. Wisdom mudrā consort 2. Activity mudrā consort 3. The explanation from the tantra of the four mudrā consorts
dang po ye shes kyi phyag rgya bsten pa'i tshul ni/

de yang bskyed rim mthar phyin pa sngon du song ba dang khyad par du yang srog gzugs grub pa sngon du song bas bsams pa tsam gyis gsal bar snang ba'i gsal snang 'byung bas rang nyid dus 'khor yab yum du gsal bar bltas la yab yum gnyis ka'i dpral bar zla ba la oM dkar po/ mgrin par nyi ma la AH dmar po/ thugs kar sgra gcan la hUM nag po/ lte bar dus me la ho:ser po/ gsang gnas su ye shes kyi dkyil 'khor la swA sngon po/ gtsug tor du nam mkha'i dkyil 'khor la hA ljang gu dgod/ de nas rang gi gsang gnas mi dmigs pa'i ngang nas hUM las byung ba'i rdo rje sngon po rtse lnga pa lte bar AHlas byung ba'i pad+ma 'dab ma brgyad pas mtshan pa/ yum gyi+i gsang gnas mi dmigs pa'i ngang las AHlas byung ba'i pad+ma dmar po 'dab ma brgyad pa hUM las byung ba'i rdo rjes mtshan pa bsgoms la snyoms 'jug byed pa'i tshul la rtse gcig tu dmigs nas sgom pa yin la/ de ltar bsgoms pas khams byang sems zhu ba dpral ba nas rdo rje nor bu'i rtse bar 'ongs pa 'dzag med du bcings pas lhan skyes kyi bde ba skyes pa'i bar yas babs kyi dga' ba bzhi dang rdo rje nor bu'i rtse nas gtsug tor gyi bar du gyen du log pa'i mas brtan gyi dga' bzhi bskyed de 'od gsal gyi sems bde ba chen po'i rang bzhin du gyur pa des rang dus su shar ba'i stong gzugs rjes mthun pa'am mtshan nyid pa skabs su gang bab pa de dang de rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong pa'i stong nyid la rtse gcig tu bzhag nas sgom par byed cing / stong gzugs phyag rgya chen mo dngos gnas la ma grub pa'i dus su yin na de dngos gnas la grub kyi bar la nang gi ting nge 'dzin dang phyag rgya gnyis sbrags nas phan tshun gcig gis cig shos la bogs dbyung gin bsgom par bya ste/

With the generation stage already accomplished, and especially with the attainment of accomplishment of form and wind accomplishment,[357] clear images can be created by thought alone. Therefore, with oneself clearly visualized as Kālacakra mother and father, on a moon disk at the forehead of both father and mother there is a white oṃ, on a sun disk at the throat a red āḥ, on a Rāhu disk at the heart a black hūḥ, on a Kālāgni disk at the navel a yellow hoḥ, on a gnosis mandala at the secret area a blue svā, and on a space mandala at the crown a green ha. From one’s secret area, which is in a nonapprehended state, arises a hūḥ, which transforms into a blue five-pointed vajra. At its center is the syllable āḥ which turns into an eight-petal lotus. From the mother’s secret area, which is in a nonapprehended state, the syllable āḥ appears and transforms into a red eight-petal lotus. In its center is the syllable hūḥ, which transforms into a vajra. With this visualization the yogi single-pointedly meditates on entering into union. This meditation brings about the melting of the bodhicitta element, which descends from the forehead to the tip of the jewel and is held there without being emitted. This generates the innate bliss of the four joys of descent, followed by the four joys of stable ascent, involving the upward return from the tip of the vajra jewel to the crown. /460/ The clear-light mind develops into the nature of this great bliss and meditates single-pointedly on the empty forms, actual or facsimile, that simultaneously appear, as well as on the emptiness that is the noninherent nature of these empty forms. If this is practiced during the period in which an actual phenomenon empty-form mahāmudrā consort has yet to be achieved, the yogi alternates between his own inner meditative concentration and the mudrā consort meditation. These provide mutual enhancement until an actual phenomenon empty-form mahāmudrā consort is attained.

d.div: [357] Accomplishment of form here refers to the first two branches of the six yogas, where empty forms are first accomplished. Wind accomplishment refers to the next two branches, where the winds are brought under control.

f.d:
de ltar yang nA ro pa chen pos/
bsgom bya zhes pa ye shes kyi phyag rgya ste phung po dang khams dang skye mched la sogs pa lha'i rnam pas sbyangs nas dkyil 'khor gyi 'khor lo ji lta bar gsal bar byas te srub cing srub pa'i sbyor bas ye shes kyi me spar la ji srid du haM yig bsregs pa 'dzag pa na ri bong can dpral ba nas mgrin pa dang snying ga dang lte ba dang rdo rje dang pad+ma_'i lte bar 'ongs pa'i byang chub kyi sems kyi ngo bo'i yul dang dbang po mtha' dag bde ba chen por ro mnyam pa'i go 'phang la gang gcig tu 'dres par gyur te de'i rang bzhin gyi ting nge 'dzin la snyoms par zhugs par gyur nas ji srid du dpal phyag rgya chen mo mngon du phyogs par gyur pa'i bar du gnas par bya'o/[355] / zhes gsungs pa ltar te/ de yang ye rgya la sbyar ba ltar las rgya dang nang gi gtum mo sgom pa la yang sbyor tshul shes par bya'o/ /

The great Nāropa says:
“Meditate” refers to meditation on the wisdom mudrā consort. The aggregates, spheres, and sources are purified by being in deity aspect. The mandalas are clearly visualized, and the yoga of constant movement causes the fire of gnosis to blaze. The letter hūḥ is burnt, and the moon descends from the forehead to the throat, heart, navel, vajra, and center of lotus. All senses and their objects possessing the nature of this bodhicitta are unified in a one-taste state of great bliss. In this meditative concentration, union is entered into and endures until the approach of the glorious mahāmudrā consort.[358] Just as this is applied to a wisdom mudrā consort, it can also be applied to meditations on an activity mudrā consort and on the caṇḍālī fire.

d.div: [355] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 255_na2_'gyur cung mi mthun/
[358] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 255a2.

f.d: gnyis pa las kyi phyag rgya bsten pa'i tshul ni/

bsten bya las kyi phyag rgya ni rgyud nas bshad pa'i mtshan nyid dang ldan paste / brtag gnyis las/
rnyed pa de yang mig yangs ma/ / gzugs dang lang tshos rnam par brgyan/ / sih+la ga bur yang dag ldan/ / byang chub sems kyis rnam par sbyang /[356] / zhes gsungs pa'i rdo rje snying 'grel las/
phyag rgya'i mtshan nyid bstan pa yin te/ 'di ltar mig dkar dmar 'byes pa la cung zad tsam yangs pa rked pa rdo rje ltar 'dug pa/ lo bcu gnyis sam bcu drug lon nas khrag 'byung ba'i dus la bab pa byang chub sems kyi bde ba la dga' ba dang / de bzhin du phyag rgya de yang sbyar bar bya ste/[357] zhes phyag rgya'i mtshan nyid dang / de sbyang dgos par gsungs nas/

The correct kind of activity mudrā consort to be relied upon is described in the tantras. The root Hevajra Tantra says:
When discovered, she will have wide open eyes, adorned with beauty and youth, camphor and sihla,[359] well trained by bodhicitta.[360] On this the Vajragarbha Commentary says:
This teaches the characteristics of a mudrā consort. Her eyes are quite large, with the red and white well separated. Her waist is like a vajra. She is one, age twelve or sixteen, whose blood is flowing and who delights in bodhicitta. Similarly that mudrā consort is to be trained.[361] /461/ This teaches the characteristics of a mudrā consort and the necessity of training.

d.div: [356] sde dge_418_bka'/ rgyud/ nga _kye rdor rgyud/ 15_na1
[357] sde dge_1180_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ka_rdo rje snying 'grel/ 82_na1
[359] Also written silhaka: incense, the olibanum tree (per Monier-Williams).
[360] Toh 418 Kangyur, rgyud, nga, 15a1.
[361] Toh 1180 Tengyur, rgyud, ka, 82a1.

f.d:
sbyong tshul ni rgyud las/
dge ba bcu las brtsams nas ni/ / de la chos ni rab tu bstan/ / lha yi gzugs su bsam pa dang / / dam tshig sems kyang gcig pa nyid/[358] / ces dge ba bcu la slob pa nas brtsams te thun mong gi lam gyis rgyud sbyangs la/ de nas/ de la chos ni rab tu bstan/ /ces pa ltar dbang bskur nas snod rung du byas te rgyud don bshad nas ji ltar 'tshams pa re shes par byas la sdom pa dang dam tshig dang ldan par bya zhing / lha'i gzugs su bsam pa'i lha'i rnal 'byor la bslab pa dang / de bzhin du 'dod pa'i sgyu rtsal la mkhas pa dang / stong pa nyid kyi lta ba phu thag chod pa dang ldan pa sogs su sbyangs te de nas de ltar sbyangs pa'i phyag rgya ma de rgyud nas bshad pa'i cho ga bzhin du bsten par bya'o/ /

On the method of training, the tantra continues:
Beginning from the ten virtues, teach her the dharma well; a mind in deity form, similarly, a well-pledged mind.[362] Beginning from the practices of the ten virtues, she is trained in the common path. Then, as the line, “teach her the dharma well” indicates, she is given initiation and transformed into a suitable receptacle for tantra. She is taught the meaning of tantra and given vows and pledges according to her level of understanding. She is trained in the deity yoga of having a “mind in deity form,” becomes wise in the arts of desire, and has a conviction on the view of emptiness. Using the rituals taught in the tantras, the yogi should rely on such a mudrā consort with these and other skills.

d.div: [358] sde dge_1180_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ka_rdo rje snying 'grel/ 82_na2
[362] Toh 1180 Tengyur, rgyud, ka, 82a2.

f.d:
de ltar du ma sbyangs na nyes dmigs shin tu che ste/ de'i mjug nyid du rgyud las/
mi mo gang zhig ma sbyangs par/ / kye rdo rje la sbyor ba de/ / dam tshig nyams te rlag 'gyur pas/ / de dag sbyang phyir chos bstan bya/[359] / zhes gsungs pa'i nyes dmigs shes par byas la/ rlung stobs sam man ngag gis thig le mi 'chor ba rgyu mtshan du byas nas phyag rgya sbyang ba ma byas par bud med gang byung byung la 'byol nyog tu spyod pa sogs mi bya'o/ /

If she is not trained in this way, very serious faults will occur. The tantra continues:
An untrained girl in Hevajra yoga weakens the pledges, and one will be ruined. Train her, therefore, by teaching dharma.[363] Knowing these faults, do not enter into erroneous liaison with any female not trained as a mudrā consort, using the power of the winds or various instructions to ensure the drop is not lost as a reason.

d.div: [359] sde dge_1180_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ka_rdo rje snying 'grel/ 82_na3
[363] Toh 1180 Tengyur, rgyud, ka, 82a3.

f.d:
de yang phyag rgya ma de rgyud nas bshad pa'i cho ga bzhin du bsten tshul ni sgrub le'i brgya bcu pa'i 'grel par rtsa rgyud drangs pa las/
bcu drug lo lon rigs can ma/ / gzugs dang lang tshos brgyan pa la/ / dang por legs par bslab byas nas/ / dbang bskur nas ni sgrub pa brtsom/ / sku gsung thugs dang chags pa ni/ / dpral ba la sogs rnams la dgod/ / swA hA gsang ba gtsug tor cher/ / de nas pad+ma rnam par sbyang / / AHyis pad+ma 'dab brgyad pa/ / hUM yig gis ni rdo rjer ldan/ / de ltar rdo rje dang bcas pa'i/ / shes rab pad+ma bskyod rgyu las/ / hUM gis rang gi rdo rje ni/ / rtse mo lnga pa rnam par bsgom/ / de dbus pad+ma 'dab brgyad pa/ / AHyig gis ni rab tu brtag / de ltar rdo rje pad+ma dang / / bcas pa byas nas pad+mar gzhug / de nas rdo rje 'dzin pa'i bsnyems/ / 'dzin cing rnal 'byor hUM phaT bya/ / b+ha gar ling+ga rab bkod nas/ / byang chub sems ni spro mi bya/ khams gsum po ni ma lus pa'i/ / sangs rgyas gzugs ni bsgom par bya/[360] / zhes gsungs pa ltar bya ste/

The way to rely upon a mudrā consort according to the rituals in the tantra is taught in the Root Tantra, quoted in verse 110 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter of the Great Commentary:
A qualified consort aged sixteen, adorned with youth and beauty; first teach her well, then initiate and begin the practice. Body, speech, mind, and desire, placed at the brow, and so forth, svā, ha, at the secret and crown. Next the lotus is purified. From the syllable āḥ, an eight-petal lotus; by the syllable hūḥ it is with vajra. The cause of movement of the wisdom lotus with vajra is one’s vajra by the syllable hūḥ, visualized with five points; in its center an eight-petal lotus conceived with the syllable āḥ. With the pride of a vajra holder, the vajra with the lotus enters the lotus. With the liṅgam placed into the bhaga, the yogi performs hūḥ phat; the bodhicitta is not emitted. The three realms in their entirety /462/ are meditated on as forms of buddhas.[364] One should practice as these verses instruct.

d.div: [360] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 233_ba2
[364] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 233b2. Most of this verse has already been explained in the section on subtle and drop yoga.

f.d: rang dang phyag rgya dus 'khor yab yum du gsal zhing nga rgyal dang ldan pa'i dpral ba sogs gnas drug tu sku gsung thugs dang zhes pa nas/ gtsug tor cher zhes pa'i bar gyis/ bstan pa ltar rigs drug gi sa bon dgod pa dang / de nas pad+ma rnam par sbyang / /zhes pa nas/ AHyig gi ni rab tu brtag /ces pa'i bar gyis bstan pa ltar mkha' gsang byin gyis brlab pa rnams ni ye shes kyi phyag rgya'i skabs su bshad pa ltar shes par bya zhing / de nas rdo rje 'dzin pa'i bsnyems/ /zhes pa ltar rang dang phyag rgya gnyis ka lha'i nga rgyal dang ldan par byas te/ de ltar rdo rje pad+ma dang / /bcas pa byas nas pad+mar gzhug /ces dang / b+ha gar ling+ga rab bkod nas/ /zhes pa ltar rang gi gsang gnas hUM las rdo rjer bskyed pa pad+ma_sa mtshan pa'am bcas pa'i ling+ga de yum gyi b+ha ga pad+mar gzhug cing rab tu bkod nas/ rnal 'byor pas hUM phaT bya zhes pa'i phaT kyis khams byang sems rdo rje nor bu'i bar phab pa'i yas babs kyi dga' ba bzhi bskyed nas/ byang chub sems ni spro mi bya/ /zhes pa ltar nor bu'i rtse nas byang sems phyir mi 'dzag par byas te/ hUM phaT kyi hUM gi don rlung sems 'dres pa'i thig le gyen du drangs pa'i mas brtan gyi dga' ba bzhi bskyed de 'od gsal gyi sems bde ba chen por skyes pa des rang dus su shar ba'i stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam pa can de stong gzugs rjes mthun pa yin na stong gzugs de nyid la rtse gcig tu mnyam par 'jog pa dang / dngos gnas la grub pa'i stong gzugs mtshan nyid pa yin na rang nyid dus 'khor yab yum gyi skur grub pa la snyoms 'jug byed pa la dmigs nas rjes chags nyid bya zhing / gzhan yang / khams gsum po ni ma lus pa'i/ /sangs rgyas gzugs su bsgom par bya/ /zhes gsungs pa ltar khams gsum ma lus pa stong gzugs kyi sangs rgyas kyi skus gang bar spro zhing bsgom par yang bya'o/ /

Oneself and the mudrā consort are visualized as Kālacakra father and mother invested with deity pride. At the six places of the forehead and so forth, the seeds of the six families are placed, as is indicated by the lines beginning from “Body, speech, mind, and desire” up to “the secret and crown.” The lines from “Next the lotus is purified” up to “conceived with the syllable āḥ” teach the blessing of the sexual organs and can be understood from the previous explanation on the wisdom mudrā consort. “With the pride of a vajra holder” indicates that both oneself and the mudrā consort hold the pride of being a deity. “The vajra with the lotus enters the lotus” together with the line “With the liṅgam placed into the bhaga” teach that a vajra is created from the hūḥ of one’s secret area and is marked by or “with” a lotus. This liṅgam is placed into the bhaga lotus of the mother. “The yogi performs hūḥ phaṭ” means that the syllable phaṭ causes the bodhicitta element to come as far as the tip of the vajra jewel to create the four joys of descent. “The bodhicitta is not emitted” indicates that the bodhicitta is not emitted from the tip of the jewel because the significance of hūḥ from the phrase “hūḥ phaṭ” is that the drop of combined mind and wind is drawn back up to create the four joys of stable ascent. The clear-light mind develops into the entity of great bliss. If the empty form appearing at the same time in the aspect of Kālacakra mother and father is a just a similitude, the clear-light mind is placed single-pointedly within it. If that empty form is the definitive and actual empty form, the clear-light mind focuses upon the sexual union of oneself established in the form of Kālacakra mother and father, and desire for the mother is created. Furthermore the lines “The three realms in their entirety are meditated on as forms of buddhas” indicate that one also meditates on emanating empty-form buddhas filling the entirety of the three realms.

de yang las kyi phyag rgya 'di bsten pa'i tshe ji ltar bya ba ni rdo rje snying 'grel las/
'di 'dra'i mi mo legs rnyed nas/ / bas mtha' dag tu gnas byas la/ / bza' btung rnam mang sta gon bya/ / glu dang sil snyan gar dang ni/ / lus la rgyan legs gdags pa dang / / me tog dag dang dri dang ni/ / bzang po'i gnas las legs 'khod la/ / yang dag ye shes snang bar bya/[361] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

Regarding one’s lifestyle while relying upon an activity mudrā consort, the Vajragarbha Commentary says:
Having discovered such a girl, dwell in distant places, well prepared with food and drink, with songs, cymbals, dance, her body adorned with ornaments, flowers, and perfumes. Live well in this good place /463/ and emanate the perfect gnosis.[365]

d.div: [361] sde dge_1180_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ka_rdo rje snying 'grel/ 82_na5
[365] Toh 1180 Tengyur, rgyud, ka, 82a5.

f.d:
yang rdo rje snying 'grel las/
yang na bdag gi nus pa yis/ / lha dang lha min mi rnams dang / / gnod sbyin mi 'am ci las kyang / / phyag rgya bkug la brtag par bya/[362] / zhes lha mo la sogs pa de rnams nus pas bkug ste las kyi phyag rgyar rung mi rung brtags nas rung ba rnams la'ang phyag rgya 'tshol bar bshad pa ltar ro/ /

From the same text it says:
With one’s powers summon mudrā consorts from the gods, asura, humans, kiṃnara, and yakṣa, and examine them well.[366] These lines teach that goddesses and so forth should be summoned with special powers and assessed for their suitability to be activity mudrā consorts. A consort should be chosen from among those who are suitable.

d.div: [362] sde dge_1180_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ka_rdo rje snying 'grel/ 82_na6
[366] Toh 1180 Tengyur, rgyud, ka, 82a6.

f.d: gsum pa zhar byung rgyud nas bshad pa'i phyag rgya bzhi'i rnam gzhag ni/

d.i: The explanation from the tantra of the four mudrā consorts

f.d:
ye she'i don bzhi pa las/
'gyur ba med pa'i bde ba'i 'bras ster phyag rgya bzhi po 'di rnams grong dang 'brog dgon dur khrod dang /[363] / zhes gsungs pa'i phyag rgya bzhi ni las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya dang / phyag rgya chen mo dang/ dam tshig gi phyag rgya dang bzhi yin la/ de la las kyi phyag rgya ni dbang mdor bstan gyi nA ro pa'i 'grel pa las/
las kyi phyag rgya ni nu ma dang skrar ldan pa 'dod pa'i khams kyi bde ba'i rgyu'o/ / las ni tsum+b+ha na dang 'khyud pa dang gsang bar reg pa dang rdo rje skyod pa la sogs pa bya ba'i bdag nyid can te/ de yis nye bar mtshon pa'i phyag rgya ni yid ches par byed pa mo yin la/ yid ches pa ni 'dir 'gyur ba'i bde ba mtshon par byed pa ste/[364] zhes bshad pa ltar las kyi phyag rgya'i ngo bo ni nu ma dang skrar ldan pa rdul phra rab bsags pa'i lus dang ldan pa'i bud med kyi rnam pa'o/ /

In verse 74 of the Gnosis chapter of the Condensed Tantra it says:
With these four mudrā consorts giving fruits of unchanging bliss, in towns, in isolation, cemeteries, unclean, and clean places.[367] This line mentions four mudrā consorts. These are activity mudrā consorts, wisdom mudrā consorts, mahāmudrā consorts, and samaya consorts. On the activity mudrā consort, Nāropa in his Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations says:
The activity mudrā has breasts and hair, a cause for bliss in the realm of desire. The activities are those of cumbanda, embracing, touching the secret area, moving the vajra, and so on. Illustrated by these activities, the mudrā is she who creates reliability. Reliability here refers to changing bliss.[368] Therefore the nature of an activity mudrā consort is a girl who has breasts and hair and a body formed from a collection of atoms.

d.div: [363] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka74_109_na1
[364] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 273_ba3
[367] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 74, 109a1.
[368] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 273b3.

f.d: de las kyi phyag rgyar 'jog pa'i las ni tsum+b+ha na 'o byed pa dang / rnal 'byor pa la 'khyud pa dang / gsang gnas la reg pa dang / rdo rje skyed pa la sogs pa yin la/ las de yis yid ches pa nye bar mtshon par byed pa phyag rgya'i don yin pas las kyi phyag rgya mo zhes bya ba yin no/ / 'o na yid ches pa de gang yin snyam na|_yid ches pa ni rang dbang du byas na 'gyur ba ste 'dzag pa'i bde ba yin la de skyed cing mtshon par byed pa'o/ /

The activities that establish her as an activity mudrā consort include cumbanda, or kissing, embracing the yogi, touching the secret area, and moving the vajra. By these activities she is an illustration of reliability.”[369] This is the meaning of mudrā, and she is known, therefore, as an activity mudrā consort. What does reliability mean here? It refers to the mudrā’s own ability to grant “changing bliss,” or the bliss of emission, which is created or illustrated by the mudrā.

d.div: [369] yid ches, āpta. Trust, conviction, reliability, guarantee; in the sense that a seal or mudrā is a guarantee of trustworthiness.

f.d: ye shes kyi phyag rgya ni 'grel pa de nyid las/ ye shes kyi phyag rgya ni rang gi sems kyis yongs su btags pa sna tshogs yum la sogs pa lha mo'i rang bzhin zhes pa nas yid ches pa ni 'dir g.yo ba'i bde ba mtshon par byed pa'o/[365] /zhes pa'i bar gyi gsungs pa ltar rnal 'byor pa rang gi rtog pas btags nas bsgoms pa'i phyag rgya sna tshogs yum la sogs pa lha mo'i rnam pa'o/ / de'i yid ches pa ni de dang snyoms 'jug byed pa la sogs par bsgoms pas phyag rgya'i rang dbang du byas na byang sems lus kyi gnas gzhan nas gzhan du g.yo bar byed pa'o/ /

The wisdom mudrā consort is explained in the same commentary from the line “The wisdom mudrā consort is completely imputed by one’s mind, goddesses such as Viśvamātā” /464/ up to the line “Concerning reliability, here she shows the moving bliss.”[370] Wisdom mudrā consorts are mentally imputed objects of meditation in the forms of goddesses such as Viśvamātā. Reliability here means that in terms of her own ability, this mudrā consort is able to move the bodhicitta from place to place within the body during meditative union.

d.div: [365] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 273_ba5
[370] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 273b5.

f.d:
phyag rgya chen mo ni 'grel pa de nyid las/ /
chen po yang 'di yin la phyag rgya yang yin pas phyag rgya chen mo'o/ / slar yang 'di'i chen mo nyid ni rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa nyi tshe ba ma yin pa nyid yin la/ byang chub kyi sems rdo rje 'dis rgyas 'debs pa'i phyir phyag rgya ste/ yid ches pa ni 'dir rang gi sems kyis yongs su btags pa'i chos dang bral ba du ba la sogs pa'i mtshan ma sngon du 'gro ba'i rang gi sems rab tu gsal ba rnal 'byor pas rtogs par bya ba pra phab pa lta bu'o/ / 'bras bu'i ngo bo phyag rgya chen po ni mu daM mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba ye shes kyi mtshan nyid de/ ra ti gang ba'i gnas skabs mi g.yo ba'i sbyor bas dus thams cad du kun nas ster ba'o zhes pa phyag rgya'o/ / 'di'i chen po nyid kyang spangs pa chen po nyid dang rtogs pa chen po nyid kyis so/ / de la spangs pa chen po nyid ni bag chags dang bcas pa'i sgrib pa thams cad spangs pa'i mtshan nyid/[366] ces sogs kyis bstan te de dag gi don cung zad cig bshad na/ chen po yang yin la phyag rgya yang yin pas na phyag rgya chen mo zhes phyag rgya chen mo'i sgra don bshad nas/ slar yang zhes pa nas/ nyid yin la zhes pa'i bar gyis chen mo'i don 'chad pa ni/ phyag rgya chen mo zhes pa'i chen mo'i don nyid ni rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa'i stong pa nyid kyi gzugs nyi tshe ba ma yin pa khams gsum ma lus pa khyab par spros pas che ba dang / de rnams kyang yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can du yod pa'i yum rnams mtshon pa'i don du'o zhes pa'o/ /

On the mahāmudrā consort the same commentary says:
Because she is great (mahā) and is a mudrā, she is known as mahāmudrā. Moreover “great” here means that being possessed of supreme characteristics, she is not insignificant. Because she is sealed by the bodhicitta vajra, she is a mudrā. “Reliability” here means being divorced from phenomena conceived by the mind and preceded by the signs of smoke and so forth. This will be understood by the yogi in the clarity of his mind, like prognostic images in a clairvoyant’s mirror. The resultant mahāmudrā is characterized by mudaṃ, the gnosis of supreme and unchanging bliss. When the yogi is filled with rati, the mudrā, by the yoga of immobility, will grant this totally and at all times. Her greatness also is of great abandonment and great insight. Great abandonment is an abandonment of all obscurations together with their propensities.[371] This passage teaches the mahāmudrā consort. It needs a little explanation. The sentence, “Because she is great and is a mudrā, she is known as mahāmudrā” explains the term mahāmudrā. The next sentence teaches the meaning of “great,” which is that the empty-form consort, “being possessed of supreme characteristics, she is not insignificant” and has emanated to pervade the entirety of the three realms. These forms are each in the aspect of mother and father in embrace. To illustrate that “mahāmudrā” refers to the mother, the female gender is used.

d.div: [366] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 273_ba6
[371] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 273b6.

f.d: de yang khams gsum ma lus par khyab par spros pa'i stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can gyi yum rnams phyag rgyar 'jog pa ni/ byang chub kyi sems rdo rje ni mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po yin la/ bde ba chen po de yum 'dis skyed pa las 'dar med pa'i tshul gyis rgyas 'debs pa'i phyir ram rgyu mtshan gyis yin no zhes bya ba'o/ / 'o na nyi tshe ba ma yin pa khams gsum ma lus pa rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa'i stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam pa can gyi khyab pa 'di la yid ches pa ci yod snyam na/ yid ches pa ni rnal 'byor pa rang gi sems rnam rtog gis yongs su btags pa'i chos dang bral ba/ du ba la sogs pa'i mtshan ma ste rtags bcu sngon du 'gro ba ste song ba'i rnal 'byor pa rang gi 'od gsal gyi sems rab tu gsal ba'i gnas skabs su rnal 'byor pas rtogs shing nyams su myong bar bya ba me long la pra phab pa lta bu 'di'o zhes pa'o/ /

Moreover the mother deity of the empty-form Kālacakra mother-and-father embrace that has emanated to pervade the three realms can be confirmed as a “mudrā” because “bodhicitta vajra” here refers to the great unchanging bliss, which is created by this mother, and by not going beyond that, she is therefore “sealed by the bodhicitta vajra.” Because of this “she is a mudrā.” In this empty-form Kālacakra of mother-and-father embrace, of great significance, /465/ possessed of supreme characteristics, and completely pervading the three realms, what does “reliability” refer to? It is that the yogi’s mind is divorced from phenomena conceived by the conceptualizing mind. The yogi, following his experience of the ten signs of smoke and so forth, will understand and experience this like prognostic images in a mirror in the great clarity of his clear-light mind.

yang stong gzugs phyag rgya chen mo de 'bras bu'i ngo bo phyag rgya chen po de ster bar byed pas na phyag rgya zhes bya'o/ / 'o na 'bras bu'i ngo bo phyag rgya chen po gang yin snyam na/ 'bras bu'i ngo bo phyag rgya chen po de ni mu daM zhes pa'i de ni mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i ye shes kyi mtshan nyid can de'o/ / phyag rgya chen mos de ster tshul ji lta bu snyam na/ phyag rgya chen mo de la ra ti'i don dga' zhing rjes su chags par byas pa las rdo rje nor bu'i rtse nas gtsug tor gyi bar khams byang chub kyi sems kyis gang ba'i gnas skabs gnas gzhan du mi g.yo bar 'dzin pa'i sbyor bas ster bar byed pa yin no/ / de yang dus thams cad du kun nas te yang dag par ster ro zhes pa'i don no/ / 'bras bu'i ngo bo'i phyag rgya chen po 'di'i chen po'i don nyid kyang spangs pa chen po nyid dang zhes sogs so/ / mdor na mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po dngos su 'dren par byed pa'i stong gzugs phyag rgya chen mo ni rjes dran gyi skabs nas grub pa'i stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam pa can gyi yum de yin par 'og tu 'chad pa ltar shes par bya'o/ /

Moreover, because this empty-form mahāmudrā consort produces the resultant mahāmudrā consort, she is known as a mudrā. What is the resultant mahāmudrā consort? “The resultant mahāmudrā consort is characterized by mudaṃ, the gnosis of supreme and unchanging bliss.” How does the mahāmudrā consort grant this bliss? She grants it “totally” or perfectly “and at all times” through this yoga. The effect of rati, meaning joy or desire for the mahāmudrā consort, is that the tip of the vajra to the crown of the head is filled with the bodhicitta element where it is held firm without moving to other places. The meaning of “great” in the term resultant mahāmudrā consort also refers to great abandonment and so on. In short the empty-form mahāmudrā consort who actually induces the supreme and unchanging bliss is the mother deity of the empty-form Kālacakra in mother-father embrace, as will be described later.

dam tshig gi phyag rgya ni nA ro pa chen pos/
las dang ye shes phyag rgya che/ / dam tshig ces bya 'od gsal rnams/ / rgyu dang bsgom bya de bzhin du/ / 'thob bya bzhi pa 'jig pa med/[367] / ces bzhi pa dam tshig gi phyag rgya 'thob bya'i 'bras bu 'jig pa med par bshad pa'i 'jig pa med pa ni mi 'gyur ba'i don yin pas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po'o/ /

Concerning the samaya mudrā consort the great Nāropa says:
Activity, wisdom, mahāmudrā, samaya: causes and meditations for clear-light minds, the fourth is the attainment, the indestructible.[372] The fourth or samaya mudrā consort is the resultant attainment or the “indestructible,” which here means “unchanging” and refers to the great unchanging bliss. /466/

f.d: bzhi pa tshad ma gang yin dpyad pa ni

rje bus rnal 'byor mngon sum du gsungs [368] na'ang rnal 'byor mngon sum ni bdag med mngon sum du rtogs pa la byed pa chos skad spyi 'gro yin la/ de yang gang zag gi bdag med rags pa mngon sum du rtogs pa ni 'dir 'ong don med la/ stong nyid phra mo bdag med mngon sum du rtogs na 'phags par 'gyur zhing / skabs 'di'i rjes dran mthar phyin tsam gyi rnal 'byor pa ni so skye yin pas so/ / rang lugs ni stong gzugs mngon sum du gsal bar snang zhing de la mi slu ba'i yid kyi mngon sum tshad ma'o/ /

Butön Rinpoché says the cognition here is a direct yogic valid cognition.[373] However direct yogic valid cognition is a term usually applied to a direct understanding of no-self. It makes no sense for the cognition here to be the direct perception of the coarse no-self of persons. Moreover, to perceive directly the subtle no-self emptiness, one must be an ārya being, whereas here the yogi who has only completed the yoga of recollection is still an ordinary being. Our own position is that the empty forms appear directly and clearly, and that the cognition is a nondeceiving, direct mental consciousness.

f.d: lnga pa dag dbye ni

sgrub le'i brgya bco lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/ g.yung mo la ni rjes su dran pa pad+ma 'dzin par 'gyur zhes pa 'du shes kyi phung po ste g.yung mo dbu ma'i rtsa la rjes su dran pa de yang rnam pa bcu ste 'dod pa'i gnas skabs bcu yi dbye ba las so/[369] / zhes gsungs pa ltar 'du shes kyi phung po/ chu'i khams/ lce/ gzugs/ rkang pa'i dbang po/ len pa ste chos drug dag par byed cing dbye na 'jig rten pa'i 'dod chags nyams su myong ba la gnas skabs bcu yod pa bzhin du dbu mar gtum mo la brten nas phyi nas gzugs brnyan sgom pa la du ba la sogs pa rnam pa bcu'o/ /

The Great Commentary on verse 115 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter states:
“Recollection of caṇḍālī fire is Amitābha” refers to the recognition aggregate. The caṇḍālī fire is recollected in the central channel. There are ten aspects divided by the ten instances of desire.[374] The recognition aggregate, the element of water, the tongue, form, the legs, and the activity of taking are the six phenomena purified. Just as there are ten occasions for the experience of worldly desire, likewise, because of the caṇḍālī fire in the central channel, there are the ten aspects of smoke and so forth in the meditations on inner and outer images.

[374] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 237a2.

f.d: drug pa 'bras bu
['di ]la gnyis las/
There are immediate and final results.

dang po gnas skabs kyi 'bras bu ni rang nyid stong gzugs kyi lhar mthong zhing ba spu'i khung bu nas 'od zer dpag tu med pa 'phros pas nam mkha'i khams 'gengs shing rang gi lus 'od skor gyi nang du chud par 'gyur ro/ / de ltar yang sgrub le'i brgya bcu dgu pa'i 'grel chen las/
rjes su dran pa legs par dag pa zhes pa la 'dir rjes su dran pa zhes pa ni gzugs la 'khyud pa'i sems rnam par rtog pa thams cad dang bral ba'o/ / de'i phyir gong gi tshe dag par gyur pa de'i tshe dri med 'od kyi dkyil 'khor du 'gyur ro/ / kyang gi sgra las ba spu'i khung bu nas 'od zer lnga 'phro zhing nges par rgyu'o/ / ye shes gzugs las so zhes pa stong pa'i gzugs las so/[370] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

The immediate results are that one sees oneself as the deity, limitless light radiates from one’s pores, filling the realms of space, and one’s body is bathed in a halo of light. The Great Commentary, on verse 119 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
“Recollection is excellently pure.” Recollection, as spoken of here, refers to a mind embracing the forms and divorced from all conception. Therefore, when they become pure, at that time there are “mandalas of pure light.” The word “also” refers to the five rays of light radiating and traveling through the pores. “From the gnosis form” means from the empty forms.[375]

f.d: gnyis pa mthar thug gi 'bras bu ni/ 'du shes phung po'i sde tshan gyi chos drug po de sgrib bral du gyur pa snang ba mtha' yas sogs drug 'grub pa'o/ /
The final results are that the six phenomena of the recognition-aggregate group become freed of obscuration to become the six enlightened phenomena, Amitābha and so forth. /467/
drug pa bsgoms pas 'grub pa'i bsgrub bya ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag bshad pa/
35. The Yoga of Meditative Concentration
gnyis pa bsgoms pas 'grub pa'i bsgrub bya ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag

d.i: The branch of meditative concentration: The final meditative attainment

f.d: ['di ]la drug / ting nge 'dzin gyi mtshan don/ bsgom pa'i dus 'tshams/ bsgom pa'i yan lag gi nges pa/ tshad ma gang yin dpyad pa/ dag dbye/ 'bras bu'o/ /
This section is under six headings: 1. Meaning of the term 2. Time for meditation 3. The meditation 4. Valid cognition 5. Purification divisions 6. Results
dang po [ting nge 'dzin gyi mtshan don ]ni

stong gzugs phyag rgya chen mo la rjes su chags pa las 'gyur ba med pa'i bde ba thob ste rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong pa nyid dang mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba dbyer med pa la sems rtse gcig tu gnas pas na ting nge 'dzin zhes bya ste/ sgrub le'i brgya bcu bdun pa'i 'grel chen las/
shes rab thabs kyi bdag nyid kyi ni zhes pa shes bya dang shes pa gcig tu 'dres par gyur pa ste 'gyur med bde ba'i dbang gis ye shes gzugs la ting nge 'dzin no/[371] / zhes dang / bde mchog stod 'grel las kyang /
de nas ting nge 'dzin zhes bya ba ni 'dod pa'i lha la rjes su chags pa las gang zhig 'gyur ba med pa'i bde ba thob pa ste/ de la gcig tu gyur pa'i sems gzung ba dang 'dzin pa dang bral ba ni de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyis ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag tu brjod do/[372] / zhes so/ /

Unchanging bliss is achieved from desire for the empty-form mahāmudrā consort. The mind is placed single-pointedly in the indivisibility of emptiness endowed with every supreme aspect and unchanging bliss, hence the term meditative concentration. The Great Commentary, on verse 117 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
“In the nature of wisdom and method” means that consciousness and the object of consciousness are mixed as one, and the power that is the unchanging bliss is a meditative concentration upon gnosis form.[376] The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary also says:
Concerning meditative concentration, unchanging bliss is achieved from the yearning for the desired goddess. This nondual mind, divorced of consciousness of subject and object, is spoken of by the tathāgatas as meditative concentration.[377]

f.d: gnyis pa bsgom pa'i dus 'tshams ni

rjes dran gyi sku grub nas las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya dang nang gi gtum mo la brten nas yas babs mas brtan gyi dga' ba bzhi'i rjes dran gyi lam la legs par sbyangs te mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed nus kyi rgyud smin par byas shing / phyag rgya chen mo la rjes chags goms par byas pa'i mthus mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'dren nus pa nas bsgom par bya'o/ / de ltar yang sgrub le'i brgya bcu gsum pa'i 'grel chen las/
de nas sgrub pa chen po ni shes rab sbyar la gang gi tshe 'pho ba med pa'i bde bar 'gyur ba de'i tshe nges par sgrub pa chen po ste/ phra mo'i rnal 'byor dag las zhes pa nges pa'i don gyi shin tu yid bzang ma'i rtsa'i steng du khu ba yang dag par sbyor ba las sgrub pa chen por gsungs te/[373] zhes shes rab phyag rgya ma la mnyam par sbyar ba la gang gi tshe thig le gnas gzhan du 'pho ba med pa la brten pa'i 'gyur ba med pa'i bde ba skye bar 'gyur ba de'i tshe ste de'i dus su nges par te gdon mi za bar sgrub pa chen po'i ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag bsgom par gsungs pa ltar ro/ / 'o na sgrub pa chen po'i ngo bo ji lta bu snyam na/ de ni phra mo'i rnal 'byor la drang don bskyed pa'i rim pa dang nges don rdzogs pa'i rim pa gnyis su bshad pa dag las nges pa'i don gyi dbang du byas na shin tu yid bzang ma dbu ma'i rtsa'i steng du ste nang du khu ba khams dkar dmar yang dag par sbyar ba gnas gzhan du 'pho ba med pa las byung ba'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po ni ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag sgrub pa chen por gsungs pa ltar yin no/ /zhes pa'o/ /

When the recollection body has been attained and the four joys of descent and stable ascent are accomplished from reliance on activity mudrā consorts, wisdom mudrā consorts, and the caṇḍālī fire, one has become well trained in the path of recollection, and the mind has been ripened for the ability to create unchanging bliss. Once the yogi has the ability to induce unchanging bliss because of familiarity with desire for the mahāmudrā consort, the meditations of meditative concentration should begin. The Great Commentary, on verse 113 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
Next is great accomplishment. When there is union with wisdom, when the unmoving bliss is to be created, this is definitely the time of great accomplishment. “From the subtle yogas” teaches that great accomplishment is achieved definitively from the fluid well joined onto the “woman of excellent mind” channel.[378] “When there is union with wisdom,” or mudrā consort, and when the unchanging bliss is to be created in reliance on the drops not moving to other places, /468/ this is definitely the time to meditate on the great accomplishment — the branch of meditative concentration. What is the nature of this great accomplishment? Subtle yoga practice is taught at two levels — the provisional generation-stage practice and the definitive completion-stage practice. In the definitive practice the red and white fluid elements are “well joined onto,” or inside, the “woman of excellent mind,” or central channel, and do not move to other places. From this arises the great unchanging bliss, explained as being the meditative concentration great accomplishment.

f.d: gsum pa bsgom pa'i yan lag gi nges pa
['di ]la gsum/ ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag gi ngo bo/ dbye ba/ ji ltar sgom pa'i tshul lo/ /
This has three outlines: 1. The nature of the branch of meditative concentration 2. Divisions 3. The way to meditate
dang po [ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag gi ngo bo ]ni

d.i: The nature of the branch of meditative concentration

f.d:
shes bya rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong pa nyid kyi gzugs dang / shes pa mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po ngo bo dbyer med pa'i ye shes phung khams skye mched thams cad sgrib bral du za bar byed nus pa gser gyi rtsi'i dngul chu lta bu ste/ 'grel chen sngar drangs pa ltar/
shes rab thabs kyi bdag nyid kyis ni zhes pa shes bya dang shes pa gcig tu 'dres par gyur ba ste 'gyur ba med pa'i dbang gis gzugs la ting nge 'dzin to/[374] / zhes dang /

Meditative concentration is a gnosis that is the indivisibility of an unchanging great-bliss consciousness and the object of that consciousness, an emptiness form endowed with every supreme aspect, which has the power to transform all aggregates, sources, and elements into nonobscured phenomena, as mercury transforms base metal into gold. As the previously quoted passage from the Great Commentary says:
“In the nature of wisdom and method” means that consciousness and the object of consciousness are mixed as one, /469/ and the power that is the unchanging bliss is a meditative concentration upon gnosis form.[379]

d.div: [374] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 237_ba2
[379] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 237b2.

f.d:
'dus pa phyi ma las/
shes rab thabs ni snyoms 'jug pas/ / dngos po thams cad mdor bsdus pa/ / byas te gong bu'i sbyor ba yis/ / dbus su gzugs brnyan rnam bsgom bya/ / skad cig ye shes rdzogs pa ni/ / ting 'dzin zhes bya'i ming can no/[375] / zhes pa'i nA ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa las/
yan lag drug pa gsungs pa/ shes rab ces pa la sogs pa ste/ shes rab thabs ni snyoms 'jug pas/ /zhes pa rgyu mthun pa la sogs pa'i rim pas nam mkha'i pad+ma_ra 'phags pa na mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i dbang gis shes bya dang shes pa gcig tu 'dres par gyur pa nyid kyis dri ma med pa'i gnas skabs su brtan pa dang g.yo ba'i dngos po thams cad rab tu gsal ba'i gzugs su mdor bsdus pa byas te zhes pa nye bar byas te gong bu'i sbyor ba yis ni 'dzag pa med pa'i mchog gi bde ba chen por bdag nyid 'od gsal gcig bu'i bzhugs kyis zos pa ste lcags la sogs pa'i khams thams cad ro gcig pa'i gzugs grub pa'i ro'i gzugs kyis bzhin no/ / 'dzag pa med pa'i mchog gi bde ba chen po ro gcig pa 'od gsal ba de'i dbus su gzugs brnyan kun rdzob kyi bden pa'i bdag nyid rnam bsgom bya ni blta bar bya'o/ / 'di'i rab tu rgyas par bshad pa skad cig ces pa la sogs pa ste ye shes bden pa gnyis gnyis su med par gyur pa'i skad cig rdzogs pa ni rtogs pa ste ting nge 'dzin zhes pa ting nge 'dzin gyi+i yan lag gi ming can no/[376] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

In the Later Guhyasamāja Tantra it says:
With wisdom and method in union, all phenomena are gathered. By the yoga of amassing, the image is meditated on in the center. An instance of gnosis complete is called meditative concentration.[380] Nāropa in his Commentary on a Short Teaching on Initiations says of this verse:
The lines beginning “With wisdom” speak of the sixth branch. “With wisdom and method in union” refers to the stages of similar-to-cause and so forth, which rise in the space of the lotuses. By the power of the unchanging bliss, consciousness and object of consciousness are mixed as one. At these uncontaminated times all animate and inanimate phenomena are “gathered,” or brought together, as well-illumined forms, and with the yoga of amassing they are consumed by the clear light solely in emptiness form, in its nature of the nonfalling supreme bliss, like the taste of forms when all the elements — iron and so forth — are made into a form of one taste. In the center of the clear light, at one with the nonfalling supreme bliss, is the image whose nature is conventional truth and is to be meditated upon. A more detailed explanation of this is found in the lines beginning “An instance.” The gnosis is nondual in terms of the two truths, and when an instance of this is complete or perceived, it is known by the name of the branch of meditative concentration.[381]

d.div: [375] sde dge_443_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_gsang 'dus rgyud phyi ma/ 154_ba5_tshig sna mi mthun/
