[380] Toh 443 Kangyur, rgyud, cha, 154b5.
[381] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 247b3.

f.d: 'grel tshig de dag gi don cud zad cig bshad na/ shes rab thabs ni snyoms 'jug pas/ /zhes pa'i don rtsa rgyud las/ rgyu mthun la sogs steng du 'gro/[377] /zhes gsungs pa ltar/ rgyu mthun la sogs pas rim pas khams byang chub kyi sems rdo rje nor bu'i rtse nas gtsug tor gyi bar d+hU tI'i nam mkha'i rtsa 'khor nas rtsa 'khor gyi pad+mar 'phags pa gnas gzhan du mi 'gyur zhing mi g.yo ba las mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po 'byung la/ mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po de'i dbang gis shes bya rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong gzugs dang shes pa mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po ngo bo gcig tu 'dres par gyur pa nyid kyis gnyen po byas pa'i sgo nas ngo skal gyi spang bya'i sgrib pa dang bral ba'i dri ma med pa'i gnas skabs su brtan pa snod kyi 'jig rten dang g.yo ba bcud kyi sems can du snang ba'i dngos po thams cad rab tu gsal ba'i stong pa nyid kyi gzugs su mdor bsdus pa ni mdor bsdus pa byas te zhes pa'i don no/ /

This passage needs a little explanation. Concerning the line “With wisdom and method in union,” the Root Tantra says, “The stages of similar-to-cause travel upward.” Therefore, by the stages of similar-to-cause and so forth,[382] the bodhicitta element rises up from the tip of the vajra jewel to the crown in the dhūtī space of the cakras from lotus to lotus. At these cakras they do not change or move to other places and therefore produce unchanging bliss. By the power of this unchanging bliss, the emptiness form, endowed with every supreme aspect as an object of consciousness, and unchanging-bliss consciousness merge to become one entity. This acts as an opponent force to destroy portions of the obscurations, and at such uncontaminated times all phenomena, as illustrated by the inanimate environment and the animate living beings in it, are gathered together as illumined empty forms. This is the meaning of the term gathered.

d.div: [377] sde dge_443_bka'/ rgyud/ ca_gsang 'dus rgyud phyi ma/ 154_ba5
[382] Similar-to-cause, ripening, personally created, eradication — the four types of results corresponding to the four drops at the navel, heart, throat, and crown lotuses or cakras respectively.

f.d: gong bu'i sbyor ba yis zhes pa'i don ni/ 'dzag pa ste 'gyur ba med pa'i mchog gi bde ba chen po'i bdag nyid du gyur pa'i 'od gsal de stong pa nyid gcig bu'i gzugs kyis phung khams skye mched thams cad sgrib bral du zos pa te/ dper na lcags la sogs pa'i khams thams cad ro gcig pa'i gzugs su grub pa'i ro gzugs dngul chus zos nas gser du sgyur ba bzhin no/ /

The meaning of the line “By the yoga of amassing” is that the “clear light solely in emptiness form, in its nature of the nonfalling,” or unchanging supreme bliss, consumes and transforms all the aggregates, elements, and sources into nonobscured phenomena. For example, “like the taste of forms when all elements — iron and so forth — are made into a form of one taste,” /470/ referring to the process in which elements are consumed by mercury and transformed into gold.

dbus su gzugs brnyan rnam bsgom bya/ /zhes pa'i don ni/ rgyu mtshan de nyid kyi phyir na 'dzag pa ste 'gyur ba med pa'i mchog gi bde ba chen por ro gcig pa 'od gsal ba de'i dbus su ste de dang dbyer med par gzugs brnyan te stong gzugs kun rdzob bden pa'i bdag nyid rnam bsgom bya ni de ltar blta bar bya'o zhes pa'i don te/ ye shes bden pa gnyis zhes sogs kyi don ni/ yul gyi ming yul can la btags pa'i stong pa nyid rtogs pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po don dam pa'i bden pa dang stong gzugs kun rdzob kyi bden pa gnyis gnyis su med par gyur pa'i skad cig rdzogs pa'i don rtogs pa ni ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag gi ming can yin no zhes pa'i don to/ /

The meaning of the line beginning “In the center of the clear light” is that because of the above reasons, one should meditate upon the image, or empty form, “whose nature is a conventional truth,” in the center of, or indivisible from, the clear light that is of “one taste with the supreme nonfalling bliss,” or unchanging bliss. The lines beginning “The gnosis is nondual” refer to the two truths. These are: the ultimate truth, which here refers to the unchanging bliss that perceives emptiness and is an example of a consciousness being given the name of its object; and the conventional truth, which is the empty forms. These become nondual, and when “an instance of this is complete or perceived, it is known by the name of the branch of meditative concentration.”
gnyis pa dbye ba
['di ]la gnyis/ rgyud dang rten gyi sgo nas dbye ba dang/ ngo bo'i sgo nas dbye ba'o/ /
This has two headings: 1. Division by cause and basis 2. Division by nature
dang po [rgyud dang rten gyi sgo nas dbye ba ]ni

las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas skyes pa dbang po rtul po'i rgyud kyi dang / ye shes kyi phyag rgya la brten nas skyes pa dbang 'bring gi rgyud kyi dang / phyag rgya chen mo 'ba' zhig la brten nas skyes pa dbang rnon gyi rgyud kyi ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag go/ / de ltar gsum du 'byed pa ni sgrub le'i brgya bcu bdun pa las/
'di rnams dman pa la sogs dbye ba rnams kyis sna tshogs gtso bo'i sgrub thabs rnam pa gsum du 'gyur/ / phyag rgya gsum dang gnas skabs gsum ni rnam gsum bgrod pa'i dbang gis las dang kun rtog mchog rnams so/[378] / zhes dang/

There is meditative concentration in the minds of those of low intelligence and developed by reliance upon an activity mudrā consort, meditative concentration in the minds of those of middling intelligence developed by reliance upon a wisdom mudrā consort, and meditative concentration in the minds of those of high intelligence developed by reliance solely upon a mahāmudrā consort. This division is taught in verse 117 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter of the Condensed Tantra:
As these are divided by being of low intelligence and so forth, there are three different and main methods of practice. Three consorts and three times by three paths, karma and conception become the supreme.[383]

d.div: [378] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka117_89_ba5
[383] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 117, 89b5.

f.d:
de'i 'grel chen las/
'di rnams dman pa la sogs dbye ba rnams kyis sna tshogs gtso bo dus kyi 'khor lo'i sgrub thabs rnam pa gsum du 'gyur/ / phyag rgya gsum dang gnas skabs gsum zhes pa ni rnam gsum bgrod pa'i dbang gis zhes pa ste 'dir byang chub kyi sems 'dzag pa'i bgrod pa ni dman pa'i gnas skabs dang g.yo ba'i bgrod pa ni 'bring po'i gnas skabs dang mi g.yo ba'i bgrod pa ni mchog gi gnas skabs so/ / 'di rnams las las kyi phyag rgya ni 'dzag pa'i bde ba sbyin pa mo dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya ni g.yo ba'i bde ba sbyin pa mo dang phyag rgya chen mo ni mi g.yo ba'i bde ba sbyin pa mo'o/ / de ltar sbyor ba yan lag drug la phyag rgya gsum bsgom par bcom ldan 'das kyis gsungs pa'i phyir rnal 'byor pas sangs rgyas nyid kyi slad du sbyor ba yan lag drug bsgom par bya'o/[379] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis bstan to/ /

The Great Commentary on this verse says:
“As these are divided by being of low intelligence and so forth, there are three different and main methods of practice” of the Kālacakra. “Three consorts and three times by three paths” refers to the path of the falling bodhicitta during the times of those of low intelligence, the path of moving bodhicitta during the times of those of middling intelligence, and the path of the nonmoving bodhicitta during the times of those of high intelligence. /471/ Among these, the activity mudrā consort is the giver of the bliss of falling, the wisdom mudrā consort is the giver of the bliss of movement, and the mahāmudrā consort is the giver of the nonmoving bliss. In this way the Buddha taught the meditations of the three mudrā consorts in the six branches. Therefore the yogi should meditate on the six yogas.[384] The divisions of meditative concentration are taught in this passage.

d.div: [379] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 237_ba3
[384] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 237b3.

f.d: de yang ji ltar na/ de ltar zhes sogs kyis bstan te/ rgyud don bshad zin pa de ltar sbyor ba yan lag drug la ste drug car la phyag rgya gsum bsgom par bcom ldan 'das kyis gsung pa'i phyir zhes pa 'dis ting nge 'dzin la yang phyag rgya gsum la brten pa gsum du 'byor dgos so/ / de ltar na rgyud 'grel 'di dag gi don cung zad cig bshad na/ sbyor ba yan lag drug po 'di rnams sgom pa'i gang zag dbang po dman pa dang la sogs pa 'bring dang mchog gi dbye ba rnams kyis sna tshogs gtso bo dus kyi 'khor lo'i sgrub thabs ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag 'di la rnam pa gsum du yod par 'gyur ro/ / de yang gnas skabs gsum ste dbang po dman 'bring mchog gi gnas skabs gsum gyis rim pa bzhin las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya dang phyag rgya chen mo la brten pa rnam pa gsum du 'gyur ro/ / de'i rgyu mtshan yang ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed pa'i rten gyi gang zag de la rnam gsum bgrod pa'i dbang gis zhes pa ste byang chub kyi sems 'dzag pa'i bgrod pa ster ba mo'i phyag rgya nyid la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'dren dgos pa dbang po dman pa'i gnas skabs kyi gang zag dang / byang chub kyi sems g.yo ba'i bgrod pa ster ba mo'i phyag rgya la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'dren dgos pa dbang po 'bring gi gnas skabs kyi gang zag dang / byang sems gnas gzhan du mi g.yo ba'i bgrod pa ster ba mo'i phyag rgya kho na la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'dren pa dbang po mchog gi gnas skabs kyi gang zag dang gsum du yod pas so zhes pa'o/ / de'i khyab 'brel ni phyag rgya gsum po 'di rnams las las kyi phyag rgya ni byang sems dbang po'i sgo nas 'jog pa'i bde ba sbyin pa mo dang / ye shes kyi phyag rgya ni byang sems lus kyi gnas gzhan du g.yo ba'i bde ba sbyin pa mo dang / phyag rgya chen mo ni mi g.yo ba ste mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba sbyin pa mo yin pas so/ /zhes pa'i don no/ /

How are they taught? The words “In this way” refer to the preceding explanation of the words of the tantra. The line “the Buddha taught the meditations of the three mudrā consorts in the six branches” refers to all six branches. The three types of reliance upon the three mudrā consorts, therefore, must be applied in the branch of meditative concentration too. The words of the tantra and corresponding commentary passage require some explanation. As these six branches are divided into meditators “of low intelligence and so forth,” meaning those of middling and high intelligence also, “there are three different and main methods of practice of the Kālacakra” in this branch of meditative concentration. “Three times” refers to the three occasions of practice for those of low, middling, and high intelligence, who rely on activity, wisdom, and mahāmudrā consorts respectively. The reason for this reliance is that “by three paths,” practitioners develop the unchanging bliss of the branch of meditative concentration. “Those of low intelligence” must rely upon a mudrā consort who grants the “path of falling bodhicitta” in order to induce the unchanging bliss. “Those of middling intelligence” rely upon a mudrā consort who grants “the path of moving bodhicitta” as a way of inducing the unchanging bliss. “Those of high intelligence” rely solely upon a mudrā consort who grants “the path of the nonmoving bodhicitta” in order to induce the unchanging bliss. Therefore, among these three consorts, “the activity mudrā consort is the giver of the bliss of falling” bodhicitta, “the wisdom mudrā consort is the giver of the bliss of movement” of bodhicitta to other places in the body, /472/ and “the mahāmudrā consort is the giver of the nonmoving,” or unchanging “bliss.”

'dir las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya 'dzag pa dang g.yo ba'i bde ba sbyin pa mor bshad pa ni phyag rgya gnyis kyi rang dbang gi nus pa'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag gi skabs 'di lta bu la sogs par ni las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas bde ba 'dren na'ang byang sems 'dzag med du 'ching bar byed pa yin no/ / de yang skabs 'di'i rgyud 'grel pa dang bcas pa 'di dag ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag la sbyor dgos pa ni/ mi g.yo ba'i bgrod pa ni mchog gi gnas skabs so zhes dang / phyag rgya chen mo ni mi g.yo ba'i bde ba sbyin pa mo'i zhes gsungs pa 'di dag gis shes te/ phyag rgya chen mos mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba ster ba ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag gi skabs ma gtogs mi 'ong ba'i phyir ro/ /

The descriptions of the activity and wisdom mudrā consorts as consorts who grant falling and moving bliss is made on the basis of these mudrā consorts’ own abilities. During practices such as the branch of meditative concentration, one can induce bliss by relying upon an activity mudrā consort, but the bodhicitta is withheld from emission. That these tantra and commentary passages refer to the branch of meditative concentration can be understood by the lines “the path of the nonmoving bodhicitta during the times of those of high intelligence” and “the mahāmudrā consort is the giver of the nonmoving bliss.” This is because the granting of unchanging bliss by a mahāmudrā consort can only occur on the branch of meditative concentration.

gzhan yang dbang mdor bstan las/
las kyi phyag rgyar snyoms 'jug dang / / ye shes phyag rgya sogs dmigs dang / / phyag rgya chen mo gcig sbyor bas/ / mi 'gyur ba ni 'phel bar byed/[380] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

Furthermore A Short Teaching on Initiations states:
By union with an activity mudrā, visualization of a wisdom mudrā, becoming one with mahāmudrā consort, increase the unchanging bliss.[385]

d.div: [380] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_dbang mdor bstan/ 17_ba5
[385] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 17b5.

f.d: gnyis pa ngo bo'i sgo nas dbye ba
['di ]la gnyis las/
This has two headings: 1. Division into two isolates[386] 2. Division by numbers

d.div: [386] ldog pa. An isolate is a particular aspect of a phenomenon that is separated out by conceptualization, often for the purposes of analysis, even though in reality that aspect is not isolated from — and is in fact of the same nature as and inseparable from — the phenomenon itself and other aspects of the phenomenon. For example, the color of coal and the coal itself are actually inseparable, but one can conceive of the blackness of coal separate from its shape and weight. The conventional truth of a phenomenon and its ultimate truth are inseparable, but they can be isolated for the purposes of analysis. Without isolates it would be impossible to conceptually analyze anything.

f.d: dang po ldog pa tha dad pa'i sgo nas dbye ba ni/

rnam med stong pa nyid la rtse gcig tu bzhugs pa'i mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po dang de dang ngo bo dbyer med pa'i stong gzugs mtshan dang dpe byad kyis brgyan pa'i dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can gnyis so/ /

These are: the supreme unchanging bliss that is single-pointedly engaged in nonaspected emptiness and, secondly, the empty-form Kālacakra, indivisible from that emptiness, in mother-and-father embrace and adorned with the features and marks of an enlightened being.
gnyis pa rim can du 'byung ba grangs kyi sgo nas dbye ba
['di ]la dbye ba dngos dang / rim can du 'byung tshul bshad pa dang / de dag la dwogs pa dpyad pa'o/ /
This is in three outlines: 1. The actual division 2. An explanation of the progression 3. An examination of areas of doubt
dang po [dbye ba dngos ]ni/

mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya'o/ / de yang sa'i dbye bas bcu gnyis su 'gyur ba ni/ rdo rje nor bu'i rtse nas gsang gnas kyi bar la cha gnyis su byas pa'i cha snga ma'i gnas byang chub kyi sems kyis gang ba mi 'gyur zhing g.yo ba med pa las mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma stong brgyad brgya sa dang po dang / de bzhin du phyi ma'i gnas byang sems kyis gang ba mi 'gyur zhing mi g.yo ba las byung ba'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skad cig ma stong brgyad brgya sa gnyis pa dang / de bzhin du lte ba'i rtsa 'khor man chad byang sems kyis gang zhing mi g.yo ba las byung ba'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma sum stong drug brgya'i stong brgyad brgya snga ma sa gsum pa dang / phyi ma sa bzhi pa dang / de nas snying ga'i bar du gang ba las byung ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma sum stong drug brgya'i snga ma stong brgyad brgya sa lnga pa dang / phyi ma stong brgyad brgya sa drug pa dang / de nas mgrin pa'i bar du gang ba las byung ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma sum stong drug brgya'i snga ma stong brgyad brgya sa bdun pa dang / phyi ma stong brgyad brgya sa brgyad pa dang / /de nas dpral ba'i bar du gang ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma sum stong drug brgya'i snga ma stong brgyad brgya sa dgu pa dang / phyi ma stong brgyad brgya sa bcu pa dang / de nas gtsug tor gyi bar byang sems kyis gang ba gnas gzhan du mi 'gyur zhing mi g.yo ba las byung ba'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skad cig ma sum stong drug brgya'i phyed snga ma stong brgyad brgya sa bcu gcig pa dang / phyed phyi ma stong brgyad brgya sa bcu gnyis pa'o/ /

This is a division into 21,600 instances of unchanging bliss. These can be divided into twelve levels. The tip of the vajra jewel to the secret area is divided into two parts. The first part filled with bodhicitta, unchanging and unmoving, produces 1,800 instances of unchanging bliss. This constitutes the first level. /473/ Likewise the second part filled with unchanging and unmoving bodhicitta also produces 1,800 instances of unchanging bliss. This is the second level. Similarly the area up to the navel cakra filled with unmoving bodhicitta will produce 3,600 instances of unchanging bliss. The first 1,800 is the third level and the second 1,800 is the fourth. 3,600 instances of unchanging bliss are produced by the bodhicitta filling the area up to the heart cakra. The first 1,800 belong to the fifth level and the second to the sixth level. 3,600 instances of unchanging bliss are produced from the bodhi citta filling the area up to the throat cakra. The first 1,800 belong to the seventh level and the second to the eighth. 3,600 instances of unchanging bliss are produced by the bodhicitta filling the area up to the forehead cakra. The first 1,800 belong to the ninth level and the second to the tenth level. 3,600 instances of unchanging bliss are produced from the bodhicitta, unmoving and unchanging, that fills the area up to the crown cakra. The first 1,800 belong to the eleventh level and the second to the twelfth level.
gnyis pa rim can du 'byung tshul bshad pa ni/

de yang rdo rje nor bu'i rtse mo'i dbu ma'i nang du thig le ldog po gcig gnas gzhan dang gzhan du mi g.yo bar gnas pa las mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig dang po de skye zhing / thig le des lus kyi bems po'i cha la nyi khri chig stong drug brgya'i char che ba'i cha gcig zos nas med par byed/ mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skad cig dang po des zhag gcig pa dbugs nyi khri chig stong drug brgya rgyu ba'i dbugs gcig bsad nas 'gag par byed pa de bzhin du [381] thig le'i 'phreng ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya po re re las bde ba'i skad cig re re skye ba dang / thig le re res lus kyi bems po'i cha re re za ba dang / bde ba'i skad cig re res dbugs sam srog re re 'gag par shes par bya'o/ / de ltar yang ye le'i brgya bcu bdun pa'i 'grel chen las/
de nas skad cig gcig gis mngon par rdzogs par byang chub pa'i mtshan nyid ni chags dang chags bral mtha' thog la gnas skad cig ma zhes pa la chags pa zhes pa ni dkar po'i phyogs te de'i mthar gnas pa ni cha bcu drug pa'i mtshan nyid do/ / chags bral ni nag po'o/ / de'i dang po la gnas pa ni nag po'i phyogs la ma zhugs pa ste mngon par rdzogs par byang chub pa'i dus kyi mtshan nyid do/ / skad cig ma de nyid kyang dbugs kyi grangs zhes pa nyi khri chig stong drug brgya'i grangs 'phel lo/ / gsang bar rdo rje nor bu'i rtse mo las skad cig ma brgya phrag sum cu rtsa drug gis 'phel te de'i grangs kyi srog rnams bsad nas gsang ba'i pad+ma_ra phyin pa des sa gnyis su 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du lte ba dang snying ga dang mgrin pa dang dpral bar bzhi dang drug dang brgyad dang sa bcu rnams su 'gyur zhing gtsug tor du srog thams cad zad pa sa bcu gnyis so/[382] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

One drop within the central channel at the very tip of the vajra jewel, staying in one place and not moving elsewhere, produces the first instance of unchanging bliss. That drop consumes and destroys one of the 21,600 larger portions that the material body is divided into. This first instance of unchanging bliss “kills” or eliminates one breath of the 21,600 breaths that flow in one day. In a similar manner, one instance of unchanging bliss is produced from each of the 21,600 drops. Each drop consumes one part of the material body, and each instance of bliss destroys one breath or wind. The Great Commentary on verse 117 of the Gnosis chapter says:
Next, full and perfect enlightenment by single instances. In the line “The instance at the end and beginning of desire and nondesire,” the word “desire” refers to the bright side of the month, and its “end” refers to the sixteenth. /474/ “Nondesire” refers to the dark side of the month, and its “beginning” means not having entered the dark side and is the time of full and perfect enlightenment. “Also the instances are the number of breaths” means that they increase to 21,600. From the tip of the secret vajra jewel, the instances are multiplied to 3,600, and that number of winds are killed. Moving to the lotus of the secret area, two levels have been reached. Similarly, at the navel, heart, throat, and forehead, four, six, eight, and ten are reached. At the crown all winds are ended. This is the twelfth.[387]

d.div: [381] ma dper 'gag par byed dpe de bzhin du zhes byung yang byed pa de bzhin du zhes bcos/
[382] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 398_na1
[387] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 398a1.

f.d: de dag gi don cung zad cig bshad na/ mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig gis mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas pa na skad cig gis mngon par rdzogs par byang chub pa'o/ / de yang ji ltar na phyi la zla ba'i dkar cha 'phel ba'i cha bco lnga yod cing bco lnga yod pa'i mthar dngos gnas la 'phel cha bcu drug pa med kyang / nag cha dang po ma zhugs pa'i 'tshams der cha bcu drug pa cig blos bcos pa dkar po'i phyogs kyi mthar gnas pa ni cha bcu drug pa'i mtshan nyid do/ / de bzhin du nang la rkang pa g.yon pa'i mthe bong nas gtsug tor gyi bar la thig le'i dkar cha 'phel ba'i cha bcu drug yod pa'i tha ma ni cha bcu drug pa'i mtshan nyid do/ / lam la byang sems gtsug tor nas rdo rje nor bu'i rtse bar babs pa'i dga' ba bcu drug pa'i cha'i mthar mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skad cig dang po 'phel ba nas gtsug tor du skad cig tha ma 'phel ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma'i mthar mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas pa ni skad cig gis mngon par rdzogs par byang chub pa'i mtshan nyid do/ / bde ba'i skad cig de'i 'phel tshul ston pa ni/ skad cig ma de nyid kyang zhes sogs te don ni gong du bshad zin pa ltar ro/ /

To explain this passage a little, “Full and perfect enlightenment by single instances” refers to instances of unchanging bliss. How is this attained? In the outer world the waxing period or bright side of the moon is divided into fifteen sections, and although in reality there is no sixteenth after these fifteen, a sixteenth is mentally created at the point of entry into the first division of the dark side. Therefore “at the end” of the bright side is the sixteenth part. Likewise, internally from the large toe of the left foot to the crown, the increase in the white part of the drops is divided into sixteen, and the last of these “refers to the sixteenth.” On the path, the bodhicitta descends from the crown to the tip of the vajra jewel to create the sixteen joys, at the end of which the first instance of unchanging bliss is formed and increases until its last increase, at the end of which full and perfect buddhahood is attained. This is “full and perfect enlightenment by single instances.” How these instances increase is taught by the lines beginning “Also, the instances.” This has been explained previously.

de yang mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba de rnams ni stong gzugs phyag rgya chen mo sna tshogs yum gyi rnam pa can gyis thun mong ma yin pa'i rgyu byas pa las byung ba yin na'ang / mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po nyi khri chig stong drug brgya po thams cad kyang rang dus kyi stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi rnam pa can rnams dang ngo bo dbyer med gcig yin pa 'jig rten las 'das pa'i dbang bzhi pa'i don yin no/ / 'di dag gi shes byed ni dbang le'i dbang bzhi pa'i don 'chad pa'i skabs su dbang mdor bstan las/ phyag rgya chen mo rjes chags las/[383] /zhes sogs rtsa 'grel gyi don zhib tu bshad zin pa rnams dran par bya'o/ /

Although these instances of supreme and unchanging bliss arise from their special cause, which is the empty-form mahāmudrā consort in the aspect of Viśvamātā, each of the 21,600 instances of unchanging bliss is indivisible from oneself as an empty-form Kālacakra in mother-and-father aspect. /475/ This is the significance of the nonworldly fourth initiation. The authority for this assertion can be known from a verse from A Short Teaching on Initiations beginning “From desire for the mahāmudrā,”[388] which was quoted in the explanation of the fourth initiation from the Initiation chapter, and the detailed explanations given there should be recalled.

d.div: [383] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_dbang mdor bstan/ 14_ba6
[388] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 14b6.

f.d: gsum pa de dag la dwogs pa dpyad pa

d.i: An examination of areas of doubt

f.d: ['di ]la mchog mi 'gyur gyi bde ba rnams sa rnams su 'jog tshul la dwogs pa dpyad pa dang / bde bas stong nyid sgom tshul la dwogs pa dpyad pa gnyis so/ /
This is under two headings: 1. How the instances of supreme and unchanging bliss are assigned to the levels 2. How bliss meditates upon emptiness
dang po [mchog mi 'gyur gyi bde ba sa rnams su 'jog tshul la dwogs pa dpyad pa ]

d.i: How the instances of supreme and unchanging bliss are assigned to the levels

f.d: ['di ]la de ltar dpyad pa'i gzhi sa bcu gnyis 'grel chen las gsungs pa dgod pa dang / de la dwogs pa dpyad pa gnyis/ /
This has two outlines: 1. The basis for the examination, the Great Commentary text on the twelve levels 2. An examination of the areas of doubt regarding this text
dang po [de ltar dpyad pa'i gzhi sa bcu gnyis 'grel chen las gsungs pa dgod pa ]ni

d.i: The basis for the examination, the Great Commentary text on the twelve levels

f.d:
mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus las/
'dir sa dang po thob pa las phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams gcig gi mthar thug par ma mthong ba'i don yang dag par mthong ngo / / zhes pa nas/
de nas stong chen po zhes bya ba grangs med pa chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams rnams te de rnams su ma mthong ba'i don yang dag par mthong bar yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi sa bcu gnyis thob pa las 'gyur gyi 'dod chags dang bral ba rnams kyis ni ma yin no/ / shes rab kyi chags pa las byung ba'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po'i skad cig rnams kyis de bzhin gshegs pa'i sa 'di rnams thob ste mi 'pho ba'i skad cig brgya phrag bco brgyad thob pas sa dang po thob bo/ / grangs 'dis sa bcu gnyis kyi mthar thug par ro/ / mi 'gyur ba'i skad cig nyi khri chig stong drug brgya rnams kyis sa bcu gnyis thob ste yan lag bcu gnyis 'gags pa ji srid par ro/[384] / zhes pa'i bar gsungs pa rnams so/ /

The relevant text is found in the Supreme and Unchanging Gnosis summary from the Gnosis chapter beginning from the lines,
From the attainment of the first level comes the perfect seeing that is ultimately the nonseeing of the world realms of the ten directions. and continues until,
“Then, the great thousand” refers to the world realms of the great uncountable. The perfect seeing that is the nonseeing of these worlds is the attainment of the twelfth level of perfect enlightenment. This is not attained by the absence of “changing” desire. It is by the instances of unchanging bliss arising from desire for wisdom that these tathāgata levels are achieved. Accomplishing 1,800 nonmoving instances is to attain the first level, and by these numbers the twelve levels are finally attained. By 21,600 unchanging instances, the twelve levels are reached and the links of dependent origination are negated.[389]

f.d: gnyis pa de la dwogs pa dpyad pa

d.i: An examination of the areas of doubt regarding this text

f.d: ['di ]la mkhas pa snga ma rnams kyi dgongs pa bkod nas de dag la 'thad mi 'thad dpyad pa dang / rang gi go tshod tsam dgod pa gnyis so/ /
This has two outlines: 1. The positions of past scholars and their invalidity 2. A statement of our own understanding
dang po [mkhas pa snga ma rnams kyi dgongs pa bkod nas de dag la 'thad mi 'thad dpyad pa ]ni

d.i: The positions of past scholars and their invalidity

f.d:
thams cad mkhyen pa bus nges don snye ma las/
'di la kha cig na re/ pha rol tu phyin pa'i sa kun du 'od ni rgyu la 'bras bu'i ming gis sangs rgyas su btags pa yin gyi sangs rgyas dngos ni ma yin nozhes zer ba'i phyogs snga bkod nas/ de 'gog pa na/
mi 'thad de/ man ngag snye ma dang kye rdor 'grel pa b+ha wa b+ha dras mdzad pa las kun tu 'od kyis sangs rgyas kyi sar gsungs shing / mu tig 'phreng bar yang bcu gcig pa sangs rgyas kyi sar gsungs so/[385] / zhes bkag nas/ khong rang gi bzhed pa ni/
des na pha rol tu phyin pa'i lugs kyi sa bcu pa la sa bcu pa tsam dang khyad par gyi lam dang bar chad med pa'i lam gsum du byed pas de'i bar chad med pa'i lam ni 'di'i lugs kyi sa bcu gcig pa yin zhing kun du 'od ni [386] sa bcu gnyis pa yin no [387] zhes gsung la/ de dag gi gzhan rnams 'thad pa'i tshul 'og tu 'chad la/ 'on kyang kun tu 'od sangs rgyas kyi sar byas nas 'di'i lugs kyi sa bcu gnyis par byed pa mi 'thad de/ 'di'i lugs kyi sa bcu gnyis pa la mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig stong brgyad brgya yod pa'i stong bdun brgya go dgu po rnams slob pa'i lam yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

The omniscient Butön in his Sheaves of Definitive Meanings says: /476/
On this, some say that the Perfection Vehicle level[390] known as all light is an instance of the cause being given the name of the effect and that it is labeled “enlightenment” but actually is not enlightenment. Here he presents the other’s position. In refutation he says:
That is incorrect. In Sheaves of Oral Transmission and the Hevajra Commentary by Bhavabhadra, it is stated that the level of all light is the level of buddha. In Garland of Pearls[391] also it is stated as being the level of buddha.[392] Concerning his own position:
Therefore, in the Perfection Vehicle system, the tenth level consists of the mere, the special, and the uninterrupted path. Of these three the uninterrupted path is the eleventh level of the Kālacakra tradition, and the level of all light is the level of buddha. The validity of other parts of these passages will be explained later, but to posit all light as the level of buddha and then to say that this is the twelfth level of the Kālacakra tradition is incorrect, because on the twelfth level in this tradition, 1,799 instances of unchanging bliss out of a set of 1,800 belong to the path of practice.[393]

d.div: [385] bu ston rin chen grub/ gsung 'bum pod/ nga nges don snye ma/ 25_na6
[386] ma dper kun du 'di ni zhes byung yang kun tu 'od ni zhes bcos/
[387] bu ston rin chen grub/ gsung 'bum pod/ nga nges don snye ma/ 25_na6

[390] In the nontantric Perfection Vehicle, ten bodhisattva levels begin upon the attainment of the path of seeing, the first moment of becoming an ārya, or “noble one.” The tenth level immediately precedes enlightenment, and it is generally accepted that the (eleventh) level, known as all light, refers to enlightenment itself.
[391] A commentary on the difficult points of Hevajra.
[392] Collected Works, vol. nga, 25a6.

[393] The first four paths (of accumulation, preparation, seeing, and meditation) are paths of practice. The fifth is a path of no further practice or no further learning, synonymous with enlightenment.

f.d: yang slob dpon shAn+ti pa dang b+ha wa b+ha dra gnyis kyis mos pas spyod pa'i sa dang byang chub sems dpa'i sa bcu dang kun tu 'od kyi sa rnams sa bcu gnyis por gsungs shing / mkhas pa gzhan dag kyang mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba stong brgyad brgya pa chen po dang po mos spyod kyis dang / tshan pa gnyis pa sa dang por rab dgar bzhed pa dang / kha cig gzhan snga ma dang 'dra ba la stong brgyad brgya pa tshan pa dang po'i skad cig tha ma nas sa dang po'i 'go 'dzin par bzhed do/ /

The master Śāntipa[394] and Bhavabhadra say that the twelve levels are made up by the level of practice by belief,[395] the ten bodhisattva levels, and the level all light. Other scholars also assert that the first set of 1,800 instances of unchanging bliss is the level of practice by belief and that the second set is the first bodhisattva level, great joy. Similarly others maintain that the first level begins with the last moment of the first set of 1,800.

d.div: [394] Author of Garland of Pearls mentioned above.
[395] mos pas spyod pa’ sa. Usually synonymous with the first two paths of accumulation and preparation, where emptiness has not been directly perceived.

f.d:
'di'i lugs kyi sa bcu gnyis kyi dang po mos spyod kyi sar 'jog pa mi 'thad do/ 'di'i lus kyi sa dang po bde ba'i skad cig stong brgyad brgya pa tshan pa dang po 'di mos spyod kyi sa yin na 'di'i lugs kyi sa bcu pa bde ba'i skad cig stong brgyad brgya pa tshan pa bcu pa de sa dgu pa legs pa'i blo glos yin dgos/ de yin na sa bcu'i dbang phyug dpal phyag na rdo rje sa dgu pa par 'byung ste/ 'grel chen las phyag rdor gyi las rlung nyi khri chig stong drug brgya'i nang gi gsum stong drug brgya ma 'gags pa 'di'i lugs kyi sa bcug gcig pa ma thob par bshad pa da lta nyid tu 'dren pa ltar yin pa'i phyir dang / nyi ma dpal gyis yon tan gyi+is 'gengs pa las/
de ltar 'khor lo so sor sa gnyis 'thob pa'i rim pas sa bcu gnyis kyi dbang phyug tu 'gyur ro/ / de ltar na gsang ba'i 'khor lo dbugs 'byung ba dang 'jug pa brgya phrag drug lhag pa'i stong phrag gsum 'gog pas rab tu dga' ba dang dri ma med pa'i sa gnyis so/ / lte ba'i 'khor lo de bzhin kho nar 'gags pas 'od byed pa dang 'od 'phro ba'i sa gnyis so/ / de bzhin kho nar snying ga'i chu skyes su shin tu thub par dka' ba dang / mngon du gyur pa'i sa gnyis so/[388] / zhes sogs dus kyi 'khor lo 'di'i lugs kyi sa bcu gnyis kyi bcu pa man chad rab tu dga' ba sogs bcur bshad pa dang yang 'gal ba'i phyir ro/ /

It is incorrect to posit the first of the twelve levels in this tradition as being the level of practice by belief. If the first level with its initial set of 1,800 instances of unchanging bliss is equated with the level of practice by belief, then the tenth set of 1,800 would have to correspond to the ninth level, excellent mind. If that were the case, “glorious Vajrapāṇi, the mighty one of the tenth level,” would have to be on the ninth level, because the Great Commentary states, as will be quoted, that of the 21,600 karmic winds of Vajrapāṇi, 3,600 remain undestroyed /477/ and that he has not reached the eleventh level of this tradition. Sūryaśrī in his Filled with Good Qualities says:
By the process of attaining two levels at each of the cakras, one becomes the mighty one of the twelve levels. In this way, by negating 3,600 in-and-out breaths at the secret cakra, the two levels of great joy and purity are attained. By negating the same at the navel cakra, the two levels of light and blazing light are attained. Similarly, at the heart lotus, the levels of hard to overcome and manifest are attained.[396] Therefore the above assertions contradict the fact that the first ten of the twelve levels of the Kālacakra tradition correspond to the ten levels of great joy and so forth.

d.div: [388] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ pa_yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 326_na5
[396] Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 326a5.

f.d:
yang mkhas pa'i gsung rab rgyud gsum gsang ba rnam 'byed ces bya ba las/
dgra bcom pa sku tshe'i 'du byed btang nas yid kyi lus su gnas pa'i gnas skabs kyi lus de srid pa bar do'i lus dang rigs 'dra zhing de bzhin du rmi lam gyi lus dang yang 'dra mod kyi/ bar do dngos ma yin la rmi lam gyi lus kyang ma yin no/ / 'on kyang theg pa chen por 'jug pa na yid kyi lus de nyid kyis 'jug cing / theg pa chen por ma zhugs pa'i snga rol tu mngon par shes pa la sogs pa'i yon tan gong nas gong du gyur pas dman pa'i sa bcu gcig bgrod nas da gzod theg pa chen por 'jug go/ / yon tan gyi khyad par mi 'dra zhe na/ de ni 'grel chen las/ 'ji+ig rten gyi khams rnams su ma mthong ba'i don yang dag par mthong ba'i grangs bzung nas [389] gsungs te/ de yang sa dang po thob pas phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams gcig dang / gnyis pa thob pas gnyis dang /[390] zhes sogs gsungs nas/ 'grel chen las mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya sa bcu gnyis su [391] gsungs pa'i sa bcu gnyis kyi yon tan rnams theg dman dgra bcom yid kyi lus can theg chen du zhugs pa'i yon tan du sbyar nas 'chad do/ /

In a work called Opening the Secrets of the Three Tantras it says:
When an arhat has exhausted his bodily formation he inhabits a mental body. This body is similar to a bardo body and to a dream body. However it is not an actual bardo body nor is it an actual dream body. Nevertheless, if he enters the Mahayana, he enters it with this mental body. Prior to entering the Mahayana he increases his powers of clairvoyance and so forth. By doing so he moves through the eleven lower levels and only then enters the Mahayana. Are there differences in the qualities of these levels? The Great Commentary says, “Counting begins from the perfect seeing, that is the nonseeing of the world realms”[397] Therefore with the attainment of the first level comes the perfect seeing of one ten-direction world realm. With the attainment of the second comes two.[398] In the Great Commentary the 21,600 instances of unchanging bliss are spoken of as the twelve levels,[399] and in the above passage the qualities of these twelve levels are assigned to the qualities of a Hinayana arhat entering the Mahayana with a mental body.

d.div: [389] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 428_na7
[390] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 428_na7
[391] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 428_ba7
[397] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 428a7.
[398] Source not found.

f.d: 'di lta bu'i 'chad tshul ni shin tu kyog pa'i 'chad tshul du snang te/ 'grel chen las 'di ltar gsungs pa rnams ni mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya pa bcu gnyis su bsdus nas 'chad pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag gi lam gyi gzhung zhing yin zhing / lam gyi gzhung zhi+ing 'di ni dus kyi 'khor lo'i ched du bya ba'i gdul bya'i gtso bo dang po nas sngags lam nyid la 'jug pa'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi/ theg dman theg chen du zhugs pa'i dbang du byas pa ga la yin/ gzhan yang theg dman theg chen du 'jug pa dang po nas ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag nas 'jug pa ni be'u bya long med par glang rgan du song ba dang mtshungs sam snyam mo/ /

This appears to be a very distorted explanation. These passages from the Great Commentary are passages at the very heart of the path of the branch of meditative concentration, /478/ which is explained by condensing the 21,600 instances of unchanging bliss into twelve levels. Such a core path is for the intended disciples of the Kālacakra who enter the path of mantra from its beginning. How could it be for those of the Hinayana who enter the Mahayana! Furthermore, for those of the Hinayana to enter the Mahayana at the branch of meditative concentration would be like a calf becoming an old bull without the intervening process of growing up.

gzhan yang mkhas pa 'di 'di ltar bzhed par mngon te/ mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya rdzogs te dus sbyor bcu gnyis kyi rlung 'gags nas ye shes kyi sku 'grub la de'i snga rol du mi 'grub pa dang / ye shes kyi sku de yang pha rol tu phyin pa'i sa'i dbang du byas nas dang po thob pa na 'thob par bzhed par mngon te/ rgyud gsum gsang ba rnam 'byed las/
'grel pa sgron ma gsal ba las/ lang kar gshegs par/ rab tu dga' ba'i sa bsgrubs nas/ / bde ba can du de 'gro 'o/ / zhes slob dpon klu sgrub kyis sa rab tu dga' ba bsgrubs pa'i don 'chad pa na/ / slob dpon gyis rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa'i rdo rje 'dzin pa'i sku brnyes par bshad pa de yang zung du 'jug pa'am ye shes kyi sku de nyid la sangs rgyas zhes brjod pa'i dbang du mdzad do zhes shes par bya'o/[392] zhes gsungs pa las so/ /

Moreover it seems that this scholar thinks the following. When the 21,600 instances of unchanging bliss have been achieved and the winds of the twelve lagna[400] have been negated, then will the gnosis body be gained and not before. Moreover this gnosis body is attained when the first of the Perfection Vehicle levels is attained. In his work Opening the Secrets of the Three Tantras, he says:
Bright Lamp says, “In the Laṅkāvatārasūtra it says, ‘Having attained the level of great joy, he will go to Sukhāvatī.’”[401] Therefore, when explaining the meaning of the master Nāgārjuna’s attainment of the level of great joy, the assertion that he gained the form of Vajradhara endowed with every supreme aspect is made on the basis of that union or gnosis body being labeled as buddha.

d.div: [392] sde dge_1785_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ hagasang 'dus 'grel pa sgron gsal/ 200_na4
[400] Here lagna refers to the twelve air movements at the navel cakra.
[401] Toh 1785 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ha, 200a4.

f.d:
gal te de lta min na sa bcu'i dbang phyug 'phags pa phyag na rdo rjes kyang sa dang po rab tu dga' ba sngon ma thob par ha cang thal bar 'gyur te/ /phyag na rdo rje'i las rlung sum stong drug brgya 'pho ba 'am dus sbyor gnyis ma 'gags par 'grel chen las gsal bar gsungs pa'i phyir te/ 'jig rten khams le'i mdor bsdus gnyis pa las/
nags kyi ri dwags kyi bdag po zhes pa bzhin du ro ldan na gnas pa gnod sbyin chen po rnams kyi bdag po'o/ nang du ni ro zhes pa dbugs 'byung ba dang 'jug pa sum stong drug brgyas dman pa'i nyi khri chig stong drug brgya rnams 'gags pa'o/ / de 'di la yod pa ni chos kyi sprin gyis te de la gnas pa ni ro ldan na gnas pa'o/[393] / zhes gsungs pa'o/ /

If this were the case, it would have to follow that the ārya Vajrapāṇi, the mighty one of the tenth level, would not have previously attained even the first level of great joy, because it is clearly stated in the Great Commentary that the movements of 3,600 karmic winds, or two lagna, of Vajrapāṇi have not been negated. The second summary from the Realms chapter of the Great Commentary says:
The master of the great yakṣa dwells in the Place of Corpses[402] like the “master of the beasts of the forests.” Internally “corpse” refers to the cessation of 21,600 in-and-out breaths less 3,600. “He dwells here, on the level of the cloud of dharma,” means that by dwelling there, he dwells in the Place of Corpses.[403]

d.div: [393] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 14_ba7

[402] ro ldan, aḍakavatī (Newman, p. 273). In Tibetan ro can mean either “corpse” or “taste.” As “taste” the Place of Tastes could be Rasavatī. Externally it is the residence of Vajrapāṇi; internally it refers to the tenth bodhisattva level.
[403] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 14b7.

f.d:
gzhan yang mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya rdzogs pa'i mthar rdo rje sems dpa' dang rdo rje 'chang 'thob par bshad pa rnams sa dang po'i skabs kyi ye shes kyi sku 'grub pa nyid la 'chad na 'grel chen las/
tha ma'i mtshan ma ni sangs rgyas nyid dang rdo rje 'chang nyid de mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i skad cig drug brgya lhag pa'i stong phrag nyi shu rtsa gcig gis sa bcu gnyis pa thob nas phyag rgya chen po'i dngos grub thob pa'o/[394] / zhes pa dang / yang de nyid las/
des na sems can thams cad la 'jig rten dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i chos bstan pa'i phyir sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das sngon sa bcu gnyis kyi dbang phyug tu gyur pa mkhas pa sgyu 'phrul chen po 'chang ba sgyu 'phrul chen po'i mig 'phrul dang ldan pa 'phags pa'i yul lu lam+bi nir shAkya'i rigs/[395] zhes sogs kyi sa bcu gnyis kyang pha rol tu phyin pa'i sa dang po'i snga rol gyi sa la byed dgos la/ de ltar na mkhas pa sgyu 'phrul chen po sogs kyang sangs rgyas mtshan nyid pa ma yin par 'chad dgos pa sogs brjod kyis mi lang ba zhig go/ / gzhan yang brjod par bya ba mang ste re zhig de tsam mo/ /

Furthermore, if the completion of the 21,600 instances of unchanging bliss explained as being the attainment of the states of Vajrasattva and Vajradhara /479/ is equated with the attainment of a gnosis body realized on the first level, then consider these passages from the Great Commentary:
The final signs are those of the Buddha and of Vajradhara. This is the twelfth level attained by 21,600 instances of supreme and unchanging bliss. This attainment is the actual attainment of the great mahāmudrā.[404] Also:
In order to teach living beings worldly and nonworldly dharma, the enlightened conqueror, the Buddha, already the mighty one of the twelve levels, wise, master of the great illusion, of the great magical and optical illusion, was born in Lumbini of the Śākya family.[405] If the above assertion were correct, the twelve levels mentioned in these passages would have to be levels attained prior to the attainment of the first level of the Perfection Vehicle tradition. In that case the description “wise, master of the great illusion” and so on would have to be explained as not referring to an actual enlightened being. This is beyond words. There is a lot more to say on this subject, but that is enough for now.

f.d: gnyis pa rang gi go tshod tsam dgod pa ni/

d.i: A statement of our own understanding

f.d: thams cad mkhyen pa bus gsungs pa ltar dus 'khor lugs kyi sa dang po ni 'phags pa'i sa dang po rab dga' la byed pa nas/ dgu pa yang dgu pa legs pa'i blo gros la byed la/ sa bcu pa chos kyi sprin la pha rol tu phyin pa'i lugs kyi sa bcu pa tsam dang / khyad par gyi lam dang / bar chad med pa'i lam dang gsum byed pa'i 'di pa'i lugs kyi sa bcu pa bcu pa tsam dang / bcu gcig pa khyad par gyi lam/ bcu gnyis pa bar chad med pa'i lam dang / bcu gnyis pa'i tha ma mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya pa'i mthar sa bcu gcig pa kun tu 'od kyis rdo rje 'chang gi go 'phang brnyes par 'jog go/ /

As the omniscient Butön has said, the first level in the Kālacakra tradition corresponds to the first ārya level, great joy, and the ninth level corresponds to the ninth ārya level, excellent mind. In the Perfection Vehicle tradition the tenth level, the cloud of dharma, is divided into the mere, the special, and the uninterrupted paths. In the Kālacakra tradition the tenth level is the mere tenth, the eleventh is the special path, and the twelfth is the uninterrupted path. The end of the twelfth, after instance 21,600 of unchanging bliss, is established as the level of all light, or the eleventh-level[406] state of Vajradhara.

d.div: [406] Therefore, although the Kālacakra tradition talks of twelve levels, in other tantras the state of Vajradhara is known as the eleventh level, all light.

f.d:
gal te 'grel chen las/ 'dir sa dang po thob pa las phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams gcig gi mthar thug par don yang dag par mthong ngo / /zhes pa nas/ sa bcu pa thob pa las phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams lnga brgya bcu gnyis kyi mthar thug par ro/[396] /zhes sogs kyi bar gsungs pa'i sa'i yon tan rnams dbu ma 'jug par gsungs pa'i sa'i yon tan rnams las ches shin tu nyung ba dang / khyad par du yang dbu ma 'jug pa las/
re shig bcu pa 'dir de'i yon tan dag / ngag gi spyod yul las ches 'das gyur cing / / ngag gi spyod yul ma yin bsdoms rnams na/ / rdul dag ji snyed yod pa de snyed 'gyur/[397] / zhes gsungs pa dang 'gal zhing / 'jug par gsungs pa 'di dag kyang sa bcu pa'i mdo'i dgongs pa bkod pa yin pas dus 'khor gyi lugs kyi sa 'di rnams 'phags pa'i sa bcur ji ltar rigs snyam na/ 'o na 'jug pa nas bshad ba'i sa'i yon tan 'di rnams dus 'khor dang 'gal bas mi rigs zhes brjod na ji ltar bgyi/ 'on kyang sangs rgyas la mtshan dpe'i sgo nas bstod pa sangs rgyas kyi yon tan gyi phyogs gcig nas brjod pa dang 'dra bar 'grel chen las/ sa'i yon tan bstan pa 'di dag kyang yon tan gyi phyogs re tsam bstan par byas na 'thad dam snyam ste dpyod ldan rnams kyis dpyad par bya dgos so/ /

The qualities gained from these levels are taught in the Great Commentary beginning from “From the attainment of the first level comes the perfect seeing that is ultimately the nonseeing of the world realms of the ten directions” up to “From the attainment of the tenth level comes the perfect seeing of 512 world realms of the ten directions.”[407] The qualities mentioned here are far fewer than those mentioned in the Madhyamakāvatāra, and they especially seem to contradict the verse from the Madhyamakāvatāra that runs:
The qualities here on the tenth /480/ are far beyond the abilities of speech; not within the realms of speech, Buddha fields gained as many in number as the number of atoms.[408] You might say that the qualities of the levels taught in the Madhyamakāvatāra come from the Sutra of the Ten Levels, so how can the levels as they are taught in the Kālacakra tradition be a valid description of the ten levels of the ārya? Well, what if you were to say that the qualities of the levels taught in the Madhyamakāvatāra are wrong because they contradict those of the Kālacakra? I think that just as praising the Buddha by talking of his features and signs of enlightenment is to speak of only a part of Buddha’s qualities, so the qualities of the levels as taught in the Great Commentary are but a fraction of his qualities, but scholars should examine this.

d.div: [396] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 428_na7
[397] sde dge_3861_bstan/ dbu ma/ 'asems bskyed/ 10_sh+loka8_216_na3
[407] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 428a7.
[408] Toh 3861 Tengyur, dbu ma, ah, chap. 10, v. 8, 216a3.

f.d: gnyis pa bde bas stong nyid sgom tshul la dwogs pa dpyad pa
['di ]la gnyis/ bsgom bya'i yul stong nyid kyi don la dwogs pa dpyad pa dang/ de bde bas sgom tshul mdor bsdus te bstan pa'o/ /
This has two outlines: 1. Examining doubts over the nature of the emptiness to be meditated upon 2. A brief explanation of how bliss meditates upon emptiness

dang po ni kha cig na re/ dpal dus kyi 'khor lor bshad pa'i bsgom bya'i stong nyid ni rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong nyid kho na yin te/ dgag bya bcad tsam gyi stong nyid phar phyin theg pa nas bshad pa ni snying po med par bshad pa'i phyir te/ rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa las/
phung po rnam dpyad stong pa ni/ / chu shing bzhin du snying po med/ / rnam pa kun gyi mchog ldan pa'i/ / stong nyid de ltar 'gyur ma yin/[398] / zhes gsungs pas so zhes zer ro/ /

Some say that the emptiness to be meditated on in the glorious Kālacakra refers solely to the emptiness endowed with every supreme aspect, because emptiness as mere negation of the object of refutation as taught in the Perfection Vehicle is explained as having no essence. This, they say, is confirmed by A Short Teaching on Our Assertions Concerning the View, which says:
The emptiness of examining the aggregates is without essence like the plantain tree. Emptiness endowed with supreme characteristics is not like that.[409]

d.div: [398] pe cing bstan 'gyur nas kha bskang ba dar thang dpar ma'i pod/ pu/ chos tshan ang / 4530_rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa/ 23_ba1
[409] P 4580 nu. Tengyur, sngags skor, bu, 23b1.

f.d:
de'i lan la 'di ltar gsung ste/
phung po rnam dpyad stong pa ni/ /chu shing bzhin du snying po med/[399] /ces pa'i don ni phung po sogs rigs pas dpyad pas ci yang ma rnyed pa na gtan nas med pa'i don du lta ba'i chad lta la snying po med bcas pa yin te/ 'di dang don gcig par mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus las/ /rdul phra rab tshogs pa'i bdag nyid kyi chos rnam par dpyad pa'i stong pa chad pa'i stong pa nyid las ring du byas pa/[400] zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /de ltar na chos thams cad kyi gnas lugs stong pa nyid la skur ba 'debs pa khyod ni ngo mtshar rozhes gsung ngo / /

In reply to this assertion it has been said:
“The emptiness of examining the aggregates is without essence like the plantain tree.” The meaning of these lines is that when examining the aggregates with analysis and nothing is found, it is “without essence” to conclude that nothing therefore exists at all and to fall to a view of nihilism. Synonymous with that is a quote from the Supreme and Unchanging summary in the Gnosis chapter: /481/ “The emptiness that comes from examining phenomena that are a collection of subtle atoms is an emptiness far from a nonexistence emptiness.”[410] Therefore you should be ashamed to deprecate the emptiness that is the nature of all phenomena.[411]

d.div: [399] pe cing bstan 'gyur nas kha bskang ba dar thang dpar ma'i pod/ pu/ chos tshan ang / 4530_rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa/ 23_ba1
[400] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 395_na6
[410] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 395a6.
[411] Text not traced.

f.d:
'on kyang lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa'i gzhung 'di dag gi don ni 'di ltar du go ste/ de yang de nyid las/ /
phung po rnam dpyad stong pa ni/ / chu shing bzhin du snying po med/ / rnam pa kun gyi mchog ldan pa'i/ / stong nyid de ltar 'gyur ma yin/ / skye ba med cing 'gag med pa'i/ / shes bya'i don rnams mthong ba yi/ / stong nyid stong pa sgom pa ni/ / phung po rnam dpyad ma yin no/ / chos rnams thams cad stong pa nyid/ / rgyal bas snying po med par gsungs/ / gang rnams stong pa nyid mthong ba'i/ sgrub thabs 'di ni gsungs pa'o/ / snying rje'i chos rnams thams cad rnams/ / snying po med par rgyal bas gsungs/ / gang rnams snying rje mthong ba yi/ / sgrub thabs 'di ni gsungs pa'o/ / thog ma tha ma med zhi ba/ / dngos dang dngos med zad pa'i gtso/ / stong nyid snying rje gnyis med pa/ / byang chub sems zhes bshad pa'o/[401] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyi don zhib tu bshad na skabs kyi don bde blag tu rtogs par 'gyur bas bshad par bya'o/ /

However the verses of A Short Teaching on Assertions Concerning the View can be understood in the following way:
The emptiness of examining the aggregates is without essence like the plantain tree. Emptiness endowed with supreme characteristics is not like that. Emptiness seen as phenomena, without birth, without cessation: Meditation upon that emptiness is not investigation of the aggregates. All phenomena are empty, said by the Buddha to be without essence. For practitioners to see emptiness, he taught this method. All phenomena of compassion are said by the Buddha to be without essence. For practitioners to see compassion, he taught this method. Pacification that is without beginning or ending, the fundamental nature[412] of phenomena and nonphenomena extinct, the indivisibility of emptiness and compassion, this is taught to be bodhicitta.[413] If these verses are explained in detail, the context will be more easily understood.

d.div: [401] pe cing bstan 'gyur nas kha bskang ba dar thang dpar ma'i pod/ pu/ chos tshan ang / 4530_rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa/ 23_ba1
[412] gtso bo, pradhāna/prakṛiti. Main, prime, universal principle, fundamental nature.
[413] P 4580 Tengyur, sngags skor, bu, 23b1.

f.d: de yang dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i cha lag lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa 'di las bshad pa'i bsgom bya'i stong nyid 'di la rnam med kyi stong nyid dang rnam bcas kyi stong nyid gnyis su yod pa las dang po rnam med kyi stong nyid ni phung sogs kyi chos rnams so sor rtog pa'i shes rab kyis rnam par dpyad pas chu shing bzhin du phung sogs kyi snying po rnyed rgyu med pa'i stong pa nyid yin zhing / rnam bcas sam rnam pa kun gyi mchog dang ldan pa'i stong pa nyid stong gzugs rnams ni dgag bya rigs pas bcad tsam gyi stong nyid de ltar du 'gyur ba ma yin no/ / 'o na ji lta bu snyam na/ rang bzhin gyis skye ba med pa dang 'gag pa med pas khyad par du byas pa'i shes bya'i don khams gsum po rnams pra phab pa lta bur mthong ba'i stong pa nyid kyi gzugs de yin no/ / de lta bu'i stong pa sgom pa de ni phung sogs kyi chos rnams so sor rtog pa'i shes rab kyis rnam par dpyad nas sgom pa'i tshul ma yin no/ /

The emptiness taught as an object of meditation in A Short Teaching on Assertions Concerning the View, which supplements the Kālacakra, is of two types: nonaspected emptiness and aspected emptiness. The first type is an emptiness in which the aggregates and so forth are investigated by an analytical mind and, like the plantain tree, their essence is not to be found. Aspected emptiness or empty-form “emptiness endowed with supreme characteristics is not like that.” It is not an emptiness that is the mere refutation of the object to be refuted by analysis. So what is it? It refers to forms of “emptiness seen as phenomena” of the three realms, characterized by being devoid of the nature of birth or cessation like images in a prognostic mirror. Meditation upon that emptiness is not like the meditation in which the aggregates and so forth are investigated by an analytical mind. /482/

de ltar na phung sogs kyi chos rnams thams cad so sor rtog pa'i shesarab kyis dpyad nas rdul tsam yang ma rnyed pa'i stong pa nyid yin pas rgyal bas chos thams cad la snying po med par gsungs so/ / lam 'di'i sgrub pa po gang yin pa rnams kyis stong pa nyid rnam bcas dang rnam med gnyis mthong ba'i thabs su sgrub thabs 'di gsungs pa'o/ / de bzhin du snying rje'i chos thun mong yin min rnams thams cad rigs pas dpyad na rdul tsam yang mi rnyed pas snying po med par chu shing bzhin du rgyal bas gsungs so/ / de lta yin pa 'on kyang lam 'di'i sgrub pa po gang yin pa rnams kyi thun mong dang thun mong ma yin pa'i snying rje mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po mthong ba'i thabs su sgrub thabs 'di gsungs pa'o/ / de ltar na thog ma dang tha ma rang bzhin gyis med pa'i zhi ba/ dngos po dang dngos med gdod ma nas zad pa'i gtso bo/ rnam bcas rnam med kyi stong pa nyid gnyis dang snying rje mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po ngo bo gnyis su dbyer med pa de la byang chub kyi sems zhes bshad pa'o/ /

Therefore when all phenomena, the aggregates and so forth, are investigated with an analytical mind, the result is an emptiness of not finding a single atom. Therefore all phenomena are said by the Buddha to be without essence. He taught this as a method for practitioners of this path to see aspected and nonaspected emptiness. Similarly, when all phenomena of compassion, common or exclusive, are investigated by analysis, not a single atom is found. Therefore the Buddha said that they were without essence like the plantain tree. Nevertheless, for practitioners of this path, he taught this as a method to see the common compassion and exclusive compassion, or unchanging bliss. In this way, the lack of any inherent beginning or ending is “pacification.” Phenomena and nonphenomena extinct since beginningless time is “the fundamental nature.” Aspected and nonaspected emptiness and compassion, or unchanging bliss, are indivisible. This is taught to be bodhicitta.

gzhung de dag sprel nas bshad pa na/ phung po rnam dpyad stong pa ni/ /zhes sogs kyi don yang de kho na bzhin du gnas pas so/ / de ltar na mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus las/ rdul phra rab ces sogs kyi don yang / / phung po rnam dpyad stong pa ni/ /zhes sogs kyi don kho bos bshad pa dang mthun par bya dgos te/ / mdor bsdus der gsungs pa'i rdul phra rab ces sogs dpe med 'tsho'i sbyor drug tu bkod pa de'i 'grel par nyi ma dpal gyis 'di ltar bshad de/ 'grel pa de nyid las/
bye brag tu smra ba dang mdo sde pa dang rnal 'byor spyod pa'i lugs kyi nang du ma lhung ba'i phyir rdul phra rab tshogs pa'i bdag nyid kyi chos rnam par dpyad pas stong pa'o/[402] / zhes 'tshams sbyar nas de'i 'jug nyid du/
tshu rol mdzes pa ba'i lugs la mi 'jug pa'i phyir chad par smra ba ring du byas pa nyid kyi phyir na chad pa'i stong pa nyid ring du byas pa'o/ / zhes bshad pas so/ /

If these verses are explained all together, the meaning of the verse beginning “The emptiness of examining the aggregates” is still as explained above. Similarly the meaning of the line from the Supreme and Unchanging summary in the Gnosis chapter that runs “The emptiness that comes from examining phenomena that are a collection of subtle atoms is an emptiness far from a nonexistence emptiness” must also accord with how I have explained the verse beginning “The emptiness of examining the aggregates.” This is because this line is quoted by Anupamarakṣita in his Six Yogas and explained by Sūryaśrī in his commentary to this text.[414]
So as not to fall into the systems of Vaibhāṣika, Sautrāntika, and Yogācāra, “The emptiness that comes from examining phenomena that are a collection of subtle atoms.” After this introduction he continues:
So as not to enter the systems of the hedonist Cārvāka, so as to cast far away the nihilist, “an emptiness far from nonexistence.”

d.div: [402] sde dge_1388_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ parnal 'byor yan lag drug gi brjed byang yon tan gyis 'gengs pa/ 307_ba7
[414] Filled with Good Qualities, Toh 1388 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 307b7.

f.d:
de ltar na/ phung po rnam dpyad stong pa ni/ /zhes sogs tshigs su bcad pa 'dis lam 'di'i bsgom bya mthar thug rnam med dang rnam bcas kyi stong pa nyid gnyis ka bstan cing / 'di'i/ chu shing bzhin du snying po med/ /ces pa'i snying po med tshul dang / snying rje'i chos rnams thams cad ni|_| snying po med par rgyal bas gsungs/ /zhes pa'i snying po med tshul rnams spyod 'jug las/
dper na chu shing sdong po dag / cha shas phye na 'ga' med pa/ / de bzhin rnam par dpyad pa yis/ / btsal na bdag kyang yang dag min/[403] / zhes dang / mdo las/
ji ltar chu shing rlon pa'i sdong po la/ / snying po 'dod phyir skyes bus de bshags kyang / / nang dang phyi rol kun na snying po med/ / chos rnams thams cad de bzhin shes par bya/[404] / zhes gsungs pa'i chu shing bzhin du snying po med tshul rnams dang 'dra bas 'di dag gi don phyin ci log tu ma 'dzin cig ces bya'o/ /

Therefore the verse beginning “The emptiness of examining the aggregates” teaches both aspected and nonaspected emptiness as ultimate meditations of this path. /483/ The lack of essence mentioned in the lines “is without essence like the plantain tree” and “All phenomena of compassion, said by the Buddha to be without essence” is explained in the Bodhicaryāvatāra:
For example, the plantain trunk, when cut up, is nothing. Likewise, when investigated, the self too is not genuine.[415] A sutra also says:
Just as someone might split the unripe trunk of the plantain tree to seek its essence only to find no essence within or without, so should you know all phenomena.[416] This lack of essence can be compared to the lack of essence of a plantain tree. Therefore do not misconstrue the meaning of this term.

d.div: [403] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ lashes rab kyi le'u/ 9_sh+loka75_34_ba4
[404] sde dge_127_bka'/ mdo sde/ dating nge 'dzin rgyal po'i mdo/ le'u/ 9_26_ba5
[415] Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, chap. 9, v. 75, 34b4.
[416] King of Meditative Concentration Sutra, Toh 127 Kangyur, mdo sde, da, chap. 9, 26b5.

f.d:
gzhan yang phar phyin theg pa'i dbu ma pas gtan la phab pa'i stong pa nyid de sngags bla med kyi bde ba chen pos bsgom bya mthar thug pa'i stong pa nyid ma yin gyi/ de las mchog tu gyur pa cig yod de zhes smra ba rnams kyang mi rigs te/ nang le'i lta ba rnam par dpyad pa'i mdor bsdus las/
dang po phyi rol pa'i lta ba rnams sun phyungs te/ de nas rang gi sde pa dang po gsum gyi lta ba sun phyungs nas/ mthar rang gi mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen pos dbu ma pas gtan la phab pa'i stong nyid de nyid bsgom par[405] gsungs so/ /

Furthermore those who say that the emptiness ascertained by a practitioner of the Madhyamaka in the Perfection Vehicle is not the emptiness that is the ultimate object of meditation for the great bliss of highest yoga tantra, because there is an even higher emptiness, are not correct. Investigation of the Views of Ourselves and Others summary from the Inner chapter of the Great Commentary states:
It is taught that first the views of the outsiders are refuted. Then the views of the first three of our tenets are refuted. Finally the unchanging great bliss meditates upon the emptiness ascertained by the Mādhyamika.

d.div: [405] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 192_na3

f.d:
de yang ji ltar gsungs na/ mdor bsdus de nyid las/
de bzhin du smras pa/ nam mkha' dang ni 'gog pa gnyis/ / 'dus ma byas gsum rtag pa ste/ / 'dus byas thams cad skad cig ma/ / bdag gis stong zhing byed po med/ / dbang skyes blo ni rnam med kyis/ / phra rab bsags pa dngos su rig / kha che'i gzhung gi chu gter gyi/ / bye brag smra ba'i gzhung 'dod 'gyur/[406] / zhes bye brag smra ba'i 'dod pa bkod nas/

Just how is this taught?[417] In the same summary it says:
Similarly the tantra says: “Space, cessation, uncompounded phenomena, these three are permanent. All that is compounded is impermanent. Self is empty, there is no doer. Perception born from the senses, without taking on the aspect, directly perceives the collection of atoms. These are the assertions of the Vaibhāṣika from the ocean of Kashmiri texts.”[418] This is a presentation of Vaibhāṣika tenets.

d.div: [406] pe cing bstan 'gyur nas kha bskang ba dar thang dpar ma'i pod/ pu/ chos tshan ang / 4530_rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa/ 41_na3
[417] For more on the “presentation of tenets” of the four Buddhist schools, see Hopkins, “The Tibetan Genre of Doxography: Structuring a Worldview,” in Cabezón and Jackson, pp. 170–86.

[418] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 196b3. The Kashmiri Vaibhāṣika are one of the three groups of Vaibhāṣika. Their main text was the Great Ocean of Specific Explanation (Mahāvibhāṣā), which was not translated into Tibetan.

f.d:
de'i de ma thag par/
shes pa rnam bcasaskye da byed ni/ / dbang po'i spyod yul snang ba min/ / nam mkha' mo gsham bu dang mtshungs/ / 'gog pa dang ni nam mkha' mtshungs/ / 'du byed bems po yod ma yin/ / dus gsum rjes 'gro dag kyang med/ / thogs pa med pa'i gzugs yod min/ / zhes pa mdo sde pa yis rig[407] / ces mdo sde pa'i 'dod pa bkod nas/ de'i mjug tu/
yan lag can zhes bya ba med/ / phra rab rdul rnams yod pa min/ / rmi lam nyams su myong ba bzhin/ / dmigs pa med par rab tu snang / / gzung dang 'dzin pa rnam grol ba'i/ / rnam par shes pa don dam yod/ / ces pa rnal 'byor spyod pa'i gzhung / / rgya mtsho'i pha rol phyin pa sgrog[408] / ces bkod nas/ de rnams kyi thun mong ma yin pa'i 'dod pa rnams 'gog cing /

The tantra continues:
Objects creating consciousness with aspect do not appear to sense organs. Space is like the barren woman’s son, cessation is like space, compositional factors have no form, the three times are not concomitant, there is no form that does not obstruct, this is understood by the Sautrāntika.[419] Having presented the Sautrāntika tenets the tantra continues:
There is no holder of parts, and subtle atoms do not exist; like experiences in a dream, they appear as nonobjects; ultimate consciousness exists, freed from subject and object. These are proclaimed for crossing the ocean /484/ of the Yogācāra doctrine.[420] After these presentations the exclusive assertions of each of these tenets is refuted.

d.div: [407] pe cing bstan 'gyur nas kha bskang ba dar thang dpar ma'i pod/ pu/ chos tshan ang / 4530_rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa/ 41_na4
[408] pe cing bstan 'gyur nas kha bskang ba dar thang dpar ma'i pod/ pu/ chos tshan ang / 4530_rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa/ 41_na6
[419] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 196b4.
[420] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 197a1.

f.d:
rgyud rtsa bar yang /
gang zhig de nyid gang zag ces bya lus la gnas par smra ba de ni rang bzhin dag gis nyams/[409] / zhes bye brag tu smra ba'i 'dod pa bkag kyang /
kun rdzob dag gi don ni smra ba po yang don dam ma rig med pa dag tu 'dod pa'o/[410] / zhes pas mdo sde pa'i 'dod pa bkag /
srid gsum mtha' dag rnam par shes pa nyid du smra ba po yang rnam par shes pa 'dod par byed/[411] / ces rnam rig pa'i 'dod pa bkod nas/ gtso bor 'dod pa de 'gog cing zhar la grub mtha' dang po gnyis kyi 'ang 'dus byas bden grub tu 'dodapa 'gog pa ni/ 'grel chen las/
de'i phyir gcig dang du ma'i rang bzhin gyis rnam par dpyad pas rnam par shes pa dang bral ba'i phyir rnam par shes pa smra ba po nyams so/[412] / zhes sogs gsungs pa rnams so/ /

The Condensed Tantra states:
Those who say that “person” inhabits the body, their tenet is weakened by examination of its nature.[421] This is a refutation of the Vaibhāṣika.
Those who hold to conventional truth also do not know the ultimate, holding it as nonexistent.[422] This is a refutation of the Sautrāntika.
Those who hold the three realms to be consciousness assert the existence of consciousness.[423] This presents the assertion of the Vijñāvāda.[424] The Great Commentary then continues primarily with a refutation of that assertion and incidentally with a refutation of the first two tenet systems’ assertion of truly existing compounded phenomena. This section begins:
Therefore, analytically searching for a consciousness with a single or manifold nature, it is not found, and so the asserters of consciousness are weakened.[425]

d.div: [409] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka167_57_na3
[410] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka167_57_na3

[424] Vijñāvāda, Cittamātra, and Yogācāra are synonymous.
[425] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 197a2.

f.d:
gzhan yang dngos smra ba'i 'dod pa skye gnas 'jig gsum rang bzhin gyis grub pa bkag nas dbu ma pa'i lta ba stong nyid phra mo gtan la 'bebs pa ni/ 'grel chen gyi de'i 'phro las/ da ni skad cig 'jig pa dang zhes pa nas/ phan tshun 'gal bas gcig pa nyid med do/[413] /zhes pa'i bar gsungs nas/ de'i de ma thag par/
de'i phyir dbu ma pas smras pa/ rnam shes de yang don dam du|_| yod par mkhas rnams mi 'dod de/ / gcig dang du ma'i rang bzhin dang / / bral ba nam mkha'i pad+ma bzhin/ / yod min med min yod med min/ / gnyis ga'i bdag nyid min pa'ang min/ / mtha' bzhi rnam par grol ba yi/ / de nyid dbu ma pa yis rig[414] / ces so/ / gang zhig phyogs nyams de ni ma nyams par 'gyur ro/ / de gang zhe na/ gang zhig snying rje stong nyid gnyis su med pa smra bo ste 'dir gang gis snying rje dmigs pa med cing rnam par rtog pa dang bral ba dang stong pa nyid rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa dus gsum yongs su shes pa'i slad du dus gsum du 'jug pa'o zhes pa na sangs rgyas pa'i grub mtha'i nges pa'o/[415] / zhes gsungs pa rnams te/

The Great Commentary continues with a refutation of the phenomena asserters,[426] who claim that creation, duration, and destruction exist by their own natures, and then proceeds to an ascertainment of the subtle emptiness that is the Madhyamaka view. This passage runs from “Now the faults of momentary birth and destruction are taught” up to “It could not arise from a combination because they would be mutually exclusive and therefore not one.”[427] The commentary continues:
“Therefore the Mādhyamika say that the wise do not assert consciousness to exist ultimately. Not possessing a nature that is one or many it is like a lotus in the sky. Not existing, not nonexisting, not possessing the natures of these two, freed from the four extremes. This is known by the Mādhyamika.” Those who weaken the extremes are not weakened. Why? “They propound nondual emptiness and compassion” means that here compassion, nonapprehending and nonconceptual, together with emptiness supreme in all aspects, will enter the three times for the sake of the knowledge of the three times. They are of the tenet of the buddhas.[428]

d.div: [413] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 197_na6
[414] pe cing bstan 'gyur nas kha bskang ba dar thang dpar ma'i pod/ pu/ chos tshan ang / 4530_rang gi lta ba'i 'dod pa mdor bstan pa/ 41_na8
[415] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 197_ba4
[426] Vaibhāṣika and Sautrāntika.
[427] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 197a6.
[428] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 197b5.

f.d: de dag gi don cung zad cig bshad na/ de yang / de nyid dbu ma pa yis rig/ /ces so/ /zhes dbu ma pas stong nyid gtan la phab tshul brjod nas/ gang zag gang zhig rtag chad kyi mtha'i phyogs nyams pa'i dbu ma pa de ni gnas lugs las ma nyams par 'gyur ro/ / dbu ma pa de gnas lugs las ma nyams par 'gyur tshul de gang zhe na/ de'i 'gyur tshul ston pa ni/ gang zhig snying rje stong nyid gnyis su med pa smra bo ste/ zhes bshad bya'i gtso bo bkod nas/ de'i don 'chad pa ni 'dir zhes sogs te/ dus kyi 'khor lo'i don gyi gtso bo nyams su len pa'i skabs 'dir rnal 'byor gang gis snying rje mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po dbu ma pas gtan la phab pa ltar gyi stong pa nyid la rtse gcig tu gnas pa'i dmigs pa med cing rnam par rtog pa dang bral ba dang stong pa nyid rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa ngo bo dbyer med du gyur pa'i zung 'jug dus gsum yongs su shes pa de 'thob pa'i slad du dbu ma pa'i de kho na nyid lta ba 'di dus gsum du 'jug par bya'o/ /zhes pa'o/ / de ltar na 'grel tshig 'di dag la nus pa thon pa'i go ba ma rnyed na bde ba chen po'i bsgom bya mthar thug gi gzhi stor bas blo gros kyi 'jug pa zhib par bya dgos so/ /

To explain this a little: the verses ending with the line “This is known by the Mādhyamika” /485/ refer to the way Mādhyamikas ascertain emptiness. Those persons of the Madhyamaka school who “weaken the two extremes” of existence and nonexistence do not fall from reality. How do Mādhyamikas not fall from reality? “They propound nondual emptiness and compassion.” This is the main topic, and is explained by the following lines. “Here,” at this juncture, when the main themes of Kālacakra are being practiced, the yoga of “compassion” or unchanging bliss, which is “nonapprehending and nonconceptual,” one-pointedly dwells in the emptiness ascertained by the Mādhyamika, in union with and indivisible from “emptiness supreme in all aspects. With the Madhyamaka view of reality, it will enter the three times for the sake of gaining “the knowledge of the three times.” If a meaningful understanding of this passage is not reached, the foundation for the ultimate great-bliss meditation will not be there. The discerning mind, therefore, needs to exercise great subtlety on this point.

de bzhin du mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus las kyang /
rgyu 'dis sangs rgyas pa bzhi po rnams kyi bag chags kyi stobs kyis bcom ldan 'das kyi gang zag smra ba rnams la gang zag mi rtag par bsgom pa gsungs so/ / don du smra ba rnams la sa la sogs pa zad par bsgom pa dang / rnam par shes pa smra ba rnams la rnam par rig pa tsam gyi ting nge 'dzin dang / dbu ma pa rnams la rmi lam lta bu 'gyur ba med cing gnyis su med pa'i ye shes bsgom pa ste de ltar gang zag la bdag med pa dang chos la bdag med pa'o/ / bye brag tu smra ba dang mdo sde pa dang rnal 'byor spyod pa ba rnams kyi lhag ma dang bcas pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa'o/ / dbu ma rnams kyi lhag ma dang bral ba rab tu mi gnas pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa ste rgyu dang 'bras bu 'gag pa'i phyir/[416] zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis kyang dbu ma pa'i lta ba sngags bla med pa'i yang bsgom bya'i lta ba mthar thug par gsungs so/ /

Furthermore it says in the Supreme and Unchanging summary:
Because of this, by the force of the instincts of the four kinds of Buddhists, the Buddha taught the meditation of the impermanence of self to those who propound the self. Those who propound phenomena are taught the totality meditations on earth, and so forth.[429] Those who propound consciousness are taught the meditative concentration upon mere perception. The Mādhyamika are taught meditations upon the dreamlike, unchanging, and nondual gnosis. In this way there is the nonself of persons and the nonself of phenomena. There is the nirvana with remainder of the Vaibhāṣika, Sautrāntika, and Yogācāra. There is the nirvana without remainder, the nonabiding, of the Mādhyamika in which all cause and effect has ceased.[430] This passage too states that the Madhyamaka view is the ultimate view of the meditations of highest mantra. /486/
