f.d: gnyis pa stong nyid bde bas sgom tshul mdor bsdus te bstan pa ni/

d.i: A brief explanation of how bliss meditates upon emptiness

f.d:
yod min med min yod med min/ /zhes sogs kyis dbu ma pas gtan la phab pa'i stong pa nyid kyi don de nyid mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen pos sgom par byed pa rgyud 'grel gyi dgongs pa yin pa bshad ma thag pa ltar yin la|_de sgom pa'i tshul yang dang por lam thun mong bas rgyud sbyong ba'i skabs su mdor ting nge 'dzin rgyal po las/
gal te chos la bdag med so sor rtog / so sor de brtags gal te sgom na ni/ / de nyid mya ngan gdas thob 'bras bu'i rgyu/ / rgyu gzhan gang yin des ni zhi mi 'gyur/[417] / zhes gsungs pa ltar mgon po klu sgrub dang dpal ldan zla bas bshad pa ltar gyi stong nyid phra mo thos bsam gyis gtan la phab pa'i don de nyid so sor rtog pa'i shes rab kyis dpyad kyin dpyad kyin sgom pa'i lhag mthong mtshan nyid pa'am rjes mthun pa'i stong nyid phra mo la nges pa gting nas rnyed pa'i myong ba thon par byas te mthar lhan skyes kyi bde ba chen po skyes pa'i tshe bde ba des stong nyid de dran par byas pa'i sgo nas yul gang la'ang mi dpyod par ma rtog pa'i ngang la 'jog sgom nyid byed pa yin na/ /

The unchanging bliss consciousness meditates on the very emptiness ascertained by the Mādhyamika through the lines “Not existing, not nonexisting,” and so forth. This is the position of the tantra and commentary as has just been explained. As to how that is accomplished, initially the mind is trained in the common path. The King of Meditative Concentration Sutra states:
If phenomena are analyzed for nonself, and if that analysis is meditated upon, this becomes the cause for the fruit of nirvana; other causes will bring no such peace.[431] As this quote indicates, the subtle emptiness as taught by the protector Nāgārjuna and the glorious Candrakīrti is initially ascertained by study and thought. That is meditatively analyzed again and again to produce an actual or similitude special insight[432] in which deep ascertainment[433] of this subtle emptiness is experienced. Eventually, when the innate bliss is generated, that emptiness is recalled by this bliss, and placement meditation is practiced on that emptiness in a meditative state where no objects are to be analyzed or conceived.

d.div: [417] sde dge_127_bka'/ mdo sde/ da27_na7_'gyur tshig sna mi mthun/
[431] Toh 127 Kangyur, mdo sde, da, 27a7.
[432] lhag mthong, vipaśyanā.
[433] nges shes. An ascertainment or conviction that is an understanding of emptiness but not a direct perception of it.

f.d: de lta bu'i bde stong gi ye shes de ni lhag mthong rnams kyi phul du byung ba yin te/ dang por lhag mthong sgom pa'i skabs su so sor rtog pa'i shes rab kyis dpyod pa'i rgyu mtshan ni stong nyid nges pa'i nges shes de'i 'dzin stangs kyi shugs je cher 'gro ba'i ched yin la/ bde ba chen pos stong nyid la ma dpyad par rtse gcig tu bzhag pa nyid kyis nges shes kyi 'dzin stangs kyi shugs je cher 'gro ba yin no/ / de'i rgyu mtshan yang bde stong gi ting nge 'dzin las ma langs kyi bar la kun rtog g.yo byedakyi rlung zhi nas med pas 'dzin stangs kyi shugs gzhan du mi 'gro zhing / bde ba chen po stong nyid sgom pa'i yul can phul du phyin pa yin pas 'dzin stangs kyi shugs je cher 'gro ba yin no/ / stong nyid yul du byed pa'i bde ba chen po yang khams byang chub kyi sems rtsa dbu ma'i nang la yas bab mas brtan byas pa dang gsan gzhan du mi g.yo bar byas pa las lus kyi bde ba khyad par can skye/ des rgyu rkyen byas pa las gnyug ma'i sems sam 'od gsal gyi sems bde ba chen po'i ngo bor skyes pa de yin no/ /

Such a bliss-and-emptiness gnosis is the supreme of all special insights. The reason for using meditative analysis[434] when one first meditates to develop special insight is that it increases the strength of the ascertaining mind’s hold on emptiness. When great bliss is nonanalytically and single-pointedly placed on emptiness, the hold of the ascertaining mind also becomes stronger. The reason for this is that for as long as one remains in the meditative concentration on bliss and emptiness, the moving winds of the conceptual minds are stilled and not present, which means that the mode of apprehension will not weaken. Moreover, because great bliss is the best consciousness for meditating upon emptiness, that apprehension will actually become stronger. Furthermore bliss that takes emptiness as its object brings about the descent and stable ascent of the bodhicitta element in the central channel and prevents it from moving elsewhere. This creates a special bliss within the body, which becomes the causal condition for the primordial or clear-light mind to develop into the entity of great bliss. /487/

d.div: [434] so sor rtog pa’i shes rab kyi dpyad pa.

f.d: gsum pa ji ltar sgom pa'i tshul

['di ]la gnyis/ mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po'i thun mong ma yin pa'i rgyu phyag rgya chen mo ngos gzung ba dang / de la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed pa'i thabs gang zag gsum po so sor sgom tshul lo/ /

This is under two headings: 1. Identifying the mahāmudrā consort, the special cause of unchanging bliss 2. How the meditations of the three types of practitioners rely on the mahāmudrā consort to develop the unchanging bliss
dang po [mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po'i thun mong ma yin pa'i rgyu phyag rgya chen mo ngos gzung ba ]ni

d.i: Identifying the mahāmudrā consort, the special cause of unchanging bliss

f.d:
rjes dran gyi skabs su dngos gnas la grub pa'i dus 'khor yab yum zhal spyor gyi rnam pa can gyi yum de la phyag rgya chen mo zhes bzhag ste/ de la dgongs nas ye le'i bdun cu rtsa gsum pa sngar drangs pa/
glog gi dbyug pa'i rjes mthun 'pho med bde ba skyed par byed ma mtshan nyid yan lag rab tu rdzogs/[418] / zhes dang /

The mahāmudrā consort is the mother deity of the Kālacakra in the aspect of mother-and-father embrace developed as an actual phenomenon during the branch of recollection. This is the meaning of the previously quoted lines from the seventy-third verse of the Gnosis chapter:
In a flash of lightning resemblance arises a definitive creator of unmoving bliss, all features complete.[435]

yang ye le'i brgya bcu gsum pa las/
sems kyi snang ba tsam ste rang gi yid las skyes pa me long gi ni gzugs brnyan lta bu nyid/ / gang zhig mtha' dag rgya ba'i sras dang sangs rgyas rnams kyis bstan pa rnal 'byor dbang pos bsten bya ste/[419] / zhes dang /

Also verse 113 says:
A mere apparition of the mind, born from the mind, like a reflection in a mirror, upon whom all bodhisattvas and buddhas have relied, upon whom the mighty yogis rely.[436]

'di dag shes byed du drangs pa'i mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus las/
byang chub kyi mthar thug pa'i bar du phyag rgya chen po rang gi sems kyi snang ba tsam 'di rnal 'byor pas bsgom par bya'o/[420] / zhes dang /

Until the finality of enlightenment the yogi meditates on this mahāmudrā, this mere appearance within the mind.[437]

f.d:
yang sgrub le'i brgya go brgyad pa las/
phyag rgya sgyu ma'i rjes su mthun pa yid dang nam mkha' la ni me long dag la gzugs bzhin te/ / 'jig rten gsum po snang bar byed cing dri med glog dang mtshungs pa'i 'od zer du ma 'phro bar byed/ / phyi dang lus la dbyer med yul dang rnam par bral bsna nga ba tsam ni mkha' la gnas pa yi/ / sems la sems kyi rang bzhin 'khyud pa gang zhig 'gro ba du ma'i gzugs can de ni gcig bu'o/[421] / zhes dang /

Furthermore, in verse 198 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, it says:
Mudrā, like an illusion, in mind and space like an image in a mirror; myriad beams radiate forth like pure lightning, illuminating the three worlds, the external inseparable from the body, a nonobject, a mere appearance, the mind dwelling in space, embracing the nature of mind, the forms of many beings are solely this mudrā.[438]

f.d:
yang de'i 'phro nyid las/
yang dag rdzogs pa'i byang chub ched du rgyal ba mchog gi skyed ma mchog gi phyag rgya gos pa med/ / rnam par 'gyur ba med cing mkha' mnyam mun bcom khyab byed rnal 'byor dag gi bgrod bya ther zug gnas/ / ye shes gzi brjid srid pa'i dri ma 'phrog cing dus kyi 'khor lo rjes su rig pa bsgom par bya/[422] / zhes sogs du ma rnams kyis bstan pa ltar yin no/ /

And further on:
For the attainment of perfect enlightenment, the she-creator of supreme buddha, supreme, unsullied mudrā consort, unchanging in aspect, all-pervading, dispelling darkness vast as space, the path traveled by yogis, forever unchanging, the radiance of gnosis destroying the impurities of existence, meditate upon this wisdom of Kālacakra.[439] /488/ The mahāmudrā consort is as described here and in many other verses.

d.div: [422] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka179_98_na2
[439] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 199, 98a2.

f.d:
de yang dus kyi 'khor los 'khyud pa'i sna tshogs yum gyi rnam pa can nyid la bya ste/ de ltar yang mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus las/
phyag rgya chen mo ni chos thams cad rang bzhin med pa'i mtshan nyid rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin ma sangs rgyas skyed par mdzad ma'o/ / chos 'byung gi sgras kyang de brjod de chos 'byung gang las rang bzhin med pa'i chos thams cad 'byung bar 'gyur ba'o/ / rang bzhin med pa'i chos rnams kyi stobs bcu dang mi 'jigs pa la sogs pa chos kyi phung po brgyad khri bzhi stong rnams so/ / de rnams 'byung bar 'gyur ba ni chos 'byung ste sangs rgyas kyi zhing ngo / / sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi gnas te bde ba'i gnas dang skye ba'i gnas so/ / gang las khrag dang gci ba dang khu ba rnams 'byung ba de ni chos 'byung ma yin no/ / 'dir 'khor ba pa rnams kyi chags pa dang chags bral gyi zhing na de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyi ma yin na/ de'i phyir chos 'byung ni chos kyi dbyings kyi rang bzhin can sna tshogs yum bcom ldan 'das dus kyi 'khor los 'khyud pa dus thams cad du sgrib pa thams cad dang bral ba'o/[423] / zhes sogs rnams kyis phyag rgya chen mo rnal 'byor pa rang nyid dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum zhal sbyor gyi rnam pa can gyi skur bzhengs pa'i yum sna tshogs yum gyi rnam pa can de nyid la gsal bar gsungs pas gong du dbang rnon gyis ri rab kyis rdul gyi grangs dang mnyam pa'i phyag rgya chen mo la snyoms 'jug byed par bshad pas phyag rgya chen mo rnams kyang phal che ba rnams sna tshogs yum gyi rnam pa can du shes par bya'o/ /

She is to be recognized as the form of Viśvamātā embraced by Kālacakra. The Supreme and Unchanging summary from the Great Commentary says:
The mahāmudrā consort is of the noninherent nature of all phenomena, endowed with every feature supreme, the Prajñāpāramitā, the creator of buddha. She is also known as “the source”[440] because from this source all noninherently existing phenomena arise. The noninherently existing phenomena include the ten powers, the non-fears, and so forth of the 84,000 groups of dharmas. The arising of these is from the source, the realm of buddha. The place of the buddhas and the bodhisattvas is a place of joy and a place of birth. That which gives rise to blood, urine, and semen is not the source. Here the realms of desire and nondesire of those of samsara are not those of the tathāgata. Therefore the source has the nature of the dharmadhātu; it is Viśvamātā embraced by Buddha Kālacakra and at all times is divorced from all obscuration.[441] These and other passages clearly teach that when the yogi arises in the form of Kālacakra in the aspect of mother-and-father embrace, the mahāmudrā consort refers to the mother in the form of Viśvamātā. Therefore, as previously explained, yogis of high intelligence enter union with as many mahāmudrā consorts as there are atoms in Mount Meru, and these mahāmudrā consorts are mostly in the form of Viśvamātā.

[440] chos ’byung.

f.d: gnyis pa phyag rgya chen mo de la brten nas mi 'gyur pa'i bde ba skyed pa'i thabs gang zag gsum po so so'i sgom tshul ni/

d.i: How the meditations of the three types of practitioners rely on the mahāmudrā consort to develop the unchanging bliss

f.d:
gang zag dbang po rno 'bring rtul po gsum kas kyang rang nyid dus 'khor yab yum gyi sku'i rnam pa can du gyur pa'i yab yum snyoms 'jug byed pa la dmigs nas rjes chags la rtse gcig tu gnas par byed dgos te/ bde mchog stod 'grel las/
des na ting nge 'dzin zhes bya ba ni 'dod pa'i lha la rjes su chags pa las gang zhig 'gyur ba med pa'i bde ba thob pa ste/[424] zhes dang /

Practitioners of high, middling, and low intelligence in the form of Kālacakra mother and father must focus on mother-and-father union and dwell single-pointedly in that desire. The Cakrasaṃvara Commentary says:
Concerning meditative concentration, unchanging bliss is achieved from the yearning for the desired goddess.[442] /489/

d.div: [424] sde dge_1402_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ba_bde mchog stod 'grel/ 131_na1
[442] Toh 1402 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ba, 131a1.

f.d:
n+wa ro pa'i dbang mdor bstan gyi 'grel pa las kyang/ ting nge 'dzin zhes bya ba ni 'dod pa'i lha la rjes su chags pa las [425] zhes sogs stod 'grel ji bzhin du gsungs pa dang / mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus su phyogs snga smra ba pos 'grel chen mdzad pa po'i dgongs pa brjod pa las/
ci ltar rnal 'byor pas rang gi sems kyi snang ba la rang gi sems rjes su chags par byas nas rang gi sems sgrib pa med par byed cing mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po'i ye shes kyang longs spyod par byed de rdul phra rab tshogs pa'i lus med pa'i phyir ro/[426] / zhes pa dang /

Nāropa’s commentary to A Short Teaching on Initiations repeats these words of the Cakrasaṃvara Commentary.[443] In the Supreme and Unchanging summary of the Great Commentary, an opponent is questioning the thinking of the Great Commentary:
How does the yogi develop desire in his mind for an apparition of the mind, then destroy the obscurations of the mind and enjoy the gnosis of unchanging bliss when this apparition is a body devoid of atoms?[444]

d.div: [425] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 252_na6
[426] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 416_na3
[443] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 252a6.
[444] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 416a3.

f.d:
dbang mdor bstan las/ /
phyag rgya chen mo'i rjes chags las/ / skyes pa g.yo med bde ba ni/ / shes rab chen pos dbang bskur ba/ / gang las g.yo med rtogs pa ste/[427] / zhes pa'i 'grel pa nA ro pas mdzad pa las/
phyag rgya chen mo zhes pa nam mkha' las byung ba'i gzugs te de'i rjes chags phyi rol rang gi nyams su sgom pa [428] zhes bya ba las skyes pa g.yo med ces pa rdo rje nor bu las phyi rol tu g.yo ba las 'dzag pa 'gog pa sku'i lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba dang gsung gi lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba dang thugs kyi lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' ba/ zhes gsungs pa rnams kyi rang nyid dus 'khor yab yum gyi skur gyur pa snyoms 'jug byed pa la rjes chags byas nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed pa 'di phyag rgya chen pos mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed tshul du gsal bar bstan par shes par bya'o/ /

A Short Teaching on Initiations says:
From desire for the mahāmudrā consort, unmoving bliss is born; initiated by the great wisdom, the unmoving is realized.[445] In commentary on this, Nāropa says:
“Mahāmudrā consort” is a form arising from space. The “desire” is one’s own meditation, from which the “unmoving” is born. This refers to the halting of the emission from the vajra jewel. This is the body innate joy, speech innate joy, and mind innate joy.[446] These passages clearly teach that with oneself in the form of Kālacakra mother and father, one develops desire for union and generates the unchanging bliss. This is the way the mahāmudrā consort generates unchanging bliss.

d.div: [427] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_dbang mdor bstan/ 14_ba6
[428] sde dge_1351_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ na_dbang mdor bstan pa'i 'grel bshad/ 243_ba2
[445] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 14b6.
[446] Toh 1351 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, na, 243b2.

f.d:
de yang dbang rtul gyis de ltar byas te bsgom pa las dang po nas phyag rgya chen mo nyid la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed par mi nus pas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba de skyed pa'i thabs su thog mar las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas byang sems rdo rje nor bu'i rtser phab la/ de ltar phab pa'i thig le de phyag rgya chen mo'i stobs kyis gnas gzhan du mi 'gyur zhing mi g.yo bar byas pa las mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma gcig skyes la de mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skad cig ma nyi khri chig stong drug brgya'i dang po de yin zhing / de nas phyag rgya chen po nyid la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma gnyis pa man chad kyang skyed pa yin no/ / de ltar yang mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus su phyag rgya chen mo bsgom pa'i shes byed du/ sems kyi snang ba tsam ste zhes sogs drangs pa'i mjug sdud du 'grel pa'i 'phro de nyid las/
bcom ldan 'das kyi nges pa'ang dbang po gnyis kyi snyoms par 'jug pas kyang phyi rol gyi dbang po las skyes pa 'gyur ba'i bde ba rnam par spangs nas byang chub kyi mthar thug pa'i bar du phyag rgya chen mo rang gi sems kyi snang ba tsam 'di rnal 'byor pas bsgom par bya'o/[429] / zhes dbang po rno 'bring rtul gsum gang yin yang rjes dran man chad du dbang po gnyis kyi snyoms 'jug gis bde ba skyed pa dang / khyad par du yang dbang rtul las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas dbang po gnyis kyi snyoms par 'jug pas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed pas kyang phyis phyag rgya chen mo nyid la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed nus pa'i 'tshams nas phyi rol gyi dbang po las skyes pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba rnam par spangs nas byang chub kyi mthar thug pa'i bar du phyag rgya chen mo rang gi sems kyi snang ba tsam 'di rnal 'byor pas bsgom par bya bar gsungs so/ / de yang rang gi sems kyi snang ba tsam zhes pa'i tsam gyi sgras dngos gnas la grub pa gcod pa min gyi/ phyi rol gyi gzugs ltar rdul phra rab las grub pa'i rdos bcas gcod pa yin no/ /

The practitioner of low intelligence meditates in this way but is unable to generate unchanging bliss by relying on a mahāmudrā consort from the very beginning, so as a method of developing unchanging bliss, he first relies upon an activity mudrā consort to bring the bodhicitta down to the tip of the vajra jewel. Thereafter this drop is prevented from changing or moving elsewhere by the power of the mahāmudrā consort, from which arises one instance of unchanging bliss. This is the first of the 21,600 instances of unchanging bliss. After this he develops the second and following instances of unchanging bliss by relying on the mahāmudrā consort. In this connection, immediately after quoting the tantra verses beginning “A mere apparition of the mind” as a source for mahāmudrā consort meditation, /490/ the Supreme and Unchanging summary says:
These are the definitive words of the Buddha. The yogi abandons the changing bliss that arises from the union of the two external organs, meditates on the mahāmudrā consort, this mere apparition of mind, until the finality of enlightenment.[447] Therefore, up to and including the branch of recollection, any or all of the three types of practitioners will generate bliss by the union of the two organs. The practitioner of low intelligence will especially rely on an activity mudrā consort and develop changing bliss through the union of the two organs. However later he will be able to generate unchanging bliss by relying on a mahāmudrā consort, and from that point onward the yogi “abandons the changing bliss that arises from the union of the two external organs and meditates upon the mahāmudrā consort, this mere apparition of mind, until the finality of enlightenment.” In the phrase “mere apparition of mind,” the word “mere” does not negate the reality of the mahāmudrā consort, but negates atom-created materiality, as in the case of external form.

d.div: [429] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 416_na1
[447] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 416a1.

f.d: dbang 'bring ye shes kyi phyag rgya la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed pa yang phyag rgya gnyis brje ba ma gtogs snga ma dang tshul mtshungs shing phyag rgya gnyis kyi bsten tshul ni rjes dran gi skabs su bshad pa ltar yin no/ /

The practitioner of middling intelligence generates unchanging bliss through reliance on a wisdom consort, and apart from the difference in consort, his practice is similar to the above. The practices of relying upon these two types of consorts have been explained in the section on recollection.

dbang rnon gyis ni mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po skyed nus pa'i 'tshams nas phyag rgya chen mo 'ba' zhig la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed par byed pa yin la/ de yang rang nyid dus 'khor yab yum gyi sku'i rnam par gyur pa snyoms 'jug byed pa'i tshul la rtse gcig tu dmigs te rjes chags bsgoms pas gtum mo 'bar te rdul gcig lus rags pa 'di'i gtsug tor du song ste der brtan pa na gtsug tor nas byang sems dkar po zhu ba rtsa dbu ma'i nang na mar babs pa rdo rje nor bu'i rtse mor phyin pa gnas de nyid du phyag rgya chen mo nyid kyi stobs kyis brtan par byas pa las mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma gcig rang dus su grub pa'i stong gzugs dus 'khor yab yum gyi sku'i rnam pa can de dang ngo bo dbyer med du skyes pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skad cig ma des rnam med kyi stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs te stong pa nyid dang chu la chu bzhag tu gyur pa de ni mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya'i dang po dang stong nyid mngon sum du gsar du mthong ba'i mthong lam dang sa [430] dang po rab tu dga' ba thob ma thag pa rnams yin no/ /

The practitioner of high intelligence, from the moment he develops the ability to produce unchanging bliss, relies solely on the mahāmudrā consort to generate unchanging bliss. In the form of Kālacakra mother and father, he focuses single-pointedly on union and meditates on desire. This causes the caṇḍālī fire to blaze, and one red speck travels to the crown of his coarse body. When it is stabilized, the white bodhicitta melts and descends through the central channel to the tip of the vajra jewel, where it is held firm by the power of the mahāmudrā consort. From this, one instance of unchanging bliss arises, and this bliss, indivisible from oneself in the form of empty-form Kālacakra mother and father, /491/ directly cognizes nonaspected emptiness like water being poured into water. This is the first of the 21,600 instances of bliss, the attainment of the path of seeing — wherein emptiness is newly seen with direct perception — and the attainment of the first level, great joy.

d.div: [430] ma dper mthong lam dngos dang po zhes byung yang mthong lam dang sa dang po zhes bcos/

f.d: de ltar 'dis mtshon nas rdo rje nor bu'i rtse nas gtsug tor gyi rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i bar du rtsa dbu ma'i nang du thig le dkar po 'phreng bar brtsegs pa nyi khri chig stong drug brgya dang / de bzhin du gtsug tor nas rdo rje nor bu'i rtse bar la rdul brtsegs pa nyi khri chig stong drug brgya dang / thig ler la brten pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po nyi khri chig stong drug brgya yod pa'i stong brgyad brgya tshan pa res rer byas pa'i sa bcu gnyis so/ /

Using the above process as an illustration, the 21,600 white drops are then stacked up in succession inside the central channel from the tip of the vajra jewel to the center of the crown cakra. Similarly 21,600 red specks are stacked from the crown to the tip of the vajra jewel, and 21,600 instances of unchanging bliss, developed in dependence on the drops and arranged in groups of 1,800, will form the twelve levels.

de yang 'di'i lugs kyi sa bcu gnyis 'phags pa slob pa'i sa bcur 'jog tshul sgrub byed dang bcas pa ni bshad zin pa ltar ro/ / de yang rdo rje nor bu'i rtse nas gsang gnas kyi rtsa 'khor gyi lta ba'i bar gyi dbu ma'i nang la thig le dkar po'i cha sum stong drug brgya 'phreng bar brtsegs pa'i phyed 'og ma stong brgyad brgya la brtan pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skad cig stong brgyad brgya sa dang po dang / phyed phyi ma la brten pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skad cig ma stong brgyad brgya sa gnyis pa/ de bzhin du gsang gnas nas lte ba sogs dbye ba 'chad pa'i skabs su bshad zin pa ltar shes par bya'o/ /

The way that the twelve levels of the Kālacakra tradition are presented as the ten levels of the ārya paths of practice and the reasons for that have already been explained. From the tip of the vajra jewel to the center of the secret-area cakra, 3,600 white drops are stacked inside the central channel. The lower 1,800 drops give rise to 1,800 instances of unchanging bliss. This is the first level. The 1,800 instances of unchanging bliss that arise in dependence on the upper 1,800 drops make up the second level. Likewise the levels from the secret area to the navel and other cakras can be known from the previous section on divisions by numbers.

de yang rdo rje nor bu'i rtse nas gtsug tor gyi bar thig le 'phreng bar [431] brtsegs pa las bde ba skad cig ma rer skye ba ni/ ye le'i don lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
byang chub sems kyi thig le gang gang dpral pa 'di nas mgrin pa dang snying ga dang lte ba dang gsang ba rnams la son pa ni srog rtsol gyi stobs kyis 'gog par 'gyur te/ gsang bar sku'i thig le 'gog cing de bzhin du gsung dang thugs dang ye shes kyi thig le ni lte ba dang snying ga dang mgrin pa la 'gog go/ / thig le 'di las g.yo ba'i khu ba gang zhes pa ni 'dir gsang ba la gnas pa sku'i thig le ska ba'i rang bzhin las gzhan sla ba'i khu ba gang yin pa de ni g.yo ba'i khu bar gsungs shing de ni rdo rje nor bu la gnas rgyal mtshan rtse la ste rtags kyi sgo la yang dag par 'gog pa'o/ / g.yo bde ni shes rab ye shes skad cig gal te thig le'i 'phreng ba 'pho ba med pa'i rgyus bde ba ster na'o/ / de'i tshe las kyi phyag rgya'i ye shes ma yin te shes rab ye shes zhes grub po/ mi g.yo ba'i rgyu ba'i phyir g.yo med bde ba'i skad cig gang yin pa 'dir ni chos kyi dbyings te shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin mas ster bar byed do/ / des na phyag rgya chen po'i bde ba ni mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'o/[432] / zhes thig le gang gang zlos pa'i tshig gis bstan pa rnams dpral ba nas gsang gnas kyi bar du son pa'i thig le ska ba rnams srog rtsol gyi stobs kyis 'dzag med du 'gog la de yang sku gsung thugs ye shes kyi thig le rnams rim pa bzhin gsang gnas lte ba snying ga mgrin pa rnams su 'gog cing gsang gnas la gnas pa sku'i thig le ska ba'i rang bzhin de las gzhan sla ba'i khu ba gang yin pa de rdo rje nor bu'i rtse rtags kyi bug pa'i sgo la yang dag par 'gog pa'o/ /

On the creation of instances of bliss from the drops stacked one after another from the tip of the vajra jewel to the crown, the Great Commentary on the seventy-fifth verse of the Gnosis chapter says:
Whatever [drops] there are of bodhicitta travel from the forehead to the throat, heart, navel, and secret place. They are stopped by the power of prāṇāyāma. At the secret place the body drop is halted. Likewise the speech, mind, and gnosis drops are halted at the navel, heart, and throat. “Of these drops, the moving fluid” means that the fluid, which is liquid by nature and different from the body drop at the secret place, which is naturally thick, is spoken of as “moving fluid.” This is stopped at the “tip of the victory banner of the vajra jewel,” meaning at the opening of the organ. /492/ This moving fluid is “wisdom gnosis, if bliss is granted by the cause of the unmoving succession of drops.” At this time this is not the gnosis of the activity mudrā consort but the accomplishment of wisdom gnosis. Because it is immobile, “the instances of unmoving bliss are dharmadhātu here” and granted by Prajñāpāramitā. Therefore the bliss of the mahāmudrā is supreme and unchanging.[448] The meaning of this passage is as follows. The drops, indicated by the word “whatever,” reach down from the forehead to the secret area. Those that are coagulated drops are stopped from falling by the power of prāṇāyāma. They are the body, speech, mind, and gnosis drops and are stopped at the secret area, navel, heart, and throat respectively. The molten fluid, which is different from the solid body drop at the secret area, is halted at the opening of the organ at the tip of the vajra jewel.

d.div: [431] ma dper 'grel par zhes byung yang gong du 'phreng bar brtsegs pa zhes byung ba ltar bcos/
[432] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 381_na1
[448] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 381a1.

f.d: de yang gang gis 'gog na phyag rgya chen mos 'gog go/ de ltar na g.yo ba'i ming can khu ba sla ba de phyag rgya chen mos g.yo med du bkag ste thig le brtsegs pa'i 'phreng ba gnas gzhan dang gzhan du 'pho ba med pa'i rgyus mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma ster na de'i tshe bde ba de shes rab ye shes bde ba'i skad cig dbang bzhi par 'gyur gyi/ de'i tshe las kyi phyag rgya'i ye shes ma yin pa'o/ / thig le'i 'phreng ba gnas gzhan du mi 'pho ba'i rgyu de'i phyir g.yo ba med pa mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig gang yin pa de la 'dir chos kyi dbyings zhes bya la/ de yang rgyu gang las byung ba ni phyag rgya chen mo shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin mas ster bar byed pa ste rgyu de las byung ba'o zhes pa'i don no/ /

By what is it blocked? By the mahāmudrā consort. Therefore this molten fluid, which is given the name “moving fluid,” is halted and made immobile by the mahāmudrā consort. If instances of unchanging bliss are granted with the succession of stacked drops prevented from moving elsewhere as a cause, then at that time this bliss is the bliss of wisdom gnosis and becomes the fourth initiation. It is “not the gnosis of the activity mudrā consort.” Because the succession of drops does not move to other places, the instances of unmoving or unchanging bliss are here called dharmadhātu. From what cause are they produced? They are granted or produced by the mahāmudrā consort Prajñāpāramitā. This is the meaning of the above passage.

de bzhin du rdul byang sems dmar cha yang gtsug tor nas rdo rje nor bu'i rtse bar la brtan par byed pa ni/ rgyud phyi ma las/
khu ba stong dang rdul yang 'og tu song bas gzhom du med pa tshangs pa'i dbyangs las ni/ sku dang gsung dang thugs kyi rdo rje dri ma gsum spangs sangs rgyas gang gis ston byed pa'o/[433] / zhes gsungs pa dang /

Similarly the specks or red bodhicitta constituents are stabilized from the crown to the tip of the vajra jewel. The Later Kālacakra Tantra says:
From fluid rising up, specks traveling down, the indestructible melody of Brahmā, from which, stains upon the vajras of body, speech, and mind are destroyed, to become an enlightened buddha.[449]

d.div: [433] sde dge_363_bka'/ rgyud/ kadapal dus kyi 'khor lo'i rgyud phyi ma rgyud kyi snying po/ 132_ba4
[449] Toh 363 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 132b4.

f.d:
rtsa ba'i rgyud dbang mdor bstan las/
lus can thams cad 'chi ba na/ / zla ba bdud rtsi thur du 'gro/ / steng du nyi rdul sgra can dang / / rnam shes srid pa'i mtshan nyid do/ / de bas zla ba bdud rtsi steng / / 'gro bar byed do rgyal po kye/ / 'og tu nyi rdul sgra gcan dang / / rnam shes mi 'gyur bde ba'o/[434] / zhes byang sems dkar po'i cha rdo rje nor bu'i rtse nas gtsug tor gyi bar yar 'phreng bar brtsegs pa dang / rdul dmar po'i cha gtsug tor nas nor bu'i rtse'i bar mar brtsegs pa las sems mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig nyi khri chig stong drug brgyar gyur pa'i mthar mi gnas pa'i mya ngan las 'das par 'gyur bar gsungs pa'o/ /

The root tantra A Short Teaching on Initiations also says:
When living beings die, moon nectar falls, sun specks of Rāhu move up, and consciousness is of samsara. Greater than that, moon nectar moves up, Sun specks of Rāhu move down, and consciousness is of unchanging bliss.[450] /493/ These verses are saying that the white bodhicitta constituent is stacked up from the tip of the vajra jewel to the crown, and the red speck constituent is stacked downward from the crown to the tip of the vajra jewel. From this the mind turns into the 21,600 instances of bliss and finally into the nonabiding nirvana.

d.div: [434] sde dge_361_bka'/ rgyud/ kadabang mdor bstan/ 17_ba1
[450] Toh 361 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 14b1.

f.d: mdor na rdo rje nor bu'i rtse'i dbu ma'i nang nas gtsug tor gyi rtsa 'khor gyi lte ba'i bar la thig le dkar cha nyi khri chig stong drug brgya brtan par byas pa'i thig le re re la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma re re skyes pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig nyi khri chig stong drug brgya pa stong pa nyid dang mnyam par sbyar bas [435] bde stong gi ye shes rnams kyi spang bya bden 'dzin bag chags dang bcas pa dang 'dzag bde bag chags dang bcas pa spong zhing / dbugs nyi khri chig stong drug brgya 'gog pa'i sgo nas 'pho ba bcu gnyis kyi rlung 'gog par byed pa yin no/ / de yang bde ba'i skad cig ma re re la bar chad med lam dang rnam grol lam gnyis gnyis su phye ba'i bar chad med lam rnams kyi stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa'i ldog pa'i cha nas bden 'dzin bag chags dang bcas pa'i gnyen po dang / mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i ldog pa'i cha nas 'dzag bde bag chags dang bcas pa'i gnyen por 'jog la de lta bu'i bar chad med lam rnams kyi rang rang gi ngo skal gyi spang bya de rnams spangs pa'i rnam grol lam yang mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba de snyed re yod pas nyi khri chig stong drug brgya'o/ /

To summarize, the 21,600 drops of the white constituent are stabilized within the central channel from the tip of the vajra jewel up to the center of the crown cakra. One instance of unchanging bliss is generated in dependence upon each drop, and by 21,600 instances of unchanging bliss joining with emptiness, the resulting gnosis of bliss and emptiness destroys the clinging to true existence and its imprints as well as the imprints of falling bliss. Also, by stopping the 21,600 breaths, the winds of the twelve wind movements are halted. Each instance of bliss is divided into a path of noninterruption and a path of freedom. Each instance of bliss as the direct cognition of emptiness on the path of noninterruption is the antidote to clinging to true existence and its imprints. Each instance of bliss in its aspect of unchanging bliss is the antidote to falling bliss and its imprints. The paths of freedom are the states of actual abandonment accomplished by the noninterrupted paths, and they are also accompanied by instances of bliss and so number 21,600.

d.div: [435] sde ma dper mnyam par sgyur bas zhes byung yang mnyam par sbyar bas zhes bcos/

f.d: yang mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba rnams skyes pas 'pho ba'i rlung rnams 'gag tshul ni rags par na 'pho ba re la dbugs stong brgyad brgya re yod pa las/ mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma re re skyes pas dbugs re re 'gag la/ de 'gag pas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma stong brgyad brgya rdzogs pa'i tshe 'pho ba gcig gi rlung 'gag go/ / de bzhin du gzhan rnams la yang rigs pa sbyar nas sa re la mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba stong brgyad brgya re yod pas sa re re rdzogs pa na rlung 'pho ba re re 'gag go/ / de ltar 'gags pas mthar mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma nyi khri chig stong drug brgya rdzogs te sa bcu gnyis pa rdzogs pa'i mthar bden 'dzin dang 'dzag bde bag chags dang bcas pa ma lus pa spangs shing / rlung 'pho ba bcu gnyis ma lus par 'gags pa'i 'bras dus kyi bden don rnam pa bcu gnyis dang de nyid bcu drug mthar thug pa grub pa yin no/ /

The way the instances of unchanging bliss halt the wind movements is as follows. Each wind movement consists of approximately 1,800 breaths, and each creation of unchanging bliss halts one breath. In this way, with the completion of 1,800 instances of unchanging bliss, one complete wind movement has been halted. Applying this process to the other wind movements, each level has 1,800 instances of unchanging bliss, and so with the completion of each level, one wind movement is halted. Finally 21,600 instances of unchanging bliss are generated, /494/ the twelve levels are accomplished, clinging to true existence and falling bliss, along with their imprints, are destroyed. The twelve wind movements are halted, and the twelve aspects of truth and the sixteen realities are achieved.[451]

d.div: [451] The twelve aspects of truth (bden don rnam pa bcu gnyis) may be the twelve bodhisattva levels of the Kālacakra tradition. If the sixteen realities (de nyid bcu drug) are indeed the sixteen emptinesses of the Perfection Vehicle, then the division into sixteen is made on the basis of there being sixteen types of basis of designation and not on the basis of emptiness itself, which has no divisions.

f.d:
gzhan yang rgyud las/
mchog tu mi 'gyur bsgom par bya/ / pad+mar rdo rje rab bkod nas/ / srog ni thig ler gzhug par bya/ / 'khor lor thig le thig le yi/ / g.yo ba rdo rjer dgag par bya/ / rtag tu rtag rengs rnal 'byor pas/ / rtag tu steng du khu bar 'gyur/ / phyag rgya chen po'i sbyor ba yis/ / rdo rje 'babs pas byin gyis brlab/ / mchog tu mi 'gyur skad cig ni/ / stong phrag nyi shu rtsa gcig dang / / drug brgya rdzogs pas rgyal po che/ / rdo rje sems dpar rang nyid 'gyur/[436] / zhes gsungs shing /

On this the tantra says:
Meditate on the supreme and unchanging. With vajra placed inside lotus, bring the winds into the drops, the drops into the cakras; the movement of drops halted at the vajra, always rigid, the yogi continuously raises fluid. With the yoga of mahāmudrā, the descent to the vajra, and by its blessing, the instances of supreme unchanging, completed at 21,600, will bring the great enlightenment, the attainment of Vajrasattva.[452]

d.div: [436] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 437_ba5
[452] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 437b5.

f.d:
de yang dbang rnon gyis mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skyed nus pa'i 'tshams dang dbang po rtul 'bring gnyis kyis kyang phyag rgya chen mo 'ba' zhig la brten nas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba 'dren nus pa'i 'tshams nas las dang ye shes kyi phyag rgya gnyis spangs nas phyag rgya chen mo 'ba' zhig la brten dgos pa ni sgrub le'i brgya go dgu pa las/
sems ni rnyog pa dang bcas las kyi phyag rgya 'di dang btags pa'i ye shes phyag rgya spang bya ste/ / yang dag rdzogs pa'i byang chub ched du rgyal ba mchog gi skyed ma mchog gi phyag rgya gos pa med/ / rnam par 'gyur ba med cing mkha' mnyam mun bcom khyab byed rnal 'byor dag gis bgrod bya ther zug gnas/ / ye shes gzi brjid srid pa'i dri ma 'phrog cing dus kyi 'khor los rjes su rig pa bsgom par bya/[437] / zhes gsungs pa dang / /

The necessity for the practitioner of high intelligence to abandon activity and wisdom mudrā consorts and to rely solely on a mahāmudrā consort once he has developed the ability to generate unchanging bliss, and for practitioners of middling and low intelligence to do the same once they have developed the ability to induce unchanging bliss solely in reliance upon the mahāmudrā consort, is taught in verse 199 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter:
Mind abandons impure activity mudrā consorts and mentally conceived wisdom mudrā consorts. For the attainment of perfect enlightenment, the she-creator of supreme buddha, supreme, unsullied mudrā consort, unchanging in aspect, all-pervading, dispelling darkness vast as space, the path traveled by yogis, forever unchanging, the radiance of gnosis destroying the impurities of existence, meditate upon this wisdom of Kālacakra.[453]

d.div: [437] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka199_98_na1
[453] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 199, 98a1.

f.d:
phyag rgya sgyu ma'i zhes sogs dang bcas pa mchog mi 'gyur gyi mdor bsdus su drangs shing /[438] de'i 'tshams sbyar du/ phyag rgya chen mo'i mtshan nyid gsungs pa [439] zhes pa dang / yang mdor bsdus de nyid du rtsa rgyud drangs pa ni/
las kyi phyag rgya btags pa yi/ / ye shes phyag rgya yongs spangs nas/ / mchog tu mi 'gyur sbyor ba yis/ / phyag rgya chen mo rnam par bsgom/[440] / zhes gsungs pa rnams kyis bstan to/ /

The verse beginning “Mudrā, like an illusion”[454] quoted in the Supreme and Unchanging summary is prefaced by the words “The characteristics of the mahāmudrā consort are spoken of.” Also the Root Tantra, quoted in the same summary, says:
Abandoning activity mudrā consorts and conceived wisdom mudrā consorts, meditate upon the mahāmudrā with the yoga of the supreme and unchanging.[455]

d.div: [438] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 414_na7
[439] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 114_na5
[440] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 414_ba1
[454] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 414a7.
[455] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 414b1.

f.d: bzhi pa tshad ma gang yin dpyad pa ni

rdo rje snying 'grel las/
rnam par rtog pa dang bral ba'i sems kyi snang brnyan mthong ba'o/ / rtog pa dang bral zhing ma 'khrul ba ni mngon sum zhes brjod par bya'o/ / de nyid rnam pa bzhi ste dbang po'i mngon sum dang / yid kyi mngon sum dang / rnal 'byor mngon sum dang / rang rig pa'i mngon sum zhes pa ste zhes pa de dag nyid ni nye bar ston par byed pa dang / 'jug par byed pa dang / thob par byed pa dang / nyams su myong ba'i mtshan nyid can no/[441] /zhes pa'o/ / zhes gsungs pa ltar sbyor ba yan lag drug mngon sum du 'jog pa ni stong gzugs kyi snang ba la rtog bral ma 'khrul ba yin pa'i cha nas mngon sum mo/ / de yang rang rang gi skabs kyi stong gzugs rnams gsal bar snang bas rtog bral dang / stong gzugs gsal bar snang ba tsam gyi cha la ma 'khrul zhing mi slu bas tshad mar 'jog pa'o/ / de la yan lag dang po lnga tshad ma gang yin pa ni bshad zin pa ltar yin zhing / 'di tshad ma gang yin pa ni stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa'i rnal 'byor mngon sum du 'os na'ang / rje bus/ mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba nyams su myong ba'i shes pa rtog bral ma 'khrul ba yin pas rang rig mngon sum mo [442] zhes gsungs shing / rgyal tshab rin po che yang rang rig mngon sum du bzhed do/ /[443]

The Vajragarbha Commentary says: /495/
Apparitions are seen by a nonconceptual mind. A nonconceptualizing and nonmistaken cognition is said to be a direct cognition. This is of four kinds: direct sensory cognition, direct mental cognition, direct yogic cognition, and direct self-knowing cognition. These reveal, engage, attain, and experience.[456] As this quote makes clear, the way that the six-branched yogas are determined as being direct cognitions is from the point of view of the cognition being nonmistaken and nonconceptual regarding the empty forms. These empty-form apparitions are clear unobstructed appearances, and the cognition therefore is nonconceptual. The cognition is unmistaken and undeceived as regards the appearance of these empty forms and is therefore a valid cognition. It has already been explained what type of valid cognition the first five branches are. This sixth branch can be classified as yogic valid cognition directly perceiving emptiness. However, because it is a nonconceptual, nonmistaken consciousness experiencing supreme and unchanging bliss, Butön Rinpoché has called it a direct self-knowing cognition.[457] Gyaltsap Rinpoché also asserts it to be a direct self-knowing cognition.[458]

f.d: lnga pa dag dbye ni/

dag bya gzugs kyi phung po'i sde tshan gyi chos drug dag par byed cing / dbye na g.yas g.yon gyi dkyil 'khor lnga lnga'i rlung bcu 'gog pas bcu'o/ / de ltar yang sgrub le'i brgya bco lnga pa'i 'grel chen las/
dpal ldan ting 'dzin 'khor lo can [444] zhes pa rnam par snang mdzad de ting 'dzin rnam pa bcu ni rlung bcu po rnams 'gog pa'i phyir ro zhes pa'o/ /

The form aggregate group of six phenomena is purified by this branch. Purification can be divided into the ten types because of the cessation of the five mandala winds of the right and five mandala winds of the left. The Great Commentary on verse 115 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter states:
“The glorious meditative concentration is the wheel carrier.” This refers to Vairocana. Meditative concentration is of ten kinds because of the cessation of the ten winds.[459]

f.d: drug pa 'bras bu
['di ]la gnyis las

dang po gnas skabs kyi 'bras bu ni sgrub le'i brgya bcu dgu pa'i 'grel chen las/
de nas ting nge 'dzin gyi dag pa zhes pa ni 'dir gzung ba dang 'dzin pa'i sems dag gcig pa nyid kyis gang zhig 'gyur ba med pa'i bde bar gyur pa'i bde ba de ni ting nge 'dzin du [445] gsungs so/ / de'i phyir ting nge 'dzin gyis dag pa dri ma med par gyur pa ni nyin zhag 'ga' zhig rnams kyis te lo gsum dang phyogs gsum gyi nyin zhag rnams kyis ye shes sku ni 'grub par 'gyur zhes pa dbang bcu la sogs thob pa'i byang chub sems dpar 'gyur te/ zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

On the immediate results the Great Commentary, on verse 119 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter, says:
“Then the purification accomplished by meditative concentration”: this refers to the apprehending consciousness and objects apprehended becoming as one. The unchanging bliss it produces is spoken of as meditative concentration. Therefore the purification accomplished by meditative concentration is that “in a few days,” referring to the days of three years and three fortnights,[460] the “gnosis form will be accomplished.” This refers to enlightenment with its attainment of the ten powers and so forth.[461] /496/

f.d:
gnyis pa mthar thug gi 'bras bu ni/ gzugs kyi phung po dang / sa'i khams dang / lus kyi dbang po dang / dri'i skye mched dang / bshang lam dang / rjod pa ste chos drug sgrib bral du gyur pa las rnam par snang mdzad sogs drug 'grub pa'o/ / de ltar na/
rjes dran stong gzugs phyag rgya'i chu skyes kyis/ / mi 'gyur bde ba chen po'i 'dren tshul shes/[446] / zhes pa'i rdo rje'i tshig gis don rgyas par bshad pa'i sgo nas rjes dran dang ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag ste rdzogs pa'i rim pa bshad zin to/ /

Concerning the ultimate results, the aggregate of form, the earth element, the organ of the body, the sensory source of smell, the anus, and the action of speaking are the six phenomena transformed into nonobscuration to become Vairocana and so forth.
Know how the lotus of the empty-form mudrā consort in recollection yoga induces great unchanging bliss.[462] Therefore, with an extensive explanation of these vajra words, the branches of recollection and meditative concentration, and the completion stage itself, have been explained.

sgron gsal las/
zhi sogs bya ba'i cho ga dang / / de bzhin grub pa brgyad dang ni/[447] / zhes bshad pa ltar dngos grub chung ngu zhi rgyas sogs las chen bcu gnyis sam brgyad kyis bsgrub pa rnams dang 'bring grub pa brgyad rnams te rgyas par rgyud 'grel chen dang bcas pa las shes par bya'o/ /

Bright Lamp says:
Activity rituals, pacification and so forth, likewise the eight siddhis.[463] The immediate results of the generation stage are the lower siddhis such as pacification and increase, which are achieved by the twelve or eight great activities, as well as the eight middling siddhis. A more extensive explanation can be known from the tantra and commentary.

f.d: rang rang gi skabs su bshad pa ltar ro/ /
These can be known from the sections on each of the branches.
gnyis pa mthar thug gi 'bras bu ni/

de yang bskyed rdzogs gnyis ka'i mthar thug gi 'bras bu ni yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang nyid yin te/
zhi sogs bya ba'i cho ga dang / de bzhin grub pa brgyad dang ni/ / sangs rgyas kyang ni mchog yin no/[448] / zhes bskyed rdzogs kyi 'bras bu la tha ma 'bring mchog gsum yod pa'i tha ma zhi rgyas sogs dang 'bring grub pa brgyad bskyed rdzogs gnyis kyi 'bras bu yin par ma zad mchog sangs rgyas kyang bskyed rdzogs gnyis ka'i 'bras bu yin no/ /zhes pa'i don yin pas so/ /

The ultimate result of the generation and completion stages is the attainment of full and perfect enlightenment:
Activity rituals, pacification and so forth, likewise the eight siddhis; enlightenment also, the supreme.[464] The generation and completion stages produce lower, middling, and supreme results. The lower results are the siddhis of pacification, increase, and so forth, and the middling results are the eight siddhis. These are not the only results, because “enlightenment also” is the supreme result of the two stages.

f.d: de yang gong du bshad pa ltar bskyed rim mthar phyin par byas nas rdzogs rim khyad par can dngos su skye ba'i rgyud smin pa na sor sdud nas ting nge 'dzin gyi yan lag gi bar bshad zin pa ltar nyams su blangs pa las skad cig gcig la mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas pa zhes bya ba mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma nyi khri chig stong drug brgya rdzogs pa'i mthar dang por mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas nas/ de'i rjes la sangs rgyas kyi bde ba chen po'i rnal 'byor skad cig thams cad la bzang ngan gyi rim pa med pa/ bzang ngan gyi rim pa'i gcig dang du ma dang bral ba mchog gi thabs shes gnyis su med par 'gyur ba yin no/ /

The generation stage, as previously explained, /497/ is completed when the mindstream has been ripened for the actual development of the special completion stage, whose branches from withdrawal to meditative concentration are practiced as has been described. From this arises “full and perfect enlightenment by single instances.” This means that after the completion of 21,600 instances of supreme and unchanging bliss comes the initial accomplishment of enlightenment. Then comes the yoga of the great bliss of complete enlightenment, where all instances are without differences of quality, whether one or many, the supreme nonduality of method and wisdom.

de ltar yang khams le'i mdor bsdus lnga pa las/
'dir skad cig thams cad rnam par sgom pa po skad cig gcig la mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas zhes pa gang yin pa de ni mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig drug brgya lhag pa'i stong phrag nyi shu rtsa gcig sgom pa po mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig dang por mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas nas de'i rjes la sangs rgyas rnams kyi rnal 'byor skad cig thams cad rim pa med pa gcig dang du ma dang bral ba mchog gi gnyis su med pa ste/[449] zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

This is spoken of in the fifth summary of the Realms chapter:
Here the meditator meditating upon all the instances attains “full and perfect enlightenment by single instances.” This means that the practitioner meditating upon the 21,600 instances of supreme unchanging bliss firstly attains full and perfect enlightenment by instances of supreme unchanging bliss. After that comes the yoga of complete enlightenment, the supreme nonduality, where all instances are without difference, whether one or many.[465]

f.d:
gzhan yang ye le'i brgya re gnyis pa las/
zla ba nyi ma'i rgyu ba nyams shing lam ni gnyi ga yi yang srog gi rlung ni chen po 'gags/ / chu skyes rdo rje rab tu sad cing ri bong can zhu nyi ma'i gzugs can pa ni rab tu zhugs/ / dngos dang dngos med gcig gyur rnam gsum srid par gnas pa'i gzhom med legs par rab tu rtogs gyur pa/ / de yi dus su rnal 'byor pa de gang la gnyis ni cung zad med pa mchog gi go 'phang 'gro/ / khro bo sangs rgyas lha mo dang bcas nges par ro yi rdo rje rnams dang sa yi snying po sogs/ / rab tu dga' ba'i thugs rnams rnal 'byor pa la grub pa'i dus su nam mkha' la ni mngon sum 'gyur/ / de yi 'dod pa'i dngos grub ri bong can gyi zhag gi tho rangs dang ni mtshan mo phyed la 'gyur/ / rin po che'am me tog char ni mchog gyur dus kyi sbyor bas sa yi steng du 'bab par 'gyur/[450] / zhes gsungs pa ltar te de dag gi don cung zad cig bshad na/ zla ba nyi ma g.yon g.yas kyi rlung gi rgyu ba nyams shing / der yang ma zad ro rkyang gi lam ni gnyi ga'i yang srog gi rlung chen po ste las rlung ma lus par 'gags pa dang / yum gyi chu skyes pad+mar rnal 'byor pa rang gi rdo rje sad cing rengs pa las dpral ba nas ri bong can thig le zhu ba rdo rje nor bu'i rtse nas gtsug tor gyi bar brtan par byas pa de nyid nyi ma'i gzugs rdul byang sems dmar po'i cha gtsug tor nas rdo rje nor bu'i bar brtan par byas na nyi ma'i gzugs chen po la ni rab tu zhugs pas dngos po thabs mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po dang dngos med shes rab stong gzugs phyag rgya chen mo ngo bo dbyer med gcig tu gyur pa rnam gsum srid par ste khams gsum na gnas pa'i sems can thams cad kyi snying la gnas pa'i gzhom med kyi sgra thams cad legs par rtogs pa de'i dus su de 'dra ba'i rnal 'byor pa gang yin pa de ni thabs shes ngo bo tha dad pa gnyis ni cung zad kyang med pa mchog gi go 'phang zung 'jug mthar thug pa der 'gro ba'o/ /

Furthermore verse 162 of the Gnosis chapter says:
The flow of the moon and sun is weakened, the great winds of the two paths also are halted, the lotus awakens the vajra, the moon melts and engages with the great form of the sun. Phenomena and nonphenomena become one, the indestructible is seen in the three-existence forms. At that time, as he moves to the supreme level, there is not the slightest nonduality for such a yogi. The wrathful, the buddhas, goddesses, Rasavajrā, Kṣitigarbha, and so forth, manifest in space minds of great joy to the yogi at this time of accomplishment. On a solar day of the moon, at dawn and midnight, the desired siddhi of the yogi arises. Because of the moment, rains of jewels or flowers fall to earth.[466] To explain these verses a little: the flow of the left and right moon and sun winds is weakened, /498/ and in the pathways of the left and right channels the “great wind,” or karmic winds, are completely halted. The lotus of the consort awakens and stiffens the vajra of the yogi, causing the moon drops to melt from the forehead and to stabilize from the tip of the vajra jewel to the crown. This “engages with the great form of the sun,” which refers to the sun specks of red bodhicitta stabilized from the crown down to the vajra jewel. Because of this, “phenomena,” referring to method or unchanging bliss, and “nonphenomena,” referring to wisdom or the empty-form mahāmudrā consort, become indivisibly one. All indestructible sounds abiding in the hearts of all beings living in the “three-existence forms,” or three realms, are well perceived and seen. At that time for such a yogi there is not the slightest separation between method and wisdom as he moves to the supreme level of ultimate union.

d.div: [450] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka162_117_ba7_dang 163
[466] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, vv. 162–63, 117b7.

f.d: mthar thug pa'i go 'phang der song ste mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i rab tu dga' ba'i thugs mthar thug pa rnams rnal 'byor pa de la grub pa'i dus su rang rgyud kyi phung khams so drug sgrib bral du gyur pa gshin rje gshed la sogs pa'i khro bo rnams dang / rdo rje sems dpa' sogs sangs rgyas rnam dang / sna tshogs yum la sogs pa'i lha mo dang bcas pa rnams dang / ro yi rdo rje ma sogs rdo rje ma rnams dang / sa'i snying po sogs byang chub sems dpa' rnams nam mkha' la ni mngon sum du 'gyur ro/ / rnal 'byor pa de'i 'dod pa'i dngos grub zung 'jug gi go 'phang mthar thug pa de ri bong can gyi nyin zhag ste nyin zhag gcig gang dang gang yin pa'i nyin zhag de'i tho rangs dang mtshan mo phyed kyi cha gang yang rung ba kho na la mngon du byed do/ / de'i dus su rin po che'i char ram me tog gi char ni mchog tu gyur pa mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas pa'i dus kyi sbyor ba'i dbang gis sa gzhi'i steng du 'bab par 'gyur ro/ /

Having arrived at this ultimate level, the yogi possesses minds of supreme and ultimate joy. At this time of accomplishment, the thirty-six phenomena associated with his being, consisting of the aggregates, elements, and so forth, are all freed of obscuration. Wrathful deities such as Yamāntaka, buddhas such as Vajrasattva, goddesses such as Viśvamātā, female vajra bodhisattvas such as Rasavajrā, and male bodhisattvas such as Kṣitigarbha all manifest in space. This desired siddhi of the yogi, the ultimate level of union, is realized on a “solar day of the moon,” meaning on a particular solar day at midnight or at dawn. Due to the power of this moment of supreme and complete enlightenment, a rain of jewels or a rain of flowers falls to earth.

de ltar bla na med pa'i byang chub mngon du byas pa'i rnal 'byor de'i lus ngag sems gsum gyi gnas tshul ston pa ni snga ma'i 'phro nyid las/
lus ni dang zhing rdul phran nyams pa nam mkha' dang mtshungs mtshan la sogs pa rnams kyis rab rdzogs 'gyur/ / sna tshogs 'jig rten gsum pa nyid ni dang zhing sgrib pa rnam par bral ba rmi lam bzhin du snang / / skad ni kun nas chad pa med cing du ma'i skad gzhan dag gis gzhan gyi snying la 'jug pa ste/ / sems ni dam pa'i bde bas gang zhing mi g.yo thams cad dus su lhan cig skyes pas 'khyud pa'o/[451] / zhes pa ste/ de'i don cung zad cig bshad na/ mthar thug gi zung 'jug mngon du byas pa'i rnal 'byor pa 'di'i lus ni rdul phran tshogs pa'i lus rags pa de nyams shing / stong gzugs dus kyi 'khor lo yab yum gyi rnam pa can shin tu dwangs shing sgrib thogs dang bral bas nam mkha' dang mtshungs pa mtshan bzang po sum cu rtsa gnyis dang / la sogs pa dpe byad rnams kyi rab tu rdzogs par gyur pa'i sku'am lus so/ / de yang rnal 'byor pa de'i rang snang la sna tshogs pa'i 'jig rten gsum po nyid ni shel ltar dwangs shing sgrib thogs dang bral ba/ sgrib gnyis kyi dri ma dang rnam par bral ba rmi lam bzhin du snang ba'o/ /

The status of the body, speech, and mind of the yogi who has realized this highest enlightenment is taught in the next verses:
The body is of clarity, devoid of atoms, like the sky, well completed by the signs and so forth. The three worlds are clear, free of obscuration, and like appearances in a dream. Speech is completely unbroken, in languages of many, entering the hearts of others. /499/ Mind is full of the highest bliss, unmoving, at all times embraced by the innate.[467] These verses will be explained a little. For the yogi who has achieved the ultimate union, the coarse body composed of atoms has gone. The empty-form Kālacakra in mother-father aspect is of total clarity, devoid of obscuration and obstruction, and is therefore like the sky. It is a body perfected by the thirty-two signs of an enlightened being and by the eighty marks, referred to by the words “and so forth.” To the mind of the yogi the three worlds are as clear as crystal, free of obscuration. They are dreamlike appearances, untainted by the contamination of the two types of obscurations.

d.div: [451] sde dge_362_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_bsdus rgyud/ sh+loka164_118_na3
[467] Toh 362 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, v. 164, 118a3.

f.d: yang rnal 'byor pa de'i skad dam gsung ni kun nas te dus nam yang rgyud chad pa med cing sems can du ma mtha' yas pa'i rang rang gi skad dang mthun pa'i skad gzhan dag gis te/ gzhan sems can mtha' yas pa'i snying la ste sems la mthun par 'jug pa'i skad dam gsung ngo / / yang rnal 'byor pa de'i sems sam thugs ni dam pa mchog tu mi 'gyur ba'i bde bas gang zhing bde ba chen po de yang stong pa nyid la rtse gcig tu mnyam par bzhag pa'i mnyam gzhag de las skad cig kyang mi g.yo zhing dus thams cad du lhan cig skyes pa'i 'od gsal gyi sems kyis 'khyud pa'i sems sam thugs so/ /

The speech of the yogi is “completely unbroken,” meaning that its continuum is never severed. “In the languages of many,” meaning in languages that accord with those of countless living beings, it enters accordingly “the hearts,” or minds, of countless other living beings. The mind of the yogi is filled with the highest and supreme bliss one-pointedly focused upon emptiness. It never moves from its meditation for an instant and at all times is embraced by the innate clear-light mind.

de ltar tshigs su bcad pa 'dis sku gsung thugs ye shes rdo rje ste rdo rje bzhi dang sku bzhi po rnams bstan to/ / de yang ji ltar du bstan na/ sku gsung thugs rdo rje gsum bstan pa ni shin tu gsal la/ ye shes rdo rje ni/ dam pa'i bde bas gang zhing zhes pa 'dis bstan te/ / bde ba chen po mthar thug pa ye shes rdo rjer 'jog pas so/ / yang sku bzhi bstan tshul ni/ lus ni dang zhing zhes sogs tshig rkang gnyis po des mtshan dpes brgyan pa'i longs sku dang / rtsa ba'i sprul sku dngos su bstan cing / des mtshon nas sprul pa'i sku mtha' yas pa rnams bstan te/ de yang mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba skad ci+ig ma tha ma'i mthar dang por mngon du byas pa'i stong gzugs mtshan dpes brgyan pa'i sku ni longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku dang / des dngos su spros pa'i khams gsum ma lus khyab pa'i stong gzugs kyi sku mtshan dpes brgyan pa du ma longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku zhes gsungs pa rnams ni rtsa ba'i sprul sku ste/ de dag ni/ lus ni dang zhing zhes sogs kyis dngos su bstan pa yin no/ /

These verses teach the four bodies and the four vajras of body, speech, mind, and gnosis. How? The body, speech, and mind vajras are clearly taught. The gnosis vajra is indicated by the line “Mind is full of the highest bliss” because the ultimate bliss is established as being the gnosis vajra. Concerning the four bodies, the two lines beginning “The body is of clarity” directly teach the saṃbhogakāya enjoyment body adorned with the signs and marks and implies the nirmāṇakāya basic emanation body with its countless emanations. The empty form adorned with signs and marks that is first actualized at the end of the last instance of unchanging bliss is the saṃbhogakāya, whereas the manifestation of empty forms or “manifold saṃbhogakāya forms” adorned with the signs and marks and directly produced by that saṃbhogakāya to pervade the three realms is the basic nirmāṇakāya. /500/ Both these are directly taught by the lines beginning “The body is of clarity.”

de yang khams gsum ma lus pa khyab pa'i stong gzugs du ma longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku zhes pa ni 'grel chen las gsal bar gsungs te/ sgrub le'i nyis brgya so gnyis pa'i 'grel chen las/
de dag las mngon sum gang yin pa dag ni de nyid sbyor bas mkha' la skar ma bzhin du 'gyur te skar ma'i tshogs bzhin du du ma longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku zhes pa ni sha la sogs pa'i mig gis gzung bar bya ba srid pa gsum dang dus gsum rmi lam dang sgyu ma dang mtshungs pa'o/[452] / zhes sogs kyis gsal bar bstan to/ /

These empty-form “manifold saṃbhogakāya forms” pervading the three realms are clearly taught in the Great Commentary. On verse 232 of the Methods of Accomplishment chapter it says:
With the application of direct cognition “manifold saṃbhogakāya forms like stars in the sky,” meaning like a host of stars, are seen with the fleshly eye and so forth in the three worlds and the three times like dreams and illusions.[468]

d.div: [452] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 258_na2
[468] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 258a2.

f.d:
gal te de ni sor sdud sogs kyi skabs kyi stong gzugs mthong tshul yin no snyam na/ de'i 'phro nyid las/
de nas yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi 'tshams kyi thugs kyi dbang gis ye shes kyi spyan gyis gzigs te/[453] zhes sangs rgyas pa'i gnas skabs su ye shes kyi spyan gyis gzigs par yang gsungs pas 'dis gzigs pa na dngos gnas la grub pa'i skar ma'i tshogs bzhin gyi sangs rgyas kyi sku mtshan dpes brgyan pa nyid yin no/ /

But isn’t this how empty forms are seen during withdrawal and the other branches? The Great Commentary continues:
With the attainment of full and perfect enlightened mind, they are seen by the gnosis eye.[469] This teaches that at the time of enlightenment, these forms are seen by the gnosis eye. Therefore the forms are actual buddha forms adorned with the signs and marks and appearing like a host of stars.

d.div: [453] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 258_na5
[469] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 258a5.

f.d:
'o na sangs rgyas kyi gzhom med kyi gsung 'di pa'i lugs kyi longs skur 'jog pa ma yin nam/ mtshan dpes brgyan pa'i longs skur ji ltar 'gyur snyam na/ sangs rgyas kyi gsung la longs skur gsungs pa bden na'ang mtshan dpes brgyan pa'i longs sku'ang rgyud 'grel las gsungs te/ khams le'i mdor bsdus gsum pa las/
sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' 'di gnyis ston pa po dang gsol ba 'debs pa por 'brel ba ni sprul pa'i sku'am longs spyod rdzogs pa'i skus kyang rung ste/ snga ma dang phyi ma la 'gal ba med do/[454] / zhes dang
rdzu 'phrul bstan nas sprul pa'i sku gang nas byon pa longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku de nyid du gshegs so/ / zhes zla bzang gis sprul pa bsdus nas rang nyid kyi longs skur gshegs par gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

But in this tradition doesn’t the saṃbhogakāya enjoyment body refer to the indestructible speech of the buddha? How can there be a saṃbhogakāya adorned with the signs and marks? It is true that the speech of the buddha is known as the saṃbhogakāya, but the tantra also talks of a saṃbhogakāya adorned with the signs and marks. In the third summary of the Realms chapter it says:
These two, the buddha and the bodhisattva, are related as teacher and requestor by way of nirmāṇakāyas or saṃbhogakāyas. The former and the latter are not contradictory.[470] Also:
He displayed the mandalas and magical creations, then entered the saṃbhogakāya, source of the nirmāṇakāya.[471] This teaches that Sucandra withdrew his emanations and entered his own saṃbhogakāya.

d.div: [454] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 21_ba1
[470] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 21b1.
[471] P 2064 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ka-2, 24b5.

f.d:
des mtshon nas bstan pa'i sprul pa'i sku mtha' yas pa ni khams le'i mdor bsdus gsum pa las/
sngon gyi smon lam gyi stobs kyi bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs yongs su rdzogs shing mi 'jigs pa la sogs pa dbang phyug gi yon tan thams cad phun sum tshogs pa'i sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das ni sangs rgyas kyi zhing stong gsum gyi stong chen po'i 'jig rten gyi khams rnams su sgyu ma'i sprul pa'i sku sgrib pa dang bral ba mtha' yas pa mtha' yas pa rnams kyis sems can mtha' yas pa rnams kyi skad mtha' yas pa mtha' yas pa rnams kyis gsol ba 'debs pa po sna tshogs kyis gsol ba btab pa na sems can thams cad kyi skad la rab tu 'jug pa thams cad mkhyen pa'i gsung gis 'jig rten dang 'jig rten las 'das pa'i chos ston par mdzad de thams cad mkhyen pa de du ma ni ma yin no/ / dper na skyes bu sgyu ma chen po 'ga' zhig gis sgyu ma'i gzugs du ma sprul te des sprul pa'i gzugs de rnams kyis shing rnams rtsa ba nas 'byin par byed cing ri'i rtse mo yang skyod par byed la lha chen po'i gzugs lta bu dang khyab 'jug lta bus lhas byin la sogs pa 'ching bar byed de skyes bu sgyu ma chen po de du ma ni ma yin no/ / de bzhin du sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi sgyu ma'i sprul pa'i sku rnams kyis srid pa gsum du sems can gyi don mdzad pa'o/[455] / zhes gsungs pa ltar te/

The nirmāṇakāya implied by the saṃbhogakāya enjoyment body is spoken of in the third summary of the Realms chapter as being of countless manifestations: /501/
By the force of previous prayers and with all wisdom and merit accumulations complete, glorious qualities such as fearlessness all perfected, the conquering Buddha in countless emanated illusory and nonobscured forms in the great thousand world realms employs the languages of every living being when various requestors request the Buddha in the limitless tongues of limitless living beings. With omniscient speech he teaches worldly and nonworldly dharma. Yet the Omniscient One is not more than one. For example, someone with great powers of illusion will manifest many forms, and with the forms he has created he will uproot trees and shake mountaintops. In the guises of Mahādeva and Viṣṇu, he will bind Devadatta and others. Yet this great illusionist is not more than one person. In this way, the illusory emanations of buddhas and bodhisattvas work for living beings.[472]

d.div: [455] sde dge_845_bka'/ rgyud/ shrI_'grel chen dri med 'od/ 20_ba7
[472] Toh 845 Kangyur, rgyud, śrī, 20b7.

f.d: de yang sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das rnams ni sngon bsags pa'i tshogs gnyis yongs su rdzogs pa dang smon lam gyi stobs kyis mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba chen po stong pa nyid dang ro gcig tu gyur pa'i rnam par mi rtog pa la skad cig gcig kyang g.yo ba med bzhin du rang snang la khams gsum po ma lus pa sgrib pa dang rnam par bral pa pra phab pa ltar dang zhing gsal ba rmi lam bzhin du snang ba dang / gzhan snang la ma dag pa'i khams gsum po sogs ma lus pa snang ba'i sgo nas shes bya ji snyed pa thams cad lag mthil du skyu ru ra bzhag pa ltar mkhyen pa'i ngang nas mtha' yas pa mtha' yas pa'i sprul pa'i sku sprul te sprul sku re res kyang mtha' yas pa mtha' yas pa'i sems can rnams la rang rang gi skad dang mthun pa'i gsung gis rang rang gi blo dang 'tshams pa'i chos ston pa sogs ji srid nam mkha' ma zhig gi bar du sems can gyi don 'ba' zhig mdzad pa rnams so/ /

As this passage indicates, by the power of prayers and the completion of the two accumulations, the conquering buddhas do not move even for an instant from the nonconceptual state of unchanging bliss and emptiness united as one taste. At the same time the three realms appear to them as a dream, without obscuration, and as clear as images in a prognostic mirror. By knowing how the three realms appear in impure aspect to the minds of others, they see the complete extent of existent conventional phenomena as clearly as a berry in the palm of the hand. From this omniscience there emerges limitless emanated forms, each of which employs speech that accords with languages of limitless living beings and teaches a dharma that is disposed to the minds of each these beings. In this way the buddhas work solely for the benefit of living beings for as long as space lasts. /502/

yang skad ni kun nas chad pa med cing zhes sogs tshig rkang gcig pu 'dis sangs rgyas kyi gsung dus nam yang rgyun chad med cing sems can du ma ste mtha' yas pa'i rang rang gi skad sna tshogs dang mthun pa gzhan sems can de dag gi snying la ste sems la sim par 'jug par bstan pa ni rnam pa thams cad pa'i sangs rgyas kyi gsung longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku'o/ / yang sems ni zhes sogs tshig rkang bzhi pa 'di'i sems ni dam pa'i bde bas gang zhing zhes pa 'dis 'gyuramed kyi bde ba chen pos stong pa nyid la ro gcig tu zhugs pas ngo bo nyid sku'am bde ba chen po'i sku bstan/ mi g.yo thams cad dus su lhan cig skyes pas 'khyud pa'o zhes pa 'dis lhan skyes 'od gsal gyi sems stong pa nyid la ro gcig tu zhugs pa'i chos sku bstan pa yin no/ /

The line from the above verses that begins “Speech is completely unbroken” teaches that the continuum of speech of the Buddha is at no time severed and “in languages of many,” meaning in accord with each of the differing languages of limitless living beings, it “enters the hearts of others,” meaning that it satisfies the minds of those living beings. This teaches the saṃbhogakāya as the speech of a buddha. The “mind” in the third line, “Mind is full of the highest bliss,” is one of unchanging bliss dwelling indivisibly in emptiness. This line, therefore, teaches the svabhāvikakāya nature body, or great bliss body. “Unmoving, at all times embraced by the innate” teaches the innate clear-light mind dwelling indivisibly with emptiness and therefore teaches the dharmakāya.

yang waM yig gis mtshon pa'i mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba mthar thug pa stong pa nyid la ro gcig tu zhugs pa dang / e yig gis mtshon pa'i rnam kun mchog ldan gyi stong gzugs ngo bo dbyer med pa'i 'bras bu mthar thug pa dang / yang waM yig gis gzugs kyi cha shas lngas mtshon pa phung sogs kyi chos sum cu rtsa drug sde tshan lngar byas pa'i sgrib bral du gyur pa dang / e yig gis gzugs kyi cha shas drug gis mtshon pa khams sogs kyi chos so drug sde tshan drug tu byas pa sgrib bral du gyur pa/ thabs shes ngo bo dbyer med pa rnams ni 'bras bu mthar thug pa'i gnas skabs so/ / de ltar 'bras bu'i rnam gzhag mdor bsdus pa tsam ste rgyas par rgyud 'grel chen dang bcas pa las shes par bya'o// //

The ultimate unchanging bliss merged inseparably with emptiness, as signified by the letter vaṃ, indivisible from form endowed with supreme characteristics, as signified by the letter e, represents the ultimate result. Furthermore the thirty-six phenomena of the aggregates and so forth, free of obscuration, and arranged in five categories are signified by the five parts of the letter vaṃ. The thirty-six phenomena of the elements and so forth, free from obscuration and arranged in six categories, are signified by the six parts of the letter e. These indivisible method and wisdom phenomena are phenomena of the final result. This has been a brief presentation of the resultant state. A more extensive description can be known from the Great Commentary and the tantra.
smon tshig dang mjug byang /

phyi nang gzhan gsum rin chen pad+mo'i tshal/ / rim gnyis 'bras bu ze 'bru'i so 'phreng can/ / gsal byed lung rigs bye ba'i 'od 'phro ba/ / legs bshad nyin byed dbang po deng 'dir shar/ / de ltar rgyud 'grel rgya mtsho'i snying po mchog/ rnam kun mchog ldan bde chen dbyer med lam/ / legs ston 'di la 'bad pa'i dge tshogs gang / / 'gro kun bla med byang chub thob phyir bsngo/ / bdag kyang tshe 'di'i snang ba nub tsam na/ / grub pa'i gnas mchog sham b+ha lar grags pa/ / rigs ldan rgyal po sa skyong sprul pa yis/ / ma nor lam ston zhing der skye bar shog/ der yang sku gsung thugs ni yongs rdzogs pa'i/ / rin chen du mas spras pa'i blos bslang der/ / yongs rdzogs dbang bskur mchog ni nod gyur nas/ / dam tshig sdom pa srog bzhin srung bar shog/ dbang gis rgyud smin rim gnyis snod gyur nas/ / bskyed rdzogs bsnyen sgrub bzhi ldan lam gyi mchog/ mi 'gyur bde ba nyi khri chig stong dang / / drug brgya'i lam gyis sku bzhi thob par shog/ rgyud 'grel rgya mtsho'i gting mtha' dpag par dka'/ / bdag ni blo gros nyam chung brtson pa zhan/ / de phyir 'di la nongs pa'i tshogs mchis pa/ / bla ma lha tshogs mkha' 'gro'i tshogs la 'chags/ / nongs pa ma lus dag par mdzad du gsol/ / zhes phyi nang gzhan gsum gyi don gsal bar byed pa dri med 'od kyi rgyan ces bya ba 'di ni/ bstan pa rin po che la mchog tu gces spras su mdzad pa'i chos rgyal chen po nang so rdo rje tshe brtan pa'i bka' stsal dang du blangs te/ bka' dang bstan bcos 'gyur ro 'tshal gyi bang mdzod ri bo sde chen chos kyi pho brang du dbu btsugs te bkra shis steng kha zhes bya ba'i ri khrod du bya ba btang ba nor bzang rgya mchos rdzogs par sbyar ba'o/ /

The precious lotus garden of the inner, outer, and other, adorned with stamen garlands of two stages and results, radiates light of millions of illuminating scripture and reasoning. May this mighty sun of excellent explanation shine here now. /503/ Whatever virtue is to be gained from these efforts to explain the path of indivisibility of great bliss with form supremely endowed, supreme essence of the ocean of tantra and commentary, is dedicated for every living being to attain the highest enlightenment. For me too, when appearances of this life fade, may I be reborn in the greatest place of practice, the land known as Shambhala, there to be taught unerringly the path by the Kalkī king Mahipala.[473] There in a three-dimensional mandala of the complete body, speech, and mind, adorned with many precious jewels, may I receive complete and supreme initiation and hold vows and pledges as I would hold my life. With mind ripened by initiation, a vessel fit for the two stages, then by the practice of the greatest of all paths, the stages of completion and generation, the four levels of approximation and accomplishment, by the path of 21,600 instances of unchanging bliss, may I attain the four bodies. /504/ The ocean of this tantra and commentary is of a depth difficult to fathom, and I am of little intelligence and lacking in effort. Therefore all mistakes I have made I confess to the gurus, deities, and ḍākinīs, and ask that you correct them. Willingly acceding to the request of Dorjé Tseten, official of the great dharma king,[474] cherisher of the precious doctrine, this work entitled Ornament of Stainless Light: An Exposition of the Outer, Inner, and Other Kālacakra was begun in the dharma palace that is Riwo Dechen Monastery, a Kangyur and Tengyur treasure house, and completed in the hermitage of Tashi Tengka by the ascetic Norsang.

d.div: [473] The sixteenth Kalkī of Shambhala, who reigned from 1427–1527.

[474] The actual reading is “Nangso Dorjé Tseten, the great dharma king.” Jado Rinpoché suggests nang so to mean “an official,” in which case a genitive is implied, and the phrase reads, “Dorjé Tseten, official of the great dharma king.”

f.d: 'dis kyang bstan pa dang sems can la phan pa rgya chen po byed nus par gyur cig/
May this also bring about vast and extensive benefit to the Buddhist teachings and to all sentient beings!
mang+ga laM/ / b+ha wan+tu/ /
Maṅgalaṁ bhavantu! (May auspiciousness prevail!)

srid gsum 'gro ba kun gyi skyabs gnas gcig pu pa/ rgyal dbang chen po blo bzang rgya mtshos/ khyod kyis glegs bam 'di'i ri mor zhus dag dgos rigs rnams gyis gnang byung bar/ zhus dag nan tan du bgyis pa'i yig nor phran bu 'dug pa rnams bcos shing / ri mo lhag bcas phran bu 'jog pa gnang ba rnams la zhib brtsis su bgyis te mchan bu 'ga' zhig bdag zug po gzhon nu'i ming can gyis bris pa'o// //

The Great Sovereign of the Conquerors, Blo bzang rgya mtsho—the sole place of refuge for all migratory beings within the three realms of existence—commanded: 'You must perform the necessary proofreading for the illustrations in this volume.' Accordingly, a meticulous proofreading was carried out, and minor orthographical errors were emended. Furthermore, a detailed assessment was conducted regarding the occasional omissions left in the illustrations, and several marginal annotations were appended. Written by the one bearing the name of the young body (zug po gzhon nu).
